```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-adapters/benches/fuel_bench.rs	fuel_bench · 57 lines	//! fuel_bench — B4 placeholder-calibration bench for `FUEL_PER_UNIT` (criterion, harness=false).\n//!\n//! ## What this bench measures\n//! The cost of running the real prepaid-tranche loop `FuelTrancheRunner::run` over a\n//! `DeterministicFuelMeter::needs(N)` for a range of guest `N` (1, 8, 64, 256 fuel units).\n//! It uses `FuelTrancheRunner::new(FUEL_PER_UNIT, 1)` — a 1-unit tranche, i.e. the\n//! exact-cost wiring that matches the B1 dispatch.rs path (each tranche loads exactly the\n//! fuel for one budget unit). Criterion reports mean time / ops-per-sec per run.\n//!\n//! ## Why FUEL_PER_UNIT is a PLACEHOLDER (the B4 gap)\n//! `FUEL_PER_UNIT` (= 100_000, kernel `ports::agent`) converts billing budget-units into\n//! wasmtime CPU-fuel. It is a **B4-pending placeholder**: the REAL value must come from\n//! measuring how much wasmtime fuel a *representative guest* consumes per budget-unit, which\n//! is only observable behind the `wasmtime-fuel` feature (the real `WasmtimeFuelMeter`).\n//! This bench deliberately runs on the deterministic in-crate meter — it establishes the\n//! **loop-overhead baseline** (the `set_fuel` call + `run_slice` + bucket `try_acquire`\n//! machinery) so a future B4 pass can subtract this fixed overhead and set `FUEL_PER_UNIT`\n//! from a *measured* guest-fuel/unit ratio.\n//!\n//! ## Deterministic, NOT noisy\n//! Per AGENTS.md this is a committed-baseline bench, not a host/noisy harness bench: the\n//! meter is the deterministic reference impl (no wasmtime, no live daemon), so the numbers\n//! are reproducible and gate-able by `benches/bench_track.py`. It does NOT touch the kernel\n//! constant, dispatch.rs, or fuel.rs logic — it only exercises the public `run` API.\n\nuse agent_adapters::fuel::{DeterministicFuelMeter, FuelTrancheRunner};\nuse criterion::{black_box, criterion_group, criterion_main, Criterion};\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::FUEL_PER_UNIT;\nuse dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::TokenBucket;\n\n/// Guest fuel-unit sizes to sweep (a 1-unit tranche → one run_slice per unit, so N units\n/// means N tranches of the loop). Covers tiny (1) up to chunky (256) guest costs.\nconst NEEDS: &[u64] = &[1, 8, 64, 256];\n\n/// The loop-overhead baseline: run the real prepaid-tranche loop for a guest needing `n`\n/// fuel units, on a bucket large enough that it never exhausts (we bench cost, not refusal).\nfn bench_fuel_loop_throughput(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    // Tranche = 1 unit → exact-cost wiring (matches B1 dispatch.rs). With a 1-unit tranche\n    // and FUEL_PER_UNIT fuel loaded per tranche, a guest needing `n` units takes `n` tranches.\n    let runner = FuelTrancheRunner::new(FUEL_PER_UNIT, 1);\n\n    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("fuel_loop_throughput");\n    for &n in NEEDS {\n        // Effectively unbounded bucket so every guest completes within budget (pure cost).\n        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(f64::MAX, 0.0);\n        group.bench_function(format!("needs_{n}"), |b| {\n            b.iter(|| {\n                let mut guest = DeterministicFuelMeter::needs(n);\n                black_box(runner.run(&mut guest, &bucket)).unwrap();\n            })\n        });\n    }\n    group.finish();\n}\n\ncriterion_group!(benches, bench_fuel_loop_throughput);\ncriterion_main!(benches);\n	3	-1	-1		bb7df6835c02978243690bff18003b855d92b5eebd50b4cfea58206f9f63c1187c20308f4443e3be4107436b6745c03854707f2f946904aaf1767690f61c68af3fabbc383fc789a8d7ddcd421582eb5239d02c2a05ecf5c18ec7aeb4f801883da870c14611df72a5cca2c61f5d40529a54bf4524adfd695cb9417456716c34f3

## 23 · /root/dowiz/agent-adapters/src/cache.rs · LongTerm

Summary: cache · 180 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-adapters/src/cache.rs	cache · 180 lines	//! cache.rs — SH-2: per-agent cache partitioning, default-deny.\n//!\n//! By DEFAULT each admitted agent gets a GENUINELY SEPARATE `AgentCache` instance (its\n//! own store, capacity, and lock) — NOT a shared store with a keyspace prefix. A separate\n//! instance has no shared mutable state between tenants, so it closes the cross-tenant\n//! request-existence timing oracle AND the eviction/contention side channels a keyspace\n//! prefix would leave open (F6).\n//!\n//! The single legitimate reason to SHARE a cache — dedup between agents the operator\n//! knows are mutually trusting — is opt-in via an OPERATOR-SIGNED `cache_group_id`, read\n//! from operator config, NEVER from the manifest (self-selection into a co-tenant's\n//! keyspace is the confused-deputy risk). Absent an explicit operator co-scope, the answer\n//! is always a separate instance (fail-closed). Note there is deliberately NO cache-group\n//! axis in the manifest lattice (`config_axis_domain(0x05) == None`), so an agent CANNOT\n//! even encode a self-declared group.\n//!\n//! Cacheability follows the LLM `CachePolicy` discipline: idempotent `read_resource` calls\n//! are cacheable (`Exact`); tool invocations default to `NoCache`.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::AgentTask;\n\n/// A single agent's private response cache (content-addressed by `sha3_256`). Hit/miss\n/// counters make the SH-2 partitioning falsifiable WITHOUT timing (crit 13).\npub struct AgentCache {\n    store: Mutex<HashMap<[u8; 32], Vec<u8>>>,\n    hits: AtomicUsize,\n    misses: AtomicUsize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for AgentCache {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        AgentCache {\n            store: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),\n            hits: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n            misses: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl AgentCache {\n    /// A fresh, empty private cache.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        AgentCache::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Whether a task is cacheable: idempotent `read_resource` under `Exact`; tool\n    /// invocations are `NoCache`.\n    pub fn is_cacheable(task: &AgentTask) -> bool {\n        matches!(\n            task,\n            AgentTask::ReadResource { .. } | AgentTask::RenderPrompt { .. }\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Canonical key for a cacheable request.\n    pub fn key(canonical_request: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n        sha3_256(canonical_request)\n    }\n\n    /// Look up a cached response, counting hit/miss.\n    pub fn get(&self, key: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        let found = self.store.lock().unwrap().get(key).cloned();\n        if found.is_some() {\n            self.hits.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        } else {\n            self.misses.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        }\n        found\n    }\n\n    /// Insert a response (idempotent).\n    pub fn put(&self, key: [u8; 32], value: Vec<u8>) {\n        self.store.lock().unwrap().insert(key, value);\n    }\n\n    /// Total hits observed.\n    pub fn hits(&self) -> usize {\n        self.hits.load(Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n    /// Total misses observed.\n    pub fn misses(&self) -> usize {\n        self.misses.load(Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Provisions each admitted agent its cache. DEFAULT: a separate private instance. A\n/// shared instance is granted ONLY when the OPERATOR co-scopes agents under a signed\n/// `cache_group_id` — never from the manifest.\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct CacheProvisioner {\n    /// Operator-signed shared groups. Populated ONLY from operator config.\n    groups: HashMap<u16, Arc<AgentCache>>,\n}\n\nimpl CacheProvisioner {\n    /// Empty provisioner.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        CacheProvisioner::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Provision an agent's cache. `operator_group` comes from OPERATOR-SIGNED config\n    /// (never the manifest): `Some(g)` co-scopes into the shared instance for group `g`;\n    /// `None` (the fail-closed default) yields a fresh private instance.\n    pub fn provision(&mut self, operator_group: Option<u16>) -> Arc<AgentCache> {\n        match operator_group {\n            Some(g) => self\n                .groups\n                .entry(g)\n                .or_insert_with(|| Arc::new(AgentCache::new()))\n                .clone(),\n            None => Arc::new(AgentCache::new()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::config_axis_domain;\n\n    // ── §4 criterion 13 — per-agent cache by default; sharing is operator-only ──\n    #[test]\n    fn crit13_no_cross_agent_hit_by_default() {\n        let mut prov = CacheProvisioner::new();\n        // Two agents, NO operator co-scope ⇒ separate instances.\n        let a = prov.provision(None);\n        let b = prov.provision(None);\n        let key = AgentCache::key(b"identical-canonical-request");\n        a.put(key, b"answer".to_vec());\n        // Agent B issues the IDENTICAL request: a MISS (separate store) — verified by the\n        // store's own miss counter, NOT by timing.\n        assert_eq!(b.get(&key), None, "no cross-agent hit by default");\n        assert_eq!(b.misses(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(a.hits(), 0, "A's store served nothing to B");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn crit13_shared_only_via_operator_group() {\n        let mut prov = CacheProvisioner::new();\n        // Operator co-scopes both agents under group 7 (operator-signed, not manifest).\n        let a = prov.provision(Some(7));\n        let b = prov.provision(Some(7));\n        let key = AgentCache::key(b"identical-canonical-request");\n        a.put(key, b"answer".to_vec());\n        assert_eq!(\n            b.get(&key),\n            Some(b"answer".to_vec()),\n            "operator co-scope ⇒ shared dedup"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(b.hits(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn crit13_self_declared_group_is_structurally_impossible() {\n        // A manifest cannot even ENCODE a cache group: there is no cache-group config axis\n        // (0x05 is unknown ⇒ decode error). Membership is operator config only. This is the\n        // structural form of "a manifest that self-declares a shared group is refused."\n        assert_eq!(\n            config_axis_domain(0x05),\n            None,\n            "no cache-group axis in the manifest lattice"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tool_invokes_are_nocache_reads_are_cacheable() {\n        assert!(!AgentCache::is_cacheable(&AgentTask::InvokeTool {\n            name: "x".into(),\n            args: vec![]\n        }));\n        assert!(AgentCache::is_cacheable(&AgentTask::ReadResource {\n            uri: "u".into()\n        }));\n    }\n}\n	24	-1	-1		9bbcb65a9d882327f111d3c7a4061b25ad969d46b9e2f4e92dd75e4e129beb067d4a3429cecdf882fc4b472b5c13b23c0fe94d207208246aa84ef604c714a8cebe267ed16032ba31dc89a202f39fe0e95a511d4b25dcf745c8163387885fd5c5e462f75f3dfb10a4f83f031f6a400fb72cb6612cdf85bb0f1733e4e9a925b670

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-adapters/src/dispatch.rs	dispatch · 479 lines	//! dispatch.rs — the `Dispatcher` pattern generalized for agents: pre-acquire the budget,\n//! refuse with a typed error, and emit exactly ONE `TrackRecord` harvest row on EVERY\n//! pole (success, backend error, budget refusal, depth refusal).\n//!\n//! F2 rate-limit is enforced at the same slot as `llm-adapters` `dispatch.rs:82-90`\n//! (acquire before the call, typed `BudgetExceeded`). F10 depth is enforced per\n//! invocation against the cryptographically-witnessed `invoke_depth`. The harvest row is\n//! the SAME schema `gov_route` already folds (`model/task/success/value/cost/backend/\n//! tokens/ms`) — one JSONL stream for LLM + agent rows.\n\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\nuse std::time::Instant;\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{\n    AgentBridge, AgentError, AgentInvocation, AgentResponse, AgentTask, FUEL_PER_UNIT,\n};\nuse dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::TokenBucket;\n\nuse crate::fuel::{DeterministicFuelMeter, FuelError, FuelTrancheRunner};\n\nuse crate::cache::AgentCache;\n\n/// One harvested dispatch record — the SAME superset schema `gov_route` consumes\n/// (`model/task/success/value/cost` + richer `backend/tokens/ms`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct TrackRecord {\n    /// Bridge identity (e.g. `"mcp:<server-id>"`).\n    pub backend_id: String,\n    /// The target the request addressed (quirks-profile id + mapped tool/resource name).\n    pub model_id: String,\n    /// Budget units of the response (0 on any failure).\n    pub total_tokens: u64,\n    /// Wall-clock latency in ms.\n    pub ms: u64,\n    /// Task label the `gov_route` fold groups by (`agent.invoke_tool` | …).\n    pub task: String,\n    /// Success (1) / failure (0).\n    pub success: bool,\n    /// Expected value (EV numerator). Default 0.0.\n    pub value: f64,\n    /// Cost (EV denominator) — budget units consumed/attempted.\n    pub cost: f64,\n}\n\nimpl TrackRecord {\n    /// The exact JSONL line shape `gov_route` reads (identical to `llm-adapters`).\n    pub fn to_jsonl(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\n            "{{\\"model\\":\\"{}\\",\\"task\\":\\"{}\\",\\"success\\":{},\\"value\\":{},\\"cost\\":{},\\"backend\\":\\"{}\\",\\"tokens\\":{},\\"ms\\":{}}}\\n",\n            self.model_id, self.task, self.success, self.value, self.cost, self.backend_id, self.total_tokens, self.ms\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// Decode one harvest line back into a `TrackRecord` (the `gov_route` fold). Returns\n/// `None` on a malformed line (fail-closed; the row is skipped). Used by crit 8 to prove a\n/// mixed LLM+agent stream parses with zero schema errors.\npub fn decode_track_record(line: &str) -> Option<TrackRecord> {\n    let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(line).ok()?;\n    let s = |k: &str| v.get(k).and_then(|x| x.as_str()).unwrap_or("").to_string();\n    let b = |k: &str| v.get(k).and_then(|x| x.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false);\n    let f = |k: &str| v.get(k).and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0);\n    let u = |k: &str| v.get(k).and_then(|x| x.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0);\n    // Require the gov_route-critical keys to be present (schema check).\n    for k in ["model", "task", "success", "value", "cost"] {\n        v.get(k)?;\n    }\n    Some(TrackRecord {\n        backend_id: s("backend"),\n        model_id: s("model"),\n        total_tokens: u("tokens"),\n        ms: u("ms"),\n        task: s("task"),\n        success: b("success"),\n        value: f("value"),\n        cost: f("cost"),\n    })\n}\n\n/// Where harvest rows go. `FileHarvest` appends to `track_record.jsonl` (M8-local, like\n/// `llm-adapters`); tests use `VecHarvest`.\npub trait HarvestSink {\n    /// Record exactly one row.\n    fn record(&self, row: &TrackRecord);\n}\n\n/// Appends to `track_record.jsonl` (telemetry must never break the call path → failures\n/// are silently dropped, matching `llm-adapters::append_harvest`).\npub struct FileHarvest;\nimpl HarvestSink for FileHarvest {\n    fn record(&self, row: &TrackRecord) {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .append(true)\n            .open("track_record.jsonl")\n        {\n            let _ = f.write_all(row.to_jsonl().as_bytes());\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// In-memory harvest capture for tests.\n#[derive(Clone, Default)]\npub struct VecHarvest(Arc<Mutex<Vec<TrackRecord>>>);\nimpl VecHarvest {\n    /// Empty capture.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        VecHarvest(Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new())))\n    }\n    /// Snapshot the captured rows.\n    pub fn rows(&self) -> Vec<TrackRecord> {\n        self.0.lock().unwrap().clone()\n    }\n}\nimpl HarvestSink for VecHarvest {\n    fn record(&self, row: &TrackRecord) {\n        self.0.lock().unwrap().push(row.clone());\n    }\n}\n\n/// Typed dispatch failure — distinct from `AgentError` (the bridge's own failure).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum AgentDispatchError {\n    /// Budget exhausted (F2) — degrade-closed.\n    BudgetExceeded,\n    /// Delegation depth reached the granted cap (F10).\n    DepthExceeded,\n    /// The bridge itself failed.\n    Backend(AgentError),\n}\n\n/// A bounded dispatcher over a shared `AgentBridge`, generalizing the `llm-adapters`\n/// `Dispatcher`.\npub struct AgentDispatcher<B: AgentBridge, H: HarvestSink> {\n    backend: Arc<B>,\n    bucket: Arc<TokenBucket>,\n    granted_depth: u8,\n    sink: H,\n    seq: AtomicU64,\n    /// This agent's PRIVATE cache instance (SH-2): provisioned per-agent from\n    /// `CacheProvisioner`, never shared unless the operator co-scoped it. `None` disables\n    /// caching (every call reaches the bridge). Only idempotent reads are cached; tool\n    /// invocations are always `NoCache`.\n    cache: Option<Arc<AgentCache>>,\n    /// Prepaid-tranche fuel runner (B1). Used in the execution path to enforce the F2\n    /// budget envelope via the SAME loop that drives the real wasmtime guest — 1-unit\n    /// tranche keeps budget accounting exact (no over-acquire) while reusing the\n    /// production fuel-control logic instead of a bare `try_acquire`.\n    fuel_runner: FuelTrancheRunner,\n}\n\nimpl<B: AgentBridge, H: HarvestSink> AgentDispatcher<B, H> {\n    /// Build a dispatcher from an admitted bridge + its minted budget envelope + granted\n    /// F10 depth (all three come FROM the `AdmissionRecord`).\n    pub fn new(backend: Arc<B>, bucket: Arc<TokenBucket>, granted_depth: u8, sink: H) -> Self {\n        AgentDispatcher {\n            backend,\n            bucket,\n            granted_depth,\n            sink,\n            seq: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            cache: None,\n            // B1: 1-unit tranche ⇒ exact-cost budget envelope (no over-acquire), while\n            // reusing the production FuelTrancheRunner loop that drives the real wasmtime\n            // guest. FUEL_PER_UNIT converts budget units → fuel for the meter.\n            fuel_runner: FuelTrancheRunner::new(FUEL_PER_UNIT, 1),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Attach this agent's PRIVATE cache instance (SH-2 per-agent partitioning). The cache\n    /// is provisioned by `CacheProvisioner`; a shared instance appears here ONLY when the\n    /// operator co-scoped the agents.\n    pub fn with_cache(mut self, cache: Arc<AgentCache>) -> Self {\n        self.cache = Some(cache);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Canonical cache key for a cacheable task (`None` ⇒ not cacheable, e.g. tool invoke).\n    fn cache_key(task: &AgentTask) -> Option<[u8; 32]> {\n        match task {\n            AgentTask::ReadResource { uri } => Some(AgentCache::key(uri.as_bytes())),\n            AgentTask::RenderPrompt { name } => Some(AgentCache::key(name.as_bytes())),\n            AgentTask::InvokeTool { .. } => None, // NoCache\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn model_id(&self, task: &AgentTask) -> String {\n        let name = match task {\n            AgentTask::InvokeTool { name, .. } => name.clone(),\n            AgentTask::ReadResource { uri } => uri.clone(),\n            AgentTask::RenderPrompt { name } => name.clone(),\n        };\n        format!("{}/{}", self.backend.id(), name)\n    }\n\n    /// Dispatch one invocation. Enforces F10 depth, then F2 budget, then calls the bridge.\n    /// Emits EXACTLY ONE `TrackRecord` on every pole.\n    pub fn dispatch(&self, inv: AgentInvocation) -> Result<AgentResponse, AgentDispatchError> {\n        self.seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let model_id = self.model_id(&inv.task);\n        let task_label = inv.task.label().to_string();\n\n        // F10 depth: refuse when the witnessed depth EXCEEDS the grant (a depth-0 direct\n        // call is allowed even at granted_depth 0; a sub-agent link is depth ≥1).\n        if inv.invoke_depth > self.granted_depth {\n            self.harvest(&model_id, &task_label, false, 0, inv.cost_units.max(1), 0);\n            return Err(AgentDispatchError::DepthExceeded);\n        }\n\n        // SH-2 read-through: a cacheable task served from THIS agent's private cache is\n        // free (no budget) and still harvested. A separate-instance cache means a hit here\n        // can only reflect THIS agent's (or its operator-co-scoped group's) prior request.\n        let ck = self.cache.as_ref().and_then(|_| Self::cache_key(&inv.task));\n        if let (Some(cache), Some(key)) = (self.cache.as_ref(), ck) {\n            if let Some(content) = cache.get(&key) {\n                let units = (content.len() as u64).max(1);\n                self.harvest(&model_id, &task_label, true, units, 0, 0);\n                return Ok(AgentResponse { content, units });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // F2 budget: enforce the envelope through the FuelTrancheRunner (B1) — the SAME\n        // prepaid, tranche-wise loop that gates the real wasmtime guest. 1-unit tranche\n        // keeps accounting exact; on bucket exhaustion it terminates with a typed refusal.\n        let cost = inv.cost_units.max(1);\n        let mut meter = DeterministicFuelMeter::needs(cost.saturating_mul(FUEL_PER_UNIT));\n        match self.fuel_runner.run(&mut meter, self.bucket.as_ref()) {\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(FuelError::BudgetExceeded { .. }) => {\n                self.harvest(&model_id, &task_label, false, 0, cost, 0);\n                return Err(AgentDispatchError::BudgetExceeded);\n            }\n            Err(FuelError::Trap(_)) => {\n                self.harvest(&model_id, &task_label, false, 0, cost, 0);\n                return Err(AgentDispatchError::Backend(AgentError::Refused(\n                    "fuel-loop trap".into(),\n                )));\n            }\n        }\n\n        let t0 = Instant::now();\n        let result = self.backend.invoke(&inv);\n        let ms = t0.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n        match result {\n            Ok(resp) => {\n                // Populate this agent's private cache for cacheable tasks (idempotent put).\n                if let (Some(cache), Some(key)) = (self.cache.as_ref(), ck) {\n                    cache.put(key, resp.content.clone());\n                }\n                self.harvest(&model_id, &task_label, true, resp.units, resp.units, ms);\n                Ok(resp)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                self.harvest(&model_id, &task_label, false, 0, cost, ms);\n                Err(AgentDispatchError::Backend(e))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn harvest(&self, model_id: &str, model_id.to_string(),\n            total_tokens: tokens,\n            ms,\n            task: task.to_string(),\n            success,\n            value: 0.0,\n            cost: cost as f64,\n        });\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{AgentCaps, AgentManifest};\n\n    /// A minimal fake bridge: succeeds, or fails on a designated tool 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-adapters/src/fuel.rs	fuel · 289 lines	//! fuel.rs — the Wasmtime fuel ↔ `TokenBucket` prepaid-tranche loop (blueprint §2.2).\n//!\n//! Fuel is NOT 1:1 with budget units: fuel meters CPU instructions, units meter billing.\n//! One pinned constant `FUEL_PER_UNIT` converts (kernel `ports::agent::FUEL_PER_UNIT`,\n//! a **B4-pending placeholder** — see below). Execution is prepaid, tranche-wise: before\n//! each guest slice the host `bucket.try_acquire(TRANCHE_UNITS)`; on grant it loads\n//! `TRANCHE_UNITS × FUEL_PER_UNIT` fuel and resumes; on the out-of-fuel trap it attempts\n//! the next tranche; if `try_acquire` returns `false`, the instance is TERMINATED with a\n//! typed `BudgetExceeded` — refusal, never silent throttling, and NO fuel is ever loaded\n//! again after the refusing acquire.\n//!\n//! The loop is generic over a [`FuelMeter`]. The default build uses the deterministic\n//! in-crate [`DeterministicFuelMeter`] that models wasmtime's `set_fuel`/consume/trap\n//! semantics exactly (so §4 criterion 4 is a real test of the real control logic). The\n//! REAL wasmtime-backed meter compiles behind the `wasmtime-fuel` feature.\n\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{FUEL_PER_UNIT, TRANCHE_UNITS};\nuse dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::TokenBucket;\n\n/// How a single prepaid guest slice ended.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SliceOutcome {\n    /// The guest finished within the loaded fuel.\n    Done,\n    /// The guest exhausted the loaded fuel and trapped (needs another tranche).\n    OutOfFuel,\n    /// The guest trapped for another reason (bad instruction, host-call error).\n    Trap(String),\n}\n\n/// Typed fuel-loop failure.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FuelError {\n    /// The budget bucket was exhausted mid-run; the instance is terminated. Never\n    /// resumed at a reduced rate, never queued.\n    BudgetExceeded {\n        /// Units consumed (prepaid) before the refusing acquire.\n        consumed_units: u64,\n    },\n    /// The guest trapped for a non-fuel reason.\n    Trap(String),\n}\n\n/// The metered-execution seam. The default reference impl models wasmtime; the real\n/// wasmtime `Store` implements this behind the `wasmtime-fuel` feature.\npub trait FuelMeter {\n    /// Load `fuel` units of CPU budget into the guest (wasmtime `store.set_fuel`).\n    fn set_fuel(&mut self, fuel: u64);\n    /// Run the guest until it finishes or traps on out-of-fuel.\n    fn run_slice(&mut self) -> SliceOutcome;\n}\n\n/// The prepaid-tranche runner. Reused for both the deterministic and wasmtime meters.\npub struct FuelTrancheRunner {\n    fuel_per_unit: u64,\n    tranche_units: u64,\n    set_fuel_calls: AtomicUsize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for FuelTrancheRunner {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        // FUEL_PER_UNIT and TRANCHE_UNITS are the kernel-pinned constants (mirror-pinned\n        // kernel↔adapter). FUEL_PER_UNIT is a PLACEHOLDER pending the B4 criterion bench.\n        FuelTrancheRunner {\n            fuel_per_unit: FUEL_PER_UNIT,\n            tranche_units: TRANCHE_UNITS,\n            set_fuel_calls: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FuelTrancheRunner {\n    /// Build a runner with explicit constants (tests may shrink the tranche).\n    pub fn new(fuel_per_unit: u64, tranche_units: u64) -> Self {\n        FuelTrancheRunner {\n            fuel_per_unit,\n            tranche_units,\n            set_fuel_calls: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// How many times fuel was loaded (crit 4: must NOT increase after the refusing acquire).\n    pub fn set_fuel_calls(&self) -> usize {\n        self.set_fuel_calls.load(Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n\n    /// Run `meter` under `bucket`, prepaid tranche by tranche. `Ok(units)` on guest\n    /// completion; `Err(BudgetExceeded)` on bucket exhaustion (terminated, never resumed).\n    pub fn run<M: FuelMeter>(&self, meter: &mut M, bucket: &TokenBucket) -> Result<u64, FuelError> {\n        let mut consumed_units = 0u64;\n        loop {\n            // Prepay the next tranche. On refusal: TERMINATE — do not load fuel again.\n            if !dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::token_bucket_try_acquire(&bucket, self.tranche_units as f64) {\n                return Err(FuelError::BudgetExceeded { consumed_units });\n            }\n            self.set_fuel_calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            meter.set_fuel(self.tranche_units.saturating_mul(self.fuel_per_unit));\n            match meter.run_slice() {\n                SliceOutcome::Done => return Ok(consumed_units + self.tranche_units),\n                SliceOutcome::OutOfFuel => {\n                    consumed_units += self.tranche_units;\n                    continue;\n                }\n                SliceOutcome::Trap(e) => return Err(FuelError::Trap(e)),\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A deterministic in-crate `FuelMeter` modelling a guest that needs `total_need` fuel\n/// units of CPU. `set_fuel(f)` loads `f`; each `run_slice` consumes `min(loaded,\n/// remaining)`; if any need remains it is `OutOfFuel`, else `Done`. `infinite()` models\n/// a compute-bomb / spin guest (always `OutOfFuel`) — the crit-4 case.\npub struct DeterministicFuelMeter {\n    remaining_need: u128,\n    loaded: u64,\n}\n\nimpl DeterministicFuelMeter {\n    /// A guest that needs `total_need` fuel to finish.\n    pub fn needs(total_need: u64) -> Self {\n        DeterministicFuelMeter {\n            remaining_need: total_need as u128,\n            loaded: 0,\n        }\n    }\n    /// A guest that never finishes (compute bomb / spin).\n    pub fn infinite() -> Self {\n        DeterministicFuelMeter {\n            remaining_need: u128::MAX,\n            loaded: 0,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FuelMeter for DeterministicFuelMeter {\n    fn set_fuel(&mut self, fuel: u64) {\n        self.loaded = fuel;\n    }\n    fn run_slice(&mut self) -> SliceOutcome {\n        let spend = (self.loaded as u128).min(self.remaining_need);\n        self.remaining_need -= spend;\n        self.loaded = 0;\n        if self.remaining_need == 0 {\n            SliceOutcome::Done\n        } else {\n            SliceOutcome::OutOfFuel\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── The real wasmtime-backed meter (feature-gated; adapter-side only) ────────────────\n#[cfg(feature = "wasmtime-fuel")]\nmod wasmtime_meter {\n    use super::{FuelMeter, SliceOutcome};\n    use wasmtime::{Engine, Instance, Module, Store, TypedFunc};\n\n    /// A real wasmtime `Store`-backed fuel meter. Runs a WASM guest slice; an out-of-fuel\n    /// trap becomes `OutOfFuel`, a normal return becomes `Done`. `set_fuel` calls the real\n    /// `Store::set_fuel`. This is the production sandbox path (§2.2), compiled only under\n    /// the `wasmtime-fuel` feature so the default build stays fast/offline.\n    pub struct WasmtimeFuelMeter {\n        store: Store<()>,\n        entry: TypedFunc<(), ()>,\n    }\n\n    impl WasmtimeFuelMeter {\n        /// Build from WAT/wasm bytes exporting a nullary `run` function. Fuel consumption\n        /// is enabled on the engine (`Config::consume_fuel`). Errors surface as `String`\n        /// so the adapter needs no direct `anyhow` dependency.\n        pub fn from_wat(wat: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {\n            let mut config = wasmtime::Config::new();\n            config.consume_fuel(true);\n            let engine = Engine::new(&config).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n            let module = Module::new(&engine, wat).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n            let mut store = Store::new(&engine, ());\n            // Start empty; the tranche loop loads fuel before each slice.\n            store.set_fuel(0).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n            let instance = Instance::new(&mut store, &module, &[]).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n            let entry = instance\n                .get_typed_func::<(), ()>(&mut store, "run")\n                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n            Ok(WasmtimeFuelMeter { store, entry })\n        }\n    }\n\n    impl FuelMeter for WasmtimeFuelMeter {\n        fn set_fuel(&mut self, fuel: u64) {\n            let _ = self.store.set_fuel(fuel);\n        }\n        fn run_slice(&mut self) -> SliceOutcome {\n            match self.entry.call(&mut self.store, ()) {\n                Ok(()) => SliceOutcome::Done,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    // A wasmtime out-of-fuel trap is the tranche-boundary signal.\n                    if let Some(trap) = e.downcast_ref::<wasmtime::Trap>() {\n                        if *trap == wasmtime::Trap::OutOfFuel {\n                            return SliceOutcome::OutOfFuel;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    SliceOutcome::Trap(format!("{e}"))\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(feature = "wasmtime-fuel")]\npub use wasmtime_meter::WasmtimeFuelMeter;\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // ── §4 criterion 4 — fuel exhaustion = refusal (never resumed, never queued) ──\n    #[test]\n    fn crit4_compute_bomb_terminates_with_budget_exceeded() {\n        // Bucket: 20 units, no refill. Tranche = 8 units, small fuel_per_unit for speed.\n        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(20 as f64, 0.0);\n        let runner = FuelTrancheRunner::new(1, 8);\n        let mut guest = DeterministicFuelMeter::infinite(); // never finishes\n        let res = runner.run(&mut guest, &bucket);\n        // Terminated with a typed refusal; consumed exactly the 2 grantable tranches (16),\n        // then the 3rd acquire (needs 8, only 4 left) refused.\n        assert_eq!(res, Err(FuelError::BudgetExceeded { consumed_units: 16 }));\n        let calls_at_refusal = runner.set_fuel_calls();\n        assert_eq!(\n            calls_at_refusal, 2,\n            "fuel loaded exactly twice (the 2 grantable tranches)"\n        );\n        // The bucket is below a tranche now; a second run loads NO fuel at all — proving\n        // the instance is never resumed at reduced rate after refusal.\n        let runner2 = FuelTrancheRunner::new(1, 8);\n        let mut guest2 = DeterministicFuelMeter::infinite();\n        let res2 = runner2.run(&mut guest2, &bucket);\n        assert_eq!(res2, Err(FuelError::BudgetExceeded { consumed_units: 0 }));\n        assert_eq!(\n            runner2.set_fuel_calls(),\n            0,\n            "NO fuel ever loaded once the bucket is exhausted"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn finite_guest_completes_within_budget() {\n        // Bucket huge; guest needs 10 * fuel_per_unit(=1000) = ... finishes within 2 tranches.\n        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(1_000_000 as f64, 0.0);\n        let runner = FuelTrancheRunner::new(1000, 8); // 1 tranche = 8*1000 = 8000 fuel\n        let mut guest = DeterministicFuelMeter::needs(10_000); // needs 2 tranches (8000 + 2000)\n        let units = runner\n            .run(&mut guest, &bucket)\n            .expect("finite guest finishes");\n        assert_eq!(units, 16, "consumed 2 prepaid tranches");\n        assert_eq!(runner.set_fuel_calls(), 2);\n    }\n\n    // ── the REAL wasmtime path (feature-gated) — same tranche loop, real guest ───\n    #[cfg(feature = "wasmtime-fuel")]\n    #[test]\n    fn wasmtime_compute_bomb_terminates_with_budget_exceeded() {\n        // A real WASM guest that spins forever, exported as `run`. Each tranche loads\n        // fuel; wasmtime traps OutOfFuel; the loop advances until the bucket is empty.\n        let wat = r#"(module (func (export "run") (loop br 0)))"#;\n        let mut meter = super::WasmtimeFuelMeter::from_wat(wat).expect("wat compiles");\n        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(24 as f64, 0.0); // 3 grantable tranches of 8\n        let runner = FuelTrancheRunner::new(1000, 8);\n        let res = runner.run(&mut meter, &bucket);\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res, Err(FuelError::BudgetExceeded { .. })),\n            "compute bomb terminated"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            runner.set_fuel_calls(),\n            3,\n            "fuel loaded exactly the 3 grantable tranches"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fuel_per_unit_is_the_kernel_placeholder() {\n        // Mirror-pinned kernel↔adapter; PLACEHOLDER pending B4 (documented, not ledger-grounded).\n        assert_eq!(FUEL_PER_UNIT, 100_000);\n        let runner = FuelTrancheRunner::default();\n        assert_eq!(runner.fuel_per_unit, FUEL_PER_UNIT);\n        assert_eq!(runner.tranche_units, TRANCHE_UNITS);\n    }\n}\n	96	-1	-1		8b5fd5975dce37a3f20d03fd98103a85d55fbfc6fd4ab5cbe85a606f8bba40192c70f0c64ec522bf050483f771c1506016795f0d552206aae0f666837e1c7aaf3ea7b4b8dea6983297d19d6015bafad233ca2c6a2192fdc1ae04a3a47004842de270d16613f7f0a55d35c65b5c6856994cbf652485cb2bf69741e55771253442

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-adapters/src/manifest.rs	manifest · 98 lines	//! manifest.rs — draft-manifest construction (adapter side).\n//!\n//! The kernel port owns the canonical TLV codec + value types; this module maps UNTRUSTED\n//! MCP discovery output → a DRAFT `AgentManifest` (closed-enum values only). The operator\n//! then encodes it (`AgentManifest::canonical_bytes`) and signs the frame — MCP's open-\n//! world grammar never enters the signed artifact. Only the closed-enum scopes drawn from\n//! the operator's tool allowlist reach the manifest.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{\n    AgentCaps, AgentManifest, BudgetRequest, CostDenomination, ExecutionModel, NodeId,\n    QuirksProfile, ResourceNeed, ValidationPolicy,\n};\n\nuse crate::quirks::AgentQuirks;\n\n/// Build a draft manifest from the agent's public keys + discovery-derived caps + the\n/// operator's quirks profile. `validation_policy` is fixed at the `RequireBoth` floor;\n/// `agent_node_id` is derived (never claimed). `extra_axes` lets the operator add bounded\n/// config beyond the transport axis (each still validated at decode).\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\npub fn draft_manifest(\n    subject_key: [u8; 32],\n    subject_key_pq: Vec<u8>,\n    quirks: &AgentQuirks,\n    caps: AgentCaps,\n    resource_needs: Vec<ResourceNeed>,\n    budget_request: BudgetRequest,\n    execution_model: ExecutionModel,\n    extra_axes: Vec<(u8, u8)>,\n    depth_request: u8,\n    nonce: [u8; 8],\n    expiry: u64,\n) -> AgentManifest {\n    let agent_node_id = NodeId::from_keys(&subject_key_pq, &subject_key).0;\n    let mut config_axes = vec![quirks.transport_kind.config_axis()];\n    config_axes.extend(extra_axes);\n    AgentManifest {\n        agent_node_id,\n        subject_key,\n        subject_key_pq,\n        agent_caps: caps,\n        action_scopes: quirks.draft_action_scopes(),\n        resource_needs,\n        cost_denomination: CostDenomination::TokenBucketUnits,\n        budget_request,\n        validation_policy: ValidationPolicy::RequireBoth,\n        execution_model,\n        config_axes,\n        depth_request,\n        quirks_profile: QuirksProfile::McpServer,\n        nonce,\n        expiry,\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{\n        Action, RefSigner, Resource, SignatureVerifier, ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN,\n    };\n    use std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn draft_has_derived_node_id_and_closed_scopes() {\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        let cls = v.classical_public(&[1u8; 32]);\n        let pq = v.pq_public(&[2u8; 32]);\n        let mut allow = BTreeMap::new();\n        allow.insert("get_menu".to_string(), (Resource::Menu, Action::Read));\n        let quirks = AgentQuirks::mcp_server(allow);\n        let caps = quirks.caps_from_discovery(true, true, false, false);\n        let m = draft_manifest(\n            cls,\n            pq.clone(),\n            &quirks,\n            caps,\n            vec![],\n            BudgetRequest {\n                capacity: 100,\n                refill_milli_units_per_sec: 1000,\n            },\n            ExecutionModel::WasmComponent,\n            vec![],\n            0,\n            [3u8; 8],\n            9999,\n        );\n        // node_id is DERIVED from the two keys, never claimed.\n        assert_eq!(m.agent_node_id, NodeId::from_keys(&pq, &cls).0);\n        assert_eq!(m.subject_key_pq.len(), ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN);\n        // Only the closed-enum allow-listed scope reached the manifest.\n        assert_eq!(m.action_scopes.grants, vec![(Resource::Menu, Action::Read)]);\n        // The transport axis is present and its round-trip decodes (bounded lattice).\n        assert!(m.config_axes.contains(&(0x01, 0)));\n        assert_eq!(AgentManifest::decode(&m.canonical_bytes()).unwrap(), m);\n    }\n}\n	108	-1	-1		fb7632516d6d49be324042e5810453054dd6a7c42f9d0403da5628eb8955a2051dd37149c8d90c8fee4004f9b9d63f358ef90704d36a8d69fa07fb0e7a98218e563d36b12d7bfe0dcd95b1491f9bad9ad16e544b251d416f983687a2d6731f4735a6f7beb1df90a9d95f8c9c4b1d9e38ccb760ec44a5348e1333d28a64e8ac92

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-adapters/src/mcp.rs	mcp · 256 lines	//! mcp.rs — `McpServerBridge`: the ONE reference `AgentBridge` implementation.\n//!\n//! Closed-scope narrowing: every host→server call goes through the operator-authored tool\n//! allowlist (unmapped ⇒ fail-closed `ToolNotAllowed` drop). Post-admission drift is\n//! detected by recomputing the live tool-map digest on each invoke and comparing it to the\n//! digest bound at admission (`listChanged` / server substitution ⇒ `DigestDrift`, refuse\n//! until re-admission). Server-initiated `sampling/createMessage` / elicitation requests\n//! are ALWAYS refused — an admitted agent must never drive the host's LLM (RC-2).\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{\n    AgentBridge, AgentCaps, AgentError, AgentInvocation, AgentManifest, AgentResponse, AgentTask,\n};\nuse serde_json::json;\n\nuse crate::quirks::AgentQuirks;\nuse crate::transport::{JsonRpcTransport, RpcChannel};\n\n/// A bridge to one MCP server. Constructed FROM an admission (the admitted manifest, the\n/// operator quirks profile, and the tool-map digest bound at admission).\npub struct McpServerBridge<C: RpcChannel> {\n    id_str: String,\n    manifest: AgentManifest,\n    quirks: AgentQuirks,\n    admitted_digest: [u8; 32],\n    caps: AgentCaps,\n    transport: JsonRpcTransport<C>,\n}\n\nimpl<C: RpcChannel> McpServerBridge<C> {\n    /// Build a bridge from an admission. `admitted_digest` is the tool-map digest captured\n    /// at admission (from the discovery snapshot the operator signed over).\n    pub fn admitted(\n        server_id: &str,\n        manifest: AgentManifest,\n        quirks: AgentQuirks,\n        admitted_digest: [u8; 32],\n        caps: AgentCaps,\n        channel: C,\n    ) -> Self {\n        McpServerBridge {\n            id_str: format!("mcp:{server_id}"),\n            manifest,\n            quirks,\n            admitted_digest,\n            caps,\n            transport: JsonRpcTransport::new(channel),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The server's currently-advertised tool names (live `tools/list`).\n    fn live_tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>, AgentError> {\n        let result = self.transport.call("tools/list", json!({}))?;\n        let tools = result\n            .get("tools")\n            .and_then(|t| t.as_array())\n            .ok_or_else(|| AgentError::BadRequest("tools/list missing tools[]".into()))?;\n        Ok(tools\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|t| {\n                t.get("name")\n                    .and_then(|n| n.as_str())\n                    .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            })\n            .collect())\n    }\n\n    /// The live tool-map digest (over the CURRENT advertised ∩ allow-listed set).\n    fn live_digest(&self) -> Result<[u8; 32], AgentError> {\n        Ok(self.quirks.tool_map_digest(&self.live_tools()?))\n    }\n\n    /// Refuse a server-initiated request that would invert control (RC-2). Sampling and\n    /// elicitation requests are always refused for the MCP profile.\n    pub fn handle_server_request(&self, method: &str) -> Result<(), AgentError> {\n        if (self.quirks.refuse_sampling && method.starts_with("sampling/"))\n            || (self.quirks.refuse_elicitation && method.starts_with("elicitation/"))\n        {\n            return Err(AgentError::ControlInversionRefused);\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<C: RpcChannel> AgentBridge for McpServerBridge<C> {\n    fn id(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.id_str\n    }\n    fn caps(&self) -> AgentCaps {\n        self.caps\n    }\n    fn manifest(&self) -> &AgentManifest {\n        &self.manifest\n    }\n\n    fn invoke(&self, req: &AgentInvocation) -> Result<AgentResponse, AgentError> {\n        // Drift check FIRST: the live tool-map must still match the admitted digest.\n        if self.live_digest()? != self.admitted_digest {\n            return Err(AgentError::DigestDrift);\n        }\n        let result = match &req.task {\n            AgentTask::InvokeTool { name, args } => {\n                // Closed-scope narrowing: an unmapped tool is a fail-closed drop.\n                if self.quirks.map_tool(name).is_none() {\n                    return Err(AgentError::ToolNotAllowed(name.clone()));\n                }\n                let arg_val: serde_json::Value = if args.is_empty() {\n                    json!({})\n                } else {\n                    serde_json::from_slice(args).unwrap_or_else(|_| json!({}))\n                };\n                self.transport\n                    .call("tools/call", json!({ "name": name, "arguments": arg_val }))?\n            }\n            AgentTask::ReadResource { uri } => self\n                .transport\n                .call("resources/read", json!({ "uri": uri }))?,\n            AgentTask::RenderPrompt { name } => self\n                .transport\n                .call("prompts/get", json!({ "name": name }))?,\n        };\n        let content = serde_json::to_vec(&result).unwrap_or_default();\n        let units = (content.len() as u64).max(1);\n        Ok(AgentResponse { content, units })\n    }\n\n    fn health(&self) -> Result<(), AgentError> {\n        self.transport\n            .call("ping", json!({}))\n            .map(|_| ())\n            .map_err(|_| AgentError::Unavailable)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::manifest::draft_manifest;\n    use crate::transport::MockChannel;\n    use dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{\n        Action, BudgetRequest, ExecutionModel, RefSigner, Resource, SignatureVerifier,\n    };\n    use std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n    fn allowlist() -> BTreeMap<String, (Resource, Action)> {\n        let mut m = BTreeMap::new();\n        m.insert("get_menu".to_string(), (Resource::Menu, Action::Read));\n        m.insert("read_order".to_string(), (Resource::Order, Action::Read));\n        m\n    }\n\n    fn tools_list(names: &[&str]) -> serde_json::Value {\n        json!({ "tools": names.iter().map(|n| json!({"name": n})).collect::<Vec<_>>() })\n    }\n\n    fn build_bridge(mock: MockChannel, advertised: &[&str]) -> McpServerBridge<MockChannel> {\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        let cls = v.classical_public(&[1u8; 32]);\n        let pq = v.pq_public(&[2u8; 32]);\n        let quirks = AgentQuirks::mcp_server(allowlist());\n        let caps = quirks.caps_from_discovery(true, true, false, false);\n        let manifest = draft_manifest(\n            cls,\n            pq,\n            &quirks,\n            caps,\n            vec![],\n            BudgetRequest {\n                capacity: 100,\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-adapters/src/quirks.rs	quirks · 178 lines	//! quirks.rs — `AgentQuirks` + the ONE reference profile `AgentQuirks::mcp_server()`.\n//!\n//! MCP's open-world string grammar NEVER enters the signed manifest. The bridge treats\n//! discovery output as UNTRUSTED input and produces a draft; the operator's keys sign the\n//! final closed-enum manifest. Tool names are free-form strings in MCP, so this profile\n//! carries an operator-authored **tool allowlist** `tool_name → (Resource, Action)`;\n//! unmapped tools are unreachable (fail-closed drop, never string passthrough). The\n//! canonical sorted tool-map is hashed (`sha3_256`) into the drift anchor so post-\n//! admission drift (`listChanged`, server substitution — registry-poisoning) is detectable.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{Action, AgentCaps, Resource, Scope};\n\n/// Transport kind — an enumerated config axis (never a free string).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum TransportKind {\n    /// Local stdio pipe (config axis 0x01 value 0).\n    Stdio,\n    /// Streamable HTTP (config axis 0x01 value 1).\n    StreamableHttp,\n}\n\nimpl TransportKind {\n    /// The `(axis_id, value_index)` this transport encodes as in the manifest lattice.\n    pub fn config_axis(&self) -> (u8, u8) {\n        match self {\n            TransportKind::Stdio => (0x01, 0),\n            TransportKind::StreamableHttp => (0x01, 1),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Per-bridge behavior deltas (the `Quirks`-pattern generalized for agents). The bridge\n/// reads these; it holds no framework knowledge itself beyond this struct.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AgentQuirks {\n    /// Stable profile id (e.g. `"mcp"`). Feeds the `TrackRecord.model` prefix.\n    pub profile_id: &'static str,\n    /// Enumerated transport axis.\n    pub transport_kind: TransportKind,\n    /// Pinned protocol epoch (e.g. an MCP spec date). Never a negotiated free string.\n    pub protocol_epoch: &'static str,\n    /// Operator-authored tool allowlist: `tool_name → (Resource, Action)`. The ONLY tool\n    /// names that are reachable; everything else is a fail-closed drop.\n    pub tool_allowlist: BTreeMap<String, (Resource, Action)>,\n    /// Refuse server-initiated `sampling/createMessage` (RC-2 control inversion). Always\n    /// `true` for MCP — an admitted agent must never drive the host's LLM.\n    pub refuse_sampling: bool,\n    /// Refuse server-initiated elicitation. Always `true` for MCP.\n    pub refuse_elicitation: bool,\n}\n\nimpl AgentQuirks {\n    /// The reference MCP-server profile. `tool_allowlist` is operator-authored.\n    pub fn mcp_server(tool_allowlist: BTreeMap<String, (Resource, Action)>) -> Self {\n        AgentQuirks {\n            profile_id: "mcp",\n            transport_kind: TransportKind::Stdio,\n            protocol_epoch: "mcp-2025-06-18",\n            tool_allowlist,\n            refuse_sampling: true,\n            refuse_elicitation: true,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Map MCP discovery flags → `AgentCaps` (§2.3): `tools ⇒ invoke_tool`, `resources ⇒\n    /// read_resource`, `prompts ⇒ render_prompt`, MCP tasks ⇒ `long_task`. MCP has NO\n    /// delegation, so `delegate` is ALWAYS `false` for this profile.\n    pub fn caps_from_discovery(\n        &self,\n        has_tools: bool,\n        has_resources: bool,\n        has_prompts: bool,\n        has_tasks: bool,\n    ) -> AgentCaps {\n        AgentCaps {\n            invoke_tool: has_tools,\n            read_resource: has_resources,\n            render_prompt: has_prompts,\n            delegate: false, // MCP has no delegation — always false for this profile.\n            long_task: has_tasks,\n            streaming: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Map a free-form MCP tool name → a closed scope. `None` ⇒ fail-closed drop (the\n    /// unmapped tool is unreachable).\n    pub fn map_tool(&self, name: &str) -> Option<(Resource, Action)> {\n        self.tool_allowlist.get(name).copied()\n    }\n\n    /// The draft `action_scopes` for the manifest: the sorted, de-duplicated set of\n    /// mapped scopes for the allow-listed tools.\n    pub fn draft_action_scopes(&self) -> Scope {\n        let mut grants: Vec<(Resource, Action)> = Vec::new();\n        for (_name, (r, a)) in &self.tool_allowlist {\n            if !grants.contains(&(*r, *a)) {\n                grants.push((*r, *a));\n            }\n        }\n        Scope::new(grants)\n    }\n\n    /// The drift anchor: `sha3_256` over the canonical sorted tool set the server\n    /// advertises AND that is allow-listed. Only names in BOTH the `advertised` set and\n    /// the operator allowlist contribute (server substitution / `listChanged` shows up as\n    /// a digest mismatch). `advertised` is the live `tools/list` result.\n    pub fn tool_map_digest(&self, advertised: &[String]) -> [u8; 32] {\n        // Canonical: sorted (name, resource_disc, action_disc) triples, length-prefixed.\n        let mut pairs: Vec<(&String, (Resource, Action))> = Vec::new();\n        for name in advertised {\n            if let Some(scope) = self.map_tool(name) {\n                pairs.push((name, scope));\n            }\n        }\n        pairs.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(b.0));\n        let mut buf = Vec::new();\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&(pairs.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        for (name, (r, a)) in pairs {\n            buf.extend_from_slice(&(name.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n            buf.extend_from_slice(name.as_bytes());\n            buf.push(r.discriminant());\n            buf.push(a.discriminant());\n        }\n        sha3_256(&buf)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn allowlist() -> BTreeMap<String, (Resource, Action)> {\n        let false"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn unmapped_tool_is_fail_closed_drop() {\n        let q = AgentQuirks::mcp_server(allowlist());\n        assert_eq!(q.map_tool("get_menu"), Some((Resource::Menu, Action::Read)));\n        assert_eq!(\n            q.map_tool("delete_everything"),\n            None,\n            "unmapped ⇒ fail-closed drop"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn digest_reacts_to_tool_set_change() {\n        let q = AgentQuirks::mcp_server(allowlist());\n        let d1 = q.tool_map_digest(&["get_menu".into(), "read_order".into()]);\n        // Server drops a tool ⇒ different digest.\n        let d2 = q.tool_map_digest(&["get_menu".into()]);\n        assert_ne!(\n            d1, d2,\n            "changing the advertised tool set changes the digest"\n        );\n        // Advertising an UNMAPPED tool does not change the digest (it is dropped).\n        let d3 = q.tool_map_digest(&["get_menu".into(), "read_order".into(), "evil".into()]);\n        assert_eq!(d1, d3, "unmapped tools do not enter the digest");\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-adapters/src/transport.rs	transport · 165 lines	//! transport.rs — one generic JSON-RPC 2.0 transport, shared by every agent bridge.\n//!\n//! Holds NO framework knowledge (mirrors `OpenAiCompatTransport`): all MCP/A2A deltas\n//! come from the `AgentQuirks` the caller passes. The byte IO is behind a [`RpcChannel`]\n//! seam (stdio pipe, streamable-HTTP, or an in-memory test double) so the transport\n//! itself is transport-agnostic and offline-testable. Maps JSON-RPC errors to typed\n//! [`AgentError`] — never a mock.\n\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::Mutex;\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::AgentError;\nuse serde_json::{json, Value};\n\n/// The byte-IO seam under the JSON-RPC framing. A real bridge supplies a stdio-pipe or\n/// streamable-HTTP channel; tests supply [`MockChannel`].\npub trait RpcChannel {\n    /// Send a framed JSON-RPC request (bytes) and return the response bytes. `Err` on any\n    /// transport failure.\n    fn request(&self, raw: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AgentError>;\n}\n\n/// A synchronous JSON-RPC 2.0 transport over any [`RpcChannel`].\npub struct JsonRpcTransport<C: RpcChannel> {\n    channel: C,\n    next_id: AtomicU64,\n}\n\nimpl<C: RpcChannel> JsonRpcTransport<C> {\n    /// Wrap a channel.\n    pub fn new(channel: C) -> Self {\n        JsonRpcTransport {\n            channel,\n            next_id: AtomicU64::new(1),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Perform one JSON-RPC 2.0 call. Maps a JSON-RPC `error` object to a typed\n    /// [`AgentError`]; returns the `result` value on success.\n    pub fn call(&self, method: &str, params: Value) -> Result<Value, AgentError> {\n        let id = self.next_id.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let req = json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "method": method, "params": params });\n        let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&req).map_err(|e| AgentError::BadRequest(e.to_string()))?;\n        let raw = self.channel.request(&bytes)?;\n        let resp: Value =\n            serde_json::from_slice(&raw).map_err(|e| AgentError::BadRequest(e.to_string()))?;\n        if let Some(err) = resp.get("error") {\n            let code = err.get("code").and_then(|c| c.as_i64()).unwrap_or(0);\n            let msg = err\n                .get("message")\n                .and_then(|m| m.as_str())\n                .unwrap_or("")\n                .to_string();\n            // JSON-RPC error → typed AgentError (a coarse, honest mapping).\n            return Err(match code {\n                -32601 => AgentError::Unsupported, // method not found\n                -32602 => AgentError::BadRequest(msg),\n                _ => AgentError::Refused(format!("jsonrpc error {code}: {msg}")),\n            });\n        }\n        resp.get("result")\n            .cloned()\n            .ok_or_else(|| AgentError::BadRequest("missing result".into()))\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow the underlying channel (tests inspect the mock).\n    pub fn channel(&self) -> &C {\n        &self.channel\n    }\n}\n\n/// An in-memory `RpcChannel` for offline tests. Canned responses per method + a call log.\n/// Mutable state (responses/log) is behind a `Mutex` so `request(&self, ...)` matches the\n/// real (shared-ref) trait shape.\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct MockChannel {\n    inner: Mutex<MockState>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Default)]\nstruct MockState {\n    /// method → canned JSON `result` value.\n    responses: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, Value>,\n    /// method → canned JSON-RPC `error` object.\n    errors: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, Value>,\n    /// Ordered log of called methods.\n    calls: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl MockChannel {\n    /// Empty mock.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        MockChannel::default()\n    }\n    /// Register a canned `result` for `method`.\n    pub fn with_result(self, method: &str, result: Value) -> Self {\n        self.inner\n            .lock()\n            .unwrap()\n            .responses\n            .insert(method.to_string(), result);\n        self\n    }\n    /// Register a canned JSON-RPC error object for `method`.\n    pub fn with_error(self, method: &str, code: i64, message: &str) -> Self {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().errors.insert(\n            method.to_string(),\n            json!({ "code": code, "message": message }),\n        );\n        self\n    }\n    /// Replace a method's canned result at runtime (e.g. the server changes its tool list).\n    pub fn set_result(&self, method: &str, result: Value) {\n        self.inner\n            .lock()\n            .unwrap()\n            .responses\n            .insert(method.to_string(), result);\n    }\n    /// The ordered method-call log.\n    pub fn calls(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().calls.clone()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl RpcChannel for MockChannel {\n    fn request(&self, raw: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AgentError> {\n        let req: Value =\n            serde_json::from_slice(raw).map_err(|e| AgentError::BadRequest(e.to_string()))?;\n        let method = req\n            .get("method")\n            .and_then(|m| m.as_str())\n            .unwrap_or("")\n            .to_string();\n        let id = req.get("id").cloned().unwrap_or(json!(0));\n        let mut st = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        st.calls.push(method.clone());\n        if let Some(err) = st.errors.get(&method).cloned() {\n            let resp = json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "error": err });\n            return Ok(serde_json::to_vec(&resp).unwrap());\n        }\n        let result = st.responses.get(&method).cloned().unwrap_or(json!(null));\n        let resp = json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "result": result });\n        Ok(serde_json::to_vec(&resp).unwrap())\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jsonrpc_result_and_error_mapping() {\n        let ch = MockChannel::new()\n            .with_result("ping", json!({"ok": true}))\n            .with_error("secret", -32601, "method not found");\n        let t = JsonRpcTransport::new(ch);\n        assert_eq!(t.call("ping", json!({})).unwrap(), json!({"ok": true}));\n        assert_eq!(t.call("secret", json!({})), Err(AgentError::Unsupported));\n        assert_eq!(\n            t.channel().calls(),\n            vec!["ping".to_string(), "secret".to_string()]\n        );\n    }\n}\n	163	-1	-1		4bb6b3fc38dfe069ab0de40b51865a8099de9d042945ee82e974e68ed3a00ee650400575468c62e3b44e032b3047f6f89f5775e63fa88698b44ef2095d0e788c840c5ffbed3e8941da178222b7fbe1cbd170fc2a255f53ceec80208efa2ba114a3aef7173e2a50fab1f92c5de24d6bea6d77c8eff6b89c280768e6f853b17577

dowiz_kernel::event_log::EventLog;\nuse dowiz_kernel::hydra::FileEventStore;\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{\n    Action, AdmissionLimiter, Admitter, AgentManifest, AnchorRoster, BudgetRequest, Capability,\n    Delegation, ExecutionModel, HybridPolicy, NodeId, RedLinePolicy, RefSigner,\n    ReferenceHybridGate, Resource, RevocationSet, Scope, SignatureVerifier, SignedFrame,\n};\nuse serde_json::json;\n\nfn allowlist() -> BTreeMap<String, (Resource, Action)> {\n    let mut m = BTreeMap::new();\n    m.insert("get_menu".to_string(), (Resource::Menu, Action::Read));\n    m\n}\n\n/// Build a valid manifest for the agent keypair.\nfn manifest(v: &RefSigner, cls: [u8; 32], pq: Vec<u8>) -> AgentManifest {\n    let quirks = AgentQuirks::mcp_server(allowlist());\n    let caps = quirks.caps_from_discovery(true, false, false, false);\n    let _ = v;\n    draft_manifest(\n        cls,\n        pq,\n        &quirks,\n        caps,\n        vec![],\n        BudgetRequest {\n            capacity: 256,\n            refill_milli_units_per_sec: 0,\n        },\n        ExecutionModel::WasmComponent,\n        vec![],\n        0,\n        [7u8; 8],\n        9999,\n    )\n}\n\n/// A fully valid admission frame + anchor-rooted chain + roster.\nfn valid_admission(\n    v: &RefSigner,\n    cls_secret: &[u8; 32],\n    pq_secret: &[u8; 32],\n    anchor_secret: &[u8; 32],\n    m: &AgentManifest,\n    nonce: [u8; 8],\n) -> (SignedFrame, AnchorRoster, Vec<Delegation>) {\n    let cls = v.classical_public(cls_secret);\n    let pq = v.pq_public(pq_secret);\n    let anchor = v.classical_public(anchor_secret);\n    let scope = Scope::single(Resource::AgentBridge, Action::AdmitAgent);\n    let cap = Capability::new_hybrid(cls, pq, scope.clone(), nonce, 9999);\n    let mut frame = SignedFrame::new(cap, m.canonical_bytes());\n    frame.sign_classical(v, cls_secret);\n    frame.sign_pq(v, pq_secret);\n    let link = Delegation::sign(\n        v,\n        anchor,\n        cls,\n        scope.clone(),\n        scope,\n        9999,\n        nonce,\n        anchor_secret,\n    );\n    let mut roster = AnchorRoster::new();\n    roster.enroll(&anchor);\n    (frame, roster, vec![link])\n}\n\nfn admitter() -> Admitter<ReferenceHybridGate<RefSigner>> {\n    let gate = ReferenceHybridGate::new_redlined(\n        HybridPolicy::RequireBoth,\n        RedLinePolicy::DenyByDefault,\n        RefSigner,\n    );\n    let limiter = AdmissionLimiter::new(1_000_000, 0.0, 8, 1_000, 0.0);\n    Admitter::new(gate, limiter, 1_000_000, [0xA0; 32])\n}\n\nfn hex(b: &[u8]) -> String {\n    b.iter().map(|x| format!("{x:02x}")).collect()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn e2e_admits_valid_and_rejects_invalid_against_real_file_event_store() {\n    let v = RefSigner;\n    let dir = std::env::temp_dir();\n    let path = dir.join(format!("dowiz_agent_admit_demo_{}.log", std::process::id()));\n    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);\n\n    let mut adm = admitter();\n    let mut log = EventLog::new(FileEventStore::open(&path).expect("open FileEventStore"));\n\n    println!("=== B1 admission DEMO RUN — real admit() over a real FileEventStore ===");\n    println!("host_event_store: {}", path.display());\n\n    // ── POLE 1: accept a real valid manifest ────────────────────────────────────\n    let (cls, pq_s, anch) = ([1u8; 32], [2u8; 32], [3u8; 32]);\n    let m = manifest(&v, v.classical_public(&cls), v.pq_public(&pq_s));\n    assert_eq!(\n        m.agent_node_id,\n        NodeId::from_keys(&m.subject_key_pq, &m.subject_key).0,\n        "node_id is derived, not claimed"\n    );\n    let (frame, roster, chain) = valid_admission(&v, &cls, &pq_s, &anch, &m, [7u8; 8]);\n    let len_before = log.len();\n    let rec = adm\n        .admit(\n            &frame,\n            &roster,\n            &chain,\n            &RevocationSet::new(),\n            &mut log,\n            0,\n            0,\n        )\n        .expect("valid manifest admits");\n    println!("ACCEPT: content_id  = {}", hex(&rec.content_id));\n    println!("ACCEPT: event_id    = {}", hex(&rec.event_id));\n    println!("ACCEPT: node_id     = {}", rec.node_id.to_hex());\n    println!("ACCEPT: tier        = {:?}", rec.tier);\n    println!(\n        "ACCEPT: budget      = cap {} refill_milli {}",\n        rec.granted_capacity, rec.granted_refill_milli\n    );\n    println!("ACCEPT: depth       = {}", rec.granted_depth);\n    assert_eq!(\n        log.len(),\n        len_before + 1,\n        "one AgentAdmitted event landed durably"\n    );\n    // The minted envelope exists and has budget (do NOT drain it — the invoke below needs it).\n    assert_eq!(rec.granted_capacity, 256);\n    assert!(\n        dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::token_bucket_available(&rec.bucket) >= 4.0,\n        "minted bucket carries the granted envelope"\n    );\n\n    // One bridged invoke through the minted envelope → exactly one TrackRecord row.\n    let quirks = AgentQuirks::mcp_server(allowlist());\n    let caps = quirks.caps_from_discovery(true, false, false, false);\n    let digest = quirks.tool_map_digest(&["get_menu".to_string()]);\n    let mock = MockChannel::new()\n        .with_result("tools/list", json!({"tools":[{"name":"get_menu"}]}))\n        .with_result("tools/call", json!({"content":"menu"}));\n    let bridge = Arc::new(McpServerBridge::admitted(\n        "demo",\n        m.clone(),\n        quirks,\n        digest,\n        caps,\n        mock,\n    ));\n    let sink = VecHarvest::new();\n    let disp = AgentDispatcher::new(\n        bridge,\n        Arc::clone(&rec.bucket),\n        rec.granted_depth,\n        sink.clone(),\n    );\n    let resp = disp\n        .dispatch(AgentInvocation {\n            task: AgentTask::InvokeTool {\n                name: "get_menu".into(),\n                args: vec![],\n            },\n            cost_units: 4,\n            invoke_depth: 0,\n        })\n        .expect("bridged invoke succeeds");\n    assert_eq!(\n        sink.rows().len(),\n        1,\n        "exactly one TrackRecord row per bridged call"\n    );\n    println!(\n        "ACCEPT: invoke ok, units={}, one TrackRecord row emitted",\n        resp.units\n    );\n\n    // ── POLE 2: reject a real invalid case (NodeId mismatch) — store byte-identical ──\n    let store_len_before = log.len();\n    let mut bad = manifest(&v, v.classical_public(&cls), v.pq_public(&pq_s));\n    bad.agent_node_id = [0xAB; 32]; // does NOT hash from its own carried keys\n    let (bad_frame, bad_roster, bad_chain) =\n        valid_admission(&v, &cls, &pq_s, &anch, &bad, [9u8; 8]);\n    let err = match adm.admit(\n        &bad_frame,\n        &bad_roster,\n        &bad_chain,\n        &RevocationSet::new(),\n        &mut log,\n        0,\n        0,\n    ) {\n        Ok(_) => panic!("identity-mismatch manifest MUST be rejected"),\n        Err(e) => e,\n    };\n    println!("REJECT: error       = {err:?}");\n    println!(\n        "REJECT: store_len   = {} (unchanged from {})",\n        log.len(),\n        store_len_before\n    );\n    assert_eq!(\n        log.len(),\n        store_len_before,\n        "store byte-identical: no event on rejection"\n    );\n\n    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);\n    println!("=== DEMO RUN complete: 1 accept, 1 reject, store durable + consistent ===");\n}\n	170	-1	-1		8386361b8c8dc372d04d64cd15575a0f05dea7d4ad53d682b845e49903dea7624dc672d1fddc459f1745c62b0ed3b6608eeb1f25f168c920f48ef22652006cce56355329387b1a215d11b348dfb3f5fa914b484a251ce54baca0209b9235c543aea2f2ce108393a8d81e8816eb170b1c6cb15044a4a8bc98163b771775f13cb0

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-facade/src/lib.rs	lib · 324 lines	//! agent-facade — P40's compilation firewall + the one concrete tool.\n//!\n//! This is the ONLY crate in the agent lane that imports `dowiz_kernel`. Downstream `agent-loop` imports `agent-facade` and nothing kernel-shaped,\n//! so `dowiz-kernel` appears in its graph only at depth 2, only via this crate\n//! (the audited chokepoint — see `agent-loop`'s firewall test).\n//!\n//! # Reachability guarantee\n//! A model's output can only select among `ToolPort` invocations; it cannot name\n//! `decide`, `fold`, `apply_tax`, or any store. Nothing else from the kernel leaks.\npub use dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::*;\npub use dowiz_kernel::ports::tool::*;\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n/// The P37 seam (soft dependency, named not built): where order status comes from.\n/// Implemented by `FixtureOrders` now and (later, P37 landed) `HttpOrderStatusSource`\n/// — same trait, inherits P37's capability-cert auth (NOT P40's job to build).\npub trait OrderStatusSource {\n    /// Returns the canonical oracle string form (e.g. "PENDING" … "COMPENSATED_REFUND",\n    /// the `order_machine.rs` vocabulary) or a typed error.\n    fn status_of(&self, order_id: &str) -> Result<String, ToolError>;\n}\n\n/// Stub source for P40's DoD: a fixed map, solo-offline by construction.\n/// LATER (P37 landed, separate PR): HttpOrderStatusSource { base_url }.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct FixtureOrders(BTreeMap<String, String>);\n\nimpl FixtureOrders {\n    /// Build from a list of `(order_id, canonical_status_string)` pairs.\n    pub fn from_pairs(pairs: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Self {\n        FixtureOrders(\n            pairs\n                .iter()\n                .map(|(id, st)| (id.to_string(), st.to_string()))\n                .collect(),\n        )\n    }\n}\n\nimpl OrderStatusSource for FixtureOrders {\n    fn status_of(&self, order_id: &str) -> Result<String, ToolError> {\n        self.0\n            .get(order_id)\n            .cloned()\n            .ok_or_else(|| ToolError::NotFound(order_id.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n\n/// The one tool. Wraps any `OrderStatusSource`; enforces scope + arg parsing.\n/// `invoke` is fail-closed: scope-cover check runs BEFORE the source is touched\n/// (proven by the adversarial test asserting zero source calls on `ScopeDenied`).\npub struct ReadOrderStatusTool<S: OrderStatusSource> {\n    source: S,\n}\n\nimpl<S: OrderStatusSource> ReadOrderStatusTool<S> {\n    /// The static declaration handed to the model (verbatim contract).\n    pub const SPEC: ToolSpec = ToolSpec {\n        name: "read_order_status",\n        description: "Read the lifecycle status of a delivery order by its id. \\\n                      Returns the canonical status vocabulary (e.g. PENDING, IN_DELIVERY, COMPENSATED_REFUND).",\n        arg_name: "order_id",\n        scope: ToolScope {\n            resource: ToolResource::OrderStatus,\n            action: ToolAction::Read,\n        },\n    };\n\n    pub fn new(source: S) -> Self {\n        ReadOrderStatusTool { source }\n    }\n\n    /// Parse `raw_arg` (the model's JSON, verbatim) into an `order_id` string.\n    /// Never panics: malformed JSON / missing key ⇒ `ToolError::BadArg`.\n    ///\n    /// Item 31 §4.4 Phase-A cutover: parses with the kernel-owned `dowiz_kernel::json` primitive\n    /// (bounded, degrade-closed, differentially proven vs serde_json) instead of `serde_json`.\n    /// LLM-originated, bounded schema; a malformed arg is already fail-closed to `BadArg`.\n    fn parse_arg(raw_arg: &str) -> Result<String, ToolError> {\n        let v = dowiz_kernel::json::parse(raw_arg)\n            .map_err(|_| ToolError::BadArg(raw_arg.to_string()))?;\n        v.get("order_id")\n            .and_then(|o| o.as_str())\n            .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            .ok_or_else(|| ToolError::BadArg(raw_arg.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<S: OrderStatusSource> ToolPort for ReadOrderStatusTool<S> {\n    fn spec(&self) -> &ToolSpec {\n        &Self::SPEC\n    }\n\n    fn invoke(&self, granted: ToolScope, inv: &ToolInvocation) -> Result<ToolOutput, ToolError> {\n        // Fail-closed: the granted scope must cover the tool's declared scope.\n        // `ToolScope` is a struct of closed enums; coverage is exact-equality here\n        // (one resource + one action). No coverage ⇒ refuse BEFORE touching the source.\n        if granted != Self::SPEC.scope {\n            return Err(ToolError::ScopeDenied);\n        }\n        let order_id = Self::parse_arg(&inv.raw_arg)?;\n        let status = self.source.status_of(&order_id)?;\n        Ok(ToolOutput {\n            content: format!("order {} status: {}", order_id, status),\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────── WebFetchTool (P40 native browsing, R&D lane) ──────\n//\n// The concrete `ToolResource::WebFetch` implementation. OFF by default (the\n// `web-fetch` Cargo feature, see Cargo.toml) — the network fetch (`ureq`) and\n// the readable-text extraction (`dowiz_kernel::readability`, always compiled,\n// pure `std`) both live here, never in the kernel, per the module firewall\n// (`ports::tool`'s doc comment: "ZERO network / HTTP / JSON / serde" in the\n// kernel; the concrete impl + framing live in downstream crates).\n//\n// Explicitly NOT interactive/JS-driven browsing — that class of capability\n// stays an external tool behind its own port (e.g. `agent-browser`), never\n// reimplemented here or in-kernel. See the native-agentic-browsing research\n// this tool's scope is drawn directly from.\n#[cfg(feature = "web-fetch")]\npub struct WebFetchTool {\n    agent: ureq::Agent,\n}\n\n#[cfg(feature = "web-fetch")]\nimpl Default for WebFetchTool {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(feature = "web-fetch")]\nimpl WebFetchTool {\n    /// Hard cap on response body bytes read — a page over this is truncated at\n    /// the byte boundary before UTF-8 decode, never buffered unbounded. Sized\n    /// generously for real article pages while refusing to let one fetch\n    /// exhaust memory (the same degrade-closed-cap discipline as the kernel's\n    /// `MAX_CHANNEL_EVENTS`/`MAX_HARMONIC_NODES` fixes).\n    const MAX_BODY_BYTES: u64 = 8 * 1024 * 1024;\n    /// Per-request timeout — a hung remote server must not hang the agent turn.\n    const TIMEOUT_S: u64 = 10;\n\n    pub const SPEC: ToolSpec = ToolSpec {\n        name: "web_fetch",\n        description: "Fetch a URL (http/https only) and return its readable text \\\n                      content, with navigation/ads/boilerplate stripped. Read-only; \\\n                      does not execute JavaScript or render the page — static \\\n                      server-rendered content only.",\n        arg_name: "url",\n        scope: ToolScope {\n            resource: ToolResource::WebFetch,\n            action: ToolAction::Read,\n        },\n    };\n\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()\n            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(Self::TIMEOUT_S))\n            .build();\n        WebFetchTool { agent }\n    }\n\n    fn parse_arg(raw_arg: &str) -> Result<String, ToolError> {\n        let v = dowiz_kernel::json::parse(raw_arg)\n            .map_err(|_| ToolError::BadArg(raw_arg.to_string()))?;\n        v.get("url")\n            .and_then(|o| o.as_str())\n            .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            .ok_or_else(|| ToolError::BadArg(raw_arg.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    /// Scheme allowlist — only `http`/`https`. Refuses `file://`, `ftp://`, and\n    /// anything else BEFORE the request is ever made (the SSRF/local-file-read\n    /// class of mistake is unrepresentable at the arg-validation step, not\n    /// merely discouraged). Full SSRF hardening (blocking private/link-local\n    /// IP ranges the DNS name resolves to) is NOT done here — named limitation,\n    /// not a silent gap: this tool is R&D-lane and network-egress-bounded by\n    /// its caller's deployment, the same posture `llm-adapters` already takes.\n    fn validate_url(url: &str) -> Result<(), ToolError> {\n        if url.starts_with("http://") || url.starts_with("https://") {\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            Err(ToolError::BadArg(format!(\n                "unsupported URL scheme (only http/https): {url}"\n            )))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(feature = "web-fetch")]\nimpl ToolPort for WebFetchTool {\n    fn spec(&self) -> &ToolSpec {\n        &Self::SPEC\n    }\n\n    fn invoke(&self, granted: ToolScope, inv: &ToolInvocation) -> Result<ToolOutput, ToolError> {\n        // Fail-closed scope check FIRST — no network call happens on a denied grant.\n        if granted != Self::SPEC.scope {\n            return Err(ToolError::ScopeDenied);\n        }\n        let url = Self::parse_arg(&inv.raw_arg)?;\n        Self::validate_url(&url)?;\n\n        let response = self\n            .agent\n            .get(&url)\n            .call()\n            .map_err(|_| ToolError::Unavailable)?;\n\n        let mut body = Vec::new();\n        {\n            use std::io::Read as _;\n            response\n                .into_reader()\n                .take(Self::MAX_BODY_BYTES)\n                .read_to_end(&mut body)\n                .map_err(|_| ToolError::Unavailable)?;\n        }\n        // Fail-open on non-UTF-8: lossy-decode rather than refuse the whole\n        // fetch over a handful of bad bytes (real pages are near-universally\n        // UTF-8; a strict reject here would be a worse failure mode than a\n        // few replacement characters in boilerplate that gets scored out\n        // anyway).\n        let html = String::from_utf8_lossy(&body);\n\n        let text = dowiz_kernel::readability::extract(&html);\n        Ok(ToolOutput { content: text })\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(all(test, feature = "web-fetch"))]\nmod web_fetch_tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // No test here makes a real network call — CI must never depend on live\n    // internet access. What IS verified without network: the fail-closed scope\n    // check runs before any I/O, URL-scheme validation refuses non-http(s)\n    // before any I/O, and arg parsing rejects malformed input before any I/O.\n    // An end-to-end fetch-against-a-local-mock-server test is a named follow-up,\n    // not silently skipped — see the tool's module doc.\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_denial_never_touches_network() {\n        let tool = WebFetchTool::new();\n        let wrong_scope = ToolScope {\n            resource: ToolResource::OrderStatus, // NOT WebFetch\n            action: ToolAction::Read,\n        };\n        let inv = ToolInvocation {\n            tool_name: "web_fetch".to_string(),\n            raw_arg: r#"{"url":"https://example.com"}"#.to_string(),\n
