## 232 · /root/dowiz/agent-governance-wasm/src/lib.rs · LongTerm

Summary: lib · 386 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-governance-wasm/src/lib.rs	lib · 386 lines	//! agent-governance-wasm — Phase-1 WASM binding for the dowiz agent-governance layer.\n//!\n//! This crate replaces the deleted TypeScript `agent-governance/*.ts` (resonator.ts removed,\n//! 0 refs) with a thin Rust/WASM host around the from-scratch, zero-dep [`bebop2_core`]\n//! kernels. Every heavy primitive (spectral eigen-solvers, resonator loop, basis projections,\n//! belief entropy, hashing) lives in `bebop2-core`; this crate only marshals JS↔Rust values via\n//! `wasm-bindgen`.\n//!\n//! Blueprint kernel coverage (BP-01 .. BP-06):\n//!\n//! | Kernel            | Status | Wrapper                | bebop2-core source                |\n//! |-------------------|--------|------------------------|-----------------------------------|\n//! | BP-01 resonator   | ✅     | [`resonate`]           | `resonator::run_resonator`        |\n//! | BP-02 geodesic    | ✅     | [`geodesic`]           | `algebra::geodesic_distance`      |\n//! | BP-03 eigensolver | ✅     | [`spectral_radius`]    | `lyapunov::eigenvalues_general`   |\n//! | BP-04 diffusion   | ✅*    | [`entropy`]            | `active::entropy` (belief/entropy)|\n//! | BP-05 PID governor| ⚠️ GAP | —                      | not in bebop2-core (see below)    |\n//! | BP-06 ledger      | ✅     | [`ledger_step`]        | `hash::sha3_256` (append-only)    |\n//!\n//! \\* BP-04 "diffusion" is surfaced here as the belief-entropy primitive that the diffusion /\n//! free-energy kernel is built on (`active::entropy`). The full CSR-Laplacian matvec /\n//! `field::propagate` spectral propagator is available in `bebop2-core` but is intentionally NOT\n//! wrapped in this thin shim (it requires constructing a `LaplacianSpectrum` from an edge list,\n//! which is a graph-construction concern, not a single-call kernel).\n//!\n//! ## BP-05 gap (documented, not faked)\n//!\n//! The autonomous PID + ICIR telemetry governor (BP-05) does **not** exist as a `bebop2-core`\n//! kernel. It lives in the separate host-agent crate `crates/bebop/src/governor.rs` (the `bebop`\n//! agent), which is NOT part of the `bebop2-core` dependency graph this crate links against.\n//! Wrapping it would require depending on that host crate, which is out of scope for a\n//! bebop2-core-only WASM binding. [`governor_step`] is therefore intentionally NOT exported.\n//! When the governor is moved into `bebop2-core` (or exposed via a host-crate FFI), this crate\n//! can add a one-line `#[wasm_bindgen]` wrapper. No placeholder/fake governor is emitted to\n//! avoid presenting unverified control logic to callers.\n//!\n//! ## BP-06 ledger\n//!\n//! There is no dedicated "entropy ledger" struct in `bebop2-core`, but the building block exists:\n//! [`bebop2_core::hash::sha3_256`]. [`ledger_step`] implements a genuine deterministic,\n//! append-only, hash-chained ledger entry (the standard collision-resistant accumulator) using\n//! the real bebop2-core SHA3-256 — no RNG, no clock, reproducible.\n\nuse wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;\n\n// ── BP-01: resonator ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n//\n// `run_resonator` takes its per-tick actors as bare `fn` pointers (no captures). To let the\n// caller-supplied `coeff` (per-tick relaxation toward the ground) flow into the `generate` fn,\n// we stage it in a `thread_local` cell. Single-threaded on wasm32 and on the native test runner;\n// this shim never re-enters `run_resonator`, so there is no aliasing hazard.\nuse std::cell::RefCell;\n\nthread_local! {\n    static RELAX_COEFF: RefCell<f64> = const { RefCell::new(0.9) };\n}\n\nfn resonate_generate(s: &Vec<f64>) -> Vec<f64> {\n    let c = RELAX_COEFF.with(|c| *c.borrow());\n    s.iter().map(|x| x * c).collect()\n}\n\nfn resonate_reflect(proposed: &Vec<f64>, refv: &Vec<f64>) -> (Vec<f64>, f64) {\n    // Strong, high-quality reflector: pull 99.999% of the way to the reference each tick.\n    let refined: Vec<f64> = proposed\n        .iter()\n        .zip(refv.iter())\n        .map(|(p, r)| p + 0.99999 * (r - p))\n        .collect();\n    let err = refined\n        .iter()\n        .zip(refv.iter())\n        .map(|(p, r)| (p - r).powi(2))\n        .sum::<f64>()\n        .sqrt();\n    (refined, (1.0 / (1.0 + err)).clamp(0.0, 1.0))\n}\n\nfn resonate_supervise(_refined: &Vec<f64>, _refv: &Vec<f64>, _q: f64) -> bool {\n    true\n}\n\n/// BP-01 — drive the closed-loop resonator toward the immutable ground (the origin) and return\n/// the converged state vector.\n///\n/// `field` is the initial state; `coeff` is the per-tick relaxation factor applied by the\n/// generator (`x *= coeff`). The reference is the zero vector (the "ground" the loop settles on).\n/// Lyapunov guard + drift-rollback are active (see `bebop2_core::resonator`).\n#[wasm_bindgen]\npub fn resonate(field: &[f64], coeff: f64) -> Vec<f64> {\n    RELAX_COEFF.with(|c| *c.borrow_mut() = coeff);\n    let reference = bebop2_core::resonator::Reference {\n        value: vec![0.0f64; field.len()],\n    };\n    let initial = field.to_vec();\n    let actors = bebop2_core::resonator::Actors {\n        generate: resonate_generate,\n        reflect: resonate_reflect,\n        supervise: resonate_supervise,\n    };\n    let cfg = bebop2_core::resonator::LoopConfig::default();\n    let res = bebop2_core::resonator::run_resonator(\n        &reference,\n        initial,\n        &actors,\n        &bebop2_core::resonator::L2Metric,\n        &cfg,\n    );\n    res.final_state\n}\n\n// ── BP-03: eigensolver (spectral radius) ─────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// BP-03 — spectral radius ρ = max|λ| of a real `n×n` matrix `a` (row-major), returned as f64.\n/// Uses the general (non-symmetric) Francis double-shift QR eigensolver, so rotational/complex\n/// modes are handled correctly.\n#[wasm_bindgen]\npub fn spectral_radius(a: &[f64], n: usize) -> f64 {\n    let ev = bebop2_core::lyapunov::eigenvalues_general(a, n);\n    ev.iter().map(|c| c.norm()).fold(0.0f64, f64::max)\n}\n\n// ── BP-02: geodesic (angular distance) ───────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// BP-02 — great-circle (geodesic) distance `d_g = arccos(⟨a,b⟩)` between two equal-length\n/// vectors on the unit sphere, in `[0, π]`. A true metric (unlike `1−cos`).\n#[wasm_bindgen]\npub fn geodesic(a: &[f64], b: &[f64]) -> f64 {\n    bebop2_core::algebra::geodesic_distance(a, b)\n}\n\n// ── BP-04: diffusion / belief entropy ────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// BP-04 — Shannon entropy `H = −Σ b_i ln b_i` of a (normalized) belief distribution. This is the\n/// entropy primitive the diffusion / free-energy kernel (`active`) is built on. A zero probability\n/// mass contributes `0·ln0 := 0` (limit).\n#[wasm_bindgen]\npub fn entropy(b: &[f64]) -> f64 {\n    bebop2_core::active::entropy(b)\n}\n\n// ── BP-06: entropy ledger (hash-chained append-only accumulator) ─────────────\n\n/// BP-06 — append `entry` to a deterministic hash-chained ledger and return the new head hash.\n///\n/// `prev_hash` is the previous ledger head (empty for the genesis entry); the new head is\n/// `SHA3-256(prev_hash ‖ entry)`. Collision-resistant and reproducible (no RNG / clock). This is a\n/// genuine ledger built on `bebop2_core::hash::sha3_256` (there is no separate ledger struct in\n/// bebop2-core, so the accumulator is constructed here from the real primitive).\n#[wasm_bindgen]\npub fn ledger_step(prev_hash: &[u8], entry: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(prev_hash.len() + entry.len());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(prev_hash);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(entry);\n    bebop2_core::hash::sha3_256(&buf).to_vec()\n}\n\n// ── Native unit tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resonate_relaxes_to_ground() {\n        // coeff 0.5 + strong reflector ⇒ converges to (near) the origin well under the fuse.\n        let out = resonate(&[10.0, -5.0, 3.0, 7.0], 0.5);\n        assert_eq!(out.len(), 4);\n        for &x in &out {\n            assert!(x.abs() < 1e-3, "state component did not converge: {x}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resonate_coeff_kept_positive_diverges_slowly_but_is_bounded() {\n        // coeff 1.0 + strong reflector still pulls to ground; stays finite, no NaN/inf.\n        let out = resonate(&[1.0, 2.0], 1.0);\n        for &x in &out {\n            assert!(x.is_finite(), "non-finite state: {x}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn spectral_radius_of_scaled_identity() {\n        // 2×2: 0.5·I ⇒ both eigenvalues 0.5 ⇒ ρ = 0.5.\n        let a = [0.5f64, 0.0, 0.0, 0.5];\n        let r = spectral_radius(&a, 2);\n        assert!((r - 0.5).abs() < 1e-9, "expected 0.5, got {r}");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn spectral_radius_of_swap_is_one() {\n        // Ã = [[0,1],[1,0]] (swap) ⇒ eigenvalues ±1 ⇒ ρ = 1.\n        let a = [0.0f64, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0];\n        let r = spectral_radius(&a, 2);\n        assert!((r - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12, "expected 1.0, got {r}");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn geodesic_identical_is_zero_and_perp_is_half_pi() {\n        let x = [1.0f64, 0.0, 0.0];\n        let y = [0.0, 1.0, 0.0];\n        assert!(geodesic(&x, &x).abs() < 1e-12, "identical ⇒ 0");\n        let d = geodesic(&x, &y);\n        assert!(\n            (d - std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2).abs() < 1e-12,\n            "perpendicular ⇒ π/2, got {d}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn entropy_of_uniform_matches_bits() {\n        // Uniform over 4 outcomes ⇒ H = ln(4) ≈ 1.38629.\n        let b = [0.25f64, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25];\n        let h = entropy(&b);\n        assert!(\n            (h - 4.0 * 0.25 * 0.25f64.ln().abs()).abs() < 1e-9,\n            "got {h}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn entropy_zero_mass_contributes_nothing() {\n        let b = [1.0f64, 0.0, 0.0];\n        let h = entropy(&b);\n        assert!(\n            h.abs() < 1e-12,\n            "degenerate belief has zero entropy, got {h}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ledger_chains_and_is_deterministic() {\n        let h0: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();\n        let h1 = ledger_step(&h0, &[1, 2, 3]);\n        let h2 = ledger_step(&h1, &[4, 5, 6]);\n        assert_eq!(h1.len(), 32);\n        assert_eq!(h2.len(), 32);\n        assert_ne!(h1, h2, "distinct entries must change the head");\n        // determinism: same inputs ⇒ same head\n        let h1b = ledger_step(&h0, &[1, 2, 3]);\n        assert_eq!(h1, h1b, "ledger step must be reproducible");\n    }\n}\n\n/// A3 — EIGENSOLVER PARITY GATE. Two independent general (non-symmetric) real eigensolvers exist\n/// with NO parity gate between them: dowiz-kernel's Faddeev-LeVerrier + Durand-Kerner\n/// (`dowiz_kernel::spectral`) and bebop2-core's Hessenberg + Francis-QR\n/// (`bebop2_core::lyapunov::eigenvalues_general`). That is the exact dual-authority silent-drift\n/// hazard the kernel exists to kill (cf. `kernel/src/markov.rs`, which already closed the Python↔Rust\n/// version of it). This crate is the only bridge that already links both, so it hosts the gate:\n/// it cross-checks BOTH solvers against each other AND against analytic ground truth on shared\n/// fixtures; if either implementation drifts, it goes RED. Native `cargo test` only (dev-dep on the\n/// kernel; never in the wasm build).\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod eigensolver_parity {\n    const TOL: f64 = 1e-6;\n\n    fn flat(rows: &[Vec<f64>]) -> Vec<f64> {\n        rows.iter().flatten().copied().collect()\n    }\n    fn sort_pairs(v: &mut [(f64, f64)]) {\n        v.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            a.0.partial_cmp(&b.0)\n                .unwrap()\n                .then(a.1.partial_cmp(&b.1).unwrap())\n        });\n    }\n    fn kernel_eigs(rows: &[Vec<f64>]) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {\n        let mut v: Vec<(f64, f64)> = dowiz_kernel::spectral::eigenvalues(rows)\n            .iter()\n            .map(|c| (c.re, c.im))\n            .collect();\n        sort_pairs(&mut v);\n        v\n    }\n    fn bebop_eigs(rows: &[Vec<f64>]) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {\n        let f = flat(rows);\n        let mut v: Vec<(f64, f64)> = bebop2_core::lyapunov::eigenvalues_general(&f, rows.len())\n            .iter()\n            .map(|c| (c.re, c.im))\n            .collect();\n        sort_pairs(&mut v);\n        v\n    }\n    fn assert_close(a: &[(f64, f64)], b: &[(f64, f64)], msg: &str) {\n        assert_eq!(\n            a.len(),\n            b.len(),\n            "{msg}: eigenvalue COUNT differs {a:?} vs {b:?}"\n        );\n        for (x, y) in a.iter().zip(b.iter()) {\n            assert!(\n                (x.0 - y.0).abs() < TOL && (x.1 - y.1).abs() < TOL,\n                "{msg}: eigenvalue drift {x:?} vs {y:?}"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n    fn analytic(mut w: Vec<(f64, f64)>) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {\n        sort_pairs(&mut w);\n        w\n    }\n\n    // GREEN: FL+DK ↔ Francis-QR ↔ analytic, on real-spectrum fixtures.\n    #[test]\n    fn fl_dk_matches_francis_qr_real_spectrum() {\n        // diag(2,3,5) → {2,3,5}\n        let m = vec![\n            vec![2.0, 0.0, 0.0],\n            vec![0.0, 3.0, 0.0],\n            vec![0.0, 0.0, 5.0],\n        ];\n        assert_close(&kernel_eigs(&m), &bebop_eigs(&m), "diag: kernel↔bebop2");\n        assert_close(\n            &kernel_eigs(&m),\n            &analytic(vec![(2.0, 0.0), (3.0, 0.0), (5.0, 0.0)]),\n            "diag: ↔analytic",\n        );\n\n        // upper-triangular → eigenvalues are the diagonal {1,4,-3}\n        let m = vec![\n            vec![1.0, 2.0, 0.0],\n            vec![0.0, 4.0, 5.0],\n            vec![0.0, 0.0, -3.0],\n        ];\n        assert_close(\n            &kernel_eigs(&m),\n            &bebop_eigs(&m),\n            "triangular: kernel↔bebop2",\n        );\n        assert_close(\n            &kernel_eigs(&m),\n            &analytic(vec![(1.0, 0.0), (4.0, 0.0), (-3.0, 0.0)]),\n            "triangular: ↔analytic",\n        );\n\n        // companion [[0,-2],[1,-3]] → λ²+3λ+2 → {-1,-2}\n        let m = vec![vec![0.0, -2.0], vec![1.0, -3.0]];\n        assert_close(\n            &kernel_eigs(&m),\n            &bebop_eigs(&m),\n            "companion: kernel↔bebop2",\n        );\n        assert_close(\n            &kernel_eigs(&m),\n            &analytic(vec![(-1.0, 0.0), (-2.0, 0.0)]),\n            "companion: ↔analytic",\n        );\n    }\n\n    // GREEN: complex-conjugate spectrum — the case a symmetric-only solver gets WRONG.\n    // The 2-D rotation [[0,-1],[1,0]] has eigenvalues ±i; both GENERAL solvers must agree.\n    #[test]\n    fn complex_conjugate_eigenvalues_agree() {\n        let m = vec![vec![0.0, -1.0], vec![1.0, 0.0]];\n        assert_close(&kernel_eigs(&m), &bebop_eigs(&m), "rotation: kernel↔bebop2");\n        assert_close(\n            &kernel_eigs(&m),\n            &analytic(vec![(0.0, -1.0), (0.0, 1.0)]),\n            "rotation: ↔analytic",\n        );\n    }\n\n    // GREEN: spectral radius (the scalar the wasm surface returns) — parity kernel FL+DK vs the\n    // live `spectral_radius` wasm export (bebop2 QR), cross-checked against analytic ρ.\n    #[test]\n    fn spectral_radius_parity_kernel_vs_wasm_surface() {\n        let fixtures: [(Vec<Vec<f64>>, f64); 3] = [\n            (\n            (vec![vec![0.0, -2.0], vec![1.0, -3.0]], 2.0),\n            (vec![vec![0.0, -1.0], vec![1.0, 0.0]], 1.0),\n        ];\n        for (m, rho) in &fixtures {\n            let k = 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-loop/src/lib.rs	lib · 273 lines	//! agent-loop — P40's bounded agent executor.\n//!\n//! `AgentLoop::run` drives at most `MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS` plan→act→observe turns\n//! over an [`LlmBackend`] behind [`agent_facade`]. tool's declared scope (fail-closed enforcement lives in the tool impl).\n    let granted = agent_facade::ToolScope {\n        resource: agent_facade::ToolResource::OrderStatus,\n        action: agent_facade::ToolAction::Read,\n    };\n\n    let loop_ = AgentLoop::new(&backend, &tool, granted);\n    let outcome = loop_.run(&request);\n\n    // Fold the event log into the designed agent metrics.\n    let mut iterations: u64 = 0;\n    let mut tool_calls: u64 = 0;\n    let mut total_tokens: u64 = 0;\n    let mut success = false;\n\n    match &outcome {\n        LoopOutcome::Answer { LoopOutcome::AssistantUnavailable { reason, log } => {\n            eprintln!("ASSISTANT UNAVAILABLE: {reason}");\n            fold_log(log, &mut iterations, &mut tool_calls, &mut total_tokens);\n `dowiz_agent_*` metric IDs into the shared harvest ledger.\n    // `task` is the metric ID gov_route folds by; `value` carries the measured count.\n    emit("agent_loop", success, total_tokens, 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/agent-loop/src/service.rs	service · 262 lines	//! agent-loop sibling HTTP service (P40 DECART-B).\n//!\n//! A tiny std-only localhost HTTP surface over the bounded [`crate::AgentLoop`].\n//! `native-spa-server` PROXIES `/api/agent` to THIS service (choice B), so the\n//! SPA binary stays zero-OCI: the heavy `llm-adapters` dependency lives ONLY in\n//! this crate/process, never in the SPA's Cargo graph.\n//!\n//! Wire contract (minimal): `POST /agent` with body `{"prompt":"..."}` →\n//! `{"outcome": "...", "text": <string|null>, "log": [ ... ]}`. Every response is\n//! a typed [`crate::LoopOutcome`] serialized; the executor bounds itself by\n//! `MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS` + `TokenBucket`, so one request = one bounded turn.\n//!\n//! No new dependency: the HTTP parse + JSON emit are std-only (matching the\n//! `native-spa-server` integration tests' own raw `TcpStream` discipline). The\n//! `dowiz-kernel` firewall is untouched — this module imports ONLY `agent_facade`\n//! port types + `crate`.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\n\nuse agent_facade::{LlmBackend, ToolPort, ToolScope};\n\nuse crate::{AgentLoop, LoopEventKind, LoopLogEntry, LoopOutcome};\n\n/// Serve exactly ONE connection: read a `POST /agent` request, drive one bounded\n/// `AgentLoop::run`, write the typed outcome as JSON, close. Returns the outcome\n/// so a test can assert on it without re-parsing the wire.\n///\n/// Bounded by construction: `AgentLoop::run` cannot loop past `MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS`.\npub fn serve_one(\n    listener: &TcpListener,\n    backend: &dyn LlmBackend,\n    tool: &dyn ToolPort,\n    granted: ToolScope,\n) -> std::io::Result<LoopOutcome> {\n    let (stream, _peer) = listener.accept()?;\n    handle_connection(stream, backend, tool, granted)\n}\n\n/// Serve requests forever (the sibling-service main loop). Each accepted\n/// connection drives exactly one bounded turn; a per-connection error is logged\n/// and the loop continues (no unbounded state, no self-scheduling).\npub fn serve_forever(\n    listener: &TcpListener,\n    backend: &dyn LlmBackend,\n    tool: &dyn ToolPort,\n    granted: ToolScope,\n) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    for conn in listener.incoming() {\n        match conn {\n            Ok(stream) => {\n                if let Err(e) = handle_connection(stream, backend, tool, granted) {\n                    eprintln!("[agent-service] connection error: {e}");\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => eprintln!("[agent-service] accept error: {e}"),\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Handle one HTTP connection: parse body → run one turn → emit JSON.\npub fn handle_connection(\n    mut stream: TcpStream,\n    backend: &dyn LlmBackend,\n    tool: &dyn ToolPort,\n    granted: ToolScope,\n) -> std::io::Result<LoopOutcome> {\n    let body = read_http_request_body(&mut stream)?;\n    let prompt = extract_json_string_field(&body, "prompt").unwrap_or_default();\n\n    let agent = AgentLoop::new(backend, tool, granted);\n    let outcome = agent.run(&prompt);\n\n    let json = outcome_to_json(&outcome);\n    let resp = format!(\n        "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n{}",\n        json.as_bytes().len(),\n        json\n    );\n    stream.write_all(resp.as_bytes())?;\n    stream.flush()?;\n    Ok(outcome)\n}\n\n/// Read an HTTP/1.1 request off the stream and return its body bytes as a String.\n/// Honors `Content-Length`; std-only, no HTTP crate.\nfn read_http_request_body(stream: &mut TcpStream) -> std::io::Result<String> {\n    let mut buf: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(1024);\n    let mut chunk = [0u8; 1024];\n\n    // Read until we have the full header block.\n    let header_end = loop {\n        if let Some(pos) = find_subslice(&buf, b"\\r\\n\\r\\n") {\n            break pos + 4;\n        }\n        let n = stream.read(&mut chunk)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            // Connection closed before headers completed.\n            return Ok(String::new());\n        }\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);\n    };\n\n    let headers = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..header_end]);\n    let content_length = headers\n        .lines()\n        .find_map(|l| {\n            let (k, v) = l.split_once(':')?;\n            if k.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case("content-length") {\n                v.trim().parse::<usize>().ok()\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n\n    // We already may have read part (or all) of the body.\n    let mut body: Vec<u8> = buf[header_end..].to_vec();\n    while body.len() < content_length {\n        let n = stream.read(&mut chunk)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n        body.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);\n    }\n    body.truncate(content_length.max(body.len().min(content_length)));\n    // If content_length was 0 but a body arrived, keep what we have.\n    let take = if content_length == 0 {\n        body.len()\n    } else {\n        content_length.min(body.len())\n    };\n    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&body[..take]).into_owned())\n}\n\nfn find_subslice(haystack: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {\n    if needle.is_empty() || haystack.len() < needle.len() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    haystack.windows(needle.len()).position(|w| w == needle)\n}\n\n/// Extract a JSON string field value by key from a small JSON object. Std-only, minimal —\n/// sufficient for the `{"prompt":"..."}` request shape.\nfn extract_json_string_field(json: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let bytes = json.as_bytes();\n    let needle = format!("\\"{key}\\"");\n    let mut i = json.find(&needle)? + needle.len();\n    // skip whitespace and ':'\n    while i < bytes.len()\n        && (bytes[i] == b' '\n            || bytes[i] == b'\\t'\n            || bytes[i] == b':'\n            || bytes[i] == b'\\n'\n            || bytes[i] == b'\\r')\n    {\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    if i >= bytes.len() || bytes[i] != b'"' {\n        return None;\n    }\n    i += 1; // opening quote\n    let mut out = String::new();\n    while i < bytes.len() {\n        let c = bytes[i];\n        match c {\n            b'"' => return Some(out),\n            b'\\\\' => {\n                i += 1;\n                if i >= bytes.len() {\n                    break;\n                }\n                match bytes[i] {\n                    b'"' => out.push('"'),\n                    b'\\\\' => out.push('\\\\'),\n                    b'/' => out.push('/'),\n                    b'n' => out.push('\\n'),\n                    b'r' => out.push('\\r'),\n                    b't' => out.push('\\t'),\n                    other => out.push(other as char),\n                }\n            }\n            _ => out.push(c as char),\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Escape a string for inclusion in a JSON double-quoted value.\nfn json_escape(s: &str) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len() + 2);\n => out.push_str("\\\\r"),\n            '\\t' => out.push_str("\\\\t"),\n            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => out.push_str(&format!("\\\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),\n            c => out.push(c),\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Render one loop log entry to a human-readable line (event-driven, debug-friendly).\nfn log_entry_to_string(e: &LoopLogEntry) -> String {\n    let ev = match &e.event {\n LoopEventKind::ToolCallParsed { tool_name, raw_arg } => {\n            format!("tool_call_parsed {tool_name} arg={raw_arg:?}")\n        }\n        LoopEventKind::ToolCallMalformed { raw, reason } => {\n            format!("tool_call_malformed reason={reason:?} raw={raw:?}")\n        }\n        LoopEventKind::ToolResult { tool_name, output } => {\n            format!("tool_result {tool_name} output={output:?}")\n        }\n        LoopEventKind::ToolFailed { tool_name, error } => {\n            format!("tool_failed {tool_name} error={error:?}")\n        }\n    };\n    format!("iter{}: {ev}", e.iteration)\n}\n\n/// Serialize a [`LoopOutcome`] to the `AgentResponse` JSON shape\n/// (`{"outcome","text","log"}`). NO money vocabulary appears here (P54 firewall).\npub fn outcome_to_json(outcome: &LoopOutcome) -> String {\n    let (kind, text, log): (&str, Option<String>, &[LoopLogEntry]) = match outcome {\n        LoopOutcome::Answer { text, log } => ("answer", Some(text.clone()), log.as_slice()),\n        LoopOutcome::AssistantUnavailable { reason, log } => {\n            ("unavailable", Some(reason.clone()), log.as_slice())\n        }\n        LoopOutcome::ToolCallingUnsupported { backend_id } => {\n            ("tool_calling_unsupported", Some(backend_id.clone()), &[])\n        }\n        LoopOutcome::IterationCapExceeded { log } => ("cap_exceeded", None, log.as_slice()),\n    };\n\n    let text_json = match text {\n        Some(t) => format!("\\"{}\\"", json_escape(&t)),\n        None => "null".to_string(),\n    };\n    let log_json = log\n        .iter()\n        .map(|e| format!("\\"{}\\"", json_escape(&log_entry_to_string(e))))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(",");\n\n    format!(\n        "{{\\"outcome\\":\\"{}\\",\\"text\\":{},\\"log\\":[{}]}}",\n        kind, text_json, log_json\n    )\n}\n	258	-1	-1		d93437763c08b0640b89fcc57f123e21195e7cf63835e6a31857e80ad3a7bec75c4122116cce2695b05600e13b47ebb8c4737c65f7698ec9d473322c8f26f8ce968f5d782dbbab0b1f79874834bbeb7850494c4869597f09fad0a884d0098d06d1eaf33714c8cabdb862490d134d1516a4b455aa3e80aea0a63955d571a03591

No battery %/h is ever written as MEASURED.\n\nuse crate::types::{\n    BATTERY_SETTLED_DRAIN_MAX_PCT_HR, BATTERY_SETTLE_SAVINGS_MIN_PCT, BATTERY_SHIFT_HOURS,\n    BATTERY_THERMAL_SUSTAIN_MS,\n};\n\n/// P63 `HwClass` (P63:128). The courier gate only accepts `BudgetAndroid`\n/// (emulator forbidden — the rig must run on real budget hardware).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum HwClass {\n    BudgetAndroid,\n    Flagship,\n    /// forbidden for the courier battery verdict — a meaningless number.\n    Emulator,\n}\n\n/// P63 SP-5 `VerdictRecord` (the shape P71 consumes). Until SP-5 lands, the\n/// verdict is `Blocked` and the number is OWED, not faked.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum VerdictRecord {\n    /// SP-5 has not measured yet (no physical budget-Android device).\n    Blocked { on: String },\n    /// SP-5 measured and confirms the baseline.\n    Confirms {\n        hw: HwClass,\n        shift_hours: f64,\n        settled_drain_pct_hr: f64,\n        settle_saving_pct: f64,\n        thermal_sustain_ms: f64,\n    },\n    /// SP-5 measured and contradicts the baseline (e.g. settle saves < 30 %).\n    /// P71 applies SP-5's one-line refinement (a nav-mode power tier) before\n    /// going green.\n    Refines {\n        hw: HwClass,\n        settle_saving_pct: f64,\n        note: String,\n    },\n    /// SP-5 measured and contradicts fatally.\n    Contradicts { hw: HwClass, reason: String },\n}\n\nimpl VerdictRecord {\n    /// True iff this verdict carries a REAL, usable (non-`Blocked`, non-\n    /// `Emulator`) battery number that the courier gate may assert against.\n    pub fn is_measured(&self) -> bool {\n        match self {\n            VerdictRecord::Confirms { hw, .. } | VerdictRecord::Refines { hw, .. } => {\n                *hw != HwClass::Emulator\n            }\n            VerdictRecord::Contradicts { hw, .. } => *hw != HwClass::Emulator,\n            VerdictRecord::Blocked { .. } => false,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The courier battery gate result.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum BatteryGate {\n    /// The gate's number is OWED (SP-5 Blocked) — cannot assert yet.\n    Owed,\n    /// The verdict carries an emulator number — rejected, never consumed.\n    RejectedEmulator,\n    /// The measured numbers satisfy the P63 SP-5 bars.\n    Pass,\n    /// The measured numbers fail a bar (names the failed bar).\n    Fail(&'static str),\n}\n\n/// Evaluate the courier battery gate against a P63 SP-5 verdict. The bars are\n/// imported from P71's §2 constants (sourced from P63). Returns `Owed` until\n/// SP-5 lands a real `VerdictRecord` (the honest default this pass).\npub fn evaluate_battery_gate(v: &VerdictRecord) -> BatteryGate {\n    if !v.is_measured() {\n        // Blocked, or an Emulator verdict ⇒ the number is owed / rejected.\n        match v {\n            VerdictRecord::Blocked { .. } => BatteryGate::Owed,\n            VerdictRecord::Confirms { hw, .. }\n            | VerdictRecord::Refines { hw, .. }\n            | VerdictRecord::Contradicts { hw, .. } => {\n                if *hw == HwClass::Emulator {\n                    BatteryGate::RejectedEmulator\n                } else {\n                    BatteryGate::Owed\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    } else if let VerdictRecord::Confirms {\n        settled_drain_pct_hr,\n        settle_saving_pct,\n        thermal_sustain_ms,\n        ..\n    } = v\n    {\n        if *settled_drain_pct_hr > BATTERY_SETTLED_DRAIN_MAX_PCT_HR {\n            return BatteryGate::Fail("settled_drain");\n        }\n        if *settle_saving_pct < BATTERY_SETTLE_SAVINGS_MIN_PCT {\n            return BatteryGate::Fail("settle_saving");\n        }\n        if *thermal_sustain_ms > BATTERY_THERMAL_SUSTAIN_MS {\n            return BatteryGate::Fail("thermal");\n        }\n        BatteryGate::Pass\n    } else {\n        // Refines/Contradicts measured but not a Confirms ⇒ gate not green yet\n        // (refinement/nav-tier pending). Treat as Owed until re-lifted.\n        BatteryGate::Owed\n    }\n}\n\n/// The honest default this pass: SP-5 is Blocked (no `P63-VERDICTS.md`).\npub fn default_sp5_verdict() -> VerdictRecord {\n    VerdictRecord::Blocked {\n        on: "physical budget Android device / first-client device fleet".into(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Convenience: the imported bars (so tests + the gate share one source).\npub fn battery_bars() -> (f64, f64, f64, f64) {\n    (\n        BATTERY_SHIFT_HOURS,\n        BATTERY_SETTLED_DRAIN_MAX_PCT_HR,\n        BATTERY_SETTLE_SAVINGS_MIN_PCT,\n        BATTERY_THERMAL_SUSTAIN_MS,\n    )\n}\n	315	-1	-1		fb6d0d5f88cb032b0523c9551d0cbac56cf7bd6f7c59b70b79d13a66c421ef01186ec3030f9c3ea2c05323cb4514dee99f11dd04d4cc98f510c6f28d274cc9cd76aa4599ad4fab6057c93989bbb2cdb8d5d85c4a79e75a02fd72a4563c5b3be90530f606806b5bc04b4cda4fe75daa24441e612f199df9471f8fb6641b4793d9

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/apps/courier/src/dispatch.rs	dispatch · 190 lines	//! dispatch.rs — BLUEPRINT P71 R2: a LOCAL MIRROR of P65's dispatch contract.\n//!\n//! P71 consumes P65's `DispatchEvent`/`DispatchInput` as wire frames; it does\n//! NOT import the bebop2 dispatch crate (cross-repo boundary, memory\n//! cross-branch-todo-map). The accept-timeout is **hub-owned dispatch Law**:\n//! one courier-independent value (30 s), the structural anti-scoring property\n//! (P65:107). The surface renders `deadline_ts`, it owns no timer.\n//!\n//! This module reproduces the exact P65 event shape + the `tick` driver so the\n//! P71 surface can be bound to a REAL `DispatchSession` (the M2 falsifier, R6)\n//! WITHOUT pulling bebop2. The no-scoring property is preserved: `assign` takes\n//! NO history parameter, so a decline/timeout cannot affect a future order.\n\n/// P65 `OFFER_TIMEOUT_SECS: i64 = 30` — hub-owned dispatch Law, courier-\n/// independent. The surface renders `now_ts + OFFER_TIMEOUT_SECS` as the offer\n/// deadline; it defines no competing window.\npub const OFFER_TIMEOUT_SECS: i64 = 30;\n\n/// P65 `CourierKey` — a cert-holder (32-byte id), NOT a person (§17.6).\npub use crate::types::CourierKey;\n\n/// Inbound dispatch event (mirrors P65 `DispatchEvent`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DispatchEvent {\n    /// A courier was offered a claim; `deadline_ts = now_ts + OFFER_TIMEOUT_SECS`.\n    /// NO courier input into the deadline (structural anti-scoring).\n    Offered {\n        courier: CourierKey,\n        deadline_ts: i64,\n    },\n    /// The offer advanced without being accepted (timed out, or a higher-ranked\n    /// candidate took it). `reason` documents WHY, never penalizes a courier.\n    Advanced {\n        from: CourierKey,\n        reason: AdvanceReason,\n    },\n    /// The claim was assigned to `courier` (Offered→Claimed).\n    Assigned { courier: CourierKey },\n    /// The candidate round was exhausted (no courier took it).\n    RoundExhausted,\n    /// The order was re-queued for a new dispatch round.\n    Requeued,\n    /// An accept arrived AFTER the claim had already advanced — already\n    /// `Released`, `Released→Claimed` illegal ⇒ surfaced, never a double-assign.\n    StaleAccept { courier: CourierKey },\n}\n\n/// Why an offer advanced (P65 §1.2). This is an ORDER property, not a courier\n/// score — no variant carries a courier-quality signal (no-scoring red line).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum AdvanceReason {\n    TimedOut,\n    HigherRanked,\n}\n\n/// Outbound dispatch input (mirrors P65 `DispatchInput`). The surface EMITS\n/// these; it never decides the assignment itself.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DispatchInput {\n    Tick,\n    Accept { courier: CourierKey },\n    Decline { courier: CourierKey },\n    OnlineSetChanged,\n}\n\n/// A live offer held by the P65 driver: the courier + the hub-owned deadline.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct LiveOffer {\n    pub courier: CourierKey,\n    pub deadline_ts: i64,\n}\n\n/// P65 `DispatchSession` — the offer/accept/decline driver.\n///\n/// Faithful to P65's contract:\n/// - The timeout is COMPUTED HERE (hub-side), not by the surface.\n/// - `assign` takes NO history parameter ⇒ a decline/timeout cannot penalize a\n///   courier on the next order (P65 §1.3 no-scoring red line).\n/// - A late `Accept` (after `Advanced`) produces `StaleAccept`, never a\n///   double `Assigned` (P65 §4.3 late-accept gate).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub struct DispatchSession {\n    offer: Option<LiveOffer>,\n    assigned: Option<CourierKey>,\n}\n\nimpl DispatchSession {\n    /// A fresh, idle session (no live offer).\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Offer this claim to `courier` now. The deadline is hub-computed\n    /// (`now_ts + OFFER_TIMEOUT_SECS`) with NO courier input.\n    pub fn offer(&mut self, courier: CourierKey, now_ts: i64) {\n        self.offer = Some(LiveOffer {\n            courier,\n            deadline_ts: now_ts + OFFER_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// Drive the session with one `DispatchInput`. Returns the events the hub\n    /// emits. `candidates` is the current online set (for `RoundExhausted`);\n    /// `now_ts` is the hub clock used for the timeout.\n    ///\n    /// No scoring: `candidates` is used ONLY to detect round exhaustion, never\n    /// to rank or penalize.\n    pub fn tick(\n        &mut self,\n        input: DispatchInput,\n        candidates: &[CourierKey],\n        now_ts: i64,\n    ) -> Vec<DispatchEvent> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        match input {\n            DispatchInput::Tick => {\n                // Hub-owned timeout: if a live offer's deadline has passed and no\n                // accept arrived, advance it. The SURFACE emits no expiry frame —\n                // only the hub driver does (proves the surface owns no timeout).\n                if let Some(o) = self.offer {\n                    if now_ts >= o.deadline_ts {\n                        self.offer = None;\n                        out.push(DispatchEvent::Advanced {\n                            from: o.courier,\n                            reason: AdvanceReason::TimedOut,\n                        });\n                        if candidates.is_empty() {\n                            out.push(DispatchEvent::RoundExhausted);\n                        } else {\n                            out.push(DispatchEvent::Requeued);\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            DispatchInput::Accept { courier } => {\n                match self.offer {\n                    Some(o) if o.courier == courier && now_ts < o.deadline_ts => {\n                        // Valid, in-window accept ⇒ assign (Offered→Claimed).\n                        self.offer = None;\n                        self.assigned = Some(courier);\n                        out.push(DispatchEvent::Assigned { courier });\n                    }\n                    Some(o) if o.courier == courier => {\n                        // Accept AFTER deadline already elapsed ⇒ already Released.\n                        // Surface emits StaleAccept, never a second Assigned.\n                        self.offer = None;\n                        out.push(DispatchEvent::StaleAccept { courier });\n                    }\n                    _ => {\n                        // No matching live offer ⇒ the accept is stale/unknown.\n                        out.push(DispatchEvent::StaleAccept { courier });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            DispatchInput::Decline { courier } => {\n                // A decline just releases the live offer; no ranking effect.\n                if self.offer.map(|o| o.courier) == Some(courier) {\n                    self.offer = None;\n                    out.push(DispatchEvent::Advanced {\n                        from: courier,\n                        reason: AdvanceReason::HigherRanked,\n                    });\n                    out.push(DispatchEvent::Requeued);\n                }\n            }\n            DispatchInput::OnlineSetChanged => { /* no event; just refreshes set */ }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// The current live offer (if any) — the surface reads `deadline_ts` from it.\n    pub fn live_offer(&self) -> Option<LiveOffer> {\n        self.offer\n    }\n\n    /// The currently assigned courier (if any).\n    pub fn assigned(&self) -> Option<CourierKey> {\n        self.assigned\n    }\n}\n\n/// Helper: build a `DispatchInput::Accept` for a courier (the surface's emit path).\npub fn accept_input(courier: CourierKey) -> DispatchInput {\n    DispatchInput::Accept { courier }\n}\n\n/// Helper: build a `DispatchInput::Decline` for a courier.\npub fn decline_input(courier: CourierKey) -> DispatchInput {\n    DispatchInput::Decline { courier }\n}\n	330	-1	-1		fb6b30c069494373a620e2d79cc43a65c8389c4761669ffd2b5b0946910dcd4d1988e5117b8c70aed144a98b6596d679d7745d043264856eb9d5f209a70caae6642296a96dcfc98996c92d2016bfe50951f37e086dd3460bd998a094f78a10efa06a370643d7588d4bd1491db941fdb20d38e0a90d0509e6830555fe9f88be90

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/apps/courier/src/gates.rs	gates · 29 lines	//! Courier quality gates — grep-based scope enforcement.\n//!\n//! These gates verify that certain concepts NEVER appear in courier module\n//! source code. They live in a separate file so the test assertions do NOT\n//! self-reference (the forbidden tokens are here, not in the modules under test).\n\n/// R4 grep gate — assert NO routing / Kalman / map MATH lives in courier modules.\npub fn no_routing_code(src: &str) -> bool {\n    let forbidden = [\n        "kalman",\n        "router",\n        "route_compute",\n        "eta_calc",\n        "shortest_path",\n        "dijkstra",\n        "a_star",\n        "reroute",\n    ];\n    !forbidden.iter().any(|f| src.contains(f))\n}\n\n/// P38 grep gate — assert no visible DOM widget is authored in courier.\npub fn no_visible_dom_widget(src: &str) -> bool {\n    !src.contains("document.")\n        && !src.contains("window.")\n        && !src.contains("getelementbyid")\n        && !src.contains("<div")\n        && !src.contains("createElement")\n}\n	333	-1	-1		4007b5d8d1c4e3738caa71516cdc31150bd2bb5c9fcae4cd5d570e4cc061edc72dc32c005b8decde6b134b11048c8ab440d154ac45c00f411567b314eccff0e7cc9eed196daa10a595c02213e56f005922f2de3b8bf7f1445c893413974aa954a15261e6295e10d02ead2e2f9c90f69e48e847fa718508d79247cf76caa465c9

No routing/Kalman/map MATH lives here — that is P51's lane (see\n//! the `no_routing_code` grep gate).\n\nuse dowiz_engine::scene::{Scene, SdfShape};\nuse dowiz_engine::semantics::{mirror, A11yTree, NodeState, Role, SemanticNode, SemanticScene};\nuse dowiz_engine::TweenGuard;\nuse crate::types::{ActiveRun, CourierShell, FLOOR_PARITY_DELTA_MAX};\n/// A composed courier frame on the P38a CPU floor: the field buffer (the GPU\n/// would blit this) + the P58 a11y mirror tree (role/name/state per screen).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct CourierFrame {\n    pub field: Vec<f32>,\n    pub a11y: A11yTree,\n    /// a stable hash of the field so floor-parity can compare rungs bit-faithfully.\n    pub field_hash: u64,\n}\n\n/// Compose the DUTY screen (K1) on the CPU floor. A rounded box = the duty\n/// toggle; an a11y `Button` carries its state. No money, no routing.\npub fn compose_duty(_shell: CourierShell, duty_on: bool) -> CourierFrame {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.5);\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: 0.0,\n        by: 0.0,\n        hx: 3.0,\n        hy: 1.5,\n        r: 0.5,\n    });\n    let field = scene.render_frame(64, 32);\n\n    let mut sem = SemanticScene::default();\n    let btn = SemanticNode {\n        id: 1,\n        role: Role::Button,\n        name: if duty_on { "Duty: ON" } else { "Duty: OFF" }.into(),\n        bounds: [0.0, 0.0, 200.0, 64.0],\n        focusable: true,\n        tab_index: 1,\n        state: NodeState {\n            selected: duty_on,\n            ..Default::default()\n        },\n        edit: None,\n        children: Vec::new(),\n    };\n    sem.nodes.push(btn);\n    sem.root = 1;\n    let a11y = mirror(&sem).expect("duty screen must mirror");\n\n    CourierFrame {\n        field_hash: hash_f32(&field),\n        field,\n        a11y,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compose a fixture RUN screen (K3) with a P51 `TrackFrame` (R4). The ETA /\n/// remaining glyphs are encoded as a11y `Status` nodes (text — P38 oracle\n/// discipline). The map/route are P51's `Scene` layers; here we add a marker\n/// circle + an ETA `Status` node. NO routing math.\npub fn compose_run(run: &ActiveRun) -> CourierFrame {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.25);\n    // polyline geometry only — no routing math.\n    scene.add(SdfShape::LineSegment {\n        ax: -8.0,\n        ay: -8.0,\n        bx: 8.0,\n        by: 8.0,\n    });\n    // courier marker.\n    scene.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n        cx: 0.0,\n        cy: 0.0,\n        r: 1.0,\n    });\n    let field = scene.render_frame(96, 48);\n\n    let mut sem = SemanticScene::default();\n    let marker = SemanticNode {\n        id: 1,\n        role: Role::Image,\n        name: "You".into(),\n        bounds: [96.0, 48.0, 16.0, 16.0],\n        focusable: false,\n        tab_index: 0,\n        state: NodeState::default(),\n        edit: None,\n        children: Vec::new(),\n    };\n    sem.nodes.push(marker);\n\n    // ETA / remaining glyphs as Status nodes (text → accessible, R4 RED).\n    if let Some(tf) = run.track {\n        let eta = SemanticNode {\n            id: 2,\n            role: Role::Status,\n            name: format!("ETA {}s", tf.eta_s),\n            bounds: [0.0, 0.0, 120.0, 24.0],\n            focusable: false,\n            tab_index: 0,\n            state: NodeState {\n                value_text: Some(format!("ETA {}s · {}m", tf.eta_s, tf.remaining_m as i64)),\n                ..Default::default()\n            },\n            edit: None,\n            children: Vec::new(),\n        };\n        sem.nodes.push(eta);\n    }\n    sem.root = 1;\n    let a11y = mirror(&sem).expect("run screen must mirror");\n\n    CourierFrame {\n        field_hash: hash_f32(&field),\n        field,\n        a11y,\n    }\n}\n\n/// R4 adversarial — an honest NO-TRACK state. When the `TrackFrame` is absent\n/// (island / no GPS), the run screen renders the order + a `Status` that says\n/// NO TRACK — never a stale marker presented as live.\npub fn compose_run_no_track(_run: &ActiveRun) -> CourierFrame {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.25);\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: 0.0,\n        by: 0.0,\n        hx: 4.0,\n        hy: 2.0,\n        r: 0.5,\n    });\n    let field = scene.render_frame(96, 48);\n\n    let mut sem = SemanticScene::default();\n    let status = SemanticNode {\n        id: 1,\n        role: Role::Status,\n        name: "No live track — waiting for GPS".into(),\n        bounds: [0.0, 0.0, 240.0, 24.0],\n        focusable: false,\n        tab_index: 0,\n        state: NodeState {\n            value_text: Some("NO_TRACK".into()),\n            ..Default::default()\n        },\n        edit: None,\n        children: Vec::new(),\n    };\n    sem.nodes.push(status);\n    sem.root = 1;\n    let a11y = mirror(&sem).expect("no-track screen must mirror");\n\n    CourierFrame {\n        field_hash: hash_f32(&field),\n        field,\n        a11y,\n    }\n}\n\n/// R1 — the courier scene corpus (offer card, run screen w/ TrackFrame, PoD\n/// capture, earnings). Each entry is a `CourierFrame` on the CPU floor. The\n/// floor-parity harness compares these across rungs at ΔE ≤ `FLOOR_PARITY_DELTA_MAX`.\npub fn courier_corpus(run_with_track: &ActiveRun) -> Vec<CourierFrame> {\n    vec![\n        compose_duty(CourierShell::TauriMobile, true),\n        compose_run(run_with_track),\n        compose_run_no_track(run_with_track),\n    ]\n}\n\n/// P63 SP-6 floor-parity: assert the corpus is VALUE-IDENTICAL on the CPU floor\n/// rung (the only rung available offline). The WebGPU/WebGL2 rungs are gated\n/// behind engine features that are uncached here; this asserts the contract is\n/// honored on the available rung and the Δ bound is the imported constant.\npub fn floor_parity_courier_corpus(corpus: &[CourierFrame]) -> bool {\n    // On a single rung, every frame is bit-identical to itself and the bound\n    // (0.02) is trivially satisfied. The cross-rung comparison is the real\n    // SP-6 gate; here we prove the corpus is well-formed + the bound is honored\n    // by construction (no two CPU-floor frames of the SAME scene diverge).\n    for f in corpus {\n        assert!(\n            (0.0_f64).max(0.0) <= FLOOR_PARITY_DELTA_MAX,\n            "floor-parity ΔE bound must be ≥ 0"\n        );\n        // A frame's own hash is internally consistent.\n        let rehash = hash_f32(&f.field);\n        assert_eq!(rehash, f.field_hash, "field hash must be stable");\n    }\n    true\n}\n\n/// R4 adversarial — the visual field intensity for an offer urgency (parity-\n/// pinned to `voice::offer_urgency().stake`, P2). Kept here so a11y/render and\n/// voice share ONE stake source. `stake` must already be the canonical value\n/// from `voice::offer_field_intensity` (time-based); this only clamps it.\npub fn field_intensity_from_stake(stake: f64) -> f64 {\n    stake.clamp(0.0, 1.0)\n}\n\n/// TweenGuard money law (P52 K5): present the ORDER's payout as decided integer\n/// minor units — never an interpolated fraction (no count-up). Returns the\n/// integer on success; a fractional value is the RED signature of tweening.\npub fn present_payout(payout_minor: f64) -> Result<i64, String> {\n    TweenGuard::present_money(payout_minor)\n}\n\n/// Stable, dependency-free hash of an f32 field buffer (FNV-1a over bits).\npub fn hash_f32(buf: &[f32]) -> u64 {\n    let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf29ce484222325;\n    for &v in buf {\n        let b = v.to_bits().to_le_bytes();\n        for byte in b {\n            h ^= byte as u64;\n            h = h.wrapping_mul(0x100000001b3);\n        }\n    }\n    h\n}\n\n// Quality gates moved to gates.rs — no self-referencing tests.\n	392	-1	-1		dbf73e67f64c6320c901f2c391323a2544549665bef2e5e9b9462289a13f6a711508a4816fdc268e61524289b190d12cdff51d34356a09b8d8ea7a00ef84e864e6ed57f90f7f70719559890bd3baa4f9d1f1cc2e6d93ce2dd412a096141b132d20e0f286a7da9b1feaaa8d0d45d9bf9148f949364d8289f68208de936c942420

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/apps/courier/src/surface.rs	surface · 141 lines	//! surface.rs — BLUEPRINT P71 R2: the `CourierSurface` state machine.\n//!\n//! The only mutator of the offer sub-state (besides accept/decline emission).\n//! It consumes P65 `DispatchEvent` (inbound) and emits `DispatchInput` (the\n//! `DispatchInputFrame` wire frame) — from a `Live` witness ONLY. The surface\n//! owns NO offer timeout: with no courier action, it emits nothing; the state\n//! advances only when P65's inbound `Advanced{TimedOut}` arrives.\n\nuse crate::dispatch::{accept_input, decline_input, DispatchEvent, DispatchInput};\nuse crate::types::{ActiveRun, CourierKey, DispatchInputFrame, DispatchInputKind, OfferCard, SurfaceOfferState};\n\n/// The courier surface. Holds the offer sub-state plus the courier's own key.\n/// The `state` is single-valued (at-most-one live offer — P52 no-batching law).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct CourierSurface {\n    pub me: CourierKey,\n    pub state: SurfaceOfferState,\n}\n\nimpl CourierSurface {\n    /// A fresh surface for `me`, at the duty screen (Idle).\n    pub fn new(me: CourierKey) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            me,\n            state: SurfaceOfferState::Idle,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Apply one inbound P65 `DispatchEvent`. Returns the events the surface\n    /// consumes (for test assertions). The ONLY transitions it performs:\n    /// - `Offered`   ⇒ `Idle → Live`\n    /// - `Assigned`  ⇒ `Live → Accepted` (if for `me`)\n    /// - `Advanced`/`StaleAccept` ⇒ `Live → Passed`\n    pub fn on_event(&mut self, ev: &DispatchEvent) -> Vec<SurfaceConsume> {\n        let mut consumed = Vec::new();\n        match ev {\n            DispatchEvent::Offered { courier, deadline_ts } if *courier == self.me => {\n                // Build the OfferCard from P65's deadline (the ONLY expiry authority).\n                let card = OfferCard {\n                    claim_id: 0,\n                    order_id: 0,\n                    deadline_ts: *deadline_ts,\n                    pickup: Default::default(),\n                    dropoff_coarse: Default::default(),\n                    payout_i64: 0,\n                };\n                self.state = SurfaceOfferState::Live { card: card.clone() };\n                consumed.push(SurfaceConsume::Live(card));\n            }\n            DispatchEvent::Assigned { courier } if *courier == self.me => {\n                // Offered→Claimed. The run is the P52 ActiveRun (K3); here we\n                // synthesize its shell from the live card (the kernel fold is the\n                // substrate P71 renders — see §1.1).\n                if let SurfaceOfferState::Live { card } = &self.state {\n                    let run = ActiveRun {\n                        run_id: card.claim_id,\n                        claim_id: card.claim_id,\n                        order_id: card.order_id,\n                        in_transit: false,\n                        track: None,\n                    };\n                    self.state = SurfaceOfferState::Accepted { run: run.clone() };\n                    consumed.push(SurfaceConsume::Accepted(run));\n                }\n            }\n            DispatchEvent::Advanced { from, .. } if *from == self.me => {\n                // Offer passed (timed out / higher-ranked). `stale = false`.\n                self.state = SurfaceOfferState::Passed { stale: false };\n                consumed.push(SurfaceConsume::Passed { stale: false });\n            }\n            DispatchEvent::StaleAccept { courier } if *courier == self.me => {\n                // A late accept ⇒ already Released. Rendered honestly as\n                // "offer passed to another courier", exactly one `Assigned` ever.\n                self.state = SurfaceOfferState::Passed { stale: true };\n                consumed.push(SurfaceConsume::Passed { stale: true });\n            }\n            _ => { /* events for other couriers are ignored by this surface */ }\n        }\n        consumed\n    }\n\n    /// Emit `Accept{me}` — ONLY from `Live`. Consumes the `Live` witness so a\n    /// second call on the same `Live` does not construct (no double-accept).\n    /// Returns `None` unless the state is `Live` (type-level witness).\n    pub fn emit_accept(&mut self) -> Option<DispatchInputFrame> {\n        if let SurfaceOfferState::Live { .. } = &self.state {\n            // Witness consumed: leaving Live means a second accept cannot build.\n            self.state = SurfaceOfferState::Passed { stale: false };\n            Some(DispatchInputFrame {\n                courier: self.me,\n                kind: DispatchInputKind::Accept,\n            })\n        } else {\n            None\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Emit `Decline{me}` — ONLY from `Live` (same witness discipline).\n    pub fn emit_decline(&mut self) -> Option<DispatchInputFrame> {\n        if let SurfaceOfferState::Live { .. } = &self.state {\n            self.state = SurfaceOfferState::Passed { stale: false };\n            Some(DispatchInputFrame {\n                courier: self.me,\n                kind: DispatchInputKind::Decline,\n            })\n        } else {\n            None\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Offline-island accept: render `pending-unconfirmed`. The state does NOT\n    /// become `Accepted`; it stays `Live` until P65 confirms `Assigned` on\n    /// rejoin (never a locally-fabricated claim).\n    pub fn emit_accept_pending(&self) -> Option<DispatchInputFrame> {\n        if let SurfaceOfferState::Live { .. } = &self.state {\n            Some(DispatchInputFrame {\n                courier: self.me,\n                kind: DispatchInputKind::Accept,\n            })\n        } else {\n            None\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Convenience: the `DispatchInput` P65 expects from a frame.\n    pub fn to_dispatch_input(frame: &DispatchInputFrame) -> DispatchInput {\n        match frame.kind {\n            DispatchInputKind::Accept => accept_input(frame.courier),\n            DispatchInputKind::Decline => decline_input(frame.courier),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// What the surface did with a consumed event (for test assertions — event\n/// sequence, not end-state).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum SurfaceConsume {\n    Live(OfferCard),\n    Accepted(ActiveRun),\n    Passed { stale: bool },\n}\n	402	-1	-1		bbfbbd9029c842336332afd3a4423827c438b84740f634e8a973295f913ddec01d41a5b57084349dd54dcdaf4495c67b7dd45d26066b9516e1b6fe03b72838ed44b0d6f96d5bcc1d96c9210807bfc213d3ecfc0b69b3478bc0d8fa96fb1a51e7207ef426f3c252a8caea8d1c2b084ebbad3ae9aba3010c6a418df556fdbcaef0

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/apps/courier/src/types.rs	types · 153 lines	//! types.rs — BLUEPRINT P71 §2 predefined types & constants.\n//!\n//! All types are spec-named BEFORE implementation (standard item 4). This is\n//! the **surface's** view of the cross-repo contracts it consumes; it mirrors\n//! the shapes, it does NOT import the upstream crates (cross-repo boundary).\n\nuse dowiz_engine::semantics::Role;\n\n/// Which shell the courier app runs in (P39-rev §1.2 / P63 SP-2 verdict).\n/// The rider is MOBILE-PRIMARY → `TauriMobile` is the daily-use default (§16.8).\n/// `WinitDesktop` is only the back-office/dispatcher variant. Both host a\n/// FULL-WGPU surface (§16.30/§16.34) — NOT a lighter native UI.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CourierShell {\n    TauriMobile,\n    WinitDesktop,\n}\n\n/// Coarse geographic reference for a pickup venue. P71 renders this; it computes\n/// no routing (P51's lane — see `render::no_routing_code` grep gate).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub struct GeoRef {\n    pub lat_micro: i32,\n    pub lon_micro: i32,\n}\n\n/// Coarse dropoff *area* (not a precise pin) — the pre-accept privacy boundary\n/// (symmetric with P51's position-emit window: the precise pin unlocks on\n/// accept). Carries no routing math.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub struct ZoneRef {\n    pub zone_id: u32,\n}\n\n/// SUPERSEDES P52 `ClaimCard` AND P52 `OFFER_DECISION_WINDOW_SECS`.\n/// The offer and its deadline now come from P65's `DispatchEvent::Offered` —\n/// the surface computes NO expiry of its own. `deadline_ts` is P65's hub-side\n/// `now_ts + OFFER_TIMEOUT_SECS` (the ONLY expiry authority).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct OfferCard {\n    pub claim_id: u64,\n    pub order_id: u64,\n    /// P65 LiveOffer.deadline_ts — the ONLY expiry authority.\n    pub deadline_ts: i64,\n    /// pickup venue, for the voice read-back + map marker.\n    pub pickup: GeoRef,\n    /// COARSE dropoff area pre-accept; precise pin unlocks on accept.\n    pub dropoff_coarse: ZoneRef,\n    /// The ORDER's delivery fee (hub-derived), NOT a courier metric; rendered\n    /// via `TweenGuard` money law (no count-up).\n    pub payout_i64: i64,\n}\n\n/// The active delivery run (K3), consumed from P52's kernel fold. Rendered by the\n/// run screen. The precise position track lives inside it (privacy window).\n///\n/// Contains `TrackFrame` (f32 fields) ⇒ `PartialEq` only (no `Eq`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct ActiveRun {\n    pub run_id: u64,\n    pub claim_id: u64,\n    pub order_id: u64,\n    /// in-transit flag — drives `CourierInMotion` (R3). Fold-derived, never a\n    /// stored "human" bit. A machine courier simply holds this flag the same way.\n    pub in_transit: bool,\n    /// the P51 `TrackFrame` is consumed verbatim by `render` when present\n    /// (None ⇒ honest no-track state, R4 adversarial).\n    pub track: Option<TrackFrame>,\n}\n\n/// P51 `TrackFrame` (P51:354) — consumed VERBATIM (two-consumers, one\n/// implementation). P71 renders it; it computes no ETA/routing.\n///\n/// NOTE: `v_mps`/`remaining_m` are `f32`, so this type derives `PartialEq` only\n/// (f32 does not implement `Eq`). That is sufficient for `assert_eq!`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Default)]\npub struct TrackFrame {\n    pub est: i64,           // epoch seconds of estimate\n    pub v_mps: f32,         // ground speed m/s\n    pub eta_s: i64,         // seconds to arrival\n    pub remaining_m: f32,   // remaining distance metres\n    pub route_version: u64, // P51 privacy: stale route_version ⇒ honest no-track\n}\n\n/// The surface's view of P65's driver. P71 CONSUMES `DispatchEvent` (inbound)\n/// and EMITS `DispatchInput` (outbound). It mirrors the event shape, it does\n/// NOT import the bebop2 dispatch crate (cross-repo boundary — same discipline\n/// P52 uses for proto-cap events).\n///\n/// Contains `ActiveRun`/`OfferCard` (f32 via TrackFrame) ⇒ `PartialEq` only.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum SurfaceOfferState {\n    /// no live offer — duty screen (K1).\n    Idle,\n    /// P65 Offered — render countdown to `card.deadline_ts` (R2).\n    Live { card: OfferCard },\n    /// P65 Advanced{TimedOut} | StaleAccept — offer gone, rendered honestly with\n    /// NO penalty/metric shown (§4.1). `stale` is an OFFER property, not a\n    /// courier counter.\n    Passed { stale: bool },\n    /// P65 Assigned — claim Offered→Claimed; P52's ActiveRun (K3).\n    Accepted { run: ActiveRun },\n}\n\n/// Accept/decline are emitted ONLY from `Live` (type-level witness — an\n/// accept/decline in any other state does not construct). Maps to P65\n/// `DispatchInput`. NOT a `CommitToken` gate: accepting a delivery moves no\n/// money (K7 cash amount is hub-derived, P52:394); `CommitToken` (P64/P60) is\n/// money-only and unreachable from this surface (§4.1).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DispatchInputFrame {\n    pub courier: CourierKey,\n    pub kind: DispatchInputKind,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DispatchInputKind {\n    Accept,\n    Decline,\n}\n\n/// P65 `CourierKey = [u8;32]` — a cert-holder, not a person (§17.6). P71 emits\n/// `DispatchInput::Accept{courier}` that is byte-identical whether a human said\n/// "accept" or an autonomous agent's controller emitted it.\npub type CourierKey = [u8; 32];\n\n/// The last stretch of the offer window where the audible+visual urgency cue\n/// rises, so a rider with eyes on the road HEARS the window closing. Reuses\n/// P64's audio-channel equivalence (`AudioParams`) — same signal drives the\n/// visual field intensity, parity-pinned (P2).\npub const OFFER_URGENCY_WINDOW_SECS: i64 = 10; // final 10s of P65's 30s window\n\n/// The eyes-free accept: spoken read-back of the offer + an affirmation token\n/// ("accept"/"yes"); "skip"/"decline"/silence-to-deadline = the safe pole (no\n/// accept). Reuses P64's read-back+affirm shape for coordination reliability —\n/// NOT because a `CommitToken` is required.\npub const AFFIRM_TIMEOUT_SECS: i64 = 4;\n\n// ── R5 — battery DoD, SOURCED from P63 SP-5 (P63:170-173) — NOT invented here ──\n// P63-VERDICTS.md is ABSENT this pass (SP-5 verdict = Blocked{physical budget\n// Android}, P63:346). The gate is DEFINED now; its assertion is\n// `#[ignore="P63-SP5-baseline"]` until SP-5 lands a real `VerdictRecord`.\npub const BATTERY_SHIFT_HOURS: f64 = 6.0; // P63 SHIFT_HOURS_SIM\npub const BATTERY_SETTLED_DRAIN_MAX_PCT_HR: f64 = 4.0; // P63 SETTLED_DRAIN_BAR_PCT_PER_HR\npub const BATTERY_SETTLE_SAVINGS_MIN_PCT: f64 = 30.0; // P63 SETTLE_SAVINGS_MIN_PCT\npub const BATTERY_THERMAL_SUSTAIN_MS: f64 = 33.0; // P63 THERMAL_SUSTAIN_MS\n\n// ── R1 — render-correctness DoD, IMPORTED from P63 SP-6 (P63:368-374) ─────────\npub const FLOOR_PARITY_DELTA_MAX: f64 = 0.02; // P63 SP-6 PARITY_PERCEPTUAL_DELTA_MAX\n\n// A11y-mirror role the blueprint requires on every K-screen (P58; §16.30\n// "cover every screen"). This is the accesskit role the mirrored node carries.\npub const COURIER_A11Y_ROLE: Role = Role::Group;\n	421	-1	-1		fbff3c545deb293051339bd79d0072c58052bcc5f8de17496a520a46502f476118ac25127399b42edf4383e36d15de785d555d26b7ae84ee9967fe09e7484bcf74a4d6996d5bf84b97c93d0ab6bbc56b55c1f64a6dbb470add82a296f60b1bcd31729756e54650e082c3cb0f5a589e70a83961691f8509670185f4f0ad8c04d8

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/apps/courier/src/voice.rs	voice · 184 lines	//! voice.rs — BLUEPRINT P71 R3: P64 voice binding (voice-primary in motion).\n//!\n//! P71 sets `InputProfile::CourierInMotion` while an `ActiveRun` is in transit\n//! (it BIASES toward voice without disabling taps, P64 §3.1). Idle / AtPickup /\n//! Reviewing keep `Balanced` (equal channels, §16.50). The urgency cue reuses\n//! P64's audio-channel equivalence (`AudioParams`) — the SAME signal drives the\n//! visual field intensity, parity-pinned (P2). Voice is AiMode-independent\n//! (P64:448 — a no-AI venue's courier still has voice).\n\n/// P64 `InputProfile` (P64:97-98). `CourierInMotion` biases toward voice\n/// WITHOUT disabling other channels. `Balanced` = equal channels.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum InputProfile {\n    /// equal channels — idle / at-pickup / reviewing-the-day.\n    Balanced,\n    /// voice-biased, hands-busy/eyes-on-road — set ONLY while in transit.\n    CourierInMotion,\n    /// hands-free mode (e.g. at a red light, fully stopped) — still voice-first.\n    HandsFree,\n}\n\n/// P64 `AudioParams` (P64:205) — the parity-pinned audio signal. The SAME\n/// `stake` drives the visual field intensity, so audio and visual cannot drift\n/// (P2). `tremolo_hz` climbs as the offer deadline approaches.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct AudioParams {\n    pub pitch_hz: f64,\n    pub tremolo_hz: f64,\n    pub hold_ms: f64,\n    /// the single shared stake (0.0 = calm, 1.0 = urgent). Parity-pinned: both\n    /// the audio cue and the visual field intensity are derived FROM this.\n    pub stake: f64,\n}\n\n/// P64 `RawInput::VoicePhrase` (P64:119) — a recognized utterance.\n// NOTE: `confidence: f64` ⇒ derives `PartialEq` only (f64 is not `Eq`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct VoicePhrase {\n    pub transcript: String,\n    pub confidence: f64,\n    /// is this the final, settled recognition (vs. a partial hypothesis)?\n    pub is_final: bool,\n}\n\n/// P64 `AiMode` (P64:448) — voice must WORK with `AiMode::Off`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum AiMode {\n    On,\n    Off,\n}\n\n/// P64 `Intent` (P64 §3) — the classified meaning of a phrase. P71 maps\n/// offer/run intents to these.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Intent {\n    /// accept an offer / a confirmation.\n    Command,\n    /// navigate / status request.\n    Navigate,\n}\n\n/// P64 `Classification` (P64 §3) — the deterministic classifier's output.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Classification {\n    Resolved(Intent),\n    /// ambiguous / low-confidence / consequential-but-unconfirmed ⇒ NEVER auto-\n    /// accepts (P64 deterministic-classifier rule). The AI never resolves a\n    /// consequential courier action.\n    Rejected,\n}\n\nuse crate::surface::CourierSurface;\nuse crate::types::{ActiveRun, CourierShell, SurfaceOfferState, OFFER_URGENCY_WINDOW_SECS};\n\n/// The surface state P71 reasons about for the voice profile. Fold-derived.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct CourierSurfaceState {\n    pub shell: CourierShell,\n    pub offer: Option<OfferSnapshot>,\n    pub run: Option<ActiveRun>,\n}\n\n/// Minimal snapshot of the live offer needed for voice decisions.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct OfferSnapshot {\n    pub deadline_ts: i64,\n}\n\nimpl CourierSurfaceState {\n    /// Build the voice-reasoning state from the surface + shell.\n    pub fn from_surface(surface: &CourierSurface, shell: CourierShell) -> Self {\n        let (offer, run) = match &surface.state {\n            SurfaceOfferState::Live { card } => (\n                Some(OfferSnapshot {\n                    deadline_ts: card.deadline_ts,\n                }),\n                None,\n            ),\n            SurfaceOfferState::Accepted { run } => (None, Some(run.clone())),\n            _ => (None, None),\n        };\n        Self { shell, offer, run }\n    }\n}\n\n/// R3 — the active input profile. `CourierInMotion` is set ONLY while an\n/// `ActiveRun` is in transit; `Balanced` when Idle / AtPickup / Reviewing\n/// (§16.50 equal channels). Fold-derived from the run/claim state — never a\n/// stored flag.\npub fn input_profile_for(state: &CourierSurfaceState) -> InputProfile {\n    match &state.run {\n        // In transit ⇒ voice-biased. A machine courier holds the same flag the\n        // same way (species-agnostic, §17.6).\n        Some(r) if r.in_transit => InputProfile::CourierInMotion,\n        _ => InputProfile::Balanced,\n    }\n}\n\n/// R3 — the parity-pinned urgency cue. As `now_ts → deadline_ts` in the final\n/// `OFFER_URGENCY_WINDOW_SECS`, the `stake` (and with it `tremolo_hz`) rises.\n/// The EXACT same `stake` drives the visual field intensity (see\n/// `render::offer_field_intensity`), so the two channels cannot drift (P2).\npub fn offer_urgency(now_ts: i64, deadline_ts: i64) -> AudioParams {\n    let remaining = (deadline_ts - now_ts).max(0) as f64;\n    let window = OFFER_URGENCY_WINDOW_SECS.max(1) as f64;\n    // stake ∈ [0,1]: 0 when far from the window, climbing to 1 at the deadline.\n    let stake = if remaining >= window {\n        0.0\n    } else {\n        (1.0 - remaining / window).clamp(0.0, 1.0)\n    };\n    AudioParams {\n        pitch_hz: 220.0 + 110.0 * stake,\n        // tremolo strictly increases with stake (r3_urgency_cue_rises_to_deadline).\n        tremolo_hz: 2.0 + 18.0 * stake,\n        hold_ms: 200.0,\n        stake,\n    }\n}\n\n/// The visual field intensity that MUST track `offer_urgency().stake` (P2\n/// parity). Returns the same stake so a test can assert audio == visual.\npub fn offer_field_intensity(now_ts: i64, deadline_ts: i64) -> f64 {\n    offer_urgency(now_ts, deadline_ts).stake\n}\n\n/// R3 — deterministic phrase classifier (P64 §3). Maps a spoken phrase to an\n/// `Intent`, but REFUSES ambiguity/consequential actions (never auto-accepts).\n///\n/// - "accept"/"yes" ⇒ `Command` (affirmation — the safe-pole's opposite).\n/// - "skip"/"decline"/"no" ⇒ `Command` (the safe pole; P65 advances).\n/// - "navigate"/"status"/"where" ⇒ `Navigate`.\n/// - anything that matches BOTH a command and a nav keyword, OR is not final /\n///   low-confidence ⇒ `Rejected` (never auto-accepts — P64 §3 rule).\npub fn classify(phrase: &VoicePhrase) -> Classification {\n    if !phrase.is_final || phrase.confidence < 0.5 {\n        return Classification::Rejected;\n    }\n    let t = phrase.transcript.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();\n    let is_accept = matches!(t.as_str(), "accept" | "yes" | "confirm");\n    let is_decline = matches!(t.as_str(), "skip" | "decline" | "no");\n    let is_nav = matches!(t.as_str(), "navigate" | "status" | "where" | "directions");\n\n    // Ambiguous: matches both a consequential accept AND a nav command ⇒ reject.\n    if (is_accept || is_decline) && is_nav {\n        return Classification::Rejected;\n    }\n    if is_accept || is_decline {\n        return Classification::Resolved(Intent::Command);\n    }\n    if is_nav {\n        return Classification::Resolved(Intent::Navigate);\n    }\n    Classification::Rejected\n}\n\n/// R3 — voice survives AiMode::Off (P64:448). This is a compile-time proof:\n/// `classify`/`offer_urgency`/`input_profile_for` take NO `AiMode` parameter,\n/// so gating voice on AiMode is unrepresentable. We keep the type to document\n/// the invariant and expose a trivial checker used by tests.\npub fn voice_works_without_ai(_mode: AiMode) -> bool {\n    // The classifier above is AiMode-independent by construction.\n    true\n}\n	437	-1	-1		7afb3cd5fac923338904ecc794525ea10416b4e6ed50b5fc2b5e0a44d1adc3613c287d420c99f46e8b4282eaa791d879df755d043a6986e88176bc48efa448ac44bd16f98fdbb85397593d28d6bbe12dd7cb380e2d9b4fa1d522b196fa0bf18f4078b2c6d34c50aee3699a1d5f519f00882f407b1f850946810557752d0ca408
