Exercises the full courier render pipeline:\n//! 1. Engine FieldFrame creation and evolution\n//! 2. CourierFrame composition from a FieldFrame\n//! 3. CourierSurface state-machine transitions (Idle→Live→Accepted→Passed)\n//! 4. Field cell value validity\n//! 5. GeoRef coordinate validity\n//! 6. DispatchInputFrame creation and consumption by DispatchSession\n\nuse dowiz_courier::*;\nuse dowiz_courier::dispatch::*;\nuse dowiz_courier::render::*;\nuse dowiz_courier::surface::*;\nuse dowiz_courier::types::*;\nuse dowiz_engine::field_frame::{FieldEquilibrium, FieldFrame};\nuse dowiz_engine::scene::{Scene, SdfShape};\n\nconst ME: CourierKey = [1u8; 32];\n\nfn geo_ref(lat: i32, lon: i32) -> GeoRef {\n    GeoRef {\n        lat_micro: lat,\n        lon_micro: lon,\n    }\n}\n\n// ── 1. FieldFrame creation and evolution ───────────────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn field_frame_creates_and_evolves() {\n    let w = 16usize;\n    let h = 16usize;\n    let eq = FieldEquilibrium::default();\n\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.5);\n    scene.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n        cx: 0.0,\n        cy: 0.0,\n        r: 3.0,\n    });\n    let source = scene.render_frame(w, h);\n\n    let mut frame = FieldFrame::new(w, h);\n    // Initial field should be all zeros\n    for &v in frame.u() {\n        assert!(v.is_finite(), "initial field must be finite");\n        assert_eq!(v, 0.0, "initial field must be zero");\n    }\n\n    // Evolve a few steps\n    for _ in 0..10 {\n        frame.step(&source, &eq);\n    }\n\n    // After evolution, field must be finite everywhere\n    for &v in frame.u() {\n        assert!(v.is_finite(), "evolved field must be finite");\n    }\n\n    // RGBA output has correct dimensions\n    let rgba = frame.frame_rgba();\n    assert_eq!(rgba.len(), w * h * 4, "RGBA frame must be w*h*4 bytes");\n\n    // RGBA bytes are all valid (0-255)\n    for &b in &rgba {\n        assert!(b <= 255, "RGBA byte must be <= 255");\n    }\n}\n\n// ── 2. CourierFrame composition from a Scene ────────────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn courier_frame_composes_from_scene() {\n    let run = ActiveRun {\n        run_id: 42,\n        claim_id: 7,\n        order_id: 100,\n        in_transit: true,\n        track: Some(TrackFrame {\n            est: 1000,\n            v_mps: 5.5,\n            eta_s: 300,\n            remaining_m: 1650.0,\n            route_version: 1,\n        }),\n    };\n\n    let frame = compose_run(&run);\n    assert!(!frame.field.is_empty(), "field must not be empty");\n    assert_eq!(frame.field.len(), 96 * 48, "run frame is 96x48");\n    assert_eq!(frame.a11y.nodes.len(), 2, "run frame has marker + ETA a11y nodes");\n\n    // hash_f32 is stable\n    let h1 = hash_f32(&frame.field);\n    let h2 = hash_f32(&frame.field);\n    assert_eq!(h1, h2, "hash_f32 must be deterministic");\n    assert_eq!(h1, frame.field_hash, "field_hash must match embedded hash");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn duty_frame_composes_correct_dims() {\n    let frame = compose_duty(CourierShell::TauriMobile, true);\n    assert_eq!(frame.field.len(), 64 * 32, "duty frame is 64x32");\n    assert!(!frame.a11y.nodes.is_empty(), "duty frame has a11y nodes");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn no_track_frame_is_honest() {\n    let run = ActiveRun {\n        run_id: 1,\n        claim_id: 1,\n        order_id: 1,\n        in_transit: false,\n        track: None,\n    };\n    let frame = compose_run_no_track(&run);\n    assert_eq!(frame.field.len(), 96 * 48, "no-track frame is 96x48");\n    // The a11y tree must contain the NO_TRACK status text\n    let has_no_track = frame.a11y.nodes.iter().any(|n| {\n        n.state.value_text.as_deref() == Some("NO_TRACK")\n    });\n    assert!(has_no_track, "no-track frame must advertise NO_TRACK");\n}\n\n// ── 3. CourierSurface state-machine transitions ────────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn surface_full_state_machine() {\n    let mut surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n\n    // Idle initially\n    assert!(matches!(surface.state, SurfaceOfferState::Idle));\n\n    // Offered → Live\n    let consumed = surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered {\n        courier: ME,\n        deadline_ts: 1000,\n    });\n    assert_eq!(consumed.len(), 1);\n    assert!(matches!(consumed[0], SurfaceConsume::Live(_)));\n    match &surface.state {\n        SurfaceOfferState::Live { card } => {\n            assert_eq!(card.deadline_ts, 1000);\n        }\n        other => panic!("expected Live, got {other:?}"),\n    }\n\n    // Accept emits a DispatchInputFrame from Live\n    let frame = surface.emit_accept();\n    assert!(frame.is_some());\n    let frame = frame.unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(frame.courier, ME);\n    assert_eq!(frame.kind, DispatchInputKind::Accept);\n\n    // State after accept is Passed (witness consumed)\n    assert!(matches!(surface.state, SurfaceOfferState::Passed { .. }));\n\n    // Double accept fails\n    assert!(surface.emit_accept().is_none());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn surface_live_to_accepted_via_assigned() {\n    let mut surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered {\n        courier: ME,\n        deadline_ts: 500,\n    });\n    assert!(matches!(surface.state, SurfaceOfferState::Live { .. }));\n\n    // Assigned by hub → Accepted with an ActiveRun\n    let consumed = surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Assigned { courier: ME });\n    assert_eq!(consumed.len(), 1);\n    match &consumed[0] {\n        SurfaceConsume::Accepted(run) => {\n            assert!(!run.in_transit, "newly accepted run is not yet in transit");\n        }\n        other => panic!("expected Accepted, got {other:?}"),\n    }\n    assert!(matches!(surface.state, SurfaceOfferState::Accepted { .. }));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn surface_decline_advances_to_passed() {\n    let mut surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered {\n        courier: ME,\n        deadline_ts: 500,\n    });\n\n    let frame = surface.emit_decline();\n    assert!(frame.is_some());\n    assert_eq!(frame.unwrap().kind, DispatchInputKind::Decline);\n    assert!(matches!(surface.state, SurfaceOfferState::Passed { .. }));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn surface_stale_accept_is_passed_stale() {\n    let mut surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    // StaleAccept while Idle (no offer was ever live)\n    let consumed = surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::StaleAccept { courier: ME });\n    assert_eq!(consumed.len(), 1);\n    match &consumed[0] {\n        SurfaceConsume::Passed { stale } => assert!(*stale),\n        other => panic!("expected Passed{{stale:true}}, got {other:?}"),\n    }\n    assert!(matches!(surface.state, SurfaceOfferState::Passed { stale: true }));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn surface_ignores_other_courier_in_all_states() {\n    let other: CourierKey = [99u8; 32];\n    let mut surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n\n    // Idle: offer to other is ignored\n    let c = surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered {\n        courier: other,\n        deadline_ts: 500,\n    });\n    assert!(c.is_empty());\n    assert!(matches!(surface.state, SurfaceOfferState::Idle));\n\n    // Give ME a live offer\n    surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered {\n        courier: ME,\n        deadline_ts: 500,\n    });\n\n    // Assigned to other is ignored\n    let c = surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Assigned { courier: other });\n    assert!(c.is_empty());\n    assert!(matches!(surface.state, SurfaceOfferState::Live { .. }));\n}\n\n// ── 4. Field cell value validity ────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn field_cell_values_are_valid() {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(1.0);\n    scene.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n        cx: 0.0,\n        cy: 0.0,\n        r: 4.0,\n    });\n    let field = scene.render_frame(32, 32);\n\n    // Every cell must be finite\n    for &v in &field {\n        assert!(v.is_finite(), "SDF value must be finite");\n    }\n\n    // Center must be inside (negative SDF)\n    let cx = 15usize;\n    let cy = 15usize;\n    let center = field[cy * 32 + cx];\n    assert!(center < 0.0, "centre cell must be inside (negative)");\n\n    // Corner must be outside (positive SDF)\n    let corner = field[0];\n    assert!(corner > 0.0, "corner cell must be outside (positive)");\n\n    // Field evolves under equilibrium and stays finite\n    let eq = FieldEquilibrium::default();\n    let mut frame = FieldFrame::new(32, 32);\n    for _ in 0..50 {\n        frame.step(&field, &eq);\n    }\n    for &v in frame.u() {\n        assert!(v.is_finite(), "evolved field must stay finite");\n    }\n}\n\n// ── 5. GeoRef coordinate validity ───────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn geo_ref_values_are_valid() {\n    let pickup = geo_ref(40_712_000, -74_006_000);\n    assert_eq!(pickup.lat_micro, 40_712_000);\n    assert_eq!(pickup.lon_micro, -74_006_000);\n\n    let dropoff = ZoneRef { zone_id: 7 };\n    assert_eq!(dropoff.zone_id, 7);\n\n    // GeoRef from OfferCard is valid\n    let card = OfferCard {\n        claim_id: 1,\n        order_id: 42,\n        deadline_ts: 1000,\n        pickup,\n        dropoff_coarse: dropoff,\n        payout_i64: 500,\n    };\n    assert_eq!(card.pickup.lat_micro, 40_712_000);\n    assert_eq!(card.pickup.lon_micro, -74_006_000);\n    assert_eq!(card.dropoff_coarse.zone_id, 7);\n    assert_eq!(card.deadline_ts, 1000);\n    assert_eq!(card.payout_i64, 500);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn geo_ref_default_is_zero() {\n    let zero = GeoRef::default();\n    assert_eq!(zero.lat_micro, 0);\n    assert_eq!(zero.lon_micro, 0);\n}\n\n// ── 6. DispatchInputFrame creation and consumption ──────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn dispatch_input_frame_creation_from_live() {\n    let mut surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    // No accept from Idle\n    assert!(surface.emit_accept().is_none());\n    assert!(surface.emit_decline().is_none());\n    assert!(surface.emit_accept_pending().is_none());\n\n    surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered {\n        courier: ME,\n        deadline_ts: 500,\n    });\n\n    // Accept frame from Live\n    let frame = surface.emit_accept().unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(frame.courier, ME);\n    assert_eq!(frame.kind, DispatchInputKind::Accept);\n\n    // Pending accept from Live (doesn't consume witness — test with fresh surface)\n    let mut s2 = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    s2.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered {\n        courier: ME,\n        deadline_ts: 500,\n    });\n    let pending = s2.emit_accept_pending().unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(pending.kind, DispatchInputKind::Accept);\n    assert!(matches!(s2.state, SurfaceOfferState::Live { .. }), "pending does NOT consume the Live witness");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn dispatch_input_frame_consumed_by_session() {\n    let mut session = DispatchSession::new();\n    let me: CourierKey = [1u8; 32];\n\n    session.offer(me, 100);\n    assert!(session.live_offer().is_some());\n\n    // Accept within window → assigned\n    let events = session.tick(accept_input(me), &[me], 110);\n    assert!(events.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, DispatchEvent::Assigned { .. })));\n    assert_eq!(session.assigned(), Some(me));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn dispatch_input_frame_declined() {\n    let mut session = DispatchSession::new();\n    let me: CourierKey = [1u8; 32];\n\n    session.offer(me, 100);\n    let events = session.tick(decline_input(me), &[me], 105);\n    assert!(events.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, DispatchEvent::Advanced { .. })));\n    assert!(events.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, DispatchEvent::Requeued)));\n    assert!(session.live_offer().is_none());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn dispatch_input_frame_expired_accept_is_stale() {\n    let mut session = DispatchSession::new();\n    let me: CourierKey = [1u8; 32];\n\n    session.offer(me, 100);\n    // Tick past deadline\n    session.tick(DispatchInput::Tick, &[], 200);\n    assert!(session.live_offer().is_none());\n    // Late accept → stale\n    let events = session.tick(accept_input(me), &[], 200);\n    assert!(events.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, DispatchEvent::StaleAccept { .. })));\n}\n\n// ── 7. Voice profile integration with surface states ────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn voice_profile_tracks_all_surface_states() {\n    // Idle → Balanced\n    let surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    let state = CourierSurfaceState::from_surface(&surface, CourierShell::TauriMobile);\n    assert_eq!(input_profile_for(&state), InputProfile::Balanced);\n\n    // Live with offer → Balanced (not in transit)\n    let mut surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered {\n        courier: ME,\n        deadline_ts: 500,\n    });\n    let state = CourierSurfaceState::from_surface(&surface, CourierShell::TauriMobile);\n    assert_eq!(input_profile_for(&state), InputProfile::Balanced);\n\n    // Accepted but not in transit → Balanced\n    let mut surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered { courier: ME, deadline_ts: 500 });\n    surface.on_event(&DispatchEvent::Assigned { courier: ME });\n    let state = CourierSurfaceState::from_surface(&surface, CourierShell::TauriMobile);\n    assert_eq!(input_profile_for(&state), InputProfile::Balanced);\n\n    // In transit run → CourierInMotion\n    let motion_state = CourierSurfaceState {\n        shell: CourierShell::TauriMobile,\n        offer: None,\n        run: Some(ActiveRun {\n            run_id: 1,\n            claim_id: 1,\n            order_id: 1,\n            in_transit: true,\n            track: None,\n        }),\n    };\n    assert_eq!(input_profile_for(&motion_state), InputProfile::CourierInMotion);\n}\n\n// ── 8. Render corpus integrity ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn render_corpus_passes_floor_parity() {\n    let run = ActiveRun {\n        run_id: 1,\n        claim_id: 1,\n        order_id: 42,\n        in_transit: true,\n        track: Some(TrackFrame {\n            est: 1000,\n            v_mps: 5.0,\n            eta_s: 120,\n            remaining_m: 600.0,\n            route_version: 1,\n        }),\n    };\n    let corpus = courier_corpus(&run);\n    assert_eq!(corpus.len(), 3, "corpus has duty, run, no-track");\n    assert!(floor_parity_courier_corpus(&corpus), "floor parity must hold");\n}\n\n// ── 9. Payout presentation (TweenGuard money law) ──────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn render_payout_law_holds() {\n    // Integer payout is accepted\n    assert_eq!(present_payout(500.0), Ok(500));\n    assert_eq!(present_payout(0.0), Ok(0));\n\n    // Fractional payout is rejected (tweening RED)\n    assert!(present_payout(500.5).is_err());\n    assert!(present_payout(-1.5).is_err());\n}\n\n// ── 10. Voice classify uses real signal processing for spectral features ────\n\n#[test]\nfn voice_classify_all_recognized_commands() {\n    for word in &["accept", "yes", "confirm", "skip", "decline", "no"] {\n        let phrase = VoicePhrase {\n            transcript: (*word).into(),\n            confidence: 1.0,\n            is_final: true,\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            classify(&phrase),\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Command),\n            "keyword '{word}' must classify as Command"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn voice_classify_navigation_keywords() {\n    for word in &["navigate", "status", "where", "directions"] {\n        let phrase = VoicePhrase {\n            transcript: (*word).into(),\n            confidence: 1.0,\n            is_final: true,\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            classify(&phrase),\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Navigate),\n            "keyword '{word}' must classify as Navigate"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn voice_arbitrary_text_is_rejected() {\n    for word in &["hello", "goodbye", "thanks", ""] {\n        let phrase = VoicePhrase {\n            transcript: (*word).into(),\n            confidence: 1.0,\n            is_final: true,\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            classify(&phrase),\n            Classification::Rejected,\n            "non-command '{word}' must be Rejected"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn voice_respects_confidence_threshold() {\n    let phrase = VoicePhrase {\n        transcript: "accept".into(),\n        confidence: 0.3,\n        is_final: true,\n    };\n    assert_eq!(classify(&phrase), Classification::Rejected);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn voice_respects_is_final() {\n    let phrase = VoicePhrase {\n        transcript: "accept".into(),\n        confidence: 0.95,\n        is_final: false,\n    };\n    assert_eq!(classify(&phrase), Classification::Rejected);\n}\n\n// ── 11. Types size contracts verify across pipeline ─────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn pipeline_types_are_compact() {\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<CourierShell>(), 1);\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<GeoRef>(), 8);\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<ZoneRef>(), 4);\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<CourierKey>(), 32);\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<DispatchInputKind>(), 1);\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<AdvanceReason>(), 1);\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<InputProfile>(), 1);\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<AiMode>(), 1);\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<HwClass>(), 1);\n    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<LiveOffer>(), 40);\n}\n	465	-1	-1		4883b25ebf8c6b314f35aac248d29a3784dcb7878f717e68c84d8018030ca6631c53aec1c0dcd4dec345840ed7d1dc299efe5592332283e2d8ea2b44fe02f4c6cc6e5681a24b10b15514f92883fbe519156ea06e29bd450f5448389cbc0bc3a6e4a9f2f693c3918bc6fc9a77e71e25e1adb1496a24b08d7e80a959567d842e21

{\n            nodes: keys.iter().map(|&k| CourierSurface::new(k)).collect(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self) -> usize { self.nodes.len() }\n}\n\n/// Marker for a courier in motion — wraps an ActiveRun in transit.\nstruct CourierInMotion {\n    run: ActiveRun,\n    start: GeoRef,\n    end: GeoRef,\n}\n\nimpl CourierInMotion {\n    fn new(start: GeoRef, end: GeoRef) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            run: ActiveRun {\n                run_id: 1,\n                claim_id: 1,\n                order_id: 100,\n                in_transit: true,\n                track: Some(TrackFrame {\n            },\n            start,\n            end,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Minimal route plan: ordered list of waypoints with a capacity gate.\nstruct RoutePlan {\n    waypoints: Vec<GeoRef>,\n    capacity: usize,\n}\n\nimpl RoutePlan {\n    fn new(waypoints: Vec<GeoRef>, capacity: usize) -> Self {\n        Self { waypoints, capacity }\n    }\n\n    fn feasible(&self) -> bool {\n        self.waypoints.len() <= self.capacity\n    }\n}\n\n// ── helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nfn geo(lat_micro: i32, lon_micro: i32) -> GeoRef {\n    GeoRef { CourierMesh::new(&[NODE1, NODE2, NODE3]);\n    assert_eq!(mesh.len(), 3);\n    for node in &mesh.nodes {\n        assert!(matches!(node.state, SurfaceOfferState::Idle));\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn scenario_3_courier_in_motion_start_to_end() {\n    let start = geo(40_712_000, -74_006_000);   // NYC\n    let end = geo(34_052_000, -118_243_000);     // LA\n    let in_motion = CourierInMotion::new(start, end);\n    assert!(in_motion.run.in_transit);\n    assert_eq!(in_motion.run.track.as_ref().unwrap().route_version, 1);\n    assert!((in_motion.run.track.unwrap().remaining_m - 6000.0).abs() < 0.01);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn scenario_4_voice_profile_transitions() {\n    // idle → balanced\n    let surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    let state = CourierSurfaceState::from_surface(&surface, CourierShell::TauriMobile);\n    assert_eq!(input_profile_for(&state), InputProfile::Balanced);\n\n    // balanced → in_transit (via ActiveRun)\n    let in_motion = CourierSurfaceState {\n        shell: CourierShell::TauriMobile,\n        offer: None,\n        run: Some(ActiveRun {\n            run_id: 1,\n            claim_id: 1,\n            order_id: 1,\n            in_transit: true,\n            track: None,\n        }),\n    };\n    assert_eq!(input_profile_for(&in_motion), Confirms, low settle savings → Fail("settle_saving")\n    let v = VerdictRecord::Confirms {\n        hw: HwClass::BudgetAndroid,\n        shift_hours: 6.0,\n        settled_drain_pct_hr: 2.0,\n        settle_saving_pct: 20.0,\n        thermal_sustain_ms: 30.0,\n    };\n    assert_eq!(evaluate_battery_gate(&v), BatteryGate::Fail("settle_saving"));\n\n    // 6. Confirms, high thermal → Fail("thermal")\n    let v = VerdictRecord::Confirms {\n        hw: HwClass::BudgetAndroid,\n        shift_hours: 6.0,\n        settled_drain_pct_hr: 2.0,\n        settle_saving_pct: 50.0,\n        thermal_sustain_ms: 50.0,\n    };\n    assert_eq!(evaluate_battery_gate(&v), BatteryGate::Fail("thermal"));\n\n    // 7. Refines on real hw → Owed\n    let v = VerdictRecord::Refines {\n        hw: HwClass::BudgetAndroid,\n        settle_saving_pct: 25.0,\n        note: "nav-tier".into(),\n    };\n    assert_eq!(evaluate_battery_gate(&v), BatteryGate::Owed);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn scenario_6_surface_consume_not_stale() {\n    let mut surface = CourierSurface::new(ME);\n    let consumed = meaningful fields)\n    let live = consumed.into_iter().next().unwrap();\n    match live {\n        SurfaceConsume::Live(c) => assert_eq!(c.deadline_ts, 200),\n        _ => unreachable!(),\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn scenario_7_geo_ref_resolution() {\n    let ref_nyc = geo(40_712_000, -74_006_000);\n    // lat_micro/lon_micro map to a coarse grid cell for pre-accept privacy.\n    // The grid cell is derived from integer division; verify bounds.\n    assert_eq!(ref_nyc.lat_micro, 40_712_000);\n    assert_eq!(ref_nyc.lon_micro, -74_006_000);\n\n    let zone = ZoneRef { zone_id: 42 };\n scenario_8_route_plan_3_point_with_capacity() {\n    let a = geo(0, 0);\n    let b = geo(1000, 500);\n    let c = geo(2000, 1000);\n\n    // Capacity = 3: feasible\n    let plan = RoutePlan::new(vec![a, b, c], 3);\n    assert!(plan.feasible());\n\n    // Capacity = 2: infeasible\n    let plan = RoutePlan::new(vec![a, b, c], 2);\n    assert!(!plan.feasible());\n\n    // Capacity = 5: feasible with headroom\n    let plan = RoutePlan::new(vec![a, b, c], 5);\n    assert!(plan.feasible());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn scenario_9_dispatch_types_send_sync() {\n    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send };\n    let result = evaluate_battery_gate(&v);\n    assert!(matches!(result, BatteryGate::Fail("settle_saving")));\n\n    // 0-capacity route plan should reject 1 waypoint\n    let plan = CourierSurface::new(NODE2),\n        CourierSurface::new(NODE3),\n    ];\n\n    // Offer to NODE1\n    let c1 = nodes[0].on_event(&DispatchEvent::Offered {\n        courier: NODE1,\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/docs/design/bebop2-mesh-tensor-hermetic-2026-07-17/reexam-builds/item1_speculation.rs	item1_speculation · 189 lines	//! ITEM 1 — Speculative/optimistic execution + rollback vs verify-before-persist.\n//!\n//! Operator claim: "it will be faster." Prior rejection: verify ≈0.1-1ms ≪ mesh RTT\n//! 10-100ms makes speculation pointless. This bench gets REAL numbers on THIS host for a\n//! realistic small, LOCAL (same-process) order transition — no network involved.\n//!\n//! We measure three things on identical input:\n//!   A) verify-before-persist  : decide(transition+money) -> content-address(sha3) -> append\n//!   B) speculative-then-maybe-rollback : snapshot -> apply mutation -> decide -> commit|rollback\n//!   V) the verify-only slice   : just decide(), the thing speculation tries to "hide"\n//! Then we sweep an injected verify-latency knob (a spin loop standing in for a signature\n//! verify / network floor) to find where — if ever — speculation could pay for itself.\n\nuse std::time::Instant;\n\n// ---- real content-addressing cost: SHA3-256, copied verbatim from kernel/src/event_log.rs ----\nfn sha3_256(input: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    const RC: [u64; 24] = [\n        0x0000000000000001,0x0000000000008082,0x800000000000808a,0x8000000080008000,\n        0x000000000000808b,0x0000000080000001,0x8000000080008081,0x8000000000008009,\n        0x000000000000008a,0x0000000000000088,0x0000000080008009,0x000000008000000a,\n        0x000000008000808b,0x800000000000008b,0x8000000000008089,0x8000000000008003,\n        0x8000000000008002,0x8000000000000080,0x000000000000800a,0x800000008000000a,\n        0x8000000080008081,0x8000000000008080,0x0000000080000001,0x8000000080008008,\n    ];\n    const R: [[u32; 5]; 5] = [\n        [0,36,3,41,18],[1,44,10,45,2],[62,6,43,15,61],[28,55,25,21,56],[27,20,39,8,14],\n    ];\n    fn keccak_f(s: &mut [u64; 25]) {\n        for r in 0..24 {\n            let mut c = [0u64; 5];\n            for x in 0..5 { c[x] = s[x]^s[x+5]^s[x+10]^s[x+15]^s[x+20]; }\n            let mut d = [0u64; 5];\n            for x in 0..5 { d[x] = c[(x+4)%5] ^ c[(x+1)%5].rotate_left(1); }\n            for x in 0..5 { for y in 0..5 { s[x+5*y] ^= d[x]; } }\n            let mut b = [0u64; 25];\n            for x in 0..5 { for y in 0..5 {\n                b[y+5*((2*x+3*y)%5)] = s[x+5*y].rotate_left(R[x][y]);\n            }}\n            for x in 0..5 { for y in 0..5 {\n                let idx = x+5*y;\n                s[idx] = b[idx] ^ ((!b[((x+1)%5)+5*y]) & b[((x+2)%5)+5*y]);\n            }}\n            s[0] ^= RC[r];\n        }\n    }\n    const RATE: usize = 136;\n    let mut msg = input.to_vec();\n    msg.push(0x06);\n    while msg.len() % RATE != 0 { msg.push(0); }\n    *msg.last_mut().unwrap() |= 0x80;\n    let mut state = [0u64; 25];\n    for block in msg.chunks_exact(RATE) {\n        for j in 0..(RATE/8) {\n            state[j] ^= u64::from_le_bytes(block[j*8..j*8+8].try_into().unwrap());\n        }\n        keccak_f(&mut state);\n    }\n    let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n    for i in 0..4 { out[i*8..i*8+8].copy_from_slice(&state[i].to_le_bytes()); }\n    out\n}\n\n// ---- realistic small, local state: one order ----\n#[derive(Clone, Copy)]\nstruct OrderState { status: u8, subtotal_cents: i64, tax_bps: i64, total_cents: i64, seq: u64 }\n\n// order_machine::allowed_next, condensed (Pending=0..PickedUp=9)\n#[inline]\nfn legal(from: u8, to: u8) -> bool {\n    match from {\n        0 => to == 1 || to == 6 || to == 7,      // Pending -> Confirmed|Rejected|Cancelled\n        1 => to == 2 || to == 4,                  // Confirmed -> Preparing|InDelivery\n        2 => to == 3,                             // Preparing -> Ready\n        3 => to == 4 || to == 9,                  // Ready -> InDelivery|PickedUp\n        4 => to == 5,                             // InDelivery -> Delivered\n        _ => false,                               // terminal\n    }\n}\n\n// money::apply_tax, integer basis-points (the eqc-rs money law shape)\n#[inline]\nfn money(subtotal: i64, tax_bps: i64) -> i64 { subtotal + subtotal * tax_bps / 10_000 }\n\n#[inline]\nfn payload_bytes(st: &OrderState, to: u8) -> [u8; 40] {\n    let mut b = [0u8; 40];\n    b[0] = st.status; b[1] = to;\n    b[2..10].copy_from_slice(&st.subtotal_cents.to_le_bytes());\n    b[10..18].copy_from_slice(&st.tax_bps.to_le_bytes());\n    b[18..26].copy_from_slice(&st.total_cents.to_le_bytes());\n    b[26..34].copy_from_slice(&st.seq.to_le_bytes());\n    b\n}\n\n// Optional injected verify latency (spin), standing in for a signature/network cost.\n#[inline]\nfn extra_verify_work(spin: u64) -> u64 {\n    let mut acc = 0u64;\n    for i in 0..spin { acc = acc.wrapping_add(i ^ (acc >> 1)); }\n    acc\n}\n\nfn main() {\n    // Build a workload: N attempts, mix of legal and illegal transitions (roughly 70% legal).\n    const N: usize = 2_000_000;\n    let mut attempts: Vec<(u8, u8)> = Vec::with_capacity(N);\n    let mut s: u64 = 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0;\n    for _ in 0..N {\n        s ^= s << 13; s ^= s >> 7; s ^= s << 17; // xorshift\n        let from = (s % 5) as u8;                 // 0..4 (non-terminal origins)\n        let to = ((s >> 8) % 10) as u8;           // 0..9 (some illegal)\n        attempts.push((from, to));\n    }\n    let base = OrderState { status: 0, subtotal_cents: 2599, tax_bps: 875, total_cents: 0, seq: 0 };\n\n    for &spin in &[0u64, 50, 200, 1000] {\n        // ---------- Path A: verify-before-persist ----------\n        let mut log: Vec<[u8; 32]> = Vec::with_capacity(N);\n        let mut committed_a: u64 = 0;\n        let t0 = Instant::now();\n        let mut sink = 0u64;\n        for &(from, to) in &attempts {\n            let st = OrderState { status: from, ..base };\n            // VERIFY (decide) first — nothing mutated yet.\n            sink = sink.wrapping_add(extra_verify_work(spin));\n            if legal(from, to) {\n                // only now do we mutate + persist\n                let mut nst = st;\n                nst.status = to;\n                nst.total_cents = money(nst.subtotal_cents, nst.tax_bps);\n                nst.seq += 1;\n                let h = sha3_256(&payload_bytes(&st, to));\n                log.push(h);\n                committed_a += 1;\n                sink ^= nst.total_cents as u64 ^ h[0] as u64;\n            }\n        }\n        let dur_a = t0.elapsed();\n\n        // ---------- Path B: speculative-apply-then-maybe-rollback ----------\n        let mut log_b: Vec<[u8; 32]> = Vec::with_capacity(N);\n        let mut committed_b: u64 = 0;\n        let t1 = Instant::now();\n        for &(from, to) in &attempts {\n            let mut st = OrderState { status: from, ..base };\n            let snapshot = st;                     // rollback checkpoint (small local copy)\n            // SPECULATE: apply the mutation optimistically, BEFORE verifying.\n            st.status = to;\n            st.total_cents = money(st.subtotal_cents, st.tax_bps);\n            st.seq += 1;\n            // Now verify.\n            sink = sink.wrapping_add(extra_verify_work(spin));\n            if legal(from, to) {\n                let h = sha3_256(&payload_bytes(&snapshot, to));\n                log_b.push(h);\n                committed_b += 1;\n                sink ^= st.total_cents as u64 ^ h[0] as u64;\n            } else {\n                st = snapshot;                     // ROLLBACK\n                sink ^= st.status as u64;\n            }\n        }\n        let dur_b = t1.elapsed();\n\n        // ---------- V: verify-only slice (what speculation tries to hide) ----------\n        let t2 = Instant::now();\n        let mut vsink = 0u64;\n        for &(from, to) in &attempts {\n            vsink = vsink.wrapping_add(extra_verify_work(spin));\n            if legal(from, to) { vsink += 1; }\n        }\n        let dur_v = t2.elapsed();\n\n        assert_eq!(committed_a, committed_b);\n        assert_eq!(log, log_b);\n        let per_a = dur_a.as_nanos() as f64 / N as f64;\n        let per_b = dur_b.as_nanos() as f64 / N as f64;\n        let per_v = dur_v.as_nanos() as f64 / N as f64;\n        println!("spin={:>4}  verify-only V={:7.2} ns  A(verify-first)={:7.2} ns  B(speculate+rollback)={:7.2} ns  | B-A overhead = {:+6.2} ns/op  ({} committed)  [sink={}]",\n            spin, per_v, per_a, per_b, per_b - per_a, committed_a, sink ^ vsink);\n    }\n    println!("\\nInterpretation:");\n    println!("  * spin=0 is the pure local path (no network/sig cost). B does strictly MORE work");\n    println!("    (snapshot + conditional rollback) than A for identical output.");\n    println!("  * The verify slice V is the ONLY thing speculation could hide. Speculation needs an");\n    println!("    in-flight window (concurrency) to hide it; a synchronous local verify has none, so");\n    println!("    on THIS host, same-process, speculation is pure overhead regardless of spin.");\n}\n	518	-1	-1		82f776be909a2da4db0ccdce7092034980d601ec0d30f6a0e268c2d9a3dde8534dc43383efcb84fbe87346e13339f1a8cead3f6ab56800899ce7322ded9ebf0eda4c51d8609a707118d71112973a89d05059c00e6979ed21b00025a45840cbf6a522e2c8b8c9921dcdfc9c4f43fc2fb565bbcd201d23eda4a4b9fef420fc2511

## 531 · /root/dowiz/docs/design/bebop2-mesh-tensor-hermetic-2026-07-17/reexam-builds/item2_witness.rs · LongTerm

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/docs/design/bebop2-mesh-tensor-hermetic-2026-07-17/reexam-builds/item2_witness.rs	item2_witness · 111 lines	//! ITEM 2 — "Self-auditing inline witnessing": naive (rejected) vs steelmanned (commitment).\n//!\n//! Rejection: self-certification = RC-2, "the check restates the claim." True for the NAIVE\n//! form. This file builds BOTH forms against the same forged artifact and shows an independent\n//! verifier catches the forgery under the steelman but NOT under the naive form.\n//!\n//! Distinction being demonstrated:\n//!   NAIVE  = "I checked my own work, it's valid"  -> a boolean/attestation the author controls.\n//!   STEELMAN = "here is a commitment to (inputs, pinned-law-id, output); recompute it yourself" ->\n//!            the VALIDITY judgment is made LATER by an independent party running an EXTERNAL law,\n//!            not asserted by the author. That is a witness/commitment, not a self-certification.\n//!\n//! Production hash = SHA3-256 (kernel/src/event_log.rs). Here we use a compact FNV-1a-64 purely\n//! to keep the file self-contained; the argument is hash-agnostic (needs only 2nd-preimage\n//! resistance, which SHA3 provides in the real path).\n\n// compact stand-in hash (SHA3-256 in production)\nfn h(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {\n    let mut x: u64 = 0xcbf29ce484222325;\n    for &b in bytes { x ^= b as u64; x = x.wrapping_mul(0x100000001b3); }\n    x\n}\nfn h_i64(v: i64) -> u64 { h(&v.to_le_bytes()) }\nfn h_inputs(subtotal: i64, tax_bps: i64) -> u64 {\n    let mut buf = [0u8; 16];\n    buf[0..8].copy_from_slice(&subtotal.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[8..16].copy_from_slice(&tax_bps.to_le_bytes());\n    h(&buf)\n}\n\n// ---- THE PINNED, DETERMINISTIC LAW (money.v1). The verifier holds this; NOT the author. ----\nfn money_v1(subtotal: i64, tax_bps: i64) -> i64 { subtotal + subtotal * tax_bps / 10_000 }\nconst LAW_ID: &str = "money.v1";\n\n// =====================================================================================\n// NAIVE self-certifying witness: author reruns the law itself and attests a boolean.\n// =====================================================================================\nstruct SelfCert { output: i64, self_valid: bool /* author's own verdict */ }\n\nfn author_selfcert(subtotal: i64, tax_bps: i64, claimed_output: i64) -> SelfCert {\n    // A malicious author simply SETS self_valid = true regardless of truth.\n    // (An honest author would compute money_v1 and compare; but the verifier can't tell which.)\n    SelfCert { output: claimed_output, self_valid: true }\n}\n\n// Verifier that TRUSTS the attestation (the only thing the naive form offers cheaply).\nfn verify_selfcert_trusting(w: &SelfCert) -> bool { w.self_valid }\n\n// Verifier that DISTRUSTS and recomputes — at which point the attestation added nothing (RC-2).\nfn verify_selfcert_recompute(w: &SelfCert, subtotal: i64, tax_bps: i64) -> bool {\n    w.output == money_v1(subtotal, tax_bps) // the boolean w.self_valid is irrelevant / ignored\n}\n\n// =====================================================================================\n// STEELMAN commitment witness: author commits (inputs, law_id, output). No validity claim.\n// =====================================================================================\nstruct WorkReceipt { input_commit: u64, law_id: &'static str, output_commit: u64, output: i64 }\n\nfn author_receipt(subtotal: i64, tax_bps: i64, claimed_output: i64) -> WorkReceipt {\n    // The author commits to WHAT they claim they computed. They do NOT assert it is correct.\n    // A malicious author can only commit to the (wrong) output they actually put on the wire.\n    WorkReceipt {\n        input_commit: h_inputs(subtotal, tax_bps),\n        law_id: LAW_ID,\n        output_commit: h_i64(claimed_output),\n        output: claimed_output,\n    }\n}\n\n// INDEPENDENT verifier: receives the inputs out-of-band, re-runs the EXTERNAL pinned law,\n// and checks the commitments. Trusts the law + the hash, NEVER the author.\nfn verify_receipt_independent(w: &WorkReceipt, subtotal: i64, tax_bps: i64) -> Result<(), &'static str> {\n    if w.law_id != LAW_ID { return Err("unknown/again law version"); }\n    if w.input_commit != h_inputs(subtotal, tax_bps) { return Err("input commitment mismatch (equivocation)"); }\n    if w.output_commit != h_i64(w.output) { return Err("output commitment mismatch (tamper)"); }\n    let recomputed = money_v1(subtotal, tax_bps);           // <-- the independent re-execution\n    if h_i64(recomputed) != w.output_commit { return Err("REPLAY MISMATCH: committed output != law(inputs)"); }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn main() {\n    let (subtotal, tax_bps) = (2599i64, 875i64);\n    let honest = money_v1(subtotal, tax_bps);   // 2826\n    let forged = subtotal;                       // 2599 — a skim-the-tax forgery\n\n    println!("law money.v1({}, {} bps) = {}   (forged claim = {})\\n", subtotal, tax_bps, honest, forged);\n\n    for (label, claimed) in [("HONEST author", honest), ("MALICIOUS author (skims tax)", forged)] {\n        println!("--- {} ---", label);\n\n        // NAIVE self-cert\n        let sc = author_selfcert(subtotal, tax_bps, claimed);\n        let trust = verify_selfcert_trusting(&sc);\n        let recompute = verify_selfcert_recompute(&sc, subtotal, tax_bps);\n        println!("  NAIVE self-cert:  trusting-verifier accepts = {:5}   (self_valid flag = {})", trust, sc.self_valid);\n        println!("                    recompute-verifier accepts = {:5}   <- but this IS just re-doing the work (RC-2)", recompute);\n\n        // STEELMAN commitment\n        let wr = author_receipt(subtotal, tax_bps, claimed);\n        let indep = verify_receipt_independent(&wr, subtotal, tax_bps);\n        println!("  STEELMAN receipt: independent-verifier result = {:?}", indep);\n        println!();\n    }\n\n    println!("MEASURED DIFFERENCE:");\n    println!("  * NAIVE trusting-verifier ACCEPTS the malicious output (self_valid=true is author-controlled).");\n    println!("  * NAIVE recompute-verifier catches it, but only by redoing the law -> the witness added nothing (RC-2).");\n    println!("  * STEELMAN independent-verifier REJECTS the malicious output via replay, WITHOUT trusting the author,");\n    println!("    and the receipt still bought: input non-equivocation, tamper-evidence, and offline/deferred/3rd-party");\n    println!("    verifiability that travels with the artifact. 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/docs/design/bebop2-mesh-tensor-hermetic-2026-07-17/reexam-builds/item4_cordic.rs	item4_cordic · 104 lines	//! ITEM 4 — Deterministic sin/cos WITHOUT libm: fixed-point CORDIC (integer-only).\n//!\n//! Objection (blueprint E13 / register #13): "transcendental float paths are NOT cross-target\n//! bit-identical" — true for f64::sin (delegates to platform libm). Operator's rebuttal: the two\n//! forms "are identical if the functions/equations inside are identical" — CORRECT if a portable\n//! deterministic implementation replaces libm. This module IS that implementation.\n//!\n//! The RUNTIME kernel below (`cordic_sincos`) uses ONLY i64 add/sub/compare and ARITHMETIC SHIFT.\n//! No f64, no libm, no platform-dependent op. The atan table + gain are FROZEN integer constants\n//! (shipped like SHA3 round constants), derived once offline — never recomputed on any target.\n//! f64 appears ONLY in the measurement/test harness (accuracy vs libm), never on the codec path.\n\n// ---- FROZEN integer constants (Q30 fixed point). Generated once; shipped as literals. ----\nconst ATAN_Q30: [i64; 31] = [843314857, 497837829, 263043837, 133525159, 67021687, 33543516,\n    16775851, 8388437, 4194283, 2097149, 1048576, 524288, 262144, 131072, 65536, 32768, 16384,\n    8192, 4096, 2048, 1024, 512, 256, 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1];\nconst CORDIC_K_Q30: i64 = 652032874; // circular gain 0.60725293...\nconst HALF_PI_Q30: i64 = 1686629713;\nconst PI_Q30: i64 = 3373259426;\nconst TWO_PI_Q30: i64 = 6746518852;\nconst ONE_Q30: i64 = 1 << 30;\n\n/// PURE-INTEGER sin/cos. Input angle in Q30 radians. Returns (cos_q30, sin_q30).\n/// Zero float ops. Only: +, -, <, ==, arithmetic >> (sign-extending, well-defined for i64).\nfn cordic_sincos(mut z: i64) -> (i64, i64) {\n    // 1) Range-fold to [-pi, pi] with integer add/sub only.\n    while z >  PI_Q30 { z -= TWO_PI_Q30; }\n    while z < -PI_Q30 { z += TWO_PI_Q30; }\n    // 2) Fold [-pi,-pi/2)U(pi/2,pi] into [-pi/2,pi/2], remembering to negate both outputs.\n    let mut negate = false;\n    if z >  HALF_PI_Q30 { z -= PI_Q30; negate = true; }\n    else if z < -HALF_PI_Q30 { z += PI_Q30; negate = true; }\n    // 3) CORDIC circular rotation. Seed x = gain (so final |(x,y)| = 1), y = 0.\n    let mut x: i64 = CORDIC_K_Q30;\n    let mut y: i64 = 0;\n    for i in 0..31u32 {\n        let dx = x >> i;               // x * 2^-i  (arithmetic shift; cross-target defined)\n        let dy = y >> i;               // y * 2^-i\n        if z >= 0 { x -= dy; y += dx; z -= ATAN_Q30[i as usize]; }\n        else      { x += dy; y -= dx; z += ATAN_Q30[i as usize]; }\n    }\n    if negate { (-x, -y) } else { (x, y) }\n}\n\n// FNV-1a over the raw output stream — the exact digest a cross-arch CI job would compare.\nfn digest(stream: &[i64]) -> u64 {\n    let mut hsh: u64 = 0xcbf29ce484222325;\n    for &v in stream { for b in v.to_le_bytes() { hsh ^= b as u64; hsh = hsh.wrapping_mul(0x100000001b3); } }\n    hsh\n}\n\nfn main() {\n    // Sweep angles across two full periods, step 1/4096 rad, in Q30 — integer-only construction.\n    const STEP_Q30: i64 = ONE_Q30 / 4096;\n    let lo = -2 * PI_Q30;\n    let n = ((2 * TWO_PI_Q30) / STEP_Q30) as usize;\n\n    let mut stream_a: Vec<i64> = Vec::with_capacity(2 * n);\n    let mut z = lo;\n    for _ in 0..n {\n        let (c, s) = cordic_sincos(z);\n        stream_a.push(c); stream_a.push(s);\n        z += STEP_Q30;\n    }\n    // Independent second run (fresh state) — determinism check.\n    let mut stream_b: Vec<i64> = Vec::with_capacity(2 * n);\n    let mut z = lo;\n    for _ in 0..n { let (c, s) = cordic_sincos(z); stream_b.push(c); stream_b.push(s); z += STEP_Q30; }\n\n    let da = digest(&stream_a);\n    let db = digest(&stream_b);\n    println!("determinism: {} samples/run, digest_run1=0x{:016x} digest_run2=0x{:016x} -> {}",\n        n, da, db, if da == db { "BIT-IDENTICAL" } else { "DIVERGED" });\n    assert_eq!(stream_a, stream_b, "pure-integer CORDIC must be reproducible");\n\n    // Accuracy vs libm (f64 used ONLY here in the harness, never in the codec).\n    let scale = ONE_Q30 as f64;\n    let mut max_err_sin = 0f64;\n    let mut max_err_cos = 0f64;\n    let mut z = -HALF_PI_Q30;\n    let mut samples = 0;\n    while z <= HALF_PI_Q30 {\n        let (c, s) = cordic_sincos(z);\n        let ang = z as f64 / scale;\n        max_err_sin = max_err_sin.max(((s as f64 / scale) - ang.sin()).abs());\n        max_err_cos = max_err_cos.max(((c as f64 / scale) - ang.cos()).abs());\n        z += STEP_Q30; samples += 1;\n    }\n    println!("accuracy vs libm over [-pi/2,pi/2], {} samples: max|sin err|={:.2e}  max|cos err|={:.2e}  (~{:.1} bits)",\n        samples, max_err_sin, max_err_cos, -(max_err_sin.max(max_err_cos)).log2());\n\n    // Spot check\n    let (c0, s0) = cordic_sincos(0);\n    let (ch, sh) = cordic_sincos(HALF_PI_Q30);\n    println!("spot: sincos(0)=(cos {:.6}, sin {:.6})  sincos(pi/2)=(cos {:.6}, sin {:.6})",\n        c0 as f64/scale, s0 as f64/scale, ch as f64/scale, sh as f64/scale);\n\n    println!("\\nWHAT CLOSES THE CROSS-ARCH LOOP (cannot run ARM here, but the loop is small & explicit):");\n    println!("  * runtime kernel touches only i64 +,-,<,==,>> (arithmetic shift). Rust guarantees");\n    println!("    i64 wrapping/shift semantics identical on every target (unlike f64 transcendentals).");\n    println!("  * CI addition: build this on x86_64 AND aarch64 (cross-compile or qemu), emit the");\n    println!("    output digest 0x{:016x}, assert byte-equal across both. That single asserted digest", da);\n    println!("    is the whole cross-target proof — no per-target float tolerance needed.");\n}\n	543	-1	-1		c3ba7e5cbe278f3d500dafcb98523031c91ab5c08719bf0bc8c8705be0ebcdcb15dc70c99f52b0fec55550b9732148bcc27def465c2b48a8b96b720257366c3ee61ad4f16bffba231cdd51089ba6cdd341f0cbdf29f8852c18482596d0282360a5a750c7d34084bb18385852c154595145b94c222e9be58409a9f77411a63925
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/docs/design/bebop2-mesh-tensor-hermetic-2026-07-17/reexam-builds/item5_laplace_beltrami.rs	item5_laplace_beltrami · 95 lines	//! ITEM 5 — Is there a genuine continuous-geometry EXTENSION of the discrete graph Laplacian?\n//!\n//! The blueprint rejects "Laplace-domain primitives + Kuen surface" as domain-mismatch. This\n//! tests the ONE part that is NOT a mismatch: the graph Laplacian (kernel/src/spectral.rs::\n//! laplacian + eigenvalues + algebraic_connectivity) is the DISCRETE form of a CONTINUOUS\n//! operator. Belkin-Niyogi (2008): as n->inf, the graph-Laplacian spectrum converges to the\n//! Laplace-Beltrami operator's spectrum on the underlying manifold.\n//!\n//! We MEASURE that convergence on the unit circle S^1, whose Laplace-Beltrami eigenvalues are\n//! known EXACTLY: {0, 1, 1, 4, 4, 9, 9, ...} = k^2 (eigenfunctions sin k*theta, cos k*theta).\n//! We build a Gaussian-weighted graph over n sampled points, symmetric-normalized Laplacian,\n//! take its low eigenvalues via cyclic Jacobi, and show the RATIOS -> {1,1,4,4,9,9} as n grows.\n//! Ratios cancel the (bandwidth-dependent) constant, so this is a clean spectrum-SHAPE match.\n\n// ---- deterministic cyclic-Jacobi symmetric eigenvalues (pure, no deps) ----\nfn jacobi_eigenvalues(mut a: Vec<Vec<f64>>) -> Vec<f64> {\n    let n = a.len();\n    for _sweep in 0..100 {\n        // off-diagonal Frobenius norm\n        let mut off = 0.0;\n        for p in 0..n { for q in (p+1)..n { off += a[p][q]*a[p][q]; } }\n        if off.sqrt() < 1e-12 { break; }\n        for p in 0..n {\n            for q in (p+1)..n {\n                if a[p][q].abs() < 1e-300 { continue; }\n                let app = a[p][p]; let aqq = a[q][q]; let apq = a[p][q];\n                let theta = (aqq - app) / (2.0 * apq);\n                let t = theta.signum() / (theta.abs() + (theta*theta + 1.0).sqrt());\n                let c = 1.0 / (t*t + 1.0).sqrt();\n                let s = t * c;\n                for k in 0..n {\n                    let akp = a[k][p]; let akq = a[k][q];\n                    a[k][p] = c*akp - s*akq;\n                    a[k][q] = s*akp + c*akq;\n                }\n                for k in 0..n {\n                    let apk = a[p][k]; let aqk = a[q][k];\n                    a[p][k] = c*apk - s*aqk;\n                    a[q][k] = s*apk + c*aqk;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    let mut ev: Vec<f64> = (0..n).map(|i| a[i][i]).collect();\n    ev.sort_by(|x,y| x.partial_cmp(y).unwrap());\n    ev\n}\n\n// graph Laplacian spectrum for n points on the unit circle\nfn circle_laplacian_spectrum(n: usize) -> Vec<f64> {\n    let spacing = 2.0*std::f64::consts::PI / n as f64;\n    let eps = 5.0 * spacing;              // Gaussian bandwidth ~5 neighbor spacings (eps->0 with n)\n    // coords\n    let pts: Vec<(f64,f64)> = (0..n).map(|i| {\n        let th = 2.0*std::f64::consts::PI * i as f64 / n as f64;\n        (th.cos(), th.sin())\n    }).collect();\n    // weighted adjacency + degree\n    let mut w = vec![vec![0.0f64; n]; n];\n    let mut deg = vec![0.0f64; n];\n    for i in 0..n { for j in 0..n { if i!=j {\n        let dx = pts[i].0 - pts[j].0; let dy = pts[i].1 - pts[j].1;\n        let d2 = dx*dx + dy*dy;\n        let wij = (-d2/(eps*eps)).exp();\n        w[i][j] = wij; deg[i] += wij;\n    }}}\n    // symmetric normalized Laplacian  L = I - D^-1/2 W D^-1/2\n    let mut l = vec![vec![0.0f64; n]; n];\n    for i in 0..n { for j in 0..n {\n        let norm = (deg[i]*deg[j]).sqrt();\n        l[i][j] = if i==j { 1.0 } else { 0.0 } - w[i][j]/norm;\n    }}\n    jacobi_eigenvalues(l)\n}\n\nfn main() {\n    println!("Laplace-Beltrami spectrum of S^1 (continuous, exact): 0, 1, 1, 4, 4, 9, 9  (= k^2)\\n");\n    println!("Discrete graph-Laplacian low eigenvalues, normalized so lambda_1 == 1 (ratios):");\n    println!("{:>6} | {:>6} {:>6} {:>6} {:>6} {:>6} {:>6}", "n", "l1", "l2", "l3", "l4", "l5", "l6");\n    println!("{}", "-".repeat(60));\n    for &n in &[24usize, 48, 96, 160] {\n        let ev = circle_laplacian_spectrum(n);\n        // ev[0] ~ 0 (constant mode). Normalize the rest by ev[1].\n        let base = ev[1];\n        let r: Vec<f64> = (1..7).map(|k| ev[k]/base).collect();\n        println!("{:>6} | {:>6.3} {:>6.3} {:>6.3} {:>6.3} {:>6.3} {:>6.3}", n, r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3], r[4], r[5]);\n    }\n    println!("\\ntarget ratios ->  1.000  1.000  4.000  4.000  9.000  9.000");\n    println!("\\nRESULT: the discrete graph Laplacian's low spectrum reproduces the CONTINUOUS");\n    println!("Laplace-Beltrami spectrum {{k^2}} — the two are the same operator at different");\n    println!("resolutions (Belkin-Niyogi 2008). This is a real continuous relaxation of the SAME");\n    println!("machinery the kernel already ships (spectral.rs eigenvalues / Fiedler / DriftClass),");\n    println!("NOT a replacement. ## 564 · /root/dowiz/engine/benches/criterion.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: criterion · 279 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/benches/criterion.rs	criterion · 279 lines	//! P81 — FIRST bench harness for the `dowiz-engine` crate.\n//!\n//! The engine crate had ZERO benchmarks before P81 and runs hot code every\n//! frame (field evolution, scene raster, motion springs, the vertex bridge's\n//! graph-Laplacian field, and the money-surface guard). This file establishes\n//! the crate's native telemetry baseline per AGENTS.md ("Mandatory native\n//! telemetry & benchmarks after every change/wave") and the engine row of the\n//! performance audit (`SYNTHESIS-PERFORMANCE-AUDIT-2026-07-18.md` §3.3-C2).\n//!\n//! Bench-id convention: `<group>/<n>` (owned by P75; P80/P81/P82 cite it).\n//! Each sweep variable is encoded as the `<n>` suffix so `bench_track.py`\n//! (the autotrack gate) keys each run into the committed `baseline.json`.\n//!\n//! IMPORTANT (constraint): this file is BENCHMARKS ONLY. No production logic\n//! is changed. Where a bench surfaces a real contract gap (see\n//! `vertex_bridge_apply_field` below) the gap is *documented*, not patched —\n//! P81 is a coverage/observability blueprint, not a rewrite.\n\nuse criterion::{black_box, criterion_group, criterion_main, BenchmarkId, Criterion};\n\nuse dowiz_engine::field_frame::{compose, laplacian_into, FieldEquilibrium, FieldFrame};\nuse dowiz_engine::{Scene, SdfShape, Spring, TweenGuard};\nuse dowiz_kernel::csr::{Csr, LaplacianKind};\n\n/// Grid sizes shared by the field-frame / laplacian sweeps.\nconst GRIDS: [(usize, &str); 3] = [(64, "64"), (128, "128"), (256, "256")];\n\n/// Build a zeroed source buffer (SDF of a single centered disk) for `w×h`.\nfn disk_source(w: usize, h: usize) -> Vec<f32> {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(1.0);\n    scene.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n        cx: 0.0,\n        cy: 0.0,\n        r: (w.min(h) as f64) * 0.25,\n    });\n    scene.render_frame(w, h)\n}\n\n// ── field_frame_step: grid-swept integration step ────────────────────────────\n// `FieldFrame::step` is THE every-frame hot path. It must stay allocation-free\n// (pre-allocated scratch + swap-rotation, see field_frame.rs). The sweep pins\n// its linear cost in grid cells so a future regression is caught by bench_track.\nfn bench_field_frame_step(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    let eq = FieldEquilibrium::default();\n    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("field_frame_step");\n    for &(n, label) in &GRIDS {\n        let source = disk_source(n, n);\n        let mut frame = FieldFrame::new(n, n);\n        // Warm: advance once so the scratch buffers are really live.\n        frame.step(&source, &eq);\n        group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(label), &n, |b, &_n| {\n            b.iter(|| {\n                frame.step(black_box(&source), black_box(&eq));\n            })\n        });\n    }\n    group.finish();\n}\n\n// ── laplacian_into: grid-swept stencil (the inner hot loop of step) ──────────\n// `laplacian_into` is the 5-point ∇²U kernel `step` calls every frame. Pinning\n// it separately isolates the per-cell stencil cost from the integrator math.\nfn bench_laplacian_into(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("laplacian_into");\n    for &(n, label) in &GRIDS {\n        let u = vec![0.0f32; n * n];\n        let mut out = vec![0.0f32; n * n];\n        group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(label), &n, |b, &_n| {\n            b.iter(|| {\n                laplacian_into(black_box(&u), n, n, black_box(&mut out));\n            })\n        });\n    }\n    group.finish();\n}\n\n/// Shape counts for the scene/compose sweep.\nconst SHAPES: [(usize, &str); 4] = [(1, "1"), (4, "4"), (16, "16"), (64, "64")];\n\n/// Build a scene with `k` heterogeneous shapes (deterministic, no RNG).\nfn shaped_scene(k: usize) -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(1.0);\n    for i in 0..k {\n        let f = i as f64;\n        match i % 4 {\n            0 => scene.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n                cx: (f - 16.0).cos() * 8.0,\n                cy: (f - 16.0).sin() * 8.0,\n                r: 3.0,\n            }),\n            1 => scene.add(SdfShape::Box {\n                bx: (f - 16.0) * 0.5,\n                by: 0.0,\n                hx: 1.0,\n                hy: 1.0,\n            }),\n            2 => scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n                bx: 0.0,\n                by: (f - 16.0) * 0.5,\n                hx: 1.0,\n                hy: 1.0,\n                r: 0.3,\n            }),\n            _ => scene.add(SdfShape::LineSegment {\n                ax: -8.0,\n                ay: f - 16.0,\n                bx: 8.0,\n                by: f - 16.0,\n            }),\n        };\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n// ── scene_render_frame: shape-swept SDF rasterization ────────────────────────\n// Fixed grid; sweep the number of composed shapes. `render_frame` allocates one\n// `Vec<f32>` per call and walks every pixel through every shape's SDF.\nfn bench_scene_render_frame(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    let (w, h) = (128usize, 96);\n    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("scene_render_frame");\n    for &(k, label) in &SHAPES {\n        let scene = shaped_scene(k);\n        group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(label), &k, |b, &_k| {\n            b.iter(|| {\n                black_box(scene.render_frame(w, h));\n            })\n        });\n    }\n    group.finish();\n}\n\n// ── frame_rgba: shape-swept field→RGBA8 mapping ──────────────────────────────\n// `FieldFrame::frame_rgba` maps the current field U to an RGBA8 display frame\n// every render. Fixed grid; sweep shapes because more shapes ⇒ a more "active"\n// (less flat) field, exercising the full hue/brightness branch spread.\nfn bench_frame_rgba(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    let (w, h) = (128usize, 96);\n    let eq = FieldEquilibrium::default();\n    let steps = 30usize;\n    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("frame_rgba");\n    for &(k, label) in &SHAPES {\n        let scene = shaped_scene(k);\n        let source = scene.render_frame(w, h);\n        let mut frame = FieldFrame::new(w, h);\n        for _ in 0..steps {\n            frame.step(&source, &eq);\n        }\n        group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(label), &k, |b, &_k| {\n            b.iter(|| {\n                black_box(frame.frame_rgba());\n            })\n        });\n    }\n    group.finish();\n}\n\n// ── compose: shape-swept full render (raster → evolve → frame) ───────────────\n// `compose` is the end-to-end single call a future `wgpu` blit would consume:\n// rasterize the scene, evolve `steps` field steps, map to RGBA8. Shape-swept.\nfn bench_compose(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    let (w, h) = (96usize, 72);\n    let eq = FieldEquilibrium::default();\n    let steps = 20usize;\n    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("compose");\n    for &(k, label) in &SHAPES {\n        let scene = shaped_scene(k);\n        group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(label), &k, |b, &_k| {\n            b.iter(|| {\n                black_box(compose(black_box(&scene), black_box(&eq), w, h, steps));\n            })\n        });\n    }\n    group.finish();\n}\n\n/// Angular-frequency sweep points (ω). Tension k = ω², friction = 2·ζ·ω with\n/// ζ = 1 (critically damped), so each `Spring` carries a distinct ω into\n/// `step`, which substeps so ω·dt_sub ≤ 0.1 — sweeping ω sweeps the per-call\n/// substep count and thus the hot arithmetic cost.\nconst OMEGAS: [(f32, &str); 4] = [(3.0, "3"), (10.0, "10"), (30.0, "30"), (100.0, "100")];\n\n// ── spring_step: ω-swept motion integrator ───────────────────────────────────\nfn bench_spring_step(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    let dt = 1.0f32 / 60.0;\n    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("spring_step");\n    for &(omega, label) in &OMEGAS {\n        let tension = omega * omega;\n        let friction = 2.0 * 1.0 * omega; // ζ = 1\n        let mut spring = Spring::new(tension, friction, 0.0);\n        spring.target = 1.0;\n        group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(label), &omega, |b, &_omega| {\n            b.iter(|| {\n                spring.step(black_box(dt));\n            })\n        });\n    }\n    group.finish();\n}\n\n/// Build an `n`-node ring graph whose nnz (= number of valid directed edges)\n/// is `n * radius`. Radius < n/2 guarantees unique (src,dst) pairs, so nnz is\n/// exactly controllable. Used to sweep the vertex bridge's field cost.\nfn ring_graph(n: usize, radius: usize) -> Csr {\n    let mut edges = Vec::with_capacity(n * radius);\n    for i in 0..n {\n        for j in 1..=radius {\n            let d = (i + j) % n;\n            edges.push((i, d, 1.0));\n        }\n    }\n    Csr::from_edges(n, &edges)\n}\n\n/// nnz sweep points: n = 256 nodes, radius ∈ {1,2,4,8} ⇒ nnz ∈ {256,512,1024,2048}.\nconst NNZ: [(usize, usize, &str); 4] = [\n    (256, 1, "256"),\n    (256, 2, "512"),\n    (256, 4, "1024"),\n    (256, 8, "2048"),\n];\n\n// ── vertex_bridge_apply_field: nnz-swept graph-Laplacian field ───────────────\n// `VertexBridge::apply_field` drives the kernel's `laplacian_spmv` (normalized\n// Laplacian) over the particle state every frame. DOCUMENTED-GAP NOTE: the\n// production method allocates a fresh `Vec<f64>` per call (`let mut y =\n// vec![0.0; n]; self.field = y;` in bridge.rs) — a per-call heap allocation\n// living inside what the module docstring calls the "no allocation in the hot\n// loop" path. P81 does NOT change this; it only PINS the cost so a future\n// allocation-free rewrite has a before/after bench gate. nnz-swept so the\n// linear-in-nnz SpMV cost is on the record.\nfn bench_vertex_bridge_apply_field(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("vertex_bridge_apply_field");\n    for &(n, radius, label) in &NNZ {\n        let graph = ring_graph(n, radius);\n        let nnz = graph.nnz();\n        let mut bridge = dowiz_engine::VertexBridge::new(n, 4);\n        bridge.set_field_graph(graph);\n        let x: Vec<f64> = (0..n).map(|i| (i as f64) * 0.01).collect();\n        group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(label), &nnz, |b, &_nnz| {\n            b.iter(|| {\n                bridge.apply_field(black_box(&x));\n            })\n        });\n    }\n    group.finish();\n}\n\n// ── money_present: RED-LINE baseline PIN ─────────────────────────────────────\n// `TweenGuard::present_money` is the money-surface value-formatting guard on the\n// FE-09 RED-LINE (money never tweens). P81 pins its cost as a STABLE baseline.\n// Logic is NOT changed — this bench only locks in the current per-call cost so a\n// future edit that makes money presentation hot is caught by bench_track. Single\n// id `pin`: the cost must stay flat, regressions are a real defect to kill.\nfn bench_money_present(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("money_present");\n    group.bench_function("pin", |b| {\n        b.iter(|| {\n            // A clean decided integer (the GREEN path) — the common case.\n            black_box(TweenGuard::present_money(black_box(155.0))).unwrap();\n        })\n    });\n    group.finish();\n    // Compile-time anchor: the absolute nnz/LaplacianKind wiring this bench\n    // relies on. Keeps the kernel↔engine seam explicit (mirrors bridge.rs).\n    let _ = LaplacianKind::Normalized;\n}\n\ncriterion_group!(\n    benches,\n    bench_field_frame_step,\n    bench_laplacian_into,\n    bench_scene_render_frame,\n    bench_frame_rgba,\n    bench_compose,\n    bench_spring_step,\n    bench_vertex_bridge_apply_field,\n    bench_money_present,\n);\ncriterion_main!(benches);\n	565	-1	-1		53fc3e6fdcbe83b3036bf2c313022b250d5cb7649d7ee4d3e648aa2bcbefe16355442a89cd1b6abea053462fa721d13c56077da0b56a85a0fa6a7a98ff16a86ee66c1d393d0f83799317a90bd7b3a9089070c8ba2193cf41d0c2b4949c018134e860f266b1cb9307d88a8c454b193b116c954c264fb79cb89449c692793a2c31
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/approach.rs	approach · 229 lines	//! Approach — кути огляду для "останньої милі" доставки.\n//!\n//! Клієнт може виставити кут огляду для адреси доставки — звідки він\n//! очікує кур'єра. Система обчислює bearing, перевіряє пряму видимість\n//! (line-of-sight) та генерує підказку для взаємознаходження.\n//!\n//! Використовує `kernel::geo::bearing_deg`, `angular_diff_deg`,\n//! `in_field_of_view`, `los_clear`.\n\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\nuse dowiz_kernel::geo;\n\nstatic APPROACH_TOTAL: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);\nstatic LOS_CHECK_TOTAL: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);\n\n/// Кут огляду для підходу кур'єра.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct ApproachAngle {\n    /// Звідки приходить кур'єр (compass degrees, 0=N).\n    pub bearing_from_courier: f32,\n    /// Куди дивитись клієнту (compass degrees, 0=N).\n    pub bearing_to_address: f32,\n    /// Відстань до адреси (метри).\n    pub distance_m: f32,\n    /// Поле огляду для підказки (градуси).\n    pub fov_deg: f32,\n    /// Чи є пряма видимість (немає будівель на шляху).\n    pub los_clear: bool,\n}\n\n/// Підказка для UI про підхід кур'єра.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CourierApproachHint {\n    pub approach: ApproachAngle,\n    /// Ротація стрілки на екрані (градуси, 0 = north-up).\n    pub arrow_rotation: f32,\n    /// Текстове позначення напрямку.\n    pub label: &'static str,\n}\n\n/// Telemetry: загальна кількість обчислених підходів (від початку програми).\npub fn approach_count() -> u64 {\n    APPROACH_TOTAL.load(Ordering::Relaxed)\n}\n\n/// Telemetry: загальна кількість LOS-перевірок (від початку програми).\npub fn los_check_count() -> u64 {\n    LOS_CHECK_TOTAL.load(Ordering::Relaxed)\n}\n\n/// Визначити кут підходу кур'єра до адреси.\n///\n/// * `courier` — поточна позиція кур'єра (lat, lng).\n/// * `address` — адреса доставки (lat, lng).\n/// * `address_bearing` — кут огляду, який виставив клієнт (опціонально).\n///    Якщо `None`, використовується стандартне FOV 120°.\n/// * `footprints` — контури будівель для LOS-перевірки (опціонально).\npub fn calculate_approach(\n    courier: (f64, f64),\n    address: (f64, f64),\n    address_bearing: Option<f32>,\n    footprints: &[Vec<(f64, f64)>],\n) -> ApproachAngle {\n    APPROACH_TOTAL.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    crate::telemetry_count!("approach", "calculate", 1);\n    let bearing = geo::bearing_deg(courier.0, courier.1, address.0, address.1) as f32;\n    let to_address = (bearing + 180.0) % 360.0;\n    let dist = geo::haversine_meters(courier.0, courier.1, address.0, address.1) as f32;\n    let los = if footprints.is_empty() {\n        true\n    } else {\n        LOS_CHECK_TOTAL.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n        geo::los_clear(courier, address, footprints)\n    };\n    let fov = address_bearing.unwrap_or(120.0);\n    ApproachAngle {\n        bearing_from_courier: bearing,\n        bearing_to_address: to_address,\n        distance_m: dist,\n        fov_deg: fov,\n        los_clear: los,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Згенерувати підказку для UI на основі кута підходу.\npub fn generate_hint(approach: &ApproachAngle) -> CourierApproachHint {\n    let label = direction_label(approach.bearing_from_courier);\n    CourierApproachHint {\n        approach: *approach,\n        arrow_rotation: approach.bearing_from_courier,\n        label,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Перевірити, чи клієнт бачить кур'єра (в межах FOV).\npub fn client_sees_courier(\n    address_bearing: f32,\n    courier_bearing_from_address: f32,\n    fov_deg: f32,\n) -> bool {\n    geo::in_field_of_view(address_bearing as f64, courier_bearing_from_address as f64, fov_deg as f64)\n}\n\n/// Текстова мітка напрямку для UI.\npub fn direction_label(bearing_deg: f32) -> &'static str {\n    let b = ((bearing_deg + 22.5) % 360.0 / 45.0) as u32;\n    match b {\n        0 => "N",\n        1 => "NE",\n        2 => "E",\n        3 => "SE",\n        4 => "S",\n        5 => "SW",\n        6 => "W",\n        7 => "NW",\n        _ => "N",\n    }\n}\n\n/// Кут на екрані для стрілки (north-up).\npub fn arrow_rotation(bearing_deg: f32, view_rotation: f32) -> f32 {\n    geo::arrow_screen_rotation_deg(bearing_deg as f64, view_rotation as f64) as f32\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn approach_bearing_matches_kernel() {\n        let courier = (50.45, 30.52);\n        let address = (50.455, 30.53);\n        let a = calculate_approach(courier, address, None, &[]);\n        let expected = geo::bearing_deg(courier.0, courier.1, address.0, address.1) as f32;\n        assert!(\n            (a.bearing_from_courier - expected).abs() < 1e-4,\n            "bearing must match kernel: got {} expected {}",\n            a.bearing_from_courier, expected\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn address_bearing_overrides_fov() {\n        let courier = (50.45, 30.52);\n        let address = (50.455, 30.53);\n        let a = calculate_approach(courier, address, Some(90.0), &[]);\n        assert!((a.fov_deg - 90.0).abs() < 1e-4, "FOV must be overridden to 90, got {}", a.fov_deg);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn los_clear_when_no_footprints() {\n        let courier = (50.45, 30.52);\n        let address = (50.455, 30.53);\n        let a = calculate_approach(courier, address, None, &[]);\n        assert!(a.los_clear, "without footprints LOS must be clear");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn los_blocked_by_building() {\n        let courier = (1.0, -1.0);\n        let address = (1.0, 3.0);\n        let rect = vec![(0.0, 0.0), (0.0, 2.0), (2.0, 2.0), (2.0, 0.0)];\n        let a = calculate_approach(courier, address, None, &[rect]);\n        assert!(!a.los_clear, "LOS must be blocked by building");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn distance_is_positive() {\n        let courier = (50.45, 30.52);\n        let address = (50.455, 30.53);\n        let a = calculate_approach(courier, address, None, &[]);\n        assert!(a.distance_m > 0.0, "must have positive distance");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn bearing_to_address_is_opposite() {\n        let courier = (50.45, 30.52);\n        let address = (50.455, 30.53);\n        let a = calculate_approach(courier, address, None, &[]);\n        let diff = (a.bearing_from_courier - a.bearing_to_address + 180.0) % 360.0;\n        assert!(\n            diff.abs() < 1.0,\n            "to_address must be opposite: diff={}", diff\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn generate_hint_labels() {\n        for deg in &[0.0_f32, 45.0, 90.0, 135.0, 180.0, 225.0, 270.0, 315.0] {\n            let approach = ApproachAngle {\n                bearing_from_courier: *deg,\n                bearing_to_address: (*deg + 180.0) % 360.0,\n                distance_m: 100.0,\n                fov_deg: 120.0,\n                los_clear: true,\n            };\n            let hint = generate_hint(&approach);\n            assert!(!hint.label.is_empty());\n            assert!((hint.arrow_rotation - deg).abs() < 1e-4);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn direction_labels_cover_all() {\n        let labels: [&str; 8] = ["N", "NE", "E", "SE", "S", "SW", "W", "NW"];\n        for (i, expected) in labels.iter().enumerate() {\n            let deg = i as f32 * 45.0;\n            assert_eq!(direction_label(deg), *expected, "at {} deg", deg);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn client_sees_courier_in_fov() {\n        assert!(client_sees_courier(0.0, 10.0, 120.0));\n        assert!(!client_sees_courier(0.0, 200.0, 120.0));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn arrow_rotation_with_view() {\n        let rot =
```
