## 1019 · /root/dowiz/engine/src/gpu_atomicity.rs · LongTerm

Summary: gpu_atomicity · 333 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/gpu_atomicity.rs	gpu_atomicity · 333 lines	//! gpu_atomicity.rs — P88 atomicity-by-default policy + spec (BLUEPRINT-P88).\n//!\n//! BLUEPRINT: `docs/design/CORE-ROADMAP-2026-07-17/`\n//!            `BLUEPRINT-P88-atomicity-by-default-physics-gpu-2026-07-19.md`\n//!\n//! This module is the **CPU-side, always-compiled** deliverable of P88:\n//!   * the shared-write classification types (§3),\n//!   * the WGSL shared-write checklist audit gate (§4.1/§4.2),\n//!   * the deterministic fixed-point reduction *reference* (§4.4),\n//!   * and the RED→GREEN falsifiers proving the policy bites (§4.2/§4.4/§4.5).\n//!\n//! It deliberately contains **ZERO WGSL / GPU code** — the shader legs (D2, the\n//! shader edits of D3–D7) are gated on the operator-owned P38 §4.2 GPU-compute\n//! decision and are NOT written here. Until that decision, P88 is a written\n//! policy + a checklist template + the deterministic-reduction spec, with no GPU\n//! adapter compiled (the default `engine` build has no GPU adapter; see\n//! `bridge.rs`).\n//!\n//! The whole module compiles on the **default** feature set (no `gpu` feature\n//! exists yet), so every gate below runs under `cargo test` with no flags. This\n//! is what lets P86/P87 *inherit* the rule (cite this module + the blueprint)\n//! before any shader is written.\n//!\n//! `// SINGLE-WRITER:` discipline (§4.5): every class-(c) `SingleWriterProof`\n//! exemption MUST carry a written structural proof at the write site. The\n//! greppable marker constant below is what the future CI grep keys on; the\n//! audit gate (`audit_blocks_merge`) enforces the *non-empty proof* half of it.\n\n// ── Greppable discipline marker (CI gate anchor, §4.5) ────────────────────\n/// The exact comment a physics/GPU non-atomic shared write MUST carry to claim\n/// the single-writer exemption (class `SingleWriterProof`). A CI grep asserts\n/// that every non-atomic `var<storage, read_write>` store in `engine/**/*.wgsl`\n/// is preceded by this marker; the audit gate asserts the referenced `proof`\n/// string is non-empty. Both halves are required — the comment is the site,\n/// the proof text is the argument a reviewer can falsify.\npub const SINGLE_WRITER_MARKER: &str = "// SINGLE-WRITER:";\n\n/// Fixed-point scale for deterministic reductions (§3, §4.4). Chosen so the\n/// field's value range (|U| ≤ 1.0 by the `field_frame` clamp) maps to i64 with\n/// headroom for N-cell accumulation without overflow: 2^20 ≈ 1.05e6, and\n/// 512² = 262_144 cells × max |scaled cell| 2^20 fits comfortably in an i64\n/// accumulator. Named, not magic.\npub const FIXED_POINT_SHIFT: u32 = 20;\n/// `2^FIXED_POINT_SHIFT` as an f64 (1_048_576.0) — the integer↔fixed-point\n/// conversion factor for every physics/GPU reduction.\npub const FIXED_POINT_SCALE: f64 = (1u64 << FIXED_POINT_SHIFT) as f64;\n\n/// Float `atomicAdd` is BANNED in the physics/GPU domain (non-associative →\n/// non-deterministic sum, §0.3/§4.4). This const documents the ban at a\n/// greppable site; enforcement is the review checklist + the reproducibility\n/// test (`red_float_atomic_reduction_is_nondeterministic`) — a float-atomic\n/// reduction fails N-run bit-identity, proving the ban answers a real hazard.\npub const FLOAT_ATOMIC_ADD_BANNED_IN_DOMAIN: bool = true;\n\n/// Classification of a single shared-write site in a physics/GPU shader — the\n/// checklist verdict (§3, §4.2). Every `var<storage, read_write>` /\n/// `var<workgroup>` write MUST resolve to exactly one of these.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SharedWriteClass {\n    /// (a) the write is an atomic op (atomicAdd/atomicMax/… on an integer\n    ///     atomic). Mandatory for any many-writer accumulation site.\n    Atomic,\n    /// (b) the write is separated from conflicting reads by a\n    ///     `workgroupBarrier()` / `storageBarrier()`.\n    BarrierSeparated,\n    /// (c) the write is proven single-writer by construction (ping-pong,\n    ///     per-invocation-disjoint output index). REQUIRES a written\n    ///     `// SINGLE-WRITER:` proof at the site (non-empty `proof`).\n    SingleWriterProof,\n}\n\n/// One row of the per-shader shared-write checklist (the review artifact, §4.2).\n/// Before a physics/GPU shader merges, every shared write must appear as a row\n/// whose `class` is set and — for class (c) — whose `proof` is non-empty.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct SharedWriteAudit {\n    /// Shader under review, e.g. `"field_step.wgsl"`.\n    pub shader: &'static str,\n    /// The binding written, e.g. `"var<storage, read_write> next: array<f32>"`.\n    pub binding: &'static str,\n    /// The classification verdict (a)/(b)/(c). A shader with any unclassified\n    /// write (or a class-(c) write with empty `proof`) is RED.\n    pub class: SharedWriteClass,\n    /// The `// SINGLE-WRITER:` text for class (c); `""` otherwise.\n    pub proof: &'static str,\n}\n\n/// The standing review gate (§4.1/§4.2). Returns `true` iff every shared write\n/// in the checklist is a *valid* exemption: a class-(c) `SingleWriterProof` MUST\n/// carry a non-empty written proof, or the whole shader is rejected (RED).\n///\n/// This is the machine-checkable half of the `// SINGLE-WRITER:` discipline: an\n/// unproven "trust me it's single-writer" entry — or any physics shared write\n/// left with an empty proof — cannot merge. Classes (a) `Atomic` and (b)\n/// `BarrierSeparated` need no single-writer proof, so an empty `proof` is\n/// acceptable for them.\npub fn audit_blocks_merge(audits: Vec<SharedWriteAudit>) -> bool {\n    audits.iter().all(|a| {\n        // A single-writer exemption WITHOUT a written proof is rejected.\n        !(matches!(a.class, SharedWriteClass::SingleWriterProof) && a.proof.is_empty())\n    })\n}\n\n/// Deterministic fixed-point reduction over a cell buffer (§4.4).\n///\n/// Each `f64` cell value is scaled to a fixed-point integer, the integers are\n/// summed as `i64` (**integer addition is associative → order-independent**),\n/// then the total is de-scaled back to `f64`. Because the sum is a pure function\n/// of the *multiset* of inputs, the result is bit-identical regardless of the\n/// accumulation order — this is exactly what makes an atomic GPU reduction\n/// reproducible (the `red_fixed_point_reduction_is_run_deterministic` gate).\n///\n/// Values must lie within the `i64` accumulator headroom; for the field's\n/// |U| ≤ 1.0 range and grids up to 512² this holds (see `FIXED_POINT_SHIFT`).\npub fn reduce_fixed_point(cells: &[f64]) -> f64 {\n    let total: i64 = cells\n        .iter()\n        .map(|&v| (v * FIXED_POINT_SCALE).round() as i64)\n        .sum();\n    total as f64 / FIXED_POINT_SCALE\n}\n\n/// Float-accumulate reduction (the NEGATIVE control, §4.4).\n///\n/// IEEE-754 `f64` addition is **non-associative**, so this fold's result depends\n/// on the accumulation order. It is the exact pattern a banned `atomicAdd<f32>`\n/// would exhibit under arbitrary GPU invocation-completion order, and the\n/// `red_float_atomic_reduction_is_nondeterministic` gate uses it to PROVE the\n/// in-domain float-atomic ban answers a real hazard (non-vacuousness).\npub fn reduce_float(cells: &[f64]) -> f64 {\n    cells.iter().fold(0.0f64, |acc, &v| acc + v)\n}\n\n/// CPU-oracle matcher (§4.4, `red_reduction_matches_cpu_oracle`).\n///\n/// The de-scaled fixed-point total must agree with a plain sequential `f64` fold\n/// (the CPU `field_energy` oracle) within the fixed-point quantization\n/// tolerance `≤ 2^-FIXED_POINT_SHIFT × N`. Per-cell rounding error is bounded by\n/// `0.5 / FIXED_POINT_SCALE`, so the N-cell total is within `N·2^-SHIFT`, making\n/// this bound tight and always satisfiable by a correct reference.\npub fn matches_cpu_oracle(fixed_total: f64, oracle_total: f64, n_cells: usize) -> bool {\n    let tol = (2.0f64).powi(-(FIXED_POINT_SHIFT as i32)) * (n_cells as f64);\n    (fixed_total - oracle_total).abs() <= tol\n}\n\n// ── Tiny deterministic PRNG (no external deps) for reproducible shuffles ──\n/// XorShift64* — used only to deterministically permute accumulation order in\n/// the RED gates, so the tests are reproducible run-to-run without `rand`.\nstruct XorShift(u64);\nimpl XorShift {\n    fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {\n        let mut x = self.0;\n        x ^= x << 13;\n        x ^= x >> 7;\n        x ^= x << 17;\n        self.0 = x;\n        x\n    }\n    fn shuffle<T>(&mut self, slice: &mut [T]) {\n        for i in (1..slice.len()).rev() {\n            let j = (self.next_u64() % (i as u64 + 1)) as usize;\n            slice.swap(i, j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // ── §4.2 D1 — an unproven single-writer exemption is rejected ──────────\n    /// RED: a checklist row with class (c) and an EMPTY proof fails the audit\n    /// (an exemption without a written proof cannot merge). GREEN once the proof\n    /// text is present.\n    #[test]\n    fn red_unclassified_shared_write_blocks_merge() {\n        // (1) EMPTY proof → audit rejects (RED for a naive "trust me" entry).\n        let unproven = SharedWriteAudit {\n            shader: "field_step.wgsl",\n            binding: "var<storage, read_write> next: array<f32>",\n            class: SharedWriteClass::SingleWriterProof,\n            proof: "",\n        };\n        assert!(\n            !audit_blocks_merge(vec![unproven]),\n            "an unproven single-writer exemption MUST be rejected"\n        );\n\n        // (2) GREEN: the same row with a written proof passes the audit.\n        let proven = SharedWriteAudit {\n            shader: "field_step.wgsl",\n            binding: "var<storage, read_write> next: array<f32>",\n            class: SharedWriteClass::SingleWriterProof,\n            proof: "// SINGLE-WRITER: ping-pong — read set `u` (disjoint prev \\\n                    buffer), write set `next`; output index == global_invocation_id; \\\n                    each cell written by exactly one invocation.",\n        };\n        assert!(\n            audit_blocks_merge(vec![proven]),\n            "a single-writer exemption WITH a written proof MUST merge"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── §4.2 D2 — the stencil step is the canonical single-writer exemption ─\n    /// RED (encodes §0.1 as a machine-checkable row): the future `field_step`\n    /// classifies its `next` write as `SingleWriterProof` with the ping-pong\n    /// proof text, and the audit passes. A future edit that turns the step into a\n    /// *shared* accumulator (a real bug) would have no valid class and fail.\n    #[test]\n    fn red_stencil_step_is_single_writer_exempt() {\n        let field_step_checklist = vec![\n            SharedWriteAudit {\n                shader: "field_step.wgsl",\n                binding: "var<storage, read_write> next: array<f32>",\n                class: SharedWriteClass::SingleWriterProof,\n                proof: "// SINGLE-WRITER: ping-pong. Read set = `u` (prev buffer); \\\n                        write set = `next` (disjoint buffer). Output index i == \\\n                        global_invocation_id; each cell written by exactly one \\\n                        invocation. The buffer rotations (CPU: field_frame.rs:217-221) \\\n                        keep read/write disjoint. No cross-invocation shared write \\\n                        exists → atomic-free is CORRECT, not merely un-benched.",\n            },\n            // A barrier-separated write (e.g. a staged intermediate) is also fine.\n            SharedWriteAudit {\n                shader: "field_step.wgsl",\n                binding: "var<workgroup> scratch: array<f32, 256>",\n                class: SharedWriteClass::BarrierSeparated,\n                proof: "",\n            },\n        ];\n        assert!(\n            audit_blocks_merge(field_step_checklist),\n            "the field_step checklist (single-writer `next` + barrier scratch) MUST pass"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── §4.4 D3 — the fixed-point reduction is run-deterministic ───────────\n    /// RED→GREEN (the key determinism proof): run the fixed-point reduction over\n    /// the SAME cell buffer N=32 times with a SHUFFLED accumulation order → all\n    /// 32 sums are bit-identical. Integer addition is associative, so the fixed-\n    /// point accumulator is a pure function of the input multiset.\n    #[test]\n    fn red_fixed_point_reduction_is_run_deterministic() {\n        // A deterministic, mixed-magnitude cell buffer (|U| ≤ 1.0 field range).\n        let mut cells: Vec<f64> = (0..1024)\n            .map(|i| {\n                let r = (i as f64 * 0.6180339887498949).fract();\n                (r - 0.5) * 1.6 // spread across ~[-0.8, 0.8]\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        let base = reduce_fixed_point(&cells);\n        let mut all_identical = true;\n        for run in 0..32u64 {\n            let mut perm = cells.clone();\n            XorShift(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15 ^ (run << 1)).shuffle(&mut perm);\n            let s = reduce_fixed_point(&perm);\n            if s.to_bits() != base.to_bits() {\n                all_identical = false;\n            }\n        }\n        assert!(\n            all_identical,\n            "fixed-point reduction MUST be bit-identical across 32 shuffled runs"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── §4.4 D4 — the float-atomic hazard is REAL (non-vacuousness) ────────\n    /// RED (the non-vacuousness proof): the SAME N=32 test over a *float*-\n    /// accumulate reduction with a shuffled summation order MUST exhibit ≥2\n    /// differing sums. Float addition is non-associative, so a `float atomicAdd`\n    /// would be run-to-run non-deterministic. This proves the in-domain ban\n    /// answers a genuine hazard, not a decorative rule.\n    ///\n    /// The buffer is engineered with large dynamic range (one unit-magnitude\n    /// anchor + many tiny values) so that WHERE the anchor sits in the\n    /// accumulation order measurably changes the rounded result — exactly the\n    /// hazard an arbitrary GPU completion order would trigger.\n    #[test]\n    fn red_float_atomic_reduction_is_nondeterministic() {\n        // 1.0 anchor + 2000 values of 1e-8. Serial-adding each 1e-8 to 1.0\n        // rounds back to 1.0 (lost), but accumulating the tinies first then\n        // adding to 1.0 yields ~1.00002 — so the result depends on the anchor's\n        // position, which the shuffle varies run-to-run.\n        let mut cells: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(2001);\n        cells.push(1.0);\n        for _ in 0..2000 {\n            cells.push(1e-8);\n        }\n\n        let mut distinct: std::collections::HashSet<u64> = std::collections::HashSet::new();\n        for run in 0..32u64 {\n            let mut perm = cells.clone();\n            XorShift(0x1234_5678_9ABC_DEF0 ^ (run << 2)).shuffle(&mut perm);\n            distinct.insert(reduce_float(&perm).to_bits());\n        }\n        assert!(\n            distinct.len() >= 2,\n            "float accumulation MUST be non-deterministic (≥2 distinct sums over 32 \\\n             shuffled runs); got {} — the float-atomic ban would be vacuous",\n            distinct.len()\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── §4.4 D5 — the GPU reduction is measured against the CPU oracle ─────\n    /// RED→GREEN: the de-scaled fixed-point total matches a simple sequential\n    /// `f64` fold (the CPU `field_energy` oracle) within the quantization\n    /// tolerance `≤ 2^-FIXED_POINT_SHIFT × N`. The GPU path is *measured\n    /// against* the authority, never replacing it.\n    #[test]\n    fn red_reduction_matches_cpu_oracle() {\n        // A plain cell buffer of N values in the field's |U| ≤ 1.0 range.\n        let n = 1024usize;\n        let cells: Vec<f64> = (0..n)\n            .map(|i| {\n                let r = (i as f64 * 0.7548776662).fract();\n                (r - 0.5) * 1.2\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        // Oracle: sequential f64 fold (the authoritative CPU reduction).\n        let oracle: f64 = cells.iter().fold(0.0f64, |acc, &v| acc + v);\n        // Fixed-point reference total.\n        let fixed = reduce_fixed_point(&cells);\n\n        assert!(\n            matches_cpu_oracle(fixed, oracle, n),\n            "fixed-point total {fixed} must match CPU oracle {oracle} within \\\n             2^-SHIFT·N = {}",\n            (2.0f64).powi(-(FIXED_POINT_SHIFT as i32)) * (n as f64)\n        );\n    }\n}\n	1020	-1	-1		df71359fdd8f0337a121abf59712632fc83ebd6e2d62f5bf3a56ae6f8383c3633c0b3182c78b7a8e915a030a2194dc285f617da4f46a0461a1ff7a0cf704fa6fe6ae56d9cfdef01817a93909d7bbed5057fb583a298bca4bd8c0b0a0c68b1584b070db6623cb528fea48460d59000f180cb9642a1d8583c4112bf6f4eb2aaef1
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/hooks.rs	hooks · 207 lines	//! PostOrderHooks — відгуки, підписки, хуки на фіналі арки.\n//!\n//! Після завершення замовлення (етап Review) система пропонує:\n//! - Залишити відгук про замовлення\n//! - Підписатись на медіа-канали власника (Instagram, Telegram, WhatsApp)\n//! - Кожен хук має власний splat-конфіг для анімованої появи\n//!\n//! Хуки відображаються як невеликі "візитівки" з іконками, які\n//! з'являються через splat-анімацію. Ніякого нав'язування — тільки\n//! м'яке запрошення (discovery).\n\n/// Канал для підписки.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum HookChannel {\n    Instagram,\n    Telegram,\n    WhatsApp,\n}\n\nimpl HookChannel {\n    pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            HookChannel::Instagram => "Instagram",\n            HookChannel::Telegram => "Telegram",\n            HookChannel::WhatsApp => "WhatsApp",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Тип хука.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum HookType {\n    Review,\n    Subscribe,\n}\n\n/// Тип анімації splat-появи.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SplatAnim {\n    FadeIn,\n    Pop,\n    SlideUp,\n    Pulse,\n}\n\n/// Конфігурація splat-іконки для хука.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct IconSplatConfig {\n    pub icon: &'static str,\n    pub size: f32,\n    pub color: [f32; 4],\n    pub animation: SplatAnim,\n}\n\n/// Один післязамовний хук.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct PostOrderHook {\n    pub hook_type: HookType,\n    pub channel: HookChannel,\n    pub text: &'static str,\n    pub icon_config: IconSplatConfig,\n    pub action_url: &'static str,\n}\n\nimpl PostOrderHook {\n    /// Хук для відгуку.\n    pub fn review() -> Self {\n        PostOrderHook {\n            hook_type: HookType::Review,\n            channel: HookChannel::Telegram,\n            text: "Залишити відгук про замовлення",\n            icon_config: IconSplatConfig {\n                icon: "★",\n                size: 32.0,\n                color: [0.831, 0.686, 0.216, 1.0],\n                animation: SplatAnim::Pop,\n            },\n            action_url: "/review",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Хук для підписки на Instagram.\n    pub fn subscribe_instagram() -> Self {\n        PostOrderHook {\n            hook_type: HookType::Subscribe,\n            channel: HookChannel::Instagram,\n            text: "Підписатись на Instagram",\n            icon_config: IconSplatConfig {\n                icon: "📷",\n                size: 28.0,\n                color: [0.9, 0.3, 0.5, 1.0],\n                animation: SplatAnim::FadeIn,\n            },\n            action_url: "https://instagram.com/",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Хук для підписки на Telegram.\n    pub fn subscribe_telegram() -> Self {\n        PostOrderHook {\n            hook_type: HookType::Subscribe,\n            channel: HookChannel::Telegram,\n            text: "Підписатись на Telegram-канал",\n            icon_config: IconSplatConfig {\n                icon: "✈",\n                size: 28.0,\n                color: [0.2, 0.6, 0.9, 1.0],\n                animation: SplatAnim::SlideUp,\n            },\n            action_url: "https://t.me/",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Хук для підписки на WhatsApp.\n    pub fn subscribe_whatsapp() -> Self {\n        PostOrderHook {\n            hook_type: HookType::Subscribe,\n            channel: HookChannel::WhatsApp,\n            text: "Отримувати сповіщення в WhatsApp",\n            icon_config: IconSplatConfig {\n                icon: "💬",\n                size: 28.0,\n                color: [0.2, 0.7, 0.3, 1.0],\n                animation: SplatAnim::Pulse,\n            },\n            action_url: "https://wa.me/",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Усі стандартні хуки для показу після замовлення.\n    pub fn default_hooks() -> Vec<PostOrderHook> {\n        vec![\n            PostOrderHook::review(),\n            PostOrderHook::subscribe_instagram(),\n            PostOrderHook::subscribe_telegram(),\n            PostOrderHook::subscribe_whatsapp(),\n        ]\n    }\n}\n\n/// Згенерувати хуки на основі конфігурації власника.\n/// channels — які канали підтримує власник (назви: "instagram", "telegram", "whatsapp").\npub fn hooks_for_owner(channels: &[HookChannel]) -> Vec<PostOrderHook> {\n    let mut hooks = vec![PostOrderHook::review()];\n    for ch in channels {\n        match ch {\n            HookChannel::Instagram => hooks.push(PostOrderHook::subscribe_instagram()),\n            HookChannel::Telegram => hooks.push(PostOrderHook::subscribe_telegram()),\n            HookChannel::WhatsApp => hooks.push(PostOrderHook::subscribe_whatsapp()),\n        }\n    }\n    hooks\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn review_hook_has_correct_type() {\n        let hook = PostOrderHook::review();\n        assert_eq!(hook.hook_type, HookType::Review);\n        assert_eq!(hook.channel, HookChannel::Telegram);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn subscribe_hooks_have_subscribe_type() {\n        for hook in &[PostOrderHook::subscribe_instagram(), PostOrderHook::subscribe_telegram(), PostOrderHook::subscribe_whatsapp()] {\n            assert_eq!(hook.hook_type, HookType::Subscribe);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn default_hooks_includes_review_and_three_subscriptions() {\n        let hooks = PostOrderHook::default_hooks();\n        assert_eq!(hooks.len(), 4);\n        assert!(hooks.iter().any(|h| h.hook_type == HookType::Review));\n        assert!(hooks.iter().any(|h| h.channel == HookChannel::Instagram));\n        assert!(hooks.iter().any(|h| h.channel == HookChannel::Telegram));\n        assert!(hooks.iter().any(|h| h.channel == HookChannel::WhatsApp));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn hooks_for_owner_filters_channels() {\n        let hooks = hooks_for_owner(&[HookChannel::Instagram, HookChannel::Telegram]);\n        assert_eq!(hooks.len(), 3); // 1 review + 2 subscribe\n        assert!(hooks.iter().any(|h| h.hook_type == HookType::Review));\n        assert!(hooks.iter().any(|h| h.channel == HookChannel::Instagram));\n        assert!(hooks.iter().any(|h| h.channel == HookChannel::Telegram));\n        assert!(hooks.iter().all(|h| h.channel != HookChannel::WhatsApp));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_hooks_have_non_empty_text() {\n        for hook in PostOrderHook::default_hooks() {\n            assert!(!hook.text.is_empty());\n            assert!(!hook.action_url.is_empty());\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn channel_names_are_displayable() {\n        assert_eq!(HookChannel::Instagram.name(), "Instagram");\n        assert_eq!(HookChannel::Telegram.name(), "Telegram");\n        assert_eq!(HookChannel::WhatsApp.name(), "WhatsApp");\n    }\n}\n	1042	-1	-1		e6c6b75697cc8abe2aaea5f28d778a0e5950a6e3ada3cf59c8ecf89761f1d7e390763c9136c92c87dece3408d0db1ea04e3f61d6fd130efcc2e8ee8de4134a3b0857fa515523b7698c87f1e1790bb0167c67f90e31ea33efdc2c13c67a4e75b4c1e28513deef347a2868ae577a1cf8fd80d14362b6c8ced284f543e1e4c1d549
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/intent.rs	intent · 744 lines	//! P64 M1 — Intent runtime v1 (deterministic classifier + router).\n//!\n//! BLUEPRINT-P64 §2.1 / §3.1. Extends P38 §11.2's intent grammar (which is\n//! 0-grep-hit baseline until here) — this module is the single owner of the\n//! `Intent`/`FieldPos`/`WidgetId`/`NavTarget`/`CommandId`/`InputSource` types and\n//! the deterministic classifier + router that turns raw input into resolved\n//! intents.\n//!\n//! Design constraints (binding):\n//! - The classifier is a PURE fn of (input, context) — no I/O, reproducible (P6\n//!   Cause-and-Effect). `classifier_is_pure` proves it.\n//! - Every raw event funnels through this seam. Nothing downstream ever sees a\n//!   concrete event type (P38-rev §12.2 c3). The `no_raw_event_leak` grep gate\n//!   (engine/tests/firewall.rs) asserts handlers live ONLY here / inference/.\n//! - A consequential candidate is never `Ambiguous` and never reaches the\n//!   optional AI ranker (§3.1 / §16.4 / P6). The classifier enforces this.\n\nuse crate::text_input::{FieldPos, WidgetId};\nuse crate::widget_store::WidgetStore;\n\n/// Which surface's command lexicon is live (P38 §11.2 `SurfaceId`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]\npub struct SurfaceId(pub u32);\n\n/// Where an input came from and the active bias. Equal-channel by default\n/// (§16.50); `CourierInMotion` biases toward voice (§16.53) WITHOUT disabling\n/// other channels — it only shifts lexicon sensitivity / pointer precision.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub enum InputProfile {\n    #[default]\n    Balanced,\n    CourierInMotion,\n    HandsFree,\n}\n\n/// Navigation target (P38 §11.2 `NavTarget`). The v1 set is the surfaces/regions\n/// the composer knows how to build.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum NavTarget {\n    Menu,\n    Cart,\n    Catalog,\n    Checkout,\n    OwnerDashboard,\n    CourierBoard,\n}\n\n/// A command identifier (P38 §11.2 `CommandId`). The surface lexicon maps\n/// spoken/typed phrases to these deterministically (Aho-Corasick-style prefix\n/// match in the v1 classifier).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum CommandId {\n    OpenMenu,\n    AcceptOrder,\n    ConfirmOrder,\n    CancelOrder,\n    DeclineOrder,\n    OpenCart,\n    OpenCatalog,\n    GoCheckout,\n    OpenOwnerDashboard,\n    OpenCourierBoard,\n}\n\n/// The intent grammar (P38 §11.2). This is the ONLY vocabulary the field UI and\n/// the renderer exchange — there is no event-type-specific path outside\n/// `InputSource` adapters.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum Intent {\n    /// Point at a field position (no widget hit).\n    Point(FieldPos),\n    /// A directed impulse at `pos` with scalar magnitude `mag` (e.g. a fling).\n    Impulse(FieldPos, f32),\n    /// Select a widget (hit-test resolved).\n    Select(WidgetId),\n    /// Navigate to a target region/surface.\n    Navigate(NavTarget),\n    /// A continuous scrub along one axis with signed delta `dx`.\n    Scrub(f32),\n    /// Issue a command (resolved from a voice/typed phrase).\n    Command(CommandId),\n}\n\nimpl Intent {\n    /// Consequential intents are the ones that MOVE MONEY or DESTROY STATE. The\n    /// classifier must never route these through the AI ranker, and the composer\n    /// must attach a `FrictionSpec` (§3.2). A consequential intent is resolved\n    /// only via the deterministic lexicon, never via `Ambiguous`.\n    pub fn is_consequential(&self) -> bool {\n        match self {\n            Intent::Command(CommandId::ConfirmOrder)\n            | Intent::Command(CommandId::AcceptOrder)\n            | Intent::Command(CommandId::CancelOrder)\n            | Intent::Command(CommandId::DeclineOrder)\n            | Intent::Command(CommandId::GoCheckout) => true,\n            // Book-keeping navigation is not consequential; exploratory nav is the\n            // AI-rankable case.\n            _ => false,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The classifier's verdict. `Resolved` is the ONLY variant a consequential\n/// action may consume (see `Classification::require_resolved`). `Ambiguous` is\n/// the ONLY place the optional AI ranker may run — and never for a consequential\n/// candidate.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum Classification {\n    Resolved(Intent),\n    /// Exploratory-navigation candidates only; ranked by the optional AI layer.\n    /// Never contains a consequential intent.\n    Ambiguous(Vec<Intent>),\n    Rejected(RejectReason),\n}\n\n/// Why a raw input was rejected.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum RejectReason {\n    NoTarget,\n    BelowThreshold,\n    UnknownCommand,\n    /// A consequential candidate appeared in an ambiguous phrase set — the AI\n    /// must never touch money/destructive intents, so we hard-reject instead of\n    /// auto-picking or deferring.\n    OutOfContext,\n}\n\nimpl Classification {\n    /// The resolved intent, if any. Consequential actions consume ONLY this.\n    pub fn require_resolved(self) -> Option<Intent> {\n        match self {\n            Classification::Resolved(i) => Some(i),\n            Classification::Ambiguous(_) | Classification::Rejected(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Raw, pre-classification input. One variant per InputSource kind. The\n/// classifier is the ONLY consumer; nothing downstream ever sees one.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum RawInput {\n    Pointer {\n        pos: FieldPos,\n        phase: PointerPhase,\n        vel: (f32, f32),\n    },\n    Key(KeyCode),\n    VoicePhrase {\n        transcript: String,\n        confidence: f32,\n        is_final: bool,\n    },\n    Gesture {\n        kind: GestureKind,\n        origin: FieldPos,\n        vector: (f32, f32),\n        held_ms: u32,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Pointer phase for a `RawInput::Pointer`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum PointerPhase {\n    Down,\n    Move,\n    Up,\n}\n\n/// Keyboard key (P38 §11.2 `KeyCode`). A small, offline-clean, no-DOM set — the\n/// in-canvas editor (P57) owns the full alphabet; this is the subset the intent\n/// classifier consumes. Kept here so the seam is closed even for key input.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum KeyCode {\n    Enter,\n    Escape,\n    Backspace,\n    ArrowUp,\n    ArrowDown,\n    ArrowLeft,\n    ArrowRight,\n    Char(char),\n}\n\n/// A gesture kind for `RawInput::Gesture`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum GestureKind {\n    Fling,\n    Hold,\n    Pull,\n    Squeeze,\n}\n\n/// The input-source seam (P38 §11.2). ONE code path: sources → classify → apply.\n/// The wgpu UI receives `Intent`s across this seam and NEVER touches raw events.\npub trait InputSource {\n    /// Poll the source for the next raw input. `None` = no new input this tick.\n    fn poll(&mut self) -> Option<RawInput>;\n}\n\n/// Aim tolerance: cos-angle threshold below which a sustained gesture is aimed\n/// at the commit well (§4.3, `AIM_TOLERANCE`).\npub const AIM_TOLERANCE: f32 = 0.35;\n\n/// Context the classifier hit-tests / disambiguates against. Borrowed, never owned.\npub struct IntentContext<'a> {\n    pub widgets: &'a WidgetStore,\n    pub surface: SurfaceId,\n    pub profile: InputProfile,\n}\n\n/// A fixed command-lexicon entry: a keyword (prefix) → `CommandId`/`NavTarget`.\n/// The v1 classifier matches the longest keyword prefix (deterministic,\n/// Aho-Corasick-shaped but a plain sorted scan in v1 — no external crate).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct LexiconEntry {\n    pub keyword: &'static str,\n    pub command: Option<CommandId>,\n    pub nav: Option<NavTarget>,\n    /// If true, matching this entry is consequential (the classifier must\n    /// resolve it directly, never `Ambiguous`).\n    pub consequential: bool,\n}\n\n/// The deterministic classifier. Pure fn of (input, context) — reproducible.\n/// Holds the per-surface command lexicon (a fixed dispatch table).\npub struct IntentClassifier {\n    lexicon: Vec<LexiconEntry>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for IntentClassifier {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IntentClassifier {\n    /// Build the default lexicon (covers the v1 command/nav set). keyword: "cancel order",\n                command: Some(CommandId::CancelOrder),\n                nav: None,\n                consequential: true,\n            },\n            LexiconEntry {\n                keyword: "cancel",\n                command: Some(CommandId::CancelOrder),\n                nav: None,\n                consequential: true,\n            },\n            LexiconEntry {\n                keyword: "decline order",\n                command: Some(CommandId::DeclineOrder),\n                nav: None,\n                consequential: true,\n            },\n            LexiconEntry {\n                keyword: "decline",\n                command: Some(CommandId::DeclineOrder),\n                nav: None,\n                consequential: true,\n            },\n        ];\n        // Keep longest-keyword-first so the longest-prefix match wins.\n        IntentClassifier { lexicon }\n    }\n\n    /// Classify a single raw input deterministically.\n    pub fn classify(&self, input: &RawInput, ctx: &IntentContext) -> Classification {\n        match input {\n            RawInput::Pointer { pos, phase, vel } => self.classify_pointer(*pos, *phase, *vel, ctx),\n            RawInput::Key(key) => self.classify_key(*key),\n            RawInput::VoicePhrase {\n                transcript,\n                confidence,\n                is_final,\n            } => self.classify_voice(transcript, *confidence, *is_final, ctx),\n            RawInput::Gesture { origin, vector, .. } => self.classify_gesture(*origin, *vector),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn classify_pointer(\n        &self,\n        pos: FieldPos,\n        phase: PointerPhase,\n        vel: (f32, f32),\n        ctx: &IntentContext,\n    ) -> Classification {\n        match phase {\n            // Down/Up: hit-test the widget store. A hit → Select; empty field → Point.\n            PointerPhase::Down | PointerPhase::Up => {\n                if let Some(w) = hit_test(ctx.widgets, pos) {\n                    Classification::Resolved(Intent::Select(w))\n                } else {\n                    Classification::Resolved(Intent::Point(pos))\n                }\n            }\n            PointerPhase::Move => {\n                let speed = (vel.0 * vel.0 + vel.1 * vel.1).sqrt();\n                if speed < AIM_TOLERANCE {\n                    // Below the impulse threshold → just a point (no scrub).\n                    if let Some(w) = hit_test(ctx.widgets, pos) {\n                        Classification::Resolved(Intent::Select(w))\n                    } else {\n                        Classification::Resolved(Intent::Point(pos))\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    // dx dominates → Scrub; else Impulse (a fling).\n                    if vel.0.abs() > vel.1.abs() {\n                        Classification::Resolved(Intent::Scrub(vel.0))\n                    } else {\n                        Classification::Resolved(Intent::Impulse(pos, speed))\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn classify_key(&self, key: KeyCode) -> Classification {\n        match key {\n            KeyCode::Enter => Classification::Resolved(Intent::Command(CommandId::ConfirmOrder)),\n            KeyCode::Escape => Classification::Resolved(Intent::Command(CommandId::CancelOrder)),\n            KeyCode::ArrowUp | KeyCode::ArrowDown | KeyCode::ArrowLeft | KeyCode::ArrowRight => {\n                // Discrete scrub along the dominant axis.\n                let dx = match key {\n                    KeyCode::ArrowLeft => -1.0,\n                    KeyCode::ArrowRight => 1.0,\n                    _ => 0.0,\n                };\n                Classification::Resolved(Intent::Scrub(dx))\n            }\n            KeyCode::Backspace | KeyCode::Char(_) => {\n                Classification::Rejected(RejectReason::NoTarget)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn classify_voice(\n        &self,\n        transcript: &str,\n        confidence: f32,\n        is_final: bool,\n        ctx: &IntentContext,\n    ) -> Classification {\n        // Non-final partials are not classified yet (the ASR stream is still\n        // refining). We don't resolve on a partial — the router drops these.\n        if !is_final {\n            return Classification::Rejected(RejectReason::NoTarget);\n        }\n        // CourierInMotion biases sensitivity up: lower confidence still accepted.\n        let min_confidence = match ctx.profile {\n            InputProfile::CourierInMotion => 0.3,\n            _ => 0.5,\n        };\n        if confidence < min_confidence {\n            return Classification::Rejected(RejectReason::BelowThreshold);\n        }\n        let phrase = transcript.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();\n\n        // Collect every lexicon keyword that is a prefix of (or equal to) the\n        // phrase, OR whose phrase is a prefix of the keyword — the latter is the\n        // exploratory case ("open" → could become "open menu" / "open cart"),\n        // which must surface as Ambiguous rather than silently resolve.\n        let matches: Vec<&LexiconEntry> = self\n            .lexicon\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|e| {\n                phrase == e.keyword\n                    || phrase.starts_with(e.keyword)\n                    || e.keyword.starts_with(&phrase)\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        if matches.is_empty() {\n            return Classification::Rejected(RejectReason::UnknownCommand);\n        }\n\n        // If any matched entry is consequential, the AI must NOT touch it. Hard\n        // reject out-of-context (the safety core: no money/destructive intent is\n        // ever auto-picked or deferred to a probabilistic ranker).\n        if matches.iter().any(|e| e.consequential) {\n            return Classification::Rejected(RejectReason::OutOfContext);\n        }\n\n        // Build the set of DISTINCT targets the phrase matches (a phrase can be a\n        // prefix of several keywords → exploratory ambiguity). Order candidates by\n        // specificity (longest keyword first) so the optional AI ranker / UI sees\n        // the most precise suggestion first.\n        let mut distinct: Vec<(Option<CommandId>, Option<NavTarget>, usize)> = matches\n            .iter()\n            .map(|e| (e.command, e.nav, e.keyword.len()))\n            .collect();\n        distinct.sort_by(|a, b| b.2.cmp(&a.2));\n        distinct.dedup_by(|a, b| a.0 == b.0 && a.1 == b.1);\n        if distinct.len() >= 2 {\n            let candidates: Vec<Intent> = distinct\n                .iter()\n                .filter_map(|(c, n, _)| c.map(Intent::Command).or_else(|| n.map(Intent::Navigate)))\n                .collect();\n            if candidates.len() >= 2 {\n                // Exploratory ambiguity — surface for the optional AI ranker; never\n                // auto-resolve (D2). E.g. "open" → {OpenMenu, OpenCart}.\n                return Classification::Ambiguous(candidates);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Exactly one distinct target matched → resolve it deterministically.\n        // Prefer the navigation target (an "open X" phrase navigates; the coupled\n        // CommandId is just the canonical id the composer also accepts).\n        let best = matches\n            .iter()\n            .max_by_key(|e| e.keyword.len())\n            .expect("matches is non-empty here");\n        if let Some(n) = best.nav {\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Navigate(n))\n        } else if let Some(c) = best.command {\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Command(c))\n        } else {\n            Classification::Rejected(RejectReason::UnknownCommand)\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn classify_gesture(&self, origin: FieldPos, vector: (f32, f32)) -> Classification {\n        let mag = (vector.0 * vector.0 + vector.1 * vector.1).sqrt();\n        if mag < AIM_TOLERANCE {\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Point(origin))\n        } else if vector.0.abs() > vector.1.abs() {\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Scrub(vector.0))\n        } else {\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Impulse(origin, mag))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Hit-test a `FieldPos` against the widget store. Returns the `WidgetId` of the\n/// nearest widget whose bounding box (centred at pos) contains the point. v1 uses\n/// the SoA `pos_x`/`pos_y`/`size_w`/`size_h` columns; a widget at index i spans\n/// `[pos_x-size_w/2, pos_x+size_w/2] × [pos_y-size_h/2, pos_y+size_h/2]`.\nfn hit_test(widgets: &WidgetStore, pos: FieldPos) -> Option<WidgetId> {\n    for i in 0..widgets.len() {\n        let cx = widgets.pos_x[i];\n        let cy = widgets.pos_y[i];\n        let hw = widgets.size_w[i] * 0.5;\n        let hh = widgets.size_h[i] * 0.5;\n        if (pos.u - cx).abs() <= hw && (pos.v - cy).abs() <= hh {\n            return Some(widgets.id[i]);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// ONE code path (P38 §11.2 invariant): sources → classify → apply.\npub struct InputRouter {\n    sources: Vec<Box<dyn InputSource>>,\n    classifier: IntentClassifier,\n}\n\nimpl InputRouter {\n    pub fn new(sources: Vec<Box<dyn InputSource>>) -> Self {\n        InputRouter {\n            sources,\n            classifier: IntentClassifier::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Poll every source, classify, emit resolved intents. Ambiguous/Rejected are\n    /// dropped from the apply stream (they are logged by telemetry item 10 and the\n    /// optional AI ranker may re-resolve Ambiguous ones elsewhere — never here).\n    ///\n    /// Each source is polled ONCE per `tick` (one frame = one event per source);\n    /// a source that has nothing this frame returns `None`. This keeps the router\n    /// bounded — a source never blocks or spins the frame loop.\n    pub fn tick(&mut self, ctx: &IntentContext) -> Vec<Intent> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        for src in self.sources.iter_mut() {\n            if let Some(raw) = src.poll() {\n                match self.classifier.classify(&raw, ctx) {\n                    Classification::Resolved(i) => out.push(i),\n                    // Drop ambiguous/rejected from the apply stream here.\n                    Classification::Ambiguous(_) | Classification::Rejected(_) => {}\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// Classify one raw input directly (used by tests and the composer path).\n    pub fn classify(&self, input: &RawInput, ctx: &IntentContext) -> Classification {\n        self.classifier.classify(input, ctx)\n    }\n\n    /// A test/router seam for the optional AI ranker: given an ambiguous set,\n    /// pick the first non-consequential candidate deterministically. The ranker\n    /// may ONLY be called on `Ambiguous` (never consequential) — enforced by the\n    /// classifier never producing `Ambiguous` with a consequential candidate.\n    pub fn rank_ambiguous(&self, candidates: &[Intent]) -> Option<Intent> {\n        candidates.iter().find(|i| !i.is_consequential()).cloned()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn ctx_for(widgets: &WidgetStore) -> IntentContext<'_> {\n        IntentContext {\n            widgets,\n            surface: SurfaceId(0),\n            profile: InputProfile::Balanced,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn widget_at(widgets: &mut WidgetStore, idx: usize, id: WidgetId, cx: f32, cy: f32) {\n        widgets.id[idx] = id;\n        widgets.pos_x[idx] = cx;\n        widgets.pos_y[idx] = cy;\n        widgets.size_w[idx] = 2.0;\n        widgets.size_h[idx] = 2.0;\n    }\n\n    // D1 — pointer over widget-7 → Resolved(Select(7)); empty field → Point.\n    #[test]\n    fn intent_types_exist_and_exercised() {\n        let mut ws = WidgetStore::new(8);\n        widget_at(&mut ws, 7, 7, 5.0, 5.0);\n        let ctx = ctx_for(&ws);\n        let classifier = IntentClassifier::new();\n\n        let down_on_widget = RawInput::Pointer {\n            pos: FieldPos {\n                u: 5.0,\n                v: 5.0,\n                w: 0.0,\n            },\n            phase: PointerPhase::Down,\n            vel: (0.0, 0.0),\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            classifier.classify(&down_on_widget, &ctx),\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Select(7))\n        );\n\n        let down_empty = RawInput::Pointer {\n            pos: FieldPos {\n                u: -40.0,\n                v: -40.0,\n                w: 0.0,\n            },\n            phase: PointerPhase::Down,\n            vel: (0.0, 0.0),\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            classifier.classify(&down_empty, &ctx),\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Point(FieldPos {\n                u: -40.0,\n                v: -40.0,\n                w: 0.0\n            }))\n        );\n\n        // Router round-trip: a source emitting the widget-down yields Select(7).\n        let mut router = InputRouter::new(vec![Box::new(ConstSource(down_on_widget.clone()))]);\n        let intents = router.tick(&ctx);\n        assert_eq!(intents, vec![Intent::Select(7)]);\n    }\n\n    // D1 — voice round-trip: "open menu" final → Navigate(Menu).\n    #[test]\n    fn voice_round_trip() {\n        let ws = WidgetStore::new(4);\n        let ctx = ctx_for(&ws);\n        let classifier = IntentClassifier::new();\n        let voice = RawInput::VoicePhrase {\n            transcript: "open menu".into(),\n            confidence: 0.9,\n            is_final: true,\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            classifier.classify(&voice, &ctx),\n            Classification::Resolved(Intent::Navigate(NavTarget::Menu))\n        );\n    }\n\n    // D2 — classifier purity: same (input, ctx) twice ⇒ identical Classification.\n    #[test]\n    fn classifier_is_pure() {\n        let ws = WidgetStore::new(4);\n        let ctx = ctx_for(&ws);\n        let a = IntentClassifier::new();\n        let b = IntentClassifier::new();\n        for phrase in ["open menu", "confirm order", "cart", "accept order", "zzz"] {\n            let raw = RawInput::VoicePhrase {\n                transcript: phrase.into(),\n                confidence: 0.8,\n                is_final: true,\n            };\n            let c1 = a.classify(&raw, &ctx);\n            let c2 = b.classify(&raw, &ctx);\n            assert_eq!(c1, c2, "classifier must be pure for {phrase}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // D2 — a consequential+nav match must Reject(OutOfContext), never Ambiguous.\n    #[test]\n    fn ambiguous_never_auto_commits() {\n        let ws = WidgetStore::new(4);\n        let ctx = ctx_for(&ws);\n        let classifier = IntentClassifier::new();\n        // "confirm" matches both AcceptOrder? No — "confirm" matches ConfirmOrder\n        // (consequential). "checkout" matches GoCheckout (consequential). Either\n        // alone must reject-out-of-context, never resolve or defer.\n        let confirm = RawInput::VoicePhrase {\n            transcript: "confirm".into(),\n            confidence: 0.9,\n            is_final: true,\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            classifier.classify(&confirm, &ctx),\n            Classification::Rejected(RejectReason::OutOfContext)\n        );\n        let checkout = RawInput::VoicePhrase {\n            transcript: "checkout".into(),\n            confidence: 0.9,\n            is_final: true,\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            classifier.classify(&checkout, &ctx),\n            Classification::Rejected(RejectReason::OutOfContext)\n        );\n    }\n\n    // D1 — exploratory ambiguity surfaces as Ambiguous (non-consequential only).\n    #[test]\n    fn exploratory_ambiguity_is_ambiguous() {\n        let ws = WidgetStore::new(4);\n        let ctx = ctx_for(&ws);\n        let classifier = IntentClassifier::new();\n  is_final: true,\n        };\n        match classifier.classify(&open, &ctx) {\n            Classification::Ambiguous(cands) => {\n                assert!(\n                    cands.iter().all(|c| !c.is_consequential()),\n                    "ambiguous set must be consequential-free"\n                );\n                assert!(cands.len() >= 2);\n            }\n            other => panic!("expected Ambiguous, got {other:?}"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// A tiny constant source for router round-trip tests.\n    struct ConstSource(RawInput);\n    impl InputSource for ConstSource ## 1147 · /root/dowiz/engine/src/loop_.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: loop_ · 167 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/loop_.rs	loop_ · 167 lines	//! FE-03 — Fixed-timestep accumulator loop.\n//!\n//! RED→GREEN GATE (per blueprint): simulate a stutter (e.g. 50ms injected frame\n//! time). The RED variable-dt integrator sees 0.05 → diverges (field tested\n//! divergent at 0.05). The GREEN fixed-timestep loop clamps frame time and only\n//! ever feeds the integrator the compile-constant `DT_STABLE`; interpolation\n//! (`alpha = accum / DT`) keeps render smooth at 60fps while physics steps at\n//! a fixed 50Hz.\n//!\n//! Guards: `MAX_FRAME` clamp (spiral-of-death), `MAX_SUBSTEPS` cap, `dt` is a\n//! compile-const equal to the kernel's `DT_STABLE`\n//! (`dowiz-kernel/src/lib.rs::DT_STABLE` — the authoritative source of truth).\n\n/// Fixed physics step — MUST equal `dowiz-kernel::DT_STABLE`\n/// (`kernel/src/lib.rs`) so the integrator never sees a divergent dt (kernel is\n/// the authority on stability). The kernel pins its value with\n/// `dt_stable_is_authoritative`; this mirror pin catches drift on the engine\n/// side. If you change one, change both.\npub const DT_STABLE: f32 = 0.02;\n\n/// Clamp for a single rendered frame time (guards spiral-of-death).\npub const MAX_FRAME: f32 = 0.25;\n\n/// Cap on substeps consumed per rendered frame.\npub const MAX_SUBSTEPS: u32 = 5;\n\n/// Records every `dt` actually handed to the integrator — the falsifiable\n/// evidence that the loop honors the fixed-step contract under stutter.\npub struct FixedTimestep {\n    accumulator: f32,\n    /// Every dt the integrator was called with this run (should all be DT_STABLE).\n    seen_dts: Vec<f32>,\n    /// Interpolation factor for the most recent render.\n    pub last_alpha: f32,\n    /// True if the MAX_FRAME clamp engaged (a dropped frame was capped).\n    pub clamped: bool,\n}\n\nimpl FixedTimestep {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        FixedTimestep {\n            accumulator: 0.0,\n            seen_dts: Vec::new(),\n            last_alpha: 0.0,\n            clamped: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Advance one rendered frame given `frame_time` (seconds, real wall clock,\n    /// possibly janky). `step` is called with the FIXED dt; `render(alpha)` is\n    /// called once with the interpolation factor.\n    pub fn frame<F, R>(&mut self, frame_time: f32, mut step: F, mut render: R)\n    where\n        F: FnMut(f32),\n        R: FnMut(f32),\n    {\n        // 1) clamp frame time to avoid spiral-of-death.\n        let ft = if frame_time > MAX_FRAME {\n            self.clamped = true;\n            MAX_FRAME\n        } else {\n            frame_time\n        };\n        self.accumulator += ft;\n\n        // 2) consume fixed steps — integrator ONLY ever sees DT_STABLE.\n        let mut substeps = 0u32;\n        while self.accumulator >= DT_STABLE && substeps < MAX_SUBSTEPS {\n            step(DT_STABLE);\n            self.seen_dts.push(DT_STABLE);\n            self.accumulator -= DT_STABLE;\n            substeps += 1;\n        }\n        // If we hit the substep cap, drop the leftover accumulator (keep stable).\n        if substeps == MAX_SUBSTEPS && self.accumulator > DT_STABLE {\n            self.accumulator = 0.0;\n        }\n\n        // 3) interpolation factor for smooth render between prev/curr.\n        self.last_alpha = (self.accumulator / DT_STABLE).clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n        render(self.last_alpha);\n    }\n\n    /// Max dt actually delivered to the integrator this run.\n    pub fn max_seen_dt(&self) -> f32 {\n        self.seen_dts.iter().cloned().fold(0.0_f32, f32::max)\n    }\n\n    /// Min dt actually delivered to the integrator this run.\n    pub fn min_seen_dt(&self) -> f32 {\n        self.seen_dts.iter().cloned().fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for FixedTimestep {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // RED→GREEN: under a 50ms stutter, the integrator ONLY ever sees DT_STABLE\n    // (0.02). A variable-dt loop would hand it 0.05 → diverge.\n    #[test]\n    fn stutter_never_feeds_divergent_dt() {\n        let mut loop_ = FixedTimestep::new();\n        let mut steps = 0u32;\n        // A janky 50ms frame followed by smooth 16.6ms frames.\n        let frames = [0.050_f32, 0.0166, 0.0166, 0.0166, 0.050, 0.0166];\n        for ft in frames {\n            loop_.frame(ft, |_dt| steps += 1, |_a| {});\n        }\n        assert_eq!(\n            loop_.max_seen_dt(),\n            DT_STABLE,\n            "integrator never receives a divergent dt (RED path would see 0.05)"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            loop_.min_seen_dt(),\n            DT_STABLE,\n            "every step is exactly DT_STABLE"\n        );\n        assert!(steps > 0);\n    }\n\n    // Smooth 60fps: alpha interpolates, dt stays fixed.\n    #[test]\n    fn smooth_60fps_fixed_step_with_interpolation() {\n        let mut loop_ = FixedTimestep::new();\n        let mut alphas = Vec::new();\n        for _ in 0..10 {\n            loop_.frame(1.0 / 60.0, |_dt| {}, |a| alphas.push(a));\n        }\n        assert!(\n            alphas.iter().all(|&a| (0.0..=1.0).contains(&a)),\n            "interpolation alpha stays within [0,1]"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(loop_.max_seen_dt(), DT_STABLE);\n    }\n\n    // Spiral-of-death guard: a pathological 10s frame must not loop forever.\n    #[test]\n    fn pathological_frame_does_not_infinite_loop() {\n        let mut loop_ = FixedTimestep::new();\n        let mut steps = 0u32;\n        loop_.frame(10.0, |_dt| steps += 1, |_a| {});\n        assert!(\n            steps <= MAX_SUBSTEPS,\n            "substep cap honored — no spiral of death"\n        );\n        assert!(loop_.clamped);\n    }\n\n    // Mirror pin for the kernel↔engine DT_STABLE contract. The authoritative\n    // value lives in `dowiz-kernel::DT_STABLE` (kernel/src/lib.rs). This catches\n    // drift on the engine side; the kernel's `dt_stable_is_authoritative` catches\n    // it on the kernel side. Both must stay 0.02 (50 Hz) or the integrator\n    // desyncs from the kernel's route-kinematics sampling cadence.\n    #[test]\n    fn dt_stable_matches_kernel_contract() {\n        assert_eq!(DT_STABLE, 0.02);\n        assert_eq!((1.0 / DT_STABLE as f64).round() as u32, 50);\n    }\n}\n	1148	-1	-1		eb4fbc5b94ee15b7890de38281223a054115de2c5d74758f815c005db1b573267d044c34d75f709fa172c7a9c515d9203eb773b4316619ba72626b8a4b14ea0c2fb774e8bf4c696831c17803859ae2196fe8c92a25a2968b8c80b0b23413f054f030163690a352bf92f8e08d29992d1a6d3d7d3e079149e4c593c4d62f022b12
```

## 1185 · /root/dowiz/engine/src/mode.rs · LongTerm

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/mode.rs	mode · 339 lines	//! ModeController — Атмосфера / Справа (Atmosphere / Business).\n//!\n//! Два режими роботи інтерфейсу:\n//! - **Atmosphere** (режисерський): повні анімації, хвилі, Turing-текстури,\n//!   microphysics, наративні переходи, discovery-ефекти. Для першого знайомства\n//!   та коли важливий досвід.\n//! - **Business** (швидкий): усі анімації, переходи, декоративні ефекти вимкнені.\n//!   Максимальна швидкість без очікування. Для досвідчених користувачів,\n//!   низького заряду батареї, або коли важлива тільки швидкість.\n//!\n//! Перемикання між режимами НІКОЛИ не втрачає стан замовлення (P64 §3.1:\n//! presentation-only — замовлення належить kernel FSM). Режим впливає тільки\n//! на презентацію: які анімації, переходи, ефекти відображаються.\n\n/// Тип режиму інтерфейсу.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub enum ModeType {\n    /// Повний досвід: анімації, хвилі, Turing-реакції, наративні переходи.\n    #[default]\n    Atmosphere,\n    /// Швидкий: усе вимкнено, максимальна продуктивність.\n    Business,\n}\n\nimpl ModeType {\n    pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            ModeType::Atmosphere => "atmosphere",\n            ModeType::Business => "business",\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_atmosphere(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, ModeType::Atmosphere)\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_business(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, ModeType::Business)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Профіль анімаційних параметрів для режиму.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct WaveProfile {\n    pub enabled: bool,\n    pub amplitude: f32,\n    pub frequency: f32,\n    pub phase: f32,\n    pub decay: f32,\n}\n\nimpl WaveProfile {\n    pub const fn disabled() -> Self {\n        WaveProfile { enabled: false, amplitude: 0.0, frequency: 0.0, phase: 0.0, decay: 0.0 }\n    }\n\n    pub const fn atmosphere() -> Self {\n        WaveProfile { enabled: true, amplitude: 0.6, frequency: 0.5, phase: 0.0, decay: 0.1 }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Профіль Turing-реакції-дифузії для режиму.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct TuringProfile {\n    pub enabled: bool,\n    pub feed_rate: f32,\n    pub kill_rate: f32,\n    pub diffusion_rate_u: f32,\n    pub diffusion_rate_v: f32,\n    pub injection_strength: f32,\n    pub injection_radius: u32,\n    pub grid_size: (u32, u32),\n}\n\nimpl TuringProfile {\n    pub const fn disabled() -> Self {\n        TuringProfile {\n            enabled: false, feed_rate: 0.0, kill_rate: 0.0,\n            diffusion_rate_u: 0.0, diffusion_rate_v: 0.0,\n            injection_strength: 0.0, injection_radius: 0, grid_size: (0, 0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub const fn atmosphere() -> Self {\n        TuringProfile {\n            enabled: true, feed_rate: 0.035, kill_rate: 0.06,\n            diffusion_rate_u: 0.16, diffusion_rate_v: 0.08,\n            injection_strength: 0.3, injection_radius: 12,\n            grid_size: (128, 128),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Профіль microphysics (пружинки) для режиму.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct MicroProfile {\n    pub enabled: bool,\n    pub stiffness: f32,\n    pub damping: f32,\n    pub max_displacement: f32,\n    pub rest_position: f32,\n}\n\nimpl MicroProfile {\n    pub const fn disabled() -> Self {\n        MicroProfile { enabled: false, stiffness: 0.0, damping: 0.0, max_displacement: 0.0, rest_position: 0.0 }\n    }\n\n    pub const fn atmosphere() -> Self {\n        MicroProfile { enabled: true, stiffness: 60.0, damping: 12.0, max_displacement: 30.0, rest_position: 0.0 }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Тип мапи для режиму.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum MapProfile {\n    Explore,\n    Minimal,\n}\n\n/// Набір активних профілів для поточного режиму.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct ActiveProfiles {\n    pub wave: WaveProfile,\n    pub turing: TuringProfile,\n    pub micro: MicroProfile,\n    pub map: MapProfile,\n    pub transitions: bool,\n    pub haptics: bool,\n}\n\n/// Контролер режимів інтерфейсу.\n///\n/// Зберігає поточний режим та сповіщає підписників про зміни.\n/// Стан замовлення НІКОЛИ не зберігається тут — це presentation-only.\npub struct ModeController {\n    mode: ModeType,\n    on_change: Vec<Box<dyn FnMut(ModeType)>>,\n}\n\nimpl ModeController {\n    /// Створити новий контролер у режимі Atmosphere (за замовчуванням).\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        ModeController {\n            mode: ModeType::Atmosphere,\n            on_change: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_mode(&self) -> ModeType {\n        self.mode\n    }\n\n    /// Встановити режим. Сповіщає підписників тільки при реальній зміні.\n    pub fn set_mode(&mut self, mode: ModeType) {\n        if mode == self.mode {\n            return;\n        }\n        self.mode = mode;\n        for cb in &mut self.on_change {\n            cb(mode);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Перемкнути між Atmosphere ↔ Business.\n    pub fn toggle(&mut self) {\n        let next = match self.mode {\n            ModeType::Atmosphere => ModeType::Business,\n            ModeType::Business => ModeType::Atmosphere,\n        };\n        self.set_mode(next);\n    }\n\n    /// Автоматично вибрати режим на основі контексту.\n    ///\n    /// Повертає рекомендований режим, але НЕ змінює поточний —\n    /// виклик [`set_mode`] окремий.\n    pub fn auto_select(context: ModeContext) -> ModeType {\n        if context.is_first_visit {\n            return ModeType::Atmosphere;\n        }\n        if context.battery_level < 0.2 {\n            return ModeType::Business;\n        }\n        if !context.is_online {\n            return ModeType::Business;\n        }\n        if context.order_count >= 3 {\n            return ModeType::Business;\n        }\n        ModeType::Atmosphere\n    }\n\n    /// Отримати активні профілі для поточного режиму.\n    pub fn get_active_profiles(&self) -> ActiveProfiles {\n        match self.mode {\n            ModeType::Business => ActiveProfiles {\n                wave: WaveProfile::disabled(),\n                turing: TuringProfile::disabled(),\n                micro: MicroProfile::disabled(),\n                map: MapProfile::Minimal,\n                transitions: false,\n                haptics: false,\n            },\n            ModeType::Atmosphere => ActiveProfiles {\n                wave: WaveProfile::atmosphere(),\n                turing: TuringProfile::atmosphere(),\n                micro: MicroProfile::atmosphere(),\n                map: MapProfile::Explore,\n                transitions: true,\n                haptics: true,\n            },\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Підписатись на зміну режиму.\n    pub fn on_mode_change(&mut self, cb: Box<dyn FnMut(ModeType)>) {\n        self.on_change.push(cb);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for ModeController {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Контекст для автоматичного вибору режиму.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct ModeContext {\n    pub is_first_visit: bool,\n    pub battery_level: f32,\n    pub is_online: bool,\n    pub order_count: u32,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn default_mode_is_atmosphere() {\n        let mc = ModeController::new();\n        assert_eq!(mc.get_mode(), ModeType::Atmosphere);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn toggle_switches_modes() {\n        let mut mc = ModeController::new();\n        assert_eq!(mc.get_mode(), ModeType::Atmosphere);\n        mc.toggle();\n        assert_eq!(mc.get_mode(), ModeType::Business);\n        mc.toggle();\n        assert_eq!(mc.get_mode(), ModeType::Atmosphere);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn set_mode_fires_callback() {\n        use std::cell::Cell;\n        use std::rc::Rc;\n        let mut mc = ModeController::new();\n        let last_mode = Rc::new(Cell::new(ModeType::Atmosphere));\n        let lm = last_mode.clone();\n        mc.on_mode_change(Box::new(move |m| { lm.set(m); }));\n\n        mc.set_mode(ModeType::Business);\n        assert_eq!(last_mode.get(), ModeType::Business);\n\n        // Same mode — no callback\n        mc.set_mode(ModeType::Business);\n        assert_eq!(last_mode.get(), ModeType::Business);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn auto_select_uses_context() {\n        // First visit → Atmosphere\n        assert_eq!(\n            ModeController::auto_select(ModeContext {\n                is_first_visit: true, battery_level: 1.0, is_online: true, order_count: 0,\n            }),\n            ModeType::Atmosphere,\n        );\n        // Low battery → Business\n        assert_eq!(\n            ModeController::auto_select(ModeContext {\n                is_first_visit: false, battery_level: 0.15, is_online: true, order_count: 0,\n            }),\n            ModeType::Business,\n        );\n        // Offline → Business\n        assert_eq!(\n            ModeController::auto_select(ModeContext {\n                is_first_visit: false, battery_level: 0.5, is_online: false, order_count: 0,\n            }),\n            ModeType::Business,\n        );\n        // 3+ orders → Business\n        assert_eq!(\n            ModeController::auto_select(ModeContext {\n                is_first_visit: false, battery_level: 0.5, is_online: true, order_count: 5,\n            }),\n            ModeType::Business,\n        );\n        // Normal → Atmosphere\n        assert_eq!(\n            ModeController::auto_select(ModeContext {\n                is_first_visit: false, battery_level: 0.8, is_online: true, order_count: 1,\n            }),\n            ModeType::Atmosphere,\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn active_profiles_match_mode() {\n        let mut mc = ModeController::new();\n\n        let atm = {\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/money_guard.rs	money_guard · 137 lines	//! FE-09 — Field↔state boundary (money-never-tween guard) 🔴 RED-LINE.\n//!\n//! RED→GREEN GATE (per blueprint): money is a DISCRETE channel, never a field\n//! channel. The field continuum interpolates screen coordinates, NOT monetary\n//! amounts. A money value must never pass through spring/interpolation; it\n//! jumps integer→integer by construction.\n//!\n//! Enforced TWO ways:\n//! 1. **Type-level (compile-time):** `Money` does NOT implement `FieldValue`,\n//!    so `Spring<Money>` / `interpolate(money, ..)` is a build error. The type\n//!    system makes the illegal path unrepresentable.\n//! 2. **Runtime guard:** `TweenGuard::present_money` refuses any fractional/\n//!    interpolated money. It takes an `f64` precisely so a fractional value is\n//!    representable and rejected (FEYNMAN-07: an `i64` parameter could never be\n//!    fractional, so the old guard was dead code). Money is integer minor-unit\n//!    by construction; a non-integer here is the RED signature of tweening.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Money(pub i64);\n\n/// Marker trait for values the field MAY interpolate (screen coordinates,\n/// opacity, scale). Deliberately NOT implemented for [`Money`].\npub trait FieldValue: Copy {\n    /// Linear interpolate `self`→`other` at `t∈[0,1]`.\n    fn lerp(self, other: Self, t: f32) -> Self;\n}\n\nimpl FieldValue for f32 {\n    fn lerp(self, other: Self, t: f32) -> Self {\n        self + (other - self) * t.clamp(0.0, 1.0)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FieldValue for (f32, f32) {\n    fn lerp(self, other: Self, t: f32) -> Self {\n        let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n        (\n            self.0 + (other.0 - self.0) * t,\n            self.1 + (other.1 - self.1) * t,\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// Animate a FIELD value from `a`→`b` over `t∈[0,1]` (lerp). Only `FieldValue`\n/// types allowed — `Money` is excluded at compile time.\npub fn interpolate<T: FieldValue>(a: T, b: T, t: f32) -> T {\n    a.lerp(b, t)\n}\n\n/// Runtime guard for presenting money. Money is emitted as the DECIDED integer\n/// — never an interpolated fraction. Takes an `f64` (not `i64`) so that a\n/// fractional/"interpolated" value is actually representable and can be\n/// rejected (FEYNMAN-07: the old `i64` parameter made the guard dead code\n/// because every `i64` is an exact integer as `f64`).\npub struct TweenGuard;\n\nimpl TweenGuard {\n    /// Present a decided money amount. `amount_minor` MUST be an integer minor\n    /// unit; the guard rejects a fractional presentation (the RED signature of\n    /// tweening). Returns the integer minor value on success.\n    pub fn present_money(amount_minor: f64) -> Result<i64, String> {\n        // Live guard: reject any fractional input. (An `f64` can be non-integral;\n        // an `i64` parameter could not, which is why the prior guard was dead.)\n        if (amount_minor.fract()).abs() > 1e-9 {\n            return Err("money must be presented as a decided integer, never interpolated".into());\n        }\n        Ok(amount_minor.round() as i64)\n    }\n\n    /// The ONLY legal money transition: jump integer→integer, no interpolation.\n    pub fn jump(_from: Money, to: Money) -> Money {\n        to\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // GREEN: field values interpolate freely.\n    #[test]\n    fn field_value_interpolates() {\n        assert!((interpolate(0.0_f32, 10.0_f32, 0.5) - 5.0).abs() < 1e-6);\n        assert_eq!(\n            interpolate((0.0_f32, 0.0_f32), (2.0_f32, 4.0_f32), 0.5),\n            (1.0, 2.0)\n        );\n    }\n\n    // GREEN: money jumps integer→integer, no intermediate.\n    #[test]\n    fn money_jumps_integer_to_integer() {\n        let m = TweenGuard::jump(Money(100), Money(250));\n        assert_eq!(m.0, 250);\n        assert!(TweenGuard::present_money(250.0).is_ok());\n    }\n\n    // RED→GREEN: the guard is LIVE — a fractional/"interpolated" amount is\n    // actually rejected (FEYNMAN-07 fixed the dead `i64` guard).\n    #[test]\n    fn present_money_rejects_fractional() {\n        // The classic tween product: lerp(100,250,0.37) = 155.5 minor units.\n        let interpolated: f64 = 100.0 + (250.0 - 100.0) * 0.37; // 155.5\n        assert!(\n            interpolated.fract().abs() > 1e-9,\n            "setup: the interpolated value is genuinely fractional"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            TweenGuard::present_money(interpolated).is_err(),\n            "fractional money (the RED tween signature) must be rejected"\n        );\n        // A clean integer presentation still succeeds.\n        assert_eq!(TweenGuard::present_money(155.0).unwrap(), 155);\n    }\n\n    // Compile-time proof that Money is NOT a FieldValue:\n    // the following would NOT compile (intentionally commented):\n    //   interpolate(Money(100), Money(250), 0.5);  // ERROR: Money: !FieldValue\n    //   Spring::<Money>::snappy(Money(0));          // ERROR: Spring requires FieldValue\n    //\n    // Runtime mirror of the compile-time guarantee: present_money rejects a\n    // genuinely fractional (interpolated) amount.\n    #[test]\n    fn compile_time_boundary_mirrored_at_runtime() {\n        // The interpolated "in-between" amount a tween would produce.\n        let interpolated: f64 = 100.0 + (250.0 - 100.0) * 0.37; // 155.5 — fractional\n        assert!(\n            TweenGuard::present_money(interpolated).is_err(),\n            "fractional (interpolated) money must be rejected by the live guard"\n        );\n        // A clean integer decides fine.\n        assert_eq!(TweenGuard::present_money(155.0).unwrap(), 155);\n        // The real guarantee: Money never enters interpolate(). We assert the\n        // type does not carry fractional state by construction.\n        let decided = Money(155);\n        assert_eq!(decided.0, 155); // integer, always\n    }\n}\n	1204	-1	-1		2ffdbf77bcde2bb00829b3c981229231201a4524acf5b52ce58e2ad985e4dc4754c47ec85f1d64a687575307f0c096306e45f124716105e8f2eaff82fe14e4d665be56f9cf78e81d55471914b7f9e148a5f8cf6b39832a23d0b3f0bafcdbdfaee0f0d20695c112aad8188f8df4292d8f6c9d6d3e3496cff737ede6cbc9802760
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/motion.rs	motion · 177 lines	//! FE-08 — Motion field (critically-damped spring easing).\n//!\n//! RED→GREEN GATE (per blueprint): ζ=1 → monotone, no overshoot; ζ<1 → bounces;\n//! heat-kernel stagger ripples outward with delay ∝ graph distance.\n//!\n//! Per-property spring integrator: `ẍ + 2ζω ẋ + ω²x = ω²·x_target`.\n//! (ω,ζ) derived from `motion.ts` tension/friction:\n//!   ω = √(k/m),  ζ = d / (2√(k·m))   (with m=1: ω=√k, ζ=d/2√k).\n//! Regions: snappy ζ=1 ω≈30 (τ_s≈130ms), fluid ζ≈0.65–0.8, playful ζ≈0.35.\n//! Semi-implicit Euler (stable). Money is NEVER a field channel (see FE-09).\n\n/// A single critically-damped-capable spring on one scalar property.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Spring {\n    /// Current value.\n    pub x: f32,\n    /// Current velocity.\n    pub v: f32,\n    /// Target value.\n    pub target: f32,\n    /// Angular frequency ω (rad/s).\n    omega: f32,\n    /// Damping ratio ζ.\n    zeta: f32,\n}\n\nimpl Spring {\n    /// `tension`→k, `friction`→d (mass m=1, so ω=√k, ζ=d/(2√k)).\n    pub fn new(tension: f32, friction: f32, initial: f32) -> Self {\n        let k = tension.max(0.0);\n        let d = friction.max(0.0);\n        let omega = k.sqrt();\n        let zeta = if omega > 0.0 {\n            (d / (2.0 * omega)).clamp(0.0, 4.0)\n        } else {\n            1.0\n        };\n        Spring {\n            x: initial,\n            v: 0.0,\n            target: initial,\n            omega,\n            zeta,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Step the integrator by fixed `dt` (semi-implicit Euler — stable for\n    /// stiff springs when dt ≤ ~1/ω). Internally substeps so ω·dt_sub ≤ 0.1\n    /// (keeps the discrete ζ=1 solution monotone, overshoot < 1e-3).\n    pub fn step(&mut self, dt: f32) {\n        let w = self.omega;\n        let sub = if w > 0.0 {\n            ((w * dt) / 0.1).ceil().max(1.0) as usize\n        } else {\n            1\n        };\n        let h = dt / sub as f32;\n        for _ in 0..sub {\n            let accel = w * w * (self.target - self.x) - 2.0 * self.zeta * w * self.v;\n            self.v += accel * h;\n            self.x += self.v * h;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Snappy preset (ζ=1, ω≈30) — used for press/enter emphasis.\n    pub fn snappy(initial: f32) -> Self {\n        Spring::new(900.0, 60.0, initial) // friction = 2·ζ·√k = 60 → exact ζ=1\n    }\n\n    /// Fluid preset (ζ≈0.7).\n    pub fn fluid(initial: f32) -> Self {\n        Spring::new(700.0, 2.0 * 0.7 * 700.0_f32.sqrt(), initial)\n    }\n\n    /// Playful preset (ζ≈0.35, bounces).\n    pub fn playful(initial: f32) -> Self {\n        Spring::new(700.0, 2.0 * 0.35 * 700.0_f32.sqrt(), initial)\n    }\n\n    pub fn zeta(&self) -> f32 {\n        self.zeta\n    }\n}\n\n/// Stagger delay by graph distance (FE-08 global transitions): delay of node `j`\n/// relative to a source node, ∝ graph distance / √α.\n///\n/// NOTE (FEYNMAN-16): this is **wave-front / ballistic** scaling (`t = d/√α`,\n/// a propagation speed of `√α`), NOT diffusive heat-kernel scaling (which would\n/// be `t ∝ d²/α`). The `√α` is a propagation speed, so the documented unit is\n/// "distance / speed" (same dimension as the caller's time unit), not seconds\n/// per se. The monotonicity (↑distance ⇒ ↑delay, ↑α ⇒ ↓delay) the callers rely\n/// on holds for the wave-front model; rename to `wavefront_delay` is deferred\n/// to avoid a cross-crate symbol churn — the physics is documented here instead.\npub fn heat_kernel_delay(graph_distance: f32, alpha: f32) -> f32 {\n    if alpha <= 0.0 {\n        return f32::INFINITY;\n    }\n    graph_distance / alpha.sqrt()\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // RED→GREEN: ζ=1 is monotone — no overshoot past the target.\n    #[test]\n    fn zeta_one_no_overshoot() {\n        let mut s = Spring::snappy(0.0);\n        s.target = 1.0;\n        let mut max_x = 0.0f32;\n        for _ in 0..600 {\n            // 60Hz, 10s of sim\n            s.step(1.0 / 60.0);\n            max_x = max_x.max(s.x);\n        }\n        assert!(\n            max_x <= 1.0 + 1e-3,\n            "ζ=1 must NOT overshoot target; max_x={max_x}"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            (s.x - 1.0).abs() < 1e-2,\n            "ζ=1 settles exactly at target; x={}",\n            s.x\n        );\n        assert_eq!(s.zeta(), 1.0);\n    }\n\n    // ζ<1 overshoots (bounces).\n    #[test]\n    fn zeta_below_one_overshoots() {\n        let mut s = Spring::playful(0.0);\n        s.target = 1.0;\n        let mut max_x = 0.0f32;\n        for _ in 0..600 {\n            s.step(1.0 / 60.0);\n            max_x = max_x.max(s.x);\n        }\n        assert!(\n            max_x > 1.0,\n            "ζ<1 must overshoot target (bounce); max_x={max_x}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Settles: velocity and distance-to-target both decay to ~0.\n    #[test]\n    fn snappy_settles_quickly() {\n        let mut s = Spring::snappy(0.0);\n        s.target = 1.0;\n        // τ_s ≈ 2/(ζω) ≈ 130ms → settle well within 1s.\n        for _ in 0..60 {\n            s.step(1.0 / 60.0);\n        }\n        assert!((s.x - 1.0).abs() < 0.05, "settled within ~1s; x={}", s.x);\n    }\n\n    // Heat-kernel delay grows with graph distance, shrinks with α.\n    #[test]\n    fn heat_kernel_delay_monotone() {\n        let near = heat_kernel_delay(1.0, 4.0);\n        let far = heat_kernel_delay(4.0, 4.0);\n        assert!(far > near, "farther node delays more");\n        let faster = heat_kernel_delay(4.0, 16.0);\n        assert!(faster < far, "higher α (diffusion) → shorter delay");\n    }\n\n    // Money guard: a Spring is a FIELD channel only — never feed it money.\n    // (compile-time proof: Spring::step takes no money type; this documents\n    //  the invariant. The FE-09 module enforces the type-level boundary.)\n    #[test]\n    fn spring_is_field_channel_not_money() {\n        let mut s = Spring::snappy(10.0);\n        s.target = 20.0; // a screen coordinate, NOT a monetary amount\n        s.step(1.0 / 60.0);\n        assert!(s.x > 10.0, "field channel interpolates freely");\n    }\n}\n	1220	-1	-1		23df3e65d0eeabb0c9199ac28b4243136116d7a4ad52f74ee5dea2d9b7ec71661d0cef806ddf40a7e17e542391d0d320faa41fb4346a00eaeaea669bfd046c06628854f9677d787910171801f38ba2facd78d82e79b08e69d022e5941c033374c4f4d25635e1b51bdaa88c8f2c9d3dc96c394d729982ccf4c7f9cc7529122722
```
