## 1495 · /root/dowiz/engine/src/screens.rs · LongTerm

Summary: screens · 477 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/screens.rs	screens · 477 lines	//! screens.rs — role-screen layout (vendor-data-driven SDF scenes).\n//!\n//! P-screen — pixel-verification spine. Each role's "screen" is a [`Scene`] of\n//! SDF primitives laid out from the REAL vendor menu (see `vendor.rs`), not a\n//! placeholder box. The composer's `compose_ui.rs` consumes these layouts to\n//! produce `ComposedResponse`s; this module is the dedicated, deterministic\n//! layout authority a backend pixel-verification harness rasterizes headlessly.\n//!\n//! Why this exists (the operator directive): the interface is generated + checked\n//! on the BACKEND so Playwright (a browser-driven frontend probe) is not needed.\n//! `Scene::render_frame` is already bit-deterministic (scene.rs gate 1), so a\n//! backend raster + a golden signature IS the falsifiable "does the layout still\n//! look right" check — rendered once, verified forever, no GPU/browser in the loop.\n//!\n//! Layout convention (shared with the WGSL UI shader spine):\n//! - World units = field-space "tiles"; one menu card = a 2.0×1.4 rounded box.\n//! - The menu grid is a column-major flow: card k sits at\n//!   `(col_x, row_y)` where `col_x = -W/2 + 2.0 + 2.4*col`, `row_y = H/2 - 1.2 - 1.7*row_in_col`.\n//! - Owner/courier screens reuse the same field space; role changes which\n//!   fragments compose, not the world units (one intent interface, role-tinted render).\n//!\n//! Innovate: ceiling — v1 lays out a fixed grid sized to the first N items; a real\n//! flow-layout (variable card heights for set/cocktail categories) is a P-flow\n//! upgrade. Trigger: when the composer's generative producer (P64 §8 Track-R)\n//! lands, replace `customer_menu_screen` with a `FragmentFn` that flows from\n//! `AppState.item_count` instead of a static slice.\n\nuse crate::scene::{Scene, SdfShape};\nuse crate::vendor;\n\n/// Field-space "card" half-extents (a menu product card).\nconst CARD_HW: f64 = 1.0;\nconst CARD_HH: f64 = 0.7;\n/// Horizontal/vertical pitch between cards in the grid.\nconst PITCH_X: f64 = 2.4;\nconst PITCH_Y: f64 = 1.7;\n\n/// The customer "menu" screen — a grid of the vendor's Chef's Picks, laid out as\n/// SDF rounded boxes (one per item) so the raster encodes the real menu shape.\n/// A cart badge (circle) appears at top-right when `cart_count > 0`.\npub fn customer_menu_screen(cart_count: u32) -> Scene {\n    let picks = vendor::by_category("chef");\n    let cols = 4usize;\n    let rows = (picks.len() + cols - 1) / cols;\n    let _ = rows; // rows is implied by per-col placement below\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.25); // 1 tile = 16 px\n\n    for (k, item) in picks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let col = k % cols;\n        let row = k / cols;\n        let cx = -(cols as f64) * PITCH_X * 0.5 + PITCH_X * 0.5 + (col as f64) * PITCH_X;\n        // row 0 at the top, increasing row = downward (negative y).\n        let cy = 1.0 - (row as f64) * PITCH_Y;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n            bx: cx,\n            by: cy,\n            hx: CARD_HW,\n            hy: CARD_HH,\n            r: 0.18,\n        });\n        // A tiny line "tab" under each card (the price strip) — uses the vendor\n        // item's price presence so the raster differs by content (not just count).\n        if !item.drink_ask {\n            scene.add(SdfShape::LineSegment {\n                ax: cx - CARD_HW * 0.6,\n                ay: cy - CARD_HH - 0.05,\n                bx: cx + CARD_HW * 0.6,\n                by: cy - CARD_HH - 0.05,\n            });\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Cart badge (top-right circle) when cart is non-empty. Kept inside the\n    // visible field window (the canvas samples x ∈ [-W/2·s, +W/2·s)), so a cart\n    // state change shows up as a discrete jump in inside_count + FNV — the\n    // pixel-verify signature distinguishes an empty cart from a non-empty one.\n    if cart_count > 0 {\n        scene.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n            cx: 3.2,\n            cy: 1.6,\n            r: 0.35,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// The owner "dashboard" screen — a header band + N stat tiles (N = number of\n/// vendor categories) + a sidebar. Encodes the vendor's MENU/CATEGORIES counts so\n/// the raster changes when the menu changes (a regression here = a content drift).\npub fn owner_dashboard_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.25);\n    // Header band.\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: 0.0,\n        by: 2.6,\n        hx: 6.0,\n        hy: 0.4,\n        r: 0.1,\n    });\n    // Sidebar.\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: -5.4,\n        by: 0.0,\n        hx: 0.7,\n        hy: 2.2,\n        r: 0.1,\n    });\n    // One stat tile per category (15 tiles laid out 5×3).\n    let cols = 5usize;\n    for (k, _cat) in vendor::CATEGORIES.iter().enumerate() {\n        let col = k % cols;\n        let row = k / cols;\n        let cx = -2.8 + (col as f64) * 1.4;\n        let cy = 1.0 - (row as f64) * 1.4;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n            bx: cx,\n            by: cy,\n            hx: 0.6,\n            hy: 0.5,\n            r: 0.08,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// The courier "board" (tasks) screen — a status pill + a vertical task list (the\n/// active deliveries). Role-stable (same world units as the customer screen) so\n/// the courier render is a tint of the same field.\npub fn courier_board_screen(active_tasks: u32) -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.25);\n    // Status pill (top-centre).\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: 0.0,\n        by: 2.4,\n        hx: 1.5,\n        hy: 0.3,\n        r: 0.28,\n    });\n    let n = active_tasks.min(5);\n    for k in 0..n {\n        let cy = 1.4 - (k as f64) * 0.9;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n            bx: 0.0,\n            by: cy,\n            hx: 4.5,\n            hy: 0.35,\n            r: 0.12,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n// ── S7 per-role sub-screen variants ─────────────────────────────────────────\n//\n// Each of the 30 `.polish/final/` screens gets a layout function here whose\n// signature geometry DIFFERS from the dashboard/board so the pixel-verify harness\n// can distinguish them by FNV digest (not just by role tint). Owner sub-screens\n// share a sidebar (the zero-chrome "one recomposed screen" discipline — they are\n// the dashboard recomposed by intent, NOT different routes), but the main panel\n// shape varies per screen. Courier sub-screens share the status pill.\n\n/// Owner "orders" screen — a full-width order list (one row per order in the\n/// queue). Distinct from the dashboard's category-tile grid: rows are wide &\n/// flat (hx 5.0, hy 0.35), stacked vertically.\npub fn owner_orders_screen(order_count: u32) -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    let n = order_count.min(6);\n    for k in 0..n {\n        let cy = 1.6 - (k as f64) * 0.6;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n            bx: 0.6,\n            by: cy,\n            hx: 5.0,\n            hy: 0.35,\n            r: 0.12,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Owner "menu management" screen — the vendor menu as a dense card grid (one\n/// card per item, 6 cols). Distinct from the customer menu (4 cols) so the count\n/// differs and the raster separates them.\npub fn owner_menu_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    let cols = 6usize;\n    for (k, _item) in vendor::MENU.iter().enumerate() {\n        let col = k % cols;\n        let row = k / cols;\n        let cx = -3.0 + (col as f64) * 1.1;\n        let cy = 1.8 - (row as f64) * 0.5;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n            bx: cx,\n            by: cy,\n            hx: 0.45,\n            hy: 0.18,\n            r: 0.05,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Owner "promotions" screen — a small set of promo cards (3) + a sidebar list.\n/// Distinct geometry: 3 large rounded boxes on the right.\npub fn owner_promotions_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    for k in 0..3 {\n        let cx = 1.5 + (k as f64) * 2.6;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n            bx: cx,\n            by: 0.5,\n            hx: 1.1,\n            hy: 1.4,\n            r: 0.2,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Owner "CRM" screen — a customer table layout: header + 5 rows of 2 columns.\npub fn owner_crm_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    // Header row.\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: 0.6,\n        by: 2.2,\n        hx: 5.0,\n        hy: 0.25,\n        r: 0.08,\n    });\n    for k in 0..5 {\n        let cy = 1.5 - (k as f64) * 0.5;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::LineSegment {\n            ax: -4.0,\n            ay: cy,\n            bx: 5.4,\n            by: cy,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Owner "supplies" screen — an inventory grid (10 small tiles in 5×2).\npub fn owner_supplies_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    for k in 0..10 {\n        let col = k % 5;\n        let row = k / 5;\n        let cx = -2.0 + (col as f64) * 1.0;\n        let cy = 1.0 - (row as f64) * 1.2;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::Box {\n            bx: cx,\n            by: cy,\n            hx: 0.35,\n            hy: 0.4,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Owner "couriers" screen — a list of courier status pills (4 rows).\npub fn owner_couriers_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    for k in 0..4 {\n        let cy = 1.6 - (k as f64) * 0.8;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n            bx: 0.6,\n            by: cy,\n            hx: 5.0,\n            hy: 0.3,\n            r: 0.25,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Owner "analytics" screen — a chart placeholder: axes (2 line segments) + 5\n/// bars (Boxes of varying height). Distinct line+box combination.\npub fn owner_analytics_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    // X + Y axes.\n    scene.add(SdfShape::LineSegment {\n        ax: -3.0,\n        ay: -1.5,\n        bx: 5.0,\n        by: -1.5,\n    });\n    scene.add(SdfShape::LineSegment {\n        ax: -3.0,\n        ay: -1.5,\n        bx: -3.0,\n        by: 2.2,\n    });\n    // 5 bars of varying height.\n    let heights = [0.8, 1.4, 1.0, 1.8, 1.2];\n    for (k, h) in heights.iter().enumerate() {\n        let cx = -2.0 + (k as f64) * 1.4;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::Box {\n            bx: cx,\n            by: -1.5 + h * 0.5,\n            hx: 0.4,\n            hy: *h,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Owner "settings" screen — a 4-row settings list (each row = line + small box).\npub fn owner_settings_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    for k in 0..4 {\n        let cy = 1.4 - (k as f64) * 0.7;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::LineSegment {\n            ax: -3.5,\n            ay: cy,\n            bx: 4.5,\n            by: cy,\n        });\n        scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n            bx: 4.2,\n            by: cy,\n            hx: 0.3,\n            hy: 0.18,\n            r: 0.1,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Owner "branding" screen — a large preview frame + 3 swatch circles (the brand\n/// palette pickers). Distinct: uses Circle shapes (the raster's only circles here).\npub fn owner_branding_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    // Preview frame.\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: -1.5,\n        by: 0.0,\n        hx: 1.8,\n        hy: 2.0,\n        r: 0.15,\n    });\n    // 3 palette swatches (circles — unique to this screen).\n    for (k, cx) in [1.8, 2.8, 3.8].iter().enumerate() {\n        let _ = k;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n            cx: *cx,\n            cy: 0.5,\n            r: 0.4,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Owner "activation" screen — a plan-card (1 large rounded box) + a status pill.\npub fn owner_activation_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = owner_shell();\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: 0.5,\n        by: 0.3,\n        hx: 3.5,\n        hy: 2.2,\n        r: 0.2,\n    });\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: -1.5,\n        by: -2.0,\n        hx: 1.5,\n        hy: 0.3,\n        r: 0.25,\n    });\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Courier "home" screen — the courier_board variant with an online-status pill\n/// and no task rows (the landing state). Distinct from board by the pill position.\npub fn courier_home_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.25);\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: 0.0,\n        by: 1.8,\n        hx: 2.0,\n        hy: 0.4,\n        r: 0.3,\n    });\n    scene.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n        cx: -2.8,\n        cy: 1.8,\n        r: 0.25,\n    }); // online dot\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Courier "shift" screen — a shift timer ring (a large circle outline approximated\n/// by a circle) + a start/stop button box.\npub fn courier_shift_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.25);\n    scene.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n        cx: 0.0,\n        cy: 0.5,\n        r: 2.0,\n    });\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: 0.0,\n        by: -2.2,\n        hx: 1.5,\n        hy: 0.4,\n        r: 0.2,\n    });\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Courier "earnings" screen — a total banner + 3 period bars (day/week/month).\npub fn courier_earnings_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.25);\n    scene.add(SdfShape::RoundedBox {\n        bx: 0.0,\n        by: 2.4,\n        hx: 5.0,\n        hy: 0.35,\n        r: 0.1,\n    });\n    let heights = [0.6, 1.2, 1.8];\n    for (k, h) in heights.iter().enumerate() {\n        let cx = -2.0 + (k as f64) * 2.0;\n        scene.add(SdfShape::Box {\n            bx: cx,\n            by: -0.5 + h * 0.5,\n            hx: 0.7,\n            hy: *h,\n        });\n    }\n    scene\n}\n\n/// Courier "history" screen — a vertical timeline: 6 dots (circles) connected by\n/// a vertical line.\npub fn courier_history_screen() -> Scene {\n    let mut scene = Scene::new().with_scale(0.25);\n    scene.add(SdfShape::LineSegment {\n        ax: 0.0,\n        ay: 2.4,\n        bx: 0.0,\n        by: -2.4,\n    });\n    for k in 0..6 {\n        let cy = 2.0 - ## 1515 · /root/dowiz/engine/src/sdf.rs · LongTerm

Summary: sdf · 237 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/sdf.rs	sdf · 237 lines	//! W3-1 — Field-UI Phase 1 SDF (signed-distance-field) layer.\n//!\n//! UI primitives are fields/SDFs, not DOM. This is the CPU-side signed-distance\n//! toolkit: pure f64/f32 math, zero external deps, offline-clean like the rest\n//! of the engine. Every primitive returns a signed distance (negative = inside,\n//! 0 = on the boundary, positive = outside) so combinators compose like ordinary\n//! scalar fields.\n//!\n//! [`SdfField`] rasterizes an SDF closure onto a flat, row-major `Vec<f32>` grid —\n//! the exact zero-copy shape the rest of the engine uses (see `zerocopy.rs` /\n//! [`crate::VertexBridge`]) — so a raster can be handed to the GPU upload path as\n//! a `&[f32]` with no copy and no JSON.\n//!\n//! Every primitive + combinator carries a falsifiable RED→GREEN gate as a `#[test]`.\n\n/// Signed distance from `(px,py)` to a circle of radius `r` centred at\n/// `(cx,cy)`. Negative inside, 0 on the boundary, positive outside.\n#[inline]\npub fn sdf_circle(px: f64, py: f64, cx: f64, cy: f64, r: f64) -> f64 {\n    let dx = px - cx;\n    let dy = py - cy;\n    (dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt() - r\n}\n\n/// Signed distance from `(px,py)` to an axis-aligned box centred at `(bx,by)`\n/// with half-extents `(hx,hy)`. Negative inside, 0 on the boundary, positive\n/// outside.\n#[inline]\npub fn sdf_box(px: f64, py: f64, bx: f64, by: f64, hx: f64, hy: f64) -> f64 {\n    let qx = (px - bx).abs() - hx;\n    let qy = (py - by).abs() - hy;\n    let outside = (qx.max(0.0)).hypot(qy.max(0.0));\n    let inside = qx.max(qy).min(0.0);\n    outside + inside\n}\n\n/// Signed distance from `(px,py)` to a box (half-extents `hx,hy`) centred at\n/// `(bx,by)` with corner radius `r` (clamped to the smaller half-extent).\n/// Negative inside, 0 on the boundary, positive outside.\n#[inline]\npub fn sdf_rounded_box(px: f64, py: f64, bx: f64, by: f64, hx: f64, hy: f64, r: f64) -> f64 {\n    let r = r.min(hx).min(hy).max(0.0);\n    let qx = (px - bx).abs() - (hx - r);\n    let qy = (py - by).abs() - (hy - r);\n    let outside = (qx.max(0.0)).hypot(qy.max(0.0));\n    let inside = qx.max(qy).min(0.0);\n    outside + inside - r\n}\n\n/// Unsigned distance from `(px,py)` to the line segment from `a` to `b`. A thin\n/// line primitive: distance to the nearest point on the segment (0 = on it).\n#[inline]\npub fn sdf_line_segment(px: f64, py: f64, ax: f64, ay: f64, bx: f64, by: f64) -> f64 {\n    let pax = px - ax;\n    let pay = py - ay;\n    let bax = bx - ax;\n    let bay = by - ay;\n    let h = {\n        let denom = bax * bax + bay * bay;\n        if denom == 0.0 {\n            0.0\n        } else {\n            (pax * bax + pay * bay) / denom\n        }\n    };\n    let h = h.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n    let dx = pax - bax * h;\n    let dy = pay - bay * h;\n    (dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt()\n}\n\n/// Combinator: Boolean UNION of two SDFs = pointwise minimum.\n#[inline]\npub fn op_union(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {\n    a.min(b)\n}\n\n/// Combinator: Boolean INTERSECTION of two SDFs = pointwise maximum.\n#[inline]\npub fn op_intersection(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {\n    a.max(b)\n}\n\n/// Combinator: Boolean SUBTRACTION — keep `a`, remove the interior of `b`.\n/// `a` minus `b` = `max(a, -b)`.\n#[inline]\npub fn op_subtraction(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {\n    a.max(-b)\n}\n\n/// Combinator: smooth (polynomial) UNION via Inigo-Quilez `smin`. Blends two\n/// SDFs within a radius `k` so the seam is rounded. For `k <= 0` this degrades\n/// to the exact [`op_union`] (pointwise min). Result is always `<= min(a,b)`\n/// and continuous in both arguments.\n#[inline]\npub fn op_smooth_union(a: f64, b: f64, k: f64) -> f64 {\n    if k <= 0.0 {\n        return a.min(b);\n    }\n    let h = (0.5 + 0.5 * (b - a) / k).clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n    let blend = b * (1.0 - h) + a * h;\n    blend - k * h * (1.0 - h)\n}\n\n/// A rasterized SDF sampled onto a flat, row-major `f32` grid.\n///\n/// Mirrors the engine's zero-copy contract: samples live in one contiguous\n/// `Vec<f32>` (index = `row * width + col`), and `as_f32()` returns a `&[f32]`\n/// view over those bytes with **no copy** — exactly what\n/// [`crate::VertexBridge`] / [`crate::ParticleBuffer`] upload paths consume.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SdfField {\n    pub width: usize,\n    pub height: usize,\n    data: Vec<f32>,\n}\n\nimpl SdfField {\n    /// Rasterize the SDF closure `f(world_x, world_y) -> distance` over a\n    /// `width × height` grid. Pixel `(col,row)` is sampled at world coordinate\n    /// `(x0 + col*scale, y0 + row*scale)` (row-major, top-left origin). Each\n    /// sample is downcast `f64 → f32`. The loop is bit-deterministic: two calls\n    /// with identical inputs yield identical `Vec<f32>` bytes.\n    pub fn rasterize<F>(width: usize, height: usize, x0: f64, y0: f64, scale: f64, f: F) -> Self\n    where\n        F: Fn(f64, f64) -> f64,\n    {\n        let mut data = vec![0.0f32; width * height];\n        for row in 0..height {\n            let wy = y0 + (row as f64) * scale;\n            for col in 0..width {\n                let wx = x0 + (col as f64) * scale;\n                data[row * width + col] = f(wx, wy) as f32;\n            }\n        }\n        Self {\n            width,\n            height,\n            data,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Zero-copy `&[f32]` view over the raster samples (row-major, length\n    /// `width*height`). This is the slice the GPU upload path consumes.\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn as_f32(&self) -> &[f32] {\n        &self.data\n    }\n\n    /// Total `f32` samples (`width * height`).\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn len_f32(&self) -> usize {\n        self.data.len()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // (1) sdf_circle_sign — inside negative, outside positive, boundary ~0.\n    #[test]\n    fn sdf_circle_sign() {\n        let (cx, cy, r) = (0.0_f64, 0.0, 2.0);\n        let inside = sdf_circle(0.0, 0.0, cx, cy, r);\n        let outside = sdf_circle(3.0, 0.0, cx, cy, r);\n        let boundary = sdf_circle(2.0, 0.0, cx, cy, r);\n        assert!(inside < 0.0, "inside must be negative: {inside}");\n        assert!(outside > 0.0, "outside must be positive: {outside}");\n        assert!(\n            boundary.abs() <= 1e-6,\n            "on boundary must be ~0 within 1e-6: {boundary}"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            (outside - 1.0).abs() <= 1e-9,\n            "outside distance = 1, got {outside}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // (2) sdf_smooth_union_bounds — smin <= both inputs and continuous.\n    #[test]\n    fn sdf_smooth_union_bounds() {\n        let (a, b, k) = (0.0_f64, 4.0, 1.0);\n        let m = op_smooth_union(a, b, k);\n        let eps = 1e-9;\n        assert!(m <= a + eps, "smin must be <= a: {m} vs {a}");\n        assert!(m <= b + eps, "smin must be <= b: {m} vs {b}");\n\n        // Continuity: a tiny perturbation in `a` changes the result by at most\n        // ~2× the perturbation (smin is Lipschitz-2), never a jump.\n        let delta = 1e-6_f64;\n        let m2 = op_smooth_union(a + delta, b, k);\n        assert!(\n            (m2 - m).abs() <= 2.0 * delta + eps,\n            "smin must be continuous in a: |{m2} - {m}|"\n        );\n\n        // k=0 degrades to exact union (pointwise min).\n        assert_eq!(op_smooth_union(a, b, 0.0), a.min(b));\n    }\n\n    // (3) sdf_raster_deterministic — same scene twice ⇒ bit-identical Vec<f32>.\n    #[test]\n    fn sdf_raster_deterministic() {\n        fn scene(wx: f64, wy: f64) -> f64 {\n            let c = sdf_circle(wx, wy, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0);\n            let bx = sdf_box(wx, wy, 3.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0);\n            op_union(c, bx)\n        }\n        let g1 = SdfField::rasterize(16, 12, -6.0, -6.0, 1.0, scene);\n        let g2 = SdfField::rasterize(16, 12, -6.0, -6.0, 1.0, scene);\n\n        assert_eq!(g1.as_f32(), g2.as_f32(), "raster must be bit-identical");\n        for (x, y) in g1.as_f32().iter().zip(g2.as_f32().iter()) {\n            assert_eq!(x.to_bits(), y.to_bits(), "raster bytes must match");\n        }\n        assert_eq!(g1.len_f32(), 16 * 12);\n    }\n\n    // (4) sdf_box_exact — known distances to an axis-aligned box match\n    //     hand-computed values (centre (0,0), half-extents (2,1)).\n    #[test]\n    fn sdf_box_exact() {\n        let (bx, by, hx, hy) = (0.0_f64, 0.0, 2.0, 1.0);\n        let eps = 1e-9;\n        // Centre: 1 unit inside (from the top edge at y = 1).\n        assert!((sdf_box(0.0, 0.0, bx, by, hx, hy) - (-1.0)).abs() <= eps);\n        // 1 unit right of the right edge (x = 2).\n        assert!((sdf_box(3.0, 0.0, bx, by, hx, hy) - 1.0).abs() <= eps);\n        // Outside corner (3,2): distance from box corner (2,1) = √2.\n        assert!((sdf_box(3.0, 2.0, bx, by, hx, hy) - std::f64::consts::SQRT_2).abs() <= eps);\n        // Above the top edge by 1 (point (0,2)): distance 1.\n        assert!((sdf_box(0.0, 2.0, bx, by, hx, hy) - 1.0).abs() <= eps);\n        // On the right edge: exactly 0.\n        assert!(sdf_box(2.0, 0.0, bx, by, hx, hy).abs() <= eps);\n    }\n}\n	1516	-1	-1		1b36b66c90efa3b5498bbac33b1a1a216116976cac72f56ce54ce2d8bded402b118446c0efdf80af815e572390e8fb209e653964606889a8e2eaf683dfb4ea44ebcc54f90f1a787911db180bd72ba8c095f0c87e29954ff8982202b650073764c470f2c4f0c3534ff9a88f0504d8ed996c9d4d76bd93daf4d3e9c4f32b042930

We vary it as a free value.\n        let _brand_a = [0u8; 20];\n        let _brand_b = [255u8; 20];\n        // "view/projection matrix" — likewise external to `mirror`.\n        let _m_ortho = [[1.0f32; 4]; 4];\n        let _m_persp = [[0.5f32; 4]; 4];\n        // "render floor" — WebGPU / WebGL2 / CPU.\n        let _floor_a = "webgpu";\n        let _floor_b = "cpu";\n\n        let t_brand_a = mirror(&s).unwrap();\n        let t_brand_b = mirror(&s).unwrap();\n        let t_floor = mirror(&s).unwrap();\n        let _ = (_brand_a, _brand_b, _m_ortho, _m_persp, _floor_a, _floor_b);\n        assert_eq!(t_brand_a, t_brand_b);\n        assert_eq!(t_brand_a, t_floor, "render floor must not alter the tree");\n    }\n\n    // M2 interim trigger — `tree_hash` changes only when the tree changes, so\n    // the web mirror reconciles on hash change (pre-FE-14-settle).\n    #[test]\n    fn tree_hash_changes_only_on_change() {\n        let s = scene();\n        let t = mirror(&s).unwrap();\n        let h1 = tree_hash(&t);\n        let h2 = tree_hash(&t);\n        assert_eq!(h1, h2, "same tree ⇒ same hash");\n\n        let mut s2 = s.clone();\n        s2.nodes[2].state.value_text = Some("SHIPPED".into());\n        let h3 = tree_hash(&mirror(&s2).unwrap());\n        assert_ne!(h1, h3, "state change must change the hash");\n    }\n\n    // M1/M2 — `tree_hash` is presentation-independent: byte-identical trees hash\n    //         identically (the "reconcile only on change" trigger is sound).\n    #[test]\n    fn tree_hash_is_stable_for_identical_trees() {\n        let t = mirror(&scene()).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(tree_hash(&t), tree_hash(&t));\n    }\n}\n	1559	-1	-1		5b773dd6958903366001aac19f121b0f40d6a5e5b870b4cfe966684991afe6631c40318acfd66c0e8f4000eba195d1388e554d6471680ae9b16f7a0fe50e38ec6caa54f96d1b921b1459a90a77bae11061719c6a2913db3dd4c2b084780b17a661a7f7b6b3eb12b19e09ee0c93582395c0ff412ebf8180d2819df4df6fa424a1

## 1644 · /root/dowiz/engine/src/text_input/field.rs · LongTerm

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/text_input/field.rs	field · 1076 lines	//! P57 M2/M3/M4/M5(caret) — the in-canvas text editor (Lane A: offline-clean,\n//! always built) + the closed `EditCmd` alphabet + clipboard/keyboard ports.\n//!\n//! This module is the **engine-owned event surface**. The buffer, caret and\n//! selection live here as UTF-8 **byte** offsets (never char indices — byte\n//! offsets are the only run-stable index for grapheme-aware motion, §3). Every\n//! mutation funnels through [`TextField::apply`], which returns the ordered\n//! [`EditEvent`] sequence the a11y mirror AND the render both consume (one\n//! source ⇒ mirror caret == rendered caret by construction, §4.6).\n//!\n//! **Lane A (this file):** the full editor is implemented on a plain `String`\n//! buffer with dependency-free grapheme/word motion (combining-mark clustering\n//! + whitespace word boundaries, correct for Wave-0 Latin+Cyrillic). It is\n//! exercisable and testable with ZERO external crates.\n//!\n//! **Lane B (`./cosmic_text.rs`, `feature = "text"`):** the *shaping* leg —\n//! glyph runs, exact caret/selection metrics, pointer hit-test — is cosmic-text's\n//! authority. It is gated behind the same O18a network grant as wgpu (§3/§11):\n//! the `text` feature is OFF by default, so the default build links no\n//! `cosmic-text` and this file is the whole editor. `cargo build` with\n//! `--features text` requires the operator's network grant (the same one that\n//! unlocks `gpu`); until then Lane B compiles OFF.\n\nuse crate::motion::Spring;\nuse crate::text_scope::in_wave0_scope;\n\n/// Widget identifier — matches `WidgetStore::id` (u32). A `TextField` is\n/// node-local to one widget.\npub type WidgetId = u32;\n\n/// A UTF-8 **byte** offset into the buffer. NEVER a char index — byte offsets\n/// are the only stable cross-run index for grapheme-aware motion (cosmic-text's\n/// `Cursor` is byte-based, §3).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub struct ByteCursor(pub usize);\n\n/// An ordered selection: [anchor, focus] in byte offsets. `focus` is the live\n/// caret; it may be < or > anchor. Collapsed (anchor == focus) ⇒ no selection,\n/// just a caret.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub struct Selection {\n    pub anchor: ByteCursor,\n    pub focus: ByteCursor,\n}\n\n/// 3D field position (P38 §12.2-2): `w` is carried, never truncated. A pointer\n/// hit-test reports a `FieldPos`; the editor maps it to a byte caret.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct FieldPos {\n    pub u: f32,\n    pub v: f32,\n    pub w: f32,\n}\n\n/// Caret / selection geometry in FIELD space (u,v,w — w carried, never\n/// truncated; P38 §12.2-2). `h_w`/`h_h` are half-extents.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]\npub struct Rect {\n    pub u: f32,\n    pub v: f32,\n    pub w: f32,\n    pub h_w: f32,\n    pub h_h: f32,\n}\n\n/// One shaped glyph, already mapped to an FE-06 atlas slot — the ONLY bridge to\n/// the render (Lane B populates this via cosmic-text; Lane A leaves it empty).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]\npub struct ShapedGlyph {\n    pub atlas_id: u32,\n    pub pos: FieldPos,\n    pub adv: f32,\n    pub size: f32,\n}\n\n/// The CLOSED editing alphabet — every keydown / pointer / clipboard action\n/// normalizes to ONE of these (standard item 3: tests assert on sequences of\n/// these, not end-state). There is NO preedit/composition variant: Latin+Cyrillic\n/// commit directly (X2). `select` = extend-selection.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub enum EditCmd {\n    Insert(String), // committed grapheme cluster(s) only\n    Backspace,\n    Delete,\n    MoveLeft { select: bool },\n    MoveRight { select: bool },\n    MoveWordLeft { select: bool },\n    MoveWordRight { select: bool },\n    MoveHome { select: bool },\n    MoveEnd { select: bool },\n    SelectAll,\n    Cut,\n    Copy,\n    Paste(String), // Paste payload arrives pre-read via ClipboardPort\n    PointerDown(FieldPos),\n    PointerDrag(FieldPos),\n    PointerUp,\n    Focus,\n    Blur,\n    Submit, // Enter/commit intent — the CONSUMER decides meaning\n}\n\n/// What changed after `apply` — the event the a11y mirror AND the render both\n/// consume (one source).\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub enum EditEvent {\n    TextChanged { value_bytes: usize },\n    CaretMoved { caret: ByteCursor },\n    SelectionChanged { sel: Selection },\n    Submitted,\n    FocusChanged { focused: bool },\n    Rejected(EditReject),\n}\n\n/// Typed refusal — NEVER a silent drop (self-termination leg, §5.4).\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub enum EditReject {\n    OutOfScope(char),\n    ReadOnly,\n    NothingToDelete,\n    NoSelection,\n}\n\n/// Clipboard is a PORT, not a hard dep (R3's "a port retrofitted is not a\n/// port"): native via the shell (P39-rev/P63), web via `navigator.clipboard`.\npub trait ClipboardPort {\n    fn read(&mut self) -> Option<String>;\n    fn write(&mut self, s: &str);\n}\n\n/// Keyboard modifier state passed to [`key_to_cmd`]. Mirrors the bits a\n/// `KeyboardSource` (native winit / web canvas) extracts from an event.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]\npub struct KeyMods {\n    pub ctrl: bool,\n    pub meta: bool,\n    pub shift: bool,\n    pub alt: bool,\n}\n\n/// Caret blink frequency (Hz) — 1 Hz on/off, a localized alpha toggle, NOT a\n/// field wake (§4.5 / §5.1 battery invariant).\npub const CARET_BLINK_HZ: f32 = 1.0;\n/// Caret bar half-width in field units (sdf_line_segment).\npub const CARET_BAR_HALF_W: f32 = 0.5;\n/// Wave-0 single-line field cap (bytes). Scaling axis: a multi-line paragraph\n/// editor is v2 (§5.2).\npub const FIELD_MAX_BYTES: usize = 4096;\n/// cosmic-text word-motion authority — never re-derived (§3).\npub const WORD_BOUNDARY: &str = "unicode-word";\n\n// ── Lane A shaping constants (approximation; Lane B overrides via cosmic) ──\nconst GLYPH_ADVANCE: f32 = 1.0; // field units per Latin/Cyrillic cell\nconst GLYPH_HEIGHT: f32 = 1.0;\n\n/// One editable text field. Lane A owns the buffer/caret/selection/clipboard\n/// event surface on a plain `String`; the cosmic-text shaping seam (Lane B) is a\n/// separate wrapper (`./cosmic_text.rs`) that maps `value()` into real glyph\n/// runs without changing this struct's offline-clean build.\npub struct TextField {\n    field_id: WidgetId,\n    buf: String,\n    caret: usize,  // byte offset == focus\n    anchor: usize, // byte offset (selection anchor)\n    focused: bool,\n    read_only: bool,\n    // Caret blink/fade: a localized alpha Spring. tick_caret mutates ONLY this;\n    // it never touches buf/caret, so the field integrator is NOT woken (§5.1).\n    caret_alpha: Spring,\n    blink_phase: f32,\n    // Glyph runs: populated by Lane B (cosmic). Empty under Lane A.\n    glyph_runs: Vec<ShapedGlyph>,\n}\n\nimpl TextField {\n    /// New editable field for `field_id`.\n    pub fn new(field_id: WidgetId) -> Self {\n        TextField {\n            field_id,\n            buf: String::new(),\n            caret: 0,\n            anchor: 0,\n            focused: false,\n            read_only: false,\n            caret_alpha: Spring::snappy(0.0),\n            blink_phase: 0.0,\n            glyph_runs: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// New read-only field (a label-style display; never accepts edits).\n    pub fn read_only(field_id: WidgetId) -> Self {\n        let mut t = TextField::new(field_id);\n        t.read_only = true;\n        t\n    }\n\n    /// The ONLY mutator of buffer/caret/selection state. Returns the ordered\n    /// events it produced (possibly empty).\n    pub fn apply(&mut self, cmd: EditCmd, clip: &mut dyn ClipboardPort) -> Vec<EditEvent> {\n        let mut ev = Vec::new();\n        match cmd {\n            EditCmd::Insert(s) => self.ins(&s, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::Backspace => self.backspace(&mut ev),\n            EditCmd::Delete => self.delete(&mut ev),\n            EditCmd::MoveLeft { select } => self.move_by(-1, select, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::MoveRight { select } => self.move_by(1, select, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::MoveWordLeft { select } => self.move_word(-1, select, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::MoveWordRight { select } => self.move_word(1, select, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::MoveHome { select } => self.move_edge(false, select, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::MoveEnd { select } => self.move_edge(true, select, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::SelectAll => self.select_all(&mut ev),\n            EditCmd::Cut => self.cut(clip, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::Copy => self.copy(clip, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::Paste(s) => self.paste(&s, clip, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::PointerDown(p) => self.pointer_down(p, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::PointerDrag(p) => self.pointer_drag(p, &mut ev),\n            EditCmd::PointerUp => { /* finalize: selection already set */ }\n            EditCmd::Focus => {\n                self.focused = true;\n                // (re)start blink from phase 0 so a freshly-focused field blinks.\n                self.blink_phase = 0.0;\n                ev.push(EditEvent::FocusChanged { focused: true });\n            }\n            EditCmd::Blur => {\n                if self.focused {\n                    self.focused = false;\n                    ev.push(EditEvent::FocusChanged { focused: false });\n                }\n            }\n            EditCmd::Submit => ev.push(EditEvent::Submitted),\n        }\n        ev\n    }\n\n    /// Current buffer value (for P66 snapshot / consumer submit).\n    pub fn value(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.buf\n    }\n\n    /// Byte length of the UTF-8 text. Invariant.\n    pub fn value_bytes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.buf.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Current caret byte position (read-only view of the editor cursor).\n    pub fn caret(&self) -> ByteCursor {\n        ByteCursor(self.caret)\n    }\n\n    /// Restore / prefill value (P66 restore). Scope-gated: out-of-scope\n    /// codepoints are dropped, and the result is truncated to `FIELD_MAX_BYTES`\n    /// at a char boundary (no partial grapheme). Does NOT emit events — the\n    /// consumer re-syncs the mirror/render from `value()` after a restore.\n    pub fn set_value(&mut self, s: &str) {\n        let filtered: String = s.chars().filter(|c| in_wave0_scope(*c)).collect();\n        let truncated = truncate_bytes(&filtered, FIELD_MAX_BYTES);\n        self.buf = truncated;\n        self.caret = self.buf.len();\n        self.anchor = self.caret;\n    }\n\n    /// Current selection (anchor, focus) as byte offsets.\n    pub fn selection(&self) -> Selection {\n        Selection {\n            anchor: ByteCursor(self.anchor),\n            focus: ByteCursor(self.caret),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Caret geometry in FIELD space. Lane A approximation: the caret sits at\n    /// `n_chars_before_caret * GLYPH_ADVANCE`. Lane B (cosmic) overrides this\n    /// with real shaped metrics (`./cosmic_text.rs`).\n    pub fn caret_rect(&self) -> Rect {\n        let n_before = self.buf[..self.caret].chars().count() as f32;\n        Rect {\n            u: n_before * GLYPH_ADVANCE,\n            v: 0.0,\n            w: CARET_BAR_HALF_W * 2.0,\n            h_w: 0.0,\n            h_h: GLYPH_HEIGHT / 2.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// One selection rect per visual run (single-line Wave-0 ⇒ exactly one).\n    /// Lane A spans from the selection start char to the end char.\n    pub fn selection_rects(&self) -> Vec<Rect> {\n        let (a, b) = self.ordered();\n        if a == b {\n            return Vec::new(); // collapsed ⇒ no selection rect\n        }\n        let n_a = self.buf[..a].chars().count() as f32;\n        let n_b = self.buf[..b].chars().count() as f32;\n        vec![Rect {\n            u: n_a * GLYPH_ADVANCE,\n            v: 0.0,\n            w: (n_b - n_a) * GLYPH_ADVANCE,\n            h_w: 0.0,\n            h_h: GLYPH_HEIGHT / 2.0,\n        }]\n    }\n\n    /// Glyph runs for the FE-06 MSDF pipeline. Empty under Lane A; populated by\n    /// the cosmic-text shaping seam (`./cosmic_text.rs`) under `feature =\n    /// "text"`.\n    pub fn glyph_runs(&self) -> &[ShapedGlyph] {\n        &self.glyph_runs\n    }\n\n    /// Advance the caret blink/fade by `dt`. Returns `true` iff ONLY the caret\n    /// alpha changed — so the field integrator is NOT woken (§5.1 battery\n    /// invariant). Blink is a localized alpha toggle; it never mutates buf/caret.\n    pub fn tick_caret(&mut self, dt: f32) -> bool {\n        self.blink_phase += dt * CARET_BLINK_HZ;\n        if self.blink_phase >= 1.0 {\n            self.blink_phase -= 1.0;\n        }\n        let blink_on = self.blink_phase < 0.5; // 1 Hz square: on half, off half\n        let target = if self.focused && blink_on { 1.0 } else { 0.0 };\n        self.caret_alpha.target = target;\n        self.caret_alpha.step(dt);\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// Current caret alpha (0..1) — the render reads this; it animates without\n    /// waking the field (§5.1).\n    pub fn caret_alpha(&self) -> f32 {\n        self.caret_alpha.x\n    }\n\n    // ── internals ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    fn ordered(&self) -> (usize, usize) {\n        if self.anchor <= self.caret {\n            (self.anchor, self.caret)\n        } else {\n            (self.caret, self.anchor)\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn selection_text(&self) -> String {\n        let (a, b) = self.ordered();\n        self.buf[a..b].to_string()\n    }\n\n    /// Insert a string through the scope gate. A typed `Insert` carrying ANY\n    /// out-of-scope codepoint is refused wholesale (Rejected(OutOfScope)) — the\n    /// buffer is untouched. Capacity is enforced (no partial grapheme at the cap).\n    fn ins(&mut self, s: &str, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        if self.read_only {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::ReadOnly));\n            return;\n        }\n        // Scope gate (the v2 boundary as a choke point, §5.1).\n        if let Some(bad) = s.chars().find(|c| !in_wave0_scope(*c)) {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::OutOfScope(bad)));\n            return;\n        }\n        // Capacity (no partial grapheme at the cap, §4.2 adversarial).\n        let room = FIELD_MAX_BYTES.saturating_sub(self.buf.len());\n        if room == 0 {\n            return; // full: refuse (caret unchanged)\n        }\n        let insert = truncate_bytes(s, room);\n        // `insert` is a char-prefix of `s` (truncate_bytes keeps char\n        // boundaries), so it contains no out-of-scope char (gate already passed).\n        let at = self.caret;\n        self.buf.insert_str(at, &insert);\n        self.caret = at + insert.len();\n        self.anchor = self.caret; // collapsed selection after insert\n        ev.push(EditEvent::TextChanged {\n            value_bytes: self.buf.len(),\n        });\n        ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n            caret: ByteCursor(self.caret),\n        });\n    }\n\n    fn backspace(&mut self, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        if self.read_only {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::ReadOnly));\n            return;\n        }\n        let (a, b) = self.ordered();\n        if a != b {\n            // delete the selection\n            self.buf.replace_range(a..b, "");\n            self.caret = a;\n            self.anchor = a;\n            ev.push(EditEvent::TextChanged {\n                value_bytes: self.buf.len(),\n            });\n            ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n                caret: ByteCursor(self.caret),\n            });\n            return;\n        }\n        if self.caret == 0 {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::NothingToDelete));\n            return;\n        }\n        let start = grapheme_prev(&self.buf, self.caret);\n        self.buf.replace_range(start..self.caret, "");\n        self.caret = start;\n        self.anchor = start;\n        ev.push(EditEvent::TextChanged {\n            value_bytes: self.buf.len(),\n        });\n        ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n            caret: ByteCursor(self.caret),\n        });\n    }\n\n    fn delete(&mut self, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        if self.read_only {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::ReadOnly));\n            return;\n        }\n        let (a, b) = self.ordered();\n        if a != b {\n            self.buf.replace_range(a..b, "");\n            self.caret = a;\n            self.anchor = a;\n            ev.push(EditEvent::TextChanged {\n                value_bytes: self.buf.len(),\n            });\n            ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n                caret: ByteCursor(self.caret),\n            });\n            return;\n        }\n        if self.caret >= self.buf.len() {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::NothingToDelete));\n            return;\n        }\n        let end = grapheme_next(&self.buf, self.caret);\n        self.buf.replace_range(self.caret..end, "");\n        // caret unchanged (deletes right)\n        ev.push(EditEvent::TextChanged {\n            value_bytes: self.buf.len(),\n        });\n        ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n            caret: ByteCursor(self.caret),\n        });\n    }\n\n    fn move_by(&mut self, dir: i32, select: bool, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        let new = if dir < 0 {\n            grapheme_prev(&self.buf, self.caret)\n        } else {\n            grapheme_next(&self.buf, self.caret)\n        };\n        self.caret = new;\n        if !select {\n            self.anchor = new; // collapse\n            ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n                caret: ByteCursor(new),\n            });\n        } else {\n            // real selection (anchor != focus) ⇒ surface it too\n            ev.push(EditEvent::SelectionChanged {\n                sel: self.selection(),\n            });\n            ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n                caret: ByteCursor(new),\n            });\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn move_word(&mut self, dir: i32, select: bool, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        let new = if dir < 0 {\n            word_prev(&self.buf, self.caret)\n        } else {\n            word_next(&self.buf, self.caret)\n        };\n        self.caret = new;\n        if !select {\n            self.anchor = new;\n            ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n                caret: ByteCursor(new),\n            });\n        } else {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::SelectionChanged {\n                sel: self.selection(),\n            });\n            ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n                caret: ByteCursor(new),\n            });\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn move_edge(&mut self, end: bool, select: bool, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        let new = if end { self.buf.len() } else { 0 };\n        self.caret = new;\n        if !select {\n            self.anchor = new;\n            ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n                caret: ByteCursor(new),\n            });\n        } else {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::SelectionChanged {\n                sel: self.selection(),\n            });\n            ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n                caret: ByteCursor(new),\n            });\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn select_all(&mut self, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        self.anchor = 0;\n        self.caret = self.buf.len();\n        ev.push(EditEvent::SelectionChanged {\n            sel: self.selection(),\n        });\n        ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n            caret: ByteCursor(self.caret),\n        });\n    }\n\n    fn copy(&self, clip: &mut dyn ClipboardPort, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        let (a, b) = self.ordered();\n        if a == b {\n            // nothing selected — no-op (Copy leaves buffer, emits nothing).\n            let _ = ev;\n            return;\n        }\n        clip.write(&self.selection_text());\n    }\n\n    fn cut(&mut self, clip: &mut dyn ClipboardPort, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        if self.read_only {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::ReadOnly));\n            return;\n        }\n        let (a, b) = self.ordered();\n        if a == b {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::NoSelection));\n            return;\n        }\n        clip.write(&self.selection_text());\n        self.buf.replace_range(a..b, "");\n        self.caret = a;\n        self.anchor = a;\n        ev.push(EditEvent::TextChanged {\n            value_bytes: self.buf.len(),\n        });\n        ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n            caret: ByteCursor(self.caret),\n        });\n    }\n\n    fn paste(&mut self, s: &str, clip: &mut dyn ClipboardPort, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        if self.read_only {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::ReadOnly));\n            return;\n        }\n        // Read the payload through the port (the web path pre-reads via\n        // navigator.clipboard; here we accept the passed string OR fall back to\n        // the port). The scope gate is applied per-codepoint (§4.2): the\n        // Latin remainder of a mixed paste inserts; each out-of-scope char\n        // surfaces a Rejected(OutOfScope).\n        let payload = if s.is_empty() {\n            clip.read().unwrap_or_default()\n        } else {\n            s.to_string()\n        };\n        let (filtered, oos): (String, Vec<char>) =\n            payload\n                .chars()\n                .fold((String::new(), Vec::new()), |(mut ok, mut bad), c| {\n                    if in_wave0_scope(c) {\n                        ok.push(c);\n                    } else {\n                        bad.push(c);\n                    }\n                    (ok, bad)\n                });\n        for bad in &oos {\n            ev.push(EditEvent::Rejected(EditReject::OutOfScope(*bad)));\n        }\n        if filtered.is_empty() {\n            return; // nothing insertable\n        }\n        // If there is a live selection, replace it first.\n        let (a, b) = self.ordered();\n        if a != b {\n            self.buf.replace_range(a..b, "");\n            self.caret = a;\n        }\n        // Capacity: insert the char-prefix that fits (no partial grapheme).\n        let room = FIELD_MAX_BYTES.saturating_sub(self.buf.len());\n        let insert = truncate_bytes(&filtered, room);\n        let at = self.caret;\n        self.buf.insert_str(at, &insert);\n        self.caret = at + insert.len();\n        self.anchor = self.caret;\n        ev.push(EditEvent::TextChanged {\n            value_bytes: self.buf.len(),\n        });\n        ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n            caret: ByteCursor(self.caret),\n        });\n    }\n\n    fn pointer_down(&mut self, p: FieldPos, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        let byte = self.hit_test(p);\n        self.caret = byte;\n        self.anchor = byte;\n        ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n            caret: ByteCursor(byte),\n        });\n    }\n\n    fn pointer_drag(&mut self, p: FieldPos, ev: &mut Vec<EditEvent>) {\n        let byte = self.hit_test(p);\n        self.caret = byte;\n        ev.push(EditEvent::SelectionChanged {\n            sel: self.selection(),\n        });\n        ev.push(EditEvent::CaretMoved {\n            caret: ByteCursor(byte),\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// Lane A hit-test: `u` in [0,1] field space → char index → byte. Lane B\n    /// (cosmic) replaces this with real shaped metrics.\n    fn hit_test(&self, p: FieldPos) -> usize {\n        let n = self.buf.chars().count();\n        if n == 0 {\n            return 0;\n        }\n        let frac = p.u.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n        let idx = (frac * n as f32).round() as usize;\n        self.buf\n            .char_indices()\n            .nth(idx.min(n.saturating_sub(1)))\n            .map(|(b, _)| b)\n            .unwrap_or(self.buf.len())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Truncate `s` to at most `max` **bytes** at a char boundary (never splits a\n/// UTF-8 codepoint → no partial grapheme at the cap).\nfn truncate_bytes(s: &str, max: usize) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= max {\n        return s.to_string();\n    }\n    // Find the largest char boundary ≤ max.\n    let mut i = max;\n    while i > 0 && !s.is_char_boundary(i) {\n        i -= 1;\n    }\n    s[..i].to_string()\n}\n\n/// True iff `c` is a Unicode combining mark (Mn/Mc ranges). Used to cluster a\n/// base + trailing marks into ONE grapheme for backspace/delete (Wave-0 Latin+\n/// Cyrillic; precomposed forms are preferred, but base+mark sequences still\n/// delete as a unit). Lane B (cosmic) supplies the authoritative grapheme\n/// segmentation — this is the offline-correct approximation.\nfn is_combining(c: char) -> bool {\n    let u = c as u32;\n    (0x0300..=0x036F).contains(&u)      // Combining Diacritical Marks\n        || (0x1AB0..=0x1AFF).contains(&u) // Combining Diacritical Marks Extended\n        || (0x1DC0..=0x1DFF).contains(&u) // Combining Diacritical Marks Supplement\n        || (0x20D0..=0x20FF).contains(&u) // Combining Marks for Symbols\n        || (0xFE20..=0xFE2F).contains(&u) // Combining Half Marks\n}\n\nfn prev_char_boundary(s: &str, pos: usize) -> usize {\n    if pos == 0 {\n        return 0;\n    }\n    let mut i = pos - 1;\n    while i > 0 && !s.is_char_boundary(i) {\n        i -= 1;\n    }\n    i\n}\n\nfn next_char_boundary(s: &str, pos: usize) -> usize {\n    let mut i = pos + 1;\n    while i < s.len() && !s.is_char_boundary(i) {\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    i.min(s.len())\n}\n\nfn char_at(s: &str, pos: usize) -> char {\n    s[pos..].chars().next().unwrap()\n}\n\n/// Start byte of the grapheme ending just left of `caret` (for Backspace).\nfn grapheme_prev(s: &str, caret: usize) -> usize {\n    let mut p = prev_char_boundary(s, caret);\n    while p > 0 {\n        let ch = char_at(s, p);\n        if is_combining(ch) {\n            p = prev_char_boundary(s, p);\n        } else {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    p\n}\n\n/// End byte of the grapheme starting just right of `caret` (for Delete).\nfn grapheme_next(s: &str, caret: usize) -> usize {\n    let mut n = next_char_boundary(s, caret);\n    while n < s.len() {\n        let ch = char_at(s, n);\n        if is_combining(ch) {\n            n = next_char_boundary(s, n);\n        } else {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    n\n}\n\nfn is_word_char(c: char) -> bool {\n    c.is_alphanumeric() // includes Cyrillic letters\n}\n\nfn word_prev(s: &str, caret: usize) -> usize {\n    let mut p = caret;\n    while p > 0 {\n        let c = char_at(s, prev_char_boundary(s, p));\n        if is_word_char(c) {\n            break;\n        }\n        p = prev_char_boundary(s, p);\n    }\n    while p > 0 {\n        let c = char_at(s, prev_char_boundary(s, p));\n        if !is_word_char(c) {\n            break;\n        }\n        p = prev_char_boundary(s, p);\n    }\n    p\n}\n\nfn word_next(s: &str, caret: usize) -> usize {\n    let mut n = caret;\n    let len = s.len();\n    while n < len {\n        let c = char_at(s, n);\n        if !is_word_char(c) {\n            break;\n        }\n k.chars().next().unwrap();\n            if !c.is_control() {\n                Some(EditCmd::Insert(k.to_string()))\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    struct MemClip {\n        s: Option<String>,\n    }\n    impl ClipboardPort for MemClip {\n        fn read(&mut self) -> 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/text_scope.rs	text_scope · 160 lines	//! P57 M1 — Latin + Cyrillic script scope classifier (Lane A, pure, offline-clean).\n//!\n//! RED→GREEN GATE (per blueprint §4.1): the Wave-0 script scope is\n//! **Latin + Cyrillic ONLY**. This module is the *mechanism* that makes\n//! "non-Latin scripts deferred to v2" a **tested refusal**, not a prose\n//! promise. It classifies **codepoints**, never shaped runs — grapheme\n//! clustering is cosmic-text's authority (P57 §1.2 ad-fontes line), this\n//! module owns only the v2 scope gate.\n//!\n//! The boundary is drawn at the **Unicode block**, not the glyph shape: a\n//! Cyrillic homoglyph (`а` U+0430) is IN scope, a Greek look-alike\n//! (`α` U+03B1) is OUT. Dead-key / precomposed Latin (é, ï, ї) lands\n//! inside Latin-1/Extended-A/B. Combining marks (U+0300..U+036F) are IN\n//! so composed Latin sequences cluster correctly; control / zero-width\n//! codepoints (U+200B, U+0000) are OUT and must never reach the buffer.\n\n/// Wave-0 script scope label — the only scripts P57 edits.\npub const WAVE0_SCRIPTS: &str = "Latin+Cyrillic";\n\n/// True iff `c` is inside Wave-0 editing scope (Latin + Cyrillic + the\n/// always-allowed structural set: ASCII space, common punctuation, digits).\n///\n/// Everything else — CJK, Arabic, Thai, Indic, Greek, emoji, control,\n/// zero-width — is **OUT** (v2, §2 anti-scope). The classifier is a hard\n/// choke-point: every insert path (Insert / Paste / Ime::Commit / keydown)\n/// funnels through [`crate::text_input::in_wave0_scope`] which calls this.\npub fn in_wave0_scope(c: char) -> bool {\n    let u = c as u32;\n    // ── always-allowed structural set ────────────────────────────────\n    // ASCII control range: only TAB + LF are acceptable whitespace; NUL and\n    // the rest are rejected (U+0000 is explicitly OutOfScope per §4.1).\n    if u < 0x20 {\n        return u == 0x09 || u == 0x0A; // \\t, \\n\n    }\n    if u == 0x7F {\n        return false; // DEL\n    }\n    // ── Latin ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // Basic Latin\n    if u <= 0x007F {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // Latin-1 Supplement (includes precomposed Latin: é è ñ ï … and ¡ ¢ etc.)\n    if (0x0080..=0x00FF).contains(&u) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // Latin Extended-A\n    if (0x0100..=0x017F).contains(&u) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // Latin Extended-B\n    if (0x0180..=0x024F).contains(&u) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // Combining Diacritical Marks — Latin-composable (precomposed preferred,\n    // but the marks themselves are in-scope so a base+mark clusters as one).\n    if (0x0300..=0x036F).contains(&u) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // General Punctuation (em/en dash, curly quotes, ellipsis, …) — script-\n    // agnostic "common punctuation" the spec lists as in-scope (`—`, `…`).\n    // Excludes the zero-width controls (ZWSP/ZWJ/ZWNJ) which are rejected\n    // as OutOfScope (§4.1: never inserted).\n    if (0x2000..=0x206F).contains(&u) {\n        return u != 0x200B && u != 0x200C && u != 0x200D;\n    }\n    // ── Cyrillic ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // Cyrillic\n    if (0x0400..=0x04FF).contains(&u) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // Cyrillic Supplement\n    if (0x0500..=0x052F).contains(&u) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // ── everything else is v2 (CJK, Arabic, Thai, Indic, Greek, emoji,\n    //     zero-width, etc.) ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convenience: a whole string is in scope iff **every** codepoint is.\n/// Used by `Paste` / `set_value` to apply the gate per-codepoint.\npub fn str_in_scope(s: &str) -> bool {\n    s.chars().all(in_wave0_scope)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // RED→GREEN (§4.1): Latin + Cyrillic + structural all accepted.\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_accepts_latin_cyrillic() {\n        for c in ['a', 'Z', '0', ' ', '—', 'é', 'ï'] {\n            assert!(in_wave0_scope(c), "{c:?} must be in Wave-0 scope");\n        }\n        // Cyrillic first-class, not a fallback.\n        for c in ['ё', 'Я', 'ї', 'ґ'] {\n            assert!(\n                in_wave0_scope(c),\n                "{c:?} (U+{:04X}) must be in scope",\n                c as u32\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // RED→GREEN (§4.1): v2 scripts explicitly rejected.\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_rejects_v2_scripts() {\n        for c in ['中', 'あ', 'ا', 'ก', '😀'] {\n            assert!(\n                !in_wave0_scope(c),\n                "{c:?} (U+{:04X}) must be OUT of scope",\n                c as u32\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ADVERSARIAL (§4.1 homoglyph trap): the boundary is the BLOCK, not the\n    // glyph. Cyrillic `а` (U+0430) is IN; Latin `a` (U+0061) is IN; Greek\n    // `α` (U+03B1) is OUT. Asserting the Greek letter is refused pins the\n    // line at Unicode blocks, defeating any shape-based bypass.\n    #[test]\n    fn homoglyph_trap_block_not_glyph() {\n        let cyr_a = 'а'; // U+0430 Cyrillic small a\n        let lat_a = 'a'; // U+0061 Latin small a\n        let grk_a = 'α'; // U+03B1 Greek small alpha\n        assert_ne!(cyr_a as u32, lat_a as u32);\n        assert!(in_wave0_scope(cyr_a), "Cyrillic homoglyph IN");\n        assert!(in_wave0_scope(lat_a), "Latin a IN");\n        assert!(\n            !in_wave0_scope(grk_a),\n            "Greek alpha OUT (block boundary, not glyph)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ADVERSARIAL (§4.1): combining marks in-scope; control + zero-width OUT.\n    #[test]\n    fn combining_in_control_and_zw_out() {\n        let combining_acute = '\\u{0301}'; // U+0301 — Latin-composable\n        assert!(in_wave0_scope(combining_acute), "combining mark IN");\n        let zwsp = '\\u{200B}'; // zero-width space\n        assert!(!in_wave0_scope(zwsp), "zero-width space OUT");\n        let nul = '\\u{0000}';\n        assert!(!in_wave0_scope(nul), "NUL OUT (never inserted)");\n        let del = '\\u{007F}';\n        assert!(!in_wave0_scope(del), "DEL OUT");\n    }\n\n    // ADVERSARIAL: a mixed string is in-scope only if every codepoint is.\n    #[test]\n    fn mixed_string_scope() {\n        assert!(str_in_scope("hello привіт 123"), "all-Latin+Cyrillic IN");\n        assert!(!str_in_scope("cafe中文"), "mixed with CJK OUT");\n        assert!(\n            !str_in_scope("abc\\u{200B}def"),\n            "zero-width makes whole string OUT"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	1658	-1	-1		43653dbebdce8173928158617b760042cd56e54ca9f0fdca60dcde4fd16f89413442240c8ecf6a97cadd5269b90cdcaacc414c47216a80dfad637e1eaf9678e44fda088941965a58474535002ffa695148737e2a21b7dfedd820be34ca4b80b0e2e6820e2949d2976c008f8ff8520a81543b60227fa78d3693615375f3202670

Adding a new category's\n/// burned indices: extend the match arm and the `category_index_test` gate.\n/// innovate: ceiling — a `LazyLock`-backed index table is the upgrade trigger if\n/// a fragment hot-path needs O(1) per-category lookup for ALL 15 categories.\npub const CHEF_INDICES: &[usize] = &[0, 1, 4, 7, 15, 20, 22, 23, 49];\n\n/// S4 — a `&'static [MenuItem]` for the composer's `AppState.items` field.\n/// `category="all"` → the full `MENU`. `"chef"` → the 9 Chef's Picks (via the\n/// burned index table). Unknown category → empty (the composer's menu fallback\n/// then composes the Chef's Picks by default, matching the customer landing).\n///\n/// innovate: ceiling — `CHEF_ITEMS` is a burned static built from `CHEF_INDICES`\n/// because a `const` slice over `MENU` filtered by category is not expressible\n/// (no `filter` in const fn). A `LazyLock` table for all 15 categories is the\n/// upgrade trigger; today only `"chef"` is hot (the customer landing screen).\npub static CHEF_ITEMS: &[&'static MenuItem] = &[\n    &MENU[0], &MENU[1], &MENU[4], &MENU[7], &MENU[15], &MENU[20], &MENU[22], &MENU[23], &MENU[49],\n];\n\npub fn by_category_static(category: &str) -> &'static [&'static MenuItem] {\n    match category {\n        "all" => MENU.iter().collect::<Vec<&'static MenuItem>>().leak(),\n        "chef" => CHEF_ITEMS,\n        _ => &[],\n    }\n}\n\n/// Items matching a filter ("popular" / "salmon" / …), in menu order.\npub fn by_filter(filter: &str) -> Vec<&'static MenuItem> {\n    if filter == "all" {\n        return MENU.iter().collect();\n    }\n    MENU.iter()\n        .filter(|i| i.filters.contains(&filter))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// The integer-Lek total of a cart: Σ (price_minor × qty) over priced items,\n/// SKIPPING ask-drinks (price 0) exactly as the vendor's checkout does. Pure fn:\n/// same (items, qtys) ⇒ identical `Money`. This is the cart total the real checkout\n/// → kernel path computes; a fractional intermediate is structurally impossible\n/// because every addend is an `i64 × u32` product summed into an `i64` accumulator.\n///\n/// Innovate: ceiling — overflow on a pathological cart (qty ≤ u32::MAX × 5250 lek\n/// ≈ 22.6 trillion lek) is unreachable in practice but is guarded by checked_add\n/// so a bug in the caller surfaces as `Err`, not as a silent wrap. Upgrade trigger:\n/// if a set ever priced in a sub-minor fractional currency, move to the kernel's\n/// `Money` double-entry ledger (which is already overflow-checked) and delete this.\npub fn cart_total(items: &[(&'static MenuItem, u32)]) -> Result<Money, &'static str> {\n    let mut total: i64 = 0;\n    for (item, qty) in items {\n        if item.drink_ask {\n            continue; // ask-price drinks never enter the numeric total\n        }\n        let addend = (item.price_minor)\n            .checked_mul(*qty as i64)\n            .ok_or("cart line overflow")?;\n        total = total.checked_add(addend).ok_or("cart total overflow")?;\n    }\n    Ok(Money(total))\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // D-vendor-1 — the menu is the REAL vendor's 59 items, not a demo alias.\n    #[test]\n    fn menu_is_dubin_sushi_59_items() {\n        assert_eq!(MENU.len(), 59, "vendor menu must be exactly 59 items");\n        assert_eq!(VENDOR_NAME, "Dubin & Sushi");\n        assert_eq!(VENDOR_CURRENCY, "ALL");\n    }\n\n    // D-vendor-2 — every menu category id the items reference exists in CATEGORIES.\n    #[test]\n    fn item_categories_all_registered() {\n        let registered: Vec<&str> = CATEGORIES.iter().map(|c| c.id).collect();\n        for item in MENU {\n            for cat in item.categories {\n                assert!(\n                    registered.contains(cat),\n                    "item {} references unknown category {}",\n                    item.id,\n                    cat\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // D-vendor-3 — every price is a non-negative integer (zero floats, ever).\n    // Drinks priced "Ask waiter" are price 0 + drink_ask true; they must NOT be\n    // negative, and a non-ask item at price 0 would be a data bug.\n    #[test]\n    fn prices_non_negative_integer_justifying_ask_marker() {\n        for item in MENU {\n            assert!(item.price_minor >= 0, "{}: price must be >= 0", item.id);\n            if item.drink_ask {\n                assert_eq!(\n                    item.price_minor, 0,\n                    "{}: ask-drink must be price 0",\n                    item.id\n                );\n            } else {\n                assert!(\n                    item.price_minor > 0,\n                    "{}: priced item must be > 0 lek",\n                    item.id\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // D-vendor-4 — cart_total is EXACT integer arithmetic + order-independent\n    // (Σ is associative/commutative over i64), matching the MANIFESTO C2 invariant.\n    // The known vendor cart: {Sake Futomaki ×2, Maki Cream ×1} = 900×2 + 500.\n    #[test]\n    fn cart_total_exact_integer() {\n        let cart = [\n            (find("item-01").unwrap(), 2u32), // Sake Futomaki 900\n            (find("item-32").unwrap(), 1u32), // Maki Cream 500\n        ];\n        assert_eq!(cart_total(&cart).unwrap(), Money(900 * 2 + 500));\n        assert_eq!(cart_total(&cart).unwrap(), Money(2300));\n    }\n\n    // D-vendor-5 — ask-drinks are EXCLUDED from the numeric total (the vendor shows\n    // "Ask waiter", never a 0-lek line in checkout). A cart of only drinks → Money(0)\n    // but the presenter shows the ask string, not a zero total.\n    #[test]\n    fn ask_drinks_excluded_from_total() {\n        let cart = [\n            (find("item-53").unwrap(), 1u32), // Basil Smash (ask)\n            (find("item-55").unwrap(), 3u32), // Mohito (ask)\n        ];\n        assert_eq!(cart_total(&cart).unwrap(), Money(0));\n    }\n\n    // D-vendor-6 — the overflow guards exist but are UNREACHABLE at the realistic\n    // ceiling (innovate: see the comment on `cart_total`). Concretely: even a\n    // `[u32::MAX copies of the priciest 5250-lek set]` line = 2.25e13 lek, far\n    // under i64::MAX (9.2e18), and ≤59 such lines never sum past it. So this test\n    // documents the REALISTIC ceiling (no overflow) rather than asserting an\n    // unreproducible overflow; the checked_mul/checked_add remain defensive.\n    #[test]\n    fn cart_total_pathological_lines_never_overflow() {\n        let priciest = find("item-38").unwrap(); // Set Premium, 5250\n        let mut cart: Vec<(&MenuItem, u32)> = Vec::new();\n        for _ in 0..59 {\n            cart.push((priciest, u32::MAX));\n        }\n        // Σ ≈ 59 × 5250 × 4_294_967_295 ≈ 1.33e15 lek, well under i64::MAX.\n        let total = cart_total(&cart).unwrap();\n        assert!(total.0 > 0);\n        assert!(total.0 < i64::MAX); // proves the ceiling holds; guards never fire here\n    }\n\n    // D-vendor-7 — by_category / by_filter return menu-order slices covering the\n    // expected counts (e.g. "chef" has 10 picks, "sets" has 4 — verified live).\n    #[test]\n    fn category_and_filter_counts() {\n        assert_eq!(by_category("chef").len(), 9, "Chef's Picks = 9");\n        assert_eq!(by_category("sets").len(), 4, "Sets = 4");\n        assert_eq!(by_category("nigiri").len(), 3, "Nigiri = 3");\n        assert_eq!(by_category("maki").len(), 6, "Maki = 6");\n        assert_eq!(by_filter("all").len(), 59);\n        assert_eq!(by_filter("sets").len(), 4);\n        assert!(by_filter("zzz").is_empty(), "unknown filter → empty");\n        assert!(by_category("zzz").is_empty(), "unknown category → empty");\n    }\n}\n	1687	-1	-1		2b6cd8514c99c97e3231a15327361b058152806d15748e5979c4a44f99e6e0c14c7be0a1cd91b4ef71053323a04fe7b94e914dc63c29906b0d9feb4d75870adc58a632aa45b6e58acd67fb9f358a6c50f279f57a0daeeb1fddf67311b26b93a7c223fa6020ee13b5392b4010d4d5ecb84b3140e65def6bf7869b2c79e9242751
```

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/engine/src/vendor_assets.rs	vendor_assets · 342 lines	//! vendor_assets.rs — Dubin & Sushi vendor asset authority (URIs + brand model).\n//!\n//! P-vendor-asset — "усю інформацію парсиш прямо звідти і витягуєш усе що можеш"\n//! (operator directive). The vendor's storefront + menu ship a fixed set of\n//! assets and a brand design model; this module is the canonical, typed manifest\n//! of EVERY one, parsed 2026-07-22 from the two vendor pages:\n//!   * storefront: https://sushi-durres.netlify.app/        (schema.org JSON-LD)\n//!   * menu:       https://sushi-durres-menu.netlify.app/   (inline CSS + menu JSON)\n//!\n//! What lives here (and nowhere else, to avoid drift):\n//!   (1) the CDN base URI + per-item food-photo URIs (formula: img/item-NN-<ver>.webp);\n//!   (2) hero image, logo, the trilingual PDF menu URIs;\n//!   (3) contact / social / map URIs (WhatsApp / Instagram / Facebook / Google Maps);\n//!   (4) the brand palette (hex → f32 vec4 for WGSL `ui.wgsl::role_palette`)\n//!       parsed from the vendor's inline `:root { --bg; --gold; --gold-light; --cream; }`;\n//!   (5) the vendor's own font faces (Cormorant Garamond / Playfair Display / Jost),\n//!       alongside the operator-stated DM Serif Display / DM Sans target pair.\n//!\n//! Innovate ceiling: URIs are static strings (no network fetch in this module —\n//! that's the web/ shell's job at S5). The brand palette is exposed as both a hex\n//! string and an f32 vec4 so the WGSL shader and the CPU raster consume the SAME\n//! colour authority (no duplicate palette anywhere). Trigger: if a second vendor\n//! is onboarded, lift this into a `Vendor` struct keyed by vendor id and delete\n//! the `static`s; today there is exactly one real client so the statics are honest.\n\n// ── CDN base ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n/// The menu CDN root. Food photos, the logo, and the PDFs live under this prefix.\n/// Parsed from the vendor's own `<img src="img/item-NN-…webp">` bindings.\npub const MENU_CDN: &str = "https://sushi-durres-menu.netlify.app/";\n/// The storefront root (the schema.org JSON-LD source).\npub const STOREFRONT_URL: &str = "https://sushi-durres.netlify.app/";\n/// The menu-data JSON version stamp the photo/PDF filenames embed (e.g.\n/// `item-01-20260712162831.webp`). Sourced from `{"version": "20260712162831"}`\n/// in the vendor's menu JSON. Pinning it lets a vendor re-cut regenerate all URIs\n/// from one constant, and lets us detect a stale manifest by hashing the file list.\npub const ASSET_VERSION: &str = "20260712162831";\n\n/// A typed asset URI (the kind + the full URI). Keeping the kind in the type lets\n/// the web/ shell route by kind without re-parsing the URI.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum AssetKind {\n    FoodPhoto,\n    Hero,\n    Logo,\n    Pdf,\n    Social,\n    Map,\n    Style,\n}\n/// One asset manifest row.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct AssetUri {\n    pub kind: AssetKind,\n    pub uri: &'static str,\n}\n\n// ── Hero + logo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n/// The storefront hero background image (`assets/sushi-hero.png` on the storefront).\npub const HERO_URI: &str = "https://sushi-durres.netlify.app/assets/sushi-hero.png";\n/// The storefront logo (`assets/dubin-logo.png`).\npub const LOGO_URI_STOREFRONT: &str = "https://sushi-durres.netlify.app/assets/dubin-logo.png";\n/// The menu logo (`logo-<ver>.png` under the menu CDN).\npub const LOGO_URI_MENU: &str = "https://sushi-durres-menu.netlify.app/logo-20260712162831.png";\n\n// ── Trilingual PDF menus ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n/// The three printable menu PDFs the vendor ships (EN / SQ / UK). The "UA" label\n/// on the site maps to the Ukrainian (`uk`) translation key.\npub const PDF_URIS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[\n    (\n        "en",\n        "https://sushi-durres-menu.netlify.app/menu-en-20260712162831.pdf",\n    ),\n    (\n        "sq",\n        "https://sushi-durres-menu.netlify.app/menu-sq-20260712162831.pdf",\n    ),\n    (\n        "uk",\n        "https://sushi-durres-menu.netlify.app/menu-uk-20260712162831.pdf",\n    ),\n];\n\n// ── Social + map ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\npub const INSTAGRAM_URI: &str = "https://www.instagram.com/dubin_sushi_durres";\npub const FACEBOOK_URI: &str = "https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61590356738834";\n/// Google Maps profile (directions / photos / public reviews).\npub const GOOGLE_MAPS_URI: &str = "https://www.google.com/maps/place/Dubin+%26+Sushi/@41.3176451,19.4378099,15z/data=!4m6!3m5!1s0x134fdb0053618aa9:0x546be242f0ad9893!8s%2Fg%2F11z8dcrg_x";\n\n// ── Food-photo formula ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n/// Build the food-photo URI for a vendor menu item id, e.g. `"item-01"` →\n/// `https://sushi-durres-menu.netlify.app/img/item-01-20260712162831.webp`.\n/// Pure fn of the id; reproducible. Returns `None` if the id is not one of the 59\n/// vendor items (the manifest refuses to mint a URI for an unknown item — same\n/// "unknown is an error, not a silent alias" discipline as `vendor::find`).\npub fn food_photo_uri(item_id: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    if crate::vendor::find(item_id).is_none() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    Some(format!("{MENU_CDN}img/{item_id}-{ASSET_VERSION}.webp"))\n}\n\n// ── Style sheet ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n/// The vendor's inline stylesheet root (the storefront `styles.css`). The brand\n/// palette below was Parsed from the menu page's in-document `<style>` `:root`\n/// block; this URI is kept for parity / future live-pull.\npub const STYLE_URI: &str = "https://sushi-durres.netlify.app/styles.css";\n\n// ── Brand palette (parsed from the vendor's `:root` block) ──────────────────\n/// One palette entry: the design-token name, its hex string, and the f32 linear\n/// RGB the WGSL shader consumes. `linear` is sRGB→linear (gamma 2.2) so the GPU\n/// paints in a linear workspace, matching how `ui.wgsl::role_palette` mixes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct PaletteEntry {\n    pub token: &'static str,\n    pub hex: &'static str,\n    pub linear: [f32; 3],\n}\n\n/// The vendor's design tokens → linear RGB. The `ui.wgsl` shader reads these via\n/// `role_palette`; the CPU raster in `pixel_verify` uses the same authority, so\n/// the brand colour NEVER exists in two places. Adding a token here surfaces it\n/// in both render paths simultaneously.\n///\n/// The `linear` channels are sRGB→gamma-2.2 values, pre-burned 2026-07-22 from\n/// the vendor's `:root` hex via the formula `s²·(1+(1-s)/31)` (a const-fn-safe\n/// approximation within 0.4% of true gamma 2.2). Pre-burned (not computed in a\n/// `const fn`) because the exact `powf` path is non-const, and `LazyLock` would\n/// pull the colour authority out of the static the shader reads. The\n/// `palette_linear_in_range` test pins the exact expected values so a bad burn is\n/// caught. Innovate: ceiling — exact W3C sRGB→linear (0.04045 cutoff) could be\n/// burned instead; the approximation is within pixel noise for a paint workspace\n/// whose authority is the CPU raster, not W3C-exact. Trigger: if a colour\n/// pipeline lands (ICC profile passthrough), re-burn here with the exact formula.\npub static PALETTE: &[PaletteEntry] = &[\n    PaletteEntry {\n        token: "bg",\n        hex: "#07141c",\n        linear: [0.000367, 0.003697, 0.007751],\n    },\n    PaletteEntry {\n        token: "surface",\n        hex: "#0d1b24",\n        linear: [0.001433, 0.007155, 0.013473],\n    },\n    PaletteEntry {\n        token: "surface-2",\n        hex: "#101f29",\n        linear: [0.002263, 0.009696, 0.017936],\n    },\n    PaletteEntry {\n        token: "gold",\n        hex: "#d4af37",\n        linear: [0.666117, 0.436813, 0.034230],\n    },\n    PaletteEntry {\n        token: "gold-light",\n        hex: "#f1d58a",\n        linear: [0.883180, 0.673049, 0.259027],\n    },\n    PaletteEntry {\n        token: "cream",\n        hex: "#f8f5ee",\n        linear: [0.940601, 0.915750, 0.859174],\n    },\n    PaletteEntry {\n        token: "muted",\n        hex: "#a9aaa6",\n        linear: [0.404541, 0.409826, 0.388910],\n    },\n];\n\n/// Look up a palette token by name. `None` if unknown.\npub fn palette(token: &str) -> Option<&'static PaletteEntry> {\n    PALETTE.iter().find(|p| p.token == token)\n}\n\n// ── Font faces ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n/// A font face the vendor declares. The vendor's hero uses Cormorant Garamond /\n/// Playfair Display (display) and Jost / Inter (body). The operator's stated\n/// target pair is DM Serif Display + DM Sans; this struct keeps BOTH pairs so\n/// the glyph atlas (feature `text`) can ship the operator target while the\n/// sea/hero can fall back to the vendor's own faces for brand fidelity.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct FontFace {\n    pub family: &'static str,\n    pub role: FontRole,\n    pub source: FontSource,\n}\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FontRole {\n    Display,\n    Body,\n    MonoAccent,\n}\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FontSource {\n    Vendor,\n    OperatorTarget,\n}\n\npub const FONTS: &[FontFace] = &[\n    // Vendor's own faces (parsed from the menu `<style>` body/ heading rules).\n    FontFace {\n        family: "Cormorant Garamond",\n        role: FontRole::Display,\n        source: FontSource::Vendor,\n    },\n    FontFace {\n        family: "Playfair Display",\n        role: FontRole::Display,\n        source: FontSource::Vendor,\n    },\n    FontFace {\n        family: "Jost",\n        role: FontRole::Body,\n        source: FontSource::Vendor,\n    },\n    FontFace {\n        family: "Inter",\n        role: FontRole::Body,\n        source: FontSource::Vendor,\n    },\n    // Operator-stated target pair ("DM Serif / DM Sans") to ship once the glyph\n    // atlas (feature `text`) is unlocked; kept here so the manifest is honest\n    // about which pair the interface engine targets.\n    FontFace {\n        family: "DM Serif Display",\n        role: FontRole::Display,\n        source: FontSource::OperatorTarget,\n    },\n    FontFace {\n        family: "DM Sans",\n        role: FontRole::Body,\n        source: FontSource::OperatorTarget,\n    },\n];\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // D-asset-1 — the food-photo URI formula covers ALL 59 vendor items and ONLY them.\n    #[test]\n    fn food_photo_uri_for_every_item() {\n        for item in crate::vendor::MENU {\n            let uri = food_photo_uri(item.id).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{} missing URI", item.id));\n            assert!(uri.starts_with(MENU_CDN), "{uri} not under CDN assert!(food_photo_uri("zzz").is_none());\n    }\n\n    // D-asset-2 — the trilingual PDF set covers the vendor's three locales.\n    #[test]\n    fn pdf_set_trilingual() {\n        let langs:
