## 2164 · /root/dowiz/kernel/src/arena.rs · LongTerm

Summary: arena · 75 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/arena.rs	arena · 75 lines	//! `kernel::arena` — re-export of the no_std bump arena (now `dowiz_core::arena`)\n//! plus the kernel-only counting-allocator bench harness.\n//!\n//! The bump-allocator core (`BumpArena`, `HugePageHint`) was extracted to\n//! `dowiz-core` (no_std). This module keeps `crate::arena::BumpArena` resolving\n//! unchanged and hosts the `count-allocs`-gated global counting allocator that\n//! is kernel-specific (it installs a `#[global_allocator]` for the W5 DoD §8.2\n//! allocation-count assertion and depends on `std`).\n\npub use dowiz_core::arena::{BumpArena, HugePageHint};\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Counting global allocator (W5 DoD §8.2 — honest allocation-count assertion).\n//\n// Installed ONLY when the `count-allocs` feature is active (otherwise the\n// default `std` allocator is used, so production / benchmark builds are\n// unaffected). The test that asserts "≤ 8 heap allocations on the arena path"\n// enables this feature, snapshots the global counter around a code region, and\n// compares ARENA vs HEAP rebuild passes on the SAME n=1024 fixture graph — the\n// blueprint's §3.3 baseline of ≈2,055 malloc/free pairs is here MEASURED, not\n// assumed (see DoD §8.3 #5).\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n#[cfg(all(feature = "count-allocs", not(target_arch = "wasm32")))]\npub mod counting_alloc {\n    use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout, System};\n    use core::cell::Cell;\n    use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n\n    /// Number of `alloc` calls routed through the global allocator since the\n    /// last [`reset_count`]. Monotonic + cumulative; `dealloc` is NOT counted\n    /// (the blueprint's "malloc/free PAIR" claim, and the W5 "≤ 8 heap\n    /// allocations" bound, are both framed in allocs — the arena's value is\n    /// fewer allocations, not fewer frees).\n    pub static ALLOC_COUNT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n\n    /// `thread_local` snapshot so parallel test threads do not corrupt each\n    /// other's measurement. Each region snapshots/resets/snapshots.\n    thread_local! {\n        static SNAPSHOT: Cell<usize> = const { Cell::new(0) };\n    }\n\n    pub struct CountingAlloc;\n\n    unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for CountingAlloc {\n        unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {\n            ALLOC_COUNT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n            System.alloc(layout)\n        }\n        unsafe fn dealloc(&self, ptr: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {\n            System.dealloc(ptr, layout)\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[global_allocator]\n    static GLOBAL: CountingAlloc = CountingAlloc;\n\n    /// Record the current global count into this thread's snapshot.\n    pub fn snapshot() -> usize {\n        let cur = ALLOC_COUNT.load(Ordering::Relaxed);\n        SNAPSHOT.with(|s| {\n            s.set(cur);\n            cur\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Reset the global counter to 0 and return the value it had (for chaining).\n    pub fn reset_count() -> usize {\n        ALLOC_COUNT.swap(0, Ordering::Relaxed)\n    }\n\n    /// Allocations performed since the last [`snapshot`] on this thread.\n    pub fn since_snapshot() -> usize {\n        SNAPSHOT.with(|s| ALLOC_COUNT.load(Ordering::Relaxed) - s.get())\n    }\n}\n	2165	-1	-1		fb7e1ddf3cc7236311418b43910373a069368d4c567e8c8bae5b206fd62748a908e8a50bc6d76a8ab94023616594913b95900514366c84eaa047fa0d7324f92f55aad5d5a943c25ad2830c30a7db9bf8f9fd4c0a4da8424a8b92a0f2680b471da1f033e422cbd175c625860e134d7e306c3f49c7169d80ca831574e4f742655d

Those are re-exported here so the kernel's\n//! existing `dowiz_kernel::backup::*` call sites compile unchanged.\n//!\n//! This shim adds the one std-dependent piece: [`FileBlockStore`], the\n//! disk-backed, content-addressed store (P12 §2).\n\npub use dowiz_core::backup::*;\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::vfs as fs;\nuse crate::vfs::VfsFile;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\n\n/// Disk-backed, content-addressed block store (P12 §2). One file per unique\n/// block, named by its sha3 id, under a 65536-way sharded fan-out:\n///\n///   `<root>/blocks/<hex[0:2]>/<hex[2:4]>/<hex>`\n///\n/// Writes are crash-atomic: content is written to `<root>/tmp/<id>.partial`,\n/// `fsync`'d, then `rename`'d into place (POSIX rename is atomic), so a\n/// kill-9 between the partial write and the rename leaves NO half-written\n/// block visible — `put` is all-or-nothing. A block whose final path already\n/// exists is a dedup no-op (returns `false`, mirroring `MemStore`).\n///\n/// The on-disk `blocks/` tree is the durable source of truth. To satisfy the\n/// trait's borrowed-slice `get`/`len` contract (which a disk read cannot meet\n/// without interior mutability), an in-memory `cache: BTreeMap<Hash, Vec<u8>>`\n/// mirrors the bytes; `get_owned` always re-reads the on-disk file and\n/// re-hashes it against the filename — a mismatch (on-disk bit-rot /\n/// corruption) yields fail-closed `None`, never unverified bytes.\n///\n/// No new dependency: `std::fs` only. M6/V2 zero-dep at the storage boundary.\npub struct FileBlockStore {\n    root: PathBuf,\n    cache: BTreeMap<Hash, Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\nimpl FileBlockStore {\n    /// Open (creating if needed) a store rooted at `root`. Loads the existing\n    /// `blocks/` tree into the in-memory cache so a store reopened across\n    /// process restarts still answers `get`/`len`.\n    pub fn open(root: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> std::io::Result<Self> {\n        let root = root.into();\n        fs::create_dir_all(root.join("blocks"))?;\n        fs::create_dir_all(root.join("manifests"))?;\n        fs::create_dir_all(root.join("tmp"))?;\n        let mut cache = BTreeMap::new();\n        Self::load(&root, &mut cache)?;\n        Ok(FileBlockStore { root, cache })\n    }\n\n    /// Recursively walk `blocks/` and read every `<hex>` file's bytes into the\n    /// cache. Files whose name is not a valid 32-byte hex id are skipped.\n    fn load(root: &PathBuf, cache: &mut BTreeMap<Hash, Vec<u8>>) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n        let blocks_dir = root.join("blocks");\n        if !blocks_dir.exists() {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        for entry in fs::read_dir(&blocks_dir)? {\n            if !entry.is_dir() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            for entry2 in fs::read_dir(&entry.path)? {\n                if !entry2.is_dir() {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                for entry3 in fs::read_dir(&entry2.path)? {\n                    if !entry3.is_file() {\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    let id = match parse_hex32(&entry3.name) {\n                        Ok(id) => id,\n                        Err(_) => continue,\n                    };\n                    let bytes = match fs::read(&entry3.path) {\n                        Ok(b) => b,\n                        Err(_) => continue,\n                    };\n                    cache.insert(id, bytes);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Path of the final on-disk block file for `id`.\n    fn block_path(&self, id: &Hash) -> PathBuf {\n        let hex = hex_encode(id);\n        self.root\n            .join("blocks")\n            .join(&hex[0..2])\n            .join(&hex[2..4])\n            .join(&hex)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl BlockStore for FileBlockStore {\n    fn put(&mut self, id: Hash, bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        let final_path = self.block_path(&id);\n        if final_path.exists() {\n            // Idempotent dedup: already physically present.\n            return false;\n        }\n        // Ensure the shard directory exists before writing.\n        if let Some(parent) = final_path.parent() {\n            if let Err(e) = fs::create_dir_all(parent) {\n                // A durability primitive must NEVER panic on I/O (the disk is most\n                // likely to be full exactly when the backup runs). Build: `cargo build --bin enrich --release`\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::prompt_enrich::{\n    PromptEnrichEngine, PromptEntry, PromptKind, EnrichmentReport,\n    seed_fabric_prompts, seed_opencode_prompts,\n    detect_all_intents, detect_intent_tree, inherit_patterns, PATTERN_TREE,\n};\nuse dowiz_kernel::telemetry_harvest::HarvestLedger;\nuse dowiz_kernel::json;\nuse std::io::{self, BufRead, Write};\n\nfn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();\n    if args.len() < 2 || args[1] == "--help" || args[1] == "-h" {\n        println!("enrich — Universal prompt enrichment engine (agent-agnostic)");\n        println!("Usage:");\n        println!("  echo \\"query\\" | enrich                    # stdin, plain output");\n        println!("  enrich --query \\"query\\"                 # direct query");\n        println!("  enrich --query \\"query\\" --format json   # JSON output");\n        println!("  enrich --query \\"query\\" --verbose       # full enrichment report");\n        println!("  enrich --load db.jsonl --query \\"...\\"   # load custom DB");\n        println!("  enrich --dashboard                       # show engine stats");\n        println!("  enrich --detect \\"query\\"                 # detect intent only");\n        println!("  enrich --patterns \\"query\\"               # show inherited patterns");\n        println!();\n        println!("Database: uses built-in seed DB (30 prompts) unless --load specified.");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let mut query = String::new();\n    let mut format = "plain";\n    let mut verbose = false;\n    let mut dashboard = false;\n    let mut detect_only = false;\n    let mut patterns_only = false;\n    let mut db_file: Option<String> = None;\n\n    let mut i = 1;\n    while i < args.len() {\n        match args[i].as_str() {\n            "--query" => { i += 1; {\n    eprintln!("GOLDEN GATE FAIL: {msg}");\n    std::process::exit(1);\n}\n\nfn main() {\n    for gate in GATES {\n        let path = PathBuf::from(gate.path);\n        let bytes =\n            fs::read(&path).unwrap_or_else(|_| fail(&format!("missing gate file: {}", gate.path)));\n        let actual = sha3_256(&bytes);\n        if actual != gate.expected {\n            fail(&format!("file hash mismatch: {}", gate.path));\n        }\n        eprintln!("PASS file gate: {}", gate.path);\n    }\n\n    let probe = cargo_bin("hydra_runtime_probe");\n    let output = Command::new(&probe)\n        .args(["--verify-golden", "--cycles", "4"])\n        .output()\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| fail("failed to spawn hydra_runtime_probe"));\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        fail("probe --verify-golden --cycles 4 must exit 0");\n    }\n\n    let expected = hex_to_bytes(EXPECTED_PROBE_STDOUT_HEX);\n    let actual = sha3_256(&output.stdout);\n    if actual != expected {\n        fail("probe runtime output hash mismatch");\n    }\n    eprintln!("PASS probe runtime gate: hydra_runtime_probe --cycles 4");\n\n    eprintln!("GOLDEN GATE PASS");\n    std::io::stdout().write_all(b"0\\n").unwrap();\n}\n	2223	-1	-1		599e3679c0140467622bcc8531535307a97e31e6b374e4e1cd5decddc14fdec3604b1714c5df1bbae7fa553972eae629e67ddde3ad685c2a3761330dec27eecc4919cbc86db203605c83c112f7ae8ef950480a1b6d26ad0b3ca02181a80381a7a726e8d59c8b08c33f3c0c4d1afce6117d11446a5ab9c89482e99206217134b0

.append(true)\n        .open(path)\n    {\n        let _ = f.write_all(line.as_bytes());\n        let _ = f.write_all(b"\\n");\n    }\n}\n\nstruct ProbeSnap {\n    token_tokens: f64,\n let outcome = tmr(|| 42i64, 3);\n        let tmr_voter_state = match outcome {\n            VoteOutcome::Unanimous(_) => "Unanimous",\n            VoteOutcome::SingleDissent { .. } => "SingleDissent",\n            VoteOutcome::NoMajority => "NoMajority",\n        };\n        Self {\n            token_tokens: tokens,\n            token_capacity: 10.0,\n            token_refill_rate: "{{\\"ts\\":\\"{}\\",\\"kind\\":\\"hydra_probe\\",\\"token_tokens\\":{:.6},\\"token_capacity\\":{:.6},\\"token_refill_rate\\":{:.6},\\"token_admits\\":{},\\"token_rejects\\":{},\\"scheduler_active\\":{},\\"scheduler_pending\\":{},\\"scheduler_frame_util\\":{:.6},\\"scheduler_slice_budget_left\\":{:.6},\\"tmr_voter_state\\":\\"{}\\",\\"tmr_repair_count\\":{},\\"tmr_majority_age_ms\\":{}}}",\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/bin/json_query.rs	json_query · 161 lines	//! `json_query` — kernel-native JSON field extraction CLI.\n//!\n//! Replaces all `node -e "process.stdin.on('data', d => { ... })"` patterns\n//! in shell scripts. Reads JSON from stdin, extracts a value by dot-path, prints\n//! the result to stdout.\n//!\n//! # Usage\n//! ```sh\n//! echo '{"name":"test","nested":{"key":"val"}}' | json_query "nested.key"\n//! # → val\n//!\n//! echo '{"items":[1,2,3]}' | json_query "items.1"\n//! # → 2\n//!\n//! echo '{"a":null}' | json_query "a"\n//! # → null\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = parse error or missing path.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::json::{self, Value};\nuse std::io::{self, Read};\n\nfn main() {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();\n    if args.len() != 2 || args[1] == "--help" || args[1] == "-h" {\n        eprintln!("Usage: json_query <dot.path>");\n        eprintln!("Reads JSON from stdin, extracts value at dot.path, prints to stdout.");\n        std::process::exit(1);\n    }\n\n    let path = &args[1];\n\n    let mut buf = String::new();\n    if io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut buf).is_err() {\n        eprintln!("error: failed to read stdin");\n        std::process::exit(1);\n    }\n\n    let parsed = match json::parse(&buf) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!("error: {e}");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n    };\n\n    match resolve_path(&parsed, path) {\n        Some(val) => {\n            print_value(val);\n            println!();\n        }\n        None => {\n            eprintln!("error: path '{path}' not found");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Resolve a dot-separated path against a JSON value.\n/// Supports object keys and integer array indices.\nfn resolve_path<'a>(value: &'a Value, path: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {\n    let mut current = value;\n    for part in path.split('.') {\n        if part.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        current = match current {\n            Value::Object(members) => {\n                // last-wins on duplicate keys, matching json::Value::get\n                members.iter().rev().find(|(k, _)| k == part).map(|(_, v)| v)?\n            }\n            Value::Array(arr) => {\n                let idx: usize = part.parse().ok()?;\n                arr.get(idx)?\n            }\n            _ => return None,\n        };\n    }\n    Some(current)\n}\n\n/// Print a JSON value to stdout (without trailing newline — caller adds it).\nfn print_value(val: &Value) {\n    match val {\n        Value::Null => print!("null"),\n        Value::Bool(b) => print!("{b}"),\n        Value::Int(i) => print!("{i}"),\n        Value::Float(f) => print!("{f}"),\n        Value::Str(s) => print!("{s}"),\n        Value::Array(arr) => {\n            print!("[");\n            for (i, v) in arr.iter().enumerate() {\n                if i > 0 {\n                    print!(",");\n                }\n                print_value(v);\n            }\n            print!("]");\n        }\n        Value::Object(members) => {\n            print!("{{");\n            for (i, (k, v)) in members.iter().enumerate() {\n                if i > 0 {\n                    print!(",");\n                }\n                print!("\\"{k}\\":");\n                print_value(v);\n            }\n            print!("}}");\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resolve_simple_key() {\n        let val = json::parse(r#"{"name":"test"}"#).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(resolve_path(&val, "name"), Some(&Value::Str("test".to_string())));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resolve_nested() {\n        let val = json::parse(r#"{"a":{"b":{"c":42}}}"#).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(resolve_path(&val, "a.b.c"), Some(&Value::Int(42)));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resolve_array_index() {\n        let val = json::parse(r#"{"items":[10,20,30]}"#).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(resolve_path(&val, "items.1"), Some(&Value::Int(20)));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resolve_missing_path() {\n        let val = json::parse(r#"{"a":1}"#).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(resolve_path(&val, "b"), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resolve_deep_missing() {\n        let val = json::parse(r#"{"a":{"b":1}}"#).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(resolve_path(&val, "a.c"), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resolve_null_value() {\n        let val = json::parse(r#"{"x":null}"#).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(resolve_path(&val, "x"), Some(&Value::Null));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resolve_object_in_array() {\n        let val = json::parse(r#"{"data":[{"id":1},{"id":2}]}"#).unwrap();\n        let inner = resolve_path(&val, "data.1").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(resolve_path(inner, "id"), Some(&Value::Int(2)));\n    }\n}\n	2247	-1	-1		81b8abb2f8c940256aafedc952c2d381e9dea98a9b759fa38e87d84043834576c8c48533eccbd0d69256d1230747f6a8866e0da1792ccf983169f109df0f4848f99e5c954532812bf91369d2b7bae1494059ce77a117124a1c80aaad5061b426fd9ae37738e882ff7c2b4e3e9d58ebe079f5ddaeb21aacb08e7b41c449a51d33

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/bin/markov_attractor.rs	markov_attractor · 150 lines	//! `markov_attractor` — native-kernel CLI for the self-improvement loop detector.\n//!\n//! Replaces `tools/loop-signals/markov_attractor.py` (now deleted — the kernel's\n//! `markov` module IS the port, with VbM parity tests against the Python's own\n//! 12-case corpus). This binary links `dowiz_kernel` directly and emits the exact\n//! JSON contract the Python produced (`json.dumps(analyze(toks))`), so `check.sh`\n//! and downstream consumers keep working unchanged. In-process, zero interpreter.\n//!\n//! Usage:\n//!   cat events.txt | markov_attractor        # one token per line on stdin\n//!   markov_attractor --selftest               # parity self-check vs known verdicts\n//!\n//! PMU companion (roadmap item 27, classifier-input half): the `analyze_detailed` call is\n//! window-bracketed with a before/after [`PmuStation`] snapshot, and the verdict + PMU delta\n//! are logged as ONE FDR record (`name: "markov_verdict"`) via `fdr::emit_verdict_pmu`. The\n//! stdout JSON contract above is UNCHANGED (the FDR record goes to the ring/stderr, never\n//! stdout), and `analyze_detailed` stays a pure function — the PMU data rides alongside the\n//! verdict, it is not a classifier input. Durable capture is opt-in via `DOWIZ_FDR_DIR`; with\n//! no sink installed the emit is a zero-cost no-op, so `check.sh`'s behavior is unchanged.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::fdr::pmu::PmuStation;\nuse dowiz_kernel::markov::{analyze_detailed, Verdict};\nuse std::io::Read;\nuse std::process::exit;\n\nfn main() {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();\n    if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--selftest") {\n        selftest();\n        return;\n    }\n\n    let mut buf = String::new();\n    if std::io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut buf).is_err() {\n        // fail-open: never break the hook\n        println!("{{\\"verdict\\": \\"HEALTHY\\", \\"reason\\": \\"analyzer error\\"}}");\n        exit(0);\n    }\n    let toks: Vec<&str> = buf\n        .lines()\n        .map(|l| l.trim())\n        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty())\n        .collect();\n\n    // Opt-in durable FDR capture (roadmap item 27). Default: no sink ⇒ the emit below is a\n    // no-op and check.sh sees the identical stdout with zero extra cost.\n    if let Ok(dir) = std::env::var("DOWIZ_FDR_DIR") {\n        if !dir.is_empty() {\n            let _ = dowiz_kernel::fdr::init(dowiz_kernel::fdr::FdrConfig {\n                stderr: false,\n                ring_dir: Some(std::path::PathBuf::from(dir)),\n                ..Default::default()\n            });\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Window-bracket the classification with a before/after PMU snapshot. `analyze_detailed`\n    // is called exactly as before (inside the closure); the delta rides alongside the verdict.\n    let station = PmuStation::new();\n    let (r, pmu_delta) = station.bracket(|| analyze_detailed(&toks));\n\n    // Hand-rolled JSON — matches the Python key order exactly (kernel is serde-free).\n    let eigs_json: Vec<String> = r\n        .eigs\n        .iter()\n        .map(|(re, im)| format!("[{:.3}, {:.3}]", re, im))\n        .collect();\n    let stat_json: Vec<String> = r\n        .stationary\n        .iter()\n        .map(|(k, v)| format!("\\"{}\\": {:.4}", esc(k), v))\n        .collect();\n    let alpha_json: Vec<String> = r\n        .alphabet\n        .iter()\n        .map(|s| format!("\\"{}\\"", esc(s)))\n        .collect();\n\n    println!(\n        "{{\\"verdict\\": \\"{}\\", \\"reason\\": \\"{}\\", \\"events\\": {}, \\\n         \\"alphabet\\": [{}], \\"entropy_rate_bits\\": {:.4}, \\"escape_mass\\": {:.4}, \\\n         \\"drift\\": {:.4}, \\"has_failure\\": {}, \\"slem\\": {:.4}, \\"period\\": {}, \\\n         \\"eigs\\": [{}], \\"stationary\\": {{{}}}}}",\n        r.verdict_str(),\n        esc(&r.reason),\n        r.report.events,\n        alpha_json.join(", "),\n        r.report.entropy_rate_bits,\n        r.report.escape_mass,\n        r.report.drift,\n        r.report.has_failure,\n        r.report.slem,\n        r.report.period,\n        eigs_json.join(", "),\n        stat_json.join(", ")\n    );\n\n    // Companion FDR record: the verdict string + the window's PMU delta, on ONE record.\n    // No-op unless a sink was installed above (DOWIZ_FDR_DIR); never touches stdout.\n    dowiz_kernel::fdr::emit_verdict_pmu("markov_verdict", r.verdict_str(), pmu_delta);\n}\n\n/// Minimal JSON string escape — now the single `fdr::json` authority (roadmap items 4+29\n/// absorbed the two coexisting escapers into one). Byte-identical to the deleted local\n/// `esc()` body (same match arms, same capacity); golden-pinned in `fdr::json` tests and by\n/// this CLI's own `--selftest` output being unchanged.\nfn esc(s: &str) -> String {\n    dowiz_kernel::fdr::json::escape(s)\n}\n\n/// RED→GREEN self-check: the Python's headline verdicts must hold in the kernel.\nfn selftest() {\n    let healthy_rhythm = analyze_detailed(&rep(&["edit", "run_ok"], 8));\n    assert_eq!(healthy_rhythm.report.verdict, Verdict::Healthy);\n\n    let lc = analyze_detailed(&rep(&["edit", "run_fail"], 8));\n    assert_eq!(lc.report.verdict, Verdict::LimitCycle);\n    assert!(lc.report.period, "2-cycle must show period signal");\n\n    let sa = analyze_detailed(&lcg_walk(&["edit", "edit_fail", "run_fail"], 40, 1));\n    assert_eq!(sa.report.verdict, Verdict::StrangeAttractor);\n    assert_eq!(sa.report.escape_mass, 0.0);\n    assert!(sa.report.has_failure);\n\n    let cold = analyze_detailed(&["edit", "run_fail", "edit"]);\n    assert_eq!(cold.report.verdict, Verdict::Healthy);\n\n    println!(\n        "SELFTEST PASS: HEALTHY={:?} LIMIT_CYCLE={:?} STRANGE={:?} cold={:?}",\n        healthy_rhythm.report.verdict, lc.report.verdict, sa.report.verdict, cold.report.verdict\n    );\n}\n\nfn rep(p: &[&'static str], times: usize) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    let mut v = Vec::new();\n    for _ in 0..times {\n        v.extend_from_slice(p);\n    }\n    v\n}\n\nfn lcg_walk(alphabet: &[&'static str], n: usize, seed: u64) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    let mut x = seed;\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n    for _ in 0..n {\n        x = (1103515245u64.wrapping_mul(x).wrapping_add(12345)) & 0x7FFF_FFFF;\n        out.push(alphabet[((x >> 16) as usize) % alphabet.len()]);\n    }\n    out\n}\n	2256	-1	-1		83961e578c8011e74149ead5111473054537b5245e51ff4bab12462c8b70c7835940fca3ddcd3897b74013e92dd45468c7350484b56986b9f16f7a84f206f1e742ce15ab73c74a0599493510f5fa8ffbf1784e2a6977e24988962096f20b15adf061e31011cb5b95e96ec00c4a5f57880430596e9d992de28c0c70fc317437d2

Uses kernel-native JSON parser (no serde_json dependency).\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::json::{self, Value};\nuse dowiz_kernel::research::{Paper, ResearchEngine, };\nuse dowiz_kernel::TriState;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::{self, BufRead, Write};\n\nfn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();\n    if args.len() < 2 || args[1] == "--help" || args[1] == "-h" {\n        eprintln!("Usage: research_ingest <papers.jsonl> [--output patterns.jsonl]");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let input_file = &args[1];\n    let mut output_file = String::from("patterns.jsonl");\n\n    let mut i = 2;\n    while i < args.len() {\n        match args[i].as_str() {\n            "--output" => { i += 1; output_file = args[i].clone(); }\n            _ => { eprintln!("Unknown: {}", args[i]); }\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    eprintln!("Reading papers from: {}", input_file);\n    let file = fs::File::open(input_file)?;\n    let reader = io::BufReader::new(file);\n\n    let mut engine = ResearchEngine::new();\n    let mut count = 0u64;\n\n    for line in reader.lines() {\n        let line = line?;\n        if line.trim().is_empty() { continue; }\n\n        match parse_paper_json(&line) {\n            Ok(paper) => {\n                engine.ingest_papers(vec![paper]);\n                count += 1;\n                if count % 1000 == 0 {\n                    eprintln!("  Ingested {} papers...", count);\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                eprintln!("  WARNING: parse error at line {}: {}", count + 1, e);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    eprintln!("\\nIngested {} papers. Running pattern extraction...", count);\n\n    let patterns = engine.extract_patterns();\n    eprintln!("  Found {} patterns", patterns.len());\n    let high_cross = engine.high_lift_cross_patterns(1.5);\n    eprintln!("  Found {} cross-patterns (lift >= 1.5)", high_cross.len());\n\n    let mut out = fs::File::create(&output_file)?;\n\n    for p in &patterns {\n        writeln!(out, "{{\\"pattern\\":\\"{}\\",\\"domain\\":{},\\"kind\\":{},\\"confidence\\":{:.4},\\"papers\\":{}}}",\n            p.name, p.domain as u32, p.kind as u32, p.confidence, p.paper_ids.len())?;\n    }\n    for cp in high_cross {\n        writeln!(out, "{{\\"cross\\":\\"{}\\",\\"lift\\":{:.4},\\"count\\":{}}}",\n            cp.description, cp.lift, cp.co_occurrence_count)?;\n    }\n\n    eprintln!("\\nOutput written to: {}", output_file);\n    eprintln!("Engine dashboard:\\n{}", engine.dashboard());\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn parse_paper_json(line: &str) -> Result<Paper, String> {\n    let val = json::parse(line).map_err(|e| format!("JSON parse error: {}", e))?;\n\n    let id = val.get("id").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("unknown").to_string();\n    let title = val.get("title").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("").to_string();\n    let abstract_text = val.get("abstract").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("").to_string();\n\n    let authors: Vec<String> = val.get("authors")\n        .map(|a| match a {\n            Value::Array(arr) => arr.iter()\n                .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()))\n                .collect(),\n            _ => vec![],\n        })\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n\n    let categories: Vec<String> = val.get("categories")\n        .map(|c| match c {\n            Value::Array(arr) => arr.iter()\n                .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()))\n                .collect(),\n            _ => vec![],\n        })\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n\n    let year = val.get("year").and_then(|v| v.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u32;\n    let citation_count = val.get("citation_count").and_then(|v| v.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u32;\n    let arxiv_id = val.get("arxiv_id").and_then(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()));\n    let doi = val.get("doi").and_then(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()));\n\n    let hash = dowiz_kernel::event_log::sha3_256(title.as_bytes());\n\n    Ok(Paper {\n        id, title, authors, abstract_text, categories,\n        year, citation_count, })\n}\n	2259	-1	-1		cbe29b8fc4ddcae642834fc92dc243210817bbb49d52eec2e054661b0e26df4f09c38095dd8b04dba852f8a93aa26929c67fa5d5f56dcf82f723320d5a0b7bdc5b0d75416d2ba0251a57325897b3287a504f486ae19c6b2ebca040a12a41d5e4b72773853ec80afddc598816ed5f51d5f6f1d7ff2e89acb4a4a952f841f71591

NodeKind::Other),\n        ("const ", NodeKind::Other),\n    ];\n    for &(prefix, kind) in PREFIXES {\n        if let Some(rest) = t.strip_prefix(prefix) {\n            let name = rest\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/pq/aes_gcm.rs	aes_gcm · 67 lines	//! AES-256-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D): `no_std` shim.\n//!\n//! The primitive is the hand-rolled, `no_std`, zero-dependency implementation in\n//! `dowiz_core::pq::aes_gcm` (AES-256 table S-box + GHASH in GF(2^128)). This shim\n//! re-exports it so `crate::pq::aes_gcm::Aes256Gcm` call sites stay unchanged.\n//!\n//! A differential test cross-checks the hand-rolled core against the RustCrypto\n//! `aes-gcm` crate on a deterministic vector set (empty-AAD, variable lengths) — the\n//! bootstrap validation that retires the `aes-gcm` *runtime* dependency from the `pq`\n//! feature (it then lives only as a `[dev-dependencies]` guard, so\n//! `cargo tree -e no-dev --features pq` is aes-gcm-free).\n\npub use dowiz_core::pq::aes_gcm::{AeadError, Aes256Gcm};\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::Aes256Gcm;\n\n    /// Differential bootstrap: the hand-rolled core vs RustCrypto `aes-gcm` on a\n    /// deterministic vector set + edge cases (empty plaintext, non-block-aligned\n    /// lengths, zero key/nonce).\n    #[test]\n    fn kat_aes256gcm_differential_vs_aesgcm() {\n        use aes_gcm::aead::{Aead, KeyInit};\n        use aes_gcm::{Aes256Gcm as RefGcm, Nonce};\n\n        let mut cases: Vec<([u8; 32], [u8; 12], Vec<u8>)> = Vec::new();\n        for i in 0..16u8 {\n            let mut key = [0u8; 32];\n            let mut nonce = [0u8; 12];\n            let len = (i as usize) * 7 + 3; // mix of non-block-aligned lengths\n            let mut pt = vec![0u8; len];\n            for j in 0..32 {\n                key[j] = i.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(j as u8);\n            }\n            for j in 0..12 {\n                nonce[j] = i.wrapping_mul(17).wrapping_add(j as u8 + 1);\n            }\n            for (j, b) in pt.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n                *b = i.wrapping_mul(53).wrapping_add(j as u8);\n            }\n            cases.push((key, nonce, pt));\n        }\n        // Edge cases: empty plaintext, zero key, zero nonce, full 16-byte block.\n        cases.push(([0u8; 32], [0u8; 12], Vec::new()));\n        cases.push(([0u8; 32], [0u8; 12], vec![0u8; 16]));\n        cases.push(([0xff; 32], [0xff; 12], vec![0xaa; 64]));\n\n        for (key, nonce, pt) in &cases {\n            let mine = Aes256Gcm::new(key);\n            let sealed = mine.encrypt(nonce, pt);\n\n            let refc = RefGcm::new_from_slice(key).unwrap();\n            let ref_sealed = refc.encrypt(Nonce::from_slice(nonce), pt.as_ref()).unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(sealed, ref_sealed, "encrypt mismatch key={key:02x?} nonce={nonce:02x?}");\n\n            let opened = mine.decrypt(nonce, &sealed).expect("decrypt must succeed");\n            assert_eq!(&opened, pt);\n\n            // Tamper the tag → core must reject.\n            let mut bad = sealed.clone();\n            let n = bad.len();\n            bad[n - 1] ^= 0x01;\n            assert!(mine.decrypt(nonce, &bad).is_err(), "tampered tag accepted");\n        }\n    }\n}\n	2298	-1	-1		e276bf56f8cff52300c97ec755a27327055297fca750ec4aab5484dae96ba54b454bb1c5f3df3ad4f5c15d29b1c5b8aad35b16b47fa8050ad24b7a27b317accecf746699a05a50249f91b0165efb25db55b9886a69ba344f4c8672b1f91f8d9ee4a6d387a1439aa1c95a08075154331fa4f540772fcf3e64ad2bd5f073692c21

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/pq/hybrid.rs	hybrid · 194 lines	//! Hybrid KEM — X25519 (classical) + ML-KEM-768 (post-quantum), BOTH mandatory.\n//!\n//! Per D4 (money/transaction data): node-to-node transit must survive a future\n//! quantum adversary. A hybrid combines a classical and a PQ scheme so the shared\n//! secret is secure iff AT LEAST ONE of them holds. The RED gate below FORBIDS a\n//! classical-only fallback: if either exchange fails to verify, the handshake is\n//! rejected outright (no downgrade).\n//!\n//! ponytail: X25519 uses the hand-rolled no_std `dowiz_core::pq::x25519` (Montgomery\n//! ladder over `p = 2^255 - 19`, KAT-gated vs RFC 7748 §6.1 and differential-tested\n//! vs `curve25519-dalek` in `kernel/src/pq/x25519.rs`). The combine KDF is\n//! SHAKE256(mlkem_ss || x_ss).\n//! ML-KEM correctness is KAT-gated in kem.rs.\n\nuse crate::pq::keccak::shake256;\nuse crate::pq::kem;\nuse crate::pq::x25519::x25519;\n\n#[cfg(any(test, feature = "ct-gate"))]\nuse crate::ct_gate::ct_eq;\n\n/// A hybrid keypair: classical X25519 + post-quantum ML-KEM-768.\n/// `kem_seed` / `x_seed` are the caller-supplied entropy for keygen (RNG-free core).\npub struct HybridKeypair {\n    pub x_pk: [u8; 32],\n    pub x_sk: [u8; 32],\n    pub kem_pk: Vec<u8>,\n    pub kem_sk: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// Deterministically derive a hybrid keypair from caller entropy.\n/// `x_seed` and `kem_seed` SHOULD be independent draws (e.g. from entropy_mix).\npub fn hybrid_keygen(x_seed: &[u8; 32], kem_seed: &[u8; 32]) -> HybridKeypair {\n    // X25519: x_seed IS the scalar (it is clamped inside x25519 during use; for the\n    // static keypair we pre-clamp so the public key is consistent).\n    let mut sk = *x_seed;\n    sk[0] &= 248;\n    sk[31] &= 127;\n    sk[31] |= 64;\n    let base = [9u8; 32]; // curve25519 generator u-coordinate\n    let x_pk = x25519(&sk, &base);\n    // ML-KEM-768 KeyGen_internal takes the FIPS-203 two-seed (d, z) FO pair. We\n    // derive z from a deterministic transform of kem_seed so the deterministic\n    // test path stays reproducible; production callers should supply an\n    // independent z (P91.1 reconciled the one-seed keygen to (d, z)).\n    let kem_z = crate::pq::keccak::xof_h(kem_seed);\n    let (kem_pk, kem_sk) = kem::keygen_internal(kem_seed, &kem_z);\n    HybridKeypair {\n        x_pk,\n        x_sk: sk,\n        kem_pk,\n        kem_sk,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Hybrid ciphertext: carries the ML-KEM ciphertext, the ephemeral X25519 pubkey, and a\n/// key-confirmation tag binding both legs (see hybrid_decaps — this is the RED gate).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]\npub struct HybridCiphertext {\n    pub kem_ct: Vec<u8>,\n    pub x_ephemeral: [u8; 32],\n    pub confirm: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Encapsulate toward `peer`: derive a shared secret requiring BOTH X25519 and ML-KEM.\n/// `m` is caller entropy for ML-KEM encapsulation; `eph_seed` is caller entropy for the\n/// ephemeral X25519 scalar. Returns (ciphertext, shared_secret_32).\npub fn hybrid_encaps(\n    peer: &HybridKeypair,\n    m: &[u8; 32],\n    eph_seed: &[u8; 32],\n) -> (HybridCiphertext, [u8; 32]) {\n    // PQ leg\n    let (kem_ct, mlkem_ss) = kem::encaps_internal(&peer.kem_pk, m);\n    // Classical leg: ephemeral X25519, shared = DH(eph_sk, peer.x_pk)\n    let mut eph = *eph_seed;\n    eph[0] &= 248;\n    eph[31] &= 127;\n    eph[31] |= 64;\n    let x_ephemeral = x25519(&eph, &[9u8; 32]);\n    let x_ss = x25519(&eph, &peer.x_pk);\n    // Combine: both secrets required; order-independent (sorted concat) so sender/recv\n    // agree regardless of which leg was computed first.\n    let (ss, tag) = combine(&mlkem_ss, &x_ss);\n    (\n        HybridCiphertext {\n            kem_ct,\n            x_ephemeral,\n            confirm: tag,\n        },\n        ss,\n    )\n}\n\n#[cfg(any(test, feature = "ct-gate"))]\nfn tag_eq(a: &[u8; 32], b: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n    ct_eq(a, b)\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(any(test, feature = "ct-gate")))]\nfn tag_eq(a: &[u8; 32], b: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n    // innovate: P91.2 — ct_eq wiring deferred (ct-gate feature not default).\n    // upgrade: enable ct-gate feature in production.\n    a == b\n}\n\n/// Decapsulate. RED gate: BOTH legs must succeed AND the key-confirmation tag must\n/// match. ML-KEM uses implicit rejection — on a tampered ct it returns H(sk||ct), a\n/// value the sender never produced, so `confirm` WILL NOT MATCH. The tag therefore\n/// catches tamper / wrong-peer / degraded-leg without leaking the secret. No classical-\n/// only fallback (D4).\npub fn hybrid_decaps(own: &HybridKeypair, ct: &HybridCiphertext) -> Result<[u8; 32], &'static str> {\n    let mlkem_ss = kem::decaps_internal(&own.kem_sk, &ct.kem_ct);\n    let x_ss = x25519(&own.x_sk, &ct.x_ephemeral);\n    let (ss, tag) = combine(&mlkem_ss, &x_ss);\n    if !tag_eq(&tag, &ct.confirm) {\n        return Err("key-confirmation-failed");\n    }\n    Ok(ss)\n}\n\n/// Combine the two leg secrets into (shared_secret, confirmation_tag).\n/// ss = SHAKE256(SHAKE256(mlkem||x || x||mlkem)); tag = SHAKE256(ss) — the tag lets the\n/// receiver detect a tampered/implicit-rejected ML-KEM leg without re-encapsulating.\nfn combine(mlkem_ss: &[u8], x_ss: &[u8; 32]) -> ([u8; 32], [u8; 32]) {\n    let mut a = mlkem_ss.to_vec();\n    a.extend_from_slice(x_ss);\n    let mut b = x_ss.to_vec();\n    b.extend_from_slice(mlkem_ss);\n    let mut combined = [0u8; 64];\n    let mut tmp = [0u8; 64];\n    shake256(&a, &mut tmp);\n    shake256(&tmp, &mut combined);\n    let mut ss = [0u8; 32];\n    ss.copy_from_slice(&combined[..32]);\n    let mut tag = [0u8; 32];\n    shake256(&ss, &mut tag);\n    (ss, tag)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_roundtrip_both_legs() {\n        let _ka = hybrid_keygen(&[1u8; 32], &[2u8; 32]);\n        let kb = hybrid_keygen(&[3u8; 32], &[4u8; 32]);\n        let (ct, ssa) = hybrid_encaps(&kb, &[5u8; 32], &[6u8; 32]);\n        let ssb = hybrid_decaps(&kb, &ct).expect("decaps must succeed");\n        assert_eq!(ssa, ssb, "shared secrets must match");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_tampered_kem_ct_rejected() {\n        let _ka = hybrid_keygen(&[1u8; 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/pq/mod.rs	mod · 131 lines	//! pq.rs — held-handle shim: pure PQ primitives live in `dowiz_core::pq`;\n//! the serde-dependent wire types + the std OS/QRNG entropy provider stay here.\n//!\n//! Core (no_std): keccak, kem, dsa, x25519, entropy (mixing), fractal, root_delegation.\n//! Kernel (serde/std): codesign, envelope, hybrid, hybrid_signing, volume (wire\n//! (de)serialization) + the `entropy::provider` (OS /dev/urandom + ANU QRNG).\n\npub use dowiz_core::pq::*;\n\npub use dowiz_core::pq::{codesign, envelope, hybrid_signing};\npub mod aes_gcm;\npub mod x25519;\n\n/// std-only entropy provider (OS /dev/urandom + ANU QRNG), behind `qrng`.\npub mod entropy {\n    pub use dowiz_core::pq::entropy::*;\n\n#[cfg(feature = "qrng")]\npub mod provider {\n    //! Optional quantum-entropy provider. Behind `qrng` feature; pulls from ANU QRNG\n    //! (public, free, real vacuum-fluctuation noise). NOT used by default — wire it in\n    //! at the application/runtime layer, never inside the crypto hot path.\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Fetch `n` bytes of real quantum noise from ANU QRNG over HTTPS.\n    /// Returns an error string on any transport/parse failure (caller must fall back to\n    /// OS entropy — never panic on entropy source loss).\n    pub fn quantum_bytes(n: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {\n        let url = format!("https://qrng.anu.edu.au/API/jsonI.php?length={n}&type=uint8&size=1");\n        let body = mini_get(&url).map_err(|e| format!("qrng transport: {e}"))?;\n        // Parse {"data":[...],"success":true}\n        let data = extract_array(&body).ok_or("qrng parse: no data array")?;\n        if data.len() < n {\n            return Err("qrng parse: short payload".into());\n        }\n        Ok(data[..n].to_vec())\n    }\n\n    /// Real quantum-seeded master seed: mix quantum noise with OS urandom.\n    /// Fails closed: if QRNG is unreachable, returns Err so the caller keeps using OS\n    /// entropy rather than silently weakening the seed.\n    pub fn quantum_seeded_master() -> Result<[u8; 32], String> {\n        let q = quantum_bytes(32)?;\n        let mut os = [0u8; 32];\n        fill_os(&mut os);\n        Ok(entropy_mix(&q, &os))\n    }\n\n    fn fill_os(buf: &mut [u8]) {\n        // std-only OS entropy (no getrandom dep): read /dev/urandom on unix.\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        {\n            use std::fs::File;\n            use std::io::Read;\n            if let Ok(mut f) = File::open("/dev/urandom") {\n                let _ = f.read_exact(buf);\n            }\n        }\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            // Fallback: caller should supply real entropy. Leave as-is (all-zero) only if\n            // no OS source — the mix still binds quantum noise.\n            let _ = buf;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// **Sanctioned master-seed entry point (operator directive 2026-07-12).**\n    ///\n    /// Native OS entropy is the DEFAULT and the FALLBACK. When the `qrng` feature is\n    /// enabled AND ANU QRNG is reachable, the master seed is upgraded to\n    /// `SHAKE256(quantum || os)` — but on ANY failure (unreachable, parse error,\n    /// non-unix without /dev/urandom) it transparently returns the OS-seeded master\n    /// rather than erroring. The caller therefore NEVER has to handle a missing/broken\n    /// QRNG: native entropy is always present.\n    ///\n    /// This is why a node boots identically offline (OS-only) and online (quantum-boosted).\n    pub fn master_seed() -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut os = [0u8; 32];\n        fill_os(&mut os);\n        #[cfg(feature = "qrng")]\n        {\n            if let Ok(q) = quantum_bytes(32) {\n                return entropy_mix(&q, &os); // quantum ⊕ os — entropy ≥ max of both\n            }\n            // fall through to OS-only on any QRNG failure\n        }\n        os\n    }\n\n    // Minimal no-dep HTTPS GET (ANU responds with a small JSON; we use reqwest only\n    // behind feature to avoid a heavy dep in the crypto crate). Blocking, std-only.\n    fn mini_get(url: &str) -> Result<String, String> {\n        // ponytail: a full TLS stack is out of scope for the crypto crate. The runtime\n        // should provide entropy; this std-only stub reaches the endpoint over plain TCP\n        // for localhost/testing only. PRODUCTION MUST use a TLS client (reqwest/rustls).\n        // Upgrade trigger: any real deployment — gate behind `qrng-tls` feature with reqwest.\n        use std::io::{Read, Write};\n        use std::net::TcpStream;\n        let host = "qrng.anu.edu.au:443";\n        let _ = (url, host); // referenced to silence unused in non-unix\n        let mut stream = TcpStream::connect("qrng.anu.edu.au:443").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n        let req = format!(\n            "GET /API/jsonI.php?length=32&type=uint8&size=1 HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: qrng.anu.edu.au\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n"\n        );\n        stream\n            .write_all(req.as_bytes())\n            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n        let mut resp = String::new();\n        stream\n            .read_to_string(&mut resp)\n            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n        // Split headers/body\n        let body = resp.split_once("\\r\\n\\r\\n").map(|x| x.1).unwrap_or(&resp);\n        Ok(body.to_string())\n    }\n\n    fn extract_array(s: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        let start = s.find("\\"data\\":[")? + 8;\n        let end = s[start..].find(']')? + start;\n        let inner = &s[start..end];\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        for part in inner.split(',') {\n            if let Ok(b) = part.trim().parse::<u8>() {\n                out.push(b);\n            }\n        }\n        Some(out)\n    }\n}\n\n}\n	2323	-1	-1		ca74bf47bd4d00f5231be8c1193352c10816969e3573f4ca89534e6bc9ef51c13843c5a2dec92abcd45593e89880ba3094a1ed2453e989aaf16ff226e7086ccec63e03d84577e0088da1205256fbedb1d15f692a2db9fc6dfec0a080d08a15dc65a7b6361ecbd29dc94088fc536c12b1451044263d8d0101370165f459b57c12

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/pq/x25519.rs	x25519 · 57 lines	//! X25519 (RFC 7748) — Curve25519 scalar multiplication: `no_std` shim.\n//!\n//! The primitive is the hand-rolled, `no_std`, zero-dependency Montgomery-ladder\n//! implementation in `dowiz_core::pq::x25519` (field arithmetic over `p = 2^255 - 19`\n//! in 5 × 51-bit limbs; branch-free ladder). Correctness is KAT-gated in core against\n//! RFC 7748 §6.1 (two vectors) + the iterated scalar-mult associativity check. This\n//! shim re-exports it so `crate::pq::x25519::x25519` call sites stay unchanged.\n//!\n//! A differential test cross-checks the hand-rolled core against the incumbent\n//! `curve25519-dalek` (`mul_clamped`) on a fixed deterministic vector set plus edge\n//! cases — the bootstrap validation that retired the dalek *runtime* dependency from\n//! the `pq` feature. dalek now lives only as a `[dev-dependencies]` guard, so\n//! `cargo tree -e no-dev --features pq` is dalek-free.\n\npub use dowiz_core::pq::x25519::x25519;\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::x25519;\n\n    /// Differential bootstrap: the hand-rolled core vs `curve25519-dalek`\n    /// `mul_clamped` on a deterministic vector set + edge cases. This is the\n    /// regression guard that pins the zero-dep reimplementation to the audited\n    /// incumbent; both clamp the scalar and mask the u-coordinate identically\n    /// (RFC 7748 §5).\n    #[test]\n    fn kat_x25519_differential_vs_dalek() {\n        use curve25519_dalek::montgomery::MontgomeryPoint;\n\n        let mut cases: Vec<([u8; 32], [u8; 32])> = Vec::with_capacity(20);\n        for i in 0..16u8 {\n            let mut k = [0u8; 32];\n            let mut u = [0u8; 32];\n            for j in 0..32 {\n                k[j] = i.wrapping_mul(37).wrapping_add(j as u8);\n                u[j] = i.wrapping_mul(91).wrapping_add(31u8.wrapping_sub(j as u8));\n            }\n            cases.push((k, u));\n        }\n        // Edge cases: zero scalar, all-ones scalar, zero u-coordinate (→ all-zero\n        // output), the RFC basepoint u = 9, and the high-bit-set u (bit 255 must be\n        // masked by both sides).\n        cases.push(([0u8; 32], [9u8; 32]));\n        cases.push(([0xff; 32], [9u8; 32]));\n        cases.push(([1u8; 32], [0u8; 32]));\n        cases.push(([0u8; 32], [0u8; 32]));\n        let mut high_bit_u = [9u8; 32];\n        high_bit_u[31] |= 0x80;\n        cases.push(([7u8; 32], high_bit_u));\n\n        for (k, u) in &cases {\n            let core = x25519(k, u);\n            let dalek = MontgomeryPoint(*u).mul_clamped(*k).0;\n            assert_eq!(core, dalek, "mismatch k={k:02x?} u={u:02x?}");\n        }\n    }\n}\n	2326	-1	-1		5a76bf67f2ef8321024350571de609a4141687e45154fd8aa9dd8a5bcceacb53d4cab596578ddafa71c9c429e48cfcead3f954c6692bcca693677e0db794e00ef67c6edd00b6520897093d0847fb6df05dfa462a29326febf0c233b0915907bde626c2f6a853dae5ed4a138541b48b1008bb48298d81ac46897bd4f0795a2ec0

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/trinary.rs	trinary · 68 lines	//! trinary.rs — std host shim (pure `Tri`/`TriMatrix`/matrix algebra live in\n//! `dowiz_core::trinary`; the two telemetry-recording methods that need\n//! `crate::telemetry_harvest::HarvestLedger` stay here as free functions).\n\npub use dowiz_core::trinary::*;\n\nuse crate::telemetry_harvest::HarvestLedger;\n\n/// Matrix multiplication with harvest telemetry recording (kernel-side seam:\n/// the no_std core has no `HarvestLedger`).\npub fn mul_with_telemetry(a: &TriMatrix, other: &TriMatrix, ledger: &mut HarvestLedger) -> TriMatrix {\n    let result = a.mul(other);\n    let success = result.stability_index() > 0.0;\n    let value = result.stability_index();\n    let cost = (a.rows * a.cols * other.cols) as f64;\n    ledger.record("trinary", "mat_mul", success, value, cost, crate::now_ms());\n    result\n}\n\n/// Kalman predict with harvest telemetry recording (kernel-side seam).\npub fn kalman_predict_with_telemetry(\n    a: &TriMatrix,\n    prev: &TriMatrix,\n    gain: f64,\n    ledger: &mut HarvestLedger,\n) -> TriMatrix {\n    let result = a.kalman_predict(prev, gain);\n    let success = result.stability_index() > 0.0;\n    let value = result.stability_index();\n    let cost = a.data.len() as f64;\n    ledger.record("trinary", "kalman_predict", success, value, cost, crate::now_ms());\n    result\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn trinary_mul_with_telemetry_emits_record() {\n        let mut ledger = HarvestLedger::new(100);\n        let mut a = TriMatrix::new(2, 2);\n        a.set(0, 0, Tri::True); a.set(0, 1, Tri::False);\n        a.set(1, 0, Tri::Unknown); a.set(1, 1, Tri::True);\n        let mut b = TriMatrix::new(2, 2);\n        b.set(0, 0, Tri::True); b.set(0, 1, Tri::Unknown);\n        b.set(1, 0, Tri::False); b.set(1, 1, Tri::True);\n        let _ = mul_with_telemetry(&a, &b, &mut ledger);\n        assert_eq!(ledger.len(), 1, "mul_with_telemetry must emit exactly 1 record");\n        let recs = ledger.records();\n        assert_eq!(recs[0].model, "trinary");\n        assert_eq!(recs[0].task, "mat_mul");\n        assert!(recs[0].success);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn trinary_kalman_with_telemetry_emits_record() {\n        let mut ledger = HarvestLedger::new(100);\n        let mut present = TriMatrix::new(1, 2);\n        present.set(0, 0, Tri::True); present.set(0, 1, Tri::False);\n        let mut past = TriMatrix::new(1, 2);\n        past.set(0, 0, Tri::True); past.set(0, 1, Tri::True);\n        let _ = kalman_predict_with_telemetry(&present, &past, 0.2, &mut ledger);\n        assert_eq!(ledger.len(), 1, "kalman_predict_with_telemetry must emit exactly 1 record");\n        let recs = ledger.records();\n        assert_eq!(recs[0].task, "kalman_predict");\n    }\n}\n	2332	-1	-1		2572bf6a308eb7b1cb47d4991b820319e1b49525ad71a469edc2a2dea1ffe83319851468cdc64487d17d5e0593c09820deae1b647348898a6ac0faa6df1ec3cc4a87541965387830c912f81af22bebcaf8f0882b312dc528dcc125a7504295b9a0b6d31635c9910df898ee44c75d25a964d15df496a2ced516f16c9529243575

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/chaos.rs	chaos · 337 lines	//! chaos.rs (kernel shim) — std-only thread-local plumbing for the fault-injection\n//! harness, over the `no_std` core in `dowiz_core::chaos`.\n//!\n//! The pure, deterministic schedule machinery — [`FaultPlan`], [`ChaosStore`],\n//! [`ChaosSite`], [`FaultInjection`], [`Trigger`], and the test-only\n//! [`FaultyStore`] — lives in `dowiz_core::chaos` and is re-exported below. This\n//! module keeps only the parts that need `std`: the `thread_local!` active plan\n//! and the `chaos_point!` seam-B macro (P-H / W-H1, Correspondence: one concept,\n//! one primitive).\n//!\n//! The whole module is gated `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "chaos"))]` at its `mod`\n//! declaration in `lib.rs`, so in a release build the macro expands to `()` and\n//! no chaos symbol reaches a production artifact.\n\npub use dowiz_core::chaos::*;\n\nthread_local! {\n    /// The active plan for seam-B (`chaos_point!`) calls on THIS thread. A\n    /// thread-local ⇒ parallel `cargo test` lanes cannot cross-inject (the\n    /// bulkhead, standard §2 item 11).\n    static ACTIVE_PLAN: core::cell::RefCell<Option<FaultPlan>> = const { core::cell::RefCell::new(None) };\n}\n\n/// Install a plan for seam-B injection on the current thread. Returns a guard\n/// that clears the thread-local on drop, so a test cannot leak its plan into a\n/// sibling test running on the same OS thread.\npub fn install_plan(plan: FaultPlan) -> ChaosGuard {\n    ACTIVE_PLAN.with(|p| *p.borrow_mut() = Some(plan));\n    ChaosGuard\n}\n\n/// RAII guard: clears the thread-local plan when dropped.\npub struct ChaosGuard;\n\nimpl Drop for ChaosGuard {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        ACTIVE_PLAN.with(|p| *p.borrow_mut() = None);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Seam B: consult the thread-local plan for `site` and, if armed, execute the\n/// fault's side effect. Compiles to `()` unless `cfg(any(test, feature =\n/// "chaos"))` (the `#[cfg]` on the whole module already guarantees that, but the\n/// arm is written so a downstream `#[cfg(not(...))]` shim would expand to `()`).\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! chaos_point {\n    ($site:expr) => {{\n        $crate::chaos::with_plan($site, |fault| match fault {\n            $crate::chaos::FaultInjection::PanicMidTransaction => {\n                panic!("chaos: F4 PanicMidTransaction at {:?}", $site);\n            }\n            // Other seam-B arms (DelayResponse) are handled by the driver that\n            // holds the claim; the inline point only performs the terminal ones.\n            _ => {}\n        });\n    }};\n}\n\n// Re-export so sibling modules can call it as `crate::chaos::chaos_point!`\n// (the `#[macro_export]` path alone is `$crate::chaos_point!`, which is\n// awkward from `token_bucket.rs`).\n#[cfg(any(test, feature = "chaos"))]\npub(crate) use chaos_point;\n\n/// Internal: run `f` with the thread-local fault for `site`, if any.\n#[doc(hidden)]\npub fn with_plan<F: FnOnce(FaultInjection)>(site: ChaosSite, f: F) {\n    let fault = ACTIVE_PLAN.with(|p| p.borrow_mut().as_mut().and_then(|plan| plan.fire(site)));\n    if let Some(fault) = fault {\n        f(fault);\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chaos_guard_clears_thread_local() {\n        {\n            let _g = install_plan(FaultPlan::new(\n                1,\n                1,\n                vec![(\n                    ChaosSite::BetweenDecideAndInsert,\n                    FaultInjection::PanicMidTransaction,\n                    Trigger::Always,\n                )],\n            ));\n            // Inside the scope the plan is armed.\n            let armed = ACTIVE_PLAN.with(|p| p.borrow().is_some());\n            assert!(armed, "plan installed within guard scope");\n        }\n        let cleared = ACTIVE_PLAN.with(|p| p.borrow().is_none());\n        assert!(cleared, "plan cleared on guard drop (no cross-test leak)");\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// P-H W-H4 — adversarial suite A1–A6. Each breaks an invariant and asserts the\n// system holds anyway (or surfaces a typed refusal). Every test has a named\n// RED arm (the defect class is inexpressible without the injection).\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod adversarial {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::event_log::{\n        AppendOutcome, ChainDefect, CommitError, EventLog, EventStore, MemEventStore, MeshEvent,\n        StoreError,\n    };\n    use crate::spool::Spool;\n\n    fn ev(prev: [u8; 32], actor: u8, seq: u64, payload: &[u8]) -> MeshEvent {\n        MeshEvent {\n            prev,\n            actor_pubkey: [actor; 32],\n            actor_seq: seq,\n            payload: payload.to_vec(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // A1 — Fault mid decide-fold under the drift-gate. The drift gate MUST fire\n    // BEFORE decide and BEFORE any store touch. RED arm: reorder the gate after\n    // `decide` (or stub insert_calls tracking) ⇒ assertion inexpressible/fails.\n    #[test]\n    fn a1_drift_gate_fires_before_store_touch() {\n        // Unstable adjacency (ρ>1): a 2-node fully-connected graph.\n        let adj: Vec<Vec<f64>> = vec![vec![0.0, 2.0], vec![2.0, 0.0]];\n        let mut log = EventLog::new(ChaosStore::new(\n            MemEventStore::new(),\n            FaultPlan::new(\n                0,\n                1,\n                vec![(\n                    ChaosSite::StoreInsert,\n                    FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail,\n                    Trigger::Always,\n                )],\n            ),\n        ));\n        let res = log.commit_after_decide_drift_gate(\n            ev([0u8; 32], 1, 1, b"mutate"),\n            &adj,\n            false, // intervention OFF ⇒ gate active\n            |_| Ok::<(), String>(()),\n        );\n        // The gate rejects on drift (Unstable ρ>1) BEFORE deciding or touching\n        // the store — so it is a Law-pole Rejected, and insert was NEVER called.\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res, Err(CommitError::Rejected(_))),\n            "drift gate must reject as Law-pole, not store fault; got {res:?}"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            log.store().insert_calls,\n            0,\n            "drift gate fires BEFORE any store touch (A1 ordering invariant)"\n        );\n        assert!(log.is_empty(), "nothing persisted under drift rejection");\n\n        // With intervention ON, the gate lifts: the injected sync-fail surfaces\n        // as the Store pole, never a fabricated commit.\n        let mut log2 = EventLog::new(ChaosStore::new(\n            MemEventStore::new(),\n            FaultPlan::new(\n                0,\n                1,\n                vec![(\n                    ChaosSite::StoreInsert,\n                    FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail,\n                    Trigger::Always,\n                )],\n            ),\n        ));\n        let res2 = log2.commit_after_decide_drift_gate(\n            ev([0u8; 32], 1, 1, b"mutate"),\n            &adj,\n            true, // intervention ON ⇒ safeties lifted\n            |_| Ok::<(), String>(()),\n        );\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res2, Err(CommitError::Store(StoreError::Sync(_)))),\n            "intervention lifts gate: accepted-but-lost-write ⇒ Store pole; got {res2:?}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // A2 — Panic mid-commit, then recovery. The commit path has no `chaos_point!`\n    // seam yet at `BetweenDecideAndInsert` (seam B is wired in token_bucket);\n    // here we prove the *content-addressing idempotency* recovery property that\n    // A2 relies on: re-committing the same event yields the identical id and is\n    // a Duplicate (structural no-op).\n    #[test]\n    fn a2_panic_mid_commit_recovers_idempotent() {\n        let mut log = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n        let e = ev([0u8; 32], 3, 1, b"Pending->Confirmed");\n        let (out, _) = log\n            .commit_after_decide(e.clone(), |_| Ok::<String, String>(String::new()))\n            .expect("first commit succeeds");\n        let id = match out {\n            AppendOutcome::Committed(id) => id,\n            _ => panic!("expected Committed"),\n        };\n        // A replay of the same content is a Duplicate (idempotent no-op).\n        let dup = log\n            .commit_after_decide(e, |_| Ok::<String, String>(String::new()))\n            .expect("replay does not re-run decide");\n        assert!(\n            matches!(dup.0, AppendOutcome::Duplicate(d) if d == id),\n            "replay is idempotent Duplicate under the same content-id"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // A3 — Silent corruption detection via verify_chain (F2). RED arm: run the\n    // same fixture without verify_chain ⇒ no observer goes red; the blindness\n    // IS the RED. We exercise the GREEN: a corrupted twin store fails verify_chain.\n    #[test]\n    fn a3_verify_chain_detects_corruption() {\n        // Build a clean 3-event chain.\n        let mut store = MemEventStore::new();\n        let e0 = ev([0u8; 32], 1, 1, b"genesis");\n        let id0 = e0.event_id();\n        store.insert(id0, e0).unwrap();\n        let e1 = ev(id0, 1, 2, b"step1");\n        let id1 = e1.event_id();\n        store.insert(id1, e1).unwrap();\n        let log = EventLog::new(store);\n        assert!(log.verify_chain().is_ok(), "clean chain verifies OK");\n\n        // Now a ChaosStore that persists a CORRUPTED twin of event 1 (F2).\n        let mut cstore = ChaosStore::new(\n            MemEventStore::new(),\n            FaultPlan::new(\n                0,\n                1,\n                vec![(\n                    ChaosSite::StoreInsert,\n                    FaultInjection::CorruptPayload {\n                        xor_mask: 0x01,\n                        byte_index: 0,\n                    },\n                    Trigger::Always,\n                )],\n            ),\n        );\n        cstore.corrupt_copy = true;\n        let mut clog = EventLog::new(cstore);\n        // Event 0 stored clean, event 1 stored corrupted (payload byte 0 flipped).\n        clog.append(ev([0u8; 32], 1, 1, b"genesis"))\n            .expect("e0 committed");\n        clog.append(ev(id0, 1, 2, b"step1"))\n            .expect("e1 committed (corrupted at rest)");\n        // verify_chain is the ONLY observer: it recomputes the id from the\n        // mutated body and finds a HashMismatch.\n        match clog.verify_chain() {\n            Err(ChainDefect::HashMismatch { .. }) => {}\n            other => panic!("expected HashMismatch, got {other:?}"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // A4 — Crash-storm on the spool. Deterministic driver: seeded plan\n    // interleaves claim/crash/reclaim/late-ack across N records. Asserts zero\n    // loss and strict FIFO among un-acked.\n    #[test]\n    fn a4_spool_crash_storm_zero_loss() {\n        use alloc::collections::BTreeSet;\n        let n = 1000u64;\n        let mut spool = Spool::new(n as usize);\n        for i in 0..n {\n            spool\n                .append(&format!("rec-{i}"))\n                .expect("append within capacity");\n        }\n        let mut already_crashed = BTreeSet::new();\n        let mut reclaimed = 0u64;\n        let mut delivered = 0u64;\n        let mut acked = 0u64;\n        // Up to 3 passes: first delivers all, second re-delivers crashed, third\n        // drains stragglers. Bounded so a logic error can't hang the suite.\n        for _ in 0..(n as usize * 3) {\n            let Some(rec) = spool.claim_next() else {\n                break;\n            };\n            delivered += 1;\n            let crashed_once = rec.id % 7 == 0 && !already_crashed.contains(&rec.id);\n            if crashed_once {\n                // Consumer crashed without ack ⇒ reclaim makes it claimable again.\n                assert!(\n                    spool.reclaim(rec.id),\n                    "reclaim must succeed for a claimed id"\n                );\n                already_crashed.insert(rec.id);\n                reclaimed += 1;\n            } else {\n                assert!(spool.ack(rec.id), "ack must succeed for a claimed id");\n                acked += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        // Every record acked exactly once; the crashed set was re-delivered and\n        // acked on its second pass. Nothing lost, nothing left pending.\n        let expected_crashed = (0..n).filter(|i| i % 7 == 0).count();\n        assert_eq!(spool.len(), 0, "every record eventually acked (zero loss)");\n        assert_eq!(\n            reclaimed, expected_crashed as u64,\n            "crash/reclaim path exercised (n/7 crashed once)"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            delivered,\n            n + reclaimed as u64,\n            "FIFO replays each crashed record exactly once"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(acked, n, "all n records acked in total");\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    fn a5_sustained_disk_full_degrade_closed() {\n        let mut log = EventLog::new(ChaosStore::new(\n            MemEventStore::new(),\n            FaultPlan::new(\n                0,\n                1,\n                vec![(\n                    ChaosSite::StoreInsert,\n                    FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail,\n                    Trigger::Always,\n                )],\n            ),\n        ));\n        for i in 0..10_000u64 {\n            let res = log.append(ev([0u8; 32], 1, i, b"durability-fault"));\n            assert!(\n                matches!(res, Err(StoreError::Sync(_))),\n                "every append is a typed Err under sustained disk-full; got {res:?}"\n            );\n            assert_eq!(log.len(), 0, "no in-memory advance on failed writes");\n        }\n    }\n}\n	2350	-1	-1		cb3eb75d9c0a92e1a30190cdd1765b2f4c7eb4a4ad50f603e946ea5f9d866b4159407583cfce4ecead5f002929d3d8a8ce634524756804abb07e761cdf86feced4af1469af169821d689380a17baa9e8f5587c0a2d14c549caa220a4508f871de832d6f3884bd08cd8bacc071f4d0f1164bb60661e998bc01fa97cf07b202c11

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/cpuid.rs	cpuid · 48 lines	//! cpuid.rs — std shim over the pure no_std core.\n//!\n//! The pure parsing (`CpuCaps`, [`detect_from`], [`parse_cache_size_kb`]) lives in\n//! `dowiz_core::cpuid` and is re-exported here. This shim adds the std `detect()`:\n//! reads `/proc/cpuinfo` + `/proc/meminfo` + the L3 cache size once (via `OnceLock`) and\n//! caches the snapshot — zero I/O after the first call.\n\npub use dowiz_core::cpuid::*;\n\nuse std::sync::OnceLock;\n\nstatic CAPS: OnceLock<CpuCaps> = OnceLock::new();\n\n/// Detect CPU capabilities once; subsequent calls return the cached result.\n///\n/// Safe to call from multiple threads — `OnceLock` guarantees exactly-one parse.\npub fn detect() -> &'static CpuCaps {\n    CAPS.get_or_init(detect_fresh)\n}\n\nfn detect_fresh() -> CpuCaps {\n    let cpuinfo = crate::vfs::read_to_string("/proc/cpuinfo").unwrap_or_default();\n    let meminfo = crate::vfs::read_to_string("/proc/meminfo").unwrap_or_default();\n    let l3 = crate::vfs::read_to_string("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache/index3/size")\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    detect_from(&cpuinfo, &meminfo, &l3)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn detect_returns_non_panicking() {\n        let caps = detect();\n        // On a real Linux host we will see real values; on wasm/non-Linux all zeros.\n        // Either way the call must not panic.\n        assert!(caps.avx2 || !caps.avx2); // always a valid bool\n        assert!(caps.cores > 0 || caps.cores == 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn detect_is_idempotent() {\n        let a = detect();\n        let b = detect();\n        assert_eq!(a as *const CpuCaps, b as *const CpuCaps, "OnceLock must return same &'static ref");\n    }\n}\n	2390	-1	-1		e3f6bb5f5fca2131e1cbe2cd41064e254192bdeeedf8f62a6945cab99b8526450546a183f7c6708fb542277b69d2976a05736da42b688549f5a3f32cc309b6bcdcaf4cc127938331cd85012917bbe1e9f8936c26850dc6ef921706c5f89715aff5e6fee590c913ad491f08ddc5695afcb1f7486ab48218f7070310e844fdfc01

Meta-tests verify the testing/evaluation infrastructure itself.\n//! Cross-tests exercise multiple modules together to validate\n//! the full stack (trinary × eigen × chronos × delta × enrich).\n//!\n//! These are NOT unit tests — they're integration tests that live in lib\n//! to exercise cross-module boundaries.\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use crate::trinary::{Tri, TriMatrix, Rgb};\n    use crate::trig::{Phase, Xyz};\n    use crate::eigen::decompose;\n    use crate::delta::{Delta, DeltaComparison, compare};\n    use crate::chronos::Chronos;\n    use crate::wave::spectral_fingerprint;\n    use crate::invert::backprop_from_deltas;\n    use crate::cross_bridge::CrossBridgeRegistry;\n    use alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n    // ─── META-1: Enrichment engine self-consistency ──────────────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn meta_enrichment_detects_known_intent() {\n        let intents = crate::prompt_enrich::detect_all_intents(\n            "fix compilation bug in rust module with idempotency invariants"\n        );\n        assert!(!intents.is_empty(), "must detect at least one intent");\n        let primary = intents[0].0;\n        assert!(\n            primary == The clock-stamped entry points (`GossipMessage::new`, `GossipBus::publish`,\n//! `GossipNode::publish`) are wrapped here as free functions that stamp\n//! `crate::now_ms()`.\n\npub use dowiz_core::gossip::*;\n\n/// `GossipMessage::new` stamped with the current wall clock.\npub fn message_new(topic: GossipTopic, payload: Vec<u8>, seq: u64) -> GossipMessage {\n    GossipMessage::new(topic, payload, seq, crate::now_ms())\n}\n\n/// `GossipBus::publish` stamped with the current wall clock.\npub fn publish_now(bus: &mut GossipBus, topic: GossipTopic, payload: &[u8]) {\n    bus.publish(topic, payload, crate::now_ms());\n}\n\n/// `GossipNode::publish` stamped with the current wall clock.\npub fn node_publish(node: &GossipNode, bus: &mut GossipBus, topic: GossipTopic, payload: &[u8]) {\n    node.publish(bus, topic, payload, crate::now_ms());\n}\n	2416	-1	-1		fa37fa4f9e23293ca09f016588b4ff8f5c368d56c559a7efe35c2a2660d7e9e57c7981f302da6e5fe673585d2956953a1be14ba615840c3f11f4d220acf43adfb4b61d90a8dbf152c7a0495806aaffb0e1114c0ace9ae5cf9908ca54a2019161b8f6669b77599368f4b0829d37411014e5f8a9b15e7118038c1020843a307a1a

## 2495 · /root/dowiz/kernel/src/ct_gate.rs · LongTerm

Summary: ct_gate · 125 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/ct_gate.rs	ct_gate · 125 lines	//! ct_gate.rs — std host shim (pure `ct_eq`/`Stats`/`welch_t` live in\n//! `dowiz_core::ct_gate`; the `std::time::Instant` timing harness stays here).\n//!\n//! `time_block` / `measure_leakage` sample a comparator under `Instant` — the\n//! wall-clock seam the no_std core cannot hold. The planted-leak dudect\n//! self-test (`dudect_gate_detects_planted_leak_and_passes_ct_eq`) is the\n//! load-bearing CI gate; run in release via `scripts/hardening-gate.sh` step E.\n\npub use dowiz_core::ct_gate::*;\n\nuse core::hint::black_box;\nuse std::time::Instant;\n\n/// Time `batch` invocations of a nullary closure, returning the average per-call nanoseconds.\n/// `black_box` on the accumulator defeats dead-code elimination of the measured work.\n#[inline]\nfn time_block<F: Fn() -> bool>(f: &F, batch: usize) -> f64 {\n    let t0 = Instant::now();\n    let mut acc = false;\n    for _ in 0..batch {\n        acc ^= black_box(f());\n    }\n    black_box(acc);\n    t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64 / batch as f64\n}\n\n/// Measure timing leakage of comparator `cmp` between two fixed input classes, returning |Welch t|.\n///\n/// `class_a`/`class_b` are `(lhs, rhs)` byte-slice pairs. The two classes are measured **interleaved**\n/// and the interleave order flips every round, so slow environmental drift (frequency scaling, cache\n/// warmup) contaminates both classes equally and cancels out of the difference of means. Inputs are\n/// fed through `black_box` so the optimizer cannot constant-fold a fixed-input comparator away.\npub fn measure_leakage<F>(\n    class_a: (&[u8], &[u8]),\n    class_b: (&[u8], &[u8]),\n    cmp: F,\n    rounds: usize,\n    batch: usize,\n) -> f64\nwhere\n    F: Fn(&[u8], &[u8]) -> bool,\n{\n    let run_a = || cmp(black_box(class_a.0), black_box(class_a.1));\n    let run_b = || cmp(black_box(class_b.0), black_box(class_b.1));\n\n    // Warm up caches / branch predictors before the timed rounds.\n    for _ in 0..batch {\n        black_box(run_a());\n        black_box(run_b());\n    }\n\n    let mut sa = Stats::default();\n    let mut sb = Stats::default();\n    for r in 0..rounds {\n        if r % 2 == 0 {\n            sa.push(time_block(&run_a, batch));\n            sb.push(time_block(&run_b, batch));\n        } else {\n            sb.push(time_block(&run_b, batch));\n            sa.push(time_block(&run_a, batch));\n        }\n    }\n    welch_t(&sa, &sb).abs()\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// PLANTED LEAK (test-only): see the core module docs; duplicated here for the timing harness.\n    fn naive_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        if a.len() != b.len() {\n            return false;\n        }\n        for i in 0..a.len() {\n            if a[i] != b[i] {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n        true\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    #[ignore = "timing self-test; run in release by scripts/hardening-gate.sh step E"]\n    fn dudect_gate_detects_planted_leak_and_passes_ct_eq() {\n        let equal_l = [0u8; 256];\n        let equal_r = [0u8; 256];\n        let diff_l = [0u8; 256];\n        let mut diff_r = [0u8; 256];\n        diff_r[0] = 1;\n        let class_a = (&equal_l[..], &equal_r[..]);\n        let class_b = (&diff_l[..], &diff_r[..]);\n\n        const ROUNDS: usize = 300;\n        const BATCH: usize = 4096;\n\n        let leak_t = (0..3)\n            .map(|_| measure_leakage(class_a, class_b, naive_eq, ROUNDS, BATCH))\n            .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);\n        assert!(\n            leak_t >= T_THRESHOLD,\n            "PLANTED LEAK NOT DETECTED: naive_eq |t|={leak_t:.2} < {T_THRESHOLD} — gate is blind"\n        );\n\n        let ct_t = (0..5)\n            .map(|_| measure_leakage(class_a, class_b, ct_eq, ROUNDS, BATCH))\n            .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);\n\n        assert!(\n            leak_t >= 3.0 * ct_t,\n            "harness failed to SEPARATE leaky from constant-time: leak |t|={leak_t:.2}, ct |t|={ct_t:.2} (need >= 3x)"\n        );\n\n        let verdict = if ct_t < T_THRESHOLD {\n            format!("ct_eq |t|={ct_t:.2} (PASS, < {T_THRESHOLD})")\n        } else {\n            format!("ct_eq |t|={ct_t:.2} (elevated under load; separation proof still holds)")\n        };\n        println!(\n            "dudect self-test PASS: planted-leak naive_eq |t|={leak_t:.1} (DETECTED, >= {T_THRESHOLD}); \\\n             {verdict}; separation {:.1}x (>= 3x required)",\n            leak_t / ct_t.max(1e-9)\n        );\n    }\n}\n	2496	-1	-1		93b3b76f39db5771130b35cb71b39a21c1deb4e5ad72f56ee968a28a817fe4f171c03149d7cd2a0e8f53473fb0d873bacc2b392c50288de934686a0c66978e0efdce68f9df331a21d58f911b66df8dd1786bfd6e295c96e29c0691945489a51eb800c7459fcf128260034f151e7805c58c18c4adde739cad806cdcf269342db0

## 2522 · /root/dowiz/kernel/src/isolation/microvm.rs · LongTerm

Summary: microvm · 99 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/isolation/microvm.rs	microvm · 99 lines	//! Host-capability probe for the microVM isolation tier (DK-06 / MV-04) — std side.\n//!\n//! The pure value types (`SandboxTier`, `AdapterRejected`) and the fail-closed\n//! `register_adapter` seam live in `dowiz_core::isolation::microvm`. This module\n//! supplies the real std host probe (reads `/dev/kvm` + `/proc/cpuinfo`) and installs\n//! it via [`set_kvm_probe`].\n//!\n//! The probe is intentionally cheap, offline, and std-only (no new crates). Real\n//! Firecracker/Kata boot is a follow-up behind this probe (DK-06 form), gated by the\n//! boolean this module advertises.\n\npub use dowiz_core::isolation::microvm::{\n    register_adapter, set_kvm_probe, AdapterRejected, SandboxTier,\n};\n\n/// Probe whether the host can back a microVM with hardware virtualization.\n///\n/// True only when BOTH hold:\n/// 1. `/dev/kvm` exists (KVM device node present), AND\n/// 2. the CPU advertises virtualization extensions (`vmx` on Intel, `svm` on AMD)\n///    in `/proc/cpuinfo`.\npub fn kvm_available() -> bool {\n    has_kvm_device() && has_vmx_or_svm()\n}\n\n/// Whether a native (`native-process`) adapter may be accepted on this host.\npub fn can_accept_native_adapter() -> bool {\n    kvm_available()\n}\n\n/// Install the std KVM probe so the core's fail-closed `register_adapter`\n/// reflects the real host capability. Idempotent; call once at runtime startup.\n/// Until this runs, `register_adapter("native-process")` fails closed (refuses),\n/// which is the safe default.\npub fn init() {\n    set_kvm_probe(kvm_available);\n}\n\n/// `/dev/kvm` present on the host?\nfn has_kvm_device() -> bool {\n    std::path::Path::new("/dev/kvm").exists()\n}\n\n/// CPU advertises hardware virtualization (`vmx` Intel / `svm` AMD)?\nfn has_vmx_or_svm() -> bool {\n    match crate::vfs::read_to_string("/proc/cpuinfo") {\n        Ok(contents) => contents\n            .split_whitespace()\n            .any(|tok| tok == "vmx" || tok == "svm"),\n        Err(_) => false,\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn r1_kvm_unavailable_on_this_host() {\n        assert!(!kvm_available(), "this host is expected to have NO /dev/kvm and NO vmx/svm; fail-closed posture requires false");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn r2_native_process_refused_without_kvm() {\n        // No probe installed in this test process → core seam fails closed.\n        let res = register_adapter("native-process");\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res, Err(AdapterRejected { reason: _ })),\n            "native-process adapter MUST be refused on a host without KVM; got {:?}",\n            res\n        );\n        if let Err(rej) = res {\n            assert_eq!(rej.reason.contains("isolate"), true);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn r3_wasm_component_accepted() {\n        assert_eq!(register_adapter("wasm-component"), Ok(()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn r4_cannot_accept_native_adapter_without_kvm() {\n        assert!(!can_accept_native_adapter());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn r5_unknown_execution_refused() {\n        assert!(register_adapter("mystery-runtime").is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn invariant_sandbox_tier_distinct() {\n        assert_ne!(\n            SandboxTier::WasmComponent,\n            SandboxTier::NativeProcessRequiresKvm\n        );\n    }\n}\n	2523	-1	-1		4fe63fd4f5436b75482a9a1509b2d2000df28f5e35d414acc94bfe469047c04360626421e2e557cbe542b3296994d56ccf714c2db36ce80a78e7fa4db71cdcd60fbbca8dc1e60100d9cc380895d93d99f7ef66222cb75d98fd94adee79c5854b28e53633f6fb50fc453d0e531e08e6f50937c0ee380501e3079d1e6d44437c59
```

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/fdr/cost_oracle.rs	cost_oracle · 94 lines	//! `fdr/cost_oracle.rs` — std shim over the pure no_std core.\n//!\n//! The classification ([`CostBucket`]/[`DecisionSurface`]/[`classify`]) and the runtime\n//! counters ([`record_group_commit`]/[`snapshot`]/…) live in `dowiz_core::fdr::cost_oracle`\n//! and are re-exported here. This shim adds ONLY the std ring round-trip test — the\n//! recoverable-from-ring oracle of the parent spec (needs a real `FdrRing`).\n\npub use dowiz_core::fdr::cost_oracle::*;\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::fdr::ring;\n    use crate::fdr::schema::{fdr_event_stamp, Kind, StampPolicy};\n    use dowiz_core::fdr::Level;\n\n    fn tmp_ring(tag: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {\n        let d = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n            "cost_oracle_ring_{}_{}_{}",\n            tag,\n            std::process::id(),\n            crate::typed_metrics::mono_now_ns()\n        ));\n        let _ = crate::vfs::create_dir_all(&d);\n        d\n    }\n\n    // Item 67/68 acceptance (parent spec): the runtime counters are recoverable from the FDR ring\n    // after the call — a genuine A/B-segment ring round-trip, not a mocked string.\n    #[test]\n    fn cost_oracle_counters_recoverable_from_fdr_ring() {\n record_crypto_latency(637);\n        let snap = snapshot();\n        assert_eq!(snap.group_commit_barriers, 1);\n        assert_eq!(snap.group_commit_inserts, 64);\n
