```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/fdr/macros.rs	macros · 96 lines	//! `fdr/macros.rs` — the `tracing`-grammar subset, as kernel-owned `macro_rules!`.\n//!\n//! Blueprint §4.1 decision: keep `tracing`'s exact macro grammar (fields-then-message,\n//! `%`=Display / `?`=Debug sigils, span-name-first) so every call-site change is a\n//! path-prefix rename (`tracing::info_span!` → `crate::fdr::info_span!`), NOT a semantic\n//! rewrite. Rejected: a `[patch]` facade literally named `tracing` (hides the cutover from\n//! `grep`); a hand-rolled `#[instrument]` proc-macro (would itself pull `syn`/`quote`,\n//! defeating the item).\n//!\n//! Macros are `#[macro_export]`ed (hoisted to crate root as `fdr_*`) and re-exported under\n//! the `fdr::` path by `mod.rs` (`pub use crate::fdr_info_span as info_span;` …), so both\n//! `crate::fdr::info_span!` (internal) and `dowiz_kernel::fdr::info_span!` (integration\n//! tests) resolve. The `fdr_*` root names are an implementation detail; call sites use the\n//! `fdr::` path.\n//!\n//! Accepted grammar losses (blueprint §5 step 3, nothing in the repo uses them): the\n//! `RUST_LOG` per-target filter grammar (only level-filtering via `DOWIZ_LOG`), span\n//! hierarchy/context propagation (the incumbent layer was already single-span).\n\n/// Internal field-list muncher (do not call directly). Accumulates `k = %v` / `k = ?v` /\n/// `k = v` fields into `$vec`, then emits with the trailing message expr. Separate literal\n/// `%`/`?` arms (not `$(:tt)?`) avoid the local-ambiguity the optional-sigil form hits.\n#[macro_export]\n#[doc(hidden)]\nmacro_rules! __fdr_munch {\n    ($lvl:expr, $vec:ident, [$k:ident = % $val:expr, $($rest:tt)*]) => {\n        $vec.push((stringify!($k), format!("{}", $val)));\n        $crate::__fdr_munch!($lvl, $vec, [$($rest)*]);\n    };\n    ($lvl:expr, $vec:ident, [$k:ident = ? $val:expr, $($rest:tt)*]) => {\n        $vec.push((stringify!($k), format!("{:?}", $val)));\n        $crate::__fdr_munch!($lvl, $vec, [$($rest)*]);\n    };\n    ($lvl:expr, $vec:ident, [$k:ident = $val:expr, $($rest:tt)*]) => {\n        $vec.push((stringify!($k), format!("{}", $val)));\n        $crate::__fdr_munch!($lvl, $vec, [$($rest)*]);\n    };\n    // Terminal: trailing message expression.\n    ($lvl:expr, $vec:ident, [$msg:expr $(,)?]) => {\n        $crate::fdr::emit_event($lvl, $msg, &$vec);\n    };\n    // Terminal: no message (fields-only, or empty).\n    ($lvl:expr, $vec:ident, []) => {\n        $crate::fdr::emit_event($lvl, "", &$vec);\n    };\n}\n\n/// `fdr::event!(level, k = v, …, "message")` — the general event macro. Evaluates its\n/// arguments and emits ONLY when a sink is installed and `level` passes (the disabled\n/// fast path is a single relaxed atomic load — matching `tracing`'s dispatch-check cost —\n/// and takes NO clock, so the `wasm32` `Instant`/`SystemTime` panic is never reached).\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! fdr_event {\n    ($lvl:expr, $($rest:tt)*) => {{\n        if $crate::fdr::event_enabled($lvl) {\n            #[allow(unused_mut)]\n            let mut __fdr_v: $crate::alloc::vec::Vec<(&'static str, $crate::alloc::string::String)> =\n                $crate::alloc::vec::Vec::new();\n            $crate::__fdr_munch!($lvl, __fdr_v, [$($rest)*]);\n        }\n    }};\n}\n\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! fdr_error {\n    ($($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::fdr_event!($crate::fdr::Level::Error, $($rest)*) };\n}\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! fdr_warn {\n    ($($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::fdr_event!($crate::fdr::Level::Warn, $($rest)*) };\n}\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! fdr_info {\n    ($($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::fdr_event!($crate::fdr::Level::Info, $($rest)*) };\n}\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! fdr_debug {\n    ($($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::fdr_event!($crate::fdr::Level::Debug, $($rest)*) };\n}\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! fdr_trace {\n    ($($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::fdr_event!($crate::fdr::Level::Trace, $($rest)*) };\n}\n\n/// `fdr::info_span!(name, k = %v, …)` → a [`crate::fdr::SpanHandle`]; `.entered()` yields a\n/// guard whose `Drop` reports the span's wall-clock duration to the observer (and, if a\n/// ring sink is installed, writes a `span_close` FDR record). Span FIELDS have no machine\n/// consumer (only the span NAME reaches `metric.jsonl`) and are intentionally not captured\n/// here — this keeps the hot path (`place_order`) allocation-free and takes NO clock until\n/// `.entered()`, where the `Instant` is gated off `wasm32` entirely.\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! fdr_info_span {\n    ($name:expr $(, $($rest:tt)*)?) => {{\n        $crate::fdr::SpanHandle::new($name)\n    }};\n}\n	2532	-1	-1		7f7d1853c21eb882284fb0c5bb3ddb0f4437bce47b50b3c0df3a5949abd4aa5f917b9d9d4463bb06dde3405d2db4966b4b31272591a3e66c9d667904c305a7ce84d823222564184bf425624af0bba88dd318dc12ec73d14ad830dab7e04f970d8c41e396434b38f47e02966fb26e4fbc6474c16fdfa1214ebf0ba8cec9b6adc2
```

## 2634 · /root/dowiz/kernel/src/fdr/mod.rs · LongTerm

Summary: mod · 1201 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/fdr/mod.rs	mod · 1201 lines	//! `fdr` — the kernel's flight-data recorder: the hand-rolled logger AND the durable\n//! post-mortem ring, sharing one event buffer (synthesis §5). This module is the terminal\n//! state of the `tracing` / `tracing-subscriber` retirement (roadmap items 4+29).\n//!\n//! # Why this exists (dependency-replacement ruling — procedure §2, steps 1–5)\n//!\n//! Recorded here per `PROCEDURE-DEPENDENCY-REPLACEMENT-STANDING-2026-07-19.md` step 9(i),\n//! and in full in `docs/design/BLUEPRINT-ITEMS-04-29-logger-fdr-rewrite-2026-07-19.md`.\n//!\n//! 1. **Trigger:** the zero-dependency push (synthesis §0.1; roadmap §B items 4+29). The\n//!    item-1 CI gate's allowlist must shrink `{regex, tracing, tracing-subscriber}` →\n//!    `{regex}` in this change. (Item 5 later closed that last survivor: `{regex}` → `{}`\n//!    via the kernel-owned `retrieval::pattern` matcher — the kernel's default no-dev tree\n//!    is now ZERO external crates.)\n//! 2. **Sweep:** the entire `tracing` surface was ~14 API lines across 7 `kernel/` files\n//!    (nothing in `engine/`, `apps/`, `tools/`); 8 span names; `init_tracing` had ZERO\n//!    production callers; no `info!`/`warn!`/`error!` ever used; `env-filter`'s grammar\n//!    used by nobody.\n//! 3. **Edge, verified in-house:** what the pair actually gave this kernel — (a) macro\n//!    ergonomics; (b) span timing for 8 spans, via a `Layer` we had to deadlock-workaround\n//!    and that mis-measured nested spans; (c) a global dispatch check (~one atomic load) —\n//!    matched by `LEVEL` here; (d) a `fmt` dev output nobody ships. Cost, measured: 19\n//!    transitive crates (a full `proc-macro2`/`quote`/`syn` toolchain to serve 6 one-line\n//!    wrappers).\n//! 4. **In-kernel alternative compile-checked BEFORE the flip:** this module lands complete\n//!    with tests while `tracing` still present (commit 1/3); call sites flip only after\n//!    green (commit 2/3); deps removed last (commit 3/3).\n//! 5. **Terminal state (a) — removed outright.** Not an opt-in feature (that would keep the\n//!    `SpanMetricsLayer` fork alive behind a flag — the exact outcome the procedure warns\n//!    of); a logger is not a syscall/wire/ABI boundary.\n//!\n//! **What removal loses (honest, blueprint §5 step 3):** third-party tracing-ecosystem\n//! interop (today an empty set by construction of the zero-dep push); `#[instrument]`\n//! sugar; the `RUST_LOG` per-target filter grammar; span hierarchy/context propagation (no\n//! consumer — the incumbent layer was explicitly single-span). **Reopening trigger (step\n//! 10):** a real deployment requirement to export kernel telemetry to an external\n//! tracing/OpenTelemetry collector, OR a mandatory (non-opt-in) kernel dependency that\n//! needs a live tracing subscriber for its own diagnostics. Nothing else reopens it.\n//!\n//! # Intentional, fixed behavior divergences\n//! - **Nested spans are now measured correctly.** Each `SpanGuard` owns its own `t0`, so\n//!   an outer span is no longer silently dropped when an inner span is entered (the\n//!   incumbent `obs.rs` thread-local stamp clobbered the outer's start — deleted here).\n//! - **The `fmt` stderr format is NOT byte-reproduced.** It had zero machine consumers and\n//!   zero production callers; the byte-compat contract is the parsed artifacts only\n//!   (`metric.jsonl` / `alert.jsonl` / the markov CLI JSON), all golden-pinned.\n\n// Pure (alloc-only) submodules re-exported from the no_std core.\npub use dowiz_core::fdr::digital_twin;\npub use dowiz_core::fdr::footprint;\npub use dowiz_core::fdr::json;\npub mod cost_oracle; // std shim: re-export + the recoverable-from-ring round-trip test\npub mod pmu;\npub mod schema;\n\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub mod ring;\n\n/// Handle type for the optional durable FDR ring mirror used by callers (`breaker`,\n/// `inference::golden`) that want an `Option<Mutex<RingHandle>>` / `Option<&mut RingHandle>`\n/// field or parameter regardless of target. Real `ring::FdrRing` off wasm32; on wasm32\n/// (no real filesystem — `ring` is never compiled there, see the `ring` module doc) this is\n/// an uninhabited stand-in — an empty enum has no values, so nothing on wasm32 can ever\n/// construct one, meaning any `Option<RingHandle>` is provably always `None` there. This\n/// keeps caller struct/fn signatures identical across targets instead of forking them.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub type RingHandle = ring::FdrRing;\n#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]\npub enum RingHandle {}\n\n// ── Pure primitives re-exported from the no_std core ──────────────────────────────\n// The core owns [`Level`], the compile-time [`crc32`] table, the enable gates, and the\n// span-id minter. The kernel keeps only the std side (ring, sink, span timing, macros).\npub use dowiz_core::fdr::{\n    crc32, emit_event, event_enabled, next_span_id, set_emit_event_hook, set_level,\n    set_sink_active, sink_active, Level,\n};\n\n/// Emit ONE `Alarm` FDR record (the fault-evidence kind; fsynced on append by the durable\n/// ring — power-loss durable, `ring.rs:134`). No-op unless an FDR sink is installed, so\n/// callers may call unconditionally; the record materializes only where FDR is enabled.\n/// `struct_name` names the corrupted live struct (item 54 Safe-State evidence); `detail`\n/// carries the fault reason. Item 54's fail-closed path is the value — the record is the\n/// forensic side-effect.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn emit_alarm(struct_name: &str, detail: &str) {\n    sink::emit_alarm(struct_name, detail);\n}\n\n/// On `wasm32` no FDR sink is ever installed, so alarm emission is inert. Item 54's\n/// decision-plane CRC check STILL runs on wasm (it is the fail-closed path that matters);\n/// only the durable record is skipped there.\n#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]\npub fn emit_alarm(_struct_name: &str, _detail: &str) {}\n\nmod macros; // hoists `fdr_*` to crate root via #[macro_export]; re-exported below.\n\n// Re-export the macros under the `fdr::` path (both `crate::fdr::info_span!` internally\n// and `dowiz_kernel::fdr::info_span!` from integration tests resolve through these).\npub use crate::{\n    fdr_debug as debug, fdr_error as error, fdr_event as event, fdr_info as info,\n    fdr_info_span as info_span, fdr_trace as trace, fdr_warn as warn,\n};\n\nuse core::cell::RefCell;\nuse core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, OnceLock};\n\n// (Level, set_level, event_enabled, SINK_ACTIVE — re-exported from the no_std core above.)\n\n/// Is span timing active (an observer OR a sink is installed)? Governs whether\n/// `SpanHandle::entered` takes an `Instant`. Always `false` on `wasm32` (neither is ever\n/// installed there), so the hot-path span never touches the wasm-panicking clock.\n#[inline]\npub fn span_active() -> bool {\n    sink_active()\n        || GLOBAL_OBSERVER.get().is_some()\n        || TL_OBSERVER.with(|o| o.borrow().is_some())\n}\n\n// (next_span_id / SPAN_SEQ — re-exported from the no_std core above.)\n\n// ── Span observer (kernel-owned port of the tracing Layer hook) ─────────────────────\n\n/// The kernel-owned replacement for `tracing_subscriber::Layer`'s span hook. The P83\n/// `SpanMetricsObserver` (in `span_metrics/obs.rs`) implements this and folds the duration\n/// into the `metric.jsonl` log-bucket histogram — byte-identical to the incumbent.\npub trait SpanObserver: Send + Sync {\n    fn on_span_close(&self, name: &'static str, dur_us: u64);\n}\n\nstatic GLOBAL_OBSERVER: OnceLock<Arc<dyn SpanObserver>> = OnceLock::new();\n\nthread_local! {\n    /// Scoped (test) observer — mirrors the incumbent `set_default`/`DefaultGuard` pattern\n    /// (thread-local, reverts on guard drop), so `span_metrics_init_wire.rs`'s scoped tests\n    /// keep working without a process-global install.\n    static TL_OBSERVER: RefCell<Option<Arc<dyn SpanObserver>>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };\n}\n\n/// Install a process-global span observer (set-once, like the incumbent\n/// `set_global_default`). `Err(())` if one is already installed.\npub fn set_global_observer(obs: Arc<dyn SpanObserver>) -> Result<(), ()> {\n    GLOBAL_OBSERVER.set(obs).map_err(|_| ())\n}\n\n/// A scoped observer install that reverts on drop (the `init_scoped` equivalent).\n#[must_use = "the scoped observer is uninstalled when this guard is dropped"]\npub struct ObserverGuard {\n    prev: Option<Arc<dyn SpanObserver>>,\n}\n\nimpl Drop for ObserverGuard {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        let prev = self.prev.take();\n        TL_OBSERVER.with(|o| *o.borrow_mut() = prev);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Install `obs` as this thread's scoped observer, returning a guard that restores the\n/// previous one on drop.\npub fn set_scoped_observer(obs: Arc<dyn SpanObserver>) -> ObserverGuard {\n    let prev = TL_OBSERVER.with(|o| o.borrow_mut().replace(obs));\n    ObserverGuard { prev }\n}\n\n/// Route a span close to the thread-local observer first (test/scoped), else the global.\nfn notify_observer(name: &'static str, dur_us: u64) {\n    let handled = TL_OBSERVER.with(|o| {\n        if let Some(obs) = o.borrow().as_ref() {\n            obs.on_span_close(name, dur_us);\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n    });\n    if !handled {\n        if let Some(obs) = GLOBAL_OBSERVER.get() {\n            obs.on_span_close(name, dur_us);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Span handle / guard ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A span handle produced by `fdr::info_span!`. Cheap (just a `&'static str` + optional\n/// parent id); does NO work until `.entered()`.\npub struct SpanHandle {\n    name: &'static str,\n    /// Item 62: the causal parent's span id, if known. `None` = root (the `Absence::NoParent`\n    /// default). Cross-process edges (subprocess spawns, agent↔LLM) seed this via\n    /// `SpanHandle::with_parent`.\n    parent_span_id: Option<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl SpanHandle {\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn new(name: &'static str) -> Self {\n        SpanHandle {\n            name,\n            parent_span_id: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Item 62: construct a span handle with an explicit causal parent (cross-process\n    /// seeding). The parent's `span_id` was passed across the boundary (one `u64`), and\n    /// this child's root record will carry it as `parent_span_id: Value(parent_id)`\n    /// instead of `Absence::NoParent`.\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn with_parent(name: &'static str, parent_span_id: u64) -> Self {\n        SpanHandle {\n            name,\n            parent_span_id: Some(parent_span_id),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Enter the span, returning a guard whose `Drop` reports the elapsed wall-clock time.\n    /// The `Instant` is taken ONLY when span timing is active, and is gated off `wasm32`\n    /// entirely (blueprint §4.1 "wasm32 trap") — a naive always-stamp guard would break the\n    /// cdylib, since `Instant::now()` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn entered(self) -> SpanGuard {\n        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\n        let t0 = if span_active() {\n            Some(std::time::Instant::now())\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n        #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]\n        let t0: Option<std::time::Instant> = None;\n        // Item 62: mint a fresh span_id for this span; the parent was provided (or None = root).\n        let span_id = next_span_id();\n        SpanGuard {\n            name: self.name,\n            t0,\n            span_id,\n            parent_span_id: self.parent_span_id,\n            work: None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The span timing guard. On drop (when a timing was taken) it reports the duration to the\n/// observer and, if a ring sink is installed, writes a `span_close` FDR record.\npub struct SpanGuard {\n    name: &'static str,\n    t0: Option<std::time::Instant>,\n    /// Item 62: the span's own id and its causal parent's id.\n    span_id: u64,\n    parent_span_id: Option<u64>,\n    /// Item 58: optional workload counter carried on SpanClose. `None` on non-work spans\n    /// (byte-identical to pre-item-58).\n    pub work: Option<schema::Work>,\n}\n\nimpl Drop for SpanGuard {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\n        if let Some(t0) = self.t0 {\n            let dur_us = t0.elapsed().as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;\n            notify_observer(self.name, dur_us);\n            emit_span_close(self.name, dur_us, self.span_id, self.parent_span_id, self.work);\n        }\n        // On wasm32, `t0` is always `None` (see `entered`) and this Drop is inert.\n        #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]\n        let _ = &self.t0;\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Event / span-close emission (sink write path) ───────────────────────────────────\n\n// `emit_event` is re-exported from the no_std core (hook-routed). The sink registers its\n// emitter via `set_emit_event_hook` in `init` below; without a sink the call is a no-op.\n\n/// Emit a span-close FDR record to the ring sink (spans do NOT go to stderr — they go to\n/// the observer's `metric.jsonl` and, when durable, the ring).\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\nfn emit_span_close(name: &'static str, dur_us: u64, span_id: u64, parent_span_id: Option<u64>, work: Option<schema::Work>) {\n    sink::emit_span_close(name, dur_us, span_id, parent_span_id, work);\n}\n\n/// Emit ONE `Tuning`-kind FDR record carrying an autonomic gain-scheduling\n/// adjustment (roadmap item 21). No-op unless a sink is installed — so callers\n/// may emit unconditionally at zero default cost; the record materializes only\n/// where FDR is enabled. The `Kind::Tuning` variant is reserved for this use\n/// (schema.rs:211).\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn emit_tuning(name: &'static str, fields: &[(&'static str, String)]) {\n    sink::emit_tuning(name, fields);\n}\n#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]\npub fn emit_tuning(_name: &'static str, _fields: &[(&'static str, String)]) {}\n\n/// Emit ONE `Event`-kind FDR record carrying a classifier verdict string plus the\n/// window-bracketed [`pmu::PmuStamp`] companion delta (roadmap item 27, classifier-input\n/// half). No-op unless a sink is installed — so callers may bracket-and-emit\n/// unconditionally at zero default cost; the record materializes only where FDR is enabled.\n/// The classifier (`markov::analyze_detailed` / `spectral::classify_drift`) is unchanged:\n/// the PMU data rides ALONGSIDE the verdict on the same record, never as a classifier input.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn emit_verdict_pmu(name: &'static str, verdict: &str, pmu: pmu::PmuStamp) {\n    sink::emit_verdict(name, verdict, pmu);\n}\n\n/// Emit a subprocess-reap record to the FDR ring (item 61, gap G6). Carries the REAL\n/// measured wall duration + `wait4` rusage — never a fabricated 0. The record is P3-plane\n/// telemetry (named `subprocess_bridge`); it is recoverable from the FDR ring after the\n/// call (the red→green oracle reads it back). No-op unless a ring sink is installed.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn emit_subprocess_record(\n    cmd: &str,\n    success: bool,\n    wall_us: u64,\n    utime_us: Option<u64>,\n    stime_us: Option<u64>,\n    maxrss_kb: Option<u64>,\n    work_kind: Option<(schema::WorkloadKind, u64)>,\n) {\n    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\n    sink::emit_subprocess_record(cmd, success, wall_us, utime_us, stime_us, maxrss_kb, work_kind);\n    #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]\n    {\n        let _ = (cmd, success, wall_us, utime_us, stime_us, maxrss_kb, work_kind);\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Sink + init (non-wasm) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Configuration for [`init`].\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct FdrConfig {\n    /// Write event records to stderr (deterministic NDJSON, no ANSI).\n    pub stderr: bool,\n    /// If `Some`, install the durable A/B segment ring under this directory.\n    pub ring_dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,\n    /// Per-segment cap (bytes).\n    pub seg_cap: u64,\n    /// Level threshold.\n    pub level: Level,\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\nimpl Default for FdrConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        FdrConfig {\n            stderr: true,\n            ring_dir: None,\n            seg_cap: ring::DEFAULT_SEG_CAP,\n            level: Level::Info,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Install the FDR sink (replaces `init_tracing()`). Reads `DOWIZ_LOG` for the level when\n/// set. Idempotent-ish: a second call is a no-op (the sink is set-once, like the incumbent\n/// global subscriber). Never installed on `wasm32`.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn init(config: FdrConfig) -> Result<(), ()> {\n    let r = sink::init(config);\n    // Wire the no_std core's emit_event hook to this sink (set-once; the hook is what makes\n    // `crate::fdr::emit_event` / the `fdr_*!` macros reach stderr + the durable ring).\n    set_emit_event_hook(sink::emit_event);\n    // Item 48 (closure a): install the panic hook on the FDR init path. Harmless when no ring is configured (the Alarm append becomes\n    // a no-op — exactly like every other FDR emit).\n    install_panic_hook();\n    r\n}\n\n// ── Item 48: FDR blind-spot closure (panic forensics + liveness heartbeat) ──────────\n\nstatic PANIC_HOOK_INSTALLED: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);\n\n/// Item 48 (closure a): install a panic hook that emits ONE fsynced `Alarm` FDR record\n/// carrying the panic `message` + `location`, then CHAINS to any previous hook. Best-effort:\n/// errors are swallowed (like `emit_event`), so a panic-in-hook double-panic aborts — the OS\n/// retains whatever bytes reached the page cache. **NOT** a `#[panic_handler]` (this is a\n/// `std` kernel); uses `std::panic::set_hook`. Reuses the existing ring sink (which fsyncs\n/// `Alarm` at `ring.rs:134`), so closure (a) needs NO new durability code — just an emitter.\n/// Chains to the prior hook so a test harness's hook is not clobbered (blueprint §10\n/// DESIGN NOTE). Non-wasm only — matches the FDR write path (no sink is ever installed on wasm).\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn install_panic_hook() {\n    if PANIC_HOOK_INSTALLED.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {\n        return; // already installed.\n    }\n    let prev = std::panic::take_hook();\n    std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(move |info: &std::panic::PanicHookInfo| {\n        // Build the forensic payload BEFORE touching the sink (keep the hook panic-safe /\n        // allocation-light). A re-panic here aborts — acceptable; the OS keeps the page-cache\n        // bytes from the first append attempt.\n        let message = match info.payload().downcast_ref::<&str>() {\n            Some(s) => (*s).to_string(),\n            None => match info.payload().downcast_ref::<String>() {\n                Some(s) => s.clone(),\n                None => "<non-string panic payload>".to_string(),\n            },\n        };\n        let location = info\n            .location()\n            .map(|l| format!("{}:{}:{}", l.file(), l.line(), l.column()))\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| "<unknown location>".to_string());\n        sink::emit_panic_alarm(message, location);\n        // Chain to the previous hook (a harness-installed hook must not be clobbered).\n        prev(info);\n    }));\n}\n\n/// Item 48 (closure b): emit ONE `Heartbeat` FDR record carrying a monotonic `seq` + the\n/// caller-supplied `progress` counters. No-op unless a ring sink is installed (matches every other FDR emit).\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn emit_heartbeat(seq: u64, progress: &[(&'static str, String)]) {\n    sink::emit_heartbeat(seq, progress);\n}\n\n/// Item 48 (clean-shutdown interplay, blueprint §5 step 3): write the `CleanShutdown`\n/// marker so an external liveness check sees an orderly stop and raises NO false alarm.\n/// No-op when no ring sink is installed (matches every other FDR emit).\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn clean_shutdown() {\n    sink::clean_shutdown();\n}\n\n// ── Item 51: shadow-mode divergence telemetry ───────────────────────────────────\n//\n// ADVISORY, non-gating. On every decision where AI advice was present, the kernel\n// records whether the proposed action AGREED with the deterministic decision D — digests\n// ONLY (never full payloads), via one `Kind::ShadowDivergence` FDR record. A single `emit_shadow_divergence` call is the whole hook; it is a no-op unless an\n// FDR sink is installed, inheriting the FDR module's zero-default-cost posture.\n\n/// Truncated (8-byte) SHA3-256 digest, rendered as a lowercase hex string. Was-safe: uses\n/// `crate::event_log::sha3_256` (pure Rust, no wasm-gated primitive). Used by item 51's\n/// `d_digest` / `act_digest` fields — a minimal statistic, never the full payload.\npub fn shadow_digest(data: &[u8]) -> String {\n    let h = crate::event_log::sha3_256(data);\n    let mut s = String::with_capacity(16);\n    for b in &h[..8] {\n        s.push_str(&format!("{b:02x}"));\n    }\n    s\n}\n\n/// Emit ONE advisory `ShadowDivergence` FDR record. No-op unless a sink is installed — so\n/// callers may emit unconditionally at zero default cost; the record materializes only where\n/// FDR is enabled. `agree` is the verdict of `proposal.action == D`; `d_digest`/`act_digest`\n/// are truncated SHA3-256 digests of D and the proposed action (payloads are NEVER logged).\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn emit_shadow_divergence(\n    site: &'static str,\n    verdict: &str,\n    agree: bool,\n    d_digest: &str,\n    act_digest: &str,\n) {\n    sink::emit_shadow_divergence(site, verdict, agree, d_digest, act_digest);\n}\n#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]\npub fn emit_shadow_divergence(\n    _site: &'static str,\n    _verdict: &str,\n    _agree: bool,\n    _d_digest: &str,\n    _act_digest: &str,\n) {\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\nmod sink {\n    use super::schema::{fdr_event_stamp, Kind, StampPolicy};\n    use super::{ring, FdrConfig, Level};\n    use std::io::Write;\n    use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n    use std::sync::{Mutex, OnceLock};\n\n    pub struct Sink {\n        pub stderr: bool,\n        pub ring: Option<Mutex<ring::FdrRing>>,\n        pub seq: AtomicU64,\n    }\n\n    static SINK: OnceLock<Sink> = OnceLock::new();\n\n    pub fn init(config: FdrConfig) -> Result<(), ()> {\n        let level = std::env::var("DOWIZ_LOG")\n            .ok()\n            .and_then(|s| Level::from_env_str(&s))\n            .unwrap_or(config.level);\n        super::set_level(level);\n\n        let ring = match &config.ring_dir {\n            Some(dir) => match ring::FdrRing::open(dir.clone(), config.seg_cap) {\n                Ok(r) => Some(Mutex::new(r)),\n                Err(_) => None, // best-effort: a failed ring open never poisons the caller.\n            },\n            None => None,\n        };\n        let sink = Sink {\n            stderr: config.stderr,\n            ring,\n            seq: AtomicU64::new(0),\n        };\n        match SINK.set(sink) {\n            Ok(()) => {\n                super::set_sink_active(true);\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            Err(_) => Err(()), // already installed.\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn next_seq(s: &Sink) -> u64 {\n        s.seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)\n    }\n\n    pub fn emit_event(level: Level, msg: &str, fields: &[(&'static str, String)]) {\n        let s = match SINK.get() {\n            Some(s) => s,\n            None => return,\n        };\n        let seq = next_seq(s);\n        // Event-kind records use the CHEAP hw policy (blueprint §4.2 cost control — high\n        // frequency; joules-per-span is a consumer delta over the alarm-class stamps).\n        let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n            seq,\n            level,\n            Kind::Event,\n            msg.to_string(),\n            StampPolicy::Cheap,\n            fields.to_vec(),\n        );\n        let line = ev.to_json();\n        if s.stderr {\n            let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr(), "{line}");\n        }\n        if let Some(r) = &s.ring {\n            if let Ok(mut r) = r.lock() {\n                let _ = r.append(&ev);\n            }\n        }\n stime_us: Option<u64>,\n        maxrss_kb: Option<u64>,\n        work_kind: Option<(super::schema::WorkloadKind, u64)>,\n    ) {\n        let s = match SINK.get() {\n            Some(s) => s,\n            None => return,\n        };\n        let r = match &s.ring {\n            Some(r) => r,\n            None => return,\n        };\n        let seq = next_seq(s);\n        let mut fields: "utime_us",\n                utime_us\n                    .map(|v| v.to_string())\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "null".into()),\n            ),\n            (\n                "stime_us",\n ev.span_id = Some(super::next_span_id());\n        ev.parent_span_id = Some(super::schema::Reading::Unavailable(super::schema::Absence::NoParent));\n        if let Some((kind, count)) = work_kind {\n emit_span_close(name: &'static str, dur_us: u64, span_id: u64, parent_span_id: Option<u64>, work: Option<super::schema::Work>) {\n        let s = match SINK.get() {\n            Some(s) => s,\n fdr_event_stamp(\n            seq,\n            Level::Info,\n            Kind::SpanClose,\n            name.to_string(),\n            StampPolicy::Full,\n            vec![("dur_us", (ring.rs:134)\n    /// so it is power-loss durable for free — the panic forensic evidence survives even a\n    /// crash before the process unwinds. No-op when no sink is installed (matches every other FDR emit).\n    pub fn emit_panic_alarm(message: String, location: String) {\n        let s = match SINK.get() {\n            Some(s) => s,\n            None => return,\n        };\n        let seq = next_seq(s);\n        let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n            seq,\n            Level::Error,\n            Kind::Alarm,\n            "panic".to_string(),\n            StampPolicy::Full,\n            vec![("message", message), ("location", location)],\n        );\n        if s.stderr {\n            let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr(), "{}", ev.to_json());\n        }\n        if let Some(r) = &s.ring {\n            if let Ok(mut r) = r.lock() {\n                let _ = r.append(&ev); // Alarm ⇒ fsync inside append (ring.rs:134).\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Item 54 Safe-State fault evidence: emit ONE `Alarm` FDR record naming a corrupted\n    /// live struct (`name`) with the fault `detail`, fsynced via the durable ring (the ring\n    /// fsyncs on `Kind::Alarm`, `ring.rs:134` — power-loss durable). This is the sink-side\n    /// impl the `fdr::emit_alarm` facade (mod.rs:101) delegates to. No-op when no sink/ring\n    /// is installed.\n    pub fn emit_alarm(name: &str, detail: &str) {\n        let s = match SINK.get() {\n            Some(s) => s,\n            None => return,\n        };\n        let seq = next_seq(s);\n        // Alarms carry a FULL hw stamp (alarm-class, blueprint §4.2) for forensic value.\n        let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n            seq,\n            Level::Error,\n            Kind::Alarm,\n            name.to_string(),\n            StampPolicy::Full,\n            vec![("detail", detail.to_string())],\n        );\n        let line = ev.to_json();\n        if s.stderr {\n            let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr(), "{line}");\n        }\n        if let Some(r) = &s.ring {\n            if let Ok(mut r) = r.lock() {\n                let _ = r.append(&ev);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Item 48 (closure b): emit ONE `Heartbeat`-kind FDR record carrying a monotonic `seq`\n    /// + the caller-supplied `progress` counters. Cheap stamp policy (high-frequency; same\n    /// rationale as `Event`). The kernel provides ONLY the record + emit fn — cadence and\n    /// JUDGMENT live externally (systemd `WatchdogSec` / `hub_supervisor`). No-op when no\n    /// sink is installed (matches every other FDR emit).\n    /// Item 21 (roadmap §E): emit ONE `Tuning`-kind FDR record carrying an\n    /// autonomic gain-scheduling adjustment. Cheap stamp policy (high-frequency\n    /// self-tuning events). No-op when no sink is installed (matches every other\n    /// FDR emit).\n    pub fn emit_tuning(name: &'static str, fields: &[(&'static str, String)]) {\n        let s = match SINK.get() {\n        name.to_string(),\n            StampPolicy::Cheap,\n            fields.to_vec(),\n        );\n        if s.stderr {\n            let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr(), "{}", ev.to_json());\n        }\n        if let Some(r) = &s.ring {\n            if let Ok(mut r) = r.lock() {\n                let _ = r.append(&ev);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn emit_heartbeat(seq: u64, progress: &[(&'static str, String)]) {\n        let s = match SINK.get() {\n            Some(s) => s,\n            None => return,\n        };\n        let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n            seq,\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/fdr/pmu.rs	pmu · 684 lines	//! `fdr/pmu.rs` — PMU (performance-monitoring-unit) companion stamps for the kernel's\n//! two classifiers, `markov::Verdict` and `spectral::DriftClass` (roadmap item 27,\n//! classifier-INPUT half; blueprint `BLUEPRINT-ITEM-27-pmu-classifier-input-2026-07-19.md`).\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//!\n//! A [`PmuStamp`] is a sibling of [`super::schema::HwStamp`], built from the SAME\n//! [`Reading<T>`]/[`Absence`] machinery and the SAME raw-monotone-counters rule: the kernel\n//! emits raw counters only; deltas/IPC/miss-rates are a consumer concern (see\n//! [`PmuStamp::delta`] which is the one sanctioned exception — a bracketed before/after\n//! subtraction, still emitted as raw `u64` counts).\n//!\n//! It carries two tiers of signal:\n//!   * **Tier A** — zero-permission, always-available: the `rdtsc` reference-cycle counter\n//!     (one stable intrinsic) plus page-fault and context-switch counters from `/proc`.\n//!     These read real data on any Linux x86_64/aarch64 host with no capabilities.\n//!   * **Tier B** — true hardware PMU events (instructions, cpu-cycles, cache-misses,\n//!     branch-misses → IPC / miss-rates). The only zero-dependency access path is a\n//!     hand-rolled `perf_event_open(2)` raw syscall (no `libc`, no `perf-event` crate).\n//!     On a host with `kernel.perf_event_paranoid >= 3` (this deploy target reads **4**)\n//!     the syscall returns `EACCES` and every Tier-B field degrades to\n//!     `Unavailable(PermissionDenied)` — a greppable named absence, never a fabricated 0.\n//!\n//! # Plane doctrine (enforced, verbatim from blueprint §4.4)\n//!\n//! PMU values are nondeterministic by nature and live on the P3 forensic/display plane,\n//! exactly like FDR wall-clock timestamps: they are categorically excluded from every hash,\n//! signature, idempotency, or gate-verdict surface. Nothing here changes a `Verdict`, a\n//! `DriftClass`, a threshold, or any behavior. `analyze_detailed`/`classify_drift` stay\n//! byte-identical pure functions; the PMU stamp rides ALONGSIDE each verdict emission on the\n//! same [`super::schema::FdrEvent`] record (correlation is exact and free — same `seq`),\n//! recorded input, never a decision variable (that is the Tier-4 response half, gated on\n//! items 9 + 21). Diagnostic-grade; NO CI job is keyed to any PMU value.\n\nuse super::schema::{Absence, Reading};\n\n// PmuStamp (struct + write + delta) is pure — re-exported from the no_std core.\npub use dowiz_core::fdr::pmu::*;\n\n// ── Tier A readers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// `rdtsc`-equivalent reference-cycle counter. x86_64: the `_rdtsc` intrinsic; aarch64: the\n/// ARM generic-timer virtual counter (`CNTVCT_EL0`, the architectural analogue of rdtsc,\n/// readable from EL0 because Linux sets `CNTKCTL_EL1.EL0VTEN` for the VDSO). Other targets\n/// report a named absence (`NoPmuInterface`) rather than a fake 0.\n#[inline]\npub fn read_tsc() -> Reading<u64> {\n    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]\n    {\n        // SAFETY: `_rdtsc` reads the timestamp counter; no memory access, no fault path in\n        // user mode on this host (rdtsc/rdtscp advertised in cpuflags).\n        let v = unsafe { core::arch::x86_64::_rdtsc() };\n        Reading::Value(v)\n    }\n    #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]\n    {\n        // SAFETY: `mrs cntvct_el0` reads the virtual counter register; no memory access and\n        // no fault path in user mode on Linux (EL0VTEN is set for the VDSO).\n        let v: u64;\n        unsafe {\n            core::arch::asm!("mrs {}, cntvct_el0", out(reg) v);\n        }\n        Reading::Value(v)\n    }\n    #[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\n    {\n        Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NoPmuInterface)\n    }\n}\n\n/// `(minflt, majflt, nswap)` from `/proc/self/stat`. Uses the SAME robust `comm`-aware\n/// parse as `typed_metrics::ProcCpuSample` (`comm` field 2 may contain `)`, so split after\n/// the LAST `)`; the remaining whitespace fields are 3..N ⇒ index = field_number − 3:\n/// minflt=field10→7, majflt=field12→9, nswap=field36→33). Any read/parse failure is a\n/// named absence, never a fabricated 0.\nfn read_proc_stat_faults() -> (Reading<u64>, Reading<u64>, Reading<u64>) {\n    let stat = match crate::vfs::read_to_string("/proc/self/stat") {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            let a = io_absence(&e);\n            return (\n                Reading::Unavailable(a),\n                Reading::Unavailable(a),\n                Reading::Unavailable(a),\n            );\n        }\n    };\n    let after = match stat.rsplit(')').next() {\n        Some(a) => a,\n        None => {\n            return (\n                Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError),\n                Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError),\n                Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError),\n            )\n        }\n    };\n    let fields: Vec<&str> = after.split_whitespace().collect();\n    let get = |idx: usize| -> Reading<u64> {\n        match fields.get(idx).and_then(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok()) {\n            Some(v) => Reading::Value(v),\n            None => Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError),\n        }\n    };\n    (get(7), get(9), get(33))\n}\n\n/// `(voluntary, nonvoluntary)` context-switch counts from `/proc/self/status`.\nfn read_proc_ctxt_switches() -> (Reading<u64>, Reading<u64>) {\n    let status = match crate::vfs::read_to_string("/proc/self/status") {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            let a = io_absence(&e);\n            return (Reading::Unavailable(a), Reading::Unavailable(a));\n        }\n    };\n    let mut vol: Reading<u64> = Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError);\n    let mut nonvol: Reading<u64> = Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError);\n    for line in status.lines() {\n        if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("voluntary_ctxt_switches:") {\n            if let Some(v) = rest\n                .trim()\n                .split_whitespace()\n                .next()\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())\n            {\n                vol = Reading::Value(v);\n            }\n        } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches:") {\n            if let Some(v) = rest\n                .trim()\n                .split_whitespace()\n                .next()\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())\n            {\n                nonvol = Reading::Value(v);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    (vol, nonvol)\n}\n\n/// Map a filesystem [`crate::vfs::VfsError`] to the closest `Absence`.\nfn io_absence(e: &crate::vfs::VfsError) -> Absence {\n    match e {\n        crate::vfs::VfsError::NotFound => Absence::NonLinuxHost, // no /proc ⇒ not Linux\n        crate::vfs::VfsError::PermissionDenied => Absence::PermissionDenied,\n        _ => Absence::ReadError,\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Tier B: hand-rolled perf_event_open(2) plumbing ─────────────────────────────────\n//\n// Zero-dependency: no `libc`, no `perf-event` crate. A `#[repr(C)]` `perf_event_attr`\n// declared to the PERF_ATTR_SIZE_VER0 (64-byte) ABI, submitted through a raw `syscall`\n// instruction via `core::arch::asm!`. On failure the errno maps to a named `Absence`.\n// EACCES/EPERM (paranoid ≥ 1..4) ⇒ PermissionDenied; ENOENT/ENODEV/EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS ⇒\n// NoPmuInterface; anything else ⇒ ReadError. This host (`perf_event_paranoid = 4`) always\n// takes the PermissionDenied branch — that is correct, tested behavior, not a bug.\n\n/// The four hardware events we open, in `PmuStamp` Tier-B field order.\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\nconst HW_EVENTS: [u64; 4] = [\n    1, // PERF_COUNT_HW_INSTRUCTIONS\n    0, // PERF_COUNT_HW_CPU_CYCLES\n    3, // PERF_COUNT_HW_CACHE_MISSES\n    5, // PERF_COUNT_HW_BRANCH_MISSES\n];\n\n/// `perf_event_attr` to the VER0 (64-byte) ABI. Exactly 64 bytes; `size` is set to 64 so\n/// the running kernel treats trailing (zero) space as compatible.\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\n#[repr(C)]\n#[derive(Default)]\nstruct PerfEventAttr {\n    type_: u32,         // offset 0  — PERF_TYPE_HARDWARE = 0\n    size: u32,          // offset 4  — PERF_ATTR_SIZE_VER0 = 64\n    config: u64,        // offset 8  — the HW_EVENTS selector\n    sample_period: u64, // offset 16\n    sample_type: u64,   // offset 24\n    read_format: u64,   // offset 32\n    flags: u64,         // offset 40 — bitfield: bit0 disabled, bit5 exclude_kernel, bit6 exclude_hv\n    wakeup_events: u32, // offset 48\n    bp_type: u32,       // offset 52\n    config1: u64,       // offset 56  (total 64)\n}\n\n/// Linux syscall numbers for the PMU path (differ per arch).\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\nconst SYS_PERF_EVENT_OPEN: i64 = 298;\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\nconst SYS_READ: i64 = 0;\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\nconst SYS_CLOSE: i64 = 3;\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "aarch64"))]\nconst SYS_PERF_EVENT_OPEN: i64 = 241;\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "aarch64"))]\nconst SYS_READ: i64 = 63;\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "aarch64"))]\nconst SYS_CLOSE: i64 = 57;\n\n/// Raw 5-argument `syscall` (x86_64 Linux): number in `rax`, args in\n/// `rdi/rsi/rdx/r10/r8`, result in `rax`; the kernel clobbers `rcx` and `r11`.\n/// Returns the raw kernel result (negative = `-errno`).\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\n#[inline]\nunsafe fn syscall5(n: i64, a1: i64, a2: i64, a3: i64, a4: i64, a5: i64) -> i64 {\n    let ret: i64;\n    core::arch::asm!(\n        "syscall",\n        inlateout("rax") n => ret,\n        in("rdi") a1,\n        in("rsi") a2,\n        in("rdx") a3,\n        in("r10") a4,\n        in("r8") a5,\n        lateout("rcx") _,\n        lateout("r11") _,\n        options(nostack),\n    );\n    ret\n}\n\n/// Raw 5-argument `syscall` (aarch64 Linux): number in `x8`, args in `x0..=x4`,\n/// result in `x0`. Returns the raw kernel result (negative = `-errno`).\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "aarch64"))]\n#[inline]\nunsafe fn syscall5(n: i64, a1: i64, a2: i64, a3: i64, a4: i64, a5: i64) -> i64 {\n    let ret: i64;\n    core::arch::asm!(\n        "svc #0",\n        in("x8") n,\n        inlateout("x0") a1 => ret,\n        in("x1") a2,\n        in("x2") a3,\n        in("x3") a4,\n        in("x4") a5,\n        options(nostack),\n    );\n    ret\n}\n\n/// Map a kernel `-errno` result to an `Absence` (blueprint §4.2 errno table).\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\nfn errno_absence(ret: i64) -> Absence {\n    match -ret {\n        1 | 13 => Absence::PermissionDenied, // EPERM / EACCES — perf_event_paranoid\n        2 | 19 | 38 | 95 => Absence::NoPmuInterface, // ENOENT/ENODEV/ENOSYS/EOPNOTSUPP\n        _ => Absence::ReadError,\n    }\n}\n\n/// A live perf fd; closes on drop.\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\nstruct PerfFd(i32);\n\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\nimpl Drop for PerfFd {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        // SAFETY: close(2) on our own fd.\n        unsafe {\n            let _ = syscall5(SYS_CLOSE, self.0 as i64, 0, 0, 0, 0);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Open one hardware-event counter for THIS process (`pid=0`), any CPU (`cpu=-1`), no\n/// group (`group_fd=-1`), running (not disabled). `Ok(fd)` or the errno-derived `Absence`.\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\nfn perf_open_one(config: u64) -> Result<PerfFd, Absence> {\n    const PERF_FLAG_FD_CLOEXEC: i64 = 8;\n    // exclude_kernel (bit5) | exclude_hv (bit6). `disabled` left 0 ⇒ counter runs at open.\n    const FLAGS: u64 = (1 << 5) | (1 << 6);\n    let attr = PerfEventAttr {\n        type_: 0, // PERF_TYPE_HARDWARE\n        size: 64, // PERF_ATTR_SIZE_VER0\n        config,\n        flags: FLAGS,\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    // SAFETY: `&attr` points at a live 64-byte repr(C) struct for the duration of the call;\n    // all other args are plain integers. The syscall reads only within `size` bytes.\n    let ret = unsafe {\n        syscall5(\n            SYS_PERF_EVENT_OPEN,\n            &attr as *const PerfEventAttr as i64,\n            0,  // pid = self\n            -1, // cpu = any\n            -1, // group_fd = none\n            PERF_FLAG_FD_CLOEXEC,\n        )\n    };\n    if ret < 0 {\n        Err(errno_absence(ret))\n    } else {\n        Ok(PerfFd(ret as i32))\n    }\n}\n\n/// `read(2)` a running counter fd into a `u64`. Any short/failed read is a named absence.\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\nfn perf_read(fd: &PerfFd) -> Reading<u64> {\n    let mut val: u64 = 0;\n    // SAFETY: read(2) into an 8-byte owned stack slot; `count = 8`.\n    let n = unsafe { syscall5(SYS_READ, fd.0 as i64, &mut val as *mut u64 as i64, 8, 0, 0) };\n    if n == 8 {\n        Reading::Value(val)\n    } else if n < 0 {\n        Reading::Unavailable(errno_absence(n))\n    } else {\n        Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The Tier-B counter station: opens the four fds ONCE (on construction) and caches the\n/// errno-derived absence per counter so a blocked host is not re-probed every sample\n/// (cost + log-noise control, blueprint §4.2). On non-Linux / non-x86_64 builds every\n/// counter is a compile-time `NoPmuInterface`.\npub struct PmuStation {\n    #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\n    fds: [Result<PerfFd, Absence>; 4],\n}\n\nimpl PmuStation {\n    /// Open the Tier-B counters once. Tier A needs no setup (sampled fresh each call).\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\n        {\n            PmuStation {\n                fds: HW_EVENTS.map(perf_open_one),\n            }\n        }\n        #[cfg(not(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64"))))]\n        {\n            PmuStation {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Read one Tier-B counter (or its cached absence). Non-Linux/x86_64 ⇒ `NoPmuInterface`.\n    #[allow(unused_variables)]\n    fn tier_b(&self, i: usize) -> Reading<u64> {\n        #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\n        {\n            match &self.fds[i] {\n                Ok(fd) => perf_read(fd),\n                Err(a) => Reading::Unavailable(*a),\n            }\n        }\n        #[cfg(not(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64"))))]\n        {\n            Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NoPmuInterface)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Take a full stamp: Tier A fresh (rdtsc + two `/proc` reads), Tier B from the\n    /// once-opened counters.\n    pub fn sample(&self) -> PmuStamp {\n        let (minflt, majflt, nswap) = read_proc_stat_faults();\n        let (vol, nonvol) = read_proc_ctxt_switches();\n        PmuStamp {\n            tsc_cycles: read_tsc(),\n            minflt,\n            majflt,\n            nswap,\n            vol_ctxt_switches: vol,\n            nonvol_ctxt_switches: nonvol,\n            hw_instructions: self.tier_b(0),\n            hw_cpu_cycles: self.tier_b(1),\n            hw_cache_misses: self.tier_b(2),\n            hw_branch_misses: self.tier_b(3),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Window-bracket a classification-relevant call: sample before, run `f`, sample after,\n    /// return `f`'s result together with the absence-propagating PMU delta. The classifier\n    /// (`analyze_detailed`/`classify_drift`) is invoked EXACTLY as before — `f` is a plain\n    /// closure over it, its signature and behavior untouched.\n    pub fn bracket<T>(&self, f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> (T, PmuStamp) {\n        let start = self.sample();\n        let out = f();\n        let end = self.sample();\n        (out, PmuStamp::delta(start, end))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for PmuStation {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    #[cfg(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64"))]\n    fn tier_a_reads_real_nonzero_counters() {\n        // rdtsc must advance across two reads, and the /proc fault/ctxt counters must parse\n        // to real Values on this Linux x86_64 host — NOT stub zeros, NOT absences.\n        let s1 = read_tsc();\n        // Do a little work so the second tsc read is strictly greater.\n        let mut acc = 0u64;\n        for i in 0..10_000u64 {\n            acc = acc.wrapping_add(i.wrapping_mul(2654435761));\n        }\n        core::hint::black_box(acc);\n        let s2 = read_tsc();\n        match (s1, s2) {\n            (Reading::Value(a), Reading::Value(b)) => {\n                assert!(b > a, "rdtsc must advance: {a} -> {b}");\n            }\n            _ => panic!("rdtsc must read a Value on x86_64"),\n        }\n\n        let (minflt, majflt, nswap) = read_proc_stat_faults();\n        assert!(\n            !minflt.is_unavailable(),\n            "minflt must be a real Value: {minflt:?}"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            !majflt.is_unavailable(),\n            "majflt must be a real Value: {majflt:?}"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            !nswap.is_unavailable(),\n            "nswap must parse (a truthful 0): {nswap:?}"\n        );\n        // A live process always has taken minor faults.\n        assert!(\n            matches!(minflt, Reading::Value(v) if v > 0),\n            "a running process must have >0 minor faults: {minflt:?}"\n        );\n\n        let (vol, nonvol) = read_proc_ctxt_switches();\n        assert!(\n            !vol.is_unavailable(),\n            "vol ctxt switches must parse: {vol:?}"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            !nonvol.is_unavailable(),\n            "nonvol ctxt switches must parse: {nonvol:?}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tier_b_never_panics_and_reports_a_value_or_a_named_absence() {\n        // The load-bearing correctness property: perf_event_open never panics/SIGSEGVs and\n        // every Tier-B field is EITHER a real Value (permissive host: paranoid<=2 OR the\n        // process holds CAP_PERFMON/root — which bypasses paranoid entirely) OR a *named*\n        // absence (PermissionDenied on a gated host, NoPmuInterface where no PMU exists) —\n        // NEVER a fabricated 0 and never silently-wrong data. A Value, when present, must be\n        // hardware-plausible (a live process has retired instructions and taken cycles),\n        // which is how we detect a garbage-returning syscall as opposed to a real read.\n        let station = PmuStation::new();\n        // Do measurable work between open and read so a working counter is strictly > 0.\n        let mut acc = 0u64;\n        for i in 0..200_000u64 {\n            acc = acc.wrapping_add(i.wrapping_mul(2654435761) ^ (i >> 3));\n        }\n        core::hint::black_box(acc);\n        let stamp = station.sample();\n        for (name, r) in [\n            ("hw_instructions", stamp.hw_instructions),\n            ("hw_cpu_cycles", stamp.hw_cpu_cycles),\n            ("hw_cache_misses", stamp.hw_cache_misses),\n            ("hw_branch_misses", stamp.hw_branch_misses),\n        ] {\n            match r {\n                Reading::Unavailable(a) => assert!(\n                    matches!(a, Absence::PermissionDenied | Absence::NoPmuInterface),\n                    "{name}: unexpected absence {a:?}"\n                ),\n                Reading::Value(v) => {\n                    // instructions & cpu_cycles MUST be nonzero on a live process if the\n                    // read succeeded (a zero would betray a bogus fd / garbage read).\n                    if name == "hw_instructions" || name == "hw_cpu_cycles" {\n                        assert!(v > 0, "{name}: a successful HW read must be > 0, got {v}");\n                    }\n                    eprintln!("TIER_B_LIVE {name} = {v}");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn stamp_always_serializes_every_field_named_absence_not_missing_key() {\n        let station = PmuStation::new();\n        let json = station\n            .sample()\n            .write(super::super::json::JsonWriter::obj())\n            .finish();\n        // Every field key present (value or {"unavailable":...}).\n        for key in [\n            "tsc_cycles",\n            "minflt",\n            "majflt",\n            "nswap",\n            "vol_ctxt_switches",\n            "nonvol_ctxt_switches",\n            "hw_instructions",\n            "hw_cpu_cycles",\n            "hw_cache_misses",\n            "hw_branch_misses",\n        ] {\n            assert!(\n                json.contains(&format!("\\"{key}\\":")),\n                "missing key {key} in {json}"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Deterministic proof of the graceful-degradation MECHANISM, independent of this\n    /// process's privilege level: every `perf_event_open` errno maps to the correct named\n    /// `Absence`, and a forced Tier-B absence serializes as a greppable `{"unavailable":...}`\n    /// (never a fabricated 0, never a missing key). This is the load-bearing property when\n    /// the process is genuinely unprivileged (paranoid>=1 without CAP_PERFMON) — which this\n    /// root+CAP_PERFMON agent process is NOT, so it is asserted here by construction.\n    #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]\n    #[test]\n    fn errno_maps_to_named_absence_and_serializes() {\n        assert_eq!(errno_absence(-1), Absence::PermissionDenied, "EPERM");\n        assert_eq!(\n            errno_absence(-13),\n            Absence::PermissionDenied,\n            "EACCES (paranoid gate)"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(errno_absence(-2), Absence::NoPmuInterface, "ENOENT");\n        assert_eq!(errno_absence(-19), Absence::NoPmuInterface, "ENODEV");\n        assert_eq!(\n            errno_absence(-38),\n            Absence::NoPmuInterface,\n            "ENOSYS (seccomp)"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(errno_absence(-95), Absence::NoPmuInterface, "EOPNOTSUPP");\n        assert_eq!(\n            errno_absence(-22),\n            Absence::ReadError,\n            "EINVAL → generic ReadError"\n        );\n\n        // A stamp whose Tier-B fields were blocked must serialize named absences.\n        let blocked = PmuStamp {\n            tsc_cycles: Reading::Value(1),\n            minflt: Reading::Value(1),\n            majflt: Reading::Value(0),\n            nswap: Reading::Value(0),\n            vol_ctxt_switches: Reading::Value(0),\n            nonvol_ctxt_switches: Reading::Value(0),\n            hw_instructions: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied),\n            hw_cpu_cycles: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied),\n            hw_cache_misses: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied),\n            hw_branch_misses: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied),\n        };\n        let json = blocked\n            .write(super::super::json::JsonWriter::obj())\n            .finish();\n        assert!(\n            json.contains("\\"hw_instructions\\":{\\"unavailable\\":\\"permission_denied\\"}"),\n            "blocked Tier B must be a greppable named absence: {json}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn delta_propagates_absence_and_subtracts_values() {\n        let start = PmuStamp {\n            tsc_cycles: Reading::Value(100),\n            minflt: Reading::Value(5),\n            majflt: Reading::Value(0),\n            nswap: Reading::Value(0),\n            vol_ctxt_switches: Reading::Value(2),\n            nonvol_ctxt_switches: Reading::Value(1),\n            hw_instructions: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied),\n            hw_cpu_cycles: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied),\n            hw_cache_misses: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied),\n            hw_branch_misses: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied),\n        };\n        let end = PmuStamp {\n            tsc_cycles: Reading::Value(180),\n            minflt: Reading::Value(9),\n            ..start\n        };\n        let d = PmuStamp::delta(start, end);\n        assert_eq!(d.tsc_cycles, Reading::Value(80));\n        assert_eq!(d.minflt, Reading::Value(4));\n        // Absence at either endpoint propagates.\n        assert_eq!(\n            d.hw_instructions,\n            Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied)\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    #[cfg(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64"))]\n    fn bracket_runs_classifier_untouched_and_records_a_delta() {\n        // Bracket a REAL markov classification. The verdict is exactly what the pure\n        // function returns (bracketing must not change it), and the PMU delta records a\n        // real, monotone rdtsc advance across the window.\n        use crate::markov::{analyze_detailed, Verdict};\n        let toks: Vec<&str> = {\n            let mut v = Vec::new();\n            for _ in 0..8 {\n                v.push("edit");\n                v.push("run_ok");\n            }\n            v\n        };\n        let station = PmuStation::new();\n        let (report, delta) = station.bracket(|| analyze_detailed(&toks));\n        // Purity: identical to the un-bracketed call.\n        assert_eq!(\n            report.report.verdict,\n            analyze_detailed(&toks).report.verdict\n        );\n        assert_eq!(report.report.verdict, Verdict::Healthy);\n        // The window's rdtsc delta is a real (nonzero, on any real classification) count.\n        assert!(\n            matches!(delta.tsc_cycles, Reading::Value(v) if v > 0),\n            "bracket must record a real tsc delta: {:?}",\n            delta.tsc_cycles\n        );\n        // The Tier-B delta is a Value on this privileged host (perf_event_open bypasses\n        // paranoid under CAP_PERFMON) or a named absence on a gated host — either is correct.\n        // If it is a Value, it must be hardware-plausible (>0 instructions retired doing the\n        // classification), never a fabricated 0.\n        match delta.hw_instructions {\n            Reading::Value(v) => {\n                assert!(\n                    v > 0,\n                    "bracketed instruction delta must be > 0 if readable: {v}"\n                );\n                eprintln!("BRACKET_TIER_B_DELTA hw_instructions = {v}");\n            }\n            Reading::Unavailable(a) => assert!(matches!(\n                a,\n                Absence::PermissionDenied | Absence::NoPmuInterface\n            )),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    #[cfg(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64"))]\n    fn drift_class_lane_bracket_preserves_verdict_and_records_pmu_delta() {\n        // Blueprint §4.3 — DriftClass lane: bracket a REAL `classify_drift` call the same\n        // way a verdict-emission point would. The `DriftClass` verdict must be EXACTLY what\n        // the pure function returns (bracketing must not change it — the classifier stays\n        // byte-identical pure), and the PMU delta records a real, monotone rdtsc advance\n        // across the window. This exercises the DriftClass emission path that the existing\n        // Verdict-lane tests do not cover, proving the companion-record design works for\n        // both classifiers.\n        use crate::spectral::{classify_drift, DriftClass};\n        // A well-formed operator with spectral radius < 1 ⇒ Damped (fail-closed guards pass).\n        let op: Vec<Vec<f64>> = vec![vec![0.5, 0.0], vec![0.0, 0.3]];\n        let station = PmuStation::new();\n        let (drift, delta) = station.bracket(|| classify_drift(&op));\n        // Purity: identical to the un-bracketed call.\n        assert_eq!(drift, classify_drift(&op));\n        assert_eq!(drift, DriftClass::Damped);\n        // The window's rdtsc delta is a real (nonzero, on any real classification) count.\n        assert!(\n delta is a Value on this privileged host (perf_event_open bypasses\n        // paranoid under CAP_PERFMON) or a named absence on a gated host — either is correct.\n        // If it is a Value, it must be hardware-plausible (>0 instructions retired doing the\n        // classification), never a fabricated 0.\n        match delta.hw_instructions {\n            Reading::Value(v) => {\n                assert!(\n                    v > 0,\n                    "drift-lane bracketed instruction delta must be > 0 if readable: {v}"\n                );\n            }\n            Reading::Unavailable(a) => {\n                assert!(matches!(\n                    a,\n                    Absence::PermissionDenied | Absence::NoPmuInterface\n                ))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n	2672	-1	-1		c77fa63ed00ecba1f901f0c58452d331eddc97eded50f726eb5f0c4ac76f0f5338c0ec864ed17ec7a15156a87980f6289f215d04fceb4d4201e37a03f70ccceedfb74ca964fbca9ba412000a87bae788d1586c0a29d9df6df782b0a65c4b9d25e060f2d693eab0bdf40c4a394a2cddb54cbdc92cbed0ece09b896ede299e2233
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/fdr/ring.rs	ring · 439 lines	//! `fdr/ring.rs` — the FDR durable layer: A/B alternating segment files with\n//! CRC32-checked NDJSON lines and `kill -9` recovery (blueprint §4.4).\n//!\n//! **Correction to the synthesis, stated plainly (blueprint §4.4 / §6-5):** synthesis §5\n//! called tier (b) an "`mmap`-backed ring — pure std". `std` has NO mmap; a literal mmap\n//! needs `libc`/`memmap2`, a new dependency the whole item forbids. The honest pure-std\n//! design is delivered here instead: two alternating fixed-cap append-only segment files\n//! (`fdr.a.jsonl`, `fdr.b.jsonl`), each line suffixed with a CRC32 of its payload.\n//! Recovery accepts CRC-valid lines only and tolerates exactly one torn tail line per\n//! segment. Append-only segments are simpler to prove correct under torn writes than an\n//! in-place byte-ring cursor.\n//!\n//! **Durability cadence, honestly separated (blueprint §4.4):**\n//!   - Surviving `kill -9` (process death) requires ONLY that `write(2)` reached the OS\n//!     page cache — no `fsync`. A fresh reader of the same file sees those bytes because\n//!     the page cache outlives the process. That is the §G.9 test's guarantee, and the\n//!     recorder writes event-kind records WITHOUT fsync to prove exactly that.\n//!   - Surviving POWER LOSS additionally requires `fsync`: [`FdrRing::append`] issues\n//!     `sync_data` on every `Alarm`/`PostMortem` record and [`FdrRing::switch`] fsyncs on\n//!     segment switch (copying `FileEventStore`'s sync-before-claim discipline). A fsync\n//!     error is surfaced as a typed `io::Error`, never swallowed.\n//!\n//! Non-wasm only: `wasm32` has no real filesystem and never installs an FDR sink.\n\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse crate::vfs::{open_file, OpenMode, StdFile, VfsFile};\n\nuse super::schema::{fdr_event_stamp, FdrEvent, Kind, StampPolicy};\nuse super::Level;\n\n/// Default per-segment cap (1 MiB) — bounded size, last-N-seconds retention.\npub const DEFAULT_SEG_CAP: u64 = 1 << 20;\n\nconst SEG_A: &str = "fdr.a.jsonl";\nconst SEG_B: &str = "fdr.b.jsonl";\n/// Where a recovery post-mortem is emitted (a fresh log — never clobbers the recovered\n/// segments, so the forensic evidence survives the recovery step).\npub const POSTMORTEM_LOG: &str = "fdr.postmortem.jsonl";\n\n// CRC32 is now the SINGLE shared implementation lifted to always-compiled `fdr::crc32`\n// (blueprint §3.2 / item 54) — shared by FDR ring (at-rest per-line CRC), item 40\n// (weights), and item 54 (live-struct Sentinel). Re-exported here for call-site\n// compatibility with the prior `fdr::ring::crc32` path. ONE implementation; the KAT\n// `crc32_matches_known_vector` below stays green.\npub use super::crc32;\n\n/// The durable writer. One active segment at a time; switches to the other (truncating\n/// it) at the cap. Fresh session: opens `fdr.a.jsonl` truncated. Use [`recover`] BEFORE\n/// constructing a writer if you need the prior session's records — the writer truncates.\npub struct FdrRing {\n    dir: PathBuf,\n    seg_cap: u64,\n    active: usize, // 0 => A, 1 => B\n    file: StdFile,\n    written: u64,\n    seq: u64,\n}\n\nfn seg_path(dir: &Path, idx: usize) -> PathBuf {\n    dir.join(if idx == 0 { SEG_A } else { SEG_B })\n}\n\nimpl FdrRing {\n    /// Open a fresh writer session (truncates segment A). `seq` starts at 0.\n    pub fn open(dir: PathBuf, seg_cap: u64) -> io::Result<Self> {\n        crate::vfs::create_dir_all(&dir)?;\n        let file = open_file(seg_path(&dir, 0), OpenMode::WriteTruncate)?;\n        Ok(FdrRing {\n            dir,\n            seg_cap,\n            active: 0,\n            file,\n            written: 0,\n            seq: 0,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Allocate the next monotonic sequence number.\n    pub fn next_seq(&mut self) -> u64 {\n        let s = self.seq;\n        self.seq += 1;\n        s\n    }\n\n    /// Append one record. `write(2)` reaches the page cache (kill-9 durable). Alarm-class\n    /// records additionally `sync_data` (power-loss durable). Errors are surfaced typed.\n    pub fn append(&mut self, ev: &FdrEvent) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let payload = ev.to_json();\n        let crc = crc32(payload.as_bytes());\n        // Line = <payload>|<crc:08x>\\n — payload never contains a raw '\\n' (escaped by\n        // JsonWriter), so '\\n' unambiguously delimits records for recovery.\n        let mut line = String::with_capacity(payload.len() + 10);\n        line.push_str(&payload);\n        line.push('|');\n        line.push_str(&format!("{crc:08x}"));\n        line.push('\\n');\n\n        if self.written > 0 && self.written + line.len() as u64 > self.seg_cap {\n            self.switch()?;\n        }\n        self.file.write_all(line.as_bytes())?;\n        self.written += line.len() as u64;\n        if matches!(ev.kind, Kind::Alarm | Kind::PostMortem) {\n            self.file.sync_data()?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Switch to the other segment (fsync current, truncate + activate the other).\n    fn switch(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.file.sync_data()?;\n        let next = 1 - self.active;\n        self.file = open_file(seg_path(&self.dir, next), OpenMode::WriteTruncate)?;\n        self.active = next;\n        self.written = 0;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Force durable flush (power-loss safety) without a record. Not required for kill-9.\n    pub fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.file.sync_data()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Write the orderly-shutdown marker (fsynced). Its presence as the tail record is\n    /// how [`recover`] distinguishes a clean stop from a crash.\n    pub fn clean_shutdown(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let seq = self.next_seq();\n        let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n            seq,\n            Level::Info,\n            Kind::CleanShutdown,\n            "clean_shutdown".into(),\n            StampPolicy::Cheap,\n            vec![],\n        );\n        self.append(&ev)?;\n        self.file.sync_data()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// One recovered record (CRC-valid). `raw` is the exact payload JSON as written.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct RecoveredRecord {\n    pub seq: u64,\n    pub kind: String,\n    pub name: String,\n    pub raw: String,\n}\n\n/// The outcome of reading back both segments.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]\npub struct Recovery {\n    /// CRC-valid records across both segments, ordered by `seq`.\n    pub records: Vec<RecoveredRecord>,\n    /// True iff a `clean_shutdown` marker was recovered (⇒ orderly stop, no post-mortem).\n    pub clean: bool,\n    /// Count of torn tail lines dropped (partial final line with no terminating `\\n`).\n    pub torn_tail: usize,\n    /// Count of complete lines whose CRC did not verify (corruption dropped).\n    pub crc_failures: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Recovery {\n    pub fn first_seq(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        self.records.first().map(|r| r.seq)\n    }\n    pub fn last_seq(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        self.records.last().map(|r| r.seq)\n    }\n}\n\n// Pure JSONL line-parsing helpers — lifted to the `no_std` core\n// (`dowiz_core::fdr::ring_parse`), re-exported here so the `fdr::ring::extract_u64` /\n// `fdr::ring::extract_str` call sites stay unchanged (seam shim).\npub use dowiz_core::fdr::ring_parse::{extract_str, extract_u64};\n\n/// **READ-ONLY** recovery: reads both segments, validates each line's CRC, drops a torn\n/// tail, and returns the CRC-valid records ordered by `seq`. Never truncates — safe to\n/// run against a crashed writer's segments (the §G.9 restart-and-recover path).\npub fn recover(dir: &Path) -> Recovery {\n    let mut out = Recovery::default();\n    for idx in [0usize, 1usize] {\n        let data = match crate::vfs::read(seg_path(dir, idx)) {\n            Ok(d) => d,\n            Err(_) => continue,\n        };\n        // Split on '\\n'. A record line ends in '\\n'; the element after the final '\\n' is\n        // "" (all records complete) or a partial (torn tail — process died mid-write).\n        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&data);\n        let parts: Vec<&str> = text.split('\\n').collect();\n        let n = parts.len();\n        for (li, part) in parts.iter().enumerate() {\n            let is_last = li == n - 1;\n            if part.is_empty() {\n                continue; // trailing "" after a clean final '\\n', or empty file.\n            }\n            if is_last {\n                // Non-empty element with no terminating '\\n' ⇒ torn tail. Dropped.\n                out.torn_tail += 1;\n                continue;\n            }\n            // Complete line: split off the trailing "|<crc:08x>".\n            match part.rfind('|') {\n                Some(bar) => {\n                    let payload = &part[..bar];\n                    let crc_hex = &part[bar + 1..];\n                    match u32::from_str_radix(crc_hex, 16) {\n                        Ok(want) if crc32(payload.as_bytes()) == want => {\n                            let seq = extract_u64(payload, "seq").unwrap_or(u64::MAX);\n                            let kind = extract_str(payload, "kind").unwrap_or_default();\n                            let name = extract_str(payload, "name").unwrap_or_default();\n                            out.records.push(RecoveredRecord {\n                                seq,\n                                kind,\n                                name,\n                                raw: payload.to_string(),\n                            });\n                        }\n                        _ => out.crc_failures += 1,\n                    }\n                }\n                None => out.crc_failures += 1,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out.records.sort_by_key(|r| r.seq);\n    out.clean = out.records.iter().any(|r| r.kind == "clean_shutdown");\n    out\n}\n\n/// Emit a `PostMortem` record naming the recovery into a FRESH log (`fdr.postmortem.jsonl`)\n/// — it does NOT touch the recovered segments. fsynced (power-loss durable). Returns the\n/// bytes written. This is the "post-mortem into a fresh log" of blueprint §4.4; routing it\n/// into the durable `EventLog` is DEFERRED behind item 2's composition-root fix.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn emit_post_mortem(dir: &Path, rec: &Recovery) -> io::Result<()> {\n    let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n        0,\n        Level::Warn,\n        Kind::PostMortem,\n        "post_mortem".into(),\n        StampPolicy::Full,\n        vec![\n            ("recovered", rec.records.len().to_string()),\n            (\n                "first_seq",\n                rec.first_seq()\n                    .map(|s| s.to_string())\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "none".into()),\n            ),\n            (\n                "last_seq",\n                rec.last_seq()\n                    .map(|s| s.to_string())\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "none".into()),\n            ),\n            ("torn_tail", rec.torn_tail.to_string()),\n            ("crc_failures", rec.crc_failures.to_string()),\n        ],\n    );\n    let payload = ev.to_json();\n    let crc = crc32(payload.as_bytes());\n    let line = format!("{payload}|{crc:08x}\\n");\n    let mut f = open_file(dir.join(POSTMORTEM_LOG), OpenMode::Append)?;\n    f.write_all(line.as_bytes())?;\n    f.sync_data()?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn tmp(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\n        let d = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n            "fdr_ring_{}_{}_{}",\n            tag,\n            std::process::id(),\n            crate::typed_metrics::mono_now_ns()\n        ));\n        let _ = crate::vfs::create_dir_all(&d);\n        d\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn crc32_matches_known_vector() {\n        // Standard CRC-32/ISO-HDLC check value for the ASCII string "123456789".\n        assert_eq!(crc32(b"123456789"), 0xCBF4_3926);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn write_then_recover_all_records_ordered() {\n        let dir = tmp("rw");\n        {\n            let mut ring = FdrRing::open(dir.clone(), DEFAULT_SEG_CAP).unwrap();\n            for i in 0..50 {\n                let seq = ring.next_seq();\n                let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n                    seq,\n                    Level::Info,\n                    Kind::Event,\n                    format!("rec-{i}"),\n                    StampPolicy::Cheap,\n                    vec![("i", i.to_string())],\n                );\n                ring.append(&ev).unwrap();\n            }\n        }\n        let rec = recover(&dir);\n        assert_eq!(rec.records.len(), 50);\n        assert_eq!(rec.first_seq(), Some(0));\n        assert_eq!(rec.last_seq(), Some(49));\n        assert_eq!(rec.torn_tail, 0);\n        assert_eq!(rec.crc_failures, 0);\n        assert!(!rec.clean, "no clean_shutdown marker was written");\n        let _ = crate::vfs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn clean_shutdown_marker_makes_recovery_clean() {\n        let dir = tmp("clean");\n        {\n            let mut ring = FdrRing::open(dir.clone(), DEFAULT_SEG_CAP).unwrap();\n            let seq = ring.next_seq();\n            let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n                seq,\n                Level::Info,\n                Kind::Event,\n                "x".into(),\n                StampPolicy::Cheap,\n                vec![],\n            );\n            ring.append(&ev).unwrap();\n            ring.clean_shutdown().unwrap();\n        }\n        let rec = recover(&dir);\n        assert!(rec.clean, "clean_shutdown marker must make recovery clean");\n        let _ = crate::vfs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn torn_tail_line_is_dropped_valid_records_survive() {\n        let dir = tmp("torn");\n        {\n            let mut ring = FdrRing::open(dir.clone(), DEFAULT_SEG_CAP).unwrap();\n            for i in 0..5 {\n                let seq = ring.next_seq();\n                let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n                    seq,\n                    Level::Info,\n                    Kind::Event,\n                    format!("r{i}"),\n                    StampPolicy::Cheap,\n                    vec![],\n                );\n                ring.append(&ev).unwrap();\n            }\n        }\n        // Simulate a process dying mid-write: append a partial line with NO terminating\n        // '\\n' and a bogus/short CRC — exactly              .unwrap();\n        }\n        let rec = recover(&dir);\n        assert_eq!(rec.records.len(), 5, "the 5 complete records must survive");\n        assert_eq!(\n            rec.torn_tail, 1,\n            "the partial tail must be counted + dropped"\n        );\n        let _ = crate::vfs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn crc_corruption_is_dropped() {\n        let dir
```
