```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/fdr/schema.rs	schema · 270 lines	//! `fdr/schema.rs` — std shim over the pure no_std core.\n//!\n//! The envelope types ([`FdrEvent`], [`HwStamp`], [`Reading`], [`Absence`], [`Kind`],\n//! [`WorkloadKind`], [`Work`]) and the deterministic NDJSON serializer (`to_json`) live in\n//! `dowiz_core::fdr::schema` and are re-exported here. This shim adds ONLY the std\n//! constructors: sampling real `/proc`/`/sys` hardware ([`hw_sample`]), stamping a record\n//! with real clocks ([`fdr_event_stamp`]), and the RAPL reader ([`read_joules_uj`]).\n\npub use dowiz_core::fdr::schema::*;\n\nuse dowiz_core::fdr::Level;\n\n/// utime+stime ticks, via the reused `typed_metrics` reader. `None` (non-Linux/unreadable)\n/// ⇒ `NonLinuxHost`.\nfn read_cpu_ticks() -> Reading<u64> {\n    match crate::typed_metrics::proc_cpu_sample_from_proc_self() {\n        Some(s) => Reading::Value(s.utime_ticks + s.stime_ticks),\n        None => Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NonLinuxHost),\n    }\n}\n\n/// VmRSS kB, via the reused `typed_metrics` reader.\nfn read_rss_kb() -> Reading<u64> {\n    match crate::typed_metrics::mem_sample_from_proc_self() {\n        Some(m) => Reading::Value(m.vm_rss_kb),\n        None => Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NonLinuxHost),\n    }\n}\n\n/// RAPL energy counter (µJ) from `intel-rapl:0`. Degrades to a *named* absence on every\n/// failure mode; never fabricates a `0`.\npub fn read_joules_uj() -> Reading<u64> {\n    #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]\n    {\n        Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NonLinuxHost)\n    }\n    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]\n    {\n        const PATH: &str = "/sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:0/energy_uj";\n        match crate::vfs::read_to_string(PATH) {\n            Ok(s) => match s.trim().parse::<u64>() {\n                Ok(v) => Reading::Value(v),\n                Err(_) => Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError),\n            },\n            Err(e) => match e {\n                crate::vfs::VfsError::NotFound => Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NoRaplInterface),\n                crate::vfs::VfsError::PermissionDenied => {\n                    Reading::Unavailable(Absence::PermissionDenied)\n                }\n                _ => Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError),\n            },\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Sample the hardware stamp under `policy`. `Cheap` is the pure [`HwStamp::cheap`];\n/// `Full` reads `/proc`+`/sys` (µs-scale syscalls) for alarm-class records.\npub fn hw_sample(policy: StampPolicy) -> HwStamp {\n    match policy {\n        StampPolicy::Cheap => HwStamp::cheap(),\n        StampPolicy::Full => HwStamp {\n            cpu_ticks: read_cpu_ticks(),\n            rss_kb: read_rss_kb(),\n            joules_uj: read_joules_uj(),\n        },\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a record and stamp `ts`/`mono`/`hw`. Non-wasm: `SystemTime::now()` and\n/// `mono_now_ns()`; the FDR write path is never reached on wasm (no sink is installed there).\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\npub fn fdr_event_stamp(\n    seq: u64,\n    level: Level,\n    kind: Kind,\n    name: String,\n    hw_policy: StampPolicy,\n    fields: Vec<(&'static str, String)>,\n) -> FdrEvent {\n    let ts_unix_ns = std::time::SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n    let mono_ns = crate::typed_metrics::mono_now_ns();\n    FdrEvent::stamp_with(\n        seq,\n        level,\n        kind,\n        name,\n        hw_sample(hw_policy),\n        ts_unix_ns,\n        mono_ns,\n        fields,\n    )\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rapl_absent_host_reports_named_absence_not_missing_key() {\n        let r = read_joules_uj();\n        assert!(\n            r.is_unavailable(),\n            "expected RAPL-less host to report Unavailable"\n        );\n        let w = r.write_field(dowiz_core::fdr::json::JsonWriter::obj(), "joules_uj").finish();\n        assert!(\n            w.contains("\\"joules_uj\\":{\\"unavailable\\":"),\n            "field must be present: {w}"\n        );\n        assert!(w.contains("unavailable"), "reason must be greppable: {w}");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn hw_sample_cheap_equals_pure_cheap() {\n        assert_eq!(hw_sample(StampPolicy::Cheap), HwStamp::cheap());\n        // Cheap stamp is all SamplingDisabled.\n        let c = HwStamp::cheap();\n        assert_eq!(c.cpu_ticks, Reading::Unavailable(Absence::SamplingDisabled));\n        assert_eq!(c.rss_kb, Reading::Unavailable(Absence::SamplingDisabled));\n        assert_eq!(c.joules_uj, Reading::Unavailable(Absence::SamplingDisabled));\n    }\n\n    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\n    #[test]\n    fn fdr_event_stamp_stamps_real_monotonic_and_wall_clocks() {\n        let ev = fdr_event_stamp(\n            1,\n            Level::Info,\n            Kind::Event,\n            "test".into(),\n            StampPolicy::Cheap,\n            vec![("k", "v".into())],\n        );\n        assert!(ev.ts_unix_ns > 0, "wall-clock must be non-zero: {}", ev.ts_unix_ns);\n        assert!(ev.mono_ns >= 0, "mono must be stamped");\n        assert_eq!(ev.kind, Kind::Event);\n        // Deterministic serialization still holds after stamping.\n        let j = ev.to_json();\n        assert!(j.contains("\\"seq\\":1"), "seq present: {j}");\n        assert!(j.contains("\\"name\\":\\"test\\""), "name present: {j}");\n    }\n\n    // ── Item 48 byte-identity (golden): an `Event` record's JSON must be byte-identical to\n    // what it would have ## 2749 · /root/dowiz/kernel/src/landing/tests.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: tests · 552 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/landing/tests.rs	tests · 552 lines	//! BLUEPRINT-P73 Lane-A unit tests — the conversion-funnel DoD (§6) + adversarial gates.\n//!\n//! These run with ZERO network (the `MockClaimService` is the contract stand-in for P67) and\n//! exercise the CLOSED `ClaimJourney` FSM, the `SignupForm` submit-boundary, the `ClaimClient`\n//! rate limit + empty-cert refusal, and the M6 opaque-cert handoff. Lane-B (wgpu render + real\n//! HTTP claim transport) is `#[ignore = "O18a"]` here, exactly as P38/P57 do.\n\nuse super::claim_client::{\n    ChallengeToken, ClaimClient, ClaimError, ClaimOutcome, ClaimRequest, ClaimedHub, HubId,\n    InterestAck, InterestSubmission, MockClaimService, OwnerRootCert,\n};\nuse super::form::{FormError, SignupForm};\nuse super::journey::{CertHandoffSink, ClaimJourney, JourneyEvent, LandingStep};\n\n/// A counting handoff sink (M6) — proves the cert is forwarded EXACTLY ONCE.\n#[derive(Default)]\nstruct CountSink {\n    calls: usize,\n    last: Vec<u8>,\n}\nimpl CertHandoffSink for CountSink {\n    fn handoff(&mut self, cert_bytes: &[u8]) {\n        self.calls += 1;\n        self.last = cert_bytes.to_vec();\n    }\n}\n\nfn form_with(challenge: bool) -> SignupForm {\n    SignupForm {\n        contact: "owner@example.com".into(),\n        venue_name: "The Sea Tavern".into(),\n        notes: String::new(),\n        challenge: if challenge {\n            Some(ChallengeToken("edge-abc".into()))\n        } else {\n            None\n        },\n    }\n}\n\n// ── M1: the conversion FSM ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Full happy fast path: Started..ClaimAssigned → Claimed with the hub_url rendered.\n#[test]\nfn journey_happy_fast_path() {\n    let mut j = ClaimJourney::Landing;\n    j = j.fold(JourneyEvent::FormOpened);\n    assert_eq!(j.step(), LandingStep::Form);\n    let f = form_with(true);\n    let submitting = ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f).submit().expect("valid form");\n    let mut sink = CountSink::default();\n    let claimed = submitting.advance_with_service(&MockClaimService::claimed(), &mut sink);\n    match &claimed {\n        ClaimJourney::Claimed(hub) => {\n            assert_eq!(hub.hub_url, "https://hub-demo001.hubs.dowiz.org");\n        }\n        other => panic!("expected Claimed, got {other:?}"),\n    }\n    // M6: cert forwarded exactly once on the fast path.\n    assert_eq!(sink.calls, 1, "cert must be handed off exactly once");\n}\n\n/// A `PoolEmpty` outcome folds to `InterestRegistered`, NEVER `Failed` (the load-bearing rule).\n#[test]\nfn journey_pool_empty_becomes_interest() {\n    let f = form_with(true);\n    let submitting = ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f).submit().expect("valid form");\n    let mut sink = CountSink::default();\n    let end = submitting.advance_with_service(&MockClaimService::pool_empty(), &mut sink);\n    match &end {\n        ClaimJourney::InterestRegistered(ack) => {\n            assert_eq!(ack.ack_id, "ack_42");\n        }\n        other => panic!("PoolEmpty must route to InterestRegistered, got {other:?}"),\n    }\n    // No cert handoff on the slow path (no hub was claimed).\n    assert_eq!(sink.calls, 0);\n}\n\n/// A `TransportFailed` then `Retried` returns to `FormEntry` with the SAME form values\n/// (the form survives a recoverable failure — never cleared).\n#[test]\nfn journey_retry_preserves_form() {\n    let f = form_with(true);\n    let submitting = ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f).submit().expect("valid form");\n    let mut sink = CountSink::default();\n    let failed = submitting.advance_with_service(&MockClaimService::timeout(), &mut sink);\n    match &failed {\n        ClaimJourney::Failed { form, error } => {\n            assert_eq!(*error, ClaimError::Timeout);\n            assert_eq!(form.contact, "owner@example.com");\n            assert_eq!(form.venue_name, "The Sea Tavern");\n        }\n        other => panic!("timeout must route to Failed, got {other:?}"),\n    }\n    // Retry returns to FormEntry with the same form.\n    let retried = failed.fold(JourneyEvent::Retried);\n    assert_eq!(retried.step(), LandingStep::Form);\n ```record
```
```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/kprocess.rs	kprocess · 93 lines	/// held-handle shim — pure types from dowiz_core::kprocess, std-dependent impls stay here.\n\npub use dowiz_core::kprocess::*;\n\n/// process.rs — subprocess seam (ledger item 4: process → kexec).\n///\n/// The no_std audit found a small set of `std::process::Command` call sites in\n/// otherwise no_std-ready modules (`span_metrics/breach`'s `perf record`,\n/// `living_knowledge`'s `node --version` availability check). A kernel module\n/// has no `std::process` — it execs via `kexec`/`call_usermodehelper`. This\n/// module is the single seam, in the same shape as [`crate::clock`]: a\n/// no_std-compatible [`Process`] trait (`&str` cmd + `String` args + i32 exit\n/// code — no `Command`/`Child`/`Stdio`), a userspace [`StdProcess`] impl, and a\n/// [`run`] free function that is the single authority. The kernel port swaps the\n/// impl, not the call sites.\n///\n/// # Out of scope (documented follow-up)\n/// The `living_knowledge` sh-bridge (`spawn` + `stdin/stdout/stderr` pipes +\n/// `wait4(2)` rusage) is a *bidirectional pipe* pattern — a `kexec` port needs a\n/// different fd-passing design, so it stays std (it already uses a raw `wait4`\n/// syscall in the native path, the same style as `fdr::pmu`).\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Result of running a command to completion.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CommandOutput {\n    /// Exit code, or `-1` if the process was signaled / could not be spawned.\n    pub code: i32,\n    /// Captured stdout.\n    pub stdout: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Captured stderr.\n    pub stderr: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nimpl CommandOutput {\n    /// Whether the command exited successfully (code 0).\n    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n        self.code == 0\n    }\n}\n\n/// The subprocess abstraction. no_std-compatible signature.\npub trait Process {\n    /// Run `cmd` with `args` to completion, capturing stdout/stderr.\n    fn run(&self, cmd: &str, args: &[String]) -> CommandOutput;\n}\n\n/// The userspace subprocess impl (`std::process::Command`).\npub struct StdProcess;\n\nimpl Process for StdProcess {\n    fn run(&self, cmd: &str, args: &[String]) -> CommandOutput {\n        match std::process::Command::new(cmd).args(args).output() {\n            Ok(o) => CommandOutput {\n                code: o.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),\n                stdout: o.stdout,\n                stderr: o.stderr,\n            },\n            Err(_) => CommandOutput {\n                code: -1,\n                stdout: Vec::new(),\n                stderr: Vec::new(),\n            },\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Single authority for "run a command". Kernel port swaps to\n/// `kexec`/`call_usermodehelper`.\npub fn run(cmd: &str, args: &[String]) -> CommandOutput {\n    StdProcess.run(cmd, args)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn run_echo_captures_stdout() {\n        // `sh -c 'echo hi'` is universally available on the test hosts.\n        let out = run("sh", &["-c".into(), "echo hi".into()]);\n        assert!(out.success(), "echo must exit 0");\n        assert_eq!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).trim(), "hi");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn run_missing_command_is_not_success() {\n        let out = run("/definitely/not/a/real/binary", &[]);\n        assert!(!out.success(), "missing binary must report failure");\n    }\n}\n	2765	-1	-1		6e77b5521ec633302849f4f72510722f8ddebc46bd567f9a899f8e4e010123e55063040a53e0625f9d43436169d48468577167a43d2487ea80747a2b5e1f784edd2e5c90cd0a015695114402f4babbf9f079444a2d0d476bcce2b29461cb1525f07252253465d2a568180e9d3f4c17a10cbf61efddd449810b7576f47830ac52
```

Summary: hw_profile · 70 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/hw_profile.rs	hw_profile · 70 lines	//! hw_profile.rs — std host shim (pure `CpuTopology`/`parse_cpuinfo`/\n//! `parse_cache_size` live in `dowiz_core::hw_profile`; the VFS `probe()` seam\n//! stays here).\n//!\n//! `probe()` reads /proc/cpuinfo and /sys through `crate::vfs`, then delegates\n//! the pure parsing to the no_std core. Fail-closed: any unreadable file →\n//! Unknown/0, never a panic.\n\npub use dowiz_core::hw_profile::*;\n\n/// Probe hardware topology from /proc/cpuinfo and /sys (fills the\n/// /sys-derived cache + NUMA fields the no_std core leaves at default).\npub fn probe() -> CpuTopology {\n    let cpuinfo_raw = crate::vfs::read_to_string("/proc/cpuinfo").unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut topo = parse_cpuinfo(&cpuinfo_raw);\n\n    // Cache sizes from /sys.\n    for idx in 0..8 {\n        let typ = crate::vfs::read_to_string(\n            format!("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache/index{idx}/type")\n        ).unwrap_or_default();\n        let size_str = crate::vfs::read_to_string(\n            format!("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache/index{idx}/size")\n        ).unwrap_or_default();\n        let size = parse_cache_size(&size_str);\n        let line = crate::vfs::read_to_string(\n            format!("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache/index{idx}/coherency_line_size")\n        ).unwrap_or_default();\n        if topo.cache_line_size == 0 {\n            topo.cache_line_size = line.trim().parse().unwrap_or(64);\n        }\n\n        match typ.trim() {\n            "Data" if size > 0 => topo.l1d_size = size,\n            "Instruction" if size > 0 => topo.l1i_size = size,\n            "Unified" => {\n                // index2 = L2, index3 = L3\n                if idx < 3 { topo.l2_size = size; }\n                else { topo.l3_size = size; }\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    // NUMA nodes.\n    topo.numa_nodes = crate::vfs::read_to_string("/sys/devices/system/node/online")\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|s| {\n            let count = s.split(',').filter(|p| !p.is_empty()).count();\n            if count > 0 { Some(count) } else { None }\n        })\n        .unwrap_or(1);\n\n    topo\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn probe_returns_default_on_no_proc() {\n        let topo = probe();\n        if topo.physical_cores == 0 {\n            assert_eq!(topo.logical_processors, 0);\n        } else {\n            assert!(topo.logical_processors >= topo.physical_cores);\n        }\n    }\n}\n	2769	-1	-1		4bb43e7e1cd6223a5dd9d2c32c02113344d69bfda578670ee9dec11a94c5925d31c78301669e64d8e0d8592884defd7425b32301bf6f44a0e4efbc0d6f07b235daa964ddc50b8149378ab80037b9eafa78dc73422568fda1951404c45ad31763e5ebb6d7bcc180cf4cf8ca06475b3efd4d554c6b78f599a107f3d0f442d73798
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/hydra_closed_loop.rs	hydra_closed_loop · 44 lines	//! hydra_closed_loop — kernel re-export shim for the `no_std` core engine.\n//!\n//! The pure closed-loop engine lives in `dowiz_core::hydra_closed_loop`; this\n//! module re-exports it so existing kernel call sites (`crate::hydra_closed_loop::…`\n//! and `dowiz_kernel::hydra_closed_loop::…`) keep working unchanged. The only\n//! std-dependent piece is the runtime-probe golden test below, which spawns a\n//! kernel binary and therefore stays in the std kernel crate.\n\npub use dowiz_core::hydra_closed_loop::*;\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    /// Cryptographic golden test: running the probe in verification mode must\n    /// emit a byte-exact stable stdout sequence. Any change to probe output\n    /// formatting or cycle behavior fails this SHA3-256 KAT.\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_runtime_probe_golden_sha3_256() {\n        use std::process::Command;\n\n        let binary = std::path::PathBuf::from("/root/dowiz/kernel/target/debug/hydra_runtime_probe");\n        let output = Command::new(&binary)\n            .args(["--verify-golden", "--cycles", "4"])\n            .output()\n            .expect("failed to spawn hydra_runtime_probe");\n\n        assert!(\n            output.status.success(),\n            "probe verify-golden must exit 0: {:?}",\n            output\n        );\n\n        let expected_hash: [u8; 32] = [\n            0xce, 0x55, 0x58, 0xcc, 0x67, 0x25, 0x5d, 0xa6,\n            0x48, 0x14, 0x97, 0x43, 0xcb, 0x20, 0x10, 0x6a,\n            0xd3, 0x1f, 0xff, 0x3c, 0x0c, 0x0d, 0x93, 0x33,\n            0x4f, 0xbe, 0xf2, 0x91, 0xed, 0x87, 0xe3, 0x31,\n        ];\n        let actual_hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(&output.stdout);\n        assert_eq!(\n            actual_hash, expected_hash,\n            "probe golden output hash mismatch"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	2772	-1	-1		693e7657dd7667663123e2a7b93103a911523da45750e102cd5aee4c017fd0a17173b514d4db58fefd584db97ddecf2f853b27cc6f2904b2baeb563c8f556e0a4af98d8851ae4964de8bc518b5da9eb17a594e1a2f24676bc3aa37b3cb8359056524fa5531ca3ae8af1dc6ca9938c27049974d6e92ed89b489f9b3df712034f1
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/inference/golden.rs	golden · 198 lines	//! Item 40 — Per-layer golden-CRC32 self-check (hard-fail to safe state): std shim.\n//!\n//! The pure no_std half — the integer/checksum math, the golden constants (`GOLDEN_L1`,\n//! `GOLDEN_HIDDEN`, `GOLDEN_LOGITS`, `PINNED_VECTORS`), the `Layer` enum, `Weights`,\n//! `ChecksumFault`, and the check driver (`self_check_core`) with the production entry\n//! points (`self_check_all`, `self_check_all_with_weights`,\n//! `self_check_all_with_activation_fault`) — lives in `dowiz_core::inference::golden` and is\n//! re-exported below. This shim keeps ONLY the std-dependent parts: `fault` (which writes\n//! the typed `Alarm` to a durable file-backed FDR `RingHandle`) and\n//! `self_check_all_into_ring` (the test/standalone entry that drives the self-check into an\n//! owned ring so the entry is recoverable/verifiable without racing the process-global sink).\n\npub use dowiz_core::inference::golden::*;\n\nuse crate::fdr::RingHandle;\nuse crate::inference::workspace::H;\n\n/// The hard-fail trap: write the typed FDR `Kind::Alarm` entry recording the faulting\n/// layer, then return `Err(ChecksumFault{layer})`. The production path calls\n/// `fdr::emit_alarm` (a no-op unless an FDR sink is installed, so a healthy run — which\n/// never reaches this fn — is silent). The test/standalone path also writes the SAME typed\n/// Alarm record directly to an owned ring so the entry is recoverable/verifiable without\n/// racing the process-global `OnceLock` sink.\nfn fault(layer: Layer, ring: Option<&mut RingHandle>) -> Result<(), ChecksumFault> {\n    crate::fdr::emit_alarm("checksum_fault", &format!("layer={}", layer.as_str()));\n    // `RingHandle`/`FdrEvent::stamp` are both native-only (no filesystem, no clock on\n    // wasm32 — see `fdr::RingHandle`/`FdrEvent::stamp` docs); `ring` is provably always\n    // `None` on wasm32 since nothing there can construct a `RingHandle` value.\n    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\n    if let Some(r) = ring {\n        let ev = crate::fdr::schema::fdr_event_stamp(\n            0,\n            crate::fdr::Level::Error,\n            crate::fdr::schema::Kind::Alarm,\n            "checksum_fault".to_string(),\n            crate::fdr::schema::StampPolicy::Full,\n            vec![("layer", layer.as_str().to_string())],\n        );\n        let _ = r.append(&ev);\n        let _ = r.sync();\n    }\n    #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]\n    let _ = ring;\n    Err(ChecksumFault { layer })\n}\n\n/// Test/standalone variant: run the self-check against an **owned** FDR ring, writing the\n/// fault's typed `Alarm` record directly to it (so the entry is recoverable and verifiable\n/// without racing the process-global `OnceLock` sink, which may be owned by another test in\n/// the same binary). The production path is [`self_check_all`] (global sink); this exists so\n/// the planted-fault proofs can assert the FDR entry deterministically.\npub fn self_check_all_into_ring(\n    ring: RingHandle,\n    wk: &Weights,\n    activation_override: Option<&[i8; H]>,\n) -> Result<(), ChecksumFault> {\n    let mut ring = Some(ring);\n    self_check_core(wk, activation_override, |layer| fault(layer, ring.as_mut()))\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::inference::spec::{B1, B2, SCALE1, SCALE2, W1, W2};\n\n    // ── FDR test harness (native only; wasm has no FDR ring) ────────────────────────\n    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]\n    mod fdr {\n        use super::*;\n        use crate::fdr::ring;\n\n        use core::cell::RefCell;\n        /// A unique FDR ring for this test process. The fault's typed Alarm is written\n        /// directly to it via [`self_check_all_into_ring`], so the entry is recoverable and\n        use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n        thread_local! {\n            static TDIR: RefCell<Option<std::path::PathBuf>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };\n        }\n        fn ring_dir() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n            let existing = TDIR.with(|c| c.borrow().clone());\n            if let Some(d) = existing {\n                d\n            } else {\n                static GLOBAL: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);\n                let n = GLOBAL.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                let d =\n                    std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("item40_fdr_{}_{}", std::process::id(), n));\n                TDIR.with(|c| c.borrow_mut().replace(d.clone()));\n                d\n            }\n        }\n        /// verifiable WITHOUT racing the process-global `OnceLock` sink (which may be owned\n        /// by another test in the same binary).\n        fn fresh_ring() -> ring::FdrRing {\n            let dir = ring_dir();\n            let _ = crate::vfs::create_dir_all(&dir);\n            ring::FdrRing::open(dir, 1 << 20).expect("open FDR ring")\n        }\n\n        fn dir() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n            ring_dir()\n        }\n\n        fn alarms_with_layer(layer: Layer) -> usize {\n            let rec = ring::recover(&dir());\n            rec.records\n                .iter()\n                .filter(|r| {\n                    r.kind == "alarm"\n                        && r.name == "checksum_fault"\n                        && r.raw.contains(&format!("\\"layer\\":\\"{}\\"", layer.as_str()))\n                })\n                .count()\n        }\n\n        /// §B5.4 — an uncorrupted run is checksum-SILENT (no false trip, no FDR entry).\n        #[test]\n        fn healthy_run_is_checksum_silent() {\n            let _ = crate::vfs::remove_dir_all(dir());\n            let r = fresh_ring();\n            let res = self_check_all_into_ring(r, &Weights::spec(), None);\n            assert!(res.is_ok(), "healthy run must not trip: {res:?}");\n            assert_eq!(\n                alarms_with_layer(Layer::L1PreRequant),\n                0,\n                "healthy run must write NO checksum_fault FDR entry"\n            );\n            assert_eq!(\n                alarms_with_layer(Layer::Hidden),\n                0,\n                "healthy run must write NO checksum_fault FDR entry"\n            );\n            assert_eq!(\n                alarms_with_layer(Layer::Logits),\n                0,\n                "healthy run must write NO checksum_fault FDR entry"\n            );\n        }\n\n        /// §B5.2 / P7 — a planted SINGLE-BIT WEIGHT corruption hard-fails to safe state\n        /// (Err at L1) AND writes the typed FDR `checksum_fault` entry. RED→GREEN: deleting\n        /// the planted fault (or the check) turns the gate GREEN — the test IS the planted\n        /// fault, re-executed by CI on every run (proof B5.5).\n        #[test]\n        fn planted_weight_fault_hard_fails_and_writes_fdr() {\n            let _ = crate::vfs::remove_dir_all(dir());\n            let r = fresh_ring();\n            // Single-bit corruption of one frozen weight (W1[0]: 2 → 3).\n            let mut w1 = W1;\n            w1[0] ^= 1;\n            let wk = Weights {\n                w1: &w1,\n                b1: &B1,\n                scale1: SCALE1,\n                w2: &W2,\n                b2: &B2,\n                scale2: SCALE2,\n            };\n            let res = self_check_all_into_ring(r, &wk, None);\n            assert!(res.is_err(), "planted weight corruption must hard-fail");\n            assert_eq!(\n                res.unwrap_err().layer,\n                Layer::L1PreRequant,\n                "fault must be caught at layer 1"\n            );\n            assert!(\n                alarms_with_layer(Layer::L1PreRequant) >= 1,\n                "FDR checksum_fault entry required on weight fault"\n            );\n        }\n\n        /// §B5.3 / P7 — a planted SINGLE-BIT ACTIVATION corruption (mid-pipeline hidden)\n        /// hard-fails (caught at the next golden-checked boundary, `Logits`) AND writes the\n        /// typed FDR `checksum_fault` entry. The corruption feeds layer 2's input, so the\n        /// first golden-checked layer that diverges is the Logits layer. RED→GREEN: the test\n        /// IS the planted fault (proof B5.5).\n        #[test]\n        fn planted_activation_fault_hard_fails_and_writes_fdr() {\n            let _ = crate::vfs::remove_dir_all(dir());\n            let r = fresh_ring();\n            // Single-bit activation corruption: vec 0's oracle hidden is all-zero; flip\n            // bit 0 → 1. This is a corrupted *activation*, not a weight.\n            let mut hidden = [0i8; H];\n            hidden[0] ^= 1;\n            let res = self_check_all_into_ring(r, &Weights::spec(), Some(&hidden));\n            assert!(res.is_err(), "planted activation corruption must hard-fail");\n            assert_eq!(\n                res.unwrap_err().layer,\n                Layer::Logits,\n                "activation fault must be caught at the Logits boundary"\n            );\n            assert!(\n                alarms_with_layer(Layer::Logits) >= 1,\n                "FDR checksum_fault entry required on activation fault"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n}\n	2788	-1	-1		ca3037fe8a85a3736305aac1d13252054476bc6ca150678e99525cc93340e633594a35d3dfe3508705730359a5d21ca887814f44bf6b8839b466ff24f304292c4edbc459ace04119ce896909f7bbcb9971e96c3aad4bc04348d6a280300f0f8de420e7f292cb158c85010e0ed07d1be868b5412c439928aa9321e4e5716729f2
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/living_knowledge.rs	living_knowledge · 541 lines	//! Living-knowledge retrieval — ADAPTER (not a reimplementation).\n//!\n//! Decision (operator, 2026-07-14): the living-knowledge engine lives on a DIVERGENT\n//! branch (`recover/stash-1-2994e6c8`, JS + bge-small ONNX embedder). This module wires\n//! it in via a clean adapter — it does NOT merge the JS spike into the kernel. The kernel\n//! defines the trait + a process-backed adapter that speaks JSON-over-stdio to a bridge\n//! command. The bridge is swappable: a minimal deterministic reference bridge ships here\n//! for offline RED→GREEN verification; the real ONNX-backed spike is plugged in at runtime\n//! by pointing `LK_BRIDGE_CMD` at it (no kernel recompile needed).\n//!\n//! Fail-closed: any spawn / I/O / protocol error returns `Err` — retrieval never silently\n//! degrades to "empty results".\n\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n\nuse dowiz_core::json::{parse, Value};\n\n// The `no_std` contract (`Hit`, `DocInput`, `LivingKnowledge`) + the PRIMARY recall\n// surface (`recall_at_k`, `primary_recall_adapter`) live in `dowiz_core::living_knowledge`\n// and are re-exported here. This shim keeps ONLY the process-backed adapter\n// (`SubprocessLivingKnowledge` + the raw `wait4` reap machinery) and its JSON bridge\n// protocol (`BridgeRequest`/`BridgeResponse`).\npub use dowiz_core::living_knowledge::{\n    primary_recall_adapter, recall_at_k, DocInput, Hit, LivingKnowledge,\n};\n\n/// Serialize the bridge stdin contract (`{"files":[...],"query":"...","k":N}`),\n/// hand-rolled (wave-59): the last `serde_json` consumer in the kernel lib graph.\nfn request_to_json(files: &[DocInput], query: &str, k: usize) -> String {\n    let files_v: Vec<Value> = files\n        .iter()\n        .map(|d| {\n            Value::Object(vec![\n                ("rel".to_string(), Value::from(d.rel.clone())),\n                ("title".to_string(), Value::from(d.title.clone())),\n                ("text".to_string(), Value::from(d.text.clone())),\n            ])\n        })\n        .collect();\n    Value::Object(vec![\n        ("files".to_string(), Value::Array(files_v)),\n        ("query".to_string(), Value::from(query.to_string())),\n        ("k".to_string(), Value::from(k as i64)),\n    ])\n    .to_string()\n}\n\n/// Parse the bridge stdout contract (`{"results":[{"id":..,"score":..},..]}`).\nfn parse_response(stdout: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Hit>, String> {\n    let s = std::str::from_utf8(stdout)\n        .map_err(|e| format!("living_knowledge: parse response: {e}"))?;\n    let v = parse(s).map_err(|e| format!("living_knowledge: parse response: {e}"))?;\n    let results = v\n        .get("results")\n        .and_then(Value::as_array)\n        .ok_or_else(|| "living_knowledge: parse response: missing results".to_string())?;\n    let mut hits = Vec::with_capacity(results.len());\n    for r in results {\n        let id = r\n            .get("id")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            .ok_or_else(|| "living_knowledge: parse response: missing id".to_string())?;\n        let score = r\n            .get("score")\n            .and_then(Value::as_f64)\n            .ok_or_else(|| "living_knowledge: parse response: missing score".to_string())?;\n        hits.push(Hit { id, score });\n    }\n    Ok(hits)\n}\n\n/// Process-backed adapter. Spawns `bridge_cmd` (default: `LK_BRIDGE_CMD` env, else the\n/// bundled reference bridge via `node`) once per `retrieve` call. Fail-closed.\npub struct SubprocessLivingKnowledge {\n    bridge_cmd: String,\n    corpus: Vec<DocInput>,\n}\n\nimpl SubprocessLivingKnowledge {\n    /// Build an adapter. `bridge_cmd` is the command invoked with the JSON request on\n    /// stdin; the JSON response is read from stdout. Use an absolute path or a command on\n    /// `PATH`. When `None`, falls back to `LK_BRIDGE_CMD` env, then to the bundled\n    /// `scripts/lk-bridge.mjs` reference (requires `node` on PATH).\n    pub fn new(corpus: Vec<DocInput>, bridge_cmd: Option<String>) -> Self {\n        let bridge_cmd = bridge_cmd\n            .or_else(|| std::env::var("LK_BRIDGE_CMD").ok())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| "node scripts/lk-bridge.mjs".to_string());\n        Self { bridge_cmd, corpus }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl LivingKnowledge for SubprocessLivingKnowledge {\n    fn retrieve(&self, query: &str, k: usize) -> Result<Vec<Hit>, String> {\n        if query.trim().is_empty() {\n            return Err("living_knowledge: empty query".to_string());\n        }\n        let payload = request_to_json(&self.corpus, query, k);\n\n        let mut child = Command::new("sh")\n            .arg("-c")\n            .arg(&self.bridge_cmd)\n            .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n            .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n            .spawn()\n            .map_err(|e| format!("living_knowledge: spawn bridge `{}`: {e}", self.bridge_cmd))?;\n\n        {\n            let mut stdin = child\n                .stdin\n                .take()\n                .ok_or_else(|| "living_knowledge: bridge stdin unavailable".to_string())?;\n            stdin\n                .write_all(payload.as_bytes())\n                .map_err(|e| format!("living_knowledge: write request: {e}"))?;\n            // Drop stdin so the child sees EOF and begins producing output.\n        }\n\n        // Item 61 (gap G6): reap the child via a hand-rolled `wait4(2)` raw syscall\n        // (zero-dep, native-only x86_64 Linux — the exact style as `fdr::pmu.rs`'s\n        // `perf_event_open`) so we capture REAL rusage (user/sys time, maxrss) and wall\n        // duration, instead of `wait_with_output` which yields only status + stdio. A\n        // hung/expensive child is now OBSERVABLE via the FDR record this emits\n        // (composes with item 48's liveness class — the record is the evidence a child\n        // ran long). Fail-closed behavior is UNCHANGED: any spawn/IO/reap error still\n        // returns `Err` (the `?` paths below), so retrieval never silently degrades to\n        // "empty results".\n        //\n        // The reaping is native-only: subprocess spawning is not a wasm capability, so on\n        // `wasm32` this whole adapter is unreachable (named absence per procedure step 9).\n        #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\n        let reap = {\n            let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();\n            let (status, rusage) = wait4(child.id(), &mut child)?;\n            let wall_us = t0.elapsed().as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;\n            (status, rusage, wall_us)\n        };\n        #[cfg(not(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64")))]\n        let reap = {\n            let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();\n            let status = child\n                .wait()\n                .map_err(|e| format!("living_knowledge: wait bridge: {e}"))?;\n            let wall_us = t0.elapsed().as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;\n            // rusage unavailable on this platform — a named absence, never a fabricated 0.\n            let rusage = ChildRusage {\n                utime_us: None,\n                stime_us: None,\n                maxrss_kb: None,\n            };\n            (status, rusage, wall_us)\n        };\n        let (status, rusage, wall_us) = reap;\n\n        // Emit the FDR record (recoverable from the ring after the call). The record is\n        // P3-plane telemetry: it carries the REAL measured numbers — never a fabricated 0.\n        // No-op unless an FDR sink (with a ring) is installed.\n        crate::fdr::emit_subprocess_record(\n            self.bridge_cmd.as_str(),\n            status_success(status),\n            wall_us,\n            rusage.utime_us,\n            rusage.stime_us,\n            rusage.maxrss_kb,\n            None,\n        );\n\n        // Read the child's captured stdio for parsing. We re-collect stdout/stderr\n        // regardless of reap path.\n        let out = collect_child_output(&mut child)\n            .map_err(|e| format!("living_knowledge: read bridge output: {e}"))?;\n        if !status_success(status) {\n            let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr);\n            return Err(format!(\n                "living_knowledge: bridge exited {}: {}",\n                status,\n                stderr.lines().next().unwrap_or("<no stderr>")\n            ));\n        }\n\n        parse_response(&out.stdout)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 61 (gap G6): a reaped child's resource usage. On x86_64 Linux the values come\n/// from the real `wait4(2)` `rusage` struct; elsewhere they are a named absence.\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\nstruct ChildRusage {\n    utime_us: Option<u64>,\n    stime_us: Option<u64>,\n    maxrss_kb: Option<u64>,\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64")))]\nstruct ChildRusage {\n    utime_us: Option<u64>,\n    stime_us: Option<u64>,\n    maxrss_kb: Option<u64>,\n}\n\n/// Exit status of a reaped child. Kept as a plain struct (not `std::process::ExitStatus`)\n/// because the `wait4` path decodes the raw `wstatus` directly and the fallback path wraps\n/// `std::process::ExitStatus`.\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\n#[derive(Clone, Copy)]\nstruct ChildStatus {\n    raw: i32,\n}\n\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\nimpl ChildStatus {\n    fn success(self) -> bool {\n        // WIFEXITED && WEXITSTATUS == 0\n        (self.raw & 0x7f) == 0 && ((self.raw >> 8) & 0xff) == 0\n    }\n}\n\n/// Mirrors `std::process::ExitStatus`'s `Display` ("exit status: N" / "signal: N") so the\n/// bridge-exited error message reads identically on the raw-`wait4` path and the fallback\n/// `std::process` path.\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\nimpl core::fmt::Display for ChildStatus {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {\n        if (self.raw & 0x7f) == 0 {\n            // WIFEXITED → WEXITSTATUS\n            write!(f, "exit status: {}", (self.raw >> 8) & 0xff)\n        } else {\n            // WIFSIGNALED (or stopped) → WTERMSIG\n            write!(f, "signal: {}", self.raw & 0x7f)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\nfn status_success(s: ChildStatus) -> bool {\n    s.success()\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64")))]\nfn status_success(s: std::process::ExitStatus) -> bool {\n    s.success()\n}\n\n/// Raw 5-argument `syscall` (x86_64 Linux): number in `rax`, args in\n/// `rdi/rsi/rdx/r10/r8`, result in `rax`; the kernel clobbers `rcx` and `r11`. Returns the\n/// raw kernel result (negative = `-errno`). Mirrors `fdr::pmu::syscall5`.\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\n#[inline]\nunsafe fn syscall5(n: i64, a1: i64, a2: i64, a3: i64, a4: i64, a5: i64) -> i64 {\n    let ret: i64;\n    core::arch::asm!(\n        "syscall",\n        inlateout("rax") n => ret,\n        in("rdi") a1,\n        in("rsi") a2,\n        in("rdx") a3,\n        in("r10") a4,\n        in("r8") a5,\n        lateout("rcx") _,\n        lateout("r11") _,\n        options(nostack),\n    );\n    ret\n}\n\n/// `rusage` to the VER0 (72-byte on x86_64) ABI. Native-only (x86_64 Linux). A\n/// `rusage` of all-zero from the kernel would mean a genuinely-idle child, NOT a missing\n/// counter — but a planted SLOW child (busy-loop / sleeps) yields BIG utime/stime/wall,\n/// which is what the red→green test asserts (never a fabricated 0).\n#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]\nfn wait4(pid: u32, child: &mut std::process::Child) -> Result<(ChildStatus, ChildRusage), String> {\n    const SYS_WAIT4: i64 = 61;\n    let options: i64 = 0; // blocking wait\n    let mut ru: Rusage = Rusage::default();\n    // SAFETY: `&mut ru` is a live repr(C) buffer for the duration of the call; the kernel\n    // writes within the `rusage` layout. `child.id()` is the PID we wait on specifically\n    // (not any-child) so we reap exactly the bridge process we spawned.\n    let ret = unsafe {\n        syscall5(\n            SYS_WAIT4,\n            pid as i64,\n            &mut ru as *mut Rusage as i64,\n            options,\n            0,\n            0,\n        )\n    };\n    if ret < 0 {\n        // Reap defensively so we don't leak a zombie, then surface the error fail-closed.\n        let _ = child.wait();\n        return Err(format!("living_knowledge: wait4 failed (errno {})", -ret));\n    }\n    let utime_us = (ru.ru_utime[0] as u64)\n        .wrapping_mul(1_000_000)\n        .wrapping_add(ru.ru_utime[1] as u64);\n    let stime_us = (ru.ru_stime[0] as u64)\n        .wrapping_mul(1_000_000)\n        .wrapping_add(ru.ru_stime[1] as u64);\n    let maxrss_kb = if ru.ru_maxrss > 0 {\n        Some(ru.ru_maxrss as u64)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    Ok((\n        ChildStatus { raw: ret as i32 },\n        ChildRusage {\n            utime_us: Some(utime_us),\n            stime_us: Some(stime_us),\n            maxrss_kb,\n        },\n    ))\n}\n\n/// Collect a child's captured stdout/stderr after reaping (used by both reaping paths).\n///\n/// One portable impl for both cfg arms: the child is ALREADY reaped by the time this is\n/// called (raw `wait4` on x86_64 Linux, `Child::wait` elsewhere), so we only drain the\n/// still-open pipe ends. The reference bridge fuses lexical + title signals\n    /// (no ONNX), so a lexical query must surface the right doc at rank 1.\n    fn corpus() -> Vec<DocInput> {\n        vec![\n            DocInput {\n                rel: "docs/pricing.md".into(),\n                title: "Pricing model".into(),\n                text: "The pricing model computes subtotal, delivery fee, tax, and total.".into(),\n            },\n            DocInput {\n                rel: "docs/delivery.md".into(),\n                title: "Delivery flow".into(),\n                text: "The delivery flow tracks the courier from pickup to dropoff.".into(),\n            },\n            DocInput {\n                rel: "docs/refund.md".into(),\n                title: "Refund policy".into(),\n                text: "The refund policy returns money to the customer within 14 days.".into(),\n            },\n        ]\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve the bundled reference bridge (repo-root `scripts/lk-bridge.mjs`) from the\n    /// kernel crate dir, so the test is cwd-independent.\n    fn bridge_cmd() -> String {\n        let here = env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"); // .../dowiz/kernel\n        let repo = std::path::Path::new(here)\n            .parent()\n            .expect("kernel crate has a parent (repo root)");\n        let script = repo.join("scripts").join("lk-bridge.mjs");\n        format!("node {}", script.display())\n    }\n\n    /// True only when a working `node` runtime AND the bundled bridge script exist.\n    /// Lets the bridge-dependent test skip cleanly on headless/kernel boxes.\n    fn bridge_available() -> bool {\n        if !crate::kprocess::run("node", &["--version".to_string()]).success() {\n            return false; // `node` not on PATH or non-zero exit\n        }\n        let here = env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR");\n        let repo = std::path::Path::new(here).parent().expect("repo root");\n        repo.join("scripts").join("lk-bridge.mjs").exists()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn adapter_routes_query_to_bridge_and_ranks_correctly() {\n        // The bridge is a node subprocess. module is gated there); the\n    // bridge-dependent test above stays skipped when node is absent, but this one\n    // needs no node and exercises the real in-kernel ranker.\n    fn from pickup to dropoff and estimates arrival".into(),\n            "refund policy returns money to the customer within fourteen days of a return".into(),\n            "catalog holds the trusted price 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/render/gpu.rs	gpu · 102 lines	//! P38 O18a — REAL minimal headless GPU bring-up (`#[cfg(feature = "gpu")]`).\n//!\n//! This is NOT a stub. It constructs a live `wgpu::Instance`, requests a real\n//! `Adapter`, and (best-effort) a `Device`/`Queue`, returning a typed\n//! `GpuContext`. GPU absence is a *typed value* (`GpuError::NoAdapter`), never a\n//! panic — the degrade-not-crash arm of BLUEPRINT-P38 §4.1. The kernel's\n//! decide/fold order authority has no GPU dependency at all; this is additive.\n//!\n//! innovate: wgpu's `request_adapter`/`request_device` are async. The kernel is\n//! a synchronous rlib with no async runtime in its canonical graph, so we bridge\n//! with `pollster::block_on` (also `gpu`-gated). Upgrade trigger: if/when the\n//! render stack grows a real event loop / async surface pump (P38a G2+ live\n//! present path), replace `block_on` with that loop's executor rather than\n//! blocking the calling thread. Until then, headless bring-up is synchronous by\n//! design (CI-runnable, no surface).\n\nuse wgpu::{Adapter, Device, Instance, Queue};\n\n/// Typed absence / failure of the GPU path. NEVER panics; the caller falls back\n/// to the CPU `compose()` floor (BLUEPRINT-P38 §3.6 ladder).\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum GpuError {\n    /// No GPU adapter available on this host (headless CI, no drivers, etc.).\n    NoAdapter,\n    /// An adapter existed but device creation failed (carries wgpu's reason).\n    DeviceRequest(String),\n}\n\nimpl core::fmt::Display for GpuError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            GpuError::NoAdapter => write!(f, "gpu: no adapter available"),\n            GpuError::DeviceRequest(e) => write!(f, "gpu: device request failed: {e}"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for GpuError {}\n\n/// A live, headless GPU context: instance → adapter → device + queue, NO surface.\n/// Presentation-only; holding this does not couple the kernel's state authority\n/// to the GPU (BLUEPRINT-P38 §4.3 bulkhead).\npub struct GpuContext {\n    pub instance: Instance,\n    pub adapter: Adapter,\n    pub device: Device,\n    pub queue: Queue,\n}\n\n/// Real minimal init: build a `wgpu::Instance`, request an `Adapter`, then a\n/// `Device`/`Queue`. Headless (no surface) so it is CI-runnable. Returns a typed\n/// error instead of panicking when no GPU is present.\npub fn init() -> Result<GpuContext, GpuError> {\n    let instance = Instance::new(wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle());\n\n    let adapter = pollster::block_on(instance.request_adapter(&wgpu::RequestAdapterOptions {\n        power_preference: wgpu::PowerPreference::default(),\n        force_fallback_adapter: false,\n        compatible_surface: None,\n        ..Default::default()\n    }))\n    .map_err(|_| GpuError::NoAdapter)?;\n\n    let (device, queue) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {\n        label: Some("dowiz-kernel-headless"),\n        required_features: wgpu::Features::empty(),\n        required_limits: wgpu::Limits::downlevel_defaults(),\n        memory_hints: wgpu::MemoryHints::default(),\n        trace: wgpu::Trace::Off,\n        ..Default::default()\n    }))\n    .map_err(|e| GpuError::DeviceRequest(e.to_string()))?;\n\n    Ok(GpuContext {\n        instance,\n        adapter,\n        device,\n        queue,\n    })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Bring-up must never panic: it either returns a live context or a typed\n    /// `GpuError` (the degrade-not-crash arm). On a headless CI box with no GPU\n    /// this exercises the `NoAdapter` path.\n    #[test]\n    fn init_never_panics() {\n        match init() {\n            Ok(ctx) => {\n                let info = ctx.adapter.get_info();\n                assert!(!info.name.is_empty() || info.name.is_empty());\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Typed absence, not a crash.\n                let _ = e.to_string();\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n	2978	-1	-1		5f24ad9fdcda2173f13af8d53a0673612cfebd0ddf6634aeaa57824c119c2025186e253be287660fe552c1eb6957fee8cff1db65b7410ee2adf07205a74e58571f9a5498418228ab958b2800b5b9ec18566f500a2175db78ccc2a2af4c59c500a8f0b3e607f05aef4e196a2f1a243af3083b4077a98c91730751eeed7d2e3470
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/miri_selftest.rs	miri_selftest · 44 lines	//! Item 52 (space-grade roadmap §J): planted-fault self-test for the `miri-gate`.\n//!\n//! A DELIBERATELY out-of-bounds read, gated so it is harmless on the native\n//! backend but UB under the Miri interpreter. `cargo miri test miri_selftest::`\n//! MUST report Undefined Behavior and halt — the gate (`scripts/miri-gate.sh`,\n//! the `mode=miri` row with `min_tests = UB`) asserts that Miri DID report the\n//! UB, so the gate is proven to detect real UB rather than passing vacuously.\n//!\n//! If a misconfigured Miri ever stopped detecting the UB (stripped\n//! instrumentation, broken toolchain, a filter matching nothing), the run would\n//! exit ZERO (UB uncaught) and the gate goes RED — the `ct_gate`/`kani_selftest`\n//! planted-fault idiom, making "the gate detects real UB" a standing property,\n//! not a one-off demo.\n//!\n//! The whole module is compiled under `cfg(test)` (so a plain `cargo test`\n//! proves it compiles and the no-op native branch runs harmlessly — zero\n//! footprint in any shipping/non-test build) AND under `cfg(miri)` (where the\n//! planted-UB branch executes). Declared in `lib.rs` as\n//! `#[cfg(any(test, miri))] mod miri_selftest;`.\n\n/// Planted out-of-bounds read. Under native `cargo test` the body is the no-op\n/// branch (proves compilation, executes NO UB). Under `cargo miri test` the\n/// `cfg(miri)` branch runs and reads one past a length-1 slice — Miri MUST\n/// report `Undefined Behavior`.\n#[test]\nfn miri_selftest_planted_oob() {\n    // Native backend: no-op. (Runs under `cargo test` to prove this module\n    // compiles; the UB branch below is compiled out here.)\n    #[cfg(not(miri))]\n    {\n        // Intentionally empty — the real check only exists under Miri.\n        let _sanity: u8 = 0;\n        core::hint::black_box(_sanity);\n    }\n    // Miri interpreter: execute the planted UB. `slice` has length 1; index 99\n    // is an out-of-bounds read that Miri is obligated to flag.\n    #[cfg(miri)]\n    {\n        let slice: &[u8] = &[1u8];\n        // SAFETY: intentionally ABSENT — this is the planted fault.\n        let _val = unsafe { *slice.as_ptr().add(99) };\n        core::hint::black_box(_val);\n    }\n}\n	2988	-1	-1		ebf7141894cee13331812c67a3a7f305a57fbe6e54d6f7ae0f502a6fd547e5090c0a752cdf9d74ef65d30129a196c4ba5f235d0415ea8c2b407f760fc704c8cf87b804bdc3cfd098c7cda1183d38cc997ceb2c1e6db57fafe58290d0005b1fbd444a8326c3fed2a75ecc425f5341c522a81fe06fbf9d29ed0313f4cdca6228d2
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/proxy_redirect.rs	proxy_redirect · 16 lines	//! proxy_redirect.rs — std host shim (pure pool/rotation logic lives in\n//! `dowiz_core::proxy_redirect`; the wall-clock `now_us()` seam stays here).\n//!\n//! The no_std core injects timestamps as explicit `now_us_val` parameters;\n//! this shim supplies the real microsecond wall clock so callers can stamp\n//! `record_success`/`record_failure` with live time.\n\npub use dowiz_core::proxy_redirect::*;\n\n/// Monotonic timestamp in microseconds (wall clock, platform-specific).\npub fn now_us() -> u64 {\n    std::time::SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_micros() as u64)\n        .unwrap_or(0)\n}\n	3003	-1	-1		ea0ef0df3dc747758051455f803e170b905a952c4451f20e6d122e169333ebf55c83a50095e1161a8474c240c0d6142a46a142d6f78904b94b07f412900baac2ce2e157981ce3bc51bbe1f5136b84c723fb1d44a9e38c7aa9a0443c057919fe710f07653bbd26211c463e6d5551c05b0ad7dcd6b59d18d3694849c7558355c10
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/retrieval/bm25.rs	bm25 · 41 lines	//! `retrieval/bm25.rs` — std shim over the pure no_std core.\n//!\n//! The Okapi BM25 ranker ([`Bm25`]/[`Document`]/[`Bm25Params`] + scoring/encode/decode) lives\n//! in `dowiz_core::retrieval::bm25` and is re-exported here. This shim adds ONLY the std\n//! on-disk persistence (P95 Option A) as free functions: [`bm25_save`]/[`bm25_load`].\n\npub use dowiz_core::retrieval::bm25::*;\n\n/// Persist a BM25 index to a std-only on-disk file (P95 Option A).\npub fn bm25_save(bm: &Bm25, path: &std::path::Path) -> Result<(), String> {\n    crate::vfs::write(path, bm.encode())\n        .map_err(|e| format!("bm25_save {}: {e}", path.display()))\n}\n\n/// Load a persisted BM25 index from a std-only on-disk file (P95 Option A).\npub fn bm25_load(path: &std::path::Path) -> Result<Bm25, String> {\n    let buf =\n        crate::vfs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("bm25_load {}: {e}", path.display()))?;\n    Bm25::decode(&buf).ok_or_else(|| format!("bm25_load {}: corrupt index", path.display()))\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn save_load_roundtrips_byte_identical() {\n        let docs = vec![\n            Document::from_text("the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"),\n            Document::from_text("never gonna give you up never gonna let you down"),\n            Document::from_text("to be or not to be that is the question"),\n        ];\n        let bm = Bm25::new(docs);\n        let path =\n            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bm25_persist_test_{}.bin", std::process::id()));\n        bm25_save(&bm, &path).expect("save");\n        let loaded = bm25_load(&path).expect("load");\n        crate::vfs::remove_file(&path).ok();\n        assert_eq!(loaded.encode(), bm.encode(), "loaded index must be byte-identical");\n    }\n}\n	3011	-1	-1		ef80bfff7d4b90510305a1fd3c865b22f9d6b1afa661358bc8a189441f90c36f806d1113745a3e525590f7234904d53c8d3915941aecc03773287221db25ea4f7e90409308233508cc097910b718c4c825405c20dc86c45c8c9031f058663a6df0553275c581c2a7cb549eb65206ffc086f145220fb25185271860c664f47dd2
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/retrieval/memory_store.rs	memory_store · 173 lines	//! `retrieval/memory_store.rs` — std shim over the pure no_std core (M4 / W4-1).\n//!\n//! The pure half — the [`MemoryStore`] trait, the content-addressed\n//! [`InMemoryStore`] (`BTreeMap` behind a spinlock), and the FNV-1a snapshot-root\n//! fold ([`fnv1a`]/[`FNV_OFFSET`]) — lives in `dowiz_core::retrieval::memory_store`\n//! and is re-exported here so the kernel's `crate::retrieval::memory_store::…`\n//! spellings keep resolving unchanged.\n//!\n//! This shim adds ONLY the std-only [`PgStore`] — the opt-in `pgrust` SQL adapter\n//! (`sqlx` + `tokio`) behind a NON-default feature flag. The default path remains\n//! the pure in-process [`InMemoryStore`].\n\npub use dowiz_core::retrieval::memory_store::*;\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Optional Postgres (`pgrust`) adapter — a REAL sqlx-backed living-memory store.\n///\n/// Compiled ONLY under the `pgrust` feature. The kernel's hard invariant is\n/// pure-`std` with NO network deps by DEFAULT; the native [`InMemoryStore`]\n/// remains the default. `pgrust` is the opt-in SQL adapter: it pulls `sqlx` +\n/// `tokio` and implements the [`MemoryStore`] contract against a Postgres `kv`\n/// table. Because the trait boundary is synchronous but sqlx is async,\n/// `PgStore` captures a Tokio runtime [`Handle`] at construction and drives\n/// each call with `block_on` — so its public API is byte-identical to\n/// [`InMemoryStore`]. DDL is NEVER auto-run; call [`PgStore::migrate`] once,\n/// explicitly, against a known database.\n#[cfg(feature = "pgrust")]\npub struct PgStore {\n    pool: sqlx::PgPool,\n    rt: tokio::runtime::Handle,\n}\n\n#[cfg(feature = "pgrust")]\nimpl PgStore {\n    /// Connect to Postgres at `database_url` and build the connection pool.\n    ///\n    /// Does NOT create the schema — call [`migrate`](Self::migrate) explicitly.\n    /// Requires a Tokio runtime to be active on the constructing thread (it\n    /// captures that runtime's [`Handle`] so later sync calls can `block_on`).\n    pub async fn new(database_url: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {\n        let pool = sqlx::postgres::PgPoolOptions::new()\n            .connect(database_url)\n            .await\n            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n        Ok(Self {\n            pool,\n            rt: tokio::runtime::Handle::current(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Idempotent schema creation — EXPLICIT, NEVER auto-called.\n    ///\n    /// Migration is a red-line op; the default/adapter path never runs this.\n    /// Callers must invoke it deliberately against a known database.\n    pub async fn migrate(&self) -> Result<(), String> {\n        sqlx::query("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kv (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value BYTEA NOT NULL);")\n            .execute(&self.pool)\n            .await\n            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(feature = "pgrust")]\nimpl MemoryStore for PgStore {\n    fn put(&self, key: &str, value: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {\n        self.rt.block_on(async {\n            sqlx::query(\n                "INSERT INTO kv(key,value) VALUES($1,$2) \\\n                     ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value=$2",\n            )\n            .bind(key)\n            .bind(value)\n            .execute(&self.pool)\n            .await\n            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())\n        })?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.rt\n            .block_on(async {\n                sqlx::query_scalar::<_, Vec<u8>>("SELECT value FROM kv WHERE key=$1")\n                    .bind(key)\n                    .fetch_optional(&self.pool)\n                    .await\n                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())\n            })\n            .ok()\n            .flatten()\n    }\n\n    fn keys(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        self.rt\n            .block_on(async {\n                sqlx::query_scalar::<_, String>("SELECT key FROM kv ORDER BY key")\n                    .fetch_all(&self.pool)\n                    .await\n                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    fn snapshot_root(&self) -> String {\n        let rows: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)> = match self.rt.block_on(async {\n            sqlx::query_as::<_, (String, Vec<u8>)>("SELECT key,value FROM kv ORDER BY key")\n                .fetch_all(&self.pool)\n                .await\n                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())\n        }) {\n            Ok(r) => r,\n            Err(_) => return "pg_error".to_string(),\n        };\n        // Fold the SAME FNV-1a over `len || bytes` frames as\n        // `InMemoryStore::snapshot_root` so roots are comparable across stores.\n        let mut h: u64 = FNV_OFFSET;\n        for (k, v) in &rows {\n            h = fnv1a(h, &(k.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());\n            h = fnv1a(h, k.as_bytes());\n            h = fnv1a(h, &(v.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());\n            h = fnv1a(h, v);\n        }\n        format!("{:016x}", h)\n    }\n}\n\n/// DB-gated integration test for the `pgrust` adapter.\n///\n/// Compiled only under `--features pgrust` AND `cfg(test)`. It is `#[ignore]`d\n/// so an OFFLINE `cargo test` stays GREEN (the test is skipped, never failed).\n/// With a live Postgres reachable via `DATABASE_URL`, run it explicitly:\n/// `DATABASE_URL=... cargo test -p dowiz-kernel --features pgrust -- --ignored`.\n#[cfg(all(test, feature = "pgrust"))]\nmod pg_tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    #[ignore = "needs DATABASE_URL"]\n    fn pg_roundtrip() {\n        // Offline-safe: early-return unless a live Postgres URL is provided.\n        let url = match std::env::var("DATABASE_URL") {\n            Ok(u) => u,\n            Err(_) => return,\n        };\n        let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().expect("tokio runtime");\n        let pg = rt.block_on(PgStore::new(&url)).expect("connect");\n        rt.block_on(pg.migrate()).expect("migrate");\n        // put / get roundtrip + overwrite semantics.\n        pg.put("roundtrip-key", b"hello-pg").expect("put");\n        assert_eq!(\n            pg.get("roundtrip-key"),\n            Some(b"hello-pg".to_vec()),\n            "get must roundtrip"\n        );\n        pg.put("roundtrip-key", b"world-pg").expect("put2");\n        assert_eq!(\n            pg.get("roundtrip-key"),\n            Some(b"world-pg".to_vec()),\n            "overwrite must replace, not append"\n        );\n        // snapshot_root parity vs an equivalent InMemoryStore (merges evidence).\n        let mut mem = InMemoryStore::new();\n        mem.put("roundtrip-key", b"world-pg").expect("mem put");\n        assert_eq!(\n            pg.snapshot_root(),\n            mem.snapshot_root(),\n            "pg snapshot_root must match InMemoryStore for identical content"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	3023	-1	-1		e9a4153d3c178221b27b21cb3013720468979465c9946ccb9b55485f91a88b277d4146814e83726f840dd36921d5d638c6a93c857460047880d7f30da60e784edc0c5799e89ac141850d2150b59ba9fae37b7c4a35d1ff5c4e14a3e0680985ada022b334034a92acca110a9d4845bbbc44b7498effc12de58f0936d611f13c63
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/retrieval/recall.rs	recall · 282 lines	//! retrieval/recall.rs — std shim over the no_std recall core.\n//!\n//! The pure ranker (`PrimaryRecall`, `build_fusion`, `fusion_rank`, the fixture\n//! corpus, `file_stem`, and the `encode_index`/`from_parts`/`trigram_docs`/\n//! `stems` accessors) lives in `dowiz_core::retrieval::recall` and is re-exported\n//! here. This shim adds ONLY the std-dependent pieces:\n//!   - the disk persistence free functions (`from_dir`, `save`, `load`, plus\n//!     `save_to`/`load_from`/`stem_list`) — they route through the kernel's\n//!     std-backed `crate::vfs` (core's `crate::vfs` is the no_std seam that\n//!     returns `NotFound`, so the I/O must live here, exactly like\n//!     `retrieval/ppr`/`diffusion` keep their disk round-trips in `std::fs`);\n//!   - the lazy `OnceLock`-backed global `PRIMARY` instance + `primary()` accessor\n//!     + the `recall_at_k` free function (the self-improvement loop's entry point);\n//!   - the std-only disk round-trip + kill-9 tests.\n//!\n//! NOTE: the `LivingKnowledge` adapter impl for `PrimaryRecall` now lives in the core\n//! (`dowiz_core::retrieval::recall`), since both the trait and the type are core items — an\n//! impl here would be an orphan-rule violation.\n\npub use dowiz_core::retrieval::recall::*;\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse dowiz_core::retrieval::bm25::{Bm25, Document};\nuse dowiz_core::retrieval::index::TrigramIndex;\n\n/// Lazy-initialized PRIMARY recall instance — the shared kernel recall source.\nstatic PRIMARY: std::sync::OnceLock<PrimaryRecall> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();\n\nfn primary() -> &'static PrimaryRecall {\n    PRIMARY.get_or_init(PrimaryRecall::new)\n}\n\n/// PRIMARY recall entry point used by the self-improvement loop (W18.2).\n///\n/// Thin, deterministic, std-only wrapper over [`PrimaryRecall::recall_at_k`]\n/// (kernel-owned BM25+trigram fusion). The (wasm-gated) `living_knowledge`\n/// adapter delegates its lexical recall here. No JS, no network.\npub fn recall_at_k(query: &str, k: usize) -> Vec<(String, f64)> {\n    primary().recall_at_k(query, k)\n}\n\n/// Ingest a real memory corpus from `dir` — every `*.md` file becomes one\n/// document, keyed by its file stem (e.g. `MEMORY` from `MEMORY.md`).\n/// Directory walk via the kernel's std-backed `crate::vfs`; no recursion into\n/// subdirs (the living-memory corpus is flat). Fail-closed: a directory that\n/// yields zero `*.md` files errors rather than returning an empty ranker.\npub fn from_dir(dir: &str) -> Result<PrimaryRecall, String> {\n    let entries = crate::vfs::read_dir(dir)\n        .map_err(|e| format!("from_dir: read_dir {dir}: {e}"))?;\n    let mut paths: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n    for e in entries {\n        if e.extension() == Some("md") {\n            paths.push(e.path);\n        }\n    }\n    if paths.is_empty() {\n        return Err(format!("from_dir: no *.md files in {dir}"));\n    }\n    // Stable order ⇒ deterministic index regardless of read_dir iteration order.\n    paths.sort();\n    let texts: Vec<String> = paths\n        .iter()\n        .map(|p| crate::vfs::read_to_string(p).unwrap_or_default())\n        .collect();\n    let docs: Vec<Document> = texts.iter().map(|s| Document::from_text(s)).collect();\n    let strs: Vec<&str> = texts.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n    let bm = Bm25::new(docs);\n    let idx = TrigramIndex::new(&strs);\n    let ids: Vec<String> = paths\n        .iter()\n        .map(|p| file_stem(p).unwrap_or("?").to_string())\n        .collect();\n    Ok(PrimaryRecall::from_parts(bm, idx, ids))\n}\n\n/// The deterministic corpus stem list (sorted, matching `from_dir`'s sort).\nfn stem_list(dir: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {\n    let mut paths: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n    for e in crate::vfs::read_dir(dir)\n        .map_err(|e| format!("stem_list: read_dir {dir}: {e}"))?\n    {\n        if e.extension() == Some("md") {\n            paths.push(e.path);\n        }\n    }\n    paths.sort();\n    Ok(paths\n        .iter()\n        .map(|p| file_stem(p).unwrap_or("?").to_string())\n        .collect())\n}\n\n/// Persist the built index to `path` (through the kernel's std-backed vfs).\npub fn save_to(recall: &PrimaryRecall, path: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n    let blob = recall.encode_index();\n    // Prefix the trigram docs so load can rebuild the TrigramIndex\n    // deterministically, and store the STEM LIST (the dirty fingerprint) so\n    // `load` can detect a changed corpus without re-reading every file.\n    let mut trig = Vec::new();\n    for d in recall.trigram_docs() {\n        trig.extend_from_slice(&(d.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());\n        trig.extend_from_slice(d.as_bytes());\n    }\n    let mut stems = Vec::new();\n    for s in recall.stems() {\n        stems.extend_from_slice(&(s.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());\n        stems.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());\n    }\n    let mut out = out.extend_from_slice(&blob);\n    crate::vfs::write(path, &out).map_err(|e| format!("save_to {path}: {e}"))\n}\n\n/// Load a persisted index from `path`. crate::vfs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("load_from {path}: {e}"))?;\n    let trig_len =\n        u64::from_le_bytes(<[u8; 8]>::try_from(&buf[0..8]).map_err(|_| "corrupt header")?)\n            as }\n    while p < end_trig {\n        let l = u64::from_le_bytes(<[u8; 8]>::try_from(&buf[p..p + 8]).map_err(|_| "corrupt")?)\n            as usize;\n        p += 8;\n        let s = &buf[p..p + l];\n section".into());\n    }\n    let mut stems = Vec::new();\n    while p < end_stems {\n        let l = u64::from_le_bytes(<[u8; 8]>::try_from(&buf[p..p + 8]).map_err(|_| "corrupt")?)\n            as usize;\n        p += 8;\n        let s = &buf[p..p + l];\n        stems.push(String::from_utf8(s.to_vec()).map_err(|_| "corrupt utf8")?);\n        p += l;\n    }\n    let bm = Bm25::decode(&buf[p..])\n        .ok_or_else(|| "load_from: corrupt bm25".to_string())?;\n    let idx = TrigramIndex::new(&trig_docs.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>());\n    // ids are RED semantics: a test that asserts the *verify* step is doing real work — if\n//! we returned raw candidates (superset), the `matches == linear-oracle`\n//! assertions would FAIL. GREEN: after the exact verify, matches equal a\n//! linear-scan oracle and false positives == 0.\n\n#[allow(unused_imports)]\nuse super::fixtures::{synthetic_corpus, FIXTURE};\nuse "grep every doc" baseline from the manifest).\nfn linear_literal(docs: &[&str], needle: &str) -> Vec<u32> {\n    docs.iter()\n        .enumerate()\n        .filter(|(_, d)| d.contains(needle))\n        .map(|(i, _)| i as u32)\n        .collect()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn fixture_index_builds_with_20_docs() {\n    let idx = build();\n    assert_eq!(idx.len(), 20);\n    assert!(idx.postings_len() > 0, "index must contain trigrams");\n    // Determinism: a rebuild yields the identical literal-keyed posting count.\n    assert_eq!(\n        TrigramIndex::new(FIXTURE).postings_len(),\n        idx.postings_len()\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn literal_query_exact_and_zero_false_positives() {\n    let idx = build();\n    // "decay" appears only in "note-salience-decay.md" (doc 2).\n    let got = idx.query_literal("decay");\n    let oracle = linear_literal(FIXTURE, "decay");\n    assert_eq!(got, oracle, "matches must equal the linear-scan oracle");\n    assert_eq!(got, vec![2]);\n    // 0 false positives: every returned doc really contains the needle.\n    for &d in &got {\n        assert!(FIXTURE[d as usize].contains("decay"));\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn candidate_reduction_strictly_smaller_than_corpus() {\n    let idx = build();\n    let needle = "recall";\n    let cand = idx.candidate_count_literal(needle);\n    let matches = idx.query_literal(needle);\n    assert!(cand <= 20, "candidates must be ≤ corpus size");\n    assert!(\n        matches.len() <= cand,\n        "verify can only shrink the candidate set (0 false positives)"\n    );\n    // A rarer needle must reduce candidates further and hit exactly one doc.\n    let rare = "quantization";\n    let c_rare = idx.candidate_count_literal(rare);\n    assert!(c_rare < 20, "rare needle must reduce candidates");\n    assert_eq!(idx.query_literal(rare), vec![18]);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn verify_filters_overbroad_candidates_no_false_positives() {\n    let idx = build();\n    // "trigram-index" shares trigrams with others, but verify must reject\n    // docs that merely share a trigram yet lack the full needle.\n    let needle = "trigram-index";\n    let cand = idx.candidate_count_literal(needle);\n    let matches = idx.query_literal(needle);\n    assert!(\n        cand >= matches.len(),\n        "candidates are a superset of matches"\n    );\n    // matches == oracle, i.e. exactly the docs containing the needle.\n    assert_eq!(matches, linear_literal(FIXTURE, needle));\n    assert_eq!(matches, vec![5]);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn pattern_query_exact_and_zero_false_positives() {\n    let idx = build();\n    // Pattern with a literal trigram run → candidate reduction + matcher verify.\n    let pat = r"note-.*-recall";\n    let got = idx.query_pattern(pat).expect("valid pattern");\n    // Frozen golden: the retired `regex` crate matched exactly doc 7 for this\n    // pattern; that verdict is preserved here as a literal (the `regex`\n    // differential that produced it lives in `pattern.rs` pre-removal history +\n    // the naive-reference cross-check). See item-5 ruling.\n    assert_eq!(got, vec![7]); // note-heat-kernel-recall.md\n                              // 0 false positives: every returned doc really matches the pattern, verified\n                              // by the kernel-owned matcher (an independent recompile of the same pattern).\n    let compiled = super::pattern::Pattern::compile(pat).unwrap();\n    for &d in &got {\n        assert!(compiled.is_match(FIXTURE[d as usize]));\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn candidate_reduction_factor_on_synthetic_corpus() {\n    // N docs, each with a UNIQUE 12-char marker ⇒ querying the marker must\n    // reduce candidates to ~1 (the planted doc) ⇒ ~N× reduction.\n    let n = 2000usize;\n    let corpus = synthetic_corpus(n);\n    let docs: Vec<&str> = corpus.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n    let idx = TrigramIndex::new(&docs);\n    let marker = corpus[1234]\n        .trim_start_matches("boilerplate-prefix-")\n        .trim_end_matches("-suffix-boilerplate");\n    let cand = idx.candidate_count_literal(marker);\n    let matches = idx.query_literal(marker);\n    let factor = n as f64 / cand.max(1) as f64;\n    println!(\n        "[retrieval::bench] synthetic n={} candidates={} matches={} reduction={:.1}x",\n        n,\n        cand,\n        matches.len(),\n        factor\n    );\n    assert_eq!(matches, vec![1234]);\n    assert!(cand <= 1, "unique marker ⇒ ≤1 candidate");\n    assert!(\n        factor >= 50.0,\n        "expected ≥50× reduction, got {:.1}x",\n        factor\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn full_suite_parity_with_linear_oracle() {\n    // Exhaustively check a battery of needles against the linear oracle.\n    let idx = build();\n    let needles = [\n        "md",\n        "note",\n        "schema",\n        "push",\n        "tier",\n        "zstd",\n        "vsa",\n        "entropy",\n        "field",\n        "divergence",\n        "coherence",\n        "ttrain",\n        "pq",\n        "cdc",\n        "graph",\n        "index",\n        "decay",\n        "recall",\n        "fusion",\n        "gate",\n        "ledger",\n    ];\n    for nd in needles {\n        assert_eq!(\n            idx.query_literal(nd),\n            linear_literal(FIXTURE, nd),\n            "needle '{}' must match the linear oracle exactly",\n            nd\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n// ── W18 — living_knowledge Rust adapter as PRIMARY recall source ──\n// Deterministic recall@k integration test. Does NOT depend on the deleted\n// 324-file JS corpus: it asserts the wired `retrieval::recall_at_k` PRIMARY\n// recall API returns the expected top-k over the kernel's own deterministic\n// fixture corpus (recall@5 == 1.0 over a hand-verified oracle). 0 JS.\n\n#[test]\nfn w18_primary_recall_at_k_returns_expected_top_k() {\n    // GREEN gate: call the wired PRIMARY recall API and assert the top-k\n    // matches a known deterministic fixture. We verify on the kernel's own\n    // FIXTURE_CORPUS (the PRIMARY source) using hand-verified queries whose\n    // relevant doc is doc-id 0..=11; we check that recall_at_k surfaces the\n    // correct doc at rank 1 with a positive score (deterministic, no JS).\n    let hits = super::recall::recall_at_k("how is the order total calculated", 5);\n    assert!(!hits.is_empty(), "recall must return at least one hit");\n    assert_eq!(hits.len(), 5, "recall@5 must return exactly 5 ranked hits");\n    // PrimaryRecall ids are `lk:<position>`; doc 0 ("pricing") must be rank 1.\n    assert_eq!(hits[0].0, "lk:0", "primary recall must surface lk:0 first");\n    assert!(hits[0].1 > 0.0, "top hit must carry a positive BM25 score");\n    // Scores must be in non-increasing order (descending ranking).\n    for w in hits.windows(2) {\n        assert!(\n            w[0].1 >= w[1].1,\n            "recall ranking must be non-increasing in score"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn w18_primary_recall_at_5_is_one_point_zero_on_deterministic_fixture() {\n    // recall@5 == 1.0 over a hand-verified oracle derived from the kernel's\n    // PRIMARY corpus, certified by the kernel's own `csr::recall_at_k`. This\n    // is the headline property the blueprint requires (deterministic, 0 JS).\n    use crate::csr::recall_at_k;\n    const K: usize = 5;\n    let oracle: Vec<(&str, usize)> = vec![\n        ("how is the order total calculated", 0),\n        ("when does the package get delivered", 1),\n        ("can i get my money back", 2),\n        ("where are product prices defined", 3),\n        ("how does exact substring search work", 4),\n        ("what ranks documents by word frequency", 5),\n        ("which algorithm measures node importance in a graph", 6),\n        ("how do related memories get surfaced", 7),\n        ("why do old notes lose weight", 8),\n        ("how is stored memory made smaller", 9),\n        ("how are embeddings compressed", 10),\n        ("what tracks information gain of improvements", 11),\n    ];\n    let mut total = 0.0f64;\n    let mut successes = 0u64;\n    for (q, relevant) in &oracle {\n        let hits = super::recall::recall_at_k(q, K);\n        // Encode the ranking as a doc-id-indexed score vector for certify.\n        let mut scores = vec![0.0f64; 12];\n        for (pos, (id, _score)) in hits.iter().enumerate() {\n            let d: usize = id.strip_prefix("lk:").unwrap().parse().unwrap();\n            scores[d] = (hits.len() - pos) as f64;\n        }\n        let r = recall_at_k(&scores, &[*relevant], K);\n        assert_eq!(\n            r, 1.0,\n            "W18 primary recall: query '{}' must recall relevant doc lk:{} in top-{}",\n            q, relevant, K\n        );\n        total += r;\n        // Each query has exactly one relevant doc ⇒ a Bernoulli trial; r==1.0 is a\n        // success. mean recall@5 == 1.0 therefore means successes/n == 12/12.\n        if r == 1.0 {\n            successes += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    let n = oracle.len() as u64;\n    let mean = total / oracle.len() as f64;\n    assert_eq!(mean, 1.0, "mean recall@5 over the W18 oracle must be 1.0");\n\n    // E2 (§4 criterion 3 / D4): the bare `1.0` is unfalsifiable as displayed — a\n    // reader cannot tell whether it rests on 12 trials or 12 000. Attach the honest\n    // 95% Wilson lower bound. At p̂=1.0 the Wald interval degenerates to [1,1]; Wilson\n    // does not — for k=n it is n/(n+z²), computed here (NOT hardcoded from the doc).\n    assert_eq!(\n        successes, 12,\n        "12/12 Bernoulli successes back the 1.0 headline"\n    );\n    let (lo, hi) = crate::stats::wilson_interval(successes, n, 1.96);\n    let closed = n as f64 / (n as f64 + 1.96 * 1.96);\n    assert!(\n        (lo - closed).abs() < 1e-12,\n        "12/12 Wilson lower must equal n/(n+z²)={closed}"\n    );\n    assert!(\n        (lo - 0.7575).abs() < 1e-4,\n        "recall@5 12-query Wilson 95% lower bound must be ≈0.7575, got {lo}"\n    );\n    assert!(\n        (hi - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12,\n        "Wilson upper clamps to 1.0 at full success"\n    );\n    // A failing query (11/12) MUST move the floor — the interval reacts to evidence,\n    // it is not an assertable constant. (§4 criterion 3, D4.)\n    let (lo_miss, _) = crate::stats::wilson_interval(11, n, 1.96);\n    assert!(\n        lo_miss < lo,\n        "an 11/12 result must drop the Wilson floor below {lo}"\n    );\n    // The reported string now carries the interval, not a bare 1.0.\n    println!(\n        "[living_knowledge] recall@5 = {:.3}  [Wilson 95% {:.4}, {:.4}]  n={} (successes={})",\n        mean, lo, hi, n, successes\n    );\n}\n	3055	-1	-1		6b573b5e0c4cbba3eb310ac55902533b6d1fb5eead52f5aaa85d887f892cc94318c23293ddfed287e3535669b1d8d12c9e377404116a4468106b320efb14f8564d8e54d1a7ffb120d5013a0a93bbb8307551d83f29b75e0908863094fc8997a5c023d2e684e3526bfad94e2edf5c8d906cb14426bebd0fe197abd4f0710220f0
```
