4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/kthread.rs	kthread · 68 lines	/// held-handle shim — pure types from dowiz_core::thread, std-dependent impls stay here.\n\npub use dowiz_core::kthread::*;\n\n/// thread.rs — thread seam (ledger item 4: thread → kthread).\n///\n/// The no_std audit found a small set of `std::thread` call sites in otherwise\n/// no_std-ready modules: `sleep` (chronos), `available_parallelism`\n/// (core_pinning, span_metrics). A kernel module has no `std::thread` — it\n/// sleeps via `schedule_timeout`/`msleep` and counts CPUs via `num_online_cpus`.\n/// This module is the single seam, in the same shape as [`crate::clock`]: a\n/// no_std-compatible [`Thread`] trait (`core::time::Duration`, `usize` — no\n/// `JoinHandle`), a userspace [`StdThread`] impl, and free functions\n/// ([`sleep`], [`available_parallelism`]) that are the single authority. The\n/// kernel port swaps the impl, not the call sites.\n///\n/// # Out of scope (documented follow-up)\n/// `std::thread::spawn` / `scope` (budget.rs) return `JoinHandle`/borrow stack\n/// data — a `kthread_create` port needs a different handle type, so those stay\n/// std until a `JoinHandle`-free spawn seam is designed.\n\nuse core::time::Duration;\n\n/// The thread abstraction. no_std-compatible signature.\npub trait Thread {\n    /// Sleep the current thread for `d`.\n    fn sleep(&self, d: Duration);\n    /// Number of usable CPU cores (degrades-closed to `1`).\n    fn available_parallelism(&self) -> usize;\n}\n\n/// The userspace thread impl (`std::thread`).\npub struct StdThread;\n\nimpl Thread for StdThread {\n    fn sleep(&self, d: Duration) {\n        std::thread::sleep(d);\n    }\n    fn available_parallelism(&self) -> usize {\n        std::thread::available_parallelism().map(|n| n.get()).unwrap_or(1)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Single authority for "sleep". Kernel port swaps to `schedule_timeout`/`msleep`.\npub fn sleep(d: Duration) {\n    StdThread.sleep(d);\n}\n\n/// Single authority for "how many CPUs". Kernel port swaps to `num_online_cpus`.\npub fn available_parallelism() -> usize {\n    StdThread.available_parallelism()\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parallelism_is_positive() {\n        assert!(available_parallelism() >= 1, "at least one CPU");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sleep_zero_is_instant() {\n        // Must not hang or panic; zero-duration sleep is a no-op.\n        sleep(Duration::from_millis(0));\n    }\n}\n	3070	-1	-1		4f26761bb9c26bb3bb3b80e5123623af99e8b5267750f5be0951864283274b65400261bbd6e87a30ad46c73bf9c73669055146847d6c0462e6657a3f9d0c48cf5cae4499c5fa695d86c9050695a8a811f8604c4aa9b4f5c58ee4b5f4603f4e68e0719ba33ec8518569f40ac60b416df2e97fc168f2e891000b11fcf47108fce9

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/span_metrics/breach.rs	breach · 193 lines	//! telemetry/breach.rs — P83 Layer 2: load-breach system-wide profiler.\n//!\n//! BLUEPRINT P83 / SYNTHESIS PERFORMANCE AUDIT 2026-07-18 §3.3-C4 (Layer 2).\n//! Extends the kernel's `load1/nproc >= 4` friction signal with a system-wide\n//! `perf record -a -g -F 99` invocation on load breach, writing an `alert.jsonl`\n//! artifact. The R6 reframe: a load1 spike could be the kernel OR the operator's\n//! own `rustc` build noise — only a system-wide `perf` capture can prove which.\n//!\n//! Safety constraints (must not hang, must not require root in a way that breaks\n//! the build):\n//!   * The capture is BEST-EFFORT and TIME-BOUNDED: `perf` runs for a fixed\n//!     `-- sleep N` duration (default 5s), never an unbounded attach. If `perf`\n//!     is unavailable / not permitted, we fall back to the `pprof` feature-gated\n//!     marker (a no-op that just writes an `alert.jsonl` row naming the fallback)\n//!     rather than erroring or hanging.\n//!   * This module compiles ONLY under the `telemetry` feature; the `pprof`\n//!     fallback path is additionally `cfg(feature = "pprof")`.\n//!   * No network, no RNG, std-only. The only side effect is the `alert.jsonl`\n//!     row (+ optionally a `perf.data` capture file in the same dir).\n//!\n//! The `load1/nproc >= 4` branch itself did NOT yet exist in the kernel — this\n//! module is its canonical home (the function `check_load_breach` is the branch;\n//! `init`/callers wire it into the engine/perf friction path per the operator).\n//!\n//! Pure no_std items (`BreachAction`, `PERF_CAPTURE_SECS`, `PERF_FREQ`) live in\n//! `dowiz_core::span_metrics::breach` and are re-exported below. This shim keeps\n//! only the std parts: `check_load_breach`, `trigger_perf`, `try_perf`, `which_perf`.\n\n// Re-export the pure no_std types from dowiz-core.\npub use dowiz_core::span_metrics::breach::*;\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse super::obs::{normalized_load1, JsonlWriter, ALERT_JSONL, LOAD_BREACH_THRESHOLD};\n\n/// Evaluate the `load1/nproc >= 4` friction branch and, on breach, trigger the\n/// system-wide profiler. `dir` is where `alert.jsonl` (+ `perf.data`) land;\n/// `None` disables the writer (still returns the action for callers that log it).\npub fn check_load_breach(dir: Option<PathBuf>) -> BreachAction {\n    let load = match normalized_load1() {\n        Some(l) => l,\n        None => {\n            // Non-Linux / unreadable load: cannot detect a breach here. Degrade closed.\n            return BreachAction::NoBreach {\n                load: f64::NEG_INFINITY,\n            };\n        }\n    };\n    if load < LOAD_BREACH_THRESHOLD {\n        return BreachAction::NoBreach { load };\n    }\n    // Breach → capture.\n    let writer = JsonlWriter::new(dir.clone());\n    let action = trigger_perf(&dir);\n    // Always record an alert row (observability of the breach itself).\n    let (captured, fallback, detail) = match &action {\n        BreachAction::Captured {\n            captured,\n            fallback,\n            detail,\n            ..\n        } => (*captured, *fallback, detail.clone()),\n        _ => (false, false, String::new()),\n    };\n    let row = format!(\n        "{{\\"alert\\":\\"load_breach\\",\\"load1_per_nproc\\":{:.4},\\"threshold\\":{:.4},\\"perf_captured\\":{},\\"fallback\\":{},\\"detail\\":{:?}}}\\n",\n        load, LOAD_BREACH_THRESHOLD, captured, fallback, detail\n    );\n    writer.append(ALERT_JSONL, &row);\n    BreachAction::Captured {\n        load,\n        captured,\n        fallback,\n        detail,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Trigger the system-wide `perf record`. Tries `perf` first; if it is not\n/// available / not permitted, takes the `pprof` feature-gated no-op fallback.\nfn trigger_perf(dir: &Option<PathBuf>) -> BreachAction {\n    match try_perf(dir) {\n        Some(action) => action,\n        None => {\n            // `perf` unavailable → feature-gated fallback (no-op marker). Never hangs,\n            // never needs root, never shells out.\n            #[cfg(feature = "pprof")]\n            {\n                BreachAction::Captured {\n                    load: normalized_load1().unwrap_or(f64::INFINITY),\n                    captured: false,\n                    fallback: true,\n                    detail: "perf unavailable; pprof feature-gated fallback (no-op marker)"\n                        .to_string(),\n                }\n            }\n            #[cfg(not(feature = "pprof"))]\n            {\n                BreachAction::Captured {\n                    load: normalized_load1().unwrap_or(f64::INFINITY),\n                    captured: false,\n                    fallback: false,\n                    detail: "perf unavailable; no pprof fallback compiled in".to_string(),\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Attempt the real `perf record -a -g -F 99 -- sleep N`. Time-bounded by the\n/// `-- sleep N` argument itself (perf detaches after N seconds). Returns None if\n/// `perf` is not on PATH / cannot be spawned (so the caller can fall back).\nfn try_perf(dir: &Option<PathBuf>) -> Option<BreachAction> {\n    let perf = which_perf()?; // None ⇒ not installed → fall back.\n    let load = normalized_load1().unwrap_or(f64::INFINITY);\n    let sleep = format!("{}", PERF_CAPTURE_SECS);\n    // -a system-wide, -g call-graph (dwarf), -F 99 sampling, time-bounded by `sleep`.\n    let mut args: Vec<String> = vec![\n        "record".into(),\n        "-a".into(),\n        "-g".into(),\n        "-F".into(),\n        format!("{}", PERF_FREQ),\n        "--".into(),\n        "sleep".into(),\n        sleep,\n    ];\n    if let Some(d) = dir {\n        // Write perf.data next to the alert artifact.\n        let _ = crate::vfs::create_dir_all(d);\n        args.push("-o".into());\n        args.push(d.join("perf.data").to_string_lossy().into_owned());\n    }\n    // Time-bounded spawn: perf detaches after the `sleep N` window. Best-effort —\n    // failure ⇒ captured=false (caller falls back to the no-op pprof marker).\n    let out = crate::kprocess::run(&perf.to_string_lossy(), &args);\n    let captured = out.success();\n    let detail = if out.success() {\n        format!("perf record ran for {}s", PERF_CAPTURE_SECS)\n    } else if out.code == -1 {\n        "perf could not be spawned (no perms?)".to_string()\n    } else {\n        format!("perf exited non-zero: code {}", out.code)\n    };\n    Some(BreachAction::Captured {\n        load,\n        captured,\n        fallback: false,\n        detail,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Locate `perf` on PATH (std-only, no `which` crate). Returns None if absent so\n/// the caller takes the safe `pprof` fallback instead of erroring.\nfn which_perf() -> Option<PathBuf> {\n    for p in std::env::var_os("PATH")?.to_string_lossy().split(':') {\n        let cand = Path::new(p).join("perf");\n        if cand.exists() && cand.is_file() {\n            return Some(cand);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n// ── Unit tests: Layer-2 logic is probe-able without invoking `perf` ──\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_load_breach_threshold_constant() {\n        assert_eq!(LOAD_BREACH_THRESHOLD, 4.0);\n        assert_eq!(PERF_FREQ, 99);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_which_perf_is_safe_when_absent() {\n        // We do not assert presence/absence of perf (host-dependent); we assert the\n        // helper NEVER panics and always returns an Option.\n        let _ = which_perf();\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_check_load_breach_does_not_hang_or_panic() {\n        // Even on a host where load > 4 (or perf present), this returns within the\n        // bounded capture window and never panics. Run with a none-dir so no file\n        // is written; just assert the action enum is constructed.\n        let action = check_load_breach(None);\n        match action {\n            BreachAction::NoBreach { .. } => {}\n            BreachAction::Captured { .. } => {}\n        }\n    }\n}	3080	-1	-1		5eb4a71fddcf4172670bd255a1265a248c76146fbd06efabe6530c695bc3867f1849650077caba9e9014c5f91086c329cff1cdc5b268846cf027720ec3202acbc79a55b9cb378b1b9ac51c001fb8ff186070441a2facf656d88231e1b0ab1d25f169d7d605d9922df0180a0d534c8e9e06bf440f7e8599010b1334f5c9761940

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/span_metrics/instrument.rs	instrument · 107 lines	//! telemetry/instrument.rs — P83 Layer 1 span wrappers for the 8 verified functions.\n//!\n//! SYNTHESIS PERFORMANCE AUDIT 2026-07-18 §3.3-C4 names exactly eight functions to\n//! instrument with production span metrics. Three already carry spans in the kernel source\n//! (`place_order`, `place_order_priced`, `fold_transitions`); this module adds the\n//! remaining five as thin wrappers so the `SpanMetricsObserver` (obs.rs) can measure them\n//! without touching the functions' bodies or their red-line logic:\n//!\n//!   * `route`              — `crate::router::route`                          (always)\n//!   * `commit_after_decide`— `crate::event_log::EventLog::commit_after_decide`(always)\n//!   * `decide_settlement`  — `crate::ports::payment::decide_settlement`      (always)\n//!   * `cap::verify_chain`  — `crate::ports::agent::cap::verify_chain`        (always)\n//!   * `mldsa verify`       — `crate::pq::dsa::verify`                (behind `pq`)\n//!\n//! Explicitly EXCLUDED (SYNTHESIS §6-E18): `assert_transition`'s inner loop is NOT\n//! instrumented — the `fold_transitions` span + Layer-2 sampler cover it.\n//!\n//! Cutover note (roadmap items 4+29): the `#[tracing::instrument]` attribute is retired —\n//! each wrapper now opens the span EXPLICITLY as its first body line\n//! (`let _g = crate::fdr::info_span!("<name>").entered();`). This deletes the last consumer\n//! of `tracing-attributes` (and with it the `proc-macro2`/`quote`/`syn` toolchain that only\n//! ever served these 6 one-line wrappers). The `mldsa_verify` wrapper that used to be\n//! DUPLICATED here and in `mldsa.rs` is now the single surviving copy (`mldsa.rs` deleted).\n//!\n//! 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/span_metrics/mod.rs	mod · 115 lines	//! telemetry/ — P83 kernel production observability (BLUEPRINT P83).\n//!\n//! Two layers, both feature/telemetry-gated (`--features telemetry`) so the SHIPPING\n//! binary is behavior- and perf-neutral and carries zero observability symbols:\n//!\n//!   * Layer 1 (`obs.rs` + `instrument.rs`) — a ZERO NEW DEP `SpanMetricsObserver`\n//!     (implements the kernel-owned `fdr::SpanObserver` trait — the hand-rolled\n//!     replacement for the retired `tracing_subscriber::Layer` hook) that consumes the\n//!     spans over the 8 verified functions and writes hand-rolled log-bucket latency\n//!     histograms to `metric.jsonl`.\n//!   * Layer 2 (`breach.rs` + `pprof.rs`) — extends the `load1/nproc >= 4` friction\n//!     branch with a system-wide `perf record -a -g -F 99` on load breach, writing an\n//!     `alert.jsonl` artifact; `pprof` is a feature-gated no-op fallback only.\n//!\n//! The three spans already placed in the kernel (`place_order`, `place_order_priced`,\n//! `fold_transitions`) are consumed here directly; the other five (`route`,\n//! `commit_after_decide`, `decide_settlement`, `cap::verify_chain`, `mldsa_verify`) are\n//! wrapped by `instrument.rs` so the layer can measure them without touching their bodies.\n//! `assert_transition` is deliberately NOT instrumented (SYNTHESIS §6-E18 — per-edge inner\n//! loop).\n//!\n//! Cutover note (roadmap items 4+29): the `tracing`/`tracing-subscriber` pair is retired.\n//! `SpanMetricsLayer` → `SpanMetricsObserver` (a `fdr::SpanObserver`), `init`/`init_scoped`\n//! rewire onto `fdr::set_global_observer` / `fdr::set_scoped_observer`. The\n//! `DOWIZ_SPAN_METRICS` + `DOWIZ_SPAN_METRICS_DIR` env contract is UNCHANGED, so\n//! `tools/telemetry kernel-spans` and `metric.jsonl` consumers work without edits. The\n//! duplicate `mldsa.rs` wrapper was deleted (its span survives in `instrument.rs`).\n\npub mod obs;\n\n#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]\npub mod breach;\n\n#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]\npub mod instrument;\n\n#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]\npub mod pprof;\n\n#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]\npub use obs::{SpanMetrics, SpanMetricsObserver};\n\n/// Install the P83 observability observer as the process-global span observer.\n///\n/// Wires a `SpanMetricsObserver` into the kernel-owned `fdr` span pipeline. After this\n/// call, every span entered over the 8 verified functions is timed and streamed to\n/// `metric.jsonl` in `dir` (or a best-effort temp dir resolved from `DOWIZ_SPAN_METRICS_DIR`).\n///\n/// Idempotent-ish: if a global observer is ALREADY set (e.g. a test harness installed its\n/// own), `fdr::set_global_observer` returns `Err` — we surface it (observability must never\n/// break the caller). Returns `Ok(())` when installed, `Err(())` when one already exists.\n///\n/// Call this from a binary's `main` or a test setup — NEVER from the shipping library hot\n/// path. The kernel's core (decide/fold/money) never calls this; it only emits spans, which\n/// are inert without an observer.\npub fn init(dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>) -> Result<(), ()> {\n    // Allow the caller (or the `telemetry kernel-spans` subcommand) to pin where\n    // `metric.jsonl` / `alert.jsonl` land via `DOWIZ_SPAN_METRICS_DIR`. When `dir` is None\n    // and the env is unset, the writer is best-effort-disabled (no file is opened), so a\n    // bare `init(None)` never surprises the caller with disk writes.\n    let dir =\n        dir.or_else(|| std::env::var_os("DOWIZ_SPAN_METRICS_DIR").map(std::path::PathBuf::from));\n    let obs = std::sync::Arc::new(SpanMetricsObserver::new(dir));\n    crate::fdr::set_global_observer(obs)\n}\n\n/// Convenience: run the Layer-2 load-breach check (system-wide `perf` on breach, else the\n/// `pprof` feature-gated fallback). See `breach::check_load_breach`.\n#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]\npub fn check_load_breach(dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>) -> breach::BreachAction {\n    breach::check_load_breach(dir)\n}\n\n/// Install the P83 Layer-1 observer as a **scoped** default, returning a guard that reverts\n/// on drop. Unlike `init` (process-global, fails if one is already installed), this works\n/// inside any test — the observer is active only for the duration of the returned guard\n/// (mirrors the incumbent `set_default`/`DefaultGuard` semantics). Used by the P83 wiring\n/// tests.\n#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]\npub fn init_scoped(dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>) -> crate::fdr::ObserverGuard {\n    let obs = std::sync::Arc::new(SpanMetricsObserver::new(dir));\n    crate::fdr::set_scoped_observer(obs)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_init_installs_observer_then_spans_are_recorded() {\n        // Use a temp dir so metric.jsonl lands somewhere we can assert on.\n        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("p83_init_{}", std::process::id()));\n        let _ = crate::vfs::create_dir_all(&dir);\n        // init may fail if a global observer is already set in this test binary; that's\n        // fine — the observer is still constructed and reachable (proven below).\n        let _ = init(Some(dir.clone()));\n\n        // Build an observer directly and prove it records a span close to metric.jsonl.\n        let obs = SpanMetricsObserver::new(Some(dir.clone()));\n        obs.metrics().record("place_order", 42);\n        obs.metrics().record("place_order", 7);\n        let p = dir.join(obs::METRIC_JSONL);\n        let contents = crate::vfs::read_to_string(&p).unwrap();\n        assert!(contents.contains("\\"span\\":\\"place_order\\""));\n        assert!(contents.contains("\\"count\\":2"));\n        let _ = crate::vfs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_init_idempotent_does_not_panic() {\n        // Calling init twice must not panic even if the second returns Err.\n        let _ = init(None);\n        let _ = init(None);\n    }\n}\n	3097	-1	-1		7b1cbf57eccf1162694d1adf92151245c276a566d554bf8b6f52986b1212c74f1968350255c3ea8fa04109590194d9280ff36f04336a8461f367330c7704a24defa21491c1ebc109d381401095abe9f87159440b2faf4548c983b8b3d08f546f6023d75e104810acda108a4d18598fb00432602eb69589c083416cd5f9682f40

State is plain `std`; no `Rng`, no\n//! network, no `serde`.\n\n// Re-export the pure no_std items from dowiz-core.\npub use dowiz_core::span_metrics::obs::*;\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Mutex;\n\n/// Compute the normalized 1-minute load: `load1 / nproc` (Linux `/proc/loadavg` +\n/// `available_parallelism`; degrades-closed to `None` off-Linux or on read failure).\n#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]\npub fn normalized_load1() -> Option<f64> {\n    let s = crate::vfs::read_to_string("/proc/loadavg").ok()?;\n    let l1: f64 = s.split_whitespace().next()?.parse().ok()?;\n    let nproc = crate::kthread::available_parallelism();\n    Some(l1 / nproc as f64)\n}\n\n/// Non-Linux: no `/proc/loadavg` → no breach can be detected here (Layer-2 is a\n/// Linux-system-wide profiler, by design). Best-effort:\n/// a single poisoned/contended lock or a failed write is swallowed (observability\n/// must never crash the shipping path).\npub struct JsonlWriter {\n    dir: Option<PathBuf>,\n}\n\nimpl JsonlWriter {\n    /// `dir = None` disables the writer (no file is opened; `append` is a silent no-op).\n    pub fn new(dir: Option<PathBuf>) -> Self {\n        JsonlWriter { dir }\n    }\n\n    /// Append one line to `name` inside the writer's directory. Returns false if the\n    /// writer is disabled or the open/append failed (best-effort — caller ignores it).\n    pub fn append(&self, name: &str, line: &str) -> bool {\n        let dir = match &self.dir {\n            Some(d) => d,\n            None => return false,\n        };\n        let path = dir.join(name);\n        crate::vfs::append(&path, line.as_bytes()).is_ok()\n    }\n}\n\n/// The registry of per-span log-bucket histograms + the shared jsonl writer.\npub struct SpanMetrics {\n    inner: Mutex<Inner>,\n}\n\nstruct Inner {\n    /// Per-span histogram, keyed by span name (BTreeMap ⇒ deterministic iteration order).\n    hist: BTreeMap<String, LogBucket>,\n    writer: JsonlWriter,\n}\n\nimpl SpanMetrics {\n    pub fn new(dir: Option<PathBuf>) -> Self {\n        SpanMetrics {\n            inner: Mutex::new(Inner {\n                hist: BTreeMap::new(),\n                writer: JsonlWriter::new(dir),\n            }),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a completed span's duration (microseconds). The pure budget primitives — [`gcra_decide`], [`GcraTokenBucket`] (lock-free `AtomicU64`\n//! TAT), and [`TokenBucket`] (a `SpinLock<Inner>`, `now_ns` injected) — live in\n//! `dowiz_core::token_bucket` and are re-exported here. This shim adds ONLY the std stamping\n//! free functions that inject `crate::clock::now_ns()`.\n\nuse core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\nuse std::time::Instant;\n\npub use dowiz_core::token_bucket::{gcra_decide, GcraTokenBucket, TokenBucket};\n\n/// Grant via [`TokenBucket`] stamped with the kernel's monotonic clock.\npub fn token_bucket_try_acquire(b: &TokenBucket, n: f64) -> bool {\n    b.try_acquire(n, crate::clock::now_ns())\n}\n\n/// Current available token count via [`TokenBucket`] stamped with the kernel's monotonic clock.\npub fn token_bucket_available(b: &TokenBucket) -> f64 {\n    b.available(crate::clock::now_ns())\n}\n\n/// Bounded refill-rate reconfiguration via [`TokenBucket`] stamped with the kernel clock.\npub fn token_bucket_set_refill_rate(b: &mut TokenBucket, r: crate::autonomic::BoundedRate) {\n    b.set_refill_rate(r, crate::clock::now_ns())\n}\n\n/// Grant via [`GcraTokenBucket`] stamped with the kernel's monotonic clock.\npub fn gcra_try_acquire(b: &GcraTokenBucket, n: f64) -> bool {\n    b.try_acquire(n, crate::clock::now_ns())\n}\n\n/// Current available budget via [`GcraTokenBucket`] stamped with the kernel's monotonic clock.\npub fn gcra_available(b: &GcraTokenBucket) -> f64 {\n    b.available(crate::clock::now_ns())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::time::Duration;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn token_bucket_grants_within_capacity() {\n        let b = TokenBucket::new(10.0, 1.0);\n        assert!(token_bucket_try_acquire(&b, 3.0));\n        assert!(token_bucket_try_acquire(&b, 3.0));\n        assert!(token_bucket_try_acquire(&b, 3.0));\n        // Only ~1 token left (refill over these µs is negligible) → 4th grant of 3.0 refused.\n        assert!(\n            !token_bucket_try_acquire(&b, 3.0),\n            "4th acquire of 3.0 must fail with ~1 token left"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn token_bucket_refills_over_time() {\n        let b = TokenBucket::new(1.0, 100.0); // 100 tokens/sec\n        assert!(token_bucket_try_acquire(&b, 1.0), "first acquire drains the full bucket");\n        assert!(!token_bucket_try_acquire(&b, 1.0), "bucket empty → refuse");\n        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)); // ~2 tokens refilled, capped at capacity=1\n        assert!(\n            token_bucket_try_acquire(&b, 1.0),\n capacity + refill_rate*elapsed + ε.\n        let capacity = 5.0;\n        let rate = 50.0; // tokens/sec\n        let b = TokenBucket::new(capacity, rate);\n        let unit = 0.001;\n        let t0 = Instant::now();\n        let mut granted = 0.0f64;\n        for _ in 0..5000 {\n            if token_bucket_try_acquire(&b, unit) {\n                granted += unit;\n            }\n        }\n        let elapsed = t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64();\n        let ceiling = capacity + rate * elapsed + 1e-6;\n        assert!(\n            granted <= ceiling,\n            "over-grant invariant violated: granted={granted} > ceiling={ceiling} (elapsed={elapsed}s)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn token_bucket_gcra_grants_within_capacity() {\n        let b = GcraTokenBucket::new(10.0, 1.0);\n        assert!(gcra_try_acquire(&b, 3.0));\n        assert!(gcra_try_acquire(&b, 3.0));\n        assert!(gcra_try_acquire(&b, 3.0));\n        assert!(\n            !gcra_try_acquire(&b, 3.0),\n            "4th acquire of 3.0 must fail with ~1 token left"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn token_bucket_gcra_never_over_grants_under_refill() {\n        // Same F33 falsifier as `token_bucket_never_over_grants_under_refill`, run against\n        // GcraTokenBucket: total granted over a window <= capacity + refill_rate*elapsed + eps.\n        let capacity = 5.0;\n        let rate = 50.0;\n        let b = GcraTokenBucket::new(capacity, rate);\n        let unit = 0.001;\n        let t0 = Instant::now();\n        let mut granted = 0.0f64;\n        for _ in 0..5000 {\n 1e-6;\n        assert!(\n            granted <= ceiling,\n            "over-grant invariant violated: granted={granted} > ceiling={ceiling} (elapsed={elapsed}s)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn token_bucket_autonomic_rate_change_never_over_grants() {\n        // Item 21 acceptance #5: an autonomic (BoundedRate-typed) rate change must\n        // NOT break the over-grant invariant. We drive `set_refill_rate` with a\n        // BoundedRate mid-flight and re-check the ceiling against the NEW rate.\n        use crate::autonomic::BoundedRate;\n        let capacity = 5.0;\n        let mut b = TokenBucket::new(capacity, 50.0);\n        let unit = 0.001;\n        let t0 = Instant::now();\n        let mut granted = 0.0f64;\n        let mut rate = 50.0f64;\n        for i in 0..5000 {\n            // Every ~500 steps, reconfigure the rate through the bounded setter.\n            if i % 500 == 0 && i > 0 {\n                rate = if rate == 50.0 { 25.0 } else { 50.0 };\n                token_bucket_set_refill_rate(&mut b, BoundedRate::from_f64(rate));\n            }\n            if token_bucket_try_acquire(&b, unit) {\n                granted += unit;\n            }\n        }\n        let elapsed = t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64();\n        // Ceiling uses the MAX rate seen during the window (the worst case for the\n        // over-grant bound; a rate change never exceeds capacity + max_rate*elapsed).\n        let max_rate = 50.0;\n        let ceiling = capacity + max_rate * elapsed + 1e-6;\n        assert!(\n            granted <= ceiling,\n            "autonomic rate change over-granted: granted={granted} > ceiling={ceiling} (elapsed={elapsed}s)"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 8's differential oracle: `GcraTokenBucket` (atomic, integer GCRA) vs a pure reference\n/// model of `TokenBucket`'s mutex/f64 refill logic (mutex, continuous float). Deterministic —\n/// no real clock is read anywhere in here, so there is no flakiness from two independently-\n/// constructed buckets observing slightly different wall-clock instants; the "clock" is a\n/// synthetic `now_ns` counter both models step forward in lockstep.\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod gcra_oracle {\n    use super::*;\n    use proptest::prelude::*;\n\n    /// Pure reference model of `TokenBucket::refill_locked` + the grant check in\n    /// `TokenBucket::try_acquire`, but over explicit `(tokens, elapsed_secs)` state instead of a\n    /// live `Mutex<Inner>` — this IS the "mutex" side of item 8's\n    /// "GCRA-atomic-vs-mutex-differential-oracle" (`HOT-PATHS.tsv` gap, closed by this module).\n    fn mutex_reference_step(\n        tokens: f64,\n        capacity: f64,\n        refill_rate: f64,\n        elapsed_secs: f64,\n        n: f64,\n    ) -> (f64, bool) {\n        let refilled = (tokens + refill_rate * elapsed_secs).min(capacity).max(0.0);\n        if refilled >= n {\n            (refilled - n, true)\n        } else {\n            (refilled, false)\n        }\n    }\n\n    proptest! {\n        /// For any POSITIVE refill rate (GCRA's native, continuous-refill domain — the realistic\n        /// rate-limit path the contended-bench originally measured), `gcra_decide` grants/denies\n        /// identically to the mutex/f64 reference model across a random walk of (elapsed, cost)\n        /// steps. Deliberately excludes `refill_rate <= 0.0` — see\n        /// `token_bucket_gcra_diverges_from_zero_refill_budget` below for why that domain is a\n        /// verified, documented SCOPE LIMIT of the swap, not silently glossed over.\n        #[test]\n        fn token_bucket_gcra_matches_mutex_reference_positive_refill(\n            capacity in 1.0f64..1e6,\n            refill_rate in 0.01f64..1e5,\n            steps in prop::collection::vec((0.0f64..0.01, 0.1f64..5.0), 1..200),\n        ) {\n            let nanos_per_token = 1e9 / refill_rate;\n            let burst_nanos = (capacity * nanos_per_token) as u64;\n            let mut mutex_tokens = capacity;\n            let mut gcra_tat: u64 = 0;\n            let mut now_ns: u64 = 0;\n            for (dt_secs, n) in steps {\n                now_ns = now_ns.saturating_add((dt_secs * 1e9) as u64);\n                let (new_tokens, mutex_grant) =\n                    mutex_reference_step(mutex_tokens, capacity, refill_rate, dt_secs, n);\n                mutex_tokens = new_tokens;\n                let cost_ns = (n * nanos_per_token) as u64;\n                let gcra_grant = match gcra_decide(now_ns, gcra_tat, cost_ns, burst_nanos) {\n                    Some(new_tat) => {\n                        gcra_tat = new_tat;\n                        true\n                    }\n                    None => false,\n                };\n                prop_assert_eq!(\n                    mutex_grant, gcra_grant,\n                    "divergence at now_ns={} n={} mutex_tokens={}", now_ns, n, mutex_tokens\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// **Planted-leak self-test (ct_gate planted-leak pattern — a gate that cannot reject\n    /// proves nothing).** Two DELIBERATELY-BROKEN GCRA variants must go RED in the same\n    /// invocation that the real `gcra_decide` goes GREEN, or the oracle itself is proven\n    /// vacuous. If either broken variant were to pass, this test fails and the whole oracle\n    /// is untrustworthy.\n    ///\n    /// Variant (i) `broken_no_idle_max` drops the `max(TAT, now)` — idle time then\n    /// accumulates as debt, so after a long idle the bucket over-grants (caught by the\n    /// shared F33 ceiling, assertion 2 in the blueprint). Variant (ii) `broken_floor_cost`\n    /// uses `floor` instead of `ceil` on the per-step cost at a very high rate — quantization\n    /// flips *permissive* (over-grants), caught by the one-sided-conservatism check.\n    #[test]\n    fn token_bucket_gcra_oracle_planted_leaks_stay_red() {\n        // **Correct planted-leak invariant:** the broken variants MUST grant STRICTLY MORE\n        // across an identical schedule than the correct `gcra_decide` (i.e. they over-grant).\n        // If a broken variant granted the same or fewer, the oracle would be vacuous. We drive\n        // the SAME sequence of (now, cost) steps through each decision fn and compare grant\n        // counts. The over-grant of (i) emerges from debt accumulation across a sequence, not a\n        // single isolated call.\n        fn simulate(use_max: bool, use_ceil: bool, steps: &[(u64, u64)], burst: u64) -> u64 {\n            let mut tat: u64 = 0;\n            let mut grants: u64 = 0;\n            for (now, cost) in steps {\n                let allow_at = if use_max { tat.max(*now) } else { tat };\n                let charged = if use_ceil {\n                    *cost\n                } else {\n                    cost.saturating_sub(1)\n                };\n                let new_tat = allow_at.checked_add(charged);\n                let limit = now.checked_add(burst);\n                if let (Some(nt), Some(lim)) = (new_tat, limit) {\n                    if nt <= lim {\n                        tat = nt;\n                        grants += 1;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            grants\n        }\n\n        // Schedule A (integer ns): build debt, then a long idle, then more requests.\n        // burst = 100ns; cost = 60ns. Correct fn grants 2 (burst exhausted at t=0); the long\n        // idle at t=200 does NOT recharge a TAT that was already advanced to 120 — so the last\n        // two requests are refused. The broken (i) fn drops `max(TAT, now)`, so its TAT stays\n        // pinned at the small arrival-time and it grants again after the idle → over-grant.\n        let burst_a: u64 = 100;\n        let cost_a: u64 = 60;\n        let steps_a = [(0u64, cost_a), (0, cost_a), (200, cost_a), (200, cost_a)];\n\n        // Correct fn (max + ceil): 2 grants over schedule A.\n        let correct_grants = simulate(true, true, &steps_a, burst_a);\n        // Broken (i): drops `max(TAT, now)` → never advances TAT with wall-clock progress →\n        // grants MORE (over-grants) than the correct fn.\n        let broken_i_grants = simulate(false, true, &steps_a, burst_a);\n\n        // Schedule B (integer ns): tight burst where a 1ns/step under-charge accumulates.\n        // burst = 5ns; cost = 1ns repeated 10×. Correct (ceil) charges 1ns each → 5 grants then\n        // exhausted. Broken (ii) `floor`s the cost to 0 → charges nothing → grants ALL 10.\n        let burst_b: u64 = 5;\n        let cost_b: u64 = 1;\n        let mut steps_b: Vec<(u64, u64)> = Vec::new();\n        for i in 0..10 {\n            steps_b.push((i, cost_b));\n        }\n        let broken_ii_grants = simulate(true, false, &steps_b, burst_b);\n\n        assert!(\n            broken_i_grants > correct_grants,\n            "planted-leak (i): dropping max(TAT,now) MUST over-grant (got broken={}, correct={})",\n            broken_i_grants,\n            correct_grants\n        );\n        assert!(\n            broken_ii_grants > correct_grants,\n            "planted-leak (ii): floor-cost MUST over-grant vs ceil (got broken={}, correct={})",\n            broken_ii_grants,\n            correct_grants\n        );\n        // The real `gcra_decide` (which IS the correct fn) over schedule A MUST respect the\n        // shared F33 ceiling: total charged <= burst + (window end) — here window end = 200ns.\n        let total_charged = correct_grants * cost_a;\n        assert!(\n            total_charged <= burst_a + 200,\n            "real gcra_decide over-granted: charged={} > ceiling={}",\n            total_charged,\n            burst_a + 200\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// `GcraTokenBucket`; across the whole window the TOTAL granted must never exceed the F33\n    /// shared ceiling `capacity + rate·elapsed + ε`. This is the std-only honest substitute for\n    /// the machine-checked concurrency argument: it excercises the single-`AtomicU64` CAS under\n    /// real interleaving and proves the *window* bound holds regardless of how the CASes order.\n    #[test]\n    fn token_bucket_gcra_8thread_stress_no_over_grant() {\n        use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n        use std::sync::Arc;\n        use std::thread;\n\n        let capacity = 1000.0;\n        let rate = 1_000_000.0; // 1M tokens/sec — high enough that the window is well-filled\n        let bucket = Arc::new(GcraTokenBucket::new(capacity, rate));\n        let unit = 1.0f64; // each thread acquires 1 token per successful grab\n        let granted_total = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));\n        let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();\n\n        const N_THREADS: usize = 8;\n        const PER_THREAD: u64 = 20_000;\n        let mut handles = Vec::with_capacity(N_THREADS);\n        for _ in 0..N_THREADS {\n            let bucket = Arc::clone(&bucket);\n            let granted_total = Arc::clone(&granted_total);\n            handles.push(thread::spawn(move || {\n                for _ in 0..PER_THREAD {\n                    if gcra_try_acquire(&bucket, unit) {\n                        granted_total.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n                    }\n                }\n            }));\n        }\n        for h in handles {\n            h.join().unwrap();\n        }\n\n        let elapsed = t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64();\n        // F33 shared ceiling: the bucket can NEVER have granted more than capacity + rate·elapsed.\n        let ceiling = capacity + rate * elapsed + 1e-6;\n        let granted = granted_total.load(Ordering::Relaxed) as f64;\n        assert!(\n            granted <= ceiling,\n            "8-thread stress over-granted: granted={} > ceiling={} (elapsed={}s)",\n            granted,\n            ceiling,\n            elapsed\n        );\n        // Sanity: the test actually exercised contention (some grants happened).\n        assert!(\n            granted > 0.0,\n            "stress test granted zero tokens — scheduler starved the test"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn token_bucket_gcra_diverges_from_zero_refill_budget() {\n        // Documented, verified boundary (not a bug in `gcra_decide` — a scope limit of the\n        // swap): several live callers (`bounded_drainer.rs`, `agent-adapters/src/fuel.rs`) use\n        // `TokenBucket::new(_, 0.0)` as a one-shot "budget" bucket, draining an initial capacity\n        // to zero across MANY acquires. GCRA models CONTINUOUS refill; at refill_rate=0,\n        // nanos_per_token is infinite, so burst_nanos and cost_ns both saturate to u64::MAX —\n        // the FIRST call's `checked_add` succeeds (u64::MAX <= u64::MAX), but the SECOND call's\n        // `tat.checked_add(cost_ns)` (u64::MAX + u64::MAX) overflows, so `gcra_decide` returns\n        // `None` from then on. Net effect: GCRA grants exactly ONCE, ever — it cannot drain a\n        // budget across multiple partial acquires the way the mutex bucket does. This is why\n        // item 8 ships `GcraTokenBucket` as a NEW type, never a call-site swap for these callers.\n        let capacity = 10.0;\n        let nanos_per_token = f64::INFINITY;\n        let burst_nanos = (capacity * nanos_per_token) as u64; // saturates to u64::MAX\n        let cost_ns = (1.0 * nanos_per_token) as u64; // saturates to u64::MAX\n        let mut tat = 0u64;\n        let mut grants = 0;\n        for i in 0..5u64 {\n            if let Some(new_tat) = gcra_decide(i, tat, cost_ns, burst_nanos) {\n                tat = new_tat;\n                grants += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        assert_eq!(\n            grants, 1,\n            "GCRA grants exactly once under refill_rate=0 — diverges from the mutex bucket's \\\n             N-partial-acquire budget-drain semantics"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 8 (space-grade roadmap §C): the two Kani harnesses item 7 pre-specified\n/// (`BLUEPRINT-ITEM-07-kani-wiring-2026-07-19.md` §5) for the pure [`gcra_decide`] transition.\n/// Compiled ONLY under `cfg(kani)` — zero footprint in every normal build (see keccak.rs header\n/// for the same pattern), nothing enters `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`.\n#[cfg(kani)]\nmod kani_proofs {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Single-step no-over-grant contract, exactly as item 7 specified: `new_tat =\n    /// max(tat,now)+cost` on grant; `deny ⇔ max(tat,now)+cost > now+burst`; no overflow under\n    /// the headroom assumption below.\n    ///\n    /// HEADROOM ASSUMPTION (documented precondition, same shape as the NTT butterfly lemmas'\n    /// bounded-magnitude assumes): all four inputs stay under 2^62 ns (~146,000 years), so the\n    /// two additions `allow_at + cost_ns` and `now_ns + burst_ns` cannot overflow `u64` — the\n    /// property this harness checks is the DECISION contract, not `gcra_decide`'s independently-\n    /// proven `checked_add` degrade-closed behavior at true `u64` extremes (already total by\n    /// construction — see the fn's own doc comment).\n    #[kani::proof]\n    fn proof_gcra_transition_contract() {\n        let now_ns: u64 = kani::any();\n        let tat_ns: u64 = kani::any();\n        let cost_ns: u64 = kani::any();\n        let burst_ns: u64 = kani::any();\n        kani::assume(now_ns < (1u64 << 62));\n        kani::assume(tat_ns < (1u64 << 62));\n        kani::assume(cost_ns < (1u64 << 62));\n        kani::assume(burst_ns < (1u64 << 62));\n\n        let allow_at = tat_ns.max(now_ns);\n        let expected_deny = allow_at + cost_ns > now_ns + burst_ns; // no overflow: both < 2^63\n        match gcra_decide(now_ns, tat_ns, cost_ns, burst_ns) {\n            Some(new_tat) => {\n                assert!(!expected_deny);\n                assert_eq!(new_tat, allow_at + cost_ns);\n            }\n            None => assert!(expected_deny),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Two sequential applications conserve `cost1+cost2` and TAT is monotone non-decreasing —\n    /// the strongest interleaving statement Kani can honestly make (item 7 §5: the full\n    /// CAS-concurrency argument is the differential oracle above + `compare_exchange`'s own\n    /// atomicity semantics, NOT this proof).\n    #[kani::proof]\n    fn proof_gcra_two_step_interleaving() {\n        let now1: u64 = kani::any();\n        let now2: u64 = kani::any();\n        let tat0: u64 = kani::any();\n        let cost1: u64 = kani::any();\n        let cost2: u64 = kani::any();\n        let burst_ns: u64 = kani::any();\n        kani::assume(now1 < (1u64 << 61));\n        kani::assume(now2 < (1u64 << 61));\n        kani::assume(now2 >= now1); // sequential = time-ordered\n        kani::assume(tat0 < (1u64 << 61));\n        kani::assume(cost1 < (1u64 << 61));\n        kani::assume(cost2 < (1u64 << 61));\n        kani::assume(burst_ns < (1u64 << 61));\n\n        if let Some(tat1) = gcra_decide(now1, tat0, cost1, burst_ns) {\n            assert!(tat1 >= tat0.max(now1));\n            if let Some(tat2) = gcra_decide(now2, tat1, cost2, burst_ns) {\n                // Cost conservation: the second grant's new TAT is exactly the pure sum of\n                // where the first grant left off plus this step's own cost — neither cost is\n                // lost nor double-counted across the pair.\n                assert!(tat2 >= tat1);\n                assert_eq!(tat2, tat1.max(now2) + cost2);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n	3151	-1	-1		d70534ff9089f674a1192fc59332596328d6b54eac10bc8bec46a059daffdbca1c4435c34f9a8c1ea35546c9b6f0ffa05ee12f04364cccaab4fe528eeb14e58e46ee75b1ad32d81b55c7990097baebeaf0c8ec0b6930c401cca020b4408912e6fce0f30eb0ca91a1d860c8c58958b9942c3f45241c9f8ac51a24747079357951

[`MetricSample`]) and the fixed-field-order `to_line()` / `parse_line()`\n//! pair. The std-dependent operations — the monotonic clock and the `/proc`\n//! readers — are redefined here (shadowing the no_std fallbacks) so the kernel\n//! reads real data:\n//! - [`mono_now_ns`] — `std::time::Instant` + `std::sync::OnceLock`.\n//! - [`proc_cpu_sample_from_proc_self`] / [`mem_sample_from_proc_self`] —\n//!   real `/proc` reads via [`crate::vfs`].\n//!\n//! The kernel port swaps the *impl* (procfs → ramfs/kernel VFS), never the\n//! call sites.\n\npub use dowiz_core::typed_metrics::*;\n\nuse std::sync::OnceLock;\nuse std::time::Instant;\n\n/// Monotonic nanosecond counter anchored at first call. `Instant::now()` is\n/// monotonic but has no absolute epoch, so we measure the delta from a\n/// lazily-captured process-start `Instant`. Uses `Instant::now()` — panics on\n/// `wasm32`, so callers on the FDR write path are all gated off wasm (no sink\n/// is ever installed there).\nstatic MONO_EPOCH: OnceLock<Instant> = OnceLock::new();\n\n/// Monotonic ns since process start. `pub` so the `fdr` event schema can stamp\n/// its replay-ordering key through the SAME clock the P08 metrics use (one mono\n/// epoch per process).\npub fn mono_now_ns() -> u128 {\n    let start = MONO_EPOCH.get_or_init(Instant::now);\n    Instant::now().duration_since(*start).as_nanos()\n}\n\n/// Read the current process's CPU accounting from `/proc/self/stat`.\n/// Returns `None` when `/proc/self/stat` is unreadable (e.g. non-Linux\n/// test envs) — typed absence, never a fake.\n///\n/// `comm` (field 2) may contain `)`, so we split on `)` and take the part\n/// after the LAST `)`, then index the remaining whitespace-separated\n/// fields. `pid` is taken from the part before the first `(`.\npub fn proc_cpu_sample_from_proc_self() -> Option<ProcCpuSample> {\n    let stat = crate::vfs::read_to_string("/proc/self/stat").ok()?;\n    let pid: u32 = stat.split('(').next()?.trim().parse().ok()?;\n    let after = stat.rsplit(')').next()?;\n    // After `comm`, fields are 3..N (1-based from line start). Field 14 =\n    // utime, field 15 = stime → indices 11 / 12 in this iterator.\n    let fields: Vec<&str> = after.split_whitespace().collect();\n    let utime_ticks: u64 = fields.get(11)?.parse().ok()?;\n    let stime_ticks: u64 = fields.get(12)?.parse().ok()?;\n    let clk_tck: u64 = 100; // Linux USER_HZ default; see struct docs.\n    let mono_ns = mono_now_ns();\n    Some(ProcCpuSample {\n        pid,\n        utime_ticks,\n        stime_ticks,\n        clk_tck,\n        mono_ns,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Read `VmRSS` / `VmHWM` from `/proc/self/status`. Returns `None` when the\n/// file is unreadable (non-Linux) — typed absence.\npub fn mem_sample_from_proc_self() -> Option<MemSample> {\n    let status = crate::vfs::read_to_string("/proc/self/status").ok()?;\n    let mut vm_rss_kb: Option<u64> = None;\n    let mut vm_hwm_kb: Option<u64> = None;\n    for line in status.lines() {\n        if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("VmRSS:") {\n            vm_rss_kb = rest\n                .trim()\n                .split_whitespace()\n                .next()\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());\n        } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("VmHWM:") {\n            vm_hwm_kb = rest\n                .trim()\n                .split_whitespace()\n                .next()\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());\n        }\n    }\n    Some(MemSample {\n        vm_rss_kb: vm_rss_kb?,\n        vm_hwm_kb: vm_hwm_kb?,\n    })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// On Linux, `proc_cpu_sample_from_proc_self()` returns `Some` with\n    /// utime+stime > 0 (the test process has used some CPU). On non-Linux, skip.\n    #[test]\n    fn proc_cpu_sample_from_proc_self_nonempty() {\n        #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]\n        {\n            return;\n        }\n        #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]\n        {\n            // Burn real CPU (ticks are 1/clk_tck ≈ 10 ms granularity, so the\n            // loop must actually execute — black_box inside prevents the\n            // optimizer from eliminating it) so the sampler observes > 0 ticks.\n            let mut acc: u64 = 0;\n            for i in 0..50_000_000u64 {\n                acc = acc.wrapping_add(i);\n                core::hint::black_box(acc);\n            }\n\n            let s = proc_cpu_sample_from_proc_self()\n                .expect("proc_cpu_sample_from_proc_self must read /proc/self/stat on Linux");\n            assert!(\n                s.utime_ticks + s.stime_ticks > 0,\n                "test process should have consumed some CPU"\n            );\n            // VmRSS/VmHWM should also be available.\n            let m = mem_sample_from_proc_self().expect("status readable on Linux");\n            assert!(m.vm_rss_kb > 0, "process should have resident memory");\n        }\n    }\n}\n	3158	-1	-1		8b76bf1b4d27e3a6a1198e5d15545221c997bfc4e662b6cbc176a47b935d20655c41be03f680605efc149ee91196d538857d45c41c6c84aaf42672ad5f46e2ef1ee104f8be73d15194db211a97bbb819d2cc681c2981e5c9d000b3a256118f6664727639b7de51a5cd4c449f49fd4d612c3fd9ae358588a01309c4ec71326a9a

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/src/brain/hydra.rs	hydra · 663 lines	//! hydra — std host shim.\n//!\n//! The pure drift-gated supervisor core (`TopoEdge`, `candidate_drift`,\n//! `INTEGRITY_BAND`, `Hydra<S: EventStore>`) lives in `dowiz_core::hydra`.\n//! `FileEventStore` (the std-fs durable append-only store) stays here.\n\npub use dowiz_core::hydra::*;\n\nuse crate::event_log::{EventStore, MeshEvent, StoreError};\n\n/// G4 — std-only durable append-only event store (Воля АНУ closed loop).\n///\n/// No external DB (sqlx/pgrust offline-uncached). Persists each event as one\n/// JSON line to a local file; `insert` appends + `fsync`s (crash-safe). On open,\n/// the file is replayed into an in-memory id/tip index so `contains`/`get`/`tip`\n/// are O(1). The log is content-addressed and idempotent — a re-inserted id is\n/// a no-op. Egress-free: only `std::fs` local IO, no network.\n///\n/// innovate: this is the durable variant that replaces MemEventStore for the\n/// organism's persistent memory. pgrust remains the node-level SQL option; this\n/// is the kernel-internal, dependency-free, offline-safe default for the Hydra.\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\nuse crate::vfs::{open_file, OpenMode, StdFile, VfsFile};\n\npub struct FileEventStore {\n    path: std::path::PathBuf,\n    by_id: BTreeMap<[u8; 32], MeshEvent>,\n    tip: Option<[u8; 32]>,\n    count: usize,\n    /// Item 61 (gap G5): durability continuous counters — running totals the\n    /// group-commit decision can read as a *live* data feed (replacing the one-time\n    /// ~637 µs bench number). `events_appended` counts every durable commit (the\n    /// `sync_all` path reached); `fsync_calls` counts the `sync_all` calls actually\n    /// issued. Both are P3-plane only — they NEVER gate the durability barrier in\n    /// `insert` (the `?` short-circuits before any decision logic) and feed no\n    /// hash/gate/replay surface (grep-firewall proof, blueprint §4).\n    events_appended: u64,\n    /// Count of `sync_all` calls issued (the `FileEventStore` `insert` is the only\n    /// issuer — `MemEventStore` is in-memory and issues none).\n    fsync_calls: u64,\n    /// Cached write handle, opened LAZILY on the first successful `insert` —\n    /// never at construction. `open()` must keep tolerating a not-yet-existing\n    /// file/parent (H1 §4 criterion 4, tested: `file_store_open_failure_surfaces_not_swallowed`\n    /// asserts an open failure surfaces via `insert`'s `Err`, not construction).\n    /// Reused on every later insert — removes the redundant per-event\n    /// open+close syscalls the item-26 audit measured (`strace`: 1 open + 1\n    /// write + 1 close per event, only the fsync is load-bearing). This half\n    /// is contract-neutral: it changes zero durability semantics, only removes\n    /// redundant syscalls around the same barrier.\n    handle: Option<StdFile>,\n    /// Item 26 group-commit: `sync_all` fires every `batch_size` inserts\n    /// instead of every one. **OFF by default** (`batch_size = 1` — today's\n    /// exact per-event-fsync behavior, byte-for-byte unchanged: with\n    /// `batch_size = 1`, `pending_since_sync` reaches the threshold on every\n    /// single insert, so the barrier fires every time, exactly as before).\n    /// Opt in via [`FileEventStore::with_batch_size`] — never a silent default\n    /// change, per the item-26 audit's own recommendation\n    /// (`AUDIT-ITEM-26-batching-measurements-2026-07-19.md` §1: "file a design\n    /// proposal for an *opt-in* group-commit mode... do NOT silently change\n    /// the default"). Measured throughput at `batch_size = 64`: ~53x (1,513 →\n    /// ~93,000 events/s) — see the same audit.\n    batch_size: usize,\n    /// Writes since the last `sync_all` — the current unsynced batch. Always\n    /// 0 immediately after `insert` returns when `batch_size == 1`.\n    pending_since_sync: usize,\n}\n\nimpl FileEventStore {\n    /// Open (or create) the append-only log at `path`. Replays existing lines\n    /// into the in-memory index. Corrupt/short lines are skipped (forward-\n    /// tolerant) — the chain tip is the last *valid* committed event.\n    pub fn open<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> std::io::Result<Self> {\n        let path = path.as_ref().to_path_buf();\n        let mut by_id = BTreeMap::new();\n        let mut tip = None;\n        let mut count = 0;\n        if path.exists() {\n            let text = crate::vfs::read_to_string(&path)?;\n            for line in text.lines() {\n                if line.is_empty() {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                match serde_json_like_parse(line) {\n                    Some(ev) => {\n                        let id = ev.event_id();\n                        by_id.insert(id, ev.clone());\n                        tip = Some(id);\n                        count += 1;\n                    }\n                    None => continue, // skip corrupt line\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(FileEventStore {\n            path,\n            by_id,\n            tip,\n            count,\n            events_appended: 0,\n            fsync_calls: 0,\n            handle: None,\n            batch_size: 1,\n            pending_since_sync: 0,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Opt in to group-commit: `sync_all` fires every `n` inserts instead of\n    /// every one. `n = 1` (the default) is today's exact per-event durability,\n    /// unchanged. `n > 1` is a REAL durability-contract change — see the\n    /// struct-level doc and the module's crash-consistency discussion: up to\n    /// `n - 1` acknowledged (`insert` returned `Ok`) events can be lost on a\n    /// crash before their batch's `sync_all` fires. Panics if called after any\n    /// insert has already buffered an unsynced write, so the barrier cadence\n    /// can never change silently mid-stream.\n    pub fn with_batch_size(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {\n        assert!(n >= 1, "batch_size must be >= 1");\n        assert_eq!(\n            self.pending_since_sync, 0,\n            "with_batch_size must be set before any insert (or right after a flush_pending)"\n        );\n        self.batch_size = n;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Force a durability barrier now, flushing whatever group-commit has\n    /// buffered. Callers doing a graceful shutdown with `batch_size > 1` MUST\n    /// call this before exiting — relying on `Drop` is NOT safe (`Drop` cannot\n    /// propagate an `fsync` error, and the kernel never swallows one silently).\n    /// A no-op returning `Ok(())` if nothing is pending (including the\n    /// `batch_size == 1` case, where nothing is ever left pending).\n    pub fn flush_pending(&mut self) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n        if self.pending_since_sync == 0 {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let f = self\n            .handle\n            .as_mut()\n            .expect("pending_since_sync > 0 implies handle is Some (set on first write)");\n        f.sync_all().map_err(|e| StoreError::Sync(e.to_string()))?;\n        self.fsync_calls += 1;\n        self.pending_since_sync = 0;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Item 61 (gap G5): live durability counters — the number of events durably\n    /// committed and the number of `sync_all` calls issued so far. Readable without\n    /// touching the durability barrier; P3 telemetry only.\n    pub fn durability_counters(&self) -> DurabilityCounters {\n        DurabilityCounters {\n            events_appended: self.events_appended,\n            fsync_calls: self.fsync_calls,\n            pending_unsynced: self.pending_since_sync as u64,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 61 (gap G5): live durability counters (P3 telemetry). Named fields so callers\n/// read intent, never tuple-position guessing.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DurabilityCounters {\n    /// Number of events durably committed (appended + fsynced) so far.\n    pub events_appended: u64,\n    /// Number of `sync_all` durability barriers issued so far.\n    pub fsync_calls: u64,\n    /// Item 26 group-commit: events written and index-acknowledged but not yet\n    /// covered by a `sync_all` — the live risk window a crash right now would\n    /// lose. Always 0 with the default `batch_size = 1`.\n    pub pending_unsynced: u64,\n}\n\n/// Minimal hand-rolled JSON parse for the 4 MeshEvent fields (std-only, no\n/// serde dependency). Tolerates the exact shape we emit; returns None on\n/// mismatch (forward-tolerant replay).\nfn serde_json_like_parse(line: &str) -> Option<MeshEvent> {\n    // Expected: {"prev":[..32 bytes..],"actor_pubkey":[..32..],"actor_seq":N,"payload":"<hex>"}\n    let prev = extract_b256(line, "\\"prev\\":")?;\n    let actor = extract_b256(line, "\\"actor_pubkey\\":")?;\n    let seq = extract_u64(line, "\\"actor_seq\\":")?;\n    let payload = extract_hex(line, "\\"payload\\":\\"")?;\n    Some(MeshEvent {\n        prev,\n        actor_pubkey: actor,\n        actor_seq: seq,\n        payload,\n    })\n}\n\nfn extract_b256(s: &str, key: &str) -> Option<[u8; 32]> {\n    let i = s.find(key)? + key.len();\n    let rest = &s[i..];\n    let end = rest.find(']')?;\n    let nums = &rest[..end];\n    let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n    let mut idx = 0;\n    for part in nums.split(',') {\n        let p = part.trim().trim_start_matches('[');\n        if let Ok(v) = p.parse::<u8>() {\n            if idx < 32 {\n                out[idx] = v;\n                idx += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if idx == 32 {\n        Some(out)\n    } else {\n        None\n    }\n}\n\nfn extract_u64(s: &str, key: &str) -> Option<u64> {\n    let i = s.find(key)? + key.len();\n    let rest = &s[i..];\n    let end = rest.find(',').or_else(|| rest.find('}'))?;\n    rest[..end].trim().parse::<u64>().ok()\n}\n\nfn extract_hex(s: &str, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    let i = s.find(key)? + key.len();\n    let rest = &s[i..];\n    let end = rest.find('"')?;\n    let hex = &rest[..end];\n    if hex.len() % 2 != 0 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    Some(\n        (0..hex.len())\n            .step_by(2)\n            .filter_map(|j| u8::from_str_radix(&hex[j..j + 2], 16).ok())\n            .collect::<Vec<u8>>(),\n    )\n}\n\nimpl EventStore for FileEventStore {\n    fn contains(&self, id: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n        self.by_id.contains_key(id)\n    }\n    fn insert(&mut self, id: [u8; 32], ev: MeshEvent) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n        if self.by_id.contains_key(&id) {\n            return Ok(()); // idempotent no-op — nothing to persist\n        }\n        // Append one JSON line + fsync (crash-safe). Uses only std::fs.\n        let line = format!(\n            "{{\\"prev\\":{:?},\\"actor_pubkey\\":{:?},\\"actor_seq\\":{},\\"payload\\":\\"{}\\"}}\\n",\n            ev.prev,\n            ev.actor_pubkey,\n            ev.actor_seq,\n            ev.payload\n                .iter()\n                .map(|b| format!("{:02x}", b))\n                .collect::<String>()\n        );\n        // Each IO step now propagates a typed StoreError instead of `let _ =`\n        // swallowing it — an open failure no longer falls through silently.\n        // The handle is opened LAZILY (only on the first insert that reaches\n        // here) and cached thereafter — construction (`open()`) keeps\n        // tolerating a not-yet-existing file/parent; only an insert can ever\n        // surface `StoreError::Open` (H1 §4 criterion 4, unchanged).\n        if self.handle.is_none() {\n            let f = open_file(&self.path, OpenMode::Append)\n                .map_err(|e| StoreError::Open(e.to_string()))?;\n            self.handle = Some(f);\n        }\n        let f = self\n            .handle\n            .as_mut()\n            .expect("handle is Some — just set above or cached from a prior insert");\n        f.write_all(line.as_bytes())\n            .map_err(|e| StoreError::Write(e.to_string()))?;\n        f.flush().map_err(|e| StoreError::Flush(e.to_string()))?;\n\n        // Item 26 group-commit: fsync every `batch_size` inserts. With the\n        // default `batch_size = 1` this fires on EVERY insert — byte-for-byte\n        // the same barrier cadence as before this change.\n        self.pending_since_sync += 1;\n        if self.pending_since_sync >= self.batch_size {\n            f.sync_all().map_err(|e| StoreError::Sync(e.to_string()))?;\n            self.fsync_calls += 1;\n            self.pending_since_sync = 0;\n        }\n        // Order is load-bearing (H1 §2.2): the in-memory index advances only\n        // after the WRITE succeeds (always true at this point — every `?`\n        // above already returned). With `batch_size = 1` this is exactly\n        // equivalent to "after sync_all succeeds" (today's invariant,\n        // unchanged, since the sync above always fires in that case). With\n        // `batch_size > 1` this is the explicit, documented acknowledged-\n        // before-durable tradeoff `with_batch_size`'s doc names: the index\n        // (and therefore this method's own idempotent-duplicate check, the\n        // `contains_key` guard at the top) reflects WRITTEN state, which may\n        // not yet be FSYNCED when the batch hasn't closed — necessary so a\n        // duplicate insert() within the same unsynced batch is still detected\n        // as a no-op rather than double-written to the file.\n        self.by_id.insert(id, ev);\n        self.tip = Some(id);\n        self.count += 1;\n        // Item 61 (gap G5): the durability counters advance alongside the\n        // index — `events_appended` counts writes (matches `count`/`by_id`);\n        // `fsync_calls` only increments when the barrier above actually fired.\n        // P3 telemetry; never gates the barrier itself.\n        self.events_appended += 1;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n    fn get(&self, id: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<MeshEvent> {\n        self.by_id.get(id).cloned()\n    }\n    fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.count\n    }\n    fn tip(&self) -> Option<[u8; 32]> {\n        self.tip\n    }\n    fn set_tip(&mut self, id: [u8; 32]) {\n        self.tip = Some(id);\n    }\n    fn ids(&self) -> Vec<[u8; 32]> {\n        self.by_id.keys().copied().collect()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod file_store_tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::env::temp_dir;\n    use crate::vfs as fs;\n\n    fn tmp_path(tag: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {\n        let mut p = temp_dir();\n        p.push(format!(\n            "hydra-volya-anu-{}-{}.log",\n            tag,\n            std::process::id()\n        ));\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&p);\n        p\n    }\n\n    /// G4 — durable: events survive a reopen (replay), idempotent re-insert,\n    /// and `get` retrieves by content-id. Egress-free (std::fs only).\n    #[test]\n    fn file_store_survives_reopen_and_replays() {\n        let path = tmp_path("reopen");\n        {\n            let mut s = FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap();\n            let ev = MeshEvent {\n                prev: [0u8; 32],\n                actor_pubkey: [7u8; 32],\n                actor_seq: 1,\n                payload: b"genesis-intent".to_vec(),\n            };\n            let id = ev.event_id();\n            s.insert(id, ev.clone()).expect("insert durable");\n            assert!(s.contains(&id));\n            assert_eq!(s.get(&id), Some(ev.clone()));\n            // Re-insert same id — idempotent no-op (count stays 1).\n            s.insert(id, ev).expect("idempotent re-insert ok");\n            assert_eq!(s.len(), 1);\n        }\n        // Reopen: replay must restore the event.\n        let s2 = FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s2.len(), 1, "event replayed from disk");\n        let ev = MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [7u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: 1,\n            payload: b"genesis-intent".to_vec(),\n        };\n        assert!(s2.contains(&ev.event_id()));\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);\n    }\n\n    /// G4 — the organism's full closed loop persists across restart: commit via\n    /// Hydra with a FileEventStore, then boot_verify after reopening.\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_durable_closed_loop_across_restart() {\n        let path = tmp_path("loop");\n        let base = vec![\n            TopoEdge {\n                from: 0,\n                to: 1,\n                weight: 1.0,\n            },\n            TopoEdge {\n                from: 1,\n                to: 2,\n                weight: 1.0,\n            },\n        ];\n        let committed_id;\n        {\n            let mut h = Hydra::new(FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap(), 3, base.clone());\n            let ev = MeshEvent {\n                prev: [0u8; 32],\n                actor_pubkey: [3u8; 32],\n                actor_seq: 1,\n                payload: b"self-mutation-A".to_vec(),\n            };\n            let delta = vec![TopoEdge {\n                from: 2,\n                to: 0,\n                weight: 0.3,\n            }];\n            let (out, _dec) = h\n                .commit(ev.clone(), &delta, false, |_| Ok::<u64, String>(1))\n                .expect("damped mutation commits");\n            committed_id = match out {\n                crate::event_log::AppendOutcome::Committed(id) => id,\n                _ => panic!("expected committed"),\n            };\n        }\n        // Reopen: the organism re-bootstraps from durable state.\n        let h2 = Hydra::new(FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap(), 3, base);\n        assert!(\n            h2.log().contains(&committed_id),\n            "event persisted across restart"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            h2.boot_verify(),\n            0.0,\n            "baseline still acyclic after restart"\n        );\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);\n    }\n\n    /// H1 §4 criterion 4 — `FileEventStore` no longer swallows. Point it at a\n    /// path whose parent directory does not exist so `OpenOptions::open` fails →\n    /// `insert` returns `Err(StoreError::Open(_))`; the in-memory by_id/tip/count\n    /// do NOT advance; the caller sees `Err`, never a fabricated success.\n    /// Falsifies the old `if let Ok(f)` fall-through at the former `hydra.rs:840`.\n    ///\n    /// Judgment call (flagged): the blueprint (§4 criterion 4) says "read-only\n    /// directory". A chmod 0555 dir does NOT make `open` fail for a root test\n    /// runner (root bypasses the mode bits), so a *missing parent directory* is\n    /// used instead — it fails `open` deterministically for any uid, exercising\n    /// the identical `StoreError::Open` pole the criterion targets.\n    #[test]\n    fn file_store_open_failure_surfaces_not_swallowed() {\n        let bogus = temp_dir()\n            .join(format!("h1-missing-parent-{}", std::process::id()))\n            .join("evlog.log");\n        // Ensure the parent directory truly does not exist.\n        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(bogus.parent().unwrap());\n        // open() lazily tolerates a not-yet-existing file (nothing to replay).\n        let mut s = FileEventStore::open(&bogus).expect("open tolerates a missing file");\n        let ev = MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [5u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: 1,\n            payload: b"x".to_vec(),\n        };\n        let id = ev.event_id();\n        let res = s.insert(id, ev);\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res, Err(StoreError::Open(_))),\n            "open failure MUST surface as Err(StoreError::Open); got {res:?}"\n        );\n        // The in-memory index MUST NOT advance on a failed open.\n        assert!(!s.contains(&id), "by_id must not advance on open failure");\n        assert!(s.tip().is_none(), "tip must not advance on open failure");\n        assert_eq!(s.len(), 0, "count must not advance on open failure");\n    }\n\n    /// Item 61 (gap G5) — durability continuous counters. Each `insert` that lands an\n    /// event ALSO bumps `events_appended`; the trailing `sync_all` bumps `fsync_calls`.\n    /// We assert BOTH: the counters move AND — critically — the index count is consistent\n    /// with `events_appended` (the counter never lies about what was durably written).\n    /// The counters are P3-plane telemetry: they never gate the `sync_all` durability\n    /// barrier (green testing of the existing no-silent-failure invariants still holds).\n    #[test]\n    fn durability_counters_advance_on_append_and_fsync() {\n        let path = tmp_path("item61-counters");\n        let mut s = FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.durability_counters().events_appended, 0);\n        assert_eq!(s.durability_counters().fsync_calls, 0);\n\n        let mk = |seq: u8| MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [9u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: seq as u64,\n            payload: vec![seq],\n        };\n        for seq in 1..=3u8 {\n            let ev = mk(seq);\n            let id = ev.event_id();\n            s.insert(id, ev).expect("append+fsync");\n        }\n        let c = s.durability_counters();\n        assert_eq!(c.events_appended, 3, "three events appended → counter = 3");\n        assert_eq!(c.fsync_calls, 3, "each insert fsyncs → fsync counter = 3");\n        assert_eq!(s.len(), 3, "index count matches appended counter");\n\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);\n    }\n\n    /// Item 26 group-commit — `with_batch_size(3)` defers `sync_all` until the\n    /// 3rd insert closes the batch. Proves the barrier cadence actually\n    /// changes (not just that the fields exist): 2 inserts leave `fsync_calls`\n    /// at 0 and `pending_unsynced` at 2; the 3rd insert fires the barrier.\n    #[test]\n    fn with_batch_size_defers_fsync_until_batch_closes() {\n        let path = tmp_path("item26-batch3");\n        let mut s = FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap().with_batch_size(3);\n\n        let mk = |seq: u8| MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [11u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: seq as u64,\n            payload: vec![seq],\n        };\n\n        s.insert(mk(1).event_id(), mk(1)).expect("insert 1");\n        let c = s.durability_counters();\n        assert_eq!(c.fsync_calls, 0, "batch not closed yet — no sync_all");\n        assert_eq!(c.pending_unsynced, 1);\n\n        s.insert(mk(2).event_id(), mk(2)).expect("insert 2");\n        let c = s.durability_counters();\n        assert_eq!(c.fsync_calls, 0, "still short of batch_size=3");\n        assert_eq!(c.pending_unsynced, 2);\n\n        s.insert(mk(3).event_id(), mk(3))\n            .expect("insert 3 closes batch");\n        let c = s.durability_counters();\n        assert_eq!(c.fsync_calls, 1, "3rd insert closes the batch → 1 sync_all");\n        assert_eq!(c.pending_unsynced, 0, "pending resets after the barrier");\n        assert_eq!(c.events_appended, 3);\n        assert_eq!(s.len(), 3, "all 3 events index-visible despite 1 fsync");\n\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);\n    }\n\n    /// Item 26 — `flush_pending` forces the durability barrier early (before\n    /// the batch naturally closes) and is a no-op when nothing is buffered.\n    #[test]\n    fn flush_pending_forces_barrier_and_is_noop_when_empty() {\n        let path = tmp_path("item26-flush");\n        let mut s = FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap().with_batch_size(10);\n\n        // No writes yet — flush_pending must be a true no-op.\n        s.flush_pending().expect("no-op flush ok");\n        assert_eq!(s.durability_counters().fsync_calls, 0);\n\n        let ev = MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [12u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: 1,\n            payload: b"partial-batch".to_vec(),\n        };\n        let id = ev.event_id();\n        s.insert(id, ev).expect("insert 1 of 10");\n        assert_eq!(s.durability_counters().pending_unsynced, 1);\n        assert_eq!(s.durability_counters().fsync_calls, 0);\n\n        s.flush_pending().expect("forced flush");\n        let c = s.durability_counters();\n        assert_eq!(c.fsync_calls, 1, "flush_pending forced a sync_all");\n        assert_eq!(c.pending_unsynced, 0);\n\n        // Reopen: the flushed event must have actually survived to disk.\n        let s2 = FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap();\n        assert!(\n            s2.contains(&id),\n            "flush_pending durably persisted the event"\n        );\n\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);\n    }\n\n    /// Item 26 — `with_batch_size` panics if called after a write is already\n    /// buffered, so the barrier cadence can never change silently mid-stream.\n    #[test]\n    #[should_panic(expected = "with_batch_size must be set before any insert")]\n    fn with_batch_size_panics_if_a_write_is_already_pending() {\n        let path = tmp_path("item26-panic");\n        let mut s = FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap().with_batch_size(5);\n        let ev = MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [13u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: 1,\n            payload: b"x".to_vec(),\n        };\n        s.insert(ev.event_id(), ev)\n            .expect("insert leaves 1 pending");\n        let _ = s.with_batch_size(2); // must panic — pending_since_sync != 0\n    }\n\n    /// Item 26 — `batch_size = 1` (the default) is byte-for-byte the old\n    /// per-event-fsync cadence: every insert closes its own batch of 1.\n    #[test]\n    fn default_batch_size_one_fsyncs_every_insert() {\n        let path = tmp_path("item26-default");\n        let mut s = FileEventStore::open(&path).unwrap(); // no with_batch_size call\n\n        let mk = |seq: u8| MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [14u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: seq as u64,\n            payload: vec![seq],\n        };\n        for seq in 1..=4u8 {\n            let ev = mk(seq);\n            s.insert(ev.event_id(), ev).expect("insert");\n            let c = s.durability_counters();\n            assert_eq!(\n                c.pending_unsynced, 0,\n                "batch_size=1 never leaves anything pending"\n            );\n            assert_eq!(\n                c.fsync_calls, seq as u64,\n                "every insert fires its own sync_all"\n            );\n        }\n\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);\n    }\n\n    /// Item 5 (cross-mesh replication) — `mesh_replication::reconcile` is\n    /// generic over `EventStore`, not just `MemEventStore`; prove it converges\n    /// two independent, disk-backed `FileEventStore`s the same way. This is\n    /// the closest this crate gets to a real 2-node scenario without an\n    /// actual transport: two separate files (durable, `std::fs`-only) stand\n    /// in for two separate nodes.\n    #[test]\n    fn file_stores_reconcile_to_identical_folded_state() {\n        use crate::mesh_replication::{reconcile, MerkleLog};\n\n        let path_a = tmp_path("item5-node-a");\n        let path_b = tmp_path("item5-node-b");\n        let mut node_a = FileEventStore::open(&path_a).unwrap();\n        let mut node_b = FileEventStore::open(&path_b).unwrap();\n\n        let a_ev = MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [21u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: 1,\n            payload: b"node-a-authored".to_vec(),\n        };\n        node_a.insert(a_ev.event_id(), a_ev).unwrap();\n\n        let b_ev = MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [22u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: 1,\n            payload: b"node-b-authored".to_vec(),\n        };\n        node_b.insert(b_ev.event_id(), b_ev).unwrap();\n\n        reconcile(&mut node_a, &node_b).expect("A pulls from B");\n        reconcile(&mut node_b, &node_a).expect("B pulls from A");\n\n        assert_eq!(\n            MerkleLog::from_store(&node_a).root(),\n            MerkleLog::from_store(&node_b).root(),\n            "two disk-backed nodes converge to the same Merkle root"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(node_a.len(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(node_b.len(), 2);\n\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path_a);\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path_b);\n    }\n}\n	3214	-1	-1		cbbb3715cc4d2373f304a8c9b1125315059e95c4ad56a482ec57e4fb9135ca8779c8378347d648fea75b53ab18b1b769cf790dc4f1288e39c0fbba0fe70e7acc64bc72e96d7388a9d40b3900b7bbe1586178ec2aadf9478fc8b220a0d817c515ac24f6b615cb14b1485acc1ecf156f116cbb646f3ea7e9ec029b567461362b30
