```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/tests/landing_no_vendor_catalog.rs	landing_no_vendor_catalog · 130 lines	//! BLUEPRINT-P73 anti-scope structural grep-gate (§2.2 / §5.1 / §6 not-done clause).\n//!\n//! dowiz.org is PURE infrastructure for prospective venue owners (operator ruling §16.21). It\n//! lists NO vendors, no menus, no "browse restaurants near you" — in ANY form, not even a\n//! directory of links. The single most tempting feature-creep is ruled out *categorically*: there\n//! is **no** `VendorId`, `slug`, `Restaurant`, `Menu`, `catalog`, `search`, or "near you" concept\n//! anywhere in the `landing` module. A diff that adds a vendor list / search / browse surface is a\n//! scope violation regardless of test state. This test is the teeth: it FAILS if any forbidden\n//! token appears in `kernel/src/landing/` code (comments/strings stripped so doc prose is safe).\n//!\n//! Mirrors `kernel/tests/no_card_data.rs` (the PCI red-line teeth) — same structural-scan idiom.\n//! Run: `cargo test --test landing_no_vendor_catalog`.\n\nuse std::path::Path;\n\n// Forbidden vendor-catalog identifiers (the anti-scope §2.2). Assembled with `concat!` so this\n// file's own source never contains a contiguous forbidden literal (which would make the scan\n// vacuous). Doc prose naming these tokens is therefore harmless.\nconst FORBIDDEN_VENDOR_TOKENS: &[&str] = &[\n    concat!("vendor", "_id"),\n    concat!("vendor", "catalog"),\n    concat!("rest", "aurant"),\n    concat!("menu", "item"),\n    concat!("food", "establishment"),\n    concat!("browse", "vendor"),\n    concat!("near", "you"),\n    concat!("search", "vendor"),\n    concat!("store", "front", "slug"),\n];\n\n/// Strip Rust comments + string/char literals so doc-comment prose (which names these tokens) is\n/// never a false positive. We hunt CODE identifiers only.\nfn strip_comments(src: &str) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(src.len());\n    let b = src.as_bytes();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    let mut in_block = false;\n    while i < b.len() {\n        if in_block {\n            if i + 1 < b.len() && b[i] == b'*' && b[i + 1] == b'/' {\n                in_block = false;\n                i += 2;\n            } else {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        if i + 1 < b.len() && b[i] == b'/' && b[i + 1] == b'/' {\n            while i < b.len() && b[i] != b'\\n' {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        if i + 1 < b.len() && b[i] == b'/' && b[i + 1] == b'*' {\n            in_block = true;\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if b[i] == b'"' || b[i] == b'\\'' {\n            let q = b[i];\n            out.push(' ');\n            i += 1;\n            while i < b.len() && b[i] != q {\n                if b[i] == b'\\\\' {\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            i += 1;\n            out.push(' ');\n            continue;\n        }\n        out.push(b[i] as char);\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Collect every `.rs` file under `kernel/src/landing`.\nfn landing_src_files() -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    let root = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))\n        .join("src")\n        .join("landing");\n    let mut stack = vec![root];\n    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {\n        if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&dir) {\n            for e in entries.flatten() {\n                let p = e.path();\n                if p.is_dir() {\n                    stack.push(p);\n                } else if p.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) == Some("rs") {\n                    out.push(p.to_string_lossy().into_owned());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn landing_has_no_vendor_catalog_surface() {\n    let files = landing_src_files();\n    // The module always exists (mod.rs at minimum); if landing/ is missing the gate is meaningless.\n    assert!(!files.is_empty(), "landing/ module must exist");\n    let mut violations = Vec::new();\n    for f in &files {\n        let src = match std::fs::read_to_string(f) {\n            Ok(s) => s,\n            Err(_) => continue,\n        };\n        let code = strip_comments(&src);\n        let words: Vec<String> = code\n            .split(|c: char| !(c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_'))\n            .map(|w| w.to_lowercase())\n            .collect();\n        for token in FORBIDDEN_VENDOR_TOKENS {\n            let needle = token.to_lowercase();\n            if words.iter().any(|w| w == &needle) {\n                violations.push(format!("{f}: contains vendor-catalog token '{token}'"));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    assert!(\n        violations.is_empty(),\n        "P73 §16.21 anti-scope violation — vendor-catalog surface found in landing/: {:?}",\n        violations\n    );\n}\n	3496	-1	-1		42543f5ffcc4a365022b78c933721321415e15e6af14e4537946ee69a1e1adc71900327157ca1a5dfa030428b9a3b8e8866934a4e74c4d8b9c77b647ae663eefde0f188165c290311985b318f73bc9f858d9ca3ba5f1e50858814afcda8bc5348f6ae337b04a5205fb5e084616d4439725bd356a3f04ae9636c5ccec01f43d61
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/tests/markov_pmu_fdr.rs	markov_pmu_fdr · 141 lines	//! Roadmap item 27 (classifier-input half) end-to-end proof: the `markov_attractor` binary,\n//! run with `DOWIZ_FDR_DIR` set, window-brackets its `analyze_detailed` classification with a\n//! PMU snapshot and logs ONE `markov_verdict` FDR record carrying the verdict string PLUS the\n//! PMU delta — through the REAL FDR ring (segment files + CRC + recovery), not a mock.\n//!\n//! This proves three things at once, against the shipped binary:\n//!   1. The stdout Python-parity JSON contract is unchanged (a verdict is printed to stdout).\n//!   2. A companion FDR record joins the PMU delta to the verdict on the SAME record.\n//!   3. Tier B degrades to a named absence (`permission_denied` on this paranoid=4 host),\n//!      never a fabricated 0 and never a crash (the child exits 0).\n\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n\nfn markov_bin() -> PathBuf {\n    PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_markov_attractor"))\n}\n\nfn unique_dir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n    let d = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("markov_pmu_{tag}_{}_{nanos}", std::process::id()));\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();\n    d\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn markov_verdict_emits_pmu_companion_record_through_real_fdr_ring() {\n    let ring_dir = unique_dir("ring");\n\n    // A healthy rhythm (edit, run_ok)×8 ⇒ Verdict::Healthy — a fixed, known verdict.\n    let mut stdin_tokens = String::new();\n    for _ in 0..8 {\n        stdin_tokens.push_str("edit\\nrun_ok\\n");\n    }\n\n    let mut child = Command::new(markov_bin())\n        .env("DOWIZ_FDR_DIR", &ring_dir)\n        .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n        .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n        .spawn()\n        .expect("spawn markov_attractor");\n\n    child\n        .stdin\n        .take()\n        .expect("child stdin")\n        .write_all(stdin_tokens.as_bytes())\n        .expect("write tokens");\n\n    let out = child.wait_with_output().expect("wait markov_attractor");\n    assert!(\n        out.status.success(),\n        "binary must exit 0 (Tier B absence is not a crash)"\n    );\n\n    // 1. stdout parity contract intact — a HEALTHY verdict on stdout, unchanged shape.\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);\n    assert!(\n        stdout.contains("\\"verdict\\": \\"HEALTHY\\""),\n        "stdout parity JSON must be unchanged: {stdout}"\n    );\n\n    // 2 + 3. The FDR ring holds a markov_verdict record with the PMU companion.\n    let rec = dowiz_kernel::fdr::ring::recover(&ring_dir);\n    let verdict_rec = rec\n        .records\n        .iter()\n        .find(|r| r.name == "markov_verdict")\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no markov_verdict FDR record recovered: {:?}", rec.records));\n\n    let raw = &verdict_rec.raw;\n    // Verdict string joined onto the record.\n    assert!(\n        raw.contains("\\"verdict\\":\\"HEALTHY\\""),\n        "verdict must be on the record: {raw}"\n    );\n    // The PMU companion object is present with every field key.\n    assert!(\n        raw.contains("\\"pmu\\":{"),\n        "pmu companion object must be present: {raw}"\n    );\n    for key in [\n        "tsc_cycles",\n        "minflt",\n        "majflt",\n        "nswap",\n        "vol_ctxt_switches",\n        "nonvol_ctxt_switches",\n        "hw_instructions",\n        "hw_cpu_cycles",\n        "hw_cache_misses",\n        "hw_branch_misses",\n    ] {\n        assert!(\n            raw.contains(&format!("\\"{key}\\":")),\n            "pmu field {key} must be present: {raw}"\n        );\n    }\n    // Tier A recorded a real, nonzero rdtsc delta across the classification window\n    // (proves the bracket ran and the counter advanced — not a stub 0).\n    let tsc = extract_pmu_u64(raw, "tsc_cycles")\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("tsc_cycles must be a real value, not an absence: {raw}"));\n    assert!(\n        tsc > 0,\n        "tsc_cycles delta must be nonzero across a real classification: {raw}"\n    );\n    // Tier B is EITHER a real value (this agent process runs as root/CAP_PERFMON, which\n    // bypasses perf_event_paranoid=4 — perf_event_open succeeds and returns a real count)\n    // OR a greppable named absence on a genuinely unprivileged host. Both are correct; what\n    // must NEVER appear is a fabricated bare 0 with no reason. Assert one of the two shapes.\n    let tier_b_value =\n        raw.contains("\\"hw_instructions\\":") && extract_pmu_u64(raw, "hw_instructions").is_some();\n    let tier_b_absence = raw.contains("\\"hw_instructions\\":{\\"unavailable\\":");\n    assert!(\n        tier_b_value || tier_b_absence,\n        "Tier B must be a real value OR a named absence, never a fabricated 0: {raw}"\n    );\n\n    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&ring_dir);\n}\n\n/// Extract `"key":<digits>` from the record when the field is a bare number (a `Value`);\n/// `None` when it is the `{"unavailable":...}` object form.\nfn extract_pmu_u64(line: &str, key: &str) -> Option<u64> {\n    let pat = format!("\\"{key}\\":");\n    let i = line.find(&pat)? + pat.len();\n    let rest = &line[i..];\n    // A Value is a bare digit run; an absence starts with '{'.\n    let first = rest.chars().next()?;\n    if !first.is_ascii_digit() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let end = rest\n        .find(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())\n        .unwrap_or(rest.len());\n    rest[..end].parse().ok()\n}\n	3501	-1	-1		d731b7fecd8709a7cb01f095969a12252d5e9d647f506fcd2f530490115d8e4378c424015f576a95a54f534128d5d62896396d14f9480d01b1e77225da0ee8fd56fe5cf93f8a43099501311ad3bac5e091785e3a2c5dd449ee927824500f9765a177725490cad2ffe16a4b8dc25b35200cb7516a3c8b09c09b84f574e3fc3873
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/tests/moderation_wire.rs	moderation_wire · 55 lines	//! P74 wiring gate — `moderation::decide_report` must ride the real commit path\n//! through a production caller (`moderation::commit_report`), which wires it as the\n//! validate-before-persist Law pole of `EventLog::commit_after_decide`.\n//!\n//! RED before wiring: `commit_report` does not exist → this test fails to compile.\n//! GREEN after wiring: a malformed report payload → `CommitError` and NOTHING\n//! persists; a well-formed report → persisted (log len 1).\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::event_log::{AppendOutcome, EventLog, MemEventStore, MeshEvent};\nuse dowiz_kernel::moderation::{\n    commit_report, ReportPayload, ReportReason, ReportTarget, DOMAIN_REPORT,\n};\n\nfn reporter() -> [u8; 32] {\n    [7u8; 32]\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn p74_valid_report_persists_through_commit_report() {\n    let mut log = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n    let p = ReportPayload {\n        target: ReportTarget::Actor([9u8; 32]),\n        reason: ReportReason::Harassment,\n        note: b"flagging repeated abuse".to_vec(),\n    };\n    let ev = MeshEvent {\n        prev: [0u8; 32],\n        actor_pubkey: reporter(),\n        actor_seq: 1,\n        payload: p.encode(),\n    };\n    let out = commit_report(&mut log, ev).expect("valid report must commit");\n    assert!(matches!(out, AppendOutcome::Committed(_)));\n    assert_eq!(log.len(), 1, "one logical report = one persisted row");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn p74_malformed_report_rejected_nothing_persists() {\n    let mut log = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n    // Adversarial: reason byte 100 is outside the abuse enum (a §16.59 quality-code\n    // smuggle). The Law pole must reject and persist nothing.\n    let mut bytes = DOMAIN_REPORT.to_vec();\n    bytes.push(0); // Hub target\n    bytes.push(100); // UnknownReason\n    bytes.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // empty note\n    let ev = MeshEvent {\n        prev: [0u8; 32],\n        actor_pubkey: reporter(),\n        actor_seq: 1,\n        payload: bytes,\n    };\n    let res = commit_report(&mut log, ev);\n    assert!(res.is_err(), "malformed report must be Law-rejected");\n    assert_eq!(log.len(), 0, "rejected report persists nothing");\n}\n	3505	-1	-1		0bac6e5fbe089366db2cd8dd55953e038dfaa0572531de0b2a4cc61cf9d78eab414270805acc79cfb369d0286fb3726aceec2489b7c9a229a86b7626871cfaeca4ab13c5b0da70251049fcc10689edd5ed58292b7c9d5606a6a62584dca7d575a616ea968a47b1a9b25f9e473625c71e65b1f42ec4aea9b58bda327e506ca830
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/tests/no_card_data.rs	no_card_data · 126 lines	//! No-card-data firewall integration test (BLUEPRINT-P60 §4.1 / §6 — the PCI red-line teeth).\n//!\n//! Scans the WHOLE `kernel/src/` tree for card-data identifiers (`pan`, `cvv`, `cvc`,\n//! `card_number`, `card_holder`, `exp_month`, `exp_year`). Adding a `struct CardNumber` or a\n//! `pan:` field anywhere in kernel/ makes this test FAIL — so the no-PAN guarantee is enforced\n//! by construction (the kernel never deserializes a card — there is no field to hold one) PLUS a\n//! CI-teeth scan that keeps it that way. Mirrors `kernel/tests/firewall_p47.rs` (structurally\n//! deterministic, no subprocess). Run: `cargo test --test no_card_data`.\n\nuse std::path::Path;\n\n// Forbidden card-data identifiers (the no-PAN structural guarantee). Assembled so this file's own\n// source never contains a contiguous forbidden literal (which would make `!contains` vacuous) —\n// the doc above uses prose rather than the raw tokens.\nconst FORBIDDEN_CARD_TOKENS: &[&str] = &[\n    concat!("card_", "number"),\n    concat!("card", "number"),\n    concat!("card_", "holder"),\n    concat!("card", "holder"),\n    concat!("exp_", "month"),\n    concat!("exp_", "year"),\n    concat!("c", "vv"),\n    concat!("c", "vc"),\n    concat!("p", "an"),\n];\n\n/// Strip Rust comments + string/char literals so doc-comment prose (which names these tokens) is\n/// never a false positive. We hunt CODE identifiers only.\nfn strip_comments(src: &str) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(src.len());\n    let b = src.as_bytes();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    let mut in_block = false;\n    while i < b.len() {\n        if in_block {\n            if i + 1 < b.len() && b[i] == b'*' && b[i + 1] == b'/' {\n                in_block = false;\n                i += 2;\n            } else {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        if i + 1 < b.len() && b[i] == b'/' && b[i + 1] == b'/' {\n            while i < b.len() && b[i] != b'\\n' {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        if i + 1 < b.len() && b[i] == b'/' && b[i + 1] == b'*' {\n            in_block = true;\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if b[i] == b'"' || b[i] == b'\\'' {\n            let q = b[i];\n            out.push(' ');\n            i += 1;\n            while i < b.len() && b[i] != q {\n                if b[i] == b'\\\\' {\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            i += 1;\n            out.push(' ');\n            continue;\n        }\n        out.push(b[i] as char);\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Collect every `.rs` file under `kernel/src`.\nfn kernel_src_files() -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    let root = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src");\n    let mut stack = vec![root];\n    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {\n        if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&dir) {\n            for e in entries.flatten() {\n                let p = e.path();\n                if p.is_dir() {\n                    stack.push(p);\n                } else if p.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) == Some("rs") {\n                    out.push(p.to_string_lossy().into_owned());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn no_card_data_type_anywhere_in_kernel_src() {\n    let files = kernel_src_files();\n    assert!(!files.is_empty(), "kernel src tree must be non-empty");\n    let mut violations = Vec::new();\n    for f in &files {\n        let src = match std::fs::read_to_string(f) {\n            Ok(s) => s,\n            Err(_) => continue,\n        };\n        // Scan CODE only (comments/strings stripped) so doc prose naming a token is harmless.\n        let code = strip_comments(&src);\n        // Tokenize into lowercase words so `pan`/`card_number` are caught regardless of case or\n        // container punctuation.\n        let words: Vec<String> = code\n            .split(|c: char| !(c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_'))\n            .map(|w| w.to_lowercase())\n            .collect();\n        for token in FORBIDDEN_CARD_TOKENS {\n            let needle = token.to_lowercase();\n            if words.iter().any(|w| w == &needle) {\n                violations.push(format!("{f}: contains card-data token '{token}'"));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    assert!(\n        violations.is_empty(),\n        "P60 PCI red-line violation — card-data type found in kernel/: {:?}",\n        violations\n    );\n}\n	3510	-1	-1		c3567f1df804a645923b78cc3a20532108fe35e68f16e4533857e848e1c1fd4759003235f74a1a5cbe0a0629b9e5f8e8c46935a5e748cd8aa476b205cf273b4fd61f18a165da90219b81b248b737e9e848d9c879e579e50850805afcd0dac534bf6be337bc4a8a0d784208462474639785b5156a3600ae8ca4e14ce445f43ee1
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/tests/span_metrics_init_wire.rs	span_metrics_init_wire · 189 lines	//! P83 Layer-1 wiring test (BLUEPRINT P83 §4.2, D1/D2/D3).\n//!\n//! Drives `init_scoped()` (which mirrors exactly what `init_tracing()` does under\n//! `DOWIZ_SPAN_METRICS=1`) and asserts that a real workload emitting the\n//! `place_order_priced` span produces a `metric.jsonl` row named for that span with\n//! `count` matching the number of spans emitted.\n//!\n//! CRITICAL: every assertion-bearing probe in this file is wrapped in a `std::thread`\n//! with a hard join timeout so that a regression in the layer (e.g. the\n//! self-deadlock that previously hung `red_flag_on_place_order_priced_counts_1000`\n//! forever) FAILS THE TEST with a panic instead of hanging the whole `cargo test`\n//! run. This is what makes the regression catchable in CI.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::{\n    catalog::PriceCatalog, domain::place_order_priced, domain::OrderItem, money::Currency,\n    vendor::VendorId,\n};\n\nfn trusted_catalog() -> PriceCatalog {\n    let mut c = PriceCatalog::new();\n    c.insert_flat("p1", 5000);\n    c.insert_flat("p2", 300);\n    c\n}\n\nfn run_priced(n: usize) {\n    let cat = trusted_catalog();\n    for i in 0..n {\n        let items = vec![OrderItem {\n            product_id: "p1".into(),\n            modifier_ids: vec![],\n            quantity: 1,\n            unit_price: 0,\n            vendor_id: VendorId(0),\n            currency: Currency::All,\n        }];\n        let _ = place_order_priced(\n            format!("p83-{i}"),\n            None,\n            items,\n            0,\n            Some("test".into()),\n            None,\n            &cat,\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run `body` on a worker thread; if it does not finish within `secs`, panic in the\n/// main test thread (proving the probe is bounded — a hang becomes a test failure, not\n/// a forever-stuck `cargo test`). Returns whatever `body` returned.\nfn bounded<T>(secs: u64, body: impl FnOnce() -> T + Send + 'static) -> T\nwhere\n    T: Send + 'static,\n{\n    let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();\n    let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        let r = body();\n        let _ = tx.send(());\n        r\n    });\n    match rx.recv_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(secs)) {\n        Ok(()) => handle.join().expect("worker panicked"),\n        Err(_) => {\n            panic!("probe did not finish within {secs}s — layer is unbounded/hung (regression)")\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Under the span-metrics layer, the `place_order_priced` spans must be folded into a\n/// `metric.jsonl` row named exactly for that span. The workload is bounded (N=50: far\n/// above any noise floor, well under any slow-but-terminating threshold) and the whole\n/// probe is wrapped in a 20s thread timeout so the historical deadlock is impossible.\n#[test]\nfn red_flag_on_place_order_priced_counts_1000() {\n    // When built WITHOUT the `telemetry` feature, the layer does not exist; the env\n    // flag is a no-op and there is nothing to assert. Skip.\n    #[cfg(not(feature = "telemetry"))]\n    {\n        return;\n    }\n    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]\n    {\n        bounded(20, || {\n            let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("p83_init_wire_{}", std::process::id()));\n            let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir);\n            // Mirror exactly what `init_tracing()` does under DOWIZ_SPAN_METRICS=1, but\n            // scoped so it does not fight a global subscriber another test already set.\n            let _guard = dowiz_kernel::span_metrics::init_scoped(Some(dir.clone()));\n            const N: usize = 50;\n            run_priced(N);\n            let p = dir.join("metric.jsonl");\n            let contents =\n                std::fs::read_to_string(&p).expect("metric.jsonl should exist under the layer");\n            assert!(\n                contents.contains("\\"span\\":\\"place_order_priced\\""),\n                "expected a metric.jsonl row for place_order_priced under the span-metrics layer"\n            );\n            let cnt: u64 = contents\n                .lines()\n                .filter(|l| l.contains("\\"span\\":\\"place_order_priced\\""))\n                .map(|l| {\n                    let s = l.find("\\"count\\":").map(|i| &l[i + 8..]).unwrap_or("0");\n                    s.chars()\n                        .take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())\n                        .collect::<String>()\n                        .parse::<u64>()\n                        .unwrap_or(0)\n                })\n                .sum();\n            assert!(\n                cnt >= N as u64,\n                "place_order_priced span count should be ~{N}, got {cnt}"\n            );\n            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n        });\n    }\n}\n\n/// REGRESSION TEST for the self-deadlock (P83). Drives an arbitrary `#[instrument]`-style\n/// span through the layer and asserts the span CLOSES (and writes its row) within a\n/// bounded time. This is the test the prior agent was missing: `on_enter`/`on_close`\n/// used to call `span.extensions_mut()` while `tracing::Span::entered()` held the same\n/// span's `Extensions` read lock → the layer hung forever on the very first span. If the\n/// deadlock ever returns, this test panics on the 20s join timeout instead of hanging.\n#[test]\nfn red_span_close_never_deadlocks() {\n    #[cfg(not(feature = "telemetry"))]\n    {\n        return;\n    }\n    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]\n    {\n        bounded(20, || {\n            let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("p83_deadlock_{}", std::process::id()));\n            let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir);\n            let _guard = dowiz_kernel::span_metrics::init_scoped(Some(dir.clone()));\n\n            // A synthetic instrumented span exercised through the observer exactly the way\n            // `place_order_priced` is (`.entered()` → guard drop → on_span_close).\n            fn synthetic_span() {\n                let _s = dowiz_kernel::fdr::info_span!("p83_synthetic").entered();\n                // trivial work\n                let _ = 1 + 1;\n            }\n            for _ in 0..20 {\n                synthetic_span();\n            }\n\n            let p = dir.join("metric.jsonl");\n            let contents =\n                std::fs::read_to_string(&p).expect("metric.jsonl should exist after closing spans");\n            assert!(\n                contents.contains("\\"span\\":\\"p83_synthetic\\""),\n                "synthetic span must be recorded by the layer (proves on_close ran)"\n            );\n            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n        });\n    }\n}\n\n/// D2: with `DOWIZ_SPAN_METRICS` UNSET, `init_tracing()` installs the ordinary `fmt`\n/// layer and NO `SpanMetricsLayer` is ever constructed — prove the default path is\n/// observability-silent (no metric.jsonl appears from the workload).\n#[test]\nfn red_default_build_unchanged_no_metric_row() {\n default branch exactly: call init_tracing without the env flag.\n    std::env::remove_var("DOWIZ_SPAN_METRICS");\n    dowiz_kernel::init_tracing();\n    run_priced(500);\n\n    // Either no metric.jsonl at all, or it has no span row. The default build must not\n    // suddenly start writing kernel span metrics.\n    let p = dir.join("metric.jsonl");\n    let has_row = match std::fs::read_to_string(&p) {\n        Ok(s) => s.contains("\\"span\\":"),\n        Err(_) => false,\n    };\n    assert!(\n        !has_row,\n        "default (no-env) init_tracing must not emit span metrics"\n    );\n\n    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n}\n	3519	-1	-1		035cbdd74c872376294d80cf1305122341168574fc54e68e7b5b98c99358c74f19e8332257c20a9ca8530fd92195e7280dd12f04916b8e61f6ef330ed304e8dfd79f54abcdaa8111d28d2803d5dba9d0f0514d5229b64f20299238b3d88f5d2ea405f2fc90cd1188eac88e8694582bd00c37447b748189c98209e4d5596caee0
```

## 3523 · /root/dowiz/kernel/tests/verify_chain_wire.rs · LongTerm

Summary: verify_chain_wire · 72 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/tests/verify_chain_wire.rs	verify_chain_wire · 72 lines	//! P-H (audit hash-chain) — kernel-local caller wiring (RED→GREEN).\n//!\n//! Wires `event_log::verify_chain_before_trust` — a real production caller for\n//! the `EventLog::verify_chain` mesh-event-log verifier that had ZERO callers\n//! (only module tests exercised it). The caller verifies a persisted/replayed\n//! audit chain BEFORE trusting it, per P-H "no chain ⇒ no mesh". Before this\n//! wiring the caller did not exist ⇒ the test fails to compile (RED). After\n//! wiring it compiles and passes (GREEN).\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::event_log::{\n    verify_chain_before_trust, ChainDefect, EventLog, MemEventStore, MeshEvent,\n};\n\nfn genesis_event(payload: &[u8]) -> MeshEvent {\n    MeshEvent {\n        prev: [0u8; 32],\n        actor_pubkey: [7u8; 32],\n        actor_seq: 0,\n        payload: payload.to_vec(),\n    }\n}\n\nfn chained(prev: [u8; 32], seq: u64, payload: &[u8]) -> MeshEvent {\n    MeshEvent {\n        prev,\n        actor_pubkey: [7u8; 32],\n        actor_seq: seq,\n        payload: payload.to_vec(),\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn ph_verify_chain_before_trust_accepts_valid_chain() {\n    let mut log = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n    let e0 = genesis_event(b"genesis");\n    let p0 = e0.event_id();\n    let e1 = chained(p0, 1, b"append-1");\n    let p1 = e1.event_id();\n    let e2 = chained(p1, 2, b"append-2");\n    let tip = e2.event_id();\n\n    let _ = log.append_raw(e0);\n    let _ = log.append_raw(e1);\n    let _ = log.append_raw(e2);\n\n    // The kernel-local caller verifies the persisted chain before trusting it.\n    let head = verify_chain_before_trust(&log).expect("valid chain must verify");\n    // Trusted head is the event-id of the final event (the chain tip).\n    assert_eq!(head, tip);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn ph_verify_chain_before_trust_rejects_broken_prev() {\n    let mut good = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n    let e0 = genesis_event(b"genesis");\n    let _ = good.append_raw(e0);\n    // A separate, corrupt chain: prev points at a non-existent hash.\n    let mut bad = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n    let mut broken = chained([0x99u8; 32], 1, b"append-1");\n    broken.prev = [0x99u8; 32];\n    let _ = bad.append_raw(broken);\n\n    // The good chain verifies; the broken one is rejected (fail-closed).\n    assert!(verify_chain_before_trust(&good).is_ok());\n    assert!(\n        matches!(\n            verify_chain_before_trust(&bad),\n            Err(ChainDefect::BrokenPrev { .. })\n        ),\n        "broken prev must be rejected, not trusted"\n    );\n}\n	3524	-1	-1		43f8275c820d4128e31de0dd15f53f354d9abcbc9d33c6a33c64ecd4d556e749f9587891678ec93f1d4d1dab084dbabec4eb55a119a8a998f4ba326dd644638d9da9534d5c57018140c3b94a0699e5d0d45f28186d304497821a29a2d08bcf15adbefed6224bb2829c449c4f23744b902db3646246bf1e8133bbe7de712832a9
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/tests/csr_spectral_parity.rs	csr_spectral_parity · 186 lines	//! Cross-module parity pins for the CSR graph after its extraction to no_std\n//! `dowiz-core`. The `csr` module was previously self-contained in the kernel\n//! and pinned against `spectral` directly inside its own `#[cfg(test)]` module.\n//! Once `csr` moved into `dowiz-core` (which cannot depend on `spectral`), those\n//! cross-module pins had to move here, where BOTH representations are in scope:\n//!\n//!   (1) ENERGY PARITY — `spectral::csr_energy(g)` (the re-homed `Csr::energy`)\n//!       must equal `spectral::graph_energy(&g.to_adjacency())`.\n//!   (2) LAPLACIAN PARITY — `Csr::laplacian_spmv(Unnormalized)` (matrix-free,\n//!       never forms L) must equal the DENSE `spectral::laplacian(adj)` applied\n//!       as an ordinary mat-vec, for every labeled undirected graph on N ≤ 5\n//!       nodes plus curated weighted/asymmetric/self-loop cases.\n//!\n//! This is the same ITEM 18 (§14 / §26(d)) parity pin as before — relocated,\n//! not weakened.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::csr::{Csr, LaplacianKind};\nuse dowiz_kernel::spectral::{csr_energy, graph_energy, laplacian};\n\nfn close(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {\n    (a - b).abs() <= tol\n}\n\n/// Dense L = D − A with row-sum degree d_i = Σ_j A_ij (self-loops cancel on the\n/// diagonal), the exact convention `spectral::laplacian` implements.\nfn dense_laplacian_matvec(adj: &[Vec<f64>], x: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64> {\n    let l = laplacian(adj);\n    let n = l.len();\n    (0..n).map(|i| (0..n).map(|j| l[i][j] * x[j]).sum()).collect()\n}\n\n/// Assert dense `laplacian()`·x == `laplacian_spmv(Unnormalized)` for one\n/// (adjacency, field) pair, to `tol`. `adj` must be square n×n.\nfn assert_unnormalized_parity(adj: &[Vec<f64>], x: &[f64], tol: f64) {\n    let n = adj.len();\n    assert_eq!(x.len(), n, "field length must equal node count");\n    let dense = dense_laplacian_matvec(adj, x);\n    let csr = Csr::from_dense(adj);\n    assert_eq!(csr.nrows(), n, "from_dense must preserve node count");\n    let mut got = vec![0.0; n];\n    csr.laplacian_spmv(x, &mut got, LaplacianKind::Unnormalized);\n    for i in 0..n {\n        assert!(\n            (got[i] - dense[i]).abs() <= tol,\n            "Unnormalized parity FAILED at node {i}: matrix-free {} != dense L·x {} (Δ={:.3e})\\n  adj = {adj:?}\\n  x   = {x:?}",\n            got[i],\n            dense[i],\n            (got[i] - dense[i]).abs(),\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n/// Deterministic NON-TRIVIAL field (never all-zeros / all-ones / constant).\nfn nontrivial_field(n: usize) -> Vec<f64> {\n    let pat = [0.3f64, -0.7, 1.1, -0.25, 0.85, -0.4, 0.6];\n    let x: Vec<f64> = (0..n)\n        .map(|i| pat[i % pat.len()] + 0.13 * i as f64)\n        .collect();\n    if n >= 2 {\n        assert!(\n            x.iter().any(|&v| v != x[0]),\n            "test field must be non-constant"\n        );\n    }\n    x\n}\n\n// The only divergence is float summation reordering, bounded well under 1e-12\n// for the small n and O(1)-magnitude weights/fields used here.\nconst PARITY_TOL: f64 = 1e-12;\n\n// ── ENERGY PARITY ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n#[test]\nfn csr_energy_matches_graph_energy_k3_and_empty() {\n    // K3 as undirected edges (both directions).\n    let edges = [\n        (0, 1, 1.0),\n        (1, 0, 1.0),\n        (1, 2, 1.0),\n        (2, 1, 1.0),\n        (0, 2, 1.0),\n        (2, 0, 1.0),\n    ];\n    let g = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges);\n    let e = csr_energy(&g);\n    assert!(close(e, 4.0, 1e-6), "csr_energy(K3)=4, got {e}");\n    // Direct pin against graph_energy (the value must be identical, not just ≈4).\n    assert!(close(e, graph_energy(&g.to_adjacency()), 1e-12));\n\n    // Empty (edgeless) graph has energy 0.\n    let empty = Csr::from_edges(4, &[]);\n    assert!(close(csr_energy(&empty), 0.0, 1e-9));\n    assert!(close(\n        csr_energy(&empty),\n        graph_energy(&empty.to_adjacency()),\n        1e-12\n    ));\n}\n\n// ── LAPLACIAN PARITY: exhaustive labeled undirected graphs N=1..=5 ─────────\n#[test]\nfn laplacian_dense_vs_spmv_parity_exhaustive_small() {\n    let mut graphs_tested = 0usize;\n    for n in 1..=5usize {\n        let pairs: Vec<(usize, usize)> = (0..n)\n            .flat_map(|i| ((i + 1)..n).map(move |j| (i, j)))\n            .collect();\n        let m = pairs.len(); // number of possible undirected edges\n        let x = nontrivial_field(n);\n        for mask in 0..(1u32 << m) {\n            let mut adj = vec![vec![0.0f64; n]; n];\n            for (b, &(i, j)) in pairs.iter().enumerate() {\n                if mask & (1 << b) != 0 {\n                    adj[i][j] = 1.0;\n                    adj[j][i] = 1.0;\n                }\n            }\n            assert_unnormalized_parity(&adj, &x, PARITY_TOL);\n            graphs_tested += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    assert_eq!(\n        graphs_tested,\n        1 + 2 + 8 + 64 + 1024,\n        "exhaustive graph count"\n    );\n}\n\n// ── LAPLACIAN PARITY: curated weighted / asymmetric / self-loop cases ──────\n#[test]\nfn laplacian_dense_vs_spmv_parity_curated() {\n    // Path P4 (non-regular, degrees 1,2,2,1).\n    let path = vec![\n        vec![0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0],\n        vec![1.0, 0.0, 1.0, &star,\n        &k4,\n        &disconnected,\n        &empty,\n        &weighted_selfloop,\n        &single_selfloop,\n    ] {\n        let x = nontrivial_field(adj.len());\n Cross-module parity pins for the Householder eigensolver after its\n//! extraction to no_std `dowiz-core`. The `householder` module previously\n//! pinned its `eigenvalues_contig` spectrum against the legacy Faddeev-LeVerrier\n//! path (`spectral::charpoly` + `spectral::roots`) inside its own test module.\n//! Once `householder` moved into `dowiz-core` (which cannot depend on\n//! `spectral`), those pins had to move here, where BOTH solvers are in scope:\n//!\n//!   `householder::eigenvalues_contig` (QR, complex) vs\n//!   `spectral::roots(&spectral::charpoly(a))` (Faddeev, complex)\n//!\n//! must agree on every hand-oracle + asymmetric/mixed matrix, sorted by\n//! (re, im). This is the same "householder ⇄ spectral" parity pin as before —\n//! relocated, not weakened.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::householder::eigenvalues_contig;\nuse dowiz_kernel::spectral::{charpoly, roots, Complex};\n\nfn cclose(a: Complex, b: Complex, tol: f64) -> bool {\n    (a.re - b.re).abs() < tol && (a.im - b.im).abs() < tol\n}\n\n/// Householder (QR) spectrum vs legacy Faddeev-LeVerrier, within `tol`.\nfn parity(a: &[Vec<f64>], tol: f64) {\n    let n = a.len();\n    let mut buf = vec![0.0f64; n * n];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        for j in 0..n {\n            buf[i * n + j] = a[i][j];\n        }\n    }\n    let got = eigenvalues_contig(&mut buf, n);\n    let want = roots(&charpoly(a));\n    assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "spectrum length mismatch");\n    // sort both by (re, im) for comparison\n    let mut g = got.clone();\n    g.sort_by(|x, y| x.re.total_cmp(&y.re).then(x.im.total_cmp(&y.im)));\n    let mut w = want.clone();\n    w.sort_by(|x, y| x.re.total_cmp(&y.re).then(x.im.total_cmp(&y.im)));\n    for (i, (x, y)) in g.iter().zip(w.iter()).enumerate() {\n        assert!(\n            cclose(*x, *y, tol),\n            "eig[{i}] mismatch: householder {x:?} vs faddeev {y:?}"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn hand_two_cycle_is_plus_minus_one() {\n    let c = vec![vec![0.0, 1.0], vec![1.0, 0.0]];\n    parity(&c, 1e-9);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn hand_diagonal_known_spectrum() {\n    let d = vec![\n        vec![2.0, 0.0, 0.0],\n        vec![0.0, 5.0, 0.0],\n        vec![0.0, 0.0, -3.0],\n    ];\n    parity(&d, 1e-9);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn hand_path_p3_laplacian_spectrum() {\n    // P₃ Laplacian = [[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]] → spectrum {0,1,3}.\n    let l = vec![\n        vec![1.0, -1.0, 0.0],\n        vec![-1.0, 2.0, -1.0],\n        vec![0.0, -1.0, 1.0],\n    ];\n    parity(&l, 1e-9);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn parity_general_3x3_asymmetric() {\n    let a = vec![\n        vec![1.0, 2.0, 3.0],\n        vec![0.0, 4.0, 5.0],\n        vec![0.0, 0.0, 6.0], // already upper-triangular, eigs 1,4,6\n    ];\n    parity(&a, 1e-9);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn parity_general_4x4_mixed() {\n    let a = vec![\n        vec![0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0],\n        vec![1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0],\n        vec![0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0],\n        vec![0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0],\n    ];\n    parity(&a, 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/kernel/tests/event_log_decide.rs	event_log_decide · 48 lines	//! Kernel-integration test: `dowiz-core::event_log` commits THROUGH the real\n//! kernel `decide`/`fold` Law (`order_machine::assert_transition`) with no I/O.\n//!\n//! This test lived inside `event_log`'s own `#[cfg(test)]` module, but\n//! `order_machine` stays kernel-side (it depends on `fdr` logging + `std::error`),\n//! so the cross-module assertion moved here: the kernel is the only crate where\n//! BOTH `event_log` (re-exported from `dowiz-core`) and `order_machine` are\n//! visible.\n\nuse dowiz_core::event_log::{AppendOutcome, EventLog, MemEventStore, MeshEvent};\nuse dowiz_kernel::order_machine::{assert_transition, OrderStatus};\n\nfn actor(byte: u8) -> [u8; 32] {\n    [byte; 32]\n}\n\n/// RED — write succeeds OFFLINE (no network dependency at all). The log is a\n/// pure in-process structure; this asserts a full commit path with the real\n/// kernel `decide`/`fold` Law (order transition validation) without any I/O.\n#[test]\nfn event_log_commits_through_kernel_decide() {\n    let mut log = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n    // Payload encodes an order transition (Pending -> Confirmed), validated\n    // by the kernel's `decide` half (assert_transition). This proves the\n    // event-log commits THROUGH the real kernel Law before any network use.\n    let payload = b"Pending->Confirmed".to_vec();\n    let e = MeshEvent {\n        prev: [0u8; 32],\n        actor_pubkey: actor(3),\n        actor_seq: 1,\n        payload,\n    };\n    let (out, dec) = log\n        .commit_after_decide(e, |ev| {\n            // The decide half: validate the encoded transition via the Law.\n            let _ = ev;\n            assert_transition(OrderStatus::Pending, OrderStatus::Confirmed)\n                .map(|_| "confirmed".to_string())\n                .map_err(|e| e.code().to_string())\n        })\n        .expect("kernel decide must accept Pending->Confirmed");\n    assert!(matches!(out, AppendOutcome::Committed(_)));\n    assert_eq!(dec.unwrap(), "confirmed");\n    assert_eq!(log.len(), 1);\n    // No network call was ever made; the function returns synchronously and\n    // the store holds exactly one event. This IS the offline-write property.\n    assert!(log.tip().is_some());\n}\n	3553	-1	-1		5b6f3657ee0e03f96b2da05fd85dfe08c417bdaf5d57f6816a50e45ac9768082596a2687df806aeefd5f81233315b578defb640155618d39bc7b722de38479ce96eb909d0cf309615080290981bbe1fce77a4c2a2da145ce8ab0b8b2d48fc355ae46f4869acbd2ed781ed25d3b4107a0ad3771278ed903a88b632ed459282a11
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/llm-adapters/benches/criterion.rs	criterion · 95 lines	//! Native benchmark harness for llm-adapters — OFFLINE paths only.\n//!\n//! Per the AGENTS.md rule, harness benches must NOT depend on the live Ollama daemon\n//! (host/noisy → not a committed baseline). The cache exact-hit decode is the deterministic\n//! hot path: every repeated chat prompt short-circuits here, so its cost MUST be tracked.\n//! Live Ollama latency is covered by the `ollama_roundtrip` integration test (a probe, pass/fail),\n//! not by a baseline-gated bench.\n//!\n//! Run: `cargo bench` (from llm-adapters/) — parsed by ../kernel/benches/bench_track.py.\n\nuse criterion::{black_box, criterion_group, criterion_main, Criterion};\nuse dowiz_kernel::backup::MemStore;\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{\n    CachePolicy, ChatRequest, LlmBackend, LlmError, Message, TaskClass,\n};\nuse llm_adapters::cache::CachingBackend;\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n/// Build a deterministic chat request (temperature 0 → cacheable under `Exact`).\nfn req() -> ChatRequest {\n    ChatRequest {\n        model_id: "qwen2.5-coder:7b".into(),\n        messages: vec![Message {\n            role: "user".into(),\n            content: "deterministic cache decode probe".into(),\n        }],\n        max_tokens: 8,\n        temperature: 0.0,\n        top_p: 1.0,\n        seed: None,\n        task_class: TaskClass::General,\n        cache_policy: CachePolicy::Exact,\n        options: BTreeMap::new(),\n        ..Default::default()\n    }\n}\n\n/// The cache HIT path: encode → store → decode. Isolates the (de)serialization cost that every\n/// repeated prompt pays instead of an HTTP round-trip. Offline, deterministic.\nfn bench_cache_decode(c: &mut Criterion) {\n    let backend = CachingBackend::with_store(FakeBackend, MemStore::new());\n    let r = req();\n    // Prime the cache once (encode + store), then bench the decode-on-hit path directly.\n    let _ = backend.chat(&r);\n    c.bench_function("cache/exact_hit_decode", |b| {\n        b.iter(|| black_box(backend.chat(&r)))\n    });\n}\n\n/// A backend that returns a fixed response and counts calls (not used for timing, just to prime).\nstruct FakeBackend;\nimpl LlmBackend for FakeBackend {\n    fn id(&self) -> &str {\n        "fake"\n    }\n    fn caps(&self) -> dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::Caps {\n        dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::Caps {\n            chat: true,\n            embed: false,\n            rerank: false,\n ## 3622 · /root/dowiz/llm-adapters/src/cache.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: cache · 488 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/llm-adapters/src/cache.rs	cache · 488 lines	//! cache.rs — WAVE 1(b): exact-match sha3 response cache (Layer A, §3.2).\n//!\n//! `CachingBackend<B, S>` wraps any `LlmBackend` `B` with a content-addressed store `S`\n//! (`dowiz_kernel::backup::{BlockStore, MemStore}`). Key = `sha3_256(BTreeMap-canonical request)`;\n//! value = the serialized `ChatResponse`. `MemStore::put`'s idempotence IS the cache-hit semantics\n//! for free. Layer B (semantic) is intentionally NOT here — it belongs to advisory call sites only,\n//! and the `CachePolicy` type on `ChatRequest` enforces that a gate-critical caller cannot opt in.\n//!\n//! Correctness = exactness: the key includes `model_id` + every sampling param, so a hit is\n//! provably identical. For `temperature > 0` / unpinned-seed calls a hit returns one valid prior\n//! sample; such callers should pass `CachePolicy::NoCache` when a fresh sample is contractually required.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::backup::{BlockStore, Hash, MemStore};\nuse dowiz_kernel::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{\n    Caps, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, EmbedRequest, EmbedResponse, LlmBackend, LlmError,\n    RerankRequest, RerankResponse, Usage,\n};\nuse serde_json::json;\nuse std::collections::{BTreeMap, VecDeque};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\n/// Default upper bound on distinct cached responses (HARNESS audit A3). The unbounded\n/// `MemStore` this used to wrap is now bounded; pick a sane local-first default. A hub\n/// may choose a different cap via `with_capacity`.\npub const DEFAULT_CACHE_CAP: usize = 1024;\n\n/// LRU-bounded wrapper over any `BlockStore` (HARNESS audit A3).\n///\n/// `put` evicts the least-recently-used entry when at `max_entries`; `touch` promotes a\n/// key to most-recent on a cache hit. This makes `CachingBackend` finite — the previous\n/// `Arc<Mutex<MemStore>>` retained every distinct prompt tuple for the process lifetime.\nstruct BoundedStore<S: BlockStore> {\n    inner: S,\n    /// LRU order: front = oldest, back = most-recently used.\n    order: VecDeque<Hash>,\n    max_entries: usize,\n}\n\nimpl<S: BlockStore> BoundedStore<S> {\n    fn new(inner: S, max_entries: usize) -> Self {\n        BoundedStore {\n            inner,\n            order: VecDeque::new(),\n            max_entries: max_entries.max(1),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Promote `id` to most-recent (called on a cache hit). No-op if absent.\n    fn touch(&mut self, id: &Hash) {\n        if self.inner.get(id).is_some() {\n            self.order.retain(|h| h != id);\n            self.order.push_back(*id);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<S: BlockStore> BlockStore for BoundedStore<S> {\n    fn put(&mut self, id: Hash, bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        // Evict LRU when at capacity AND this is a genuinely new id.\n        if self.inner.get(&id).is_none() && self.order.len() >= self.max_entries {\n            if let Some(old) = self.order.pop_front() {\n                self.inner.remove(&old);\n            }\n        }\n        let is_new = self.inner.put(id, bytes);\n        if is_new {\n            self.order.retain(|h| h != &id);\n            self.order.push_back(id);\n        }\n        is_new\n    }\n    fn get(&self, id: &Hash) -> Option<&[u8]> {\n        self.inner.get(id)\n    }\n    fn get_owned(&self, id: &Hash) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.inner.get_owned(id)\n    }\n    fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.inner.len()\n    }\n    fn remove(&mut self, id: &Hash) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.order.retain(|h| h != id);\n        self.inner.remove(id)\n    }\n}\n\n/// A response cache over any `LlmBackend`. Generic over the store so tests can supply a\n/// call-counting `BlockStore` double (done-check: second identical call makes ZERO HTTP calls).\n///\n/// `store` is an `Arc<Mutex<_>>` (NOT `RefCell`) so the cache is `Sync` and can be shared behind an\n/// `Arc` across the `Dispatcher`'s worker threads (WAVE 1(d) bound `B: Send + Sync`). The `Arc`\n/// ALSO makes `CachingBackend` `Clone` without re-cloning the store — so the `Dispatcher`'s\n/// backend handle and the `Harness`'s direct backend handle share the SAME cache contents.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct CachingBackend<B: LlmBackend, S: BlockStore> {\n    inner: B,\n    store: Arc<Mutex<BoundedStore<S>>>,\n}\n\nimpl<B: LlmBackend> CachingBackend<B, MemStore> {\n    /// Convenience: wrap with the in-memory `MemStore` (default for single-node/local-first),\n    /// bounded at [`DEFAULT_CACHE_CAP`].\n    pub fn new(inner: B) -> Self {\n        CachingBackend {\n            inner,\n            store: Arc::new(Mutex::new(BoundedStore::new(\n                MemStore::new(),\n                DEFAULT_CACHE_CAP,\n            ))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<B: LlmBackend, S: BlockStore> CachingBackend<B, S> {\n    pub fn with_store(inner: B, store: S) -> Self {\n        CachingBackend {\n            inner,\n            store: Arc::new(Mutex::new(BoundedStore::new(store, DEFAULT_CACHE_CAP))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Wrap with an explicit entry cap (HARNESS audit A3 — finite cache).\n    pub fn with_capacity(inner: B, store: S, max_entries: usize) -> Self {\n        CachingBackend {\n            inner,\n            store: Arc::new(Mutex::new(BoundedStore::new(store, max_entries))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Canonical, deterministic request key (BTreeMap → sorted JSON → sha3_256). Only cacheable\n    /// requests (`Exact` policy, or `SemanticOk` which falls back to Exact on a miss) participate;\n    /// `NoCache` bypasses entirely.\n    fn cache_key(req: &ChatRequest) -> Option<[u8; 32]> {\n        if matches!(\n            req.cache_policy,\n            dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::CachePolicy::NoCache\n        ) {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let mut m = BTreeMap::new();\n        m.insert("model_id", req.model_id.clone());\n        m.insert(\n            "messages",\n            req.messages\n                .iter()\n                .map(|msg| format!("{}:{}", msg.role, msg.content))\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join("\\n"),\n        );\n        m.insert("temperature", format!("{:.6}", req.temperature));\n        m.insert("top_p", format!("{:.6}", req.top_p));\n        m.insert("max_tokens", req.max_tokens.to_string());\n        m.insert("seed", req.seed.map(|s| s.to_string()).unwrap_or_default());\n        m.insert("task_class", format!("{:?}", req.task_class));\n        // `options` (Ollama knobs) affect the output ⇒ part of the key.\n        let opts: BTreeMap<String, String> = req.options.clone();\n        m.insert("options", serde_json::to_string(&opts).unwrap_or_default());\n        // HARNESS §3.2: a tool-bearing request partitions the cache from its\n        // tool-less twin. Omitting `tools` here would poison the cache — a cached\n        // tool-less answer served to a tool run (or vice versa). The key carries a\n        // stable, comparable form: each tool's name+arg_name (the declaration, not\n        // the description text, which is model-facing prose and excludes nothing\n        // semantically). Sorted for determinism.\n        let mut tool_keys: Vec<String> = req\n            .tools\n            .iter()\n            .map(|t| format!("{}:{}", t.name, t.arg_name))\n            .collect();\n        tool_keys.sort();\n        m.insert("tools", tool_keys.join(","));\n        let canonical = serde_json::to_vec(&json!(m)).unwrap_or_default();\n        Some(sha3_256(&canonical))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<B: LlmBackend, S: BlockStore> LlmBackend for CachingBackend<B, S> {\n    fn id(&self) -> &str {\n        self.inner.id()\n    }\n    fn caps(&self) -> Caps {\n        self.inner.caps()\n    }\n    fn chat(&self, req: &ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, LlmError> {\n        let key = Self::cache_key(req);\n        if let Some(k) = key {\n            // Peek (owned clone) + promote to MRU under one lock; decode outside the lock.\n            let hit = {\n                let mut g = self.store.lock().unwrap();\n                let bytes = g.get(&k).map(|b| b.to_vec());\n                if bytes.is_some() {\n                    g.touch(&k);\n                }\n                bytes\n            };\n            if let Some(bytes) = hit {\n                if let Some(resp) = decode_response(&bytes) {\n                    return Ok(resp); // EXACT hit — zero upstream call.\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        let resp = self.inner.chat(req)?;\n        if let Some(k) = key {\n            // BoundedStore::put evicts LRU when at cap (HARNESS audit A3).\n            let bytes = encode_response(&resp);\n            self.store.lock().unwrap().put(k, &bytes);\n        }\n        Ok(resp)\n    }\n    fn embed(&self, req: &EmbedRequest) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n        self.inner.embed(req)\n    }\n    fn rerank(&self, req: &RerankRequest) -> Result<RerankResponse, LlmError> {\n        self.inner.rerank(req)\n    }\n    fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n        self.inner.health()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Manual (de)serialization of `ChatResponse` — kept local so the kernel's `llm.rs` value types\n/// stay serde-free (zero-dep invariant). Format: three lines — content, then\n/// `prompt|completion|total`, then `model_id|utterance_id`. The provenance line is mandatory\n/// (L1 opacity): a cache hit must restore the real model tag, never fabricate one.\nfn encode_response(resp: &ChatResponse) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    out.extend_from_slice(resp.content.as_bytes());\n    out.push(b'\\n');\n    out.extend_from_slice(\n        format!(\n            "{}|{}|{}",\n            resp.usage.prompt_tokens, resp.usage.completion_tokens, resp.usage.total_tokens\n        )\n        .as_bytes(),\n    );\n    out.push(b'\\n');\n    out.extend_from_slice(format!("{}|{}", resp.model_id, resp.utterance_id).as_bytes());\n    out\n}\n\n/// Inverse of `encode_response`. Returns `None` on any malformed row (degrade to miss, never panic).\n/// The provenance line MUST be present and well-formed — a decoded reply without a model tag is\n/// refused (L1: no provenance-less output can re-enter the supervisor from cache).\nfn decode_response(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<ChatResponse> {\n    let s = std::str::from_utf8(bytes).ok()?;\n    let mut lines = s.splitn(3, '\\n');\n    let content = lines.next()?;\n    let usage = lines.next()?;\n    let prov = lines.next()?;\n    let mut uparts = usage.split('|');\n    let prompt = uparts.next()?.parse::<u32>().ok()?;\n    let completion = uparts.next()?.parse::<u32>().ok()?;\n    let total = uparts.next()?.parse::<u32>().ok()?;\n    let mut pparts = prov.split('|');\n    let model_id = pparts.next()?.to_string();\n    let utterance_id = pparts.next()?.parse::<u64>().ok()?;\n    if model_id.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    Some(ChatResponse {\n        content: content.to_string(),\n        usage: Usage {\n            prompt_tokens: prompt,\n            completion_tokens: completion,\n            total_tokens: total,\n        },\n        model_id,\n        utterance_id,\n        tool_calls: Vec::new(),\n    })\n}\n/// A no-op store: every `get` misses, every `put` is dropped. Used to compile-time-disable\n/// caching (M5 config: `StackBuilder::with_cache(false)`) without a separate code path.\n#[derive(Clone, Default)]\npub struct NoCache;\n\nimpl BlockStore for NoCache {\n    fn put(&mut self, _id: Hash, _bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        false // never persists — disables the cache\n    }\n    fn get(&self, _id: &Hash) -> Option<&[u8]> {\n        None // always a miss\n    }\n    fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        0 // holds no blocks\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use dowiz_kernel::backup::MemStore;\n    use dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{\n        Caps, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, EmbedRequest, EmbedResponse, LlmBackend, LlmError,\n        Message, RerankRequest, RerankResponse, TaskClass,\n    };\n    use std::cell::RefCell;\n    use std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n    /// A call-counting double: records how many times `chat` ran.\n    struct CountingBackend {\n        calls: RefCell<usize>,\n    }\n    impl CountingBackend {\n        fn new() -> Self {\n            CountingBackend {\n                calls: RefCell::new(0),\n            }\n        }\n        fn call_count(&self) -> usize {\n            *self.calls.borrow()\n        }\n    }\n    impl LlmBackend for CountingBackend {\n        fn id(&self) -> &str {\n            "double"\n        }\n        fn caps(&self) -> Caps {\n            Caps {\n                chat: true,\n                embed: false,\n                rerank: false,\n                tool_calling: false,\n            }\n        }\n        fn chat(&self, req: &ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, LlmError> {\n            *self.calls.borrow_mut() += 1;\n            Ok(ChatResponse {\n                content: "cached-answer".into(),\n                usage: dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::Usage {\n                    prompt_tokens: 3,\n                    completion_tokens: 2,\n                    total_tokens: 5,\n                },\n                model_id: req.model_id.clone(),\n                utterance_id: 1,\n                tool_calls: Vec::new(),\n            })\n        }\n        fn embed(&self, _req: &EmbedRequest) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n            Err(LlmError::Unsupported)\n        }\n        fn rerank(&self, _req: &RerankRequest) -> Result<RerankResponse, LlmError> {\n            Err(LlmError::Unsupported)\n        }\n        fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n            Ok(())\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn req(temp: f32) -> ChatRequest {\n        ChatRequest {\n            model_id: "m:tag".into(),\n            messages: vec![dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::Message {\n                role: "user".into(),\n                content: "hi".into(),\n            }],\n            temperature: temp,\n            max_tokens: 8,\n            task_class: TaskClass::General,\n            cache_policy: dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::CachePolicy::Exact,\n            options: BTreeMap::new(),\n            ..Default::default()\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn exact_hit_makes_zero_upstream_calls() {\n        let backend = CountingBackend::new();\n        let cached = CachingBackend::with_store(backend, MemStore::new());\n        let r1 = cached.chat(&req(0.0)).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(r1.content, "cached-answer");\n        assert_eq!(cached.inner.call_count(), 1);\n        // Identical temperature=0 request → served from cache, NO upstream call.\n        let r2 = cached.chat(&req(0.0)).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(r2.content, "cached-answer");\n        assert_eq!(\n            cached.inner.call_count(),\n            1,\n            "second identical call must hit cache (0 HTTP)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn changed_param_is_a_miss() {\n        let backend = CountingBackend::new();\n        let cached = CachingBackend::with_store(backend, MemStore::new());\n        let _ = cached.chat(&req(0.0)).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(cached.inner.call_count(), 1);\n        // Different temperature → different canonical key → miss → upstream call.\n        let _ = cached.chat(&req(0.5)).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(\n            cached.inner.call_count(),\n            2,\n            "changed sampling param must miss"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn no_cache_policy_bypasses() {\n        let backend = CountingBackend::new();\n        let cached = CachingBackend::with_store(backend, MemStore::new());\n        let mut r = req(0.0);\n        r.cache_policy = dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::CachePolicy::NoCache;\n        let _ = cached.chat(&r).unwrap();\n        let _ = cached.chat(&r).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(cached.inner.call_count(), 2, "NoCache must never hit cache");\n    }\n\n    // B-c (HARNESS §3.2): a tool-bearing request PARTITIONS the cache from its\n    // tool-less twin. Two requests that are identical except for `tools=[]` vs\n    // `tools=[read_order_status]` must produce two distinct cache entries and\n    // therefore TWO upstream calls (never a poisoned shared hit). This is the\n    // regression guard against cache-poisoning once `ChatRequest.tools` lands.\n    #[test]\n    fn tools_field_partitions_the_cache() {\n        let backend = CountingBackend::new();\n        let cached = CachingBackend::with_store(backend, MemStore::new());\n        let plain = req(0.0);\n        let mut tooled = req(0.0);\n        tooled.tools.push(dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::ToolDecl {\n            name: "read_order_status".to_string(),\n            description: "Read order status.".to_string(),\n            arg_name: "order_id".to_string(),\n        });\n\n        let _ = cached.chat(&plain).unwrap();\n        let _ = cached.chat(&tooled).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(\n            cached.inner.call_count(),\n            2,\n            "tool-bearing request must NOT collide with its tool-less twin in the cache"\n        );\n\n        // A repeat of each still hits its own partition (no extra upstream call).\n        let _ = cached.chat(&plain).unwrap();\n        let _ = cached.chat(&tooled).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(\n            cached.inner.call_count(),\n            2,\n            "identical re-requests must each hit their own distinct cache partition"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// HARNESS audit A3 — the cache is now BOUNDED: once `max_entries` distinct keys exist,\n    /// the least-recently-used is evicted, so a previously-cached (now-evicted) key misses and\n    /// re-calls upstream instead of being retained for the process lifetime.\n    #[test]\n    fn cache_is_bounded_lru_evicts() {\n        // cap = 2 distinct entries\n        let backend = CountingBackend::new();\n        let cached = CachingBackend::with_capacity(backend, MemStore::new(), 2);\n\n        // Three DISTINCT temperature=0 prompts → only the 2 most-recent survive.\n        let mut a = req(0.0);\n        a.messages = vec![Message {\n            role: "user".into(),\n            content: "A".into(),\n        }];\n        let mut b = req(0.0);\n        b.messages = vec![Message {\n            role: "user".into(),\n            content: "B".into(),\n        }];\n        let mut c = req(0.0);\n        c.messages = vec![Message {\n            role: "user".into(),\n            content: "C".into(),\n        }];\n\n        let _ = cached.chat(&a).unwrap();\n        let _ = cached.chat(&b).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(cached.inner.call_count(), 2);\n        // Re-request A → still cached (it's one of the 2 most-recent).
```
