```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/llm-adapters/src/compose.rs	compose · 689 lines	//! compose.rs — the harness composition call-site (§4.2 / M5).\n//!\n//! Stacks the port adapters into ONE bounded, cache-fronted LLM surface:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//!     Harness\n//!       └─ Dispatcher { TokenBucket-bounded }            (WAVE 1(d): budget + typed refusal)\n//!            └─ CachingBackend { OllamaAdapter, MemStore } (WAVE 1(b): exact-match cache)\n//!                 └─ OllamaAdapter                        (WAVE 0b: live OpenAI-compat backend)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! The backend choice is CONFIG (M5), never a hard-coded fork: `StackBuilder` selects the live\n//! Ollama (or a later-managed backend) and whether the cache is on. This is the single entry\n//! point a consuming engine (FE render loop, agent step, research-argue loop) calls — `harness.chat`\n//! / `harness.embed` — and it is the DISPATCH call-site where token budget + cache + EV harvest\n//! are enforced, never a side-channel around the event-sourced substrate.\n//!\n//! NOTE: the GPU/particle `engine` crate is intentionally NOT the consumer — it is offline-clean\n//! (kernel-only, no network) by mandate. The LLM consumer is the harness, i.e. this crate.\n\nuse crate::cache::{CachingBackend, NoCache};\nuse crate::dispatch::{DispatchError, Dispatcher, PressureLimits};\nuse crate::managed::ManagedApiAdapter;\nuse crate::ollama::{ModelMap, OllamaAdapter};\nuse dowiz_kernel::backup::MemStore;\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{\n    AiMode, BackendConfig, Caps, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, ConfigError, EmbedRequest,\n    EmbedResponse, LlmBackend, LlmError, RerankRequest, RerankResponse,\n};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Default Ollama base URL (the daemon already running on this host).\npub const DEFAULT_OLLAMA_BASE: &str = "http://127.0.0.1:11434";\n\n/// P106 §2.3 — env override keys for the configurable `TaskClass → model_id` map.\n/// Unconfigured behavior is bit-identical to the hardcoded defaults (fail-closed).\nconst ENV_MODEL_CODE: &str = "DOWIZ_MODEL_CODE";\nconst ENV_MODEL_GENERAL: &str = "DOWIZ_MODEL_GENERAL";\nconst ENV_MODEL_EMBEDDING: &str = "DOWIZ_MODEL_EMBEDDING";\n\n/// A fully-wired harness over a concrete backend `B` and store `S`\n/// (`MemStore` = caching on, `NoCache` = off).\n///\n/// Chat goes through the bounded `Dispatcher` (token budget + typed `BudgetExceeded` refusal,\n/// H1 EV harvest); embed/rerank go through the same cache-fronted backend directly (embed caching\n/// powers the semantic-leak gate; the dispatcher's per-call budget does not apply to embeddings).\n///\n/// Made generic over `B: LlmBackend` so production composition can select the backend at runtime\n/// from [`BackendConfig`] (blueprint §2.2) — `OllamaAdapter` (LocalOffline) or the managed\n/// `OpenAiCompatTransport` (Connected) — while the existing `StackBuilder` fluent API stays\n/// Ollama-only for tests/embedders that want explicit control.\npub struct Harness<\n    B: LlmBackend + Send + Sync + 'static,\n    S: dowiz_kernel::backup::BlockStore + Send + Sync + 'static,\n> {\n    dispatcher: Dispatcher<CachingBackend<B, S>>,\n    backend: Arc<CachingBackend<B, S>>,\n}\n\nimpl<\n        B: LlmBackend + Send + Sync + 'static,\n        S: dowiz_kernel::backup::BlockStore + Send + Sync + 'static,\n    > Harness<B, S>\n{\n    /// Dispatch a chat request through the bounded dispatcher (budget + EV harvest).\n    pub fn chat(&self, req: ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, DispatchError> {\n        self.dispatcher.dispatch(req)\n    }\n\n    /// Embed through the cache-fronted backend (bypasses the per-call token budget; shares cache).\n    pub fn embed(&self, req: &EmbedRequest) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n        self.backend.embed(req)\n    }\n\n    /// Rerank through the backend (Ollama has no rerank endpoint → `Err(Unsupported)` fail-closed).\n    pub fn rerank(&self, req: &RerankRequest) -> Result<RerankResponse, LlmError> {\n        self.backend.rerank(req)\n    }\n\n    /// Degrade-closed health passthrough.\n    pub fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n        self.backend.health()\n    }\n\n    /// Capability surface of the underlying adapter.\n    pub fn caps(&self) -> Caps {\n        self.backend.caps()\n    }\n\n    /// Backend id (cache-key/telemetry provenance).\n    pub fn backend_id(&self) -> &str {\n        self.backend.id()\n    }\n}\n\n/// A ready, fully-wired LLM surface produced by [`StackBuilder::from_config`].\n///\n/// The two live modes construct different concrete backends (LocalOffline →\n/// `OllamaAdapter`; Connected → `ManagedApiAdapter` over `OpenAiCompatTransport`), but both\n/// present the same `chat`/`embed`/`rerank`/`health`/`caps` surface. Callers match on `Ready`\n/// and dispatch against the inner harness without naming the concrete backend type.\npub enum Stack {\n    /// Local Ollama (loopback) backend.\n    Local(Harness<OllamaAdapter, MemStore>),\n    /// Managed/remote OpenAI-compatible backend (Connected mode).\n    Managed(Harness<ManagedApiAdapter, MemStore>),\n}\n\nimpl Stack {\n    /// Dispatch a chat request through the bounded dispatcher.\n    pub fn chat(&self, req: ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, DispatchError> {\n        match self {\n            Stack::Local(h) => h.chat(req),\n            Stack::Managed(h) => h.chat(req),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Embed through the cache-fronted backend.\n    pub fn embed(&self, req: &EmbedRequest) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n        match self {\n            Stack::Local(h) => h.embed(req),\n            Stack::Managed(h) => h.embed(req),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Rerank through the backend (Ollama → `Err(Unsupported)` fail-closed).\n    pub fn rerank(&self, req: &RerankRequest) -> Result<RerankResponse, LlmError> {\n        match self {\n            Stack::Local(h) => h.rerank(req),\n            Stack::Managed(h) => h.rerank(req),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Degrade-closed health passthrough.\n    pub fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n        match self {\n            Stack::Local(h) => h.health(),\n            Stack::Managed(h) => h.health(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Capability surface of the wired backend.\n    pub fn caps(&self) -> Caps {\n        match self {\n            Stack::Local(h) => h.caps(),\n            Stack::Managed(h) => h.caps(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Backend id (cache-key/telemetry provenance).\n    pub fn backend_id(&self) -> &str {\n        match self {\n            Stack::Local(h) => h.backend_id(),\n            Stack::Managed(h) => h.backend_id(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Composition result of [`StackBuilder::from_config`].\n///\n/// `Disabled` is **feature absence, not failure**: for `AiMode::Off` no adapter, transport, or\n/// thread pool is constructed, and callers treat the agent surface as absent — every LLM-backed\n/// feature degrades closed rather than surfacing errors at call time. Only the deliberate `Off`\n/// state is silent-by-design; every other misconfiguration surfaces as a typed [`ConfigError`]\n/// returned from `from_config` (blueprint §2.2).\npub enum Composed {\n    /// No backend is constructed. The agent surface is absent by design.\n    Disabled,\n    /// A backend was successfully wired and is ready to serve requests.\n    Ready(Stack),\n}\n\n/// Config-driven builder for the harness stack (M5: backend choice is config, not a fork).\n///\n/// Defaults target the local Ollama daemon with caching on and a conservative token budget\n/// (≈8 tokens/s refill, 64 burst) — local-first, never a surprise managed-API call.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct StackBuilder {\n    base: String,\n    workers: usize,\n    capacity: u64,\n    refill_rate: f64,\n    cache: bool,\n    /// P106 §2.3 — configurable `TaskClass → model_id` routing.\n    model_map: ModelMap,\n}\n\nimpl Default for StackBuilder {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        StackBuilder {\n            base: DEFAULT_OLLAMA_BASE.to_string(),\n            workers: 2,\n            capacity: 64,\n            refill_rate: 8.0,\n            cache: true,\n            model_map: ModelMap::default(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl StackBuilder {\n    /// Point the stack at a different Ollama base URL (or a future OpenAI-compat endpoint).\n    pub fn ollama(mut self, base: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        self.base = base.into();\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Worker-pool size (≤ backend parallelism cap; Ollama ≈ 2).\n    pub fn workers(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {\n        self.workers = n.max(1);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Token-bucket budget: `capacity` burst tokens, `refill_rate` tokens/second.\n    pub fn budget(mut self, capacity: u64, refill_rate: f64) -> Self {\n        self.capacity = capacity;\n        self.refill_rate = refill_rate;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Enable/disable the exact-match response cache (default on).\n    pub fn with_cache(mut self, on: bool) -> Self {\n        self.cache = on;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// P106 §2.3 — override the model id for a specific `TaskClass`. When unconfigured,\n    /// the hardcoded defaults (`qwen2.5-coder:7b`, `llama3.1:8b`, `nomic-embed-text`) apply\n    /// and behavior is bit-identical to the pre-P106 routing.\n    pub fn model_for(mut self, class: dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::TaskClass, model: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        use dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::TaskClass;\n        match class {\n            TaskClass::Code => self.model_map.code = model.into(),\n            TaskClass::General => self.model_map.general = model.into(),\n            TaskClass::Embedding => self.model_map.embedding = model.into(),\n        }\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Build the wired harness. `S` is `MemStore` (cache on) or `NoCache` (cache off) per\n    /// `with_cache`; the caller selects by calling `build_cached` / `build_uncached`.\n    fn build_with<S: dowiz_kernel::backup::BlockStore + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static>(\n        self,\n        store: S,\n    ) -> Harness<OllamaAdapter, S> {\n        let ollama = OllamaAdapter::with_model_map(&self.base, self.model_map);\n        let backend = Arc::new(CachingBackend::with_store(ollama, store));\n        // `Dispatcher::new` Arcs the backend again; both handles share the SAME cache store\n        // (Arc clone inside CachingBackend is a Mutex clone = same inner store).\n        let dispatcher = Dispatcher::new(\n            (*backend).clone(),\n            self.workers,\n            self.capacity,\n            self.refill_rate,\n            PressureLimits::default(),\n        );\n        Harness {\n            dispatcher,\n            backend,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Build with the in-memory cache enabled.\n    pub fn build_cached(self) -> Harness<OllamaAdapter, MemStore> {\n        self.build_with(MemStore::new())\n    }\n\n    /// Build with caching disabled (every call reaches the backend).\n    pub fn build_uncached(self) -> Harness<OllamaAdapter, NoCache> {\n        self.build_with(NoCache)\n    }\n\n    /// Compose a harness from resolved [`BackendConfig`] (blueprint §2.2 — `AiMode` becomes the\n    /// real composition switch).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a typed [`Composed`]:\n    /// - `AiMode::Off` ⇒ `Composed::Disabled` — **no** adapter/transport/pool is constructed.\n    ///   This is feature absence, not failure; callers degrade closed.\n    /// - `AiMode::LocalOffline` ⇒ `Composed::Ready(Stack::Local(Harness<OllamaAdapter>))`, fed the\n    ///   loopback-verified `cfg.base_url`. The loopback pin is enforced upstream by\n    ///   `BackendConfig`; composition never re-validates or widens.\n    /// - `AiMode::Connected` ⇒ `Composed::Ready(Stack::Managed(Harness<ManagedApiAdapter>))`\n    ///   wired with `Quirks::managed_api(api_key)` over `cfg.base_url`.\n    ///\n    /// `BackendConfig` is already fail-closed (it refuses partial `Connected` config and non-loopback\n    /// `LocalOffline` in `from_env`), so resolution errors (`NonLoopbackLocal` / `MissingBaseUrl` /\n    /// `MissingApiKey` / `UnknownMode`) surface before `from_config` ever runs — misconfiguration is\n    /// loud and early. `from_config` itself only adds a guard that `Connected` carries its key.\n    ///\n    /// The caller normally resolves `cfg` via `BackendConfig::from_env()`; tests use the injected\n    /// `from_env_get` and pass the resolved `&BackendConfig` directly, no global env mutation.\n    pub fn from_config(&self, cfg: &BackendConfig) -> Result<Composed, ConfigError> {\n        // P106 §2.3 — resolve model overrides from env. Unconfigured = default (fail-closed).\n        let model_map = self.resolve_model_map();\n\n        match cfg.mode {\n            // No backend — feature absence, degrade closed. Nothing is constructed.\n            AiMode::Off => Ok(Composed::Disabled),\n\n            // Local loopback Ollama. Loopback already enforced by BackendConfig::from_env; we\n            // trust `cfg.base_url` verbatim (never re-validate, never widen).\n            AiMode::LocalOffline => {\n                let ollama = OllamaAdapter::with_model_map(&cfg.base_url, model_map);\n                let backend = Arc::new(CachingBackend::with_store(ollama, MemStore::new()));\n                let dispatcher = Dispatcher::new(\n                    (*backend).clone(),\n                    self.workers,\n                    self.capacity,\n                    self.refill_rate,\n                    PressureLimits::default(),\n                );\n                Ok(Composed::Ready(Stack::Local(Harness {\n                    dispatcher,\n                    backend,\n                })))\n            }\n\n            // Connected managed/remote backend. api_key already loaded from file by\n            // BackendConfig::from_env (never placed in process env).\n            AiMode::Connected => {\n                let key = cfg.api_key.clone().ok_or(ConfigError::MissingApiKey)?;\n                let managed = ManagedApiAdapter::new(cfg.base_url.clone(), &key);\n                let backend = Arc::new(CachingBackend::with_store(managed, MemStore::new()));\n                let dispatcher = Dispatcher::new(\n                    (*backend).clone(),\n                    self.workers,\n                    self.capacity,\n                    self.refill_rate,\n                    PressureLimits::default(),\n                );\n                Ok(Composed::Ready(Stack::Managed(Harness {\n                    dispatcher,\n                    backend,\n                })))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// P106 §2.3 — build a `ModelMap` from env overrides + builder overrides. The builder's\n    /// explicit `model_for` calls take precedence over env (set-first-wins: the first non-empty\n    /// source wins per field, env is checked first, builder override is applied after).\n    fn resolve_model_map(&self) -> ModelMap {\n        let mut map = self.model_map.clone();\n        // Env overrides fill in any field still at its default (builder override takes precedence\n        // because it was applied first — if the builder set a non-default value, we keep it).\n        if map.code == crate::ollama::DEFAULT_MODEL_CODE {\n            if let Ok(v) = std::env::var(ENV_MODEL_CODE) {\n                if !v.is_empty() {\n                    map.code = v;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        if map.general == crate::ollama::DEFAULT_MODEL_GENERAL {\n            if let Ok(v) = std::env::var(ENV_MODEL_GENERAL) {\n                if !v.is_empty() {\n                    map.general = v;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        if map.embedding == crate::ollama::DEFAULT_MODEL_EMBEDDING {\n            if let Ok(v) = std::env::var(ENV_MODEL_EMBEDDING) {\n                if !v.is_empty() {\n                    map.embedding = v;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        map\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{AiMode, BackendConfig, ConfigError, Message, TaskClass};\n\n    fn chat_req(model: &str, text: &str) -> ChatRequest {\n        ChatRequest {\n            model_id: model.to_string(),\n            messages: vec![Message {\n                role: "user".into(),\n                content: text.into(),\n            }],\n            max_tokens: 8,\n            task_class: TaskClass::General,\n            ..Default::default()\n        }\n    }\n\n    // The composition compiles AND is Sync (Dispatcher's Send+Sync bound is satisfied through the\n    // Mutex-backed cache). This is the root-cause fix that made Dispatcher<cache<ollama>> possible.\n    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}\n    #[test]\n    fn harness_stack_is_send_sync() {\n        assert_send_sync::<Harness<OllamaAdapter, MemStore>>();\n    }\n\n    // Live: build the default stack, run one chat — exercises ollama → cache → dispatcher end-to-end.\n    #[test]\n    fn harness_live_chat_through_full_stack() {\n        let h = StackBuilder::default().build_cached();\n        let r = h\n            .chat(chat_req("qwen2.5-coder:7b", "Reply with exactly: OK"))\n            .expect("live chat through full stack");\n        assert!(!r.content.is_empty(), "received a non-empty response");\n        assert!(r.usage.total_tokens > 0, "usage reported");\n    }\n\n    // Live: identical second call is served from the cache (exact-hit) — proves the stack is wired\n    // cache-front, not just pass-through.\n    #[test]\n    fn harness_live_second_call_is_cache_hit() {\n        let h = StackBuilder::default().build_cached();\n        let req = chat_req("qwen2.5-coder:7b", "cache hit test — say PONG");\n        let r1 = h.chat(req.clone()).expect("chat 1");\n        let r2 = h.chat(req.clone()).expect("chat 2 (cache)");\n        assert_eq!(\n            r1.content, r2.content,\n            "cache hit returns identical content"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Live: embed path works through the same cache-fronted backend.\n    #[test]\n    fn harness_live_embed_through_stack() {\n        let h = StackBuilder::default().build_cached();\n        let r = h\n            .embed(&EmbedRequest {\n                model_id: "nomic-embed-text".into(),\n                input: "semantic gate probe".into(),\n            })\n            .expect("live embed through stack");\n        assert_eq!(\n            r.embedding.len(),\n            768,\n            "nomic-embed-text returns 768-d vectors"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── Phase 1: `AiMode` becomes the real composition switch (BLUEPRINT §2.2 / §8) ──\n    // Deterministic logic tests — no global env mutation (uses a temp key file for the\n    // Connected path). Hidden behind the `cfg(test)` module so they share the crate's deps.\n\n    /// Inject an environment reader backed by a fixed map (mirrors the kernel's `from_env_get`).\n    fn env<'a>(map: &'a [(&'a str, &'a str)]) -> impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String> + 'a {\n        move |k: &str| {\n            map.iter()\n                .find(|(key, _)| *key == k)\n                .map(|(_, v)| v.to_string())\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Write a temp key file for the Connected happy-path; returns its path. Caller removes it.\n    fn temp_key_file(contents: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {\n        // Unique per call (counter) so parallel/concurrent tests never clobber each other's file.\n        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n        static COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);\n        let n = COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        let p =\n            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("swave_lmw_p1_key_{}_{}.txt", std::process::id(), n));\n        std::fs::write(&p, contents).unwrap();\n        p\n    }\n\n    // (1) Off (and unset DOWIZ_AI_MODE) composes to Disabled: NO adapter/transport/pool is built.\n    //     Matching on `Composed::Disabled` is the proof nothing was constructed.\n    #[test]\n    fn from_config_off_is_disabled_feature_absent() {\n        // unset env ⇒ Off by the fail-closed default.\n        let cfg = BackendConfig::from_env_get(env(&[])).expect("unset env ⇒ Off");\n matches!(composed, Composed::Disabled),\n            "Off must compose to Composed::Disabled (no backend constructed)"\n        );\n\n        // explicit "off" string is also Disabled.\n        let cfg_off = BackendConfig::from_env_get(env(&[("DOWIZ_AI_MODE", "off")])).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(cfg_off.mode, AiMode::Off);\n        assert!(\n            matches!(\n                StackBuilder::default().from_config(&cfg_off).unwrap(),\n                Composed::Disabled\n            ),\n            "explicit off ⇒ Disabled"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // (2) Non-loopback panic!("expected Ready(Stack::Local) for explicit loopback base"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // (4) Connected with COMPLETE config composes to Ready on the OpenAiCompatTransport +\n    // 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/llm-adapters/src/dispatch.rs	dispatch · 612 lines	//! dispatch.rs — WAVE 1(d)+adaptive: `TokenBucket`(F33)-bounded, `std::thread` dispatcher (§4.2).\n//!\n//! Bounds concurrency on LLM calls WITHOUT tokio. A fixed-size worker pool pulls jobs off an\n//! `mpsc` channel; each worker does `bucket.try_acquire(cost)` → `false` ⇒ returns\n//! `Err(DispatchError::BudgetExceeded)` immediately (degrade-closed, never silently queued-then-\n//! downgraded); `true` ⇒ calls the (blocking) backend and ships the result back over the caller's\n//! `Sender`. N workers ≤ the backend's own parallelism cap (e.g. 2 for Ollama, §4.1), so the\n//! harness's own queue is where back-pressure becomes visible — not Ollama's `MAX_QUEUE` 503.\n//!\n//! Swarm pressure brake: when recent latency or failure rate exceeds fixed thresholds, the\n//! dispatcher ratchets the effective worker count down after each dispatch. Default limits are\n//! unchanged for a healthy harness; only a hot path tightens automatically. No operator change\n//! required.\n//!\n//! Every dispatched call emits an H1 harvest row (`track_record.jsonl`) priced by the backend's\n//! returned `usage.total_tokens`, closing the EV loop so `gov_route` can price local-vs-managed.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{ChatRequest, ChatResponse, LlmBackend, LlmError};\nuse dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::TokenBucket;\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::mpsc::{channel, Sender};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::thread;\nuse std::time::SystemTime;\n\n/// Typed dispatch failure — distinct from `LlmError` (the backend's own failure).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DispatchError {\n    /// Budget exhausted — degrade-closed, the caller must handle (don't retry-silently).\n    BudgetExceeded,\n    /// All worker slots busy — the concurrency cap (HARNESS audit A4, degrade-closed).\n    /// Refused immediately rather than queued-and-downgraded; the caller retries/backs off.\n    Busy,\n    /// The backend itself failed (health/chat error surfaced through).\n    Backend(LlmError),\n}\n\n/// One harvested dispatch record (H1 EV ledger row).\n///\n/// Schema is a SUPERSET of what `tools/telemetry/governance.sh::gov_route` consumes\n/// (`model`, `task`, `success`, `value`, `cost`) so the same row feeds the EV pricing loop\n/// directly — closing the local-vs-managed loop without a schema-migration shim. The extra\n/// fields (`backend`, `tokens`, `ms`) are richer analytics kept in the same row.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TrackRecord {\n    /// Dispatcher-side identity of the backend (e.g. "ollama").\n    pub backend_id: String,\n    /// The model the request targeted (the `model` key gov_route groups by).\n    pub model_id: String,\n    /// Total tokens of the response (0 on failure).\n    pub total_tokens: u64,\n    /// Wall-clock latency of the (blocking) call in ms.\n    pub ms: u64,\n    /// Task class label gov_route folds by (default "chat"; a caller may pass a richer label).\n    pub task: String,\n    /// Whether the call succeeded (1) or failed (0) — drives gov_route's success-rate.\n    pub success: bool,\n    /// Expected value of the call (EV numerator). Default 0.0; the caller/agent loop may supply it.\n    pub value: f64,\n    /// Cost of the call (EV denominator). For local Ollama we proxy cost ≈ total_tokens.\n    pub cost: f64,\n}\n\n/// A bounded dispatcher over a shared `LlmBackend`.\npub struct Dispatcher<B: LlmBackend + Send + Sync + 'static> {\n    backend: Arc<B>,\n    bucket: Arc<TokenBucket>,\n    /// Concurrency cap (HARNESS audit A4): at most `workers` calls may be\n    /// in-flight at once. `try_acquire` refuses immediately when exhausted\n    /// (degrade-closed `Busy`), so the bound is actually enforced — it is no\n    /// longer dead config.\n    slots: Arc<WorkerSlots>,\n    limits: PressureLimits,\n}\n\n/// Swarm pressure-brake knobs. All defaults keep the harness at its existing static limit\n/// until the path is actually hot; adaptive tightening is opt-in through raised limits.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct PressureLimits {\n    /// Successful/latency-ok sample window for the success-rate counter.\n    pub window: usize,\n    /// Treat an rpc as slow beyond this latency ms.\n    pub latency_threshold_ms: u64,\n    /// Steps of `(1, 1, 1, 1, 1)` after `failure_rate_threshold` is crossed — this means\n    /// every dispatching call sees at least 5 chronic failures before the cap drops by 1.\n    pub lag_samples_to_drop: usize,\n    /// Recent failure rate ≥ this fraction triggers ratcheting down.\n    pub failure_rate_threshold: f64,\n    /// Floor after adaptive ratcheting: the dispatcher keeps at least this many workers\n    /// so it does not collapse to zero under sustained load.\n    pub min_workers: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for PressureLimits {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            window: 32,\n            latency_threshold_ms: 3_500,\n            lag_samples_to_drop: 5,\n            failure_rate_threshold: 0.45,\n            min_workers: 1,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl PressureLimits {\n    /// Tighter limits for hot/test harnesses.\n    pub fn aggressive() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            window: 8,\n            latency_threshold_ms: 1_200,\n            lag_samples_to_drop: 2,\n            failure_rate_threshold: 0.25,\n            min_workers: 1,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Track recent dispatch outcomes for adaptive pressure control.\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct PressureTelemetry {\n    /// Sliding window of recent outcomes: `true` = recent call was healthy.\n    outcomes: Vec<bool>,\n    /// Rolling counter of recent latencies greater than the threshold.\n    lag_count: usize,\n    limits: PressureLimits,\n    last_report: Option<SystemTime>,\n}\n\nimpl PressureTelemetry {\n    fn new(limits: PressureLimits) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            outcomes: Vec::with_capacity(limits.window),\n            lag_count: 0,\n            limits,\n            last_report: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn record(&mut self, ms: u64, success: bool) {\n        let healthy = success && ms < self.limits.latency_threshold_ms;\n        if self.outcomes.len() >= self.limits.window {\n            self.outcomes.remove(0);\n        }\n        self.outcomes.push(healthy);\n        if !success || ms >= self.limits.latency_threshold_ms {\n            self.lag_count = self.lag_count.saturating_add(1);\n            if self.lag_count >= self.limits.lag_samples_to_drop {\n                self.maybe_report("pressure ratchet: lagstorm detected");\n            }\n        } else {\n            self.lag_count = self.lag_count.saturating_sub(1);\n        }\n        if self.outcomes.len() == self.limits.window {\n            self.maybe_report("pressure window complete");\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn maybe_report(&mut self, cause: &str) {\n        let now = SystemTime::now();\n        if let Some(t0) = self.last_report {\n            if now.duration_since(t0).map(|d| d.as_secs()).unwrap_or(0) < 1 {\n                return;\n            }\n        }\n        let healthy = self.outcomes.iter().filter(|v| **v).count();\n        let rate = healthy as f64 / self.outcomes.len().max(1) as f64;\n        let last = self.lag_count;\n        let max_lag = self.limits.lag_samples_to_drop;\n        eprintln!("[pressure] {cause}: healthy_rate={rate:.2} lag={last}/{max_lag}");\n        self.last_report = Some(now);\n    }\n\n    fn recent_failure_rate(&self) -> f64 {\n        if self.outcomes.is_empty() {\n            return 0.0;\n        }\n        self.outcomes.iter().filter(|health| !**health).count() as f64 / self.outcomes.len() as f64\n    }\n}\n\n/// A minimal std-only counting semaphore (no tokio): `cap` permits, non-blocking\n/// `try_acquire` returns a RAII `SlotGuard` whose `Drop` releases the permit. Used by\n/// `Dispatcher` to bound in-flight calls (HARNESS audit A4) — the guard is moved into the\n/// worker thread so in-flight count ≤ `cap` for the job's duration.\nstruct WorkerSlots {\n    cap: usize,\n    in_flight: AtomicUsize,\n}\n\nimpl WorkerSlots {\n    fn new(cap: usize) -> Self {\n        WorkerSlots {\n            cap: cap.max(1),\n            in_flight: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn cap(&self) -> usize {\n        self.cap\n    }\n\n    /// Acquire a slot if one is free; otherwise `None` (caller refuses with `Busy`).\n    fn try_acquire(self: &Arc<Self>) -> Option<SlotGuard> {\n        let mut cur = self.in_flight.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        loop {\n            if cur >= self.cap {\n                return None;\n            }\n            match self.in_flight.compare_exchange_weak(\n                cur,\n                cur + 1,\n                Ordering::SeqCst,\n                Ordering::SeqCst,\n            ) {\n                Ok(_) => {\n                    return Some(SlotGuard {\n                        slots: Arc::clone(self),\n                    })\n                }\n                Err(c) => cur = c,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// RAII permit for a `WorkerSlots` slot; released on drop.\nstruct SlotGuard {\n    slots: Arc<WorkerSlots>,\n}\n\nimpl Drop for SlotGuard {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        self.slots.in_flight.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<B: LlmBackend + Send + Sync + 'static> Dispatcher<B> {\n    /// `workers` = pool size (≤ backend parallelism cap). `capacity`/`refill_rate` size the bucket\n    /// in token units (1 token = 1 unit; see `Usage::cost`).\n    ///\n    /// `limits` tunes adaptive pressure: by default the dispatcher behaves identically to earlier\n    /// WAVE 1(d). Pass `PressureLimits::aggressive()` to enable early tightening during hot-path\n    /// load testing.\n    pub fn new(\n        backend: B,\n        workers: usize,\n        capacity: u64,\n        refill_rate: f64,\n        limits: PressureLimits,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Dispatcher {\n            backend: Arc::new(backend),\n            bucket: Arc::new(TokenBucket::new(capacity as f64, refill_rate)),\n            slots: Arc::new(WorkerSlots::new(workers)),\n            limits,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Backwards-compatible constructor with default pressure limits.\n    pub fn with_default_limits(\n        backend: B,\n        workers: usize,\n        capacity: u64,\n        refill_rate: f64,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self::new(\n            backend,\n            workers,\n            capacity,\n            refill_rate,\n            PressureLimits::default(),\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Dispatch one chat request. Returns the response, or a typed `DispatchError`.\n    ///\n    /// Concurrency is bounded by `WorkerSlots` of `workers` permits (HARNESS audit\n    /// A4): `try_acquire` refuses immediately with `Busy` when all slots are in\n    /// flight, so the cap is enforced rather than dead config. The acquired guard\n    /// is moved into the worker thread and released when the job finishes, keeping\n    /// in-flight count ≤ `workers`. Budget is checked inside the job\n    /// (`TokenBucket` bounds volume over time; the slots bound concurrency).\n    pub fn dispatch(&self, req: ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, DispatchError> {\n        // A4: enforce the concurrency cap — refuse (degrade-closed) when full.\n        let guard = match self.slots.try_acquire() {\n            Some(g) => g,\n            None => return Err(DispatchError::Busy),\n        };\n        let (tx, rx) = channel::<Result<ChatResponse, DispatchError>>();\n        let backend = Arc::clone(&self.backend);\n        let bucket = Arc::clone(&self.bucket);\n        let cost = (req.max_tokens as f64).max(1.0); // budget in approx-output units; degrade-closed.\n\n        // Adaptive pressure: one recent-failure-rate counter lives on the dispatcher so\n        // consecutive bad windows ratchet the effective worker cap down, and a healthy\n        // window brings it back up.\n        let _slots_ref = Arc::clone(&self.slots);\n\n        // Hold the slot for the job's duration so in-flight is bounded at `workers`.\n        thread::spawn(move || {\n            let _guard = guard; // dropped at end of this closure ⇒ slot freed\n            let result = if dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::token_bucket_try_acquire(&bucket, cost) {\n                let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();\n                let r = backend.chat(&req).map_err(DispatchError::Backend);\n                let ms = t0.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n                // H1 harvest — record BOTH success and failure so gov_route's success-rate folds\n                // honestly. Tokens/cost are 0 on failure (no response emitted).\n                let (tokens, ok) = match &r {\n                    Ok(resp) => (resp.usage.cost(), true),\n                    Err(_) => (0, false),\n                };\n                let rec = TrackRecord {\n                    backend_id: backend.id().to_string(),\n                    model_id: req.model_id.clone(),\n                    total_tokens: tokens,\n                    ms,\n                    task: "chat".to_string(),\n                    success: ok,\n                    value: 0.0,\n                    cost: tokens as f64,\n                };\n                append_harvest(&rec);\n                r\n            } else {\n                Err(DispatchError::BudgetExceeded)\n            };\n            let _ = tx.send(result);\n        });\n        rx.recv()\n            .map_err(|_| DispatchError::Backend(LlmError::Unavailable))?\n    }\n\n    /// A clone of the shared backend handle (for cache-fronted embed/rerank paths that bypass the\n    /// dispatcher's per-call token budget but still share the SAME cache store).\n    pub fn backend(&self) -> Arc<B> {\n        Arc::clone(&self.backend)\n    }\n\n    /// Health passthrough (degrade-closed).\n    pub fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n        self.backend.health()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Append a harvested record to `track_record.jsonl` (H1 EV ledger). Local-only, M8-compliant.\n/// Emits the `gov_route`-compatible superset schema so the EV pricing loop can fold it directly.\n/// Failures are non-fatal (telemetry must never break the call path).\n///\n/// Made `pub` so other consumers of the harvest ledger (e.g. the `agent-loop` host binary) emit\n/// the EXACT same row the `Dispatcher` writes — one channel, no schema drift (AGENTS.md:\n/// "extend that ledger, do not invent a parallel channel").\npub fn append_harvest(rec: &TrackRecord) {\n    use std::io::Write;\n    let line = format!(\n    "{{\\"model\\":\\"{}\\",\\"task\\":\\"{}\\",\\"success\\":{},\\"value\\":{},\\"cost\\":{},\\"backend\\":\\"{}\\",\\"tokens\\":{},\\"ms\\":{}}}\\n",\n    rec.model_id, rec.task, rec.success, rec.value, rec.cost, rec.backend_id, rec.total_tokens, rec.ms\n  );\n    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n        .create(true)\n        .append(true)\n        .open("track_record.jsonl")\n    {\n        let _ = f.write_all(line.as_bytes());\n    }\n}\n\n/// Backwards-compatible alias so the plan's `Sender` reference resolves cleanly.\npub type RecordSender = Sender<Result<ChatResponse, DispatchError>>;\n\n/// Decode one harvest-ledger line (the inverse of `append_harvest`). Used by the telemetry fold\n/// (`telemetry.rs`) so the same row gov_route reads is the row the in-process aggregator consumes —\n/// one schema, no drift. Returns `None` on a malformed line (fail-closed; the row is skipped).\npub(crate) fn decode_track_record(line: &str) -> Result<TrackRecord, serde_json::Error> {\n    let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(line)?;\n    let get_str = |k: &str| v.get(k).and_then(|x| x.as_str()).unwrap_or("").to_string();\n    let get_bool = |k: &str| v.get(k).and_then(|x| x.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false);\n    let get_f64 = |k: &str| v.get(k).and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0);\n    Ok(TrackRecord {\n        backend_id: get_str("backend"),\n        model_id: get_str("model"),\n        total_tokens: v.get("tokens").and_then(|x| x.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0),\n        ms: v.get("ms").and_then(|x| x.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0),\n        task: get_str("task"),\n        success: get_bool("success"),\n        value: get_f64("value"),\n        cost: get_f64("cost"),\n    })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{\n        Caps, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, EmbedRequest, EmbedResponse, LlmBackend, LlmError,\n        RerankRequest, RerankResponse, Usage,\n    };\n    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n    use std::sync::Arc;\n\n    /// A fake backend that counts calls. No network.\n    struct FakeBackend {\n        calls: AtomicUsize,\n    }\n    impl LlmBackend for FakeBackend {\n        fn id(&self) -> &str {\n            "fake"\n        }\n        fn caps(&self) -> Caps {\n            Caps {\n                chat: true,\n                embed: false,\n                rerank: false,\n                tool_calling: false,\n            }\n        }\n        fn chat(&self, req: &ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, LlmError> {\n            self.calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            Ok(ChatResponse {\n                content: "ok".into(),\n req.model_id.clone(),\n                utterance_id: 1,\n                tool_calls: Vec::new(),\n            })\n        }\n        fn embed(&self, _req: &EmbedRequest) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n            Err(LlmError::Unsupported)\n        }\n        fn rerank(&self, _req: &RerankRequest) -> Result<RerankResponse, LlmError> {\n            Err(LlmError::Unsupported)\n        }\n        fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n            Ok(())\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn req() -> ChatRequest {\n        ChatRequest {\n            max_tokens: 8,\n            ..Default::default()\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn budget_exhausted_returns_typed_refusal() {\n        // capacity=8, refill_rate=0 ⇒ exactly one call (cost=max_tokens=8) fits; the 2nd is refused.\n        let d = Dispatcher::new(\n            FakeBackend {\n                calls: AtomicUsize::new(0),\n            },\n            1,\n            8,\n            0.0,\n assert_eq!(d.backend.calls.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3);\n    }\n\n    // Keep `Arc` import meaningful even if a test is removed.\n    #[test]\n    fn backend_is_shared_arc() {\n        let d = and a slow backend, firing many dispatches concurrently must keep\n    /// in-flight ≤ 1 AND refuse the overflow with a typed `Busy` (degrade-closed) rather than\n    /// spawning unbounded threads or silently queuing.\n    struct SlowBackend {\n        in_flight: Arc<AtomicUsize>,\n        max_in_flight: Arc<AtomicUsize>,\n    }\n    impl LlmBackend for SlowBackend {\n        fn id(&self) -> &str {\n            "slow"\n        }\n        fn caps(&self) -> Caps {\n            Caps {\n                chat: true,\n                embed: false,\n                rerank: false,\n                tool_calling: false,\n            }\n        }\n        fn chat(&self, req: &ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, LlmError> {\n            let cur = self.in_flight.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) + 1;\n            // track max in-flight via a CAS loop\n            let mut m = self.max_in_flight.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n            while cur > m\n                && self\n                    .max_in_flight\n                    .compare_exchange(m, cur, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst)\n                    .is_err()\n            {\n                m = self.max_in_flight.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n            }\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(30));\n            self.in_flight.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            Ok(ChatResponse {\n                content: "ok".into(),\n                usage: Usage {\n                    prompt_tokens: 1,\n                    completion_tokens: 1,\n                    total_tokens: 2,\n                },\n                model_id: req.model_id.clone(),\n                utterance_id: 1,\n                tool_calls: Vec::new(),\n            })\n        }\n        fn embed(&self, _req: &EmbedRequest) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n            Err(LlmError::Unsupported)\n        }\n        fn rerank(&self, _req: &RerankRequest) -> Result<RerankResponse, LlmError> {\n            Err(LlmError::Unsupported)\n        }\n        fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n            Ok(())\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn concurrency_cap_enforced_degrade_closed() {\n        let in_flight = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));\n        let max_in_flight = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));\n        // workers=1 ⇒ at most ONE in-flight call at a time.\n        let d = Arc::new(Dispatcher::new(\n            SlowBackend {\n                in_flight: Arc::clone(&in_flight),\n                max_in_flight: Arc::clone(&max_in_flight),\n            },\n            1,\n            1_000_000,\n            0.0,\n            PressureLimits::default(),\n        ));\n        let workers = 1u64;\n\n        // Fire 8 dispatches concurrently from separate threads.\n        let mut handles = Vec::new();\n        let busy_count = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));\n        for _ in 0..8 {\n            let d = Arc::clone(&d);\n            let bc = Arc::clone(&busy_count);\n            handles.push(std::thread::spawn(move || match d.dispatch(req()) {\n                Err(DispatchError::Busy) => {\n                    bc.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                }\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(other) => panic!("unexpected dispatch error: {:?}", other),\n            }));\n        }\n        for h in handles {\n            let _ = h.join();\n        }\n\n        let max_seen = max_in_flight.load(Ordering::SeqCst);\n        assert!(\n            max_seen <= workers as usize,\n            "in-flight ({}) must be ≤ workers ({})",\n            max_seen,\n            workers\n        );\n        assert!(\n            busy_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst) >= 1,\n            "overflow must be refused with Busy (degrade-closed)"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	3730	-1	-1		d376b5fa91cf0373bb23cdc302027a8101de9fa42dd2a58a295666c7c07b8b230d00b4815fc26097a847c32d40148a2cce57652675680ccaf042f2800304f0ce1c9c5339657bc869d20f3910b7bba57295e1fc6a6df7dbc5ccb471b47849c20470f2f31795cb51f3c3dc0a8cc9544fb06c774dfa9e89ace4178974f4b3a03df1

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/llm-adapters/src/managed.rs	managed · 69 lines	//! managed.rs — `ManagedApiAdapter`: the thin managed/remote backend (Connected mode).\n//!\n//! This is the constructor blueprint §2.2 says `Connected` mode "necessarily creates": the\n//! `OpenAiCompatTransport` already does the wire work; `ManagedApiAdapter` is the `LlmBackend`\n//! shell around it carrying `Quirks::managed_api(api_key)` (bearer auth + standard OpenAI\n//! envelope). It is NOT a new crate and NOT a new dependency — exactly the "Quirks preset +\n//! thin constructor" extension mechanism the blueprint locks in (§1.5). `VllmAdapter` would be\n//! the same shape with `Quirks::vllm()`.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{\n    Caps, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, EmbedRequest, EmbedResponse, LlmBackend, LlmError,\n    RerankRequest, RerankResponse,\n};\n\nuse crate::quirks::Quirks;\nuse crate::transport::OpenAiCompatTransport;\n\n/// A managed/remote OpenAI-compatible backend (Connected mode). Wraps the shared\n/// `OpenAiCompatTransport`; the only delta vs `OllamaAdapter` is the `Quirks` preset\n/// (`managed_api`), so this is a constructor, not a backend build.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct ManagedApiAdapter {\n    transport: OpenAiCompatTransport,\n}\n\nimpl ManagedApiAdapter {\n    /// Build a managed backend over `base_url` with `api_key` (bearer auth). The key is supplied\n    /// by the caller (resolved from `DOWIZ_LLM_API_KEY_FILE` by `BackendConfig`); it is never read\n    /// from the process env.\n    pub fn new(base_url: impl Into<String>, api_key: &str) -> Self {\n        ManagedApiAdapter {\n            transport: OpenAiCompatTransport::new(base_url, Quirks::managed_api(api_key)),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl LlmBackend for ManagedApiAdapter {\n    fn id(&self) -> &str {\n        "openai-compat"\n    }\n\n    fn caps(&self) -> Caps {\n        // A managed API is assumed to support chat + embeddings; rerank is not standard OpenAI and\n        // is not wired here. Tool calling passes through the standard OpenAI envelope.\n        Caps {\n            chat: true,\n            embed: true,\n            rerank: false,\n            tool_calling: true,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn chat(&self, req: &ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, LlmError> {\n        self.transport.chat(req)\n    }\n\n    fn embed(&self, req: &EmbedRequest) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n        self.transport.embed(req)\n    }\n\n    fn rerank(&self, _req: &RerankRequest) -> Result<RerankResponse, LlmError> {\n        // No rerank endpoint in the standard OpenAI surface → fail closed.\n        Err(LlmError::Unsupported)\n    }\n\n    fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n        self.transport.health()\n    }\n}\n	3751	-1	-1		ff4f35d23dcd89b73951e3a3f5865a04c3b69c64e8d6b5fb2955786ec36143011d09750d56f1783f8540533d6505dc684f50d7275662bceb70effa0a3b7c40ee51b44289ad7fef09ca976b0055baa558d7621c6a25c753ea4bb6b8a76f01c72f7872f73e31f851aeea86aa8deb4048ff2c3ee43a3f9545cd8739e6dcbb28cd51

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/llm-adapters/src/ollama.rs	ollama · 180 lines	//! ollama.rs — `OllamaAdapter`: the live Tier-1 backend (already running on this host).\n//!\n//! Implements `dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::LlmBackend`. Model routing by `TaskClass` (§2.2):\n//! Code→qwen2.5-coder:7b, General→llama3.1:8b, Embedding→nomic-embed-text (qwen3-embedding:0.6b\n//! as the higher-quality option). `:tag` ids pass through verbatim; `fp_ollama` sentinel is ignored.\n//!\n//! P106 §2.3: the `TaskClass → model_id` map is now configurable via [`ModelMap`] and env\n//! overrides (`DOWIZ_MODEL_CODE` / `DOWIZ_MODEL_GENERAL` / `DOWIZ_MODEL_EMBEDDING`). Unconfigured\n//! behavior is bit-identical to the prior hardcoded defaults.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::sync::Mutex;\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{\n    Caps, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, EmbedRequest, EmbedResponse, LlmBackend, LlmError,\n    RerankRequest, RerankResponse, TaskClass,\n};\n\nuse crate::quirks::Quirks;\nuse crate::transport::OpenAiCompatTransport;\n\n/// Default model ids — the hardcoded baseline that `ModelMap::default()` returns.\n/// These match the models physically resident on the production box.\npub const DEFAULT_MODEL_CODE: &str = "qwen2.5-coder:7b";\npub const DEFAULT_MODEL_GENERAL: &str = "llama3.1:8b";\npub const DEFAULT_MODEL_EMBEDDING: &str = "nomic-embed-text";\n\n/// P106 §2.3 — configurable `TaskClass → model_id` map. Each field defaults to the\n/// hardcoded model id; env overrides (`DOWIZ_MODEL_CODE` / `DOWIZ_MODEL_GENERAL` /\n/// `DOWIZ_MODEL_EMBEDDING`) and `StackBuilder::model_for` both feed into this.\n///\n/// Behavior when unconfigured is bit-identical to the prior hardcoded routing — this\n/// struct is the *mechanism* for configurability, not a behavior change.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ModelMap {\n    pub code: String,\n    pub general: String,\n    pub embedding: String,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ModelMap {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        ModelMap {\n            code: DEFAULT_MODEL_CODE.to_string(),\n            general: DEFAULT_MODEL_GENERAL.to_string(),\n            embedding: DEFAULT_MODEL_EMBEDDING.to_string(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ModelMap {\n    /// Resolve model id for a given `TaskClass`.\n    pub fn resolve(&self, class: TaskClass) -> &str {\n        match class {\n            TaskClass::Code => &self.code,\n            TaskClass::General => &self.general,\n            TaskClass::Embedding => &self.embedding,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The Ollama adapter. Construct with a base URL (default `http://127.0.0.1:11434`).\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct OllamaAdapter {\n    transport: OpenAiCompatTransport,\n    /// Memoized per-model `tool_calling` probe results. The probe runs lazily on\n    /// the first `caps()` call (never at construction, so building an adapter while\n    /// the daemon is down stays cheap and non-failing). A probe failure is recorded\n    /// as `false` (fail-closed) — never a panic, never a stale `true`.\n    toolkit: std::sync::Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<String, bool>>>,\n    /// P106 §2.3 — configurable `TaskClass → model_id` routing.\n    model_map: ModelMap,\n}\n\nimpl OllamaAdapter {\n    pub fn new(base_url: &str) -> Self {\n        OllamaAdapter {\n            transport: OpenAiCompatTransport::new(base_url, Quirks::ollama()),\n            toolkit: std::sync::Arc::new(Mutex::new(BTreeMap::new())),\n            model_map: ModelMap::default(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Construct with a custom model map (P106 §2.3 — `StackBuilder::model_for` / env overrides).\n    pub fn with_model_map(base_url: &str, model_map: ModelMap) -> Self {\n        OllamaAdapter {\n            transport: OpenAiCompatTransport::new(base_url, Quirks::ollama()),\n            toolkit: std::sync::Arc::new(Mutex::new(BTreeMap::new())),\n            model_map,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Default constructor pointing at the already-running local daemon.\n    pub fn local() -> Self {\n        Self::new("http://127.0.0.1:11434")\n    }\n\n    /// Map `TaskClass` → concrete Ollama model id (within-adapter routing, distinct from Phase-5's\n    /// `gov_route` dev-tooling router). Uses the configurable `ModelMap`; the caller may still\n    /// override `model_id` directly on the request for any ad-hoc model.\n    fn route_model(&self, req: &ChatRequest) -> String {\n        if !req.model_id.is_empty() {\n            return req.model_id.clone();\n        }\n        self.model_map.resolve(req.task_class).to_string()\n    }\n\n    /// Probe (and memoize) whether `model_id` supports tool calling, via Ollama's\n    /// native `/api/show` capabilities. Fail-closed: any failure ⇒ `false`\n    /// (recorded so the same model is never re-probed into a `true`).\n    fn tool_calling_for(&self, model_id: &str) -> bool {\n        // Fast path: reuse a prior probe.\n        if let Some(&v) = self.toolkit.lock().unwrap().get(model_id) {\n            return v;\n        }\n        let ok = self\n            .transport\n            .show_capabilities(model_id)\n            .map(|caps| caps.iter().any(|c| c.eq_ignore_ascii_case("tools")))\n            .unwrap_or(false);\n        self.toolkit\n            .lock()\n            .unwrap()\n            .insert(model_id.to_string(), ok);\n        ok\n    }\n\n    /// Public probe entry point used by tests and callers wanting to check an\n    /// arbitrary model id (not just the General route). Shares the memoized logic\n    /// and the same fail-closed semantics as `caps()`.\n    pub fn probe_tool_calling(&self, model_id: &str) -> bool {\n        self.tool_calling_for(model_id)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl LlmBackend for OllamaAdapter {\n    fn id(&self) -> &str {\n        "ollama"\n    }\n\n    fn caps(&self) -> Caps {\n        // Ollama on this host: chat + embed confirmed live (§1.2). Rerank not wired.\n        // `tool_calling` is NO LONGER hard-pinned: it is discovered live per the\n        // General-route model the loop actually uses (llama3.1:8b), with a\n        // fail-closed probe (failure ⇒ false, never fail-open).\n        let model = self.route_model(&ChatRequest {\n            task_class: TaskClass::General,\n            ..Default::default()\n        });\n        Caps {\n            chat: true,\n            embed: true,\n            rerank: false,\n            tool_calling: self.tool_calling_for(&model),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn chat(&self, req: &ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, LlmError> {\n        let mut routed = req.clone();\n        routed.model_id = self.route_model(req);\n        self.transport.chat(&routed)\n    }\n\n    fn embed(&self, req: &EmbedRequest) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n        self.transport.embed(req)\n    }\n\n    fn rerank(&self, _req: &RerankRequest) -> Result<RerankResponse, LlmError> {\n        // Ollama (this host) has no rerank endpoint wired → fail closed, caller falls back.\n        Err(LlmError::Unsupported)\n    }\n\n    fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n        self.transport.health()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Backwards-compatible alias so the plan's `OllamaQuirks` reference resolves (the adapter uses\n/// `Quirks::ollama()` directly; this type is a thin marker, kept so the public surface matches docs).\npub type OllamaQuirks = Quirks;\n	3776	-1	-1		efdffdd079db024b391fcbdbe9823a26c3568d0c69d415ce3b572a4282237b23184e342556c869359448b36939ef5e31cdfde5a73561bca2f046fe0d67cf32c85a88f3997511ad01d08b2b82b79ba3fad34ebc4829349dd78c9783963a4b17053172776fb8c21ab4cff98b0d294d6bbba4324928de842c6707f9e4fd71315ff0

This struct encodes them so the single `OpenAiCompatTransport` can serve every\n//! backend by passing a different `Quirks`. This is the Hermes-proven `Quirks`-pattern the repo\n//! already cites.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n/// Per-adapter wire deltas. The transport reads these; it holds no vendor knowledge itself.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Quirks {\n    /// Pass `:tag` model ids through verbatim — never strip/normalize after `:`\n    /// (Ollama `llama3.1:8b`). Default: true (safe).\n    pub pass_tag_ids_verbatim: bool,\n    /// `system_fingerprint:"fp_ollama"` is a constant sentinel — never key caching/dedup on it.\n    /// The transport already strips it; this flag documents intent + lets vLLM assert absence.\n    pub strip_sentinel_fingerprint: bool,\n    /// Embeddings endpoint path. Ollama: `/v1/embeddings` (OpenAI-parity). vLLM: `/v1/embeddings`.\n    pub embeddings_path: String,\n    /// Native (non-`/v1`) embeddings fallback path, if the adapter wants it (Ollama `/api/embed`).\n    pub native_embeddings_path: Option<String>,\n    /// Surface `options` (Ollama-only knobs: `keep_alive`, `num_ctx`, `think`). When false, the\n    /// transport drops `options` from the wire envelope entirely (vLLM/managed-API).\n    pub surface_options: bool,\n    /// Extra headers (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer …` for managed-API). Sent on every request.\n    pub extra_headers: BTreeMap<String, String>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Quirks {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Quirks {\n            pass_tag_ids_verbatim: true,\n            strip_sentinel_fingerprint: true,\n            embeddings_path: "/v1/embeddings".to_string(),\n            native_embeddings_path: None,\n            surface_options: false,\n            extra_headers: BTreeMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Quirks {\n    /// Ollama-specific quirks (live-verified §1.2 / §2.2).\n    pub fn ollama() -> Self {\n        Quirks {\n            pass_tag_ids_verbatim: true,\n            strip_sentinel_fingerprint: true,\n            embeddings_path: "/v1/embeddings".to_string(),\n            native_embeddings_path: Some("/api/embed".to_string()),\n            surface_options: true,\n            extra_headers: BTreeMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// vLLM (Tier-2, GPU-gated) — native OpenAI-compat, no `:tag` normalization needed, no\n    /// Ollama-only options.\n    pub fn vllm() -> Self {\n        Quirks {\n            pass_tag_ids_verbatim: false,\n            strip_sentinel_fingerprint: false,\n  /// Managed-API proxy (Tier-0 default) — standard OpenAI envelope + bearer auth.\n    pub fn managed_api(api_key: &str) -> Self {\n        let mut headers = BTreeMap::new();\n        headers.insert("Authorization".to_string(), format!("Bearer {}", api_key));\n        Quirks {\n            pass_tag_ids_verbatim: false,\n            strip_sentinel_fingerprint: false,\n ```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/llm-adapters/src/telemetry.rs	telemetry · 141 lines	//! telemetry.rs — native harvest-ledger aggregation (H1 EV loop, zero extra deps).\n//!\n//! The `Dispatcher` already writes one JSON row per dispatch to the harvest ledger\n//! (`track_record.jsonl`, gov_route-compatible schema `{model,task,success,value,cost,...}`).\n//! This module reads that ledger and folds it into per-model telemetry: dispatch count, success\n//! rate, mean token cost, total cost — the same aggregates `gov_route` consumes, but as a\n//! in-process struct the harness can surface on demand (no new telemetry channel, no network).\n//!\n//! Fail-closed: an empty/missing ledger yields `Telemetry::default()` (all-zeros), never a panic.\n//! The fold is deterministic (sorted by model id) so two runs over the same ledger are byte-identical.\n\nuse crate::dispatch::TrackRecord;\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\n/// Aggregated telemetry for ONE model.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]\npub struct ModelStats {\n    /// Number of dispatches recorded for this model.\n    pub dispatches: u64,\n    /// Number of successful (backend-returned-ok) dispatches.\n    pub successes: u64,\n    /// Total tokens consumed (sum of `cost`/total_tokens across rows).\n    pub total_tokens: u64,\n    /// Sum of outcome `value` (EV numerator) across rows.\n    pub total_value: f64,\n}\n\nimpl ModelStats {\n    /// Success rate in [0.0, 1.0]. 0.0 when no dispatches (fail-closed).\n    pub fn success_rate(&self) -> f64 {\n        if self.dispatches == 0 {\n            0.0\n        } else {\n            self.successes as f64 / self.dispatches as f64\n        }\n    }\n    /// Mean token cost per dispatch (0.0 when none).\n    pub fn mean_tokens(&self) -> f64 {\n        if self.dispatches == 0 {\n            0.0\n        } else {\n            self.total_tokens as f64 / self.dispatches as f64\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A full telemetry fold over a harvest ledger.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct Telemetry {\n    /// Per-model aggregates, sorted by model id (deterministic).\n    pub by_model: BTreeMap<String, ModelStats>,\n    /// Total dispatches across all models.\n    pub total_dispatches: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Telemetry {\n    /// Fold a single `TrackRecord` into the aggregate (call once per ledger row).\n    pub fn ingest(&mut self, rec: &TrackRecord) {\n        self.total_dispatches += 1;\n        let s = self.by_model.entry(rec.model_id.clone()).or_default();\n        s.dispatches += 1;\n        if rec.success {\n            s.successes += 1;\n        }\n        s.total_tokens += rec.cost.round() as u64;\n        s.total_value += rec.value;\n    }\n\n    /// Read and fold a harvest ledger file (one JSON object per line). Fail-closed:\n    /// a missing/unreadable file yields an empty `Telemetry` rather than an error.\n    pub fn from_ledger(path: &Path) -> Self {\n        let mut t = Telemetry::default();\n        let text = match fs::read_to_string(path) {\n            Ok(t) => t,\n            Err(_) => return t, // missing ledger → empty telemetry\n        };\n        for line in text.lines() {\n            let line = line.trim();\n            if line.is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            // Reuse the same decode the Dispatcher uses for its harvest row.\n            if let Ok(rec) = crate::dispatch::decode_track_record(line) {\n                t.ingest(&rec);\n            }\n        }\n        t\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::dispatch::TrackRecord;\n\n    fn rec(model: &str, success: bool, tokens: u64, value: f64) -> TrackRecord {\n        TrackRecord {\n            backend_id: "ollama".into(),\n            model_id: model.into(),\n            total_tokens: tokens,\n            ms: 100,\n            task: "chat".into(),\n            success,\n            value,\n            cost: tokens as f64,\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Native telemetry must fold the same ledger gov_route reads — fail-closed + deterministic.\n    #[test]\n    fn green_folds_per_model_and_success_rate() {\n        let mut t = Telemetry::default();\n        t.ingest(&rec("qwen2.5-coder:7b", true, 33, 0.0)); // ok\n        t.ingest(&rec("qwen2.5-coder:7b", true, 40, 0.0)); // ok\n        t.ingest(&rec("qwen2.5-coder:7b", false, 0, 0.0)); // fail (no tokens)\n        t.ingest(&rec("llama3.1:8b", true, 50, 1.0)); // different model\n\n        assert_eq!(t.total_dispatches, 4);\n        let q = t.by_model.get("qwen2.5-coder:7b").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(q.dispatches, 3);\n        assert_eq!(q.successes, 2);\n        assert_eq!(q.success_rate(), 2.0 / 3.0);\n        assert_eq!(q.total_tokens, 73);\n        assert_eq!(q.mean_tokens(), 73.0 / 3.0);\n        // BTreeMap ⇒ deterministic ordering: llama3.1 sorts before qwen2.5.\n        let first = t.by_model.keys().next().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(first, "llama3.1:8b");\n        // value aggregates per model only.\n        assert_eq!(t.by_model.get("llama3.1:8b").unwrap().total_value, 1.0);\n    }\n\n    // Fail-closed: missing ledger ⇒ empty telemetry (never panic).\n    #[test]\n    fn green_missing_ledger_is_empty() {\n        let t = Telemetry::from_ledger(Path::new("/nonexistent/track_record.jsonl"));\n        assert_eq!(t.total_dispatches, 0);\n        assert!(t.by_model.is_empty());\n    }\n}\n	3797	-1	-1		ff77bee211fb63f55973fbdb63233a22e1ca14aca854c5cd7dd3a25b8367b03b1c4cb4e95dc7ecb690711343a1f3d26cceddf72731488c9ab0cae2cf673ef3c4589c73294c1bd879524a1902f73ba1e257e0d42a69fa6643dc2003d43e45b787a0f6b756bcca8479ebad4f0c2e1c6cc0a07445b49ac68a6516fde4d4f3a435e0

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/llm-adapters/src/transport.rs	transport · 272 lines	//! transport.rs — one ureq-based OpenAI-compatible transport, shared by every adapter.\n//!\n//! Holds NO vendor knowledge: all Ollama/vLLM deltas come from the `Quirks` the caller passes.\n//! Synchronous (ureq, no tokio). Maps transport failures to typed `LlmError` — never a mock.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{\n    ChatRequest, ChatResponse, EmbedRequest, EmbedResponse, LlmError, Message, ToolCallReq, Usage,\n};\nuse serde_json::{json, Value};\n\nuse crate::quirks::Quirks;\n\n/// A synchronous OpenAI-compatible transport over `ureq`. Cheap to construct (clones the base URL\n/// + quirks); the underlying agent is created per-request (ureq 2 pools connections internally).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct OpenAiCompatTransport {\n    base_url: String,\n    quirks: Quirks,\n}\n\nimpl OpenAiCompatTransport {\n    pub fn new(base_url: impl Into<String>, quirks: Quirks) -> Self {\n        let mut base = base_url.into();\n        // Normalize: no trailing slash (we append paths).\n        while base.ends_with('/') {\n            base.pop();\n        }\n        OpenAiCompatTransport {\n            base_url: base,\n            quirks,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Chat completion → `/v1/chat/completions`.\n    pub fn chat(&self, req: &ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, LlmError> {\n        if req.messages.is_empty() {\n            return Err(LlmError::BadRequest("empty messages".into()));\n        }\n        let messages: Vec<Value> = req\n            .messages\n            .iter()\n            .map(|m| json!({ "role": m.role, "content": m.content }))\n            .collect();\n        let mut body = json!({\n            "model": req.model_id,\n            "messages": messages,\n            "temperature": req.temperature,\n            "top_p": req.top_p,\n            "max_tokens": req.max_tokens,\n            "stream": false,\n        });\n        if let Some(seed) = req.seed {\n            body["seed"] = json!(seed);\n        }\n        // Tool declarations (OpenAI `tools` array). Empty when no tool call is\n        // requested. The adapter owns all JSON framing; the kernel struct carries\n        // plain strings. Declaring tools does NOT force the model to call one — a\n        // tool-less reply still returns `tool_calls: []` (handled in parse_chat).\n        if !req.tools.is_empty() {\n            let tools: Vec<Value> = req\n                .tools\n                .iter()\n                .map(|t| {\n                    json!({\n                        "type": "function",\n                        "function": {\n                            "name": t.name,\n                            "description": t.description,\n                            "parameters": {\n                                "type": "object",\n                                "properties": {\n                                    t.arg_name.to_string(): { "type": "string", "description": t.arg_name }\n                                },\n                                "required": [t.arg_name],\n                            }\n                        }\n                    })\n                })\n                .collect();\n            body["tools"] = Value::Array(tools);\n        }\n        // Ollama-only options (keep_alive/num_ctx/think) surfaced verbatim when the adapter wants.\n        if self.quirks.surface_options && !req.options.is_empty() {\n            let mut opts = serde_json::Map::new();\n            for (k, v) in &req.options {\n                // Values are plain strings per the kernel type; parse bool/int when possible.\n                if let Ok(b) = v.parse::<bool>() {\n                    opts.insert(k.clone(), json!(b));\n                } else if let Ok(i) = v.parse::<i64>() {\n                    opts.insert(k.clone(), json!(i));\n                } else {\n                    opts.insert(k.clone(), json!(v));\n                }\n            }\n            body["options"] = Value::Object(opts);\n        }\n\n        let raw = self.post("/v1/chat/completions", &body)?;\n        parse_chat(&raw, &req.model_id)\n    }\n\n    /// Embedding → the adapter's `embeddings_path` (Ollama `/v1/embeddings`; vLLM same).\n    pub fn embed(&self, req: &EmbedRequest) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n        if req.input.trim().is_empty() {\n            return Err(LlmError::BadRequest("empty embedding input".into()));\n        }\n        let body = json!({ "model": req.model_id, "input": req.input });\n        let raw = self.post(&self.quirks.embeddings_path, &body)?;\n        parse_embed(&raw, &req.model_id)\n    }\n\n    /// Send a POST, returning the parsed JSON body. Translates HTTP/transport failures to `LlmError`.\n    fn post(&self, path: &str, body: &Value) -> Result<Value, LlmError> {\n        let url = format!("{}{}", self.base_url, path);\n        let mut reqb = ureq::post(&url).timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(120));\n        for (k, v) in &self.quirks.extra_headers {\n            reqb = reqb.set(k, v);\n        }\n        let resp = reqb.send_json(body.clone());\n        let resp = match resp {\n            Ok(r) => r,\n            Err(e) => {\n                // ureq error kinds: status (non-2xx), transport (DNS/conn/TLS), etc.\n                if let ureq::Error::Status(code, _r) = &e {\n                    if *code == 404 {\n                        return Err(LlmError::Unsupported);\n                    }\n                    if (500..=599).contains(code) {\n                        return Err(LlmError::Unavailable);\n                    }\n                    return Err(LlmError::BadRequest(format!("HTTP {}", code)));\n                }\n                // Transport-level (connection refused, timeout, TLS) ⇒ backend unavailable.\n                return Err(LlmError::Unavailable);\n            }\n        };\n        resp.into_json().map_err(|_| LlmError::Unavailable)\n    }\n\n    /// Typed health probe: a cheap `/v1/models` GET. `Err(Unavailable)` when unreachable.\n    pub fn health(&self) -> Result<(), LlmError> {\n        let url = format!("{}/v1/models", self.base_url);\n        let mut reqb = ureq::get(&url).timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10));\n        for (k, v) in &self.quirks.extra_headers {\n            reqb = reqb.set(k, v);\n        }\n        match reqb.call() {\n            Ok(_) => Ok(()),\n            Err(_) => Err(LlmError::Unavailable),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Per-model capability probe against Ollama's native `POST /api/show`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the `capabilities` array for `model_id` (e.g. `["tools", "completion"]`\n    /// for tool-capable models). ANY failure — HTTP error, transport error, missing\n    /// field, or a non-array `capabilities` — maps to `Err(LlmError::Unsupported)`,\n    /// which callers interpret as "tool_calling == false" (fail-closed: a probe\n    /// failure is indistinguishable from "no capability").\n    pub fn show_capabilities(&self, model_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, LlmError> {\n        let url = format!("{}/api/show", self.base_url);\n        let body = json!({ "model": model_id });\n        let mut reqb = ureq::post(&url).timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(20));\n        for (k, v) in &self.quirks.extra_headers {\n            reqb = reqb.set(k, v);\n        }\n        let resp = reqb.send_json(body);\n        let raw: serde_json::Value = match resp {\n            Ok(r) => r.into_json().map_err(|_| LlmError::Unsupported)?,\n            Err(_) => return Err(LlmError::Unsupported),\n        };\n        let caps = raw\n            .get("capabilities")\n            .and_then(|c| c.as_array())\n            .ok_or(LlmError::Unsupported)?;\n        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(caps.len());\n        for c in caps {\n            if let Some(s) = c.as_str() {\n                out.push(s.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse an OpenAI chat/completions response into `ChatResponse`. `model_id` is the\n/// provenance tag (L1 opacity) carried from the request onto the response.\nfn parse_chat(raw: &Value, model_id: &str) -> Result<ChatResponse, LlmError> {\n    let content = raw\n        .get("choices")\n        .and_then(|c| c.get(0))\n        .and_then(|c| c.get("message"))\n        .and_then(|m| m.get("content"))\n        .and_then(|c| c.as_str())\n        .unwrap_or("")\n        .to_string();\n    let usage = raw.get("usage").map(parse_usage).unwrap_or_default();\n    // Tool calls (OpenAI `message.tool_calls[].function.{name,arguments}`).\n    // Absent ⇒ empty vec ⇒ the loop treats the reply as a direct answer.\n    let tool_calls = raw\n        .get("choices")\n        .and_then(|c| c.get(0))\n        .and_then(|c| c.get("message"))\n        .and_then(|m| m.get("tool_calls"))\n        .and_then(|t| t.as_array())\n        .map(|arr| {\n            arr.iter()\n                .filter_map(|tc| {\n                    let fn_obj = tc.get("function")?;\n                    let name = fn_obj.get("name")?.as_str()?.to_string();\n                    let arguments_json = fn_obj\n                        .get("arguments")\n                        .and_then(|a| a.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or("{}")\n                        .to_string();\n                    Some(ToolCallReq {\n                        name,\n                        arguments_json,\n                    })\n                })\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        })\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    Ok(ChatResponse {\n        content,\n        usage,\n        model_id: model_id.to_string(),\n        utterance_id: 1,\n        tool_calls,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Parse an OpenAI `/v1/embeddings` response (`data:[{embedding:[…]}]`). `model_id` is the\n/// provenance tag (L1 opacity) carried from the request onto the response.\nfn parse_embed(raw: &Value, model_id: &str) -> Result<EmbedResponse, LlmError> {\n    let arr = raw\n        .get("data")\n        .and_then(|d| d.get(0))\n        .and_then(|d| d.get("embedding"))\n        .and_then(|e| e.as_array())\n        .ok_or_else(|| LlmError::BadRequest("missing data[0].embedding".into()))?;\n    let embedding = arr\n        .iter()\n        .filter_map(|v| v.as_f64().map(|f| f as f32))\n        .collect::<Vec<f32>>();\n    if embedding.is_empty() {\n        return Err(LlmError::BadRequest("empty embedding vector".into()));\n    }\n    Ok(EmbedResponse {\n        embedding,\n        model_id: model_id.to_string(),\n    })\n}\n\nfn parse_usage(v: &Value) -> Usage {\n    Usage {\n        prompt_tokens: v.get("prompt_tokens").and_then(|x| x.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0) as u32,\n        completion_tokens: v\n            .get("completion_tokens")\n            .and_then(|x| x.as_u64())\n            .unwrap_or(0) as u32,\n        total_tokens: v.get("total_tokens").and_then(|x| x.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0) as u32,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Helper for adapters/tests: build a `Message`.\npub fn message(role: &str, content: &str) -> Message {\n    Message {\n        role: role.to_string(),\n        content: content.to_string(),\n    }\n}\n	3810	-1	-1		d2f6ffd450df00671bc3efc984963a2601d69fb4391bb6c3e975ee41d3fa1f67114184614ccd62153444832d38377e28a67bef65f1699ee03463b2271b0e78ce5c9d5729e53bc021d81f221a17ba67bb93ee7c6a659552ce3c8488a44a090163803ef313b4ca88b6dd7b481f025d58bca7b64d2aa7842d341709f6f453a33df1

P40 B-d live end-to-end proof (§3.4). `#[ignore]`d: requires a live Ollama\n//! daemon with `llama3.1:8b` resident. Runs on demand (`cargo test -- --ignored`\n//! from llm-adapters/) for a REAL proof; skips cleanly in offline CI (no fake-green).\n//!\n//! Exercises the full stack: `OllamaAdapter` (real `/api/show` tool_calling probe)\n//! → `ReadOrderStatusTool<FixtureOrders>` → `AgentLoop::run`, and asserts the agent\n//! DID call the tool (event sequence) — the "agent can DO something" falsifiable gate.\n\nuse agent_facade::{FixtureOrders, ReadOrderStatusTool, ToolAction, ToolResource, ToolScope};\nuse agent_loop::{AgentLoop, LoopEventKind, LoopOutcome, MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS};\nuse llm_adapters::OllamaAdapter;\n\n#[test]\n#[ignore] // live-daemon proof; run with `cargo test -- --ignored`\nfn agent_reads_order_status_end_to_end() {\n    // Live adapter (General route → llama3.1:8b). The probe must report true.\n    let backend = OllamaAdapter::new("http://127.0.0.1:11434");\n    let caps = <OllamaAdapter as agent_facade::LlmBackend>::caps(&backend);\n    assert!(\n        caps.tool_calling,\n        "live probe must report tool_calling=true for llama3.1:8b (got {:?})",\n        caps\n    );\n\n    // Fixture source: ord-7 → IN_DELIVERY.\n    let src = FixtureOrders::from_pairs(&[("ord-7", "IN_DELIVERY")]);\n    let tool = ReadOrderStatusTool::new(src);\n    let granted = ToolScope {\n        resource: ToolResource::OrderStatus,\n        action: ToolAction::Read,\n    };\n\n    let loop_ = AgentLoop::new(&backend, &tool, granted);\n    let out = loop_.run("What is the status of order ord-7?");\n\n    match out {\n        LoopOutcome::Answer { log, .. } => {\n            // The agent DID something: it parsed a tool call for read_order_status.\n            let parsed = log.iter().any(|e| {\n                matches!(\n                    e.event,\n                    LoopEventKind::ToolCallParsed { ref tool_name, .. }\n                        if tool_name == "read_order_status"\n                )\n            });\n            assert!(\n                parsed,\n                "agent must have called read_order_status, log={log:?}"\n            );\n            // And it observed a real result.\n            let result = log\n                .iter()\n                .any(|e| matches!(e.event, LoopEventKind::ToolResult { .. }));\n            assert!(result, "agent must have observed a ToolResult, log={log:?}");\n        }\n        LoopOutcome::ToolCallingUnsupported { .. } => {\n            panic!("live probe said tool_calling=false — daemon/model mismatch");\n        }\n        other => panic!("expected Answer, got }\n}\n	3812	-1	-1		8f7bb54a958b123e916590eff942ba2b09dfbff52d90e428d85d4a53deb7b78124c234476fc451af953f06e97056a8b69efa3c0ca1c280ca0dfb7734634457ccd7ff70d93d9bcf41d781a30ab3bbe8fb94423d8e29353748acb0aaa7d033191361f8e8fe374a93cc6a6d44add10c5d378d3b6020040ba5e0113946dd71a1bcb1

serde_json::Value {\n    let tools: Vec<serde_json::Value> = tool_names\n        .iter()\n        .map(|name| {\n            let (description, param_name) = match name.as_str() {\n                "read_order_status" => (\n                    "Read the lifecycle status of a delivery order by its id.",\n                    "order_id",\n                ),\n                "web_fetch" => (\n                    "Fetch a URL and return its readable text content.",\n                    "url",\n                ),\n                _ => ("Unknown tool", "input"),\n            };\n            serde_json::json!({\n                "type": "function",\n                "function": {\n                    "name": name,\n                    "description": description,\n                    "parameters": {\n                        "type": "object",\n                        "properties": {\n                            param_name: {\n                                "type": "string",\n                                "description": param_name\n                            }\n                        },\n                        "required": [param_name]\n                    }\n                }\n            })\n        })\n        .collect();\n    serde_json::json!(tools)\n}\n\n/// Parse the model's response to detect tool calls. Returns `None` if no tool was called,\n/// or `Some((tool_name, args))` if a tool call was detected.\nfn parse_tool_call(response: &str) -> Option<(String, serde_json::Value)> {\n    // Try to find a tool call in the response. Models may emit tool calls in several formats:\n    // 1. OpenAI-style `tool_calls` in the response (handled by the adapter, not visible here)\n    // 2. The model might emit a JSON block with tool call info\n    // 3.
