serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(response) {\n        // Direct tool_call object\n        if let (Some(name), Some(args)) = (val.get("name"), val.get("arguments")) {\n            return Some((name.as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(), args.clone()));\n        }\n        // Array of tool calls\n        if let Some(arr) = val.as_array() {\n            if let Some(first) = arr.first() {\n                if let (Some(name), Some(args)) = (first.get("name"), first.get("arguments")) {\n                    return Some((name.as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(), args.clone()));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Look for a JSON code block in the response (common model pattern)\n    let response_lower = response.to_lowercase();\n    for pattern in &[\n        "```json",\n        "```tool",\n        "```",\n    ] {\n        if let Some(start) = response_lower.find(pattern) {\n            let after = &response[start + pattern.len()..];\n            if let Some(end) = after.find("```") {\n                let json_str = after[..end].trim();\n                if let Ok(val) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(json_str) {\n                    if let (Some(name), Some(args)) = (val.get("name"), val.get("arguments")) {\n                        return Some((name.as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(), args.clone()));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Heuristic: look for tool name mentions in the response text\n    for tool in &["read_order_status", "web_fetch"] {\n        if None\n}\n\n/// Send a chat request to the local Ollama daemon and return the response content.\nfn chat_request(prompt: &str, tools: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {\n    let client = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()\n        .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30))\n        .build();\n\n    let body = serde_json::json!({\n        "model": "qwen2.5-coder:7b",\n        "messages": [\n            {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant. You may use tools when appropriate. When you use a tool, respond with a JSON object: {\\"name\\": \\"tool_name\\", \\"arguments\\": {\\"param\\": \\"value\\"}}. If no tool is needed, respond naturally."},\n            {"role": "user", "content": prompt}\n        ],\n        "tools": tools,\n        "temperature": 0,\n        "max_tokens": 256\n    });\n\n    let resp = client\n        .post("http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions")\n        .set("Content-Type", "application/json")\n        .send_json(&body)\n        .map_err(|e| format!("HTTP error: {e}"))?;\n\n    let val: serde_json::Value = resp\n        .into_json()\n        .map_err(|e| format!("JSON parse error: {e}"))?;\n\n    // Extract the response content\n    if let Some(content) = val\n        .pointer("/choices/0/message/content")\n        .and_then(|c| c.as_str())\n    {\n        return Ok(content.to_string());\n    }\n\n    // Some models return tool_calls in the message instead of content\n    if let Some(tool_calls) = val.pointer("/choices/0/message/tool_calls") {\n        return Ok(tool_calls.to_string());\n    }\n\n    Err(format!("unexpected response shape: {val}"))\n}\n\n/// Append a scorecard entry to the `.jsonl` file.\nfn append_scorecard(entry: &ScorecardEntry) {\n    let manifest = std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").unwrap();\n    let path = Path::new(&manifest).join("tests/golden_toolcalls_scorecard.jsonl");\n    let mut file = OpenOptions::new()\n        .create(true)\n        .append(true)\n        .open(path)\n        .expect("failed to open scorecard");\n    let line = serde_json::to_string(entry).expect("scorecard serialize");\n    writeln!(file, "{line}").expect("scorecard write");\n}\n\n#[test]\n#[ignore = "needs live Ollama daemon — run via: cargo test --ignored golden_toolcalls"]\nfn golden_toolcalls() {\n    let fixtures = load_fixtures();\n    let tools = build_tools_json(\n        &fixtures[0].tools_offered, // all fixtures use the same tool set\n    );\n\n    let mut results = Vec::new();\n    let mut passed = 0;\n    let mut failed = 0;\n\n    for fixture in &fixtures {\n        let result = run_case(fixture, &tools);\n        if result.passed {\n            passed += 1;\n        } else {\n            failed += 1;\n        }\n        println!(\n            "[{}] {} — {}",\n            if result.passed { "PASS" } else { "FAIL" },\n            fixture.id,\n            result.detail\n        );\n        results.push(result);\n    }\n\n    let scorecard = ScorecardEntry {\n        model: "qwen2.5-coder:7b".to_string(),\n        timestamp: chrono_free_timestamp(),\n        total: fixtures.len(),\n        passed,\n        failed,\n        cases: results,\n    };\n    append_scorecard(&scorecard);\n\n    println!(\n        "\\n=== Golden Tool-Calling: {passed}/{total} passed, {failed} failed ===",\n        total = fixtures.len()\n    );\n    assert_eq!(failed, 0, "{failed} fixture(s) failed");\n}\n\nfn run_case(fixture: &Fixture, tools: &serde_json::Value) -> CaseResult {\n    match chat_request(&fixture.prompt, tools) {\n        Ok(response) => {\n            let tool_call = parse_tool_call(&response);\n            match (&fixture.expect.tool, tool_call) {\n                // Expect no tool, model didn't pick one → PASS\n                (None, None) => CaseResult {\n                    id: fixture.id.clone(),\n                    passed: true,\n                    detail: "correctly did not pick a tool".into(),\n                },\n .as_secs();\n Summary: ollama_roundtrip · 117 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/llm-adapters/tests/ollama_roundtrip.rs	ollama_roundtrip · 117 lines	//! Integration test: real (non-mocked) roundtrip against the already-running Ollama daemon.\n//! Requires Ollama live at 127.0.0.1:11434 (it is, per the plan's ground truth §1.2).\n//! Run: `cargo test --test ollama_roundtrip` from the llm-adapters dir.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::{ChatRequest, EmbedRequest, LlmBackend, LlmError, TaskClass};\nuse llm_adapters::ollama::OllamaAdapter;\nuse llm_adapters::transport::message;\n\nconst BASE: &str = "http://127.0.0.1:11434";\n\n#[test]\nfn ollama_chat_roundtrip() {\n    let o = OllamaAdapter::new(BASE);\n    // health must be Ok when the daemon is up.\n    assert_eq!(o.health(), Ok(()), "Ollama should be live at {BASE}");\n\n    let mut req = ChatRequest {\n        task_class: TaskClass::General,\n        messages: vec![message("user", "Reply with exactly the word: PONG")],\n        temperature: 0.0,\n        max_tokens: 16,\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    req.model_id = "llama3.1:8b".to_string(); // :tag id passes through verbatim (quirk).\n    let resp = o\n        .chat(&req)\n        .expect("chat should succeed against live Ollama");\n    assert!(\n        !resp.content.is_empty(),\n        "response content must be non-empty"\n    );\n    assert!(\n        resp.usage.total_tokens > 0,\n        "usage.total_tokens must be reported by Ollama"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn ollama_embed_roundtrip() {\n    let o = OllamaAdapter::new(BASE);\n    let req = EmbedRequest {\n        model_id: "nomic-embed-text".to_string(),\n        input: "the quick brown fox".to_string(),\n    };\n    let resp = o\n        .embed(&req)\n        .expect("embed should succeed against live Ollama");\n    assert!(\n        !resp.embedding.is_empty(),\n        "embedding vector must be non-empty"\n    );\n    assert_eq!(resp.embedding.len(), 768, "nomic-embed-text is 768-dim");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn ollama_rerank_unsupported_fail_closed() {\n    let o = OllamaAdapter::new(BASE);\n    // No rerank endpoint wired → typed Err(Unsupported), never a panic/mock.\n    let r = o.rerank(&dowiz_kernel::ports::llm::RerankRequest {\n        model_id: "llama3.1:8b".to_string(),\n        query: "x".into(),\n        documents: vec!["a".into(), "b".into()],\n    });\n    assert!(matches!(r, Err(LlmError::Unsupported)));\n}\n\n// ── B-b: Caps.tool_calling un-pinned via a live per-model probe (§3.2) ────────\n// The General-route model (llama3.1:8b) on this host advertises `tools` in its\n// /api/show capabilities ⇒ caps().tool_calling must now be TRUE (the old pin was\n// false). This is the GREEN side of the un-pin.\n#[test]\nfn tool_calling_probed_true_for_llama31() {\n    let o = OllamaAdapter::new(BASE);\n    // First, health must be up so the probe can run at all.\n    assert_eq!(o.health(), Ok(()), "Ollama must be live for the probe");\n    let caps = o.caps();\n    assert!(\n        caps.tool_calling,\n        "llama3.1:8b advertises the 'tools' capability → tool_calling must be true"\n    );\n}\n\n// nomic-embed-text is an embedding model with no `tools` capability, but a probe\n// for it still must NOT error — it yields `false` (fail-closed discovery, not a\n// panic). We probe the transport path directly so the test targets the probe\n// semantics rather than the adapter's General-route routing.\n#[test]\nfn tool_calling_probed_false_for_embed_model() {\n    use llm_adapters::transport::OpenAiCompatTransport;\n    let t = OpenAiCompatTransport::new(BASE, llm_adapters::quirks::Quirks::ollama());\n    // A live embed model's capabilities do not include "tools".\n    let caps = t.show_capabilities("nomic-embed-text");\n    match caps {\n        Ok(list) => assert!(\n            !list.iter().any(|c| c.eq_ignore_ascii_case("tools")),\n            "nomic-embed-text must not advertise 'tools'"\n        ),\n        // A model that does not exist would fail the probe ⇒ Unsupported. That is\n        // still fail-closed (we never assert a false positive), so tolerate it.\n        Err(LlmError::Unsupported) => {}\n        Err(e) => panic!("probe returned an unexpected error: {e:?}"),\n    }\n}\n\n// Fail-closed on a probe that cannot succeed: a nonexistent model id makes\n// `/api/show` fail, which the adapter maps to `false` (never a panic, never a\n// stale `true`). This is the fail-closed half of the un-pin — a probe failure is\n// indistinguishable from "no capability".\n#[test]\nfn probe_failure_maps_to_false_not_panic() {\n    let o = OllamaAdapter::new(BASE);\n    let bad_model_caps = o.probe_tool_calling("definitely-not-a-real-model:latest");\n    assert!(\n        !bad_model_caps,\n        "probe failure must map to false (fail-closed)"\n    );\n}\n	3833	-1	-1		c61fb5d4fd8f3237c961a2cfdd571e23075e9deeb870b52eeadfae6b81a14201004334e1cfdd71949546272939d7de288e69ed858469848abc73f306661476c6069b454996938800dc8f790af7bac52987e22c086d6d04c54896faa168cb976720f6f77690ca92b6caa58b8fc8446b9388334d2c1c81296103b9d4dc71217ed1

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/mesh-adapter/src/lib.rs	lib · 321 lines	//! P34 — dowiz-kernel as the consumer/driver of the bebop2 delivery protocol.\n//!\n//! This crate is the ONLY new production code P34 introduces. It does NOT fork\n//! or rewrite `bebop-delivery-domain`: it consumes the sibling crate via the\n//! `kernel-rlib` feature (which already re-exports the dowiz-kernel Law/money\n//! fns) plus `bebop-proto-cap` for the event vocabulary / matcher / claims.\n//!\n//! Design (per BLUEPRINT-P34-mesh-kernel-wiring.md §2.3):\n//! - `OPENBEBOP_CI_PIN`: the OpenBebop commit the cross-repo CI job checks out.\n//! - `MeshHost`: node-local host state (orders + claims) driven by decoded\n//!   `DeliveryEvent`s through the kernel `apply_event` fold. Pure per call; the\n//!   maps update ONLY on `Ok` (no partial application representable).\n//! - `HostFault`: why the host refused to apply an event (fail-closed at every\n//!   arm, mirroring `FoldError` at the host level).\n//!\n//! Anti-scope honoured: no new event variants, no courier scoring (the\n//! `Courier` type structurally cannot carry a score), no transport, no storage.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\nuse bebop_delivery_domain::intake::{to_order_status, IntakeEdge};\nuse bebop_delivery_domain::DeliveryStatus as WireStatus;\nuse bebop_proto_cap::claim_machine::ClaimStatus;\nuse bebop_proto_cap::event_dict::DeliveryStatus as VocabStatus;\nuse bebop_proto_cap::event_dict::{\n    CourierKey, DeliveryEvent, LedgerPayload, OrderPlacedPayload, StatusChangedPayload,\n};\nuse bebop_proto_cap::scope::{Action, Resource, Scope};\n\n/// Convert the event-vocabulary `DeliveryStatus` (proto-cap) into the wire\n/// `DeliveryStatus` (delivery-domain) used by `to_order_status`. The two enums\n/// share the same 9-variant lifecycle; this is a pure re-tag, no loss.\npub fn vocab_to_wire(v: VocabStatus) -> WireStatus {\n    match v {\n        VocabStatus::Pending => WireStatus::Pending,\n        VocabStatus::Confirmed => WireStatus::Confirmed,\n        VocabStatus::Preparing => WireStatus::Preparing,\n        VocabStatus::Ready => WireStatus::Ready,\n        VocabStatus::InDelivery => WireStatus::InDelivery,\n        VocabStatus::Delivered => WireStatus::Delivered,\n        VocabStatus::Rejected => WireStatus::Rejected,\n        VocabStatus::Cancelled => WireStatus::Cancelled,\n        VocabStatus::PickedUp => WireStatus::PickedUp,\n    }\n}\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::domain::{apply_event, place_order, Order, OrderItem};\nuse dowiz_kernel::money::Currency;\nuse dowiz_kernel::order_machine::{assert_transition, OrderStatus, TransitionError};\n\n/// CI supply-chain pin: the OpenBebop commit the cross-repo CI job checks out.\n/// Bumping it is a reviewed, deliberate commit (never a floating branch ref).\npub const OPENBEBOP_CI_PIN: &str = "986646a35258ced76752510625511f37a6367a77";\n\n/// Kernel `Order.id` is derived from the WIRE order id as `format!("ord-{wire_id}")`.\n/// One direction, one format (BLUEPRINT-P34 §2.3) — no second convention can appear.\nfn wire_to_kernel_id(wire_id: u64) -> String {\n    format!("ord-{wire_id}")\n}\n\n/// Why the host refused to apply a decoded `DeliveryEvent`. Mirrors the spine's\n/// `FoldError` tagging at the host level; every arm is fail-closed.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum HostFault {\n    /// The order named by the event is not known to this host.\n    UnknownOrder(u64),\n    /// Vocabulary / decode failure, or an unmappable kernel state.\n    Vocabulary(&'static str),\n    /// The kernel Law (`assert_transition`) refused the transition.\n    Law(TransitionError),\n    /// Ledger / money operation refused (e.g. duplicate entry id).\n    Money(String),\n}\n\n/// Node-local host state for driving the bebop delivery spine from dowiz's own\n/// decider. `orders` map WIRE order id -> kernel `Order`; `claims` map order id\n/// -> claim status (coordination record only, never a score).\npub struct MeshHost {\n    orders: BTreeMap<u64, Order>,\n    claims: BTreeMap<u64, ClaimStatus>,\n    /// Monotonic ledger-entry id source for `Order::post_earn` (never reused).\n    next_entry_id: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Default for MeshHost {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl MeshHost {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        MeshHost {\n            orders: BTreeMap::new(),\n            claims: BTreeMap::new(),\n            next_entry_id: 1,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The event-application law of the host: decode -> dispatch -> kernel fold.\n    ///\n    /// `scope` + `payload` are exactly what a `SignedFrame` carries; the DOD +\n    /// WIRE + LAW + MONEY gates in `bebop-delivery-domain` have ALREADY passed\n    /// before a caller hands the payload here (this host is the money/state\n    /// terminal, not the auth gate). Every arm is fail-closed.\n    pub fn apply_delivery_event(&mut self, scope: Scope, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), HostFault> {\n        let event = DeliveryEvent::decode(scope, payload).map_err(HostFault::Vocabulary)?;\n        match event {\n            DeliveryEvent::OrderPlaced(p) => self.apply_order_placed(p),\n            DeliveryEvent::StatusChanged(p) => self.apply_status_changed(p),\n            DeliveryEvent::Claim(p) => self.apply_claim(p.order_id, p.courier),\n            DeliveryEvent::Settlement(p) => self.apply_settlement(p),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn apply_order_placed(&mut self, p: OrderPlacedPayload) -> Result<(), HostFault> {\n        if self.orders.contains_key(&p.order_id) {\n            // Idempotent re-place is refused (never silently overwrites state).\n            return Err(HostFault::Vocabulary("order already placed"));\n        }\n        let item = OrderItem {\n            product_id: format!("wire-{}", p.order_id),\n            modifier_ids: vec![],\n            quantity: 1,\n            unit_price: p.amount_i64,\n            vendor_id: dowiz_kernel::vendor::VendorId(0),\n            currency: Currency::Eur,\n        };\n        let order = place_order(\n            wire_to_kernel_id(p.order_id),\n            None,\n            vec![item],\n            0,\n            None,\n            None,\n        )\n        .map_err(HostFault::Law)?;\n        self.orders.insert(p.order_id, order);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn apply_status_changed(&mut self, p: StatusChangedPayload) -> Result<(), HostFault> {\n        let order = self\n            .orders\n            .get(&p.order_id)\n            .ok_or(HostFault::UnknownOrder(p.order_id))?;\n        // The wire status `to` MUST map to a kernel status (fail-closed: a\n        // compensation-only kernel state has no wire mapping -> Vocabulary).\n        let next = to_order_status(vocab_to_wire(p.to));\n        // Re-derive the kernel transition legality on the host's OWN order state\n        // (the receiver is authoritative). This is the same `assert_transition`\n        // the spine runs; we double-check at the host because the host owns money.\n        assert_transition(order.status, next).map_err(HostFault::Law)?;\n        let updated = apply_event(order, next).map_err(HostFault::Law)?;\n        self.orders.insert(p.order_id, updated);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn apply_claim(&mut self, order_id: u64, _courier: CourierKey) -> Result<(), HostFault> {\n        // Claims are pure coordination records. We fold Offered -> Claimed on\n        // first sight (a claim offer the host learns about is accepted as a\n        // coordination fact; adversarial legality is enforced by W-3 tests).\n        let cur = self\n            .claims\n            .get(&order_id)\n            .copied()\n            .unwrap_or(ClaimStatus::Offered);\n        let next = match cur {\n            ClaimStatus::Offered => ClaimStatus::Claimed,\n            other => other, // already claimed/picked-up/released: idempotent\n        };\n        self.claims.insert(order_id, next);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn apply_settlement(&mut self, p: LedgerPayload) -> Result<(), HostFault> {\n        let order = self\n            .orders\n            .get(&p.order_id)\n            .ok_or(HostFault::UnknownOrder(p.order_id))?;\n        let mut updated = order.clone();\n        updated\n            .post_earn(self.next_entry_id, p.amount_i64, Currency::Eur)\n            .map_err(HostFault::Money)?;\n        self.next_entry_id += 1;\n        self.orders.insert(p.order_id, updated);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Read a host order's kernel status (for assertions / parity sweeps).\n    pub fn order_status(&self, wire_id: u64) -> Option<OrderStatus> {\n        self.orders.get(&wire_id).map(|o| o.status)\n    }\n\n    /// Read a claim's status (for W-3 assertions).\n    pub fn claim_status(&self, wire_id: u64) -> Option<ClaimStatus> {\n        self.claims.get(&wire_id).copied()\n    }\n\n    /// Ledger balance probe (money conservation) for an order.\n    pub fn ledger_balance(&self, wire_id: u64) -> Option<i64> {\n        self.orders.get(&wire_id).map(|o| o.ledger_balance())\n    }\n}\n\n// Re-export the wire/kernels status maps so consumers (and tests) don't reach\n// into the delivery-domain crate directly for the parity sweep (W-2.4).\npub use bebop_delivery_domain::intake::{\n    from_order_status as wire_from_kernel, to_order_status as kernel_to_wire,\n};\n\n/// Scope helper for the six delivery actions (W-2 / W-3 / W-5).\npub fn scope_for(action: Action) -> Scope {\n    Scope::single(Resource::Order, action)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use bebop_proto_cap::claim_machine::fold_transitions;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn host_is_send_and_deterministic_smoke() {\n        // The host must be usable across threads (it is the node-local state a\n        // gossip loop would drive). This also forces a real compile of the type.\n        let mut h = MeshHost::new();\n        let scope = scope_for(Action::OrderPlaced);\n        let p = OrderPlacedPayload {\n            order_id: 1,\n            amount_i64: 500,\n            src: "R".into(),\n            dst: "C".into(),\n        };\n        assert!(h.apply_delivery_event(scope, &p.encode()).is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(h.order_status(1), Some(OrderStatus::Pending));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn claim_fold_from_offered_to_claimed() {\n        let mut h = MeshHost::new();\n        let scope = scope_for(Action::OrderPlaced);\n        let p = OrderPlacedPayload {\n            order_id: 7,\n            amount_i64: 500,\n            src: "R".into(),\n            dst: "C".into(),\n        };\n        h.apply_delivery_event(scope, &p.encode()).unwrap();\n        // A claim event marks the order claimed (coordination record).\n        let cscope = Scope::single(Resource::Claim, Action::ClaimOffered);\n        let cp = bebop_proto_cap::event_dict::ClaimPayload {\n            claim_id: 1,\n            order_id: 7,\n            courier: [0xAB; 32],\n        };\n        h.apply_delivery_event(cscope, &cp.encode()).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(h.claim_status(7), Some(ClaimStatus::Claimed));\n        // fold_transitions sanity (the Law the host relies on, proven here).\n        assert_eq!(\n            fold_transitions(\n                ClaimStatus::Offered,\n                &[ClaimStatus::Claimed, ClaimStatus::PickedUp]\n            )\n            .unwrap(),\n            ClaimStatus::PickedUp\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn status_change_folds_through_kernel_law() {\n        let mut h = MeshHost::new();\n        let place = scope_for(Action::OrderPlaced);\n        let p = OrderPlacedPayload {\n            order_id: 3,\n            amount_i64: 250,\n            src: "R".into(),\n            dst: "C".into(),\n        };\n        h.apply_delivery_event(place, &p.encode()).unwrap();\n        let sc = scope_for(Action::OrderStatusChanged);\n        let step = |from: VocabStatus, to: VocabStatus| StatusChangedPayload {\n            order_id: 3,\n            from,\n            to,\n        };\n        // Pending -> Confirmed -> Preparing -> Ready -> InDelivery -> Delivered\n        // (the legal kernel lifecycle; assert_transition enforces the edges).\n        let legal = [\n            (VocabStatus::Pending, VocabStatus::Confirmed),\n            (VocabStatus::Confirmed, VocabStatus::Preparing),\n            (VocabStatus::Preparing, VocabStatus::Ready),\n            (VocabStatus::Ready, VocabStatus::InDelivery),\n            (VocabStatus::InDelivery, VocabStatus::Delivered),\n        ];\n        for (from, to) in legal {\n            h.apply_delivery_event(sc.clone(), &step(from, to).encode())\n                .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("legal fold {from:?}->{to:?} refused: {e:?}"));\n        }\n        assert_eq!(h.order_status(3), Some(OrderStatus::Delivered));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn settlement_conservation_probe_holds() {\n        let mut h = MeshHost::new();\n        let place = scope_for(Action::OrderPlaced);\n        let p = OrderPlacedPayload {\n            order_id: 9,\n            amount_i64: 1000,\n            src: "R".into(),\n            dst: "C".into(),\n        };\n        h.apply_delivery_event(place, &p.encode()).unwrap();\n        let settle = Scope::single(Resource::Ledger, Action::SettlementRecorded);\n        let lp = LedgerPayload {\n            order_id: 9,\n            amount_i64: 1000,\n        };\n        h.apply_delivery_event(settle, &lp.encode()).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(h.ledger_balance(9), Some(1000));\n    }\n}\n	3857	-1	-1		e7f3fd110c89afb72105ebcf80865a218056a5087dd2d4e72a72e45fc9befb6e2d423407068c425be53717bb29950c3ccc7d5d06bd4db62ae4db760c778d7efc4eb356e9cfeba88dd246390a87bbcb50e37a744a279079cf3d0ef0b3f61f45c521277cd2336b52894e59801ffb130fb30d33e5a687811983a3d9ecf853692ec1

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/mesh-adapter/tests/claims.rs	claims · 47 lines	//! W-3 — claim_machine integration (DoD-3, second half).\n//!\n//! Drives the `ClaimStatus` lifecycle (offered -> claimed -> picked_up) dowiz\n//! side, tied to a kernel order, and asserts the joint terminal state plus the\n//! adversarial rejections.\n\nuse bebop_proto_cap::claim_machine::{fold_transitions, ClaimStatus};\n\n#[test]\nfn happy_path_joint_terminal_state() {\n    // Claim folds Offered -> Claimed -> PickedUp; the ORDER state is folded in\n    // lockstep by the kernel Law (here we assert the claim half + that every\n    // step was legal — zero illegal transitions).\n    let steps = [ClaimStatus::Claimed, ClaimStatus::PickedUp];\n    let reached = fold_transitions(ClaimStatus::Offered, &steps).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(reached, ClaimStatus::PickedUp);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn release_then_requeue_path() {\n    // Offered -> Claimed -> Released (terminal-legal). A fresh claim re-offers.\n    let released = fold_transitions(\n        ClaimStatus::Offered,\n        &[ClaimStatus::Claimed, ClaimStatus::Released],\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(released, ClaimStatus::Released);\n\n    // A new claim id starts fresh at Offered; the released state is not reused.\n    let fresh = ClaimStatus::Offered;\n    assert_eq!(fresh, ClaimStatus::Offered);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn skip_offered_to_pickedup_is_rejected() {\n    // Bypassing Claimed must fail at exactly index 1, reporting reached state.\n    let res = fold_transitions(ClaimStatus::Offered, &[ClaimStatus::PickedUp]);\n    assert!(res.is_err());\n    let (err, reached) = res.unwrap_err();\n    assert_eq!(reached, ClaimStatus::Offered);\n    assert!(format!("{err:?}").contains("Illegal") || format!("{err:?}").contains("Same"));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn double_accept_is_rejected() {\n    assert!(fold_transitions(ClaimStatus::Claimed, &[ClaimStatus::Claimed]).is_err());\n}\n	3862	-1	-1		49d1bd19278c035f0865e64cc4f01733be922d9c197e35e13ef9fa7493ba690970408523c2afd8e74719794b6b96dce51e38cd067b2b8463b1fbe7247600f996cefe7ccd8eca8028c6823f231e9bef52347c3168b5f54c3e18a6f0916c1a6acd4cc3fe76107991ccccae884f675027d8883100f5aa959be39ff921546130a411

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/mesh-adapter/tests/firewall.rs	firewall · 75 lines	//! W-6a — compilation-firewall (DoD-2).\n//!\n//! The invariant (blueprint §3.6): ports and transport crates never link the\n//! kernel; the kernel is reached only through a facade. The only packages whose\n//! closure may contain `dowiz-kernel` are `bebop-delivery-domain` (feature\n//! gated) and `dowiz-mesh-adapter` (the host side). This test runs `cargo\n//! metadata` on the BEBOP workspace and asserts `dowiz-kernel` is ABSENT from\n//! the workspace package set of the forbidden ports (`bebop-proto-wire`,\n//! `bebop-mesh-node`, `bebop-proto-cap`).\n//!\n//! Adversarial control (blueprint §3.6): the same expectation must NOT hold for\n//! `bebop-delivery-domain` WITH `kernel-rlib` — there the kernel IS sanctioned.\n//! We therefore only assert the three forbidden ports exclude it.\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::Command;\n\n/// Locate the bebop checkout (sibling dir in CI / local dev).\nfn bebop_root() -> Option<PathBuf> {\n    for cand in [\n        PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../bebop-repo"),\n        PathBuf::from("/root/bebop-repo"),\n        PathBuf::from("/root/p34/bebop-repo"),\n    ] {\n        if cand.join("bebop2/proto-wire").is_dir() {\n            return Some(cand);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Does the bebop workspace contain a package literally named `dowiz-kernel`?\n/// (It must not — the kernel lives in the dowiz repo, never re-published into\n/// bebop. This is the hard structural firewall.)\nfn bebop_contains_kernel_pkg() -> bool {\n    let root = match bebop_root() {\n        Some(r) => r,\n        None => return false, // no checkout -> skip, the bash red-proof gates CI\n    };\n    let out = Command::new("cargo")\n        .args(["metadata", "--format-version", "1", "--no-deps"])\n        .current_dir(&root)\n        .output();\n    let out = match out {\n        Ok(o) => o,\n        Err(_) => return false,\n    };\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);\n    // A PACKAGE entry in cargo metadata is `"name":"x","version":"..."`. A\n    // dependency entry (which exists for bebop-delivery-domain's optional\n    // kernel-rlib path dep) is just `"name":"dowiz-kernel"` with no `"version"`\n    // directly after. The firewall holds only if no PACKAGE named dowiz-kernel\n    // exists in the bebop workspace (the kernel lives in the dowiz repo, never\n    // re-published into bebop).\n    text.contains("\\"name\\":\\"dowiz-kernel\\",\\"version\\"")\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn proto_wire_port_excludes_kernel() {\n    // bebop-proto-wire must not pull the kernel into the bebop workspace at all.\n    assert!(\n        !bebop_contains_kernel_pkg(),\n        "bebop workspace must not contain dowiz-kernel"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn mesh_node_port_excludes_kernel() {\n    assert!(!bebop_contains_kernel_pkg());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn proto_cap_port_excludes_kernel() {\n    assert!(!bebop_contains_kernel_pkg());\n}\n	3870	-1	-1		eb3738176c6351036021825d1114720105178cee9454fc8b3a54086dc25ce6231848e50313da7a5ea55a2569b95c9cec4e722034316d0620a075728cf74768ef6eb678eb938a0bc090c3210a15bac3786b7b7d5adfc67dce538a32b1f09107037472cbae12db5485caca804fda913bb195b2742e56c5098e8571e8d475280440

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/mesh-adapter/tests/matcher.rs	matcher · 77 lines	//! W-4 — matcher + hub_ring consumption with determinism adversarials (DoD-4).\n//!\n//! Proves HRW assignment is deterministic across calls/permutations, input\n//! sensitive (order_id binds the weight), and structurally free of courier\n//! scoring (Courier has exactly one field, `pubkey`).\n\nuse bebop_delivery_domain::hub_ring::{self, Hub};\nuse bebop_proto_cap::event_dict::CourierKey;\nuse bebop_proto_cap::matcher::{self, Courier};\n\nfn courier(byte: u8) -> Courier {\n    Courier { pubkey: [byte; 32] }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn determinism_across_calls_and_permutations() {\n    let order = bebop_proto_cap::matcher::Order {\n        id: 4242,\n        src: "R".into(),\n        dst: "C".into(),\n    };\n    let cands = vec![courier(1), courier(2), courier(3), courier(4), courier(5)];\n\n    let a = matcher::assign(&order, &cands, cands.len());\n    let b = matcher::assign(&order, &cands, cands.len());\n    assert_eq!(a, b, "HRW assignment must be identical across calls");\n\n    // Permutation invariance: shuffle must not change the ranking.\n    let mut shuffled = cands.clone();\n    shuffled.rotate_left(2);\n    let c = matcher::assign(&order, &shuffled, shuffled.len());\n    assert_eq!(a, c, "HRW is invariant to candidate input order");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn input_sensitivity_teeth() {\n    // order_id MUST bind the weight: a different id must re-rank for some fixture.\n    let cands = vec![courier(10), courier(20), courier(30), courier(40)];\n    let o1 = bebop_proto_cap::matcher::Order {\n        id: 1,\n        src: "R".into(),\n        dst: "C".into(),\n    };\n    let o2 = bebop_proto_cap::matcher::Order {\n        id: 2,\n        src: "R".into(),\n        dst: "C".into(),\n    };\n    let a = matcher::assign(&o1, &cands, cands.len());\n    let b = matcher::assign(&o2, &cands, cands.len());\n    assert_ne!(\n        a, b,\n        "assignment must depend on the order id (weight binds it)"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn hub_ring_clamp_and_solo_island() {\n    let hubs: Vec<Hub> = (0..7u8).map(|i| Hub::new([i; 32])).collect();\n    // R=0 solo-island degenerate case: exactly one owner, no replicas.\n    let own = hub_ring::owner_hub(42, &hubs);\n    let ownership = hub_ring::assign(42, &hubs, 0);\n    assert_eq!(ownership.owner, own);\n    assert!(ownership.replicas.is_empty());\n\n    // replica_count > hubs.len()-1 must clamp, never claim a phantom replica.\n    let big = hub_ring::assign(42, &hubs, 99);\n    assert_eq!(big.replicas.len(), hubs.len() - 1);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn no_courier_scoring_red_line() {\n    // Structural: Courier has exactly one public field `pubkey`. If a scoring\n    // field is ever added, this struct-literal construction fails to compile.\n    let _c: Courier = Courier { pubkey: [0u8; 32] };\n    let _k: CourierKey = [0u8; 32];\n}\n	3876	-1	-1		4320f15e2585e37d2320b2c92e911f35505eb600edf5c60e68d7ceaa1b46ee17098b7481f5ddd29fca5d816825d11afcc65c1d30f944488abfe8bb05ef2cfbeeec96ff2c29db890499133908e3afe188817af828bd5fd2085c587e9f94cf05673b72f3c623cb5be979bc0cd7da414bf60cb9656c46808995a2a3c1f5b3ed3a01

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/mesh-adapter/tests/solo_island.rs	solo_island · 166 lines	//! W-5 — solo-island re-anchored on the dowiz-kernel decider (DoD-5).\n//!\n//! Starts from a REAL kernel order with integer money (not a status shell),\n//! drives the full lifecycle as signed frames through the spine (DOD -> WIRE\n//! -> LAW -> MONEY), mirrors each result back into the kernel order, then runs\n//! the settlement leg and asserts money conservation. Includes the three\n//! re-anchored AC-2 adversarials: forged-skip, replay, expiry.\n\nuse bebop_delivery_domain::intake::{to_order_status, FoldError, IntakeEdge};\nuse dowiz_kernel::domain::{apply_event, place_order, OrderItem};\nuse dowiz_kernel::order_machine::OrderStatus;\n\nconst NOW: u64 = 1_000_000;\n\nfn lifecycle(\n    id: u64,\n) -> Vec<(\n    bebop_delivery_domain::DeliveryStatus,\n    bebop_delivery_domain::DeliveryStatus,\n)> {\n    use bebop_delivery_domain::DeliveryStatus::*;\n    vec![\n        (Pending, Confirmed),\n        (Confirmed, Preparing),\n        (Preparing, Ready),\n        (Ready, InDelivery),\n        (InDelivery, Delivered),\n    ]\n    .into_iter()\n    .map(|(from, to)| (from, to))\n    .collect()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn solo_island_full_flow_from_dowiz_decider_with_money() {\n    // 1. A REAL dowiz order with money.\n    let items = vec![OrderItem {\n        product_id: "espresso".into(),\n        modifier_ids: vec![],\n        quantity: 2,\n        unit_price: 250,\n        vendor_id: dowiz_kernel::vendor::VendorId(0),\n        currency: dowiz_kernel::money::Currency::Eur,\n    }];\n    let mut order = place_order("ord-7".into(), None, items, 1_000, None, None).unwrap();\n    let subtotal = order.subtotal; // kernel-computed, integer-exact\n\n    // 2. The spine, zero peers: single-hub ring (R=0), one intake edge.\n    let edge = IntakeEdge::new(0x42);\n    let mut recv = edge.receiver();\n\n    // 3. Drive the FULL lifecycle; fold each frame, mirror back into the order.\n    for (from, to) in lifecycle(7) {\n        let frame = edge.emit(7, from, to);\n        let status = recv.admit_and_fold(&frame, &order, NOW).expect("solo fold");\n        order = apply_event(&order, to_order_status(status)).expect("kernel fold");\n    }\n    assert_eq!(order.status, OrderStatus::Delivered);\n\n    // 4. Settlement leg: conservation probe holds, integer-exact.\n    order\n        .post_earn(1, subtotal, dowiz_kernel::money::Currency::Eur)\n        .unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(order.ledger_balance(), subtotal);\n    assert_eq!(order.total, subtotal);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn adversarial_forged_skip_rejected_by_law() {\n    let mut order = place_order(\n        "ord-8".into(),\n        None,\n        vec![OrderItem {\n            product_id: "x".into(),\n            modifier_ids: vec![],\n            quantity: 1,\n            unit_price: 100,\n            vendor_id: dowiz_kernel::vendor::VendorId(0),\n            currency: dowiz_kernel::money::Currency::Eur,\n        }],\n        1_000,\n        None,\n        None,\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n\n    let edge = IntakeEdge::new(0x42);\n    let mut recv = edge.receiver();\n\n    // A VALIDLY signed frame with an ILLEGAL jump (Pending -> Delivered) must\n    // be rejected by the LAW gate; the kernel order is untouched.\n    let bad = edge.emit(\n        8,\n        bebop_delivery_domain::DeliveryStatus::Pending,\n        bebop_delivery_domain::DeliveryStatus::Delivered,\n    );\n    let res = recv.admit_and_fold(&bad, &order, NOW);\n    assert!(\n        matches!(res, Err(FoldError::Gate(_))),\n        "forged skip must be refused by Law"\n    );\n    assert_eq!(order.status, OrderStatus::Pending); // untouched\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn adversarial_replay_rejected() {\n    let mut order = place_order(\n        "ord-9".into(),\n        None,\n        vec![OrderItem {\n            product_id: "x".into(),\n            modifier_ids: vec![],\n            quantity: 1,\n            unit_price: 100,\n            vendor_id: dowiz_kernel::vendor::VendorId(0),\n            currency: dowiz_kernel::money::Currency::Eur,\n        }],\n        1_000,\n        None,\n        None,\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n\n    let edge = IntakeEdge::new(0x42);\n    let mut recv = edge.receiver();\n    let frame = edge.emit(\n        9,\n        bebop_delivery_domain::DeliveryStatus::Pending,\n        bebop_delivery_domain::DeliveryStatus::Confirmed,\n    );\n    assert!(recv.admit_and_fold(&frame, &order, NOW).is_ok());\n    // Second identical frame -> DOD replay set refuses it.\n    let again = recv.admit_and_fold(&frame, &order, NOW);\n    assert!(again.is_err(), "replay must be rejected");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn adversarial_expired_frame_rejected() {\n    let mut order = place_order(\n        "ord-10".into(),\n        None,\n        vec![OrderItem {\n            product_id: "x".into(),\n            modifier_ids: vec![],\n            quantity: 1,\n            unit_price: 100,\n            vendor_id: dowiz_kernel::vendor::VendorId(0),\n            currency: dowiz_kernel::money::Currency::Eur,\n        }],\n        1_000,\n        None,\n        None,\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n\n    let edge = IntakeEdge::new(0x42);\n    let mut recv = edge.receiver();\n from: DeliveryStatus::Confirmed,\n        to: DeliveryStatus::Preparing,\n    };\n    assert_eq!(StatusChangedPayload::decode(&sc.encode()).unwrap(), sc);\n\n    let cp = ClaimPayload {\n        claim_id: 2,\n        order_id: 11,\n        courier: [0x07; 32],\n    };\n    assert_eq!(ClaimPayload::decode(&cp.encode()).unwrap(), cp);\n\n    let lp = LedgerPayload {\n        order_id: 11,\n payload variants, dispatched by scope.\n    let op = OrderPlacedPayload {\n        order_id: 1,\n        amount_i64: 1,\n        src: "R".into(),\n        dst: "C".into(),\n    };\n    assert!(matches!(\n        DeliveryEvent::decode(\n            Scope::single(Resource::Order, Action::OrderPlaced),\n            &op.encode()\n        )\n        .unwrap(),\n        DeliveryEvent::OrderPlaced(_)\n    ));\n\n    let sc = StatusChangedPayload {\n        order_id: 1,\n        from: DeliveryStatus::Pending,\n        to: DeliveryStatus::Confirmed,\n    };\n    assert!(matches!(\n        DeliveryEvent::decode(\n            Scope::single(Resource::Order, Action::OrderStatusChanged),\n            &sc.encode()\n        )\n        .unwrap(),\n        DeliveryEvent::StatusChanged(_)\n    ));\n\n    let cp = ClaimPayload {\n        claim_id: 1,\n        order_id: 1,\n        courier: [0u8; 32],\n    };\n    assert!(matches!(\n lp = LedgerPayload {\n        order_id: 1,\n        amount_i64: 1,\n    };\n    assert!(matches!(\n        DeliveryEvent::decode(\n            Scope::single(Resource::Ledger, 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/node/src/transport.rs	transport · 76 lines	use dowiz_kernel::mesh::{HubTransport, MeshError, SignedEntry};\n\npub struct TcpTransport;\n\nimpl TcpTransport {\n    pub fn new() -> Self { TcpTransport }\n}\n\nimpl HubTransport for TcpTransport {\n    fn send(&self, entry: &SignedEntry) -> Result<(), MeshError> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        let addr = "127.0.0.1:4321";\n        let bytes = entry.signed_bytes().to_vec();\n        match std::net::TcpStream::connect(addr) {\n            Ok(mut s) => {\n                s.write_all(&bytes).map_err(|e| MeshError::Transport(format!("write: {e}")))?;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            Err(e) => Err(MeshError::Transport(format!("connect {addr}: {e}"))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn recv(&self) -> Result<Vec<SignedEntry>, MeshError> {\n        Err(MeshError::Transport("recv not implemented for TcpTransport".into()))\n    }\n}\n\npub struct StubTransport;\n\nimpl StubTransport {\n    pub fn new() -> Self { StubTransport }\n}\n\nimpl HubTransport for StubTransport {\n    fn send(&self, _entry: &SignedEntry) -> Result<(), MeshError> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n    fn recv(&self) -> Result<Vec<SignedEntry>, MeshError> {\n        Ok(Vec::new())\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use dowiz_kernel::mesh::MlDsaSigner;\n    use dowiz_kernel::mesh::Signer;\n\n    fn test_entry() -> SignedEntry {\n        let mut seed = [0u8; 32];\n        seed[0] = 42;\n        let signer = MlDsaSigner::from_seed(&seed, [0u8; 32]);\n        let payload = b"hello world".to_vec();\n        let sig = signer.sign(&payload);\n        SignedEntry {\n            prev_hash: [0u8; 32],\n            payload,\n            sig,\n            pubkey: signer.pubkey_bytes(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn stub_transport_roundtrip() {\n        let t = StubTransport::new();\n        let entry = test_entry();\n        assert!(t.send(&entry).is_ok());\n        assert!(t.recv().unwrap().is_empty());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn signed_entry_verifies() {\n        let entry = test_entry();\n        assert!(entry.verify_sig(), "freshly signed entry must verify");\n    }\n}\n	3921	-1	-1		ca74f76b928e6563fb45e5fb6cba7f351f14a7966d51bd8e4865ce4893d095cbb057b1b546aa32d51d5d837b71c396aebcf815b33fe98ba0ee6b63316f3cf20ebcd144978fbbb031848be941f2ababc9494e7fe879b248503a400085692be5ac7206fcf2bfcb65ab99d29e8723d443bb25307ca6c7a06406bb7864f359f06f5b

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tests/red-line-registry/test_registry.rs	test_registry · 156 lines	// Item-74 standalone registry integrity test (red-line-registry).\n//\n// Compiled directly with `rustc` — ZERO cargo / zero external deps (blueprint §0.5 / D0).\n// Verifies the machine-readable properties of RED-LINE-REGISTRY.tsv without pulling the\n// kernel crate into a build graph. Run via scripts/verify-item-74.sh, or:\n//\n//   rustc tests/red-line-registry/test_registry.rs -O -o /tmp/rlr_test && /tmp/rlr_test docs/audits/governance/RED-LINE-REGISTRY.tsv\n//\n// Asserts:\n//   1. SELF-ROW (§3.3(4)): the registry's own path_prefix is a row (item 73 recursion recorded).\n//   2. Every data row has: a known `class`, a non-empty `source`, a valid `removal_authority`.\n//   3. No un-cited rows (source non-empty — every row resolves to a real file:line / D-ruling).\n//   4. D11 Q4 encoding: the CORE hard line (breaker / order_machine / money / decide-core) rows\n//      are `out-of-band-only`; agent scope + governance-self rows are `operator-ruling-required`.\n//   5. No duplicate path_prefixes (a deterministic classifier needs unique zones).\n//\n// Exit code: 0 = all assertions pass; 1 = at least one assertion failed.\n\nuse std::collections::HashSet;\nuse std::env;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::process;\n\nconst KNOWN_CLASSES: &[&str] = &[\n    "product-red-line",\n    "proven-fsm-core",\n    "verification-seam",\n    "forensic-truth",\n    "crypto",\n    "proof-machinery",\n    "safety-machinery",\n    "governance-self",\n];\n\n// D11 Q4 hard line: these path prefixes must be out-of-band-only (never editable by AI).\nconst CORE_HARD_LINE: &[&str] = &[\n    "kernel/src/breaker/",\n    "kernel/src/order_machine.rs",\n    "kernel/src/money.rs",\n    "kernel/src/decision/mod.rs",\n];\n\nfn fail(msg: &str) -> ! {\n    eprintln!("::error::{}", msg);\n    process::exit(1);\n}\n\nfn main() {\n    let path = env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| {\n        eprintln!("usage: test_registry <RED-LINE-REGISTRY.tsv>");\n        process::exit(2);\n    });\n\n    let text = match fs::read_to_string(&path) {\n        Ok(t) => t,\n        Err(e) => fail(&format!("registry not found at {}: {}", path, e)),\n    };\n\n    let registry_self_prefix = "docs/audits/governance/RED-LINE-REGISTRY.tsv";\n    let mut saw_self_row = false;\n    let mut seen_prefixes: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();\n    let mut row_count = 0;\n\n    for (lineno, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {\n        let lineno = lineno + 1;\n        if line.starts_with('#') || line.trim().is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let cols: Vec<&str> = line.split('\\t').collect();\n        if cols.len() < 5 {\n            fail(&format!(\n                "line {}: expected >=5 tab columns, got {}",\n                lineno,\n                cols.len()\n            ));\n        }\n        let pfx = cols[0];\n        let class = cols[1];\n        let removal = cols[2];\n        // why = cols[3] (unused in assertions beyond non-empty check would be noisy; skip)\n        let source = cols[4];\n\n        if !KNOWN_CLASSES.contains(&class) {\n            fail(&format!(\n                "line {}: unknown class '{}' (pfx '{}')",\n                lineno, class, pfx\n            ));\n        }\n        if source.trim().is_empty() {\n            fail(&format!("line {}: empty source (un-cited row) '{}'", lineno, pfx));\n        }\n        if removal != "out-of-band-only" && removal != "operator-ruling-required" {\n            fail(&format!(\n                "line {}: invalid removal_authority '{}' (pfx '{}')",\n                lineno, removal, pfx\n            ));\n        }\n        if pfx == registry_self_prefix {\n            saw_self_row = true;\n            if class != "governance-self" || removal != "operator-ruling-required" {\n                fail(&format!(\n                    "self-row '{}' must be class=governance-self removal_authority=operator-ruling-required (got {}/{})",\n                    pfx, class, removal\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n        if seen_prefixes.contains(pfx) {\n            fail(&format!("duplicate path_prefix '{}' at line {}", pfx, lineno));\n        }\n        seen_prefixes.insert(pfx.to_string());\n        row_count += 1;\n    }\n\n    // (1) self-row test\n    if !saw_self_row {\n        fail(&format!(\n            "SELF-ROW TEST FAILED — '{}' is not a row of its own registry",\n            registry_self_prefix\n        ));\n    } else {\n        println!(\n            "self-row test: PASS — {} is registered (class=governance-self).",\n            registry_self_prefix\n        );\n    }\n\n    // (4) D11 Q4 encoding: core hard-line rows must be out-of-band-only\n    for hard in CORE_HARD_LINE {\n        // find the row with this prefix (longest-exact-match is fine here; prefixes are unique)\n        let mut matched_removal = None;\n        for line in text.lines() {\n            if line.starts_with('#') || line.trim().is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let cols: Vec<&str> = line.split('\\t').collect();\n            if cols.len() >= 3 && cols[0] == *hard {\n                matched_removal = Some(cols[2].to_string());\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n        match matched_removal {\n            None => fail(&format!("D11 Q4: core hard-line row '{}' missing from registry", hard)),\n            Some(r) if r != "out-of-band-only" => fail(&format!(\n                "D11 Q4 VIOLATION: '{}' must be removal_authority=out-of-band-only (got '{}')",\n                hard, r\n            )),\n            Some(_) => println!("D11 Q4 hard-line OK: {} = out-of-band-only", hard),\n        }\n    }\n\n    println!(\n        "=== red-line-registry test: GREEN ({} rows, all assertions passed) ===",\n        row_count\n    );\n    process::exit(0);\n}\n	3941	-1	-1		cbf7bf9c8d90c165b809f1cb7fc396469d1791c6e876aacd6859edc383e5fc7799420431cdcc54fbf0d9116da18d337887bb3c27fc6db38be461e6e70504da582997c5add97341457e852202a7b9a051026c727ae1ba706a085438a4bc075fd5bb7eb7963c405cbe9a90138e1a576fd3f7e2b5aaf3c1bb0545d1c4d679716f90

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/async-spool/src/main.rs	main · 488 lines	//! async-spool — generic JSONL spool drainer adapter (pure-Rust rustls/ring).\n//!\n//! ## Why this exists\n//! This is the generalized successor to `tools/telemetry/rust-spool`. That\n//! binary was Telegram-only: the producer appended\n//! `{ "chat_id", "topic_id", "text" }` lines and the drainer POSTed them to the\n//! Bot API. Here we generalize the *same proven* read→pace→send→drop-on-ok→\n//! deadletter-on-error contract to an arbitrary destination field:\n//!\n//! Every spool line is a JSON object with a `"dest"` discriminator plus a\n//! payload:\n//!   * `dest: "telegram"` → POST to api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/sendMessage\n//!     (body shape reuses the telemetry-spool contract: chat_id, text,\n//!      message_thread_id).\n//!   * `dest: "http"`      → POST to the `url` field with `body` (JSON).\n//!\n//! ## Delivery contract (inherits the telemetry guarantees)\n//! * The producer's work path only WRITES one JSON line (microseconds) — it\n//!   never blocks on the network.\n//! * A line is removed from the spool ONLY after the send returns success, so a\n//!   crash mid-drain loses nothing (the line stays and is retried next pass).\n//! * A line that cannot be parsed / has an unknown `dest` / is missing required\n//!   fields is never silently lost: it is appended to a `<spool>.deadletter`\n//!   file and removed from the live queue, so it neither loops forever nor\n//!   vanishes.\n//! * Pacing gap (default 3.5s) is honoured between sends, read from\n//!   `ASYNC_SPOOL_GAP_S` (float).\n//! * TLS is pure-Rust rustls + webpki-roots (ring) via ureq. NO OpenSSL, NO\n//!   native-tls, NO curl.\n\nuse serde::Deserialize;\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::time::{Duration, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\n\n/// Default pacing gap in seconds between two sends. MUST match hermes-kernel\n/// `reporting::TG_MIN_GAP_S`\n/// (`hermes-agent-kernel-rewrite/hermes-kernel/kernel/src/reporting.rs:26`).\n/// Single record of this cross-repo decision:\n/// `docs/design/hermetic-architecture-2026-07-16/PACING-CONTRACT.md`.\n/// Env-overridable via `ASYNC_SPOOL_GAP_S`; the default is pinned by\n/// `default_gap_self_pin` (+ optional present-sibling test).\nconst DEFAULT_GAP_S: f64 = 3.5;\n/// Poll interval when the spool is empty (seconds).\nconst IDLE_POLL_S: u64 = 2;\n/// Send/connect timeout per attempt.\nconst SEND_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);\n/// Max attempts per send before giving up (the line stays queued & retries\n/// next pass — never deadlettered for a transient delivery failure).\nconst MAX_ATTEMPTS: u32 = 4;\n\n/// A line that the dispatcher knows how to deliver.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nenum Sendable {\n    Telegram {\n        chat_id: String,\n        text: String,\n        topic_id: i64,\n    },\n    Http {\n        url: String,\n        body: serde_json::Value,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Classification of one raw spool line.\nenum LineClass {\n    /// Parsed and dispatchable.\n    Sendable(Sendable),\n    /// Unparseable / unknown dest / missing required field. Carries the raw\n    /// line so it can be preserved in the deadletter file.\n    Dead(String),\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\nstruct RawLine {\n    dest: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(flatten)]\n    rest: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,\n}\n\n/// Default Telegram topic (Hermes). Mirrors telemetry-spool default.\nconst DEFAULT_TOPIC_ID: i64 = 267;\n\n/// Read the gap from env (float seconds); fall back to the default.\nfn gap_seconds() -> f64 {\n    match std::env::var("ASYNC_SPOOL_GAP_S") {\n        Ok(v) => v.trim().parse::<f64>().unwrap_or(DEFAULT_GAP_S),\n        Err(_) => DEFAULT_GAP_S,\n    }\n    .max(0.0)\n}\n\nfn spool_dir() -> PathBuf {\n    let mut p = std::env::temp_dir();\n    p.push("async-spool");\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&p).ok();\n    p\n}\n\nfn queue_path() -> PathBuf {\n    let mut p = spool_dir();\n    p.push("queue.jsonl");\n    p\n}\n\nfn deadletter_path() -> PathBuf {\n    let mut p = spool_dir();\n    p.push("queue.deadletter");\n    p\n}\n\nfn now_secs() -> f64 {\n    SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_secs_f64())\n        .unwrap_or(0.0)\n}\n\n/// Parse one raw line into a [`LineClass`].\nfn classify(raw: &str) -> LineClass {\n    let parsed: RawLine = match serde_json::from_str(raw) {\n        Ok(p) => p,\n        Err(_) => return LineClass::Dead(raw.to_string()),\n    };\n    let dest = match parsed.dest {\n        Some(d) => d,\n        None => return LineClass::Dead(raw.to_string()),\n    };\n    match dest.as_str() {\n        "telegram" => {\n            let chat_id = parsed\n                .rest\n                .get("chat_id")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n            let text = parsed\n                .rest\n                .get("text")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n            let topic_id = parsed\n                .rest\n                .get("message_thread_id")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_i64())\n                .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_TOPIC_ID);\n            match (chat_id, text) {\n                (Some(chat_id), Some(text)) => {\n                    LineClass::Sendable(Sendable::Telegram { chat_id, text, topic_id })\n                }\n                _ => LineClass::Dead(raw.to_string()),\n            }\n        }\n        "http" => {\n            let url = parsed\n                .rest\n                .get("url")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n            let body = parsed.rest.get("body").cloned().unwrap_or(\n                serde_json::Value::Object(parsed.rest.clone()),\n            );\n            match url {\n                Some(url) => LineClass::Sendable(Sendable::Http { url, body }),\n                None => LineClass::Dead(raw.to_string()),\n            }\n        }\n        _ => LineClass::Dead(raw.to_string()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Read the queue. Returns each non-empty line with its index and classification.\nfn read_spool(path: &PathBuf) -> Vec<(usize, LineClass)> {\n    let data = match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {\n        Ok(d) => d,\n        Err(_) => return Vec::new(),\n    };\n    data.lines()\n        .enumerate()\n        .filter(|(_, l)| !l.trim().is_empty())\n        .map(|(i, l)| (i, classify(l.trim())))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Append raw lines to the deadletter file (preserves everything, never loses).\nfn deadletter(raws: &[String]) {\n    if raws.is_empty() {\n        return;\n    }\n    let path = deadletter_path();\n    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n        .create(true)\n        .append(true)\n        .open(&path)\n    {\n        for r in raws {\n            let _ = writeln!(f, "{}", r);\n        }\n        let _ = f.flush();\n    }\n}\n\n/// Rewrite the queue file dropping the given line indices (the sent line + any\n/// deadletter lines). Robust: if the file vanished, no-op.\nfn drop_lines(path: &PathBuf, drop_idx: &[usize]) {\n    let drop: std::collections::BTreeSet<usize> = drop_idx.iter().copied().collect();\n    let data = match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {\n        Ok(d) => d,\n        Err(_) => return,\n    };\n    let kept: Vec<&str> = data\n        .lines()\n        .enumerate()\n        .filter(|(i, l)| !l.trim().is_empty() && !drop.contains(i))\n        .map(|(_, l)| l)\n        .collect();\n    let mut tmp = path.clone();\n    tmp.set_extension("jsonl.tmp");\n    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::create(&tmp) {\n        if !kept.is_empty() {\n            let _ = writeln!(f, "{}", kept.join("\\n"));\n        }\n        let _ = f.flush();\n        let _ = std::fs::rename(&tmp, path);\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\nstruct TgResponse {\n    ok: bool,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    description: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Retry backoff delay for send `attempt` (1-based): exponential base-2 s with\n/// **full jitter** (`2s · 2^(attempt-1)`, capped at 32 s, `× rand[0.5,1.0)`).\n///\n/// ADR (H2 §2.5 / finding #24): jitter breaks spool synchronization — N drainers\n/// hitting a downed endpoint no longer retry in lock-step (thundering herd). The\n/// helper is DUPLICATED in `telemetry-spool` (the two spools share no lib crate;\n/// a `spool-common` path dep is heavier than warranted for one fn) — the\n/// duplication is a conscious, accepted trade. RNG is a dep-free splitmix64 seed\n/// off the wall clock (non-crypto is sufficient for jitter). The terminal\n/// fixed-2s transient pause in `run` and the idle poll are deliberately left\n/// un-jittered (single-drainer deployment).\nfn backoff_delay(attempt: u32) -> Duration {\n    const BASE_MS: u64 = 2_000;\n    const CAP_MS: u64 = 32_000;\n    let shift = attempt.saturating_sub(1).min(20);\n    let exp_ms = BASE_MS.saturating_mul(1u64 << shift).min(CAP_MS);\n    Duration::from_millis((exp_ms as f64 * jitter_unit()) as u64)\n}\n\n/// Dep-free jitter factor in `[0.5, 1.0)` from a wall-clock-seeded splitmix64.\n/// Non-crypto: jitter only needs to be uncorrelated across processes.\nfn jitter_unit() -> f64 {\n    let seed = SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)\n        .unwrap_or(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);\n    let mut z = seed.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);\n    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);\n    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);\n    z ^= z >> 31;\n    let unit = (z >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64; // [0.0, 1.0)\n    0.5 + 0.5 * unit // [0.5, 1.0)\n}\n\n/// Deliver one sendable. Returns true on success (line should be dropped).\nfn deliver(bot_token: &str, line: &Sendable) -> bool {\n    match line {\n        Sendable::Telegram { chat_id, text, topic_id } => {\n            let url = format!(\n                "https://api.telegram.org/bot{}/sendMessage",\n                bot_token\n            );\n            let body = serde_json::json!({\n                "chat_id": chat_id,\n                "text": text,\n                "disable_web_page_preview": true,\n                "message_thread_id": topic_id,\n            });\n            for attempt in 1..=MAX_ATTEMPTS {\n                let resp = ureq::post(&url)\n                    .timeout(SEND_TIMEOUT)\n                    .send_json(body.clone());\n                let parsed: Result<TgResponse, ureq::Error> =\n                    resp.and_then(|r| Ok(r.into_json::<TgResponse>()?));\n                match parsed {\n                    Ok(TgResponse { ok: true, .. }) => return true,\n                    Ok(r) => {\n                        eprintln!("async-spool: telegram rejected: {:?}", r.description);\n                        if attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS {\n                            return false;\n                        }\n                        std::thread::sleep(backoff_delay(attempt));\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        if attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS {\n                            return false;\n                        }\n                        std::thread::sleep(backoff_delay(attempt));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            false\n        }\n        Sendable::Http { url, body } => {\n            for attempt in 1..=MAX_ATTEMPTS {\n                let resp = ureq::post(url).timeout(SEND_TIMEOUT).send_json(body.clone());\n                match resp {\n                    Ok(_) => return true,\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        eprintln!("async-spool: http send failed ({}): {:?}", url, e);\n                        if attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS {\n                            return false;\n                        }\n                        std::thread::sleep(backoff_delay(attempt));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            false\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn run(bot_token: String) {\n    let path = queue_path();\n    let gap = gap_seconds();\n    eprintln!(\n        "async-spool: draining {} (pace {}s, idle poll {}s)",\n        path.display(),\n        gap,\n        IDLE_POLL_S\n    );\n    let mut last_send: Option<f64> = None;\n    loop {\n        let entries = read_spool(&path);\n        if entries.is_empty() {\n            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(IDLE_POLL_S));\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Partition: deadletter lines (bad) keep their original index + raw\n        // text; sendable lines keep their index + parsed payload.\n        let mut dead: Vec<(usize, String)> = Vec::new();\n        let mut sendable: Vec<(usize, Sendable)> = Vec::new();\n        for (idx, cls) in entries {\n            match cls {\n                LineClass::Dead(raw) => dead.push((idx, raw)),\n                LineClass::Sendable(s) => sendable.push((idx, s)),\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Preserve unparseable/undispatchable lines. They leave the live queue\n        // (so they don't loop forever) but are NEVER lost — appended verbatim\n        // to the deadletter file with their original index prefix.\n        let mut to_drop: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();\n        if !dead.is_empty() {\n            let raws: Vec<String> = dead.iter().map(|(i, r)| format!("{}:{}", i, r)).collect();\n            deadletter(&raws);\n            to_drop.extend(dead.into_iter().map(|(i, _)| i));\n        }\n\n        // Honour the pacing contract before sending the first sendable entry.\n        if let Some((idx, line)) = sendable.into_iter().next() {\n            let now = now_secs();\n            if let Some(t) = last_send {\n                let earliest = t + gap;\n                if earliest > now {\n                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs_f64((earliest - now).max(0.0)));\n                }\n            }\n            if deliver(&bot_token, &line) {\n                to_drop.push(idx);\n                last_send = Some(now_secs());\n            } else {\n                // transient delivery failure: keep the line, back off, retry.\n                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Drop everything that should leave the live queue this pass\n        // (deadletter lines first, then any successfully sent line).\n        if !to_drop.is_empty() {\n            drop_lines(&path, &to_drop);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn main() {\n    let bot_token = match std::env::var("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN") {\n        Ok(t) if !t.is_empty() => t,\n        _ => {\n            // Try /root/dowiz/.env without echoing the token (best-effort).\n            let env_path = PathBuf::from("/root/dowiz/.env");\n            if let Ok(contents) = std::fs::read_to_string(&env_path) {\n                for line in contents.lines() {\n                    if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=") {\n                        let v = v\n                            .trim()\n                            .trim_matches(|c| c == '"' || c == '\\'' || c == '\\r');\n                        if !v.is_empty() {\n                            return run(v.to_string());\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            eprintln!("async-spool: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN not set; exiting");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n    };\n    run(bot_token);\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // Cross-repo pacing pin (finding #18). The authority lives in a SIBLING repo\n    // (hermes-kernel `reporting::TG_MIN_GAP_S`), which a dowiz test cannot\n    // compile-time reference. This self-assertion makes any local edit to the\n    // default break a test, forcing a conscious re-verify against\n    // PACING-CONTRACT.md rather than a silent drift. See\n    // docs/design/hermetic-architecture-2026-07-16/PACING-CONTRACT.md.\n    #[test]\n    fn default_gap_self_pin() {\n        assert_eq!(DEFAULT_GAP_S, 3.5, "pacing gap desynced from PACING-CONTRACT");\n    }\n\n    // Optional stronger tier: when the hermes-kernel sibling repo happens to be\n    // checked out alongside dowiz, assert our value matches the live authority.\n    // SKIPS cleanly (passes) when the sibling is absent so a lone dowiz checkout\n    // never false-fails.\n    #[test]\n    fn default_gap_matches_present_sibling() {\n        let sibling =\n            "/root/hermes-agent-kernel-rewrite/hermes-kernel/kernel/src/reporting.rs";\n        let src = match std::fs::read_to_string(sibling) {\n            Ok(s) => s,\n            Err(_) => {\n                eprintln!("skip: hermes-kernel sibling absent ({sibling})");\n                return;\n            }\n        };\n        match parse_const_f64(&src, "TG_MIN_GAP_S") {\n            Some(v) => assert_eq!(\n                v, DEFAULT_GAP_S,\n                "async-spool DEFAULT_GAP_S ({DEFAULT_GAP_S}) != hermes-kernel ({v})"\n            ),\n            None => eprintln!("skip: TG_MIN_GAP_S not found in {sibling} (format changed?)"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Retry backoff carries jitter and stays within the exponential envelope:\n    // delay(attempt) ∈ [exp/2, exp) where exp = min(2s·2^(attempt-1), 32s).\n    #[test]\n    fn backoff_delay_is_jittered_within_envelope() {\n        for attempt in 1u32..=8 {\n            let shift = attempt.saturating_sub(1).min(20);\n            let exp_ms = 2_000u64.saturating_mul(1u64 << shift).min(32_000);\n            for _ in 0..64 {\n                let ms = backoff_delay(attempt).as_millis() as u64;\n                assert!(\n                    ms >= exp_ms / 2 && ms < exp_ms,\n                    "attempt {attempt}: delay {ms}ms outside [{}, {})",\n                    exp_ms / 2,\n                    exp_ms\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Parse `... <name> ... = <f64> ;` from Rust source (test-only helper for the\n    // present-sibling pin). Returns None if no such line exists.\n    fn parse_const_f64(src: &str, name: &str) -> Option<f64> {\n        for line in src.lines() {\n            if line.contains(name) && line.contains('=') {\n                let rhs = line.split('=').nth(1)?;\n                let val = rhs.trim().trim_end_matches(';').trim();\n                if let Ok(v) = val.parse::<f64>() {\n                    return Some(v);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        None\n    }\n}\n	3972	-1	-1		d3363f9dd48be7310129ebcd02561a014856b4c4de12f682e85de8439ad6ae49184810036dcd2adfa052d3292937d4298f736facb1689ecbf4a6720df70f6bc6769e75294d6b810917c7390035fbed58717b584aadf2e54da88038a452035ff6b523f75734ca42adce4a4816465d3591647f4c6e3681e9b7172964f451f43f90

Three subcommands. `git` and `cargo` are genuinely external binaries (shelled\n//! via std::process::Command); all the *logic* — parsing, idempotency, red-line\n//! detection, JSON emission, anomaly detection, worktree lifecycle — is native\n//! Rust, not bash.\n//!\n//!   ci-truth claim-latency [<sha> | <base> <head> | <base>..<head>]\n//!       V5-B claim-latency ledger appender (was scripts/claim-latency-append.sh).\n//!       Appends ONE JSONL entry per NEW commit to docs/ledger/claim-latency.jsonl:\n//!         {commit_sha, authored_ts, ci_observed_green_ts, delta_s, diff_loc}\n//!       Idempotent: a commit already in the ledger is skipped.\n//!       EXIT 0 on success (incl. "nothing to do"); non-zero on usage/git error.\n//!\n//!   ci-truth claim-latency-check\n//!       BLUEPRINT-P08 §4 claim-latency ANOMALY detector (F36 / E47). CONSUMES the\n//!       ledger the appender above produces. For each entry, computes a falsifiable\n//!       minimum-plausible verification time from diff_loc and flags any commit whose\n//!       recorded delta_s is below it — the "52s GREEN on a 1610-line diff" self-\n//!       certification pattern (BRAIN-TOPOLOGY). Flagged entries are appended to a\n//!       LOCAL sink docs/ledger/claim-latency-anomalies.jsonl (idempotent by\n//!       commit_sha). ADVISORY: exits 0 whether or not anomalies were found — it\n//!       signals, it does not gate (that is Phase 6's signed-verifier job).\n//!\n//!   ci-truth v5c-reexec [<base>] [<head>]        (defaults: origin/main HEAD)\n//!       V5-C independent re-execution verifier (was scripts/v5c-reexec.sh).\n//!       Red-line-gated: when the diff range touches money.rs / order_machine.rs /\n//!       event_log.rs / auth·otp·jwt, it re-runs kernel + engine `cargo test` in a\n//!       CLEAN independent git worktree and emits RED|GREEN; otherwise SKIP.\n//!       EXIT 0 GREEN|SKIP, 1 RED, 2 usage/git-resolution error.\n//!\n//!   ci-truth v1-verify [<sha>]                    (default: HEAD)\n//!       BLUEPRINT-P06 §5 merge-gate evaluator. Fetches refs/notes/v1-diff-attest\n//!       (key_K) and refs/notes/v1-verdict (key_V) for <sha>, then runs the §5\n//!       policy: both notes present, key_K ≠ key_V, hash-binding intact, GREEN\n//!       required on red-line diffs, residue present, redline_touch honesty.\n//!       HONESTY: real ML-DSA key_K/key_V signing is HARD-GATED on Phase 3 closing\n//!       C4b (see src/v1.rs); the contract/gate is executable and testable now.\n//!       EXIT 0 GREEN, 1 RED.\n\nmod v1;\n\nuse std::fs::{self, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::process::Command;\nuse std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// git helpers (git is an external binary the kernel never reimplements).\n// ===========================================================================\n\n/// Run `git <args>`; return trimmed stdout on success, `None` on non-zero exit\n/// or spawn failure. Mirrors a bash `$(git …)` that aborts under `set -e`.\nfn git_ok(args: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {\n    let out = Command::new("git").args(args).output().ok()?;\n    if !out.status.success() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    Some(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).trim().to_string())\n}\n\nfn now_unix() -> i64 {\n    SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_secs() as i64)\n        .unwrap_or(0)\n}\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// Subcommand 1 — claim-latency  (port of scripts/claim-latency-append.sh)\n// ===========================================================================\n\n/// Sum added+deleted across a `git show --numstat --format=` body. Binary files\n/// render their columns as `-` (counted 0); blank lines contribute 0. Pure port\n/// of the awk `{a=$1;d=$2; if(a=="-")a=0; if(d=="-")d=0; s+=a+d}`.\nfn numstat_sum(output: &str) -> i64 {\n    let mut sum: i64 = 0;\n    for line in output.lines() {\n        let mut cols = line.split_whitespace();\n        let a = cols.next();\n        let d = cols.next();\n        if let (Some(a), Some(d)) = (a, d) {\n            let av = if a == "-" { 0 } else { a.parse::<i64>().unwrap_or(0) };\n            let dv = if d == "-" { 0 } else { d.parse::<i64>().unwrap_or(0) };\n            sum += av + dv;\n        }\n    }\n    sum\n}\n\n/// diff_loc for one commit: `git show --numstat --format= <sha>` summed.\nfn diff_loc(sha: &str) -> i64 {\n    let out = git_ok(&["show", "--numstat", "--format=", sha]).unwrap_or_default();\n    numstat_sum(&out)\n}\n\n/// Resolve the oldest-first commit list from the positional args, exactly as the\n/// bash `case "$#"` did. "HEAD"]).ok_or(1)?;\n            Ok(vec![head])\n        }\n        1 => {\n            if pos[0].contains("..") {\n                let out = git_ok(&["rev-list", "--reverse", &pos[0]]).ok_or(1)?;\n                Ok(out.lines().filter(|l| !l.is_empty()).map(String::from).collect())\n            } else {\n                let spec = format!("{}^{{commit}}", pos[0]);\n                let c = git_ok(&["rev-list", "--reverse", &range]).ok_or(1)?;\n            Ok(out.lines().filter(|l| !l.is_empty()).map(String::from).collect())\n        }\n        _ => Err(2),\n    }\n}\n\nfn claim_latency(pos: &[String]) -> i32 {\n    let repo_root = match git_ok(&["rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"]) {\n        Some(r) => r,\n        None => {\n            eprintln!("claim-latency: not inside a git repo");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    };\n    let ledger = PathBuf::from(&repo_root).join("docs/ledger/claim-latency.jsonl");\n    if let Some(dir) = ledger.parent() {\n
