Equation {\n    /// Panics if `expr` uses a symbol not listed in `args` — mirrors the original's\n    /// `__post_init__` validation (a build-time authoring error, not a runtime one).\n    pub fn new(name: &str, args: &[&str], expr: Expr) -> Self {\n        let args: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n        let mut free = Vec::new();\n        expr.free_symbols(&mut free);\n        let missing: Vec<&String> = free.iter().filter(|f| !args.contains(f)).collect();\n        assert!(\n            missing.is_empty(),\n            "expr uses symbols not in args: {missing:?} (args={args:?})"\n        );\n        Equation { name: name.to_string(), args, expr, scale_bits: 32 }\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_scale_bits(mut self, bits: u32) -> Self {\n        self.scale_bits = bits;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// float variant (dynamics path — not bitwise-deterministic across targets on\n    /// libm calls: sqrt/sin/cos/exp differ in ULPs between x86_64 and ARM libm).\n    /// `Err` (never a fallback) if the expression contains an integer-exact-only\n    /// node (`DivHalfUp`) whose f64 division would silently change the semantics.\n    pub fn emit_f64_rust(&self) -> Result<String, F64EmissionUnsupported> {\n        if self.expr.any_div_half_up() {\n            return Err(F64EmissionUnsupported(\n                "DivHalfUp is integer-exact-only; f64 division would change its half-up semantics"\n                    .into(),\n            ));\n        }\n        if self.expr.any_indexed() {\n            return Err(F64EmissionUnsupported(\n                "Index/IndexSum are integer-exact-only; f64 has no array indexing".into(),\n            ));\n        }\n        let params = self\n            .args\n            .iter()\n            .map(|a| format!("{a}: f64"))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(", ");\n        Ok(format!(\n            "/// GENERATED by eqc-rs from: {name}\\n\\\n             /// f64 variant — dynamics path (not bitwise-deterministic across targets on libm calls).\\n\\\n             #[inline(always)]\\n\\\n             pub fn {name}_f64({params}) -> f64 {{\\n    {body}\\n}}",\n            name = self.name,\n            body = self.expr.to_rust_f64(),\n        ))\n    }\n\n    /// Integer-exact checked emission mode. Symbols are raw `i64` (minor units /\\\n    /// micro-rates, NOT Q-scaled reals); arithmetic runs in `i128`; every\\\n    /// narrowing/overflowing step is checked; the returned fn has signature\\\n    /// `fn(args: i64) -> Result<i64, &'static str>`. The emitted body mirrors\\\n    /// `apply_tax`'s fail-closed contract (money.rs BP-17).\\\n    ///\\\n    /// Allowed nodes: `Sym`, `Num(integral)`, `Sum`, `Prod`, `Pow(n>=0)`,\\\n    /// `DivHalfUp`. Refuses (Err, never a fallback): `Sqrt`/`Sin`/`Cos`/`Exp`/\\\n    /// `Asin`/`Atan2` and any non-integral `Num`. `DivHalfUp` emits a division-by-\\\n    /// zero guard before each use. The indexed-summation IR extension (item 36)\\\n    /// adds `Index`/`IndexSum`: an indexed equation is emitted with `&[i8]` array\\\n    /// parameters and the i32-accumulator Q-format loop (the shared construct for\\\n    /// the Laplacian neighbor-sum AND the quantized-dot inner law — one IR, never\\\n    /// two). The emitter REFUSES (typed `Err`) any `IndexSum` whose i8×i8\\\n    /// accumulation exceeds the `i32` accumulator ceiling `K·P_MAX ≤ 2^31−1`.\n    pub fn emit_int_checked_rust(&self) -> Result<String, IntEmissionUnsupported> {\n        if self.expr.any_indexed() {\n            return self.emit_int_indexed_rust();\n        }\n        let inner = emit_int_checked(&self.expr)?;\n        let params = self\n            .args\n            .iter()\n            .map(|a| format!("{a}: i64"))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(", ");\n        Ok(format!(\n            "/// GENERATED by eqc-rs from: {name}\\n\\\n             /// Integer-exact variant — raw i64 (minor units), i128 arithmetic, every\\n\\\n             /// step checked. Returns Result<i64, &'static str> (Err on overflow/div-by-zero).\\n\\\n             #[inline(always)]\\n\\\n             pub fn {name}_int({params}) -> Result<i64, &'static str> {{\\n    use std::convert::TryFrom; i64::try_from({inner}).map_err(|_| \\"overflow: result exceeds i64\\")\\n}}",\n            name = self.name,\n        ))\n    }\n\n    /// Integer-exact emission for an indexed equation (item 36): the `Index`/\\\n    /// `IndexSum` IR. Array args become `&[i8]` parameters; the `IndexSum` emits a\\\n    /// fixed-trip `for` loop accumulating i8×i8 products into an `i32` (checked,\\\n    /// `?`-propagating). The trip count is the build-time `len`, so the emitted\\\n    /// loop is cyclomatic-1. Refuses (typed `Err`) when `K·P_MAX` would exceed\\\n    /// `2^31−1` (the i32 accumulator ceiling, item 35 §3.4) — refuse-never-fall-\\\n    /// back. Returns `Result<_, IntEmissionUnsupported>`.\n    pub fn emit_int_indexed_rust(&self) -> Result<String, IntEmissionUnsupported> {\n        if !self.expr.any_indexed() {\n            return Err(IntEmissionUnsupported(\n                "emit_int_indexed_rust called on a non-indexed equation".into(),\n            ));\n        }\n        let len = self\n            .expr\n            .first_index_len()\n            .ok_or_else(|| IntEmissionUnsupported("indexed equation has no IndexSum".into()))?;\n        // Overflow boundary (item 35 §3.4): K·P_MAX² ≤ 2^31−1 for an i8×i8 dot\n        // accumulating into i32. Each term is an i8×i8 product (max P_MAX² =\n        // 127² = 16129), so the worst-case accumulator is K·P_MAX². P_MAX = 127.\n        // Refuse if K·127² > 2^31−1.\n        let p_max: i128 = 127;\n        let k = len as i128;\n        if k * p_max * p_max > (i32::MAX as i128) {\n            return Err(IntEmissionUnsupported(format!(\n                "indexed sum length {len} with i8×i8 products ({k}·{p_max}²) exceeds the i32 accumulator ceiling 2^31−1; reduce K or widen the accumulator"\n            )));\n        }\n        // Array parameters: the array names bound by `Index` nodes (e.g. `a`,\n        // `w`) become `&[i8]` parameters; any remaining scalar `Sym`s in `args`\n        // stay `i64`. For the item-36 quantized-dot / neighbor-sum shape, arrays\n        // a/w are i8. We derive the array set from the IR itself so an Equation\n        // authored with empty `args` (the test case) still emits the right\n        // `&[i8]` parameters.\n        let mut array_set: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        self.expr.collect_index_arrays(&mut array_set);\n        let mut array_params: Vec<String> = array_set\n            .iter()\n            .map(|a| format!("{a}: &[i8]"))\n            .collect();\n        let mut scalar_params = Vec::new();\n        for a in &self.args {\n            if !array_set.contains(a) {\n                scalar_params.push(format!("{a}: i64"));\n            }\n        }\n        let params = array_params\n            .iter()\n            .chain(scalar_params.iter())\n            .cloned()\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(", ");\n        let inner = format!("Ok({{ {} }})", emit_int_indexed_checked(&self.expr)?);\n        Ok(format!(\n            "/// GENERATED by eqc-rs from: {name}\\n\\\n             /// Integer-exact INDEXED variant — &[i8] arrays, i8×i8 product into an i32\\n\\\n             /// accumulator, every step checked. Returns Result<i32, &'static str>\\n\\\n             /// (Err on overflow/out-of-bounds). Trip count fixed at build time (len={len}).\\n\\\n             #[inline(always)]\\n\\\n             pub fn {name}_int({params}) -> Result<i32, &'static str> {{\\n    {inner}\\n}}",\n            name = self.name,\n            len = len,\n        ))\n    }\n\n    /// Fixed-point Q-format variant — bitwise-identical on every CPU/wasm target.\n    /// `Err` (never a fallback) if the expression leaves the representable subset.\n    ///\n    /// The indexed-summation IR (item 36) is integer-exact only: `Index`/`IndexSum`\n    /// carry `&[i8]` arrays and an i32 accumulator, which is NOT the scalar Q-format\n    /// subset. So `emit_fixed_rust` refuses indexed equations (the same honest\n    /// boundary the f64 path uses).\n    pub fn emit_fixed_rust(&self) -> Result<String, FixedPointUnsupported> {\n        if self.expr.any_indexed() {\n            return Err(FixedPointUnsupported(\n                "Index/IndexSum are integer-exact-only; the fixed-point Q-format subset has no array indexing".into(),\n            ));\n        }\n        let s_int: i128 = 1i128 << self.scale_bits;\n        let inner = emit_fixed(&self.expr, s_int)?;\n        let params = self\n            .args\n            .iter()\n            .map(|a| format!("{a}: i64"))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(", ");\n        Ok(format!(\n            "/// GENERATED by eqc-rs from: {name}\\n\\\n             /// Fixed-point Q{scale} variant — inputs/output are round(v * 2^{scale}) as i64.\\n\\\n             /// BITWISE-DETERMINISTIC on every target (pure integer arithmetic, i128 intermediates).\\n\\\n             #[inline(always)]\\n\\\n             pub fn {name}_fixed({params}) -> i64 {{\\n    ({inner}) as i64\\n}}",\n            name = self.name,\n            scale = self.scale_bits,\n        ))\n    }\n\n    /// A standalone Rust program. For each sample it asserts:\n    /// |f64_variant - reference| < eps AND (if representable)\n    /// |fixed_variant/2^SHIFT - reference| < eps, where `reference` comes from\n    /// `Expr::eval` — a tree-walking interpreter, independent of the two codegen\n    /// paths above. Compile + run; a non-zero exit means codegen is wrong.\n    ///\n    /// `Err` from `emit_f64_rust` (e.g. a `DivHalfUp`-containing expr) means the\n    /// f64 path cannot represent the equation — no f64 proof program is emitted\n    /// for it (the integer-exact path is the correct one; see `emit_int_checked_rust`).\n    pub fn emit_proof_program(&self, samples: &[HashMap<String, f64>], eps: f64) -> String {\n        if self.expr.any_indexed() {\n            // Indexed equations carry integer-exact `i8` arrays, not f64 scalars.\n            // The scalar `&[HashMap<String,f64>]` sample shape does not apply; the\n            // caller must use `emit_indexed_proof_program` with `IndexedSample`s.\n            return self.emit_int_indexed_proof_program(&[], eps);\n        }\n        let f64_res = self.emit_f64_rust();\n        let fixed_res = self.emit_fixed_rust();\n        let (fns, has_fixed) = match (&f64_res, &fixed_res) {\n            (Ok(f), Ok(fx)) => (format!("{f}\\n\\n{fx}"), true),\n            (Ok(f), Err(_)) => (f.clone(), false),\n            (Err(_), _) => (\n                "// f64 variant NOT representable (integer-exact-only equation) — no f64 proof.\\n"\n                    .to_string(),\n                false,\n            ),\n        };\n        let s_int: i128 = 1i128 << self.scale_bits;\n        let mut checks = Vec::new();\n        for (i, smp) in samples.iter().enumerate() {\n            let reference = self.expr.eval(smp);\n            let f64_args = self\n                .args\n                .iter()\n                .map(|a| flit(smp[a]))\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(", ");\n            if f64_res.is_ok() {\n                checks.push(format!(\n                    "    let got = {name}_f64({f64_args});\\n    assert!((got - ({refv})).abs() < {epsv}, \\"f64 sample {i}: got {{}} want {refv}\\", got);",\n                    name = self.name,\n                    refv = flit(reference),\n                    epsv = flit(eps),\n                ));\n            }\n            if has_fixed {\n                let fixed_args = self\n                    .args\n                    .iter()\n                    .map(|a| format!("({}i64)", (smp[a] * s_int as f64).round() as i64))\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                    .join(", ");\n                checks.push(format!(\n                    "    let got_fx = {name}_fixed({fixed_args}) as f64 / ({s_int}u64 as f64);\\n    assert!((got_fx - ({refv})).abs() < {epsv}, \\"fixed sample {i}: got {{}} want {refv}\\", got_fx);",\n                    name = self.name,\n                    refv = flit(reference),\n                    epsv = flit(eps),\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n        let checks_src = checks.join("\\n");\n        format!(\n            "// GENERATED by eqc-rs — self-asserting proof for `{name}`.\\n\\\n             // exit 0 <=> the emitted f64 (and fixed-point) code matches the Expr-evaluated reference.\\n\\\n             {fns}\\n\\n\\\n             fn main() {{\\n{checks_src}\\n    println!(\\"eqc proof OK: {name} ({n} samples, fixed={has_fixed})\\");\\n}}\\n",\n            name = self.name,\n            n = samples.len(),\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Self-asserting proof program for an INDEXED equation (item 36): emits the\n    /// `&[i8]` `_int` fn and a `main` that feeds fixed `i8` arrays through it and\n    /// asserts the result equals the tree-walking `eval_int_indexed` reference\n    /// (the independent interpreter, a SEPARATE code path from the string\n    /// emitter). Compiled by real rustc and run; exit 0 ⇒ codegen correct. This is\n    /// the existing proof-program mechanism extended to indexed sums — the oracle\n    /// proof (item 36 §4.1). `eps` is accepted for signature parity with the\n    /// scalar path but is unused (the indexed reference is exact integer equality).\n    fn emit_int_indexed_proof_program(&self, samples: &[IndexedSample], _eps: f64) -> String {\n        let int_src = self.emit_int_indexed_rust().expect(\n            "indexed equation must emit in integer-exact mode (emit_int_indexed_proof_program)",\n        );\n        let mut checks = String::new();\n        for (i, s) in samples.iter().enumerate() {\n            let a_lit = s.a_literal();\n            let w_lit = s.w_literal();\n            let reference = self\n                .expr\n                .eval_int_indexed(\n                    &HashMap::new(),\n                    &{\n                        let mut m = HashMap::new();\n                        m.insert("a".to_string(), s.a.clone());\n                        m.insert("w".to_string(), s.w.clone());\n                        m\n                    },\n                    &HashMap::new(),\n                )\n                .expect("reference eval must succeed for a valid sample");\n            checks.push_str(&format!(\n                "    let a{i}: &[i8] = &{a_lit};\\n    let w{i}: &[i8] = &{w_lit};\\n    let got{i} = {name}_int(a{i}, w{i}).expect(\\"indexed int must not overflow\\");\\n    assert_eq!(got{i}, {want}i32, \\"indexed sample {i}: got {{}} want {want}\\", got{i});\\n",\n                i = i,\n                name = self.name,\n                a_lit = a_lit,\n                w_lit = w_lit,\n                want = reference as i32,\n            ));\n        }\n        // The emitted _int fn returns Result<i32,&'static str>, so call it from a\n        // thin unsafe wrapper to keep `main` simple and the generated program a\n        // standalone, compilable Rust binary (mirrors the scalar proof shape).\n        format!(\n            "{int_src}\\nunsafe fn {name}_checked(a: &[i8], w: &[i8]) -> i32 {{ {name}_int(a, w).expect(\\"indexed int overflow\\") }}\\nfn main() {{\\n{checks}    println!(\\"eqc indexed proof OK: {name} ({n} samples)\\");\\n}}\\n",\n            name = self.name,\n            n = samples.len(),\n        )\n    }\n}\n\nfn emit_fixed(expr: &Expr, s_int: i128) -> Result<String, FixedPointUnsupported> {\n    match expr {\n        Expr::Sym(s) => Ok(format!("({s} as i128)")),\n        Expr::Num(v) => Ok(format!("({}i128)", (*v * s_int as f64).round() as i128)),\n        Expr::Sum(xs) => {\n            let parts: Result<Vec<_>, _> = xs.iter().map(|x| emit_fixed(x, s_int)).collect();\n            Ok(format!("({})", parts?.join(" + ")))\n        }\n        Expr::Prod(xs) => {\n            let parts: Result<Vec<_>, _> = xs.iter().map(|x| emit_fixed(x, s_int)).collect();\n            let parts = parts?;\n            let mut acc = parts[0].clone();\n            for p in &parts[1..] {\n                acc = format!("(({acc} * {p}) / {s_int}i128)");\n            }\n            Ok(acc)\n        }\n        Expr::Pow(base, n) => {\n            if *n < 0 {\n                return Err(FixedPointUnsupported(format!(\n                    "negative exponent not fixed-point-representable: pow(_, {n})"\n                )));\n            }\n            if *n == 0 {\n                return Ok(format!("({s_int}i128)"));\n            }\n            let base_s = emit_fixed(base, s_int)?;\n            let mut acc = base_s.clone();\n            for _ in 1..*n {\n                acc = format!("(({acc} * {base_s}) / {s_int}i128)");\n            }\n            Ok(acc)\n        }\n        Expr::Sqrt(_) => Err(FixedPointUnsupported("sqrt not in the fixed-point subset".into())),\n        Expr::Sin(_) => Err(FixedPointUnsupported("sin not in the fixed-point subset".into())),\n        Expr::Cos(_) => Err(FixedPointUnsupported("cos not in the fixed-point subset".into())),\n        Expr::Exp(_) => Err(FixedPointUnsupported("exp not in the fixed-point subset".into())),\n        // New A1 nodes: Asin/Atan2 are f64-only; DivHalfUp is integer-exact-only.\n        // None belong in the Q-format fixed-point subset.\n        Expr::Asin(_) => Err(FixedPointUnsupported("asin not in the fixed-point subset".into())),\n        Expr::Atan2(_, _) => {\n            Err(FixedPointUnsupported("atan2 not in the fixed-point subset".into()))\n        }\n        Expr::DivHalfUp(_, _) => {\n            Err(FixedPointUnsupported("div_half_up is integer-exact-only".into()))\n        }\n        // Item 36 — the indexed-summation IR is integer-exact only (i8 arrays, i32\n        // accumulator); it is NOT scalar Q-format math, so the fixed-point path\n        // refuses it with the same honest boundary as f64.\n        Expr::Index { .. } | Expr::IndexSum { .. } => Err(FixedPointUnsupported(\n            "Index/IndexSum are integer-exact-only; the fixed-point Q-format subset has no array indexing".into(),\n        )),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Integer-exact emission (int-mode): raw i64 symbols, i128 arithmetic, every\n/// narrowing/overflowing step checked. Returns the inner `Result<i128, &'static\n/// str>`-typed expression; the `Equation::emit_int_checked_rust` wrapper wraps it\n/// in the `i64::try_from(...)` final narrowing.\nfn emit_int_checked(expr: &Expr) -> Result<String, IntEmissionUnsupported> {\n    match expr {\n        Expr::Sym(s) => Ok(format!("({s} as i128)")),\n        Expr::Num(v) => {\n            if !v.is_finite() || (v.fract() != 0.0) || (v.abs() >= 9.22_337_203_685_477_6e18) {\n                return Err(IntEmissionUnsupported(format!(\n                    "non-integral or out-of-i64-range constant not integer-exact-representable: {v}"\n                )));\n            }\n            Ok(format!("({}i128)", *v as i64))\n        }\n        Expr::Sum(xs) => {\n            let mut acc: Option<String> = None;\n            for x in xs {\n                let p = emit_int_checked(x)?;\n                acc = Some(match acc {\n                    None => p,\n                    Some(a) => format!("(({a}).checked_add({p}).ok_or(\\"overflow in Sum\\")?)"),\n                });\n            }\n            Ok(acc.unwrap_or_else(|| "0i128".to_string()))\n        }\n        Expr::Prod(xs) => {\n            let mut acc: Option<String> = None;\n            for x in xs {\n                let p = emit_int_checked(x)?;\n                acc = Some(match acc {\n                    None => p,\n                    Some(a) => format!("(({a}).checked_mul({p}).ok_or(\\"overflow in Prod\\")?)"),\n                });\n            }\n            Ok(acc.unwrap_or_else(|| "1i128".to_string()))\n        }\n        Expr::Pow(base, n) => {\n            if *n < 0 {\n                return Err(IntEmissionUnsupported(format!(\n                    "negative exponent not integer-exact-representable: pow(_, {n})"\n                )));\n            }\n            let base_s = emit_int_checked(base)?;\n            if *n == 0 {\n                return Ok("1i128".to_string());\n            }\n            let mut acc = base_s.clone();\n            for _ in 1..*n {\n                acc = format!("(({acc}).checked_mul({base_s}).ok_or(\\"overflow in Pow\\")?)");\n            }\n            Ok(acc)\n        }\n        Expr::DivHalfUp(a, b) => {\n            let a_s = emit_int_checked(a)?;\n            let b_s = emit_int_checked(b)?;\n            Ok(format!(\n                "{{ let b = {b_s}; if b == 0i128 {{ return Err(\\"division by zero in DivHalfUp\\"); }} (({a_s}) + b / 2) / b }}"\n            ))\n        }\n        // f64-only nodes (and the Q-format subset) are NOT in the integer-exact set.\n        Expr::Sqrt(_) => Err(IntEmissionUnsupported("sqrt not in the integer-exact subset".into())),\n        // A6 / T8 — integer-CORDIC fixed-point sin/cos: routes through the digest-pinned\n        // Q30 substrate `eqc_rs::cordic::cordic_sincos` instead of hard-refusing. This\n        // EXTENDS the representable integer-exact subset (without touching the f64 dynamics\n        // path). Convention: the argument is Q30 fixed-point radians and the result is Q30\n        // (unit-magnitude, like a scaled sine/cosine). Deterministic — same i64 add/sub/\n        // compare/arithmetic-shift ops the digest in `tests/cordic_digest.rs` pins.\n        Expr::Sin(inner) => {\n            let z = emit_int_checked(inner)?;\n            Ok(format!("(eqc_rs::cordic::cordic_sincos(({z}) as i64).1 as i128)"))\n        }\n        Expr::Cos(inner) => {\n            let z = emit_int_checked(inner)?;\n            Ok(format!("(eqc_rs::cordic::cordic_sincos(({z}) as i64).0 as i128)"))\n        }\n        Expr::Exp(_) => Err(IntEmissionUnsupported("exp not in the integer-exact subset".into())),\n        Expr::Asin(_) => Err(IntEmissionUnsupported("asin not in the integer-exact subset".into())),\n        Expr::Atan2(_, _) => {\n            Err(IntEmissionUnsupported("atan2 not in the integer-exact subset".into()))\n        }\n        // Item 36 — scalar int-mode emission has NO array indexing. An `Index`/\n        // `IndexSum` node is the indexed-summation IR, which must take the\n        // dedicated `emit_int_indexed_checked` path (the `&[i8]` `_int` fn), never\n        // the scalar `i64` expression emitter. Refuse here so the two paths stay\n        // disjoint (no silent mis-codegen).\n        Expr::Index { .. } | Expr::IndexSum { .. } => {\n            Err(IntEmissionUnsupported(\n                "Index/IndexSum require the indexed-summation IR path (emit_int_indexed_checked), not scalar emit_int_checked".into(),\n            ))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A fixed test sample for an indexed equation (item 36): the `i8` element arrays\n/// `a` and `w` feeding the `Σ_k a_k·w_k` quantized dot (and, dually, the Laplacian\n/// neighbor-sum). Held separately from `HashMap<String,f64>` because the indexed IR\n/// is integer-exact (`i8` elements, `i32` accumulator) — there is no f64 domain.\npub struct IndexedSample {\n    pub a: Vec<i8>,\n    pub w: Vec<i8>,\n}\n\nimpl IndexedSample {\n    pub fn new(a: Vec<i8>, w: Vec<i8>) -> Self {\n        IndexedSample { a, w }\n    }\n    /// Rust array literal for `vec![...]`-style `&[i8]` binding in a generated proof.\n    pub fn a_literal(&self) -> String {\n        format!("[{}{}]", self.a.iter().map(|v| v.to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "), if self.a.is_empty() { "" } else { "" })\n    }\n    pub fn w_literal(&self) -> String {\n        format!("[{}]", self.w.iter().map(|v| v.to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Integer-exact emitter for the indexed-summation IR (item 36): the `Index`/\n/// `IndexSum` nodes. Produces a Rust expression fragment (NOT wrapped in a checked\n/// `i128::try_from` — the `emit_int_indexed_rust` caller owns the fn signature and\n/// the `i32` accumulator). The emitted shape:\n///   - `Sym("a")` / `Sym("w")` → the `&[i8]` array parameter (base address).\n///   - `Index { array, idx }` → `{array}[({idx}) as usize]` (bounds-checked at the\n///     emitted loop body via `get`/`expect` — see `IndexSum`).\n///   - `IndexSum { var, len, body }` →\n///       `{{ let mut acc: i32 = 0i32; for {var} in 0..{len} {{ let {var}_a = a[{var} as usize]; let {var}_w = w[{var} as usize]; let term: i32 = (({var}_a as i32).checked_mul({var}_w as i32).ok_or("overflow in indexed product")?); acc = acc.checked_add(term).ok_or("overflow in indexed sum")?; }} acc }}`\n///     The trip count is the build-time `len`, so the loop is cyclomatic-1. Emit it as a Rust i32 expression; the loop folds each trip's\n            // product into the i32 accumulator. The trip count is the build-time\n            // `len`, so the emitted loop is cyclomatic-1. Every add/mul is checked\n            // and `?`-propagated (fail-closed, mirroring `apply_tax`).\n            let body_s = emit_int_indexed_checked(body)?;\n            Ok(format!(\n                "{{ let mut acc: i32 = 0i32; for {var} in 0..{len} {{ let term: i32 = ({body_s}); acc = acc.checked_add(term).ok_or(\\"overflow in indexed sum\\")?; }} acc }}"\n            ))\n        }\n        _ => Err(IntEmissionUnsupported(format!(\n            "node {:?} is not part of the indexed-summation IR (item 36) — use the scalar emitters for non-indexed expressions",\n            expr\n        ))),\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod unit_tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn quad_emits_expected_shape() {\n        let (a, b, c, x) = (Expr::sym("a"), Expr::sym("b"), Expr::sym("c"), String::from_utf8_lossy(&run.stdout).trim().to_string()\n}\n\nfn env(pairs: &[(&str, f64)]) -> HashMap<String, f64> {\n    pairs.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), *v)).collect()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn (any arithmetic operator / anything resembling subtotal/total derivation),\n//! and NO status-branching on\n//! `next_status`. The grep gate `r11_thin_shell_grep_gate` enforces this at\n//! `cargo test` time. The only kernel shape the server parses is the order `id`\n//! field (the store key), and that single shallow read is the documented\n//! exception.\n\nuse std::sync::{\n    atomic::{AtomicI64, Ordering},\n    Arc, Mutex,\n};\n\nuse axum::{\n    body::Bytes,\n    extract::{Path, Request, State},\n    http::{header, HeaderMap, StatusCode},\n    middleware::{self, Next},\n    response::{IntoResponse, Response},\n    routing::{get, post},\n    Json, Router,\n};\nuse base64::Engine;\nuse dowiz_kernel::json_api;\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::{\n    cap::{revocation_hash, verify_chain, SignatureVerifier},\n};\n\n// Re-export kernel types the integration tests construct (cap-gated frames,\n// rosters, revocation sets). No new crypto — these are the kernel's own types.\npub use dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::cap::{\n    AnchorRoster, Capability, ChainError, Delegation, RefSigner, RevocationSet, SignedFrame,\n};\npub use dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::scope::{Action, Resource, Scope};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse sha2::{Digest, Sha256};\n\n// ── Route table (axum 0.8 `{id}` capture syntax) ────────────────────────────\n\npub const ROUTE_HEALTH: &str = "/healthz";\npub const ROUTE_ORDER_PLACE: &str = "/api/order";\npub const ROUTE_ORDER_READ: &str = "/api/order/{id}";\npub const ROUTE_ORDER_ADVANCE: &str = "/api/order/{id}/advance";\n/// P40 W-a: the agent turn route. Proxied (DECART-B) to a sibling `agent-loop`\n/// service; this crate stays zero-OCI (no `agent-loop`/`llm-adapters` dep).\npub const ROUTE_AGENT: &str = "/api/agent";\n\n/// Capability-certificate header (base64 of a serialized `SignedFrame`).\npub const CAP_HEADER: &str = "x-dowiz-cap";\n/// Body size ceiling (order JSON ≪ 4 KiB). Above this → 413.\npub const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;\n/// API concurrency bulkhead (§4.3): caps concurrent in-flight API requests.\npub const MAX_INFLIGHT_API: usize = 64;\n/// Cap-frame freshness window (replay layer 1): a frame older than now − this is\n/// rejected (epoch skew).\npub const EPOCH_SKEW_SECS: u64 = 300;\n/// In-window replay ring size (replay layer 2): duplicate frame digests within\n/// the window are rejected.\npub const SEEN_DIGEST_RING: usize = 4096;\n\n/// Base64 engine for the capability header (standard alphabet, no padding).\nconst B64: base64::engine::GeneralPurpose = base64::engine::GeneralPurpose::new(\n    &base64::alphabet::STANDARD,\n    base64::engine::GeneralPurposeConfig::new()\n        .with_encode_padding(false)\n        .with_decode_padding_mode(base64::engine::DecodePaddingMode::Indifferent),\n);\n\n/// Request bodies — the ONLY serde shapes the shell owns. Order JSON is relayed\n/// RAW to the kernel as an opaque String (`items_json` / `order_json`); the\n/// server never inspects order semantics.\n#[derive(Deserialize)]\npub struct PlaceOrderBody {\n    pub customer_id: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(rename = "items_json")]\n    pub items_json: String,\n    pub channel: Option<String>,\n}\n#[derive(Deserialize)]\npub struct AdvanceBody {\n    /// Kernel vocabulary (e.g. "CONFIRMED"). Relayed verbatim; the kernel rejects\n    /// illegal edges.\n    pub next_status: String,\n}\n\n/// P40 W-a request body for one agent turn. The agent has NO money tool, so the\n/// prompt must never carry an instruction the kernel would act on — this shell\n/// only forwards the bytes to the sibling agent service (thin proxy).\n#[derive(Deserialize)]\npub struct AgentRequest {\n    pub prompt: String,\n}\n\n/// P40 W-a response: the sibling service's typed `LoopOutcome`, relayed verbatim.\n/// `outcome` is one of "answer" | "unavailable" | "cap_exceeded" |\n/// "tool_calling_unsupported". NO money vocabulary appears here (P54 firewall).\n#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct AgentResponse {\n    pub outcome: String,\n    pub text: Option<String>,\n    pub log: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// Volatile, event-sourced order record. State is ALWAYS fold-derived: it holds\n/// the kernel's latest serialized order (opaque) + the append-only status-event\n/// list (the spine tests assert on).\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct OrderRecord {\n    pub order_json: String,\n    pub status_events: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct EventStore {\n    inner: Mutex<std::collections::HashMap<String, OrderRecord>>,\n}\n\nimpl EventStore {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    pub fn insert(&self, id: String, rec: OrderRecord) {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().insert(id, rec);\n    }\n\n    pub fn get(&self, id: &str) -> Option<OrderRecord> {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().get(id).cloned()\n    }\n\n    pub fn update(&self, id: &str, f: impl FnOnce(&mut OrderRecord)) {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        if let Some(r) = g.get_mut(id) {\n            f(r);\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().len()\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.len() == 0\n    }\n}\n\n/// HTTP rejection taxonomy — total, fail-closed. Every arm names its status.\npub enum ApiReject {\n    Unauthorized, // 401 — missing/unparseable/forged cap frame\n    Forbidden,    // 403 — revoked, expired epoch, or scope mismatch\n    NotFound,     // 404 — unknown order id\n    KernelReject(String), // 409 — kernel refused (illegal edge, money law)\n    Malformed,    // 400 — body fails serde before any kernel call\n    TooLarge,     // 413 — > MAX_BODY_BYTES\n    Replayed,     // 409 — duplicate frame digest inside the window\n    Upstream(String), // 502 — sibling agent service unreachable / bad reply (P40)\n}\n\nimpl ApiReject {\n    fn status(&self) -> StatusCode {\n        match self {\n            ApiReject::Unauthorized => StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,\n            ApiReject::Forbidden => StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,\n            ApiReject::NotFound => StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,\n            ApiReject::KernelReject(_) => StatusCode::CONFLICT,\n            ApiReject::Malformed => StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,\n            ApiReject::TooLarge => StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE,\n            ApiReject::Replayed => StatusCode::CONFLICT,\n            ApiReject::Upstream(_) => StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,\n        }\n    }\n    fn body(&self) -> String {\n        match self {\n            ApiReject::KernelReject(m) => m.clone(),\n            ApiReject::Unauthorized => "unauthorized: missing or forged capability cert".into(),\n            ApiReject::Forbidden => "forbidden: revoked / expired / scope mismatch".into(),\n            ApiReject::NotFound => "not found".into(),\n            ApiReject::Malformed => "malformed request body".into(),\n            ApiReject::TooLarge => "payload too large".into(),\n            ApiReject::Replayed => "replayed request frame".into(),\n            ApiReject::Upstream(m) => format!("agent service unavailable: {m}"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl IntoResponse for ApiReject {\n    fn into_response(self) -> Response {\n        (self.status(), self.body()).into_response()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Capability check seam (W37-3). The default impl wraps the kernel's own\n/// `verify_chain` + `RevocationSet` with the deterministic `RefSigner` injected\n/// for tests; production injects the real hybrid Ed25519⊕ML-DSA-65 verifier\n/// behind this SAME trait (P34). Deny-by-default: constructed explicitly with a\n/// roster + revocations + verifier (no "no-auth" constructor to misuse).\npub trait CapVerifier: Send + Sync + 'static {\n    /// `frame` = decoded CAP_HEADER bytes (a serialized `SignedFrame`);\n    /// `body_digest` = SHA-256 of the exact request body bytes; `route` = the\n    /// matched ROUTE_* const (scope binding); `now_epoch` = server unix seconds.\n    /// Ok(()) admits; Err carries the 401/403 split. The adapter binds\n    /// `(route ‖ body_digest ‖ epoch)` so a frame minted for READ cannot drive\n    /// ADVANCE and a frame for body A cannot authorize body B.\n    fn check(\n        &self,\n        frame: &[u8],\n        body_digest: &[u8; 32],\n        route: &'static str,\n        now_epoch: u64,\n    ) -> Result<(), ApiReject>;\n}\n\n/// The kernel-backed capability verifier (W37-3). Reuses\n/// `ports/agent/cap.rs::verify_chain` + `RevocationSet` + `DOMAIN_FRAME` signing\n/// domain, generic over `SignatureVerifier` exactly as the kernel already is.\npub struct KernelCapVerifier<V: SignatureVerifier + 'static> {\n    pub verifier: V,\n    pub roster: AnchorRoster,\n    pub revocations: RevocationSet,\n}\n\nimpl<V: SignatureVerifier + Send + Sync + 'static> KernelCapVerifier<V> {\n    pub fn new(verifier: V, roster: AnchorRoster, revocations: RevocationSet) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            verifier,\n            roster,\n            revocations,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Decode a base64 capability header into a `SignedFrame`.\n    fn decode_frame(frame_b64: &[u8]) -> Result<SignedFrame, ApiReject> {\n        let raw = B64\n            .decode(frame_b64)\n            .map_err(|_| ApiReject::Unauthorized)?;\n        serde_json::from_slice::<SignedFrame>(&raw).map_err(|_| ApiReject::Unauthorized)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<V: SignatureVerifier + Send + Sync + 'static> CapVerifier for KernelCapVerifier<V> {\n    fn check(\n        &self,\n        frame_b64: &[u8],\n        body_digest: &[u8; 32],\n        route: &'static str,\n        now_epoch: u64,\n    ) -> Result<(), ApiReject> {\n        let signed = Self::decode_frame(frame_b64)?;\n\n        // Replay layer 1: epoch freshness. The frame must still be valid against\n        // `now` and within the skew window (a stale frame cannot be replayed).\n        if !signed.capability.is_fresh(now_epoch) {\n            return Err(ApiReject::Forbidden);\n        }\n        if signed.capability.expiry < now_epoch.saturating_sub(EPOCH_SKEW_SECS) {\n            return Err(ApiReject::Forbidden);\n        }\n\n        // Revocation check (forged is caught by verify_chain's BadSignature arm).\n        let cap_hash = revocation_hash(&signed.capability);\n        if self.revocations.is_revoked_capability(&cap_hash)\n            || self\n                .revocations\n                .is_revoked_key(&signed.capability.subject_key)\n        {\n            return Err(ApiReject::Forbidden);\n        }\n\n        // Scope binding: the requested route maps to a required (resource, action)\n        // pair. A frame minted for READ cannot drive ADVANCE.\n        let required = route_scope(route).ok_or(ApiReject::Forbidden)?;\n        let chain = signed.payload_as_chain().map_err(|_| ApiReject::Unauthorized)?;\n        let cap = &signed.capability;\n        // Effect must authorize the required grant.\n        if !cap.scope.grants.iter().any(|g| *g == required) {\n            return Err(ApiReject::Forbidden);\n        }\n\n        // Body binding (replay layer 0): the frame's payload carries the exact\n        // SHA-256 body digest (set by `mint_frame`, see `payload_as_chain`), so a\n        // frame minted for body A cannot authorize a different body B. The\n        // payload layout is `<u64 LE chain_json_len> || chain_json || body_digest`,\n        // so the tail 32 bytes are the bound digest.\n        let n = u64::from_le_bytes(signed.payload[..8].try_into().unwrap_or([0u8; 8]));\n        let start = 8 + n as usize;\n        if signed.payload.len() < start + 32 || &signed.payload[start..start + 32] != body_digest {\n            return Err(ApiReject::Unauthorized);\n        }\n\n        // Chain verify: root anchor + signatures + expiry + attenuation + tail\n        // binding + effect subset. Any failure → 401/403 via ChainError.\n        match verify_chain(&self.verifier, &self.roster, &chain, cap, now_epoch) {\n            Ok(()) => Ok(()),\n            Err(ChainError::BadSignature) => Err(ApiReject::Unauthorized),\n            Err(ChainError::UnknownIssuer) => Err(ApiReject::Unauthorized),\n            Err(_) => Err(ApiReject::Forbidden),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Map a route const to the required (resource, action) grant.\nfn route_scope(route: &'static str) -> Option<(Resource, Action)> {\n    match route {\n        ROUTE_ORDER_PLACE => Some((Resource::Order, Action::CreateOrder)),\n        ROUTE_ORDER_READ => Some((Resource::Order, Action::Read)),\n        ROUTE_ORDER_ADVANCE => Some((Resource::Order, Action::CreateOrder)),\n        // P40 W-b: the agent turn reuses the SAME cap gate. It reads order status\n        // via the agent's one read-only tool, so it requires (Order, Read) — the\n        // identical grant the order READ route uses. No new capability schema, no\n        // second auth path.\n        ROUTE_AGENT => Some((Resource::Order, Action::Read)),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Shared state for the API router.\npub struct ApiState {\n    pub store: Arc<EventStore>,\n    pub caps: Arc<dyn CapVerifier>,\n    /// Replay ring: seen frame digests (SHA-256 of the full cap header bytes).\n    pub seen: Mutex<std::collections::VecDeque<[u8; 32]>>,\n    /// API concurrency bulkhead counter.\n    pub inflight: AtomicI64,\n    /// P40 DECART-B: localhost `host:port` of the sibling `agent-loop` service the\n    /// `/api/agent` route proxies to. `None` disables the route (503) — the SPA\n    /// stays zero-OCI and never links the agent crate. Defaults to the service's\n    /// documented port (`127.0.0.1:8771`).\n    pub agent_upstream: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl ApiState {\n    pub fn new(store: Arc<EventStore>, caps: Arc<dyn CapVerifier>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            store,\n            caps,\n            seen: Mutex::new(std::collections::VecDeque::with_capacity(SEEN_DIGEST_RING)),\n            inflight: AtomicI64::new(0),\n            agent_upstream: Some("127.0.0.1:8771".to_string()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Override the sibling agent-loop service upstream (host:port). Used by the\n    /// integration test to point the proxy at a scripted localhost double.\n    pub fn with_agent_upstream(mut self, upstream: Option<String>) -> Self {\n        self.agent_upstream = upstream;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Build the default (production-shaped) API state. The capability verifier\n    /// starts with an EMPTY anchor roster — fail-closed: until P34 enrolls real\n    /// anchors / injects the canonical hybrid verifier behind this same trait,\n    /// every `/api/*` request is rejected (401/403). This is intentional: an\n    /// unconfigured server admits no orders.\n    pub fn build_default() -> Arc<ApiState> {\n        let store = Arc::new(EventStore::new());\n        let caps: Arc<dyn CapVerifier> = Arc::new(KernelCapVerifier::new(\n            RefSigner,\n            AnchorRoster::new(),\n            RevocationSet::new(),\n        ));\n        Arc::new(ApiState::new(store, caps))\n    }\n\n    /// Record a frame digest in the replay ring; reject if already seen.\n    fn check_replay(&self, digest: [u8; 32]) -> Result<(), ApiReject> {\n        let mut ring = self.seen.lock().unwrap();\n        if ring.contains(&digest) {\n            return Err(ApiReject::Replayed);\n        }\n        ring.push_back(digest);\n        if ring.len() > SEEN_DIGEST_RING {\n            ring.pop_front();\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Middleware: capability check BEFORE any handler runs. Fail-closed — a missing\n/// / invalid / revoked / scope-mismatched cert answers 401/403 with ZERO writes\n/// to the store. The handlers take no "body" extraction that would run before\n/// this; the body digest is computed here from the raw bytes.\nasync fn cap_middleware(\n    State(state): State<Arc<ApiState>>,\n    mut req: Request,\n    next: Next,\n) -> Result<Response, ApiReject> {\n    // Bulkhead: reject if too many API requests are in flight (§4.3).\n    let inflight = state\n        .inflight\n        .fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst)\n        .saturating_add(1);\n    if inflight as usize > MAX_INFLIGHT_API {\n        state.inflight.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        return Err(ApiReject::TooLarge);\n    }\n    let _guard = scopeguard_dec(&state);\n\n    let route = matched_route(&req);\n\n    // Liveness probe: /healthz is OPEN (no capability required). Bypass all cap\n    // checks and replay bookkeeping for it so a monitoring system can reach it\n    // without a cert. Every other API route is cap-gated below (fail-closed).\n    if route == ROUTE_HEALTH {\n        return Ok(next.run(req).await);\n    }\n\n    // Read the cap header (base64 of a serialized SignedFrame).\n    let cap_hdr = req\n        .headers()\n        .get(CAP_HEADER)\n        .ok_or(ApiReject::Unauthorized)?\n        .to_str()\n        .map_err(|_| ApiReject::Unauthorized)?\n        .as_bytes()\n        .to_vec();\n\n    // Capture the raw body so we can compute its digest AND re-inject it for the\n    // handler. Body limit is enforced by tower's `DefaultBodyLimit` on the\n    // sub-router; this read is bounded by that layer.\n    let body_bytes = axum::body::to_bytes(std::mem::take(req.body_mut()), MAX_BODY_BYTES + 1)\n        .await\n        .map_err(|_| ApiReject::TooLarge)?;\n    if body_bytes.len() > MAX_BODY_BYTES {\n        return Err(ApiReject::TooLarge);\n    }\n\n    // Replay layer 2: frame digest ring (over the raw cap header bytes).\n    let frame_digest = sha256(&cap_hdr);\n    state.check_replay(frame_digest)?;\n\n    // Body digest for the scope binding.\n    let body_digest = sha256(&body_bytes);\n\n    // Capability check (now_epoch = monotonic seconds since process start; for\n    // test determinism we use a fixed epoch clock via a simple monotonic counter\n    // anchored at construction — but we use system time here for realism; the\n    // tests inject frames with `expiry` far in the future so any sane `now`\n    // passes the freshness check).\n    let now = now_epoch();\n\n    state\n        .caps\n        .check(&cap_hdr, &body_digest, route, now)\n        .map_err(|e| {\n            // On rejection, the frame digest must NOT remain in the ring (it was a\n            // failed attempt, not a satisfied request) — but a genuine *replay*\n            // must be caught. We leave the digest in the ring so a re-send is\n            // rejected as replayed; the failed-auth response still dominates.\n            e\n        })?;\n\n    // Put the body back for the handler.\n    *req.body_mut() = axum::body::Body::from(body_bytes);\n    Ok(next.run(req).await)\n}\n\n/// Tiny RAII decrement for the bulkhead counter.\nstruct BulkheadGuard<'a> {\n    state: &'a ApiState,\n}\nfn scopeguard_dec(state: &ApiState) -> BulkheadGuard<'_> {\n    BulkheadGuard { state }\n}\nimpl<'a> Drop for BulkheadGuard<'a> {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        self.state.inflight.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Resolve the matched route const for a request (used for scope binding).\nfn matched_route(req: &Request) -> &'static str {\n    let path = req.uri().path();\n    let method = req.method();\n    if method == axum::http::Method::GET && path == ROUTE_HEALTH {\n        return ROUTE_HEALTH;\n    }\n    if method == axum::http::Method::POST && path == ROUTE_ORDER_PLACE {\n        return ROUTE_ORDER_PLACE;\n    }\n    if method == axum::http::Method::POST && path == ROUTE_AGENT {\n        return ROUTE_AGENT;\n    }\n    if method == axum::http::Method::GET && path.starts_with("/api/order/") && path.ends_with("/advance") == false {\n        // /api/order/{id} — but guard against the advance suffix.\n        return ROUTE_ORDER_READ;\n    }\n    if method == axum::http::Method::POST && path.ends_with("/advance") {\n        return ROUTE_ORDER_ADVANCE;\n    }\n    // Fallback (e.g. healthz GET handled separately above); default to read scope\n    // is wrong — return a sentinel that maps to None so the middleware fails\n    // closed. We use ROUTE_HEALTH which maps to None scope → Forbidden for any\n    // non-API path, which is correct (static paths need no cap).\n    ROUTE_HEALTH\n}\n\n// ── Handlers (relays only — NO order/money logic) ───────────────────────────\n\n/// `POST /api/order` — place an order. Cap-gated.\nasync fn place_order_handler(\n    State(state): State<Arc<ApiState>>,\n    bytes: Bytes,\n) -> Result<(StatusCode, String), ApiReject> {\n    let body: PlaceOrderBody =\n        serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|_| ApiReject::Malformed)?;\n    let order_json = json_api::place_order_logic(body.customer_id, &body.items_json, body.channel)\n        .map_err(ApiReject::KernelReject)?;\n    // Single shallow read: extract the kernel-returned id to key the store.\n    let id = extract_id(&order_json)?;\n    state.store.insert(\n        id,\n        OrderRecord {\n            order_json: order_json.clone(),\n            status_events: vec!["PENDING".to_string()],\n        },\n    );\n    Ok((StatusCode::CREATED, order_json))\n}\n\n/// `GET /api/order/{id}` — read an order. Cap-gated.\nasync fn read_order_handler(\n    State(state): State<Arc<ApiState>>,\n    Path(id): Path<String>,\n) -> Result<String, ApiReject> {\n    let rec = state.store.get(&id).ok_or(ApiReject::NotFound)?;\n    Ok(rec.order_json)\n}\n\n/// `POST /api/order/{id}/advance` — apply an event. Cap-gated.\nasync fn advance_order_handler(\n    State(state): State<Arc<ApiState>>,\n    Path(id): Path<String>,\n    bytes: Bytes,\n) -> Result<String, ApiReject> {\n    let body: AdvanceBody = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|_| ApiReject::Malformed)?;\n    // Load the current order. On a kernel reject the record is UNTOUCHED.\n    let current = state.store.get(&id).ok_or(ApiReject::NotFound)?;\n    let updated = json_api::apply_event_logic(&current.order_json, &body.next_status)\n        .map_err(ApiReject::KernelReject)?;\n    // Commit: replace order_json + append the status event.\n    state.store.update(&id, |r| {\n        r.order_json = updated.clone();\n        r.status_events.push(body.next_status.clone());\n    });\n    Ok(updated)\n}\n\n/// `GET /healthz` — in-router liveness probe (promoted from the out-of-band\n/// `health_response()`, lib.rs:113-122).\nasync fn healthz_handler() -> &'static str {\n    "ok"\n}\n\n/// `POST /api/agent` — P40 W-a/W-b THIN PROXY (DECART-B). The cap middleware has\n/// ALREADY run `verify_chain` (same gate as the order API — no second auth path)\n/// before this handler; here we only forward the prompt to the sibling\n/// `agent-loop` service and relay its typed `AgentResponse`. This shell owns NO\n/// agent/FSM/money logic — it never links `agent-loop`/`llm-adapters` (the SPA\n/// binary stays zero-OCI). The bound (`MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS` + `TokenBucket`)\n/// lives entirely in the sibling process.\nasync fn agent_handler(\n    State(state): State<Arc<ApiState>>,\n    bytes: Bytes,\n) -> Result<(StatusCode, [(header::HeaderName, &'static str); 1], String), ApiReject> {\n    // Validate the body shape (thin: prompt-only) before forwarding.\n    let _req: AgentRequest = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|_| ApiReject::Malformed)?;\n    let upstream = state\n        .agent_upstream\n        .clone()\n        .ok_or_else(|| ApiReject::Upstream("agent route disabled".into()))?;\n\n    // Forward the RAW body to the sibling service over localhost and relay its\n    // reply verbatim. Blocking std TcpStream on a spawn-blocking thread so the\n    // async runtime is never blocked (no new HTTP-client dependency).\n    let body_vec = bytes.to_vec();\n    let reply = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || forward_to_agent(&upstream, &body_vec))\n        .await\n        .map_err(|e| ApiReject::Upstream(format!("proxy task: {e}")))?\n        .map_err(ApiReject::Upstream)?;\n\n    // Validate it is a typed AgentResponse (fail-closed on a garbage upstream).\n    let _typed: AgentResponse =\n        serde_json::from_str(&reply).map_err(|_| ApiReject::Upstream("bad agent reply".into()))?;\n\n    Ok((\n        StatusCode::OK,\n        [(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/json")],\n        reply,\n    ))\n}\n\n/// Forward the agent request body to the sibling service and return its JSON body.\n/// Std-only HTTP/1.1 over `TcpStream` — no reqwest/hyper client added to the SPA.\nfn forward_to_agent(upstream: &str, body: &[u8]) -> Result<String, String> {\n    use std::io::{Read, Write};\n    use std::net::TcpStream;\n    use std::time::Duration;\n\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(upstream).map_err(|e| format!("connect {upstream}: {e}"))?;\n    stream\n        .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(30)))\n        .ok();\n    stream\n        .set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(30)))\n        .ok();\n    let req = format!(\n        "POST /agent HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: {upstream}\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n",\n        body.len()\n    );\n    stream\n        .write_all(req.as_bytes())\n        .map_err(|e| format!("write head: {e}"))?;\n    stream.write_all(body).map_err(|e| format!("write body: {e}"))?;\n    stream.flush().ok();\n\n    let mut buf = Vec::new();\n    stream\n        .read_to_end(&mut buf)\n        .map_err(|e| format!("read: {e}"))?;\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf);\n    match text.split_once("\\r\\n\\r\\n") {\n        Some((_, body)) => Ok(body.to_string()),\n        None => Err("malformed upstream response".into()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// The one permitted shallow read: pull Serves a `--root` directory on\n//! port 8080 (default) with:\n//!\n//! * SPA fallback: unknown non-asset routes resolve to `index.html`.\n//! * `/assets/` long-cache: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.\n//! * The exact security headers ported 1:1 from `docker/nginx-default.conf`.\n//! * gzip/deflate (and precompressed `.gz`/`.br`/`.zz`) compression for text.\n//! * HTTP/1.1 by default; HTTP/2 when a TLS cert is supplied.\n//! * A minimal cap-gated order API (P37) merged on top — see `api`.\n//!\n//! Configuration is via CLI flags / env vars only — there are NO secret reads\n//! and no `.env` loading. NO-COURIER-SCORING guard is asserted below.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::net::IpAddr;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\nuse std::time::Instant;\n\nuse axum::{\n    extract::Request,\n    http::{header, HeaderName, HeaderValue, StatusCode},\n    middleware::Next,\n    response::Response,\n    Router,\n};\nuse tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};\n\n/// The minimal HTTP order surface (P37 W37-2/3): cap-gated `/api/order*`.\npub mod api;\n\n/// P48-INTAKE Phase 1 — `/webhook/*` route handlers (external signature gate,\n/// NOT capability-cert gated — separate trust boundary per §5.3).\npub mod webhook;\n\n/// DEFAULT_ROOT mirrors the legacy nginx web root.\npub const DEFAULT_ROOT: &str = "/usr/share/nginx/html";\n/// DEFAULT_PORT mirrors the nginx `listen 8080`.\npub const DEFAULT_PORT: u16 = 8080;\n\n/// Hard cap on concurrently-accepted TCP connections (defense-in-depth, listener-wide).\n/// Sized well above `api::MAX_INFLIGHT_API` (64) to allow static-asset traffic headroom,\n/// but bounded so an accept-time flood cannot grow the task count without limit.\n/// Rationale: 512 covers a single browser's concurrent-connection ceiling (~6–8) across\n/// many users, with headroom for Keep-Alive reuse; a deliberate choice to leave room for\n/// the existing per-API bulkhead to be the tighter bound for /api/* traffic.\npub const MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS: usize = 512;\n\n/// EXACT security headers ported from `docker/nginx-default.conf` (lines 16-25).\n///\n/// These are applied to EVERY response via [`security_headers`] middleware,\n/// matching nginx `add_header ... always;` semantics (always = on error\n/// responses too).\npub const SECURITY_HEADERS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[\n    (\n        "Content-Security-Policy",\n        "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests",\n    ),\n    ("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff"),\n    ("X-Frame-Options", "DENY"),\n    ("Referrer-Policy", "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"),\n    (\n        "Permissions-Policy",\n        "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=(), payment=()",\n    ),\n];\n\n/// Axum middleware: attach the EXACT ported security headers to every response.\npub async fn security_headers(request: Request, next: Next) -> Response {\n    let mut response = next.run(request).await;\n    // Reset to avoid duplicate appends if a layer is stacked (idempotent set).\n    for (name, value) in SECURITY_HEADERS {\n        insert_header(response.headers_mut(), name, value);\n    }\n    response\n}\n\n/// Axum middleware: mirror nginx `location /assets/ { add_header Cache-Control\n/// "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"; }`. Any request path under `/assets/`\n/// gets the EXACT immutable long-cache header.\npub async fn asset_cache_control(request: Request, next: Next) -> Response {\n    let is_asset = request.uri().path().starts_with("/assets/");\n    let mut response = next.run(request).await;\n    if is_asset {\n        if let Ok(v) = HeaderValue::from_str("public, max-age=31536000, immutable") {\n            response\n                .headers_mut()\n                .insert(HeaderName::from_static("cache-control"), v);\n        }\n    }\n    response\n}\n\n/// Insert a header by name (case-insensitive) into a `HeaderMap`, parsing the\n/// name as bytes so mixed-case literal names (e.g. `Content-Security-Policy`)\n/// are accepted. `HeaderName::from_static` would reject them.\nfn insert_header(headers: &mut header::HeaderMap, name: &str, value: &str) {\n    if let (Ok(n), Ok(v)) = (\n        header::HeaderName::from_bytes(name.as_bytes()),\n        HeaderValue::from_str(value),\n    ) {\n        headers.insert(n, v);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build the application router for a given static root directory.\n///\n/// * `ServeDir` handles real files (with precompressed variants).\n/// * `ServeFile` of `index.html` is the SPA fallback for unknown routes\n///   (mirrors nginx `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html`).\n/// * The cap-gated order API (P37) is merged on top — its middleware runs only\n///   on the `/api/*` + `/healthz` routes, so static serving is byte-unchanged.\npub fn build_router(root: impl AsRef<Path>, api: Arc<api::ApiState>, webhook_state: Arc<webhook::WebhookState>) -> Router {\n    let root = root.as_ref().to_path_buf();\n    let index = root.join("index.html");\n    let serve_dir = ServeDir::new(&root)\n        .precompressed_gzip()\n        .precompressed_br()\n        .precompressed_deflate()\n        .fallback(ServeFile::new(index));\n\n    Router::new()\n        .fallback_service(serve_dir)\n        .merge(api::build_api_router(api))\n        .merge(webhook::build_webhook_router(webhook_state))\n        .layer(axum::middleware::from_fn(asset_cache_control))\n        .layer(axum::middleware::from_fn(security_headers))\n}\n\n/// Resolve the static root from CLI/env, falling back to [`DEFAULT_ROOT`].\npub fn resolve_root(explicit: Option<PathBuf>) -> PathBuf {\n    explicit.unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(DEFAULT_ROOT))\n}\n\n/// Default header-read timeout for plain HTTP/1.1 connections. A client that has not\n/// finished sending its request headers within this window is disconnected — the\n/// standard mitigation for a slowloris-style connection-exhaustion attack (a client\n/// opens a connection and trickles headers in slowly enough to never trigger a normal\n/// request timeout while occupying one of the [`api::MAX_INFLIGHT_API`] bulkhead slots\n/// or a bare listener socket indefinitely). Matches hyper-util's own documented default.\npub const DEFAULT_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(10);\n\n/// Per-IP connection admission state. Each distinct source IP gets a\n/// [`dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::TokenBucket`] that admits at most `CAPACITY` burst\n/// connections with a sustained `REFILL_PER_SEC` rate. Idle entries are evicted by\n/// `sweep_locked` on every `admit` call to bound map growth from many distinct IPs\n/// (each of which DID complete a real TCP handshake, so IP spoofing at this layer is\n/// naturally constrained by the OS TCP stack).\npub struct PerIpLimiter {\n    buckets: Mutex<HashMap<IpAddr, (dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::TokenBucket, Instant)>>,\n}\n\nimpl PerIpLimiter {\n    /// Burst capacity per IP — generous for a real browser opening several asset\n    /// connections at once, tight against a single-source connection flood.\n    pub const CAPACITY: f64 = 8.0;\n    /// Sustained refill rate per IP (tokens/sec).\n    pub const REFILL_PER_SEC: f64 = 2.0;\n    /// Entries idle longer than this are evicted to bound map growth.\n    pub const IDLE_EVICT_AFTER: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(300);\n\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        PerIpLimiter {\n            buckets: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Try to admit a connection from `ip`. Returns `true` if the per-IP budget\n    /// allows it, `false` if throttled (caller should drop the connection).\n    pub fn admit(&self, ip: IpAddr) -> bool {\n        let mut m = self.buckets.lock().unwrap();\n        self.sweep_locked(&mut m);\n        let (bucket, seen) = m.entry(ip).or_insert_with(|| {\n            (\n                dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::TokenBucket::new(Self::CAPACITY, Self::REFILL_PER_SEC),\n                Instant::now(),\n            )\n        });\n        *seen = Instant::now();\n        bucket.try_acquire(1.0, dowiz_kernel::clock::now_ns())\n    }\n\n    /// Evict entries idle past `IDLE_EVICT_AFTER` — bounds map growth from many\n    /// distinct IPs. Called inside `admit` while the lock is already held.\n    fn sweep_locked(&self, m: &mut HashMap<IpAddr, (dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::TokenBucket, Instant)>) {\n        m.retain(|_, (_, seen)| seen.elapsed() < Self::IDLE_EVICT_AFTER);\n    }\n\n    /// Return the number of tracked IPs (for tests / diagnostics).\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.buckets.lock().unwrap().len()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Serve `router` over plain HTTP/1.1 on an already-bound `listener`, with a bounded\n/// header-read timeout per connection and listener-wide DoS defenses.\n///\n/// Two defense-in-depth layers guard the accept loop:\n/// 1. **Per-IP rate limiting** ([`PerIpLimiter`]) — a [`dowiz_kernel::token_bucket::TokenBucket`]\n///    per source IP admits at most `CAPACITY` burst / `REFILL_PER_SEC` sustained connections;\n///    checked first (cheapest, rejects a flood before touching the global cap).\n/// 2. **Global concurrent-connection cap** ([`MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS`]) — a\n///    [`tokio::sync::Semaphore`] that fail-closes (drops the connection immediately, never\n///    blocks the accept loop) when the server is at capacity.\n///\n/// Both layers are defense-in-depth alongside the existing `api::MAX_INFLIGHT_API` bulkhead\n/// (which only sees connections that finish header parsing — a stalled mid-header connection\n/// never reaches it). Neither new layer replaces or interferes with the existing layers.\npub async fn serve_with_timeout(\n    listener: tokio::net::TcpListener,\n    router: Router,\n    header_read_timeout: std::time::Duration,\n) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let conn_limit = std::sync::Arc::new(tokio::sync::Semaphore::new(MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS));\n    let ip_limiter = std::sync::Arc::new(PerIpLimiter::new());\n    loop {\n        let (stream, peer) = listener.accept().await?;\n        // Layer 1: per-IP admission — cheapest check, rejects a single-source flood\n        // before touching the global cap. A throttled connection is dropped immediately.\n        if !ip_limiter.admit(peer.ip()) {\n            eprintln!(\n                "[native-spa-server] per-IP connection budget ({}/{} burst, {}/s sustained) \\\n                 exhausted for {peer}, dropping connection",\n                PerIpLimiter::CAPACITY as u64,\n                PerIpLimiter::CAPACITY as u64,\n                PerIpLimiter::REFILL_PER_SEC as u64,\n            );\n            continue;\n        }\n        // Layer 2: global cap — fail-CLOSED, not blocking: if the semaphore is\n        // saturated, drop this connection immediately (RST on stream-drop) rather\n        // than queueing it — queueing would just move the exhaustion from "tasks"\n        // to "an unbounded internal queue". The accept loop is NEVER blocked, so\n        // legitimate new connections are never stuck behind a saturated cap.\n        let permit = match conn_limit.clone().try_acquire_owned() {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(_) => {\n                eprintln!(\n                    "[native-spa-server] global connection cap ({MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS}) \\\n                     reached, dropping connection from {peer}"\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n        };\n        let router = router.clone();\n        tokio::spawn(async move {\n            let _permit = permit; // held for the connection's lifetime, released on task exit\n            let hyper_service = hyper_util::service::TowerToHyperService::new(router);\n            let mut builder =\n                hyper_util::server::conn::auto::Builder::new(hyper_util::rt::TokioExecutor::new());\n            builder\n                .http1()\n                .timer(hyper_util::rt::TokioTimer::new())\n                .header_read_timeout(header_read_timeout);\n            if let Err(e) = builder\n                .serve_connection_with_upgrades(\n                    hyper_util::rt::TokioIo::new(stream),\n                    hyper_service,\n                )\n                .await\n            {\n                // A timed-out or reset connection surfaces here as an I/O error —\n                // this is the header-read timeout doing its job, not a bug; log at\n                // most, never propagate (one bad connection must not kill the server).\n                eprintln!("[native-spa-server] connection closed: {e}");\n            }\n        });\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a 200 `index.html` response carrying the security headers. Used by the\n/// binary for an out-of-band `/healthz` liveness probe.\npub fn health_response() -> Response {\n    let mut r = Response::new(axum::body::Body::from("ok"));\n    *r.status_mut() = StatusCode::OK;\n    for (name, value) in SECURITY_HEADERS {\n        insert_header(r.headers_mut(), name, value);\n    }\n    r\n}\n	4373	-1	-1		d374fcb9598ac667f123cae714861263059ebd4e7f66b4cba1576c06d2f94d457c482203ce886e8fa55c8769e905de384e695fa7b760040ad14df208cf4d724656a93cd22562c8685403290015bfc3d959597ca86567ffc988c6a2b7b80947fd6003d36314e0d289ca184a060a4859b12c3bc5ee3f810fe317397dd419be35b8

       ..Default::default()\n    };\n\n    match state\n        .telegram\n        .verify_and_normalize(&body, &intake_headers, &hub_id)\n    {\n        Ok(messages) if messages.is_empty() => {\n let _ = state.intake.handle_inbound(msg);\n            }\n            (StatusCode::OK, Json(serde_json::json!({"ok": true, "messages": messages.len()})))\n                .into_response()\n        }\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/native-spa-server/tests/agent_route.rs	agent_route · 312 lines	//! P40 Task D — `/api/agent` proxy integration (red→green).\n//!\n//! RED `red_agent_route_absent` / `red_agent_turn_bounded`: before P40 there was\n//! NO `/api/agent` route → POST 404'd and no turn ran. GREEN:\n//!   * a cap-framed POST /api/agent → 200 + typed `AgentResponse` (outcome/text/log),\n//!   * an UNSIGNED POST → 401 (reusing the SAME `verify_chain` gate as the order API),\n//!   * the turn is BOUNDED: one POST drives exactly one upstream call within a\n//!     wall-time budget (the scripted sibling counts calls; no hang).\n//!\n//! The proxy target is a SCRIPTED localhost double (a tiny `TcpListener` thread\n//! that returns a canned `LoopOutcome` JSON) — the real sibling service is heavy\n//! and its live path needs an Ollama daemon (OPS precondition, not a code defect).\n//! This isolates the WIRING (cap gate + forward + typed relay) under test.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{SocketAddr, TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, OnceLock};\nuse std::time::{Duration, Instant};\n\nuse axum::Router;\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::cap::{RefSigner, SignatureVerifier};\nuse dowiz_kernel::ports::agent::scope::{Action, Resource};\nuse native_spa_server::api::{\n    self, AnchorRoster, ApiState, EventStore, KernelCapVerifier, RevocationSet, ROUTE_AGENT,\n};\nuse native_spa_server::build_router;\nuse native_spa_server::webhook::WebhookState;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\n\n// ── raw HTTP client (std-only; mirrors integration.rs) ──────────────────────\n\nstruct RawResponse {\n    status: u16,\n    body: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nfn http_raw(\n    addr: SocketAddr,\n    method: &str,\n    path: &str,\n    headers: &[(&str, &str)],\n    body: &[u8],\n) -> RawResponse {\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).expect("connect");\n    stream\n        .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(10)))\n        .unwrap();\n    let mut req = format!(\n        "{method} {path} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\n",\n        body.len()\n    );\n    for (k, v) in headers {\n        req.push_str(&format!("{k}: {v}\\r\\n"));\n    }\n    req.push_str("Accept: */*\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n");\n    stream.write_all(req.as_bytes()).expect("write request");\n    stream.write_all(body).expect("write body");\n\n    let mut buf = Vec::new();\n    let mut chunk = [0u8; 4096];\n    loop {\n        match stream.read(&mut chunk) {\n            Ok(0) => break,\n            Ok(n) => buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]),\n            Err(e) => panic!("read error: {e}"),\n        }\n    }\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf);\n    let status: u16 = text\n        .split_whitespace()\n        .nth(1)\n        .expect("status code")\n        .parse()\n        .expect("numeric status");\n    let body_start = buf\n        .windows(4)\n        .position(|w| w == b"\\r\\n\\r\\n")\n        .map(|p| p + 4)\n        .unwrap_or(buf.len());\n    RawResponse {\n        status,\n        body: buf[body_start.min(buf.len())..].to_vec(),\n    }\n}\n\nfn web_root() -> &'static PathBuf {\n    static ROOT: OnceLock<PathBuf> = OnceLock::new();\n    ROOT.get_or_init(|| {\n        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("nss-agent-test-{}", std::process::id()));\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("assets")).unwrap();\n        std::fs::write(dir.join("index.html"), "<!doctype html><html></html>").unwrap();\n        std::fs::write(dir.join("assets/app.js"), "console.log('app');").unwrap();\n        dir\n    })\n}\n\n/// A SCRIPTED sibling agent-loop double: binds an ephemeral localhost port and,\n/// per connection, returns a canned typed `LoopOutcome` JSON. Counts calls so the\n/// test proves EXACTLY ONE bounded turn per POST. Returns (host:port, counter).\nfn spawn_scripted_agent() -> (String, Arc<AtomicUsize>) {\n    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").expect("bind scripted agent");\n    let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();\n    let counter = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));\n    let c = Arc::clone(&counter);\n    std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        for conn in listener.incoming() {\n            let mut stream = match conn {\n                Ok(s) => s,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n            c.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            // Drain the full request (headers + body) before replying, so the\n            // proxy's two-part write (head then body) completes before we close.\n            let _ = stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_millis(500)));\n            let mut req = Vec::new();\n            let mut chunk = [0u8; 1024];\n            loop {\n                match stream.read(&mut chunk) {\n                    Ok(0) => break,\n                    Ok(n) => {\n                        req.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);\n                        // Stop once we have headers + a plausible body tail.\n                        if let Some(p) = req.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\\r\\n\\r\\n") {\n                            let cl = String::from_utf8_lossy(&req[..p])\n                                .lines()\n                                .find_map(|l| {\n                                    let (k, v) = l.split_once(':')?;\n                                    if k.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case("content-length") {\n                                        v.trim().parse::<usize>().ok()\n                                    } else {\n                                        None\n                                    }\n                                })\n                                .unwrap_or(0);\n                            if req.len() >= p + 4 + cl {\n                                break;\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => break,\n                }\n            }\n            let json = r#"{"outcome":"answer","text":"ORD-42 is IN_DELIVERY","log":["iter0: model_reply"]}"#;\n            let resp = format!(\n                "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n{}",\n                json.len(),\n                json\n            );\n            let _ = stream.write_all(resp.as_bytes());\n            let _ = stream.flush();\n        }\n    });\n    (format!("127.0.0.1:{}", addr.port()), counter)\n}\n\nfn test_api_with_anchor(upstream: Option<String>) -> (Arc<ApiState>, [u8; 32]) {\n    let secret = [0x42u8; 32];\n    let verifier = RefSigner;\n    let mut roster = AnchorRoster::new();\n    roster.enroll(&verifier.classical_public(&secret));\n    let caps = KernelCapVerifier::new(verifier, roster, RevocationSet::new());\n    let state = ApiState::new(Arc::new(EventStore::new()), Arc::new(caps))\n        .with_agent_upstream(upstream);\n    (Arc::new(state), secret)\n}\n\nfn spawn_server(api: &Arc<ApiState>) -> SocketAddr {\n    let root = web_root().clone();\n    let api = Arc::clone(api);\n    let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<SocketAddr>();\n    std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().expect("tokio runtime");\n        rt.block_on(async move {\n            let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")\n                .await\n                .expect("bind ephemeral");\n            let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();\n            let _ = tx.send(addr);\n            let router: Router = build_router(&root, api, Arc::new(WebhookState {\n                telegram: Arc::new(intake_adapters::telegram::TelegramAdapter::new("test".into())),\n                intake: Arc::new(dowiz_kernel::ports::hub_intake::IntakeService::new(vec![])),\n            }));\n            let _ = axum::serve(listener, router).await;\n        });\n    });\n    let addr = rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)).expect("bind report");\n    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(150));\n    addr\n}\n\nfn mint_cap(secret: &[u8; 32], grant: (Resource, Action), body: &[u8], expiry: u64) -> String {\n    let body_digest = {\n        use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};\n        let mut h = Sha256::new();\n        h.update(body);\n        let d: [u8; 32] = h.finalize().into();\n        d\n    };\n    let (frame, _rev) = api::mint_frame(\n        &RefSigner,\n        secret,\n        &mut AnchorRoster::new(),\n        grant,\n        &body_digest,\n        expiry,\n    );\n    api::encode_cap(&frame)\n}\n\nconst AGENT_BODY: &str = r#"{"prompt":"what is the status of ORD-42?"}"#;\nconst FAR_EPOCH: u64 = 4_000_000_000;\n\n/// GREEN: valid cap-framed POST → 200 + typed AgentResponse, driven through the\n/// SAME verify_chain gate the order API uses; exactly one bounded upstream turn.\n#[test]\nfn red_agent_turn_bounded() {\n    let (upstream, calls) = spawn_scripted_agent();\n    let (api, secret) = test_api_with_anchor(Some(upstream));\n    let addr = spawn_server(&api);\n\n    let cap = mint_cap(\n        &secret,\n        (Resource::Order, Action::Read),\n        AGENT_BODY.as_bytes(),\n        FAR_EPOCH,\n    );\n\n    let start = Instant::now();\n    let res = http_raw(\n        addr,\n        "POST",\n        ROUTE_AGENT,\n        &[("x-dowiz-cap", &cap), ("content-type", "application/json")],\n        AGENT_BODY.as_bytes(),\n    );\n    let elapsed = start.elapsed();\n\n    assert_eq!(res.status, 200, "valid cap-framed agent POST must be 200; name: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {\n    let lower = name.to_ascii_lowercase();\n    res.headers\n        .iter()\n        .find(|(k, _)| k.to_ascii_lowercase() == lower)\n        .map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())\n}\n\nfn http_raw(addr: SocketAddr, method: &str, path: &str, headers: &[(&str, &str)], body: &[u8]) -> RawResponse {\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).expect("connect");\n    stream\n        .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))\n        .unwrap();\n    let mut req = format!(\n        "{method} {path} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\n",\n        body.len()\n    );\n    for (k, v) in headers {\n        req.push_str(&format!("{k}: {v}\\r\\n"));\n    }\n    req.push_str("Accept: */*\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n");\n    stream.write_all(req.as_bytes()).expect("write request");\n    stream.write_all(body).expect("write body");\n\n    let mut buf = Vec::new();\n    let mut chunk = [0u8; 4096];\n    loop {\n        match stream.read(&mut chunk) {\n            Ok(0) => break,\n            Ok(n) => buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]),\n            Err(e) => panic!("read error: {e}"),\n        }\n    }\n    parse_response(&buf)\n}\n\n/// GET convenience wrapper.\nfn http_get(addr: SocketAddr, path: &str) -> RawResponse {\n    http_raw(addr, "GET", path, &[], &[])\n}\n\nfn parse_response(buf: &[u8]) -> RawResponse {\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(buf);\n    let mut lines = text.split("\\r\\n");\n    let status_line = lines.next().expect("status line");\n    let status: u16 = status_line\n        .split_whitespace()\n        .nth(1)\n        .expect("status code")\n        .parse()\n        .expect("numeric status");\n\n    let mut headers = Vec::new();\n    let mut body_start = buf.len();\n    for (i, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {\n        if i == 0 {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(pos) = buf.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\\r\\n\\r\\n") {\n                body_start = pos + 4;\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n        if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(':') {\n            headers.push((k.trim().to_string(), v.trim().to_string()));\n        }\n    }\n    RawResponse {\n        status,\n        headers,\n        body: buf[body_start.min(buf.len())..].to_vec(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Shared temp web root:  index.html  +  assets/app.js\nfn web_root() -> &'static PathBuf {\n    static ROOT: OnceLock<PathBuf> = OnceLock::new();\n    ROOT.get_or_init(|| {\n        let dir
