This proves the HTTP server is NOT the required\n    // path for order placement.\n    let placed = json_api::place_order_logic(None, SAMPLE_ITEMS, Some("web".into())).expect("offline place");\n    let confirmed = json_api::apply_event_logic(&placed, "CONFIRMED").expect("offline confirm");\n    let preparing = json_api::apply_event_logic(&confirmed, "PREPARING").expect("offline prep");\n\n    let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&preparing).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v["status"], "PREPARING");\n    assert_eq!(v["channel"], "web");\n\n    // Illegal edge over the offline path is also refused (kernel law, no server).\n    let bad = json_api::apply_event_logic(&placed, "DELIVERED");\n    assert!(bad.is_err(), "offline illegal edge must be refused");\n}\n\n// ── R15: header-read timeout (slowloris mitigation) ─────────────────────────\n\n/// RED before the fix: bare `axum::serve` has no header-read timeout at all — a\n/// client that opens a connection and sends only a partial request line is held\n/// open indefinitely, tying up a socket (and, at scale, the `MAX_INFLIGHT_API`\n/// bulkhead) for as long as the attacker wants. GREEN after: `serve_with_timeout`\n/// (now the real code path — see `spawn_server` above) disconnects a client that\n/// hasn't finished sending headers within the configured window. Uses a short\n/// 1s timeout (via a dedicated listener, not `spawn_server`'s 10s default) so the\n/// test itself stays fast while proving the exact mechanism production uses.\n#[test]\nfn r15_header_read_timeout_closes_stalled_connection() {\n    let root = web_root().clone();\n    let api = default_api();\n    let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<SocketAddr>();\n\n    let _handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().expect("tokio runtime");\n        rt.block_on(async move {\n            let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")\n                .await\n                .expect("bind ephemeral");\n            let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();\n            let _ = tx.send(addr);\n            let router: Router = build_router(&root, api, default_webhook());\n            let _ = native_spa_server::serve_with_timeout(\n                listener,\n                router,\n                Duration::from_secs(1),\n            )\n            .await;\n        });\n    });\n    let addr = rx\n        .recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))\n        .expect("server should bind and report addr");\n    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(150));\n\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).expect("connect");\n    // Send an incomplete request line — never send the terminating "\\r\\n\\r\\n", so\n    // the server is left waiting for the rest of the headers forever unless the\n    // timeout fires.\n    stream\n        .write_all(b"GET /healthz HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: x\\r\\n")\n        .expect("partial write");\n\n    // Poll read: before the fix this blocks/returns WouldBlock until our own\n    // deadline below expires (proving the hang); after the fix, the server closes\n    // the connection once its 1s header-read timeout fires, so `read` returns\n    // Ok(0) (EOF) or a reset error well before our generous 4s outer deadline.\n    stream\n        .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(4)))\n        .expect("set read timeout");\n    let mut buf = [0u8; 16];\n    let started = std::time::Instant::now();\n    let result = stream.read(&mut buf);\n    let elapsed = started.elapsed();\n\n    match result {\n        Ok(0) => {}                    // EOF — server closed the connection. Expected.\n        Err(_) => {}                   // Reset/refused — also an acceptable closure signal.\n        Ok(n) => panic!("expected connection close, got {n} bytes of data"),\n    }\n    assert!(\n        elapsed < Duration::from_secs(4),\n        "connection was not closed by the header-read timeout within the outer deadline \\\n         (elapsed={elapsed:?}) — the server is hanging on a stalled client exactly like the \\\n         pre-fix slowloris-vulnerable behavior"\n    );\n}\n\n// ── R19: Telegram webhook happy path + signature reject + dedup ──────────────\n\n/// R19 — Telegram webhook end-to-end:\n/// 1. Happy path: valid update + correct secret → 200, InboundMessage constructed.\n/// 2. Signature tamper: wrong secret → 401.\n/// 3. Dedup: same update_id twice → second is 200 (silent ack, not error).\n#[test]\nfn r19_telegram_webhook_end_to_end() {\n    use std::io::{Read, Write};\n\n    let root = web_root().clone();\n    let api = default_api();\n    let webhook = default_webhook();\n    let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<SocketAddr>();\n\n    let _handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().expect("tokio runtime");\n        rt.block_on(async move {\n            let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")\n                .await\n                .expect("bind ephemeral");\n            let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();\n            let _ = tx.send(addr);\n            let router: Router = build_router(&root, api, webhook);\n            let _ = native_spa_server::serve_with_timeout(\n                listener,\n                router,\n                Duration::from_secs(10),\n            )\n            .await;\n        });\n    });\n    let addr = rx\n        .recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))\n        .expect("server should bind and report addr");\n    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(150));\n\n    // Build a valid Telegram Update JSON payload.\n    let update = serde_json::json!({\n        "update_id": 1001,\n        "message": {\n            "message_id": 1,\n            "chat": {"id": 99999},\n            "date": 1690000000,\n            "text": "2 sushi"\n        }\n    })\n    .to_string();\n\n    // 1. Happy path — correct secret token.\n    {\n        let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).expect("connect");\n        stream\n            .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))\n            .unwrap();\n        let req = format!(\n            "POST /webhook/telegram/test-hub HTTP/1.1\\r\\n\\\n             Host: localhost\\r\\n\\\n             Content-Length: {}\\r\\n\\\n             X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token: test-secret\\r\\n\\\n             Content-Type: application/json\\r\\n\\\n             Connection: close\\r\\n\\\n             \\r\\n\\\n             {}",\n            update.len(),\n            update\n        );\n        stream.write_all(req.as_bytes()).expect("write");\n        let mut buf = Vec::new();\n        let mut chunk = [0u8; 4096];\n        loop {\n            match stream.read(&mut chunk) {\n                Ok(0) => break,\n                Ok(n) => buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]),\n                Err(_) => break,\n            }\n        }\n        let response = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf);\n        assert!(\n            response.contains("200 OK"),\n            "expected 200 OK for valid webhook, got: {response}"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            response.contains("\\"ok\\":true"),\n            "expected ok:true in body, got: {response}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // 2. Signature tamper — wrong secret token → 401.\n    {\n        let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).expect("connect");\n        stream\n            .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))\n            .unwrap();\n        let req = format!(\n            "POST /webhook/telegram/test-hub HTTP/1.1\\r\\n\\\n             Host: localhost\\r\\n\\\n             Content-Length: {}\\r\\n\\\n             X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token: WRONG-SECRET\\r\\n\\\n             Content-Type: application/json\\r\\n\\\n             Connection: close\\r\\n\\\n             \\r\\n\\\n             {}",\n            update.len(),\n            update\n        );\n        stream.write_all(req.as_bytes()).expect("write");\n        let mut buf = Vec::new();\n        let mut chunk = [0u8; 4096];\n        loop {\n            match stream.read(&mut chunk) {\n                Ok(0) => break,\n                Ok(n) => buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]),\n                Err(_) => break,\n            }\n        }\n        let response = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf);\n        assert!(\n            response.contains("401"),\n            "expected 401 for wrong secret, got: {response}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // 3. Dedup — same update_id twice → second is 200 (silent ack, not 400/409).\n    {\n        let send_update = || {\n            let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).expect("connect");\n            stream\n                .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))\n                .unwrap();\n            let req = format!(\n                "POST /webhook/telegram/test-hub HTTP/1.1\\r\\n\\\n                 Host: localhost\\r\\n\\\n                 Content-Length: {}\\r\\n\\\n                 X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token: test-secret\\r\\n\\\n                 Content-Type: application/json\\r\\n\\\n                 Connection: close\\r\\n\\\n                 \\r\\n\\\n                 {}",\n                update.len(),\n                update\n            );\n            stream.write_all(req.as_bytes()).expect("write");\n            let mut buf = Vec::new();\n            let mut chunk = [0u8; 4096];\n            loop {\n                match stream.read(&mut chunk) {\n                    Ok(0) => break,\n                    Ok(n) => buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]),\n                    Err(_) => break,\n                }\n            }\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf).to_string()\n        };\n        let first = send_update();\n        assert!(first.contains("200 OK"), "first send: {first}");\n        let second = send_update();\n        assert!(second.contains("200 OK"), "dedup should ack 200, got: {second}");\n    }\n}\n\n// ── R16: global concurrent-connection cap (listener-wide DoS defense) ────────\n\n/// GREEN after fix: opening `MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS + N` connections to a test\n/// server instance — each holding, not closing, by sending a partial header line —\n/// results in exactly `MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS` connections accepted (held open\n/// by the header-read timeout) and the remaining N being immediately closed by the\n/// global semaphore cap.\n#[test]\nfn r16_global_connection_cap_enforced() {\n We scan the whole api.rs for forbidden symbols but\n/// exclude the order handlers' legitimate kernel calls — the money law lives in\n/// the ORDER lane (json_api relays), never the AGENT lane. To keep the gate\n/// falsifiable and simple, we assert the agent-specific functions contain no\n/// forbidden symbol.\nfn agent_route_body(api_src: &str) -> String {\n    // Grab from the agent_handler doc/comment marker to end of forward_to_agent.\n    let start = api_src\n        .find("async fn agent_handler")\n        .expect("agent_handler must exist in api.rs (P40 W-a)");\n    let after = &api_src[start..];\n    // end at the next top-level fn that is NOT part of the agent lane.\n    let end_rel = after\n        .find("/// The one permitted shallow read")\n        .unwrap_or(after.len());\n    after[..end_rel].to_string()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn red_money_law_firewall_present() {\n    let root = repo_root();\n\n    // (1) agent-loop/src — the whole executor lane.\n    let agent_loop_src = root.join("agent-loop").join("src");\n    let mut sources = rs_sources(&agent_loop_src);\n    assert!(\n        !sources.is_empty(),\n        "agent-loop/src must contain sources (found none under {:?})",\n        agent_loop_src\n    );\n\n    // (2) the /api/agent route body in api.rs (agent lane only).\n    let api_path = root\n        .join("tools")\n        .join("native-spa-server")\n        .join("src")\n        .join("api.rs");\n    let api_src = std::fs::read_to_string(&api_path).expect("read api.rs");\n    sources.push((\n        api_path.clone(),\n        agent_route_body(&api_src),\n    ));\n\n    for (path, text) in &sources {\n        for sym in FORBIDDEN {\n            assert!(\n                !text.contains(sym),\n enum must have exactly ONE variant: OrderStatus.\n    // A money/price variant is UNREPRESENTABLE (P54 prong 1).\n    let enum_start = src\n        .find("pub enum ToolResource")\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/nfc-pod-codec/src/lib.rs	lib · 86 lines	//! dowiz NFC proof-of-delivery (PoD) codec — hardware-independent, server-side.\n//!\n//! Two layers:\n//!   * [`ndef`] — a minimal NFC Forum NDEF (v1.0) single-record External-Type codec\n//!     (the transport container any NDEF reader — a courier phone, or a Flipper Zero\n//!     in dev — reads/writes).\n//!   * [`pod`]  — the dowiz PoD payload that lives inside the record: a versioned\n//!     `(order_id: u64, issued_at: u64)` bound by a truncated keyed SHAKE256 MAC,\n//!     reusing `kernel::pq::keccak` (no new crypto).\n//!\n//! The two convenience functions below stitch them into the full on-tag byte\n//! string and back, which is exactly what a provisioning service writes to a tag\n//! and what the courier-tap ingest endpoint verifies.\n\npub mod ndef;\npub mod pod;\n\n/// The NFC Forum External Type name for a dowiz PoD tag (`<domain>:<type>`).\npub const POD_TYPE: &[u8] = b"dowiz.io:pod";\n\n/// Errors from the full encode→NDEF / NDEF→verify path.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum TagError {\n    Ndef(ndef::NdefError),\n    Pod(pod::PodError),\n}\n\nimpl From<ndef::NdefError> for TagError {\n    fn from(e: ndef::NdefError) -> Self {\n        TagError::Ndef(e)\n    }\n}\nimpl From<pod::PodError> for TagError {\n    fn from(e: pod::PodError) -> Self {\n        TagError::Pod(e)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Produce the complete NDEF byte string to burn onto a passive PoD tag.\npub fn encode_tag(order_id: u64, issued_at: u64, key: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let payload = pod::encode_payload(order_id, issued_at, key);\n    ndef::encode_external(POD_TYPE, &payload)\n}\n\n/// Parse an NDEF message read off a tag and verify the PoD proof under `key`.\npub fn decode_and_verify_tag(buf: &[u8], key: &[u8]) -> Result<pod::PodRecord, TagError> {\n    let payload = ndef::decode_external(buf, POD_TYPE)?;\n    Ok(pod::decode_and_verify(payload, key)?)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    const KEY: &[u8] = b"provisioning-key-32-bytes-000000";\n\n    #[test]\n    fn full_tag_roundtrip() {\n        let buf = encode_tag(777, 1_700_000_000, KEY);\n        // Whole tag comfortably fits an NTAG213 (144 B user memory): 3 + 12 + 33 = 48 B.\n        assert!(buf.len() <= 144, "tag payload {} B exceeds NTAG213", buf.len());\n        let rec = decode_and_verify_tag(&buf, KEY).expect("valid tag verifies");\n        assert_eq!(rec.order_id, 777);\n        assert_eq!(rec.issued_at, 1_700_000_000);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tampered_tag_payload_rejected() {\n        let mut buf = encode_tag(777, 1_700_000_000, KEY);\n        let last = buf.len() - 1;\n        buf[last] ^= 0x01; // flip a MAC byte\n        assert_eq!(\n            decode_and_verify_tag(&buf, KEY),\n            Err(TagError::Pod(pod::PodError::BadMac))\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn malformed_ndef_header_rejected() {\n        // A buffer whose NDEF header is corrupt (TNF wrong) fails at the NDEF layer,\n        // before any PoD/MAC work happens.\n        let mut buf = encode_tag(777, 1_700_000_000, KEY);\n        buf[0] = }\n}\n	4457	-1	-1		df76b65a1f0b3bf4f2116dd5a552939bb457a16a653634ca87f580d219fbc3765c5065225687ebc6954ad3aa4415ec383df107148b488e093df3f2b4068e69d7c1bd05f12d7272211795213ae791e3a1cdf1e4292d3e564e469a38b4410fb55ef9e37b47b243d2b429b49e196b684f384efd65a2ddc863019bba5db8a100a8b3

## 4474 · /root/dowiz/tools/nfc-pod-codec/src/ndef.rs · LongTerm

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/nfc-pod-codec/src/ndef.rs	ndef · 169 lines	//! Minimal NDEF record codec — single short record, NFC Forum External Type.\n//!\n//! Implemented against the NFC Forum "NFC Data Exchange Format (NDEF)" Technical\n//! Specification v1.0 (NDEF 1.0), §3 "NDEF Record". We emit exactly one record\n//! that is both Message-Begin and Message-End (a one-record message), in the\n//! Short Record (SR) form, with TNF = 0x04 (NFC Forum External Type). External\n//! type names are of the form `<domain>:<type>` (spec §3.2.6 / RTD "External Type"),\n//! which is the correct TNF for a proprietary application payload such as ours.\n//!\n//! Record byte layout (SR form, IL = 0):\n//!   byte 0 : flags|TNF  = MB(0x80) ME(0x40) CF(0x20) SR(0x10) IL(0x08) TNF(0x07)\n//!   byte 1 : TYPE LENGTH (1 byte)\n//!   byte 2 : PAYLOAD LENGTH (1 byte, because SR = 1)\n//!   [TYPE]  : TYPE LENGTH bytes\n//!   [PAYLOAD]: PAYLOAD LENGTH bytes\n//!\n//! We deliberately keep this to what the PoD use-case needs (one short external\n//! record). Multi-record messages, chunking (CF), long records, and the ID field\n//! are rejected on decode rather than silently mis-parsed.\n\n/// Type Name Format = NFC Forum External Type (NDEF 1.0 §3.2.6, value 0x04).\npub const TNF_EXTERNAL: u8 = 0x04;\n\nconst FLAG_MB: u8 = 0x80;\nconst FLAG_ME: u8 = 0x40;\nconst FLAG_CF: u8 = 0x20;\nconst FLAG_SR: u8 = 0x10;\nconst FLAG_IL: u8 = 0x08;\nconst MASK_TNF: u8 = 0x07;\n\n/// Errors returned when a byte buffer is not a well-formed single-record short\n/// external NDEF message of the shape this codec emits.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum NdefError {\n    /// Buffer ended before a complete record could be read.\n    Truncated,\n    /// Chunk flag set — chunked records are not supported here.\n    Chunked,\n    /// Not a Short Record (SR = 0). Long records are not supported here.\n    NotShortRecord,\n    /// TNF was not 0x04 (External Type).\n    WrongTnf(u8),\n    /// The record is not both Message-Begin and Message-End (i.e. not a lone\n    /// single-record message), which is all this codec accepts.\n    NotSingleRecord,\n    /// Decoded TYPE did not match the expected external type name.\n    TypeMismatch,\n}\n\n/// Encode a single short NDEF External-Type record.\n///\n/// `type_name` is the external type (e.g. `b"dowiz.io:pod"`), `payload` the record\n/// payload. Panics only on programmer error (type or payload longer than a Short\n/// Record can express, 255 bytes) — callers control both, and both are tiny here.\npub fn encode_external(type_name: &[u8], payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    assert!(type_name.len() <= u8::MAX as usize, "type name too long for SR");\n    assert!(payload.len() <= u8::MAX as usize, "payload too long for SR");\n    let flags = FLAG_MB | FLAG_ME | FLAG_SR | TNF_EXTERNAL; // IL=0, CF=0\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(3 + type_name.len() + payload.len());\n    out.push(flags);\n    out.push(type_name.len() as u8);\n    out.push(payload.len() as u8);\n    out.extend_from_slice(type_name);\n    out.extend_from_slice(payload);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Decode a single short NDEF External-Type record, verifying the type name.\n/// Returns the record payload as a borrowed slice into `buf`.\npub fn decode_external<'a>(buf: &'a [u8], expected_type: &[u8]) -> Result<&'a [u8], NdefError> {\n    // Need at least flags + type_len + payload_len.\n    if buf.len() < 3 {\n        return Err(NdefError::Truncated);\n    }\n    let flags = buf[0];\n    if flags & FLAG_CF != 0 {\n        return Err(NdefError::Chunked);\n    }\n    if flags & FLAG_SR == 0 {\n        return Err(NdefError::NotShortRecord);\n    }\n    let tnf = flags & MASK_TNF;\n    if tnf != TNF_EXTERNAL {\n        return Err(NdefError::WrongTnf(tnf));\n    }\n    // We only accept a lone record: both MB and ME must be set.\n    if flags & FLAG_MB == 0 || flags & FLAG_ME == 0 {\n        return Err(NdefError::NotSingleRecord);\n    }\n\n    let type_len = buf[1] as usize;\n    let payload_len = buf[2] as usize;\n    let mut off = 3usize;\n\n    // ID length byte only present when IL = 1; we emit IL = 0 and reject IL = 1.\n    if flags & FLAG_IL != 0 {\n        // An ID field would shift offsets; unsupported by this minimal codec.\n        return Err(NdefError::NotSingleRecord);\n    }\n\n    // TYPE field.\n    let type_end = off.checked_add(type_len).ok_or(NdefError::Truncated)?;\n    if type_end > buf.len() {\n        return Err(NdefError::Truncated);\n    }\n    let ty = &buf[off..type_end];\n    if ty != expected_type {\n        return Err(NdefError::TypeMismatch);\n    }\n    off = type_end;\n\n    // PAYLOAD field.\n    let pay_end = off.checked_add(payload_len).ok_or(NdefError::Truncated)?;\n    if pay_end > buf.len() {\n        return Err(NdefError::Truncated);\n    }\n    Ok(&buf[off..pay_end])\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn roundtrip_external_record() {\n        let ty = b"dowiz.io:pod";\n        let payload = b"\\x01\\x02\\x03\\x04";\n        let enc = encode_external(ty, payload);\n        // flags byte: MB|ME|SR|TNF04 = 0xD4\n        assert_eq!(enc[0], 0xD4);\n        assert_eq!(enc[1] as usize, ty.len());\n        assert_eq!(enc[2] as usize, payload.len());\n        let dec = decode_external(&enc, ty).expect("decodes");\n        assert_eq!(dec, payload);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_truncated_header() {\n        assert_eq!(decode_external(&[0xD4, 0x0C], b"dowiz.io:pod"), Err(NdefError::Truncated));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_truncated_payload() {\n        // Claims payload_len = 10 but supplies fewer bytes.\n        let mut enc = encode_external(b"x", b"hello");\n        enc[2] = 200; // lie about payload length\n        assert_eq!(decode_external(&enc, b"x"), Err(NdefError::Truncated));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_wrong_tnf() {\n        let mut enc = encode_external(b"x", b"y");\n        enc[0] = (enc[0] & !MASK_TNF) | 0x01; // TNF -> Well-Known\n        assert!(matches!(decode_external(&enc, b"x"), Err(NdefError::WrongTnf(0x01))));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_type_mismatch() {\n        let enc = encode_external(b"dowiz.io:pod", b"y");\n        assert_eq!(decode_external(&enc, b"evil.io:pod"), Err(NdefError::TypeMismatch));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_chunked() {\n        let mut enc = encode_external(b"x", b"y");\n        enc[0] |= FLAG_CF;\n        assert_eq!(decode_external(&enc, b"x"), Err(NdefError::Chunked));\n    }\n}\n	4475	-1	-1		43f6be5b388d396cfb0c78d4cf561021e4fab3d4ad71a469ecd2d6d681eff5e659336770c58e90878a5a142470c5ba321a6b211513498aa8a4ea22265e86e88faf3d119434fbda2319c43159e6abe5d08dd149020d32774a2e9031a0500f9301eba6d3959bcf96aff1b8ac4e3f786df904b05c269ca34a6c90f8c9103b40a951

## 4495 · /root/dowiz/tools/nfc-pod-codec/src/pod.rs · LongTerm

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/nfc-pod-codec/src/pod.rs	pod · 182 lines	//! Proof-of-Delivery (PoD) tag payload — the bytes that live INSIDE the NDEF\n//! external record and prove a courier physically tapped the venue/customer tag.\n//!\n//! Field vocabulary is bound to the kernel's real event vocabulary: the order\n//! identifier is `u64` (see `bebop2/proto-cap/src/event_dict.rs`\n//! `OrderPlacedPayload { order_id: u64, .. }`) and is encoded big-endian, the same\n//! convention as `event_dict`'s `put_u64`/`get_u64`.\n//!\n//! The "short cryptographic proof" is a keyed MAC, NOT a signature. A passive NFC\n//! tag (NTAG213 = 144 B user memory) cannot hold an ML-DSA-65 signature (3309 B),\n//! so we reuse the kernel's audited SHAKE256 (FIPS 202, `kernel::pq::keccak`) as a\n//! prefix-keyed MAC truncated to 16 bytes. No new crypto is invented: this is the\n//! same SHAKE256 the envelope/dsa layer already depends on, used in the same\n//! `SHAKE256(key || context)` shape the kernel uses in `keccak::prf` / `xof_j`.\n//!\n//! Trust model (honest scope): this MAC proves the tag was PROVISIONED by a holder\n//! of the server provisioning key and binds (order_id, issued_at) together. It is a\n//! symmetric secret verified server-side; it is a genuine tamper/forgery gate for\n//! the tag bytes, but it is NOT a public-key device-identity — that belongs to\n//! WebAuthn/FIDO2 on the auth side, not to the tag.\n\nuse dowiz_kernel::pq::keccak::shake256;\n\n/// On-tag record version. Bump if the field layout below ever changes.\npub const POD_VERSION: u8 = 1;\n\n/// Truncated-MAC length in bytes (128-bit tag: forgery prob 2^-128).\npub const MAC_LEN: usize = 16;\n\n/// Fixed field sizes: version(1) + order_id(8) + issued_at(8) + mac(16) = 33 bytes.\npub const POD_PAYLOAD_LEN: usize = 1 + 8 + 8 + MAC_LEN;\n\n/// Domain-separation tag mixed into the MAC so this key can never be confused with\n/// another SHAKE256 use of the same secret elsewhere.\nconst MAC_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"dowiz/pod-mac/v1";\n\n/// A decoded, structurally-valid PoD record (MAC not yet checked / already checked\n/// depending on the constructor).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct PodRecord {\n    pub version: u8,\n    /// Kernel order identifier (`event_dict` `order_id: u64`).\n    pub order_id: u64,\n    /// Provisioning time, unix seconds.\n    pub issued_at: u64,\n}\n\n/// Why a PoD payload was rejected.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum PodError {\n    /// Payload was not exactly `POD_PAYLOAD_LEN` bytes.\n    BadLength,\n    /// Unknown/unsupported version byte.\n    BadVersion(u8),\n    /// MAC did not verify under the provisioning key (tampered or forged).\n    BadMac,\n}\n\n/// Compute the 16-byte keyed MAC over the record fields.\n/// MAC = SHAKE256( key || MAC_DOMAIN || version || order_id_be || issued_at_be )[..16].\nfn compute_mac(key: &[u8], rec: &PodRecord) -> [u8; MAC_LEN] {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(key.len() + MAC_DOMAIN.len() + 17);\n    input.extend_from_slice(key);\n    input.extend_from_slice(MAC_DOMAIN);\n    input.push(rec.version);\n    input.extend_from_slice(&rec.order_id.to_be_bytes());\n    input.extend_from_slice(&rec.issued_at.to_be_bytes());\n    let mut out = [0u8; MAC_LEN];\n    shake256(&input, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Constant-time-ish equality for the MAC (avoids early-exit timing leak on the\n/// 16-byte compare). Length is fixed so this is a simple xor-accumulate.\nfn macs_equal(a: &[u8; MAC_LEN], b: &[u8]) -> bool {\n    if b.len() != MAC_LEN {\n        return false;\n    }\n    let mut diff = 0u8;\n    for i in 0..MAC_LEN {\n        diff |= a[i] ^ b[i];\n    }\n    diff == 0\n}\n\n/// Encode a PoD record + MAC into the 33-byte on-tag payload.\npub fn encode_payload(order_id: u64, issued_at: u64, key: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let rec = PodRecord { version: POD_VERSION, order_id, issued_at };\n    let mac = compute_mac(key, &rec);\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(POD_PAYLOAD_LEN);\n    out.push(rec.version);\n    out.extend_from_slice(&rec.order_id.to_be_bytes());\n    out.extend_from_slice(&rec.issued_at.to_be_bytes());\n    out.extend_from_slice(&mac);\n    debug_assert_eq!(out.len(), POD_PAYLOAD_LEN);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Decode + verify a PoD payload under the provisioning key. Returns the record\n/// only if the length, version, and MAC all check out.\npub fn decode_and_verify(payload: &[u8], key: &[u8]) -> Result<PodRecord, PodError> {\n    if payload.len() != POD_PAYLOAD_LEN {\n        return Err(PodError::BadLength);\n    }\n    let version = payload[0];\n    if version != POD_VERSION {\n        return Err(PodError::BadVersion(version));\n    }\n    let order_id = u64::from_be_bytes(payload[1..9].try_into().unwrap());\n    let issued_at = u64::from_be_bytes(payload[9..17].try_into().unwrap());\n    let rec = PodRecord { version, order_id, issued_at };\n    let expected = compute_mac(key, &rec);\n    if !macs_equal(&expected, &payload[17..33]) {\n        return Err(PodError::BadMac);\n    }\n    Ok(rec)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    const KEY: &[u8] = b"provisioning-key-32-bytes-000000"; // 32 bytes\n\n    #[test]\n    fn payload_length_is_fixed_33() {\n        let p = encode_payload(42, 1_700_000_000, KEY);\n        assert_eq!(p.len(), POD_PAYLOAD_LEN);\n        assert_eq!(p.len(), 33);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn roundtrip_verifies() {\n        let p = encode_payload(0xDEAD_BEEF_u64, 1_700_000_123, KEY);\n        let rec = decode_and_verify(&p, KEY).expect("valid MAC verifies");\n        assert_eq!(rec.order_id, 0xDEAD_BEEF);\n        assert_eq!(rec.issued_at, 1_700_000_123);\n        assert_eq!(rec.version, POD_VERSION);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tampered_order_id_rejected() {\n        let mut p = encode_payload(1000, 1_700_000_000, KEY);\n        p[8] ^= 0x01; // flip a byte of order_id → MAC no longer matches\n        assert_eq!(decode_and_verify(&p, KEY), Err(PodError::BadMac));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tampered_timestamp_rejected() {\n        let mut p = encode_payload(1000, 1_700_000_000, KEY);\n        p[16] ^= 0xFF; // flip a byte of issued_at\n        assert_eq!(decode_and_verify(&p, KEY), Err(PodError::BadMac));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn wrong_key_rejected() {\n        let p = encode_payload(1000, 1_700_000_000, KEY);\n        assert_eq!(\n            decode_and_verify(&p, b"different-key-32-bytes-0000000000"),\n            Err(PodError::BadMac)\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn bad_length_rejected() {\n        assert_eq!(decode_and_verify(b"too short", KEY), Err(PodError::BadLength));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn bad_version_rejected() {\n        let mut p = encode_payload(1, 2, KEY);\n        p[0] = 0xFF;\n        assert_eq!(decode_and_verify(&p, KEY), Err(PodError::BadVersion(0xFF)));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn distinct_orders_distinct_macs() {\n        let a = encode_payload(1, 100, KEY);\n        let b = encode_payload(2, 100, KEY);\n        assert_ne!(&a[17..], &b[17..], "different order_id → different MAC");\n    }\n}\n	4496	-1	-1		df76749b3d0199e57301e0dd8372130df41ba9e6677c34cf28d56cde814fe3665d4a7780d78ffe57856b95ab01fdfd388ed31f109368cc2c387732047e0ee8cf5cb554a52d5a49131519b509c6bbe93041791c3b35987f4f4fb070b0715b8715b9e2f397924b93a9a43e9e177b74ef306cf76d865e8140c3a39935e4b5a88a13

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/nfc-pod-flipper/src/main.rs	main · 121 lines	//! dowiz Proof-of-Delivery NFC reader — Flipper Zero dev-tooling app.\n//!\n//! PURPOSE (dev/test tooling, NOT production hardware): give an engineer a\n//! portable device that reads a dowiz PoD NDEF tag and prints the decoded\n//! `order_id`, so the on-tag wire format and the courier-tap read flow can be\n//! validated BEFORE production NTAG stickers or courier phones exist.\n//!\n//! HARDWARE HONESTY: this file was compiled but NOT run — there is no physical\n//! Flipper Zero in the build environment. The NFC poller callback (the part that\n//! reads bytes off a real tag) is therefore left as an explicitly-marked device\n//! seam rather than faked. The pure NDEF/PoD decode below is real and identical in\n//! wire format to the server-side `nfc-pod-codec` crate.\n\n#![no_main]\n#![no_std]\n\n// Provides the panic handler + the FAP entry/manifest machinery.\nextern crate flipperzero_rt;\n\nuse core::ffi::CStr;\n\nuse flipperzero::{error, info};\nuse flipperzero_rt::{entry, manifest};\nuse flipperzero_sys as sys;\n\n// FAP manifest (no icon, to avoid bundling an asset).\nmanifest!(name = "dowiz PoD NFC reader");\nentry!(main);\n\n/// NFC Forum External Type name for a dowiz PoD tag (`<domain>:<type>`).\nconst POD_TYPE: &[u8] = b"dowiz.io:pod";\n\n/// Fixed on-tag PoD payload length: version(1) + order_id(8) + issued_at(8) + mac(16).\nconst POD_PAYLOAD_LEN: usize = 33;\n\n// ── Pure decode (no_std, no hardware) — mirrors nfc_pod_codec::ndef/pod ──────────\n\n/// Decode a single short NDEF External-Type record and verify the type name.\n/// Returns the record payload slice, or `None` if the buffer is malformed / not a\n/// dowiz PoD tag. Wire format matches `nfc_pod_codec::ndef::decode_external`.\nfn decode_external<'a>(buf: &'a [u8], expected_type: &[u8]) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {\n    if buf.len() < 3 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let flags = buf[0];\n    // Require: MB(0x80) ME(0x40) set, CF(0x20) clear, SR(0x10) set, IL(0x08) clear,\n    // TNF(0x07) == 0x04 (External).\n    if flags & 0x20 != 0 || flags & 0x10 == 0 || flags & 0x08 != 0 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    if flags & 0x80 == 0 || flags & 0x40 == 0 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    if flags & 0x07 != 0x04 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let type_len = buf[1] as usize;\n    let payload_len = buf[2] as usize;\n    let type_end = 3usize.checked_add(type_len)?;\n    if type_end > buf.len() || &buf[3..type_end] != expected_type {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let pay_end = type_end.checked_add(payload_len)?;\n    if pay_end > buf.len() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    Some(&buf[type_end..pay_end])\n}\n\n/// Extract `order_id` from a structurally-valid PoD payload. The MAC is NOT\n/// verified on-device (no provisioning key lives on the Flipper — verification is\n/// server-side). This is display-only.\nfn pod_order_id(payload: &[u8]) -> Option<u64> {\n    if payload.len() != POD_PAYLOAD_LEN || payload[0] != 1 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let mut oid = [0u8; 8];\n    oid.copy_from_slice(&payload[1..9]);\n    Some(u64::from_be_bytes(oid))\n}\n\n/// A sample PoD tag byte string (order_id = 42), used to exercise the decode path\n/// at build time in the absence of a physical tag. Byte layout:\n///   D4 0C 21 | "dowiz.io:pod" | 01 <order_id BE=42> <ts BE> <16-byte MAC placeholder>\n#[rustfmt::skip]\nconst SAMPLE_TAG: [u8; 48] = [\n    0xD4, 0x0C, 0x21,\n    b'd', b'o', b'w', b'i', b'z', b'.', b'i', b'o', b':', b'p', b'o', b'd',\n    0x01,                                           // version\n    0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x2A, // order_id = 42\n    0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x65, 0x50, 0x8D, 0x00, // issued_at (arbitrary)\n    0xAA, 0xBB, 0xCC, 0xDD, 0xEE, 0xFF, 0x11, 0x22, // MAC (placeholder — verified server-side)\n    0x33, 0x44, 0x55, 0x66, 0x77, 0x88, 0x99, 0x00,\n];\n\nfn main(_args: Option<&CStr>) -> i32 {\n    // ── Device NFC seam (real flipperzero-sys calls) ────────────────────────────\n    // Allocate the NFC HAL and an ISO14443-3A poller (NTAG21x are ISO14443-3A).\n    // On a physical Flipper this is followed by `nfc_poller_start(poller, cb, ctx)`\n    // whose callback, on `NfcPollerEventTypeReady`, reads the tag's NDEF memory into\n    // a buffer that is then fed to `decode_external`/`pod_order_id` below. That\n    // callback cannot be exercised without hardware, so it is intentionally NOT\n    // faked here — only the real alloc/free lifecycle is wired.\n    unsafe {\n        let nfc = sys::nfc_alloc();\n        let poller = sys::nfc_poller_alloc(nfc, sys::NfcProtocolIso14443_3a);\n        // <-- nfc_poller_start(...) + callback would run here on real hardware -->\n        sys::nfc_poller_free(poller);\n        sys::nfc_free(nfc);\n    }\n\n    // ── Pure decode demo (compiled + reasoned, no hardware needed) ──────────────\n    // Decodes the SAMPLE_TAG exactly as the on-device read path would decode bytes\n    // read off a real tag, and logs the order_id.\n    match decode_external(&SAMPLE_TAG, POD_TYPE).and_then(pod_order_id) {\n        Some(order_id) => info!("dowiz PoD tag: order_id={}", order_id),\n        None => error!("not a dowiz PoD tag (malformed NDEF or wrong type)"),\n    }\n\n    0\n}\n	4503	-1	-1		5f74bb197c0930b5632b60c43436162b6c57a18ea574b44fabf627d3918fc36659024d06670e1a4b805291ab6440dc388bd12d56b34884a82dfd7a046f8ec8c7d33501f06dd2d82accddb13276f8ebe15c70f8222bd0dd480a923ab6508b1547ed6373410a4ad625795c8e14ba61ca34487d452a5de803cb9390d4f83998a882

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/ops-alert/src/regression_digest.rs	regression_digest · 212 lines	// P45-W0 §4c.2 regression-digest — generate docs/regressions/REGRESSION-DIGEST.md\n// from the LIVE rows of docs/regressions/REGRESSION-LEDGER.md (§3 VIEW schema).\n// Pure std. Emits a one-line-per-row human-readable table + a header summary.\n// Status is derived cheaply (no re-run of the world): if the guardrail's `Where`\n// references a path that exists in the repo it is GREEN; rows whose referenced\n// artifacts are gone (deleted legacy code) are UNVERIFIED — never fabricated green.\n// Drift gate: CI regenerates and `git diff`s against the committed digest; a stale\n// or hand-edited digest is RED (same regenerate-and-diff pattern as P-A codegen gate).\nuse std::env;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::exit;\n\nstruct Row {\n    id: String,\n    class: String,\n    guardrail_type: String,\n    where_col: String,\n    last_verified: String,\n}\n\nfn find_root() -> PathBuf {\n    if let Ok(r) = env::var("DIGEST_ROOT") {\n        return PathBuf::from(r);\n    }\n    let mut dir = env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("."));\n    loop {\n        if dir.join("docs/regressions/REGRESSION-LEDGER.md").exists() {\n            return dir;\n        }\n        if !dir.pop() {\n            return env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("."));\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Extract LIVE-section table rows only.\nfn parse_live_rows(txt: &str) -> Vec<Row> {\n    let lines: Vec<&str> = txt.lines().collect();\n    let mut in_live = false;\n    let mut rows = Vec::new();\n    for line in lines {\n        let t = line.trim();\n        if t.starts_with("## Ledger — LIVE") {\n            in_live = true;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if in_live && t.starts_with("## ") {\n            break; // next section\n        }\n        if !in_live {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if !t.starts_with('|') {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let cells: Vec<&str> = t.split('|').map(|c| c.trim()).collect();\n        // table: ["" , #, Symptom, Root cause, Guardrail type, Where, Date/commit, ""]\n        if cells.len() < 7 {\n            continue;\n        }\n        // skip header + separator\n        if cells[1] == "#" || cells[1].starts_with("---") || cells[1].is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let id = cells[1].to_string();\n        let symptom = strip_md(cells[2]);\n        let class = first_words(&symptom, 15);\n        let guardrail_type =\n            strip_md(cells[4]).split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>()[0..].join(" ");\n        let where_col = strip_md(cells[5]);\n        let last_verified = strip_md(cells[6]);\n        rows.push(Row {\n            id,\n            class,\n            guardrail_type,\n            where_col,\n            last_verified,\n        });\n    }\n    rows\n}\n\nfn strip_md(s: &str) -> String {\n    s.replace('`', "")\n        .replace("**", "")\n        .replace('*', "")\n        .split_whitespace()\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(" ")\n}\n\nfn first_words(s: &str, n: usize) -> String {\n    let words: Vec<&str> = s.split_whitespace().collect();\n    let take = words.len().min(n);\n    words[..take].join(" ")\n}\n\n// Derive status: if `where_col` names a path that exists in the repo -> GREEN,\n// else UNVERIFIED. We search for a plausible path token (file or dir) in the column.\nfn derive_status(root: &PathBuf, where_col: &str) -> &'static str {\n    for tok in where_col\n        .split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric() && c != '/' && c != '.' && c != '_' && c != '-')\n    {\n        if tok.len() < 3 {\n            continue;\n        }\n        // try a few normalizations\n        for cand in [tok.to_string(), tok.trim_start_matches("./").to_string()] {\n            if cand.contains('/')\n                || cand.ends_with(".rs")\n                || cand.ends_with(".sh")\n                || cand.ends_with(".toml")\n                || cand.ends_with(".ts")\n                || cand.ends_with(".sql")\n                || cand.ends_with(".py")\n                || cand.ends_with(".md")\n            {\n                if root.join(&cand).exists() {\n                    return "GREEN";\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    "UNVERIFIED"\n}\n\nfn main() {\n    let root = find_root();\n    let ledger = root.join("docs/regressions/REGRESSION-LEDGER.md");\n    let txt = match fs::read_to_string(&ledger) {\n        Ok(t) => t,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!("regression-digest: cannot read {}: {e}", ledger.display());\n            exit(2);\n        }\n    };\n    let rows = parse_live_rows(&txt);\n    let mut green = 0usize;\n    let mut unverified = 0usize;\n    let mut out = String::new();\n    out.push_str("# Regression Digest — dowiz / DeliveryOS\\n\\n");\n    out.push_str("> GENERATED VIEW. The `REGRESSION-LEDGER.md` is authoritative; this digest is\\n");\n    out.push_str("> a one-line-per-row readable projection. Each row links back via its id.\\n");\n    out.push_str("> Regenerate with `cargo run --manifest-path tools/ops-alert/Cargo.toml --bin regression-digest`.\\n\\n");\n    // summary line (machine-checkable)\n    for r in &rows {\n        let st = derive_status(&root, &r.where_col);\n        if st == "GREEN" {\n            green += 1;\n        } else {\n            unverified += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    out.push_str(&format!(\n        "SUMMARY: {} live guardrails | {} green | {} unverified (generated {} by regression-digest)\\n\\n",\n        rows.len(),\n        green,\n        unverified,\n        now_str()\n    ));\n    out.push_str(\n        "| # | class (≤15 words) | guardrail type | how to run | status | last verified |\\n",\n    );\n    out.push_str("|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n");\n    for r in &rows {\n        let st = derive_status(&root, &r.where_col);\n        let run = if r.where_col.contains("CI:") {\n            r.where_col.clone()\n        } else {\n            format!("path: {}", r.where_col)\n        };\n        out.push_str(&format!(\n            "| {} | {} | {} | {} | {} | {} |\\n",\n            r.id, r.class, r.guardrail_type, run, st, r.last_verified\n        ));\n    }\n    out.push_str("\\n---\\n*Readability sign-off (operator): ___ how many live / which red / re-run row N ___ (DoD-c)\\n");\n\n    if let Some(arg) = env::args().nth(1) {\n        if arg == "--check" {\n            // drift gate: compare to committed file; 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/shell-spike/src/floor_parity.rs	floor_parity · 357 lines	//! BLUEPRINT-P63 §3.6 — SP-6 floor-parity method: the *reusable* gate that\n//! proves any future surface renders **correctly** on the WebGL2 and CPU rungs\n//! of the FE-16 ladder (protecting the ~18% of web users without WebGPU).\n//!\n//! This is the ONE SP output that is **durable, not throwaway** — the blueprint\n//! keeps it as a gate like P58's a11y harness. On close, the same method is\n//! mirrored into `engine/tests/floor_parity/` (a permanent home inside the\n//! engine crate) and the `web/tests/floor-parity.spec.mjs` Playwright driver.\n//! This module is the reference-frame core the durable copy is built from.\n//!\n//! Method. For a given scene corpus we render the **CPU `compose()`** frame\n//! (`dowiz-engine::field_frame::compose`, bit-deterministic — the oracle whose\n//! determinism is proven at `engine/src/field_frame.rs::compose_returns_deterministic_frame`)\n//! and treat it as ground truth. Each other rung is diffed against that reference\n//! with a per-pixel perceptual delta (normalized ΔE / `(1−SSIM)` tolerance). The\n//! rung *passes* when its delta ≤ `PARITY_PERCEPTUAL_DELTA_MAX` (0.02).\n//!\n//! The adversarial cases (§3.6) are the load-bearing proof that the gate is real:\n//!   * (i) a deliberately **WebGPU-only** effect (a rung whose pixel set departs\n//!     from the reference) MUST fail the gate — otherwise the gate can't catch the\n//!     exclusion it exists to catch;\n//!   * (ii) a deliberately **blank** rung MUST fail (blank ≠ reference), not pass\n//!     by rendering nothing;\n//!   * (iii) the CPU reference must be run twice and be byte-identical, or the\n//!     harness aborts (guards against a future `compose()` regression breaking the\n//!     oracle — reuses the determinism assertion as a precondition).\n//!\n//! This module is `#[cfg(feature = "floor_parity")]`-gated so the throwaway\n//! spike crate never pulls the perceptual-delta machinery into its default build;\n//! the durable copy in `engine/tests/` does not need the gate (it is always\n//! exercised there).\n\n#![cfg(feature = "floor_parity")]\n\nuse crate::{tiny_scene, PARITY_PERCEPTUAL_DELTA_MAX, SPIKE_STEPS};\nuse dowiz_engine::field_frame::{self, FieldEquilibrium};\nuse dowiz_engine::scene::{Scene, SdfShape};\n\n/// A single scene in the parity corpus. Each rung is rendered at this size/steps\n/// and diffed against the CPU reference.\npub struct ParityScene {\n    pub name: &'static str,\n    pub scene: Scene,\n    pub w: usize,\n    pub h: usize,\n}\n\n/// A render "rung" of the FE-16 ladder. The CPU `compose()` rung is the oracle.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Rung {\n    CpuReference,\n    Webgl2,\n    Webgpu,\n}\n\n/// The result of diffing one rung against the CPU reference for one scene.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct RungDelta {\n    pub rung: Rung,\n    pub scene: &'static str,\n    /// Per-pixel perceptual delta against the bit-deterministic CPU reference.\n    pub delta: f64,\n    /// True when `delta ≤ PARITY_PERCEPTUAL_DELTA_MAX`.\n    pub passes: bool,\n}\n\n/// A synthetic "rung" renderer for the spike. The durable gate later wraps the\n/// real WebGL2/WebGPU captures; in the spike we MODEL each rung as a transform\n/// applied to the CPU reference so the gate's *logic* (delta compute + the two\n/// adversarial catches) is proven headless and offline:\n///\n///   * `CpuReference`  → the oracle itself (delta == 0, always passes).\n///   * `Webgl2`/`Webgpu` in the *happy* path → a tiny deterministic perturbation\n///     well within tolerance (proves a faithful rung passes).\n///   * `Webgpu` in the *WebGPU-only-effect* adversarial → a structural departure\n///     (a bright bar drawn nowhere in the reference) → delta > tolerance → FAILS.\n///   * `Webgl2` in the *blank* adversarial → a fully-zero frame → diverges from\n///     the reference → FAILS.\n///\n/// The boundary being tested is the GATE, not the GPU math (which the real\n/// backend replaces on close). That is exactly reuse-first (§1.1): the reference\n/// frame is the CPU `compose()`, never forked. The `rung` parameter tags which\n/// ladder rung produced the bytes (for the durable API shape); the rendered\n/// bytes themselves are driven entirely by `mode` over the reference.\npub fn render_rung(_rung: Rung, scene: &ParityScene, mode: RungMode) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let reference = field_frame::compose(\n        &scene.scene,\n        &FieldEquilibrium::default(),\n        scene.w,\n        scene.h,\n        SPIKE_STEPS,\n    );\n    match mode {\n        RungMode::Faithful => reference,\n        RungMode::WebgpuOnlyEffect => webgpu_only_effect(&reference, scene.w, scene.h),\n        RungMode::Blank => vec![0u8; scene.w * scene.h * 4],\n    }\n}\n\n/// How the synthetic rung deviates from the reference.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum RungMode {\n    /// Identical to the CPU reference (a faithful GPU rung passes the gate).\n    Faithful,\n    /// A deliberately WebGPU-only effect: a bright vertical bar introduced on the\n    /// GPU rung that the CPU reference does NOT have → must fail parity.\n    WebgpuOnlyEffect,\n    /// A deliberately blank rung (a backend that renders nothing): must fail\n    /// (blank ≠ reference), not pass by rendering nothing.\n    Blank,\n}\n\n/// Insert a deliberately WebGPU-only effect: a large bright block (the right\n/// half of the frame) that the CPU reference does NOT have. This must push the\n/// gate's delta past the bar so the adversarial case (i) actually REDs — proving\n/// the parity check can catch a GPU-only visual that would silently exclude\n/// ~18% of web users without WebGPU.\nfn webgpu_only_effect(reference: &[u8], w: usize, h: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut out = reference.to_vec();\n    for y in 0..h {\n        for x in w / 2..w {\n            let idx = (y * w + x) * 4;\n            if idx + 3 < out.len() {\n                out[idx] = 255;\n                out[idx + 1] = 255;\n                out[idx + 2] = 255;\n                out[idx + 3] = 255;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// A small corpus: a storefront card, a text field, a settled map placeholder\n/// (BLUEPRINT-P63 §3.6). Each is built from `dowiz-engine` public types only.\n///\n/// Every scene carries a very large background SDF box so the reference frame is\n/// *robustly covered* (coverage ≈ 1.0). That matters for the gate's structural\n/// term: a BLANK rung has coverage 0, so `coverage_delta` is large even when the\n/// reference is mostly dark — without this, a sparse reference would let a blank\n/// frame slip through under a pure intensity metric.\npub fn parity_corpus() -> Vec<ParityScene> {\n    vec![\n        ParityScene {\n            name: "storefront_card",\n            scene: {\n                let mut s = Scene::new().with_scale(0.5);\n                s.add(dowiz_engine::scene::SdfShape::Box {\n                    bx: 0.0,\n                    by: 0.0,\n                    hx: 1000.0,\n                    hy: 1000.0,\n                })\n                .add(SdfShape::Circle { cx: 2.0, cy: 0.0, r: 6.0 })\n                .add(SdfShape::Box { bx: -3.0, by: 4.0, hx: 1.0, hy: 1.0 });\n                s\n            },\n            w: 32,\n            h: 32,\n        },\n        ParityScene {\n            name: "text_field",\n            scene: {\n                let mut s = Scene::new().with_scale(0.5);\n                s.add(dowiz_engine::scene::SdfShape::Box {\n                    bx: 0.0,\n                    by: 0.0,\n                    hx: 1000.0,\n                    hy: 1000.0,\n                })\n                .add(dowiz_engine::scene::SdfShape::Box {\n                    bx: 0.0,\n                    by: 0.0,\n                    hx: 6.0,\n                    hy: 1.0,\n                });\n                s\n            },\n            w: 48,\n            h: 16,\n        },\n        ParityScene {\n            name: "settled_map_placeholder",\n            scene: {\n                let mut s = Scene::new().with_scale(0.5);\n                s.add(dowiz_engine::scene::SdfShape::Box {\n                    bx: 0.0,\n                    by: 0.0,\n                    hx: 1000.0,\n                    hy: 1000.0,\n                })\n                .add(dowiz_engine::scene::SdfShape::Circle {\n                    cx: 2.0,\n                    cy: -2.0,\n                    r: 4.0,\n                })\n                .add(dowiz_engine::scene::SdfShape::Box {\n                    bx: -4.0,\n                    by: 3.0,\n                    hx: 2.0,\n                    hy: 2.0,\n                });\n                s\n            },\n            w: 40,\n            h: 28,\n        },\n    ]\n}\n\n/// Compute the perceptual delta between a rung frame and the bit-deterministic\n/// CPU reference. This is the offline-safe scalar core of "ΔE / (1−SSIM)"; the\n/// real backend swaps in a full SSIM, but the gate's *threshold logic* is\n/// identical.\n///\n/// The metric is `max(intensity_delta, coverage_delta)`:\n///   * `intensity_delta` — mean over all bytes of `|a−b|/255` ∈ [0,1]. Catches a\n///     faithful frame (0) and a uniformly-bright GPU-only block (≈1).\n///   * `coverage_delta` — `|fraction of lit pixels in A − fraction in B|` ∈ [0,1].\n///     This is the structural term: a BLANK rung has 0 coverage so it diverges\n///     from a covered reference even when the reference is mostly dark, and a\n///     GPU-only block that adds/removes lit area also diverges here.\n///\n/// Either term alone exceeding the bar fails the rung.\npub fn perceptual_delta(rung_frame: &[u8], reference: &[u8]) -> f64 {\n    assert_eq!(\n        rung_frame.len(),\n        reference.len(),\n        "rung and reference must be the same size"\n    );\n    if rung_frame.is_empty() {\n        return 1.0; // a size-0 frame is maximally divergent\n    }\n    let npix = rung_frame.len() / 4;\n    let mut intensity_sum = 0.0f64;\n    let mut rung_lit = 0usize;\n    let mut ref_lit = 0usize;\n    for p in 0..npix {\n        let rb = &rung_frame[p * 4..p * 4 + 4];\n        let rf = &reference[p * 4..p * 4 + 4];\n        for c in 0..4 {\n            intensity_sum += ((rb[c] as f64) - (rf[c] as f64)).abs() / 255.0;\n        }\n        if rb.iter().any(|&v| v != 0) {\n            rung_lit += 1;\n        }\n        if rf.iter().any(|&v| v != 0) {\n            ref_lit += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    let intensity_delta = intensity_sum / (rung_frame.len() as f64);\n    let coverage_delta = (rung_lit as f64 - ref_lit as f64).abs() / (npix as f64);\n    intensity_delta.max(coverage_delta)\n}\n\n/// Diff a single rung against the CPU reference over one scene. The reference is\n/// rendered TWICE and asserted byte-identical (adversarial case iii — guards the\n/// oracle against a `compose()` regression).\npub fn diff_rung(rung: Rung, scene: &ParityScene, mode: RungMode) -> RungDelta {\n    let ref_a = field_frame::compose(&scene.scene, &FieldEquilibrium::default(), scene.w, scene.h, SPIKE_STEPS);\n    let ref_b = field_frame::compose(&scene.scene, &FieldEquilibrium::default(), scene.w, scene.h, SPIKE_STEPS);\n    assert_eq!(ref_a, ref_b, "oracle nondeterminism — compose() must be bit-identical");\n\n    let frame = match rung {\n        Rung::CpuReference => ref_a.clone(),\n        _ => render_rung(rung, scene, mode),\n    };\n    let delta = perceptual_delta(&frame, &ref_a);\n    RungDelta {\n        rung,\n        scene: scene.name,\n        delta,\n        passes: delta <= PARITY_PERCEPTUAL_DELTA_MAX,\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cpu_reference_is_bit_deterministic_oracle() {\n        // Adversarial case (iii): the oracle must be stable across calls.\n        let corpus = parity_corpus();\n        for s in &corpus {\n            let a = field_frame::compose(&s.scene, &FieldEquilibrium::default(), s.w, s.h, SPIKE_STEPS);\n            let b = field_frame::compose(&s.scene, &FieldEquilibrium::default(), s.w, s.h, SPIKE_STEPS);\n            assert_eq!(a, b, "compose() oracle not bit-deterministic for {}", s.name);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn faithful_rung_passes_parity_on_corpus() {\n        // The happy path: a faithful GPU rung (byte-identical to the reference)\n        // passes on every scene.\n        for s in &parity_corpus() {\n            let d = diff_rung(Rung::Webgl2, s, RungMode::Faithful);\n            assert!(\n                d.passes,\n                "faithful WebGL2 rung must pass parity on {} (delta={})",\n                s.name, d.delta\n            );\n            let d2 = diff_rung(Rung::Webgpu, s, RungMode::Faithful);\n            assert!(\n                d2.passes,\n                "faithful WebGPU rung must pass parity on {} (delta={})",\n                s.name, d2.delta\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn gate_catches_webgpu_only_effect() {\n        // Adversarial case (i): a deliberately WebGPU-only effect must RED the\n        // gate — otherwise the parity check is worthless (it would let a GPU-only\n        // visual silently exclude ~18% of web users).\n        for s in &parity_corpus() {\n            let d = diff_rung(Rung::Webgpu, s, RungMode::WebgpuOnlyEffect);\n            assert!(\n                !d.passes,\n                "WebGPU-only effect MUST fail parity on {} (delta={})",\n                s.name, d.delta\n            );\n            assert!(\n                d.delta > PARITY_PERCEPTUAL_DELTA_MAX,\n                "delta must exceed the bar for a GPU-only effect"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn gate_catches_blank_rung() {\n        // Adversarial case (ii): a rung that renders a BLANK frame must FAIL\n        // (blank ≠ reference), not pass by rendering nothing.\n        for s in &parity_corpus() {\n            let d = diff_rung(Rung::Webgl2, s, RungMode::Blank);\n            assert!(\n                !d.passes,\n                "blank WebGL2 rung MUST fail parity on {} (delta={})",\n                s.name, d.delta\n            );\n            assert!(\n                d.delta > PARITY_PERCEPTUAL_DELTA_MAX,\n                "blank frame diverges from a covered reference"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cpu_reference_pass_is_zero_delta() {\n        for s in &parity_corpus() {\n            let d = diff_rung(Rung::CpuReference, s, RungMode::Faithful);\n            assert_eq!(d.delta, 0.0, "the oracle diffs to itself");\n            assert!(d.passes);\n        }\n    }\n}\n	4539	-1	-1		c77e74775f8b21224919b2d5b522f327693f954cfd72f5ebab566a0b81ffc3601c49698355df6c8fa353418bae90d129df711d24b76a84b2b1627a0eff1cf86e7ea85499e7dfc939969b300ad7baac29f16a680a29814f281402b2d6540b93247060f7a6b0cf5125d27a8c1dca50af116c3b44ae59858b70010f7ed0732a1410

This crate is the **runnable, falsifiable core** of P63. P63's full contract\n//! (`docs/design/CORE-ROADMAP-2026-07-17/BLUEPRINT-P63-shell-platform-spike.md`)\n//! is six *measurement* spikes (SP-1..SP-6). Five of them (SP-1..SP-5) need\n//! physical hardware — a real desktop GPU, a budget Android, an iOS device, a\n//! native-payment SDK, a soft-keyboard on a real mobile browser. Those cannot\n//! run headless, so they are encoded here as the **verdict schema + the honesty\n//! gate** (§2 / §4.1 / §4.3) and committed as honestly-`Blocked` rows in\n//! `docs/design/.../P63-VERDICTS.md`.\n//!\n//! What this crate *does* prove — the one thing that does not need hardware —\n//! is **the boundary holds**:\n//!   * frames travel engine→platform unmodified through a `&[u8]`/`FrameSink`\n//!     contract (the generalization of `bridge::GpuUploadSink` to a settled\n//!     RGBA frame, not a vertex slice — reuse-first, BLUEPRINT-P63 §1.1);\n//!   * the platform never sees engine internals (`Scene`/`FieldEquilibrium`);\n//!   * the engine never sees platform events (`ShellEvent`/`PlatformShell`);\n//!   * events are translated to render intents ONLY at the `RenderLoop`;\n//!   * SP-6's floor-parity METHOD is real and catches both adversarial cases\n//!     (a deliberately-blank rung and a deliberately-WebGPU-only effect).\n//!\n//! Dependency direction (the boundary contract):\n//!   * Platform depends on `FrameSink` (`&[u8]`) — never on `Scene`.\n//!   * Engine depends on `RenderEngine` (`Vec<u8>` + a settle gate) — never on\n//!     `ShellEvent`.\n//!   * `RenderLoop` is the ONLY coupling point.\n//!\n//! Isolation (BLUEPRINT-P63 §4.3 bulkhead): this is a standalone crate with a\n//! **one-directional** dependency (it depends on `dowiz-engine`; `dowiz-engine`\n//! does NOT and cannot depend on it). The canonical order/money graph never\n//! compiles this code. At close, `rm -rf tools/shell-spike/` leaves the product\n//! tree byte-unchanged (§4.5).\n\nuse dowiz_engine::field_frame::{self, FieldEquilibrium};\nuse dowiz_engine::scene::{Scene, SdfShape};\nuse dowiz_engine::FrameProfiler;\n\npub mod floor_parity;\npub mod verdict;\n\npub use verdict::{\n    BatteryVerdictRecord, DesktopOs, HwClass, Platform, SpikeId, SpikeVerdict, VerdictError,\n    VerdictRecord,\n};\n\n// ── Falsifiable bars (BLUEPRINT-P63 §2, named BEFORE any prototype) ──────────\npub const DESKTOP_FRAME_BUDGET_MS: f64 = 16.7; // 60 FPS interactive target\npub const DESKTOP_FRAME_FLOOR_MS: f64 = 33.0; // 30 FPS hard floor (P38 §6)\npub const INPUT_LATENCY_BAR_MS_P95: f64 = 50.0; // tap/keystroke→pixel, p95\npub const MOBILE_SOAK_MIN: u32 = 30; // continuous render soak\npub const MOBILE_FLICKER_FRAMES_MAX: u32 = 0; // webview↔wgpu contention flicker\npub const MOBILE_FRAME_FLOOR_MS: f64 = 33.0;\npub const SHEET_PRESENT_DROPPED_MAX: u32 = 3; // frames lost presenting SDK sheet\npub const SHEET_RECOVERY_MS_MAX: f64 = 250.0; // render loop back within budget\npub const SHIFT_HOURS_SIM: f64 = 6.0; // simulated shift length\npub const SETTLED_DRAIN_BAR_PCT_PER_HR: f64 = 4.0; // settled screen, foreground\npub const SETTLE_SAVINGS_MIN_PCT: f64 = 30.0; // settle-ON beats settle-OFF by ≥30%\npub const THERMAL_SUSTAIN_MS: f64 = 33.0; // sustained frame time over soak\npub const PARITY_PERCEPTUAL_DELTA_MAX: f64 = 0.02; // normalized per-pixel ΔE / (1−SSIM)\n\n/// Steps the spike's reference frame evolves. Small — this is a boundary proof,\n/// not a visual-quality render.\nconst SPIKE_STEPS: usize = 4;\n\n// ── The thin boundary traits ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The contract the ENGINE writes through. The platform's present path\n/// implements this; the engine only ever sees `&[u8]`. This is the\n/// generalization of `bridge::GpuUploadSink` to a settled RGBA frame rather\n/// than a vertex slice (reuse-first, BLUEPRINT-P63 §1.1: extend, don't fork).\npub trait FrameSink {\n    /// Receive one fully-rendered RGBA8 frame from the engine. The platform owns\n    /// how it gets to the swapchain; the engine does not know.\n    fn accept_frame(&mut self, frame: &[u8]);\n}\n\n/// The render side as seen by the shell. A `RenderEngine` produces frames and\n/// exposes its FE-14 settle gate (`should_render`) — but it knows NOTHING about\n/// windows, events, or platforms.\npub trait RenderEngine {\n    /// Produce one RGBA8 frame at `w×h` after `steps` evolution steps.\n    fn render_frame(&mut self, w: usize, h: usize, steps: usize) -> Vec<u8>;\n    /// FE-14 lazy-render-on-settle (BLUEPRINT-P63 §0 cites P38 §3.5). When the\n    /// field is settled the engine asks NOT to be rendered — the platform must\n    /// honor this without knowing *why*.\n    fn should_render(&self) -> bool;\n}\n\n/// Platform-side input event. Defined on the platform side of the boundary; the\n/// engine type system never names it.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub enum ShellEvent {\n    Close,\n    Resize(u32, u32),\n    Pointer(f32, f32),\n    Key(u32),\n}\n\n/// A platform shell: owns the window + input, and presents frames via `FrameSink`.\n/// `RenderLoop` is the only place that talks to both `PlatformShell` and\n/// `RenderEngine`.\npub trait PlatformShell: FrameSink {\n    /// Return the next pending input event, or `None` if the queue is empty.\n    fn poll_event(&mut self) -> Option<ShellEvent>;\n    /// Current swapchain size in physical pixels.\n    fn size(&self) -> (u32, u32);\n    /// Platform-side response to a resize intent: update the swapchain/viewport.\n    fn apply_resize(&mut self, w: u32, h: u32);\n    /// Platform-side response to a close intent: mark the shell closing.\n    fn request_close(&mut self);\n}\n\n// ── Engine-side implementation (wraps the real `compose()`) ──────────────────\n\n/// A `RenderEngine` backed by the engine's bit-deterministic\n/// `field_frame::compose`. Holds the scene + equilibrium; never references any\n/// platform type.\npub struct SceneRenderer {\n    scene: Scene,\n    eq: FieldEquilibrium,\n    /// FE-14 settle state. When `true`, `should_render()` reports the field is\n    /// settled and the shell should skip rendering (the battery lever, SP-5).\n    settled: bool,\n    /// Count of times `render_frame` was actually invoked (boundary-behavior probe).\n    pub render_calls: usize,\n    /// Last (w,h) the loop asked us to render at (proves resize reached the engine).\n    pub last_size: (usize, usize),\n}\n\nimpl SceneRenderer {\n    pub fn new(scene: Scene, eq: FieldEquilibrium) -> Self {\n        SceneRenderer {\n            scene,\n            eq,\n            settled: false,\n            render_calls: 0,\n            last_size: (0, 0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set the FE-14 settle state. The render side decides this from its own\n    /// energy/settled predicate; the platform never computes it.\n    pub fn set_settled(&mut self, settled: bool) {\n        self.settled = settled;\n    }\n}\n\nimpl RenderEngine for SceneRenderer {\n    fn render_frame(&mut self, w: usize, h: usize, steps: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n        self.render_calls += 1;\n        self.last_size = (w, h);\n        field_frame::compose(&self.scene, &self.eq, w, h, steps)\n    }\n\n    fn should_render(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.settled\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Platform-side implementation (headless mock — proves the boundary headless)\n\n/// A headless `PlatformShell` used by the spike's proof. It records every frame\n/// the engine delivers (the swapchain mirror) and replays a scripted event\n/// queue. It never imports `Scene`/`FieldEquilibrium` — it only sees `&[u8]`.\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct HeadlessShell {\n    events: Vec<ShellEvent>,\n    cursor: usize,\n    width: u32,\n    height: u32,\n    /// The swapchain mirror: every `&[u8]` the engine delivered, in order.\n    pub presented: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    /// Number of `accept_frame` calls (= frames actually presented).\n    pub present_calls: usize,\n    /// The last resize the loop translated into a render request.\n    pub last_resize: Option<(u32, u32)>,\n    /// Whether a `Close` event was observed and honored.\n    pub closed: bool,\n}\n\nimpl HeadlessShell {\n    pub fn new(width: u32, height: u32) -> Self {\n        HeadlessShell {\n            events: Vec::new(),\n            cursor: 0,\n            width,\n            height,\n            presented: Vec::new(),\n            present_calls: 0,\n            last_resize: None,\n            closed: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Queue scripted input events for the loop to consume.\n    pub fn with_events(mut self, events: Vec<ShellEvent>) -> Self {\n        self.events = events;\n        self\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FrameSink for HeadlessShell {\n    fn accept_frame(&mut self, frame: &[u8]) {\n        self.presented.push(frame.to_vec());\n        self.present_calls += 1;\n    }\n}\n\nimpl PlatformShell for HeadlessShell {\n    fn poll_event(&mut self) -> Option<ShellEvent> {\n        if self.cursor < self.events.len() {\n            let ev = self.events[self.cursor];\n            self.cursor += 1;\n            Some(ev)\n        } else {\n            None\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn size(&self) -> (u32, u32) {\n        (self.width, self.height)\n    }\n\n    fn apply_resize(&mut self, w: u32, h: u32) {\n        self.last_resize = Some((w, h));\n        self.width = w;\n        self.height = h;\n    }\n\n    fn request_close(&mut self) {\n        self.closed = true;\n    }\n}\n\n// ── The glue: the ONLY coupling point between engine and platform ────────────\n\n/// Drives the shell+engine pair. This is the sole place that knows both trait\n/// families: it translates `ShellEvent` → render intents (platform→engine) and\n/// feeds engine output into the platform's `FrameSink` (engine→platform). The\n/// engine and platform never reference each other's types.\npub struct RenderLoop {\n    profiler: FrameProfiler,\n}\n\nimpl Default for RenderLoop {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        RenderLoop {\n            profiler: FrameProfiler::default(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl RenderLoop {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Run up to `max_frames` render iterations, or until the shell closes.\n    /// Returns the number of frames actually presented.\n    pub fn run<P, E>(&mut self, shell: &mut P, engine: &mut E, max_frames: usize) -> usize\n    where\n        P: PlatformShell,\n        E: RenderEngine,\n    {\n        let mut presented = 0usize;\n        let mut frames = 0usize;\n        while frames < max_frames {\n            // Platform → engine: translate input events to render intents.\n            // The engine never sees `ShellEvent`; only size/settle intents.\n            while let Some(ev) = shell.poll_event() {\n                match ev {\n                    ShellEvent::Close => {\n                        shell.request_close();\n                        return presented;\n                    }\n                    ShellEvent::Resize(w, h) => {\n                        // The platform reports a new size; the engine learns it\n                        // only through the next `render_frame(w,h,..)` call.\n                        shell.apply_resize(w, h);\n                    }\n                    ShellEvent::Pointer(..) | ShellEvent::Key(..) => {\n                        // Intent routing: a pointer/key event is an engine input\n                        // intent. In this spike it is a no-op beyond proving the\n                        // boundary translated it (no JSON, no DOM).\n                        self.profiler.json_parse_calls += 0; // explicitly 0 — no JSON in the loop\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Engine → platform: honor the settle gate, then render+present.\n            if engine.should_render() {\n                let (w, h) = shell.size();\n                let frame = engine.render_frame(w as usize, h as usize, SPIKE_STEPS);\n                shell.accept_frame(&frame); // through the FrameSink boundary\n                self.profiler.write_buffer_calls += 1; // one present per frame\n                presented += 1;\n                frames += 1;\n            } else {\n                // Settled: the boundary SKIPS the engine entirely. No render, no\n                // present. The platform does not need to know why.\n                frames += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        presented\n    }\n\n    /// The GREEN gate: zero JSON (no (de)serialize in the loop) and exactly one\n    /// present per rendered frame.\n    pub fn profiler(&self) -> &FrameProfiler {\n        &self.profiler\n    }\n}\n\n/// The bit-deterministic reference frame (BLUEPRINT-P63 §3.6 oracle): the CPU\n/// `compose()` output the platform-side boundary must reproduce unmodified. Used\n/// by the boundary tests to prove the `FrameSink` pipe is transparent.\npub fn field_frame_compose(scene: &Scene, w: usize, h: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n    field_frame::compose(scene, &FieldEquilibrium::default(), w, h, SPIKE_STEPS)\n}\n\n/// Build a small scene for the boundary proof (a couple of SDF instances, like\n/// SP-1's "~1–2k SDF instances" reduced to a minimal, deterministic corpus).\npub fn tiny_scene() -> Scene {\n    let mut s = Scene::new().with_scale(0.5);\n    s.add(SdfShape::Circle {\n        cx: 0.0,\n        cy: 0.0,\n        r: 8.0,\n    })\n    .add(SdfShape::Box {\n        bx: 4.0,\n        by: 2.0,\n        hx: 1.0,\n        hy: 1.0,\n    });\n    s\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests;\n	4595	-1	-1		fbff3dd599df2937a33b93d3b1127a74cc379f457dc6f5eaab56484fc8ebcb251c6a640357936c2eab5b55ab29b0563a57715d24356a05faf8627a8c573c78cd5ca8dcd9edffc92197cb390997baa03b53d8dc2a29e75fa2ce06b296fe8b810ce072f4a6f2ca30b51a598e0d68486bbd6dbf60aa1fc589e50383f6fca120c971

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/shell-spike/src/tests.rs	tests · 170 lines	//! BLUEPRINT-P63 — boundary-proof tests (the runnable, headless core of the spike).\n//!\n//! These tests assert the thin engine⇄platform boundary actually holds:\n//!   * frames travel engine→platform BYTE-IDENTICAL through `FrameSink` (`&[u8]`);\n//!   * the platform never sees engine internals (`Scene` is never named on the\n//!     platform side — `HeadlessShell` only ever holds `&[u8]`);\n//!   * the engine never sees platform events (`SceneRenderer` never names\n//!     `ShellEvent`);\n//!   * the GREEN loop performs zero JSON and exactly one present per frame;\n//!   * the FE-14 settle gate skips the engine entirely across the boundary;\n//!   * resize / close intents are translated at the `RenderLoop` and reach the\n//!     right side without leaking types.\n\nuse crate::{\n    tiny_scene, DesktopOs, FieldEquilibrium, HwClass, Platform, RenderEngine, RenderLoop,\n    SceneRenderer, ShellEvent, SpikeId, SpikeVerdict, HeadlessShell, VerdictRecord,\n};\n\n#[test]\nfn boundary_delivers_engine_frame_unmodified_to_platform() {\n    let scene = tiny_scene();\n    let eq = FieldEquilibrium::default();\n    let (w, h) = (32u32, 32u32);\n\n    let mut shell = HeadlessShell::new(w, h);\n    let mut engine = SceneRenderer::new(scene.clone(), eq);\n    let mut loop_ = RenderLoop::new();\n\n    let presented = loop_.run(&mut shell, &mut engine, 3);\n\n    // Every rendered frame was presented to the platform.\n    assert_eq!(presented, 3, "loop presented exactly max_frames frames");\n    assert_eq!(shell.present_calls, 3);\n    assert_eq!(engine.render_calls, 3, "engine rendered once per frame");\n\n    // The platform received EXACTLY the engine's compose() output, unmodified —\n    // the boundary is a transparent &[u8] pipe, not a transform.\n    let expected = crate::field_frame_compose(&scene, w as usize, h as usize);\n    for (i, frame) in shell.presented.iter().enumerate() {\n        assert_eq!(\n            frame.len(),\n            expected.len(),\n            "frame {i} byte length matches compose()"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            frame == &expected,\n            "frame {i} is byte-identical to the engine's compose() output (boundary unmodified)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // GREEN gate: zero JSON, one present per frame.\n    assert_eq!(\n        loop_.profiler().json_parse_calls,\n        0,\n        "GREEN loop: ZERO JSON in the frame path"\n    );\n    assert_eq!(\n        loop_.profiler().write_buffer_calls,\n        3,\n        "one present per rendered frame"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn settle_gate_skips_engine_render_across_boundary() {\n    let mut shell = HeadlessShell::new(32, 32);\n    let mut engine = SceneRenderer::new(tiny_scene(), FieldEquilibrium::default());\n    engine.set_settled(true); // field is settled → don't render\n    let mut loop_ = RenderLoop::new();\n\n    let presented = loop_.run(&mut shell, &mut engine, 5);\n\n    assert_eq!(presented, 0, "settled: nothing presented");\n    assert_eq!(\n        engine.render_calls, 0,\n        "settled: engine NOT rendered across the boundary"\n    );\n    assert_eq!(shell.present_calls, 0);\n    // The platform has no field-energy state; it only saw the gate's decision.\n    assert!(!shell.closed);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn resize_intent_reaches_engine_across_boundary() {\n    // Resize, then pointer/key intents (NO Close) — frames render and the\n    // resize intent must reach the engine via the next render size.\n    let mut shell = HeadlessShell::new(32, 32).with_events(vec![\n        ShellEvent::Resize(64, 48),\n        ShellEvent::Pointer(10.0, 20.0),\n        ShellEvent::Key(65),\n    ]);\n    let mut engine = SceneRenderer::new(tiny_scene(), FieldEquilibrium::default());\n    let mut loop_ = RenderLoop::new();\n\n    let presented = loop_.run(&mut shell, &mut engine, 5);\n    assert_eq!(presented, 5, "rendered all frames when no Close");\n    assert_eq!(\n        shell.last_resize,\n        Some((64, 48)),\n        "Resize reached the shell at the boundary"\n    );\n    assert_eq!(\n        engine.last_size,\n        (64, 48),\n        "Resize intent reached the engine via render size"\n    );\n    // All presented frames are at the post-resize size.\n    assert!(shell.presented.iter().all(|f| f.len() == 64 * 48 * 4));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn close_intent_terminates_loop_at_boundary() {\n    let mut shell = HeadlessShell::new(32, 32)\n        .with_events(vec![ShellEvent::Resize(64, 48), ShellEvent::Close]);\n    let mut engine = SceneRenderer::new(tiny_scene(), FieldEquilibrium::default());\n    let mut loop_ = RenderLoop::new();\n\n    let presented = loop_.run(&mut shell, &mut engine, 100);\n    // Close fired before any render frame → loop returns immediately.\n    assert_eq!(presented, 0, "Close fired before any render frame");\n    assert!(shell.closed, "Close event was honored at the boundary");\n    // Resize intent still reached the shell even though no frame rendered.\n    assert_eq!(shell.last_resize, Some((64, 48)), "Resize observed on shell");\n    // The engine (which depends only on FrameSink/render intents) never ran.\n    assert_eq!(engine.last_size, (0, 0), "engine untouched when loop closed early");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn resize_applied_to_subsequent_renders() {\n    let mut shell = HeadlessShell::new(32, 32).with_events(vec![ShellEvent::Resize(16, 16)]);\n    let mut engine = SceneRenderer::new(tiny_scene(), FieldEquilibrium::default());\n    let mut loop_ = RenderLoop::new();\n    loop_.run(&mut shell, &mut engine, 2);\n    assert_eq!(engine.last_size, (16, 16), "resize applied to subsequent renders");\n    assert!(shell.presented.iter().all(|f| f.len() == 16 * 16 * 4));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn verdict_honesty_gate_blocks_non_confirms() {\n    let base = VerdictRecord {\n        spike: SpikeId::Sp1Desktop,\n        hypothesis: "winit+wgpu+AccessKit meets budget",\n        method: "FrameProfiler distribution",\n        bar: "p95 ≤ 16.7ms",\n        measured: "BLOCKED: no
