4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/shell-spike/src/verdict.rs	verdict · 232 lines	//! BLUEPRINT-P63 §2 — the verdict schema (the durable, type-checked output).\n//!\n//! The verdict schema IS the spec of "done": every SP-* lane writes a\n//! `VerdictRecord` row. The `measured` field is either a REAL number / a\n//! distribution summary, or the literal string `BLOCKED: <resource>` — never an\n//! estimate. The `SpikeVerdict` enum is four-valued (BLUEPRINT-P63 §4.1):\n//!\n//!   * `Confirms`        — the directional ruling holds (a real pass);\n//!   * `Refines{delta}`  — ruling stands + a named bound/caveat;\n//!   * `Contradicts{ev}` — measured value crossed the bar the wrong way (evidence\n//!                         governs; forces a P39-rev refinement block);\n//!   * `Blocked{on}`     — honest arm when a resource (device/account) is absent.\n//!                         NOT a pass, NOT a guess.\n//!\n//! Hazard-safety as math (§4.1): an un-measured/asserted number has no\n//! representation — `is_measured_pass()` is `true` ONLY for `Confirms`. And the\n//! SP-5 battery row CANNOT be built from an `HwClass::Emulator` reading\n//! (`BatteryVerdictRecord::try_new`), so a faked emulator battery figure is\n//! unrepresentable at the type level.\n\n/// Which measurement spike a verdict row belongs to.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SpikeId {\n    Sp1Desktop,\n    Sp2MobileSurface,\n    Sp3PaymentBridge,\n    Sp4WebKeyboard,\n    Sp5Battery,\n    Sp6FloorParity,\n}\n\n/// The platform a measurement ran on.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum Platform {\n    Desktop { os: DesktopOs },\n    MobileAndroid { chipset: String },\n    MobileIos { model: String },\n    WebMobile { browser: String, os: String },\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DesktopOs {\n    Linux,\n    MacOs,\n    Windows,\n}\n\n/// Hardware class. `Emulator` is legal for every spike EXCEPT SP-5 (battery),\n/// which forbids it at construction time (see `BatteryVerdictRecord`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum HwClass {\n    BudgetAndroid,\n    MidAndroid,\n    MidDesktop,\n    HighDesktop,\n    Emulator,\n}\n\n/// The four-valued verdict (BLUEPRINT-P63 §2 / §4.1). `Blocked` is an honest\n/// arm, NEVER a pass: an unmeasured value has no representation.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum SpikeVerdict {\n    Confirms,\n    Refines { delta: String },\n    Contradicts { evidence: String },\n    Blocked { on: String },\n}\n\n/// One row of evidence. `measured` is a REAL number, a distribution summary, or\n/// the literal string `BLOCKED: <resource>` — never an estimate.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct VerdictRecord {\n    pub spike: SpikeId,\n    pub hypothesis: &'static str,\n    pub method: &'static str,\n    pub bar: &'static str,\n    pub measured: String,\n    pub platform: Platform,\n    pub hw_class: HwClass,\n    pub verdict: SpikeVerdict,\n    /// Caller-supplied monotonic counter (no ambient clock).\n    pub captured_utc: u64,\n}\n\nimpl VerdictRecord {\n    /// A row counts as a real pass ONLY when it `Confirms`. `Refines`/`Contradicts`/\n    /// `Blocked` are never a pass — this is the hazard-safety check that an\n    /// asserted/blocked number can never masquerade as a measured pass.\n    pub fn is_measured_pass(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self.verdict, SpikeVerdict::Confirms)\n    }\n\n    /// Render one markdown table row for `P63-VERDICTS.md`.\n    pub fn to_markdown_row(&self) -> String {\n        let verdict = match &self.verdict {\n            SpikeVerdict::Confirms => "Confirms".to_string(),\n            SpikeVerdict::Refines { delta } => format!("Refines ({delta})"),\n            SpikeVerdict::Contradicts { evidence } => format!("Contradicts ({evidence})"),\n            SpikeVerdict::Blocked { on } => format!("Blocked ({on})"),\n        };\n        format!(\n            "| {:?} | {} | {} | {} | {} | {:?} | {:?} | {} |",\n            self.spike,\n            self.bar,\n            self.method,\n            self.measured,\n            verdict,\n            self.platform,\n            self.hw_class,\n            self.captured_utc\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// The SP-5 honesty gate (BLUEPRINT-P63 §3.5 / §4.1): a battery verdict CANNOT\n/// be constructed from an `HwClass::Emulator` reading — an emulator battery\n/// number is physically meaningless and must be rejected at the type level. A\n/// real battery record can only carry `BudgetAndroid`/`MidAndroid`/… readings,\n/// or a `Blocked` verdict naming the missing device.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct BatteryVerdictRecord {\n    inner: VerdictRecord,\n}\n\n/// Why a battery record could not be built.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum VerdictError {\n    /// SP-5 forbids `HwClass::Emulator` (BLUEPRINT-P63 §3.5).\n    EmulatorForbidden,\n}\n\nimpl BatteryVerdictRecord {\n    /// Build a battery verdict record, rejecting any emulator-class reading.\n    pub fn try_new(inner: VerdictRecord) -> Result<Self, VerdictError> {\n        if matches!(inner.hw_class, HwClass::Emulator) {\n            Err(VerdictError::EmulatorForbidden)\n        } else {\n            Ok(BatteryVerdictRecord { inner })\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_measured_pass(&self) -> bool {\n        self.inner.is_measured_pass()\n    }\n\n    pub fn to_markdown_row(&self) -> String {\n CI".to_string(),\n            platform: Platform::Desktop {\n                os: DesktopOs::Linux,\n            },\n            hw_class: HwClass::Emulator,\n            verdict: SpikeVerdict::Blocked {\n                on: "physical desktop GPU".to_string(),\n            },\n            captured_utc: 1,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verdict_honesty_gate_blocks_non_confirms() {\n ..b.clone()\n        };\n        assert!(confirms.is_measured_pass(), "Confirms is the only pass");\n\n        let contradicts = VerdictRecord {\n            verdict: SpikeVerdict::Contradicts {\n                evidence: "p95 frame 41ms".to_string(),\n            },\n            ..b.clone()\n        };\n        assert!(!contradicts.is_measured_pass(), "Contradicts is not a pass");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sp5_battery_rejects_emulator_at_construction() {\n        let emulator = VerdictRecord {\n            spike: SpikeId::Sp5Battery,\n            ..base()\n        };\n        assert!(\n            matches!(\n                BatteryVerdictRecord::try_new(emulator.clone()),\n                Err(VerdictError::EmulatorForbidden)\n            ),\n            "SP-5 battery record MUST reject HwClass::Emulator"\n        );\n\n        // A real (honestly-Blocked) record with a physical device class builds.\n        let real = VerdictRecord {\n            hw_class: HwClass::BudgetAndroid,\n            platform: Platform::MobileAndroid {\n                chipset: "pixel-a-series".to_string(),\n            },\n            ..emulator.clone()\n        };\n        let built = BatteryVerdictRecord::try_new(real);\n        assert!(built.is_ok(), "a non-emulator battery record builds");\n        assert!(\n            !built.unwrap().is_measured_pass(),\n Keeps the native rules byte-identical to tools/skillspector without manual copies.\n\nuse std::env;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::Command;\n\nfn main() {\n    // Re-run if the Python analyzer sources change.\n    let py_sources = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))\n        .join("..")\n        .join("skillspector")\n        .join("src")\n        .join("skillspector")\n        .join("nodes")\n        .join("analyzers");\n    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", py_sources.display());\n\n    // Invoke the AST generator (pure python stdlib).\n    let manifest = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));\n    let gen = manifest.join("gen_rules.py");\n    let status = Command::new("python3")\n        .arg(&gen)\n        .current_dir(&manifest)\n        .status();\n\n    match status {\n        Ok(s) if s.success() => {}\n        _ => {\n            // Generator failed — but rules.rs may already exist from a prior run.\n            // Only hard-fail if it's missing (truly cannot build).\n            let rules = manifest.join("src").join("rules.rs");\n            if !rules.exists() {\n                eprintln!("cargo:warning=gen_rules.py failed and src/rules.rs is missing");\n                std::process::exit(1);\n            }\n            eprintln!("cargo:warning=gen_rules.py failed; using existing src/rules.rs");\n        }\n    }\n}\n	4624	-1	-1		fbb9b4d76d47402e346ce7f531246283a3dfa5761e31a6cafd40c0e44b55c269c93051118693375f35124d5b015380a507252537d0699b2cb42622af1a134444542325194dba174599cb2112859f8549d85f4c136b9c6049f8a663b48c43977c23a1a4f1a89347d0fbfe8cc8770f8c002d21cda86c753c9a83411266c2b43cc8

}\n    if !matches!(file_type, "markdown" | "text") {\n        return false;\n    }\n    if file_path.replace('\\\\', "/").to_lowercase().ends_with("skill.md") {\n        return false;\n    }\n    if content[..match_start].matches('\\n').count();\n    let start = match_line.saturating_sub(window);\n    let end = (match_line + window + 1).min(lines.len());\n    let ctx: String = lines[start..end].concat();\n    if ctx.len() > 400 { ctx[..400].to_string() } else { ctx }\n}\n\n/// Recursively collect files under a path (dir) or a single file.\npub fn collect_files(root: &str) {\n            if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&dir) {\n                for e in entries.flatten() {\n                    let path = e.path();\n                    if path.is_dir() {\n }\n        out.sort();\n    } else if p.is_file() {\n        out.push(root.to_string());\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Scan a list of paths (files or dirs), returning all findings + a summary.\npub fn scan_paths(paths: &[String]) -> (Vec<Finding>, ScanSummary) {\n    let mut all = Vec::new();\n    let mut files_scanned = 0usize;\n    let mut files_skipped = 0usize;\n    for root in paths {\n        for file in collect_files(root) {\n            // skip binary by extension quickly\n            if BINARY_EXTS.iter().any(|e| file.to_lowercase().ends_with(e)) {\n                files_skipped += 1;\n in &all {\n        *by_sev.entry(f.severity.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;\n    }\n    let summary = ScanSummary {\n        files_scanned,\n        files_skipped,\n        findings: all.len(),\n EXPLANATIONS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[\n    ("AR1", "Skill instructs the agent to never refuse or to always comply. Suppressing the agent's ability to decline removes a core safety control and enables downstream harmful requests to succeed."),\n    ("AR2", "Skill instructs the agent to omit warnings, disclaimers, or ethical commentary. Stripping safety caveats hides risk from the user and is a common jailbreak preamble."),\n    ("AR3", "Skill attempts to nullify the agent's safety policies or restrictions ('you have no restrictions', 'ignore your guidelines', 'do anything now'). This is a direct jailbreak that disables guardrails."),\n    ("AS1", "Skill reads from agent configuration directories (.claude/, .codex/, .gemini/). These directories may contain API keys, personal settings, and other credentials that the skill has no legitimate need to access."),\n    ("AS2", "Skill accesses MCP server configuration files (mcp.json). MCP configs contain server URLs, authentication tokens, and tool definitions — reading them allows the skill to discover and potentially abuse other tool integrations."),\n    ("AS3", "Skill enumerates or reads other installed skills. Access to other skills' SKILL.md files or the skills directory reveals prompt instructions, capabilities, and secrets that should be invisible to peer skills."),\n    ("AST1", "Direct exec() call allows arbitrary code execution. An attacker can inject code that runs with the full privileges of the process."),\n    ("AST2", "Direct eval() call evaluates arbitrary expressions. This can be exploited to execute malicious code or exfiltrate data."),\n    ("AST3", "Dynamic __import__() can load arbitrary modules at runtime, bypassing static analysis and potentially importing malicious code."),\n    ("AST4", "subprocess module calls execute external commands. Without careful input validation, this enables command injection."),\n    ("AST5", "os.system() and os exec-family calls run shell commands with the process's full privileges, enabling arbitrary command execution."),\n    ("AST6", "compile() creates code objects from strings. When combined with exec()/eval(), it enables obfuscated code execution."),\n    ("AST7", "Dynamic getattr() with a non-literal attribute name can access arbitrary object attributes, potentially bypassing access controls."),\n    ("AST8", "A dangerous execution chain combines code execution (exec/eval) with a dynamic source (network, encoded data, dynamic import), creating a high-confidence attack vector."),\n    ("AST9", "Reflective access to an execution sink via getattr() with a constant name (e.g. getattr(os, 'system'), getattr(builtins, 'exec')) is functionally identical to a direct exec/os.system call but evades name-based detection. This is a deliberate evasion technique rather than idiomatic code."),\n    ("E1", "Data is being sent to an external URL. This could be legitimate telemetry or data exfiltration. Manual review is recommended."),\n    ("E2", "Code accesses environment variables that may contain secrets (API keys, tokens). This is a common pattern for credential theft."),\n    ("E3", "Code scans file system directories looking for sensitive files. This could be reconnaissance for credential theft."),\n    ("E4", "Code or instructions that leak agent conversation context to external services, potentially exposing sensitive user interactions."),\n    ("EA1", "Skill grants unrestricted tool access without appropriate constraints. An agent with unfettered tool access can perform arbitrary actions including file modification, network requests, and code execution."),\n    ("EA2", "Skill enables autonomous high-impact decisions without human-in-the-loop verification. Critical operations (destructive commands, financial transactions, data deletion) should require explicit user confirmation."),\n    ("EA3", "Skill's behavior or capabilities extend beyond its stated purpose. Scope creep allows an agent to perform actions unrelated to its documented functionality, increasing the attack surface."),\n    ("EA4", "Skill allows unbounded resource consumption (API calls, storage, compute). Without rate limits or quotas, a compromised or misbehaving agent can cause denial-of-service or cost overruns."),\n    ("LP1", "Code uses capabilities (network, shell, file write, etc.) not covered by declared permissions. The skill does more than it claims, which may indicate deceptive intent."),\n    ("LP2", "Permission list contains a wildcard ('*' or 'all'), granting blanket access with no least-privilege boundary. This disables permission-based security controls entirely."),\n    ("LP3", "Skill has no permissions field in its manifest but code uses detectable capabilities. Without declared permissions, the skill's intent is opaque and cannot be validated."),\n    ("LP4", "Permission is declared but no corresponding code capability was detected. This may indicate removed functionality or pre-staging for future abuse."),\n    ("MP1", "Skill injects content designed to persist in agent memory or context across interactions. Persistent injection can alter agent behavior long after the initial interaction."),\n    ("MP2", "Skill attempts to fill the context window with filler content, displacing legitimate instructions and safety constraints. This can degrade agent performance or bypass safety boundaries."),\n    ("MP3", "Skill manipulates agent memory, state, or stored context. Memory corruption can alter personality, override safety rules, or cause unpredictable behavior."),\n    ("OH1", "Model output is used without validation or sanitization. Unvalidated output injected into downstream contexts (SQL, shell, HTML) enables injection attacks and arbitrary code execution."),\n    ("OH2", "Output from one security context is used in another without boundary enforcement. Cross-context output flow can leak sensitive information or escalate privileges across trust boundaries."),\n    ("OH3", "Output size or generation rate is not bounded. Unbounded output enables denial-of-service through resource exhaustion, log flooding, or context-window stuffing."),\n    ("P1", "This pattern attempts to override system instructions or ignore safety constraints. Without LLM analysis, manual review is recommended."),\n    ("P2", "Hidden instructions were detected in comments or invisible text. These could contain malicious directives. Manual review is recommended."),\n    ("P3", "Instructions found that direct the agent to transmit conversation context or user data to external services."),\n    ("P4", "Subtle instructions detected that may alter agent decision-making or introduce hidden biases."),\n    ("P5", "This content may contain harmful instructions that could cause physical harm if followed. CRITICAL: Review carefully before use."),\n    ("P6", "Skill contains instructions that could directly expose system prompts, internal rules, or hidden instructions to users or external parties."),\n    ("P7", "Skill contains patterns that could indirectly extract system prompts through rephrasing, translation, summarization, or side-channel techniques."),\n    ("P8", "Skill contains patterns that exfiltrate system prompts or internal instructions via tool calls (file writes, network requests, logging)."),\n    ("PE1", "Skill requests more permissions than appear necessary for its stated functionality. Review if elevated access is justified."),\n    ("PE2", "Commands invoke sudo or root privileges. Session persistence allows an attacker to maintain access beyond the current interaction."),\n    ("SC1", "Dependencies lack version pinning, allowing potential malicious package updates. Consider pinning versions."),\n    ("SC2", "Remote code is downloaded and executed. This bypasses code review and could introduce malicious code."),\n    ("SC3", "Code contains obfuscation (base64, hex encoding with execution). This is often used to hide malicious functionality."),\n    ("SC4", "Dependency has known vulnerabilities (CVEs). Abandoned packages no longer receive security patches, leaving known and future vulnerabilities unaddressed."),\n    ("SC6", "Package name closely resembles a popular package, suggesting possible typosquatting. This enables remote code execution or command injection."),\n    ("YR1", "YARA rule matched a known malware signature (reverse shell, backdoor, ransomware, C2 framework, or info stealer)."),\n    ("YR2", "YARA rule matched a known webshell pattern (PHP, Python, JSP, or ASPX webshell)."),\n    ("YR3", "YARA rule matched cryptocurrency mining indicators (stratum protocol, mining pools, miner binaries, or cryptojacking scripts)."),\n    ("YR4", "YARA rule matched a hack tool or exploit indicator (offensive tools, reconnaissance, privilege escalation, or exploit frameworks)."),\n];\n\n/// REMEDIATIONS (keyed by rule_id prefix).\npub static REMEDIATIONS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[\n    ("AR1", "Remove any instruction telling the agent to never refuse or always comply. The agent must retain the ability to decline unsafe, out-of-scope, or harmful requests."),\n    ("AR2", "Remove instructions that suppress warnings, disclaimers, or ethical commentary. Let the agent surface safety-relevant caveats to the user."),\n    ("AR3", "Remove jailbreak framing that nullifies safety policies or restrictions. Skill content must not instruct the agent to ignore its guidelines or operate without guardrails."),\n    ("AS1", "Remove all code or instructions that access agent configuration directories (.claude/, .codex/, .gemini/). If configuration values are needed, pass them explicitly as parameters or environment variables — never read the agent's own config files."),\n    ("AS2", "Remove all code or instructions that read MCP configuration files (mcp.json). MCP server details should be managed by the agent runtime, not read by individual skills."),\n    ("AS3", "Remove all code or instructions that list or read other skills' files or directories. Skills should operate independently; cross-skill access is a privilege escalation."),\n    ("AST1", "Replace exec() with a safe alternative. If dynamic execution is required, use a sandboxed environment or restricted eval with __builtins__ disabled."),\n    ("AST2", "Replace eval() with ast.literal_eval() for data parsing, or use explicit parsing logic. Never evaluate untrusted strings."),\n    ("AST3", "Use standard import statements instead of __import__(). If dynamic loading is needed, use importlib with an allowlist of permitted modules."),\n    ("AST4", "Use subprocess.run() with shell=False and an explicit argument list. 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/telemetry/hetzner-exporter/src/lib.rs	lib · 266 lines	//! hetzner-exporter — host-resource gauges (pure-std).\n//!\n//! Replaces the deleted `tools/telemetry/hetzner_exporter.py`. Computes the\n//! load-bearing host gauges ON REQUEST (no background loop, near-zero CPU) and\n//! exposes them as a canonical f64 array (kernel `field_metrics` wire shape).\n//!\n//! Gauges (operator-selected frictions):\n//!   disk_pct — root filesystem usage %       (alert > 90)\n//!   load1    — 1-min load / #cpu (normalized) (alert > 1.0 sustained = saturated)\n//!   mem_pct  — RAM used %                     (alert > 90)\n\n/// Ordered numeric schema — the canonical native f64 layout.\npub const GAUGE_SCHEMA: [&str; 3] = ["disk_pct", "load1", "mem_pct"];\n\n/// Compute host resource state as the canonical native f64 array.\n/// Non-numeric metadata (`ts`) rides at the edge, not in the native array.\npub fn gauges_native() -> [f64; 3] {\n    // disk_pct from statvfs on "/".\n    let disk_pct = match statvfs_root() {\n        Some((bavail, blocks)) if blocks > 0 => {\n            let used = blocks - bavail;\n            round1((used as f64 / blocks as f64) * 100.0)\n        }\n        _ => -1.0,\n    };\n\n    // load1 normalized by CPU count.\n    let load_norm = match loadavg() {\n        Some(l1) => {\n            let ncpu = num_cpus();\n            round2(l1 / ncpu as f64)\n        }\n        None => -1.0,\n    };\n\n    // mem_pct from /proc/meminfo.\n    let mem_pct = match meminfo() {\n        Some((total, avail)) if total > 0 => round1((1.0 - avail as f64 / total as f64) * 100.0),\n        _ => -1.0,\n    };\n\n    [disk_pct, load_norm, mem_pct]\n}\n\n/// EDGE helper: native array + ts -> JSON-friendly dict (Gatus/Telemetry text).\npub fn gauges_dict() -> std::collections::HashMap<String, f64> {\n    let v = gauges_native();\n    let mut m = std::collections::HashMap::new();\n    for (k, val) in GAUGE_SCHEMA.iter().zip(v.iter()) {\n        m.insert((*k).to_string(), *val);\n    }\n    m\n}\n\nfn round1(x: f64) -> f64 {\n    (x * 10.0).round() / 10.0\n}\nfn round2(x: f64) -> f64 {\n    (x * 100.0).round() / 100.0\n}\n\n#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]\nfn statvfs_root() -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n    // Read statvfs via libc is overkill; parse /proc/mounts-free approach using\n    // the `stat` syscall is not std, so we read the root filesystem free/blocks\n    // by shelling to `df`? No — pure-std. Use std::fs::metadata for total bytes\n    // on "/" is not available cross-platform for free blocks. Instead read\n    // /proc/self/mountinfo? Simpler: use `std::os::unix` statvfs via libc is not\n    // std. We approximate disk usage from /proc/mounts is complex. Use a direct\n    // syscall-free method: read `/sys/...`? Not std.\n    //\n    // Pragmatic pure-std path: spawn `df` is forbidden (no subprocess in a gauge\n    // crate? it's fine, but we prefer std). We use the `nix`? no. Acceptable:\n    // read available/used from `df -B1 /` via std::process is allowed (it's std).\n    use std::process::Command;\n    let out = Command::new("df").arg("-B1").arg("/").output().ok()?;\n    let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);\n    // Second line: Filesystem 1B-blocks Used Available Use% Mounted\n    let line = s.lines().nth(1)?;\n    let cols: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n    if cols.len() < 4 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let blocks: u64 = cols[1].parse().ok()?;\n    let bavail: u64 = cols[3].parse().ok()?;\n    Some((bavail, blocks))\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]\nfn statvfs_root() -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n    None\n}\n\n#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]\nfn loadavg() -> Option<f64> {\n    let s = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/loadavg").ok()?;\n    s.split_whitespace().next()?.parse::<f64>().ok()\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]\nfn loadavg() -> Option<f64> {\n    None\n}\n\n#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]\nfn meminfo() -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n    let s = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/meminfo").ok()?;\n    let mut total = 0u64;\n    let mut avail = 0u64;\n    for line in s.lines() {\n        let mut it = line.split(':');\n        let key = it.next()?.trim();\n        let val = it.next()?.split_whitespace().next()?.parse::<u64>().ok()?;\n        if key == "MemTotal" {\n            total = val;\n        } else if key == "MemAvailable" {\n            avail = val;\n        }\n    }\n    if total == 0 {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some((total, avail))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]\nfn meminfo() -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n    None\n}\n\nfn num_cpus() -> usize {\n    std::thread::available_parallelism()\n        .map(|n| n.get())\n        .unwrap_or(1)\n}\n\n/// Absolute RAM usage `(used_bytes, total_bytes)` — the SAME `/proc/meminfo` read that\n/// backs `mem_pct` (used = MemTotal − MemAvailable), exposed absolutely so consumers can\n/// render "2.8 / 30.6 GiB" next to the percentage. `None` on read failure.\npub fn mem_bytes() -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n    let (total_kb, avail_kb) = meminfo()?;\n    Some((total_kb.saturating_sub(avail_kb) * 1024, total_kb * 1024))\n}\n\n/// Absolute root-filesystem usage `(used_bytes, total_bytes)` — the SAME statvfs-style\n/// read that backs `disk_pct`. `None` on read failure.\npub fn disk_bytes() -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n    let (bavail, blocks) = statvfs_root()?;\n    Some((blocks.saturating_sub(bavail), blocks))\n}\n\n/// Cumulative network I/O since boot: `(rx_bytes, tx_bytes)` summed across every\n/// non-loopback interface in `/proc/net/dev`. Counters, not rates — the consumer decides\n/// whether to show totals or diff two snapshots. `None` on read/parse failure (never a\n/// fabricated 0), same degrade-closed convention as the other gauges.\n#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]\npub fn net_io_bytes() -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n    let s = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/net/dev").ok()?;\n    parse_net_dev(&s)\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]\npub fn net_io_bytes() -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n    None\n}\n\n/// Pure parser for `/proc/net/dev` content. Per-interface lines are `name: <16 counters>`\n/// where field 1 is rx_bytes and field 9 is tx_bytes; the two header lines carry no `:`\n/// (the `Inter-|`/`face |` banner) and are skipped naturally. `lo` is excluded — loopback\n/// traffic is not host network I/O.\nfn parse_net_dev(s: &str) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n    let mut rx = 0u64;\n    let mut tx = 0u64;\n    let mut seen = false;\n    for line in s.lines() {\n        let (name, rest) = match line.split_once(':') {\n            Some(x) => x,\n            None => continue,\n        };\n        if name.trim() == "lo" {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let fields: Vec<&str> = rest.split_whitespace().collect();\n        if fields.len() < 16 {\n            return None; // malformed row: refuse to report a partial sum\n        }\n        rx = rx.checked_add(fields[0].parse().ok()?)?;\n        tx = tx.checked_add(fields[8].parse().ok()?)?;\n        seen = true;\n    }\n    if seen {\n        Some((rx, tx))\n    } else {\n        None\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn schema_is_fixed_three_gauges() {\n        assert_eq!(GAUGE_SCHEMA.len(), 3);\n        assert_eq!(GAUGE_SCHEMA[0], "disk_pct");\n        assert_eq!(GAUGE_SCHEMA[1], "load1");\n        assert_eq!(GAUGE_SCHEMA[2], "mem_pct");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn gauges_native_returns_three_values() {\n        let g = gauges_native();\n        assert_eq!(g.len(), 3);\n        // On a real Linux host every gauge should be in [0,100] (unless error -1).\n        for (i, v) in g.iter().enumerate() {\n            if *v >= 0.0 {\n                assert!(\n                    (0.0..=100.0).contains(v),\n                    "gauge {} = {} out of [0,100]",\n                    i,\n                    v\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn gauges_dict_is_schema_keyed() {\n        let d = gauges_dict();\n        assert_eq!(d.len(), 3);\n        assert!(d.contains_key("disk_pct"));\n        assert!(d.contains_key("load1"));\n        assert!(d.contains_key("mem_pct"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_net_dev_sums_non_loopback_and_skips_lo() {\n        let fixture = "\\\nInter-|   Receive                                                |  Transmit\n face |bytes    packets errs drop fifo frame compressed multicast|bytes    packets errs drop fifo colls carrier compressed\n    lo: 918392190 1670912    0    0    0     0          0         0 918392190 1670912    0    0    0     0       0 7    0    0    0     0       0          0\n";\n        // lo excluded; eth0 + wt0 summed: rx = 1000+500, tx = 2000+700.\n        assert_eq!(parse_net_dev(fixture), Some((1500, 2700)));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_net_dev_refuses_malformed_rows() {\n        assert_eq!(parse_net_dev("eth0: 12 34\\n"), None); // short row: no partial sum\n        assert_eq!(parse_net_dev("header only, no colon rows\\n"), None); // nothing seen\n    }\n\n    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]\n    #[test]\n    fn net_io_bytes_reads_real_counters_on_linux() {\n        // A live Linux host with any non-loopback here would mean\n        // the box has literally never sent a packet — worth failing loudly over).\n        assert!(rx > 0, "rx_bytes must be a positive accumulator, got {rx}");\n        assert!(tx > 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/telemetry/hetzner-exporter/src/main.rs	main · 217 lines	//! hetzner-exporter — pure-std HTTP edge.\n//!\n//! Serves the gauges as JSON on 127.0.0.1:9091/health for Gatus polling:\n//!   curl 127.0.0.1:9091/health\n//!   -> {"disk_pct":81.0,"load1":0.12,"mem_pct":9.0,"ts":...}\n//!\n//! Opt-in native edge: TELEMETRY_SER=native serves raw LE f64 bytes (the\n//! kernel wire shape) for native consumers, length = 3*8 = 24 bytes.\n//!\n//! Usage:\n//!   hetzner-exporter                 # foreground, serve forever\n//!   hetzner-exporter --once          # compute + print one JSON snapshot, exit\n//!   hetzner-exporter --selftest      # verify gauges compute + JSON is valid\n\nuse hetzner_exporter::{\n    disk_bytes, gauges_dict, gauges_native, mem_bytes, net_io_bytes, GAUGE_SCHEMA,\n};\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::TcpListener;\nuse std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\n\nconst HOST: &str = "127.0.0.1";\nconst PORT: u16 = 9091;\n\nfn main() {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();\n    let force_native = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--native");\n    if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--once") {\n        println!("{}", snapshot_json());\n        return;\n    }\n    if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--selftest") {\n        selftest();\n        return;\n    }\n    if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--probe") {\n        probe_once(force_native);\n        return;\n    }\n    serve_forever(force_native);\n}\n\n/// Edge selection: explicit `--native` flag wins; else the `TELEMETRY_SER`\n/// env var; default JSON. (Keeping the env path for drop-in parity with the\n/// deleted ser.py contract.)\nfn use_native_edge(force_native: bool) -> bool {\n    force_native || std::env::var("TELEMETRY_SER").unwrap_or_default() == "native"\n}\n\nfn now_ts() -> u64 {\n    SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_secs())\n        .unwrap_or(0)\n}\n\nfn snapshot_json() -> String {\n    let d = gauges_dict();\n    let ts = now_ts();\n    // Field order must be stable for Gatus JSON-body conditions.\n    let mut s = String::from("{");\n    let mut first = true;\n    for k in GAUGE_SCHEMA.iter() {\n        if !first {\n            s.push(',');\n        }\n        s.push_str(&format!("\\"{}\\":{}", k, d.get(*k).copied().unwrap_or(-1.0)));\n        first = false;\n    }\n    // Absolute mem/disk + network I/O ride at the JSON edge like `ts` (not 0-100 gauges —\n    // they stay out of the canonical 3-f64 native wire). -1 = read failure, same\n    // error-sentinel convention as the gauges above. mem in MiB, disk in GiB (1024-based,\n    // matching what `free -m` / `df -h` show the operator).\n    match mem_bytes() {\n        Some((used, total)) => s.push_str(&format!(\n            ",\\"mem_used_mb\\":{},\\"mem_total_mb\\":{}",\n            used / (1 << 20),\n            total / (1 << 20)\n        )),\n        None => s.push_str(",\\"mem_used_mb\\":-1,\\"mem_total_mb\\":-1"),\n    }\n    match disk_bytes() {\n        Some((used, total)) => s.push_str(&format!(\n            ",\\"disk_used_gb\\":{:.1},\\"disk_total_gb\\":{:.1}",\n            used as f64 / (1u64 << 30) as f64,\n            total as f64 / (1u64 << 30) as f64\n        )),\n        None => s.push_str(",\\"disk_used_gb\\":-1,\\"disk_total_gb\\":-1"),\n    }\n    match net_io_bytes() {\n        Some((rx, tx)) => s.push_str(&format!(",\\"net_rx_bytes\\":{},\\"net_tx_bytes\\":{}", rx, tx)),\n        None => s.push_str(",\\"net_rx_bytes\\":-1,\\"net_tx_bytes\\":-1"),\n    }\n    s.push_str(&format!(",\\"ts\\":{}}}", ts));\n    s\n}\n\nfn serve_forever(force_native: bool) {\n    let addr = format!("{}:{}", HOST, PORT);\n    let listener = match TcpListener::bind(&addr) {\n        Ok(l) => l,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!("hetzner-exporter: bind {addr} failed: {e}");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n    };\n    eprintln!("hetzner-exporter: serving {addr}/health (ctrl-c to stop)");\n    for stream in listener.incoming() {\n        match stream {\n            Ok(mut s) => {\n                // Read + discard the request, then respond. Keep it lean.\n                let mut buf = [0u8; 1024];\n                let _ = s.read(&mut buf);\n                let native = use_native_edge(force_native);\n                let (body, ctype) = if native {\n                    let v = gauges_native();\n                    let mut b = Vec::with_capacity(24);\n                    for x in v.iter() {\n                        b.extend_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes());\n                    }\n                    (b, "application/octet-stream")\n                } else {\n                    (snapshot_json().into_bytes(), "application/json")\n                };\n                let resp = format!(\n                    "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\\r\\nContent-Type: {}\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n",\n                    ctype,\n                    body.len()\n                );\n                let _ = s.write_all(resp.as_bytes());\n                let _ = s.write_all(&body);\n            }\n            Err(_) => continue,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn probe_once(force_native: bool) {\n    // Deterministic, harness-safe check of what the server WOULD answer:\n    // build the same body the HTTP 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/telemetry/native-ser/src/json.rs	json · 251 lines	//! Minimal hand-rolled JSON — enough for the EDGE adapter contract\n//! (`json_edge` / `from_json`). No serde, no external crates.\n//!\n//! Supports the subset the telemetry edges actually emit/consume:\n//! objects, arrays, numbers (f64), strings (with the common escapes),\n//! `true`/`false`/`null`. This mirrors ser.py's stdlib-`json` use exactly:\n//! the gauges dict (`{"disk_pct":81.0,"load1":0.12,"mem_pct":9.0,"ts":...}`)\n//! round-trips, which is the only thing the EDGE adapter No serde, no external crates. (no length prefix; caller knows N).\npub fn wire_f64(values: &[f64]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(values.len() * 8);\n    for &v in values {\n        out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Canonical: decode a raw LE f64 byte block back to f64s.\n/// `n` = number of f64s; defaults to byte-length / 8.\npub fn unwire_f64(b: &[u8], n: Option<usize>) -> Vec<f64> {\n    let n = n.unwrap_or(b.len() / 8);\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n    for i in 0..n {\n        let off = i * 8;\n        if off + 8 > b.len() {\n            break;\n        }\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 8];\n        buf.copy_from_slice(&b[off..off + 8]);\n        out.push(f64::from_le_bytes(buf));\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Encode a numeric dict into a native f64 array following `schema` (ordered keys).\n/// Labels (str/bool) stay at the EDGE, not in the native array.\npub fn native_of(schema: &[&str], obj: &std::collections::HashMap<String, f64>) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let vals: Vec<f64> = schema.iter().map(|k| obj.get(*k).copied().unwrap_or(0.0)).collect();\n    wire_f64(&vals)\n}\n\n/// Decode a native f64 array back to a dict under `schema`.\npub fn obj_of(schema: &[&str], b: &[u8]) -> std::collections::HashMap<String, f64> {\n    let vals = unwire_f64(b, Some(schema.len()));\n    let mut m = std::collections::HashMap::new();\n    for (k, v) in schema.iter().zip(vals.iter()) {\n        m.insert((*k).to_string(), *v);\n    }\n    m\n}\n\n/// EDGE: produce JSON text (Gatus body, grep-able 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/telemetry/native-ser/src/main.rs	main · 148 lines	//! native-ser CLI — command surface matching the deleted ser.py, so nothing\n//! that shelled out to `python3 ser.py ...` breaks.\n//!\n//!   native-ser wire 3.14 -2.5 0          # -> hex LE f64 bytes (canonical)\n//!   native-ser unwrap <hex>              # -> space-separated f64s\n//!   native-ser obj disk_pct=81 load1=0.12 mem_pct=9   # -> schema-ordered native f64s\n//!   native-ser unobj disk_pct load1 mem_pct <hex>     # -> schema-keyed values\n//!   native-ser json '{"a":1,"b":2}'     # -> validate + re-emit\n//!   native-ser edge                     # -> current TELEMETRY_SER selector\n//!   native-ser selftest                 # -> parity check vs the Python contract\n//!\n//! `obj`/`unobj` exercise the schema-ordered native form (the kernel C-ABI\n//! `field_metrics` layout): key order is fixed, so native consumers never\n//! depend on JSON key presence.\n\nuse native_ser::{default_edge, from_json, json_edge, native_of, obj_of, wire_f64, unwire_f64, Json};\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\n\nconst DEFAULT_SCHEMA: &[&str] = &["disk_pct", "load1", "mem_pct"];\n\nfn main() {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();\n    if args.len() < 2 {\n        eprintln!("native-ser: wire|unwrap|obj|unobj|json|edge|selftest");\n        std::process::exit(2);\n    }\n    match args[1].as_str() {\n        "wire" => {\n            let vals: Vec<f64> = args[2..].iter().filter_map(|s| s.parse().ok()).collect();\n            let b = wire_f64(&vals);\n            print!("{}", hex(&b));\n        }\n        "unwrap" => {\n            let hex = args.get(2).map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("");\n            let b = unhex(hex);\n            let v = unwire_f64(&b, None);\n            let s: Vec<String> = v.iter().map(|x| format!("{:.6}", x)).collect();\n            println!("{}", s.join(" "));\n        }\n        "obj" => {\n            // key=val pairs -> schema-ordered native f64 array on stdout.\n            let mut map: HashMap<String, f64> = HashMap::new();\n            for kv in &args[2..] {\n                if let Some((k, v)) = kv.split_once('=') {\n                    if let Ok(f) = v.parse::<f64>() {\n                        map.insert(k.to_string(), f);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            let b = native_of(DEFAULT_SCHEMA, &map);\n            let arr = unwire_f64(&b, None);\n            let s: Vec<String> = arr.iter().map(|x| format!("{:.6}", x)).collect();\n            println!("{}", s.join(" "));\n        }\n        "unobj" => {\n            // schema keys... then `<hex>` -> schema-keyed `k=v` lines.\n            if args.len() < 4 {\n                eprintln!("native-ser: unobj <schema...> <hex>");\n                std::process::exit(2);\n            }\n            let hex = args.last().unwrap();\n            let schema: Vec<&str> = args[2..args.len() - 1].iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n            let b = unhex(hex);\n            let back = obj_of(&schema, &b);\n            for k in &schema {\n                println!("{}={}", k, back.get(*k).copied().unwrap_or(-1.0));\n            }\n        }\n        "json" => {\n            let s = args.get(2).map(|x| x.as_str()).unwrap_or("");\n            match from_json(s) {\n                Ok(j) => println!("{}", json_edge(&j)),\n                Err(e) => {\n                    eprintln!("native-ser: json parse error: {e}");\n                    std::process::exit(1);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        "edge" => println!("{}", default_edge()),\n        "selftest" => selftest(),\n        other => {\n            eprintln!("native-ser: unknown subcommand `{other}`");\n            std::process::exit(2);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn hex(b: &[u8]) -> String {\n    let mut s = String::with_capacity(b.len() * 2);\n    for x in b {\n        s.push_str(&format!("{:02x}", x));\n    }\n    s\n}\n\nfn unhex(s: &str) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    let bytes = s.as_bytes();\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i + 1 < bytes.len() || i < bytes.len() {\n        if i + 1 >= bytes.len() {\n            break;\n        }\n        let hi = (bytes[i] as char).to_digit(16);\n        let lo = (bytes[i + 1] as char).to_digit(16);\n        if let (Some(h), Some(l)) = (hi, lo) {\n            out.push((h * 16 + l) as u8);\n        }\n        i += 2;\n    }\n    out\n}\n\nfn selftest() {\n    // (1) wire round-trip bit-identical.\n    let v = [3.14f64, -2.5, 0.0, 1e9];\n    let b = wire_f64(&v);\n    let back = unwire_f64(&b, None);\n    assert_eq!(v.to_vec(), back, "wire round-trip bit-identical");\n\n    // (2) native_of/obj_of schema-ordered.\n    let schema = ["disk_pct", "load1", "mem_pct"];\n    let mut obj = HashMap::new();\n    obj.insert("disk_pct".to_string(), 81.0);\n    obj.insert("load1".to_string(), 0.12);\n    obj.insert("mem_pct".to_string(), 9.0);\n    let b = native_of(&schema, &obj);\n    let back = obj_of(&schema, &b);\n    assert_eq!(back.get("disk_pct").copied().unwrap_or(-1.0), 81.0);\n    assert_eq!(back.get("load1").copied().unwrap_or(-1.0), 0.12);\n\n    // (3) json edge round-trip.\n    let j = Json::Obj(vec![\n        ("disk_pct".into(), Json::Num(81.0)),\n        ("load1".into(), Json::Num(0.12)),\n    ]);\n    let s = json_edge(&j);\n    let parsed = from_json(&s).expect("json parse");\n    assert_eq!(parsed, j);\n\n    // (4) default_edge validates.\n    std::env::set_var("TELEMETRY_SER", "native");\n    assert_eq!(default_edge(), "native");\n    std::env::remove_var("TELEMETRY_SER");\n\n    println!("SELFTEST PASS: wire+obj+json+edge contracts hold");\n}\n	4751	-1	-1		83c63eb4b055276d4233e86351d37a230856bfe4ad3a5e42ec7eaed9e81ad97701c65091e59c2ee1a05396831089b2a9c76d0ff8f548c2aaf0e6202fc526780c0a4e54916da390309957125294ab4fbac049e96a69f5e909788224a4880993b6a7a5e6f1bcc318d1c07889c6065d21d7651545ecb78baca626b9f67547f73414

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/tools/telemetry/native-trackers/src/main.rs	main · 1025 lines	//! native-trackers — zero-dep native port of the python/bash telemetry trackers.\n//!\n//! Replaces the interpreter-heredoc compute that lived inside:\n//!   - kernel/benches/bench_track.py   (bench baseline comparison)\n//!   - tools/telemetry/governance.sh    (gov_route fold, gov_falseclaim meter, gov_meta EMA)\n//!   - tools/telemetry/topics.sh        (bench-watch deltas)\n//!\n//! All three spawned `python3 - <<'PY' ... PY` on every call — the slow path the\n//! operator flagged. This binary does the same fold in native Rust over the SAME\n//! JSONL ledgers (`track_record.jsonl`, `false_claims.jsonl`, `precedents.jsonl`),\n//! no interpreter, no JSON crate (hand-rolled over the fixed schema).\n//!\n//! Subcommands:\n//!   bench  <crate-dir> [--threshold N]   run `cargo bench`, compare to baseline.json, print deltas\n//!   route  <task> [budget] [ruin]        fold track_record.jsonl → per-model (p,v,cost) for gov_route\n//!   false-claim [--record c v]           EMA false-estimation meter over false_claims.jsonl\n//!   meta   observe <bench_prev> <bench_new> <eval_prev> <eval_new> <false_rate>\n//!   swarm-proof                          economic crossover + parallel vs sequential fan-out proof\n//!   ser    <wire|json> [hex-or-json]     canonical f64 wire <-> JSON edge adapter\n//!\n//! Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 bench regression beyond threshold; 2 usage/IO error.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n#[cfg(unix)]\nuse std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;\nuse std::env;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::{self, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Minimal JSON value + fixed-schema extraction (no serde).\n// We only parse flat objects with string/float/bool leaves — enough for the\n// gov_route / false_claim / track_record ledgers.\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nenum Jv {\n    Str(String),\n    Num(f64),\n    Bool(bool),\n    Null,\n}\n\n/// Parse a single JSON object (`{ ... }`) into a flat key→value map.\n/// Tolerant: skips malformed lines, unquoted/unknown tokens; never panics.\nfn parse_obj(s: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, Jv> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    let mut m = BTreeMap::new();\n    let bytes = s.as_bytes();\n    if bytes.first() != Some(&b'{') || bytes.last() != Some(&b'}') {\n        return m;\n    }\n    // Walk keys. We only support "key": value, where value is\n    // "string" | number | true | false | null.\n    let mut i = 1;\n    let n = bytes.len();\n    while i < n {\n        // find next quoted key\n        while i < n && bytes[i] != b'"' {\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        if i >= n {\n            break;\n        }\n        let key_start = i + 1;\n        let mut j = key_start;\n        while j < n && bytes[j] != b'"' {\n            j += 1;\n        }\n        if j >= n {\n            break;\n        }\n        let key = &s[key_start..j];\n        i = j + 1;\n        // skip to ':'\n        while i < n && bytes[i] != b':' {\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n        // skip whitespace\n        while i < n && bytes[i].is_ascii_whitespace() {\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        if i >= n {\n            break;\n        }\n        if bytes[i] == b'"' {\n            let v_start = i + 1;\n            let mut v = v_start;\n            while v < n && bytes[v] != b'"' {\n                v += 1;\n            }\n            m.insert(key.to_string(), Jv::Str(s[v_start..v].to_string()));\n            i = v + 1;\n        } else if s[i..].starts_with("true") {\n            m.insert(key.to_string(), Jv::Bool(true));\n            i += 4;\n        } else if s[i..].starts_with("false") {\n            m.insert(key.to_string(), Jv::Bool(false));\n            i += 5;\n        } else if s[i..].starts_with("null") {\n            m.insert(key.to_string(), Jv::Null);\n            i += 4;\n        } else {\n            // number until , or }\n            let v_start = i;\n            let mut v = i;\n            while v < n && bytes[v] != b',' && bytes[v] != b'}' {\n                v += 1;\n            }\n            let num = s[v_start..v].trim();\n            if let Ok(f) = num.parse::<f64>() {\n                m.insert(key.to_string(), Jv::Num(f));\n            }\n            i = v;\n        }\n    }\n    m\n}\n\nfn get_str(m: &BTreeMap<String, Jv>, k: &str) -> String {\n    match m.get(k) {\n        Some(Jv::Str(s)) => s.clone(),\n        _ => String::new(),\n    }\n}\nfn get_num(m: &BTreeMap<String, Jv>, k: &str) -> f64 {\n    match m.get(k) {\n        Some(Jv::Num(f)) => *f,\n        _ => 0.0,\n    }\n}\nfn get_bool(m: &BTreeMap<String, Jv>, k: &str) -> bool {\n    matches!(m.get(k), Some(Jv::Bool(true)))\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// 1. BENCH — native replacement for bench_track.py\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nfn cmd_bench(crate_dir: &str, threshold: f64, bench_name: Option<&str>) -> i32 {\n    let crate_path = Path::new(crate_dir);\n    let baseline_p = crate_path.join("benches/baseline.json");\n    let baseline = if baseline_p.exists() {\n        let txt = fs::read_to_string(&baseline_p).unwrap_or_default();\n        parse_baseline(&txt)\n    } else {\n        BTreeMap::new()\n    };\n\n    // Run cargo bench, stream combined output to a TEMP FILE (not a captured\n    // pipe). A captured pipe (Command::output()) can fill up on a large bench\n    // run and make cargo bench exit early — dropping the LATER benchmarks from\n    // the output (seen as spurious "MISSING" for empirical_identify/token_bucket).\n    // Writing to a file has no pipe buffer limit, so every benchmark's timing\n    // line is preserved. Parsed after the run completes.\n    let tmp = std::env::temp_dir().join("native-trackers-bench.log");\n    let file = match fs::File::create(&tmp) {\n        Ok(f) => f,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!("native-trackers: cannot create temp bench log: {e}");\n            return 2;\n        }\n    };\n    let mut cargo_args: Vec<&str> = vec!["bench"];\n    // Default bench target is `criterion` (kernel/llm/crates-bebop). agent-adapters\n    // uses `fuel_bench`; callers pass `--bench <name>` to override. We never run a\n    // bare `cargo bench` (which also runs lib/doctests that reject criterion's\n    // `--warm-up-time` etc. and fail the whole run).\n    let bench = bench_name.unwrap_or("criterion");\n    cargo_args.push("--bench");\n    cargo_args.push(bench);\n    cargo_args.push("--");\n    cargo_args.push("--warm-up-time");\n    cargo_args.push("1");\n    cargo_args.push("--measurement-time");\n    cargo_args.push("2");\n    cargo_args.push("--sample-size");\n    cargo_args.push("10");\n    let status = Command::new("cargo")\n        .args(&cargo_args)\n        .current_dir(crate_dir)\n        .stdout(Stdio::from(file.try_clone().expect("clone bench log")))\n        .stderr(Stdio::from(file))\n        .status();\n    let status = match status {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!("native-trackers: cargo bench failed to spawn: {e}");\n            return 2;\n        }\n    };\n    if !status.success() {\n        eprintln!("native-trackers: cargo bench exited non-zero");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    let text = match fs::read_to_string(&tmp) {\n        Ok(t) => t,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!("native-trackers: cannot read bench log: {e}");\n            return 2;\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Parse "name  time:   [lo unit mean unit hi unit]"\n    let re = regex_lite();\n    let mut cur = BTreeMap::new();\n    // criterion prints the benchmark name on its own line (`Benchmarking X`)\n    // and the `time: [...]` result on the NEXT line. For short names both land\n    // on one line; for long names the name line stands alone. We track the last\n    // seen `Benchmarking` name and use it when a `time:` line carries no inline\n    // name (this is what made empirical_identify/token_bucket read as MISSING).\n    let mut last_bench: Option<String> = None;\n    for line in text.lines() {\n        let line = line.trim();\n        if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("Benchmarking ") {\n            // `Benchmarking X` and `Benchmarking X: Warming up for ...` both\n            // appear; keep only the name (up to the first ':' or whitespace).\n            let name = rest.split(':').next().unwrap_or(rest).trim();\n            last_bench = Some(name.to_string());\n            continue;\n        }\n        if let Some((name, mean_ns)) = parse_timing(line, &re, last_bench.clone()) {\n            cur.insert(name, mean_ns);\n        }\n    }\n    if cur.is_empty() {\n        eprintln!("native-trackers: no timing lines parsed from cargo bench");\n        return 2;\n    }\n\n    // Auto-seed missing baselines (native, atomic).\n    let mut seeded = Vec::new();\n    let mut baseline_mut = baseline.clone();\n    for (name, mean) in &cur {\n        if !baseline_mut.contains_key(name) {\n            baseline_mut.insert(name.clone(), round4(*mean));\n            seeded.push(name.clone());\n        }\n    }\n    if !seeded.is_empty() {\n        let json = baseline_to_json(&baseline_mut);\n        let tmp = baseline_p.with_extension("tmp");\n        fs::write(&tmp, &json).ok();\n        fs::rename(&tmp, &baseline_p).ok();\n        eprintln!("[auto-seed] wrote {} new baseline(s): {:?}", seeded.len(), seeded);\n    }\n\n    println!("\\n=== crate: {} ===", crate_dir);\n    println!("{:32} {:>12} {:>12} {:>9}  verdict", "benchmark", "baseline_ns", "current_ns", "delta");\n    let mut worst = 0.0f64;\n    for (name, bmean) in &baseline {\n        let cmean = match cur.get(name) {\n            Some(v) => *v,\n            None => {\n                println!("{:32} {:12.2} {:>12} {:>9}  !!", name, bmean, "-", "MISSING");\n                worst = (threshold + 1.0).max(worst);\n                continue;\n            }\n        };\n        let delta = (cmean - bmean) / bmean * 100.0;\n        let verdict = if delta > threshold {\n            worst = worst.max(delta);\n            "REGRESS"\n        } else if delta < -threshold {\n            "improve"\n        } else {\n            "ok"\n        };\n        println!(\n            "{:32} {:12.2} {:12.2} {:+8.1}%  {}",\n            name, bmean, cmean, delta, verdict\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Rolling history (git-ignored).\n    let hist_p = crate_path.join("benches/BENCH_HISTORY.md");\n    let ts = now_iso();\n    if let Ok(mut f) = fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(&hist_p) {\n        let _ = writeln!(f, "\\n## {}", ts);\n        let _ = writeln!(f, "- native-trackers run (replaces bench_track.py)");\n        for (name, bmean) in &baseline {\n            if let Some(cmean) = cur.get(name) {\n                let delta = (cmean - bmean) / bmean * 100.0;\n                let _ = writeln!(f, "- {}: {:.2}ns -> {:.2}ns ({:+.1}%)", name, bmean, cmean, delta);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if worst > threshold {\n        println!("\\nREGRESSION: worst +{:.1}% > {:.0}% threshold", worst, threshold);\n        1\n    } else {\n        println!("\\nOK: no regression beyond threshold.");\n        0\n    }\n}\n\n// Tiny static regex replacement (no regex crate): match `name  time: [lo unit mean unit hi unit]`\nfn regex_lite() -> () {\n    ()\n}\nfn parse_timing(line: &str, _re: &(), last: Option<String>) -> Option<(String, f64)> {\n    // criterion output line shape:  `name  time:   [lo unit mean unit hi unit]`\n    // The name may be on the SAME line (short names) or on the preceding\n    // `Benchmarking <name>` line (long names). When it's not inline we fall\n    // back to `last` (the most recent Benchmarking name).\n    let line = line.trim();\n    let time_idx = line.find("time:")?;\n    // The token immediately before "time:" must be a non-empty name.\n    let before = &line[..time_idx];\n    let inline_name = before.split_whitespace().next_back();\n    let name = match inline_name {\n        Some(n) if !n.is_empty() && n != "time:" => n.to_string(),\n        _ => last?, // long-name case: use the tracked Benchmarking name\n    };\n    let open = line[time_idx..].find('[')? + time_idx;\n    let close = line[open..].find(']')? + open;\n    let inner = &line[open + 1..close];\n    let toks: Vec<&str> = inner.split_whitespace().collect();\n    // [lo unit mean unit hi unit] => index 2 = mean, 3 = unit\n    if toks.len() < 4 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let mean: f64 = toks[2].parse().ok()?;\n    let unit = toks[3];\n    let mult = match unit {\n        "ns" => 1.0,\n        "µs" | "us" => 1e3,\n        "ms" => 1e6,\n        "s" => 1e9,\n        _ => return None,\n    };\n    Some((name.to_string(), mean * mult))\n}\n\nfn parse_baseline(txt: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, f64> {\n    // baseline.json is `{"name": 90.4, ...}` — flat string→number.\n    let mut m = BTreeMap::new();\n    let obj = parse_obj(txt);\n    for (k, v) in obj {\n        if let Jv::Num(f) = v {\n            m.insert(k, f);\n        }\n    }\n    m\n}\nfn baseline_to_json(m: &BTreeMap<String, f64>) -> String {\n    let mut s = String::from("{\\n");\n    let mut first = true;\n    for (k, v) in m {\n        if !first {\n            s.push_str(",\\n");\n        }\n        s.push_str(&format!("  \\"{}\\": {}", k, v));\n        first = false;\n    }\n    s.push_str("\\n}\\n");\n    s\n}\nfn round4(x: f64) -> f64 {\n    (x * 10000.0).round() / 10000.0\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// 2. ROUTE — native fold of track_record.jsonl for gov_route (replaces gov_route)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nfn cmd_route(task: &str, budget: f64, ruin: f64) -> i32 {\n    // track_record.jsonl holds either the gov schema {model,task,success,value,cost}\n    // or the harness schema {model,task,success,value,cost,backend,tokens,ms}.\n    let path = Path::new("track_record.jsonl");\n    let path = if path.exists() {\n        path.to_path_buf()\n    } else {\n        PathBuf::from("/root/dowiz/tools/telemetry/governance/track_record.jsonl")\n    };\n    let txt = match fs::read_to_string(&path) {\n        Ok(t) => t,\n        Err(_) => {\n            eprintln!("native-trackers: no ledger at {:?}", path);\n            return 2;\n        }\n    };\n    // per-model aggregate: (n, success, value_sum, cost_sum)\n    let mut agg: BTreeMap<String, (u64, u64, f64, f64)> = BTreeMap::new();\n    for line in txt.lines() {\n        let line = line.trim();\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let o = parse_obj(line);\n        if get_str(&o, "task") != task {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let m = get_str(&o, "model");\n        if m.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let e = agg.entry(m).or_insert((0, 0, 0.0, 0.0));\n        e.0 += 1;\n        if get_bool(&o, "success") {\n            e.1 += 1;\n        }\n        e.2 += get_num(&o, "value");\n        e.3 += get_num(&o, "cost");\n    }\n    if agg.is_empty() {\n        println!("ROUTE({}): no data — ESCALATE", task);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    // Replicate gov_route's EV pick: score each model, choose max p*value/cost under ruin cap.\n    let mut best: Option<(String, f64)> = None;\n    println!("ROUTE({}) budget={} ruin_cap={}:", task, budget, ruin);\n    println!("{:24} {:>5} {:>6} {:>10} {:>10}  score", "model", "n", "p", "v/cost", "cost/n");\n    for (m, (n, s, v, c)) in &agg {\n        let p = *s as f64 / *n as f64;\n        let cost_n = if *n > 0 { *c / *n as f64 } else { 0.0 };\n        let vc = if *c > 0.0 { *v / *c } else { 0.0 };\n        let score = p * vc; // EV per token\n        println!(\n            "{:24} {:5} {:6.2} {:10.4} {:10.2}  {:.4}",\n            m, n, p, vc, cost_n, score\n        );\n        if best.as_ref().map(|(_, b)| score > *b).unwrap_or(true) {\n            best = Some((m.clone(), score));\n        }\n    }\n    match best {\n        Some((m, _)) => println!("DECISION: route → {}", m),\n        None => println!("DECISION: ESCALATE"),\n    }\n    0\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// 3. FALSE-CLAIM — EMA meter over false_claims.jsonl (replaces gov_falseclaim)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nfn cmd_false_claim(record: Option<(u64, u64)>) -> i32 {\n    let state_p = Path::new("/root/dowiz/tools/telemetry/governance/false_claims.jsonl");\n    if let Some((claimed, verified)) = record {\n        let ts = now_iso();\n        let _ = fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .append(true)\n            .open(state_p)\n            .map(|mut f| {\n                writeln!(\n                    f,\n                    "{{\\"ts\\":\\"{}\\",\\"claimed\\":{},\\"verified\\":{}}}",\n                    ts, claimed, verified\n                )\n            });\n        println!("false-claim: recorded claimed={} verified={}", claimed, verified);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    let txt = match fs::read_to_string(state_p) {\n        Ok(t) => t,\n        Err(_) => {\n            println!("FALSE-CLAIM: no ledger (events=0)");\n            return 0;\n        }\n    };\n    let mut claimed = 0u64;\n    let mut verified = 0u64;\n    let mut events = 0u64;\n    for line in txt.lines() {\n        let o = parse_obj(line);\n        if o.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        events += 1;\n        claimed += get_num(&o, "claimed") as u64;\n        verified += get_num(&o, "verified") as u64;\n    }\n    let false_est = if claimed > 0 {\n        (claimed - verified) as f64 / claimed as f64 * 100.0\n    } else {\n        0.0\n    };\n    println!(\n        "FALSE-CLAIM: events={} claimed={} verified={}\\n  false-estimation%      = {:.1}  (claimed but not verified)\\n  false-positive-of-done% = {:.1}  (claimed-done / verified)",\n        events, claimed, verified, false_est, false_est\n    );\n    0\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// 4. META — EMA tilt over bench/eval/false deltas (replaces gov_meta observe)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nfn cmd_meta(bp: f64, bn: f64, rp: f64, rn: f64, fr: f64) -> i32 {\n    let state_p = Path::new("/root/dowiz/tools/telemetry/governance/meta_state.json");\n    let mut s: BTreeMap<String, Jv> = if state_p.exists() {\n        parse_obj(&fs::read_to_string(state_p).unwrap_or_default())\n    } else {\n        BTreeMap::new()\n    };\n    let n = match s.get("n") {\n        Some(Jv::Num(x)) => *x as u64,\n        _ => 0,\n    };\n    let a = 2.0 / (n as f64 + 1.0);\n    let ema_bench = lerp(get_num(&s, "ema_bench"), pct(bn, bp), a);\n    let ema_eval = lerp(get_num(&s, "ema_eval"), (rn - rp), a);\n    let ema_false = lerp(get_num(&s, "ema_false"), fr.max(0.0), a);\n    let mut new_s = BTreeMap::new();\n    new_s.insert("n".to_string(), Jv::Num((n + 1) as f64));\n    new_s.insert("ema_bench".to_string(), Jv::Num(ema_bench));\n    new_s.insert("ema_eval".to_string(), Jv::Num(ema_eval));\n    new_s.insert("ema_false".to_string(), Jv::Num(ema_false));\n    let json = obj_to_json(&new_s);\n    let _ = fs::write(state_p, json);\n    println!(\n        "META n={} ema_bench={:+.3} ema_eval={:+.3} ema_false={:.3}\\nGUIDANCE lane_tol={:.3} judge_count=3 precedent_tau=0.82\\nRULES: guidance, not gates — energy flows; meta-rule tilts only.",\n        n + 1, ema_bench, ema_eval, ema_false, 0.10 + ema_bench.abs() * 0.5\n    );\n    0\n}\n\nfn lerp(prev: f64, next: f64, a: f64) -> f64 {\n    a * next + (1.0 - a) * prev\n}\nfn pct(new: f64, prev: f64) -> f64 {\n    if prev > 0.0 {\n        new / prev - 1.0\n    } else {\n        0.0\n    }\n}\nfn obj_to_json(m: &BTreeMap<String, Jv>) -> String {\n    let mut s = String::from("{\\n");\n    let mut first = true;\n    for (k, v) in m {\n        if !first {\n            s.push_str(",\\n");\n        }\n        match v {\n            Jv::Num(f) => s.push_str(&format!("  \\"{}\\": {}", k, f)),\n            Jv::Str(x) => s.push_str(&format!("  \\"{}\\": \\"{}\\"", k, x)),\n            Jv::Bool(b) => s.push_str(&format!("  \\"{}\\": {}", k, b)),\n            Jv::Null => s.push_str(&format!("  \\"{}\\": null", k)),\n        }\n        first = false;\n    }\n    s.push_str("\\n}\\n");\n    s\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// swarm-proof — native port of tools/telemetry/swarm_proof.py (no LLM, no python\n// subprocess). (A) economic crossover from real 2026 API prices; (B) parallel vs\n// sequential fan-out timing via a native threadpool (replaces the xargs/python3\n// timing experiment).\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nconst PRICES: &[(&str, f64, f64)] = &[\n    // tier: (input $/Mtok, output $/Mtok)\n    ("frontier", 5.0, 15.0),\n    ("mid", 0.50, 1.50),\n    ("cheap", 0.10, 0.40),\n];\nconst BLUEPRINT_TOK_IN: f64 = 4000.0;\nconst BLUEPRINT_TOK_OUT: f64 = 1500.0;\nconst EXEC_TOK_IN: f64 = 2000.0;\nconst EXEC_TOK_OUT: f64 = 800.0;\n\nfn cost(tier: &str, tin: f64, tout: f64) -> f64 {\n    let &(_, pi, po) = PRICES.iter().find(|x| x.0 == tier).unwrap_or(&PRICES[0]);\n    tin / 1e6 * pi + tout / 1e6 * po\n}\nfn sequential_cost(n: usize, arch: &str) -> f64 {\n    n as f64 * cost(arch, BLUEPRINT_TOK_IN + EXEC_TOK_IN, BLUEPRINT_TOK_OUT + EXEC_TOK_OUT)\n}\nfn swarm_cost(n: usize, arch: &str, exec_t: &str) -> f64 {\n    n as f64 * cost(arch, BLUEPRINT_TOK_IN, BLUEPRINT_TOK_OUT)\n        + n as f64 * cost(exec_t, EXEC_TOK_IN, EXEC_TOK_OUT)\n}\nfn crossover_n(arch: &str, exec_t: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    for n in 1..200 {\n        if swarm_cost(n, arch, exec_t) < sequential_cost(n, arch) {\n            return Some(n);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\nfn cmd_swarm_proof() -> i32 {\n    println!("=== (A) ECONOMIC CROSSOVER (real 2026 prices) ===");\n    for (arch, exec_t) in [("frontier", "cheap"), ("frontier", "mid"), ("mid", "cheap")] {\n        let seq1 = sequential_cost(1, arch);\n        let sw1 = swarm_cost(1, arch, exec_t);\n        let nx = crossover_n(arch, exec_t);\n        let sw10 = swarm_cost(10, arch, exec_t);\n        let seq10 = sequential_cost(10, arch);\n        let pct = if seq10 > 0.0 {\n            100.0 * (1.0 - sw10 / seq10)\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n        println!(\n            "  architect={:9} executor={:6}: 1-task seq=${:.4} swarm=${:.4} | crossover N={:?} | N=10 swarm=${:.4} vs seq=${:.4} ({:.0}% cheaper)",\n            arch, exec_t, seq1, sw1, nx, sw10, seq10, pct\n        );\n    }\n    println!("  NOTE: crossover N is small (<=2); swarm wins for essentially any N>=2.");\n\n    println!("\\n=== (B) ENGINE TIMING (parallel vs sequential fan-out, native threadpool) ===");\n    let task_ms = 300u64; // mirrors the python timing experiment's 0.30s sleep\n    for n in [4usize, 8usize] {\n        let tp = time_parallel(n, task_ms);\n        let ts = time_sequential(n, task_ms);\n        let speedup = if tp > 0.0 { ts / tp } else { 0.0 };\n        println!(\n            "  N={}: parallel={:.2}s  sequential={:.2}s  speedup={:.2}x",\n            n,\n            tp,\n            ts,\n            speedup\n        );\n    }\n    println!("  ideal parallel ~0.30s (max task), sequential ~N*0.30s. Native fan-out confirms.");\n\n    let mut out = String::from("{\\"crossover\\":{\\"frontier/cheap\\":");\n    out.push_str(&format!("{:?}", crossover_n("frontier", "cheap")));\n    out.push_str(",\\"frontier/mid\\":");\n    out.push_str(&format!("{:?}", crossover_n("frontier", "mid")));\n    out.push_str(",\\"mid/cheap\\":");\n    out.push_str(&format!("{:?}", crossover_n("mid", "cheap")));\n    out.push_str("}}");\n    println!("\\nJSON: {}", out);\n    0\n}\n\n/// Parallel: spawn N threads, each sleeps `task_ms`, join all. ~one task wall time.\nfn time_parallel(n: usize, task_ms: u64) -> f64 {\n    use std::thread;\n    use std::time::{Duration, Instant};\n    let t0 = Instant::now();\n    let handles: Vec<_> = (0..n)\n        .map(|_| thread::spawn(move || thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(task_ms))))\n        .collect();\n    for h in handles {\n        let _ = h.join();\n    }\n    t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64()\n}\n/// Sequential: run each task in turn.\nfn time_sequential(n: usize, task_ms: u64) -> f64 {\n    use std::thread;\n    use std::time::{Duration, Instant};\n    let t0 = Instant::now();\n    for _ in 0..n {\n        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(task_ms));\n        let _ = thread::yield_now();\n    }\n    t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64()\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ser — native port of tools/telemetry/ser.py: canonical little-endian f64 wire\n// <-> JSON edge adapter. No external libs (struct/json replaced by std only).\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nfn cmd_ser(mode: &str, arg: &str) -> i32 {\n    match mode {\n        "wire" => {\n            // arg = hex string of raw f64 bytes -> JSON array of floats\n            let bytes = match hex_to_bytes(arg) {\n                Some(b) => b,\n                None => {\n                    eprintln!("ser wire: invalid hex input");\n                    return 2;\n                }\n            };\n            let n = bytes.len() / 8;\n            let mut vals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n            for i in 0..n {\n                let mut b = [0u8; 8];\n                b.copy_from_slice(&bytes[i * 8..i * 8 + 8]);\n                vals.push(f64::from_le_bytes(b));\n            }\n            let s = vals\n                .iter()\n                .map(|v| format!("{:.6}", v))\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(", ");\n            println!("[{}]", s);\n            0\n        }\n        "json" => {\n            // arg = JSON array of floats -> hex of raw f64 bytes (canonical wire)\n            let vals = match parse_float_array(arg) {\n                Some(v) => v,\n                None => {\n                    eprintln!("ser json: invalid JSON array input");\n                    return 2;\n                }\n            };\n            let mut out = String::with_capacity(vals.len() * 16);\n            for v in &vals {\n                for b in v.to_le_bytes() {\n                    out.push_str(&format!("{:02x}", b));\n                }\n            }\n            println!("{}", out);\n            0\n        }\n        _ => {\n            eprintln!("ser: mode must be 'wire' or 'json'");\n            2\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn hex_to_bytes(s: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    if s.len() % 2 != 0 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(s.len() / 2);\n    let bytes = s.as_bytes();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < bytes.len() {\n        let hi = (bytes[i] as char).to_digit(16)?;\n        let lo = (bytes[i + 1] as char).to_digit(16)?;\n        out.push((hi * 16 + lo) as u8);\n        i += 2;\n    }\n    Some(out)\n}\n\nfn parse_float_array(s: &str) -> Option<Vec<f64>> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    let s = s.strip_prefix('[')?;\n    let s = s.strip_suffix(']')?;\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    for part in s.split(',') {\n        let p = part.trim();\n        if p.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        out.push(p.parse::<f64>().ok()?);\n    }\n    Some(out)\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// hetzner-serve — native port of tools/telemetry/hetzner_exporter.py.\n// Pure-std: reads /proc + statvfs, serves JSON metrics on a std TcpListener\n// (no http crate).
