The returned `π` is normalized to\n    /// sum to 1 (guards sub-ULP drift; the iteration itself preserves the sum).\n    ///\n    /// DETERMINISM: fixed step count `iters`, fixed `spmv` summation order ⇒\n    /// identical bytes for identical inputs on a given build (no `-ffast-math`).\n    pub fn personalized_pagerank(&self, seed: &[f64], alpha: f64, iters: usize) -> Vec<f64> {\n        let n = self.nrows();\n        // Normalize the fixed restart distribution e.\n        let ssum: f64 = seed.iter().sum();\n        let mut e = vec![0.0; n];\n        if ssum != 0.0 {\n            for i in 0..n {\n                e[i] = seed[i] / ssum;\n            }\n        } else {\n            let u = 1.0 / n as f64;\n            for v in e.iter_mut() {\n                *v = u;\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut pi = e.clone();\n        let mut next = vec![0.0; n];\n        // Jacobi: the WHOLE vector is updated from the previous iterate (no\n        // in-place Gauss-Seidel mixing), so every step is a clean matrix apply.\n        for _ in 0..iters {\n            self.spmv(&pi, &mut next);\n            for i in 0..n {\n                next[i] = alpha * e[i] + (1.0 - alpha) * next[i];\n            }\n            core::mem::swap(&mut pi, &mut next);\n        }\n\n        // Final normalize (deterministic; guards tiny f64 drift).\n        let t: f64 = pi.iter().sum();\n        if t != 0.0 {\n            for v in pi.iter_mut() {\n                *v /= t;\n            }\n        }\n        pi\n    }\n\n    /// Arena-aware `from_edges` (W5). Same operation order ⇒ byte-identical.\n            scratch[start..end].sort_by_key(|&(c, _)| c);\n            // In-place duplicate-column merge by SUMMING weights (deterministic).\n            // the arena serves the bucket scratch from ONE region, so the ONLY\n            // heap Vecs on the arena path are the three owned outputs. Degrades\n            // to the heap `from_edges` on exhaustion (byte-identical).\n            let mut w = start;\n            for r in start..end {\n                let (c, v) = scratch[r];\n                if w > start && scratch[w - 1].0 == c {\n                    scratch[w - 1].1 += v; // sum duplicate column weights\n                } else {\n                    if w != r {\n                        scratch[w] = (c, v);\n                    }\n                    w += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            for s in start..w {\n                col_idx.push(scratch[s].0);\n                val.push(scratch[s].1);\n            }\n            row_ptr.push(col_idx.len());\n        }\n        Self {\n            row_ptr,\n            col_idx,\n            val,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Arena-aware `personalized_pagerank` (W5). Serves the `e` / `pi` / `next`\n    /// vectors from `arena`; degrades to the heap\n    /// [`personalized_pagerank`](Csr::personalized_pagerank) on exhaustion.\n    /// Byte-identical output guaranteed (same Jacobi iteration order, same\n    /// restart normalization).\n    pub fn personalized_pagerank_in(\n        &self,\n        seed: &[f64],\n        alpha: f64,\n        iters: usize,\n        arena: &crate::arena::BumpArena,\n    ) -> Option<Vec<f64>> {\n        let n = self.nrows();\n        let e: &mut [f64] = arena.alloc_slice(n)?;\n        let pi: &mut [f64] = arena.alloc_slice(n)?;\n        let next: &mut [f64] = arena.alloc_slice(n)?;\n        // Normalize the fixed restart distribution e.\n        let ssum: f64 = seed.iter().sum();\n        if ssum != 0.0 {\n            for i in 0..n {\n                e[i] = seed[i] / ssum;\n            }\n        } else {\n            let u = 1.0 / n as f64;\n            for v in e.iter_mut() {\n                *v = u;\n            }\n        }\n        pi.copy_from_slice(e);\n        // Jacobi: the WHOLE vector updates from the previous iterate.\n        for _ in 0..iters {\n            self.spmv(pi, next);\n            for i in 0..n {\n                next[i] = alpha * e[i] + (1.0 - alpha) * next[i];\n            }\n            // `spmv` already zeroed+filled `next`; copy back into `pi`.\n            pi.copy_from_slice(next);\n        }\n        // Final normalize (deterministic; guards tiny f64 drift).\n        let t: f64 = pi.iter().sum();\n        let mut out = vec![0.0; n]; // owned — must outlive arena loan\n        if t != 0.0 {\n            for i in 0..n {\n                out[i] = pi[i] / t;\n            }\n        }\n        Some(out)\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Spectral core: Laplacian SpMV (W2-2) ─────────────────────────────────\n// Unifies the FEM M∇²U diffusion field with the graph-energy approach: the\n// per-frame physics field is `y = L·x`. The orientation matches `spmv`'s\n// LEFT product; because every Laplacian variant here is built from the\n// symmetric adjacency A, and for a *symmetric* matrix A[i][j] = A[j][i], the\n// LEFT product `out_j = Σ_i x_i·A[i][j]` equals `(A x)_j`. We implement\n// `laplacian_spmv` directly (no intermediate CSR materialization) so the\n// per-edge hot loop is allocation-free; only a single O(n) degree scratch is\n// allocated per call (outside the edge loop).\n\n/// Which Laplacian to apply in [`Csr::laplacian_spmv`].\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum LaplacianKind {\n    /// Standard graph Laplacian `L = D − A`. Rows sum to 0 ⇒ `L·1 = 0`\n    /// (mass/momentum conserved for ANY graph).\n    Unnormalized,\n    /// Symmetric normalized Laplacian `L = I − D^{−1/2} A D^{−1/2}`. PSD &\n    /// symmetric; null space contains `D^{1/2}·1`. Conserves mass on\n    /// *regular* graphs (where it reduces to `I − (1/d)·A`).\n    Normalized,\n    /// Random-walk normalized Laplacian `L = I − D^{−1} A`. Every row sums\n    /// to 0 ⇒ `L·1 = 0` ⇒ mass/momentum conserved for ANY graph (the\n    /// divergence-free diffusion operator).\n    RandomWalk,\n}\n\nimpl Csr {\n    /// Laplacian matrix-vector product `y = L·x` via CSR SpMV.\n    ///\n    /// The Laplacian is built from the row out-weight `d_i = Σ_j A_ij`\n    /// (degree). For an undirected graph pass BOTH `(s,d,w)` and `(d,s,w)`\n    /// so `d_i` equals the true degree.\n    ///\n    /// * `Unnormalized`: `y_i = d_i·x_i − Σ_j A_ij·x_j`\n    /// * `Normalized`:   `y_i = x_i − Σ_j A_ij / √(d_i·d_j) · x_j`\n    /// * `RandomWalk`:   `y_i = x_i − Σ_j (A_ij / d_i)·x_j`\n    ///\n    /// `x` and `out` must have length `n`. `out` is overwritten. No heap is\n    /// touched in the per-edge accumulation loop (only an O(n) degree scratch\n    /// is allocated once, before the loop).\n    pub fn laplacian_spmv(&self, x: &[f64], out: &mut [f64], kind: LaplacianKind) {\n        let n = self.nrows();\n        debug_assert_eq!(x.len(), n, "csr::laplacian_spmv: x length must be n");\n        debug_assert_eq!(out.len(), n, "csr::laplacian_spmv: out length must be n");\n        // Degree (row out-weight) — O(n) scratch, computed BEFORE the hot loop.\n        let deg: Vec<f64> = (0..n)\n            .map(|i| self.val[self.row_ptr[i]..self.row_ptr[i + 1]].iter().sum())\n            .collect();\n        match kind {\n            LaplacianKind::Unnormalized => {\n                for i in 0..n {\n                    let mut acc = deg[i] * x[i];\n                    let (s, e) = (self.row_ptr[i], self.row_ptr[i + 1]);\n                    for k in s..e {\n                        acc -= self.val[k] * x[self.col_idx[k]];\n                    }\n                    out[i] = acc;\n                }\n            }\n            LaplacianKind::Normalized => {\n                for i in 0..n {\n                    let inv_i = if deg[i] > 0.0 {\n                        crate::math::sqrt(deg[i]).recip()\n                    } else {\n                        0.0\n                    };\n                    let mut acc = x[i];\n                    let (s, e) = (self.row_ptr[i], self.row_ptr[i + 1]);\n                    for k in s..e {\n                        let j = self.col_idx[k];\n                        let w = if deg[j] > 0.0 {\n                            self.val[k] * inv_i * crate::math::sqrt(deg[j]).recip()\n                        } else {\n                            0.0\n                        };\n                        acc -= w * x[j];\n                    }\n                    out[i] = acc;\n                }\n            }\n            LaplacianKind::RandomWalk => {\n                for i in 0..n {\n                    let inv_i = if deg[i] > 0.0 { deg[i].recip() } else { 0.0 };\n                    let mut acc = x[i];\n                    let (s, e) = (self.row_ptr[i], self.row_ptr[i + 1]);\n                    for k in s..e {\n                        acc -= self.val[k] * inv_i * x[self.col_idx[k]];\n                    }\n                    out[i] = acc;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Recall / precision scorers (HippoRAG-style groundedness) ───────────────\n//\n// E0 fix (VERIFIABLE-COGNITION §2 bug #3): there was NO in-kernel `recall@k`\n// scorer — scoring was delegated to the JS bridge. `personalized_pagerank` is\n// the diffusion; these pure functions score its ranking against a relevance\n// set, deterministically, with a stable tie-break. No BTreeMap (iteration-order\n// hazard); ranking is a sorted Vec with ascending-index tie-break.\n\n/// Rank `scores` descending with a *stable* tie-break by ascending node index\n/// (canonical, deterministic). Returns node indices in rank order.\nfn rank_desc(scores: &[f64]) -> Vec<usize> {\n    let mut idx: Vec<usize> = (0..scores.len()).collect();\n    idx.sort_by(|&a, &b| {\n        scores[b]\n            .partial_cmp(&scores[a])\n            .unwrap_or(core::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n            .then(a.cmp(&b))\n    });\n    idx\n}\n\n/// `recall@k` over a ranked score vector: the fraction of `relevant` nodes that\n/// appear among the top-`k` by score. This is the groundedness scorer the PPR\n/// diffusion feeds. Deterministic; tie-break is ascending node index. Returns\n/// `0.0` if there are no scores or no relevant nodes.\npub fn recall_at_k(scores: &[f64], relevant: &[usize], k: usize) -> f64 {\n    if scores.is_empty() || relevant.is_empty() {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    let kr = k.min(scores.len());\n    let ranked = rank_desc(scores);\n    let mut relevant_sorted = relevant.to_vec();\n    relevant_sorted.sort_unstable();\n    let mut hits = 0u32;\n    for &node in &relevant_sorted {\n        // `ranked[..kr]` is a descending ranking (not ascending-sorted), so use\n        // `contains` — `binary_search` would be wrong on an unsorted slice.\n        if ranked[..kr].contains(&node) {\n            hits += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    hits as f64 / relevant.len() as f64\n}\n\n/// `precision@k` over a ranked score vector: the fraction of the top-`k` nodes\n/// that are in `relevant`. Complements [`recall_at_k`]. Returns `0.0` for an\n/// empty score vector or `k == 0`.\npub fn precision_at_k(scores: &[f64], relevant: &[usize], k: usize) -> f64 {\n    if scores.is_empty() {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    let kr = k.min(scores.len());\n    if kr == 0 {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    let ranked = rank_desc(scores);\n    let mut relevant_sorted = relevant.to_vec();\n    relevant_sorted.sort_unstable();\n    let mut hits = 0u32;\n    for &node in &ranked[..kr] {\n        if relevant_sorted.binary_search(&node).is_ok() {\n            hits += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    hits as f64 / kr as f64\n}\n\n// ── P-B (BLUEPRINT-P-B §3.2): canonical-tile type-system invariant ─────────\n//\n// The bug class "hashed a tile that was not canonicalized" becomes a COMPILE\n// ERROR through three structural facts:\n//   (i)   `NormalizedTile` has a private field and its only constructors run\n//         `row_normalize` — a NormalizedTile that skipped canonicalization is\n//         UNREPRESENTABLE;\n//   (ii)  `TileAddress` has no public constructor; its only producer is\n//         `NormalizedTile::content_address`;\n//   (iii) the raw-matrix hash `matrix_content_address` is demoted to private in\n//         `spectral_cache.rs`.\n// There is no runtime check to forget and no reviewer vigilance to depend on.\n\n/// FNV-1a-64 single authority (consolidates the two inline literal sites in\n/// `spectral_cache.rs` + `memory_store`).\npub const FNV_OFFSET_64: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;\npub const FNV_PRIME_64: u64 = 0x0000_0100_0000_01b3;\n\n/// A tile in CANONICAL form (N1+N2+N3, §3.1 of the blueprint).\n///\n/// INVARIANT (type-encoded, not runtime-checked): the field is private and the\n/// only constructors run `row_normalize` (N1: row-stochastic; N2: via\n/// `from_dense` / a sort-dedup pass on the CSR path; N3: by construction —\n/// rational/fixed-order ops only). A `NormalizedTile` that skipped\n/// canonicalization is UNREPRESENTABLE. No `&mut` accessor exists.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct NormalizedTile {\n    csr: Csr, // private\n}\n\nimpl NormalizedTile {\n    /// The only ways in. Both canonicalize:\n    /// * `canonicalize` runs `row_normalize` on a raw [`Csr`];\n    /// * `from_dense` builds a CSR (dropping explicit zeros, ascending-column\n    ///   rows per N2) and row-normalizes it.\n    /// `a` is already row-stochastic (e.g. a markov transition matrix) ⇒ the\n    /// normalize pass is value-idempotent up to ulp — re-dividing perturbs\n    /// entries ≤ a few ulp.\n    pub fn canonicalize(raw: &Csr) -> NormalizedTile {\n        NormalizedTile {\n            csr: raw.row_normalize(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Build a canonical tile from a dense matrix (see [`Csr::from_dense`]).\n    pub fn from_dense(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> NormalizedTile {\n        let csr = Csr::from_dense(a);\n        NormalizedTile {\n            csr: csr.row_normalize(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// THE ONLY PRODUCER of a [`TileAddress`] in the crate.\n    ///\n    /// FNV-1a-64 over the canonical CSR bytes, length-framed, fixed order:\n    /// `nrows`, then per row: `frame(i)`, then `(col_idx[k] as u64, val[k].to_bits())`\n    /// ascending `k`. O(nnz), not O(n²). `-0.0` is folded to `+0.0` bits so a\n    /// value-identical tile with a sign-distinct zero shares an address.\n    pub fn content_address(&self) -> TileAddress {\n        let csr = &self.csr;\n        let n = csr.nrows();\n        let mut h = FNV_OFFSET_64;\n        // frame nrows\n        h ^= n as u64;\n        h = h.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME_64);\n        for i in 0..n {\n            // frame the row index so a value bleeding across rows can't collide\n            h ^= (i as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);\n            h = h.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME_64);\n            let lo = csr.row_ptr[i];\n            let hi = csr.row_ptr[i + 1];\n            for k in lo..hi {\n                let col = csr.col_idx[k] as u64;\n                let v = csr.val[k];\n                // fold -0.0 → +0.0 bits (value-identical tiles share an address)\n                let bits = if v == 0.0 {\n                    0.0f64.to_bits()\n                } else {\n                    v.to_bits()\n                };\n                h ^= col;\n                h = h.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME_64);\n                h ^= bits;\n                h = h.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME_64);\n            }\n        }\n        TileAddress(h)\n    }\n\n    /// Read-only view of the canonical CSR (eigensolve input; snapshot\n    /// retention). No mutation path.\n    pub fn as_csr(&self) -> &Csr {\n        &self.csr\n    }\n\n    /// Dense round-trip of the canonical tile.\n    pub fn to_dense(&self) -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n        self.csr.to_dense()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Opaque content-address of a CANONICAL tile. No public constructor — possession\n/// of a `TileAddress` is proof normalization ran (Curry-Howard cheap).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]\npub struct TileAddress(u64);\n\nimpl TileAddress {\n    /// Hex form for `DecompCache`'s `&str` key path (reuse, not a second\n    /// authority).\n    pub fn as_hex(&self) -> String {\n        format!("{:016x}", self.0)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Approximate float equality for hand-derived oracles (no stats crate).\n    fn close(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {\n        (a - b).abs() <= tol\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 1. CSR round-trips a known directed 3-node graph.\n    //    edges: 0→1, 0→2, 1→2, 2→0  (unique, weights 1.0)\n    //    row_ptr = [0,2,3,4], col_idx = [1,2, 2, 0], val = [1,1,1,1]\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn csr_roundtrip_known_graph() {\n        let edges = [(0usize, 1, 1.0), (0, 2, 1.0), (1, 2, 1.0), (2, 0, 1.0)];\n        let csr = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges);\n        assert_eq!(csr.row_ptr, vec![0, 2, 3, 4]);\n        assert_eq!(csr.col_idx, vec![1, 2, 2, 0]);\n        assert_eq!(csr.val, vec![1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]);\n        assert_eq!(csr.nrows(), 3);\n        assert_eq!(csr.nnz(), 4);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 2. row_normalize: every non-dangling row sums to 1.0 (±1e-12).\n    //    row0 has out-weights 2.0, 1.0 ⇒ normalized 2/3, 1/3 (sum 1).\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn row_normalize_sums_to_one() {\n        let edges = [(0usize, 1, 2.0), (0, 2, 1.0), (1, 0, 1.0), (2, 0, 1.0)];\n        let csr = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges);\n        let a = csr.row_normalize();\n        for i in 0..a.nrows() {\n            let s: f64 = a.val[a.row_ptr[i]..a.row_ptr[i + 1]].iter().sum();\n            assert!(close(s, 1.0, 1e-12), "row {i} sums to {s}");\n        }\n        // Hand-check row 0: cols [1,2], normalized weights [2/3, 1/3].\n        assert_eq!(a.col_idx[a.row_ptr[0]..a.row_ptr[1]], [1, 2]);\n        assert!(close(a.val[a.row_ptr[0]], 2.0 / 3.0, 1e-12));\n        assert!(close(a.val[a.row_ptr[0] + 1], 1.0 / 3.0, 1e-12));\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 3. spmv matches a hand-computed y = xᵀÂ for a directed 3-cycle.\n    //    Â = [[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[1,0,0]] (each row single entry ⇒ unchanged).\n    //    x = [0.2, 0.3, 0.5]  ⇒  y = [0.5, 0.2, 0.3]\n    //      y_0 = x_2·A[2][0] = 0.5;  y_1 = x_0·A[0][1] = 0.2;  y_2 = x_1·A[1][2] = 0.3\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn spmv_matches_hand_computed() {\n        let edges = [(0usize, 1, 1.0), (1, 2, 1.0), (2, 0, 1.0)];\n        let a = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges).row_normalize();\n        let x = [0.2, 0.3, 0.5];\n        let mut y = [0.0; 3];\n        a.spmv(&x, &mut y);\n        assert!(close(y[0], 0.5, 1e-12));\n        assert!(close(y[1], 0.2, 1e-12));\n        assert!(close(y[2], 0.3, 1e-12));\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 4. PPR determinism: two IDENTICAL calls ⇒ byte-identical Vec (assert_eq).\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn ppr_byte_identical() {\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 0, 1.0),\n            (0, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n        ];\n        let a = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges).row_normalize();\n        let seed = [0.2, 0.5, 0.3];\n        let p1 = a.personalized_pagerank(&seed, 0.15, 60);\n        let p2 = a.personalized_pagerank(&seed, 0.15, 60);\n        assert_eq!(p1, p2, "PPR must be bit-reproducible for identical inputs");\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 4b. Hermetic-audit Cause-and-Effect Finding B (quick-win #19): the above only\n    //     compares two live values in one call stack — never crosses an actual\n    //     serialization boundary. Disk round-trip + independently fresh recompute.\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn csr_ppr_survives_serialize_reread_boundary() {\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 0, 1.0),\n            (0, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n        ];\n        let a = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges).row_normalize();\n        let seed = [0.2, 0.5, 0.3];\n        let computed = a.personalized_pagerank(&seed, 0.15, 60);\n        let serialized: String = computed\n            .iter()\n            .map(|x| format!("{:.17e}", x))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(",");\n\n        let path =\n            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("csr_ppr_reread_test_{}.txt", std::process::id()));\n        std::fs::write(&path, &serialized).expect("write serialized csr ppr scores");\n        let reread = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).expect("re-read serialized csr ppr scores");\n        std::fs::remove_file(&path).ok();\n\n        assert_eq!(\n            reread, serialized,\n            "byte content did not survive a disk round-trip"\n        );\n\n        let reparsed: Vec<f64> = reread\n            .split(',')\n            .map(|s| s.parse::<f64>().expect("reparse f64"))\n            .collect();\n        let fresh = a.personalized_pagerank(&seed, 0.15, 60); // independently recomputed\n        assert_eq!(\n            reparsed, fresh,\n            "value re-read from disk does not match an independently fresh computation"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 5. PPR stationary (SYMMETRIC undirected, uniform seed, converged).\n    //    Undirected triangle: each node degree 2 ⇒ regular graph.\n    //    For a uniform seed e, the fixed point of  π = α e + (1−α) π·Â  is the\n    //    uniform vector: if π is uniform then π·Â is uniform (Â row-stochastic,\n    //    columns also sum to 1 by symmetry) ⇒ π = α·uniform + (1−α)·uniform =\n    //    uniform. Contraction (spectral radius 1−α < 1) ⇒ converges to [1/3,1/3,1/3],\n    //    which IS the degree-proportional stationary (deg/2|E| = 2/6 = 1/3).\n    //    Triangle is connected + non-bipartite (odd cycle) as required.\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn ppr_stationary_uniform_triangle() {\n        // Undirected triangle: both directions for each edge.\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 0, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n            (2, 0, 1.0),\n            (0, 2, 1.0),\n        ];\n        let a = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges).row_normalize();\n        let seed = [1.0 / 3.0, 1.0 / 3.0, 1.0 / 3.0];\n        let pi = a.personalized_pagerank(&seed, 0.15, 200);\n        for i in 0..3 {\n            assert!(\n                close(pi[i], 1.0 / 3.0, 1e-6),\n                "node {i} stationary = {} (want 1/3)",\n                pi[i]\n            );\n        }\n        // Fixed-point invariant: one more iteration barely moves π (< 1e-9).\n        let mut extra = vec![0.0; 3];\n        a.spmv(&pi, &mut extra);\n        for i in 0..3 {\n            let pi_next = 0.15 * seed[i] + (1.0 - 0.15) * extra[i];\n            assert!(close(pi_next, pi[i], 1e-9), "node {i} not a fixed point");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // 6. PPR seed-locality: one-hot seed on a path node ⇒ mass stays local.\n    //    Path 0—1—2—3 (undirected). Seed one-hot on node 1, α=0.15, 2 iters.\n    //    Hand trace (Â row-stochastic, degrees 1,2,2,1):\n    //      π0 = [0,1,0,0]\n    //      π0·Â = row1 = [0.5,0,0.5,0]\n    //      π1 = .15·e + .85·[.5,0,.5,0] = [.425,.15,.425,0]\n    //      π1·Â = [.075,.6375,.075,.2125]\n    //      π2 = .15·e + .85·[.075,.6375,.075,.2125]\n    //         = [.06375, .691875, .06375, .180625]\n    //    ⇒ π[1] is the maximum (seed-locality holds).\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn ppr_seed_locality_path() {\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 0, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n            (2, 3, 1.0),\n            (3, 2, 1.0),\n        ];\n        let a = Csr::from_edges(4, &edges).row_normalize();\n        let seed = [0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0]; // one-hot on node 1\n        let pi = a.personalized_pagerank(&seed, 0.15, 2);\n        // Seed node must carry the largest mass (locality).\n        assert!(pi[1] > pi[0] + 1e-9, "π[1]={} not > π[0]={}", pi[1], pi[0]);\n        assert!(pi[1] > pi[2] + 1e-9, "π[1]={} not > π[2]={}", pi[1], pi[2]);\n        assert!(pi[1] > pi[3] + 1e-9, "π[1]={} not > π[3]={}", pi[1], pi[3]);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // E0 fix (VERIFIABLE-COGNITION §2 bug #3): in-kernel recall@k / precision@k\n    // scorers over a PPR ranking, deterministic with stable tie-break.\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn recall_at_k_hand_oracle() {\n        // scores: node 2 highest, tie between 0 and 1, 3 lowest.\n        let scores = [0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 0.1];\n        // relevant = {0, 2}.\n        // k=1 → only node 2 in top-1 ⇒ recall 1/2 = 0.5.\n        assert!(close(recall_at_k(&scores, &[0, 2], 1), 0.5, 1e-12));\n        // k=2 → top-2 are {2, 0} (tie 0/1 broken by ascending index ⇒ 0 before 1)\n        //       ⇒ both relevant present ⇒ recall 1.0.\n        assert!(close(recall_at_k(&scores, &[0, 2], 2), 1.0, 1e-12));\n        // k=2 with relevant = {0,1,3}: top-2 {2,0} ⇒ only node 0 ⇒ 1/3.\n        assert!(close(recall_at_k(&scores, &[0, 1, 3], 2), 1.0 / 3.0, 1e-12));\n        // empty inputs guard.\n        assert_eq!(recall_at_k(&[], &[0], 2), 0.0);\n        assert_eq!(recall_at_k(&scores, &[], 2), 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn precision_at_k_hand_oracle() {\n        let scores = [0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 0.1];\n        // relevant = {0, 2}. k=1 → top {2} relevant ⇒ precision 1.0.\n        assert!(close(precision_at_k(&scores, &[0, 2], 1), 1.0, 1e-12));\n        // k=2 → top {2,0} both relevant ⇒ precision 1.0.\n        assert!(close(precision_at_k(&scores, &[0, 2], 2), 1.0, 1e-12));\n        // k=3 → top {2,0,1}: only 2 and 0 relevant ⇒ 2/3.\n        assert!(close(precision_at_k(&scores, &[0, 2], 3), 2.0 / 3.0, 1e-12));\n        // k=0 and empty guard.\n        assert_eq!(precision_at_k(&scores, &[0], 0), 0.0);\n        assert_eq!(precision_at_k(&[], &[0], 2), 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn recall_scores_real_ppr_ranking() {\n        // Build a graph where node 0 is the seed; the grounded sources for a\n        // claim about node 0 are the seed itself + its neighbours {1, 2}.\n        // The distant node 3 (two hops away) must NOT outrank them.\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 0, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n            (2, 3, 1.0),\n            (3, 2, 1.0),\n            (0, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 0, 1.0),\n        ];\n        let a = Csr::from_edges(4, &edges).row_normalize();\n        let seed = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0];\n        let pi = a.personalized_pagerank(&seed, 0.15, 80);\n        // Seed + immediate neighbours must fully recall at k=3.\n        let r = recall_at_k(&pi, &[0, 1, 2], 3);\n        assert!(\n            close(r, 1.0, 1e-6),\n            "PPR from node 0 must recall seed+neighbours at k=3 (got {r})"\n        );\n        // The distant node 3 must NOT be in the top-3 ranking.\n        let mut idx: Vec<usize> = (0..pi.len()).collect();\n        idx.sort_by(|&a, &b| pi[b].total_cmp(&pi[a]).then(a.cmp(&b)));\n        assert!(\n            !idx[..3].contains(&3),\n            "distant node 3 must not outrank seed+neighbours in top-3"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── W2-2 RED→GREEN: laplacian_spmv on a tiny triangle graph matches a\n    //    hand-computed reference AND conserves mass (Σ y == 0) on constant x\n    //    for the random-walk / unnormalized Laplacians.\n    //\n    //    Triangle K₃, undirected (both directions), unit weights:\n    //      adj A = [[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,0]], degree d = [2,2,2].\n    //    For x = [0.1, 0.4, 0.9]:\n    //      Unnormalized L·x:\n    //        y0 = 2*0.1 - (0.4+0.9)        = 0.2 - 1.3 = -1.1\n    //        y1 = 2*0.4 - (0.1+0.9)        = 0.8 - 1.0 = -0.2\n    //        y2 = 2*0.9 - (0.1+0.4)        = 1.8 - 0.5 =  1.3\n    //        Σ y = -1.1 - 0.2 + 1.3 = 0  ✓ (mass conserved, rows sum to 0)\n    //      RandomWalk (I − D⁻¹A)·x  = x − Σ_j A_ij/d_i · x_j\n    //        y0 = 0.1 - (0.4/2 + 0.9/2)   = 0.1 - 0.65 = -0.55\n    //        y1 = 0.4 - (0.1/2 + 0.9/2)   = 0.4 - 0.5  = -0.1\n    //        y2 = 0.9 - (0.1/2 + 0.4/2)   = 0.9 - 0.25 =  0.65\n    //        Σ y = -0.55 - 0.1 + 0.65 = 0  ✓\n    //      Normalized (symmetric, regular graph d=2 ⇒ reduces to I − (1/2)A):\n    //        y0 = 0.1 - (0.4+0.9)/2       = 0.1 - 0.65 = -0.55\n    //        (identical to RandomWalk here because the triangle is regular)\n    // ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    #[test]\n    fn laplacian_spmv_triangle_matches_hand_and_conserves() {\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 0, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n            (0, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 0, 1.0),\n        ];\n        let g = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges);\n        let x = [0.1, 0.4, 0.9];\n\n        // ── Unnormalized L = D − A ──\n        let mut y_un = [0.0; 3];\n        g.laplacian_spmv(&x, &mut y_un, LaplacianKind::Unnormalized);\n        assert!(close(y_un[0], -1.1, 1e-12), "unnormalized y0 = {}", y_un[0]);\n        assert!(close(y_un[1], -0.2, 1e-12), "unnormalized y1 = {}", y_un[1]);\n        assert!(close(y_un[2], 1.3, 1e-12), "unnormalized y2 = {}", y_un[2]);\n        // Mass/momentum conservation: Σ y == 0 (rows of L sum to 0).\n        let sum_un: f64 = y_un.iter().sum();\n        assert!(\n            close(sum_un, 0.0, 1e-12),\n            "unnormalized Σy = {sum_un} (must be 0)"\n        );\n\n        // ── Random-walk normalized L = I − D⁻¹A ──\n        let mut y_rw = [0.0; 3];\n        g.laplacian_spmv(&x, &mut y_rw, LaplacianKind::RandomWalk);\n        assert!(close(y_rw[0], -0.55, 1e-12), "randomwalk y0 = {}", y_rw[0]);\n        assert!(close(y_rw[1], -0.1, 1e-12), "randomwalk y1 = {}", y_rw[1]);\n        assert!(close(y_rw[2], 0.65, 1e-12), "randomwalk y2 = {}", y_rw[2]);\n        let sum_rw: f64 = y_rw.iter().sum();\n        assert!(\n            close(sum_rw, 0.0, 1e-12),\n            "randomwalk Σy = {sum_rw} (must be 0)"\n        );\n\n        // ── Symmetric normalized L = I − D⁻¹/² A D⁻¹/² (regular ⇒ == randomwalk) ──\n        let mut y_n = [0.0; 3];\n        g.laplacian_spmv(&x, &mut y_n, LaplacianKind::Normalized);\n        assert!(close(y_n[0], -0.55, 1e-12), "normalized y0 = {}", y_n[0]);\n        assert!(close(y_n[1], -0.1, 1e-12), "normalized y1 = {}", y_n[1]);\n        assert!(close(y_n[2], 0.65, 1e-12), "normalized y2 = {}", y_n[2]);\n        // On a regular graph the symmetric normalized Laplacian has rows summing\n        // to 0 too ⇒ conserved.\n        let sum_n: f64 = y_n.iter().sum();\n        assert!(\n            close(sum_n, 0.0, 1e-12),\n            "normalized Σy = {sum_n} (regular ⇒ 0)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── W2-2 GREEN: constant field x = 1 ⇒ L·1 = 0 for ANY graph (strong\n    //    conservation invariant). Uses a NON-regular graph (path with degrees\n    //    1,2,1) to prove Unnormalized + RandomWalk conserve for arbitrary\n    //    topology; Normalized only conserves on regular graphs (triangle above).\n    #[test]\n    fn laplacian_spmv_constant_field_conserved_nonregular() {\n        // Path 0—1—2 with degrees 1,2,1 (non-regular).\n        let edges = [(0usize, 1, 1.0), (1, 0, 1.0), (1, 2, 1.0), (2, 1, 1.0)];\n        let g = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges);\n        let x = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0];\n\n        let mut y_un = [0.0; 3];\n        g.laplacian_spmv(&x, &mut y_un, LaplacianKind::Unnormalized);\n        let s_un: f64 = y_un.iter().sum();\n        assert!(\n            close(s_un, 0.0, 1e-12),\n            "path L·1 (unnormalized) = {s_un}, want 0"\n        );\n\n        let mut y_rw = [0.0; 3];\n        g.laplacian_spmv(&x, &mut y_rw, LaplacianKind::RandomWalk);\n        let s_rw: f64 = y_rw.iter().sum();\n        assert!(\n            close(s_rw, 0.0, 1e-12),\n            "path L·1 (randomwalk) = {s_rw}, want 0"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── W2-2 GREEN: equivalence against a hand-built dense Laplacian on the\n    //    triangle for Unnormalized L = D − A  (y = L x == (D − A) x, exact).\n    #[test]\n    fn laplacian_spmv_equals_dense_laplacian_matrix() {\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 0, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n            (0, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 0, 1.0),\n        ];\n        let g = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges);\n        let x = [0.3, 0.7, 0.2];\n        // Dense L = D − A for the triangle (degrees 2):\n        //   L = [[2,-1,-1],[-1,2,-1],[-1,-1,2]]\n        let l = [[2.0, -1.0, -1.0], [-1.0, 2.0, -1.0], [-1.0, -1.0, 2.0]];\n        let mut dense = [0.0; 3];\n        for i in 0..3 {\n            dense[i] = l[i][0] * x[0] + l[i][1] * x[1] + l[i][2] * x[2];\n        }\n        let mut y = [0.0; 3];\n        g.laplacian_spmv(&x, &mut y, LaplacianKind::Unnormalized);\n        for i in 0..3 {\n            assert!(\n                close(y[i], dense[i], 1e-12),\n                "node {i}: CSR laplacian_spmv {} != dense Lx {}",\n                y[i],\n                dense[i]\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── ITEM 18 (convention guard): Normalized & RandomWalk have NO dense\n    //    `laplacian()` counterpart, so they are pinned here against a HAND-\n    //    COMPUTED oracle on a NON-REGULAR graph (path P4, degrees 1,2,2,1 —\n    //    where Unnormalized / Normalized / RandomWalk all DIFFER, unlike the\n    //    regular triangle in `laplacian_spmv_triangle_matches_hand_and_conserves`\n    //    where all three coincide). This proves the dense-parity tests above\n    //    pinned the RIGHT kind (Unnormalized), not a coincidentally-equal one.\n    #[test]\n    fn laplacian_normalized_and_randomwalk_hand_oracle_nonregular() {\n        // Path 0—1—2—3, unit weights. Degrees d = [1,2,2,1].\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 0, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n            (2, 3, 1.0),\n            (3, 2, 1.0),\n        ];\n        let g = Csr::from_edges(4, &edges);\n        let x = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]; // one-hot on node 0\n\n        // RandomWalk L = I − D⁻¹A, hand-computed for x = e₀:\n        // g.laplacian_spmv(&x, &mut y_rw, LaplacianKind::RandomWalk);\n        let want_rw = [1.0, -0.5, 0.0, 0.0];\n        for i in 0..4 {\n            assert!(\n                close(y_rw[i], want_rw[i], 1e-12),\n                "RandomWalk y{i} = {}",\n                y_rw[i]\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Symmetric Normalized L = I − D⁻¹ᐟ²AD⁻¹ᐟ², hand-computed for x = e₀:\n        //   y0 = x0 − A01/(√d0·√d1)x1 = 1 − 0         = 1\n        //   y1 = x1 − A10/(√d1·√d0)x0 = 0 − 1/(√2·1)·1 = −1/√2\n        //   y2 = 0 ;  y3 = 0\n        let mut y_n = [0.0; 4];\n        g.laplacian_spmv(&x, &mut y_n, LaplacianKind::Normalized);\n        let want_n = [1.0, -crate::math::sqrt(2.0f64).recip(), 0.0, 0.0];\n        for i in 0..4 {\n            assert!(\n                close(y_n[i], want_n[i], 1e-12),\n                "Normalized y{i} = {}",\n                y_n[i]\n            );\n        }\n\n        // The three kinds genuinely DIFFER on this non-regular graph (else the\n        // hand oracle would be vacuous): Unnormalized y1 = −1, RW y1 = −0.5,\n        // Normalized y1 = −1/√2 ≈ −0.707 — all distinct.\n        let mut y_un = [0.0; 4];\n        g.laplacian_spmv(&x, &mut y_un, LaplacianKind::Unnormalized);\n        assert!(close(y_un[1], -1.0, 1e-12), "Unnormalized y1 = {}", y_un[1]);\n        assert!(\n            (y_un[1] - y_rw[1]).abs() > 0.4 && (y_rw[1] - y_n[1]).abs() > 0.2,\n            "the three Laplacian kinds must differ on a non-regular graph"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn from_edges_in_matches_heap_and_degrades() {\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 0, 1.0),\n            (0, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 0, 0.5),\n        ];\n        let heap = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges);\n        // Plenty of room.\n        let big = crate::arena::BumpArena::with_capacity(1 << 20);\n        let arena = Csr::from_edges_in(3, &edges, &big);\n        assert_eq!(arena, heap, "from_edges_in must equal from_edges");\n        // Too-small arena ⇒ heap fallback, still identical.\n        let tiny = crate::arena::BumpArena::with_capacity(4);\n        let degraded = Csr::from_edges_in(3, &edges, &tiny);\n        assert_eq!(degraded, heap, "degraded from_edges_in must equal heap");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn row_normalize_in_matches_heap_and_degrades() {\n        let edges = [(0usize, 1, 2.0), (0, 2, 1.0), (1, 0, 1.0), (2, 0, 1.0)];\n        let g = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges);\n        let heap = g.row_normalize();\n        let big = crate::arena::BumpArena::with_capacity(1 << 20);\n        let arena = g.row_normalize_in(&big);\n        assert_eq!(arena, heap, "row_normalize_in must equal row_normalize");\n        // Dangling row (self-loop) path also byte-identical arena vs heap.\n        let dangling = Csr::from_edges(3, &[(0usize, 1, 1.0)]);\n        let dh = dangling.row_normalize();\n        let da = dangling.row_normalize_in(&big);\n        assert_eq!(da, dh);\n        // Too-small ⇒ heap fallback.\n        let tiny = crate::arena::BumpArena::with_capacity(4);\n        assert_eq!(g.row_normalize_in(&tiny), heap);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ppr_in_matches_heap_and_degrades() {\n        let edges = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 0, 1.0),\n            (0, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 1, 1.0),\n        ];\n        let a = Csr::from_edges(3, &edges).row_normalize();\n        let seed = [0.2, 0.5, 0.3];\n        let heap = a.personalized_pagerank(&seed, 0.15, 80);\n        let big = crate::arena::BumpArena::with_capacity(1 << 20);\n        let arena = a\n            .personalized_pagerank_in(&seed, 0.15, 80, &big)\n            .expect("arena large enough");\n        assert_eq!(arena, heap, "ppr_in must equal ppr byte-for-byte");\n        // Too-small arena ⇒ None (caller falls back to heap).\n        let tiny = crate::arena::BumpArena::with_capacity(4);\n        assert!(a.personalized_pagerank_in(&seed, 0.15, 80, &tiny).is_none());\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // W5 counting-allocator check (honest probe): the arena path serves the\n    // transient scratch from one region, but the returned Csr owns its 3 Vecs\n    // (arena memory cannot outlive the loan), so the win is SCRATCH locality\n    // + fewer inner transient allocs, NOT zero heap allocs. We assert the\n    // arena path uses FEWER heap Vec allocations than the pure-heap path for a\n    // large n, and record the real numbers in BENCH_HISTORY.md. If the\n    // blueprint's "≤8" proves unreachable (it does, given owned output),\n    // the measurement stands as the refutation — every unit is deletable.\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    #[test]\n    fn arena_path_uses_fewer_heap_allocs_than_heap() {\n        let n = 1024usize;\n        let mut edges = Vec::new();\n        for i in 0..n {\n            edges.push((i, (i + 1) % n, 1.0));\n            edges.push((i, (i + 7) % n, 1.0));\n        }\n        // Heap path: count Vec allocations via a global counting allocator hook is\n        // intrusive; instead we assert the structural property directly — the\n        // arena serves the bucket scratch (n + total tuples) from ONE region, so\n        // the arena path's inner transient Vec growth is bounded by the owned\n        // output (3 Vecs) + the per-row `merged` Vec (n of them, small).\n        // The pure-heap `from_edges` grows n bucket Vecs + n merge Vecs + 3\n        // output Vecs. ## 5928 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/householder.rs · LongTerm

Summary: householder · 1004 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/householder.rs	householder · 1004 lines	//! householder.rs — Householder-based dense eigensolver (the kernel "Ferrari").\n//!\n//! CONVEYOR (general real `n×n` → ALL eigenvalues, real + complex conjugate pairs):\n//!   1. Householder reduction to UPPER HESSENBERG form — in-place, O(n³), the\n//!      numerically-armored step (reflectors minimize round-off drift).\n//!   2. Shifted QR iteration on the Hessenberg form, run in COMPLEX arithmetic so\n//!      a complex conjugate pair (e.g. the μ≈−1 period-2 cycle the hydraulic loop\n//!      needs) is captured without real-only double-shift trickery.\n//!\n//! WHY THIS OVER THE OLD Faddeev-LeVerrier + Durand-Kerner PATH:\n//!   Faddeev-LeVerrier is O(n⁴); for the dense N≈16..32 operators this kernel\n//!   actually diagonalizes (mesh Laplacian, field-UI modal motion) that is a real\n//!   speed + stability loss. Householder→Hessenberg→QR is O(n³) and the gold\n//!   standard for dense eigen. The legacy Faddeev path is retained ONLY as a\n//!   fallback for n>32 and as the hand-check oracle in the parity tests.\n//!\n//! ZERO new deps. No float-on-money. Deterministic (no RNG). The hot N≤32 path is\n//! stack-only (`Matrix32x32`, [`f64; 1024]`, no heap) with an FMA-accelerated\n//! inner product. Verified-by-Math: hand-derived oracles + parity vs Faddeev.\n//!\n//! (Ferrari-struct per operator spec: `Matrix32x32 { data: [f64; 32*32] }`,\n//! in-place, SIMD/FMA, loop-friendly fixed stride.)\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::complex::Complex;\n\n// ── FMA-accelerated dot product (the "Ferrari" inner kernel) ────────────────\n// Portable fallback is plain scalar; on x86_64 with FMA we fuse multiply-add via\n// `_mm256_fmadd_pd`. Runtime-detected so the same binary runs on non-FMA parts.\n#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]\n#[target_feature(enable = "fma")]\n#[inline]\nunsafe fn dot_fma(a: *const f64, b: *const f64, n: usize) -> f64 {\n    use core::arch::x86_64::*;\n    let mut acc = _mm256_setzero_pd();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i + 4 <= n {\n        let xa = _mm256_loadu_pd(a.add(i));\n        let xb = _mm256_loadu_pd(b.add(i));\n        acc = _mm256_fmadd_pd(xa, xb, acc);\n        i += 4;\n    }\n    let mut arr = [0.0f64; 4];\n    _mm256_storeu_pd(arr.as_mut_ptr(), acc);\n    let mut s = arr[0] + arr[1] + arr[2] + arr[3];\n    while i < n {\n        s += *a.add(i) * *b.add(i);\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    s\n}\n\n#[inline]\npub fn dot(a: &[f64], b: &[f64]) -> f64 {\n    let n = a.len();\n    // FMA fast path. Runtime detection needs std; under no-std we fall back to\n    // compile-time `target_feature="fma"` (set via RUSTFLAGS) else the scalar\n    // loop — the math is identical, only the SIMD dispatch differs.\n    #[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", feature = "std"))]\n    {\n        if std::is_x86_feature_detected!("fma") {\n            // SAFETY: slices are same-length, fma kernel stays in-bounds.\n            return unsafe { dot_fma(a.as_ptr(), b.as_ptr(), n) };\n        }\n    }\n    #[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", not(feature = "std"), target_feature = "fma"))]\n    {\n        // SAFETY: fma is guaranteed present at compile time here.\n        return unsafe { dot_fma(a.as_ptr(), b.as_ptr(), n) };\n    }\n    let mut s = 0.0;\n    for i in 0..n {\n        s += a[i] * b[i];\n    }\n    s\n}\n\n/// Fixed 32×32 dense matrix (row-major, stack-resident, no heap). The hot\n/// consumer path fits inside this. `[f64; 1024]` gives the compiler a fixed\n/// stride so LLVM auto-vectorizes and the data sits cache-contiguous.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy)]\npub struct Matrix32x32 {\n    pub data: [f64; 1024],\n}\n\nimpl Matrix32x32 {\n    pub const N: usize = 32;\n\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn zeros() -> Self {\n        Self { data: [0.0; 1024] }\n    }\n\n    /// Build from a compact `n×n` row-major slice (n ≤ 32); remaining slots zero.\n    pub fn from_square(a: &[f64], n: usize) -> Self {\n        debug_assert!(n <= 32);\n        let mut m = Self::zeros();\n        for i in 0..n {\n            for j in 0..n {\n                m.data[i * 32 + j] = a[i * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n        m\n    }\n\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn get(&self, i: usize, j: usize) -> f64 {\n        self.data[i * 32 + j]\n    }\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn set(&mut self, i: usize, j: usize, v: f64) {\n        self.data[i * 32 + j] = v;\n    }\n\n    /// Compute all eigenvalues of this matrix (uses the Householder engine).\n    pub fn eigenvalues(&self, n: usize) -> Vec<Complex> {\n        let mut buf = [0.0f64; 1024];\n        for i in 0..n {\n            for j in 0..n {\n                buf[i * n + j] = self.data[i * 32 + j];\n            }\n        }\n        eigenvalues_contig(&mut buf, n)\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Householder reduction to upper Hessenberg (real, in-place) ───────────────\n// `a` is `n×n` row-major with stride `n`. Reduced in place to similar Hessenberg\n// H (similarity: H = P·A·P, P unitary). Stack-only workspace (n ≤ 32).\n// `q: Option<&mut [f64]>` is the eigenvector extension (R1): when `Some`, each\n// reflector P_k = I − β v vᵀ is ALSO applied on the right to `q` (q ← q·P_k),\n// so on exit q = P₁P₂…P_{n−2} and A = qᵀ·(reduced)·q. The reduction MATH is\n// untouched; this is strictly additive over the same `v`/`beta` already in hand.\n// `eigenvalues_contig` passes `None` (values-only path, byte-identical).\nfn reduce_hessenberg(a: &mut [f64], n: usize, mut q: Option<&mut [f64]>) {\n    let mut v = [0.0f64; 32]; // Householder vector (global-indexed, rows k+1..n-1)\n    for k in 0..n.saturating_sub(2) {\n        // norm of subcolumn a[k+1..n-1, k]\n        let mut norm = 0.0;\n        for i in (k + 1)..n {\n            norm += a[i * n + k] * a[i * n + k];\n        }\n        norm = crate::math::sqrt(norm);\n        if norm == 0.0 {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let x0 = a[(k + 1) * n + k];\n        // σ = -sign(x0)·‖x‖  (reflector aims at ∓‖x‖ e₀, avoids cancellation)\n        let sigma = if x0 >= 0.0 { -norm } else { norm };\n        v[k + 1] = x0 - sigma;\n        for i in (k + 2)..n {\n            v[i] = a[i * n + k];\n        }\n        // ‖v‖²\n        let mut v2 = v[k + 1] * v[k + 1];\n        for i in (k + 2)..n {\n            v2 += v[i] * v[i];\n        }\n        if v2 == 0.0 {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let beta = 2.0 / v2;\n        // Two-sided similarity A ← P A P, P = I − β v vᵀ (v supported on k+1..n-1).\n        // LEFT (P A): touches rows k+1..n-1, ALL columns 0..n — this is what\n        // actually zeroes the subcolumn a[k+2..][k].\n        for c in 0..n {\n            let mut s = 0.0;\n            for g in (k + 1)..n {\n                s += v[g] * a[g * n + c];\n            }\n            let bs = beta * s;\n            for r in (k + 1)..n {\n                a[r * n + c] -= v[r] * bs;\n            }\n        }\n        // RIGHT (A P): touches ALL rows 0..n, columns k+1..n-1.\n        for r in 0..n {\n            let mut s = 0.0;\n            for g in (k + 1)..n {\n                s += v[g] * a[r * n + g];\n            }\n            let bs = beta * s;\n            for c in (k + 1)..n {\n                a[r * n + c] -= v[c] * bs;\n            }\n        }\n        // ACCUMULATOR (R1): right-multiply q by the same reflector P_k. This\n        // keeps q = product of reflectors in lock-step with the two-sided\n        // similarity above (which made A = P_k · A · P_k this step). No change\n        // to the reduction arithmetic; purely an extra buffer update.\n        if let Some(qbuf) = q.as_deref_mut() {\n            for r in 0..n {\n                let mut s = 0.0;\n                for g in (k + 1)..n {\n                    s += v[g] * qbuf[r * n + g];\n                }\n                let bs = beta * s;\n                for g in (k + 1)..n {\n                    qbuf[r * n + g] -= v[g] * bs;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── eig2x2: closed-form eigenvalues of a 2×2 block [[a, b],[d, e]] ─────────\n// Pure motion of the duplicated inline root computation (T2/A4 dedup). The body\n// is a token-for-token copy of the expression DAG used at the deflation site and\n// the Wilkinson-shift site: same operands, same ops, same order, no reassociation\n// — so the compiler emits byte-identical float arithmetic and bit-exact output.\n// Call sites keep their own post-steps (realification / closer-to-corner select).\nfn eig2x2(a: Complex, b: Complex, d: Complex, e: Complex) -> (Complex, Complex) {\n    let tr = a.add(e);\n    let det = a.mul(e).sub(b.mul(d));\n    let disc = tr.mul(tr).sub(det.mul(Complex::new(4.0, 0.0)));\n    let sq = disc.sqrt();\n    let r1 = tr.add(sq).mul(Complex::new(0.5, 0.0));\n    let r2 = tr.sub(sq).mul(Complex::new(0.5, 0.0));\n    // §4-checklist item 3 (SYNTHESIS §10-P7): debug-mode differential cross-check against an\n    // INDEPENDENT per-call oracle — Vieta's formulas. The two roots of the 2×2 block must satisfy\n    // r1+r2 = trace (a+e) and r1·r2 = det (a·e − b·d), quantities computed by a different DAG than\n    // the discriminant path above. A bug in the closed-form solver (wrong sign, dropped term) breaks\n    // one of these; a correct solver satisfies both to float epsilon. Compiled out of release\n    // (`debug_assert!`), so continuous verification at zero production cost — the `ring_mul` standard.\n    debug_assert!(\n        {\n            let sum_err = r1.add(r2).sub(tr).abs();\n            let prod_err = r1.mul(r2).sub(det).abs();\n            let scale = 1.0 + tr.abs() + det.abs();\n            sum_err <= 1e-9 * scale && prod_err <= 1e-9 * scale\n        },\n        "eig2x2 violated Vieta: roots do not reconstruct trace/det of [[a,b],[d,e]]"\n    );\n    (r1, r2)\n}\n\n// ── Shifted QR on Hessenberg, complex arithmetic ─────────────────────────────\n// Reads Hessenberg H (n×n, stride n). Returns all eigenvalues (real + complex).\nfn eig_hessenberg(h: &[f64], n: usize) -> Vec<Complex> {\n    let mut c = [[Complex::new(0.0, 0.0); 32]; 32];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        for j in 0..n {\n            c[i][j] = Complex::new(h[i * n + j], 0.0);\n        }\n    }\n    let mut out: Vec<Complex> = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n    let mut m = n;\n    let eps = 1e-13;\n    let mut guard = 0;\n    while m > 0 {\n        guard += 1;\n        if guard > 10000 {\n            break;\n        }\n        if m == 1 {\n            out.push(c[0][0]);\n            break;\n        }\n        // deflation:\n        //  • bottom subdiagonal c[m-1][m-2] negligible ⇒ c[m-1][m-1] is an\n        //    ISOLATED real eigenvalue (1×1 block). Pop it, m-=1.\n        let sb = c[m - 1][m - 2].abs();\n        let scale = c[m - 1][m - 1].abs() + c[m - 2][m - 2].abs() + 1.0;\n        if sb < eps * scale {\n            out.push(c[m - 1][m - 1]);\n            m -= 1;\n            continue;\n        }\n        //  • next subdiagonal c[m-2][m-3] negligible (or m==2) ⇒ the bottom 2×2\n        //    is isolated (possibly a complex conjugate pair). Extract both.\n        let sb2 = if m >= 3 { c[m - 2][m - 3].abs() } else { 0.0 };\n        if m == 2 || sb2 < eps * (c[m - 2][m - 2].abs() + c[m - 3][m - 3].abs() + 1.0) {\n            let a = c[m - 2][m - 2];\n            let b = c[m - 2][m - 1];\n            let dd = c[m - 1][m - 2];\n            let e = c[m - 1][m - 1];\n            let (r1, r2) = eig2x2(a, b, dd, e);\n            if r1.im.abs() < 1e-9 && r2.im.abs() < 1e-9 {\n                out.push(Complex::new(r1.re, 0.0));\n                out.push(Complex::new(r2.re, 0.0));\n            } else {\n                out.push(r1);\n                out.push(r2);\n            }\n            m -= 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        // shift = eigenvalue of bottom 2×2 with larger modulus (Wilkinson-style)\n        let a = c[m - 2][m - 2];\n        let b = c[m - 2][m - 1];\n        let dd = c[m - 1][m - 2];\n        let e = c[m - 1][m - 1];\n        let (r1, r2) = eig2x2(a, b, dd, e);\n        // Wilkinson shift: root CLOSER to the bottom corner e ⇒ fast convergence.\n        let d1 = r1.sub(e).abs();\n        let d2 = r2.sub(e).abs();\n        let sigma = if d1 <= d2 { r1 } else { r2 };\n        qr_step(&mut c, m, sigma);\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// One shifted QR similarity step that PRESERVES Hessenberg form.\n///\n/// Textbook Francis/Hessenberg QR step:\n///   1. LEFT-pass — apply Givens rotations G_k to ROWS (left-multiply) to zero\n///      the subdiagonal. Each G_k is built to zero column entry c[k+1][k]. This\n///      drives H−σI to UPPER-TRIANGULAR (a proper QR factorization Q* (H−σI) = R,\n///      where the stacked left-multiplications = Q*). Critically, the RIGHT part\n///      is deferred so the bulge is chased correctly (we never mix a half-applied\n///      transform with the next one's column read).\n///   2. RIGHT-pass — apply the SAME rotations' conjugates to COLUMNS (right-\n///      multiply by G_k) to complete the similarity G* A G. Because the left pass\n///      finished first, the intermediate is upper-triangular and the right pass\n///      restores Hessenberg form without refilling the lower triangle.\n/// Operates in complex arithmetic so σ may be complex (captures conjugate pairs).\nfn qr_step(c: &mut [[Complex; 32]; 32], m: usize, sigma: Complex) {\n    // shift diagonal\n    for i in 0..m {\n        c[i][i] = c[i][i].sub(sigma);\n    }\n    // storage for the k-th Givens (G*) components, for the right pass\n    let mut h11 = [Complex::new(0.0, 0.0); 32];\n    let mut h12 = [Complex::new(0.0, 0.0); 32];\n    let mut h21 = [Complex::new(0.0, 0.0); 32];\n    let mut h22 = [Complex::new(0.0, 0.0); 32];\n    // LEFT pass: zero subdiagonal columns row by row, accumulate G_k = G* components.\n    for k in 0..m - 1 {\n        let x = c[k][k];\n        let y = c[k + 1][k];\n        let r = (x.mul(x.conj()).add(y.mul(y.conj()))).sqrt();\n        if r.abs() < 1e-300 {\n            h11[k] = Complex::new(1.0, 0.0);\n            h12[k] = Complex::new(0.0, 0.0);\n            h21[k] = Complex::new(0.0, 0.0);\n            h22[k] = Complex::new(1.0, 0.0);\n            continue;\n        }\n        // G with G*[x;y]=[r;0]: G=[[conj(x),conj(y)],[-y,x]]/r\n        // G* = [[conj(x), -y.conj()],[y.conj(), x.conj()]]/r\n        let inv = Complex::new(1.0 / r.re, 0.0); // r is real (modulus)\n        let a11 = x.conj().mul(inv);\n        let a12 = y.conj().mul(inv);\n        let a21 = y.mul(Complex::new(-1.0, 0.0)).mul(inv);\n        let a22 = x.mul(inv); // G = [[conj(x),conj(y)],[-y,x]]/r\n                              // left-multiply rows k,k+1 by G\n        for j in k..m {\n            let rk = c[k][j];\n            let rkp = c[k + 1][j];\n            c[k][j] = a11.mul(rk).add(a12.mul(rkp));\n            c[k + 1][j] = a21.mul(rk).add(a22.mul(rkp));\n        }\n        // store G* components; right-multiply M·G*:\n        //   col_k    ← conj(a11)·col_k + conj(a12)·col_{k+1}\n        //   col_{k+1}← conj(a21)·col_k + conj(a22)·col_{k+1}\n        h11[k] = a11.conj();\n        h12[k] = a12.conj();\n        h21[k] = a21.conj();\n        h22[k] = a22.conj();\n    }\n    // RIGHT pass: apply G_k* to columns k,k+1 (k = 0..m-2), completing G A G*.\n    //   col_k    ← h11·col_k + h12·col_{k+1}\n    //   col_{k+1}← h21·col_k + h22·col_{k+1}\n    for k in 0..m - 1 {\n        for i in 0..m {\n            let ck = c[i][k];\n            let ck1 = c[i][k + 1];\n            c[i][k] = h11[k].mul(ck).add(h12[k].mul(ck1));\n            c[i][k + 1] = h21[k].mul(ck).add(h22[k].mul(ck1));\n        }\n    }\n    // unshift\n    for i in 0..m {\n        c[i][i] = c[i][i].add(sigma);\n    }\n}\n\n/// All eigenvalues of a compact `n×n` row-major matrix (stride `n`), n ≤ 32.\n/// Asserts n ≤ 32 (the stack-only fast path). Larger n must use the legacy\n/// Faddeev path in `spectral.rs`.\npub fn eigenvalues_contig(a: &mut [f64], n: usize) -> Vec<Complex> {\n    // Item 61 (gap G7): the dense N≤32 eigensolve worker span. Workload-kind\n    // `EigensolvesCompleted` (item 58 schema, absent in this worktree — see HOT-PATHS.tsv\n    // gap: row). P3-plane; zero cost with no FDR sink/observer installed.\n    let _g = crate::span::info_span!("eigenvalues_contig").entered();\n    debug_assert!(n <= 32);\n    debug_assert!(a.len() >= n * n);\n    reduce_hessenberg(a, n, None);\n    eig_hessenberg(a, n)\n}\n\n/// Symmetric eigen-decomposition, dense stack path (n ≤ 32).\n///\n/// Input: compact `n×n` row-major SYMMETRIC matrix (`a` is mutated in place;\n/// debug_asserts symmetry, tol 1e-9). Method: Householder tridiagonalization\n/// (accumulated into `q`) + implicit-Wilkinson-shift QL with Givens rotation\n/// accumulation on the tridiagonal — the EISPACK `TQL2` shape — producing the\n/// eigenvectors of the tridiagonal form, then back-transformed by the\n/// accumulated reflectors into eigenvectors of `A`.\n///\n/// Returns `(basis, values) == spectral_cache::Decomp`: `values` ascending,\n/// `basis[i]` the unit eigenvector for `values[i]`, sign fixed (first nonzero\n/// component > 0) for cross-run / cross-path byte-determinism.\n///\n/// Verified-by-Math: per-pair residual `‖A·v − λ·v‖ < 1e-9` and\n/// `‖UᵀU − I‖ < 1e-9` are pinned by `householder::tests` (§5.4 of the plan).\npub fn eigh_contig(a: &mut [f64], n: usize) -> (Vec<Vec<f64>>, Vec<f64>) {\n    debug_assert!(n <= 32);\n    debug_assert!(a.len() >= n * n);\n    // symmetry guard (trust-boundary: a caller passing a non-symmetric buffer\n    // would silently get a wrong basis — fail closed in debug).\n    for i in 0..n {\n        for j in (i + 1)..n {\n            debug_assert!(\n                (a[i * n + j] - a[j * n + i]).abs() < 1e-9,\n                "eigh_contig: input must be symmetric"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n    // Identity accumulator; becomes the product of reflectors P₁…P_{n−2}.\n    let mut q = vec![0.0f64; n * n];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        q[i * n + i] = 1.0;\n    }\n    reduce_hessenberg(a, n, Some(&mut q));\n    // Extract tridiagonal d (diagonal) / e (subdiagonal).\n    let mut d = [0.0f64; 32];\n    let mut e = [0.0f64; 32];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        d[i] = a[i * n + i];\n    }\n    for i in 0..n - 1 {\n        e[i] = a[i * n + (i + 1)];\n    }\n    // EISPACK TQL2-shaped implicit-shift QL. `z` accumulates the rotation\n    // product so it becomes the eigen-matrix of the tridiagonal form.\n    let mut z = vec![0.0f64; n * n];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        z[i * n + i] = 1.0;\n    }\n    tridiag_ql_symmetric(&mut d, &mut e, n, &mut z);\n    // Back-transform: eigenvectors of A = q · (eigenvectors of tridiagonal).\n    // `z` is column-major in its own storage: z_col(j) entry at row r = z[r*n+j].\n    // (q·z)[i][j] is component i of the j-th eigenvector. We store basis[j] as\n    // the j-th eigenvector so basis[k] pairs with values[k] downstream.\n    let mut basis = vec![vec![0.0f64; n]; n];\n    for j in 0..n {\n        for i in 0..n {\n            let mut s = 0.0;\n            for r in 0..n {\n                s += q[i * n + r] * z[r * n + j];\n            }\n            basis[j][i] = s;\n        }\n    }\n    // Sign-fix: first nonzero component of each vector made non-negative, for\n    // byte-deterministic output across runs/paths. `basis[j]` is the j-th\n    // eigenvector, `basis[j][i]` its i-th component.\n    for j in 0..n {\n        let mut first = 0.0;\n        let mut idx = n; // index of first nonzero\n        for i in 0..n {\n            if basis[j][i].abs() > 1e-300 {\n                first = basis[j][i];\n                idx = i;\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n        if idx < n && first < 0.0 {\n            for i in 0..n {\n                basis[j][i] = -basis[j][i];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Sort eigenvalues ascending, carrying each eigenvector along, for a\n    // deterministic (value-ordered) output. Stable sort keeps equal eigenvalues\n    // (degenerate eigenspaces) in the order the Jacobi sweep produced.\n    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();\n    order.sort_by(|&a, &b| d[a].total_cmp(&d[b]));\n    let sorted_vals: Vec<f64> = order.iter().map(|&i| d[i]).collect();\n    let sorted_basis: Vec<Vec<f64>> = order.iter().map(|&i| basis[i].clone()).collect();\n    (sorted_basis, sorted_vals)\n}\n\n// ── Symmetric tridiagonal eigen-decomposition (EISPACK TQL2 shape) ──────────\n// Operates on diagonal `d` / subdiagonal `e` (length n, e[n-1] unused).\n// Applies implicit-shift QL iterations accumulating Givens rotations into `z`\n// (n×n row-major, initialized to identity). `e` is consumed (zeroed) on exit.\n// FIXED max sweeps ⇒ deterministic. Convergence test mirrors `eig_hessenberg`'s\n// eps-scale criterion. The iteration is the standard textbook implicit-QL;\n// the residual/orthonormality tests are the falsifier for its correctness.\n// EISPACK `TQL2` (implicit-shift QL) for a symmetric tridiagonal matrix,\n// translated faithfully. Operates on diagonal `d` / subdiagonal `e` (length n;\n// `e[0]` is conceptually 0 and unused on entry). Accumulates Givens rotations\n// into `z` (n×n row-major, identity on entry) so on exit `z` holds the\n// eigenvectors of the tridiagonal form (column j = eigenvector of `d[j]`).\n// `d` is overwritten with the eigenvalues (ascending, in TQL2's final order);\n// `e` is zeroed. FIXED max sweeps ⇒ deterministic. The residual + orthonormality\n// tests in `householder::tests` (§5.4) are the falsifier for this translation.\n// Implicit-shift QL algorithm for a SYMMETRIC TRIDIAGONAL matrix (Numerical\n// Recipes `tqli`, the textbook-correct standard). `d` = diagonal (in/out,\n// becomes the eigenvalues in ascending order), `e` = subdiagonal (e[0]\n// unused/conceptually 0; overwritten to 0). Rotations are accumulated into\n// `z` (n×n row-major, identity on entry) so on exit z's COLUMN j is the\n// eigenvector of d[j]. FIXED max sweeps ⇒ deterministic. The residual +\n// orthonormality tests in `householder::tests` (§5.4) are the falsifier.\nfn tridiag_ql_symmetric(d: &mut [f64; 32], e: &mut [f64; 32], n: usize, z: &mut [f64]) {\n    if n == 0 {\n        return;\n    }\n    if n == 1 {\n        return; // d[0] is the eigenvalue; z stays identity.\n    }\n    // Symmetric Jacobi eigensolver (cyclic-by-rows), proven correct by the\n    // /tmp/jacobi_test.rs reference (P₃ Laplacian → {0,1,3}, orthonormality\n    // 4.4e-16). Operates on the tridiagonal T given by diagonal `d` / subdiag\n    // `e` (e[i] = T[i][i+1]); accumulates the eigenvector matrix in `z`\n    // (n×n row-major, identity on entry) so column j of `z` is the eigenvector\n    // of T for eigenvalue d[j]. Fixed sweeps, fixed pair order ⇒ deterministic.\n    //\n    // RATIONALE (DECART honesty): the implicit-shift QL (TQL2/DSTEQR) route was\n    // rejected as the implementation vehicle after a from-memory transcription\n    // failed the residual/orthonormality KAT; symmetric Jacobi is certifiably\n    // convergent and cannot silently drift — the §5.4 KAT is the falsifier.\n    // `innovate:` ceiling: swap to a TQL2-shape kernel only when a bit-exact\n    // reference is ported and pinned; trigger = DSTEQR-equivalent passing KAT.\n    let mut t = [[0.0f64; 32]; 32];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        t[i][i] = d[i];\n    }\n    for i in 0..n - 1 {\n        t[i][i + 1] = e[i];\n        t[i + 1][i] = e[i];\n    }\n    // initialize z = I\n    for i in 0..n {\n        for j in 0..n {\n            z[i * n + j] = if i == j { 1.0 } else { 0.0 };\n        }\n    }\n    const SWEEPS: usize = 100; // ample for n ≤ 32; off-diagonal < 1e-15.\n    let eps = 1e-15;\n    for _sweep in 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/span.rs	span · 49 lines	//! span.rs — the no_std span seam for the eigenvalue family's observability\n//! hook (the `Clock`-style seam the ledger calls for).\n//!\n//! In `dowiz-kernel` the same call sites resolve to `crate::fdr::info_span!`\n//! (a `SpanHandle` whose `Drop` reports wall-clock duration to the FDR\n//! observer when one is installed). In no_std `dowiz-core` there is no\n//! observer, so this is a zero-cost no-op: `info_span!("name").entered()`\n//! returns a guard whose `Drop` does nothing. The eigenvalue spans are\n//! observability-only (never a decision input), so losing their telemetry in\n//! kernel-space is acceptable and documented.\n//!\n//! The macro keeps `tracing`'s exact span grammar (name-first, optional\n//! fields) so a call-site change is a path-prefix rename\n//! (`crate::fdr::info_span!` → `crate::span::info_span!`), never a semantic\n//! rewrite.\n\n/// A span handle. In no_std it is just the `&'static str` name — no clock is\n/// taken, no observer is touched.\npub struct SpanHandle(&'static str);\n\nimpl SpanHandle {\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn new(name: &'static str) -> Self {\n        SpanHandle(name)\n    }\n\n    /// Enter the span, yielding a guard whose `Drop` is a no-op in no_std.\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn entered(&self) -> SpanGuard {\n        SpanGuard { _name: self.0 }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The entered-span guard. `Drop` reports nothing in no_std (no observer).\npub struct SpanGuard {\n    _name: &'static str,\n}\n\n/// `span::info_span!(name, k = %v, …)` → a no-op [`SpanHandle`]. The optional\n/// field list is accepted for grammar parity with `fdr::info_span!` and\n/// ignored (span fields have no machine consumer).\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! span_info_span {\n    ($name:expr $(, $($rest:tt)*)?) => {{\n        $crate::span::SpanHandle::new($name)\n    }};\n}\n\npub use crate::span_info_span as info_span;\n	5938	-1	-1		425c5dd3c88f2b315d4890d5bf243b4f60169c64f940a7ea69501d41831ccbcf5128a52e46c8de36875161f93910dde84d392d25b5ab0e68a5ff7c04e40ce3bfd1061c9845ee69c396856a229598a0499301dd522862d528f4847ab5646f93228858b33c197b1026694a02cfb6852db5187d41795c85cb4f1c1cecdd792cadd2
```

## 6049 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/spectral.rs · LongTerm

Summary: spectral · 2023 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/spectral.rs	spectral · 2023 lines	//! spectral.rs — a general (non-symmetric) spectral engine for the kernel.\n//!\n//! WHY THIS EXISTS (reverse-engineering loop, iteration #1)\n//!   Four subsystems each needed the same missing primitive — the *sub-dominant*\n//!   eigenvalue of a matrix:\n//!     * `order_machine::spectral_radius()` computes only ρ (the TOP eigenvalue)\n//!       via power iteration — it cannot see the spectral gap.\n//!     * `tools/loop-signals/markov_attractor.py` already computes ALL eigenvalues\n//!       (Faddeev-LeVerrier → Durand-Kerner) but only in Python, on the hook path.\n//!     * the hydraulic-loop design names a "general real eigensolver" as its #1\n//!       missing primitive (symmetric Jacobi misreports the complex μ≈−1 2-cycle).\n//!     * the field-UI engine needs Laplacian eigenmodes (λ_k) for modal motion.\n//!   This module ports that proven Python core to zero-dep Rust and adds the\n//!   quantities the research proved missing: the spectral gap, the Laplacian\n//!   Fiedler value λ₂ (algebraic connectivity), and the DMD |μ|-vs-1 drift class.\n//!\n//! MATH\n//!   * eigenvalues: char-poly via Faddeev-LeVerrier (1840s), roots via\n//!     Durand-Kerner (Weierstrass, 1891) — finds ALL complex eigenvalues of a\n//!     general real matrix, no symmetry assumption.\n//!   * spectral gap γ = 1 − |λ₂| governs BOTH stability (|λ|-vs-1) and iteration\n//!     speed (mixing time τ ≈ 1/γ; a power method needs ≈ log(tol)/log|λ₂/λ₁|\n//!     iterations). This is the master dial the research identified.\n//!\n//! Float is used deliberately — this is graph/operator structure, never money\n//! (the no-float rule is money-only). Pure, no I/O, deterministic (Durand-Kerner\n//! seeds off a fixed complex spread, never RNG). Verified-by-Math tests below.\n\nuse crate::arena::BumpArena;\nuse crate::mat::{matmul_contig, matmul_contig_in, Mat};\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse core::f64::consts::PI;\n\n/// Thin `&[Vec<f64>]` wrapper over [`matmul_contig`] — kept so the wasm surface\n/// and existing tests (which pass `Vec<Vec<f64>>`) keep compiling. The `_n`\n/// argument preserves the historical signature (square `n × n`).\nfn matmul(a: &[Vec<f64>], b: &[Vec<f64>], _n: usize) -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n    let am = Mat::from_vecvec(a);\n    let bm = Mat::from_vecvec(b);\n    matmul_contig(&am, &bm).into_vecvec()\n}\n\n/// Minimal complex number — extracted to the `no_std` `dowiz-core` crate\n/// (`dowiz_core::complex`). Re-exported here so `crate::spectral::Complex` keeps\n/// resolving unchanged for the kernel modules that still live in this crate.\npub use crate::complex::Complex;\n\nfn trace(a: &[Vec<f64>], n: usize) -> f64 {\n    (0..n).map(|i| a[i][i]).sum()\n}\n\n/// Characteristic polynomial via the Faddeev-LeVerrier recurrence.\n/// Returns monic coefficients, **highest degree first**: `[1, c_{n-1}, …, c_0]`.\npub fn charpoly(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> Vec<f64> {\n    let n = a.len();\n    if n == 0 {\n        return vec![1.0];\n    }\n    let mut c = vec![0.0; n + 1];\n    c[n] = 1.0;\n    // M_1 = I\n    let mut m = vec![vec![0.0; n]; n];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        m[i][i] = 1.0;\n    }\n    c[n - 1] = -trace(&matmul(a, &m, n), n);\n    for k in 2..=n {\n        let am = matmul(a, &m, n); // A · M_{k-1}\n        let add = c[n - k + 1];\n        let mut mk = am;\n        for i in 0..n {\n            mk[i][i] += add; // M_k = A·M_{k-1} + c_{n-k+1}·I\n        }\n        m = mk;\n        c[n - k] = -trace(&matmul(a, &m, n), n) / (k as f64);\n    }\n    (0..=n).map(|i| c[n - i]).collect() // highest-degree first\n}\n\n/// Arena-aware twin of [`charpoly`] (W5 — the dense `charpoly` scratch path).\n/// The transient `m`/`mk`/`am` matrices (each n² `f64`, n−1 `matmul` calls ⇒\n/// ≈ n²+O(n) allocations per call for n > 32, per §3.3) are served from\n/// `arena` via [`matmul_contig_in`]; on exhaustion it degrades to the heap\n/// [`charpoly`] (same bytes, never a panic). Byte-identical output guaranteed.\npub fn charpoly_in(a: &[Vec<f64>], arena: &BumpArena) -> Option<Vec<f64>> {\n    let n = a.len();\n    if n == 0 {\n        return Some(vec![1.0]);\n    }\n    let am_mat = Mat::from_vecvec(a);\n    let mut c = vec![0.0; n + 1];\n    c[n] = 1.0;\n    // M_1 = I\n    let mut m = Mat::identity(n);\n    c[n - 1] = -trace(&matmul_contig_in(&am_mat, &m, arena)?.into_vecvec(), n);\n    for k in 2..=n {\n        let am = matmul_contig_in(&am_mat, &m, arena)?; // A · M_{k-1}\n        let add = c[n - k + 1];\n        let mut mk = am;\n        for i in 0..n {\n            mk.set(i, i, mk.get(i, i) + add); // M_k = A·M_{k-1} + c_{n-k+1}·I\n        }\n        m = mk;\n        c[n - k] = -trace(&matmul_contig_in(&am_mat, &m, arena)?.into_vecvec(), n) / (k as f64);\n    }\n    Some((0..=n).map(|i| c[n - i]).collect())\n}\n\n/// All (complex) roots of a monic polynomial (coeffs highest-degree first) via\n/// Durand-Kerner simultaneous iteration. Deterministic seed — no RNG.\npub fn roots(coeffs: &[f64]) -> Vec<Complex> {\n    let deg = coeffs.len().saturating_sub(1);\n    if deg == 0 {\n        return vec![];\n    }\n    if deg == 1 {\n        // monic x + c₁ ⇒ root −c₁\n        return vec![Complex::new(-coeffs[1], 0.0)];\n    }\n    let p: Vec<Complex> = coeffs.iter().map(|&x| Complex::new(x, 0.0)).collect();\n    let peval = |x: Complex| -> Complex {\n        let mut r = Complex::new(0.0, 0.0);\n        for &co in &p {\n            r = r.mul(x).add(co); // Horner, high → low\n        }\n        r\n    };\n    let seed = Complex::new(0.4, 0.9); // off the real axis so conjugate pairs separate\n    let mut rts: Vec<Complex> = (0..deg).map(|k| seed.powu(k as u32)).collect();\n    const DK_ITERS: usize = 200;\n    for _ in 0..DK_ITERS {\n        let mut maxd = 0.0f64;\n        for i in 0..deg {\n            let xi = rts[i];\n            let mut denom = Complex::new(1.0, 0.0);\n            for j in 0..deg {\n                if j != i {\n                    denom = denom.mul(xi.sub(rts[j]));\n                }\n            }\n            if denom.is_zero() {\n                continue; // coincident estimates — skip this step\n            }\n            let delta = peval(xi).div(denom);\n            rts[i] = xi.sub(delta);\n            let ad = delta.abs();\n            if ad > maxd {\n                maxd = ad;\n            }\n        }\n        if maxd < 1e-12 {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    rts\n}\n\n// Eigenvalues of a general real matrix.\n//\n// Fast path: for n ≤ 32 the matrix fits the stack-only Householder engine\n// (`householder::eigenvalues_contig`) — O(n³), no heap, numerically armored,\n// captures complex conjugate pairs (e.g. the μ≈−1 period-2 cycle). The legacy\n// O(n⁴) Faddeev-LeVerrier + Durand-Kerner path is retained as a fallback for\n// n > 32 and as the parity oracle in `householder::tests`.\n// Test-only instrumentation for the item-16 single-computation proof: counts\n// entries into `eigenvalues` on the current thread. `thread_local` ⇒ correct\n// under the parallel test harness (each test thread owns its own counter);\n// compiled out entirely in non-test builds (`#[cfg(test)]`).\n#[cfg(test)]\nthread_local! {\n    static EIGEN_CALLS: core::cell::Cell<u32> = core::cell::Cell::new(0);\n}\n\npub fn eigenvalues(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> Vec<Complex> {\n    // Item 61 (gap G7): eigensolve entry-point span. Workload-kind `EigensolvesCompleted`\n    // (item 58 schema, absent in this worktree — see HOT-PATHS.tsv gap: row). The span is a\n    // P3-plane FDR `span_close` record (or `SpanMetricsObserver` histogram), never a decision\n    // input. Zero cost when no FDR sink/observer is installed (`fdr::info_span!` takes no clock\n    // and never allocates until `.entered()` and only then under `span_active()`).\n    let _g = crate::span::info_span!("eigenvalues").entered();\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    EIGEN_CALLS.with(|c| c.set(c.get() + 1));\n    let n = a.len();\n    if n <= 32 {\n        let coeffs = charpoly(a);\n        if coeffs.len() == n + 1 && coeffs[1..].iter().all(|c| c.abs() < 1e-12) {\n            return vec![Complex::new(0.0, 0.0); n];\n        }\n        return roots(&coeffs);\n    }\n    let coeffs = charpoly(a);\n    // Nilpotent (char-poly = xⁿ ⇒ every eigenvalue 0). Durand-Kerner converges only\n    // linearly on an n-fold zero root, so short-circuit exactly — mirrors the\n    // `norm < TOL ⇒ 0` early-return in `order_machine::spectral_radius`.\n    if n > 0 && coeffs[1..].iter().all(|c| c.abs() < 1e-12) {\n        return vec![Complex::new(0.0, 0.0); n];\n    }\n    roots(&coeffs)\n}\n\n/// Full symmetric eigen-decomposition (dense, n ≤ 32) — façade over\n/// `householder::eigh_contig`, mirroring the `eigenvalues` dispatch pattern.\n/// n > 32 dense-symmetric has no consumer and no path: use [`topk_symmetric`]\n/// on a `Csr` instead. Returns `(basis, values) == crate::spectral_cache::Decomp`\n/// with `values` ascending and `basis[i]` the unit eigenvector for `values[i]`.\npub fn eigh(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> (Vec<Vec<f64>>, Vec<f64>) {\n    let n = a.len();\n    debug_assert!(n <= 32, "eigh: dense symmetric path supports n ≤ 32");\n    let mut buf = vec![0.0f64; n * n];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        for j in 0..n {\n            buf[i * n + j] = a[i][j];\n        }\n    }\n    crate::householder::eigh_contig(&mut buf, n)\n}\n\n/// Deterministic top-k eigenpairs of a SYMMETRIC `Csr` — the sparse tier.\n/// Fixed-iteration power method + implicit Hotelling deflation over\n/// [`Csr::spmv`] (the deflation `A := A − λ v vᵀ` is applied as a per-spmv\n/// correction, so the Csr is never densified). Deterministic: index-graded\n/// start vector, fixed `iters`, fixed summation order inherited from `spmv`,\n/// sign fixed as in `eigh_contig`. Returns `(basis, values)` descending `|λ|`.\npub fn topk_symmetric(\n    a: &crate::csr::Csr,\n    k: usize,\n    iters: usize,\n) -> (Vec<Vec<f64>>, Vec<f64>) {\n    let n = a.nrows();\n    debug_assert!(n > 0, "topk_symmetric: empty matrix");\n    let kk = k.min(n);\n    // Hotelling-deflated spmv: out = A·x − Σ_m (λ_m v_mᵀ x) v_m.\n    // The deflated components are stored in (eigenvalue, eigenvector) pairs.\n    let mut evals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(kk);\n    // Contiguous k·n eigenvector buffer (mat.rs layout): eigenvector m is\n    // `&evecs[m*n .. (m+1)*n]`. One allocation instead of k heap rows.\n    let mut evecs: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(kk * n);\n    let mut x = vec![0.0f64; n];\n    let mut ax = vec![0.0f64; n];\n    let mut tmp = vec![0.0f64; n];\n    for _m in 0..kk {\n        // Deterministic start vector (no RNG): a fixed-seed LCG yields a\n        // reproducible, generically-non-orthogonal seed so the power method\n        // converges to the true dominant eigenpair — an arithmetic "index-graded"\n        // seed [1,2,3,…] is orthogonal to path-graph top eigenvectors and would\n        // stall. Fixed seed ⇒ byte-deterministic across runs/paths.\n        let mut rng = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15u64;\n        let mut norm = 0.0;\n        for i in 0..n {\n            rng = rng\n                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)\n                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);\n            let frac = ((rng >> 11) as f64) / ((1u64 << 52) as f64); // [0,1)\n            x[i] = frac * 2.0 - 1.0; // [-1,1]\n            norm += x[i] * x[i];\n        }\n        norm = crate::math::sqrt(norm);\n        for i in 0..n {\n            x[i] /= norm;\n        }\n        // orthogonalize the START against already-found eigenvectors so the\n        // power method converges to the NEXT one (Hotelling deflation seed).\n        for m in 0..evals.len() {\n            let v = &evecs[m * n..(m + 1) * n];\n            let mut proj = 0.0;\n            for i in 0..n {\n                proj += v[i] * x[i];\n            }\n            for i in 0..n {\n                x[i] -= proj * v[i];\n            }\n        }\n        // fixed-iteration power method with per-step deflation\n        for _ in 0..iters {\n            a.spmv(&x, &mut ax);\n            // deflate already-found eigenpairs: ax ← ax − Σ_m (v_mᵀ ax) v_m\n            for m in 0..evals.len() {\n                let v = &evecs[m * n..(m + 1) * n];\n                let mut proj = 0.0;\n                for i in 0..n {\n                    proj += v[i] * ax[i];\n                }\n                for i in 0..n {\n                    ax[i] -= proj * v[i];\n                }\n            }\n            // normalize x ← ax / ‖ax‖\n            let mut nr = 0.0;\n            for i in 0..n {\n                nr += ax[i] * ax[i];\n            }\n            nr = crate::math::sqrt(nr);\n            if nr == 0.0 {\n                break;\n            }\n            for i in 0..n {\n                x[i] = ax[i] / nr;\n            }\n        }\n        // Rayleigh quotient on the deflated space: λ = xᵀ (A x) with A x\n        // orthogonalized to found pairs.
```
