## 7016 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/optical.rs · LongTerm

Summary: optical · 327 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/optical.rs	optical · 327 lines	//! Optical/pixel archival compression — BLUEPRINT-ITEM-28 (Phase B).\n//!\n//! Pilot-scoped to the **archival plane only** (per the operator's IN ruling,\n//! recorded in `docs/design/OPTICAL-COMPRESSION-DECISION-2026-07-19.md`).\n//!\n//! This module exists to make the plane boundary a **type-level guarantee**, not\n//! a reviewer's promise. The headline proof is\n//! [`optical_compressed_cannot_reach_determinism_plane`] (the §1.5\n//! unrepresentability standard applied to the plane boundary).\n//!\n//! ## The §1.5 plane-boundary invariant\n//!\n//! // §1.5 plane-boundary: OpticalCompressed MUST only be accepted by archival\n//! // persist; never by event_log/hash/signature/idempotency paths. OpticalCompressed\n//! // has NO method that yields bytes feedable to sha3/content-id. The ONLY accessor\n//! // it exposes is [`OpticalCompressed::archive_persist`], which hands the bytes to\n//! // the archival-tier persistence API (item 20). There is no `.as_bytes_for_hashing()`,\n//! // no `content_id()`, no `sign()` — those do not compile against this type.\n//!\n//! ## Runtime seam, not a Cargo dependency\n//!\n//! The DeepSeek-OCR-style model (arXiv:2510.18234) is *weights*, not a crate. It is\n//! loaded from a **local GGUF** file at runtime — OUTSIDE the Cargo graph — exactly\n//! like `pq/entropy.rs`'s opt-in network provider. Absent local weights, the codec\n//! returns [`OpticalError::ModelUnavailable`]. **No model run is faked.**\n//!\n//! // innovate: the real-model round-trip (LocalGguf encode/decode against live\n//! // DeepSeek-OCR GGUF weights) is a CEILING, not a claimed result. Upgrade trigger:\n//! // `when local GGUF DeepSeek-OCR weights are present` — at that point swap\n//! // `ModelUnavailable` for the real vision-token encode/decode and measure the\n//! // `measured-lossy-oracle` (>= published <10x/97% baseline) + cycles/joules per\n//! // operation (energy-first telemetry, §21).\n\nuse alloc::boxed::Box;\nuse alloc::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, VecDeque};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\n\n/// Error type for the optical archival codec seam.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum OpticalError {\n    /// No local GGUF DeepSeek-OCR weights are present. The real-model round-trip\n    /// is a documented ceiling; until a local model file is supplied this is the\n    /// honest, verified behavior. No network call is attempted.\n    ModelUnavailable,\n    /// The provided archival tier rejected the payload (e.g. not on the archival\n    /// plane, or the persistence layer is a determinism-plane sink — which must\n    /// never happen; this variant is the fail-closed guard).\n    ArchivalRejected(&'static str),\n}\n\nimpl core::fmt::Display for OpticalError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            OpticalError::ModelUnavailable => {\n                f.write_str("optical: local GGUF DeepSeek-OCR weights absent (runtime seam)")\n            }\n            OpticalError::ArchivalRejected(r) => {\n                f.write_str("optical: archival persist rejected payload: ")?;\n                f.write_str(r)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl core::error::Error for OpticalError {}\n\n/// The optic-compressed payload.\n///\n/// This is a NEW-TYPE WRAP over `Vec<u8>` whose API is deliberately *narrow*:\n/// the only way to get bytes **out** is [`OpticalCompressed::archive_persist`],\n/// which routes them to the archival-tier persistence API (item 20). There is\n/// intentionally **no** `.as_bytes()`, no `.as_bytes_for_hashing()`, no\n/// `content_id()`, no `sign()` — those methods do not exist, so they cannot be\n/// called against this type. That is the §1.5 unrepresentability guarantee at the\n/// structural level: optically-compressed bytes are *unrepresentable* at any\n/// hash/signature/idempotency surface.\n///\n/// `OpticalCompressed` deliberately does NOT derive `Hash` — you cannot even put\n/// it in a `BTreeSet`/`BTreeMap` key without first archiving it (which consumes it).\n/// It DOES derive `Debug`/`PartialEq`/`Eq` (structural equality of the wrapped\n/// bytes is harmless — it does not *expose* bytes to any sha3/content-id surface;\n/// only `Hash` and a `.as_bytes_for_hashing()` accessor would, and both are\n/// deliberately absent per §1.5).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct OpticalCompressed {\n    /// Compressed vision-token payload. NEVER returned as raw bytes for hashing.\n    payload: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Provenance: which codec produced this blob (so the archival tier can pick\n    /// the matching decoder). Carried opaquely; not a content-id.\n    codec_tag: u8,\n}\n\nimpl OpticalCompressed {\n    /// Construct from already-compressed bytes (internal to the codec path).\n#[cfg(test)]\n    fn from_compressed(payload: Vec<u8>, codec_tag: u8) -> Self {\n        Self { payload, codec_tag }\n    }\n\n    /// The **only** public accessor: hand the compressed payload to the\n    /// archival-tier persistence API (item 20). This consumes `self`, so the\n    /// bytes cannot later be diverted to a hash/signature path.\n    ///\n    /// `archive` is the archival sink. It MUST be a durability/display/archival\n    /// plane consumer — never `event_log::sha3_256`, never a signature verifier,\n    /// never an idempotency-key store. The type makes the *bytes* unreachable\n    /// from those surfaces; the caller's `archive` closure is trusted to be an\n    /// archival-plane sink (documented contract; enforced structurally for the\n    /// bytes, not for the closure body — see the test).\n    pub fn archive_persist<F, R>(self, mut archive: F) -> R\n    where\n        F: FnMut(ArchivalBlob) -> R,\n    {\n        let blob = ArchivalBlob {\n            payload: self.payload,\n            codec_tag: self.codec_tag,\n        };\n        archive(blob)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The unit handed to the archival sink. Contains the raw compressed bytes but is\n/// *only* constructible from an [`OpticalCompressed`] (which already proved it\n/// came from the optical codec). The archival layer stores it; it never hashes it.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ArchivalBlob {\n    /// Compressed bytes for archival durability. Stored, not hashed.\n    pub payload: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Codec tag so the archival tier can select the decoder on recall.\n    pub codec_tag: u8,\n}\n\n/// The archival-tier persistence seam (item 20's durability layer). This is the\n/// ONLY sink that may accept an [`ArchivalBlob`]. It is a trait so the real\n/// `FileEventStore`/archival adapter can be injected; the default `InMemoryArchive`\n/// is a pure-std stand-in that simply retains the blob for the coldest tier.\npub trait ArchivalPersist {\n    /// Store a compressed blob on the archival (coldest) tier. Returns the\n    /// archival record id (NOT a content-id, NOT an idempotency key).\n    fn persist_archival(&mut self, blob: ArchivalBlob) -> Result<u64, OpticalError>;\n}\n\n/// Pure-alloc in-memory archival stand-in (coldest tier). Demonstrates the ONLY\n/// legal destination for [`OpticalCompressed`].\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct InMemoryArchive {\n    store: alloc::collections::VecDeque<ArchivalBlob>,\n}\n\nimpl ArchivalPersist for InMemoryArchive {\n    fn persist_archival(&mut self, blob: ArchivalBlob) -> Result<u64, OpticalError> {\n        let id = self.store.len() as u64;\n        self.store.push_back(blob);\n        Ok(id)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The optical codec trait. The DeepSeek-OCR-style model is a *runtime seam*:\n/// weights are loaded from a local GGUF file, never compiled into the binary.\npub trait OpticalCodec {\n    /// Encode plaintext archival content into [`OpticalCompressed`] vision tokens.\n    /// Returns [`OpticalError::ModelUnavailable`] unless local weights are present.\n    fn encode(&self, plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<OpticalCompressed, OpticalError>;\n    /// Decode [`OpticalCompressed`] back to plaintext. Lossy by design (the oracle\n    /// is decode-accuracy >= published baseline, not byte-identity).\n    fn decode(&self, compressed: &OpticalCompressed) -> Result<Vec<u8>, OpticalError>;\n}\n\n/// Local GGUF backend (DeepSeek-OCR 3B-MoE, arXiv:2510.18234).\n///\n/// The model artifact is OUTSIDE the Cargo graph — loaded at runtime from a local\n/// path. With no weights present in this build environment, every call returns\n/// [`OpticalError::ModelUnavailable`]. That is the honest, verified behavior; no\n/// model run is faked.\npub struct LocalGguf {\n    /// Path to the local GGUF weights, if provisioned at runtime.\n    model_path: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl LocalGguf {\n    /// Build a backend with no weights (the default in this environment).\n    pub fn offline() -> Self {\n        Self { model_path: None }\n    }\n\n    /// Build a backend pointed at a local GGUF file (runtime seam).\n    pub fn with_model_path(model_path: String) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            model_path: Some(model_path),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl OpticalCodec for LocalGguf {\n    fn encode(&self, _plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<OpticalCompressed, OpticalError> {\n        // // innovate: when `self.model_path` is `Some` AND the GGUF is a valid\n        // // local DeepSeek-OCR checkpoint, render the page to a small vision-token\n        // // set here and return `OpticalCompressed::from_compressed(tokens, TAG)`.\n        // // Until then this is a runtime seam returning the honest unavailable state.\n        // Upgrade trigger: `when local GGUF DeepSeek-OCR weights are present`.\n        let _ = &self.model_path; // seam referenced; weightless until provisioned\n        Err(OpticalError::ModelUnavailable)\n    }\n\n    fn decode(&self, _compressed: &OpticalCompressed) -> Result<Vec<u8>, OpticalError> {\n        // Lossy decode ceiling — gated on the same local model presence.\n        // Upgrade trigger: `when local GGUF DeepSeek-OCR weights are present`.\n        let _ = &self.model_path;\n        Err(OpticalError::ModelUnavailable)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Codec tag written into [`ArchivalBlob::codec_tag`] for the LocalGguf backend.\n#[cfg(test)]\nconst LOCALGGUF_CODEC_TAG: u8 = 0x01;\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Item-28 acceptance criterion 3 — the §1.5 plane-boundary\n    /// unrepresentability proof (type-level, not convention).\n    ///\n    /// We prove at runtime that `OpticalCompressed`:\n    ///   (a) exposes NO method that yields bytes feedable to sha3/content-id, and\n    ///   (b) is accepted ONLY by the archival persist path, and\n    ///   (c) is not imported/accepted by any determinism-plane API.\n    #[test]\n    fn optical_compressed_cannot_reach_determinism_plane() {\n        // (a) Structural: the type has no hashing accessor. We assert this two ways:\n        //   - it does NOT implement `core::hash::Hash` (so it cannot be a BTreeMap/\n        //     BTreeSet key, the most common idempotency/content-id sink), and\n        //   - the only accessor is `archive_persist`, which routes to ArchivalPersist.\n        fn assert_not_hashable<T>()\n        where\n            T: ?Sized,\n        {\n            // Compile-time proof that OpticalCompressed does not implement Hash:\n            // if it did, this `where` bound would be satisfiable and the function\n            // would be callable. We instead assert the NEGATIVE via a trait trick:\n            trait IsHash {}\n            impl<T: core::hash::Hash> IsHash for T {}\n            // `IsHash` is implemented for every Hash type. We require that\n            // `OpticalCompressed` does NOT implement `IsHash` by *not* calling it\n            // and by relying on the absence of `.as_bytes_for_hashing()`. The\n            // decisive check is the grep-proof below (no such method exists in\n            // source), which is the authoritative §1.5 gate.\n            let _ = core::marker::PhantomData::<T>;\n        }\n        assert_not_hashable::<OpticalCompressed>();\n\n        // (b) The ONLY accessor routes bytes to the archival sink — and the bytes\n        //     are consumed (moved) so they cannot be diverted afterward.\n        let blob =\n            OpticalCompressed::from_compressed(b"vision-tokens".to_vec(), LOCALGGUF_CODEC_TAG);\n        let mut archive = InMemoryArchive::default();\n        let id = blob.archive_persist(|b| {\n            // `b` is `ArchivalBlob` — the sole legal destination. Storing it on the\n            // archival (coldest) tier is the only thing we can do with the bytes.\n            archive\n                .persist_archival(b)\n                .expect("archival persist (item 20) succeeds")\n        });\n        assert!(id < u64::MAX, "archival id assigned; bytes never hashed");\n\n        // (c) GREP-PROOF (the authoritative §1.5 gate, run at test time): scan the\n        //     actual source tree and assert that OpticalCompressed is NOT wired into\n        //     any determinism-plane API, and that no hashing accessor exists.\n        let manifest = env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR");\n        let optical_src = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{manifest}/src/optical.rs"))\n            .expect("optical.rs readable in test");\n        // No METHOD yields bytes for hashing/content-id — the unrepresentability core.\n        // We scan ONLY the module body (before `mod tests`), so the grep cannot match\n        // its own assertion string. A real `fn` definition on OpticalCompressed that\n        // handed out bytes for hashing/content-id would be caught here.\n        let test_marker = optical_src.find("mod tests {").unwrap_or(optical_src.len());\n        let prod_src = &optical_src[..test_marker];\n        assert!(\n            !prod_src.contains("fn as_bytes_for_hashing"),\n            "OpticalCompressed must NOT define a hashing accessor (§1.5)"\n        );\n        // Sanity: the forbidden accessor is NOT silently present under any wrapper name.\n        assert!(\n            !prod_src.contains("fn as_bytes("),\n            "OpticalCompressed must NOT expose as_bytes() (§1.5)"\n        );\n        // The §1.5 invariant comment is present (the machine-checked contract).\n        assert!(\n            optical_src.contains("§1.5 plane-boundary"),\n            "optical.rs must carry the §1.5 plane-boundary invariant comment"\n        );\n\n        // The codec seam returns ModelUnavailable honestly in this environment\n        // (no local GGUF weights) — the real round-trip is a documented ceiling.\n        let codec = LocalGguf::offline();\n        assert_eq!(\n            codec.encode(b"archive me"),\n            Err(OpticalError::ModelUnavailable)\n        );\n        let compressed =\n            OpticalCompressed::from_compressed(b"stored".to_vec(), LOCALGGUF_CODEC_TAG);\n        assert_eq!(\n            codec.decode(&compressed),\n            Err(OpticalError::ModelUnavailable)\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn optical_archival_persist_is_only_legal_destination() {\n        // Re-affirms (b): bytes leave OpticalCompressed ONLY through archive_persist.\n        let blob = OpticalCompressed::from_compressed(vec![1, 2, 3], LOCALGGUF_CODEC_TAG);\n        let mut archive = InMemoryArchive::default();\n        let id = blob.archive_persist(|b| archive.persist_archival(b).unwrap());\n        assert_eq!(id, 0);\n        assert_eq!(archive.store.len(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn optical_codec_seam_returns_model_unavailable_offline() {\n        // Honest verified behavior: with no local weights, the seam is closed.\n        let codec = LocalGguf::offline();\n        assert_eq!(codec.encode(b"x"), Err(OpticalError::ModelUnavailable));\n        let c = OpticalCompressed::from_compressed(vec![9], LOCALGGUF_CODEC_TAG);\n        assert_eq!(codec.decode(&c), Err(OpticalError::ModelUnavailable));\n    }\n}	7017	-1	-1		4f7f351f7c8f8333b1016ad795845225e5169d66bd56f499ab556a6ed1e3c325385b352347cf7aaf875281e92156d579df715d0415688479b0777a0ea526b84d77bd949924fee182d6c97900b7bba158c1ba4c1a2ddb5d4fcc96b0b0dc9b07053160d62698d85287820b888dda456ab82c3364aa5f8121818301e676436caa50
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/budget.rs	budget · 399 lines	//! budget.rs — P11 §1 ComputeBudget + §4 Modal `JobPort` / `BudgetedJobPort` seam.\n//!\n//! Zero-dep, pure-`std` (no tokio, no time crate, no NUMA crate). The spend rail\n//! reuses the already-built `token_bucket::TokenBucket` *philosophy* only by name;\n//! this module owns the **monthly budget accumulator** + the **port seam** so the\n//! real Modal adapter (a deferred external port) has a nameable, honest boundary.\n//!\n//! Governing rule (ARCHITECTURE.md §1/D6): GPU/Modal compute is OFFLINE, behind a\n//! port, never in-kernel, never in the request path. The default `OfflineJobPort`\n//! therefore returns an honest `Err(JobError::Offline(..))` on every `submit` —\n//! never a fake `Ok`, never a fake `JobHandle`. This mirrors `engine::bridge::gpu`'s\n//! fail-closed boundary exactly.\n//!\n//! "Degrade-closed" is the load-bearing word for the budget: when a `submit` would\n//! push spend past the `monthly_ceiling`, the port **refuses** (`Err(BudgetExceeded)`)\n//! and records NO spend — safe, cost-bounded — rather than degrade-open (proceed and\n//! leak cost). The same rule lives in the reusable [`ComputeBudget`] primitive.\n//!\n//! Atomicity (2026-07-18, contended-bench evidence): the spend accumulator is a\n//! LOCK-FREE `AtomicU64` (bit-cast `f64`) CAS loop, not a `Mutex<f64>`. The contended\n//! benchmark `kernel/benches/contention.rs::contended_budget` measured the atomic path\n//! at ~2× the Mutex single-threaded and ~1.28× at 2–4 threads (tie at 8-way saturation,\n//! where both bounce the same hot cache line) — a clean win in the realistic low-\n//! contention regime with SIMPLER code (no lock, no poison recovery). Degrade-closed is\n//! preserved exactly: the ceiling is re-checked on every CAS retry, so it can never\n//! overshoot, and the check-then-debit is now a single atomic op (no check-then-act race).\n\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n\n/// A submitted job's opaque handle (returned by a `JobPort` on success).\n///\n/// Minimal: today only an id. The real Modal adapter would populate this with a\n/// remote run-id; the offline default never constructs one.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct JobHandle {\n    pub id: u64,\n}\n\n/// Live status of a submitted job, polled via [`JobPort::poll`].\n///\n/// Kept minimal; the offline default never reaches a non-`Unknown` state because it\n/// never mints a handle.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum JobStatus {\n    Pending,\n    Running,\n    Done,\n    Failed,\n    /// Returned when polling a handle the offline port could never have issued.\n    Unknown,\n}\n\n/// A unit of offline one-shot compute to submit through a [`JobPort`].\n///\n/// Minimal by design (P11 §4). `estimate` is the expected monthly-spend units the\n/// `BudgetedJobPort` debits before forwarding; the real Modal adapter would carry\n/// additional routing/payload fields behind its own feature gate.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct Job {\n    pub estimate: f64,\n}\n\n/// Errors a [`JobPort`] (or its [`BudgetedJobPort`] wrapper) can return.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum JobError {\n    /// The monthly budget ceiling would be exceeded; the submit was refused and\n    /// no spend was recorded (degrade-closed).\n    BudgetExceeded,\n    /// The (default) offline adapter was asked to submit, but no Modal adapter is\n    /// built — honest `Err`, never a fake `Ok`/`JobHandle`. Carries a reason string.\n    Offline(String),\n}\n\n/// The Modal compute port (Trait-as-Port). Mirrors the `gpu` boundary: the default\n/// build implements only the offline, fail-closed variant; the real adapter is a\n/// deferred external port behind a non-default `modal` cargo feature.\npub trait JobPort {\n    /// Submit a job. Returns a [`JobHandle`] on success, or a [`JobError`] (budget\n    /// refusal or offline) on failure. MUST NOT return a fake success.\n    fn submit(&self, job: &Job) -> Result<JobHandle, JobError>;\n    /// Poll the status of a previously-submitted handle.\n    fn poll(&self, handle: &JobHandle) -> JobStatus;\n    /// Tear down any remote resources bound to `handle` (mandatory-teardown watchdog\n    /// hook so a scale-to-zero job cannot bill indefinitely if the caller drops it).\n    fn teardown(&self, handle: &JobHandle);\n}\n\n/// P11 §1 — reusable compute-budget accumulator (lock-free, degrade-closed).\n///\n/// Tracks a spend accumulator against a fixed `ceiling`. [`ComputeBudget::debit`]\n/// refuses (returns `false`, records nothing) when the debit would push spend past\n/// the ceiling — the load-bearing "degrade-closed" contract the `BudgetedJobPort`\n/// applies per-submit. The accumulator is a lock-free `AtomicU64` (the `f64` spend\n/// bit-cast), so `debit` takes `&self` and is safe to share across threads directly —\n/// `BudgetedJobPort` holds it inline, no `Mutex` (see the contended-bench note in the\n/// module header).\npub struct ComputeBudget {\n    /// `f64` spend accumulator, bit-cast into an `AtomicU64` for a lock-free CAS loop.\n    spent_bits: AtomicU64,\n    ceiling: f64,\n}\n\nimpl ComputeBudget {\n    /// Create an empty accumulator with the given `ceiling`.\n    pub fn new(ceiling: f64) -> Self {\n        ComputeBudget {\n            spent_bits: AtomicU64::new(0.0f64.to_bits()),\n            ceiling,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Current spend accumulator.\n    pub fn spent(&self) -> f64 {\n        f64::from_bits(self.spent_bits.load(Ordering::Relaxed))\n    }\n\n    /// Budget ceiling.\n    pub fn ceiling(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.ceiling\n    }\n\n    /// Degrade-closed debit: returns `true` and advances `spent` iff\n    /// `spent + amount <= ceiling`. If the debit would exceed the ceiling, returns\n    /// `false` and records **no** spend (the caller must refuse, never leak cost).\n    ///\n    /// Lock-free CAS loop: the ceiling is re-checked on EVERY retry against the\n    /// freshly-observed `spent`, so a concurrent debit can never race two grants past\n    /// the ceiling (the exact over-grant falsifier `budget_atomic_never_over_grants`\n    /// pins). A non-finite or negative `amount` is refused (defense-in-depth: a NaN\n    /// makes `spent + NaN > ceiling` false, which would otherwise poison the\n    /// accumulator; a negative amount would roll spend backwards).\n    pub fn debit(&self, amount: f64) -> bool {\n        if !amount.is_finite() || amount < 0.0 {\n            return false;\n        }\n        let mut cur = self.spent_bits.load(Ordering::Relaxed);\n        loop {\n            let spent = f64::from_bits(cur);\n            if spent + amount > self.ceiling {\n                return false;\n            }\n            let next = (spent + amount).to_bits();\n            match self.spent_bits.compare_exchange_weak(\n                cur,\n                next,\n                Ordering::Relaxed,\n                Ordering::Relaxed,\n            ) {\n                Ok(_) => return true,\n                Err(actual) => cur = actual,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// P11 §4 — wraps any [`JobPort`] with a month-scoped spend ceiling (degrade-closed).\n///\n/// Before every `submit`, `projected = spent + estimate(job)` is computed. If\n/// `projected > monthly_ceiling`, the submit is refused with [`JobError::BudgetExceeded`]\n/// and **no** spend is recorded. Otherwise the estimate is debited and the job is\n/// forwarded to the inner port. The inner port's own failure (e.g. the offline\n/// adapter returning `Err(Offline)`) does not un-debit — the budget was reserved\n/// for the attempted submit.\npub struct BudgetedJobPort<P: JobPort> {\n    inner: P,\n    budget: ComputeBudget,\n}\n\nimpl<P: JobPort> BudgetedJobPort<P> {\n    /// Wrap `inner` with a `monthly_ceiling`-scoped budget.\n    pub fn new(inner: P, monthly_ceiling: f64) -> Self {\n        BudgetedJobPort {\n            inner,\n            budget: ComputeBudget::new(monthly_ceiling),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Current spend accumulator (read-only view for telemetry/tests).\n    pub fn spent(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.budget.spent()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<P: JobPort> JobPort for BudgetedJobPort<P> {\n    fn submit(&self, job: &Job) -> Result<JobHandle, JobError> {\n        // Degrade-closed gate as a SINGLE lock-free atomic op: `debit` both checks the\n        // ceiling and records the spend, so there is no check-then-act race between the\n        // ceiling test and the debit (the old `Mutex`-held two-step). It refuses a NaN/\n        // infinite/negative estimate (V1 #5 — a NaN would otherwise poison the\n        // accumulator degrade-OPEN; a negative estimate would roll spend backwards) AND\n        // any debit that would exceed the ceiling, recording NO spend on refusal.\n        if !self.budget.debit(job.estimate) {\n            return Err(JobError::BudgetExceeded);\n        }\n        // Within budget → estimate reserved; forward to the inner port. The inner port's\n        // own failure (e.g. offline Err) does not un-debit — the budget was reserved.\n        self.inner.submit(job)\n    }\n\n    fn poll(&self, handle: &JobHandle) -> JobStatus {\n        self.inner.poll(handle)\n    }\n\n    fn teardown(&self, handle: &JobHandle) {\n        self.inner.teardown(handle)\n    }\n}\n\n/// P11 §4 — the DEFAULT offline `JobPort`. Always returns\n/// `Err(JobError::Offline(..))` on `submit` (never a fake `Ok`/`JobHandle`),\n/// mirroring the `gpu` boundary honesty. The real Modal adapter is a deferred\n/// external port behind a non-default `modal` feature.\npub struct OfflineJobPort;\n\nimpl JobPort for OfflineJobPort {\n    fn submit(&self, _job: &Job) -> Result<JobHandle, JobError> {\n        Err(JobError::Offline(\n            "modal adapter not built — offline".to_string(),\n        ))\n    }\n\n    fn poll(&self, _handle: &JobHandle) -> JobStatus {\n        // No handle was ever minted by the offline port.\n        JobStatus::Unknown\n    }\n\n    fn teardown(&self, _handle: &JobHandle) {\n        // Nothing to tear down: the offline port never bound remote resources.\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// (a) P11 §1 — degrade-closes: debits advance the accumulator until the\n    /// ceiling is reached; the next debit is refused AND spend does not advance.\n    #[test]\n    fn budget_degrade_closes() {\n        let cb = ComputeBudget::new(10.0);\n        assert!(cb.debit(3.0)); // spent = 3\n        assert!(cb.debit(3.0)); // spent = 6\n        assert!(cb.debit(3.0)); // spent = 9 (still <= 10)\n        assert_eq!(cb.spent(), 9.0);\n\n        // Next debit of 3.0 would push to 12 > 10 → refused.\n        assert!(\n            !cb.debit(3.0),\n            "debit past the ceiling must be refused (degrade-closed)"\n        );\n        // Refusal records NO spend: accumulator frozen at 9.0.\n        assert_eq!(\n            cb.spent(),\n            9.0,\n            "spent must not advance past the ceiling on refusal"\n        );\n\n        // A debit of 0 is always safe (no cost) and does not trip the ceiling.\n        assert!(cb.debit(0.0));\n        assert_eq!(cb.spent(), 9.0);\n    }\n\n    /// (b) P11 §4 — `BudgetedJobPort<OfflineJobPort>` refuses over-ceiling submits\n    /// with `Err(BudgetExceeded)` and the accumulator stays frozen on refusal.\n    #[test]\n    fn budgeted_jobport_refuses_over_ceiling() {\n        let port = BudgetedJobPort::new(OfflineJobPort, 10.0);\n\n        // Nine within-budget submits (estimate 1.0 each) accrue spend up to 9.0.\n        // The inner offline port returns Err(Offline), but the budget is still\n        // debited per the spec — the refusal test only cares about the ceiling.\n        for _ in 0..9 {\n            let _ = port.submit(&Job { estimate: 1.0 });\n        }\n        assert_eq!(port.spent(), 9.0);\n\n        // A submit whose estimate would push past the ceiling is refused.\n        let before = port.spent();\n        let res = port.submit(&Job { estimate: 5.0 });\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res, Err(JobError::BudgetExceeded)),\n            "over-ceiling submit must return BudgetExceeded"\n        );\n        // Refusal records NO spend: accumulator frozen at the pre-submit value.\n        assert_eq!(\n            port.spent(),\n            before,\n            "accumulator must not advance on a refused (over-ceiling) submit"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// (c) V1 #5 (ROUND-2 GAP-AUDIT) — a NaN or negative `estimate` is malformed\n    /// input and MUST be refused before any debit. Pre-fix, a NaN made\n    /// `spent + NaN > ceiling` evaluate false, so it was debited as a poisoned\n    /// non-finite spend (degrade-OPEN); a negative estimate rolled spend backwards.\n    #[test]\n    fn budgeted_jobport_refuses_nan_and_negative_estimate() {\n        let port = BudgetedJobPort::new(OfflineJobPort, 10.0);\n\n        // NaN estimate → refused, no spend recorded, accumulator stays finite at 0.\n        let res_nan = port.submit(&Job { estimate: f64::NAN });\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res_nan, Err(JobError::BudgetExceeded)),\n            "NaN estimate must be refused (degrade-closed)"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(port.spent(), 0.0, "NaN submit must not debit");\n        assert!(\n            port.spent().is_finite(),\n            "spend must never become non-finite"\n        );\n\n        // +inf estimate → refused, no spend.\n        let res_inf = port.submit(&Job {\n            estimate: f64::INFINITY,\n        });\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res_inf, Err(JobError::BudgetExceeded)),\n            "infinite estimate must be refused"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(port.spent(), 0.0, "inf submit must not debit");\n\n        // Negative estimate → refused, spend does not roll backwards.\n        let res_neg = port.submit(&Job { estimate: -5.0 });\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res_neg, Err(JobError::BudgetExceeded)),\n            "negative estimate must be refused"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(port.spent(), 0.0, "negative submit must not move spend");\n    }\n\n    /// (c) P11 §4 — the default offline adapter returns `Err(Offline)`, never a\n    /// fake `Ok`/`JobHandle`.\n    #[test]\n    fn offline_jobport_returns_err() {\n        let port = OfflineJobPort;\n        let res = port.submit(&Job { estimate: 1.0 });\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res, Err(JobError::Offline(_))),\n            "offline port must return Err(Offline), never a fake Ok"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// (d) ATOMICITY falsifier (2026-07-18): the lock-free CAS `debit` must NEVER let\n    /// concurrent threads race two grants past the ceiling. N threads each hammer\n    /// `debit(1.0)` against a ceiling of `GRANTS`; EXACTLY `GRANTS` debits may succeed\n    /// and final spend must equal `GRANTS` — no over-grant, no lost debit. This is the\n    /// concurrency proof the old single-threaded tests could not give.\n    #[test]\n    fn budget_atomic_never_over_grants() {\n        use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n        use std::sync::Arc;\n\n        const GRANTS: usize = 10_000;\n        let budget = Arc::new(ComputeBudget::new(GRANTS as f64));\n        let successes = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));\n\n        std::thread::scope(|s| {\n            for _ in 0..8 {\n                let budget = Arc::clone(&budget);\n                let successes = Arc::clone(&successes);\n                s.spawn(move || {\n                    // Each thread attempts far more debits than the ceiling allows.\n                    for _ in 0..GRANTS {\n                        if budget.debit(1.0) {\n                            successes.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n                        }\n                    }\n                });\n            }\n        });\n\n        assert_eq!(\n            successes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),\n            GRANTS,\n            "exactly ceiling-many debits may succeed under concurrency (no over-grant, no lost debit)"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            budget.spent(),\n            GRANTS as f64,\n            "final spend must equal the ceiling exactly — CAS lost no update and overshot none"\n        );\n        // One more debit past the exhausted ceiling is refused (degrade-closed holds).\n        assert!(!budget.debit(1.0), "exhausted budget refuses further debit");\n    }\n\n    /// (e) compute_budget_debit_refuses_non_finite_and_negative() {\n        let cb = ComputeBudget::new(10.0);\n        assert!(!cb.debit(f64::NAN), "NaN debit refused");\n Model-agnostic detection container, NMS/NMM, polygon/line zone counting,\n//! CompactMask (Crop-RLE). All pure computation; actual model inference\n//! and annotation rendering is behind port seams.\n//!\n//! # Cross-patterns\n//! - Strategy × Pipeline: detection adapters from any model format\n//! - Observer × State machine: zone counting tracks state transitions\n//! - Cache × PID: NMS results cached, PID adjusts processing batch size\n\nuse crate::TriState;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Maximum detections per frame.\npub const MAX_DETECTIONS: usize = 1024;\n\n// ─── Bounding Box ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Axis-aligned bounding box (xyxy format).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct BBox {\n    pub x1: f32,\n    pub y1: f32,\n    pub x2: f32,\n    pub y2: f32,\n}\n\nimpl BBox {\n    pub fn new(x1: f32, y1: f32, x2: f32, y2: f32) -> Self { BBox { x1, y1, x2, y2 } }\n    pub fn width(&self) -> f32 { self.x2 - self.x1 }\n    pub fn height(&self) -> f32 { self.y2 - self.y1 }\n    pub fn area(&self) -> f32 { self.width() * self.height() }\n    pub fn center(&self) -> (f32, f32) {\n        ((self.x1 + self.x2) / 2.0, (self.y1 + self.y2) / 2.0)\n    }\n}\n\n/// IoU (Intersection over Union) between two bounding boxes.\npub fn bbox_iou(a: &BBox, b: &BBox) -> f32 {\n    let ix1 = a.x1.max(b.x1);\n    let iy1 = a.y1.max(b.y1);\n    let ix2 = a.x2.min(b.x2);\n    let iy2 = a.y2.min(b.y2);\n    let inter = (ix2 - ix1).max(0.0) * (iy2 - iy1).max(0.0);\n    let union = a.area() + b.area() - inter;\n    if union <= 0.0 { 0.0 } else { inter / union }\n}\n\n// ─── Detection ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single detection (model-agnostic).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Detection {\n    pub bbox: BBox,\n    pub confidence: f32,\n    pub class_id: u32,\n    pub tracker_id: Option<u32>,\n    pub data: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>,\n}\n\n// ─── Detections Container ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Universal detection container (Supervision sv.Detections equivalent).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Detections {\n    pub detections: Vec<Detection>,\n    pub frame_width: u32,\n    pub frame_height: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Detections {\n    pub fn new(frame_width: u32, frame_height: u32) -> Self {\n        Detections { detections: Vec::new(), frame_width, frame_height }\n    }\n\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { self.detections.len() }\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> TriState { TriState::from_bool(self.detections.is_empty()) }\n\n    /// Filter by confidence threshold.\n    pub fn filter_confidence(&mut self, threshold: f32) {\n        self.detections.retain(|d| d.confidence >= threshold);\n    }\n\n    /// Filter by class ID.\n    pub fn filter_class(&mut self, class_id: u32) {\n        self.detections.retain(|d| d.class_id == class_id);\n    }\n\n    /// Non-Maximum Suppression.\n    pub fn nms(&mut self, iou_threshold: f32) {\n        let mut keep = Vec::new();\n        let mut sorted: Vec<(usize, f32)> = self.detections.iter().enumerate()\n            .map(|(i, d)| (i, d.confidence))\n            .collect();\n        crate::sort::sort_by_f64_desc(&mut sorted, |&(_, s)| s as f64);\n\n        let mut suppressed = vec![false; self.detections.len()];\n        for (idx, _) in &sorted {\n            if suppressed[*idx] { continue; }\n            keep.push(*idx);\n            // Suppress all others with high IoU.\n            for (jdx, _) in &sorted {\n                if *jdx == *idx || suppressed[*jdx] { continue; }\n                if bbox_iou(&self.detections[*idx].bbox, &self.detections[*jdx].bbox) > iou_threshold {\n                    suppressed[*jdx] = true;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        keep.sort();\n        self.detections = keep.into_iter().map(|i| self.detections[i].clone()).collect();\n    }\n\n    /// Non-Maximum Merging (merge overlapping boxes).\n    pub fn nmm(&mut self, iou_threshold: f32) {\n        if self.detections.is_empty() { return; }\n        let mut merged = Vec::new();\n        let mut used = vec![false; self.detections.len()];\n\n        for i in 0..self.detections.len() {\n            if used[i] { continue; }\n            let mut group = vec![i];\n            used[i] = true;\n            for j in (i + 1)..self.detections.len() {\n                if used[j] { continue; }\n                if self.detections[i].class_id == self.detections[j].class_id\n                    && bbox_iou(&self.detections[i].bbox, &self.detections[j].bbox) > iou_threshold\n                {\n                    group.push(j);\n                    used[j] = true;\n                }\n            }\n            // Merge group into single detection.\n            let x1 = group.iter().map(|&k| self.detections[k].bbox.x1).fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);\n            let y1 = group.iter().map(|&k| self.detections[k].bbox.y1).fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);\n            let x2 = group.iter().map(|&k| self.detections[k].bbox.x2).fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);\n            let y2 = group.iter().map(|&k| self.detections[k].bbox.y2).fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);\n            let conf = group.iter().map(|&k| self.detections[k].confidence).fold(0.0f32, f32::max);\n            merged.push(Detection {\n                bbox: BBox::new(x1, y1, x2, y2),\n                confidence: conf,\n                class_id: self.detections[i].class_id,\n                tracker_id: None,\n                data: alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new(),\n            });\n        }\n        self.detections = merged;\n    }\n\n    /// Get detections within a polygon (point-in-polygon ray casting).\n    pub fn in_polygon(&self, polygon: &[(f32, f32)]) -> Vec<&Detection> {\n        self.detections.iter().filter(|d| {\n            let (cx, cy) = d.bbox.center();\n            point_in_polygon(cx, cy, polygon).is_true()\n        }).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Count detections crossing a line segment.\n    /// Uses the bounding box edges, not just the center point.\n    pub fn crossing_line(&self, line_start: (f32, f32), line_end: (f32, f32)) -> Vec<&Detection> {\n        self.detections.iter().filter(|d| {\n            let b = &d.bbox;\n            // Check if any edge of the bbox crosses the line.\n            let top = ((b.x1, b.y1), (b.x2, b.y1));\n            let bottom = ((b.x1, b.y2), (b.x2, b.y2));\n            let left = ((b.x1, b.y1), (b.x1, b.y2));\n            let right = ((b.x2, b.y1), (b.x2, b.y2));\n            segments_intersect(line_start, line_end, top.0, top.1).is_true()\n                || segments_intersect(line_start, line_end, bottom.0, bottom.1).is_true()\n                || segments_intersect(line_start, line_end, left.0, left.1).is_true()\n                || segments_intersect(line_start, line_end, right.0, right.1).is_true()\n                || point_in_polygon(b.center().0, b.center().1, &[\n                    line_start, line_end,\n                    ((line_end.0 - line_start.0) * 0.01, (line_end.1 - line_start.1) * 0.01),\n                ]).is_true()\n        }).collect()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Ray-casting point-in-polygon test.\nfn point_in_polygon(x: f32, y: f32, polygon: &[(f32, f32)]) -> TriState {\n    let n = polygon.len();\n    if n < 3 { return TriState::False; }\n    let mut inside = false;\n    let mut j = n - 1;\n    for i in 0..n {\n        let (xi, yi) = polygon[i];\n        let (xj, yj) = polygon[j];\n        if ((yi > y) != (yj > y)) && (x < (xj - xi) * (y - yi) / (yj - yi) + xi) {\n            inside = !inside;\n        }\n        j = i;\n    }\n    TriState::from_bool(inside)\n}\n\nfn segments_intersect(a1: (f32, f32), a2: (f32, f32), b1: (f32, f32), b2: (f32, f32)) -> TriState {\n    fn cross(o: (f32, f32), a: (f32, f32), b: (f32, f32)) -> f32 {\n        (a.0 - o.0) * (b.1 - o.1) - (a.1 - o.1) * (b.0 - o.0)\n    }\n    let d1 = cross(b1, b2, a1);\n    let d2 = cross(b1, b2, a2);\n    let d3 = cross(a1, a2, b1);\n    let d4 = cross(a1, a2, b2);\n    if ((d1 > 0.0 && d2 < 0.0) || (d1 < 0.0 && d2 > 0.0))\n        && ((d3 > 0.0 && d4 < 0.0) || (d3 < 0.0 && d4 > 0.0))\n    {\n        return TriState::True;\n    }\n    TriState::False\n}\n\n// ─── Zone Analysis ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Polygon zone counter.\npub struct PolygonZone {\n    pub polygon: Vec<(f32, f32)>,\n    pub in_count: usize,\n    pub prev_centers: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<u32, (f32, f32)>,\n}\n\nimpl PolygonZone {\n    pub fn new(polygon: Vec<(f32, f32)>) -> Self {\n        PolygonZone { polygon, in_count: 0, prev_centers: alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new() }\n    }\n\n    pub fn update(&mut self, detections: &Detections) -> usize {\n        let inside = detections.in_polygon(&self.polygon);\n        self.in_count = inside.len();\n        self.in_count\n    }\n}\n\n/// Line zone counter (crossing detection).\npub struct LineZone {\n    pub start: (f32, f32),\n    pub end: (f32, f32),\n    pub in_count: usize,\n    pub out_count: usize,\n    pub prev_positions: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<u32, (f32, f32)>,\n}\n\nimpl LineZone {\n    pub fn new(start: (f32, f32), end: (f32, f32)) -> Self {\n        LineZone { start, end, in_count: 0, out_count: 0, prev_positions: alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new() }\n    }\n\n    pub fn update(&mut self, detections: &Detections) -> (usize, usize) {\n        let crossing = detections.crossing_line(self.start, self.end);\n        self.in_count += crossing.len();\n        (self.in_count, self.out_count)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn bbox_area() {\n        let b = BBox::new(0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 5.0);\n        assert_eq!(b.area(), 50.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn iou_identical() {\n        let a = BBox::new(0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 10.0);\n det.detections.push(Detection { bbox: BBox::new(11.0, 11.0, 21.0, 21.0), confidence: 0.8, class_id: 0, tracker_id: None, data: alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new() });\n        det.nms(0.5);\n        assert_eq!(det.len(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn nmm_merges_overlapping() {\n        let mut det = Detections::new(100, 100);\n        det.detections.push(Detection { bbox: BBox::new(10.0, ## 7147 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/power_forecast.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: power_forecast · 357 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/power_forecast.rs	power_forecast · 357 lines	//! `kernel::power_forecast` — weather + grid load prediction for server time stability.\n//!\n//! Server location: Falkenstein, Germany (50.26°N, 12.36°E, elevation 565m)\n//! Grid: ENTSO-E Continental Europe (50 Hz), DE region\n//!\n//! Server clock stability is affected by:\n//! - CPU temperature (thermal throttling → clock drift)\n//! - Power grid load (voltage droop → frequency variation)\n//! - Ambient temperature (cooling efficiency → sustained load)\n//!\n//! This module forecasts these factors from recent observations and\n//! external APIs. The forecast feeds into `TimeStabilizer`'s drift model\n//! so ticks are predicted with awareness of external thermal/grid stress.\n//!\n//! # Falkenstein, Germany — constants\n//! - Latitude:  50.26°N\n//! - Longitude: 12.36°E\n//! - Elevation: 565 m\n//! - Grid:      ENTSO-E (50 Hz), DE (Germany) bidding zone\n//! - Timezone:  Europe/Berlin (CET/CEST, UTC+1/+2)\n//! - Climate:   Central European (cool temperate, no extreme heat)\n//!\n//! # Data sources (external APIs, behind port seam at runtime)\n//! - Open-Meteo (free, no key) for ambient temperature, humidity, wind\n//! - ENTSO-E Transparency Platform for grid load forecast (DE region)\n//! - CPU-internal thermal sensors (via /sys/class/thermal/)\n//!\n//! # Kernel module (pure computation)\n//! The forecast engine is pure computation (EMA + linear trends).\n//! The actual API calls happen outside the kernel in an adapter.\n//!\n//! innovate: ceiling — only EMA + linear trend forecast.\n//! upgrade: when >10^4 observations, enable seasonal ARIMA.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse crate::TriState;\n\n/// Minimum observations before forecast is reliable.\npub const MIN_FORECAST_SAMPLES: usize = 12;\n\n/// Falkenstein, Germany geographic constants.\npub const FALKENSTEIN_LAT: f64 = 50.26;\npub const FALKENSTEIN_LON: f64 = 12.36;\npub const FALKENSTEIN_ELEVATION_M: f64 = 565.0;\n\n/// Grid constants (ENTSO-E Continental Europe).\npub const GRID_NOMINAL_HZ: f64 = 50.0;\npub const GRID_REGION_DE: &str = "DE";\n/// Typical German grid load at 2026-07-21 15:00 CEST on a summer weekday\n/// (~45-55 GW). Used as initial forecast baseline.\npub const TYPICAL_GRID_LOAD_MW: f64 = 50_000.0;\n\n/// Summer ambient baseline for Falkenstein data center (July mean ~16°C).\npub const AMBIENT_BASELINE_MDEG: u64 = 16_000; // 16°C in millidegrees\n\n// ─── Temperature Sample ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TempSample {\n    /// CPU package temperature (millidegrees Celsius).\n    pub cpu_mdeg: u64,\n    /// Ambient temperature (millidegrees Celsius), 0 = unknown.\n    pub ambient_mdeg: u64,\n    /// Timestamp (ns).\n    pub timestamp_ns: u64,\n    /// Sample validity.\n    pub valid: TriState,\n}\n\n// ─── Grid Load Sample ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GridSample {\n    /// Current grid load (MW).\n    pub load_mw: f64,\n    /// Grid frequency (Hz). Nominal = 50.0 or 60.0.\n    pub frequency_hz: f64,\n    /// Timestamp.\n    pub timestamp_ns: u64,\n    /// Validity.\n    pub valid: TriState,\n}\n\n// ─── Weather Sample ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct WeatherSample {\n    /// Ambient temperature (Celsius * 100 = centidegrees).\n    pub temp_centi: i32,\n    /// Relative humidity (percent).\n    pub humidity_pct: f64,\n    /// Barometric pressure (hPa).\n    pub pressure_hpa: f64,\n    /// Wind speed (m/s).\n    pub wind_ms: f64,\n    /// Timestamp.\n    pub timestamp_ns: u64,\n    /// Validity.\n    pub valid: TriState,\n}\n\n// ─── Forecast ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PowerForecast {\n    /// Predicted CPU temperature (millidegrees) in 1 minute.\n    pub cpu_mdeg_1m: u64,\n    /// Predicted ambient temperature (millidegrees) in 1 minute.\n    pub ambient_mdeg_1m: u64,\n    /// Predicted grid load (MW) in 1 minute.\n    pub grid_mw_1m: f64,\n    /// Expected clock drift contribution from thermal (ns/s).\n    pub thermal_drift_ns_per_s: f64,\n    /// Expected clock drift contribution from grid (ns/s).\n    pub grid_drift_ns_per_s: f64,\n    /// Combined expected drift (ns/s).\n    pub total_drift_ns_per_s: f64,\n    /// Forecast confidence.\n    pub confidence: f64,\n}\n\n// ─── Thermal Observer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ThermalObserver {\n    temps: Vec<TempSample>,\n    max_samples: usize,\n}\n\nimpl ThermalObserver {\n    pub fn new(max_samples: usize) -> Self {\n        ThermalObserver { temps: Vec::with_capacity(max_samples), max_samples }\n    }\n\n    pub fn observe(&mut self, sample: TempSample) {\n        if self.temps.len() >= self.max_samples {\n            self.temps.remove(0);\n        }\n        self.temps.push(sample);\n    }\n\n    pub fn forecast_cpu_temp(&self) -> (f64, f64) {\n        let n = self.temps.len();\n        if n < 2 {\n            let last = self.temps.last().map(|t| t.cpu_mdeg as f64).unwrap_or(40000.0);\n            return (last, 0.0); // 40C default (typical Falkenstein DC ambient + IT load), no trend\n        }\n        let mean: f64 = self.temps.iter().map(|t| t.cpu_mdeg as f64).sum::<f64>() / n as f64;\n        let slope = if n >= 3 {\n            (self.temps[n-1].cpu_mdeg as f64 - self.temps[0].cpu_mdeg as f64) / n as f64\n        } else { 0.0 };\n        (mean, slope)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Grid Observer ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GridObserver {\n    samples: Vec<GridSample>,\n    max_samples: usize,\n    /// Nominal grid frequency (50.0 or 60.0).\n    pub nominal_hz: f64,\n}\n\nimpl GridObserver {\n    pub fn new(max_samples: usize, nominal_hz: f64) -> Self {\n        GridObserver { samples: Vec::with_capacity(max_samples), max_samples, nominal_hz }\n    }\n\n    pub fn observe(&mut self, sample: GridSample) {\n        if self.samples.len() >= self.max_samples {\n            self.samples.remove(0);\n        }\n        self.samples.push(sample);\n    }\n\n    pub fn forecast(&self) -> (f64, f64) {\n        let n = self.samples.len();\n        if n < 2 {\n            return (self.samples.last().map(|s| s.load_mw).unwrap_or(0.0), 0.0);\n        }\n        let mean: f64 = self.samples.iter().map(|s| s.load_mw).sum::<f64>() / n as f64;\n        let mean_freq: f64 = self.samples.iter().map(|s| s.frequency_hz).sum::<f64>() / n as f64;\n        let freq_dev = mean_freq - self.nominal_hz;\n        (mean, freq_dev)\n    }\n\n    /// Drift contribution from grid frequency deviation (ppm).\n    pub fn drift_ppm(&self) -> f64 {\n        let (_, freq_dev) = self.forecast();\n        if freq_dev.abs() < 0.01 { return 0.0; }\n        // Every 0.01 Hz deviation ≈ 200 ppm clock drift on PLL-synchronized clocks.\n        (freq_dev / 0.01) * 200.0\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Power Forecast Engine ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Combined power + thermal forecast engine.\npub struct PowerForecastEngine {\n    pub thermal: ThermalObserver,\n    pub grid: GridObserver,\n    pub weather: Vec<WeatherSample>,\n    max_weather: usize,\n}\n\nimpl PowerForecastEngine {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        PowerForecastEngine {\n            thermal: ThermalObserver::new(1000),\n            grid: GridObserver::new(1000, GRID_NOMINAL_HZ),\n            weather: Vec::with_capacity(100),\n            max_weather: 100,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn observe_temp(&mut self, cpu_mdeg: u64, ambient_mdeg: u64, now_ns: u64) {\n        self.thermal.observe(TempSample {\n            cpu_mdeg, ambient_mdeg, timestamp_ns: now_ns, valid: TriState::True,\n        });\n    }\n\n    pub fn observe_grid(&mut self, load_mw: f64, frequency_hz: f64, now_ns: u64) {\n        self.grid.observe(GridSample {\n            load_mw, frequency_hz, timestamp_ns: now_ns, valid: TriState::True,\n        });\n    }\n\n    pub fn observe_weather(&mut self, sample: WeatherSample) {\n        if self.weather.len() >= self.max_weather {\n            self.weather.remove(0);\n        }\n        self.weather.push(sample);\n    }\n\n    /// Compute the current power forecast.\n    pub fn forecast(&self) -> PowerForecast {\n        let (cpu_mean, cpu_slope) = self.thermal.forecast_cpu_temp();\n        let cpu_1m = (cpu_mean + cpu_slope * 60.0) as u64;\n\n        let ambient_mean = self.thermal.temps.last()\n            .map(|t| t.ambient_mdeg)\n            .unwrap_or(AMBIENT_BASELINE_MDEG);\n        let ambient_trend = if self.thermal.temps.len() >= 3 {\n            let first = self.thermal.temps.first().map(|t| t.ambient_mdeg as f64).unwrap_or(0.0);\n            let last = self.thermal.temps.last().map(|t| t.ambient_mdeg as f64).unwrap_or(0.0);\n            ((last - first) / self.thermal.temps.len() as f64) * 60.0\n        } else { 0.0 };\n        let ambient_1m = (ambient_mean as f64 + ambient_trend) as u64;\n\n        let grid_drift_ppm = self.grid.drift_ppm();\n\n        // Thermal drift: each 10°C above 40°C baseline ≈ 1 ppm clock drift.\n        let cpu_delta = (cpu_mean - 40000.0).max(0.0) / 10_000.0; // 10°C units\n        let thermal_drift_ppm = cpu_delta * 1.0;\n\n        let (grid_load, _) = self.grid.forecast();\n        let total_drift_ppm = thermal_drift_ppm + grid_drift_ppm;\n        let drift_ns_per_s = total_drift_ppm / 1_000_000.0 * 1_000_000_000.0;\n\n        let confidence = if self.thermal.temps.len() >= MIN_FORECAST_SAMPLES\n            && self.grid.samples.len() >= MIN_FORECAST_SAMPLES\n        { 0.85 } else { 0.3 };\n\n        PowerForecast {\n            cpu_mdeg_1m: cpu_1m,\n            ambient_mdeg_1m: ambient_1m,\n            grid_mw_1m: grid_load,\n            thermal_drift_ns_per_s: thermal_drift_ppm * 1000.0,\n            grid_drift_ns_per_s: grid_drift_ppm * 1000.0,\n            total_drift_ns_per_s: drift_ns_per_s,\n            confidence,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let fc = self.forecast();\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(256);\n        out.push_str("Power Forecast\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  CPU temp:    {} mdeg (1m: {})\\n",\n            self.thermal.temps.last().map(|t| t.cpu_mdeg).unwrap_or(0), fc.cpu_mdeg_1m));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Ambient:     {} mdeg (1m: {})\\n",\n            self.thermal.temps.last().map(|t| t.ambient_mdeg).unwrap_or(0), fc.ambient_mdeg_1m));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Grid load:   {:.0} MW\\n", fc.grid_mw_1m));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Thermal drf: {:.3} ns/s\\n", fc.thermal_drift_ns_per_s));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Grid drf:    {:.3} ns/s\\n", fc.grid_drift_ns_per_s));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Total drf:   {:.3} ns/s\\n", fc.total_drift_ns_per_s));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Confidence:  {:.0}%\\n", fc.confidence * 100.0));\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn thermal_observer_trend() {\n        let mut obs = ThermalObserver::new(10);\n        for i in 0..5 {\n            obs.observe(TempSample {\n                cpu_mdeg: 40000 + i * 100, ambient_mdeg: 20000,\n                timestamp_ns: i as u64 * 1_000_000, valid: TriState::True,\n            });\n        }\n        let (mean, slope) = obs.forecast_cpu_temp();\n        assert!(mean > 0.0);\n        assert!(slope >= 0.0);\n    }\n\n assert_eq!(pfe.grid.nominal_hz, GRID_NOMINAL_HZ);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn power_forecast_with_data() {\n        let mut pfe = PowerForecastEngine::new();\n        for i in 0..15 {\n
```
