## 7184 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/cgraph.rs · LongTerm

Summary: cgraph · 780 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/cgraph.rs	cgraph · 780 lines	//! cgraph.rs — semi-Markovian causal **graph** primitives for the ID / IDC\n//! identification algorithms (Shpitser & Pearl, 2006/2008; 2012).\n//!\n//! This module is the *structural* half of the do-calculus identifiability\n//! decider. `causal.rs` owns the recursive `id()` / `idc()` procedures; this\n//! module owns the graph algebra they recurse over:\n//!\n//! * a [`CGraph`] carrying both **directed** arcs (`parents[i]` — `i`'s direct\n//!   causes) and **bidirected** arcs (`bidirected[i]` — latent confounding /\n//!   "spurious correlation" between `i` and the listed nodes);\n//! * [`ancestors`] / [`descendants`] closures over directed edges;\n//! * [`c_components`] — the maximal confounded-component partition, the spine of\n//!   the ID recursion (Def. 9, Shpitser–Pearl 2008);\n//! * [`d_separated_bi`] — d-separation **extended to bidirected arcs** (Def. 4 in\n//!   the JMLR 2008 paper): a path is blocked by `z` if it contains a chain\n//!   `i→m→j`, a fork `i←m→j`, or a **bidirected** `i↔m→j` / `i←m↔j` with `m∈z`,\n//!   or a collider `i→m←j` whose descendants avoid `z`. The ordinary\n//!   [`causal::d_separated`] is the bidirected-free special case.\n//! * subgraph constructors `g_x_removed` (`G\\X`), `subgraph_on` (`G[V]`), and a\n//!   `[nodes]` listing.\n//!\n//! Trust boundary: every public constructor validates node indices and rejects\n//! self-loops / reflexive bidirected arcs (those would be degenerate or\n//! malformed); invalid input yields `Err`, never a panic.\n\nuse alloc::collections::{BTreeSet, VecDeque};\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A semi-Markovian causal diagram: observable nodes `0..n`, directed parent\n/// lists, and a bidirected-adjacency list (symmetric — `i↔j` appears in both\n/// `bidirected[i]` and `bidirected[j]`).\n///\n/// `bidirected` models *latent* (unobserved) confounding: `i↔j` means some\n/// hidden common cause drives both. It is exactly the structure no prior\n/// function in this crate could even *detect* as non-identifiable (the bow-arc\n/// case `X→Z←Y` with `Z` unobserved ⇒ `X↔Y` ⇔ a hedge).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CGraph {\n    pub n: usize,\n    /// `parents[i]` = direct causes of node `i` (directed edges `p → i`).\n    pub parents: Vec<Vec<usize>>,\n    /// `bidirected[i]` = nodes `j` with a latent-confounding arc `i↔j`.\n    pub bidirected: Vec<Vec<usize>>,\n    /// `present[i]` = whether node `i` is part of the *current* (sub)graph.\n    /// Subgraph constructors (`subgraph_on`, `g_x_removed`) drop nodes by\n    /// clearing this flag rather than reindexing, so node indices stay stable\n    /// across the ID recursion (which threads the vertex set `v` explicitly,\n    /// mirroring `igraph::induced.subgraph` in the reference `causaleffect`\n    /// implementation). `ancestors`, `c_components`, and `nodes` all ignore\n    /// absent nodes.\n    present: Vec<bool>,\n}\n\nimpl CGraph {\n    /// Build a `CGraph`, validating indices and bidirected symmetry.\n    ///\n    /// `parents[i]` lists `i`'s direct causes; `bidirected[i]` lists `i`'s latent\n    /// confounders (the pair `i↔j` must be listed in *both*). We accept it either\n    /// way and *enforce* symmetry internally so callers cannot create an\n    /// asymmetric (malformed) graph by accident.\n    pub fn new(parents: Vec<Vec<usize>>, bidirected: Vec<Vec<usize>>) -> Result<Self, String> {\n        let n = parents.len();\n        if bidirected.len() != n {\n            return Err(format!(\n                "parents.len()={n} != bidirected.len()={}",\n                bidirected.len()\n            ));\n        }\n        for i in 0..n {\n            for &p in &parents[i] {\n                if p >= n {\n                    return Err(format!("parent {p} of node {i} out of range (n={n})"));\n                }\n                if p == i {\n                    return Err(format!("self-loop parent on node {i} (degenerate DAG)"));\n                }\n            }\n            for &b in &bidirected[i] {\n                if b >= n {\n                    return Err(format!(\n                        "bidirected neighbour {b} of node {i} out of range (n={n})"\n                    ));\n                }\n                if b == i {\n                    return Err(format!("reflexive bidirected arc on node {i} (malformed)"));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // Enforce bidirected symmetry.\n        let mut bi = bidirected;\n        for i in 0..n {\n            let neighbors: Vec<usize> = bi[i].clone();\n            for j in neighbors {\n                if !bi[j].contains(&i) {\n                    bi[j].push(i);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // Sort + dedup for deterministic c-component / d-sep behaviour.\n        for v in bi.iter_mut() {\n            v.sort_unstable();\n            v.dedup();\n        }\n        Ok(CGraph {\n            n,\n            parents,\n            bidirected: bi,\n            present: vec![true; n],\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Nodes currently present in this (sub)graph, in ascending index order.\n    /// This is the vertex set `v` the ID recursion threads through every call.\n    pub fn nodes(&self) -> Vec<usize> {\n        (0..self.n).filter(|&i| self.present[i]).collect()\n    }\n    pub fn ancestors(&self, set: &[usize]) -> Vec<bool> {\n        let mut anc = vec![false; self.n];\n        let mut stack: Vec<usize> = set.to_vec();\n        for &s in set {\n            anc[s] = true;\n        }\n        while let Some(v) = stack.pop() {\n            if !self.present[v] {\n                continue;\n            }\n            for &p in &self.parents[v] {\n                if !anc[p] && self.present[p] {\n                    anc[p] = true;\n                    stack.push(p);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        anc\n    }\n\n    /// Directed descendants of `set` (inclusive), BFS over child edges.\n    pub fn descendants(&self, set: &[usize]) -> Vec<bool> {\n        let mut children: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); self.n];\n        for (i, ps) in self.parents.iter().enumerate() {\n            for &p in ps {\n                children[p].push(i);\n            }\n        }\n        let mut desc = vec![false; self.n];\n        let mut stack: Vec<usize> = set.to_vec();\n        for &s in set {\n            desc[s] = true;\n        }\n        while let Some(v) = stack.pop() {\n            for &c in &children[v] {\n                if !desc[c] {\n                    desc[c] = true;\n                    stack.push(c);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        desc\n    }\n\n    /// Maximal **c-components** (confounded components, Def. 9, Shpitser–Pearl\n    /// 2008). Two observable nodes belong to the same c-component iff they are\n    /// connected by a path of **bidirected** arcs (latent confounding). This is\n    /// the connected-components of the *bidirected subgraph only* — directed\n    /// edges are deliberately **NOT** part of the c-component relation. (A common\n    /// error is to moralize the directed edges too; that collapses every DAG into\n    /// a single c-component and makes the ID recursion hedge every identifiable\n    /// chain. The ID algorithm's correctness relies on c-components being\n    /// bidirected-only.)\n    ///\n    /// Returns the partition as a list of node-sets (each sorted, ascending).\n    ///\n    /// P04 parity-swap: delegates to the canonical DSU primitive\n    /// ([`c_components_dsu`]). The byte-parity contract (members ascending\n    /// within a set; sets ordered by ascending minimum member) is preserved —\n    /// verified by `green_c_components_dsu_parity` across every fixture.\n    pub fn c_components(&self) -> Vec<Vec<usize>> {\n        self.c_components_dsu()\n    }\n\n    /// DSU-backed c-components: union every bidirected arc `(i,j)` with `j > i`\n    /// over the present nodes (exactly the flood-fill's bidirected subgraph),\n    /// then emit [`crate::dsu::Dsu::components`]. Byte-identical to the original\n    /// stack flood-fill by construction of the DSU ordering contract.\n    pub fn c_components_dsu(&self) -> Vec<Vec<usize>> {\n        let mut dsu = crate::dsu::Dsu::new(self.n);\n        for i in 0..self.n {\n            if !self.present[i] {\n                continue;\n            }\n            for &j in &self.bidirected[i] {\n                if j > i && self.present[j] {\n                    dsu.union(i, j);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        dsu.components(&self.present)\n    }\n\n    /// `G_{\\overline{X}}` — keep every node but **delete only the incoming edges**\n    /// of `X` (intervened nodes stay in the graph, their causes are severed).\n    /// This is the exact graph `An(Y)_{G_{\\overline{X}}}` is computed on (ID line 2).\n    /// Distinct from [`g_x_removed`] (`G_{\\underline{X}}`), which deletes `X` and\n    /// all incident edges — that one is line 1's marginalization, NOT line 2.\n    pub fn g_x_incoming_removed(&self, x: &[usize]) -> CGraph {\n        let mut removed = vec![false; self.n];\n        for &v in x {\n            removed[v] = true;\n        }\n        let mut parents = vec![Vec::new(); self.n];\n        let bidirected = self.bidirected.clone();\n        for i in 0..self.n {\n            if removed[i] {\n                // delete incoming edges of i (i is intervened); keep the node\n                parents[i] = Vec::new();\n            } else {\n                parents[i] = self.parents[i].clone();\n            }\n        }\n        CGraph {\n            n: self.n,\n            parents,\n            bidirected,\n            present: self.present.clone(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// `G\\\\\\\\X` — delete `X` and all edges (directed or bidirected) incident to any\n    /// node in `X`. Used by the ID recursion to express `P_x(·)` over the\n    /// post-intervention graph.\n    pub fn g_x_removed(&self, x: &[usize]) -> CGraph {\n        let mut removed = vec![false; self.n];\n        for &v in x {\n            removed[v] = true;\n        }\n        let mut parents = vec![Vec::new(); self.n];\n        let mut bidirected = vec![Vec::new(); self.n];\n        let mut present = vec![false; self.n];\n        for i in 0..self.n {\n            if removed[i] {\n                continue;\n            }\n            present[i] = true;\n            parents[i] = self.parents[i]\n                .iter()\n                .copied()\n                .filter(|&p| !removed[p])\n                .collect();\n            bidirected[i] = self.bidirected[i]\n                .iter()\n                .copied()\n                .filter(|&b| !removed[b])\n                .collect();\n        }\n        CGraph {\n            n: self.n,\n            parents,\n            bidirected,\n            present,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// `G[V]` — restrict to node set `V` (node indices preserved). All edges\n    /// (directed + bidirected) between surviving nodes are kept. Used by the\n    /// `An(Y)G` restriction in `id`.\n    pub fn subgraph_on(&self, v: &[usize]) -> CGraph {\n        let mut keep = vec![false; self.n];\n        for &node in v {\n            keep[node] = true;\n        }\n        let mut parents = vec![Vec::new(); self.n];\n        let mut bidirected = vec![Vec::new(); self.n];\n        let mut present = vec![false; self.n];\n        for &i in v {\n            present[i] = true;\n            parents[i] = self.parents[i]\n                .iter()\n                .copied()\n                .filter(|&p| keep[p])\n                .collect();\n            bidirected[i] = self.bidirected[i]\n                .iter()\n                .copied()\n                .filter(|&b| keep[b])\n                .collect();\n        }\n        CGraph {\n            n: self.n,\n            parents,\n            bidirected,\n            present,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// In `G\\X`, is `a` d-separated from `b` given `given`? Bidirected-aware\n    /// (Def. 4, JMLR 2008). This is the single structural primitive the ID\n    /// recursion needs to recognise colliders and confounded forks.\n    pub fn d_separated_bi(\n        &self,\n        x: &[usize],\n        a: usize,\n        b: usize,\n        given: &[usize],\n    ) -> Result<bool, String> {\n        let g = self.g_x_removed(x);\n        g.d_separated_raw(a, b, given)\n    }\n\n    /// Raw d-separation over this graph (already in `G\\X` form). Walks active\n    /// trails treating bidirected arcs as the *open* (confounded) third case.\n    fn d_separated_raw(&self, a: usize, b: usize, given: &[usize]) -> Result<bool, String> {\n        let n = self.n;\n        if a >= n || b >= n {\n            return Err(format!("d-sep node out of range: a={a}, b={b}, n={n}"));\n        }\n        let mut given_set = vec![false; n];\n        for &z in given {\n            if z >= n {\n                return Err(format!("conditioning node out of range: z={z}, n={n}"));\n            }\n            given_set[z] = true;\n        }\n        // children[i] = nodes that have i as a parent\n        let mut children: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n];\n        for (i, ps) in self.parents.iter().enumerate() {\n            for &p in ps {\n                children[p].push(i);\n            }\n        }\n        // descendant closure of `given` opens colliders\n        let mut desc = vec![false; n];\n        let mut stack: Vec<usize> = given.to_vec();\n        while let Some(v) = stack.pop() {\n            if desc[v] {\n                continue;\n            }\n            desc[v] = true;\n            for &c in &children[v] {\n                if !desc[c] {\n                    stack.push(c);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // BFS over active trails. State = (node, dir, via):\n        //   dir = 0 start | 1 arrived downstream (from a parent) | 2 from a child\n        //   via = node we came from (n = sentinel at start)\n        // A trail is open iff every triple along it is open.\n        let mut visited: BTreeSet<(usize, u8, usize)> = BTreeSet::new();\n        let mut queue: VecDeque<(usize, u8, usize)> = VecDeque::new();\n        for &c in &children[a] {\n            queue.push_back((c, 1, a));\n        }\n        for &p in &self.parents[a] {\n            queue.push_back((p, 2, a));\n        }\n        // Bidirected arcs off the start node are active (latent common cause):\n        // open iff `a` is NOT in the conditioning set (Def. 4 case (c)).\n        if !given_set[a] {\n            for &w in &self.bidirected[a] {\n                queue.push_back((w, 0, a));\n            }\n        }\n        // start node is "traversed" — mark to avoid re-expansion\n        visited.insert((a, 0, n));\n        while let Some((u, dir, via)) = queue.pop_back() {\n            if u == b {\n                return Ok(false); // active trail reached target ⇒ d-CONNECTED\n            }\n            if !visited.insert((u, dir, via)) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            // Walk to children u → c: chain/fork/bidirected-child at u.\n            if !given_set[u] {\n                for &c in &children[u] {\n                    if c != via {\n                        queue.push_back((c, 1, u));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            // Walk to parents p → u.\n            for &p in &self.parents[u] {\n                if p == via {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                if dir == 1 {\n                    // arrived downstream (parent→u): prev→u←p is a COLLIDER —\n                    // open iff u's descendant is in `given`.\n                    if desc[u] {\n                        queue.push_back((p, 2, u));\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    // arrived upstream (child→u): p→u→prev is a CHAIN —\n                    // open iff u ∉ given.\n                    if !given_set[u] {\n                        queue.push_back((p, 2, u));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            // Walk bidirected u ↔ w: open iff u (hence the confounded pair) is in\n            // `given`. The latent common cause is "conditioned" precisely when u\n            // is in the conditioning set — exactly Def. 4 case (c).\n            if !given_set[u] {\n                for &w in &self.bidirected[u] {\n                    if w != via {\n                        queue.push_back((w, 0, u));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(true) // no active trail ⇒ d-SEPARATED\n    }\n\n    /// Kahn topological order of the **directed** edges (bidirected arcs are\n    /// ignored — they never constrain a topological order). Returns `None` if a\n    /// directed cycle exists (an invariant a valid semi-Markovian diagram must\n    /// satisfy). Used to linearise the factorization `P(v) = ∏ P(v_i | pa(v_i))`.\n    pub fn topological_order(&self) -> Option<Vec<usize>> {\n        let mut indeg = vec![0usize; self.n];\n        let mut children: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); self.n];\n        for (i, ps) in self.parents.iter().enumerate() {\n            indeg[i] = ps.len();\n            for &p in ps {\n                children[p].push(i);\n            }\n        }\n        let mut queue: Vec<usize> = (0..self.n).filter(|&i| indeg[i] == 0).collect();\n        let mut order = Vec::with_capacity(self.n);\n        while let Some(u) = queue.pop() {\n            order.push(u);\n            for &c in &children[u] {\n                indeg[c] -= 1;\n                if indeg[c] == 0 {\n                    queue.push(c);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        if order.len() == self.n {\n            Some(order)\n        } else {\n            None\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// d-separation in `G_{X, Z̲}` — the *underlined* do-calculus graph for\n    /// rule 2 / rule 3: nodes in `removed` are deleted entirely (as in `G\\\\X`),\n    /// while nodes in `remove_incoming` keep their vertex but lose their\n    /// **incoming directed edges** (they are intervened, so their causes are\n    /// severed but they remain queryable). Bidirected arcs incident to a removed\n    /// node are dropped; all others survive. Used by `idc` to test the swap\n    /// `(Y ⊥ Z' | X, Z\\\\Z')_{G_{X, Z̲}}`.\n    pub fn d_separated_underlined(\n        &self,\n        removed: &[usize],\n        remove_incoming: &[usize],\n        a: usize,\n        b: usize,\n        given: &[usize],\n    ) -> Result<bool, String> {\n        let mut rem = vec![false; self.n];\n        for &v in removed {\n            if v >= self.n {\n                return Err(format!("underlined removed node {v} out of range"));\n            }\n            rem[v] = true;\n        }\n        let mut inc = vec![false; self.n];\n        for &v in remove_incoming {\n            if v >= self.n {\n                return Err(format!("underlined remove_incoming node {v} out of range"));\n            }\n            inc[v] = true;\n        }\n        let mut parents = vec![Vec::new(); self.n];\n        let mut bidirected = vec![Vec::new(); self.n];\n        let mut present = vec![false; self.n];\n        for i in 0..self.n {\n            if rem[i] {\n                continue;\n            }\n            present[i] = true;\n            for &p in &self.parents[i] {\n                if rem[p] {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                if inc[i] {\n                    continue; // drop incoming edges of i (i is intervened)\n                }\n                parents[i].push(p);\n            }\n            for &bd in &self.bidirected[i] {\n                if rem[bd] {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                bidirected[i].push(bd);\n            }\n        }\n        let g = CGraph {\n            n: self.n,\n            parents,\n            bidirected,\n            present,\n        };\n        g.d_separated_raw(a, b, given)\n    }\n\n    /// Root set of a subgraph: nodes with **no directed parent** within it. A\n    /// maximal c-component rooted at these is an R-rooted C-forest (the `R` in\n    /// the hedge definition). Used to populate [`HedgeWitness::root`].\n    pub fn roots(&self) -> Vec<usize> {\n        let mut r = Vec::new();\n        for i in 0..self.n {\n            if self.present[i] && self.parents[i].is_empty() {\n                r.push(i);\n            }\n        }\n        r\n    }\n\n    /// Does `vec` (as a set) contain every element of `subset`?\n    pub fn contains_all(vec: &[usize], subset: &[usize]) -> bool {\n        let set: BTreeSet<usize> = vec.iter().copied().collect();\n        subset.iter().all(|&s| set.contains(&s))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // Simple DAG: chain 0→1→2 (no bidirected). c-components = singletons.\n    fn chain_graph() -> CGraph {\n        CGraph::new(\n            vec![vec![], vec![0], vec![1]], // 0 root, 1 pa 0, 2 pa 1\n            vec![vec![], vec![], vec![]],\n        )\n        .unwrap()\n    }\n\n    // Bow-arc / M-graph: 0→2←1  with 2 unobserved ⇒ bidirected 0↔1.\n    // c-components: {0,1} (confounded) and {2}.\n    fn m_graph() -> CGraph {\n        CGraph::new(\n            vec![vec![], vec![], vec![0, 1]], // 2 has parents 0 and 1\n            vec![vec![1], vec![0], vec![]],   // 0↔1 latent confound\n        )\n        .unwrap()\n    }\n\n    // ── GREEN: c-components of a pure DAG are singletons ──\n    #[test]\n    fn green_dag_c_components_are_singletons() {\n        let g = chain_graph();\n        let comps = g.c_components();\n        assert_eq!(comps.len(), 3, "three singleton c-components");\n        for c in &comps {\n            assert_eq!(c.len(), 1, "each c-component is a single node");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── GREEN: bow-arc (M-graph) yields a confounded {0,1} c-component ──\n    #[test]\n    fn green_bow_arc_groups_confounded_pair() {\n        let g = m_graph();\n        let comps = g.c_components();\n        // Exactly two c-components: {0,1} and {2}.\n        assert_eq!(comps.len(), 2, "two c-components");\n        let pair = comps\n            .iter()\n            .find(|c| c.len() == 2)\n            .expect("a 2-node c-comp");\n        assert_eq!(pair, &vec![0, 1], "the confounded pair {{0,1}}");\n    }\n\n    // ── GREEN: d-separation is preserved for plain chains (no bidirected) ──\n    #[test]\n    fn green_chain_dsep_matches_plain_oracle() {\n        let g = chain_graph();\n        // 0 and 2 d-connected via 0→1→2; blocked by conditioning on 1.\n        assert!(!g.d_separated_raw(0, 2, &[]).unwrap(), "chain open");\n        assert!(g.d_separated_raw(0, 2, &[1]).unwrap(), "chain blocked by 1");\n    }\n\n    // ── GREEN: bidirected confounded pair is fundamentally non-separable ──\n    #[test]\n    fn green_bidirected_fork_opens_then_closes() {\n        let g = m_graph();\n        // 0↔1 (latent confound) plus 0→2←1 (collider). The bidirected arc makes\n        // 0,1 d-connected under empty given (Def. 4 case (c)). Conditioning on\n        // the shared child 2 OPENS the collider, so they stay connected. And\n        // conditioning on 0 closes the bidirected arc but, because 2 is a\n        // descendant of 0, opens the collider 0→2←1 again — still connected.\n        // Symmetrically for conditioning on 1. The pair is therefore d-connected\n        // under EVERY non-trivial conditioning set — this non-separability is\n        // precisely why {0,1} is ONE c-component.\n        assert!(\n            !g.d_separated_raw(0, 1, &[]).unwrap(),\n            "bidirected 0↔1 d-connected (empty)"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            !g.d_separated_raw(0, 1, &[2]).unwrap(),\n            "conditioning on collider child keeps 0,1 connected"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            !g.d_separated_raw(0, 1, &[0]).unwrap(),\n            "conditioning on 0 opens collider via descendant 2 — still connected"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            !g.d_separated_raw(0, 1, &[1]).unwrap(),\n            "conditioning on 1 opens collider via descendant 2 — still connected"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── GREEN (P04 parity): DSU c-components == reference flood-fill ──\n    // Reference is the ORIGINAL stack flood-fill; DSU (now the live impl) must\n    // be byte-identical across every fixture. If this diverges the DSU ordering\n    // is wrong — fix the primitive, never the fixture.\n    fn ref_flood_c_components(g: &CGraph) -> Vec<Vec<usize>> {\n        let n = g.n;\n        let mut adj: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n];\n        for i in 0..n {\n            for &j in &g.bidirected[i] {\n                if j > i {\n                    adj[i].push(j);\n                    adj[j].push(i);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // present is private; reconstruct via c_components on a node-complete\n        // fixture is not possible — instead exercise full graphs (all present).\n        let mut seen = vec![false; n];\n        let mut comps = Vec::new();\n        for start in 0..n {\n            if seen[start] {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let mut comp = Vec::new();\n            let mut stack = vec![start];\n            seen[start] = true;\n            while let Some(v) = stack.pop() {\n                comp.push(v);\n                for &w in &adj[v] {\n                    if !seen[w] {\n                        seen[w] = true;\n                        stack.push(w);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            comp.sort_unstable();\n            comps.push(comp);\n        }\n        comps\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_c_components_dsu_parity() {\n        for g in [chain_graph(), m_graph()] {\n            // live (delegates to DSU) == DSU == reference flood-fill\n            assert_eq!(g.c_components(), g.c_components_dsu());\n            assert_eq!(g.c_components_dsu(), ref_flood_c_components(&g));\n        }\n        // subgraph fixtures (absent nodes) — parity of live vs dsu holds.\n        let g = m_graph();\n        let sub = g.g_x_removed(&[1]); // drop node 1\n        assert_eq!(sub.c_components(), sub.c_components_dsu());\n    }\n\n    // ── RED (trust boundary): malformed graph rejected, never panic ──\n    #[test]\n    fn red_malformed_graph_rejected() {\n        assert!(CGraph::new(\n            vec![vec![], vec![9], vec![]], // parent 9 out of range\n            vec![vec![], vec![], vec![]],\n        )\n        .is_err());\n        assert!(CGraph::new(\n            vec![vec![], vec![], vec![]],\n            vec![vec![1], vec![], vec![]], // asymmetric bidirected (0↔1, 1 missing 0)\n        )\n        .is_ok()); // symmetry is enforced, not required at input\n                   // reflexive bidirected rejected\n        assert!(CGraph::new(vec![vec![], vec![], vec![]], vec![vec![0], vec![], vec![]],).is_err());\n    }\n\n    // ── injected: empty / single-node / dense / disconnected / invalid / neg-weight / removal-cascade ──\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_graph_no_nodes() {\n        let g = CGraph::new(vec![], vec![]).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(g.n, 0);\n        assert!(g.nodes().is_empty());\n        assert!(g.roots().is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(g.c_components().len(), 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn single_node_graph() {\n        let g = CGraph::new(vec![vec![]], vec![vec![]]).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(g.n, 1);\n        assert_eq!(g.nodes(), vec![0]);\n        assert_eq!(g.roots(), vec![0]);\n        let comps = g.c_components();\n        assert_eq!(comps, vec![vec![0]]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn self_loop_parent_rejected() {\n        assert!(CGraph::new(vec![vec![0]], vec![vec![]]).is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dense_complete_dag() {\n        let n = 5;\n        let mut parents: Vec<Vec<usize>> = Vec::new();\n        for i in 0..n {\n            parents.push((0..i).collect());\n        }\n        let bi = vec![Vec::new(); n];\n        let g = CGraph::new(parents, bi).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(g.c_components().len(), n); // no bidirected => singletons\n        let topo = g.topological_order().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(topo.len(), n); ## 7216 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/support.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: support · 242 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/support.rs	support · 242 lines	//! support.rs — customer-support domain: ticket lifecycle FSM + conversation\n//! thread (item #13, Chatwoot), zero-dep.\n//!\n//! Chatwoot itself is a web SaaS (out of scope), but its *domain core* — a\n//! ticket state machine, a multi-channel conversation, and canned responses —\n//! is pure state-transition logic, the same discipline as `order_machine`.\n//! Closed enum + single transition table + wire codes, no floats, no I/O.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\n/// Support ticket lifecycle states.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\n#[repr(u8)]\npub enum TicketState {\n    Open = 0,\n    Pending = 1,\n    Resolved = 2,\n    Escalated = 3,\n    Closed = 4,\n}\n\nimpl TicketState {\n    /// Wire code for storage (closed enum discipline).\n    pub const fn wire(self) -> u8 {\n        self as u8\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a wire code; `None` for unknown (never fabricate a state).\n    pub const fn from_wire(code: u8) -> Option<Self> {\n        match code {\n            0 => Some(TicketState::Open),\n            1 => Some(TicketState::Pending),\n            2 => Some(TicketState::Resolved),\n            3 => Some(TicketState::Escalated),\n            4 => Some(TicketState::Closed),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            TicketState::Open => "open",\n            TicketState::Pending => "pending",\n            TicketState::Resolved => "resolved",\n            TicketState::Escalated => "escalated",\n            TicketState::Closed => "closed",\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub const fn is_terminal(self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, TicketState::Closed)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Ticket actions that drive transitions.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum TicketAction {\n    Assign,\n    Reply,\n    Hold,\n    Escalate,\n    Resolve,\n    Reopen,\n    Close,\n}\n\n/// The single transition table (single source of truth). Returns the next\n/// state or `None` if the transition is illegal.\npub fn transition(state: TicketState, action: TicketAction) -> Option<TicketState> {\n    use TicketAction::*;\n    use TicketState::*;\n    match (state, action) {\n        (Open, Assign) | (Open, Reply) => Some(Open),\n        (Open, Hold) => Some(Pending),\n        (Open, Escalate) => Some(Escalated),\n        (Open, Resolve) => Some(Resolved),\n        (Pending, Assign) | (Pending, Reply) | (Pending, Hold) => Some(Pending),\n        (Pending, Resolve) => Some(Resolved),\n        (Pending, Escalate) => Some(Escalated),\n        (Escalated, Reply) | (Escalated, Assign) => Some(Escalated),\n        (Escalated, Resolve) => Some(Resolved),\n        (Resolved, Reopen) => Some(Open),\n        (Resolved, Close) => Some(Closed),\n        (Closed, _) => None, // terminal: no transition out\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// A conversation message channel.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\n#[repr(u8)]\npub enum Channel {\n    Email = 0,\n    Chat = 1,\n    Sms = 2,\n    Social = 3,\n}\n\n/// A conversation message.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Message {\n    pub channel: Channel,\n    pub author: String,\n    pub body: String,\n    pub ts: u64,\n}\n\n/// A conversation thread (ordered messages) attached to a ticket.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct Conversation {\n    messages: Vec<Message>,\n}\n\nimpl Conversation {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self { messages: Vec::new() }\n    }\n\n    pub fn push(&mut self, m: Message) {\n        self.messages.push(m);\n    }\n\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.messages.len()\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.messages.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Message> {\n        self.messages.iter()\n    }\n\n    /// Messages from a specific channel, in order.\n    pub fn by_channel(&self, ch: Channel) -> Vec<&Message> {\n        self.messages.iter().filter(|m| m.channel == ch).collect()\n    }\n}\n\n/// A support ticket: state + conversation + resolution flag.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Ticket {\n    pub id: u64,\n    pub state: TicketState,\n    pub conversation: Conversation,\n}\n\nimpl Ticket {\n    pub fn new(id: u64) -> Self {\n        Self { id, state: TicketState::Open, conversation: Conversation::new() }\n    }\n\n    /// Apply an action; updates state if the transition is legal. Returns the\n    /// new state (unchanged on illegal transition).\n    pub fn apply(&mut self, action: TicketAction) -> TicketState {\n        if let Some(next) = transition(self.state, action) {\n            self.state = next;\n        }\n        self.state\n    }\n\n    /// Append a message and (for reply actions) keep the ticket alive.\n    pub fn reply(&mut self, m: Message) {\n        self.conversation.push(m);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Canned-response store: a const LUT of (key, template). Lookup is O(1) via\n/// a small match (the kernel's closed-enum / const-table discipline).\npub fn canned_response(key: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {\n    Some(match key {\n        "greeting" => "Hi! How can we help you today?",\n        "thanks" => "You're welcome — anything else we can do?",\n        "closing" => "Thanks for reaching out. We're closing this ticket; reply any time to reopen.",\n        _ => return None,\n    })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn open_to_closed_path() {\n        let mut t = Ticket::new(0);\n        assert_eq!(t.state, TicketState::Open);\n        t.apply(TicketAction::Assign);\n        assert_eq!(t.state, TicketState::Open);\n        t.apply(TicketAction::Resolve);\n        assert_eq!(t.state, TicketState::Resolved);\n        t.apply(TicketAction::Close);\n        assert_eq!(t.state, TicketState::Closed);\n        assert!(t.state.is_terminal());\n        // No transition out of Closed.\n        assert_eq!(t.apply(TicketAction::Reopen), TicketState::Closed);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn escalate_and_resolve() {\n        let mut t = Ticket::new(1);\n        t.apply(TicketAction::Escalate);\n        assert_eq!(t.state, TicketState::Escalated);\n        t.apply(TicketAction::Resolve);\n        assert_eq!(t.state, TicketState::Resolved);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reopen_resolved() {\n        let mut t = Ticket::new(2);\n        t.apply(TicketAction::Resolve);\n        assert_eq!(t.state, TicketState::Resolved);\n        t.apply(TicketAction::Reopen);\n        assert_eq!(t.state, TicketState::Open);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn wire_roundtrip() {\n        for code in 0..=4u8 {\n            let st = TicketState::from_wire(code).unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(st.wire(), code);\n        }\n        assert_eq!(TicketState::from_wire(9), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn conversation_filters_by_channel() {\n        let mut c = Conversation::new();\n        c.push(Message { channel: Channel::Email, author: "a".into(), body: "1".into(), ts: 0 });\n        c.push(Message { channel: Channel::Chat, author: "b".into(), body: "2".into(), ts: 1 });\n        c.push(Message { channel: Channel::Email, author: "c".into(), body: "3".into(), ts: 2 });\n        assert_eq!(c.by_channel(Channel::Email).len(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(c.by_channel(Channel::Chat).len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(c.by_channel(Channel::Sms).len(), 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn canned_responses() {\n        assert_eq!(canned_response("greeting"), Some("Hi! How can we help you today?"));\n        assert_eq!(canned_response("nope"), None);\n    }\n}\n	7217	-1	-1		431ffcf03bc9ebc72e0dfbcdc3d01a6443fea484f5f06f8e3717223e91a5ff655d70b4807ec4e446d75d942ba9c11d32cc3f1d363b8a1eeaa86bf04d66aeaade08b5d4eb267b933124d1310ba6df75c96290246a29da4f6f9880af8f7b0f65be01225237b0ea52e1ac391e1e9e4c6f30659761eb9e91164f872165b67920b540
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/json.rs	json · 688 lines	//! `kernel::json` — hand-rolled, always-compiled, pure-`std` JSON parse + serialize primitive.\n//!\n//! Roadmap item 31 §4 (enactment half). This is the PARSE-side home for the serde carriers\n//! being cut over (Phase A: `agent-facade`, `skillspector-rs`). It is deliberately SEPARATE from\n//! `kernel::fdr::json` (which is *serialize*-only, fixed-schema, golden-pinned — see its module\n//! doc): bolting a parser onto that writer would break the narrowness that is its whole value.\n//!\n//! Scope (honest, per §4.2): bounded config / API / JSON-RPC shapes with an explicit max depth\n//! and max input length. This is NOT a hardened parser for the attacker-facing HTTP boundary —\n//! `tools/native-spa-server` deliberately KEEPS `serde_json` there (a decade of fuzz hardening),\n//! and cutting it over would be a security regression until this hand-roll has carried equivalent\n//! differential-fuzz load (§4.4 Phase-B trigger). Every malformed input returns `Err` (never a\n//! panic, never a wrong-but-silent value); deep nesting is bounded, not stack-exhausting.\n//!\n//! `serde_json` is retained ONLY as a **dev-dependency differential oracle** (see\n//! `kernel/tests/json_oracle.rs`); it sits outside the `-e no-dev` zero-dep proof surface, so the\n//! kernel's empty allowlist stays empty.\n\nuse alloc::borrow::ToOwned;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse core::fmt::Write as _;\n\n/// Maximum nesting depth the parser will descend before refusing (degrade-closed vs stack\n/// exhaustion on adversarial deep input). Comfortably above any real config/API/RPC shape.\npub const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 128;\n\n/// Maximum input length the parser will accept, in bytes. Above any real carrier payload; a\n/// bound, not a promise of unbounded-input safety.\npub const MAX_LEN: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;\n\n/// A parsed JSON value. Mirrors the `serde_json::Value` shape and the accessor subset the\n/// carriers actually use (`get`, `as_str`, `as_array`, `as_i64`, `as_f64`, `as_bool`). Numbers\n/// are split into `Int`/`Float` (like `serde_json`'s integer/float distinction) so JSON-RPC ids\n/// and integer counts round-trip without a spurious decimal point.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum Value {\n    Null,\n    Bool(bool),\n    Int(i64),\n    Float(f64),\n    Str(String),\n    Array(Vec<Value>),\n    /// Insertion-ordered members. Duplicate keys are preserved as parsed; `get` returns the\n    /// LAST occurrence, matching `serde_json`'s last-wins semantics.\n    Object(Vec<(String, Value)>),\n}\n\n/// A parse failure. Degrade-closed: the caller gets `Err`, never a panic.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Error {\n    pub msg: &'static str,\n    /// Byte offset into the input where the failure was detected.\n    pub pos: usize,\n}\n\nimpl core::fmt::Display for Error {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {\n        write!(f, "json parse error at byte {}: {}", self.pos, self.msg)\n    }\n}\nimpl core::error::Error for Error {}\n\nimpl Value {\n    /// Object member lookup (last-wins on duplicate keys). `None` for non-objects/missing keys.\n    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&Value> {\n        match self {\n            Value::Object(m) => m.iter().rev().find(|(k, _)| k == key).map(|(_, v)| v),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        match self {\n            Value::Str(s) => Some(s),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n    pub fn as_array(&self) -> Option<&[Value]> {\n        match self {\n            Value::Array(a) => Some(a),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n    pub fn as_bool(&self) -> Option<bool> {\n        match self {\n            Value::Bool(b) => Some(*b),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n    pub fn as_i64(&self) -> Option<i64> {\n        match self {\n            Value::Int(i) => Some(*i),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n    pub fn as_f64(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n        match self {\n            Value::Int(i) => Some(*i as f64),\n            Value::Float(f) => Some(*f),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n    pub fn is_null(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, Value::Null)\n    }\n\n    /// Serialize to compact JSON (no insignificant whitespace). Valid RFC 8259 output:\n    /// strings are minimally escaped, non-ASCII passes through as UTF-8, `Int` prints with no\n    /// decimal point, `Float` uses Rust's shortest round-tripping `Display`.\n    pub fn to_string(&self) -> String {\n        let mut s = String::new();\n        self.write_to(&mut s);\n        s\n    }\n\n    fn write_to(&self, out: &mut String) {\n        match self {\n            Value::Null => out.push_str("null"),\n            Value::Bool(true) => out.push_str("true"),\n            Value::Bool(false) => out.push_str("false"),\n            Value::Int(i) => {\n                let _ = write!(out, "{}", i);\n            }\n            Value::Float(f) => {\n                if !f.is_finite() {\n                    // JSON has no NaN/Inf — degrade-closed to null rather than emit invalid JSON.\n                    out.push_str("null");\n                } else {\n                    // Rust's `{}` prints large-magnitude floats in full NON-scientific integer form\n                    // (e.g. 2.3e136 → a 137-digit integer). A JSON reader re-parses that integer with\n                    // different rounding — no round-trip. When the shortest form is a bare integer\n                    // AND the magnitude is past 2^53 (where f64 can no longer represent every integer\n                    // exactly), emit scientific `{:e}` instead — it always round-trips and matches\n                    // serde_json's ryu style. Normal-range numbers keep the readable `{}` form.\n                    let s = format!("{}", f);\n                    if !s.contains(['.', 'e', 'E']) && f.abs() >= 9_007_199_254_740_992.0 {\n                        let _ = write!(out, "{:e}", f);\n                    } else {\n                        out.push_str(&s);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Value::Str(s) => write_json_string(s, out),\n            Value::Array(a) => {\n                out.push('[');\n                for (i, v) in a.iter().enumerate() {\n                    if i > 0 {\n                        out.push(',');\n                    }\n                    v.write_to(out);\n                }\n                out.push(']');\n            }\n            Value::Object(m) => {\n                out.push('{');\n                for (i, (k, v)) in m.iter().enumerate() {\n                    if i > 0 {\n                        out.push(',');\n                    }\n                    write_json_string(k, out);\n                    out.push(':');\n                    v.write_to(out);\n                }\n                out.push('}');\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ---- Value construction helpers (for carriers that BUILD output, e.g. skillspector-rs) --------\nimpl From<&str> for Value {\n    fn from(s: &str) -> Self {\n        Value::Str(s.to_owned())\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/spectral_cache.rs	spectral_cache · 717 lines	//! spectral_cache.rs — `DecompCache`: a content-addressed spectral\n//! eigensolve cache (P11 §2).\n//!\n//! Zero-dep kernel primitive (no operator decisions, non-red-line). The kernel\n//! spends real time in `spectral::eigenvalues` (Faddeev-LeVerrier +\n//! Durand-Kerner) every time `markov` re-analyses a window. When the underlying\n//! operator/transition matrix is unchanged the spectrum is identical, so we\n//! cache it behind a content-address string (a store `snapshot_root`, or a\n//! deterministic hash of matrix contents).\n//!\n//! The honesty device is the monotonic `recomputes` counter — a *falsifier*.\n//! It must be exactly 0 across repeated identical roots (proving we are NOT\n//! thrashing — recomputing on every call) and must increment by exactly 1 on a\n//! genuine root change (proving we are NOT serving a stale stuck cache). The\n//! initial population of an empty cache is not a "recompute"; only a change of\n//! key is. Two downstream tests below pin this invariant.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n\nuse crate::csr::{Csr, NormalizedTile, TileAddress, FNV_OFFSET_64, FNV_PRIME_64};\nuse crate::spectral::{classify_drift, DriftClass};\n\n/// Cached spectral decomposition payload.\n/// `(basis, values)` — `basis` is the (possibly deferred) eigenvector matrix\n/// and `values` is the eigenvalue payload. For the kernel's vectorless\n/// spectrum usage (`slem`, `dominant_period`) the eigenvalue moduli are the\n/// operative quantity, so the cache stores them directly; an eigenvector basis\n/// may be supplied by callers that solve for one. This is the "simpler payload\n/// representing the eigensolve result" the P11 §2 spec allows.\npub type Decomp = (Vec<Vec<f64>>, Vec<f64>);\n\n/// Content-addressed cache for an expensive eigen-decomposition.\n///\n/// * `key`     — the content-address of the cached input (None until first fill).\n/// * `cached`  — the cached decomposition `(basis, values)`, or None when empty.\n/// * `recomputes` — monotonic count of *key changes* that forced a recompute.\n///\n/// Usable behind `&mut` only; no interior mutex — keeps it std-only and simple.\npub struct DecompCache {\n    key: Option<String>,\n    cached: Option<Decomp>,\n    recomputes: AtomicU64,\n}\n\nimpl DecompCache {\n    /// Empty cache: no key, no payload, zero recomputes.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            key: None,\n            cached: None,\n            recomputes: AtomicU64::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return the cached decomposition for `root`, recomputing ONLY when the\n    /// root differs from the cached key.\n    ///\n    /// * HIT (`root == self.key`): the closure is NOT called and `recomputes`\n    ///   is NOT touched — the cached reference is returned directly.\n    /// * MISS: `compute()` runs, the result is stored, `self.key = root`, and\n    ///   `recomputes` is incremented by exactly 1 — **but only when an existing\n    ///   key is being replaced**. The very first population of an empty cache\n    ///   is initialisation, not a recompute, so it does not increment.\n    pub fn get_or_recompute(&mut self, root: &str, compute: impl FnOnce() -> Decomp) -> &Decomp {\n        if self.key.as_deref() == Some(root) {\n            // HIT — serve the cached decomposition, no recompute.\n            return self.cached.as_ref().expect("key set implies payload set");\n        }\n        // MISS — solve, store, and (if we are replacing a prior key) count it.\n        let replacing = self.key.is_some();\n        let payload = compute();\n        self.cached = Some(payload);\n        self.key = Some(root.to_string());\n        if replacing {\n            self.recomputes.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n        }\n        self.cached.as_ref().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Monotonic count of recomputations forced by a root change (read atomically).\n    pub fn recomputes(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.recomputes.load(Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for DecompCache {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Deterministic content-address for a real matrix — FNV-1a 64 over a canonical\n/// (row-major, index-framed) byte layout. Two matrices with identical contents\n/// yield the same root on every platform/run; any entry change changes the root.\n/// Keeps the cache honest and content-addressed without a store handle.\n///\n/// DEMOTED to private (was `pub`) by BLUEPRINT-P-B §3.2: the raw-matrix hash\n/// ceases to be a public entry point — the compiler is the gate. The only\n/// content-address that should ever be hashed for a tile is\n/// [`NormalizedTile::content_address`]. This function survives because the\n/// adversarial test reconstructs the raw path inline (it does NOT call it), and\n/// `RetainedBase::admit` is the sole caller here that needs a raw digest.\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nfn matrix_content_address(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> String {\n    let mut h = FNV_OFFSET_64;\n    for (i, row) in a.iter().enumerate() {\n        // frame the row index so a value bleeding across rows can't collide\n        h ^= (i as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);\n        h = h.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME_64);\n        for &x in row {\n            h ^= x.to_bits();\n            h = h.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME_64);\n        }\n    }\n    format!("{:016x}", h)\n}\n\n/// Bit pattern of a canonical quiet-NaN used by [`canonical_content_address`] to\n/// map any NaN input to a single deterministic id (so corrupted tiles are\n/// content-addressed identically across runs/platforms).\npub const CANONICAL_QUIET_NAN: u64 = 0x7ff8_0000_0000_0000;\n\n/// Normalise one entry to its hashable bit pattern on the canonical path:\n/// * `-0.0` and `+0.0` both collapse to the `+0.0` bit pattern (value-identical\n///   tiles must share a key);\n/// * any NaN folds to [`CANONICAL_QUIET_NAN`] (deterministic corruption id).\n/// No transcendental appears here — only `f64::to_bits`, which is exact.\n#[inline]\nfn canonical_bits(v: f64) -> u64 {\n    if v == 0.0 {\n        // collapses both -0.0 and +0.0 to +0.0 bits\n        0.0f64.to_bits()\n    } else if v.is_nan() {\n        CANONICAL_QUIET_NAN\n    } else {\n        v.to_bits()\n    }\n}\n\n/// In debug builds, flag NaN input up front (the canonical hash is for\n/// well-formed numeric tiles; NaN is corruption that must be surfaced, not\n/// silently canonicalised). Release builds keep NaN → `CANONICAL_QUIET_NAN`\n/// for deterministic cross-run ids (adversarial determinism test).\n#[cfg(debug_assertions)]\nfn assert_no_nan(a: &[Vec<f64>]) {\n    for row in a {\n        for &x in row {\n            assert!(\n                !x.is_nan(),\n                "canonical_content_address: NaN-bearing tile is flagged in debug (release folds to CANONICAL_QUIET_NAN)"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Canonical (scale-invariant) content-address for `slem_cached`.\n///\n/// Global-pivot scaling, NOT row-stochastic normalisation: row-normalising\n/// would equate matrices that differ by *per-row* scale and have genuinely\n/// different spectra (a worse bug than the one being fixed). Global-pivot\n/// scaling equates exactly the uniform-scale family `{c·W : c > 0}`, whose\n/// spectra differ only by the known factor `c`.\n///\n/// Mechanics (hazard-safety-as-math, blueprint item 6): let `p` = |first\n/// nonzero entry| in row-major order. Hash the entries `x / p` with the same\n/// FNV-1a framing as [`matrix_content_address`], mapping `-0.0 → +0.0` and any\n/// NaN → [`CANONICAL_QUIET_NAN`]. IEEE-754 mandates correctly-rounded division,\n/// so for an exactly-scaled family (`c·x` representable exactly — integer\n/// counts, power-of-two `c`) `fl((c·x)/(c·p)) ≡ fl(x/p)` bitwise on every\n/// conforming target. No summation and no transcendental appear on this path\n/// (both would break scale-commutativity), so the two V2 §A constraints hold\n/// structurally. Zero matrix ⇒ no pivot ⇒ hash raw entries (well-defined).\npub fn canonical_content_address(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> String {\n    #[cfg(debug_assertions)]\n    assert_no_nan(a);\n\n    let mut h = FNV_OFFSET_64;\n\n    // pivot p = |first nonzero entry| in row-major order\n    let mut pivot = 0.0f64;\n    'outer: for row in a {\n        for &x in row {\n            if x != 0.0 {\n                pivot = x.abs();\n                break 'outer;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    for (i, row) in a.iter().enumerate() {\n        // frame the row index so a value bleeding across rows can't collide\n        h ^= (i as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);\n        h = h.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME_64);\n        for &x in row {\n            let v = if pivot > 0.0 { x / pivot } else { x };\n            h ^= canonical_bits(v);\n            h = h.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME_64);\n        }\n    }\n    format!("{:016x}", h)\n}\n\n/// Content-addressed `spectral::slem` (second-largest eigenvalue modulus) routed\n/// through a `DecompCache`. The expensive `eigenvalues` solve is performed only\n/// when the tile's canonical content-address changes; otherwise the cached\n/// spectrum is reused.\n///\n/// CHANGED SIGNATURE (BLUEPRINT-P-B §3.2 — the fix): the cache key AND the\n/// eigensolve input both derive from the SAME `NormalizedTile` — key/payload\n/// coherence by construction. `tile.content_address()` keys the cache, and\n/// `tile.to_dense()` is the operator eigensolved. For a row-stochastic canonical\n/// tile ρ = 1 exactly and SLEM is the operative quantity (precisely what\n/// `spectral::slem` measures); no semantic loss versus the raw path.\npub fn slem_cached(cache: &mut DecompCache, tile: &NormalizedTile) -> f64 {\n    let root = tile.content_address().as_hex();\n    let (_basis, values) = cache.get_or_recompute(&root, || {\n        let dense = tile.to_dense();\n        let eigs = crate::spectral::eigenvalues(&dense);\n        // vectorless usage only needs the eigenvalue moduli as the payload.\n        (\n            Vec::new(),\n            eigs.iter().map(|e| e.abs()).collect::<Vec<f64>>(),\n        )\n    });\n    let mut mags: Vec<f64> = values.clone();\n    crate::sort_by_f64_desc(&mut mags, |&m| m);\n    if mags.len() > 1 {\n        mags[1]\n    } else {\n        0.0\n    }\n}\n\n/// A drift-admitted, canonicalized, content-addressed retained snapshot — node\n/// (b) of the doc-19 pipeline, with (d) as its ONLY door.\n///\n/// INVARIANT (type-encoded): the only constructor is `admit`, which runs\n/// `classify_drift` on the RAW operator BEFORE canonicalization+addressing.\n/// A retained Unstable base is UNREPRESENTABLE.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct RetainedBase {\n    tile: NormalizedTile, // private\n    address: TileAddress, // private\n    epoch: u64,           // private — logical, max-merge, NO wall-clock\n}\n\n/// Law-pole rejection (mirror of `CommitError::Rejected` — never retry; nothing\n/// retained).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SnapshotRejected {\n    /// ρ > 1 + BAND on the raw rebuilt operator: retaining it would snapshot a\n    /// divergent dynamics. "Organism endures by NOT persisting" (same law as\n    /// `event_log.rs` drift-gate).\n    UnstableSpectrum,\n}\n\nimpl RetainedBase {\n    /// Verify-before-persist, INLINE on the causal path: the `RetainedBase` the\n    /// caller wants cannot exist unless the gate ran. Order inside:\n    /// `classify_drift(raw.to_dense())` → reject Unstable →\n    /// `NormalizedTile::canonicalize(raw)` → `content_address()` → construct.\n    ///\n    /// The gate runs on the RAW rebuilt operator `W` (the dynamics a rebuild\n    /// would induce); the hash runs on the canonical form. Two forms, two roles,\n    /// one pipeline — `(e)→(c)→(a)→(b) gated by (d)`. A row-stochastic tile has\n    /// ρ = 1 always, so gating on the normalized form would be vacuous (never\n    /// reject) — the anti-vacuity finding of BLUEPRINT-P-B §4.2.\n    pub fn admit(raw: &Csr, epoch: u64) -> Result<RetainedBase, SnapshotRejected> {\n        if matches!(classify_drift(&raw.to_dense()), DriftClass::Unstable) {\n            return Err(SnapshotRejected::UnstableSpectrum);\n        }\n        let tile = NormalizedTile::canonicalize(raw);\n        let address = tile.content_address();\n        Ok(RetainedBase {\n            tile,\n            address,\n            epoch,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Read-only view of the canonical retained tile.\n    pub fn tile(&self) -> &NormalizedTile {\n        &self.tile\n    }\n\n    /// Content-address of the retained tile.\n    pub fn address(&self) -> TileAddress {\n        self.address\n    }\n\n    /// Logical retention epoch (no wall-clock).\n    pub fn epoch(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.epoch\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Fixed dummy decomposition used by the falsifier tests.\n    fn dummy() -> Decomp {\n        (vec![vec![1.0, 0.0], vec![0.0, 1.0]], vec![0.5, 0.3])\n    }\n\n    /// FALSIFIER (no-thrash): 1000 `get_or_recompute` calls with the SAME root\n    /// must NOT increment `recomputes` — the closure runs exactly once (the\n    /// initial population) and every subsequent call is a HIT. If the cache\n    /// thrashed (recomputed on every call) this would be ~1000, not 0.\n    #[test]\n    fn decomp_cache_zero_recomputes_on_unchanged_root() {\n        let mut cache = DecompCache::new();\n        let root = "root::unchanged";\n        let mut compute_calls = 0usize;\n        for _ in 0..1000 {\n            let got = cache.get_or_recompute(root, || {\n                compute_calls += 1;\n                dummy()\n            });\n            // the returned decomposition must be the dummy, every time (no stale).\n            assert_eq!(got.1, vec![0.5, 0.3]);\n        }\n        assert_eq!(compute_calls, 1, "compute must run exactly once (warmup)");\n        assert_eq!(\n            cache.recomputes(),\n            0,\n            "identical root ⇒ zero recomputes (no thrashing)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// FALSIFIER (no-stale): after the 1000 identical calls, a root CHANGE must\n    /// increment `recomputes` by exactly 1 and return the NEW decomposition. If\n    /// the cache were stuck/serving-stale it would stay 0 and return the old\n    /// payload; if it thrashed it would be >1.\n    #[test]\n    fn decomp_cache_exactly_one_recompute_on_change() {\n        let mut cache = DecompCache::new();\n        let root_a = "root::A";\n        for _ in 0..1000 {\n            cache.get_or_recompute(root_a, dummy);\n        }\n        assert_eq!(cache.recomputes(), 0);\n\n        let root_b = "root::B";\n        // Scope `got` so its `&Decomp` mutable borrow ends before we query\n        // `recomputes()` (an immutable borrow). Ending the &Decomp borrow first\n        // is the natural usage; the cache stays a `&mut`-only API.\n        let vals_b = {\n            let got = cache.get_or_recompute(root_b, || {\n                (vec![vec![2.0, 0.0], vec![0.0, 2.0]], vec![0.9, 0.7])\n            });\n            got.1.clone()\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            cache.recomputes(),\n            1,\n            "exactly one recompute on a genuine root change"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(vals_b, vec![0.9, 0.7], "new decomposition is served");\n\n        // and a second identical call on the new root stays a hit (still 1).\n        let vals_b2 = {\n            let got2 = cache.get_or_recompute(root_b, dummy);\n            got2.1.clone()\n        };\n        assert_eq!(cache.recomputes(), 1, "no thrash on the new root either");\n        assert_eq!(vals_b2, vec![0.9, 0.7]);\n    }\n\n    // ── T3/A5 (W1-L10, doc-19 bridge-gap #1) RED tests ────────────────────────\n    /// Integer-valued fixture tile whose uniform-scale family is exactly\n    /// representable (power-of-two and small-int scales). This is the canonical\n    /// "logical tile" two nodes may build at different scale.\n    fn fixture_tile() -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n        // A simple stochastic-like matrix of small integers.\n        vec![\n            vec![1.0, 2.0, 0.0],\n            vec![3.0, 1.0, 2.0],\n            vec![0.0, 1.0, 3.0],\n        ]\n    }\n\n    /// Multiply every entry of `a` by `c` (uniform scale).\n    fn scale(a: &[Vec<f64>], c: f64) -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n        a.iter()\n            .map(|row| row.iter().map(|&x| x * c).collect::<Vec<f64>>())\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Build a 1×1 tile containing exactly `x`.\n    fn tile_with(x: f64) -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n        vec![vec![x]]\n    }\n\n    /// RED (scale-invariance bug): `W`, `2·W`, `3·W` are the same logical tile;\n    /// the cache must fill once and HIT twice → `recomputes() == 0`. Today the\n    /// raw hash keyed on `to_bits` makes each scale a distinct key ⇒ 2 recomputes.\n    /// TODAY this FAILS (recomputes == 2) — proving the bug live before the fix.\n    #[test]\n    fn slem_cached_scale_invariant_key_and_payload() {\n        let w = fixture_tile();\n        let w_tile = crate::csr::NormalizedTile::from_dense(&w);\n        let mut cache = DecompCache::new();\n        let s1 = slem_cached(&mut cache, &w_tile);\n        let w2 = scale(&w, 2.0);\n        let w2_tile = crate::csr::NormalizedTile::from_dense(&w2);\n        let w3 = scale(&w, 3.0);\n        let w3_tile = crate::csr::NormalizedTile::from_dense(&w3);\n        let s2 = slem_cached(&mut cache, &w2_tile);\n        let s3 = slem_cached(&mut cache, &w3_tile);\n        assert_eq!(\n            cache.recomputes(),\n            0,\n            "W, 2W, 3W share one canonical key ⇒ zero recomputes"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            (s2 - s1).abs() < 1e-12 && (s3 - s1).abs() < 1e-12,\n            "W, 2W, 3W normalize to the SAME tile ⇒ identical slem (s1={s1}, s2={s2}, s3={s3})"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// RED (`-0.0`/`+0.0`): value-identical but bit-distinct tiles must canonicalise\n    /// to the SAME id. Today `to_bits` differs for -0.0 vs +0.0 ⇒ distinct roots.\n    /// TODAY this FAILS (ids differ) — proving the latent case live before the fix.\n    #[test]\n    fn neg_zero_and_pos_zero_are_the_same_tile() {\n        assert_eq!(\n            canonical_content_address(&tile_with(0.0)),\n            canonical_content_address(&tile_with(-0.0)),\n            "-0.0 and +0.0 must canonicalise to the same content id"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── T3/A5 adversarial guards (designed to break a wrong fix) ──────────────\n\n    /// ADVERSARIAL (i) over-normalization guard: row-stochastic normalisation\n    /// would equate `W` with `D·W` for DISTINCT per-row factors D — but those\n    /// matrices have genuinely different spectra, so they MUST keep distinct\n    /// canonical keys. This is the test that goes RED if an implementer\n    /// "helpfully" switches to per-row normalisation.\n    #[test]\n    fn distinct_per_row_scale_does_not_collide() {\n        let w = fixture_tile();\n        // D·W with DISTINCT per-row factors (2,1,3): NOT a uniform scale.\n        let dw = vec![\n            vec![2.0 * w[0][0], 2.0 * w[0][1], 2.0 * w[0][2]],\n            vec![1.0 * w[1][0], 1.0 * w[1][1], 1.0 * w[1][2]],\n            vec![3.0 * w[2][0], 3.0 * w[2][1], 3.0 * w[2][2]],\n        ];\n        assert_ne!(\n            canonical_content_address(&w),\n            canonical_content_address(&dw),\n            "per-row scaling changes the spectrum ⇒ must NOT share a canonical key"\n        );\n        // Sanity: it is still scale-invariant under a UNIFORM scale (2·W == 4·W key).\n        assert_eq!(\n            canonical_content_address(&scale(&w, 2.0)),\n            canonical_content_address(&scale(&w, 4.0)),\n            "uniform scale family MUST collide"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// ADVERSARIAL (iii) all-zero tile: id is stable (same across calls) and\n    /// distinct from a nonzero tile. No pivot ⇒ raw-hash branch must be sound.\n    #[test]\n    fn all_zero_tile_stable_and_distinct() {\n        let zero = vec![vec![0.0, 0.0], vec![0.0, 0.0]];\n        assert_eq!(\n            canonical_content_address(&zero),\n            canonical_content_address(&zero),\n            "zero tile id is stable across calls"\n        );\n        assert_ne!(\n            canonical_content_address(&zero),\n            canonical_content_address(&tile_with(1.0)),\n            "zero tile id is distinct from a nonzero tile"\n        );\n        // -0.0 in a zero tile must still equal a +0.0 zero tile.\n        let nzero = vec![vec![-0.0, 0.0], vec![0.0, -0.0]];\n        assert_eq!(\n            canonical_content_address(&zero),\n            canonical_content_address(&nzero),\n            "zero tile with -0.0 entries == zero tile with +0.0 entries"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// ADVERSARIAL (ii, release) NaN-bearing tile: deterministic id across runs.\n    /// Release builds fold NaN → `CANONICAL_QUIET_NAN`, so two NaNs hash to the\n    /// SAME id (corruption is content-addressed identically across runs).\n    #[cfg(not(debug_assertions))]\n    #[test]\n    fn nan_tile_deterministic_id_across_runs() {\n        let nan_tile = vec![vec![f64::NAN, 1.0], vec![2.0, f64::NAN]];\n        let id_a = canonical_content_address(&nan_tile);\n        let id_b = canonical_content_address(&nan_tile);\n        assert_eq!(id_a, id_b, "NaN tile ⇒ deterministic id across runs");\n        // A different layout must not accidentally collide with the NaN id.\n        assert_ne!(\n            id_a,\n            canonical_content_address(&vec![vec![1.0, 1.0], vec![2.0, 1.0]]),\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// ADVERSARIAL (ii, debug) NaN-bearing tile is flagged. In debug builds the\n    /// `debug_assert!` must FIRE on NaN input (corruption surfaced, not masked).\n    #[cfg(debug_assertions)]\n    #[test]\n    fn nan_tile_is_flagged_in_debug() {\n        let nan_tile = vec![vec![f64::NAN, 1.0], vec![2.0, 3.0]];\n        let res = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| {\n            canonical_content_address(&nan_tile);\n        });\n        assert!(\n            res.is_err(),\n            "debug build must panic (debug_assert fires) on NaN input"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── P-B (BLUEPRINT-P-B §5): normalize-before-hash type invariant ─────────\n\n    /// Reconstruct the OLD raw-FNV path inline (the body of the now-private\n    /// `matrix_content_address`) so the hazard stays proven forever: two nodes\n    /// that hash the SAME logical tile at two scales MUST diverge on the raw\n    /// path, and MUST converge once normalized.\n    fn raw_fnv_path(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> String {\n        const OFFSET: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;\n        const PRIME: u64 = 0x0000_0100_0000_01b3;\n        let mut h = OFFSET;\n        for (i, row) in a.iter().enumerate() {\n            h ^= (i as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);\n            h = h.wrapping_mul(PRIME);\n            for &x in row {\n                h ^= x.to_bits();\n                h = h.wrapping_mul(PRIME);\n            }\n        }\n        format!("{:016x}", h)\n    }\n\n    /// ADVERSARIAL (permanent RED-keeping test) — reproduces the bug as its own\n    /// clause (i) and the fix as clause (ii):\n    ///   (i)  the raw FNV path (reconstructed inline) yields DIFFERENT hashes for\n    ///        tile `A` and `B = 2^k·A` — the divergence two nodes WOULD get;\n    ///   (ii) `NormalizedTile::from_dense(A).content_address() ==\n    ///        NormalizedTile::from_dense(B).content_address()` — the fix.\n    /// If (i) ever fails, the raw path stopped diverging and the whole design\n    /// premise must be re-derived.\n    #[test]\n    fn adversarial_two_node_hash_divergence_without_normalization() {\n        // A simple stochastic-like tile of small integers.\n        let a = vec![\n            vec![1.0, 2.0, 0.0],\n            vec![3.0, 1.0, 2.0],\n            vec![0.0, 1.0, 3.0],\n        ];\n        // B = 4·A (a power-of-two scale ⇒ exactly representable, so the two nodes\n        // are the SAME logical tile at a different scale).\n        let b: Vec<Vec<f64>> = a\n            .iter()\n            .map(|row| row.iter().map(|&x| x * 4.0).collect())\n            .collect();\n\n        // (i) the raw path the old code used MUST diverge — this is the hazard.\n        let raw_a = raw_fnv_path(&a);\n        let raw_b = raw_fnv_path(&b);\n        assert_ne!(raw_a, raw_b, "raw FNV path MUST diverge on scale (the bug)");\n\n        // (ii) the normalized content-address MUST converge — the fix.\n        let addr_a = crate::csr::NormalizedTile::from_dense(&a).content_address();\n        let addr_b = crate::csr::NormalizedTile::from_dense(&b).content_address();\n        assert_eq!(\n            addr_a, addr_b,\n            "two nodes at different scales of the SAME logical tile MUST share a canonical address"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Guards the §3.3 key/payload-poisoning class: two raw tiles with the same\n    /// canonical form get the SAME address AND `slem_cached` serves the IDENTICAL\n    /// slem for both (cache HIT, `recomputes == 0` across the pair).\n    #[test]\n    fn canonical_address_and_spectrum_derive_from_same_object() {\n        let tile = vec![\n            vec![1.0, 2.0, 0.0],\n            vec![3.0, 1.0, 2.0],\n            vec![0.0, 1.0, 3.0],\n        ];\n        let scaled = tile\n            .iter()\n            .map(|row| row.iter().map(|&x| x * 4.0).collect())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n        let nt = crate::csr::NormalizedTile::from_dense(&tile);\n        let ns = crate::csr::NormalizedTile::from_dense(&scaled);\n        // Same canonical object ⇒ same address.\n        assert_eq!(nt.content_address(), ns.content_address());\n\n        let mut cache = DecompCache::new();\n        let slem_first = slem_cached(&mut cache, &nt);\n        // Second, a DIFFERENT NormalizedTile object but the SAME canonical form.\n        let slem_second = slem_cached(&mut cache, &ns);\n        assert!(\n            (slem_first - slem_second).abs() < 1e-12,\n            "same canonical object ⇒ identical slem"\n        );\n        // And the cross-scale second call reused the shared key (no recompute).\n        assert_eq!(\n            cache.recomputes(),\n            0,\n            "same canonical address ⇒ cache HIT, recomputes == 0"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// The drift gate REFUSES an Unstable (ρ>1) raw rebuild, and ADMITS a Damped\n    /// (ρ<1) one — constructing a `RetainedBase` whose address matches the\n    /// canonical tile's address and whose epoch is the requested one.\n    #[test]\n    fn unstable_raw_rebuild_is_refused_retention() {\n        // ρ = 2 raw operator (unstable dynamics). Use a 2×2 with diagonal 2.\n        let unstable = crate::csr::Csr::from_dense(&vec![vec![2.0, 0.0], vec![0.0, 2.0]]);\n        let res = RetainedBase::admit(&unstable, 7);\n        assert_eq!(\n            res,\n            Err(SnapshotRejected::UnstableSpectrum),\n            "Unstable rebuild MUST be refused retention"\n        );\n\n        // ρ = 0.5 raw operator (damped). Diagonal 0.5 ⇒ ρ = 0.5.\n        let damped = crate::csr::Csr::from_dense(&vec![vec![0.5, 0.0], vec![0.0, 0.5]]);\n        let retained = RetainedBase::admit(&damped, 11).expect("damped admit Ok");\n        let expected_addr = crate::csr::NormalizedTile::canonicalize(&damped).content_address();\n        assert_eq!(\n            retained.address(),\n            expected_addr,\n            "address == canonical tile address"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(retained.epoch(), 11, "epoch preserved");\n    }\n\n    /// Anti-vacuity chaos test (the intentionally-breaking one): a raw operator\n    /// with ρ = 2 whose row-normalized form necessarily has ρ = 1 (Resonant)\n    /// MUST STILL be refused. If a future refactor moves the gate after\n    /// canonicalization, this test goes red.\n    #[test]\n    fn drift_gate_measures_raw_dynamics_not_normalized_form() {\n        // Raw operator with a large uniform scale k ⇒ spectral_radius = k.\n        // Its row-normalized form is the uniform self-loop (ρ = 1, Resonant),\n        // which a vacuous (normalized-form) gate would ADMIT. The gate must run\n        // on the RAW operator and REJECT.\n        let k = 2.0;\n        let raw = crate::csr::Csr::from_dense(&vec![vec![k, 0.0], vec![0.0, k]]);\n        let res = RetainedBase::admit(&raw, 3);\n        assert_eq!(\n            res,\n            Err(SnapshotRejected::UnstableSpectrum),\n            "gate measures RAW ρ=2, not the normalized ρ=1 form ⇒ reject"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// FAIL-CLOSED (gap-audit round-2): a raw rebuild carrying a NaN/±inf entry\n    /// MUST be refused retention. Pre-fix, `classify_drift` let NaN slip through\n    /// `f64::max` as `Resonant`, so the poisoned snapshot was silently admitted.\n    #[test]\n    fn nan_poisoned_raw_rebuild_is_refused_retention() {\n        let poisoned = crate::csr::Csr::from_dense(&vec![vec![0.0, f64::NAN], vec![0.0, 0.0]]);\n        assert_eq!(\n            RetainedBase::admit(&poisoned, 7),\n            Err(SnapshotRejected::UnstableSpectrum),\n            "NaN-poisoned rebuild MUST be refused (was silently admitted pre-fix)"\n        );\n\n        let inf_poisoned =\n            crate::csr::Csr::from_dense(&vec![vec![f64::INFINITY, 0.0], vec![0.0, 0.0]]);\n        assert_eq!(\n            RetainedBase::admit(&inf_poisoned, 7),\n            Err(SnapshotRejected::UnstableSpectrum),\n            "±inf-poisoned rebuild MUST be refused"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// N2 (structural canonicality): `from_dense` with explicit `0.0` entries and\n    /// permuted insertion order reaches the SAME `TileAddress` as the clean\n    /// build.
```
