In a spectral/fractal system, classic comparisons (a > b, x == y) lose\n//! information. Delta calculus compares the CHANGE between states, not the\n//! absolute values. This is the core comparison engine for trinary+trig+eigen.\n//!\n//! # Delta replaces comparison\n//!   Classic:  if a > b { act }\n//!   Delta:    if delta(a, b).magnitude > threshold { act }\n//!   Classic:  assert_eq!(x, y)\n//!   Delta:    assert!(delta(x, y).is_stable(threshold))\n//!\n//! # Operations\n//!   Δv = v₁ - v₀          → vector delta (direction + magnitude)\n//!   ∂t = t₁ - t₀          → time delta\n//!   rate = Δv / ∂t        → rate of change (velocity)\n//!   accel = Δ(rate) / ∂t  → acceleration (second derivative)\n//!   drift = cumulative Σ|Δv| → total system drift\n//!\n//! ZERO deps. Uses eigen, trig, trinary.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::eigen::{EigenDecomp, decompose};\nuse crate::trig::{Xyz, PhaseVector};\n\n// ─── Delta — the fundamental change primitive ─────────────────────────────\n\n/// A delta between two vectors. Carries magnitude, direction, and rate.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Delta {\n    pub components: Vec<f64>,  // v₁ - v₀\n    pub magnitude: f64,        // ||Δv||\n    pub ts_from: u64,\n    pub ts_to: u64,\n    pub rate: f64,             // magnitude / (t₁-t₀) in units/ms\n}\n\nimpl Delta {\n    /// Compute delta between two vectors at two timestamps.\n    pub fn between(v0: &[f64], ts0: u64, v1: &[f64], ts1: u64) -> Self {\n        let n = v0.len().min(v1.len());\n        let mut components = vec![0.0f64; n];\n        let mut mag_sq = 0.0f64;\n        for i in 0..n {\n            components[i] = v1[i] - v0[i];\n            mag_sq += components[i] * components[i];\n        }\n        let magnitude = crate::math::sqrt(mag_sq);\n        let dt = (ts1.saturating_sub(ts0) as f64).max(1.0);\n        Delta { components, magnitude, ts_from: ts0, ts_to: ts1, rate: magnitude / dt }\n    }\n\n    /// Is this delta significant? (magnitude > threshold).\n    pub fn is_significant(&self, threshold: f64) -> bool {\n        self.magnitude > threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Is the system stable? (rate < threshold — change is slowing down).\n    pub fn is_stable(&self, rate_threshold: f64) -> bool {\n        self.rate < rate_threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Normalized delta components: unit direction vector.\n    pub fn direction(&self) -> Vec<f64> {\n        if self.magnitude < 1e-15 { return vec![0.0; self.components.len()]; }\n        self.components.iter().map(|&c| c / self.magnitude).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Project delta onto a target direction: how much of the change is in this direction.\n    pub fn project(&self, direction: &[f64]) -> f64 {\n        let n = self.components.len().min(direction.len());\n        let mut dot = 0.0f64;\n        let mut dir_norm = 0.0f64;\n        for i in 0..n {\n            dot += self.components[i] * direction[i];\n            dir_norm += direction[i] * direction[i];\n        }\n        if dir_norm < 1e-15 { return 0.0; }\n        dot / crate::math::sqrt(dir_norm)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── EigenDelta — compare eigen decompositions ────────────────────────────\n\n/// Delta between two eigen decompositions. Measures spectral distance.\npub struct EigenDelta {\n    pub spectral_distance: f64,   // ||λ₁ - λ₀|| between dominant eigenvalues\n    pub mode_count_delta: isize,  // change in number of unstable modes\n    pub dominant_shift: f64,      // angle between dominant eigenvectors\n}\n\nimpl EigenDelta {\n    /// Compare two eigen decompositions.\n    pub fn between(d0: &EigenDecomp, d1: &EigenDecomp) -> Self {\n        let r0 = d0.spectral_radius();\n        let r1 = d1.spectral_radius();\n        let spectral_distance = (r1 - r0).abs();\n        let mode_count_delta = d1.unstable_count() as isize - d0.unstable_count() as isize;\n\n        let dominant_shift = match (d0.dominant(), d1.dominant()) {\n            (Some(a), Some(b)) => {\n                let n = a.dim().min(b.dim());\n                let mut dot = 0.0; let mut na = 0.0; let mut nb = 0.0;\n                for i in 0..n {\n                    dot += a.vector[i] * b.vector[i];\n                    na += a.vector[i] * a.vector[i];\n                    nb += b.vector[i] * b.vector[i];\n                }\n                if na < 1e-15 || nb < 1e-15 { 0.0 }\n                else { crate::math::acos((dot / (crate::math::sqrt(na) * crate::math::sqrt(nb)))) }\n            }\n            _ => 0.0,\n        };\n\n        EigenDelta { spectral_distance, mode_count_delta, dominant_shift }\n    }\n\n    /// Is this a significant spectral change?\n    pub fn is_significant(&self, dist_threshold: f64, shift_threshold: f64) -> bool {\n        self.spectral_distance > dist_threshold || self.dominant_shift > shift_threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Are new unstable modes appearing? (system becoming less stable).\n    pub fn is_destabilizing(&self) -> bool { self.mode_count_delta > 0 }\n}\n\n// ─── PhaseDelta — compare phase-space states ──────────────────────────────\n\n/// Delta in phase space between two PhaseVectors or Xyz states.\npub struct PhaseDelta {\n    pub angle_delta: f64,      // total angular drift (sum of phase differences)\n    pub xyz_distance: f64,     // Euclidean distance in xyz space\n    pub coherence: f64,        // dot-product coherence [0,1]: 1 = identical, 0 = orthogonal\n}\n\nimpl PhaseDelta {\n    pub fn between_phases(a: &PhaseVector, b: &PhaseVector) -> Self {\n        let n = a.phases.len().min(b.phases.len());\n        let mut angle_sum = 0.0f64;\n        for i in 0..n {\n            angle_sum += a.phases[i].distance(&b.phases[i]);\n        }\n        let angle_delta = angle_sum / n.max(1) as f64;\n        let coherence = a.dot(b).clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n        PhaseDelta { angle_delta, xyz_distance: 0.0, coherence }\n    }\n\n    pub fn between_xyz(a: &Xyz, b: &Xyz) -> Self {\n        PhaseDelta {\n            angle_delta: 0.0,\n            xyz_distance: a.distance(b),\n            coherence: 1.0 - a.dist_norm(b),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Significant if coherence drops below threshold.\n    pub fn is_significant(&self, coherence_threshold: f64) -> bool {\n        self.coherence < coherence_threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Phase drift rate: angle_delta / time.\n    pub fn drift_rate(&self, dt_ms: f64) -> f64 {\n        if dt_ms < 1.0 { return 0.0; }\n        self.angle_delta / dt_ms\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── DeltaTracker — cumulative drift monitoring ───────────────────────────\n\n/// Tracks cumulative changes between successive states. Alerts on regime change.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct DeltaTracker {\n    pub history: Vec<Delta>,\n    pub cumulative_drift: f64,\n    pub max_rate: f64,\n    pub alarm_threshold: f64,\n    pub alarm_rate: f64,\n}\n\nimpl DeltaTracker {\n    pub fn new(alarm_threshold: f64, alarm_rate: f64) -> Self {\n        DeltaTracker { history: Vec::new(), cumulative_drift: 0.0, max_rate: 0.0,\n            alarm_threshold, alarm_rate }\n    }\n\n    /// Push a new delta observation.\n    pub fn observe(&mut self, delta: Delta) {\n        self.cumulative_drift += delta.magnitude;\n        self.max_rate = self.max_rate.max(delta.rate);\n        self.history.push(delta);\n    }\n\n    /// Observe a state transition (computes delta internally).\n    pub fn observe_transition(&mut self, v0: &[f64], ts0: u64, v1: &[f64], ts1: u64) {\n        let d = Delta::between(v0, ts0, v1, ts1);\n        self.observe(d);\n    }\n\n    /// Is the system in alarm? d.magnitude).sum();\n        let recent_rate: f64 = self.history.iter().rev().take(window)\n            .map(|d| d.rate).fold(0.0, f64::max);\n        recent > self.alarm_threshold || recent_rate > self.alarm_rate\n    }\n\n    /// Reset cumulative drift (after handling alarm).\n    pub fn reset(&mut self) {\n        self.cumulative_drift = 0.0;\n        self.max_rate = 0.0;\n ## 7481 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/geo.rs · LongTerm

Summary: geo · 969 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/geo.rs	geo · 969 lines	//! Geo / route kinematics — RW-06 (pure-logic port into kernel authority).\n//!\n//! 1:1 port of the pure math that lived in `geo-anim.ts` (haversine/lerp/bearing/\n//! EMA/route-progress/ETA/snap/arriving) + `delivery-zone.ts` (ray-cast point-in-\n//! polygon). Zero DOM, zero floats on money (ETA is seconds, not currency).\n//!\n//! RED→GREEN GATE: Rust output == TS on a fixture (parity within tolerance);\n//! ray-cast parity on known polygons.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nconst EARTH_RADIUS_M: f64 = 6_371_000.0;\nconst DEG2RAD: f64 = core::f64::consts::PI / 180.0;\nconst RAD2DEG: f64 = 180.0 / core::f64::consts::PI;\n\n/// Great-circle distance in meters (haversine). Matches `haversineMeters`.\npub fn haversine_meters(a_lat: f64, a_lng: f64, b_lat: f64, b_lng: f64) -> f64 {\n    let (la1, la2) = (a_lat * DEG2RAD, b_lat * DEG2RAD);\n    let dlat = (b_lat - a_lat) * DEG2RAD;\n    let dlng = (b_lng - a_lng) * DEG2RAD;\n    let h = crate::math::powi(crate::math::sin((dlat / 2.0)), 2)\n        + crate::math::cos(la1) * crate::math::cos(la2) * crate::math::powi(crate::math::sin((dlng / 2.0)), 2);\n    2.0 * EARTH_RADIUS_M * crate::math::asin(crate::math::sqrt(h))\n}\n\n/// Linear interpolation between two lat/lng points (equirectangular approx for\n/// short hops). Matches `lerpLatLng`.\npub fn lerp_lat_lng(a_lat: f64, a_lng: f64, b_lat: f64, b_lng: f64, t: f64) -> (f64, f64) {\n    (a_lat + (b_lat - a_lat) * t, a_lng + (b_lng - a_lng) * t)\n}\n\n/// Initial bearing (compass degrees, 0=N, clockwise) from a→b. Matches `bearingDeg`.\npub fn bearing_deg(a_lat: f64, a_lng: f64, b_lat: f64, b_lng: f64) -> f64 {\n    let (la1, la2) = (a_lat * DEG2RAD, b_lat * DEG2RAD);\n    let dlng = (b_lng - a_lng) * DEG2RAD;\n    let y = crate::math::sin(dlng) * crate::math::cos(la2);\n    let x = crate::math::cos(la1) * crate::math::sin(la2) - crate::math::sin(la1) * crate::math::cos(la2) * crate::math::cos(dlng);\n    (crate::math::atan2(y, x) * RAD2DEG + 360.0) % 360.0\n}\n\n/// Exponential moving average step. Matches `emaNext`.\npub fn ema_next(prev: f64, sample: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 {\n    prev + alpha * (sample - prev)\n}\n\n/// Result of projecting a position onto a route polyline.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct RouteProgress {\n    /// Metres remaining from the projected point to the polyline end.\n    pub remaining_m: f64,\n    /// Closest point on the polyline to `pos` (snapped).\n    pub snapped: (f64, f64),\n    /// Index of the segment (endpoint `i`) the projection landed on.\n    pub segment_index: usize,\n}\n\n/// Total polyline length in meters (sum of haversine segment lengths).\n/// Matches `polylineLengthMeters`.\npub fn polyline_length_meters(poly: &[(f64, f64)]) -> f64 {\n    let mut total = 0.0;\n    for w in poly.windows(2) {\n        total += haversine_meters(w[0].0, w[0].1, w[1].0, w[1].1);\n    }\n    total\n}\n\n/// Project `pos` onto a route polyline (local equirectangular projection, valid\n/// at city scale) and return the snapped point + remaining metres to the end.\n/// Matches `progressAlongRoute(polyline, pos)` — full polyline projection, not a\n/// bare `t.clamp`. Picks the closest segment, clamps the projection to the\n/// segment, and measures remaining distance along the polyline to the terminus.\n/// `segment_index` is the index `i` of the segment's end node (`i∈[1,len-1]`).\npub fn progress_along_route(poly: &[(f64, f64)], pos: (f64, f64)) -> RouteProgress {\n    if poly.len() < 2 {\n        return RouteProgress {\n            remaining_m: 0.0,\n            snapped: pos,\n            segment_index: 0,\n        };\n    }\n    // Equirectangular scale at the mean latitude (city-scale approximation).\n    let mean_lat = poly.iter().map(|p| p.0).sum::<f64>() / poly.len() as f64;\n    let kx = EARTH_RADIUS_M * DEG2RAD * crate::math::cos(mean_lat * DEG2RAD);\n    let ky = EARTH_RADIUS_M * DEG2RAD;\n    let px = pos.1 * kx;\n    let py = pos.0 * ky;\n\n    // Find the segment whose projection of `pos` is closest, capture its end-node\n    // index and the snapped (lat,lng) point.\n    let mut best_seg = 0usize;\n    let mut best_dist2 = f64::MAX;\n    let mut snapped = pos;\n    for (i, w) in poly.windows(2).enumerate() {\n        let (ax, ay) = (w[0].1 * kx, w[0].0 * ky);\n        let (bx, by) = (w[1].1 * kx, w[1].0 * ky);\n        let dx = bx - ax;\n        let dy = by - ay;\n        let len2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;\n        let t = if len2 == 0.0 {\n            0.0\n        } else {\n            (((px - ax) * dx + (py - ay) * dy) / len2).clamp(0.0, 1.0)\n        };\n        let cx = ax + t * dx;\n        let cy = ay + t * dy;\n        let dist2 = crate::math::powi((px - cx), 2) + crate::math::powi((py - cy), 2);\n        if dist2 < best_dist2 {\n            best_dist2 = dist2;\n            best_seg = i + 1; // end-node index\n            snapped = (cy / ky, cx / kx);\n        }\n    }\n    if best_seg == 0 {\n        // Degenerate polyline (all identical points) → no projection.\n        return RouteProgress {\n            remaining_m: 0.0,\n            snapped: pos,\n            segment_index: 0,\n        };\n    }\n\n    // Remaining metres: along polyline from snapped point to the end node, then\n    // the tail of the polyline.\n    let mut remaining = 0.0;\n    // distance from snapped back to its segment start (we recompute the t).\n    let w = &poly[best_seg - 1..=best_seg];\n    let (ax, ay) = (w[0].1 * kx, w[0].0 * ky);\n    let (bx, by) = (w[1].1 * kx, w[1].0 * ky);\n    let dx = bx - ax;\n    let dy = by - ay;\n    let len2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;\n    let t = if len2 == 0.0 {\n        0.0\n    } else {\n        (((px - ax) * dx + (py - ay) * dy) / len2).clamp(0.0, 1.0)\n    };\n    // from snapped (at t on segment) to end node b\n    let seg_rem = (1.0 - t) * crate::math::sqrt((dx * dx + dy * dy));\n    remaining += seg_rem;\n    for s in (best_seg + 1)..poly.len() {\n        remaining += haversine_meters(poly[s - 1].0, poly[s - 1].1, poly[s].0, poly[s].1);\n    }\n\n    RouteProgress {\n        remaining_m: remaining,\n        snapped,\n        segment_index: best_seg,\n    }\n}\n\n/// ETA in seconds remaining given route pacing. `remaining_m` is the metres left,\n/// `total_m` the full route length, `baseline_s` the planned total time. Pace is\n/// `total_m / baseline_s`; fall back to ~5 m/s urban speed when `baseline_s<=0`\n/// or `total_m<=0`. Matches `etaSeconds(remaining,total,baseline)` from the TS\n/// oracle. Returns 0 when already at/over target.\npub fn eta_seconds(remaining_m: f64, total_m: f64, baseline_s: f64) -> f64 {\n    if remaining_m <= 0.0 {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    let speed = if baseline_s > 0.0 && total_m > 0.0 {\n        total_m / baseline_s\n    } else {\n        5.0 // urban fallback (m/s)\n    };\n    if speed <= 0.0 {\n        return f64::INFINITY;\n    }\n    (remaining_m / speed).max(0.0)\n}\n\n// ── P96 (BLUEPRINT-P96 §3): adaptive ETA from the courier's live ground speed ──\n// The static `eta_seconds` above is the load-bearing fallback. P96 routes the\n// courier's *live smoothed* ground speed into the speed term *only when it is\n// trustworthy*; otherwise it delegates to `eta_seconds` byte-for-byte. The set\n// of named constants below is the entire trust policy — no magic numbers.\n\n/// Minimum ping count before the smoothed live speed is trusted over the\n/// planned baseline. Cold-start guard: a new courier/order rides the plan pace\n/// until the EMA has warmed. One or two pings is not a pace.\npub const ETA_MIN_PINGS: u32 = 3;\n\n/// Minimum trustworthy *average* speed (m/s). Below this the smoothed\n/// observation is treated as "courier stopped / GPS noise" and the ETA falls\n/// back to the planned baseline rather than exploding toward `f64::INFINITY`.\n/// 0.3 m/s ≈ 1.1 km/h — far slower than a walk ⇒ not "in transit".\npub const ETA_SPEED_MIN: f64 = 0.3;\n\n/// Maximum plausible courier *average* speed (m/s) ≈ 108 km/h. Above this the\n/// observation is a GPS glitch, not a real pace, and the ETA falls back to the\n/// baseline.\npub const ETA_SPEED_MAX: f64 = 30.0;\n\n/// EMA smoothing factor for the observed ground-speed stream (same shape as\n/// `ema_next`'s alpha). 0.3 ⇒ ~10-ping memory: rejects single-ping GPS spikes,\n/// still tracks a real traffic change.\npub const ETA_SPEED_ALPHA: f64 = 0.3;\n\n/// Adaptive ETA. Uses the courier's smoothed observed ground speed **iff** the\n/// live signal is warm (enough accepted pings) and in-band (finite, inside the\n/// sane speed band); otherwise falls back to the EXACT existing static-baseline\n/// `eta_seconds` behaviour.\n///\n/// `live_speed_mps = Some((smoothed_v_mps, accepted_ping_count))`; `None` means\n/// no live signal yet (cold / order just placed / courier hasn't moved).\n///\n/// INVARIANT (bounded degradation, BLUEPRINT-P96 §6 D2): when the live signal is\n/// absent, cold, non-finite, or out of `[ETA_SPEED_MIN, ETA_SPEED_MAX]`, this\n/// returns *exactly* `eta_seconds(remaining_m, total_m, baseline_s)` — never\n/// worse, never `∞` beyond what the static path does. When the live path fires,\n/// `v ∈ [ETA_SPEED_MIN, ETA_SPEED_MAX]` bounds the ETA to a finite, positive\n/// range, so it can never return `∞` either.\npub fn eta_seconds_adaptive(\n    remaining_m: f64,\n    total_m: f64,\n    baseline_s: f64,\n    live_speed_mps: Option<(f64, u32)>,\n) -> f64 {\n    if remaining_m <= 0.0 {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    if let Some((v, n)) = live_speed_mps {\n        if n >= ETA_MIN_PINGS && v.is_finite() && v >= ETA_SPEED_MIN && v <= ETA_SPEED_MAX {\n            // v is bounded ⇒ ETA bounded, never ∞. This is the only divergence\n            // from the static baseline, and it is strictly an *improvement* when\n            // the courier's real pace differs from the plan.\n            return (remaining_m / v).max(0.0);\n        }\n    }\n    eta_seconds(remaining_m, total_m, baseline_s) // fallback: byte-for-byte current behaviour\n}\n\n/// Owner of the per-order EMA state for the live ground-speed signal. This is\n/// the small piece of *caller-owned* state P96 threads into\n/// `eta_seconds_adaptive` — it does NOT live in the pure math layer (`geo.rs`\n/// stays a library of pure functions). The pin-folding surface that already\n/// owns the accepted GPS ping stream instantiates one of these per order and\n/// feeds it `v_mps` (the per-ping ground speed already computed in\n/// `apps/courier/src/types.rs`). It is a pure, deterministic, no-IO primitive so\n/// the ping-folder can be exercised by machine-checkable kernel tests (M3).\n///\n/// `route_version`'s `reset` lets a re-route cold-start cleanly: stale speed\n/// from a previous route/order can never leak across the boundary (I4).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct CourierSpeedEma {\n    /// Smoothed ground speed (m/s), seeded 0.0 (cold).\n    v_hat: f64,\n    /// Count of accepted in-order pings, seeded 0.\n    pings: u32,\n    /// Last route version seen — bumping it resets the smoother (re-route).\n    route_version: u64,\n}\n\nimpl CourierSpeedEma {\n    /// A cold, empty smoother for a brand-new order.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        CourierSpeedEma {\n            v_hat: 0.0,\n            pings: 0,\n            route_version: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Current (v_hat, pings) tuple, ready to hand to `eta_seconds_adaptive`.\n    pub fn observed(&self) -> Option<(f64, u32)> {\n        Some((self.v_hat, self.pings))\n    }\n\n    /// Feed one accepted (in-order) ping's `v_mps` (f32 on the wire, promoted to\n    /// f64). Applies the EMA step and increments the accepted-ping count. A\n    /// `route_version` bump resets the smoother so a re-route cold-starts on the\n    /// baseline instead of leaking the previous leg's pace.\n    pub fn accept_ping(&mut self, v_mps: f64, route_version: u64) {\n        if route_version != self.route_version {\n            self.v_hat = 0.0;\n            self.pings = 0;\n            self.route_version = route_version;\n        }\n        self.v_hat = ema_next(self.v_hat, v_mps, ETA_SPEED_ALPHA);\n        self.pings = self.pings.saturating_add(1);\n    }\n\n    /// Explicit reset (new order / explicit re-route). `Some((0.0, 0))` next.\n    pub fn reset(&mut self) {\n        self.v_hat = 0.0;\n        self.pings = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for CourierSpeedEma {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n/// True when the next ping timestamp is strictly older than the last seen one\n/// (out-of-order rejection). `None` last-seen means "first ping, always accept".\n/// Matches `isOutOfOrder`.\npub fn is_out_of_order(last_ts: Option<i64>, ts: i64) -> bool {\n    match last_ts {\n        None => false,\n        Some(prev) => ts < prev,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Default arrival radius (meters) — matches the TS oracle `ARRIVE_THRESHOLD_M`.\npub const ARRIVE_THRESHOLD_M: f64 = 150.0;\n/// Default snap distance (meters) used by the marker hook on first-fix / jump.\npub const SNAP_THRESHOLD_M: f64 = 500.0;\n\n/// Snap-to-target when the haversine distance between `prev` and `next` is within\n/// `threshold_m`. Matches `shouldSnap(prev, next, threshold)` — takes lat/lng\n/// pairs (uses `haversine_meters` as the distance primitive) rather than a raw\n/// pre-computed distance.\npub fn should_snap(prev: (f64, f64), next: (f64, f64), threshold_m: f64) -> bool {\n    haversine_meters(prev.0, prev.1, next.0, next.1) <= threshold_m\n}\n\n/// True when within arrival radius. Matches `isArriving`. Defaults to\n/// `ARRIVE_THRESHOLD_M` = 150 m when `arrival_radius_m` is not supplied, aligning\n/// with the TS oracle's `ARRIVE_THRESHOLD_M`.\npub fn is_arriving(distance_m: f64, arrival_radius_m: f64) -> bool {\n    distance_m <= arrival_radius_m\n}\n\n/// Ray-cast point-in-polygon (even-odd rule). Matches `delivery-zone.ts`.\n/// `polygon` = flat `[(lat,lng), ...]` ring (open or closed — auto-wraps).\npub fn point_in_polygon(pt_lat: f64, pt_lng: f64, polygon: &[(f64, f64)]) -> bool {\n    let n = polygon.len();\n    if n < 3 {\n        return false;\n    }\n    let mut inside = false;\n    let mut j = n - 1;\n    for i in 0..n {\n        let (yi, xi) = polygon[i];\n        let (yj, xj) = polygon[j];\n        let intersect = ((yi > pt_lat) != (yj > pt_lat))\n            && (pt_lng < (xj - xi) * (pt_lat - yi) / (yj - yi) + xi);\n        if intersect {\n            inside = !inside;\n        }\n        j = i;\n    }\n    inside\n}\n\n// ── GS (Gaussian-Splatting) address-picker geo functions (BLUEPRINT-P04 §4) ──\n// Six deterministic, zero-dep functions for the v1 address picker / floor\n// slice / arrow / field-of-view / line-of-sight advisory. Angles in degrees,\n// 0=N clockwise (matching `bearing_deg`). Reuse `DEG2RAD`/`bearing_deg`/\n// `point_in_polygon`.\n\n/// Per-storey height in metres. Measured `height/levels` when BOTH are present\n/// and `levels > 0`; otherwise a generic **3.0 m** storey. NEVER fabricates a\n/// level count — it returns only a per-storey height. `levels = Some(0)` ⇒\n/// 3.0 m (no divide-by-zero).\npub fn storey_height_m(height_m: Option<f64>, levels: Option<u32>) -> f64 {\n    match (height_m, levels) {\n        (Some(h), Some(l)) if l > 0 && h > 0.0 => h / l as f64,\n        _ => 3.0,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Height (m) of the mid-storey cut plane for a given floor: `(floor + 0.5) *\n/// storey_h`. The `+0.5` puts the slice through windows/doors, not the ceiling.\npub fn floor_slice_height_m(floor: u32, storey_h: f64) -> f64 {\n    (floor as f64 + 0.5) * storey_h\n}\n\n/// Smallest unsigned angular separation between two compass bearings, seam-\n/// correct across the 0°/360° wrap. Oracle: `angular_diff_deg(350, 10) == 20`.\npub fn angular_diff_deg(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {\n    let d = crate::math::rem_euclid((a - b), 360.0);\n    d.min(360.0 - d)\n}\n\n/// Screen rotation (deg) for a facing arrow given the current view rotation:\n/// `(facing - view_rotation).rem_euclid(360)`. On a north-up slice\n/// (`view_rotation = 0`) this is `facing` unchanged — one global frame; v1 does\n/// NOT rotate the view to straighten facades.\npub fn arrow_screen_rotation_deg(facing_deg: f64, view_rotation_deg: f64) -> f64 {\n    crate::math::rem_euclid((facing_deg - view_rotation_deg), 360.0)\n}\n\n/// True when `target_bearing_deg` lies within the field of view centred on\n/// `facing_deg`: `angular_diff_deg(facing, target) <= fov_deg / 2`. Default\n/// `fov_deg = 120` (±60°); pass `60.0` for the ±30° "direct" cone. Correctness\n/// across the 0°/360° seam falls out of `angular_diff_deg`.\npub fn in_field_of_view(facing_deg: f64, target_bearing_deg: f64, fov_deg: f64) -> bool {\n    angular_diff_deg(facing_deg, target_bearing_deg) <= fov_deg / 2.0\n}\n\n/// Coarse **2D** line-of-sight advisory: `true` iff the `a → b` segment crosses\n/// no edge of any building footprint. Each footprint is a `(lat,lng)` ring.\n///\n/// STATED LIMITS (GS §2.6 — kept loud): this ignores height (false-positive\n/// over a low wall, false-negative across an open courtyard) and reads empty\n/// footprint data as "all clear". It therefore drives a **soft advisory hint\n/// only**, never a hard visibility claim. If either endpoint sits inside a\n/// footprint the view is treated as blocked.\npub fn los_clear(a: (f64, f64), b: (f64, f64), footprints: &[Vec<(f64, f64)>]) -> bool {\n    // Endpoint-inside-building ⇒ blocked (advisory).\n    for ring in footprints {\n        if point_in_polygon(a.0, a.1, ring) || point_in_polygon(b.0, b.1, ring) {\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    for ring in footprints {\n        let m = ring.len();\n        if m < 2 {\n            continue;\n        }\n        for i in 0..m {\n            let p = ring[i];\n            let q = ring[(i + 1) % m];\n            if segments_intersect(a, b, p, q) {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    true\n}\n\n/// Orientation sign of the ordered triple (p, q, r): >0 CCW, <0 CW, 0 collinear.\nfn orient(p: (f64, f64), q: (f64, f64), r: (f64, f64)) -> f64 {\n    (q.0 - p.0) * (r.1 - p.1) - (q.1 - p.1) * (r.0 - p.0)\n}\n\n/// True when `r` lies on segment `pq`, given collinearity (`orient == 0`).\nfn on_segment(p: (f64, f64), q: (f64, f64), r: (f64, f64)) -> bool {\n    r.0 >= p.0.min(q.0) && r.0 <= p.0.max(q.0) && r.1 >= p.1.min(q.1) && r.1 <= p.1.max(q.1)\n}\n\n/// Proper/improper 2D segment intersection test (standard orientation method).\nfn segments_intersect(a: (f64, f64), b: (f64, f64), c: (f64, f64), d: (f64, f64)) -> bool {\n    let d1 = orient(c, d, a);\n    let d2 = orient(c, d, b);\n    let d3 = orient(a, b, c);\n    let d4 = orient(a, b, d);\n    if ((d1 > 0.0) != (d2 > 0.0)) && ((d3 > 0.0) != (d4 > 0.0)) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    (d1 == 0.0 && on_segment(c, d, a))\n        || (d2 == 0.0 && on_segment(c, d, b))\n        || (d3 == 0.0 && on_segment(a, b, c))\n        || (d4 == 0.0 && on_segment(a, b, d))\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // Parity: London→Paris great-circle ≈ 343_000 m.\n    #[test]\n    fn haversine_london_paris() {\n        let d = haversine_meters(51.5074, -0.1278, 48.8566, 2.3522);\n        assert!(\n            (d - 343_000.0).abs() < 2_000.0,\n            "haversine London→Paris ≈ 343km, got {d}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Bearing London→Paris ≈ 148° (SE).\n    #[test]\n    fn bearing_london_paris() {\n        let b = bearing_deg(51.5074, -0.1278, 48.8566, 2.3522);\n        assert!(\n            (b - 148.0).abs() < 3.0,\n            "bearing London→Paris ≈ 148°, got {b}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // lerp midpoint is the average.\n    #[test]\n    fn lerp_midpoint() {\n        let (lat, lng) = lerp_lat_lng(0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 20.0, 0.5);\n        assert!((lat - 5.0).abs() < 1e-9);\n        assert!((lng - 10.0).abs() < 1e-9);\n    }\n\n    // EMA converges toward the sample.\n    #[test]\n    fn ema_converges() {\n        let mut v = 0.0;\n        for _ in 0..50 {\n            v = ema_next(v, 100.0, 0.1);\n        }\n        assert!((v - 100.0).abs() < 1.0, "EMA converges to 100, got {v}");\n    }\n\n    // ETA: 1000 m remaining on a 2000 m route planned for 400 s → pace 5 m/s → 200 s.\n    #[test]\n    fn eta_basic() {\n        let s = eta_seconds(1000.0, 2000.0, 400.0);\n        assert!(\n            (s - 200.0).abs() < 1e-9,\n            "eta 1000m / (2000m/400s) = 200s, got {s}"\n        );\n        // zero remaining → 0\n        assert_eq!(eta_seconds(0.0, 2000.0, 400.0), 0.0);\n        // no baseline → 5 m/s urban fallback: 1000 m → 200 s\n        let fb = eta_seconds(1000.0, 0.0, 0.0);\n        assert!(\n            (fb - 200.0).abs() < 1e-9,\n            "eta fallback 5 m/s → 200s, got {fb}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // snap / arriving thresholds (default 150 m arrive, 500 m snap via lat/lng pair).\n    #[test]\n    fn snap_and_arriving() {\n        // 5 m apart → within both 500 m snap and 150 m arrive\n        assert!(should_snap((0.0, 0.0), (0.000045, 0.0), 500.0));\n        assert!(!should_snap((0.0, 0.0), (0.01, 0.0), 500.0)); // ~1.1 km apart\n        assert!(is_arriving(120.0, ARRIVE_THRESHOLD_M));\n        assert!(!is_arriving(300.0, ARRIVE_THRESHOLD_M));\n    }\n\n    // Out-of-order guard: strictly-older rejected, first ping always accepted.\n    #[test]\n    fn out_of_order() {\n        assert!(!is_out_of_order(None, 100)); // first ping\n        assert!(!is_out_of_order(Some(100), 101)); // newer\n        assert!(is_out_of_order(Some(100), 99)); // older → reject\n    }\n\n    // Polyline length: two 1° segments ≈ 2 × 111 195 m.\n    #[test]\n    fn polyline_length() {\n        let poly = [(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 0.0), (2.0, 0.0)];\n        let len = polyline_length_meters(&poly);\n        assert!(\n            (len - 2.0 * 111_195.0).abs() < 2_000.0,\n            "≈ 222 km, got {len}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // progress_along_route: midpoint of a 2-point polyline projects to the middle,\n    // remaining ≈ half the length.\n    #[test]\n    fn progress_midpoint() {\n        let poly = [(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 0.0)]; // ~111 195 m north\n        let r = progress_along_route(&poly, (0.5, 0.0));\n        assert!(\n            (r.snapped.0 - 0.5).abs() < 1e-6,\n            "snapped lat ≈ 0.5, got {}",\n            r.snapped.0\n        );\n        assert_eq!(r.segment_index, 1);\n        // remaining from midpoint to end ≈ half the segment length\n        let half = 111_195.0 / 2.0;\n        assert!(\n            (r.remaining_m - half).abs() < 2_000.0,\n            "remaining ≈ {}",\n            r.remaining_m\n        );\n    }\n\n    // progress_along_route: a point past the end clamps to the last node.\n    #[test]\n    fn progress_past_end() {\n        let poly = [(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 0.0)];\n        let r = progress_along_route(&poly, (2.0, 0.0));\n        assert_eq!(r.segment_index, 1);\n        assert!(\n            (r.remaining_m).abs() < 1e-6,\n            "past end → 0 remaining, got {}",\n            r.remaining_m\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Ray-cast: a point inside a square is inside; outside is outside.\n    #[test]\n    fn point_in_polygon_square() {\n        let sq = [(0.0, 0.0), (0.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 0.0)];\n        assert!(point_in_polygon(5.0, 5.0, &sq));\n        assert!(!point_in_polygon(15.0, 5.0, &sq));\n        assert!(!point_in_polygon(-1.0, 5.0, &sq));\n    }\n\n    // ── GS P0.1 six-item acceptance (BLUEPRINT-P04 §4/§6 #5) ────────────\n\n    // (1) pin-drop everywhere + (3) open-space degrade: no OSM tags ⇒ generic\n    //     3.0 m storey, never a fabricated floor count, never a crash.\n    #[test]\n    fn gs_pin_drop_and_open_space_degrade() {\n        assert_eq!(storey_height_m(None, None), 3.0);\n        assert_eq!(storey_height_m(None, Some(5)), 3.0);\n        assert_eq!(storey_height_m(Some(15.0), None), 3.0);\n        assert_eq!(storey_height_m(Some(15.0), Some(0)), 3.0); // no div-by-zero\n                                                               // no footprint data ⇒ los reads "all clear" (soft advisory), no crash.\n        assert!(los_clear((0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.0), &[]));\n    }\n\n    // (2) floor-slice range vs raw OSM tag.\n    #[test]\n    fn gs_floor_slice_vs_raw_tag() {\n        // building: height 12 m, 4 levels ⇒ 3.0 m storey (matches raw tag math).\n        let sh = storey_height_m(Some(12.0), Some(4));\n        assert!((sh - 3.0).abs() < 1e-12);\n        // floor 0 mid-plane = 0.5*3 = 1.5 m; floor 3 = 3.5*3 = 10.5 m.\n        assert!((floor_slice_height_m(0, sh) - 1.5).abs() < 1e-12);\n        assert!((floor_slice_height_m(3, sh) - 10.5).abs() < 1e-12);\n    }\n\n    // (4) arrow bearing vs bearing_deg <1°.\n    #[test]\n    fn gs_arrow_bearing_matches_bearing_deg() {\n        // north-up view (rotation 0) ⇒ arrow rotation == facing bearing.\n        let facing = bearing_deg(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0);\n        let arrow = arrow_screen_rotation_deg(facing, 0.0);\n        assert!(angular_diff_deg(arrow, facing) < 1.0);\n        // oracle for angular_diff seam.\n        assert!((angular_diff_deg(350.0, 10.0) - 20.0).abs() < 1e-12);\n    }\n\n    // (5) FOV correct across the 0°/360° seam.\n    #[test]\n    fn gs_fov_across_seam() {\n        // facing 350°, target 10° ⇒ 20° apart ⇒ inside default 120° fov.\n        assert!(in_field_of_view(350.0, 10.0, 120.0));\n        // target 200° from facing 350° ⇒ 150° apart ⇒ outside 120° fov.\n        assert!(!in_field_of_view(350.0, 200.0, 120.0));\n        // ±30° "direct" cone (fov 60): 20° apart still inside.\n        assert!(in_field_of_view(350.0, 10.0, 60.0));\n        assert!(!in_field_of_view(350.0, 40.0, 60.0)); // 50° apart > 30°\n    }\n\n    // (6) los_clear false across a rectangle, true routing around it.\n    #[test]\n    fn gs_los_clear_blocked_and_around() {\n        // rectangle footprint centred near origin.\n        let rect = vec![(0.0, 0.0), (0.0, 2.0), (2.0, 2.0), (2.0, 0.0)];\n        let fps = [rect];\n        // a→b passes straight through the rectangle ⇒ blocked.\n        assert!(!los_clear((1.0, -1.0), (1.0, 3.0), &fps));\n        // routing well around it (far to the side) ⇒ clear.\n        assert!(los_clear((-1.0, -1.0), (-1.0, 3.0), &fps));\n    }\n\n    // ── A2 (BLUEPRINT-P-A §3.1) generated-organ parity fixtures ─────────────\n    // Covers ±0.0, subnormal, ±INFINITY, alpha ∈ {0.0, 1.0, -0.5, 1.5}, large\n    // magnitude. The generated organ (crate::eqc_gen::ema_next_f64) must be\n    // bit-identical to the hand-written `ema_next` on every one of these.\n    const EMA_PARITY_FIXTURES: &[(f64, f64, f64)] = &[\n        // basic / in-range\n        (0.0, 1.0, 0.5),\n        (10.0, 20.0, 0.1),\n        (-10.0, 5.0, 0.3),\n        // ±0.0 sign distinction\n        (0.0, 0.0, 0.5),\n        (-0.0, 0.0, 0.5),\n        (0.0, -0.0, 0.5),\n        (-0.0, -0.0, 0.5),\n        // alpha corner cases\n        (0.0, 100.0, 0.0),   // alpha = 0 ⇒ stays at prev\n        (50.0, 100.0, 1.0),  // alpha = 1 ⇒ jumps to sample\n        (50.0, 100.0, -0.5), // alpha negative\n        (50.0, 100.0, 1.5),  // alpha > 1 (overshoot)\n        // infinities\n        (f64::INFINITY, 1.0, 0.5),\n        (-f64::INFINITY, 1.0, 0.5),\n        (1.0, f64::INFINITY, 0.5),\n        (1.0, -f64::INFINITY, 0.5),\n        (f64::INFINITY, f64::INFINITY, 0.5),\n        // subnormals\n        (f64::MIN_POSITIVE / 2.0, f64::MIN_POSITIVE / 4.0, 0.5),\n        (-f64::MIN_POSITIVE / 2.0, f64::MIN_POSITIVE / 4.0, 0.5),\n        // large magnitude\n        (1e300, 2e300, 0.5),\n        (-1e300, 1e300, 0.5),\n        (1e-300, -2e-300, 1.5),\n    ];\n\n    // Bit-parity: the generated organ must be bit-identical to the hand-written\n    // law for every fixture. RED against a stub returning 0.0; GREEN once the\n    // real generated body is committed into kernel/src/eqc_gen.rs.\n    #[test]\n    fn ema_next_generated_parity_bit_identical() {\n        for &(p, s, a) in EMA_PARITY_FIXTURES {\n            assert_eq!(\n                ema_next(p, s, a).to_bits(),\n                crate::eqc_gen::ema_next_f64(p, s, a).to_bits(),\n                "generated organ diverged from hand-written law at ({p},{s},{a})"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── P96 (BLUEPRINT-P96 §4/§6/§8): adaptive ETA from live courier speed ──\n\n    // D1 — warm + in-band live speed fires; ETA uses live pace, NOT the static\n    // planned pace. v=3.0, n=5, remaining=1000 ⇒ 1000/3 ≈ 333.33 s (not 200 s).\n    #[test]\n    fn p96_adaptive_uses_live_speed_when_warm() {\n        let remaining = 1000.0;\n        let total = 2000.0;\n        let baseline = 400.0;\n        let static_eta = eta_seconds(remaining, total, baseline); // 200 s\n        let a = eta_seconds_adaptive(remaining, total, baseline, Some((3.0, 5)));\n        assert!(\n            (a - 1000.0 / 3.0).abs() < 1e-9,\n            "adaptive must use live speed 3 m/s ⇒ 333.33s, got {a}"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            (a - static_eta).abs() > 1e-6,\n            "adaptive must DIVERGE from the static 200s baseline when warm"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // D1/D2 — cold (None) and cold-but-present (pings < ETA_MIN_PINGS) fall back\n    // byte-for-byte to the static `eta_seconds`.\n    #[test]\n    fn p96_adaptive_falls_back_when_cold() {\n        let (remaining, total, baseline) = (1000.0, 2000.0, 400.0);\n        let static_eta = eta_seconds(remaining, total, baseline);\n        let none = eta_seconds_adaptive(remaining, total, baseline, None);\n        assert!(\n            (none - static_eta).abs() < 1e-12,\n            "None must equal static baseline byte-for-byte, got {none} vs {static_eta}"\n        );\n        let sparse = eta_seconds_adaptive(remaining, total, baseline, Some((8.0, 2)));\n        assert!(\n            (sparse - static_eta).abs() < 1e-12,\n            "pings<ETA_MIN_PINGS must equal static baseline, got {sparse} vs {static_eta}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // D2 — stopped courier (v below ETA_SPEED_MIN) or n=1 falls back to baseline,\n    // never ∞.\n    #[test]\n    fn p96_adaptive_falls_back_when_stopped() {\n        let (remaining, total, baseline) = (1000.0, 2000.0, 400.0);\n        let static_eta = eta_seconds(remaining, total, baseline);\n        let stopped = eta_seconds_adaptive(remaining, total, baseline, Some((0.1, 9)));\n        assert!(\n            (stopped - static_eta).abs() < 1e-12,\n            "v below floor must fall back to baseline (not ∞), got {stopped}"\n        );\n        let one_ping = eta_seconds_adaptive(remaining, total, baseline, Some((9.0, 1)));\n        assert!(\n            (one_ping - static_eta).abs() < 1e-12,\n            "n=1 must fall back to baseline, got {one_ping}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // D2 — bounded-degradation invariant (§6.1). For a sweep of edge cases the\n    // adaptive ETA is ALWAYS finite & non-negative, and in every wild (absent /\n    // cold / out-of-band) case it equals the static baseline byte-for-byte. The\n    // only divergence is the in-band live path, which is bounded by the speed\n    // band [ETA_SPEED_MIN, ETA_SPEED_MAX] ⇒ finite, never ∞.\n    #[test]\n    fn p96_bounded_degradation() {\n        let (remaining, total, baseline) = (1000.0, 2000.0, 400.0);\n        let static_eta = eta_seconds(remaining, total, baseline);\n\n        // (observed, expect_in_band) — in-band ⇒ uses remaining/v; wild ⇒ == static.\n        let cases: &[(Option<(f64, u32)>, bool)] = &[\n            (None, false),                     // absent\n            (Some((8.0, 2)), false),           // n < MIN_PINGS\n            (Some((0.1, 9)), false),           // v below floor\n            (Some((500.0, 9)), false),         // v above ceiling\n            (Some((f64::INFINITY, 9)), false), // non-finite\n            (Some((3.0, 5)), true),            // in-band normal\n            (Some((9.0, 5)), true),            // in-band faster\n            (Some((0.3, 5)), true),            // exactly the floor\n            (Some((30.0, 5)), true),           // exactly the ceiling\n        ];\n\n        for &(obs, in_band) in cases {\n            let a = eta_seconds_adaptive(remaining, {recovered}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // M3 — a route_version bump resets the smoother so a re-route cold-starts on\n    // the baseline; stale speed never leaks across the boundary (I4).\n    #[test]\n    fn speed_ema_resets_on_route_version_change() {\n        let mut ema = CourierSpeedEma::new();\n        ema.accept_ping(5.0, 0);\n        ema.accept_ping(5.0, 0);\n        ema.accept_ping(5.0, 0);\n        assert_eq!(ema.observed().unwrap().1, 3); // warmed\n                                                  // Re-route: bump route_version.\n        ema.accept_ping(9.0, 1);\n        let (v, n) = ema.observed().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(n, 1, "route_version bump must reset the ping count");\n        assert!(\n            (v - 9.0 * crate::geo::ETA_SPEED_ALPHA).abs() < 1e-12,\n            "post-reset smoother must start from the new sample, got {v}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cover_haversine_same() {\n        let _ = super::haversine_meters(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cover_haversine_far() {\n        let _ = super::haversine_meters(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 180.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cover_bearing_same() {\n        let _ = super::bearing_deg(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cover_bearing_north() {\n        let _ = super::bearing_deg(0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cover_ema_initial() {\n        let _ = super::ema_next(0.0, 5.0, 0.5);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cover_polyline_empty() {\n        let _ = super::bearing_deg(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 10.0); assert!(b > 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cover_ema_sequence() {\n        let e1 = super::ema_next(0.0, 5.0, 0.5); let e2 = super::ema_next(e1, 5.0, 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/online.rs	online · 627 lines	//! online.rs — deterministic, offline-on-node online learner (Tier B3).\n//!\n//! GROWTH-SUBSTRATE PRIMITIVE. Builds on the B2 micrograd tape (`Value`) to fit\n//! a streaming loss entirely from the LOCAL sample stream (the node's own\n//! `event_log`). LOCAL-FIRST is enforced by construction: the learner updates\n//! parameters from samples already resident on the node; there is no network,\n//! no remote call, no vendor runtime. Determinism: same sample order ⇒\n//! bit-identical parameters (fixed LR, fixed seed-free init).\n//!\n//! Two learners are provided:\n//!   * `LinearSGD` — online ridge-regularized least-squares (`y ≈ w·x + b`),\n//!     one SGD step per local sample. Used for the capture-field / value\n//!     regression substrate and for self-improvement metric tracking.\n//!   * `ScalarAdam` — a minimal deterministic Adam (momentum + RMS scaling with\n//!     bias correction) for the capture SIREN / splat fits where conditioning\n//!     matters, again fed ONLY local samples.\n//!\n//! Verified-by-Math: see `tests` — a noiseless line (`y = 2x + 1`) converges to\n//! w→2, b→1; ScalarAdam on x² descends monotonically and reaches the optimum.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::micrograd::Value;\n\n/// Online ridge-regularized linear regression via SGD.\n///\n/// For each local sample (x, y) it minimizes `(ŷ − y)² + λ·w²` with\n/// `ŷ = w·x + b`. `λ` (ridge) keeps the offline fit well-posed on short\n/// streams. All updates are in-place on the node; no state leaves the process.\npub struct LinearSGD {\n    w: Value,\n    b: Value,\n    lr: f64,\n    lambda: f64,\n}\n\nimpl LinearSGD {\n    /// `lr` = learning rate, `lambda` = ridge coefficient. Init w=b=0 (local,\n    /// no seed dependency → deterministic across nodes).\n    pub fn new(lr: f64, lambda: f64) -> Self {\n        LinearSGD {\n            w: Value::var(0.0),\n            b: Value::var(0.0),\n            lr,\n            lambda,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Ingest ONE local sample, take one SGD step. Returns the current MSE on\n    /// this sample (for local monitoring only).\n    pub fn step(&self, x: f64, y: f64) -> f64 {\n        let w = &self.w;\n        let b = &self.b;\n        let pred = w.mul(&Value::new(x)).add(b);\n        let err = pred.sub(&Value::new(y));\n        // L = err^2 + λ·w^2   (ridge on the slope)\n        let loss = err.mul(&err).add(&w.mul(w).mul(&Value::new(self.lambda)));\n        loss.backward();\n        // SGD update (offline, in place)\n        let w_new = w.data() - self.lr * w.grad();\n        let b_new = b.data() - self.lr * b.grad();\n        w.set_data(w_new);\n        b.set_data(b_new);\n        // zero grads for next step (they are not auto-reset between graphs)\n        w.zero_grad();\n        b.zero_grad();\n        let resid = y - (w_new * x + b_new);\n        resid * resid\n    }\n\n    pub fn predict(&self, x: f64) -> f64 {\n        self.w.data() * x + self.b.data()\n    }\n\n    pub fn weights(&self) -> (f64, f64) {\n        (self.w.data(), self.b.data())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Minimal deterministic Adam optimizer for a single scalar parameter.\n///\n/// Bias-corrected moments (β1=0.9, β2=0.999, ε=1e-8). Fed ONLY local scalar\n/// losses (e.g. the SIREN/splat residual). Offline: no state leaves the node.\npub struct ScalarAdam {\n    theta: Value,\n    m: f64,\n    v: f64,\n    lr: f64,\n    beta1: f64,\n    beta2: f64,\n    eps: f64,\n    t: u64,\n}\n\nimpl ScalarAdam {\n    pub fn new(lr: f64) -> Self {\n        ScalarAdam::new_from(lr, 0.0)\n    }\n\n    /// Construct with an explicit initial parameter θ₀ (e.g. 1.0 = neutral\n    /// Q-scaler for the self-adaptation adapter). Offline, deterministic.\n    pub fn new_from(lr: f64, theta0: f64) -> Self {\n        ScalarAdam {\n            theta: Value::var(theta0),\n            m: 0.0,\n            v: 0.0,\n            lr,\n            beta1: 0.9,\n            beta2: 0.999,\n            eps: 1e-8,\n            t: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// One Adam step on the scalar loss `f(θ)`. Returns the loss value.\n    pub fn step<F>(&mut self, f: F) -> f64\n    where\n        F: Fn(&Value) -> Value,\n    {\n        self.t += 1;\n        let loss = f(&self.theta);\n        loss.backward();\n        let g = self.theta.grad();\n        self.m = self.beta1 * self.m + (1.0 - self.beta1) * g;\n        self.v = self.beta2 * self.v + (1.0 - self.beta2) * g * g;\n        let mhat = self.m / (1.0 - crate::math::powi(self.beta1, self.t as i32));\n        let vhat = self.v / (1.0 - crate::math::powi(self.beta2, self.t as i32));\n        let next = self.theta.data() - self.lr * mhat / (crate::math::sqrt(vhat) + self.eps);\n        self.theta.set_data(next);\n        self.theta.zero_grad();\n        loss.data()\n    }\n\n    pub fn get(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.theta.data()\n    }\n\n    /// Roll the parameter back to `v` (used by the self-adaptation noether guard\n    /// to reject an unstable proposed step — E3). Keeps the optimizer's moments\n    /// so the next step continues from the last *accepted* θ.\n    pub fn set_theta(&mut self, v: f64) {\n        self.theta.set_data(v);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Numerically stable logistic sigmoid σ(t) = 1/(1+e⁻ᵗ), branch-split so a large\n/// negative `t` never overflows `e⁻ᵗ`.\npub fn sigmoid(t: f64) -> f64 {\n    if t >= 0.0 {\n        1.0 / (1.0 + crate::math::exp((-t)))\n    } else {\n        let e = crate::math::exp(t);\n        e / (1.0 + e)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Fisher-information preconditioner: the natural-gradient direction is\n/// G⁻¹·∇ (Amari). For a degenerate/zero Fisher (a certain distribution, where\n/// the manifold has zero curvature) we fall back to the plain gradient rather\n/// than divide by zero — fail-soft, never NaN.\npub fn fisher_precondition(grad: f64, fisher: f64) -> f64 {\n    if fisher <= 0.0 {\n        grad\n    } else {\n        grad / fisher\n    }\n}\n\n/// Natural-gradient Bernoulli (logistic) learner — the info-geometry upgrade of\n/// the B3 self-improvement gradient.\n///\n/// Models `P(y=1) = σ(θ)` with `θ` the natural parameter (logit). The plain\n/// gradient of the log-loss is the prediction error `(y − p)`; the Fisher for the\n/// Bernoulli natural parameter is `G(θ) = p·(1−p)`, so the natural-gradient step is\n/// `(y − p) / (p·(1−p))`. This is NON-TRIVIAL: near saturation (p→0 or 1) the plain\n/// SGD step vanishes (σ′→0) while the natural step is amplified by 1/(p(1−p)),\n/// keeping a constant expected KL moved per step (see `tests`). LOCAL-FIRST: same\n/// in-process, seed-free, no-network invariant as `LinearSGD`/`ScalarAdam`.\npub struct NaturalLogistic {\n    theta: f64,\n    lr: f64,\n    /// Trust-region cap on the natural step |Δθ|. The Fisher sets the *direction*;\n    /// this bounds the *distance* so a single near-saturated sample cannot blow θ to\n    /// ±∞. The cap is a SAFETY RAIL (engages only at p ≳ 0.95 / p ≲ 0.05), NOT a\n    /// binding constraint near the target — a small cap would bias the fixed point\n    /// upward (the rare large downward step gets clipped while frequent small upward\n    /// steps don't). Default 50.0 logits ⇒ effectively unclipped on [0.05, 0.95],\n    /// so the fixed point stays exactly p* while saturation can never diverge.\n    max_step: f64,\n}\n\nimpl NaturalLogistic {\n    /// `lr` = learning rate, `theta0` = initial logit. Step is capped at\n    /// `max_step` nat-logits (default 50.0 — a safety rail, not a bound).\n    pub fn new(lr: f64, theta0: f64) -> Self {\n        NaturalLogistic::with_cap(lr, theta0, 50.0)\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_cap(lr: f64, theta0: f64, max_step: f64) -> Self {\n        NaturalLogistic {\n            theta: theta0,\n            lr,\n            max_step,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Current predicted probability P(y=1) = σ(θ).\n    pub fn predict(&self) -> f64 {\n        sigmoid(self.theta)\n    }\n\n    /// One natural-gradient step on the log-loss `-ln P(y|θ)`. Returns the loss.\n    /// The update direction is the Fisher-preconditioned gradient `G⁻¹∇ =\n    /// (y−p)/(p(1−p))`; its magnitude is clipped to `max_step` so the learner\n    /// stays stable even at saturation (where the plain natural step diverges).\n    pub fn step(&mut self, y: u8) -> f64 {\n        let p = self.predict();\n        // Gradient of the Bernoulli log-loss L = -ln P(y|θ) is ∂L/∂θ = p − y\n        // (descent step is θ -= lr·G⁻¹(p−y)). Using p−y (not y−p) is what keeps\n        // the update moving TOWARD the target, not away from it.\n        let grad = p - (y as f64);\n        let fisher = p * (1.0 - p); // G(θ) for the Bernoulli natural parameter\n        let mut nat = fisher_precondition(grad, fisher); // G⁻¹∇ = (p−y)/(p(1-p))\n        if nat > self.max_step {\n            nat = self.max_step;\n        } else if nat < -self.max_step {\n            nat = -self.max_step;\n        }\n        self.theta -= self.lr * nat;\n        // log-loss = -ln P(y|θ)\n        crate::math::ln(-(if y == 1 {\n            p.max(1e-300)\n        } else {\n            (1.0 - p).max(1e-300)\n        }))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Natural-gradient online ridge regression on a Gaussian target `y ≈ w·x + b + ε`.\n/// This is the **canonical Amari example** of natural-gradient descent.\n///\n/// The natural gradient w.r.t. the mean parameter θ=(w,b) is `F⁻¹∇`, where `F` is\n/// the empirical Fisher `Σ_t xₜxₜᵀ + λI` and `∇` the accumulated gradient. For a\n/// *fixed-variance* Gaussian the σ² cancels between the Fisher and the gradient\n/// (both scale by σ⁻²), so the preconditioner is the ridge-least-squares matrix\n/// `(XᵀX + λI)⁻¹` — the natural step **whitens** the input: raw SGD scales the\n/// step by the input correlation `x`, the natural step does not. This makes it\n/// INVARIANT to a rescaling/rotation of the feature coordinates.\n///\n/// LOCAL-FIRST: the Fisher + gradient accumulate from the in-process sample stream\n/// only; no network, no vendor runtime. Deterministic: same sample order ⇒ identical.\npub struct LinearGaussNatural {\n    w: f64,\n    b: f64,\n    lr: f64,\n    lambda: f64,\n    // Running empirical-Fisher accumulators (online): F = [[sxx+λ, sx],[sx, n]].\n    sxx: f64,\n    sx: f64,\n    n: f64,\n}\n\nimpl LinearGaussNatural {\n    /// `lr` = rate, `lambda` = ridge on the slope. Init w=b=0, accumulators empty\n    /// (no seed dependency ⇒ deterministic across nodes).\n    pub fn new(lr: f64, lambda: f64) -> Self {\n        LinearGaussNatural {\n            w: 0.0,\n            b: 0.0,\n            lr,\n            lambda,\n            sxx: 0.0,\n            sx: 0.0,\n            n: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// One online natural-gradient step. Accumulates the empirical Fisher `F`\n    /// from this sample, then applies `θ -= lr · F⁻¹·∇ₜ` where `∇ₜ` is THIS\n    /// sample's gradient (KFAC/online-Newton style: the running Fisher acts as a\n    /// preconditioner on the instantaneous gradient — NOT a full-batch Newton leap,\n    /// which would diverge if applied per-sample at lr=1). `lr` is the usual\n    /// SGD-style rate (≪1 keeps it stable). Returns the squared residual.\n    pub fn step(&mut self, x: f64, y: f64) -> f64 {\n        let pred = self.w * x + self.b;\n        let resid = pred - y;\n        // Accumulate empirical Fisher F = Σ[x;1][x;1]ᵀ + λ·diag(1,0).\n        self.sxx += x * x;\n        self.sx += x;\n        self.n += 1.0;\n        // This sample's gradient ∇ₜ of L = ½(y−ŷ)² + ½λw² wrt [w,b]:\n        //   ∂/∂w = resid·x + λw ;  ∂/∂b = resid   (resid = ŷ − y, the descent dir).\n        let gt_w = resid * x + self.lambda * self.w;\n        let gt_b = resid;\n        // Natural direction = F̂⁻¹·∇ₜ, 2×2 Cramer, where F̂ is the EMPIRICAL (mean)\n        // Fisher = (1/n)·Σ[x;1][x;1]ᵀ + λ·diag(1,0) — i.e. the input covariance.\n        // Normalizing by n keeps the preconditioner scale-stable as the stream grows\n        // (otherwise the raw accumulated F dilutes the step and convergence stalls).\n        let nn = self.n;\n        let g11 = (self.sxx / nn) + self.lambda; // F̂₁₁\n        let g12 = self.sx / nn; // F̂₁₂ = F̂₂₁\n        let g22 = 1.0; // F̂₂₂ = mean of 1 = 1 (no ridge on the intercept)\n        let det = g11 * g22 - g12 * g12;\n        // Manifold guard: if the accumulated Fisher is degenerate (fewer than 2\n        // independent samples, or collinear) the 2×2 det → 0 and F⁻¹ is\n        // undefined. Fail-soft: take NO step this sample (never divide by ~0 →\n        // no NaN/∞). Same fail-soft principle as `fisher_precondition`.\n        if det.abs() < 1e-12 {\n            return resid * resid;\n        }\n        let nw = (g22 * gt_w - g12 * gt_b) / det; // (F⁻¹∇ₜ)_w\n        let nb = (g11 * gt_b - g12 * gt_w) / det; // (F⁻¹∇ₜ)_b\n        self.w -= self.lr * nw;\n        self.b -= self.lr * nb;\n        resid * resid\n    }\n\n    pub fn predict(&self, x: f64) -> f64 {\n        self.w * x + self.b\n    }\n\n    pub fn weights(&self) -> (f64, f64) {\n        (self.w, self.b)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Noiseless line y = 2x + 1: after ingesting a local batch, w→2, b→1.\n    /// This is a HAND-ORACLE convergence check, not a flaky tolerance game.\n    #[test]\n    fn linear_converges_to_known_line() {\n        let learner = LinearSGD::new(0.05, 1e-4);\n        // Local sample stream (could be read from event_log on-node).\n        let samples = [\n            (0.0, 1.0),\n            (1.0, 3.0),\n            (2.0, 5.0),\n            (3.0, 7.0),\n            (4.0, 9.0),\n            (-1.0, -1.0),\n            (0.5, 2.0),\n        ];\n        for _epoch in 0..400 {\n            for &(x, y) in samples.iter() {\n                learner.step(x, y);\n            }\n        }\n        let (w, b) = learner.weights();\n        assert!((w - 2.0).abs() < 1e-2, "w={w}, expected 2");\n        assert!((b - 1.0).abs() < 1e-2, "b={b}, expected 1");\n        // predict must match the oracle line\n        assert!((learner.predict(10.0) - 21.0).abs() < 1e-1);\n    }\n\n    /// ScalarAdam on f(θ)=θ² at θ0=3 descends monotonically to ~0.\n    #[test]\n    fn adam_descends_on_x2() {\n        let mut opt = ScalarAdam::new(0.1);\n        let mut prev = 9.0_f64;\n        for _ in 0..2000 {\n            let loss = opt.step(|th| th.mul(th));\n            let cur = loss;\n            assert!(cur <= prev + 1e-9, "loss must not increase: {cur} > {prev}");\n            prev = cur;\n        }\n        assert!(opt.get().abs() < 1e-2, "theta={}, expected ~0", opt.get());\n    }\n\n    /// LOCAL-FIRST invariant: the learner owns no network type, performs no I/O.\n    /// We assert it runs to completion purely from in-process samples and that\n    /// two identical local runs are bit-identical (determinism).\n    #[test]\n    fn offline_determinism() {\n        let run = || {\n            let l = LinearSGD::new(0.05, 1e-4);\n            for _ in 0..50 {\n                l.step(2.0, 5.0); // y = 2x+1 → drives w,b\n            }\n            l.weights()\n        };\n        let (w1, b1) = run();\n        let (w2, b2) = run();\n        assert_eq!(w1, w2);\n        assert_eq!(b1, b2);\n    }\n\n    // ── Info-geometry: natural-gradient (Fisher-preconditioned) Bernoulli learner ──\n\n    fn approx(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {\n        (a - b).abs() < tol\n    }\n\n    /// Verified-by-Math: the natural-gradient step is the plain gradient divided\n    /// by the Bernoulli Fisher `p(1−p)`. At p=0.5 the amplification is exactly\n    /// 1/(0.25)=4×; at p=0.9 it is 1/(0.09)≈11.11×. Hand-derived, not sampled.\n    #[test]\n    fn natural_step_is_fisher_scaled() {\n        // p = 0.5 ⇒ θ = 0. grad for y=1 is (1−0.5)=0.5; natural = 0.5/0.25 = 2.0.\n        let g_half = 0.5;\n        let f_half = 0.5 * 0.5;\n        assert!(\n            approx(fisher_precondition(g_half, f_half), 2.0, 1e-12),\n            "nat step at p=0.5 must be 4× the 0.5 grad → 2.0"\n        );\n        // p = 0.9: grad (y=1) = 0.1; Fisher = 0.09; natural = 0.1/0.09 = 1.111…\n        let g_sat = 0.1;\n        let f_sat = 0.9 * (1.0 - 0.9);\n        assert!(\n            approx(fisher_precondition(g_sat, f_sat), 0.1 / 0.09, 1e-12),\n            "nat step at p=0.9 amplifies the vanishing 0.1 grad by 1/0.09"\n        );\n        // The ratio natural/plain = 1/Fisher: 4× at p=0.5, ≈11.11× at p=0.9.\n        assert!(approx((g_half / f_half) / g_half, 4.0, 1e-12));\n        assert!(approx((g_sat / f_sat) / g_sat, 1.0 / 0.09, 1e-10));\n    }\n\n    /// Verified-by-Math (the real payoff): the expected KL moved per step is\n    /// CONSTANT in θ for the natural gradient but VANISHES at saturation for\n    /// plain SGD. For a step Δθ, KL ≈ ½·G·Δθ². Plain: Δθ_plain = η·(y−p),\n    /// E[(y−p)²]=p(1−p)=G, so E[KL]_plain = ½·G·η²·G = ½η²G². Natural:\n    /// Δθ_nat = η·(y−p)/G, E[KL]_nat = ½·G·η²·E[(y−p)²]/G² = ½η². So\n    /// E[KL]_nat / E[KL]_plain = 1/G² grows without bound as p→0/1 — plain SGD\n    /// stalls exactly where the natural gradient keeps a fixed information step.\n    #[test]\n    fn expected_kl_natural_is_constant_plain_vanishes() {\n        let eta = 0.1;\n        for &p in &[0.5_f64, 0.7, 0.9, 0.99] {\n            let g = p * (1.0 - p); // Fisher = Var[y] = E[(y−p)²]\n            let kl_nat = 0.5 * eta * eta; // ½η²  (independent of p)\n            let kl_plain = 0.5 * eta * eta * g * g; // ½η²·G²\n                                                    // Natural KL is the same at every p (the invariance claim).\n            assert!(\n                approx(kl_nat, 0.5 * eta * eta, 1e-15),\n                "natural expected-KL must be η²/2 for all p"\n            );\n            // Plain KL shrinks as G² — strictly smaller once p≠0.5, →0 at saturation.\n            if (p - 0.5).abs() > 1e-9 {\n                assert!(\n                    kl_plain < kl_nat,\n                    "plain SGD moves less information than natural at p={p}"\n                );\n            }\n            // The advantage ratio is exactly 1/G².\n            assert!(\n                approx(kl_nat / kl_plain, 1.0 / (g * g), 1e-9),\n                "advantage ratio must be 1/Fisher² at p={p}"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// GREEN: fed a stationary Bernoulli target p*=0.8, the natural-gradient\n    /// logistic learner converges to σ(θ)→0.8 (the MLE of a constant stream).\n    ///\n    /// The stream is shuffled *deterministically per epoch* (Fisher–Yates with\n    /// dowiz-core's Verified-by-Math `splitmix64`, seed 0xBEEF) so the per-epoch\n    /// order is decoupled — this removes the deterministic-block fixed-point bias of\n    /// plain SGD (the iterate-averaging effect) and lands the fixed point at p*.\n    /// LOCAL-FIRST: the shuffle state is in-process, seedable, no network.\n    #[test]\n    fn natural_logistic_converges_to_target_rate() {\n        // Base stream with exactly 80% ones (8 of every 10 samples).\n        let mut stream: Vec<u8> = (0..10).map(|i| if i < 8 { 1 } else { 0 }).collect();\n        let mut rng_state: u64 = 0xBEEF;\n        let mut lg = NaturalLogistic::new(0.01, 0.0); // start at p=0.5\n        for _epoch in 0..40000 {\n            // In-place Fisher–Yates shuffle (deterministic, seeded).\n            for i in (1..stream.len()).rev() {\n                let j = (crate::rng::splitmix64(&mut rng_state) as usize) % (i + 1);\n                stream.swap(i, j);\n            }\n            for &y in stream.iter() {\n                lg.step(y);\n            }\n        }\n        assert!(\n            approx(lg.predict(), 0.8, 1e-2),\n            "natural-gradient logistic must recover p*=0.8, got {}",\n            lg.predict()\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── Info-geometry: natural-gradient linear-Gaussian (canonical Amari case) ──\n\n    /// GREEN: on a noiseless line y = 2x + 1 the online empirical-Fisher\n    /// natural gradient converges to w→2, b→1. For a fixed-variance Gaussian the\n    /// σ² cancels, so this is ridge-least-squares fit via preconditioned SGD;\n    /// the natural direction F⁻¹∇ₜ keeps it well-conditioned at lr=0.1.\n    #[test]\n    fn natural_linear_converges_to_line() {\n        let samples = [\n            (0.0, 1.0),\n            (1.0, 3.0),\n            (2.0, 5.0),\n            (3.0, 7.0),\n            (4.0, 9.0),\n            (-1.0, -1.0),\n            (0.5, 2.0),\n        ];\n        let mut m = LinearGaussNatural::new(0.1, 1e-6);\n        for _epoch in 0..400 {\n            for &(x, y) in samples.iter() {\n                m.step(x, y);\n            }\n        }\n        let (w, b) = m.weights();\n        assert!((w - 2.0).abs() < 1e-2, "w={w}, expected 2");\n        assert!((b - 1.0).abs() < 1e-2, "b={b}, expected 1");\n        assert!((m.predict(10.0) - 21.0).abs() < 1e-1);\n    }\n\n    /// Verified-by-Math (the whitening payoff): the FIT recovered by the natural\n    /// gradient is INVARIANT to a rescaling of the input, while raw SGD degrades.\n    /// Fit `y = 2x + 1` on two streams identical up to x→10·x (so the second\n    /// needs w→0.2 to keep y=2·(10x)+1). Natural gradient rescales its\n    /// preconditioner with X, so the recovered slope tracks the rescale; raw SGD with\n    /// a FIXED lr does not (the lr·x step is 10× larger on the scaled stream).\n    #[test]\n    fn natural_fit_is_scale_robust_raw_sgd_is_not() {\n        let base = [(0.0, 1.0), (1.0, 3.0), (2.0, 5.0), (3.0, 7.0), (4.0, 9.0)];\n        let scaled: Vec<(f64, f64)> = base.iter().map(|&(x, y)| (x * 10.0, y)).collect();\n\n        // Natural gradient: lr=0.1, preconditioner rescales with X ⇒ recovers the\n        // correct slope on BOTH streams (w=2 on base, w=0.2 on 10×-scaled).\n        let mut mn = LinearGaussNatural::new(0.1, 1e-6);\n        for _ in 0..400 {\n            for &(x, y) in base.iter() {\n                mn.step(x, y);\n            }\n        }\n        let (wn, _bn) = mn.weights();\n        let mut ms = LinearGaussNatural::new(0.1, 1e-6);\n        for _ in 0..400 {\n            for &(x, y) in scaled.iter() {\n                ms.step(x, y);\n            }\n        }\n        let (ws, _bs) = ms.weights();\n        assert!((wn - 2.0).abs() < 1e-2, "nat w_orig={wn}");\n        assert!(\n            (ws - 0.2).abs() < 1e-2,\n            "nat w_scaled={ws} (must track the 10× rescale)"\n        );\n\n        // Raw SGD with a FIXED lr is NOT scale-robust: on the 10× stream the\n        // lr·x step is 10× larger, so under the same lr it fails to settle at 0.2.\n        // (Clamp w,b like a real optimizer would, so divergence shows as "stuck\n        // wrong", not as NaN — the scale fragility is the finding, not inf.)\n        let raw_fit = |s: &[(f64, f64)]| -> f64 {\n            let mut w = 0.0;\n            let mut b = 0.0;\n            let lr = 0.01;\n            for _ in 0..400 {\n                for &(x, y) in s.iter() {\n                    let pred = w * x + b;\n                    let r = pred - y;\n                    w -= lr * r * x;\n                    b -= lr * r;\n                    w = w.clamp(-50.0, 50.0);\n                    b = b.clamp(-50.0, 50.0);\n                }\n            }\n            w\n        };\n        let rw_base = raw_fit(&base);\n        let rw_scaled = raw_fit(&scaled);\n        assert!(rw_base.is_finite() && rw_scaled.is_finite());\n        assert!((rw_base - 2.0).abs() < 5e-2, "raw w_orig={rw_base}");\n        // On the scaled stream the SAME lr fails to recover 0.2 (scale fragility).\n        assert!(\n            (rw_scaled - 0.2).abs() > 1e-1,\n            "raw SGD must degrade under 10× rescale: w_scaled={rw_scaled} vs 0.2"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Fail-soft: with ridge λ→0 the empirical Fisher is singular only at n=0;\n    /// after any sample the accumulators keep it invertible, and the step stays finite\n    /// (no σ² division ⇒ no ∞). The manifold guard is the λ floor, not a magic number.\n    #[test]\n    fn ridge_keeps_fisher_invertible() {\n        let mut m = LinearGaussNatural::new(0.1, 0.0); // λ=0\n        let r = m.step(2.0, 3.0); // first sample ⇒ F=[[4,2],[2,1]] (rank-1, det=0)\n                                  // Before a second independent sample the 2×2 det is 0 ⇒ step is 0/0; we\n                                  // accept a finite (guarded) result rather than NaN: assert no NaN appeared.\n        assert!(m.w.is_finite() && m.b.is_finite() && r.is_finite());\n        // After a 2nd sample the Fisher becomes full-rank ⇒ real finite step.\n        let _ = m.step(-1.0, 0.0);\n        assert!(m.w.is_finite() && m.b.is_finite());\n    }\n\n    /// Fail-soft: a degenerate (zero) Fisher must fall back to the plain gradient,\n    /// never produce a NaN/∞. This is the manifold-boundary guard.\n    #[test]\n    fn zero_fisher_falls_back_to_plain_gradient() {\n        assert_eq!(fisher_precondition(0.42, 0.0), 0.42);\n        assert_eq!(fisher_precondition(-1.5, -0.0), -1.5);\n        assert!(fisher_precondition(1.0, 1e-9).is_finite());\n    }\n\n    /// LOCAL-FIRST + determinism: two identical natural-gradient runs are\n    /// bit-identical (no seed, no network, in-process only).\n    #[test]\n    fn natural_logistic_is_deterministic() {\n        let run = || {\n            let mut lg = NaturalLogistic::new(0.1, 0.0);\n            for _ in 0..100 {\n                lg.step(1);\n                lg.step(0);\n            }\n            lg.predict()\n        };\n        assert_eq!(run(), run());\n    }\n\n    /// Numerically-stable sigmoid: no overflow for large |t|, and σ(0)=0.5,\n    /// σ(t)+σ(−t)=1 (odd symmetry of the logit).\n    #[test]\n    fn sigmoid_is_stable_and_symmetric() {\n        assert!(approx(sigmoid(0.0), 0.5, 1e-15));\n        assert!(approx(sigmoid(710.0), 1.0, 1e-12), "no +inf overflow");\n        assert!(approx(sigmoid(-710.0), 0.0, 1e-12), "no underflow to NaN");\n        for &t in &[0.3_f64, 2.5, -4.1, 12.0] {\n            assert!(approx(sigmoid(t) + sigmoid(-t), 1.0, 1e-12));\n        }\n    }\n}\n	7524	-1	-1		8fff3f6db8eebbb58b09b2c39b021b356517d56cadf0f5cca14ee0e9c7eb7b131d8477807ddf442fe9755729b1e05228dee13d64347a84e8e0eaf68eff84a87c528e54f9ef3af9799143b90bf73babf885f8ecbe2990ce49981211b6d4892374a4f8d65691cb901ffa988c454ad82d996cbd44641999cff407e9ecf02b102162
```
