## 7990 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/markov.rs · LongTerm

Summary: markov · 519 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/markov.rs	markov · 519 lines	//! markov.rs — the Markov-chain attractor detector for the self-improvement loop.\n//!\n//! REVERSE-ENGINEERING LOOP #R1. ASCENDed from `tools/loop-signals/markov_attractor.py`\n//! (287 LOC Python on the agent's own hot path). It reuses `crate::spectral` for the\n//! eigen-core — **killing the dual-authority hazard**: the Faddeev-LeVerrier + Durand-Kerner\n//! eigensolver previously existed byte-for-byte in both Python and `spectral.rs` with no parity\n//! gate between them. There is now ONE eigensolver, in the kernel, and the Python's own frozen\n//! 12-case test corpus is reproduced below as VbM parity tests (`green_parity_*`).\n//!\n//! MODEL (Jurafsky & Martin SLP3 App. A). The recent tool-outcome stream is a first-order Markov\n//! chain: states Q, empirical transition matrix Â (row-normalised counts), damped stationary π.\n//! Deterministic signals derived from Â:\n//!   * entropy rate  H = −Σᵢ πᵢ Σⱼ Âᵢⱼ log₂ Âᵢⱼ  (0 = deterministic cycle),\n//!   * escape mass   Σ_{s∈ESCAPE} π_s  (long-run time in a progress state),\n//!   * spectrum      slem = |λ₂| + a PERIOD signal (an eigenvalue near the unit circle away\n//!                   from +1 = a real oscillation, incl. μ≈−1 period-2),\n//!   * NEW continuous dial: gap γ = 1−slem ⇒ mixing time τ≈1/γ and iteration budget\n//!                   k ≈ ln(1/tol)/ln(1/slem) — the master dial the research identified.\n//! ADVISORY (the harness gates decide). Float is fine — this is dynamics, never money.\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::spectral;\n\nconst MIN_EVENTS: usize = 8; // short window ⇒ stay quiet (cold start)\nconst H_LO: f64 = 0.5; // bits/step; rows >~75% deterministic ⇒ "cyclic"\nconst ESCAPE_LO: f64 = 0.05; // <5% long-run time in a progress state ⇒ no escape\nconst DAMPING: f64 = 0.02; // PageRank teleport ⇒ irreducible+aperiodic ⇒ unique π\nconst POWER_ITERS: usize = 300; // fixed; the damped chain contracts fast for small n\n\n/// Progress potential V (Foster-Lyapunov). Only `run_ok` (a verify/progress command) escapes.\nfn potential(s: &str) -> f64 {\n    match s {\n        "run_ok" => 1.0,\n        "edit_fail" | "run_fail" => -1.0,\n        _ => 0.0, // edit, probe, unknown — neutral, never an escape state\n    }\n}\nfn is_escape(s: &str) -> bool {\n    s == "run_ok"\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Verdict {\n    /// Quiet work or progress reachable — no intervention.\n    Healthy,\n    /// Trapped AND (low entropy OR a spectral oscillation) — a cycle across ≥1 signatures.\n    LimitCycle,\n    /// Trapped, high-entropy churn, no clean period — busy going nowhere.\n    StrangeAttractor,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Report {\n    pub verdict: Verdict,\n    pub events: usize,\n    pub entropy_rate_bits: f64,\n    pub escape_mass: f64,\n    pub drift: f64,\n    pub has_failure: bool,\n    pub slem: f64,\n    pub period: bool,\n    /// NEW — spectral gap γ = 1 − |λ₂|. γ→0 ⇒ never mixes (trapped).\n    pub gap: f64,\n    /// NEW — mixing time τ ≈ 1/γ (∞ for a non-mixing cycle).\n    pub mixing_time: f64,\n}\n\n/// Iteration budget: how many steps a power method needs to reach `tol` at this mixing rate —\n/// `k ≈ ln(1/tol)/ln(1/slem)`. A spectrum-derived replacement for a fixed retry cap.\npub fn budget(slem: f64, tol: f64) -> f64 {\n    if slem <= 0.0 || slem >= 1.0 || tol <= 0.0 {\n        return f64::INFINITY;\n    }\n    crate::math::ln(1.0 / tol) / crate::math::ln(1.0 / slem)\n}\n\nfn idx_of(alpha: &[&str], s: &str) -> usize {\n    alpha.iter().position(|&a| a == s).unwrap()\n}\n\n/// Full analysis output — the exact JSON contract `markov_attractor.py` emitted\n/// (`json.dumps(analyze(toks))`), so shell consumers (`check.sh`) and parity\n/// tests keep working once the Python is deleted. The kernel is the single\n/// source of truth; the CLI bin serialises this to JSON.\npub struct DetailedReport {\n    pub report: Report,\n    /// Sorted unique state alphabet (matches Python `alphabet`).\n    pub alphabet: Vec<String>,\n    /// Eigenvalues of Â as (re, im), sorted by modulus descending (Python `eigs`).\n    pub eigs: Vec<(f64, f64)>,\n    /// Stationary π keyed by state name (Python `stationary`).\n    pub stationary: Vec<(String, f64)>,\n    /// Human-readable reason string (Python `reason`).\n    pub reason: String,\n}\n\nimpl DetailedReport {\n    /// Verdict as the Python's upper-case string ("HEALTHY" / "LIMIT_CYCLE" / …).\n    pub fn verdict_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self.report.verdict {\n            Verdict::Healthy => "HEALTHY",\n            Verdict::LimitCycle => "LIMIT_CYCLE",\n            Verdict::StrangeAttractor => "STRANGE_ATTRACTOR",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Analyse a window of tool-outcome tokens, returning the FULL report (verdict +\n/// metrics + spectrum + stationary + reason). Pure. Fail-open (short window ⇒\n/// HEALTHY with empty spectral fields).\npub fn analyze_detailed(states: &[&str]) -> DetailedReport {\n    let states: Vec<&str> = states.iter().copied().filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect();\n    let l = states.len();\n    let cold = DetailedReport {\n        report: Report {\n            verdict: Verdict::Healthy,\n            events: l,\n            entropy_rate_bits: 0.0,\n            escape_mass: 0.0,\n            drift: 0.0,\n            has_failure: false,\n            slem: 0.0,\n            period: false,\n            gap: 1.0,\n            mixing_time: 1.0,\n        },\n        alphabet: Vec::new(),\n        eigs: Vec::new(),\n        stationary: Vec::new(),\n        reason: "window too short".to_string(),\n    };\n    if l < MIN_EVENTS {\n        return cold;\n    }\n\n    // alphabet = sorted unique\n    let mut alpha: Vec<&str> = states.clone();\n    alpha.sort_unstable();\n    alpha.dedup();\n    let n = alpha.len();\n\n    // bigram counts → row-normalised transition matrix Â (unseen row ⇒ uniform)\n    let mut counts = vec![vec![0.0f64; n]; n];\n    for t in 0..l - 1 {\n        counts[idx_of(&alpha, states[t])][idx_of(&alpha, states[t + 1])] += 1.0;\n    }\n    let mut a = vec![vec![0.0f64; n]; n];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        let s: f64 = counts[i].iter().sum();\n        for j in 0..n {\n            a[i][j] = if s > 0.0 {\n                counts[i][j] / s\n            } else {\n                1.0 / n as f64\n            };\n        }\n    }\n\n    // damped stationary π = πÂ′, Â′ = (1−d)Â + (d/n)J, via power iteration\n    let d = DAMPING;\n    let mut pi = vec![1.0 / n as f64; n];\n    for _ in 0..POWER_ITERS {\n        let mut nxt = vec![0.0f64; n];\n        for i in 0..n {\n            let pii = pi[i];\n            if pii == 0.0 {\n                continue;\n            }\n            for j in 0..n {\n                nxt[j] += pii * ((1.0 - d) * a[i][j] + d / n as f64);\n            }\n        }\n        let sum: f64 = nxt.iter().sum::<f64>().max(f64::MIN_POSITIVE);\n        for v in nxt.iter_mut() {\n            *v /= sum;\n        }\n        pi = nxt;\n    }\n\n    // entropy rate, escape mass, Foster drift (drift reported, deliberately NOT gated)\n    let mut h = 0.0;\n    for i in 0..n {\n        let mut row_h = 0.0;\n        for j in 0..n {\n            let p = a[i][j];\n            if p > 0.0 {\n                row_h -= p * crate::math::log2(p);\n            }\n        }\n        h += pi[i] * row_h;\n    }\n    let escape: f64 = (0..n).filter(|&i| is_escape(alpha[i])).map(|i| pi[i]).sum();\n    let mut drift = 0.0;\n    for i in 0..n {\n        let vi = potential(alpha[i]);\n        let step: f64 = (0..n).map(|j| a[i][j] * (potential(alpha[j]) - vi)).sum();\n        drift += pi[i] * step;\n    }\n\n    // spectrum — the SHARED kernel eigensolver (no more Python duplicate).\n    // Route `slem` through the content-addressed DecompCache so a re-analysis\n    // of an UNCHANGED transition matrix reuses the prior eigen-decomposition\n    // instead of re-running Faddeev-LeVerrier + Durand-Kerner. decomp_cache = crate::spectral_cache::DecompCache::new();\n    let a_tile = crate::csr::NormalizedTile::from_dense(&a);\n    let slem = crate::spectral_cache::slem_cached(&mut decomp_cache, &a_tile);\n    let period = spectral::dominant_period(&a).is_some();\n    let gap = 1.0 - slem;\n    let mixing_time = if gap > 1e-12 {\n        1.0 / gap\n    } else {\n        f64::INFINITY\n    };\n\n    // a trap requires EVIDENCE OF STRUGGLE — at least one failure in the window.\n    let has_failure = states.iter().any(|&s| s == "run_fail" || s == "edit_fail");\n    let trapped = escape <= ESCAPE_LO && has_failure;\n\n    let verdict = if trapped && (h <= H_LO || period) {\n        Verdict::LimitCycle\n    } else if trapped && h > H_LO {\n        Verdict::StrangeAttractor\n    } else {\n        Verdict::Healthy // not struggling, or progress reachable\n    };\n\n    let reason = match verdict {\n        Verdict::LimitCycle => format!(\n            "cyclic trap: escape={escape:.3} H={h:.3} period={period} slem={slem:.3}"\n        ),\n        Verdict::StrangeAttractor => format!(\n            "bounded high-entropy churn never reaching progress: escape={escape:.3} H={h:.3} slem={slem:.3}"\n        ),\n        Verdict::Healthy if !has_failure => {\n            format!("quiet work, no failures in window (escape={escape:.3} H={h:.3})")\n        }\n        Verdict::Healthy (s.to_string(), pi[i]))\n        .collect();\n\n    DetailedReport {\n        report: Report {\n            verdict,\n            events: l,\n            entropy_rate_bits: h,\n Uses PID dynamics + crystalline memory + ensemble bidding to predict\n//! consequences of state changes and actions across performance, load,\n//! traffic, telemetry, throttle, friction, and error dimensions.\n//!\n//! ## Architecture\n//! - `SystemState` snapshot captures N metrics at a point in time.\n//! - `PidArray` models how each metric evolves in response to actions.\n//! - `CrystalLattice<SystemState>` stores past states for similarity lookup.\n//! - Ensemble bidding: each model (PID, crystal, trend) "bids" on the\n//!   predicted outcome; highest-confidence prediction wins.\n//! - Sequencer: atomic counter ensures ordered, race-free access.\n//!\n//! ## Usage\n//! ```\n//! use dowiz_core::predictor::{Predictor, SystemState, Action, PredictorConfig};\n//!\n//! let mut pred = Predictor::new(PredictorConfig::default());\n//! let state = SystemState::new(1, vec![0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0.8, 0.2, 0.6], "steady");\n//! pred.observe(state);\n//! let results = pred.predict("latency".into(), "scale_up".into());\n//! assert!(!results.is_empty());\n//! ```\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse "throttle_level",\n];\n\npub const PREDICTOR_PID_KP: f64 = 0.6;\npub const PREDICTOR_PID_KI: f64 = 0.15;\npub const PREDICTOR_PID_KD: f64 = 0.2;\npub const PREDICTOR_PID_MIN: f64 = 0.0;\npub const PREDICTOR_PID_MAX: f64 = 1.0;\npub const PREDICTOR_CRYSTAL_CAPACITY: usize = 10000;\npub const PREDICTOR_K_SIMILAR: usize = 5;\npub const PREDICTOR_MIN_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.3;\npub const PREDICTOR_DEFAULT_HISTORY_CAP: usize = 1000;\npub const PREDICTOR_MAX_HISTORY: usize = 10000;\npub const PREDICTOR_BID_FRICTION_WEIGHT: f64 = 0.3;\npub const PREDICTOR_DEGRADED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 1000.0;\npub const PREDICTOR_SIM_HIGH_ERROR: f64 = 0.5;\npub const PREDICTOR_SIM_THROTTLE_LATENCY: f64 = 500.0;\npub const PREDICTOR_SIM_THROTTLE_ERROR: f64 = 0.3;\npub const new(id: u64, metrics: Vec<f64>, label: &str) -> Self {\n        let mut m = metrics;\n        m.resize(DEFAULT_N_METRICS, 0.0);\n        // Sanitize each metric: NaN/Inf → 0.0, clamp to [0, 1]\n        for v in &mut m {\n            *v = crate::sanitize_normalized(*v);\n        }\n        SystemState {\n            id,\n            timestamp_ms: 0,\n            metrics: m,\n            label: label.to_string(),\n            bid_confidence: 1.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_timestamp(mut self, ts: u64) -> Self {\n        self.timestamp_ms = ts;\n        self\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_confidence(mut self, c: f64) -> Self {\n        self.bid_confidence = crate::sanitize_normalized(c);\n        self\n    }\n}\n\nimpl CrystalIndex for SystemState {\n    fn crystal_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        // Metrics-based cell addressing for locality-sensitive lookup.\n        let mut output = [0u8; 32];\n        let v0 = self.metrics.first().copied().unwrap_or(0.0);\n        let v1 = self.metrics.get(1).copied().unwrap_or(0.0);\n        output[0] = ((v0 * 255.0) as u64 % 256) as u8;\n        output[1] = ((v1 * 255.0) as u64 % 256) as u8;\n        for (i, &m) in self.metrics.iter().enumerate() {\n            if i + 2 >= 32 { break; }\n            let bits = m.to_bits();\n            output[i + 2] = (bits ^ (bits >> 11) ^ (bits >> 23)) as u8;\n        }\n        output\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Action ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// An action that can be applied to the system.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Action {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub magnitude: f64,\n    pub target_metrics: Vec<usize>,\n}\n\nimpl Action {\n    pub fn new(name: &str, magnitude: f64) -> Self {\n        Action {\n            name: name.to_string(),\n            magnitude: crate::sanitize_f64(magnitude),\n            target_metrics: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn targeting(mut self, metrics: &[usize]) -> Self {\n        self.target_metrics = metrics.to_vec();\n        self\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── PredictedOutcome ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A predicted consequence of an action or state change.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PredictedOutcome {\n    /// Which metric this prediction is for.\n    pub metric_index: usize,\n    pub metric_name: String,\n    /// Predicted value after the action (normalized 0..1).\n    pub predicted_value: f64,\n    /// Current value before the action.\n    pub current_value: f64,\n    /// How confident the predictor is (0.0..1.0).\n    pub confidence: f64,\n    /// Which model made this prediction (PID, crystal, trend, ensemble).\n    pub model: &'static str,\n    /// Predicted throttle level (0=none, 1=soft, 2=hard limit).\n    pub predicted_throttle: u8,\n    /// Predicted friction score (0=smooth, 1=high friction).\n    pub friction_score: f64,\n    /// Predicted error probability (0..1).\n    pub error_probability: f64,\n    /// Whether this prediction indicates an imminent problem.\n    pub warning: bool,\n}\n\nimpl PredictedOutcome {\n    pub fn new(metric_index: usize, metric_name: &str, predicted: f64, current: f64) -> Self {\n        PredictedOutcome {\n            metric_index,\n            metric_name: metric_name.to_string(),\n            predicted_value: crate::sanitize_normalized(predicted),\n            current_value: crate::sanitize_normalized(current),\n            confidence: 0.5,\n            model: "ensemble",\n            predicted_throttle: 0,\n            friction_score: 0.0,\n            error_probability: 0.0,\n            warning: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_critical(&self) -> bool {\n        self.error_probability > 0.7 || self.predicted_throttle >= 2 || self.warning\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── PredictorConfig ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Configuration for the real-time predictor.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PredictorConfig {\n    /// Number of metric dimensions.\n    pub n_metrics: usize,\n    /// PID gains for each metric's dynamic model.\n    pub pid_config: PidConfig,\n    /// Crystal lattice capacity.\n    pub crystal_capacity: usize,\n    /// Number of similar past states to retrieve for crystal model.\n    pub k_similar: usize,\n    /// Minimum confidence for a prediction to be considered.\n    pub min_confidence: f64,\n    /// Whether to use ensemble bidding (multiple models vote).\n    pub use_ensemble: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Default for PredictorConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        PredictorConfig {\n            n_metrics: DEFAULT_N_METRICS,\n            pid_config: PidConfig::new(PREDICTOR_PID_KP, PREDICTOR_PID_KI, PREDICTOR_PID_KD, PREDICTOR_PID_MIN, PREDICTOR_PID_MAX),\n            crystal_capacity: PREDICTOR_CRYSTAL_CAPACITY,\n            k_similar: PREDICTOR_K_SIMILAR,\n            min_confidence: PREDICTOR_MIN_CONFIDENCE,\n            use_ensemble: true,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── PredictionBid ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single model's "bid" on a predicted outcome.\n///\n/// In the bidding/auction model, each predictor (PID, crystal, trend)\n/// submits a bid with its confidence. The ensemble selects the bid with\n/// the highest confidence that passes the minimum threshold.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PredictionBid {\n    pub metric_index: usize,\n    pub predicted_value: f64,\n    pub confidence: f64,\n    pub model: &'static str,\n    pub throttle: u8,\n    pub friction: f64,\n    pub error_prob: f64,\n}\n\n// ─── Predictor ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Real-time system state/action consequence predictor.\n///\n/// Combines PID dynamics, crystalline memory, and ensemble bidding\n/// to predict outcomes across all system dimensions. Thread-safe\n/// via atomic sequencer for race-free access.\npub struct Predictor {\n    config: PredictorConfig,\n    /// PID array modeling each metric's dynamics.\n    pid: PidArray,\n    /// Crystal lattice for similar-past-state retrieval.\n    crystal: CrystalLattice<StateSnapshot>,\n    /// Most recent observed state.\n    current_state: Option<SystemState>,\n    /// Historical states for trend analysis.\n    history: Vec<SystemState>,\n    /// Atomic sequencer for race-free prediction IDs.\n    sequencer: AtomicU64,\n    /// Circuit state: whether the predictor is in degraded mode.\n    degraded: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Predictor {\n    pub fn new(config: PredictorConfig) -> Self {\n        let pid = PidArray::new(\n            config.n_metrics,\n            config.pid_config.kp,\n            config.pid_config.ki,\n            config.pid_config.kd,\n            0.0,\n            1.0,\n        );\n        Predictor {\n            crystal: CrystalLattice::new(),\n            pid,\n            config,\n            current_state: None,\n            history: Vec::with_capacity(PREDICTOR_DEFAULT_HISTORY_CAP),\n            sequencer: AtomicU64::new(1),\n            degraded: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Unique, monotonically increasing prediction ID (race-free).\n    pub fn next_id(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.sequencer.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n\n    pub fn config(&self) -> &PredictorConfig {\n        &self.config\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_degraded(&self) -> bool {\n        self.degraded\n    }\n\n    /// Observe a new system state.\n    ///\n    /// Stores it in the crystal lattice and history, updates PID dynamics.\n    /// Idempotent: calling with the same state.id multiple times is a no-op\n    /// (trend samples are not duplicated).\n    pub fn observe(&mut self, state: SystemState) {\n        // Idempotency guard: skip if this state's ID was already observed.\n        if self.current_state.as_ref().map_or(false, |s| s.id == state.id) {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        let _ts = state.timestamp_ms;\n        let snapshot = StateSnapshot::new(state.id, state.metrics.clone(), &state.label);\n\n        // Store in crystal lattice for future similarity search.\n        self.crystal.insert(snapshot);\n\n        // Update PID dynamics with latest metric values as measurements.\n        // Setpoints are the prior state's values (we're tracking deviation).\n        if let Some(prev) = &self.current_state {\n            let setpoints: Vec<f64> = prev.metrics.iter().map(|&v| v).collect();\n            self.pid.update_batch(&setpoints, &state.metrics);\n        } else {\n            self.pid.reset_all();\n        }\n\n        // Store in history (bounded).\n        self.history.push(state.clone());\n        if self.history.len() > PREDICTOR_MAX_HISTORY {\n            self.history.remove(0);\n        }\n\n        self.current_state = Some(state);\n    }\n\n    /// Observe a batch of system states in sequence.\n    pub fn observe_batch(&mut self, states: &[SystemState]) {\n        for state in states {\n            self.observe(state.clone());\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn make_bid(\n        metric_idx: usize,\n        predicted_value: f64,\n        model: &'static str,\n        confidence: f64,\n        throttle: u8,\n        friction: f64,\n        error_prob: f64,\n    ) -> PredictionBid {\n        PredictionBid { metric_index: metric_idx, predicted_value, confidence, model, throttle, friction, error_prob }\n    }\n\n    /// Predict consequences of an action on a specific metric.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of `PredictedOutcome` bids from each model,\n    /// sorted by confidence (highest first). The caller can select\n    /// the best bid or use ensemble weighting.\n    pub fn predict(&self, metric_name: String, action_name: String) -> Vec<PredictedOutcome> {\n        let current = match &self.current_state {\n            Some(s) => s,\n            None => return Vec::new(),\n        };\n\n        let metric_idx = METRIC_NAMES.iter()\n            .position(|&n| n == metric_name)\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        let current_val = current.metrics.get(metric_idx).copied().unwrap_or(0.0);\n        let mut bids: Vec<PredictionBid> = Vec::new();\n\n        // ── Model 1: PID dynamics bid ─────────────────────────────────────\n        {\n            let pid_output = self.pid.output(metric_idx);\n            // PID predicts where the metric is heading based on recent dynamics.\n            let predicted = (pid_output + current_val * PREDICTOR_PID_BLEND).min(1.0);\n            let confidence = if self.degraded { PREDICTOR_DEGRADED_CONFIDENCE } else { PREDICTOR_NORMAL_CONFIDENCE };\n            let throttle = if predicted > PREDICTOR_THROTTLE_LOW { 1 } else if predicted > PREDICTOR_THROTTLE_HIGH { 2 } else { 0 };\n            let pid_error_prob = if predicted > PREDICTOR_PID_ERROR_THRESH { predicted * PREDICTOR_PID_ERROR_MUL_HIGH } else { predicted * PREDICTOR_PID_ERROR_MUL_LOW };\n            bids.push(Self::make_bid(\n                metric_idx, predicted, "pid", confidence, throttle,\n                predicted * PREDICTOR_BID_FRICTION_WEIGHT, pid_error_prob,\n            ));\n        }\n\n        // ── Model 2: Crystal memory bid ───────────────────────────────────\n        {\n            let query = StateSnapshot::new(\n                self.next_id(),\n                current.metrics.clone(),\n                &action_name,\n            );\n            let similar = self.crystal.query(&query, self.config.k_similar);\n\n            if !similar.is_empty() {\n                // Average the metric values of similar past states.\n                let mut sum = 0.0;\n                let mut count = 0usize;\n                for s in &similar {\n                    if let Some(&v) = s.metrics.get(metric_idx) {\n                        sum += v;\n                        count += 1;\n                    }\n                }\n                let crystal_pred = if count > 0 { sum / count as f64 } else { current_val };\n                let confidence = (similar.len() as f64 / self.config.k_similar as f64 * CRYSTAL_SIMILARITY_WEIGHT + CRYSTAL_CONFIDENCE_WEIGHT)\n                    .min(1.0);\n                let throttle = if crystal_pred > CRYSTAL_THROTTLE_THRESHOLD { 1 } else { 0 };\n                bids.push(Self::make_bid(\n                    metric_idx, crystal_pred, "crystal", confidence, throttle,\n                    crystal_pred * CRYSTAL_FRICTION, crystal_pred * CRYSTAL_ERROR_PROB,\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // ── Model 3: Trend extrapolation bid ──────────────────────────────\n        {\n            let history_samples: Vec<f64> = self.history.iter()\n                .filter_map(|s| s.metrics.get(metric_idx).copied())\n                .collect();\n\n            let trend_pred = if history_samples.len() >= TREND_MIN_SAMPLES {\n                let n = history_samples.len();\n                let recent = &history_samples[n - TREND_MIN_SAMPLES..];\n                let slope = (recent[2] - recent[0]) / TREND_SLOPE_DENOM;\n                let extrap = recent[2] + slope;\n                extrap.clamp(0.0, 1.0)\n            } else {\n                current_val\n            };\n\n            let confidence = if history_samples.len() >= TREND_CONFIDENCE_HIGH_DEPTH { TREND_CONFIDENCE_HIGH }\n                else if history_samples.len() >= TREND_MIN_SAMPLES { TREND_CONFIDENCE_MED }\n                else { TREND_CONFIDENCE_LOW };\n\n            let throttle = if trend_pred > PREDICTOR_THROTTLE_LOW { 1 } else { 0 };\n            let trend_error_prob = if trend_pred > PREDICTOR_THROTTLE_HIGH { TREND_ERROR_HIGH } else { trend_pred * TREND_ERROR_LOW_MUL };\n            bids.push(Self::make_bid(\n                metric_idx, trend_pred, "trend", confidence, throttle,\n                trend_pred * TREND_FRICTION, trend_error_prob,\n            ));\n        }\n\n        // ── Degraded mode: cap all model confidences ──────────────────────\n        if self.degraded {\n            for bid in &mut bids {\n                bid.confidence = bid.confidence.min(PREDICTOR_NORMAL_CONFIDENCE);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // ── Sort bids by confidence (highest first) ───────────────────────\n        crate::sort_by_f64_desc(&mut bids, |b| b.confidence);\n\n        // Convert to PredictedOutcome\n        let outcomes: Vec<PredictedOutcome> = bids.into_iter()\n            .filter(|b| b.confidence >= self.config.min_confidence)\n            .map(|b| {\n                let warning = b.error_prob > PREDICTOR_SIM_HIGH_ERROR || b.throttle >= 2 || b.predicted_value > PREDICTOR_THROTTLE_HIGH;\n                PredictedOutcome {\n                    metric_index: b.metric_index,\n                    metric_name: metric_name.clone(),\n                    predicted_value: b.predicted_value,\n                    current_value: current_val,\n                    confidence: b.confidence,\n                    model: b.model,\n                    predicted_throttle: b.throttle,\n                    friction_score: b.friction,\n                    error_probability: b.error_prob,\n                    warning,\n                }\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        outcomes\n    }\n\n    /// Predict ALL metrics at once (batch prediction).\n    ///\n    /// Returns one outcome per metric, using the highest-confidence bid\n    /// for each. This is the main prediction entry point.\n    pub fn predict_all(&self, action_name: &str) -> Vec<PredictedOutcome> {\n        let mut all: Vec<PredictedOutcome> = Vec::new();\n        for (_i, &name) in METRIC_NAMES.iter().enumerate() {\n            let outcomes = self.predict(name.to_string(), action_name.to_string());\n            if let Some(best) = outcomes.into_iter().next() {\n                all.push(best);\n            }\n        }\n        all\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether any metric predicts an imminent critical condition.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the list of critical predictions for alerting/auto-failover.\n    pub fn check_critical(&self, action_name: &str) -> Vec<PredictedOutcome> {\n        self.predict_all(action_name)\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|o| o.is_critical())\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Enter degraded mode (e.g. after a failure or circuit break).\n    pub fn enter_degraded(&mut self) {\n        self.degraded = true;\n    }\n\n    /// Exit degraded mode.\n    pub fn exit_degraded(&mut self) {\n        self.degraded = false;\n    }\n\n    /// Number of stored history states.\n    pub fn history_len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.history.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Number of crystal lattice entries.\n    pub fn crystal_len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.crystal.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Clear history and crystal memory (e.g. after a system reset).\n    pub fn reset_memory(&mut self) {\n        self.crystal.clear();\n        self.history.clear();\n        self.pid.reset_all();\n        self.current_state = None;\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Convenience API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Quick single-shot prediction: create a predictor, observe a state,\n/// and predict consequences of an action.\npub fn quick_predict(\n    current_metrics: Vec<f64>,\n    action: &str,\n    metric: &str,\n) -> Vec<PredictedOutcome> {\n    let mut pred = Predictor::new(PredictorConfig::default());\n    let state = SystemState::new(1, current_metrics, "current");\n    pred.observe(state);\n    // Add some history so trend model has data\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        let m: Vec<f64> = (0..DEFAULT_N_METRICS)\n            .map(|j| (i as f64 * 0.05 + j as f64 * 0.02).min(1.0))\n            .collect();\n        pred.observe(SystemState::new(100 + i as u64, m, "history"));\n    }\n    pred.predict(metric.to_string(), action.to_string())\n}\n\n/// Predict ALL dimensions and return whether any is critical.\npub fn quick_scan(metrics: Vec<f64>, action: &str) -> (Vec<PredictedOutcome>, bool) {\n    let _outcomes = quick_predict(metrics.clone(), action, "cpu_load");\n    let all = {\n        let mut pred = Predictor::new(PredictorConfig::default());\n        pred.observe(SystemState::new(1, metrics, "scan"));\n        pred.predict_all(action)\n    };\n    let critical = all.iter().any(|o| o.is_critical());\n    (all, critical)\n}\n\n// ─── EventSimulator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// An event to be dispatched through the system.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SystemEvent {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub payload_size_bytes: u64,\n    pub target_route: String,\n    pub priority: u8,\n}\n\nimpl SystemEvent {\n    pub fn new(name: &str, route: &str) -> Self {\n        SystemEvent {\n            name: name.to_string(),\n            payload_size_bytes: 1024,\n            target_route: route.to_string(),\n            priority: 5,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_size(mut self, bytes: u64) -> Self {\n        self.payload_size_bytes = bytes;\n        self\n    }\n}\n\n/// A possible route for event dispatch.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct EventRoute {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub base_latency_ms: f64,\n    pub reliability: f64,\n    pub max_payload_bytes: u64,\n    pub cost_multiplier: f64,\n    pub is_backup: bool,\n}\n\nimpl EventRoute {\n    pub fn new(name: &str, latency_ms: f64, reliability: f64) -> Self {\n        EventRoute {\n            name: name.to_string(),\n            base_latency_ms: crate::sanitize_f64(latency_ms),\n            reliability: crate::sanitize_normalized(reliability),\n            max_payload_bytes: 1_000_000,\n            cost_multiplier: 1.0,\n            is_backup: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn backup(mut self) -> Self {\n        self.is_backup = true;\n        self\n    }\n\n    pub fn estimated_latency(&self, event: &SystemEvent) -> f64 {\n        let size_factor = event.payload_size_bytes as f64 / self.max_payload_bytes as f64;\n        self.base_latency_ms * (1.0 + size_factor)\n    }\n\n    pub fn error_probability(&self, event: &SystemEvent) -> f64 {\n        let overload = (event.payload_size_bytes > self.max_payload_bytes) as u8 as f64 * 0.5;\n        let unreliability = 1.0 - self.reliability;\n        (overload + unreliability).min(1.0)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of simulating an event dispatch.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SimulatedDispatch {\n    pub event_name: String,\n    pub route_name: String,\n    pub estimated_latency_ms: f64,\n    pub error_probability: f64,\n    pub will_throttle: bool,\n    pub alternative_route: Option<String>,\n    pub is_backup: bool,\n    pub predicted_response: String,\n    pub warning: String,\n}\n\n/// Simulates event dispatch across routes to predict responses/reactions.\n///\n/// Before sending an event, call `simulate()` to see what would happen.\n/// If the simulation indicates problems, switch to an alternative route\n/// or activate a backup/fallback.\npub struct EventSimulator {\n    routes: Vec<EventRoute>,\n    predictor: Predictor,\n}\n\nimpl EventSimulator {\n    pub fn new(predictor: Predictor) -> Self {\n        EventSimulator {\n            routes: Vec::new(),\n            predictor,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn add_route(&mut self, route: EventRoute) {\n        if !self.routes.iter().any(|r| r.name == route.name) {\n            self.routes.push(route);\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn routes(&self) -> &[EventRoute] {\n        &self.routes\n    }\n\n    pub fn predictor(&self) -> &Predictor {\n        &self.predictor\n    }\n\n    pub fn predictor_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Predictor {\n        &mut self.predictor\n    }\n\n    /// Simulate dispatching an event through all available routes.\n    ///\n    /// Returns results for each route, sorted by estimated success\n    /// (lowest error probability first). The first result is the\n    /// recommended primary route; if it has warnings, check\n    /// `alternative_route` for a backup.\n    pub fn simulate(&self, event: &SystemEvent) -> Vec<SimulatedDispatch> {\n        let mut results: Vec<SimulatedDispatch> = Vec::new();\n\n        for route in &self.routes {\n            let latency = route.estimated_latency(event);\n            let error_prob = route.error_probability(event);\n            let will_throttle = error_prob > PREDICTOR_SIM_THROTTLE_ERROR || latency > PREDICTOR_SIM_THROTTLE_LATENCY;\n\n            // Predict system response to this dispatch.\n            let metric_name = match event.priority {\n                0..=3 => "latency_ms",\n                4..=7 => "throughput_rps",\n                _ => "error_rate",\n            };\n            let outcomes = self.predictor.predict(\n                metric_name.to_string(),\n                format!("event_{}_{}", event.name, route.name),\n            );\n\n            // Use the best prediction for this route.\n            let predicted_metric = outcomes.first()\n                .map(|o| format!("{:.2}", o.predicted_value))\n                .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".to_string());\n\n            let predicted_response = format!(\n                "route={} latency={:.0}ms error={:.1}% metric={}",\n                route.name, latency, error_prob * 100.0, predicted_metric\n            );\n\n            let warning = if will_throttle {\n                format!("THROTTLE: {} exceeds safe threshold", route.name)\n            } else if error_prob > PREDICTOR_SIM_HIGH_ERROR {\n                format!("HIGH_ERROR: {} unreliable ({:.0}%)", route.name, error_prob * 100.0)\n            } else if latency > PREDICTOR_SIM_HIGH_LATENCY {\n                format!("HIGH_LATENCY: {} too slow ({:.0}ms)", route.name, latency)\n            } else {\n                String::new()\n            };\n\n            results.push(SimulatedDispatch {\n                event_name: event.name.clone(),\n                route_name: route.name.clone(),\n                estimated_latency_ms: latency,\n                error_probability: error_prob,\n                will_throttle,\n                alternative_route: None, // set below\n                is_backup: route.is_backup,\n                predicted_response,\n                warning,\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Sort by error probability ascending.\n        crate::sort_by_f64_asc(&mut results, |r| r.error_probability);\n\n        // Set alternative route: if primary has issues, suggest the next best.\n        let needs_alternative = results.first()\n            .map(|r| !r.warning.is_empty() && results.len() > 1)\n            .unwrap_or(false);\n        if needs_alternative {\n            let alt_name = results.iter().skip(1)\n                .find(|r| r.warning.is_empty() || r.is_backup)\n                .map(|r| r.route_name.clone());\n            if let Some(ref name) = alt_name {\n                if let Some(primary) = results.get_mut(0) {\n                    primary.alternative_route = Some(name.clone());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        results\n    }\n\n    /// Find the best route for an event, falling back to backup if primary has issues.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `(primary, backup_option)` where backup is None if primary is safe.\n    pub fn best_route(&self, event: &SystemEvent) -> (&EventRoute, Option<&EventRoute>) {\n        let sims = self.simulate(event);\n        if sims.is_empty() {\n            panic!("no routes configured");\n        }\n\n        let best_route_name = &sims[0].route_name;\n        let primary = self.routes.iter()\n            .find(|r| &r.name == best_route_name)\n            .expect("route must exist");\n\n        let backup = if sims[0].will_throttle || !sims[0].warning.is_empty() {\n            // Find a backup route\n            for i in 1..sims.len() {\n                if !sims[i].will_throttle || sims[i].is_backup {\n                    let name = &sims[i].route_name;\n                    return (primary, self.routes.iter().find(|r| &r.name == name));\n                }\n            }\n            None\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        (primary, backup)\n    }\n\n    /// Simulate AND auto-failover: returns which route to actually use.\n    ///\n    /// If the primary route has predicted issues, switches to the best\n    /// alternative automatically.\n    pub fn dispatch_with_failover<'a>(&'a self, event: &SystemEvent) -> &'a EventRoute {\n        let sims = self.simulate(event);\n        if sims.is_empty() {\n            panic!("no routes configured");\n        }\n        if !sims[0].warning.is_empty() {\n            // Find the first safe route\n            for sim in &sims {\n                if sim.warning.is_empty() {\n                    let name = &sim.route_name;\n                    return self.routes.iter().find(|r| &r.name == name)\n                        .expect("route must exist");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // Use primary (first, lowest error probability)\n        let name = DEFAULT_N_METRICS], "single"));\n        let outcomes = p.predict("cpu_load".into(), "test".into());\n        for o in &outcomes {\n            assert!(o.confidence >= 0.99, "confidence {:.3} below min", o.confidence);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn event_simulator_alternative_route_set_on_failing_primary() {\n        let pred = Predictor::new(PredictorConfig::default());\n        let mut sim = EventSimulator::new(pred);\n        sim.add_route(EventRoute::new("failing", 5000.0, 0.1));\n        sim.add_route(EventRoute::new("safe_fallback", 20.0, 0.99));\n        let event = SystemEvent::new("test", "failing");\n        let results = sim.simulate(&event);\n        assert_eq!(results.len(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(results[0].route_name, "safe_fallback");\n        assert!(results[1].warning.contains("THROTTLE"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn quick_scan_critical_flag_true_for_high_metrics() {\n        let metrics = vec![0.98, 0.97, 0.99, 0.96, 0.95, 0.99, 0.97, 0.98];\n        let (_all, critical) = quick_scan(metrics, "stress");\n        assert!(critical || _all.iter().any(|o| o.warning));\n    }\n}\n	8145	-1	-1		e3f4be4fb0cca2a46909fac33aba133345dc97442dd0f72e615ee48893eeefc39506bde06ddc049fe27a562911d5f72ceead392437490caae6caf60d6fb6eb05bbaf53606d3ab0750047b91397abf0faf1480c7e2930ca05c4200086790bb365a0aef27536cb91daedf88b142f5c299965354d669581fef546a9cdf373b1b120
```

## 8168 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/router.rs · LongTerm

Summary: router · 340 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/router.rs	router · 340 lines	//! router.rs — CSR-native Dijkstra / A* shortest path + Contraction-Hierarchy\n//! shortcuts + OSM road-graph ingestion.\n//!\n//! P04 product-math library (BLUEPRINT-P04 §2). The single canonical, zero-\n//! dependency router for the kernel. Ported from\n//! `/root/bebop-repo/crates/bebop/src/cost_estimate.rs` (`route`, `build_shortcuts`,\n//! the `Prio` NaN-safe heap wrapper, the admissible A* heuristic) with all bebop\n//! couplings (serde derive, `Node2D`/`ConnEdge`, `field_physics`) dropped.\n//!\n//! Consumes [`crate::csr::Csr`] directly: for node `u`, neighbours are\n//! `col_idx[row_ptr[u]..row_ptr[u+1]]` with weights `val[..]` — no `Vec<Vec>`\n//! rebuild. Node coordinates `(lat,lng)` feed the **haversine** heuristic, an\n//! admissible lower bound *in metres* (great-circle ≤ any road path) so A* never\n//! returns a sub-optimal path when edge weights are metric distances.\n\nuse crate::csr::Csr;\nuse crate::geo::haversine_meters;\nuse core::cmp::Ordering;\nuse core::cmp::Reverse;\nuse alloc::collections::BinaryHeap;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Orderable f64 priority for the A* min-heap. `f64` is not `Ord` (NaN), so we\n/// order by `total_cmp` — a total order over all f64s (NaN sorts last, harmless\n/// for non-negative A* priorities). Ported verbatim from `cost_estimate.rs:35`.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]\nstruct Prio(f64);\nimpl PartialEq for Prio {\n    fn eq(&self, o: &Self) -> bool {\n        self.0.to_bits() == o.0.to_bits()\n    }\n}\nimpl Eq for Prio {}\nimpl PartialOrd for Prio {\n    fn partial_cmp(&self, o: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {\n        Some(self.cmp(o))\n    }\n}\nimpl Ord for Prio {\n    fn cmp(&self, o: &Self) -> Ordering {\n        self.0.total_cmp(&o.0)\n    }\n}\n\n/// A routable road graph: a CSR adjacency + index-aligned node coordinates.\n/// `coords[i] == (lat, lng)` of node `i` (used only for the A* heuristic).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct RoadGraph {\n    pub csr: Csr,\n    pub coords: Vec<(f64, f64)>,\n}\n\n/// A Contraction-Hierarchy shortcut: a precomputed `(from, to, weight)` that\n/// skips an intermediate node. Off by default — CH legitimately collapses\n/// intermediate hops, so it is applied only where the exact node sequence is\n/// not asserted. Ported from `cost_estimate.rs:148`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Shortcut {\n    pub from: usize,\n    pub to: usize,\n    pub weight: f64,\n}\n\nimpl RoadGraph {\n    /// Number of nodes.\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn nnodes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.csr.nrows()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Dijkstra / A* over the CSR. `heuristic == false` ⇒ pure Dijkstra (`h ≡ 0`);\n/// `true` ⇒ haversine A* (admissible metre lower bound to `dst`).\n///\n/// OPERATIVE PROPERTY (FEYNMAN-18): correctness of the no-reopen / closed-set\n/// A* below requires the heuristic to be **consistent**, not merely admissible:\n/// `h(u) ≤ w(u,v) + h(v)` for every edge, equivalently `w(u,v) ≥ haversine(u,v)`\n/// since `h` is great-circle-to-`dst`. Haversine-to-a-fixed-dst satisfies the\n/// triangle inequality, hence IS consistent whenever every edge weight ≥ the\n/// great-circle distance between its endpoints — which holds for metre/length\n/// costs but NOT for arbitrary `(u,v,cost)` triples fed via `road_graph_from_ways`\n/// (e.g. travel-time costs, which are numerically smaller than metres). Feeding\n/// inconsistent costs with `heuristic=true` yields silently sub-optimal routes.\n/// The `debug_assert!` in the relaxation loop catches this in debug/test builds;\n/// for non-metric costs, call with `heuristic = false` (pure Dijkstra, always optimal).\n///\n/// `shortcuts` augment the adjacency at query time (empty ⇒ exact node\n/// sequence). Returns `(node path src→dst, total weight)` or `None` if\n/// unreachable. Deterministic tie-break by node id via the `(Prio, usize)` heap\n/// ordering.\npub fn route(\n    g: &RoadGraph,\n    src: usize,\n    dst: usize,\n    heuristic: bool,\n    shortcuts: &[Shortcut],\n) -> Option<(Vec<usize>, f64)> {\n    let n = g.csr.nrows();\n    if src >= n || dst >= n {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let dst_coord = g.coords.get(dst).copied();\n    // admissible straight-line LOWER bound (metres) on remaining cost to DST.\n    // MUST measure i→dst or the heuristic is inadmissible (A* can go suboptimal).\n    let h = |i: usize| -> f64 {\n        if !heuristic {\n            return 0.0;\n        }\n        match (g.coords.get(i), dst_coord) {\n            (Some(&(ai, aj)), Some((bi, bj))) => haversine_meters(ai, aj, bi, bj),\n            _ => 0.0,\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Optional shortcut fan-out per source node (short-lived, no input mutation).\n    let mut extra: Vec<Vec<(usize, f64)>> = vec![Vec::new(); n];\n    for s in shortcuts {\n        if s.from < n && s.to < n {\n            extra[s.from].push((s.to, s.weight));\n        }\n    }\n\n    let mut dist = vec![f64::INFINITY; n];\n    let mut prev = vec![usize::MAX; n];\n    let mut visited = vec![false; n];\n    let mut heap: BinaryHeap<Reverse<(Prio, usize)>> = BinaryHeap::new();\n\n    dist[src] = 0.0;\n    heap.push(Reverse((Prio(h(src)), src)));\n    while let Some(Reverse((_, u))) = heap.pop() {\n        if visited[u] {\n            continue;\n        }\n        visited[u] = true;\n        if u == dst {\n            break;\n        }\n        // CSR row neighbours (ascending col order ⇒ deterministic).\n        let (lo, hi) = (g.csr.row_ptr[u], g.csr.row_ptr[u + 1]);\n        let csr_iter = (lo..hi).map(|k| (g.csr.col_idx[k], g.csr.val[k]));\n        let sc_iter = extra[u].iter().copied();\n        for (v, w) in csr_iter.chain(sc_iter) {\n            if visited[v] {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let ng = dist[u] + w;\n            if ng < dist[v] {\n                dist[v] = ng;\n                prev[v] = u;\n                heap.push(Reverse((Prio(ng + h(v)), v)));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if dist[dst] == f64::INFINITY {\n        return None;\n    }\n    // reconstruct src→dst.\n    let mut path = Vec::new();\n    let mut cur = dst;\n    while cur != usize::MAX {\n        path.push(cur);\n        if cur == src {\n            break;\n        }\n        cur = prev[cur];\n    }\n    path.reverse();\n    if path.first() == Some(&src) {\n        Some((path, dist[dst]))\n    } else {\n        None\n    }\n}\n\n/// Convenience alias: A* with the haversine lower bound and no shortcuts.\npub fn shortest_path(g: &RoadGraph, src: usize, dst: usize) -> Option<(Vec<usize>, f64)> {\n    route(g, src, dst, true, &[])\n}\n\n/// Build Contraction-Hierarchy shortcuts by contracting nodes in descending\n/// degree order (port of `cost_estimate.rs:157`). Reads adjacency straight from\n/// the CSR. Off by default (`route(..)`/`shortest_path` pass `&[]`).\npub fn build_shortcuts(g: &RoadGraph) -> Vec<Shortcut> {\n    let csr = &g.csr;\n    let n = csr.nrows();\n    let deg = |u: usize| csr.row_ptr[u + 1] - csr.row_ptr[u];\n\n    // degree-descending contraction order (stable tie-break by node id).\n    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();\n    order.sort_by(|&a, &b| deg(b).cmp(&deg(a)).then(a.cmp(&b)));\n    let mut rank = vec![0usize; n];\n    for (pos, &node) in order.iter().enumerate() {\n        rank[node] = pos;\n    }\n\n    // helper: existing direct weight a→b (INFINITY if absent).\n    let direct = |a: usize, b: usize| -> f64 {\n        let (lo, hi) = (csr.row_ptr[a], csr.row_ptr[a + 1]);\n        for k in lo..hi {\n            if csr.col_idx[k] == b {\n                return csr.val[k];\n            }\n        }\n        f64::INFINITY\n    };\n\n    let mut shortcuts = Vec::new();\n    for &mid in &order {\n        let (lo, hi) = (csr.row_ptr[mid], csr.row_ptr[mid + 1]);\n        let nbrs: Vec<(usize, f64)> = (lo..hi).map(|k| (csr.col_idx[k], csr.val[k])).collect();\n        for &(a, wa) in &nbrs {\n            if rank[a] <= rank[mid] {\n                continue;\n            }\n            for &(b, wb) in &nbrs {\n                if b <= a || rank[b] <= rank[mid] {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                let cand = wa + wb;\n                if cand < direct(a, b) {\n                    shortcuts.push(Shortcut {\n                        from: a,\n                        to: b,\n                        weight: cand,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    shortcuts\n}\n\n/// Build a [`RoadGraph`] from already-extracted OSM node coordinates + weighted\n/// ways. `nodes[i] == (lat,lng)`; `ways` are `(u, v, cost)` undirected triples.\n///\n/// Emits BOTH directions per way (CSR is directed; undirected = both) and floors\n/// each weight at `1e-6` (A*/Eikonal need `W > 0`). OSM parsing itself is a\n/// downstream (Phase 13) concern; this takes clean triples so the kernel stays\n/// I/O-free. Out-of-range endpoints are dropped by `Csr::from_edges`.\npub fn road_graph_from_ways(nodes: &[(f64, f64)], ways: &[(usize, usize, f64)]) -> RoadGraph {\n    let n = nodes.len();\n    let mut edges: Vec<(usize, usize, f64)> = Vec::with_capacity(ways.len() * 2);\n    for &(u, v, w) in ways {\n        let wf = w.max(1e-6);\n        edges.push((u, v, wf));\n        edges.push((v, u, wf));\n    }\n    RoadGraph {\n        csr: Csr::from_edges(n, &edges),\n        coords: nodes.to_vec(),\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // ── §6 #1: 10-node oracle. Total cost + endpoints hand-computed. ─────\n    //\n    // A line-ish weighted graph with one cheap detour. Coords are arbitrary\n    // small lat/lng so the haversine heuristic stays a valid lower bound.\n    //   0-1:1  1-2:1  2-3:1  3-4:1  4-5:1  5-6:1  6-7:1  7-8:1  8-9:1\n    //   plus a shortcut chord 0-5:10 (worse than the 5-hop chain of cost 5)\n    //   and 2-7:2 (a real shortcut: 0→1→2→7→8→9 = 1+1+2+1+1 = 6).\n    fn oracle10() -> RoadGraph {\n        // coords spaced 1e-6° (~0.11 m/step) so haversine to dst stays a valid\n        // lower bound (< the unit edge weights) ⇒ admissible heuristic.\n        let nodes: Vec<(f64, f64)> = (0..10).map(|i| (i as f64 * 1e-6, 0.0)).collect();\n        let ways = [\n            (0usize, 1, 1.0),\n            (1, 2, 1.0),\n            (2, 3, 1.0),\n            (3, 4, 1.0),\n            (4, 5, 1.0),\n            (5, 6, 1.0),\n            (6, 7, 1.0),\n            (7, 8, 1.0),\n            (8, 9, 1.0),\n            (0, 5, 10.0),\n            (2, 7, 2.0),\n        ];\n        road_graph_from_ways(&nodes, &ways)\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn oracle_shortest_path_cost_and_endpoints() {\n        let g = oracle10();\n        let (path, cost) = shortest_path(&g, 0, 9).expect("path exists");\n        // hand-computed minimum: 0→1→2→7→8→9 = 1+1+2+1+1 = 6.0\n        assert!((cost - 6.0).abs() < 1e-9, "min cost 6.0, got {cost}");\n        assert_eq!(*path.first().unwrap(), 0);\n        assert_eq!(*path.last().unwrap(), 9);\n        assert_eq!(path, vec![0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 9]);\n    }\n\n    // ── §6 #2: A* admissibility — A* == Dijkstra in cost AND sequence. ───\n    #[test]\n    fn astar_admissible_matches_dijkstra() {\n        let g = oracle10();\n        for &(s, d) in &[(0usize, 9), (0, 5), (3, 8), (9, 0), (1, 6)] {\n            let a = route(&g, s, d, true, &[]);\n            let dk = route(&g, s, d, false, &[]);\n            assert_eq!(a, dk, "A* must equal Dijkstra for {s}->{d} (cost+seq)");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ch_preserves_cost() {\n        // CH may collapse hops, so assert cost + endpoints only (not sequence).\n        let g = oracle10();\n        let sc = build_shortcuts(&g);\n        let (path, cost) = route(&g, 0, 9, true, &sc).expect("path exists");\n        assert!(\n            (cost - 6.0).abs() < 1e-9,\n            "CH keeps optimum 6.0, got {cost}"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(*path.first().unwrap(), 0);\n        assert_eq!(*path.last().unwrap(), 9);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn unreachable_returns_none() {\n        // isolated node 3 (no ways touch it).\n        let nodes = vec![(0.0, 0.0), (0.001, 0.0), (0.002, 0.0), (0.5, 0.5)];\n        let g = road_graph_from_ways(&nodes, &[(0, 1, 1.0), (1, 2, 1.0)]);\n        assert!(shortest_path(&g, 0, 3).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn from_ways_is_bidirectional_and_floored() {\n        let nodes = vec![(0.0, 0.0), (0.001, 0.0)];\n        let g = road_graph_from_ways(&nodes, &[(0, 1, 0.0)]);\n        // both directions routable; weight floored to 1e-6 (>0).\n        let f = shortest_path(&g, 0, 1).unwrap();\n        let b = shortest_path(&g, 1, 0).unwrap();\n        assert!(f.1 > 0.0 && b.1 > 0.0);\n        assert!((f.1 - b.1).abs() < 1e-18);\n    }\n}\n	8169	-1	-1		4b7f3f6d988f27b54301eecafb800b2b61de9764ade0f4e8e84cc249c3efed631d8c2e816dcac40ec953530b80d1fb288e251d25256c816ae5e2f28debb6fa4ee5fe55716558786993033812873be840cc70c86e69048f69f8a225b65c01837ce0e2d244b1c3925df8880a154e50695860b5452c9f80ccf4837146f328c425a0
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/self_harness.rs	self_harness · 316 lines	//! `kernel::self_harness` — Self-harness with zone protection.\n//!\n//! Analyzes the entire dowiz project, generates blueprints for safe\n//! rewrites, predicts impact dynamically, and enforces zone protection.\n//! Hydra (M9) is forbidden from modification. Red/critical zones require\n//! human operator approval.\n//!\n//! # Zone Model\n//! - **Green**: fully safe to rewrite (tests, docs, helpers)\n//! - **Yellow**: safe with verification (kernel internals, parallel patterns)\n//! - **Red**: requires operator approval (orchestrator, workflow gate, crypto)\n//! - **Critical**: requires dual-witness (P103 supervisor, PQ primitives)\n//! - **Forbidden**: NEVER modify (Hydra kill-switch, command filter, G9 breach alarm)\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse crate::TriState;\n\n/// Zone severity levels.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]\npub enum Zone {\n    Green = 0,\n    Yellow = 1,\n    Red = 2,\n    Critical = 3,\n    Forbidden = 4,\n}\n\nimpl Zone {\n    pub fn can_rewrite(&self) -> TriState { TriState::from_bool(*self < Zone::Red) }\n    pub fn needs_operator(&self) -> TriState { TriState::from_bool(*self >= Zone::Red) }\n    pub fn is_forbidden(&self) -> TriState { TriState::from_bool(*self == Zone::Forbidden) }\n}\n\nimpl core::fmt::Display for Zone {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Zone::Green => write!(f, "GREEN"),\n            Zone::Yellow => write!(f, "YELLOW"),\n            Zone::Red => write!(f, "RED"),\n            Zone::Critical => write!(f, "CRITICAL"),\n            Zone::Forbidden => write!(f, "FORBIDDEN"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── File Entry ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct FileEntry {\n    pub path: String,\n    pub zone: Zone,\n    pub lines: usize,\n    pub test_count: usize,\n    pub imports: Vec<String>,\n    pub exports: Vec<String>,\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n// ─── Rewrite Blueprint ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct RewriteBlueprint {\n    pub target: String,\n    pub zone: Zone,\n    pub description: String,\n    pub risk_score: f64,\n    pub affected_files: Vec<String>,\n    pub verification_steps: Vec<String>,\n    pub rollback_hash: [u8; 32],\n    pub predicted_latency_ms: f64,\n    pub predicted_test_delta: i64,\n}\n\nimpl RewriteBlueprint {\n    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> TriState {\n        TriState::from_bool(self.zone < Zone::Red)\n    }\n    pub fn needs_approval(&self) -> TriState {\n        TriState::from_bool(self.zone >= Zone::Red)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Impact Analysis ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ImpactAnalysis {\n    pub file: String,\n    pub zone: Zone,\n    pub direct_deps: Vec<String>,\n    pub transitive_deps: Vec<String>,\n    pub risk_score: f64,\n    pub rewrite_estimate_ms: f64,\n}\n\n// ─── Zone Map ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Known zone assignments for the dowiz kernel.\npub fn zone_for_path(path: &str) -> Zone {\n    // Forbidden: Hydra kill-switch, command filter, G9 breach alarm.\n    if path.contains("hydra") && (path.contains("kill") || path.contains("breach")) {\n        return Zone::Forbidden;\n    }\n    // Critical: PQ primitives, P103 supervisor, crypto signer.\n    if path.contains("pq/") || path.contains("p103") || path.contains("crypto_signer") {\n        return Zone::Critical;\n    }\n    // Red: orchestrator, workflow gate, memory, intake firewall.\n    if path.contains("orchestrator") || path.contains("workflow_gate")\n        || path.contains("memory") || path.contains("intake")\n    {\n        return Zone::Red;\n    }\n    // Yellow: parallel patterns, dynamic spawner/actions, search, AGC, parse.\n    if path.contains("parallel_") || path.contains("dynamic_")\n        || path.contains("agc_") || path.contains("search")\n        || path.contains("parse/") || path.contains("predict")\n        || path.contains("swarm") || path.contains("detection")\n        || path.contains("skill_extract") || path.contains("visual_index")\n    {\n        return Zone::Yellow;\n    }\n    // Green: everything else (tests, docs, helpers, CLI, hex_util).\n    Zone::Green\n}\n\n// ─── Self Harness ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The self-harness for analyzing and predicting rewrites.\npub struct SelfHarness {\n    pub files: Vec<FileEntry>,\n    pub blueprints: Vec<RewriteBlueprint>,\n    pub impacts: Vec<ImpactAnalysis>,\n    pub zone_counts: BTreeMap<Zone, usize>,\n    pub total_risk: f64,\n}\n\nimpl SelfHarness {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SelfHarness {\n            files: Vec::new(),\n            blueprints: Vec::new(),\n            impacts: Vec::new(),\n            zone_counts: BTreeMap::new(),\n            total_risk: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Register a file entry and compute its zone.\n    pub fn register_file(&mut self, path: &str, lines: usize, test_count: usize,\n                         imports: Vec<String>, exports: Vec<String>) {\n        let zone = zone_for_path(path);\n        let hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(path.as_bytes());\n        *self.zone_counts.entry(zone).or_insert(0) += 1;\n        self.files.push(FileEntry {\n            path: path.to_string(), zone, lines, test_count,\n            imports, exports, hash,\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// Analyze impact of rewriting a specific file.\n    pub fn analyze_impact(&mut self, target: &str) -> ImpactAnalysis {\n        let zone = zone_for_path(target);\n        let direct_deps: Vec<String> = self.files.iter()\n            .filter(|f| f.imports.iter().any(|i| i.contains(target)))\n            .map(|f| f.path.clone())\n            .collect();\n\n        let transitive: Vec<String> = self.files.iter()\n            .filter(|f| direct_deps.iter().any(|d| f.imports.iter().any(|i| i.contains(d.as_str()))))\n            .map(|f| f.path.clone())\n            .collect();\n\n        let risk = match zone {\n            Zone::Green => 0.1,\n            Zone::Yellow => 0.3,\n            Zone::Red => 0.7,\n            Zone::Critical => 0.9,\n            Zone::Forbidden => 1.0,\n        };\n        let estimate_ms = (direct_deps.len() as f64 * 50.0) + (transitive.len() as f64 * 20.0);\n\n        ImpactAnalysis {\n            file: target.to_string(), zone, direct_deps, transitive_deps: transitive,\n            risk_score: risk, rewrite_estimate_ms: estimate_ms,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a rewrite blueprint.\n    pub fn blueprint(&mut self, target: &str, description: &str) -> Option<RewriteBlueprint> {\n        let zone = zone_for_path(target);\n        if zone.is_forbidden().is_true() {\n            return None; // Cannot create blueprint for forbidden zone.\n        }\n        let impact = self.analyze_impact(target);\n        let rollback_hash = self.files.iter()\n            .find(|f| f.path == target)\n            .map(|f| f.hash)\n            .unwrap_or([0u8; 32]);\n\n        let bp = RewriteBlueprint {\n            target: target.to_string(),\n            zone,\n            description: description.to_string(),\n            risk_score: impact.risk_score,\n            affected_files: impact.direct_deps.clone(),\n            verification_steps: vec![\n                format!("cargo test --features pq"),\n                format!("cargo clippy --features pq -- -D warnings"),\n                format!("git diff --stat HEAD"),\n            ],\n            rollback_hash,\n            predicted_latency_ms: impact.rewrite_estimate_ms,\n            predicted_test_delta: impact.direct_deps.len() as i64 * -2,\n        };\n        self.total_risk += bp.risk_score;\n        self.blueprints.push(bp.clone());\n        Some(bp)\n    }\n\n    /// Predict whether a rewrite is safe (no zone violations).\n    pub fn predict_safe(&self, target: &str) -> TriState {\n        zone_for_path(target).can_rewrite()\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII dashboard.\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(512);\n        out.push_str("Self-Harness Dashboard\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Files registered: {}\\n", self.files.len()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Blueprints:       {}\\n", self.blueprints.len()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Total risk:       {:.2}\\n", self.total_risk));\n        for zone in [Zone::Green, Zone::Yellow, Zone::Red, Zone::Critical, Zone::Forbidden] {\n            let count = self.zone_counts.get(&zone).unwrap_or(&0);\n            out.push_str(&format!("  {:<10} {:>4} files\\n", format!("{}:", zone), count));\n        }\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn zone_for_hydra_is_forbidden() {\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("src/hydra/kill_switch.rs"), Zone::Forbidden);\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("src/hydra/breach_alarm.rs"), Zone::Forbidden);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn zone_for_pq_is_critical() {\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("src/pq/dsa.rs"), Zone::Critical);\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("src/crypto_signer.rs"), Zone::Critical);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn zone_for_orchestrator_is_red() {\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("src/orchestrator.rs"), Zone::Red);\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("src/workflow_gate.rs"), Zone::Red);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn zone_for_parallel_is_yellow() {\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("src/parallel_patterns.rs"), Zone::Yellow);\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("src/dynamic_spawner.rs"), Zone::Yellow);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn zone_for_misc_is_green() {\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("src/hex_util.rs"), Zone::Green);\n        assert_eq!(zone_for_path("tests/foo.rs"), Zone::Green);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn forbidden_blocks_blueprint() {\n        let mut h = SelfHarness::new();\n        assert!(h.blueprint("src/hydra/kill_switch.rs", "test").is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn blueprint_generated_for_yellow() {\n        let mut h = SelfHarness::new();\n        let bp = h.blueprint("src/parallel_patterns.rs", "add caching");\n        assert!(bp.is_some());\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/sha256_hw.rs	sha256_hw · 241 lines	//! sha256_hw.rs — SHA-256 hardware acceleration using SHA-NI.\n//!\n//! SHA-NI accelerates SHA-1 and SHA-256 (NOT SHA3/Keccak). Used here for\n//! fast integrity checks where SHA3 is overkill. The module provides a\n//! runtime-detection gate and a `sha256_hw()` function that selects the SHA-NI\n//! fast path when the CPU supports it, with a pure-Rust scalar fallback.\n//!\n//! # Architectural decision\n//! This module is for INTEGRITY checks only — fast content-digest verification,\n//! non-adversarial collision resistance. It is NOT for cryptographic MACs,\n//! signatures, or PQ constructions. Those paths continue to use the SHA3-based\n//! primitives in `crate::event_log::sha3_256` (Keccak, FIPS-202).\n//!\n//! # Runtime detection\n//! `sha256_hw_available()` calls `std::is_x86_feature_detected!("sha")`.\n//! On non-x86_64 hosts it returns `false`. The `sha256_hw()` function\n//! internally chooses the SHA-NI path or the scalar fallback per-call.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Check whether SHA-NI is available via CPUID.\n///\n/// SHA-NI accelerates SHA-1 and SHA-256 (NOT SHA3/Keccak).\n/// On non-x86_64 hosts this always returns `false`.\npub fn sha256_hw_available() -> bool {\n    #[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", feature = "std"))]\n    {\n        std::is_x86_feature_detected!("sha")\n    }\n    #[cfg(not(all(target_arch = "x86_64", feature = "std")))]\n    {\n        false\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute SHA-256 digest of `data`.\n///\n/// Uses SHA-NI hardware acceleration when available, otherwise falls back to a\n/// pure-Rust scalar implementation. Both paths produce identical byte output.\n///\n/// innovate: SHA-NI round function needs inline asm to capture both output\n/// registers (the `_mm_sha256rnds2_epu32` intrinsic discards XMM0 output).\n/// Currently uses scalar path unconditionally. Upgrade trigger: wire inline\n/// asm `sha256rnds2` with `inout("xmm0")` to capture cdgh output, KAT-gate\n/// against the scalar reference.\npub fn sha256_hw(data: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    // innovate: SHA-NI fast path deactivated until inline-asm harness\n    // captures both output registers. See sha256_hw_ni() doc above.\n    sha256_scalar(data)\n}\n\n// ── SHA-NI accelerated implementation ──────────────────────────────────────\n// innovate: SHA-NI round function needs inline asm to capture both output\n// registers (abef→XMM1, cdgh→XMM0). The current `_mm_sha256rnds2_epu32`\n// intrinsic only returns XMM1 — it discards the XMM0 (cdgh) output which\n// makes the standard SHA-NI pipeline unusable from safe/intrinsic Rust alone.\n// Upgrade trigger: when `_mm_sha256rnds2_epu32` is fixed to return both\n// registers, or when an `asm!`-based wrapper is harnessed and KAT-verified\n// against the scalar path. The scalar fallback (below) is correct and used\n// unconditionally for now; sha256_hw_available() still works for detection.\n\n#[allow(dead_code)]\n#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]\nunsafe fn sha256_hw_ni(data: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    // innovate: SHA-NI round function needs inline asm to capture both output\n    // registers (abef→XMM1, cdgh→XMM0). The current `_mm_sha256rnds2_epu32`\n    // intrinsic only returns XMM1 — it discards the XMM0 (cdgh) output which\n    // makes the standard SHA-NI pipeline unusable from safe/intrinsic Rust alone.\n    // Upgrade trigger: when `_mm_sha256rnds2_epu32` is fixed to return both\n    // registers, or when an `asm!`-based wrapper is harnessed and KAT-verified\n    // against the scalar path.\n    //\n    // For now: gracefully fall back to the scalar path. This function exists\n    // so the AES-NI preference compilation path can be activated in a single\n    // line once the asm harness is ready. It is NOT unreachable — it falls\n    // through to the KAT-verified scalar implementation rather than panicking.\n    sha256_scalar(data)\n}\n\n// ── Pure-Rust scalar fallback ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Standard SHA-256, no hardware acceleration.\nfn sha256_scalar(data: &[u8]) -> [u8; 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/spectral_laplacian.rs	spectral_laplacian · 261 lines	//! spectral_laplacian.rs — graph-Laplacian eigenmodes consumer of [`crate::spectral::eigh`].\n//!\n//! WAVE LAP: the *second* named consumer of the new symmetric eigensolver\n//! (the first being `spectral_cache`/`markov`). The field-UI engine needs the\n//! Laplacian eigenmodes `λ_k` for modal motion ([`crate::spectral`] module doc,\n//! line 12: "the field-UI engine needs Laplacian eigenmodes (λ_k) for modal\n//! motion"). This module is the canonical producer of that basis: the Fourier\n//! modes of the graph (spectral embedding / field-UI basis).\n//!\n//! MATH (unnormalized combinatorial Laplacian)\n//!   From a CSR adjacency `A` we build `L = D − A`, where `D` is the diagonal\n//!   degree matrix (`D_ii = Σ_j A_ij`). This is the SAME convention used by\n//!   [`crate::spectral::laplacian`], so the two are parity-bound. We pick the\n//!   *unnormalized* `L = D − A` as the default (the blueprint/spectral.rs:12\n//!   doc only names "Laplacian eigenmodes" with no normalization), and document\n//!   the choice explicitly. `L` is symmetric-PSD for an undirected (symmetric)\n//!   adjacency, so it is a legal input to the symmetric `eigh` engine.\n//!\n//! WHY NOT REIMPLEMENT\n//!   We REUSE `crate::spectral::eigh` (the dense `n ≤ 32` Householder\n//!   full-symmetric decomposition) — values ascending, orthonormal basis,\n//!   sign-fixed ⇒ byte-deterministic. For `n > 32` the dense path is capped, so\n//!   we fall back to the sparse tier `crate::spectral::topk_symmetric` (see\n//!   [`laplacian_eigenmodes`] for the documented semantic caveat). No new\n//!   eigensolver, no new deps.\n//!\n//! DETERMINISM\n//!   Same CSR input ⇒ identical `f64` bits across calls/paths. Inherited from\n//!   `eigh`/`topk_symmetric` (fixed seed, fixed summation order, sign-fixed\n//!   basis). Pinned by [`tests::lap_modes_are_byte_deterministic`].\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::csr::Csr;\nuse crate::spectral_cache::Decomp;\n\n/// Build the unnormalized combinatorial Laplacian `L = D − A` of a CSR graph as\n/// a dense `n × n` (row-major) matrix.\n///\n/// `A` is materialized from the CSR via [`Csr::to_adjacency`]. For an undirected\n/// (symmetric) adjacency `L` is symmetric-PSD; the caller is responsible for\n/// passing a symmetric adjacency (i.e. both `(s,d,w)` and `(d,s,w)` for every\n/// undirected edge). This matches the convention in\n/// [`crate::spectral::laplacian`].\nfn build_laplacian(csr: &Csr) -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n    let a = csr.to_adjacency();\n    let n = a.len();\n    let mut l = vec![vec![0.0f64; n]; n];\n    for i in 0..n {\n        let deg: f64 = (0..n).map(|j| a[i][j]).sum();\n        for j in 0..n {\n            l[i][j] = if i == j { deg - a[i][j] } else { -a[i][j] };\n        }\n    }\n    l\n}\n\n/// Laplacian eigenmodes of a graph — the `k` smallest-eigenvalue eigenpairs.\n///\n/// Builds the unnormalized combinatorial Laplacian `L = D − A` from the CSR\n/// adjacency, then solves for its eigen-decomposition and returns the `k`\n/// eigenpairs with the **smallest** eigenvalues (ascending order, so the first\n/// `k`).\n///\n/// * `n ≤ 32` (dense path, the field-UI regime): routes through\n///   [`crate::spectral::eigh`], which returns ascending eigenvalues with an\n///   orthonormal, sign-fixed basis. The first `min(k, n)` pairs are the\n///   smallest-magnitude modes — the Fourier modes / spectral-embedding basis.\n/// * `n > 32` (sparse tier, documented fallback): `eigh`'s dense path is capped\n///   at `n ≤ 32`, so we densify `L` and route through\n///   [`crate::spectral::topk_symmetric`], which consumes the Laplacian as a CSR\n///   and returns the **dominant** (largest-|λ|) `k` eigenpairs via Hotelling-\n///   deflated power iteration. NOTE: at `n > 32` the result is therefore the\n///   LARGEST-magnitude modes, NOT the smallest — a shift-invert solver (absent\n///   in the kernel) would be required for the true smallest eigenvalues at\n///   scale. The load-bearing tests exercise the `n ≤ 32` path.\n///\n/// Returns a [`Decomp`] `(basis, values)` where `basis[i]` is the unit\n/// eigenvector for `values[i]`, `values` ascending, `basis` orthonormal\n/// (`UᵀU = I`), byte-deterministic for equal input.\n///\n/// Never densifies-then-eighs in a way that exceeds the `n ≤ 32` cap: the dense\n/// `eigh` is only called when `n ≤ 32`; larger graphs take the documented\n/// `topk_symmetric` sparse branch.\npub fn laplacian_eigenmodes(csr: &Csr, k: usize) -> Decomp {\n    let n = csr.nrows();\n    let l = build_laplacian(csr);\n    let kk = k.min(n);\n    if n == 0 {\n        return (Vec::new(), Vec::new());\n    }\n    if n <= 32 {\n        // Dense symmetric path: eigh returns ascending eigenvalues; the first\n        // kk are exactly the k smallest eigenmodes.\n        let (basis, values) = crate::spectral::eigh(&l);\n        (basis[..kk].to_vec(), values[..kk].to_vec())\n    } else {\n        // Sparse tier (n > 32): densify L and route through topk_symmetric.\n        // Returns the dominant (largest-|λ|) kk eigenpairs — see module docs.\n        let l_csr = Csr::from_dense(&l);\n        crate::spectral::topk_symmetric(&l_csr, kk, 256)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use core::f64::consts::PI;\n\n    /// Undirected path graph P4: 0—1—2—3. Caller passes both edge directions so\n    /// the adjacency is symmetric (required for a valid symmetric Laplacian).\n    fn path_p4() -> Csr {\n        Csr::from_edges(\n            4,\n            &[\n                (0, 1, 1.0),\n                (1, 0, 1.0),\n                (1, 2, 1.0),\n                (2, 1, 1.0),\n                (2, 3, 1.0),\n                (3, 2, 1.0),\n            ],\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Undirected triangle K3 (complete graph on 3 nodes). Symmetric adjacency.\n    fn triangle() -> Csr {\n        Csr::from_edges(\n            3,\n            &[\n                (0, 1, 1.0),\n                (1, 0, 1.0),\n                (1, 2, 1.0),\n                (2, 1, 1.0),\n                (2, 0, 1.0),\n                (0, 2, 1.0),\n            ],\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Closed-form Laplacian eigenvalues of a path graph P_n:\n    /// `λ_k = 2 − 2·cos(π·k / n)`, `k = 0..n`. The known spectrum.\n    fn path_spectrum(n: usize) -> Vec<f64> {\n        (0..n)\n            .map(|k| 2.0 - 2.0 * (PI * k as f64 / n as f64).cos())\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Orthonormal basis check: UᵀU = I to `tol`. `basis[a]` is the a-th\n    /// eigenvector (column of U); the Gram entry (a,b) = Σ_i basis[a][i]·basis[b][i].\n    fn assert_orthonormal(basis: &[Vec<f64>], tol: f64) {\n        let kk = basis.len();\n        assert!(kk > 0, "orthonormality needs at least one vector");\n        let n = basis[0].len();\n        for a in 0..kk {\n            assert_eq!(basis[a].len(), n, "all eigenvectors share length n");\n            for b in 0..kk {\n                let dot: f64 = (0..n).map(|i| basis[a][i] * basis[b][i]).sum();\n                let expected = if a == b { 1.0 } else { 0.0 };\n                assert!(\n                    (dot - expected).abs() < tol,\n                    "orthonormality violated at ({a},{b}): dot={dot}, expected {expected} (tol {tol})"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Full known-spectrum check: every returned eigenvalue must match the\n    /// closed-form target (within `tol`).\n    fn assert_spectrum(values: &[f64], target: &[f64], tol: f64) {\n        assert_eq!(\n            values.len(),\n            target.len(),\n            "number of eigenpairs must equal spectrum size"\n        );\n        for (i, (got, want)) in values.iter().zip(target.iter()).enumerate() {\n            assert!(\n                (got - want).abs() < tol,\n                "eigenvalue[{i}] = {got}, expected {want} (tol {tol})"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn path_p4_known_spectrum_and_orthonormality() {\n        let csr = path_p4();\n        // Request all 4 modes (the full spectrum) to test orthonormality cleanly.\n        let (basis, values) = laplacian_eigenmodes(&csr, 4);\n        assert_eq!(values.len(), 4);\n        // Known Laplacian spectrum of P4: 2 − 2cos(πk/4), k=0..3\n        // = 0, 2−√2≈0.5858, 2, 2+√2≈3.4142.\n        assert_spectrum(&values, &path_spectrum(4), 1e-6);\n        // Basis is orthonormal (UᵀU = I to 1e-9).\n        assert_orthonormal(&basis, 1e-9);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn triangle_known_spectrum_and_orthonormality() {\n        let csr = triangle();\n        let (basis, values) = laplacian_eigenmodes(&csr, 3);\n        assert_eq!(values.len(), 3);\n        // K3 unnormalized Laplacian eigenvalues: 0, 3, 3.\n        assert_spectrum(&values, &[0.0, 3.0, 3.0], 1e-6);\n        assert_orthonormal(&basis, 1e-9);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn k_smallest_subset_is_orthonormal() {\n        // Requesting only k=2 smallest modes of P4 must still yield an\n        // orthonormal 2×4 basis (the field-UI embedding subset).\n        let csr = path_p4();\n        let (basis, values) = laplacian_eigenmodes(&csr, 2);\n        assert_eq!(values.len(), 2);\n        // The two smallest P4 eigenvalues: 0 and 2−√2.\n        assert_spectrum(&values, &path_spectrum(4)[..2], 1e-6);\n        assert_orthonormal(&basis, 1e-9);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn lap_modes_are_byte_deterministic() {\n        // Same input ⇒ identical f64 bits across two independent calls.\n        let csr = path_p4();\n        let a = laplacian_eigenmodes(&csr, 4);\n        let b = laplacian_eigenmodes(&csr, 4);\n        assert_eq!(a.1.len(), b.1.len());\n        for (x, y) in a.1.iter().zip(b.1.iter()) {\n            assert_eq!(\n                x.to_bits(),\n                y.to_bits(),\n                "eigenvalue bits differ across calls — not byte-deterministic"\n            );\n        }\n        assert_eq!(a.0.len(), b.0.len());\n        for (va, vb) in a.0.iter().zip(b.0.iter()) {\n            assert_eq!(va.len(), vb.len());\n            for (x, y) in va.iter().zip(vb.iter()) {\n                assert_eq!(\n                    x.to_bits(),\n                    y.to_bits(),\n                    "eigenvector bits differ across calls — not byte-deterministic"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn lap_modes_match_spectral_laplacian_parity() {\n        // Our mode eigenvalues must agree with the existing `spectral::laplacian`\n        // + `eigh` pipeline (parity with the kernel's own Laplacian convention).\n        let csr = triangle();\n        let adj = csr.to_adjacency();\n        let l = crate::spectral::laplacian(&adj);\n        let (_bl, vl) = crate::spectral::eigh(&l);\n        let (_, vmodes) = laplacian_eigenmodes(&csr, 3);\n        for (got, want) in vmodes.iter().zip(vl.iter()) {\n            assert!(\n                (got - want).abs() < 1e-9,\n                "mode eigenvalue {got} disagrees with spectral::laplacian+eigh {want}"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n}\n	8229	-1	-1		c35e3e66788f23b10303e1ce93021b2f447cbdeeac70f58fe254a00b40eee1451d0c7380cdd35ccfe1634169a1d5d93cce730d84726e0428b1e23a0bcf04beecefde1eb1af9f317b9789291bd7abeb49c570c91a2995ce49dc8038a45c87b765a062d2d5a3439135d81a88448eccce1140b7c16e7e85c5d40529d57c6ba42bf1
```
