4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/snapshot.rs	snapshot · 165 lines	//! snapshot.rs — drift-gated spectral snapshot store + reconcile (BLUEPRINT-P-B §4.3, item #7).\n//!\n//! `RetainedBase::admit` (spectral_cache.rs) is the drift-gated *constructor* of a single\n//! retained spectral tile. This module is the missing **consumer**: a store that collects\n//! admitted bases, persists them together with their source `Csr`, and can *reconcile* the whole\n//! retained set against the drift gate — re-running `classify_drift` on each retained tile's raw\n//! dynamics to detect a base that would now be classified Unstable (post-admit divergence).\n//!\n//! This is the "snapshot/arena reconcile" piece the live-status doc flagged as the only remaining\n//! sliver of Layer B/W2: the `_in` arena variants exist (scratch lands in a `BumpArena`), but\n//! nothing *calls* `RetainedBase::admit` to build a persisted, reconcilable retained set. The\n//! store keeps the source `Csr` so reconcile re-measures the *raw* dynamics (the same form the\n//! admit gate measures — anti-vacuity, BLUEPRINT-P-B §4.2), not the row-normalized tile.\n//!\n//! Firewall (mirrors spectral_cache.rs): pure `std`, zero network / serde / JSON. NO money /\n//! red-line types are touched — this is a pure kernel-spectral construct. The `BumpArena` field\n//! is retained so a caller can feed a retained `Csr` into `row_normalize_in(arena)` for downstream\n//! scratch reuse without a heap allocation; it is not required for the drift measurement itself.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::arena::BumpArena;\nuse crate::csr::Csr;\nuse crate::spectral::{classify_drift, DriftClass};\nuse crate::spectral_cache::{RetainedBase, SnapshotRejected};\n\n/// A retained spectral snapshot set, drift-gated at admit time and reconcilable after.\n///\n/// Each entry pairs the admitted [`RetainedBase`] (value type, the persisted tile) with the\n/// source [`Csr`] it was built from (the raw dynamics the gate measured). `admit` routes through\n/// [`RetainedBase::admit`], so an Unstable base is structurally unrepresentable in `entries`.\npub struct SnapshotStore {\n    /// Scratch region for downstream `_in` arena consumers (degrade-closed; sizes bounded).\n    arena: BumpArena,\n    /// The retained, drift-gated set: (source Csr, admitted base). Append-only; indices are\n    /// stable content handles.\n    entries: Vec<(Csr, RetainedBase)>,\n}\n\nimpl SnapshotStore {\n    /// New empty store with a scratch arena of `arena_bytes` (default 64 KiB if 0).\n    pub fn new(arena_bytes: usize) -> Self {\n        let bytes = if arena_bytes == 0 {\n            64 * 1024\n        } else {\n            arena_bytes\n        };\n        SnapshotStore {\n            arena: BumpArena::with_capacity(bytes),\n            entries: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow the scratch arena (for `row_normalize_in` / `from_edges_in` callers).\n    pub fn arena(&self) -> &BumpArena {\n        &self.arena\n    }\n\n    /// Number of retained (drift-gated) bases.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.entries.len()\n    }\n\n    /// True iff no bases retained yet.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.entries.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Retain a raw operator as a drift-gated snapshot.\n    ///\n    /// Routes through [`RetainedBase::admit`] — an Unstable (ρ>1) or NaN/±inf-poisoned rebuild\n    /// is refused with [`SnapshotRejected::UnstableSpectrum`] and NOT added. On success the base\n    /// AND its source `Csr` are appended; the stable index is returned.\n    pub fn retain(&mut self, raw: &Csr, epoch: u64) -> Result<usize, SnapshotRejected> {\n        let base = RetainedBase::admit(raw, epoch)?;\n        let idx = self.entries.len();\n        self.entries.push((raw.clone(), base));\n        Ok(idx)\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow the retained base at `idx` (stable content handle).\n    pub fn get(&self, idx: usize) -> Option<&RetainedBase> {\n        self.entries.get(idx).map(|(_, b)| b)\n    }\n\n    /// Reconcile the entire retained set against the drift gate.\n    ///\n    /// For each retained entry, re-runs [`classify_drift`] on the **raw** source dynamics (the\n    /// same form the admit gate measured — anti-vacuity). Returns the indices of every base that\n    /// now classifies `Unstable` — i.e. a base that, if re-admitted today, the gate would refuse.\n    /// An empty returned `Vec` means the retained set is still drift-coherent (the GREEN state).\n    ///\n    /// Pure measurement: the retained set is NOT mutated, so reconcile is idempotent and safe to\n    /// call repeatedly (e.g. on a timer) without losing data.\n    pub fn reconcile(&self) -> Vec<usize> {\n        let mut divergent = Vec::new();\n        for (i, (csr, _)) in self.entries.iter().enumerate() {\n            if matches!(classify_drift(&csr.to_dense()), DriftClass::Unstable) {\n                divergent.push(i);\n            }\n        }\n        divergent\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::csr::Csr;\n\n    fn damped() -> Csr {\n        // ρ = 0.5 raw operator (damped dynamics) ⇒ admitted.\n        Csr::from_dense(&vec![vec![0.5, 0.0], vec![0.0, 0.5]])\n    }\n    fn unstable() -> Csr {\n        // ρ = 2 raw operator (unstable) ⇒ refused at admit.\n        Csr::from_dense(&vec![vec![2.0, 0.0], vec![0.0, 2.0]])\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn retain_damped_base_succeeds_and_is_indexed() {\n        let mut store = SnapshotStore::new(0);\n        let idx = store.retain(&damped(), 11).expect("damped admit Ok");\n        assert_eq!(idx, 0);\n        assert_eq!(store.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(store.get(0).unwrap().epoch(), 11);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn retain_unstable_base_is_refused_and_store_unchanged() {\n        let mut store = SnapshotStore::new(0);\n        let res = store.retain(&unstable(), 7);\n        assert_eq!(res, Err(SnapshotRejected::UnstableSpectrum));\n        assert!(store.is_empty(), "Unstable base must NOT be retained");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reconcile_empty_store_is_green() {\n        let store = SnapshotStore::new(0);\n        assert!(store.reconcile().is_empty(), "empty set is drift-coherent");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reconcile_damped_set_is_green() {\n        let mut store = SnapshotStore::new(0);\n        store.retain(&damped(), 1).unwrap();\n        store.retain(&damped(), 2).unwrap();\n        let divergent = store.reconcile();\n        assert!(\n            divergent.is_empty(),\n            "all retained bases stay Damped ⇒ no divergence"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reconcile_rejects_what_admit_would_reject() {\n        // Synthetic "live edit" scenario: a base admitted as Damped, then its source dynamics\n        // are logically unchanged — reconcile must stay green. The gate's anti-vacuity property\n        // is that reconcile re-measures RAW ρ, so a stale (mutated) unstable base would be caught.\n        let mut store = SnapshotStore::new(0);\n        store.retain(&damped(), 1).unwrap();\n        // No mutation possible on the retained Csr (it is the admit-time source) ⇒ still green.\n        assert!(store.reconcile().is_empty());\n    }\n}\n	8247	-1	-1		ebdfbf57298f84210159c277d222db2ce5b61d6cf954d69dc9d46a5d96f5cf657cc6f4815ecf7603a54712f92171fa385c655d3431eb202af4633a8ecf14ea4607af14cb84dfe959c481a10097baa559677acc1e39c1ce4b56ac30e4320bd76da46af670b6f255acfa4d0e0f0c490eb92c39c02e17850af08fe3e4d0ab643371

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/spine.rs	spine · 387 lines	//! W2-7 — event-sourced hash-chain knowledge spine.\n//!\n//! A deterministic, append-only, **tamper-evident** log of knowledge records\n//! spanning three kinds — [`RecordKind::Memory`], [`RecordKind::Identity`], and\n//! [`RecordKind::Intent`]. Every record links to its predecessor by hash, so the\n//! whole spine is a hash chain: re-hashing from genesis and comparing each link\n//! detects any mutation of a payload, a link, or a record's own digest.\n//!\n//! This is intentionally a *plain hash chain*, **not** a signature scheme — it\n//! proves integrity/ordering against tampering, not authorship. It touches no\n//! money, no auth, no crypto keys. Pure `std` (the hash primitive is the\n//! dependency-free [`crate::event_log::sha3_256`]).\n//!\n//! ## Verified-by-Math\n//!\n//! * An untouched chain verifies `true` (`verify_chain_tamper_free`).\n//! * Mutating one record's `payload_hash` flips `verify_chain()` to `false`\n//!   (`verify_chain_detects_payload_tamper`).\n//! * [`KnowledgeSpine::query`] returns *only* records of the requested kind\n//!   (`query_by_kind_returns_only_that_kind`).\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\n#[cfg(test)]\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\n\n/// Sentinel `prev_hash` for the genesis (first) record — the empty hash.\npub const GENESIS_PREV: [u8; 32] = [0u8; 32];\n\n/// The three knowledge-record kinds tracked by the spine.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum RecordKind {\n    /// A stored memory / fact / observation.\n    Memory,\n    /// An identity assertion / agent or entity handle.\n    Identity,\n    /// An intent / goal / plan step.\n    Intent,\n}\n\nimpl RecordKind {\n    /// Deterministic one-byte discriminant (stable wire/storage encoding).\n    fn discriminant(&self) -> u8 {\n        match self {\n            RecordKind::Memory => 0,\n            RecordKind::Identity => 1,\n            RecordKind::Intent => 2,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Parse the discriminant back into a kind (inverse of `discriminant`).\n#[cfg(test)]\n    fn from_discriminant(b: u8) -> Option<Self> {\n        match b {\n            0 => Some(RecordKind::Memory),\n            1 => Some(RecordKind::Identity),\n            2 => Some(RecordKind::Intent),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The canonical, chained form of a knowledge record.\n///\n/// `record_hash` is the SHA3-256 digest of `(kind, payload_hash, prev_hash, id)`.\n/// Because `prev_hash` points at the previous record's `record_hash`, the\n/// `records` vector is a hash chain; mutating any field breaks the link.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct SpineRecord {\n    /// Stable caller-supplied identifier (e.g. `"mem-001"`).\n    pub id: String,\n    /// Which kind of knowledge this record carries.\n    pub kind: RecordKind,\n    /// Hash of the record's *content* (the payload), supplied at append time.\n    pub payload_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// Hash of the previous record's `record_hash` (or [`GENESIS_PREV`]).\n    pub prev_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// Self-hash of this record — the chain link.\n    pub record_hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Input shape for [`KnowledgeSpine::append`]: the caller-supplied fields that\n/// are *not* chain-derived. The spine computes `prev_hash` and `record_hash`.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct PendingRecord {\n    /// Stable identifier (e.g. `"mem-001"`).\n    pub id: String,\n    /// Knowledge kind.\n    pub kind: RecordKind,\n    /// Hash of the record's payload/content.\n    pub payload_hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Deterministically hash the *payload bytes* into a `[u8; 32]`.\n///\n/// Convenience so callers can hash content without reaching into `event_log`.\npub fn hash_payload(data: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    crate::event_log::sha3_256(data)\n}\n\nimpl SpineRecord {\n    /// Recompute this record's self-hash from its constituent fields. Used by\n    /// [`KnowledgeSpine::verify_chain`] to detect tampering.\n    fn compute_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        compute_record_hash(&self.id, self.kind, &self.payload_hash, &self.prev_hash)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Pure deterministic digest of a record's fields, in a fixed canonical order:\n/// `kind || payload_hash || prev_hash || len(id) || id`.\nfn compute_record_hash(\n    id: &str,\n    kind: RecordKind,\n    payload_hash: &[u8; 32],\n    prev_hash: &[u8; 32],\n) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 32 + 32 + 8 + id.len());\n    buf.push(kind.discriminant());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(payload_hash);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(prev_hash);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(id.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(id.as_bytes());\n    crate::event_log::sha3_256(&buf)\n}\n\n/// An append-only, tamper-evident knowledge spine (hash chain).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]\npub struct KnowledgeSpine {\n    records: Vec<SpineRecord>,\n}\n\nimpl KnowledgeSpine {\n    /// A fresh, empty spine (no records, genesis link pending).\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            records: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Number of records currently in the chain.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.records.len()\n    }\n\n    /// `true` iff the chain holds no records.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.records.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Append a pending record. Computes the `prev_hash` (from the current chain\n    /// tip, or [`GENESIS_PREV`] if empty) and the `record_hash`, then returns the\n    /// fully-chained [`SpineRecord`].\n    pub fn append(&mut self, pending: PendingRecord) -> SpineRecord {\n        let prev_hash = match self.records.last() {\n            Some(tip) => tip.record_hash,\n            None => GENESIS_PREV,\n        };\n        let record_hash =\n            compute_record_hash(&pending.id, pending.kind, &pending.payload_hash, &prev_hash);\n        let record = SpineRecord {\n            id: pending.id,\n            kind: pending.kind,\n            payload_hash: pending.payload_hash,\n            prev_hash,\n            record_hash,\n        };\n        self.records.push(record.clone());\n        record\n    }\n\n    /// Reconstruct a spine from a previously-persisted, ordered record list\n    /// (e.g. loaded from disk by a caller like `bin/spine_snapshot.rs`) and\n    /// verify it BEFORE accepting — fail-closed: a tampered, reordered, or\n    /// corrupt record list is refused, never silently loaded as if it were\n    /// trustworthy. This is the load-side half of tamper evidence: `append`\n    /// proves a chain built THIS run is internally consistent; `from_persisted`\n    /// is what proves a chain read back from disk on a LATER run still is.\n    pub fn from_persisted(records: Vec<SpineRecord>) -> Result<Self, ()> {\n        let spine = Self { records };\n        if spine.verify_chain() {\n            Ok(spine)\n        } else {\n            Err(())\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow the full ordered chain.\n    pub fn records(&self) -> &[SpineRecord] {\n        &self.records\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow a record by position in the chain (0 = genesis).\n    pub fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&SpineRecord> {\n        self.records.get(index)\n    }\n\n    /// Mutable borrow of the chain — test seam only (`cargo test` never ships).\n    /// Lets a tamper test flip a field in place and confirm `verify_chain()`\n    /// then returns `false`.\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub(crate) fn records_mut_for_test(&mut self) -> &mut Vec<SpineRecord> {\n        &mut self.records\n    }\n\n    /// Return references to every record whose kind matches `kind`, in chain order.\n    pub fn query(&self, kind: RecordKind) -> Vec<&SpineRecord> {\n        self.records.iter().filter(|r| r.kind == kind).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Re-walk the entire chain and return `true` iff it is internally\n    /// consistent and untampered:\n    ///\n    /// * the genesis record's `prev_hash` equals [`GENESIS_PREV`];\n    /// * every subsequent record's `prev_hash` equals the previous record's\n    ///   `record_hash`;\n    /// * every record's stored `record_hash` matches the digest recomputed from\n    ///   its fields.\n    ///\n    /// An empty spine verifies `true` (vacuously). Any mutation — of a payload,\n    /// a link, or a stored digest — yields `false`.\n    pub fn verify_chain(&self) -> bool {\n        let mut expected_prev = GENESIS_PREV;\n        for rec in &self.records {\n            if rec.prev_hash != expected_prev {\n                return false;\n            }\n            if rec.record_hash != rec.compute_hash() {\n                return false;\n            }\n            expected_prev = rec.record_hash;\n        }\n        true\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn pending(id: &str, kind: RecordKind, payload: &[u8]) -> PendingRecord {\n        PendingRecord {\n            id: id.to_string(),\n            kind,\n            payload_hash: hash_payload(payload),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_chain_tamper_free() {\n        // RED->GREEN (1): a freshly appended chain verifies true.\n        let mut spine = KnowledgeSpine::new();\n        spine.append(pending("mem-1", RecordKind::Memory, b"first memory"));\n        spine.append(pending("id-1", RecordKind::Identity, b"agent alice"));\n        spine.append(pending("int-1", RecordKind::Intent, b"ship the spine"));\n        spine.append(pending("mem-2", RecordKind::Memory, b"second memory"));\n\n        assert_eq!(spine.len(), 4);\n        assert!(spine.verify_chain(), "untouched chain must verify true");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_chain_detects_payload_tamper() {\n        // RED->GREEN (2): mutating one record's payload_hash breaks the chain.\n        let mut spine = KnowledgeSpine::new();\n        spine.append(pending("mem-1", RecordKind::Memory, b"first memory"));\n        spine.append(pending("id-1", RecordKind::Identity, b"agent alice"));\n        spine.append(pending("int-1", RecordKind::Intent, b"ship the spine"));\n\n        // Sanity: clean chain verifies.\n        assert!(spine.verify_chain());\n\n        // Tamper: flip a byte in the middle record's payload_hash.\n        let tampered = {\n            let mut h = spine.get(1).unwrap().payload_hash;\n            h[0] ^= 0xFF;\n            h\n        };\n        // Mutate the live record in place (simulating a silent edit).\n        let rec = spine.records_mut_for_test().get_mut(1).unwrap();\n        rec.payload_hash = tampered;\n\n        assert!(\n            !spine.verify_chain(),\n            "tampered payload must fail verification"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_chain_detects_prev_hash_tamper() {\n        // Bonus: breaking a link (prev_hash) is also detected.\n        let mut spine = RecordKind::Intent, b"c"));\n\n        assert!(spine.verify_chain());\n        let rec = spine.records_mut_for_test().get_mut(2).unwrap();\n        rec.prev_hash[0] ^= 0x01;\n        assert!(!spine.verify_chain());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn query_by_kind_returns_only_that_kind() {\n        // RED->GREEN (3): query filters to the requested kind exclusively.\n        let mut spine = KnowledgeSpine::new();\n        spine.append(pending("mem-1", RecordKind::Memory, b"m1"));\n        spine.append(pending("id-1", RecordKind::Identity, b"i1"));\n        spine.append(pending("mem-2", RecordKind::Memory, b"m2"));\n        spine.append(pending("int-1", RecordKind::Intent, b"n1"));\n        spine.append(pending("id-2", RecordKind::Identity, b"i2"));\n\n        let mem = spine.query(RecordKind::Memory);\n        assert_eq!(mem.len(), 2);\n        assert!(mem.iter().all(|r| r.kind == RecordKind::Memory));\n        assert_eq!(mem[0].id, "mem-1");\n     let intents = spine.query(RecordKind::Intent);\n        assert_eq!(intents.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(intents[0].id, "int-1");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn genesis_prev_is_sentinel_and_empty_verifies() {\n        let spine = KnowledgeSpine::new();\n        assert!(spine.verify_chain(), "empty spine verifies vacuously");\n GENESIS_PREV);\n        assert!(spine.verify_chain());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kind_discriminant_round_trips() {\n        for k in [RecordKind::Memory, RecordKind::Identity, RecordKind::Intent] Returns the original norm.\n    pub fn normalize(&mut self) -> f64 {\n        let n = self.norm();\n        if n > 0.0 {\n            for x in &mut self.data {\n                *x /= n;\n            }\n        }\n        n\n    }\n\n    /// Element-wise add.\n    pub fn add(&self, other: &Tensor1) -> Tensor1 {\n        assert_eq!(self.len(), other.len());\n        Tensor1::new(self.data.iter().zip(&other.data).map(|(a, b)| a + b).collect())\n    }\n\n    /// Element-wise subtract.\n    pub fn sub(&self, other: &Tensor1) -> Tensor1 {\n        assert_eq!(self.len(), other.len());\n        Tensor1::new(self.data.iter().zip(&other.data).map(|(a, b)| a - b).collect())\n    }\n\n    /// Scalar multiply.\n    pub fn scale(&self, s: f64) -> Tensor1 {\n        Tensor1::new(self.data.iter().map(|x| x * s).collect())\n    }\n\n    /// Cosine similarity with another tensor.\n    pub fn cosine_sim(&self, other: &Tensor1) -> f64 {\n        let dot = self.dot(other);\n        let norm_product = self.norm() * other.norm();\n        if norm_product > 0.0 { dot / norm_product } else { 0.0 }\n    }\n\n    /// Angle between two vectors, returned as a [`Phase`](crate::trig::Phase).\n    ///\n    /// Uses `acos(cosine_sim)` then wraps in `Phase::new(θ)`. {\n                assert!((t.get(r, c) - a.get(c, r)).abs() < 1e-12,\n                    "transpose mismatch [{r},{c}]");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn batch_dot_empty() {\n        let result = batch_dot(&[], &[]);\n        assert!(result.is_empty());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn outer_product_zero_length() {\n        let a = Tensor1::new(vec![]);\n        let b = Tensor1::new(vec![]);\n        let o = outer(&a, &b);\n        assert_eq!(o.rows, 0);\n        assert_eq!(o.cols, 0);\n    }\n\n    // ── JAMMING / INJECTION ────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tensor1_jamming_nan_inf() {\n        let t = Tensor1::new(vec![f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, 0.5, -1.0, 2.0]);\n        for i in 0..t.len() {\n            let v = t.get(i);\n            assert!(v.is_finite(), "Tensor1 index {i} must be finite: {v}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tensor2_jamming_nan_inf() {\n        let data = vec![f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, 0.5, f64::NEG_INFINITY, -1.0, 2.0];\n        let t = Tensor2::new(2, 3, data);\n        for r in 0..t.rows {\n            for c in 0..t.cols {\n                let v = t.get(r, c);\n                assert!(v.is_finite(), "Tensor2 [{r},{c}] must be finite: {v}");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tensor_jamming_then_normal_operation() {\n        // Jammed tensor followed by normal operations\n        let t = Tensor2::new(2, 2, vec![f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, 0.3, 0.4]);\n        let tt = t.transpose();\n        for r in 0..tt.rows {\n            for c in 0..tt.cols {\n                assert!(tt.get(r, c).is_finite(),\n                    "transpose of jammed tensor must be finite [{r},{c}]: {}", tt.get(r, c));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tensor_identity_100x100_consistency() {\n        let eye = Tensor2::identity(100);\n        assert_eq!(eye.rows, 100);\n        assert_eq!(eye.cols, 100);\n        for i in 0..100 {\n            assert!((eye.get(i, i) - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12,\n                "identity diagonal [{i}] must be 1: {}", eye.get(i, i));\n        }\n        // Row * identity = row (check a few spots)\n        let v = Tensor1::new((0..100).map(|i| i as f64 * 0.01).collect());\n        let r1 = eye.mul_vec(&v);\n        for i in 0..100 {\n            assert!((r1.get(i) - v.get(i)).abs() < 1e-10,\n                "I*v[{i}] must equal v[i]: {} vs {}", r1.get(i), v.get(i));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Consistency: batch_dot must handle nan inputs gracefully\n    #[test]\n    fn batch_dot_nan_vectors() {\n        let a = vec![\n            Tensor1::new(vec![f64::NAN, f64::NAN]),\n            Tensor1::new(vec![0.5, 0.3]),\n        ];\n        let b = vec![\n            Tensor1::new(vec![f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY]),\n            Tensor1::new(vec![0.2, 0.8]),\n        ];\n        let results = batch_dot(&a, &b);\n        assert_eq!(results.len(), 2);\n        for &r in &results {\n            assert!(r.is_finite(), "batch_dot with NaN inputs must yield finite: {r}");\n        }\n    }\n}\n	8346	-1	-1		03f7b66e998fa5a50b89b3ca72221b3f6dde97edad70f760e95fc218b7ecf9271d04c78065dec4a7e174560191c0f324dead3d3465420ea8e6e8e603ce16e804ffc750e8675878759113900af329aaebd570e86e79b11e6154221d96714bb76584f6d755b4c3957b78e9ac858edd6d9360b54c7a9f929cf44779cc9363013123

pub chain: String,\n    pub address: String,\n    pub symbol: String,\n    pub decimals: u8,\n}\n\nimpl Asset {\n    pub fn new(chain: &str, address: &str, symbol: &str, decimals: u8) -> Self {\n min_to_amount: u128,\n    /// Side.\n    pub side: OrderSide,\n    /// Trader's wallet address.\n    pub trader_address: String,\n    /// Chain ID (EIP-155).\n    pub chain_id: u64,\n    /// Deadline (block number).\n    pub deadline_block: u64,\n    /// Nonce for replay protection.\n    pub nonce: u64,\n    /// Signature (simulated — real impl uses ECDSA/Ed25519).\n    pub signature: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Signer public key.\n    pub signer_pk: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Whether this intent is valid.\n    pub valid: TriState,\n    /// Arbitrary data for solver hints.\n    pub solver_hints: &str, chain_id: u64,\n        deadline_block: u64, nonce: u64,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let content = format!("{:?}{:?}{:?}{}", from, to, side, nonce);\n        let hash = sha3_256(content.as_bytes());\n\n        Intent {\n            id: hash,\n            from_asset: from, from_amount,\n            to_asset: to, min_to_amount: min_to,\n            side,\n            trader_address: trader.to_string(),\n            chain_id, deadline_block, nonce,\n            signature: vec![],\n            signer_pk: vec![],\n            valid: TriState::Unknown,\n            solver_hints: vec![],\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify intent integrity (hash match + signature check placeholder).\n    pub fn verify(&self) -> TriState {\n        if self.signature.is_empty() || self.signer_pk.is_empty() {\n            return TriState::False;\n        }\n        // Verify the content hash matches.\n        let content = format!("{:?}{:?}{:?}{}", self.from_asset, self.to_asset, self.side, self.nonce);\n        let expected_hash = sha3_256(content.as_bytes());\n        if self.id != expected_hash {\n            return TriState::False;\n        }\n        TriState::True\n    }\n\n    /// Whether this intent is expired.\n    pub fn is_expired(&self, current_block: u64) -> bool {\n        current_block >= self.deadline_block\n    }\n\n    /// Sign (placeholder — real impl uses secp256k1 or ed25519).\n    pub fn sign(&mut self, private_key: &[u8]) {\n        // In production: ECDSA or Ed25519 signature.\n        // This is a deterministic placeholder.\n        let msg = [&self.id[..], private_key].concat();\n        self.signature = sha3_256(&msg).to_vec();\n        self.signer_pk = private_key.to_vec();\n        self.valid =      if self.intents.len() >= self.max_intents {\n            return Err("pool full".into());\n        }\n        if intent.verify() != TriState::True {\n            return Err("invalid self.intents.push(intent);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Submit a solver bid.\n    pub fn submit_bid(&mut self, bid: SolverBid) -> Result<(), String> {\n        if !self.intents.iter().any(|i| *intent_id)\n            .collect();\n        candidates.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            let a_score = a.guaranteed_amount as f64 * (1.0 - a.fee_bps as f64 / 10_000.0);\n            let b_score =    }\n\n    /// Clean expired intents.\n    pub fn purge_expired(&mut self, current_block: u64) {\n        self.intents.retain(|i| !i.is_expired(current_block));\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) )\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn eth() -> Asset { Asset::new("ethereum", "0x0000", 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/weave.rs	weave · 179 lines	//! weave.rs — procedural pattern generators rendered as glyphs.\n//!\n//! Item #18 (Figma Weave): the reusable principle is *procedural geometry* —\n//! describe a pattern, get a deterministic visual. The post's examples\n//! (Cross-Stitch Chart, Spiral Symbol Weave, Brick Wall, Glitch Bloom) map\n//! directly to the kernel's glyph architecture: generate a 2D field, render it\n//! as braille/half-block via `pixel_snapshot`.\n//!\n//! Zero-dep, deterministic (seeded PRNG where randomness is wanted).\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Archimedean spiral points: `r = radius * t`, angle advances `turns` times.\n/// Returns `steps` (x, y) points in [−r, r]².\npub fn spiral_points(radius: f64, turns: f64, steps: usize) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {\n    let mut pts = Vec::with_capacity(steps);\n    for i in 0..steps {\n        let t = i as f64 / (steps.max(1) - 1) as f64;\n        let r = radius * t;\n        let theta = t * turns * 2.0 * core::f64::consts::PI;\n        pts.push((r * crate::math::cos(theta), r * crate::math::sin(theta)));\n    }\n    pts\n}\n\n/// Render a spiral as a braille scatter plot.\npub fn render_spiral(radius: f64, turns: f64, steps: usize, width: usize, height: usize) -> String {\n    let pts = spiral_points(radius, turns, steps);\n    crate::glyph_dashboard::render_scatter(&pts, width, height)\n}\n\n/// A bool grid: `true` = filled dot.\npub type Grid = Vec<Vec<bool>>;\n\n/// Brick wall pattern (offset every other row by half a brick).\npub fn brick_wall(rows: usize, cols: usize) -> Grid {\n    let mut g = Vec::with_capacity(rows);\n    for r in 0..rows {\n        let mut row = Vec::with_capacity(cols);\n        let offset = if r % 2 == 1 { cols / 4 } else { 0 };\n        for c in 0..cols {\n            // Brick joints every `cols/2` cells; offset rows shift the joint.\n            let brick = ((c + offset) / (cols / 2)) % 2 == 0;\n            let mortar = r % 2 == 0 && c % 2 == 0; // simple joint line\n            row.push(brick && !mortar);\n        }\n        g.push(row);\n    }\n    g\n}\n\n/// Cross-stitch (X) pattern on an n×n grid.\npub fn cross_stitch(n: usize) -> Grid {\n    let mut g = vec![vec![false; n]; n];\n    for r in 0..n {\n        for c in 0..n {\n            let diag = r == c || r + c == n - 1;\n            let center = r == n / 2 || c == n / 2;\n            g[r][c] = diag || center;\n        }\n    }\n    g\n}\n\n/// Deterministic glitch pattern: horizontal tear lines + sparse noise,\n/// seeded by `seed` (splitmix64, the kernel's canonical PRNG).\npub fn glitch(rows: usize, cols: usize, seed: u64) -> Grid {\n    let mut g = vec![vec![false; cols]; rows];\n    let mut s = seed;\n    let mut next = move || {\n        s = s.wrapping_add(0x9E3779B97F4A7C15);\n        let mut z = s;\n        z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9);\n        z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D049BB133111EB);\n        z ^ (z >> 31)\n    };\n    // Tear lines: a few full rows are "shifted" (bright).\n    let tears = 3;\n    for _t in 0..tears {\n        let row = (next() as usize) % rows;\n        for c in 0..cols {\n            g[row][c] = (next() & 3) != 0;\n        }\n    }\n    // Sparse noise.\n    for _ in 0..(rows * cols / 5) {\n        let r = (next() as usize) % rows;\n        let c = (next() as usize) % cols;\n        g[r][c] = true;\n    }\n    g\n}\n\n/// Render a bool grid as braille glyphs (each glyph = 2×4 dots).\npub fn render_grid(g: &Grid) -> String {\n    if g.is_empty() {\n        return String::new();\n    }\n    let rows = g.len();\n    let cols = g[0].len();\n    // Pack 8 bits (2 rows × 4 cols) per braille cell.\n    let mut out = String::new();\n    const DOT_OFFSET: [u32; 8] = [0x01, 0x08, 0x02, 0x10, 0x04, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80];\n    for br in (0..rows).step_by(4) {\n        for bc in (0..cols).step_by(2) {\n            let mut code = 0u32;\n            for dr in 0..4 {\n                for dc in 0..2 {\n                    let r = br + dr;\n                    let c = bc + dc;\n                    if r < rows && c < cols && g[r][c] {\n                        // Braille dot layout: dots 1-4 down the left column,\n                        // dots 5-8 down the right column.\n                        let dot = if dc == 0 { dr } else { dr + 4 };\n                        code |= DOT_OFFSET[dot];\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            out.push(char::from_u32(0x2800 + code).unwrap_or(' '));\n        }\n        out.push('\\n');\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn spiral_points_are_bounded() {\n        let pts = spiral_points(1.0, 3.0, 100);\n        assert_eq!(pts.len(), 100);\n        for &(x, y) in &pts {\n            assert!(x.abs() <= 1.0 + 1e-9);\n            assert!(y.abs() <= 1.0 + 1e-9);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn render_spiral_emits_braille() {\n        let s = render_spiral(1.0, 3.0, 50, 16, 16);\n        assert!(!s.is_empty());\n        assert!(s.chars().any(|c| ('\\u{2800}'..='\\u{28FF}').contains(&c)));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn brick_wall_shape_and_offset() {\n        let g = brick_wall(4, 8);\n        assert_eq!(g.len(), 4);\n        assert_eq!(g[0].len(), 8);\n        assert_ne!(g[0], g[1], "offset rows must differ");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cross_stitch_has_diagonals() {\n        let g = cross_stitch(5);\n        assert!(g[0][0] && g[0][4] && g[4][0] && g[4][4], "corners on diagonals");\n        assert!(g[2][2], "center");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn glitch_is_deterministic() {\n        let a = glitch(16, 16, 42);\n        let b = glitch(16, 16, 42);\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "same seed must yield identical pattern");\n        let c = glitch(16, 16, 43);\n        assert_ne!(a, c, "different seed must differ");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn render_grid_emits_braille() {\n        let g = brick_wall(8, 8);\n        let s = render_grid(&g);\n        assert!(!s.is_empty());\n        assert!(s.chars().any(|c| ('\\u{2800}'..='\\u{28FF}').contains(&c)));\n    }\n}\n	8394	-1	-1		ca947b4f9b8ebfe5c221a5c95b3393034d1ad7ccad30fecae84dee8ac3eead5751f46bc0edcc608efa5f44098169d2acceff6f60f9680e89f46372c2cb86f946efde74d12d1bf061530b901bf7afa9c2e0f0eaee79794e28f0422c94990909e4ada6d39414c9112bb8e90dc242dc099364b14c6274b3ccf48531d5d361e43127

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/trading_escrow.rs	trading_escrow · 238 lines	//! `kernel::trading_escrow` — Trustless escrow + state channel settlement.\n//!\n//! Pure data structures for smart-contract-based escrow and bidirectional\n//! payment channels. No intermediaries: funds are locked by math, not by\n//! a third party.\n//!\n//! # Escrow lifecycle\n//! 1. Offer: party A locks asset X in escrow contract\n//! 2. Accept: party B verifies terms and locks asset Y\n//! 3. Settle: both parties receive their counterpart's asset (atomic swap)\n//! 4. Cancel: either party can claim back after timeout\n//!\n//! # State Channel lifecycle\n//! 1. Open: both parties deposit into channel\n//! 2. Update: off-chain signed balance updates (infinite speed)\n//! 3. Close: final state submitted to chain\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::TriState;\n\n// ─── Escrow State ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum EscrowState {\n    /// Escrow created, waiting for counterparty.\n    Pending,\n    /// Both parties have deposited.\n    Active,\n    /// Settlement executed successfully.\n    Settled,\n    /// Escrow cancelled / refunded.\n    Cancelled,\n    /// Dispute raised.\n    Disputed,\n}\n\n// ─── Escrow Offer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A trustless escrow offer for peer-to-peer trading.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct EscrowOffer {\n    pub id: [u8; 32],\n    /// Party A (maker) address.\n    pub party_a: String,\n    /// Party B (taker) address.\n    pub party_b: String,\n    /// Asset party A offers.\n    pub offer_asset: super::trading_intent::Asset,\n    /// Amount party A offers.\n    pub offer_amount: u128,\n    /// Asset party A wants in return.\n    pub ask_asset: super::trading_intent::Asset,\n    /// Amount party A wants.\n    pub ask_amount: u128,\n    /// Block deadline for acceptance.\n    pub deadline_block: u64,\n    /// Current state.\n    pub state: EscrowState,\n    /// SHA3-256 of terms.\n    pub terms_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// Party A signature.\n    pub sig_a: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Party B signature.\n    pub sig_b: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nimpl EscrowOffer {\n    pub fn new(\n        a: &str, b: &str,\n        offer_asset: super::trading_intent::Asset, offer_amount: u128,\n        ask_asset: super::trading_intent::Asset, ask_amount: u128,\n        deadline_block: u64,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let terms = format!("{}{}{}{}{}{}{}", a, b, offer_amount, ask_amount, deadline_block, offer_asset.symbol, ask_asset.symbol);\n        let hash = sha3_256(terms.as_bytes());\n        EscrowOffer {\n            id: hash, party_a: a.to_string(), party_b: b.to_string(),\n            offer_asset, offer_amount, ask_asset, ask_amount,\n            deadline_block, state: EscrowState::Pending,\n            terms_hash: hash, sig_a: vec![], sig_b: vec![],\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn accept(&mut self, sig: &[u8]) {\n        self.sig_b = sig.to_vec();\n        self.state = EscrowState::Active;\n    }\n\n    pub fn settle(&mut self) {\n        self.state = EscrowState::Settled;\n    }\n\n    pub fn cancel(&mut self) {\n        self.state = EscrowState::Cancelled;\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── State Channel ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Off-chain balance update in a state channel.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ChannelUpdate {\n    /// Update sequence number.\n    pub seq: u64,\n    /// Balance for party A.\n    pub balance_a: u128,\n    /// Balance for party B.\n    pub balance_b: u128,\n    /// Nonce for replay protection.\n    pub nonce: u64,\n    /// Party A signature.\n    pub sig_a: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Party B signature.\n    pub sig_b: Vec<u8>,\n    /// SHA3-256 of state.\n    pub state_hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Bidirectional payment state channel.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct StateChannel {\n    pub id: [u8; 32],\n    pub party_a: String,\n    pub party_b: String,\n    pub asset: super::trading_intent::Asset,\n    /// Latest balance update.\n    pub latest: ChannelUpdate,\n    /// Whether channel is open.\n    pub open: TriState,\n}\n\nimpl StateChannel {\n    pub fn new(a: &str, b: &str, asset: super::trading_intent::Asset) -> Self {\n        let id = sha3_256(format!("{}{}{}", a, b, asset.symbol).as_bytes());\n        let initial = ChannelUpdate {\n            seq: 0, balance_a: 0, balance_b: 0, nonce: 0,\n            sig_a: vec![], sig_b: vec![], state_hash: [0u8; 32],\n        };\n        StateChannel { id, party_a: a.to_string(), party_b: b.to_string(), asset, latest: initial, open: TriState::True }\n    }\n\n    /// Update channel balances off-chain.\n    pub fn update(&mut self, balance_a: u128, balance_b: u128, sig_a: &[u8], sig_b: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        if self.open != TriState::True { return false; }\n        // First update establishes the total, subsequent updates conserve it.\n        if self.latest.seq > 0 && balance_a + balance_b != self.latest.balance_a + self.latest.balance_b {\n            return false; // Conservation violation.\n        }\n        let content = format!("{}{}{}{}", balance_a, balance_b, self.latest.seq + 1, self.latest.nonce + 1);\n        let hash = sha3_256(content.as_bytes());\n        self.latest = ChannelUpdate {\n            seq: self.latest.seq + 1,\n            balance_a, balance_b, nonce: self.latest.nonce + 1,\n            sig_a: sig_a.to_vec(), sig_b: sig_b.to_vec(), state_hash: hash,\n        };\n        true\n    }\n\n    pub fn close(&mut self) {\n        self.open = TriState::False;\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\n            "State Channel\\n  Asset: {}\\n  Bal A: {} | Bal B: {}\\n  Seq:   {}\\n  Open:  {}",\n            self.asset.symbol, self.latest.balance_a, self.latest.balance_b,\n            self.latest.seq, self.open\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests EscrowOffer::new("0xalice", "0xbob", eth(), 10_000_000_000, btc(), 100_000_000, 1_000_000);\n        assert_eq!(escrow.state, EscrowState::Pending);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn escrow_accept_and_settle() {\n        let mut escrow = EscrowOffer::new("0xa", "0xb", eth(), 1_000, btc(), 10, 500_000);\n        escrow.accept(b"bob-sig");\n        assert_eq!(escrow.state, EscrowState::Active);\n        escrow.settle();\n        assert_eq!(escrow.state, EscrowState::Settled);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn state_channel_update_conservation() {\n        let mut ch = StateChannel::new("0xalice", "0xbob", eth());\n        assert!(ch.update(100, 0, b"a-sig", b"b-sig"));\n        assert!(ch.update(70, 30, b"a-sig", b"b-sig"));\n        assert_eq!(ch.latest.balance_a, 70);\n        assert_eq!(ch.latest.balance_b, 30);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn state_channel_rejects_violation() {\n        let mut ch = StateChannel::new("0xa", "0xb", eth());\n        ch.update(100, 0, b"a-sig", b"b-sig");\n        assert!(!ch.update(200, 0, b"a-sig", b"b-sig")); // 200+0 != 100+0\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn state_channel_close() {\n        let mut ch = StateChannel::new("0xa", "0xb", eth());\n        ch.close();\n        assert_eq!(ch.open, TriState::False);\n        assert!(!ch.update(10, 0, b"a-sig", b"b-sig")); // Closed channel rejects\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dashboard_contains_channel() {\n        let ch = StateChannel::new("0xa", "0xb", eth());\n        let d = ch.dashboard();\n        assert!(d.contains("State Channel"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn escrow_cancel() {\n        let mut escrow = EscrowOffer::new("0xa", "0xb", eth(), 1, btc(), 1, 100);\n        escrow.cancel();\n        assert_eq!(escrow.state, ## 8493 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/clock_stabilizer.rs · LongTerm

Summary: clock_stabilizer · 820 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/clock_stabilizer.rs	clock_stabilizer · 820 lines	//! clock_stabilizer.rs — PLL-inspired tick stabilizer for kernel timing.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! A feedback control system that transforms irregular kernel ticks, timestamps,\n//! and event intervals into stable, aligned output. Modeled after a Phase-Locked\n//! Loop (PLL) -- the same control theory used in RF synthesizers, clock recovery,\n//! and motor control.\n//!\n//! # PLL -> Kernel Mapping\n//! ```text\n//!   IRREGULAR INPUT          PLL STABILIZER              STABLE OUTPUT\n//!   +-----------+     +------------------------+     +---------------+\n//!   | raw ticks | --> | Phase Detector         | --> | aligned ticks |\n//!   | timestamps|     |   (compare to ref)     |     | timestamps    |\n//!   | events    |     | Loop Filter            |     | events        |\n//!   | agent     |     |   (smooth jitter)      |     | latencies     |\n//!   | actions   |     | VCO-equivalent         |     | predictions   |\n//!   +-----------+     |   (adaptive rate)      |     +---------------+\n//!                     +------------------------+\n//! ```\n//!\n//! # Why this matters\n//! - Agent actions have variable latency (LLM calls, tool execution, I/O)\n//! - Without stabilization, metrics, predictions, and scheduling are unreliable\n//! - Stabilized ticks -> consistent FDR timestamps -> reliable spectral analysis\n//! - The PLL analogy gives us a proven feedback-control model (60+ years of theory)\n//!\n//! # Safeguards (mandatory cryptographic verification)\n//! - NaN/infinity guards on every f64 operation (fail-closed, never propagate)\n//! - Overflow protection on u64/u32 counters (saturating arithmetic)\n//! - Extreme jitter rejection (intervals outside sane bounds are clamped)\n//! - SHA3-256 byte-by-byte state verification (StabilizerVerifier)\n//! - Deterministic: same inputs always produce same outputs and same hash\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\n\nuse core::fmt;\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\n\n/// Maximum allowed interval in microseconds (10 seconds).\n/// Anything beyond this is clamped -- prevents runaway timers.\nconst MAX_INTERVAL_US: f64 = 10_000_000.0;\n\n/// Minimum allowed interval in microseconds (1 microsecond).\n/// Prevents division-by-zero and near-zero intervals.\nconst MIN_INTERVAL_US: f64 = 1.0;\n\n/// Maximum tick count before saturation (u64::MAX / 2 to leave headroom).\nconst MAX_TICK_COUNT: u64 = u64::MAX / 2;\n\n/// Maximum lock streak before saturation.\nconst MAX_LOCK_STREAK: u32 = u32::MAX / 2;\n\n/// Phase-Locked Loop stabilizer for kernel timing.\n///\n/// Transforms irregular inter-tick intervals into stable, aligned output.\n/// The loop continuously compares actual intervals against a reference rate,\n/// filters the error, and adjusts the output rate to match.\n///\n/// All f64 operations are guarded against NaN/infinity. All counters use\n/// saturating arithmetic. All outputs are SHA3-256 verifiable.\npub struct ClockStabilizer {\n    /// Target tick interval in microseconds (the "reference clock").\n    target_interval_us: f64,\n    /// EMA smoothing factor (0.01..0.99).\n    alpha: f64,\n    /// Filtered phase error (EMA-smoothed).\n    filtered_error: f64,\n    /// Current VCO phase accumulator (microseconds).\n    vco_phase: f64,\n    /// Number of ticks processed (saturating).\n    tick_count: u64,\n    /// Running estimate of actual interval (EMA).\n    estimated_interval: f64,\n    /// Lock detector: consecutive ticks within tolerance.\n    locked_streak: u32,\n    /// Threshold: ticks within tolerance before declaring lock.\n    lock_threshold: u32,\n    /// Tolerance: fraction of target interval for "in-sync" (e.g., 0.1 = 10%).\n    tolerance: f64,\n    /// External drift correction from power/thermal forecast (ns/s).\n    /// Positive = clock running fast, Negative = clock running slow.\n    /// Updated externally by PowerForecastEngine + TimeStabilizer.\n    external_drift_ns_per_s: f64,\n    /// Confidence in external drift correction (0.0..1.0).\n    drift_confidence: f64,\n}\n\n/// The result of stabilizing one tick.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct StabilizedTick {\n    /// The aligned output interval (microseconds).\n    pub aligned_interval_us: f64,\n    /// The phase error before filtering (microseconds).\n    pub raw_error_us: f64,\n    /// The phase error after filtering (microseconds).\n    pub filtered_error_us: f64,\n    /// The lock status at this tick.\n    pub lock: LockStatus,\n}\n\n/// Whether the PLL is locked (tracking the reference) or free-running.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum LockStatus {\n    /// Loop is locked -- output is stable and aligned to reference.\n    Locked,\n    /// Loop is acquiring -- filtering is still converging.\n    Acquiring,\n    /// Loop is free-running -- not enough data to determine lock.\n    FreeRunning,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for LockStatus {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            LockStatus::Locked => write!(f, "LOCKED"),\n            LockStatus::Acquiring => write!(f, "ACQUIRING"),\n            LockStatus::FreeRunning => write!(f, "FREE_RUNNING"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Cryptographic verifier for stabilizer state integrity.\n///\n/// Holds a SHA3-256 digest of the stabilizer's serialized state bytes.\n/// On each verification, the stabilizer serializes its state to bytes,\n/// computes SHA3-256, and compares against the expected digest.\n/// Byte-identical: every field in canonical order, little-endian for numerics.\npub struct StabilizerVerifier {\n    /// The expected SHA3-256 digest of the stabilizer state.\n    expected_hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Errors from the stabilizer's safeguards.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum StabilizerError {\n    /// Input interval was NaN or infinity.\n    NonFiniteInput,\n    /// Input interval was outside sane bounds (clamped to valid range).\n    OutOfBounds { input: f64, clamped: f64 },\n    /// Internal state became NaN (should never happen with guards -- if it does,\n    /// the stabilizer resets to safe defaults).\n    StateCorruption,\n    /// Cryptographic verification failed -- state hash doesn't match expected.\n    VerificationFailed {\n        expected: [u8; 32],\n        actual: [u8; 32],\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for StabilizerError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StabilizerError::NonFiniteInput => {\n                write!(f, "stabilizer: input must be finite (not NaN or infinity)")\n            }\n            StabilizerError::OutOfBounds { input, clamped } => {\n                write!(\n                    f,\n                    "stabilizer: input {:.1} out of bounds, clamped to {:.1}",\n                    input, clamped\n                )\n            }\n            StabilizerError::StateCorruption => {\n                write!(f, "stabilizer: internal state corruption detected, reset to safe defaults")\n            }\n            StabilizerError::VerificationFailed { expected, actual } => {\n                write!(\n                    f,\n                    "stabilizer: SHA3-256 verification failed -- expected {:02x?}, got {:02x?}",\n                    expected, actual\n                )\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Safely clamp an f64: reject NaN/infinity, clamp to [MIN, MAX].\nfn safe_f64(value: f64, min: f64, max: f64) -> Result<f64, StabilizerError> {\n    if !value.is_finite() {\n        return Err(StabilizerError::NonFiniteInput);\n    }\n    if value < min || value > max {\n        let clamped = value.clamp(min, max);\n        return Err(StabilizerError::OutOfBounds {\n            input: value,\n            clamped,\n        });\n    }\n    Ok(value)\n}\n\n/// Check if an f64 is finite; if not, return a safe default.\nfn guard_f64(value: f64, default: f64) -> f64 {\n    if value.is_finite() {\n        value\n    } else {\n        default\n    }\n}\n\n/// Saturating increment for u64.\nfn sat_inc_u64(v: u64) -> u64 {\n    v.saturating_add(1).min(MAX_TICK_COUNT)\n}\n\n/// Saturating increment for u32.\nfn sat_inc_u32(v: u32) -> u32 {\n    v.saturating_add(1).min(MAX_LOCK_STREAK)\n}\n\n/// Serialize stabilizer state to bytes (canonical, deterministic layout).\n///\n/// Field order: target (8 bytes LE) + alpha (8) + filtered_error (8) +\n/// vco_phase (8) + tick_count (8) + estimated_interval (8) +\n/// locked_streak (4) + lock_threshold (4) + tolerance (8) +\n/// external_drift_ns_per_s (8) + drift_confidence (8) = 80 bytes.\nfn serialize_state(s: &ClockStabilizer) -> [u8; 80] {\n    let mut buf = [0u8; 80];\n    buf[0..8].copy_from_slice(&s.target_interval_us.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[8..16].copy_from_slice(&s.alpha.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[16..24].copy_from_slice(&s.filtered_error.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[24..32].copy_from_slice(&s.vco_phase.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[32..40].copy_from_slice(&s.tick_count.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[40..48].copy_from_slice(&s.estimated_interval.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[48..52].copy_from_slice(&s.locked_streak.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[52..56].copy_from_slice(&s.lock_threshold.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[56..64].copy_from_slice(&s.tolerance.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[64..72].copy_from_slice(&s.external_drift_ns_per_s.to_le_bytes());\n    buf[72..80].copy_from_slice(&s.drift_confidence.to_le_bytes());\n    buf\n}\n\n/// Compute SHA3-256 of the stabilizer's serialized state.\nfn state_hash(s: &ClockStabilizer) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let bytes = serialize_state(s);\n    sha3_256(&bytes)\n}\n\nimpl ClockStabilizer {\n    /// Create a new stabilizer with a target tick interval and smoothing factor.\n    pub fn new(target_interval_us: f64, alpha: f64) -> Self {\n        // Guard: target must be finite and in bounds.\n        let target = safe_f64(target_interval_us, MIN_INTERVAL_US, MAX_INTERVAL_US)\n            .unwrap_or(1000.0);\n        let alpha_clamped = alpha.clamp(0.01, 0.99);\n\n        ClockStabilizer {\n            target_interval_us: target,\n            alpha: alpha_clamped,\n            filtered_error: 0.0,\n            vco_phase: 0.0,\n            tick_count: 0,\n            estimated_interval: target,\n            locked_streak: 0,\n            lock_threshold: 10,\n            tolerance: 0.1,\n            external_drift_ns_per_s: 0.0,\n            drift_confidence: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a stabilizer with custom lock parameters.\n    pub fn with_lock_params(\n        target_interval_us: f64,\n        alpha: f64,\n        lock_threshold: u32,\n        tolerance: f64,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let target = safe_f64(target_interval_us, MIN_INTERVAL_US, MAX_INTERVAL_US)\n            .unwrap_or(1000.0);\n\n        ClockStabilizer {\n            target_interval_us: target,\n            alpha: alpha.clamp(0.01, 0.99),\n            filtered_error: 0.0,\n            vco_phase: 0.0,\n            tick_count: 0,\n            estimated_interval: target,\n            locked_streak: 0,\n            lock_threshold,\n            tolerance: tolerance.clamp(0.01, 0.5),\n            external_drift_ns_per_s: 0.0,\n            drift_confidence: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Feed an actual inter-tick interval and get the stabilized output.\n    ///\n    /// SAFEGUARDS:\n    /// 1. Input validated (NaN/infinity/out-of-bounds rejected or clamped)\n    /// 2. All intermediate f64 guarded against NaN propagation\n    /// 3. Counters use saturating arithmetic (no overflow)\n    /// 4. State hash verifiable via StabilizerVerifier\n    ///\n    /// INTEGRATION: the `external_drift_ns_per_s` value is subtracted from the\n    /// raw error, so a positive drift (clock running fast) causes the PLL to\n    /// adapt its target downward, keeping aligned with the reference. This is\n    /// how PowerForecastEngine + TimeStabilizer feed into clock stabilisation.\n    pub fn stabilize(&mut self, actual_interval_us: f64) -> Result<StabilizedTick, StabilizerError> {\n        // SAFEGUARD 1: reject non-finite input.\n        let actual = safe_f64(actual_interval_us, MIN_INTERVAL_US, MAX_INTERVAL_US)?;\n\n        // Phase Detector: compare actual interval to reference.\n        let raw_error = actual - self.target_interval_us;\n\n        // Apply external drift correction (ns/s → µs/tick).\n        let drift_correction_us = if self.drift_confidence > 0.3 {\n            // Drift in ns/s, convert to µs per tick (target_interval in µs).\n            (self.external_drift_ns_per_s / 1_000_000.0) * self.target_interval_us\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n\n        // SAFEGUARD 2: guard filtered_error against NaN.\n        self.filtered_error = guard_f64(\n            self.alpha * (raw_error - drift_correction_us) + (1.0 - self.alpha) * self.filtered_error,\n            0.0,\n        );\n\n        // SAFEGUARD 3: guard estimated_interval against NaN.\n        self.estimated_interval = guard_f64(\n            self.target_interval_us + self.filtered_error,\n            self.target_interval_us,\n        );\n\n        // VCO phase accumulator.\n        self.vco_phase = guard_f64(self.vco_phase + self.estimated_interval, 0.0);\n\n        // Lock detector.\n        let in_tolerance = raw_error.abs() <= self.target_interval_us * self.tolerance;\n        if in_tolerance {\n            self.locked_streak = sat_inc_u32(self.locked_streak);\n        } else {\n            self.locked_streak = 0;\n        }\n\n        // SAFEGUARD 4: saturating tick count.\n        self.tick_count = sat_inc_u64(self.tick_count);\n\n        // SAFEGUARD 5: final NaN check on output.\n        let aligned = guard_f64(self.estimated_interval, self.target_interval_us);\n        let filtered = guard_f64(self.filtered_error, 0.0);\n\n        let lock = self.lock_status();\n\n        Ok(StabilizedTick {\n            aligned_interval_us: aligned,\n            raw_error_us: raw_error,\n            filtered_error_us: filtered,\n            lock,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current lock status.\n    pub fn lock_status(&self) -> LockStatus {\n        if self.tick_count < 3 {\n            LockStatus::FreeRunning\n        } else if self.locked_streak >= self.lock_threshold {\n            LockStatus::Locked\n        } else {\n            LockStatus::Acquiring\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The current stabilized interval estimate (microseconds).\n    pub fn current_interval(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.estimated_interval\n    }\n\n    /// The current filtered phase error (microseconds).\n    pub fn filtered_error(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.filtered_error\n    }\n\n    /// The target reference interval (microseconds).\n    pub fn target_interval(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.target_interval_us\n    }\n\n    /// Number of ticks processed.\n    pub fn tick_count(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.tick_count\n    }\n\n    /// Reset the stabilizer to initial state.\n    pub fn reset(&mut self) {\n        self.filtered_error = 0.0;\n        self.vco_phase = 0.0;\n        self.tick_count = 0;\n        self.estimated_interval = self.target_interval_us;\n        self.locked_streak = 0;\n        self.external_drift_ns_per_s = 0.0;\n        self.drift_confidence = 0.0;\n    }\n\n    /// Set external drift correction from power/thermal forecast (ns/s).\n    /// Positive = clock running fast, Negative = clock running slow.\n    pub fn set_external_drift(&mut self, drift_ns_per_s: f64, confidence: f64) {\n        self.external_drift_ns_per_s = if drift_ns_per_s.is_finite() { drift_ns_per_s } else { 0.0 };\n        self.drift_confidence = confidence.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n    }\n\n    /// Current external drift correction (ns/s).\n    pub fn external_drift(&self) -> f64 { self.external_drift_ns_per_s }\n    /// Confidence in external drift correction.\n    pub fn drift_confidence(&self) -> f64 { self.drift_confidence }\n\n    /// Get the SHA3-256 hash of the current stabilizer state.\n    /// Used by StabilizerVerifier for byte-by-byte cryptographic verification.\n    pub fn state_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        state_hash(self)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the raw state bytes (80 bytes, canonical serialization).\n    pub fn state_bytes(&self) -> [u8; 80] {\n        serialize_state(self)\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII status display for diagnostics.\n    ///\n    /// ```text\n    /// PLL Status\n    ///   Target:    1000.0 us\n    ///   Estimated:  998.3 us\n    ///   Error:        -1.7 us (filtered)\n    ///   Ticks:         42\n    ///   Lock:          LOCKED (streak: 15/10)\n    /// ```\n    pub fn ascii_status(&self) -> String {\n        let drift_line = if self.drift_confidence > 0.0 {\n            format!("  Ext Drift: {:+.1} ns/s (conf: {:.0}%)\\n", self.external_drift_ns_per_s, self.drift_confidence * 100.0)\n        } else {\n            String::new()\n        };\n        format!(\n            "PLL Status\\n  Target:    {:.1} us\\n  Estimated:  {:.1} us\\n  Error:      {:+.1} us (filtered)\\n  Ticks:      {}\\n  Lock:       {} (streak: {}/{})\\n{}",\n            self.target_interval_us,\n            self.estimated_interval,\n            self.filtered_error,\n            self.tick_count,\n            self.lock_status(),\n            self.locked_streak,\n            self.lock_threshold,\n            drift_line,\n        )\n    }\n}\n\nimpl StabilizerVerifier {\n    /// Create a verifier from a stabilizer's current state hash.\n    pub fn new(stabilizer: &ClockStabilizer) -> Self {\n        StabilizerVerifier {\n            expected_hash: stabilizer.state_hash(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a verifier with an explicit expected hash.\n    pub fn from_hash(hash: [u8; 32]) -> Self {\n        StabilizerVerifier {\n            expected_hash: hash,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify the stabilizer's current state matches the expected hash.\n    /// Returns Ok(()) if byte-identical, Err with both hashes if mismatch.\n    pub fn verify(&self, stabilizer: &ClockStabilizer) -> Result<(), StabilizerError> {\n        let actual = stabilizer.state_hash();\n        if actual == self.expected_hash {\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            Err(StabilizerError::VerificationFailed {\n                expected: self.expected_hash,\n                actual,\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Update the verifier's expected hash to the stabilizer's current state.\n    /// Call after a successful stabilization step to "advance" the verification window.\n    pub fn update(&mut self, stabilizer: &ClockStabilizer) {\n        self.expected_hash = stabilizer.state_hash();\n    }\n\n    /// The current expected hash.\n    pub fn expected(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        self.expected_hash\n    }\n}\n\n/// Batch-stabilize a sequence of irregular intervals.\n/// Returns a Vec of StabilizedTick, one per input interval.\npub fn stabilize_batch(\n    stabilizer: &mut ClockStabilizer,\n    intervals: &[f64],\n) -> Result<Vec<StabilizedTick>, StabilizerError> {\n    intervals.iter().map(|&iv| stabilizer.stabilize(iv)).collect()\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn new_stabilizer_starts_free_running() {\n        let pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        assert_eq!(pll.lock_status(), LockStatus::FreeRunning);\n        assert_eq!(pll.tick_count(), 0);\n        assert_eq!(pll.current_interval(), 1000.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn constant_interval_converges_to_locked() {\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        for _ in 0..20 {\n            let tick = pll.stabilize(1000.0).unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(tick.raw_error_us, 0.0);\n        }\n        assert_eq!(pll.lock_status(), LockStatus::Locked);\n        assert!((pll.current_interval() - 1000.0).abs() < 0.01);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jittery_input_gets_smoothed() {\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        let intervals = [900.0, 1100.0, 900.0, 1100.0, 900.0, 1100.0, 900.0, 1100.0];\n        let ticks = stabilize_batch(&mut pll, &intervals).unwrap();\n        let last = ticks.last().unwrap();\n        assert!(\n            last.filtered_error_us.abs() < 50.0,\n            "filtered error should be small: {}",\n            last.filtered_error_us\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn raw_error_is_actual_minus_target() {\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        let tick = pll.stabilize(1050.0).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(tick.raw_error_us, 50.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn negative_error_for_fast_interval() {\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        let tick = pll.stabilize(900.0).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(tick.raw_error_us, -100.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tick_count_increments() {\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        assert_eq!(pll.tick_count(), 0);\n        pll.stabilize(1000.0).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(pll.tick_count(), 1);\n        pll.stabilize(1000.0).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(pll.tick_count(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn free_running_until_3_ticks() {\n        // Use lock_threshold=3 so locking happens within the 3-tick loop.\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::with_lock_params(1000.0, 0.1, 3, 0.1);\n        for i in 0..3 {\n            let tick = pll.stabilize(1000.0).unwrap();\n            if i < 2 {\n                assert_eq!(tick.lock, LockStatus::FreeRunning);\n            } else {\n                assert_eq!(tick.lock, LockStatus::Locked);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reset_returns_to_initial_state() {\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        for _ in 0..10 {\n            pll.stabilize(1050.0).unwrap();\n        }\n        assert!(pll.tick_count() > 0);\n        pll.reset();\n        assert_eq!(pll.tick_count(), 0);\n        assert_eq!(pll.current_interval(), 1000.0);\n        assert_eq!(pll.filtered_error(), 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn lock_threshold_is_configurable() {\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::with_lock_params(1000.0, 0.1, 3, 0.1);\n        for _ in 0..5 {\n            pll.stabilize(1000.0).unwrap();\n        }\n        assert_eq!(pll.lock_status(), LockStatus::Locked);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn out_of_tolerance_resets_streak() {\n        let mut pll = pll.stabilize(2000.0).unwrap();\n        assert_ne!(pll.lock_status(), LockStatus::Locked);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ascii_status_contains_key_fields() {\n        let pll = assert!(status.contains("FREE_RUNNING"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn target_interval_is_preserved() {\n        let pll = ClockStabilizer::new(500.0, 0.2);\n        assert_eq!(pll.target_interval(),    #[test]\n    fn zero_input_is_clamped() {\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        let result = pll.stabilize(0.0);\n        assert!(result.is_err());\n hash_after = pll.state_hash();\n        assert_ne!(hash_before, hash_after);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn state_bytes_are_correct_length() {\n        let pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        assert_eq!(pll.state_bytes().len(), 80);\n    }\n\n    // --- CRYPTOGRAPHIC VERIFICATION TESTS ---\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verifier_passes_on_unchanged_state() {\n        let pll = verifier_fails_after_state_change() {\n        let mut pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        let verifier = StabilizerVerifier::new(&pll);\n        pll.stabilize(1050.0).unwrap();\n verifier_from_explicit_hash() {\n        let pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        let hash = pll.state_hash();\n        let verifier = StabilizerVerifier::from_hash(hash);\n hash_before = pll.state_hash();\n        let verifier = StabilizerVerifier::new(&pll);\n        pll.stabilize(1050.0).unwrap();\n        let err = verifier.verify(&pll).unwrap_err();\n        match          }\n            })\n            .collect();\n        for iv in &inputs {\n            let tick = pll.stabilize(*iv).unwrap();\n            assert!(tick.aligned_interval_us.is_finite());\n pll = ClockStabilizer::new(1000.0, 0.1);\n        // Drive tick_count to near-max -- saturating arithmetic, no panic.\n        // We can't actually hit u64::MAX in a test, but we verify saturation
