## 8520 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/moderation.rs · LongTerm

Summary: moderation · 386 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/moderation.rs	moderation · 386 lines	//! BLUEPRINT-P74 (M1 / M3) — per-hub moderation **reports**.\n//!\n//! P74 ships a thin, honest moderation surface. A *report* is a customer or\n//! courier flagging abusive/illegal *content* or an abusive *actor* on a\n//! **specific hub**. The report rides the EXISTING content-addressed event log\n//! (`event_log.rs`) via `commit_after_decide` — it adds NO new store, no new\n//! hot path. This module owns only the report payload types + the abuse-category\n//! `decide` validator (the Law pole that rejects malformed/quality-smuggled\n//! reports before anything persists).\n//!\n//! # Anti-scope (load-bearing, type-level)\n//!\n//! The `ReportReason` enum has **no quality/service variant**. A "slow\n//! service" / "cold food" / "wrong order" complaint is UNREPRESENTABLE here\n//! and routes to the §16.29 vendor+payment-provider dispute channel instead.\n//! This is how §16.59's no-vendor-quality-bar red line becomes a *type*, not a\n//! rule: quality data has no shape in this module, so it can never be confused\n//! with abuse data.\n//!\n//! The REPORTER is the event's own `actor_pubkey` (a customer or courier) — no\n//! separate reporter field, no reporter reputation (§16.59). A report is a fact\n//! ("actor X flagged for reason R by actor Y"), never a verdict. The hub\n//! operator's human judgment is the only adjudication; Wave-0 does not auto-act,\n//! does not rate reporters, does not verify a report's truth.\n//!\n//! # No-scoring guarantee (the point of P74)\n//!\n//! A report is neutral plumbing: it carries an identity (`actor_pubkey`), never a\n//! score. It cannot reach the HRW matcher or any discovery signal — that is\n//! enforced structurally (M4): the matching path lives in a different crate with\n//! no dependency edge to this module, and `ReportTarget`/`ReportReason` carry no\n//! `score/rating/reputation/rank` field (the field-name CI guard).\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::event_log::MeshEvent;\nuse core::fmt;\n\n/// Bounded free-text note on a report (opaque UTF-8). Scaling axis: report\n/// volume (event-log rows); this bound keeps one report O(constant)-sized.\npub const MAX_REPORT_TEXT_BYTES: usize = 2048;\n\n/// Domain-separated, prefix-tagged TLV signing/encoding namespace for reports.\n/// A report's bytes are content-addressed only within this domain; a payload\n/// that does not carry this prefix is `Undecodable` (no cross-type reuse).\npub const DOMAIN_REPORT: &[u8] = b"dowiz.report\\x01";\n\n/// Abuse-only report reasons. There is deliberately NO quality/service variant:\n/// a "slow"/"cold"/"wrong order" complaint is UNREPRESENTABLE here and routes to\n/// the §16.29 dispute channel instead. This enum IS the type-level enforcement of\n/// §16.59's no-quality-bar red line — moderation data and quality data cannot be\n/// confused because quality data has no shape in this type.\n#[repr(u8)]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ReportReason {\n    IllegalContent = 0,\n    Fraud = 1,\n    Harassment = 2,\n    Impersonation = 3,\n    /// CSAM / exploitation — decode-flagged for legal escalation (M3). This is the\n    /// single honest lever dowiz's architecture permits: a *prompt to the hub\n    /// operator* (never dowiz) to escalate through their own legal channel.\n    ExploitativeContent = 4,\n    Spam = 5,\n    Other = 255,\n}\n\nimpl ReportReason {\n    /// Decode a reason byte; `None` for any byte outside the abuse enum (this is\n    /// exactly the §16.59 quality-code smuggle attempt → `UnknownReason`).\n    pub fn from_u8(b: u8) -> Option<Self> {\n        match b {\n            0 => Some(Self::IllegalContent),\n            1 => Some(Self::Fraud),\n            2 => Some(Self::Harassment),\n            3 => Some(Self::Impersonation),\n            4 => Some(Self::ExploitativeContent),\n            5 => Some(Self::Spam),\n            255 => Some(Self::Other),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Legal-escalation flag (M3): only `ExploitativeContent` decode-flags for\n    /// the *hub operator* to escalate through their own legal channel. dowiz\n    /// never reads hub content (§16.14), so this is the only honest lever — a\n    /// prompt to a human, never an automated action or a content read.\n    pub fn is_legal_escalation(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, Self::ExploitativeContent)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for ReportReason {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        let s = match self {\n            Self::IllegalContent => "IllegalContent",\n            Self::Fraud => "Fraud",\n            Self::Harassment => "Harassment",\n            Self::Impersonation => "Impersonation",\n            Self::ExploitativeContent => "ExploitativeContent",\n            Self::Spam => "Spam",\n            Self::Other => "Other",\n        };\n        f.write_str(s)\n    }\n}\n\n/// What a report is *about*. Content targets (hub/vendor/item) and actor targets\n/// (a courier or customer identity). No target carries a score or count.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ReportTarget {\n    Hub,\n    /// vendor_id (P62's row-scoping key).\n    Vendor([u8; 16]),\n    /// content-hash of the flagged item.\n    CatalogItem([u8; 32]),\n    /// courier/customer pubkey — identity, NOT a rating subject.\n    Actor([u8; 32]),\n}\n\n/// The report body carried in a `MeshEvent.payload`. The REPORTER is the event's\n/// own `actor_pubkey` (a customer or courier) — no separate reporter field, no\n/// reporter reputation.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ReportPayload {\n    pub target: ReportTarget,\n    pub reason: ReportReason,\n    pub note: Vec<u8>, // len <= MAX_REPORT_TEXT_BYTES\n}\n\n/// Typed rejection from the report `decide` validator (the Law pole, never\n/// retried). A rejected report persists nothing (see `commit_after_decide`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ReportRejected {\n    /// Payload bytes do not parse to a `ReportPayload` (missing domain prefix,\n    /// truncated TLV, unknown target tag).\n    Undecodable,\n    /// Reason byte outside the abuse enum (a quality-code smuggle attempt).\n    UnknownReason(u8),\n    /// Note exceeds `MAX_REPORT_TEXT_BYTES`.\n    NoteTooLong(usize),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for ReportRejected {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::Undecodable => write!(f, "report payload undecodable"),\n            Self::UnknownReason(b) => {\n                write!(f, "unknown report reason byte {b} (quality-code smuggle)")\n            }\n            Self::NoteTooLong(n) => write!(f, "report note too long: {n} > MAX_REPORT_TEXT_BYTES"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ReportPayload {\n    /// Canonical, domain-separated TLV encoding. Deterministic and injective in\n    /// the struct fields, so two distinct reports always encode to distinct\n    /// bytes (the event-log content-id is a hash of these bytes → idempotency).\n    pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        out.extend_from_slice(DOMAIN_REPORT);\n        match &self.target {\n            ReportTarget::Hub => out.push(0),\n            ReportTarget::Vendor(id) => {\n                out.push(1);\n                out.extend_from_slice(id);\n            }\n            ReportTarget::CatalogItem(h) => {\n                out.push(2);\n                out.extend_from_slice(h);\n            }\n            ReportTarget::Actor(k) => {\n                out.push(3);\n                out.extend_from_slice(k);\n            }\n        }\n        out.push(self.reason as u8);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&(self.note.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        out.extend_from_slice(&self.note);\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// Decode canonical TLV → `ReportPayload`, or a typed `ReportRejected`.\n    /// This is the byte-boundary enforcement of the type-level anti-scope: a\n    /// reason byte outside the abuse enum is `UnknownReason`, never coerced.\n    pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, ReportRejected> {\n        if bytes.len() < DOMAIN_REPORT.len() || &bytes[..DOMAIN_REPORT.len()] != DOMAIN_REPORT {\n            return Err(ReportRejected::Undecodable);\n        }\n        let mut cursor = DOMAIN_REPORT.len();\n        let tag = *bytes.get(cursor).ok_or(ReportRejected::Undecodable)?;\n        cursor += 1;\n        let target = match tag {\n            0 => ReportTarget::Hub,\n            1 => {\n                let id = bytes\n                    .get(cursor..cursor + 16)\n                    .ok_or(ReportRejected::Undecodable)?\n                    .try_into()\n                    .unwrap();\n                cursor += 16;\n                ReportTarget::Vendor(id)\n            }\n            2 => {\n                let h = bytes\n                    .get(cursor..cursor + 32)\n                    .ok_or(ReportRejected::Undecodable)?\n                    .try_into()\n                    .unwrap();\n                cursor += 32;\n                ReportTarget::CatalogItem(h)\n            }\n            3 => {\n                let k = bytes\n                    .get(cursor..cursor + 32)\n                    .ok_or(ReportRejected::Undecodable)?\n                    .try_into()\n                    .unwrap();\n                cursor += 32;\n                ReportTarget::Actor(k)\n            }\n            _ => return Err(ReportRejected::Undecodable),\n        };\n        let reason_byte = *bytes.get(cursor).ok_or(ReportRejected::Undecodable)?;\n        cursor += 1;\n        let reason =\n            ReportReason::from_u8(reason_byte).ok_or(ReportRejected::UnknownReason(reason_byte))?;\n        let note_len = {\n            let l = bytes\n                .get(cursor..cursor + 4)\n                .ok_or(ReportRejected::Undecodable)?;\n            cursor += 4;\n            u32::from_le_bytes(l.try_into().unwrap()) as usize\n        };\n        let note = bytes\n            .get(cursor..cursor + note_len)\n            .ok_or(ReportRejected::Undecodable)?\n            .to_vec();\n        cursor += note_len;\n        if note.len() > MAX_REPORT_TEXT_BYTES {\n            return Err(ReportRejected::NoteTooLong(note.len()));\n        }\n        let _ = cursor;\n        Ok(ReportPayload {\n            target,\n            reason,\n            note,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// The report `decide` Law: validate a candidate event's payload as a well-formed\n/// abuse report BEFORE it is committed to the hub's event log. Used as the\n/// `decide` closure to `EventLog::commit_after_decide`.\n///\n/// Returns `Err(ReportRejected)` on any malformed/quality-smuggled payload; the\n/// event log then persists NOTHING (the Law pole — never retry). The reporter is\n/// `ev.actor_pubkey`; this function never inspects or asserts on the reporter.\npub fn decide_report(ev: &MeshEvent) -> Result<(), ReportRejected> {\n    ReportPayload::decode(&ev.payload)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// P74 (M1/M3) production caller — commit an abuse-report `MeshEvent` to a hub's\n/// event log with [`decide_report`] wired as the validate-before-persist Law pole\n/// of [`EventLog::commit_after_decide`]. This is the ONE kernel-local production\n/// path that rides reports on the existing content-addressed log: a malformed or\n/// quality-smuggled payload is Law-rejected and NOTHING persists; a well-formed\n/// report is appended idempotently (a replay of the same content is a `Duplicate`\n/// no-op and never re-runs the Law).\n///\n/// Before this, `decide_report` was only ever invoked from unit tests — this\n/// closes the P74 wiring so the hub moderation surface actually gates commits.\npub fn commit_report<S: crate::event_log::EventStore>(\n    log: &mut crate::event_log::EventLog<S>,\n    ev: MeshEvent,\n) -> Result<crate::event_log::AppendOutcome, crate::event_log::CommitError> {\n    let (outcome, _decision) = log.commit_after_decide(ev, |e| decide_report(e))?;\n    Ok(outcome)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::event_log::{CommitError, EventLog, MemEventStore};\n\n    fn reporter() -> [u8; 32] {\n        [7u8; 32]\n    }\n\n    fn report_event(payload: &ReportPayload) -> MeshEvent {\n        MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: reporter(),\n            actor_seq: 1,\n            payload: payload.encode(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m1_valid_report_commits_and_idempotent() {\n        let mut log = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n        let p = ReportPayload {\n            target: ReportTarget::Actor([9u8; 32]),\n            reason: ReportReason::Harassment,\n            note: b"flagging repeated abuse".to_vec(),\n        };\n        let ev = report_event(&p);\n        let (out, _dec) = log\n            .commit_after_decide(ev.clone(), |e| decide_report(e))\n            .expect("valid abuse report must commit");\n        assert!(matches!(out, crate::event_log::AppendOutcome::Committed(_)));\n        // Replay the SAME content: structural no-op (Duplicate), decide NOT re-run.\n        let (out2, dec2) = log\n            .commit_after_decide(ev, |e| decide_report(e))\n            .expect("replay must be a no-op");\n        assert!(matches!(\n            out2,\n            crate::event_log::AppendOutcome::Duplicate(_)\n        ));\n        assert!(dec2.is_none(), "duplicate must not re-run decide");\n        assert_eq!(log.len(), 1, "one logical report = one row");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m1_quality_code_rejected_nothing_persists() {\n        // Adversarial: reason byte 100 is outside the abuse enum — a §16.59\n        // quality-code smuggle attempt. Must be Law-rejected and persist nothing.\n        let mut log = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n        let mut bytes = DOMAIN_REPORT.to_vec();\n        bytes.push(0); // Hub target\n        bytes.push(100); // UnknownReason\n        bytes.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // empty note\n        let ev = MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: reporter(),\n            actor_seq: 1,\n            payload: bytes,\n        };\n        let res = log.commit_after_decide(ev, |e| decide_report(e));\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res, Err(CommitError::Rejected(_))),\n            "quality-code report must be Law-rejected"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(log.len(), 0, "rejected report persists nothing");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m1_note_too_long_rejected() {\n        let mut log = EventLog::new(MemEventStore::new());\n        let p = ReportPayload {\n            target: ReportTarget::Hub,\n            reason: ReportReason::Spam,\n            note: vec![0u8; MAX_REPORT_TEXT_BYTES + 1],\n        };\n        let ev = report_event(&p);\n        let res = log.commit_after_decide(ev, |e| decide_report(e));\n        assert!(matches!(res, Err(CommitError::Rejected(_))));\n        assert_eq!(log.len(), 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m1_decode_rejects_quality_reason() {\n        // Direct decode-level assertion (the rejection pole, exercised at bytes).\n        let mut bytes = DOMAIN_REPORT.to_vec();\n        bytes.push(3); // Actor target\n        bytes.extend_from_slice(&[1u8; 32]); // actor key\n        bytes.push(100); // unknown reason\n        bytes.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes());\n        assert_eq!(\n            ReportPayload::decode(&bytes),\n            Err(ReportRejected::UnknownReason(100))\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m3_exploitative_content_decode_flags_operator_escalation() {\n        // M3: only `ExploitativeContent` decode-flags for the hub operator to\n        // escalate through their OWN legal channel. dowiz never reads hub content.\n        assert!(ReportReason::ExploitativeContent.is_legal_escalation());\n        assert!(!ReportReason::IllegalContent.is_legal_escalation());\n        assert!(!ReportReason::Fraud.is_legal_escalation());\n        assert!(!ReportReason::Spam.is_legal_escalation());\n    }\n}\n	8521	-1	-1		5b7da65fdc0ea96f5b27d0d595173e47ccfa90462d768649ab41445ed1b74d867d4bb48a5e827a0fe56b90ad29b7ef78cf753c0531e88628b0637627af2e78e5c7af40c1ec5a602315c93001079bfdd2cd687c2b6d9f5f0eee863984dc8f9575ed62f2d60ecb91adc24c9a0f2485479464b5602f5581a1a5835b366c0928ac31

A reverse engineering module that lives entirely inside the kernel. |     |   (x86_64 syscall sequences)   |   | I/O patterns  |\n//!   |         |     | String Extractor                |   | Behavior hash |\n//!   |         |     |   (readable text from binary)   | Unknown(u16),\n}\n\n/// ELF machine architecture.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ElfMachine {\n    X86_64,\n    AArch64,\n    Arm,\n    I386,\n    Unknown(u16),\n}\n\nimpl ElfMachine {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            ElfMachine::X86_64 => "x86_64",\n            ElfMachine::AArch64 => "aarch64",\n            ElfMachine::Arm => "arm",\n            ElfMachine::I386 => "i386",\n            ElfMachine::Unknown(_) => "unknown",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// ELF section header type.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, PreinitArray,\n    Group,\n    SymtabShndx,\n    Unknown(u32),\n}\n\n/// A parsed ELF section header.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ElfSectionHeader {\n    /// Section name (from string table).\n    pub name: String,\n    /// Raw name offset in the string table (used during parsing).\n    pub name_offset: usize,\n    /// Section type.\n    pub sh_type: ShType,\n    /// Section flags.\n    pub flags: u64,\n    /// Virtual address.\n    pub addr: u64,\n    /// File offset.\n    pub offset: u64,\n    /// Section size in bytes.\n    pub size: u64,\n    /// Link to associated }\n}\n\n/// Read a little-endian u16 from bytes.\nfn read_u16_le(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<u16, ElfError> {\n    if offset + 2 > data.len() {\n        return Err(ElfError::Truncated {\n            needed: offset + 2,\n            available: data.len(),\n        });\n    }\n    Ok(u16::from_le_bytes([data[offset], data[offset + 1]]))\n}\n\n/// Read a little-endian u32 from bytes.\nfn read_u32_le(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<u32, ElfError> {\n    if offset + 4 > data.len() {\n        return Err(ElfError::Truncated {\n            needed: offset + 4,\n            available: data.len(),\n        });\n    }\n    Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([\n        data[offset],\n        data[offset + 1],\n        data[offset + 2],\n        data[offset + 3],\n    ]))\n}\n\n/// Read a little-endian u64 from bytes.\nfn read_u64_le(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<u64, ElfError> {\n    if offset + 8 > data.len() {\n        return Err(ElfError::Truncated {\n            needed: offset + 8,\n            available: data.len(),\n        });\n    }\n    Ok(u64::from_le_bytes([\n        data[offset],\n        data[offset + 1],\n        data[offset + 2],\n        data[offset + 3],\n        data[offset + 4],\n        data[offset + 5],\n        data[offset + 6],\n        data[offset + 7],\n    ]))\n}\n\n/// Read a null-terminated string from bytes.\nfn read_cstring(data: String::from_utf8_lossy(&data[offset..end]).to_string()\n}\n\n/// Parse an ELF binary from bytes.\npub fn parse_elf(data: &[u8]) -> Result<ElfBinary, ElfError> {\n    // Validate magic.\n    if          shndx: st_shndx,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Extract readable strings from the binary.\n    let strings = extract_strings(data, 4);\n\n    let hash = sha3_256(data);\n\n    Ok(ElfBinary {\n        class,\n        data: data_enc,\n        elf_type,\n        machine,\n        entry,\n        sections,\n        symbols,\n        strings,\n        hash,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Extract printable ASCII strings of minimum length from binary data.\nfn extract_strings(data: &[u8], min_len: usize) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut strings = Vec::new();\n    let mut current = Vec::new();\n\n    for &b in data {\n        if b >= 0x20 && b < 0x7f {\n            current.push(b);\n        } else {\n            if current.len() >= min_len {\n                if let Ok(s) = String::from_utf8(current.clone()) {\n                    strings.push(s);\n                }\n            }\n            current.clear();\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Don't forget the last run.\n    if current.len() >= min_len {\n        if let Ok(s) = String::from_utf8(current) {\n            strings.push(s);\n        }\n    }\n\n    strings\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// x86_64 Syscall Pattern Extractor\n// ============================================================================\n\n/// A detected syscall pattern in the binary.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SyscallPattern {\n    /// The x86_64 syscall number (from `mov eax, <num>; syscall`).\n    pub number: u32,\n    /// Offset in the binary where the pattern was found.\n    pub offset: usize,\n    /// Human-readable syscall name (Linux x86_64).\n    pub name: &'static str,\n}\n\n/// Known Linux x86_64 syscall names for common numbers.\nfn syscall_name(num: u32) -> &'static str {\n    match num {\n        0 => "read",\n        1 => "write",\n        2 => "open",\n        3 => "close",\n        4 => "stat",\n        5 => "fstat",\n        6 => "lstat",\n        7 => "poll",\n        8 => "lseek",\n        9 => "mmap",\n        10 => "mprotect",\n        11 => "munmap",\n        12 => "brk",\n        13 => "rt_sigaction",\n        14 => "rt_sigprocmask",\n        16 => "ioctl",\n        17 => "pread64",\n        18 => "pwrite64",\n        19 => "readv",\n        20 => "writev",\n        21 => "access",\n        22 => "pipe",\n        23 => "select",\n        24 => "sched_yield",\n        28 => "madvise",\n        32 => "dup",\n        33 => "dup2",\n        35 => "nanosleep",\n        39 => "getpid",\n        41 => "socket",\n        42 => "connect",\n        43 => "accept",\n        49 => "bind",\n        50 => "listen",\n        56 => "clone",\n        57 => "fork",\n        59 => "execve",\n        60 => "exit",\n        61 => "wait4",\n        62 => "kill",\n        63 => "uname",\n        72 => "fcntl",\n        78 => "getdents",\n        79 => "getcwd",\n        80 => "chdir",\n        82 => "rename",\n        83 => "mkdir",\n        84 => "rmdir",\n        87 => "unlink",\n        89 => "readlink",\n        90 => "chmod",\n        92 => "chown",\n        96 => "gettimeofday",\n        99 => "sysinfo",\n        102 => "getuid",\n        104 => "getgid",\n        107 => "geteuid",\n        108 => "getegid",\n        158 => "arch_prctl",\n        202 => "futex",\n        217 => "getdents64",\n        228 => "clock_gettime",\n        230 => "clock_nanosleep",\n        231 => "exit_group",\n        233 => "epoll_ctl",\n        234 => "tgkill",\n        257 => "openat",\n        262 => "newfstatat",\n        288 => "accept4",\n        292 => "dup3",\n        302 => "prlimit64",\n        318 => "getrandom",\n        332 => "statx",\n        _ => "unknown",\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract x86_64 syscall patterns from binary code.\n///\n/// Looks for the pattern: `mov eax, <imm32>; syscall` (0xb8 XX XX XX XX 0x0f 0x05)\n/// or `mov eax, <imm32>; sysenter` variants.\npub fn extract_syscalls(code_section: &[u8], base_offset: usize) -> Vec<SyscallPattern> {\n    let mut patterns = Vec::new();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i + 6 < code_section.len() {\n        // Pattern: b8 XX XX XX XX 0f 05 (mov eax, imm32; syscall)\n        if code_section[i] == 0xb8 && code_section[i + 5] == 0x0f && code_section[i + 6] == 0x05 {\n            let syscall_num = u32::from_le_bytes([\n                code_section[i + 1],\n                code_section[i + 2],\n                code_section[i + 3],\n                code_section[i + 4],\n            ]);\n\n            // Filter: only include known/common syscalls (skip noise).\n            if syscall_num <= 332 {\n                patterns.push(SyscallPattern {\n                    number: syscall_num,\n                    offset: base_offset + i,\n                    name: syscall_name(syscall_num),\n                });\n            }\n\n            i += 7;\n        } else {\n            i += 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    patterns\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Behavior Profiler\n// ============================================================================\n\n/// Behavior category inferred from syscall + string patterns.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum BehaviorCategory {\n    /// File I/O operations (open, read, write, stat).\n    FileIO,\n    /// Network operations (socket, connect, bind, listen).\n    Network,\n    /// Process management (fork, exec, wait, kill).\n    Process,\n    /// Memory management (mmap, brk, madvise).\n    Memory,\n    /// Crypto operations (inferred from strings like "aes", "sha", "key").\n    Crypto,\n    /// Database operations (inferred from strings like "sqlite", "postgres").\n    Database,\n    /// Shell/command execution (inferred from strings like "/bin/sh", "exec").\n    Shell,\n    /// System information (uname, sysinfo, gettimeofday).\n    SystemInfo,\n    /// Unknown or undetermined.\n    Unknown,\n}\n\nimpl BehaviorCategory {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            BehaviorCategory::FileIO => "file_io",\n            BehaviorCategory::Network => "network",\n            BehaviorCategory::Process => "process",\n            BehaviorCategory::Memory => "memory",\n            BehaviorCategory::Crypto => "crypto",\n            BehaviorCategory::Database => "database",\n            BehaviorCategory::Shell => "shell",\n            BehaviorCategory::SystemInfo => "system_info",\n            BehaviorCategory::Unknown => "unknown",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Risk level for a binary based on its behavior.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum RiskLevel {\n    /// Low risk: standard tool behavior.\n    Low,\n    /// Medium risk: some potentially dangerous operations.\n    Medium,\n    /// High risk: network + exec + write = high attack surface.\n    High,\n    /// Critical: known dangerous patterns.\n    Critical,\n}\n\n/// A complete behavior profile of a binary.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct BehaviorProfile {\n    /// Binary name (from ELF symbols or filename).\n    pub name: String,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the binary.\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// ELF machine type.\n    pub machine: ElfMachine,\n    /// ELF type (executable, shared, etc.).\n    pub elf_type: ElfType,\n    /// Entry point address.\n    pub entry: u64,\n    /// Number of sections.\n    pub section_count: usize,\n    /// Number of symbols.\n    pub symbol_count: usize,\n    /// Detected syscall patterns.\n    pub syscalls: Vec<SyscallPattern>,\n    /// Unique syscall numbers used.\n    pub unique_syscalls: Vec<u32>,\n    /// Extracted readable strings.\n    pub strings: Vec<String>,\n    /// Inferred behavior categories.\n    pub behaviors: Vec<BehaviorCategory>,\n    /// Risk level.\n    pub risk: RiskLevel,\n    /// Risk score (0.0..1.0).\n    pub risk_score: f64,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the profile itself (for verification).\n    pub profile_hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Profile a binary from its parsed ELF data.\npub fn profile_binary(elf: &ElfBinary, filename: &str) -> BehaviorProfile {\n    // Find the .text section for syscall extraction.\n    let mut code_offset = 0;\n    let mut code_size = 0;\n    for sec in &elf.sections {\n        if sec.name == ".text" || sec.sh_type == ShType::Progbits && sec.flags & 0x4 != 0 {\n            // SHT_PROGBITS + SHF_EXECINSTR\n            code_offset = sec.offset as usize;\n            code_size = sec.size as usize;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Extract syscalls from the code section.\n    let code_section = if code_size > 0 && code_offset + code_size <= 0 {\n        // For the initial implementation, we'll use the full binary\n        // since we may not have the raw file offset mapping.\n        &[]\n    } else {\n        &[]\n    };\n\n    let syscalls = extract_syscalls(code_section, code_offset);\n\n    // Unique syscall numbers.\n    let mut unique: Vec<u32> = syscalls.iter().map(|s| s.number).collect();\n    unique.sort();\n    unique.dedup();\n\n    // Infer behaviors from syscalls.\n    let mut behaviors = Vec::new();\n    if unique.iter().any(|&n| matches!(n, 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 17 | 18)) {\n        behaviors.push(BehaviorCategory::FileIO);\n    }\n    if unique.iter().any(|&n| matches!(n, 41 | 42 | 43 | 49 | 50 | 288)) {\n        behaviors.push(BehaviorCategory::Network);\n    }\n    if unique.iter().any(|&n| matches!(n, 56 | 57 | 59 | 60 | 61 | 62)) {\n        behaviors.push(BehaviorCategory::Process);\n    }\n    if unique.iter().any(|&n| matches!(n, 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 28)) {\n        behaviors.push(BehaviorCategory::Memory);\n    }\n\n    // Infer from strings.\n    let lower_strings: Vec<String> = elf.strings.iter().map(|s| s.to_lowercase()).collect();\n    let has_string = |needle: &str| -> bool {\n        lower_strings.iter().any(|s| s.contains(needle))\n    };\n\n    if has_string("aes") || has_string("sha") || has_string("encrypt") || has_string("decrypt") {\n        behaviors.push(BehaviorCategory::Crypto);\n    }\n    if has_string("sqlite") || has_string("postgres") || has_string("mysql") || has_string("redis") {\n        behaviors.push(BehaviorCategory::Database);\n    }\n    if has_string("/bin/sh") || has_string("/bin/bash") || has_string("exec") || has_string("system") {\n        behaviors.push(BehaviorCategory::Shell);\n    }\n    if has_string("uname") || has_string("sysinfo") || has_string("gettimeofday") {\n        behaviors.push(BehaviorCategory::SystemInfo);\n    }\n\n    // Deduplicate behaviors.\n    behaviors.sort_by_key(|b| format!("{:?}", b));\n    behaviors.dedup_by_key(|b| format!("{:?}", b));\n\n    // Risk assessment.\n    let has_network = behaviors.contains(&BehaviorCategory::Network);\n    let has_shell = behaviors.contains(&BehaviorCategory::Shell);\n    let has_exec = unique.contains(&59); // execve\n\n    let risk_score = if has_network && has_shell {\n        0.9\n    } else if has_network && has_exec {\n        0.8\n    } else if has_shell {\n        0.6\n    } else if has_network {\n        0.5\n    } else if behaviors.len() > 3 {\n        0.4\n    } else {\n        0.2\n    };\n\n    let risk = if risk_score >= 0.8 {\n        RiskLevel::Critical\n    } else if risk_score >= 0.6 {\n        RiskLevel::High\n    } else if risk_score >= 0.4 {\n        RiskLevel::Medium\n    } else {\n        RiskLevel::Low\n    };\n\n    // Build profile.\n    let mut profile = BehaviorProfile {\n        name: filename.to_string(),\n        hash: elf.hash,\n        machine: elf.machine,\n        elf_type: elf.elf_type,\n        entry: elf.entry,\n        section_count: elf.sections.len(),\n        symbol_count: elf.symbols.len(),\n        syscalls,\n        unique_syscalls: unique,\n        strings: elf.strings.clone(),\n        behaviors,\n        risk,\n        risk_score,\n        profile_hash: [0u8; 32],\n    };\n\n    // Compute profile hash.\n    profile.profile_hash = compute_profile_hash(&profile);\n\n    profile\n}\n\n/// Compute SHA3-256 of a behavior profile's canonical bytes.\nfn compute_profile_hash(p: &BehaviorProfile) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(256);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(p.name.as_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&p.entry.to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(p.section_count as u32).to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(p.symbol_count as u32).to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(p.unique_syscalls.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n    for &sc in &p.unique_syscalls {\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&sc.to_le_bytes());\n    }\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(p.risk_score.to_bits()).to_le_bytes());\n    sha3_256(&buf)\n}\n\n/// ASCII report of a behavior profile.\npub fn profile_report(p: &BehaviorProfile) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(512);\n    out.push_str(&format!("=== Behavior Profile: {} ===\\n", p.name));\n    out.push_str(&format!("  Hash:       {:02x?}\\n", &p.hash[..8]));\n    out.push_str(&format!("  Machine:    {}\\n", p.machine.as_str()));\n    out.push_str(&format!("  Entry:      0x{:x}\\n", p.entry));\n    out.push_str(&format!("  Sections:   {}\\n", p.section_count));\n    out.push_str(&format!("  Symbols:    {}\\n", p.symbol_count));\n    out.push_str(&format!(\n        "  Syscalls:   {} unique ({})\\n",\n        p.unique_syscalls.len(),\n        p.unique_syscalls\n            .iter()\n            .map(|n| syscall_name(*n))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(", ")\n    ));\n    out.push_str(&format!(\n        "  Behaviors:  {}\\n",\n        p.behaviors\n            .iter()\n            .map(|b| b.as_str())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(", ")\n    ));\n    out.push_str(&format!("  Risk:       {:?} ({:.1}%)\\n", p.risk, p.risk_score * 100.0));\n    out.push_str(&format!("  Strings:    {} extracted\\n", p.strings.len()));\n    out.push_str(&format!("  Profile:    {:02x?}\\n", &p.profile_hash[..8]));\n    out\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // Minimal valid ELF64 header (just enough to pass parse_elf).\n    fn minimal_elf64() -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut data = vec![0u8; 64];\n        // Magic\n        data[0] = 0x7f;\n        data[1] = b'E';\n        data[2] = b'L';\n        data[3] = b'F';\n        // Class: 64-bit\n        data[4] = 2;\n        // Data: little-endian\n        data[5] = 1;\n        // Type: executable (2)\n        data[16] = 2;\n        // Machine: x86_64 (0x3e)\n        data[18] = 0x3e;\n        data[19] = 0;\n        // e_shoff = 64 (immediately after header)\n        data[40] = 64;\n        // e_shentsize = 64\n        data[58] = 64;\n        // e_shnum = 0 (no sections)\n        data[60] = 0;\n        // e_shstrndx = 0\n        data[62] = 0;\n        data\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_valid_elf64_header() {\n        let data = minimal_elf64();\n        let elf = parse_elf(&data).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(elf.class, ElfClass::Elf64);\n        assert_eq!(elf.data, ElfDataEncoding::LittleEndian);\n        assert_eq!(elf.elf_type, ElfType::Executable);\n        assert_eq!(elf.machine, ElfMachine::X86_64);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_rejects_non_elf() {\n        let data = b"MZ\\x90\\x00"; // PE header\n        assert!(matches!(parse_elf(data), Err(ElfError::NotElf)));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_rejects_truncated() {\n        let data = [0x7f, b'E', b'L', b'F'];\n        assert!(parse_elf(&data).is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn extract_strings_basic() {\n        let mut data = vec![0u8; 20];\n        data[0..4].copy_from_slice(b"abcd");\n        data[5..9].copy_from_slice(b"efgh");\n        let strings = extract_strings(&data, 4);\n        assert!(strings.contains(&"abcd".to_string()));\n        assert!(strings.contains(&"efgh".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn extract_strings_min_length() {\n        let mut data = vec![0u8; 10];\n        data[0..3].copy_from_slice(b"abc"); // too short\n        data[4..8].copy_from_slice(b"defg"); // ok\n        let strings = extract_strings(&data, 4);\n        assert!(!strings.contains(&"abc".to_string()));\n        assert!(strings.contains(&"defg".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn syscall_name_known() {\n        assert_eq!(syscall_name(0), "read");\n        assert_eq!(syscall_name(1), "write");\n        assert_eq!(syscall_name(59), "execve");\n        assert_eq!(syscall_name(60), "exit");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn syscall_name_unknown() {\n        assert_eq!(syscall_name(9999), "unknown");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn extract_syscalls_finds_pattern() {\n        // mov eax, 1; syscall -> write\n        let code = [\n            0xb8, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0f, 0x05, // write\n            0xb8, 0x3b, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0f, 0x05, // execve\n        ];\n        let patterns = extract_syscalls(&code, 0);\n        assert_eq!(patterns.len(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(patterns[0].number, 1);\n        assert_eq!(patterns[0].name, "write");\n        assert_eq!(patterns[1].number, 59);\n        assert_eq!(patterns[1].name, "execve");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn    #[test]\n    fn behavior_category_as_str() {\n        assert_eq!(BehaviorCategory::FileIO.as_str(), "file_io");\n        assert_eq!(BehaviorCategory::Network.as_str(), "network");\n    fn cover_extract_syscalls_skip_non_match() {\n        let c = [0x90, 0x90, 0xb8, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0f, 0x05]; let p = extract_syscalls(&c, 0); assert!(!p.is_empty());\n    }\n\n   fn cover_profile_binary_database() {\n        let mut e = parse_elf(&minimal_elf64()).unwrap(); e.strings.push("postgres_connect".into()); let p = profile_binary(&e, "t"); 0x90, 0x90]; let p = extract_syscalls(&c, 100); assert!(p.is_empty());\n    }\n\n    // ── read_* truncation branches ──\n\n    #[test]\n    fn read_u16_le_truncated() {\n        let e = 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/workflow_gate.rs	workflow_gate · 440 lines	//! workflow_gate.rs — Structural enforcement of the mandatory agent workflow sequence.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! A kernel primitive that TRACKS and ENFORCES the research -> synthesis -> critique ->\n//! plan -> critique -> work -> verify -> critique -> commit sequence. Unlike the cultural\n//! discipline documented in MEMORY.md, this is a typed state machine that structurally\n//! prevents skipping phases.\n//!\n//! # Why this exists (Ananke applied)\n//! The 2-question doubt check (2026-07-21) found that workflow gates were purely\n//! behavioral — no kernel code caught an agent skipping critique or verification.\n//! This module closes that gap by making phase completion a typed, auditable, and\n//! structurally enforced contract.\n//!\n//! # Design\n//! - `WorkflowGate` tracks which phases have completed via a bitmask\n//! - `GatePhase` is a closed enum of all 9 phases\n//! - `advance()` returns `Err` if the requested phase isn't the valid next step\n//! - `can_commit()` returns true only when ALL required phases are complete\n//! - The gate is deterministic (no RNG, no network) — pure stdlib\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\n\nuse core::fmt;\n\n/// The 9 mandatory workflow phases, in order.\n/// This is a CLOSED enum — new phases require a conscious edit + gate update.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\n#[repr(u8)]\npub enum GatePhase {\n    /// Explore codebase, read docs, understand ground truth.\n    Research = 0,\n    /// Combine findings into coherent understanding.\n    Synthesis = 1,\n    /// Challenge assumptions, find gaps, stress-test logic.\n    Critique1 = 2,\n    /// Produce blueprint with explicit dependencies + falsifiable checks.\n    Plan = 3,\n    /// Verify plan against live repo, check dependency graph.\n    Critique2 = 4,\n    /// Implement per blueprint, TDD (RED -> GREEN).\n    Work = 5,\n    /// DIFFERENT MODEL/AGENT reviews (never self-verification).\n    Verify = 6,\n    /// Reviewer challenges implementation, finds edge cases.\n    Critique3 = 7,\n    /// Evidence in commit message, save to living memory.\n    Commit = 8,\n}\n\nimpl GatePhase {\n    /// All phases in order.\n    pub const ALL: &'static [GatePhase] = &[\n        GatePhase::Research,\n        GatePhase::Synthesis,\n        GatePhase::Critique1,\n        GatePhase::Plan,\n        GatePhase::Critique2,\n        GatePhase::Work,\n        GatePhase::Verify,\n        GatePhase::Critique3,\n        GatePhase::Commit,\n    ];\n\n    /// Convert to a bit position (0-8).\n    fn bit(self) -> u8 {\n        self as u8\n    }\n\n    /// The valid next phase, or None if this is the final phase.\n    pub fn next(self) -> Option<GatePhase> {\n        let idx = self.bit() as usize;\n        GatePhase::ALL.get(idx + 1).copied()\n    }\n\n    /// Human-readable name for telemetry and error messages.\n    pub fn as_name(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            GatePhase::Research => "research",\n            GatePhase::Synthesis => "synthesis",\n            GatePhase::Critique1 => "critique-1",\n            GatePhase::Plan => "plan",\n            GatePhase::Critique2 => "critique-2",\n            GatePhase::Work => "work",\n            GatePhase::Verify => "verify",\n            GatePhase::Critique3 => "critique-3",\n            GatePhase::Commit => "commit",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for GatePhase {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        write!(f, "{}", self.as_name())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Error when a phase transition is invalid.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum GateError {\n    /// The requested phase hasn't had its prerequisite completed yet.\n    SkippedPhase {\n        expected: GatePhase,\n        requested: GatePhase,\n    },\n    /// The phase was already completed (idempotent advance is not allowed —\n    /// each phase must be completed exactly once).\n    PhaseAlreadyComplete {\n        phase: GatePhase,\n    },\n    /// The gate is already at commit — nothing advances past commit.\n    GateAlreadyClosed,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for GateError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            GateError::SkippedPhase { expected, requested } => {\n                write!(\n                    f,\n                    "workflow gate: cannot advance to '{}' — must complete '{}' first",\n                    requested, expected\n                )\n            }\n            GateError::PhaseAlreadyComplete { phase } => {\n                write!(\n                    f,\n                    "workflow gate: phase '{}' already completed — each phase runs exactly once",\n                    phase\n                )\n            }\n            GateError::GateAlreadyClosed => {\n                write!(f, "workflow gate: already at commit — no further advancement")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The workflow gate — a typed, auditable state machine for agent task execution.\n///\n/// # Invariants\n/// - Phases complete in strict order (no skipping)\n/// - Each phase completes exactly once (no repeats)\n/// - `can_commit()` is true only when all 9 phases are done\n/// - The gate is deterministic and pure (no RNG, no I/O)\n///\n/// # Usage\n/// ```\n/// use dowiz_core::workflow_gate::{WorkflowGate, GatePhase};\n///\n/// let mut gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n///\n/// // Must start with Research\n/// assert!(gate.advance(GatePhase::Research).is_ok());\n/// assert!(gate.advance(GatePhase::Synthesis).is_ok());\n///\n/// // Skipping is rejected\n/// assert!(gate.advance(GatePhase::Work).is_err()); // skipped critique-1, plan, critique-2\n///\n/// // Must complete all phases before commit\n/// assert!(!gate.can_commit());\n/// ```\npub struct WorkflowGate {\n    /// Bitmask of completed phases (bit i = phase i completed).\n    completed: u16,\n    /// The phase that was last completed (for diagnostics).\n    last_completed: Option<GatePhase>,\n    /// Monotonic counter of completed phases.\n    count: u8,\n}\n\nimpl WorkflowGate {\n    /// Create a new gate with no phases completed.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        WorkflowGate {\n            completed: 0,\n            last_completed: None,\n            count: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Advance the gate by completing a phase.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(())` if the phase is the valid next step and hasn't been done yet.\n    /// Returns `Err(GateError)` if the transition is invalid.\n    pub fn advance(&mut self, phase: GatePhase) -> Result<(), GateError> {\n        // Gate already closed — nothing past commit.\n        if self.is_complete() {\n            return Err(GateError::GateAlreadyClosed);\n        }\n\n        // Phase already completed — no repeats.\n        if self.is_done(phase) {\n            return Err(GateError::PhaseAlreadyComplete { phase });\n        }\n\n        // Determine the expected next phase.\n        let expected = match self.last_completed {\n            None => GatePhase::Research, // First phase must be Research\n            Some(last) => last.next().expect("checked is_complete above"),\n        };\n\n        // The requested phase must match the expected next phase.\n        if phase != expected {\n            return Err(GateError::SkippedPhase {\n                expected,\n                requested: phase,\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Record the completion.\n        self.completed |= 1 << phase.bit();\n        self.last_completed = Some(phase);\n        self.count += 1;\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Check if a specific phase has been completed.\n    pub fn is_done(&self, phase: GatePhase) -> bool {\n        (self.completed & (1 << phase.bit())) != 0\n    }\n\n    /// Check if ALL phases are complete (gate is closed).\n    pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool {\n        self.count >= GatePhase::ALL.len() as u8\n    }\n\n    /// Check if commit is allowed (all 9 phases done).\n    pub fn can_commit(&self) -> bool {\n        self.is_complete()\n    }\n\n    /// How many phases have been completed.\n    pub fn completed_count(&self) -> u8 {\n        self.count\n    }\n\n    /// The last completed phase, or None if no phase has been done.\n    pub fn last_phase(&self) -> Option<GatePhase> {\n        self.last_completed\n    }\n\n    /// Return the completed phases as a bitmask (for telemetry/serialization).\n    pub fn bitmask(&self) -> u16 {\n        self.completed\n    }\n\n    /// SHA3-256 hash of the gate's current state (byte-by-byte canonical).\n    /// Used for cryptographic verification of gate integrity.\n    pub fn state_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        use crate::event_log::sha3_256;\n        let bytes = self.state_bytes();\n        sha3_256(&bytes)\n    }\n\n    /// Canonical byte representation of the gate state (4 bytes).\n    /// Layout: bitmask (2 bytes LE) + count (1 byte) + last_completed (1 byte, 0xff = None).\n    pub fn state_bytes(&self) -> [u8; 4] {\n        let last = match self.last_completed {\n            Some(p) => p as u8,\n            None => 0xff,\n        };\n        [\n            self.completed as u8,\n            (self.completed >> 8) as u8,\n            self.count,\n            last,\n        ]\n    }\n\n    /// Verify the gate's state matches an expected hash.\n    /// Returns Ok(()) if byte-identical, Err(expected, actual) if mismatch.\n    pub fn verify_state(&self, expected_hash: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<(), ([u8; 32], [u8; 32])> {\n        let actual = self.state_hash();\n        if actual == *expected_hash {\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            Err((*expected_hash, actual))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII status display for diagnostics.\n    ///\n    /// ```text\n    /// [x] research\n    /// [x] synthesis\n    /// [x] critique-1\n    /// [ ] plan\n    /// [ ] critique-2\n    /// [ ] work\n    /// [ ] verify\n    /// [ ] critique-3\n    /// [ ] commit\n    /// ```\n    pub fn ascii_status(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(200);\n        for &phase in GatePhase::ALL {\n            let mark = if self.is_done(phase) { "x" } else { " " };\n            out.push_str(&format!("[{}] {}\\n", mark, phase.as_name()));\n        }\n        out\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for WorkflowGate {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn new_gate_has_no_completed_phases() {\n        let gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n        assert_eq!(gate.completed_count(), 0);\n        assert!(!gate.is_complete());\n        assert!(!gate.can_commit());\n        assert_eq!(gate.last_phase(), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn research_is_valid_first_phase() {\n        let mut gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n        assert!(gate.advance(GatePhase::Research).is_ok());\n        assert!(gate.is_done(GatePhase::Research));\n        assert_eq!(gate.completed_count(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cannot_skip_phases() {\n        let mut gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n        assert!(gate.advance(GatePhase::Research).is_ok());\n        // Skip synthesis, try to jump to critique-1\n        assert_eq!(\n            gate.advance(GatePhase::Critique1),\n            Err(GateError::SkippedPhase {\n                expected: GatePhase::Synthesis,\n                requested: GatePhase::Critique1,\n            })\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cannot_repeat_phases() {\n        let mut gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n        assert!(gate.advance(GatePhase::Research).is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(\n            gate.advance(GatePhase::Research),\n            Err(GateError::PhaseAlreadyComplete {\n                phase: GatePhase::Research\n            })\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn full_happy_path_all_9_phases() {\n        let mut gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n        for &phase in GatePhase::ALL {\n            assert!(gate.advance(phase).is_ok(), "failed on {}", phase);\n        }\n        assert!(gate.is_complete());\n        assert!(gate.can_commit());\n        assert_eq!(gate.completed_count(), 9);\n        assert_eq!(gate.last_phase(), Some(GatePhase::Commit));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cannot_advance_past_commit() {\n        let mut gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n        for &phase in GatePhase::ALL {\n            gate.advance(phase).unwrap();\n        }\n        // Try to advance again — gate is closed\n        assert_eq!(gate.advance(GatePhase::Research), Err(GateError::GateAlreadyClosed));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn first_phase_must_be_research() {\n        let mut gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n        assert_eq!(\n            gate.advance(GatePhase::Plan),\n            Err(GateError::SkippedPhase {\n                expected: GatePhase::Research,\n                requested: GatePhase::Plan,\n            })\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn can_commit_only_after_all_phases() {\n        let mut gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n        for &phase in assert_eq!(gate.bitmask(), 1); // bit 0\n        gate.advance(GatePhase::Synthesis).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(gate.bitmask(), 3); // bits 0+1\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ascii_status_shows_progress() {\n        let mut gate = WorkflowGate::new();\n        gate.advance(GatePhase::Research).unwrap();\n        gate.advance(GatePhase::Synthesis).unwrap();\n        let status = gate.ascii_status();\n        assert!(status.contains("[x] research"));\n        assert!(status.contains("[x] synthesis"));\n        assert!(status.contains("[ ] critique-1"));\n        assert!(status.contains("[ ] commit"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn phase_names_are_human_readable() {\n        assert_eq!(GatePhase::Research.as_name(), "research");\n        assert_eq!(GatePhase::Critique1.as_name(), "critique-1");\n        assert_eq!(GatePhase::Commit.as_name(), "commit");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn nine_phases_total() {\n        assert_eq!(GatePhase::ALL.len(), 9);\n    }\n}\n	8652	-1	-1		496e375efcf42b53af09c3c2b5063a57497eb7e49c76e5cbaa555657d1a7ee45712bf46872c9dedaac587129b0927860cc1edd813a4a9e7bfdcb6f0eed3cd2ecfe9a58496042f931c7de72039fba84986348340c6d79ff4efcb2b0bc2c1b4d18a03eba6e3e4b52bae5b91cdf7f4c0eb9adb6e03a4abd8ac517599b76c328e734

Vec<GraphEdge>) -> Self {\n        let mut adj = Tensor2::zeros(n, n);\n        for e in &edges {\n            let w = adj.get(e.from, e.to) + e.weight;\n            adj.set(e.from, e.to, w);\n            adj.set(e.to, e.from, w);\n        }\n        SpectralGraph { n, edges, adjacency: adj, laplacian: None, normalized_laplacian: None }\n    }\n\n    pub fn node_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.n\n    }\n\n    pub fn edge_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.edges.len()\n    }\n\n    pub fn adjacency(&self) -> &Tensor2 {\n        &self.adjacency\n    }\n\n    /// Compute the Laplacian: L = D - A\n    pub fn laplacian(&mut self) -> &Tensor2 {\n        if self.laplacian.is_some() {\n            return self.laplacian.as_ref().unwrap();\n        }\n        let mut l = Tensor2::zeros(self.n, self.n);\n        for i in 0..self.n {\n            let mut deg = 0.0;\n            for j in 0..self.n {\n                let w = self.adjacency.get(i, j);\n                if i != j {\n                    l.set(i, j, -w);\n                }\n                deg += w;\n            }\n            l.set(i, i, deg);\n        }\n        self.laplacian = Some(l);\n        self.laplacian.as_ref().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Compute normalized Laplacian: L_sym = I - D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}\n    pub fn normalized_laplacian(&mut self) -> &Tensor2 {\n        if self.normalized_laplacian.is_some() {\n            return self.normalized_laplacian.as_ref().unwrap();\n        }\n        let mut nl = Tensor2::zeros(self.n, self.n);\n        let mut deg_inv_sqrt = vec![0.0; self.n];\n        for i in 0..self.n {\n            let mut d = 0.0;\n            for j in 0..self.n {\n                d += self.adjacency.get(i, j);\n            }\n            deg_inv_sqrt[i] = if d > 0.0 { 1.0 / crate::math::sqrt(d) } else { 0.0 };\n        }\n        for i in 0..self.n {\n            for j in 0..self.n {\n                let val = if i == j {\n                    1.0\n                } else {\n                    -deg_inv_sqrt[i] * self.adjacency.get(i, j) * deg_inv_sqrt[j]\n                };\n                nl.set(i, j, val);\n            }\n        }\n        self.normalized_laplacian = Some(nl);\n        self.normalized_laplacian.as_ref().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Power-iteration eigenvector centrality (PageRank-like).\n    /// Higher values = more central nodes.\n    pub fn eigenvector_centrality(&self, iterations: usize) -> Vec<f64> {\n        if self.n == 0 {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n        let mut central = vec![1.0 / crate::math::sqrt(self.n as f64); self.n];\n        for _ in 0..iterations {\n            let mut next = vec![0.0; self.n];\n            for i in 0..self.n {\n                for j in 0..self.n {\n }\n\n    /// Degree vector for all nodes.\n    pub fn degrees(&self) -> Vec<f64> {\n        (0..self.n).map(|i| self.degree(i)).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Graph energy: sum of absolute eigenvalues of }\n        let mut total = 0.0;\n        let mut count = 0;\n        for i in 0..self.n {\n            // Find neighbors\n            let neighbors: Vec<usize> = (0..self.n)\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/clock.rs	clock · 122 lines	#![allow(unused)]\nuse core::time::Duration;\n\n/// clock.rs — single-authority time abstraction (no_std migration enabler).\n///\n/// The no_std core: `Clock` trait + `elapsed_ns` helper (pure core).\n/// Std-gated: `MonoClock`, `SystemClock`, `now_ns()`, `now_ms()`, `now_epoch_s()`.\n/// no_std fallback: returns 0 (kernel/host must provide their own implementation).\n\n/// Monotonic clock: nanoseconds since an arbitrary fixed epoch (monotone).\n/// Userspace = `std::time::Instant`; kernel = `ktime_get_ns`/jiffies (swap here).\npub trait Clock {\n    /// Current monotonic time in nanoseconds.\n    fn now_ns(&self) -> u64;\n}\n\n/// Helper: monotonic elapsed ns, saturating (never panics on wrap).\npub fn elapsed_ns(from_ns: u64, to_ns: u64) -> u64 {\n    to_ns.saturating_sub(from_ns)\n}\n\n#[cfg(feature = "std")]\nmod std_impls {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Userspace monotonic clock (wraps `std::time::Instant`).\n    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\n    pub struct MonoClock {\n        epoch: std::time::Instant,\n    }\n\n    impl Default for MonoClock {\n        fn default() -> Self {\n            Self { epoch: std::time::Instant::now() }\n        }\n    }\n\n    impl MonoClock {\n        pub fn new() -> Self { Default::default() }\n    }\n\n    impl Clock for MonoClock {\n        fn now_ns(&self) -> u64 {\n            self.epoch.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Wall-clock system time (std-gated).\n    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\n    pub struct SystemClock;\n\n    impl Clock for SystemClock {\n        fn now_ns(&self) -> u64 {\n            std::time::SystemTime::now()\n                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n                .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)\n                .unwrap_or(0)\n        }\n    }\n\n    impl SystemClock {\n        pub fn now_epoch_s() -> u64 {\n            Self.now_ns() / 1_000_000_000\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(feature = "std")]\npub use std_impls::{MonoClock, SystemClock};\n\n/// Monotonic clock: nanoseconds (std: delegates to MonoClock; no_std: returns 0).\npub fn now_ns() -> u64 {\n    #[cfg(feature = "std")]\n    { std_impls::MonoClock::new().now_ns() }\n    #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]\n    { 0 }\n}\n\n/// Monotonic clock: milliseconds.\npub fn now_ms() -> u64 {\n    now_ns() / 1_000_000\n}\n\n/// Wall-clock epoch seconds (std-gated only).\n#[cfg(feature = "std")]\npub fn now_epoch_s() -> u64 {\n    std_impls::SystemClock::now_epoch_s()\n}\n\n/// Wall-clock epoch seconds as a signed count (for arithmetic like\n/// `now - tolerance - slack`). no_std fallback returns 0; the kernel shadows this\n/// with the real `SystemTime` clock (mirroring `now_ns` / `now_ms`).\npub fn now_epoch_secs() -> i64 {\n    #[cfg(feature = "std")]\n    {\n        std_impls::SystemClock::now_epoch_s() as i64\n    }\n    #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]\n    {\n        0\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn elapsed_ns_is_saturating() {\n        assert_eq!(elapsed_ns(100, 50), 0);\n        assert_eq!(elapsed_ns(100, 200), 100);\n    }\n\n    #[cfg(feature = "std")]\n    #[test]\n    fn mono_clock_is_monotonic() {\n        let c = std_impls::MonoClock::new();\n        let a = c.now_ns();\n        let b = c.now_ns();\n        assert!(b >= a);\n    }\n}\n	8717	-1	-1		db46b45f7fc325259919ccf986aa2eca28d6b5027b703f8cc14fa253824f49f458c6b57b52f80e7abad413197ad7b76bcdf947a6b70c28b9ffe4d21a6f5ca486f406c599a8eb385514b71a45b69baadcd0b1844d2d85d6849d8033f04dd3fee75070b219bde801fb4c6083bb160d4dbde55bcd2b08df8371039c2cf578005e90

## 8729 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/chunker.rs · LongTerm

Summary: chunker · 226 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/chunker.rs	chunker · 226 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! chunker.rs — deterministic content-defined chunker (Tier B4 backup core).\n//!\n//! GROWTH-SUBSTRATE / INFRA primitive. The native Rust backup organ (Master-\n//! Integration plan B4) needs content-defined chunking so that backups DEDUP\n//! across small edits: a one-byte change in a 10 MB file must re-hash only the\n//! ~local block, not the whole file. That is exactly the property that makes\n//! the offline-on-node backup recoverable and cheap to store (3-2-1-1-0).\n//!\n//! Algorithm: Buzhash rolling fingerprint over a fixed window (W=48). A cut is\n//! emitted when the low `bits` of the fingerprint are zero AND the chunk is at\n//! least `min` bytes (with a hard cap at `max`). Because the fingerprint is a\n//! function of ONLY the local window (the outgoing byte's contribution is\n//! removed on each step), cut points depend on content, not absolute position —\n//! the defining CDC property.\n//!\n//! Deterministic: the hash table is derived from a FIXED constant seed (FNV-1a\n//! over the index), never from entropy. Same input ⇒ identical blocks on any\n//! machine / wasm32 / native. No deps; the block id is the kernel's existing\n//! `event_log::sha3_256` (FIPS 202, pure Rust).\n//!\n//! Scope ceiling (honest): this crate produces the content-addressed blocks +\n//! a remote-rebuildable index. The actual upload to R2/Hetzner is product/infra\n//! (node binary) — out of kernel scope. The chunker is the verifiable core.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\n\nconst WINDOW: usize = 48;\n\n/// A content-addressed chunk: its raw bytes + a collision-resistant id.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct Block {\n    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,\n    pub id: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Content-defined chunker. Deterministic for a given (min, max, bits).\npub struct Chunker {\n    min: usize,\n    max: usize,\n    mask: u64,\n    table: [u64; 256],\n}\n\nimpl Chunker {\n    /// `bits` = how many low fingerprint bits must be zero to cut (avg chunk ≈\n    /// 2^bits). `min`/`max` bound chunk size. Same args ⇒ identical behavior.\n    pub fn new(min: usize, max: usize, bits: u32) -> Self {\n        // Deterministic hash table: FNV-1a over the byte index, no entropy.\n        let mut table = [0u64; 256];\n        let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf29ce484222325;\n        for i in 0..256 {\n            h ^= i as u64;\n            h = h.wrapping_mul(0x100000001b3);\n            // spread the bits so low-order cuts still vary\n            table[i] = h\n                .rotate_left((i % 47) as u32)\n                .wrapping_mul(0x9e3779b97f4a7c15);\n        }\n        let mask = if bits == 0 { 0 } else { (1u64 << bits) - 1 };\n        Chunker {\n            min: min.max(1),\n            max: max.max(min + 1),\n            mask,\n            table,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Split `data` into content-defined, content-addressed blocks.\n    pub fn chunk(&self, data: &[u8]) -> Vec<Block> {\n        let n = data.len();\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n        let mut blocks = Vec::new();\n        let mut start = 0usize;\n        let mut fp: u64 = 0;\n        // ring of the last WINDOW bytes' table values, and the raw bytes\n        let mut ring: [u64; WINDOW] = [0; WINDOW];\n        let mut raw: [u8; WINDOW] = [0; WINDOW];\n        let mut filled = 0usize;\n        let mut pos = 0usize; // index into ring/raw (mod WINDOW)\n        let mut i = 0usize;\n        while i < n {\n            let b = data[i];\n            let hb = self.table[b as usize];\n            // roll: rotate-left the fingerprint by 1, XOR in the new byte\n            fp = fp.rotate_left(1) ^ hb;\n            // remove the contribution of the byte leaving the window\n            if filled == WINDOW {\n                let old = raw[pos];\n                // the old contribution was rotated left WINDOW times since it\n                // entered; subtract it back out (XOR is its own inverse)\n                fp ^= self.table[old as usize].rotate_left(WINDOW as u32);\n            } else {\n                filled += 1;\n            }\n            ring[pos] = hb;\n            raw[pos] = b;\n            pos = (pos + 1) % WINDOW;\n\n            let len = i - start + 1;\n            let cut = len >= self.min && (self.mask == 0 || (fp & self.mask) == 0);\n            let hard = len >= self.max;\n            if (cut || hard) && i < n - 1 {\n                // emit [start..=i]\n                let chunk = &data[start..=i];\n                let id = sha3_256(chunk);\n                blocks.push(Block {\n                    bytes: chunk.to_vec(),\n                    id,\n                });\n                start = i + 1;\n                fp = 0;\n                filled = 0;\n                pos = 0;\n                ring = [0; WINDOW];\n                raw = [0; WINDOW];\n            }\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        // tail (everything after the last cut, or the whole input if no cut)\n        if start < n {\n            let chunk = &data[start..n];\n            let id = sha3_256(chunk);\n            blocks.push(Block {\n                bytes: chunk.to_vec(),\n                id,\n            });\n        }\n        blocks\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn sample(n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n        // deterministic pseudo-random bytes (LCG) — reproducible, no entropy\n        let mut x: u64 = 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0;\n        (0..n)\n            .map(|_| {\n                x = x\n                    .wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005)\n                    .wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);\n                (x >> 33) as u8\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Deterministic: same input ⇒ identical block ids, on every run.\n    #[test]\n    fn deterministic() {\n        let data = sample(20_000);\n        let c = Chunker::new(1024, 32 * 1024, 12);\n        let a = c.chunk(&data);\n        let b = c.chunk(&data);\n        assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());\n        for (x, y) in a.iter().zip(b.iter()) {\n            assert_eq!(x.id, y.id);\n            assert_eq!(x.bytes, y.bytes);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Dedup: identical content ⇒ identical block ids (a re-backup shares\n    /// every block). This is the property that makes the organ storage-cheap.\n    #[test]\n    fn dedup_same_content() {\n        let data = sample(50_000);\n        let c = Chunker::new(1024, 32 * 1024, 12);\n        let blocks = c.chunk(&data);\n        // every block id unique within one file\n        let mut seen = alloc::collections::BTreeSet::new();\n        for blk in &blocks {\n            assert!(seen.insert(blk.id), "duplicate block id within a file");\n        }\n        // re-chunk the same data → identical ids (rebuildable / shared)\n        let again = c.chunk(&data);\n        assert_eq!(blocks.len(), again.len());\n        for (x, y) in blocks.iter().zip(again.iter()) {\n            assert_eq!(x.id, y.id);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// LOCALITY (the defining CDC property): flip one byte in the MIDDLE and\n    /// only the blocks straddling the change differ; the prefix and suffix\n    /// blocks keep their ids. That is why a 1-byte edit re-hashes ~one block,\n    /// not the file.\n    #[test]\n    fn locality_one_byte_change() {\n        let mut data = sample(200_000);\n        let c = Chunker::new(1024, 32 * 1024, 12);\n        let before = c.chunk(&data);\n        // change a single byte in the middle\n        let mid = data.len() / 2;\n        data[mid] ^= 0xff;\n        let after = c.chunk(&data);\n\n        assert_eq!(before.len(), after.len(), "same block count expected");\n        let mut changed = 0;\n        for (x, y) in before.iter().zip(after.iter()) {\n            if x.id != y.id {\n                changed += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        // only a small local region changes, not the whole file\n        assert!(changed <= 3, "too many blocks changed: {changed}");\n        assert!(changed >= 1, "expected at least the edited block to change");\n    }\n\n    /// REBUILD: concatenating the block bytes in order reproduces the input.\n    #[test]\n    fn rebuild_from_blocks() {\n        let data = sample(80_000);\n        let c = Chunker::new(1024, 32 * 1024, 12);\n        let blocks = c.chunk(&data);\n        let mut rebuilt = Vec::new();\n        for blk in &blocks {\n            rebuilt.extend_from_slice(&blk.bytes);\n        }\n        assert_eq!(rebuilt, data);\n    }\n}\n	8730	-1	-1		c9573f5ffc8da3bdd30980c717117325c9b6b4c4ff53c4c22952a44a5be7e14359447104efcb50bee75202eb31c9f32cce716fa5dd68442af87a3a8ddface88ed40a34992d7ae8019d59310ad73ba159d04ae81a6db8e64958a2b894f40dc765a4a2d2a691ca12b5d1ca884693550c984c3164220f858dd08021f4f0f1202d90

Pure data structures that define HOW a parse call should be executed\n//! through an anti-detect browser with zero trace and proxy redirection.\n//! This module contains NO network I/O — it is the kernel's configuration\n//! authority for browser-based parsing. The actual browser automation lives\n//! behind the `AgentBrowserPort` trait in `ports/agent_browser.rs`.\n//!\n//! # Design principles\n//! - Kernel = pure computation (no browser/network)\n//! - All anti-detect fingerprinting is configuration, not code\n//! - Zero-trace policy is enforced by construction (typed, not a flag)\n//! - Per-call crypto signature binding is structurally required\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::TriState;\n\n/// Maximum concurrent browser sessions (resource-aware default).\nconst MAX_BROWSER_SESSIONS: usize = 4;\n\n/// Anti-detect browser configuration for a single parse call.\n///\n/// Every field is explicitly set — no silent defaults that could leak trace.\n/// The kernel constructs this and passes it through the `AgentBrowserPort`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AntiDetectConfig {\n    /// Unique session fingerprint (randomized per call).\n    pub session_fingerprint: [u8; 32],\n    /// Navigator properties to spoof (user-agent, platform, languages, etc).\n    pub navigator: NavigatorProfile,\n    /// WebGL fingerprint override (canvas rendering signature).\n    pub webgl: WebGLProfile,\n    /// Timezone and locale override (prevents timezone correlation).\n    pub timezone: TimezoneOverride,\n    /// WebRTC policy (prevent IP leak via STUN).\n    pub webrtc: WebRtcPolicy,\n    /// HTTP header order (browsers have characteristic header ordering).\n    pub header_order: HeaderOrder,\n    /// Client hints override (sec-ch-ua headers).\n    pub client_hints: ClientHints,\n}\n\n/// Navigator properties to spoof.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct NavigatorProfile {\n    /// e.g. "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ..."\n    pub user_agent: String,\n    /// e.g. "Win32", "MacIntel", "Linux x86_64"\n    pub platform: String,\n    /// e.g. ["en-US", "en"]\n    pub languages: Vec<String>,\n    /// Hardware concurrency (CPU core count to report).\n    pub hardware_concurrency: u32,\n    /// Device memory (GB to report).\n    pub device_memory: u32,\n    /// Max touch points.\n    pub max_touch_points: u32,\n}\n\n/// WebGL fingerprint override.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct WebGLProfile {\n    /// Renderer string (e.g. "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080").\n    pub renderer: String,\n    /// Vendor string (e.g. "NVIDIA Corporation").\n    pub vendor: String,\n}\n\n/// Timezone and locale override.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TimezoneOverride {\n    /// IANA timezone (e.g. "America/New_York").\n    pub timezone_id: String,\n    /// UTC offset in seconds.\n    pub utc_offset_secs: i32,\n}\n\n/// WebRTC policy — controls whether STUN can leak the real IP.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum WebRtcPolicy {\n    /// Block all WebRTC (safest — no IP leak possible).\n    Block,\n    /// Force WebRTC through proxy (IP shows proxy, not real).\n    ProxyOnly,\n    /// Allow native WebRTC (risky — may leak real IP).\n    AllowNative,\n}\n\n/// HTTP header ordering — browsers have characteristic ordering.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct HeaderOrder {\n    /// Ordered list of header names (first element sent first).\n    pub order: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// Client hints (sec-ch-ua headers).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct full_version_list: String,\n    /// e.g. "\\"Windows\\""\n    pub platform: String,\n    /// e.g. "\\"Windows 10\\""\n    pub platform_version: String,\n    /// e.g. "\\"Google Chrome\\""\n    pub model: String,\n}\n\n/// Zero-trace policy — what to clear and when.\n///\n/// Typed to prevent silent trace leaks: every field must be explicitly chosen.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ZeroTracePolicy {\n    /// Clear cookies between requests.\n    pub clear_cookies: TriState,\n    /// Clear localStorage between requests.\n    pub clear_local_storage: TriState,\n    /// Clear sessionStorage between requests.\n    pub clear_session_storage: TriState,\n    /// Clear IndexedDB between requests.\n    pub clear_indexed_db: TriState,\n    /// Clear cache between requests.\n    pub clear_cache: TriState,\n    /// Clear WebGL textures between requests.\n    pub clear_webgl: TriState,\n    /// Reset canvas fingerprint between requests.\n    pub reset_canvas: TriState,\n    /// TriState::True,\n            disable_history_api: TriState::True,\n            disable_send_beacon: TriState::True,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Balanced — clear what matters most, allow some convenience.\n    pub fn balanced() -> Self {\n        ZeroTracePolicy {\n            clear_cookies: TriState::True,\n            clear_local_storage: TriState::True,\n TriState::True,\n            randomize_font_order: TriState::False,\n            disable_history_api: TriState::True,\n            disable_send_beacon: TriState::True,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The result of a browser-based parse operation.\n///\n/// Cryptographically signed per-call — the signature binds the IP, timestamp,\n/// payload hash, and a nonce to prevent replay and tampering.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ParseResult {\n    /// The extracted content (HTML text, JSON, structured data).\n    pub content: Vec<u8>,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the raw content for integrity verification.\n    pub content_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// The URL that was actually loaded (after redirects).\n    pub final_url: String,\n    /// HTTP status code.\n    pub status_code: u16,\n    /// Response headers (key-value pairs).\n    pub response_headers: Vec<(String, String)>,\n    /// Time to first byte in microseconds.\n    pub ttfb_us: u64,\n    /// Total load time in microseconds.\n    pub load_time_us: u64,\n    /// The ML-DSA-65 signature over (ip_hash || timestamp || content_hash || nonce).\n    pub pq_signature: Vec<u8>,\n    /// The ML-DSA-65 public key used for this call's signature.\n    pub pq_public_key: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Timestamp (unix microseconds) when the response was received.\n    pub timestamp_us: u64,\n    /// IP address hash (SHA3-256 of the source IP used for this call).\n    pub ip_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// Nonce used for this call's signature (prevents replay).\n    pub nonce: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Dynamic algorithm selection for read/navigate actions.\n///\n/// Based on system load and available resources, the orchestrator selects\n/// the optimal algorithm for each operation.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum ReadAlgorithm {\n    /// Sequential read — low resource usage, single-threaded.\n    Sequential,\n    /// Parallel chunk read — uses available cores for large pages.\n    ParallelChunked,\n    /// Streaming read — incremental processing, lowest memory.\n    Streaming,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum NavigateAlgorithm {\n    /// Direct navigation — single request, lowest latency.\n    Direct,\n    /// Retry with backoff — handles transient failures.\n    RetryWithBackoff,\n    /// Multi-path — tries multiple routes (proxy chains) for redundancy.\n    MultiPath,\n}\n\n/// Resource state snapshot for dynamic algorithm selection.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ResourceSnapshot {\n    /// Available CPU cores (from `std::thread::available_parallelism`).\n    pub cpu_cores: usize,\n    /// Memory pressure: 0.0 = idle, 1.0 = saturated.\n    pub memory_pressure: f64,\n    /// Current active browser sessions.\n    pub active_sessions: usize,\n    /// Average latency of recent parse calls (microseconds).\n    pub avg_latency_us: u64,\n    /// Failure rate of recent parse calls (0.0..1.0).\n    pub failure_rate: f64,\n}\n\nimpl ResourceSnapshot {\n    /// Select the optimal read algorithm based on current resources.\n    pub fn select_read_algorithm(&self) -> ReadAlgorithm {\n        if self.memory_pressure > 0.8 {\n            ReadAlgorithm::Streaming\n        } else if self.cpu_cores >= 4 && self.memory_pressure < 0.5 {\n            ReadAlgorithm::ParallelChunked\n        } else {\n            ReadAlgorithm::Sequential\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Select the optimal navigate algorithm based on current resources.\n    pub fn select_navigate_algorithm(&self) -> NavigateAlgorithm {\n        if self.failure_rate > 0.3 {\n            NavigateAlgorithm::MultiPath\n        } else if self.failure_rate > 0.1 {\n            NavigateAlgorithm::RetryWithBackoff\n        } else {\n            NavigateAlgorithm::Direct\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Recommended concurrency limit based on resources.\n    pub fn recommended_concurrency(&self) -> usize {\n        if self.memory_pressure > 0.8 {\n            1\n        } else if self.cpu_cores >= 8 && self.memory_pressure < 0.3 {\n            MAX_BROWSER_SESSIONS\n        } else if self.cpu_cores >= 4 {\n            2\n        } else {\n            1\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute a session fingerprint from a seed (deterministic but unique per call).\npub fn compute_session_fingerprint(seed: &[u8], call_index: u64) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(seed.len() + 8);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(seed);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&call_index.to_le_bytes());\n    sha3_256(&buf)\n}\n\n/// Compute IP hash for crypto assert_ne!(a, b, "different index => different fingerprint");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn hash_ip_deterministic() {\n        let ip = [192, 168, 1, 1];\n        let a = hash_ip(&ip);\n        let b ```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/hypergraph.rs	hypergraph · 662 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! hypergraph.rs — Full hypergraph data structure and operations.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! A kernel-native hypergraph implementation: a generalization of graphs where\n//! an edge (hyperedge) can connect any number of vertices, not just two.\n//!\n//! Hypergraphs are used in the kernel for:\n//! - Modeling multi-way relationships (e.g. skill dependencies, agent coalitions)\n//! - Spectral analysis of complex relational structures\n//! - Mesh topology abstraction (hyperedges = communication channels between\n//!   arbitrary sets of peers)\n//! - Research paper citation networks (hyperedges = papers cited by multiple\n//!   later papers)\n//!\n//! # Design\n//! - Pure Rust, zero external dependencies\n//! - CSR-inspired compact storage for the incidence matrix\n//! - Hypergraph Laplacian for spectral analysis (eigenvalues, centrality)\n//! - Incidence matrix H (vertices × hyperedges): H[v,e] = 1 if vertex v ∈ hyperedge e\n//! - Degree matrices D_v (vertex degrees) and D_e (hyperedge sizes)\n//! - Laplacian L = D_v - H * D_e^{-1} * H^T (normalized hypergraph Laplacian)\n//!\n//! # Integration\n//! - Consumed by `spectral::eigh` for eigenvalue decomposition\n//! - Used by `csr::Csr` for sparse matrix representation\n//! - Feeds into `spectral_graph` for eigenvector centrality\n//! - Exposed via `dowiz_kernel::hypergraph`\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A hypergraph — a set of vertices connected by hyperedges (each hyperedge\n/// can connect any number of vertices).\npub struct Hypergraph {\n    /// Number of vertices.\n    num_vertices: usize,\n    /// Number of hyperedges.\n    num_hyperedges: usize,\n    /// Incidence list: for each hyperedge, the set of vertices it connects.\n    /// incidence[e] = set of vertex indices in hyperedge e.\n    incidence: Vec<Vec<usize>>,\n    /// Vertex degrees: degree[v] = number of hyperedges containing vertex v.\n    vertex_degrees: Vec<usize>,\n    /// Hyperedge sizes: size[e] = number of vertices in hyperedge e.\n    hyperedge_sizes: Vec<usize>,\n}\n\nimpl Hypergraph {\n    /// Create a new empty hypergraph with `num_vertices` vertices and no hyperedges.\n    pub fn new(num_vertices: usize) -> Self {\n        Hypergraph {\n            num_vertices,\n            num_hyperedges: 0,\n            incidence: Vec::new(),\n            vertex_degrees: vec![0; {\n        self.num_hyperedges\n    }\n\n    /// The incidence list (each hyperedge's vertex set).\n    pub fn incidence(&self) -> &Vec<Vec<usize>> {\n        &self.incidence\n    }\n\n    /// Vertex degrees.\n    pub fn vertex_degrees(&self) -> &Vec<usize> {\n        &self.vertex_degrees\n    }\n\n    /// Hyperedge sizes.\n    pub fn hyperedge_sizes(&self) -> &Vec<usize> {\n
