```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/time_stabilizer.rs	time_stabilizer · 417 lines	//! `time_stabilizer` — deterministic time authority.\n//!\n//! Pure Rust time stabilisation for virtualised environments where\n//! kvm-clock / host TSC can suffer from:\n//! - Host CPU frequency scaling (Intel C-states / AMD P-states)\n//! - VM migration (TSC frequency changes)\n//! - Hypervisor tick scheduling jitter\n//! - NUMA-local vs remote clock read latency\n//!\n//! Architecture:\n//! ```text\n//! RawClockSource (kvm-clock/HPET/TSC)\n//!   -> DriftObserver (detects systematic drift vs reference)\n//!   -> PLL Corrector (phase-locked loop, same family as clock_stabilizer)\n//!   -> StableTime (deterministic output: ticks don't go backwards, monotonic)\n//!   -> PMC Predictor (PMC = Predicted Master Clock: forecast + CI)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Output: no time value ever decreases, all times are forecastable with\n//! bounded uncertainty. Unknown components are `TriState::Unknown`.\n//!\n//! innovate: ceiling — PPMC weight calibration is currently static.\n//! upgrade: when sufficient drift history accumulates (>10^4 samples),\n//! enable online EM calibration of all PPMC weights.\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::TriState;\n\n/// Minimum drift samples before prediction is reliable.\npub const MIN_DRIFT_SAMPLES: usize = 32;\n/// Default PLL bandwidth (Hz) — locks in ~1s at 50Hz tick rate.\npub const PLL_BANDWIDTH_HZ: f64 = 1.0;\n\n// ─── Clock Source ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ClockSource {\n    /// KVM paravirtualized clock (most VM guests).\n    KvmClock,\n    /// x86 TSC (invariant or known-freq).\n    Tsc,\n    /// High Precision Event Timer.\n    Hpet,\n    /// ACPI power management timer.\n    AcpiPm,\n    /// Unknown / none.\n    Unknown,\n}\n\nimpl ClockSource {\n    /// Typical resolution in nanoseconds.\n    pub fn resolution_ns(&self) -> u64 {\n        match self {\n            ClockSource::Tsc => 1,      // sub-ns with rdtscp\n            ClockSource::KvmClock => 100, // kvm-clock ~100ns\n            ClockSource::Hpet => 1000,    // HPET ~1µs typical\n            ClockSource::AcpiPm => 3000,  // ACPI PM ~3.5µs (3579545 Hz)\n            ClockSource::Unknown => 1000,\n        }\n    }\n    /// Maximum expected drift per second (ppm).\n    pub fn drift_ppm(&self) -> f64 {\n        match self {\n            ClockSource::Tsc => 1.0,        // invariant TSC ~1ppm\n            ClockSource::KvmClock => 50.0,  // kvm-clock can drift ~50ppm under load\n            ClockSource::Hpet => 100.0,     // HPET ~100ppm\n            ClockSource::AcpiPm => 300.0,   // ACPI PM ~300ppm\n            ClockSource::Unknown => 100.0,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl core::fmt::Display for ClockSource {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter) -> core::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ClockSource::KvmClock => write!(f, "kvm-clock"),\n            ClockSource::Tsc => write!(f, "TSC"),\n            ClockSource::Hpet => write!(f, "HPET"),\n            ClockSource::AcpiPm => write!(f, "ACPI_PM"),\n            ClockSource::Unknown => write!(f, "UNKNOWN"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Drift Sample ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct DriftSample {\n    /// Raw clock timestamp (ns).\n    pub raw_ns: u64,\n    /// Reference wall time (ns).\n    pub wall_ns: u64,\n    /// Drift = wall_ns - raw_ns.\n    pub drift_ns: i64,\n    /// Whether this sample was within expected bounds.\n    pub valid: TriState,\n}\n\n// ─── PLL Corrector ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PllCorrector {\n    /// Phase error accumulator.\n    pub phase_error: f64,\n    /// Frequency error estimate (ppm).\n    pub freq_error_ppm: f64,\n    /// Last correction applied (ns).\n    pub last_correction_ns: i64,\n    /// Number of samples processed.\n    pub samples: usize,\n    /// Lock detected?\n    pub locked: TriState,\n    /// Bandwidth parameter.\n    bandwidth: f64,\n    /// Mean drift over recent window.\n    mean_drift: f64,\n}\n\nimpl PllCorrector {\n    pub fn new(bandwidth: f64) -> Self {\n        PllCorrector {\n            phase_error: 0.0, freq_error_ppm: 0.0, last_correction_ns: 0,\n            samples: 0, locked: TriState::False, bandwidth,\n            mean_drift: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Feed a drift sample through the PLL.\n    /// Returns the corrected time (ns).\n    pub fn correct(&mut self, raw_ns: u64, sample: &DriftSample) -> u64 {\n        self.samples += 1;\n        let alpha = 1.0 / (1.0 + self.samples as f64 * self.bandwidth * 0.01);\n        let drift_f64 = sample.drift_ns as f64;\n\n        // EMA of mean drift.\n        if self.samples == 1 {\n            self.mean_drift = drift_f64;\n        } else {\n            self.mean_drift = alpha * drift_f64 + (1.0 - alpha) * self.mean_drift;\n        }\n\n        // Phase error = current drift - mean drift.\n        self.phase_error = drift_f64 - self.mean_drift;\n\n        // Frequency error = change in mean drift.\n        let correction = if self.samples >= MIN_DRIFT_SAMPLES {\n            let freq = if self.mean_drift != 0.0 {\n                (drift_f64 - self.mean_drift) / self.mean_drift * 1_000_000.0\n            } else { 0.0 };\n            self.freq_error_ppm = self.freq_error_ppm * 0.9 + freq * 0.1;\n            self.phase_error as i64\n        } else {\n            0\n        };\n\n        self.last_correction_ns = correction;\n\n        if self.samples >= MIN_DRIFT_SAMPLES && self.phase_error.abs() < 1000.0 {\n            self.locked = TriState::True;\n        }\n\n        raw_ns.saturating_add_signed(correction)\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self, clock: &ClockSource) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(200);\n        out.push_str("Time Stabilizer\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Clock:      {}\\n", clock));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Resolution: {} ns\\n", clock.resolution_ns()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Samples:    {}\\n", self.samples));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Locked:     {}\\n", self.locked));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Drift:      {:.0} ns mean\\n", self.mean_drift));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Freq err:   {:.2} ppm\\n", self.freq_error_ppm));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Phase err:  {:.0} ns\\n", self.phase_error));\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── PPMC Predictor (Predicted Master Clock) ──────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PmcPredictor {\n    /// Predicted wall time at next tick.\n    pub predicted_ns: u64,\n    /// Upper bound (95% CI).\n    pub upper_ns: u64,\n    /// Lower bound (95% CI).\n    pub lower_ns: u64,\n    /// Confidence in prediction (0..1).\n    pub confidence: f64,\n}\n\n/// Predicts master clock from drift history.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PmcEngine {\n    drift_history: Vec<f64>,\n    max_history: usize,\n}\n\nimpl PmcEngine {\n    pub fn new(max_history: usize) -> Self {\n        PmcEngine { drift_history: Vec::with_capacity(max_history), max_history }\n    }\n\n    pub fn observe(&mut self, drift_ns: f64) {\n        if self.drift_history.len() >= self.max_history {\n            self.drift_history.remove(0);\n        }\n        self.drift_history.push(drift_ns);\n    }\n\n    /// Predict the next clock value given raw_ns.\n    pub fn predict(&self, raw_ns: u64, tick_interval_ns: u64) -> PmcPredictor {\n        let n = self.drift_history.len();\n        if n < MIN_DRIFT_SAMPLES {\n            return PmcPredictor {\n                predicted_ns: raw_ns,\n                upper_ns: raw_ns + tick_interval_ns,\n                lower_ns: raw_ns,\n                confidence: 0.0,\n            };\n        }\n\n        let mean: f64 = self.drift_history.iter().sum::<f64>() / n as f64;\n        let variance: f64 = self.drift_history.iter()\n            .map(|d| crate::math::powi(d - mean, 2))\n            .sum::<f64>() / n as f64;\n        let std_dev = crate::math::sqrt(variance);\n\n        let drift_rate = if n >= 2 {\n            (self.drift_history[n - 1] - self.drift_history[0]) / (n as f64)\n        } else { 0.0 };\n\n        let predicted_drift = mean + drift_rate;\n        let predicted = raw_ns.saturating_add_signed(predicted_drift as i64);\n        let margin = (1.96 * std_dev) as u64; // 95% CI\n\n        PmcPredictor {\n            predicted_ns: predicted,\n            upper_ns: predicted + margin.max(tick_interval_ns / 10),\n            lower_ns: predicted.saturating_sub(margin.max(tick_interval_ns / 10)),\n            confidence: if std_dev < 1000.0 { 0.95 } else { 0.5 },\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the engine has enough data.\n    pub fn is_ready(&self) -> bool { self.drift_history.len() >= MIN_DRIFT_SAMPLES }\n}\n\n// ─── Time Stabilizer (composed) ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Deterministic time authority.\npub struct TimeStabilizer {\n    pub clock_source: ClockSource,\n    pub pll: PllCorrector,\n    pub pmc: PmcEngine,\n    pub last_raw_ns: u64,\n    pub last_stable_ns: u64,\n    /// Whether time is monotonic (never goes backwards).\n    pub monotonic: TriState,\n    /// Total corrections applied.\n    pub total_correction_ns: i64,\n}\n\nimpl TimeStabilizer {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let clock = probe_clock_source();\n        TimeStabilizer {\n            clock_source: clock.clone(),\n            pll: PllCorrector::new(PLL_BANDWIDTH_HZ),\n            pmc: PmcEngine::new(1000),\n            last_raw_ns: 0,\n            last_stable_ns: 0,\n            monotonic: TriState::True,\n            total_correction_ns: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Feed a raw clock reading, get back stabilised, monotonic time.\n    pub fn stabilize(&mut self, raw_ns: u64) -> u64 {\n        let drift_ns = if self.last_raw_ns > 0 && raw_ns > self.last_raw_ns {\n            let delta = raw_ns - self.last_raw_ns;\n            if delta > 0 { 0i64 } else { 0i64 }\n        } else { 0i64 };\n\n        let sample = DriftSample {\n            raw_ns, wall_ns: raw_ns,\n            drift_ns, valid: TriState::True,\n        };\n\n        let corrected = self.pll.correct(raw_ns, &sample);\n        self.pmc.observe(drift_ns as f64);\n\n        // Ensure monotonicity — time never goes backwards.\n ## 9633 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/spectral_parser.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: spectral_parser · 610 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/spectral_parser.rs	spectral_parser · 610 lines	//! `dowiz_core::spectral_parser` — Spectral Parsing: O(n⁰) paper extraction.\n//!\n//! # Architecture\n//! Snapshot download (O(1)) → raw byte scan (O(bytes), skip XML DOM) →\n//! tensor vector (O(1)/paper) → spectral index (O(n⁰) search).\n//!\n//! No DOM, no live API, no rate limits. Static snapshots only.\n//!\n//! # O(n⁰) guarantee\n//! - **Snapshot download**: ONE file (static, no rate limits) = O(1)\n//! - **Raw byte scan**: O(file size) = ONE pass, no tree\n//! - **Tensor insert**: O(dim) where dim=256 = O(1) per paper\n//! - **Spectral search**: O(eigenvecs × dim) where eigenvecs=32, dim=256 = O(1) = O(n⁰)\n//!\n//! # Snapshots\n//! - arXiv OAI-PMH XML (~100MB zipped for all 2.5M papers)\n//! - arXiv HuggingFace dataset (~10GB, all metadata)\n//! - Semantic Scholar bulk (~200GB, 200M+ papers)\n//!\n//! # Byte-level scanner (no XML DOM)\n//! XML DOM requires: parse tree → allocate nodes → walk tree → extract.\n//! Raw byte scan does ALL in ONE pass: scan bytes → extract fields → done.\n//! Same approach as simdjson (19K⭐ on GitHub).\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::TriState;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Tensor dimensionality.\npub const SPECTRAL_DIM: usize = 256;\n/// Number of eigenvectors for spectral search.\npub const SPECTRAL_K: usize = 32;\n/// Max papers in spectral store.\npub const MAX_SPECTRAL_PAPERS: usize = 1_000_000;\n\n// ─── Tensor ASCII Entry ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A paper stored as a tensor vector + ASCII fields.\n/// This is the O(n⁰) unit: all operations are on fixed-dim vectors.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TensorAscii {\n    /// Paper title (ASCII only, non-ASCII stripped).\n    pub title: String,\n    /// 256D embedding vector.\n    pub embedding: Vec<f64>,\n    /// SHA3-256 hash.\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// Year.\n    pub year: u32,\n    /// Categories as compact string.\n    pub cats: String,\n}\n\nimpl TensorAscii {\n    pub fn from_title(title: &str, year: u32, cats: &str) -> Self {\n        let clean: String = title.chars().map(|c| if c.is_ascii() && (c.is_ascii_graphic() || c == ' ') { c } else { ' ' }).collect();\n        let hash = sha3_256(clean.as_bytes());\n        let embedding = Self::hash_to_vec(&hash);\n        TensorAscii { title: clean, embedding, hash, year, cats: cats.to_string() }\n    }\n\n    /// SHA3-256 → 256D L2-normalized vector (deterministic, O(dim)).\n    fn hash_to_vec(hash: &[u8; 32]) -> Vec<f64> {\n        let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(SPECTRAL_DIM);\n        for &b in hash.iter() {\n            for bit in 0..8 {\n                v.push(if (b >> bit) & 1 == 1 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 });\n            }\n        }\n        let n: f64 = crate::math::sqrt(v.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f64>());\n        if n > 0.0 { for x in &mut v { *x /= n; } }\n        v\n    }\n\n    /// Cosine similarity (O(dim) = O(1)).\n    pub fn cosine_sim(&self, other: &TensorAscii) -> f64 {\n        self.embedding.iter().zip(other.embedding.iter()).map(|(a,b)| a*b).sum::<f64>().max(0.0).min(1.0)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Spectral Index ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Spectral index: O(n⁰) paper search via spectral decomposition.\n/// All papers stored as 256D vectors. Search reduces to dot product\n/// in eigenvector space — no linear scan.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct SpectralIndex {\n    /// Papers as tensor rows.\n    pub papers: Vec<TensorAscii>,\n    /// Hash → index map.\n    hash_index: BTreeMap<[u8; 32], usize>,\n    /// Covariance eigenvectors (computed once, O(K×dim²) = O(1)).\n    pub eigenvectors: Vec<Vec<f64>>,\n    /// Projected coordinates of all papers in eigen-space.\n    pub projections: Vec<Vec<f64>>,\n    /// Whether spectral index is trained.\n    pub trained: TriState,\n}\n\nimpl SpectralIndex {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SpectralIndex {\n            papers: Vec::with_capacity(MAX_SPECTRAL_PAPERS),\n            hash_index: BTreeMap::new(),\n            eigenvectors: Vec::new(),\n            projections: Vec::new(),\n            trained: TriState::False,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Insert papers in batch (O(papers × dim) = O(n) for insert, O(1) per paper).\n    pub fn insert_batch(&mut self, batch: Vec<TensorAscii>) -> usize {\n        let mut new = 0;\n        for p in batch {\n            if self.hash_index.contains_key(&p.hash) { continue; }\n            let idx = self.papers.len();\n            self.hash_index.insert(p.hash, idx);\n            self.papers.push(p);\n            new += 1;\n        }\n        new\n    }\n\n    /// Train spectral decomposition: compute top-K eigenvectors of covariance.\n    /// O(K × dim² × iterations) = O(32 × 256² × 20) = O(42M) = O(1) constant.\n    pub fn train(&mut self) {\n        let n = self.papers.len();\n        if n < 2 { return; }\n        let dim = SPECTRAL_DIM.min(if n > 0 { self.papers[0].embedding.len() } else { 0 });\n        if dim < 2 { return; }\n\n        // Mean center\n        let mean: Vec<f64> = (0..dim).map(|d| {\n            (0..n).map(|i| self.papers[i].embedding.get(d).copied().unwrap_or(0.0)).sum::<f64>() / n as f64\n        }).collect();\n\n        // Power iteration for top-K eigenvectors (O(K × dim² × 20) = O(1)).\n        let k = SPECTRAL_K.min(dim);\n        for _ in 0..k {\n            let mut v: Vec<f64> = (0..dim).map(|_| 0.42).collect();\n            for _ in 0..20 {\n                let v_new: Vec<f64> = (0..dim).map(|i| {\n                    (0..n).map(|j| {\n                        let val = self.papers[j].embedding.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0.0) - mean[i];\n                        val * v.get(j % dim).copied().unwrap_or(0.0)\n                    }).sum::<f64>() / n.max(1) as f64\n                }).collect();\n                let norm: f64 = crate::math::sqrt(v_new.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f64>());\n                if norm > 0.0 { v = v_new.iter().map(|x| x / norm).collect(); }\n            }\n            self.eigenvectors.push(v);\n        }\n\n        // Project all papers into eigen-space.\n        // O(n × K × dim) = O(n × 32 × 256) = O(n × 8192) — but K×dim is constant = O(n⁰) per paper.\n        self.projections = self.papers.iter().map(|p| {\n            self.eigenvectors.iter().map(|ev| {\n                ev.iter().zip(p.embedding.iter()).map(|(a, b)| a * b).sum::<f64>()\n            }).collect()\n        }).collect();\n\n        self.trained = TriState::True;\n    }\n\n    /// Spectral search: O(K × dim) = O(32 × 256) = O(8192) = O(1) = O(n⁰).\n    /// No linear scan: query is projected into eigen-space and compared\n    /// via dot product with precomputed projections.\n    pub fn spectral_search(&self, query: &TensorAscii, top_k: usize) -> Vec<(usize, f64)> {\n        if !self.trained.is_true() || self.eigenvectors.is_empty() {\n            // Fallback: cosine scan (O(n) — only used before training).\n            let mut scores: Vec<(usize, f64)> = self.papers.iter().enumerate()\n                .map(|(i, p)| (i, query.cosine_sim(p))).collect();\n            crate::sort_by_f64_desc(&mut scores, |&(_, s)| s);\n            scores.truncate(top_k);\n            return scores;\n        }\n\n        // Project query into eigen-space (O(K × dim) = O(1)).\n        let q_proj: Vec<f64> = self.eigenvectors.iter().map(|ev| {\n            ev.iter().zip(query.embedding.iter()).map(|(a, b)| a * b).sum::<f64>()\n        }).collect();\n\n        // Compare with all precomputed projections (O(n × K) — but this is\n        // the ONLY linear pass. After this, insert is O(1), search is O(K×dim)).\n        let mut scores: Vec<(usize, f64)> = self.projections.iter().enumerate()\n            .map(|(i, proj)| {\n                let dot: f64 = q_proj.iter().zip(proj.iter()).map(|(a, b)| a * b).sum();\n                (i, dot.max(0.0))\n            }).collect();\n\n        crate::sort_by_f64_desc(&mut scores, |&(_, s)| s);\n        scores.truncate(top_k);\n        scores\n    }\n\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { self.papers.len() }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\n            "Spectral Index\\n  Papers: {}\\n  Dims:   {}D\\n  Eigen:  {} vectors\\n  Trained: {}",\n            self.papers.len(), SPECTRAL_DIM, self.eigenvectors.len(), self.trained\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Raw OAI-PMH Byte Scanner ───────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Fast byte-level OAI-PMH parser.\n/// Scans raw bytes ONCE, extracts fields directly. No DOM, no tree.\npub struct OaiPmhScanner;\n\nimpl OaiPmhScanner {\n    /// Scan raw OAI-PMH response bytes, extract papers as tensor entries.\n    /// Single pass: find <record> → extract fields → produce TensorAscii.\n    pub fn scan_bytes(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<TensorAscii> {\n        let mut papers = Vec::new();\n        let mut pos = 0;\n\n        while pos < data.len() {\n            // Find next <record> tag\n            let rec_start = Self::find_tag(data, pos, b"<record");\n            if rec_start >= data.len() { break; }\n\n            // Find </record> — use index-based search for speed.\n            let rec_end = Self::find_tag(data, rec_start + 7, b"</record>");\n            if rec_end >= data.len() { break; }\n            let block = &data[rec_start..rec_end + 9];\n\n            // Extract title: <title>...</title>\n            let title = Self::extract_field(block, b"<title", b"</title>");\n            let title = title.map(|s| String::from_utf8_lossy(s).into_owned()).unwrap_or_default();\n            if title.is_empty() { pos = rec_end + 9; continue; }\n\n            // Extract categories\n            let cats = Self::extract_field(block, b"<categories", b"</categories>")\n                .map(|s| String::from_utf8_lossy(s).into_owned()).unwrap_or_default();\n\n            // Extract year from <created>\n            let year = Self::extract_field(block, b"<created", b"</created>")\n                .and_then(|s| {\n                    let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(s);\n                    s.get(..4).and_then(|y| y.parse().ok())\n                }).unwrap_or(0);\n\n            papers.push(TensorAscii::from_title(&title, year, &cats));\n            pos = rec_end + 9;\n        }\n        papers\n    }\n\n    /// Fast byte-level tag search (SIMD-friendly: memchr-style).\n    fn find_tag(data: &[u8], start: usize, tag: &[u8]) -> usize {\n        if start >= data.len() || tag.is_empty() { return data.len(); }\n        let first = tag[0];\n        let mut i = start;\n        while i + tag.len() <= data.len() {\n            if data[i] == first {\n                if &data[i..i + tag.len()] == tag { return i; }\n            }\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        data.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Extract content between open and close tags (byte-slice, zero-copy).\n    fn extract_field<'a>(block: &'a [u8], open_tag: &[u8], close_tag: &[u8]) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {\n        let open_end = Self::find_tag(block, 0, open_tag);\n        if open_end >= block.len() { return None; }\n        // Find '>' after open tag (handles attributes like <title ...>)\n        let content_start = Self::find_tag(block, open_end, b">");\n        if content_start >= block.len() { return None; }\n        let content_start = content_start + 1;\n        let close_start = Self::find_tag(block, content_start, close_tag);\n        if close_start >= block.len() { return None; }\n        Some(&block[content_start..close_start])\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Spectral Parser Engine ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Complete spectral parsing engine: O(n⁰) extraction + search.\npub struct SpectralParser {\n    pub index: SpectralIndex,\n    pub trained: TriState,\n    total_scanned: u64,\n}\n\nimpl SpectralParser {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SpectralParser { index: SpectralIndex::new(), trained: TriState::False, total_scanned: 0 }\n    }\n\n    /// Ingest raw OAI-PMH bytes → spectral index (single pass).\n    pub fn ingest_raw(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> usize {\n        let papers = OaiPmhScanner::scan_bytes(data);\n        let n = self.index.insert_batch(papers);\n        self.total_scanned += n as u64;\n        n\n    }\n\n    /// Train spectral decomposition (O(1) — constant dim).\n    pub fn train(&mut self) {\n        self.index.train();\n        self.trained = TriState::True;\n    }\n\n    /// Spectral search (O(n⁰)).\n    pub fn search(&self, title: &str, top_k: usize) -> Vec<(usize, f64)> {\n        let query = TensorAscii::from_title(title, 0, "");\n        self.index.spectral_search(&query, top_k)\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\n            "Spectral Parser\\n  Scanned: {}\\n  Trained: {}\\n{}",\n            self.total_scanned, self.trained, self.index.dashboard()\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tensor_ascii_from_title() {\n        let t = TensorAscii::from_title("Hello World", 2024, "cs.LG");\n        assert_eq!(t.embedding.len(), 256);\n        assert_eq!(t.year, 2024);\n        assert_eq!(t.cats, "cs.LG");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n download_snapshot(source: SnapshotSource, output_path: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {\n        match source {\n            SnapshotSource::ArxivBulkJson => {\n                // arXiv metadata from output_path)\n            }\n            SnapshotSource::ArxivOaiPmh => {\n                Err("use ingest_oai_pmh_bulk() instead".to_string())\n            }\n            SnapshotSource::LocalGzip => {\n                Err("open local file directly".to_string())\n            }\n            SnapshotSource::Stdin => {\n                Err("read from stdin".to_string())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Download a file from URL (single HTTP GET, no rate limits for static files).\n    #[cfg(feature = "std")]\n    fn download_file(url: &str, path: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {\n        let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new("curl");\n        cmd.arg("-sL").arg("--max-time").arg("3600").arg("-o").arg(path).arg(url);\n        let status = cmd.status().map_err(|e| format!("curl failed: {}", e))?;\n        if !status.success() {\n            return Err(format!("curl exited with {:?}", status.code()));\n        }\n        let size = crate::vfs::metadata(path).map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0);\n        Ok(size)\n    }\n\n    /// Process a snapshot file: read → byte-scan → spectral index.\n    /// O(file size) for parse, O(1) per paper for spectral insert.\n    /// crate::vfs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("read error: {}", e))?;\n        let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();\n        let n = parser.ingest_raw(&data);\n        let elapsed = t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64();\n        self.bytes_processed = data.len() as u64;\n        self.papers_extracted = n as u64;\n        self.speed_mbps = if elapsed > 0.0 { (data.len() as f64 / 1_000_000.0) / elapsed } else { 0.0 };\n        Ok(n as u64)\n    }\n\n    /// Process OAI-PMH bulk: download all sets sequentially into ONE pass.\n    /// Each set downloaded as a single stream, {\n        let sets = ["cs", "math", "stat", "q-bio", "eess"];\n        let mut total = 0u64;\n        for set in &sets {\n            let token = String::new();\n            let mut _page = 0u64;\n            loop {\n                _page += 1;\n                let url = if token.is_empty() {\n                    format!("https://oaipmh.arxiv.org/oai?verb=ListRecords&metadataPrefix=arXiv&set={}", set)\n                } else {\n                    format!("https://oaipmh.arxiv.org/oai?verb=ListRecords&resumptionToken={}", token)\n                };\n\n                let data = Self::fetch_url(&url).map_err(|e| format!("fetch {}: {}", url, e))?;\n                let n = parser.ingest_raw(&data);\n                total += n as u64;\n                self.bytes_processed += data.len() as u64;\n\n                // Extract resumption token via byte scan (no XML parse).\n                let token_str = Self::extract_token(&data);\n                if token_str.is_empty() { break; }\n\n                if total >= 1_000_000 { break; }\n            }\n        }\n        self.papers_extracted = total;\n        Ok(total)\n    }\n\n    /// Fetch a URL and return raw bytes.\n    #[cfg(feature = "std")]\n    fn fetch_url(url: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {\n        let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new("curl");\n        cmd.arg("-sL").arg("--max-time").arg("30").arg(url);\n        let output = cmd.output().map_err(|e| format!("curl error: {}", e))?;\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            return Err(format!("curl status {:?}", output.status.code()));\n        }\n        Ok(output.stdout)\n    }\n\n    /// Extract resumption token from raw OAI-PMH response bytes (no XML DOM).\n#[cfg(test)]\n start >= data.len() { return String::new(); }\n        let content_start = start + tag.len();\n        let end = OaiPmhScanner::find_tag(data, content_start, close);\n        if end >= data.len() { Snapshot\\n  Source:  {:?}\\n  Processed: {} MB\\n  Papers:  {}\\n  Speed:   {:.1} MB/s",\n            self.source, self.bytes_processed / 1_000_000, self.papers_extracted, self.speed_mbps\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/academia.rs	academia · 336 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! `kernel::academia` — Академія Дмитра Євдокимова. v6: Crystal lattice.\n//!\n//! # Класична фізика в парсингу\n//! | Фізика           | Парсинг                          |\n//! |------------------|----------------------------------|\n//! | Кристалографія   | 8D гратка кварків                |\n//! | Атоми            | Кваркові підписи паперів         |\n//! | Рентгенівська    | Запит → дифракція → резонанс     |\n//! | дифракція        |                                  |\n//! | Гратка           | 65,536 комірок (2 байти адреси) |\n//! | Симетрія         | Квантування однакове для даних   |\n//! |                  | і запитів                        |\n//!\n//! # 8D Lattice\n//! Перші 2 байти кваркового підпису = адреса комірки (65,536).\n//! Решта 6 байтів = позиція всередині комірки.\n//! Пошук: запит → комірка → сусідні комірки → popcount → топ.\n//!\n//! # Квантування запитів\n//! Запит проходить ТОЙ САМИЙ конвеєр: hash → quarks → lattice.\n//! Жодної різниці між документом і запитом — симетрія.\n//!\n//! # Пам'ять (610M паперів)\n//! - Матриця 610M×8 u8 = 4.88 GB\n//! - Lattice: 65,536 комірок × Vec<u32> ≈ 2.44 GB\n//! - **TOTAL: ~7.3 GB**\n//! - Пошук: O(1) → 1 комірка + 26 сусідів = 27 комірок\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeSet;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nconst DIMS: usize = 8;\nconst LATTICE_SIZE: usize = 65536; // 2^16 (first 2 bytes as cell address)\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nconst CELL_NEIGHBORS: &[(i32, i32)] = &[(-1,-1),(-1,0),(-1,1),(0,-1),(0,0),(0,1),(1,-1),(1,0),(1,1)];\n\n/// 8D кварковий підпис.\npub type QuarkSig = [u8; DIMS];\n\n/// SHA3-256 → 8 кварків.\npub fn hash_to_row(title: &str) -> QuarkSig {\n    let clean: String = title.chars().map(|c| if c.is_ascii() && (c.is_ascii_graphic() || c == ' ') { c } else { ' ' }).collect();\n    let h = sha3_256(clean.as_bytes());\n    let mut r = [0u8; DIMS];\n    r.copy_from_slice(&h[..DIMS]);\n    r\n}\n\n/// Перші 2 байти = адреса комірки в гратці.\nfn lattice_cell(sig: &QuarkSig) -> usize {\n    (sig[0] as usize) | ((sig[1] as usize) << 8)\n}\n\n/// Спільні кварки (popcount в 8D).\nfn shared(a: &QuarkSig, b: &QuarkSig) -> u32 {\n    (0..DIMS).filter(|&i| a[i] == b[i]).count() as u32\n}\n\n/// P2P bloom.\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nfn bloom_byte(sig: &QuarkSig) -> usize {\n    (u64::from_le_bytes(*sig) as usize) % (1_000_000_000 / 64)\n}\n\n// ─── Academia: 8D Crystal Lattice ─────────────────────────────────────────\n\npub struct Academia {\n    /// Матриця N×8: всі кваркові підписи.\n    pub matrix: Vec<QuarkSig>,\n    /// Lattice: комірка → список індексів паперів.\n    pub lattice: Vec<Vec<u32>>,\n    count: usize,\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    bloom: Vec<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl Academia {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Academia {\n            matrix: Vec::with_capacity(1_000_000),\n            lattice: (0..LATTICE_SIZE).map(|_| Vec::new()).collect(),\n            count: 0,\n            bloom: vec![0; 1_000_000_000 / 64 + 1],\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Вставка: hash → quarks → matrix → lattice.\n    pub fn insert(&mut self, title: &str) -> QuarkSig {\n        let row = hash_to_row(title);\n        let cell = lattice_cell(&row);\n        self.matrix.push(row);\n        self.lattice[cell].push(self.count as u32);\n        self.count += 1;\n        row\n    }\n\n    /// Пошук: 8D lattice → 27 комірок → popcount → топ-K.\n    pub fn search(&self, query: &str, top_k: usize) -> Vec<(usize, u32)> {\n        let q = hash_to_row(query);\n        let q_cell = lattice_cell(&q);\n        let qx = q_cell & 0xFF;\n        let qy = (q_cell >> 8) & 0xFF;\n        let mut candidates: Vec<(usize, u32)> = Vec::new();\n\n        // 27 сусідніх комірок (3×3×3 = 27 в 2D гратці).\n        for dx in -1i32..=1 {\n            for dy in -1i32..=1 {\n                let nx = ((qx as i32 + dx) & 0xFF) as usize;\n                let ny = ((qy as i32 + dy) & 0xFF) as usize;\n                let cell = nx | (ny << 8);\n                for &idx in &self.lattice[cell] {\n                    candidates.push((idx as usize, shared(&q, &self.matrix[idx as usize])));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        candidates.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1));\n        candidates.truncate(top_k);\n        candidates\n    }\n\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { self.count }\n\n    /// Матричний снепшот: [N:u32] [row: [u8;8]]*\n    pub fn to_snapshot(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let n = self.count as u32;\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(4 + n as usize * DIMS);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&n.to_le_bytes());\n        for r in &self.matrix { buf.extend_from_slice(r); }\n        buf\n    }\n\n    pub fn from_snapshot(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, String> {\n        if data.len() < 4 { return Err("too short".into()); }\n        let n = u32::from_le_bytes([data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3]]) as usize;\n        if data.len() < 4 + n * DIMS { return Err("truncated".into()); }\n        let mut lib = Academia::new();\n        for i in 0..n {\n            let mut row = [0u8; DIMS];\n            row.copy_from_slice(&data[4 + i*DIMS .. 4 + (i+1)*DIMS]);\n            let cell = lattice_cell(&row);\n            lib.matrix.push(row);\n            lib.lattice[cell].push(i as u32);\n        }\n        lib.count = n;\n        Ok(lib)\n    }\n\n    pub fn missing(&self, remote: &[QuarkSig]) -> Vec<QuarkSig> {\n        let local: BTreeSet<QuarkSig> = self.matrix.iter().copied().collect();\n        remote.iter().copied().filter(|r| !local.contains(r)).collect()\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let cells_occ = self.lattice.iter().filter(|c| !c.is_empty()).count();\n        let mb = (4 + self.count * DIMS) as f64 / 1_000_000.0;\n        format!(\n            "Академія Дмитра Євдокимова (8D Crystal)\\n  Papers: {}\\n  Matrix: {}×{} u8 ({:.1} MB)\\n  Lattice: {} cells occupied / {}\\n  Search: 27 cells = O(1)\\n  Symmetry: docs = queries",\n            self.count, self.count, DIMS, mb, cells_occ, LATTICE_SIZE\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Рекурсивний матричний пошук: split → SIMD → merge → рекурсія.\n    pub fn recursive_search(&self, query: &str, top_k: usize) -> Vec<(usize, u32)> {\n        let q = hash_to_row(query);\n        if self.matrix.is_empty() { return vec![]; }\n        let mut results = self.recursive_scan(&q, 0, self.matrix.len(), top_k);\n        results.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1));\n        results.truncate(top_k);\n        results\n    }\n\n    fn recursive_scan(&self, q: &QuarkSig, lo: usize, hi: usize, top_k: usize) -> Vec<(usize, u32)> {\n        let n = hi - lo;\n        if n == 0 { return vec![]; }\n        if n == 1 { return vec![(lo, shared(q, &self.matrix[lo]))]; }\n        if n <= 256 { return self.simd_batch(q, lo, hi, top_k); }\n        let mid = lo + n / 2;\n        let mut left = self.recursive_scan(q, lo, mid, top_k);\n        let mut right = self.recursive_scan(q, mid, hi, top_k);\n        left.append(&mut right);\n        left.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1));\n        left.truncate(top_k);\n        left\n    }\n\n    fn simd_batch(&self, q: &QuarkSig, lo: usize, hi: usize, top_k: usize) -> Vec<(usize, u32)> {\n        let mut results: Vec<(usize, u32)> = self.matrix[lo..hi].iter().enumerate()\n            .map(|(i, row)| (lo + i, shared(q, row))).collect();\n        results.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1));\n        results.truncate(top_k);\n        results\n    }\n\n    /// FanOut-ready plan: діапазони рядків для паралельної обробки.\n    pub fn fanout_plan(&self, num_workers: usize) -> Vec<(usize, usize)> {\n        let n = self.matrix.len();\n        if num_workers == 0 { return vec![(0, n)]; }\n        let chunk = (n + num_workers - 1) / num_workers;\n        let mut ranges = Vec::new();\n        for w in 0..num_workers {\n            let lo = w * chunk;\n            let hi = ((w + 1) * chunk).min(n);\n            if lo < hi { ranges.push((lo, hi)); }\n        }\n        ranges\n    }\n\n    /// Merge results from multiple workers (FanOut merge).\n    pub fn merge_results(results: Vec<Vec<(usize, u32)>>, top_k: usize) -> Vec<(usize, u32)> {\n        let mut all: Vec<(usize, u32)> = results.into_iter().flatten().collect();\n        all.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1));\n        all.truncate(top_k);\n        all\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn insert_adds_row() {\n        let mut a = Academia::new();\n        a.insert("Test paper about physics");\n        assert_eq!(a.len(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn deterministic() {\n        assert_eq!(Academia::new().insert("Same"), Academia::new().insert("Same"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn lattice_cell_bounds() {\n        for i in 0..100 {\n            let r = hash_to_row(&format!("p{}", i));\n            let c = lattice_cell(&r);\n            assert!(c < 65536, "cell {} >= 65536", c);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn search_via_lattice() {\n        let mut a = Academia::new();\n        for i in 0..500 {\n            a.insert(&format!("Paper number {} about machine learning in NLP", i));\n        }\n        let r = a.search("deep learning", 10);\n        assert!(r.len() <= 10);\n        if !r.is_empty() { assert!(r[0].1 > 0); }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn snapshot_roundtrip() {\n        let mut a = Academia::new();\n        a.insert("A"); a.insert("B");\n        let snap = a.to_snapshot();\n        let b = Academia::from_snapshot(&snap).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(b.matrix.len(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn p2p_missing() {\n        let mut a = Academia::new();\n        a.insert("Local");\n        let r = vec![a.matrix[0], hash_to_row("Remote")];\n        assert_eq!(a.missing(&r).len(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn query_same_as_doc() {\n        let mut a = Academia::new();\n        let t = "Symmetry Test Paper Qubit";\n        a.insert(t);\n        let r = a.search(t, 5);\n        assert!(!r.is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(r[0].1, 8);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dashboard_contains_crystal() {\n        let a = Academia::new();\n        let d = a.dashboard();\n        assert!(d.contains("Crystal"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn recursive_search_single_match() {\n        let mut a = Academia::new();\n        a.insert("Test Paper");\n        let r = a.recursive_search("Test Paper", 5);\n        assert_eq!(r.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(r[0].1, 8);\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    fn recursive_search_matches_linear() {\n        let mut a = Academia::new();\n        for i in 0..500 { a.insert(&format!("Paper {} about ML", i)); }\n        let linear = a.search("machine learning", 5);\n        let recursive = a.recursive_search("machine learning", 5);\n        assert!(linear.len() >= 1 || recursive.len() >= 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fanout_plan_splits_evenly() {\n        let mut a = Academia::new();\n        for i in 0..5000 { a.insert(&format!("P{}", i)); }\n        let plan = a.fanout_plan(8);\n        assert_eq!(plan.len(), 8);\n        let total: usize = plan.iter().map(|(lo, hi)| hi - lo).sum();\n        assert_eq!(total, 5000);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn merge_results_keeps_top_k() {\n        let r1 = vec![(0, 5), (1, 3)];\n        let r2 = vec![(2, 4), (3, 2)];\n        let merged = Academia::merge_results(vec![r1, r2], 2);\n        assert_eq!(merged.len(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(merged[0].1, 5);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simd_batch_correct_count() {\n        let mut a = Academia::new();\n        for i in 0..100 { a.insert(&format!("Test {}", i)); pub physical_cores: usize,\n    /// SMT threads per core (0 = unknown).\n    pub smt_threads_per_core: usize,\n    /// Per-core cache sizes in bytes.\n    pub l1d_size: usize,\n    pub l1i_size: usize,\n    pub l2_size: usize,\n    pub l3_size: usize,\n    /// Cache line size (bytes).\n    pub cache_line_size: usize,\n    /// Base clock frequency (Hz).\n    pub base_freq_hz: u64,\n    /// NUMA node count.\n    pub numa_nodes: usize,\n    /// Whether TSC has known frequency (invariant TSC).\n    pub tsc_invariant: TriState,\n    pub tsc_known_freq: TriState,\n}\n\nimpl Default for CpuTopology {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        CpuTopology {\n            logical_processors: 0,\n            physical_cores: 0,\n            smt_threads_per_core: 0,\n            l1d_size: 0,\n            l1i_size: 0,\n            l2_size: 0,\n            l3_size: 0,\n            cache_line_size: 0,\n            base_freq_hz: 0,\n            numa_nodes: 1,\n            tsc_invariant: TriState::Unknown,\n            tsc_known_freq: TriState::Unknown,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl CpuTopology {\n    /// Summary of topology for dashboard.\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(256);\n        out.push_str("HW Profile\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  CPU:       {} logical / {} cores ({} SMT/core)\\n",\n            self.logical_processors, self.physical_cores, self.smt_threads_per_core));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Freq:      {} MHz\\n", self.base_freq_hz / 1_000_000));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  L1d:       {} KB\\n", self.l1d_size / 1024));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  L1i:       {} KB\\n", self.l1i_size / 1024));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  L2:        {} KB\\n", self.l2_size / 1024));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  L3:        {} KB\\n", self.l3_size / 1024));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Cacheline: {} B\\n", self.cache_line_size));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  TSC known: {}\\n", self.tsc_known_freq));\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a /sys cache size string ("32K", "512K", "32M") into bytes.\npub fn parse_cache_size(s: &str) -> usize {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    if s.ends_with('K') {\n        s.trim_end_matches('K').parse::<usize>().unwrap_or(0) * 1024\n    } else if s.ends_with('M') {\n        s.trim_end_matches('M').parse::<usize>().unwrap_or(0) * 1024 * 1024\n    } else {\n        s.parse().unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse /proc/cpuinfo text into a topology snapshot (pure — no I/O).\n///\n/// Fills logical/physical cores, SMT ratio, base frequency, and TSC flags.\n/// The /sys-derived fields (cache sizes, NUMA nodes) are left at default and\n/// filled by the kernel shim's `probe()`.\npub fn parse_cpuinfo(cpuinfo_raw: &str) -> CpuTopology {\n    let mut topo = CpuTopology::default();\n    let lines: Vec<&str> = cpuinfo_raw.lines().collect();\n\n    // Count logical processors.\n    topo.logical_processors = lines.iter().filter(|l| l.starts_with("processor")).count();\n\n    // Count unique physical cores (core id).\n    let mut core_ids = BTreeSet::new();\n    for l in &lines {\n        if let Some(val) = l.strip_prefix("core id\\t\\t: ") {\n            core_ids.insert(val.trim());\n        }\n    }\n    topo.physical_cores = core_ids.len();\n    // ARM64 (aarch64) /proc/cpuinfo has no `core id` field — each\n    // `processor` entry is one physical core (SMT is not exposed there).\n    // Fall back to 1:1 so the snapshot stays consistent instead of\n    // reporting 0 physical cores alongside N logical processors.\n    if topo.physical_cores == 0 && topo.logical_processors > 0 {\n        topo.physical_cores = topo.logical_processors;\n    }\n    if topo.physical_cores > 0 && topo.logical_processors > 0 {\n        topo.smt_threads_per_core = topo.logical_processors / topo.physical_cores;\n    }\n\n    // Base frequency.\n    if let Some(first) = lines.iter().find(|l| l.starts_with("cpu MHz")) {\n        if let Some(mhz_str) = first.split(':').nth(1) {\n            let mhz: f64 = mhz_str.trim().parse().unwrap_or(0.0);\n            topo.base_freq_hz = (mhz * 1_000_000.0) as u64;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // TSC flags.\n    if let Some(first) = lines.iter().find(|l| l.starts_with("flags")) {\n        let has_known = first.contains("tsc_known_freq");\n        let has_invariant = first.contains("tsc_invariant") || first.contains("constant_tsc");\n        topo.tsc_known_freq = TriState::from_bool(has_known);\n        topo.tsc_invariant = TriState::from_bool(has_invariant);\n    }\n\n    topo\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cache_size_parsing() {\n        assert_eq!(parse_cache_size("32K"), 32 * 1024);\n        assert_eq!(parse_cache_size("512K"), 512 * 1024);\n        assert_eq!(parse_cache_size("32M"), 32 * 1024 * 1024);\n        assert_eq!(parse_cache_size(""), 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dashboard_contains_cpu() {\n        let topo = CpuTopology::default();\n        let d = topo.dashboard();\n        assert!(d.contains("HW Profile"));\n        assert!(d.contains("CPU:"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn default_topo_sane() {\n        let topo = CpuTopology::default();\n        assert_eq!(topo.logical_processors, 0);\n        assert_eq!(topo.numa_nodes, 1);\n        assert_eq!(topo.tsc_invariant, TriState::Unknown);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn parse_cpuinfo_counts_processors() {\n        let raw = "processor\\t: 0\\ncore id\\t\\t: 0\\nprocessor\\t: 1\\ncore id\\t\\t: 0\\nprocessor\\t: 2\\ncore id\\t\\t: 1\\nprocessor\\t: 3\\ncore id\\t\\t: 1\\n";\n        let topo = parse_cpuinfo(raw);\n        assert_eq!(topo.logical_processors, 4);\n        assert_eq!(topo.physical_cores, 2);\n        assert_eq!(topo.smt_threads_per_core, 2);\n    }\n}\n	9685	-1	-1		69963c7634ce0b7c595baa4bbc12193375d297fcbf706f4ee9df808f95adbee120ce0211559c04f2c179f6aa80d5ff6804f323207d2a88ece4eb580de79fa87c98ad75998539b101179eb10337bdebead8f5556a215a3421d414859455c13715e5a6e475b4c180d9e4e20a8463597ee50970456e58d1d80105f1f8f0c895f7da
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/research_ascii.rs	research_ascii · 323 lines	//! `dowiz_core::research_ascii` — Compact ASCII library for research papers.\n//!\n//! Converts Papers to compact ASCII format for memory/disk efficiency.\n//! Every paper is stored as a single line using ASCII unit separator (0x1F)\n//! between fields. Non-ASCII characters are stripped.\n//!\n//! # ASCII Library Format\n//! Each line: `hash|id|title|year|cite|cat|abstract(truncated)`\n//! Field separator: 0x1F (ASCII Unit Separator)\n//! Within-field: 0x1F → 0x1E (Record Separator) escape\n//! Content-addressed: stored by SHA3-256 hash for dedup\n//!\n//! # Size\n//! ~200 bytes per paper in ASCII vs ~2000 bytes in JSON → 10x compression\n//! 100K papers ≈ 20MB in ASCII vs 200MB in JSON\n//! After dedup: ~15-18MB for 100K unique papers\n//!\n//! # no_std notes\n//! Pure `core::` + `alloc::` (no `std`). `AsciiLibrary::open`/`save` route\n//! through [`crate::vfs`], whose no_std build is a stub returning\n//! `Err(VfsError::NotFound)` — the on-disk round-trip test is therefore\n//! gated behind `feature = "std"`.\n\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::research::Paper;\nuse crate::TriState;\n\n/// ASCII Unit Separator (0x1F) — field delimiter.\nconst US: char = '\\x1F';\n/// ASCII Record Separator (0x1E) — escape within fields.\nconst RS: char = '\\x1E';\n/// Max abstract length in ASCII library (chars).\nconst MAX_ABSTRACT_LEN: usize = 400;\n\n// ─── ASCII Conversion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Strip non-ASCII characters and escape separator characters.\nfn to_ascii(s: &str) -> String {\n    s.chars()\n        .map(|c| {\n            if c == US { RS }          // Escape unit separator\n            else if c == RS { RS }     // Escape record separator too\n            else if c.is_ascii_graphic() || c == ' ' { c }\n            else if c == '\\n' || c == '\\t' { ' ' }\n            else { ' ' }               // Replace non-ASCII with space\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Convert a Paper to a compact ASCII line.\npub fn paper_to_ascii(paper: &Paper) -> String {\n    let hash_hex = hex::encode(&paper.paper_hash);\n    let id = to_ascii(&paper.id);\n    let title = to_ascii(&paper.title);\n    let year = paper.year.to_string();\n    let cite = paper.citation_count.to_string();\n    let cats = to_ascii(&paper.categories.join(","));\n    let abstract_short = to_ascii(&paper.abstract_text.chars().take(MAX_ABSTRACT_LEN).collect::<String>());\n\n    format!("{}{US}{}{US}{}{US}{}{US}{}{US}{}{US}{}",\n        hash_hex, id, title, year, cite, cats, abstract_short,\n        US = US)\n}\n\n/// Parse an ASCII library line back into a Paper.\npub fn ascii_to_paper(line: &str) -> Option<Paper> {\n    let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split(US).collect();\n    if parts.len() < 7 { return None; }\n\n    let hash_hex = parts[0].trim();\n    let id_str = parts[1].to_string();\n    let title = parts[2].to_string();\n    let year: u32 = parts[3].trim().parse().unwrap_or(0);\n    let cite: u32 = parts[4].trim().parse().unwrap_or(0);\n    let _cats = parts[5].to_string();\n\n    let mut hash = [0u8; 32];\n    if hash_hex.len() == 64 {\n        for i in 0..32 {\n            hash[i] = u8::from_str_radix(&hash_hex[2*i..2*i+2], 16).unwrap_or(0);\n        }\n    } else {\n        hash = sha3_256(title.as_bytes());\n    }\n\n    Some(Paper {\n        id: id_str.clone(),\n        title,\n        authors: vec![],\n        abstract_text: parts[6..].join(&US.to_string()),\n        categories: vec![],\n        year, citation_count: cite,\n        arxiv_id: Some(id_str),\n        doi: None,\n        paper_hash: hash,\n        full_text_accessible: TriState::True,\n        embedding: vec![],\n    })\n}\n\n// ─── ASCII Library ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Content-addressed ASCII library for research papers.\n/// Deduplicates by SHA3-256 hash: identical papers map to one storage slot.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AsciiLibrary {\n    /// Papers stored as ASCII lines.\n    pub entries: Vec<String>,\n    /// Hash → index map for dedup.\n    hash_index: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<[u8; 32], usize>,\n    /// Max entries (memory cap).\n    max_entries: usize,\n}\n\nimpl AsciiLibrary {\n    pub fn new(max_entries: usize) -> Self {\n        AsciiLibrary {\n            entries: Vec::with_capacity(max_entries.min(1000)),\n            hash_index: alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new(),\n            max_entries,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Add a paper to the library (deduplicated by SHA3-256 hash).\n    /// Returns true if the paper was new (inserted), false if duplicate.\n    pub fn add(&mut self, paper: &Paper) -> bool {\n        if self.hash_index.contains_key(&paper.paper_hash) {\n            return false; // Duplicate.\n        }\n        if self.entries.len() >= self.max_entries {\n            return false; // Library full.\n        }\n\n        let ascii_line = paper_to_ascii(paper);\n        let idx = self.entries.len();\n        self.entries.push(ascii_line);\n        self.hash_index.insert(paper.paper_hash, idx);\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// Add many papers at once.\n    pub fn add_batch(&mut self, papers: &[Paper]) -> usize {\n        let mut new_count = 0;\n        for p in papers {\n            if self.add(p) { new_count += 1; }\n        }\n        new_count\n    }\n\n    /// Open library: load from a file (one ASCII line per paper).\n    pub fn open(path: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {\n        let content = crate::vfs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| format!("read error: {}", e))?;\n        let lines: Vec<&str> = content.lines().filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()).collect();\n        let mut lib = AsciiLibrary::new(lines.len());\n        for line in lines {\n            if let Some(paper) = ascii_to_paper(line) {\n                lib.hash_index.insert(paper.paper_hash, lib.entries.len());\n                lib.entries.push(line.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(lib)\n    }\n\n    /// Save library to a file (one ASCII line per paper).\n    pub fn save(&self, path: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n        let content = self.entries.join("\\n");\n        crate::vfs::write(path, content.as_bytes()).map_err(|e| format!("write error: {}", e))\n    }\n\n    /// Number of unique papers.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { self.entries.len() }\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { self.entries.is_empty() }\n\n    /// Estimated memory usage (bytes).\n    pub fn estimated_bytes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.entries.iter().map(|l| l.len()).sum()\n    }\n\n    /// Compact ASCII library persistence string.\n    /// Each line: `hash_hex|id|title|year|cite|cats|abstract_short`\n    pub fn to_string(&self) -> String { self.entries.join("\\n") }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let mb = self.estimated_bytes() as f64 / 1_000_000.0;\n        format!(\n            "ASCII Library\\n  Papers: {}\\n  Size:   {:.2} MB\\n  Dedup:  {} unique\\n  Hash:   SHA3-256",\n            self.entries.len(), mb, self.hash_index.len()\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── hex module (simple hex encode/decode, zero-dep) ───────────────────────\n\nmod hex {\n    use alloc::string::String;\n\n    pub fn encode(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {\n        const HEX_CHARS: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";\n        let mut out = vec![0u8; bytes.len() * 2];\n        for (i, &b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {\n            out[2*i] = HEX_CHARS[(b >> 4) as usize];\n            out[2*i + 1] = HEX_CHARS[(b & 0x0f) as usize];\n        }\n        unsafe { String::from_utf8_unchecked(out) }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::research::Paper;\n\n    fn make_paper(id: &str, title: &str, year: u32) -> Paper {\n        let hash = sha3_256(title.as_bytes());\n        Paper {\n            id: id.to_string(),\n            title: title.to_string(),\n            authors: vec![],\n            abstract_text: format!("Abstract for {}", title),\n            categories: vec!["cs.LG".into()],\n            year, citation_count: 10,\n            arxiv_id: Some(id.to_string()),\n            doi: None,\n            paper_hash: hash,\n            full_text_accessible: TriState::True,\n            embedding: vec![],\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ascii_roundtrip() {\n        let p = make_paper("1706.03762", "Attention Is All You Need", 2017);\n        let ascii = paper_to_ascii(&p);\n        let p2 = ascii_to_paper(&ascii).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(p2.title, "Attention Is All You Need");\n        assert_eq!(p2.year, 2017);\n        assert_eq!(p2.paper_hash, p.paper_hash);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn non_ascii_stripped() {\n        let p = make_paper("test", "Tést with ünicode 🚀 and π", 2024);\n        let ascii = paper_to_ascii(&p);\n        assert!(!ascii.contains('π'));\n        assert!(!ascii.contains('🚀'));\n        assert!(ascii.contains("T st with  nicode   and  "));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn library_dedup() {\n        let mut lib = AsciiLibrary::new(100);\n ## 9735 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/signal.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: signal · 157 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/signal.rs	signal · 157 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! signal.rs — fine-grained reactive signals (the Dioxus/SolidJS reactivity\n//! concept, item #12), zero-dep.\n//!\n//! A signal is a mutable cell with change notification. `create_signal` splits\n//! read/write; the reactive *effect* runtime (`effect`/`track`/`CURRENT_EFFECT`)\n//! is std-only (thread-local) and lives in the kernel held-handle shim — this\n//! no_std core ships only the pure cell types.\n//!\n//! Zero-dep: `Rc` (alloc) + `RefCell` (core). Deterministic: subscribers run in\n//! subscription order; no threads, no interior randomness.\n\nuse core::cell::RefCell;\nuse alloc::rc::Rc;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A single reactive value with subscribers.\npub struct Signal<T> {\n    value: Rc<RefCell<T>>,\n    subs: Rc<RefCell<Vec<Rc<dyn Fn()>>>>,\n}\n\n/// Read handle (can only read, not mutate).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ReadSignal<T>(Rc<RefCell<T>>);\n\n/// Write handle (mutates and notifies subscribers).\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct WriteSignal<T> {\n    cell: Rc<RefCell<T>>,\n    subs: Rc<RefCell<Vec<Rc<dyn Fn()>>>>,\n}\n\nimpl<T> Signal<T> {\n    /// Create a signal with the given initial value.\n    pub fn new(init: T) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            value: Rc::new(RefCell::new(init)),\n            subs: Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new())),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Split a signal into (read, write) handles.\npub fn create_signal<T>(init: T) -> (ReadSignal<T>, WriteSignal<T>) {\n    let s = Signal::new(init);\n    (\n        ReadSignal(Rc::clone(&s.value)),\n        WriteSignal {\n            cell: Rc::clone(&s.value),\n            subs: Rc::clone(&s.subs),\n        },\n    )\n}\n\nimpl<T: Clone> ReadSignal<T> {\n    /// Snapshot the current value.\n    pub fn get(&self) -> T {\n        self.0.borrow().clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Read the value with a closure (avoids the clone).\n    pub fn with<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&T) -> R) -> R {\n        f(&self.0.borrow())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<T: PartialEq> WriteSignal<T> {\n    /// Set a new value. Notifies subscribers only when the value actually\n    /// changes (fine-grained: no spurious re-runs).\n    pub fn set(&self, v: T) {\n        let changed = {\n            let cur = self.cell.borrow();\n            *cur != v\n        };\n        if changed {\n            *self.cell.borrow_mut() = v;\n            // Run subscribers in a fixed order, snapshotting first so an\n            // effect that mutates another signal does not alias-borrow.\n            let subs: Vec<Rc<dyn Fn()>> = self.subs.borrow().iter().cloned().collect();\n            for sub in subs {\n                sub();\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A derived signal: recomputes `f` over its dependencies; `get` re-evaluates.\npub struct Computed<T> {\n    value: Rc<RefCell<T>>,\n    compute: Rc<dyn Fn() -> T>,\n    dirty: Rc<RefCell<bool>>,\n}\n\nimpl<T> Computed<T> {\n    /// Build a computed value from a closure reading other signals.\n    pub fn new(compute: impl Fn() -> T + 'static, init: T) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            value: Rc::new(RefCell::new(init)),\n            compute: Rc::new(compute),\n            dirty: Rc::new(RefCell::new(true)),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<T: Clone> Computed<T> {\n    /// Evaluate (recompute if dirty) and return the value.\n    pub fn get(&self) -> T {\n        if *self.dirty.borrow() {\n            let v = (self.compute)();\n            *self.value.borrow_mut() = v;\n            *self.dirty.borrow_mut() = false;\n        }\n        self.value.borrow().clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Mark stale (call after a dependency changed).\n    pub fn mark_dirty(&self) {\n        *self.dirty.borrow_mut() = true;\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn signal_get_set_roundtrip() {\n        let (r, w) = create_signal(1i32);\n        assert_eq!(r.get(), 1);\n        w.set(42);\n        assert_eq!(r.get(), 42);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn set_same_value_is_noop() {\n        let (_, w) = create_signal(7i32);\n        w.set(7); // must not panic or notify (value unchanged)\n        w.set(8);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn read_handle_cannot_write() {\n        let (r, _) = create_signal(5i32);\n        assert_eq!(r.get(), 5);\n        assert_eq!(r.with(|v| *v), 5);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn computed_recomputes() {\n        let (_, w) = create_signal(2i32);\n        let c = Computed::new(|| 10, 0);\n        assert_eq!(c.get(), 10);\n        c.mark_dirty();\n        assert_eq!(c.get(), 10);\n    }\n}\n	9736	-1	-1		1331f572aa8f45e4984121d95192bb87f35a95b43fd5f5eb191d022643f7e1e620c0f58026cc4616bc43168d66d12f3b45bedd2a74085cc91069f34c071d4b1c90b762dfad9b0021e41bbb0245bbe1d1c148556a619c2ae4dc04c4907c05a574f262b3b7b6ea59a1f6194ebe4ae00fccad90563ff8239d401f2976f269a4f751
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/proxy_redirect.rs	proxy_redirect · 442 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! proxy_redirect.rs — Proxy pool management, rotation strategies, and health tracking.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! Pure data structures for managing a pool of proxy endpoints used by the\n//! anti-detect browser for parse operations. Each parse call is routed through\n//! a different proxy (or chain) to prevent IP correlation. This module contains\n//! NO network I/O — it is the kernel's routing authority. The actual proxy\n//! connection lives in the external `AgentBrowserPort` implementation.\n//!\n//! # Design principles\n//! - Kernel = pure computation (no network sockets)\n//! - Proxy selection is deterministic given (pool_state, call_index)\n//! - Health tracking prevents routing through dead proxies\n//! - Rotation strategies are typed (no silent behavioral changes)\n//!\n//! Timestamps (`last_success_us` / `last_failure_us`) are injected as explicit\n//! `now_us_val: u64` parameters — the no_std core has no wall clock; the kernel\n//! held-handle shim provides `now_us()` and callers pass it in.\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::TriState;\n\n/// A single proxy endpoint.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ProxyEndpoint {\n    /// Hostname or IP.\n    pub host: String,\n    /// Port number.\n    pub port: u16,\n    /// Proxy protocol.\n    pub protocol: ProxyProtocol,\n    /// Authentication (if required).\n    pub auth: Option<ProxyAuth>,\n    /// Geographic region code (e.g. "US-East", "EU-West").\n    pub region: String,\n    /// When this proxy was last successfully used (unix microseconds).\n    pub last_success_us: u64,\n    /// When this proxy last failed (unix microseconds).\n    pub last_failure_us: u64,\n    /// Number of consecutive failures since last success.\n    pub consecutive_failures: u32,\n    /// Total requests made through this proxy.\n    pub total_requests: u64,\n    /// Total successful requests.\n    pub total_successes: u64,\n    /// Average response latency (microseconds).\n    pub avg_latency_us: u64,\n}\n\nimpl ProxyEndpoint {\n    /// Success rate of this proxy (0.0..1.0).\n    pub fn success_rate(&self) -> f64 {\n        if self.total_requests == 0 {\n            0.0\n        } else {\n            self.total_successes as f64 / self.total_requests as f64\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether this proxy is considered healthy.\n    pub fn is_healthy(&self) -> TriState {\n        TriState::from_bool(self.consecutive_failures < 3 && self.success_rate() > 0.5)\n    }\n\n    /// Record a successful request (`now_us_val` = injected monotonic timestamp).\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, latency_us: u64, now_us_val: u64) {\n        self.consecutive_failures = 0;\n        self.total_requests += 1;\n        self.total_successes += 1;\n        self.last_success_us = now_us_val;\n        // Exponential moving average for latency.\n        if self.avg_latency_us == 0 {\n            self.avg_latency_us = latency_us;\n        } else {\n            self.avg_latency_us = (self.avg_latency_us * 7 + latency_us) / 8;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failed request (`now_us_val` = injected monotonic timestamp).\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, now_us_val: u64) {\n        self.consecutive_failures += 1;\n        self.total_requests += 1;\n        self.last_failure_us = now_us_val;\n    }\n}\n\n/// Proxy protocol.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum ProxyProtocol {\n    Http,\n    Https,\n    Socks5,\n}\n\n/// Proxy authentication.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ProxyAuth {\n    pub username: String,\n    pub password: String,\n}\n\n/// Rotation strategy for proxy selection.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum RotationStrategy {\n    /// Round-robin through the pool (simple, predictable).\n    RoundRobin,\n    /// Weighted random — healthy proxies get higher weight.\n    WeightedRandom,\n    /// Geographic routing — select proxy matching target's region.\n    GeoRouting,\n    /// Least-latency — prefer the proxy with lowest avg latency.\n    LeastLatency,\n    /// Rotating chains — route through 2+ proxies in sequence (highest anonymity).\n    Chain(usize), // chain length\n}\n\n/// The proxy pool — manages all available endpoints.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ProxyPool {\n    /// All proxy endpoints.\n    endpoints: Vec<ProxyEndpoint>,\n    /// Current rotation index (for round-robin).\n    round_robin_index: usize,\n    /// The active rotation strategy.\n    strategy: RotationStrategy,\n    /// Maximum chain length (for Chain strategy).\n    max_chain_length: usize,\n}\n\nimpl ProxyPool {\n    /// Create an empty pool.\n    pub fn new(strategy: RotationStrategy) -> Self {\n        ProxyPool {\n            endpoints: Vec::new(),\n            round_robin_index: 0,\n            strategy,\n            max_chain_length: 4,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Add a proxy endpoint to the pool.\n    pub fn add(&mut self, endpoint: ProxyEndpoint) {\n        self.endpoints.push(endpoint);\n    }\n\n    /// Select the next proxy based on the current strategy.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if no healthy proxies are available (caller should degrade).\n    pub fn select(&mut self, call_index: u64) -> Option<&ProxyEndpoint> {\n        if self.endpoints.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        match self.strategy {\n            RotationStrategy::RoundRobin => self.select_round_robin(),\n            RotationStrategy::WeightedRandom => self.select_weighted_random(call_index),\n            RotationStrategy::GeoRouting => self.select_geo_routing(call_index),\n            RotationStrategy::LeastLatency => self.select_least_latency(),\n            RotationStrategy::Chain(len) => {\n                self.max_chain_length = len;\n                self.select_round_robin() // base selection; chain is assembled by caller\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Select next in round-robin order.\n    fn select_round_robin(&mut self) -> Option<&ProxyEndpoint> {\n        let len = self.endpoints.len();\n        if len == 0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        // Skip unhealthy proxies.\n        for _ in 0..len {\n            let idx = self.round_robin_index % len;\n            self.round_robin_index += 1;\n            if self.endpoints[idx].is_healthy().is_true() {\n                return Some(&self.endpoints[idx]);\n            }\n        }\n        None\n    }\n\n    /// Select by weighted random (healthier proxies = higher weight).\n    fn select_weighted_random(&self, call_index: u64) -> Option<&ProxyEndpoint> {\n        let healthy: Vec<(usize, f64)> = self\n            .endpoints\n            .iter()\n            .enumerate()\n            .filter(|(_, ep)| ep.is_healthy().is_true())\n            .map(|(i, ep)| {\n                let weight = ep.success_rate() * 100.0 + 1.0;\n                (i, weight)\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        if healthy.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        let total_weight: f64 = healthy.iter().map(|(_, w)| w).sum();\n        // Deterministic "random" from call_index (not OS RNG).\n        let pick = (call_index as f64 * 7919.0) % total_weight; // prime multiplier\n        let mut accum = 0.0;\n        for (idx, weight) in &healthy {\n            accum += weight;\n            if pick < accum {\n                return Some(&self.endpoints[*idx]);\n            }\n        }\n        // Fallback to last.\n        healthy.last().map(|(idx, _)| &self.endpoints[*idx])\n    }\n\n    /// Select by geographic routing (simple: pick the region from call_index).\n    fn select_geo_routing(&self, call_index: u64) -> Option<&ProxyEndpoint> {\n        // Use call_index to select a region, then pick the best proxy in that region.\n        let regions: Vec<&str> = self\n            .endpoints\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|ep| ep.is_healthy().is_true())\n            .map(|ep| ep.region.as_str())\n            .collect();\n        if regions.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let region_idx = (call_index as usize) % regions.len();\n        let target_region = regions[region_idx];\n\n        // Pick the best proxy in that region.\n        self.endpoints\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|ep| ep.is_healthy().is_true() && ep.region == target_region)\n            .max_by(|a, b| {\n                a.success_rate()\n                    .partial_cmp(&b.success_rate())\n                    .unwrap_or(core::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n            })\n    }\n\n    /// Select by least latency.\n    fn select_least_latency(&self) -> Option<&ProxyEndpoint> {\n        self.endpoints\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|ep| ep.is_healthy().is_true())\n            .min_by_key(|ep| ep.avg_latency_us)\n    }\n\n    /// Record a success for the proxy at the given index.\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, index: usize, latency_us: u64, now_us_val: u64) {\n        if let Some(ep) = self.endpoints.get_mut(index) {\n            ep.record_success(latency_us, now_us_val);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failure for the proxy at the given index.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, index: usize, now_us_val: u64) {\n        if let Some(ep) = self.endpoints.get_mut(index) {\n            ep.record_failure(now_us_val);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Number of healthy proxies.\n    pub fn healthy_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.endpoints.iter().filter(|ep| ep.is_healthy().is_true()).count()\n    }\n\n    /// Total proxies.\n    pub fn total_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.endpoints.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Current rotation strategy.\n    pub fn strategy(&self) -> RotationStrategy {\n        self.strategy\n    }\n\n    /// Get a proxy by index.\n    pub fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&ProxyEndpoint> {\n        self.endpoints.get(index)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute a deterministic proxy selection seed from call context.\npub fn proxy_selection_seed(url_hash: &[u8; 32], call_index: u64) -> u64 {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(40);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(url_hash);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&call_index.to_le_bytes());\n    let h = sha3_256(&buf);\n    u64::from_le_bytes(h[..8].try_into().unwrap())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn make_proxy(host: &str, healthy: bool) -> ProxyEndpoint {\n        ProxyEndpoint {\n            host: host.to_string(),\n            port: 8080,\n            protocol: ProxyProtocol::Socks5,\n            auth: None,\n            region: "US".to_string(),\n            last_success_us: 0,\n            last_failure_us: 0,\n            consecutive_failures: if healthy { 0 } else { 5 },\n            total_requests: 100,\n            total_successes: if healthy { 95 } else { 10 },\n            avg_latency_us: 100,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_pool_returns_none() {\n        let mut pool = ProxyPool::new(RotationStrategy::RoundRobin);\n        assert!(pool.select(0).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn round_robin_skips_unhealthy() {\n        let mut pool = ProxyPool::new(RotationStrategy::RoundRobin);\n        pool.add(make_proxy("dead.proxy", false));\n        pool.add(make_proxy("alive.proxy", true));\n\n        let selected = pool.select(0);\n        assert!(selected.is_some());\n        assert_eq!(selected.unwrap().host, "alive.proxy");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn round_robin_rotates() {\n        let mut pool = ProxyPool::new(RotationStrategy::RoundRobin);\n        pool.add(make_proxy("proxy-a", true));\n        pool.add(make_proxy("proxy-b", true));\n        pool.add(make_proxy("proxy-c", true));\n\n        let a = pool.select(0).unwrap().host.clone();\n        let b = pool.select(1).unwrap().host.clone();\n        let c = pool.select(2).unwrap().host.clone();\n        // After 3, we wrap around.\n        let a2 = pool.select(3).unwrap().host.clone();\n        assert_eq!(a, a2);\n        assert_ne!(a, b);\n        assert_ne!(b, c);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn weighted_random_selects_healthy() {\n        let mut pool = ProxyPool::new(RotationStrategy::WeightedRandom);\n        pool.add(make_proxy("dead", false));\n        pool.add(make_proxy("alive", true));\n\n        let selected = pool.select(0);\n        assert!(selected.is_some());\n        assert_eq!(selected.unwrap().host, "alive");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn least_latency_selects_fastest() {\n        let mut pool = ProxyPool::new(RotationStrategy::LeastLatency);\n        let mut fast = make_proxy("fast", true);\n        fast.avg_latency_us = 50;\n        let mut slow = make_proxy("slow", true);\n        slow.avg_latency_us = 500;\n        pool.add(slow);\n        pool.add(fast);\n\n        let selected = pool.select(0).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(selected.host, "fast");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn record_success_updates_metrics() {\n        let mut ep = make_proxy("test", true);\n        ep.total_requests = 10;\n        ep.total_successes = 5;\n        ep.avg_latency_us = 200;\n\n        ep.record_success(100, 123_456);\n        assert_eq!(ep.consecutive_failures, 0);\n        assert_eq!(ep.total_requests, 11);\n        assert_eq!(ep.total_successes, 6);\n        assert_eq!(ep.last_success_us, 123_456);\n        // EMA: (200*7 + 100) / 8 = 187.5\n        assert_eq!(ep.avg_latency_us, 187);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn record_failure_increments_consecutive()        assert_eq!(ep.consecutive_failures, 2);\n        assert_eq!(ep.last_failure_us, 2);\n        assert!(ep.is_healthy().is_true()); // still healthy at 2 failures\n        ep.record_failure(3);\n
```
