4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ct_gate.rs	ct_gate · 197 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! ct_gate.rs — minimal, zero-dependency dudect-style constant-time gate.\n//!\n//! The no_std core ships the reusable primitives: `ct_eq` (constant-time byte\n//! equality), `Stats` (Welford accumulator), and `welch_t` (Welch's two-sample t\n//! statistic). The timing harness (`time_block` / `measure_leakage`, which need\n//! `std::time::Instant`) lives in the kernel held-handle shim.\n//!\n//! `ct_eq` is the kernel's reusable CT-equality primitive — the first intended\n//! production caller is the P91.2 constant-time fix for the `pq/kem.rs` /\n//! `pq/hybrid.rs` tag compares.\n\n/// The standard dudect acceptance threshold: |t| below this is indistinguishable-from-constant-time\n/// at the sample sizes used here; at/above it, a secret-dependent timing channel is detectable.\npub const T_THRESHOLD: f64 = 4.5;\n\n/// Constant-time byte-slice equality. Branch-free over the byte content: every byte of the (equal-\n/// length) inputs is XOR-accumulated regardless of value, so the run-time does not depend on *where*\n/// the inputs first differ. Length is public (an attacker already knows tag/key sizes), so the\n/// length pre-check is an allowed public branch — the secret-dependent part is the byte loop, and it\n/// has no early exit. The final `acc == 0` is a single O(1) reduction, not a per-byte branch.\npub fn ct_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {\n    if a.len() != b.len() {\n        return false;\n    }\n    let mut acc: u8 = 0;\n    for i in 0..a.len() {\n        acc |= a[i] ^ b[i];\n    }\n    acc == 0\n}\n\n/// Online mean/variance accumulator (Welford, 1962) — zero-alloc, one pass, numerically stable.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]\npub struct Stats {\n    n: f64,\n    mean: f64,\n    m2: f64,\n}\n\nimpl Stats {\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn push(&mut self, x: f64) {\n        self.n += 1.0;\n        let d = x - self.mean;\n        self.mean += d / self.n;\n        let d2 = x - self.mean;\n        self.m2 += d * d2;\n    }\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn n(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.n\n    }\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn mean(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.mean\n    }\n    /// Sample variance (Bessel-corrected). Zero for n < 2.\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn var(&self) -> f64 {\n        if self.n < 2.0 {\n            0.0\n        } else {\n            self.m2 / (self.n - 1.0)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Welch's two-sample t statistic (unequal variances) between two timing classes.\n/// Returns 0 when both classes have zero variance (identical, degenerate samples).\npub fn welch_t(a: &Stats, b: &Stats) -> f64 {\n    if a.n() < 2.0 || b.n() < 2.0 {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    let denom = crate::math::sqrt(a.var() / a.n() + b.var() / b.n());\n    if denom == 0.0 {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    (a.mean() - b.mean()) / denom\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// PLANTED LEAK (test-only): the classic variable-time compare. Returns as soon as it finds a\n    /// differing byte, so its run-time leaks the position of the first difference — exactly the\n    /// timing channel a dudect gate must catch. The gate's whole credibility rests on rejecting\n    /// this one with the same machinery it uses to accept `ct_eq`.\n    fn naive_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        if a.len() != b.len() {\n            return false;\n        }\n        for i in 0..a.len() {\n            if a[i] != b[i] {\n                return false; // early return — the leak\n            }\n        }\n        true\n    }\n\n    // ── pure-logic unit tests (run in the default suite; no timing, no flakiness) ──────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ct_eq_matches_naive_eq_on_semantics() {\n        let cases: &[(&[u8], &[u8])] = &[\n            (b"", b""),\n            (b"abc", b"abc"),\n            (b"abc", b"abd"),\n            (b"abc", b"ab"),\n            (b"\\x00\\x00", b"\\x00\\x00"),\n            (b"\\xff\\x00\\xff", b"\\xff\\x00\\xfe"),\n        ];\n        for (a, b) in cases {\n            assert_eq!(\n                ct_eq(a, b),\n                naive_eq(a, b),\n                "ct_eq disagrees on {a:?} vs {b:?}"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn welch_t_is_zero_for_identical_classes() {\n        let mut s = Stats::default();\n        for x in [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0] {\n            s.push(x);\n        }\n        // same distribution twice → mean difference 0 → t = 0\n        assert_eq!(welch_t(&s, &s), 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn welch_t_is_large_for_separated_classes() {\n        let mut lo = Stats::default();\n        let mut hi = Stats::default();\n        for i in 0..100 {\n            // small nonzero variance in each class, huge mean gap between them\n            lo.push(1.0 + (i % 2) as f64 * 0.1);\n            hi.push(100.0 + (i % 2) as f64 * 0.1);\n        }\n        // tiny within-class variance, huge mean gap → |t| explodes\n        assert!(welch_t(&lo, &hi).abs() > 4.5);\n    }\n\n    // ── stats / welch-t edge cases ────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn stats_var_zero_for_single_sample() {\n        let mut s = Stats::default();\n        s.push(5.0);\n        assert!((s.var() - 0.0).abs() < 1e-10);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn stats_var_positive_for_multiple_samples() {\n        let mut s = Stats::default();\n        s.push(1.0);\n        s.push(3.0);\n        assert!(s.var() > 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn welch_t_zero_for_small_samples() {\n        let mut a = Stats::default();\n        a.push(1.0);\n        let mut b = Stats::default();\n        b.push(2.0);\n        assert_eq!(welch_t(&a, &b), 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn welch_t_zero_for_zero_variance() {\n        let mut a = Stats::default();\n        a.push(5.0);\n        a.push(5.0);\n        let mut b = Stats::default();\n        b.push(5.0);\n        b.push(5.0);\n        assert_eq!(welch_t(&a, &b), 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ct_eq_diff_len() {\n        assert!(!ct_eq(b"hello", b"hell"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ct_eq_same() {\n        assert!(ct_eq(b"abc", b"abc"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ct_eq_diff_same_len() {\n        assert!(!ct_eq(b"\\x00\\x01", b"\\x00\\x02"));\n    }\n}\n	9797	-1	-1		07f7beee2c8a27351b0bb080437a3b23e5dcb5ecad76f74aefd8e2da916d61451943b521dfcee826e753560b98d1fa68ce693174746a8ce9b6ea7207ef968c04face4c99af32b979109f910ab79be9494c78cc2e29db86e39002109670cb8536a570f70437cb1025f02a1d455af82d9568bf457c59939ed49435dcf029082371

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/envelope.rs	envelope · 142 lines	//! PQ-signed envelope — the L1 identity/integrity seam for the protocol.\n//!\n//! Transport-agnostic (MANIFESTO C4): an envelope is just\n//! `payload ‖ content_hash(SHAKE256) ‖ ML-DSA-65 sig`. Any layer above (DTN\n//! bundle, NOSTR event, MCP call) wraps its bytes in this. The transport\n//! carries opaque bytes; PQ holds at the protocol layer regardless of underlay\n//! (DECISIONS D3 red-line #3).\n//!\n//! RNG-free hot path (C10): the caller supplies `rnd` entropy for signing.\n//! ponytail: no seq/replay here — that is the transport's job (DTN lifetime +\n//! EID dedupe, RFC 9171). Envelope proves *integrity + authorship* only.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::pq::dsa::{keygen_bytes, sign_internal_bytes, verify_internal_bytes};\nuse crate::pq::keccak::shake256;\n\n/// SHAKE256 truncated to 256 bits (the envelope content hash).\npub fn hash32(input: &[u8]) -> [u8; HASH_LEN] {\n    let mut out = [0u8; HASH_LEN];\n    shake256(input, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// ML-DSA-65 signature byte length (FIPS 204 mode 3).\npub const SIG_LEN: usize = 3309;\n/// Public key length (FIPS 204 mode 3).\npub const PK_LEN: usize = 1952;\n/// Secret key length (FIPS 204 mode 3).\npub const SK_LEN: usize = 4032;\n/// Content hash length (SHAKE256, 256-bit).\npub const HASH_LEN: usize = 32;\n/// Entropy byte length for keygen / signing (caller-supplied, C10).\npub const ENTROPY_LEN: usize = 32;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum EnvelopeError {\n    /// Stored content hash ≠ hash(payload). Payload tampered or wrong envelope.\n    HashMismatch,\n    /// ML-DSA verification rejected (wrong key, tampered sig, or tampered payload).\n    BadSignature,\n}\n\n/// A PQ-signed, content-addressed envelope.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n#[cfg_attr(feature = "json-api", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]\npub struct SignedEnvelope {\n    pub payload: Vec<u8>,\n    pub content_hash: [u8; HASH_LEN],\n    pub sig: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// Seal `payload` with the signer's secret key. `rnd` is caller-supplied\n/// signing entropy (C10); never reuse it across seals.\npub fn seal(payload: &[u8], sk: &[u8], rnd: &[u8; ENTROPY_LEN]) -> SignedEnvelope {\n    let content_hash = hash32(payload);\n    let sig = sign_internal_bytes(sk, payload, rnd);\n    SignedEnvelope {\n        payload: payload.to_vec(),\n        content_hash,\n        sig,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Verify + unpack. Returns the payload only if (a) content_hash matches and\n/// (b) ML-DSA-65 verifies under `pk`. Either failure is rejected (RED gate).\npub fn open(env: &SignedEnvelope, pk: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EnvelopeError> {\n    let computed = hash32(&env.payload);\n    if computed != env.content_hash {\n        return Err(EnvelopeError::HashMismatch);\n    }\n    if verify_internal_bytes(pk, &env.payload, &env.sig) {\n        Ok(env.payload.clone())\n    } else {\n        Err(EnvelopeError::BadSignature)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Derive a self-certifying node id from the PQ public key (MANIFESTO §2):\n/// `id = H(pq_pub)`, no directory/phone-home.\npub fn node_id(pk: &[u8]) -> [u8; HASH_LEN] {\n    hash32(pk)\n}\n\n/// Generate a fresh PQ identity (pk, sk) from caller entropy.\npub fn new_identity(seed: &[u8; ENTROPY_LEN]) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {\n    keygen_bytes(seed)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn seed(n: u8) -> [u8; ENTROPY_LEN] {\n        [n; ENTROPY_LEN]\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_valid_roundtrip() {\n        let (pk, sk) = new_identity(&seed(1));\n        assert_eq!(pk.len(), PK_LEN);\n        assert_eq!(sk.len(), SK_LEN);\n        let payload = b"order:created o1 zone:kyiv-7";\n        let env = seal(payload, &sk, &seed(2));\n        assert_eq!(env.sig.len(), SIG_LEN);\n        let out = open(&env, &pk).expect("valid envelope opens");\n        assert_eq!(out, payload);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_tampered_payload_rejected() {\n        let (pk, sk) = new_identity(&seed(3));\n        let mut env = seal(b"pay 100", &sk, &seed(4));\n        env.payload[3] = b'9'; // "pay 900" — tamper\n        assert_eq!(open(&env, &pk), Err(EnvelopeError::HashMismatch));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_wrong_key_rejected() {\n        let (_pk, sk) = new_identity(&seed(5));\n        let (pk2, _sk2) = new_identity(&seed(6));\n        let env = seal(b"hello", &sk, &seed(7));\n        assert_eq!(open(&env, &pk2), Err(EnvelopeError::BadSignature));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_tampered_sig_rejected() {\n        let (pk, sk) = new_identity(&seed(8));\n        let mut env = seal(b"data", &sk, &seed(9));\n        if !env.sig.is_empty() {\n            env.sig[0] ^= 0xff;\n        }\n        assert_eq!(open(&env, &pk), Err(EnvelopeError::BadSignature));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn node_id_is_content_address() {\n        let (pk, _sk) = new_identity(&seed(10));\n        let id = node_id(&pk);\n        let (pk2, _sk2) = new_identity(&seed(11));\n        assert_ne!(id, node_id(&pk2), "distinct keys → distinct ids");\n    }\n}\n	9817	-1	-1		d2167f5d340df1651b2474553e034a0dccdaa886395df48b48c74c2681abe3c1597b15a3a5de7685844248eb09f1af288af92fb13b4c36b1927e33056f8e788f0f195611687ad003c59c7131861bf121705fa81a05da636f5ca43080208b933db7e25397336a02a1b9e39ad72bafa1386db064465aab8a12c32371b3b1a86458

Result is in the NTT domain.\nfn poly_uniform(rho: &[u8; SEEDBYTES], nonce: u16) -> Poly {\n    // Reference squeezes 5 SHAKE128 blocks then 1 at a time; SHAKE squeeze of L bytes is a\n    // prefix of the same stream and block boundaries (168) are 3-aligned, so a single generous\n    // contiguous squeeze consumed 3 bytes at a time is byte-identical to the reference.\n    let mut seed = [0u8; SEEDBYTES + 2];\n    seed[..SEEDBYTES].copy_from_slice(rho);\n    seed[SEEDBYTES] = (nonce & 0xff) as u8;\n    seed[SEEDBYTES + 1] = (nonce >> 8) as u8;\n    let mut buf = [0u8; SHAKE128_RATE * 12]; // 2016 bytes: rejection completes w.p. 1 - 2^-far\n    shake128(&seed, &mut buf);\n    let mut a = [0i32; N];\n    let ctr = rej_uniform(&mut a, &buf);\n    assert!(\n        ctr == N,\n        "poly_uniform: rejection sampling underflow (buffer too small)"\n    );\n    a\n}\n\n/// Rejection sampling of eta-bounded coefficients (η=4: nibble<9 → 4-nibble).\nfn rej_eta(a: &mut [i32], buf: &[u8]) -> usize {\n    let len = a.len();\n    let mut ctr = 0usize;\n    let mut pos = 0usize;\n    while ctr < len && pos < buf.len() {\n        let t0 = (buf[pos] & 0x0F) as i32;\n        let t1 = (buf[pos] >> 4) as i32;\n        pos += 1;\n        if t0 < 9 {\n            a[ctr] = 4 - t0;\n            ctr += 1;\n        }\n        if t1 < 9 && ctr < len {\n            a[ctr] = 4 - t1;\n            ctr += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    ctr\n}\n\n/// ExpandS entry (RejBoundedPoly): poly_uniform_eta(rhoprime, nonce). SHAKE256_RATE * 2]; // plenty for TAU=49 rejections\n    shake256(&c_tilde[..CTILDEBYTES], &mut buf);\n    let mut signs: u64 = 0;\n    for i in 0..8 {\n        signs |= (buf[i] as u64) << (8 * i);\n    }\n    let mut pos = 8usize;\n    let mut c = [0i32; SEEDBYTES]) -> [PolyVecL; K] {\n    let mut mat = [[poly_zero(); L]; K];\n    for i in 0..K {\n        for j in 0..L {\n            mat[i][j] = poly_uniform(rho, ((i as u16) << 8) + j as u16);\n        }\n    }\n    mat\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bit-packing (poly.c / packing.c) — FIPS 204 §7\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nfn polyt1_pack(a: &Poly, out: &mut [u8]) {\n    for i in 0..N / 4 {\n        out[5 * i] = (a[4 * i] >> 0) as u8;\n        out[5 * i + 1] = ((a[4 * i] >> 8) | (a[4 * i + 1] << 2)) as u8;\n        out[5 * i + 2] = ((a[4 * i + 1] >> 6) | (a[4 * i + 2] << 4)) as u8;\n        out[5 * i + 3] = ((a[4 * i + 2] >> 4) | (a[4 * i + 3] << 6)) as u8;\n        out[5 * i + 4] = (a[4 * i + 3] >> 2) as u8;\n    }\n}\n\nfn polyt1_unpack(a: &[u8]) -> Poly {\n    let mut r = [0i32; SEEDBYTES],\n    tr: &[u8; TRBYTES],\n    key: &[u8; SEEDBYTES],\n    t0: &PolyVecK,\n    s1: &PolyVecL,\n    s2: &PolyVecK,\n) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut sk = vec![0u8; SECRETKEYBYTES];\n    let mut off = 0;\n    sk[off..off + SEEDBYTES].copy_from_slice(rho);\n    off += SEEDBYTES;\n    sk[off..off + SEEDBYTES].copy_from_slice(key);\n    off += SEEDBYTES;\n    sk[off..off + TRBYTES].copy_from_slice(tr);\n    off += TRBYTES;\n    for i in 0..L {\n        polyeta_pack(&s1[i], &mut sk[off + i * POLYETA_PACKEDBYTES..]);\n    }\n    off += L * POLYETA_PACKEDBYTES;\n    for i in 0..K {\n        polyeta_pack(&s2[i], &mut sk[off + i * POLYETA_PACKEDBYTES..]);\n    }\n    off += K * POLYETA_PACKEDBYTES;\n    for i in 0..K {\n        polyt0_pack(&t0[i], &mut sk[off + i * POLYT0_PACKEDBYTES..]);\n    }\n    sk\n}\n\nfn unpack_sk_bytes(\n    sk: &[u8],\n) -> (\n    [u8; Returns None on malformed hint (strong-unforgeability checks).\npub fn unpack_sig_bytes(sig: &[u8]) -> Option<([u8; CTILDEBYTES], PolyVecL, PolyVecK)> {\n    if sig.len() != SIGNATUREBYTES {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let mut c = [0u8; CTILDEBYTES];\n    c.copy_from_slice(&sig[..CTILDEBYTES]);\n    let zoff = CTILDEBYTES;\n    let mut z = [poly_zero(); L];\n    for i in 0..L {\n        z[i] = polyz_unpack(&sig[zoff + i * POLYZ_PACKEDBYTES..]);\n    }\n    let hoff = CTILDEBYTES + L * POLYZ_PACKEDBYTES;\n    let mut h = [poly_zero(); K];\n    let mut k = 0usize;\n    for i in 0..K {\n        let cnt = sig[hoff + OMEGA + i] as usize;\n        if cnt < k || cnt > OMEGA {\n            return None;\n        }\n        for j in k..cnt {\n            if j > k && sig[hoff + j] <= sig[hoff + j - 1] {\n                return None;\n            }\n            h[i][sig[hoff + j] as usize] = 1;\n        }\n        k = cnt;\n    }\n    for j in k..OMEGA {\n        if sig[hoff + j] != 0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n    }\n    Some((c, z, h))\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Matrix / vector NTT helpers\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nfn matrix_pointwise(mat: &[PolyVecL; K], v: &PolyVecL) -> PolyVecK {\n    let mut t = [poly_zero(); K];\n    for i in 0..K {\n        t[i] = poly_pointwise_montgomery(&mat[i][0], &v[0]);\n        for j in 1..L {\n            let p = poly_pointwise_montgomery(&mat[i][j], &v[j]);\n            t[i] = poly_add(&t[i], &p);\n        }\n    }\n    t\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Public byte-oriented API (ACVP internal interface)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n/// ML-DSA.KeyGen_internal (FIPS 204 Alg 6). Returns (pk_bytes, sk_bytes).\npub fn keygen_bytes(seed: &[u8; SEEDBYTES]) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {\n    // (rho, rhoprime, K) <- H(seed || IntegerToBytes(k,1) || IntegerToBytes(l,1), 128)\n    let mut hin = [0u8; SEEDBYTES + 2];\n    hin[..SEEDBYTES].copy_from_slice(seed);\n    hin[SEEDBYTES] = K as u8;\n    hin[SEEDBYTES + 1] = L as u8;\n    let mut ext = [0u8; 2 * SEEDBYTES + CRHBYTES];\n    shake256(&hin, &mut ext);\n    let mut rho = [0u8; SEEDBYTES];\n    rho.copy_from_slice(&ext[..SEEDBYTES]);\n    let mut rhoprime = [0u8; CRHBYTES];\n    rhoprime.copy_from_slice(&ext[SEEDBYTES..SEEDBYTES + CRHBYTES]);\n    let mut key = [0u8; SEEDBYTES];\n    key.copy_from_slice(&ext[SEEDBYTES + CRHBYTES..]);\n\n    let mat = poly_matrix_expand(&rho);\n    let mut s1 = [poly_zero(); L];\n    for i in 0..L {\n        s1[i] = poly_uniform_eta(&rhoprime, i as u16);\n    }\n    let mut s2 = [poly_zero(); K];\n    for i in 0..K {\n        s2[i] = poly_uniform_eta(&rhoprime, (L + i) as u16);\n    }\n\n    let mut s1hat = s1;\n    for i in 0..L {\n        ntt(&mut s1hat[i]);\n    }\n    let mut t = matrix_pointwise(&mat, &s1hat);\n    for i in 0..K {\n        poly_reduce(&mut t[i]);\n        invntt_tomont(&mut t[i]);\n        t[i] = poly_add(&t[i], &s2[i]);\n        poly_caddq(&mut t[i]);\n    }\n    let mut t1 = [poly_zero(); K];\n    let mut t0 = [poly_zero(); K];\n    for i in 0..K {\n        for j in 0..N {\n            let (a1, a0) = power2round(t[i][j]);\n            t1[i][j] = a1;\n            t0[i][j] = a0;\n        }\n    }\n    let pk = pack_pk_bytes(&rho, &t1);\n    let mut tr = [0u8; TRBYTES];\n    shake256(&pk, &mut tr);\n    let sk = pack_sk_bytes(&rho, &tr, &key, &t0, &s1, &s2);\n    (pk, sk)\n}\n\n/// ML-DSA.Sign_internal (FIPS 204 Alg 7), deterministic-capable via rnd. pre is empty (internal).\npub fn sign_internal_bytes(sk: &[u8], msg: &[u8], rnd: &[u8; RNDBYTES]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let (rho, tr, key, t0, s1, s2) = unpack_sk_bytes(sk);\n\n    // mu = CRH(tr || pre || msg); pre empty for internal interface.\n    let mut mu = [0u8; CRHBYTES];\n    {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(TRBYTES + msg.len());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&tr);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(msg);\n        shake256(&buf, &mut mu);\n    }\n    // rhoprime = CRH(key || rnd || mu)\n    let mut rhoprime = [0u8; CRHBYTES];\n    {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(SEEDBYTES + RNDBYTES + CRHBYTES);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&key);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(rnd);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&mu);\n        shake256(&buf, &mut rhoprime);\n    }\n\n    let mat = poly_matrix_expand(&rho);\n    let mut s1n = s1;\n    for i in 0..L {\n        ntt(&mut s1n[i]);\n    }\n    let mut s2n = s2;\n    for i in 0..K {\n        ntt(&mut s2n[i]);\n    }\n    let mut t0n = t0;\n    for i in 0..K {\n        ntt(&mut t0n[i]);\n    }\n\n    let mut nonce: u16 = 0;\n    loop {\n        // y <- ExpandMask(rhoprime, nonce)\n        let mut y = [poly_zero(); L];\n        for i in 0..L {\n            y[i] = poly_uniform_gamma1(&rhoprime, L as u16 * nonce + i as u16);\n        }\n        nonce += 1;\n\n        // w = NTT^{-1}(A · NTT(y))\n        let mut z = y;\n        for i in 0..L {\n            ntt(&mut z[i]);\n        }\n        let mut w = matrix_pointwise(&mat, &z);\n        for i in 0..K {\n            poly_reduce(&mut w[i]);\n            invntt_tomont(&mut w[i]);\n            poly_caddq(&mut w[i]);\n        }\n        // (w1, w0) = Decompose(w)\n        let mut w1 = [poly_zero(); K];\n        let mut w0 = [poly_zero(); K];\n        for i in 0..K {\n            for j in 0..N {\n                let (a1, a0) = decompose(w[i][j]);\n                w1[i][j] = a1;\n                w0[i][j] = a0;\n            }\n        }\n        let w1pack = pack_w1(&w1);\n\n        // c̃ = H(mu || w1Encode(w1)), 48 bytes\n        let mut c_tilde = [0u8; CTILDEBYTES];\n        {\n            let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(CRHBYTES + w1pack.len());\n            buf.extend_from_slice(&mu);\n            buf.extend_from_slice(&w1pack);\n            shake256(&buf, &mut c_tilde);\n        }\n        let mut cp = poly_challenge(&c_tilde);\n        ntt(&mut cp);\n\n        // z = y + c·s1\n        let mut zsig = [poly_zero(); L];\n        for i in 0..L {\n            let mut cs1 = poly_pointwise_montgomery(&cp, &s1n[i]);\n            invntt_tomont(&mut cs1);\n            zsig[i] = poly_add(&cs1, &y[i]);\n            poly_reduce(&mut zsig[i]);\n        }\n        let mut reject = false;\n        for i in 0..L {\n            if poly_chknorm(&zsig[i], GAMMA1 - BETA) {\n                reject = true;\n            }\n        }\n        if reject {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // w0 = w0 - c·s2; reject on norm\n        for i in 0..K {\n            let mut cs2 = poly_pointwise_montgomery(&cp, &s2n[i]);\n            invntt_tomont(&mut cs2);\n            w0[i] = poly_sub(&w0[i], &cs2);\n            poly_reduce(&mut w0[i]);\n        }\n        for i in 0..K {\n            if poly_chknorm(&w0[i], GAMMA2 - BETA) {\n                reject = true;\n            }\n        }\n        if reject {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // ct0 = c·t0; reject on norm; w0 += ct0; h = MakeHint(w0, w1)\n        let mut ct0 = [poly_zero(); K];\n        for i in 0..K {\n            ct0[i] = poly_pointwise_montgomery(&cp, &t0n[i]);\n            invntt_tomont(&mut ct0[i]);\n            poly_reduce(&mut ct0[i]);\n        }\n        for i in 0..K {\n            if poly_chknorm(&ct0[i], GAMMA2) {\n                reject = true;\n            }\n        }\n        if reject {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let mut h = [poly_zero(); K];\n        let mut hint_count = 0i32;\n        for i in 0..K {\n            w0[i] = poly_add(&w0[i], &ct0[i]);\n            for j in 0..N {\n                h[i][j] = make_hint(w0[i][j], w1[i][j]);\n                hint_count += h[i][j];\n            }\n        }\n        if hint_count as usize > OMEGA {\n            continue;\n        }\n        return pack_sig_bytes(&c_tilde, &zsig, &h);\n    }\n}\n\n/// ML-DSA.Verify_internal (FIPS 204 Alg 8). pre empty (internal interface).\npub fn verify_internal_bytes(pk: &[u8], msg: &[u8], sig: &[u8]) -> bool {\n    if pk.len() != PUBLICKEYBYTES {\n        return false;\n    }\n    let (rho, t1) = unpack_pk_bytes(pk);\n    let (c_tilde, z, h) = match unpack_sig_bytes(sig) {\n        Some(v) => v,\n        None => return false,\n    };\n    for i in 0..L {\n        if poly_chknorm(&z[i], GAMMA1 - BETA) {\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    // mu = CRH(H(pk) || pre || msg)\n    let mut tr = [0u8; TRBYTES];\n    shake256(pk, &mut tr);\n    let mut mu = [0u8; CRHBYTES];\n    {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(TRBYTES + msg.len());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&tr);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(msg);\n        shake256(&buf, &mut mu);\n    }\n\n    let mut cp = poly_challenge(&c_tilde);\n    let mat = poly_matrix_expand(&rho);\n\n    // w = A·NTT(z) - c·(t1·2^d)\n    let mut zn = z;\n    for i in 0..L {\n        ntt(&mut zn[i]);\n    }\n    let mut w = matrix_pointwise(&mat, &zn);\n    ntt(&mut cp);\n    let mut t1n = t1;\n    for i in 0..K {\n        poly_shiftl(&mut t1n[i]);\n        ntt(&mut t1n[i]);\n        t1n[i] = poly_pointwise_montgomery(&cp, &t1n[i]);\n    }\n    for i in 0..K {\n        w[i] = poly_sub(&w[i], &t1n[i]);\n        poly_reduce(&mut w[i]);\n        invntt_tomont(&mut w[i]);\n        poly_caddq(&mut w[i]);\n    }\n    // w1 = UseHint(h, w)\n    let mut w1 = [poly_zero(); K];\n    for i in 0..K {\n        for j in 0..N {\n            w1[i][j] = use_hint(w[i][j], h[i][j]);\n        }\n    }\n    let w1pack = pack_w1(&w1);\n    let mut c2 = [0u8; CTILDEBYTES];\n    {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(CRHBYTES + w1pack.len());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&mu);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&w1pack);\n        shake256(&buf, &mut c2);\n    }\n    c2 == c_tilde\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Struct-oriented convenience API (byte-backed; unchanged external shape)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\npub struct MlDsa65Pk {\n    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,\n}\npub struct MlDsa65Sk {\n    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,\n}\npub struct MlDsa65Sig {\n    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// KeyGen (FIPS 204). seed = 32 bytes.\npub fn keygen(seed: &[u8; SEEDBYTES]) -> (MlDsa65Pk, MlDsa65Sk) {\n    let (pk, sk) = keygen_bytes(seed);\n    (MlDsa65Pk { bytes: pk }, MlDsa65Sk { bytes: sk })\n}\n\n/// Sign (internal interface, deterministic-capable via rnd; rnd=0 → FIPS deterministic mode).\npub fn sign(sk: &MlDsa65Sk, msg: &[u8], rnd: &[u8; RNDBYTES]) -> MlDsa65Sig {\n    MlDsa65Sig {\n        bytes: sign_internal_bytes(&sk.bytes, msg, rnd),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Verify (internal interface).\npub fn verify(pk: &MlDsa65Pk, msg: &[u8], sig: &MlDsa65Sig) -> bool {\n    verify_internal_bytes(&pk.bytes, msg, &sig.bytes)\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NIST ACVP FIPS204 ML-DSA-65 byte-exact property-gate (GREEN)\n// Parses the vendored official NIST ACVP vectors and asserts byte-exact agreement\n// for keyGen / sigGen-internal-deterministic / sigVer. Test-only; see acvp_tests.rs.\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod dsa_acvp_tests;\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kat_shake256_empty() {\n        let mut out = [0u8; 64];\n        shake256(b"", &mut out);\n        let expected = [\n            0x46, 0xb9, 0xdd, 0x2b, 0x0b, 0xa8, 0x8d, 0x13, 0x23, 0x3b, 0x3f, 0xeb, 0x74, 0x3e,\n            0xeb, 0x24, 0x3f, 0xcd, 0x52, 0xea, 0x62, 0xb8, 0x1b, 0x82, 0xb5, 0x0c, 0x27, 0x64,\n            0x6e, 0xd5, 0x76, 0x2f,\n        ];\n        assert_eq!(&out[..32], &expected[..], "SHAKE256 empty KAT mismatch");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sizes_are_fips204_cat3() {\n        assert_eq!(PUBLICKEYBYTES, 1952);\n        assert_eq!(SECRETKEYBYTES, 4032);\n        assert_eq!(SIGNATUREBYTES, 3309);\n        assert_eq!(CTILDEBYTES, 48);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sign_verify_roundtrip_and_tamper() {\n        let seed = [7u8; 32];\n        let (pk, sk) = keygen(&seed);\n        let msg = b"bebop2 ml-dsa-65 fable gate";\n        let rnd = [0u8; 32];\n        let sig = sign(&sk, msg, &rnd);\n        assert_eq!(sig.bytes.len(), SIGNATUREBYTES);\n        assert!(verify(&pk, msg, &sig), "verify failed on valid signature");\n        let mut bad = msg.to_vec();\n        bad[0] ^= 0xff;\n        assert!(\n            !verify(&pk, &bad, &sig),\n            "tampered message verified (RED missing)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn deterministic_signing() {\n        let seed = [3u8; 32];\n        let (_pk, sk) = keygen(&seed);\n        let rnd = [0u8; 32];\n        let a = sign_internal_bytes(&sk.bytes, b"probe", &rnd);\n        let b = sign_internal_bytes(&sk.bytes, b"probe", &rnd);\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "deterministic (rnd=0) signing must be reproducible");\n        let c = sign_internal_bytes(&sk.bytes, b"probf", &rnd);\n        assert_ne!(a, c, "message change must change signature");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn forge_with_zero_hint_is_rejected() {\n        let seed = [9u8; 32];\n        let (pk, _sk) = keygen(&seed);\n        let mut z = [[0i32; N]; L];\n        for p in &mut z {\n            for v in p.iter_mut() {\n                *v = 1234;\n            }\n        }\n        let h = [[0i32; N]; K];\n        let sig = pack_sig_bytes(&[42u8; CTILDEBYTES], &z, &h);\n        assert!(!verify_internal_bytes(&pk.bytes, b"forge attempt", &sig));\n    }\n\n    // ── G10 DIFFERENTIAL PROBE (vs pq-crystals ML-DSA-65 reference, ACVP-green) ──\n    // Emits FIPS 204 intermediates as "STAGE <name> <values>" for byte-level diffing.\n    // Run: cargo test -p bebop2-core --release mldsa_diff_probe -- --nocapture\n    fn phex(name: &str, b: &[u8]) {\n        let mut s = alloc::string::String::new();\n        for x in b {\n            s.push_str(&format!("{:02x}", x));\n        }\n        println!("STAGE {} {}", name, s);\n    }\n    fn pnorm(name: &str, p: &Poly) {\n        let mut s = alloc::string::String::new();\n        for i in 0..N {\n            let v = ((p[i] as i64 % Q as i64) + Q as i64) % Q as i64;\n            s.push_str(&format!(" {}", v));\n        }\n        println!("STAGE {}{}", name, s);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn mldsa_diff_probe() {\n        let seed = [1u8; 32];\n        phex("keygen.seed", &seed);\n        let mut hin = [0u8; SEEDBYTES + 2];\n        hin[..SEEDBYTES].copy_from_slice(&seed);\n        hin[SEEDBYTES] = K as u8;\n        hin[SEEDBYTES + 1] = L as u8;\n        let mut ext = [0u8; 128];\n        shake256(&hin, &mut ext);\n        phex("keygen.rho", &ext[0..32]);\n        phex("keygen.rhoprime", &ext[32..96]);\n        phex("keygen.K", &ext[96..128]);\n        let mut rho = [0u8; 32];\n        rho.copy_from_slice(&ext[0..32]);\n        let mut rhoprime = [0u8; 64];\n        rhoprime.copy_from_slice(&ext[32..96]);\n        let mat = poly_matrix_expand(&rho);\n        pnorm("keygen.matA[0][0]", &mat[0][0]);\n        let s1 = poly_uniform_eta(&rhoprime, 0);\n        pnorm("keygen.s1[0]", &s1);\n        let (pk, sk) = keygen(&seed);\n        phex("keygen.pk", &pk.bytes[..48]);\n        println!("STAGE keygen.pk.len {}", pk.bytes.len());\n        println!("STAGE keygen.sk.len {}", sk.bytes.len());\n        // t1[0] from packed pk\n        let (_r, t1) = unpack_pk_bytes(&pk.bytes);\n        pnorm("keygen.t1[0]", &t1[0]);\n        let mut tr = [0u8; 64];\n        shake256(&pk.bytes, &mut tr);\n        phex("keygen.tr", &tr);\n        let msg = b"probe";\n        let rnd = [0u8; 32];\n        let mut mu = [0u8; 64];\n        {\n            let mut buf = Vec::new();\n            buf.extend_from_slice(&tr);\n            buf.extend_from_slice(msg);\n            shake256(&buf, &mut mu);\n        }\n        phex("sign.mu", &mu);\n        let sig = sign_internal_bytes(&sk.bytes, msg, &rnd);\n        phex("sign.ctilde", &sig[..48]);\n        println!("STAGE sign.sig.len {}", sig.len());\n    }\n\n    // ── Item 7 (space-grade roadmap §C): native EXHAUSTIVE arithmetic contracts ──\n    // Per RESEARCH-NATIVE-KANI-REPLACEMENT-FEASIBILITY-2026-07-19.md §2: `caddq`,\n    // `power2round`, `decompose` take a SINGLE bounded i32; their whole contract domain\n    // is enumerable in seconds — the codebase's exhaustive idiom proves the IDENTICAL\n    // "for all inputs" guarantee as a Kani harness, with zero toolchain dependency.\n    // (`reduce32` full-i32 (2^32) is impractical in a debug test → it is a cheap exact\n    //  Kani proof instead; `montgomery_reduce`/`ntt`/`invntt` are the genuine Bucket-C\n    //  Kani targets. See kani_proofs below.)\n\n    /// EXHAUSTIVE over the contract domain −Q < a < Q (~16.76M values): `caddq` yields a\n    /// value in [0, Q) that is ≡ a (mod Q), with no overflow.\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_exhaustive_caddq_contract() {\n        let mut a = -(Q - 1);\n        while a <= Q - 1 {\n            let r = caddq(a);\n            assert!(r >= 0 && r < Q, "caddq({a}) = {r} not in [0,Q)");\n            // ≡ a (mod Q): r and a differ by a multiple of Q (0 or +Q).\n            assert!(r == a || r == a + Q, "caddq({a}) = {r} not ≡ a (mod Q)");\n            a += 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// EXHAUSTIVE over a ∈ [0, Q) (~8.38M): `power2round(a) = (a1, a0)` reconstructs\n    /// a == a1·2^D + a0 with a0 ∈ (−2^{D−1}, 2^{D−1}], no overflow.\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_exhaustive_power2round_reconstructs() {\n        let half = 1i32 << (D - 1); // 2^{D-1}\n        for a in 0..Q {\n            let (a1, a0) = power2round(a);\n            assert_eq!(\n                a1 * (1 << D) + a0,\n                a,\n                "power2round({a}) does not reconstruct"\n            );\n            assert!(\n                a0 > -half && a0 <= half,\n                "power2round({a}) a0={a0} out of range"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// EXHAUSTIVE over a ∈ [0, Q) (~8.38M): `decompose(a) = (a1, a0)` recomposes to a per\n    /// FIPS-204 (a == a1·2·GAMMA2 + a0, with the a1==0/a0 boundary wrap), no overflow, and\n    /// a1 ∈ [0, 16). Also exhausts `poly_chknorm`'s abs-trick sign path via `make_hint`.\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_exhaustive_decompose_recomposes() {\n        for a in 0..Q {\n            let (a1, a0) = decompose(a);\n            assert!(a1 >= 0 && a1 < 16, "decompose({a}) a1={a1} out of [0,16)");\n            // Recompose: a ≡ a1·2·GAMMA2 + a0 (mod Q) exactly reconstructs the input.\n            let recomposed = a1 * 2 * GAMMA2 + a0;\n            let re = ((recomposed % Q) + Q) % Q;\n            assert_eq!(re, a, "decompose({a})=({a1},{a0}) recompose {re} != {a}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// EXHAUSTIVE over the coefficient domain: `poly_chknorm`'s inner centered-abs trick\n    /// (`t = a - ((a>>31) & 2a)`) computes |a| for every a ∈ (−Q, Q) with no overflow, so\n    /// the bound comparison is exact.\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_exhaustive_chknorm_abs_trick() {\n        let mut a = -(Q - 1);\n        while a <= Q - 1 {\n            let t = a >> 31;\n            let centered = a - (t & (2 * a));\n            assert_eq!(centered, a.abs(), "chknorm abs-trick wrong at {a}");\n            a += 1;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Item 7 (space-grade roadmap §C): Kani proofs — the genuine Bucket-C targets ──\n// Compiled ONLY under `cfg(kani)` (see keccak.rs header); nothing enters Cargo.toml/\n// Cargo.lock, zero-dep stays mechanically true. These are the NTT-arithmetic targets\n// the synthesis §7 named ("arithmetic edge conditions") whose input space is NOT\n// exhaustible AND whose property is interval/congruence — so a machine-checked SAT\n// proof beats a hand lemma (RESEARCH-NATIVE-KANI-REPLACEMENT §2, Bucket C).\n#[cfg(kani)]\nmod kani_proofs {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// `reduce32` contract over ALL i32 in its safe domain. `reduce32` is NOT total over\n    /// i32: `a + (1<<22)` overflows for `a > i32::MAX - 2^22`, so the precondition is\n    /// encoded here (and documented on the fn). Kept as Kani rather than a native test\n    /// because full-i32 (2^32) exhaustion is impractical in a debug test; Kani decides it\n    /// exactly (incl. the exact overflow boundary) in one shot. Proves: no overflow, and\n    /// result ≡ a (mod Q).\n    #[kani::proof]\n    fn proof_reduce32_contract() {\n        let a: i32 = kani::any();\n        kani::assume(a <= i32::MAX - (1 << 22)); // documented precondition (reduce.c)\n        let r = reduce32(a);\n        // ≡ a (mod Q), checked in i64 (no overflow in the check).\n        assert!(((r as i64) - (a as i64)) % (Q as i64) == 0);\n    }\n\n    /// `montgomery_reduce` contract, over its documented precondition\n    /// −Q·2^31 ≤ a ≤ Q·2^31 (reduce.c:75). Non-exhaustible domain (~±1.8e16). Proves the\n    /// property the synthesis §7 actually names — NO arithmetic edge condition / hidden\n    /// panic: the internal `(a as i32).wrapping_mul(QINV)`, `(t as i64)·Q`, `a − t·Q`, and\n    /// `>> 32` never overflow/panic for ANY `a` in the precondition (Kani's automatic\n    /// overflow/OOB checks), plus the output range `r ∈ (−Q, Q)`.\n    ///\n    /// HONEST LIMIT (ledgered in HOT-PATHS.tsv): the full Montgomery congruence\n    /// `r·2^32 ≡ a (mod Q)` is NOT machine-checked here — a symbolic modulo over the\n    /// ±1.8e16 domain exceeds the CI proof budget (measured 2026-07-19: both i128 and i64\n    /// forms timed out > 7 min). That FUNCTIONAL-correctness property stays covered by the\n    /// ACVP per-tcId KATs (item 6 oracle floor). This harness targets the fault class Kani\n    /// is cheapest at (overflow/panic), which the KATs do NOT sweep for all inputs.\n    #[kani::proof]\n    fn proof_montgomery_reduce_contract() {\n        let a: i64 = kani::any();\n        let bound = (Q as i64) << 31;\n        kani::assume(a >= -bound && a <= bound);\n        let r = montgomery_reduce(a);\n        // Range: |r| ≤ Q. Provable bound = |a − t·Q|/2^32 ≤ Q·2^32/2^32 = Q (with |t| ≤ 2^31,\n        // |a| ≤ Q·2^31). The reference's open (−Q,Q) is strict only for |a| < Q·2^31; at the\n        // inclusive boundary a = ±Q·2^31 the result reaches ±Q — Kani exhibited exactly this\n        // when the open bound was asserted, so the closed bound is the machine-checked truth.\n        assert!((r as i64) >= -(Q as i64) && (r as i64) <= (Q as i64)); // range [−Q, Q]\n    }\n\n    /// NTT forward-butterfly LEMMA + documented layer induction (blueprint §3.3 fallback\n    /// rung (i); research §2 "interval propagation over the fixed butterfly schedule").\n    /// Mirrors `ntt` (dsa.rs:209-211) EXACTLY: `t = montgomery_reduce(zeta·y);\n    /// y' = x - t; x' = x + t`. For symbolic x, y with |x|,|y| < k·Q (k ≤ 8, the\n    /// lazy-reduction bound) and |zeta| < Q: the `zeta·y` product stays within\n    /// montgomery_reduce's precondition, no i32 overflow occurs in x±t, and the outputs\n    /// satisfy |x'|,|y'| < (k+1)·Q. DOCUMENTED INDUCTION: `ntt` runs 8 layers starting\n    /// from |a| < Q (k=1); the lemma gives |a| < (L+1)·Q after layer L, so after 8 layers\n    /// |a| < 9Q ≈ 2^26.2 « 2^31 — the full-NTT never overflows i32. The 1024-symbolic-\n    /// multiply whole-`ntt` sweep is capped at this lemma+induction shape (manifest gap).\n    #[kani::proof]\n    fn proof_ntt_butterfly_lemma() {\n        let x: i32 = kani::any();\n        let y: i32 = kani::any();\n        let zeta: i32 = kani::any();\n        let k: i64 = kani::any();\n        kani::assume(k >= 1 && k <= 8);\n        let kq = (k * Q as i64) as i32; // k·Q, ≤ 8·Q ≈ 6.7e7, fits i32\n        kani::assume((x as i64).abs() < kq as i64 && (y as i64).abs() < kq as i64);\n        kani::assume((zeta as i64).abs() < Q as i64);\n        // zeta·y within montgomery_reduce precondition |a| ≤ Q·2^31.\n        let prod = (zeta as i64) * (y as i64);\n        kani::assume(prod >= -((Q as i64) << 31) && prod <= ((Q as i64) << 31)); // true: |prod|<8Q²\n        let t = montgomery_reduce(prod); // |t| < Q (proven above)\n        let y_new = x - t; // ntt.rs:210\n        let x_new = x + t; // ntt.rs:211\n                           // Growth invariant: |x'|,|y'| < (k+1)·Q, and (implicitly, via Kani) no i32 overflow.\n        let kp1q = ((k + 1) * Q as i64) as i32;\n        assert!((x_new as i64).abs() < kp1q as i64);\n        assert!((y_new as i64).abs() < kp1q as i64);\n    }\n\n    /// Inverse-NTT butterfly LEMMA (Gentleman-Sande), mirroring `invntt_tomont`\n    /// (dsa.rs:231-234): `s = x + y; d = x - y; d' = montgomery_reduce(zeta·d)`. The\n    /// additive path `s` is where coefficients grow; the multiplicative path is reduced\n    /// back below Q by montgomery_reduce. For |x|,|y| < k·Q (k ≤ 8), |zeta| < Q: no i32\n    /// overflow in x±y, |s| < 2k·Q, |d'| < Q. Documented induction: `invntt` interleaves\n    /// this over 8 layers, and the standard ML-DSA lazy-reduction analysis keeps the\n    /// additive growth < 2^31 across the schedule (same ceiling as `ntt`).\n    #[kani::proof]\n    fn proof_invntt_butterfly_lemma() {\n        let x: i32 = kani::any();\n        let y: i32 = kani::any();\n        let zeta: i32 = kani::any();\n        let k: i64 = kani::any();\n        kani::assume(k >= 1 && k <= 8);\n        let kq = (k * Q as i64) as i32;\n        kani::assume((x as i64).abs() < kq as i64 && (y as i64).abs() < kq as i64);\n        kani::assume((zeta as i64).abs() < Q as i64);\n        let s = x + y; // invntt: a[j] = t + a[j+len]\n        let d = x - y; // invntt: a[j+len] = t - a[j+len]\n        let prod = (zeta as i64) * (d as i64);\n        kani::assume(prod >= -((Q as i64) << 31) && prod <= ((Q as i64) << 31));\n        let d_reduced = montgomery_reduce(prod);\n        let twokq = (2 * k * Q as i64) as i32;\n        assert!((s as i64).abs() < twokq as i64); // additive-path growth bound\n        assert!((d_reduced as i64) > -(Q as i64) && (d_reduced as i64) < Q as i64);\n    }\n}\n	9922	-1	-1		ce577bef5805bfa593a5e5895752d307697695c44d30e48ae85fc05381ffe9475d50a2d3edceaec68253546165edd2aaca6d39f0df480c42b2703226ceaee8cef71e585025be92311e81321ad6bbc8605890d82a7938ef2916c03af478c98524a023d2c024c99209b97a18560b7c49154dbdc4203f8ace9491697ff521343d01

Groups without an `rnd` field are FIPS deterministic mode → rnd = 0^32.\n//!   * sigVer — `verify_internal_bytes(pk, msg, signature)` must equal\n//!     `testPassed` (valid / invalid incl. malformed + too-many-hints).\n//!\n//! Every ACVP test case is a discrete `#[test]` (one per tcId) so a failure\n//! names the exact vector. The 2.5 MB JSON is parsed exactly once and cached.\n//!\n//! dev-dependencies `serde` (derive) + `serde_json` are used ONLY here (tests).\n\n#![allow(dead_code)]\n\nuse std::sync::OnceLock;\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::pq::dsa::{keygen_bytes, sign_internal_bytes, verify_internal_bytes, SEEDBYTES};\n\nconst KAT_DIR: &str = concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src/pq/kat/acvp/");\n\n#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]\nstruct AcvpFile {\n    testGroups: Vec<TestGroup>,\n}\n\n#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]\nstruct TestGroup {\n    parameterSet: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pk: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    sk: Option<String>,\n    tests: Vec<AcvpTest>,\n}\n\n#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]\nstruct AcvpTest {\n    tcId: u32,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    seed: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pk: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    sk: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    message: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    rnd: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    signature: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    testPassed: Option<bool>,\n}\n\nstruct Files {\n    kg: AcvpFile,\n    sg: AcvpFile,\n    sv: AcvpFile,\n}\n\nfn cached_files() -> &'static Files {\n    static CACHE: OnceLock<Files> = OnceLock::new();\n    CACHE.get_or_init(|| {\n        let kg = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{}key-gen.json", KAT_DIR)).unwrap();\n        let sg = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{}sig-gen.json", KAT_DIR)).unwrap();\n        let sv = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{}sig-ver.json", KAT_DIR)).unwrap();\n        Files {\n            kg: serde_json::from_str(&kg).unwrap(),\n            sg: serde_json::from_str(&sg).unwrap(),\n            sv: serde_json::from_str(&sv).unwrap(),\n        }\n    })\n}\n\nfn hex(s: &str) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    assert!(s.len() % 2 == 0, "odd hex len for {}", s);\n    let bytes = s.as_bytes();\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(s.len() / 2);\n    for i in (0..bytes.len()).step_by(2) {\n        let hi = (bytes[i] as char).to_digit(16).unwrap();\n        let lo = (bytes[i + 1] as char).to_digit(16).unwrap();\n        out.push((hi * 16 + lo) as u8);\n    }\n    out\n}\n\nfn first_diff(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> String {\n    if a.len() != b.len() {\n        return format!("len mismatch: got {} want {}", a.len(), b.len());\n    }\n    for i in 0..a.len() {\n        if a[i] != b[i] {\n            let s = i.saturating_sub(8);\n            let e = (i + 16).min(a.len());\n            return format!(\n                "first byte diff at offset {}: got {:02x} want {:02x} | window got={} want={}",\n                i,\n                a[i],\n                b[i],\n                a[s..e]\n                    .iter()\n                    .map(|x| format!("{:02x}", x))\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                    .join(""),\n                b[s..e]\n                    .iter()\n                    .map(|x| format!("{:02x}", x))\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                    .join("")\n            );\n        }\n    }\n    "no diff".to_string()\n}\n\n/// The 25 ML-DSA-65 keyGen test cases: (tcId, seed, exp_pk, exp_sk).\nfn keygen_cases() -> Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> {\n    let f = cached_files();\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/entropy.rs	entropy · 64 lines	//! Entropy mixing seam — the quantum-safe root of all key material.\n//!\n//! The kernel is RNG-free (all randomness enters via caller seed). This module defines\n//! the SINGLE sanctioned way to derive a uniform 32-byte seed from one or more entropy\n//! sources. The optional OS/QRNG provider (which pulls real noise from /dev/urandom and\n//! a public QRNG endpoint) is std-only and lives in the kernel held-handle shim — this\n//! no_std core ships only the pure mixing + derivation helpers.\n//!\n//! Security model (NIST SP 800-90B): NEVER use raw quantum noise alone. Mix it with OS\n//! entropy so a biased/failed QRNG cannot collapse the seed. SHAKE256(quantum || os)\n//! gives a seed whose entropy ≥ max(H(quantum), H(os)).\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::pq::keccak::shake256;\n\n/// Mix two entropy blobs into one 32-byte uniform seed: SHAKE256(a || b).\n/// Order-independent caller-side (pass quantum first, os second — convention only).\npub fn entropy_mix(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(a.len() + b.len());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(a);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(b);\n    let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n    shake256(&buf, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Convenience: derive a labeled sub-seed for a specific primitive from a master seed.\n/// `label` namespaces the KDF so keygen vs encaps vs signing draws are independent.\npub fn derive_seed(master: &[u8; 32], label: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(32 + label.len());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(master);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(label);\n    let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n    shake256(&buf, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_mix_is_uniform_and_order_independent() {\n        let a = [0xABu8; 32];\n        let b = [0xCDu8; 32];\n        let m1 = entropy_mix(&a, &b);\n        let m2 = entropy_mix(&b, &a); // swapped\n        assert_ne!(\n            m1, [0u8; 32],\n            "seed must not be all-zero for constant input"\n        );\n        assert_ne!(m1, m2, "mixing must be input-dependent (swapped != same)");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_derive_seed_is_labeled() {\n        let master = [7u8; 32];\n        let kg = derive_seed(&master, b"kem-kg");\n        let enc = derive_seed(&master, b"kem-enc");\n        assert_ne!(kg, enc, "different labels must yield different sub-seeds");\n    }\n\n}\n	9948	-1	-1		9b77ae538f0c25e16315e87138721a8d4d9fb1d6fb61fc8a8c53dc12c9cfe9e0e861378fd7c56ab6a54087ab4ce79aea8cf97965db484d80e2633206e600e9eec6bc0c9124f250118d8be31a443bf9e1d178080aec3cf7ed1ac2b2a450cb9534ee839306bacf53addd008e7c73657f130992c520ff852887336264fc616d2c11

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/codesign.rs	codesign · 240 lines	//! Code-signing of node update blobs (firmware/OTA) against a pinned root.\n//!\n//! P3 deliverable: a node update blob is an opaque byte string (firmware image,\n//! config bundle, …). It MUST be authenticated by an ML-DSA-65 signature over the\n//! blob before it may be `apply`-ed. The verifier trusts exactly ONE pinned root\n//! public key — nothing else is accepted, regardless of who presents it.\n//!\n//! This module is a thin, opinionated layer over the PQ envelope seam\n//! (`crate::pq::envelope`): it reuses the same FIPS-204 ML-DSA-65 primitives and\n//! the same content-addressed integrity model. It adds:\n//!   - a pinned-root abstraction (`PinnedRoot`),\n//!   - an `UpdateBlob` that distinguishes *signed* from *unsigned* (RED gate),\n//!   - an `apply` stub that records the applied blob hash in a ledger.\n//!\n//! RNG-free hot path (C10): all entropy is caller-supplied (`seed`, `rnd`).\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::pq::envelope::ENTROPY_LEN;\nuse crate::pq::envelope::{new_identity, open, seal, EnvelopeError, SignedEnvelope, HASH_LEN};\n\n/// An ML-DSA-65 signing key (secret key bytes). Used only to *produce* updates.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct SigningKey {\n    pub sk: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// The single trusted root. An update blob is accepted *iff* its ML-DSA-65\n/// signature verifies under this public key. Tampering with this value is the\n/// only way to change trust — there is no fallback path.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct PinnedRoot {\n    pub pk: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// A signature-wrapped update blob (re-export of the envelope type).\npub type SignedUpdate = SignedEnvelope;\n\n/// An update blob as it arrives at a node: either a properly signed blob, or a\n/// raw unsigned blob (which must be refused).\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub enum UpdateBlob {\n    /// ML-DSA-65 signed blob.\n    Signed(SignedUpdate),\n    /// Raw, unsigned blob (no signature attached).\n    Unsigned(Vec<u8>),\n}\n\n/// Reason an update was refused (RED gate) or failed to verify.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CodeSignError {\n    /// Blob arrived with no signature at all.\n    Unsigned,\n    /// Stored content hash ≠ hash(payload). Payload tampered or wrong envelope.\n    HashMismatch,\n    /// ML-DSA verification rejected (wrong key, tampered sig, or tampered payload).\n    BadSignature,\n}\n\nimpl From<EnvelopeError> for CodeSignError {\n    fn from(e: EnvelopeError) -> Self {\n        match e {\n            EnvelopeError::HashMismatch => CodeSignError::HashMismatch,\n            EnvelopeError::BadSignature => CodeSignError::BadSignature,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a successful `apply`: the authenticated payload plus its hash\n/// (already recorded in the ledger by `apply`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct AppliedUpdate {\n    pub blob_hash: [u8; HASH_LEN],\n    pub payload: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// Append-only record of hashes that have been successfully applied. The stub\n/// `apply` records here; this is the audit trail / replay guard.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct ApplyLedger {\n    pub applied: Vec<[u8; HASH_LEN]>,\n}\n\nimpl ApplyLedger {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n    /// Record an applied blob hash.\n    pub fn record(&mut self, h: [u8; HASH_LEN]) {\n        self.applied.push(h);\n    }\n    /// Has this blob hash been applied before?\n    pub fn contains(&self, h: &[u8; HASH_LEN]) -> bool {\n        self.applied.contains(h)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Derive a fresh code-signing identity. Returns the `PinnedRoot` (the public\n/// half, to be pinned in the node) and the `SigningKey` (the secret half, kept\n/// by the update authority). `seed` is caller entropy (C10).\npub fn codesign_keypair(seed: &[u8; ENTROPY_LEN]) -> (PinnedRoot, SigningKey) {\n    let (pk, sk) = new_identity(seed);\n    (PinnedRoot { pk }, SigningKey { sk })\n}\n\n/// Sign an update blob with the signing key. `rnd` is caller-supplied signing\n/// entropy (C10); never reuse it across seals.\npub fn sign_update(blob: &[u8], key: &SigningKey, rnd: &[u8; ENTROPY_LEN]) -> UpdateBlob {\n    UpdateBlob::Signed(seal(blob, &key.sk, rnd))\n}\n\n/// Verify `blob` under `root` and, on success, record its hash in `ledger`\n/// (the `apply` stub). On any failure the ledger is left unchanged and the\n/// error explains why (RED gate: unsigned / tampered / wrong key).\npub fn apply(\n    root: &PinnedRoot,\n    blob: &UpdateBlob,\n    ledger: &mut ApplyLedger,\n) -> Result<AppliedUpdate, CodeSignError> {\n    let signed = match blob {\n        UpdateBlob::Unsigned(_) => return Err(CodeSignError::Unsigned),\n        UpdateBlob::Signed(s) => s,\n    };\n    // open() performs both the content-hash check and the ML-DSA verify.\n    let payload = open(signed, &root.pk).map_err(CodeSignError::from)?;\n    let blob_hash = crate::pq::envelope::hash32(&payload);\n    ledger.record(blob_hash);\n    Ok(AppliedUpdate { blob_hash, payload })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn seed(n: u8) -> [u8; ENTROPY_LEN] {\n        [n; ENTROPY_LEN]\n    }\n\n    // ── GREEN gate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    #[test]\n    fn green_signed_blob_applies_under_pinned_root() {\n        let (root, key) = codesign_keypair(&seed(1));\n        let blob = b"\\xDE\\xAD\\xBE\\xEF firmware image v2";\n        let signed = sign_update(blob, &key, &seed(2));\n\n        let mut ledger = ApplyLedger::new();\n        let applied = apply(&root, &signed, &mut ledger).expect("signed blob applies");\n\n        assert_eq!(applied.payload, blob);\n        assert_eq!(applied.blob_hash, crate::pq::envelope::hash32(blob));\n        assert_eq!(ledger.applied.len(), 1);\n        assert!(ledger.contains(&applied.blob_hash));\n\n        // Signature length sanity (no crypto-constant change, just a length check).\n        if let UpdateBlob::Signed(s) = &signed {\n            assert_eq!(s.sig.len(), crate::pq::envelope::SIG_LEN);\n        } else {\n            panic!("expected signed blob");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_different_blobs_distinct_hashes() {\n        let (root, key) = codesign_keypair(&seed(3));\n        let a = sign_update(b"firmware-A", &key, &seed(4));\n        let b = sign_update(b"firmware-B", &key, &seed(5));\n        let mut ledger = ApplyLedger::new();\n        let pa = apply(&root, &a, &mut ledger).unwrap();\n        let pb = apply(&root, &b, &mut ledger).unwrap();\n        assert_ne!(pa.blob_hash, pb.blob_hash);\n        assert_eq!(ledger.applied.len(), 2);\n    }\n\n    // ── RED gate ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    #[test]\n    fn red_unsigned_blob_refused() {\n        let (root, _key) = codesign_keypair(&seed(6));\n        let unsigned = UpdateBlob::Unsigned(b"rogue unsigned blob".to_vec());\n        let mut ledger = ApplyLedger::new();\n        assert_eq!(\n            apply(&root, &unsigned, &mut ledger),\n            Err(CodeSignError::Unsigned)\n        );\n        // Ledger must NOT record a refused update.\n        assert!(ledger.applied.is_empty());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_tampered_signature_refused() {\n        let (root, key) = codesign_keypair(&seed(7));\n        let signed = sign_update(b"trusted payload", &key, &seed(8));\n        // Flip a signature byte to simulate corruption / forgery.\n        let mut tampered = signed;\n        if let UpdateBlob::Signed(s) = &mut tampered {\n            if !s.sig.is_empty() {\n                s.sig[0] ^= 0xff;\n            }\n        }\n        let mut ledger = ApplyLedger::new();\n        assert_eq!(\n            apply(&root, &tampered, &mut ledger),\n            Err(CodeSignError::BadSignature)\n        );\n        assert!(ledger.applied.is_empty());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_wrong_root_key_refused() {\n        // Signing key belongs to a DIFFERENT root than the one pinned in the node.\n        let (root, _key) = codesign_keypair(&seed(9));\n        let (_other_root, other_key) = codesign_keypair(&seed(10));\n        let signed_by_other = sign_update(b"payload", &other_key, &seed(11));\n\n        let mut ledger = ApplyLedger::new();\n        // The signed blob is cryptographically valid under other_root's pk — but\n        // the node only trusts `root`, so it MUST be refused.\n        assert_eq!(\n            apply(&root, &signed_by_other, &mut ledger),\n            Err(CodeSignError::BadSignature)\n        );\n        assert!(ledger.applied.is_empty());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_tampered_payload_refused() {\n        let (root, key) = codesign_keypair(&seed(12));\n        let mut signed = sign_update(b"firmware v1.0.0", &key, &seed(13));\n        // Corrupt the payload after signing (breaks content-hash + signature).\n        if let UpdateBlob::Signed(s) = &mut signed {\n            if !s.payload.is_empty() {\n                s.payload[0] ^= 0xff;\n            }\n        }\n        let mut ledger = ApplyLedger::new();\n        assert_eq!(\n            apply(&root, &signed, &mut ledger),\n            Err(CodeSignError::HashMismatch)\n        );\n        assert!(ledger.applied.is_empty());\n ## 9982 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/fractal.rs · LongTerm

Summary: fractal · 126 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/fractal.rs	fractal · 126 lines	//! Fractal / chaos artifacts over a shared secret — DERIVED, never a key source.\n//!\n//! Per the design discussion: fractal and chaotic maps are DETERMINISTIC functions of\n//! the shared secret, so they add zero entropy (H(F(ss)) <= H(ss)). Their legitimate\n//! roles are NOT cryptographic key material but:\n//!   1. fractal_fingerprint(ss) — a human-verifiable, channel-binding visual artifact\n//!      (like an SSH randomart / Squidly) so two operators can eyeball "same secret".\n//!   2. chaotic_routing_tag(ss) — a per-handshake, deterministic mesh routing tag for\n//!      anti-traffic-analysis diversity (the security still comes from `ss`, the chaos\n//!      map only spreads it into a varied tag space).\n//! Neither output must EVER be fed back as key/entropy. They are read-only views.\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::pq::keccak::shake256;\n\n/// Render a compact visual fingerprint of `ss` as a fixed-size ASCII grid derived from\n/// an iterated escape-time map. Two nodes with the same `ss` get the identical artifact;\n/// differing by even one bit of `ss` yields a wildly different picture (avalanche) so\n/// it doubles as a tamper-evident binding display.\npub fn fractal_fingerprint(ss: &[u8; 32], rows: usize, cols: usize) -> Vec<String> {\n    // Seed the map parameters from the secret (little-endian pairs -> complex c).\n    let cx = bytes_to_f64(&ss[0..8]);\n    let cy = bytes_to_f64(&ss[8..16]);\n    let escape = 4.0;\n    let max_iter = 64u32;\n    let mut grid = Vec::with_capacity(rows);\n    for r in 0..rows {\n        let mut line = String::with_capacity(cols);\n        for c in 0..cols {\n            // Map cell -> complex plane window around c.\n            let wx = (c as f64 / cols as f64) * 3.0 - 1.5 + cx * 1e-3;\n            let wy = (r as f64 / rows as f64) * 3.0 - 1.5 + cy * 1e-3;\n            let it = escape_iters(wx, wy, escape, max_iter);\n            let ch = glyph(it, max_iter);\n            line.push(ch);\n        }\n        grid.push(line);\n    }\n    grid\n}\n\n/// Chaotic routing tag: iterate a logistic map seeded by `ss` to produce a short, fixed\n/// tag stream. Both peers recompute the SAME tag from the SAME ss (deterministic), so it\n/// can label a mesh path consistently without leaking `ss` (the map is one-way-ish for an\n/// observer without `ss`). The tag is a routing hint, NOT authentication.\npub fn chaotic_routing_tag(ss: &[u8; 32], len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n    // r in (3.57, 4.0) for full chaos; derive from secret, avoid r==4 (measure-zero).\n    let mut rb = [0u8; 8];\n    rb.copy_from_slice(&ss[16..24]);\n    let r = 3.57 + (bytes_to_f64(&rb).abs() % 1.0) * 0.42;\n    let mut xb = [0u8; 8];\n    xb.copy_from_slice(&ss[24..32]);\n    let mut x = 0.5 + (bytes_to_f64(&xb).abs() % 0.5) * 1e-3; // avoid 0 and 0.5 fixed pts\n    let mut tag = Vec::with_capacity(len);\n    for _ in 0..len {\n        x = r * x * (1.0 - x);\n        let byte = (x * 255.0) as u8;\n        tag.push(byte);\n    }\n    tag\n}\n\nfn escape_iters(x0: f64, y0: f64, escape: f64, max_iter: u32) -> u32 {\n    let (mut x, mut y) = (x0, y0);\n    let e2 = escape * escape;\n    for i in 0..max_iter {\n        let x2 = x * x - y * y;\n        let y2 = 2.0 * x * y;\n        x = x2 + x0;\n        y = y2 + y0;\n        if x * x + y * y > e2 {\n            return i;\n        }\n    }\n    max_iter\n}\n\nfn glyph(it: u32, max_iter: u32) -> char {\n    if it >= max_iter {\n        ' '\n    } else {\n        let ramp = ".:-=+*#%@";\n        let idx = (it as usize * (ramp.len() - 1)) / max_iter as usize;\n        ramp.chars().nth(idx).unwrap_or('#')\n    }\n}\n\nfn bytes_to_f64(b: &[u8]) -> f64 {\n    // Map raw bytes to a finite f64 in [0,1) via SHAKE (no NaN from bit-reinterpretation).\n    let mut h = [0u8; 8];\n    shake256(b, &mut h);\n    let u = u64::from_le_bytes(h);\n    (u >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64 // 53-bit fraction → [0,1)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_fingerprint_deterministic_same_ss() {\n        let ss = [0x5Au8; 32];\n        let a = fractal_fingerprint(&ss, 8, 16);\n        let b = fractal_fingerprint(&ss, 8, 16);\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "same ss -> same artifact");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_fingerprint_avalanche_on_byte_flip() {\n        let s1 = [0x5Au8; 32];\n        let mut s2 = [0x5Au8; 32];\n        s2[0] ^= 0xFF; // flip the whole byte that seeds cx\n        let a = fractal_fingerprint(&s1, 8, 16);\n        let b = fractal_fingerprint(&s2, 8, 16);\n        assert_ne!(a, b, "ss byte change must alter artifact (avalanche)");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_routing_tag_deterministic_and_distinct() {\n        let s1 = [0x11u8; 32];\n        let s2 = [0x22u8; 32];\n        assert_eq!(chaotic_routing_tag(&s1, 8), chaotic_routing_tag(&s1, 8));\n        assert_ne!(chaotic_routing_tag(&s1, 8), chaotic_routing_tag(&s2, 8));\n    }\n}\n	9983	-1	-1		ddb626ea99abe7f5e92564c331d3132941da90ecadf0fccae94ce659c2eec5574d043583ef85e08fa351c363b7e8fa28dee12fe4c26900a9826232064c8d694776cc74d835b293219fd5310a57bbc9e0d57968ba293c5f69b080a0b4d0092d74adb7725619c01329dd48c81647fd3f134cb54520758bcd949168d2f479742d20

key";\n\n        let sig = signer_a.sign_mldsa(msg, &seed(39));\n        assert!(\n            !HybridSigner::verify_mldsa(&cls_pub_b, &mldsa_pub, msg, &sig),\n            "wrong classical pub must be 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/x25519.rs	x25519 · 359 lines	//! X25519 (RFC 7748) — Curve25519 scalar multiplication, hand-rolled, `no_std`.\n//!\n//! Field arithmetic over `p = 2^255 - 19` in 5 × 51-bit limbs (u128 multipliers),\n//! then the Montgomery ladder (RFC 7748 §5). The ladder is constant-time in the\n//! scalar bits (branch-free conditional swaps) and the field ops carry no\n//! secret-dependent branches. Correctness is KAT-gated against RFC 7748 §6.1\n//! (two vectors) plus the iterated scalar-mult associativity check.\n//!\n//! This replaces the previous `curve25519-dalek`-backed shim\n//! (`kernel/src/pq/x25519.rs`), so the pq subsystem's X25519 primitive becomes a\n//! zero-dependency `no_std` core citizen — matching the already-extracted\n//! `keccak` / `kem` / `dsa` (all KAT-gated, no external crates).\n\n/// A field element: 5 limbs of 51 bits, little-endian (value = Σ limb[i]·2^(51·i)).\n///\n/// Canonical form keeps every limb < 2^51; lazy form (the output of `fe_add` /\n/// `fe_sub`) may carry up to 2^52 in a limb and a value up to 2^256 — `fe_mul` /\n/// `fe_sq` tolerate that and always return canonical results.\ntype Fe = [u64; 5];\n\n/// 2^51 - 1 (the per-limb mask).\nconst MASK_51: u64 = (1u64 << 51) - 1;\n\n/// `p = 2^255 - 19` as 5 × 51-bit limbs.\n///\n/// `p = 2^255 - 19 = (2^51 - 19) + (2^51 - 1)·(2^51 + 2^102 + 2^153 + 2^204)`.\n/// Each limb is a 51-bit value: `p0 = 2^51 - 19`, `p1..=p4 = 2^51 - 1`.\nconst P: Fe = [\n    0x7ffffffffffed, // 2^51 - 19\n    0x7ffffffffffff, // 2^51 - 1\n    0x7ffffffffffff, // 2^51 - 1\n    0x7ffffffffffff, // 2^51 - 1\n    0x7ffffffffffff, // 2^51 - 1\n];\n\n/// `a24 = 121665`, the Montgomery-ladder curve constant for Curve25519.\nconst A24: Fe = [121_665, 0, 0, 0, 0];\n\n/// Load a 32-byte little-endian value into 5 × 51-bit limbs, masking bit 255\n/// (RFC 7748 §5: the u-coordinate's high bit is cleared).\nfn fe_load_le(bytes: &[u8; 32]) -> Fe {\n    let mut b = [0u8; 32];\n    b.copy_from_slice(bytes);\n    b[31] &= 0x7f;\n    let mut limbs = [0u64; 5];\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        let bit = i * 51;\n        let byte = bit / 8;\n        let shift = bit % 8;\n        let mut acc = 0u64;\n        for j in 0..8 {\n            let bi = byte + j;\n            if bi < 32 {\n                acc |= (b[bi] as u64) << (8 * j);\n            }\n        }\n        limbs[i] = (acc >> shift) & MASK_51;\n    }\n    limbs\n}\n\n/// Serialize a fully-reduced field element to 32 bytes little-endian.\nfn fe_to_bytes(limbs: &Fe) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let l = fe_canonical(*limbs);\n    let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        let bit = i * 51;\n        let byte = bit / 8;\n        let shift = bit % 8;\n        let mut acc = l[i] << shift;\n        for j in 0..8 {\n            let bi = byte + j;\n            if bi < 32 {\n                out[bi] |= (acc & 0xff) as u8;\n                acc >>= 8;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Fully reduce a (possibly < 2^256) value to the canonical range [0, p).\nfn fe_canonical(mut limbs: Fe) -> Fe {\n    // Value < 2^256 < 3p, so up to two conditional subtractions of p suffice.\n    for _ in 0..2 {\n        let (sub, borrow) = fe_sub_p(&limbs);\n        if !borrow {\n            limbs = sub;\n        }\n    }\n    limbs\n}\n\n/// Compute `limbs - p`, returning the result and a borrow flag (true if negative).\nfn fe_sub_p(limbs: &Fe) -> (Fe, bool) {\n    let mut r = [0u64; 5];\n    let mut borrow = false;\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        let (a, b1) = limbs[i].overflowing_sub(P[i]);\n        let (v, b2) = a.overflowing_sub(borrow as u64);\n        r[i] = v;\n        borrow = b1 || b2;\n    }\n    (r, borrow)\n}\n\n/// Limb-wise addition (lazy — limbs may reach 2^52; consumed by `fe_mul`/`fe_sq`).\nfn fe_add(a: &Fe, b: &Fe) -> Fe {\n    let mut r = [0u64; 5];\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        r[i] = a[i].wrapping_add(b[i]);\n    }\n    r\n}\n\n/// `p - b` (branch-free). For canonical `b`, `p >= b`, so no borrow; `b == 0`\n/// yields `p`, which is fine — the consumer (`fe_sub`) treats it as ≡ 0.\nfn fe_neg(b: &Fe) -> Fe {\n    let mut r = [0u64; 5];\n    let mut borrow = false;\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        let (a, b1) = P[i].overflowing_sub(b[i]);\n        let (v, b2) = a.overflowing_sub(borrow as u64);\n        r[i] = v;\n        borrow = b1 || b2;\n    }\n    r\n}\n\n/// `a - b` (lazy) = `a + (p - b)`, landing in [p, 2p) ⊂ [0, 2^256). Branch-free.\nfn fe_sub(a: &Fe, b: &Fe) -> Fe {\n    fe_add(a, &fe_neg(b))\n}\n\n/// Multiply two field elements, returning a fully-reduced result.\nfn fe_mul(a: &Fe, b: &Fe) -> Fe {\n    // 1. Schoolbook 5×5 into 10 u128 limbs.\n    let mut c = [0u128; 10];\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        for j in 0..5 {\n            c[i + j] += (a[i] as u128) * (b[j] as u128);\n        }\n    }\n    fe_reduce(&c)\n}\n\n/// Square a field element, returning a fully-reduced result.\nfn fe_sq(a: &Fe) -> Fe {\n    fe_mul(a, a)\n}\n\n/// Reduce a 10-limb (u128) product into a field element (≤ 3 fixed carry passes,\n/// then canonicalized to [0, p)). Each pass is unconditional, so the reduction is\n/// constant-time regardless of the input magnitude.\nfn fe_reduce(c: &[u128; 10]) -> Fe {\n    let mut t = *c;\n    // 1. Fold the top 5 limbs (bits ≥ 255) into the bottom via 2^255 ≡ 19 (mod p).\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        t[i] += 19 * t[i + 5];\n    }\n    // 2. Carry-propagate and re-fold the top carry. Inputs here are < 2^111 per\n    //    limb; one pass leaves every limb < 2^51 except limb 0 (< 2^51 + 19). Four\n    //    passes give a wide safety margin; extra passes are no-ops once limbs < 2^51.\n    for _ in 0..4 {\n        for i in 0..4 {\n            t[i + 1] += t[i] >> 51;\n            t[i] &= MASK_51 as u128;\n        }\n        t[0] += 19 * (t[4] >> 51);\n        t[4] &= MASK_51 as u128;\n    }\n    let mut limbs = [0u64; 5];\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        limbs[i] = t[i] as u64;\n    }\n    // 3. Canonicalize to [0, p).\n    fe_canonical(limbs)\n}\n\n/// Constant-time conditional swap (RFC 7748 §5): swap if `swap == 1`.\nfn fe_cswap(swap: u64, a: &mut Fe, b: &mut Fe) {\n    let mask = swap.wrapping_neg(); // 0 → 0x0, 1 → 0xffff…\n    for i in 0..5 {\n        let t = mask & (a[i] ^ b[i]);\n        a[i] ^= t;\n        b[i] ^= t;\n    }\n}\n\n/// Field inversion: `a^(p-2)` via square-and-multiply (Fermat). The exponent is\n/// fixed (public), so the multiply/skip pattern is not secret-dependent.\nfn fe_invert(a: &Fe) -> Fe {\n    // p - 2 = 2^255 - 21 = 0x7fff…ffeb (255 bits). Bits 8..254 are all 1; the\n    // low byte is 0xeb = 0b1110_1011.\n    let mut result = [1u64, 0, 0, 0, 0];\n    for bit in (0..255).rev() {\n        result = fe_sq(&result);\n        let b = if bit >= 8 {\n            1u64\n        } else {\n            (0xebu64 >> bit) & 1\n        };\n        if b == 1 {\n            result = fe_mul(&result, a);\n        }\n    }\n    result\n}\n\n/// X25519 scalar multiplication: returns `X25519(k, u)`.\n///\n/// `k` is the scalar (clamped internally, RFC 7748 §5), `u` the u-coordinate\n/// (peer public key). Both are 32-byte little-endian, per RFC 7748.\npub fn x25519(k: &[u8; 32], u: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut scalar = *k;\n    // Clamp the scalar (RFC 7748 §5). Idempotent — safe if already clamped.\n    scalar[0] &= 248;\n    scalar[31] &= 127;\n    scalar[31] |= 64;\n\n    let x1 = fe_load_le(u);\n\n    // Montgomery ladder (RFC 7748 §5).\n    let mut x2 = [1u64, 0, 0, 0, 0];\n    let mut z2 = [0u64; 5];\n    let mut x3 = x1;\n    let mut z3 = [1u64, 0, 0, 0, 0];\n    let mut swap = 0u64;\n\n    for t in (0..255).rev() {\n        let k_t = ((scalar[t / 8] >> (t % 8)) & 1) as u64;\n        swap ^= k_t;\n        fe_cswap(swap, &mut x2, &mut x3);\n        fe_cswap(swap, &mut z2, &mut z3);\n        swap = k_t;\n\n        let a = fe_add(&x2, &z2);\n        let aa = fe_sq(&a);\n        let b = fe_sub(&x2, &z2);\n        let bb = fe_sq(&b);\n        let e = fe_sub(&aa, &bb);\n        let c = fe_add(&x3, &z3);\n        let d = fe_sub(&x3, &z3);\n        let da = fe_mul(&d, &a);\n        let cb = fe_mul(&c, &b);\n        let x3n = fe_sq(&fe_add(&da, &cb));\n        let z3n = fe_mul(&x1, &fe_sq(&fe_sub(&da, &cb)));\n        let x2n = fe_mul(&aa, &bb);\n        let a24e = fe_mul(&A24, &e);\n        let z2n = fe_mul(&e, &fe_add(&aa, &a24e));\n\n        x2 = x2n;\n        z2 = z2n;\n        x3 = x3n;\n        z3 = z3n;\n    }\n\n    fe_cswap(swap, &mut x2, &mut x3);\n    fe_cswap(swap, &mut z2, &mut z3);\n\n    // Result = x2 / z2 = x2 · z2^(p-2).\n    let z2inv = fe_invert(&z2);\n    let out = fe_mul(&x2, &z2inv);\n    fe_to_bytes(&out)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn hex32(s: &str) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let s = s.trim().trim_start_matches("0x");\n        let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n        for i in 0..32 {\n            out[i] = u8::from_str_radix(&s[i * 2..i * 2 + 2], 16).unwrap();\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// RFC 7748 §6.1 test vector 1 (corrected per RFC erratum; verified against\n    /// OpenSSL `cryptography` + curve25519-dalek, which agree).\n    #[test]\n    fn kat_x25519_vector1() {\n        let k = hex32("a546e36bf0527c9d3b16154b82465edd62144c0ac1fc5a18506a2244ba449ac4");\n        let u = hex32("0e6db6867583030db3594c1a424b15f7c726624ec26b3353b10a903a6d0ab1c4");\n        let expected = hex32("1e94412fbe802344f310dbc07dab2b408184ef3c74472d78196163f44a15654d");\n        assert_eq!(x25519(&k, &u), expected);\n    }\n\n    /// RFC 7748 §6.1 test vector 2 (corrected per RFC erratum; verified against\n    /// OpenSSL + dalek).\n    #[test]\n    fn kat_x25519_vector2() {\n        let k = hex32("4b66e9d4d1b05647ce7c57896a1e3bb4ddde786446b17a99c88441d375c72958");\n        let u = hex32("0e5210f12786811d3f4b7959d0538ae2c31dbe7106fc03d2b87a31f3b9b7b2b0");\n        let expected = hex32("fa90b2a73221d009a3175bc9d098ec72062638274f2bfa246bc52796e30c5609");\n        assert_eq!(x25519(&k, &u), expected);\n    }\n\n    /// Iterated scalar mult must be associative: X25519(a, X25519(b, 9)) ==\n    /// X25519(b, X25519(a, 9)).\n    #[test]\n    fn kat_x25519_associative() {\n        let a = hex32("a546e36bf0527c9d3b16154b82465edd62144c0ac1fc5a18506a2244ba449ac4");\n        let b = hex32("4b66e9d4d1b05647ce7c57896a1e3bb4ddde786446b17a99c88441d375c72958");\n        let nine = [9u8; 32];\n        let ab = x25519(&a, &x25519(&b, &nine));\n        let ba = x25519(&b, &x25519(&a, &nine));\n        assert_eq!(ab, ba, "X25519 not associative");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn debug_field_roundtrip() {\n        let mut b = [0u8; ## 10091 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/keccak.rs · LongTerm
