```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/keccak.rs	keccak · 417 lines	//! Zero-dependency Keccak-f[1600] + SHAKE128/256 (FIPS 202).\n//!\n//! Inlined on purpose (no `sha2`/`tiny-keccak`/`pqc` crates allowed). Every other\n//! module in this directory depends on `shake128`/`shake256`; this file is the one\n//! and only digest primitive. A FIPS 202 KAT is included so a single bit error in\n//! the sponge is caught before any scheme math touches it.\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n// ── Keccak-f[1600] ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// State = 25 lanes of u64. Round constants (RC) and rotation offsets (RHO) per\n// FIPS 202 §3.2.1 / §3.2.2.\n\nconst RC: [u64; 24] = [\n    0x0000000000000001,\n    0x0000000000008082,\n    0x800000000000808a,\n    0x8000000080008000,\n    0x000000000000808b,\n    0x0000000080000001,\n    0x8000000080008081,\n    0x8000000000008009,\n    0x000000000000008a,\n    0x0000000000000088,\n    0x0000000080008009,\n    0x000000008000000a,\n    0x000000008000808b,\n    0x800000000000008b,\n    0x8000000000008089,\n    0x8000000000008003,\n    0x8000000000008002,\n    0x8000000000000080,\n    0x000000000000800a,\n    0x800000008000000a,\n    0x8000000080008081,\n    0x8000000000008080,\n    0x0000000080000001,\n    0x8000000080008008,\n];\n\n// Rotation offsets r[x][y] (FIPS 202 §3.2.2), flat-indexed by x + 5*y.\nconst RHO: [u32; 25] = [\n    0, 1, 62, 28, 27, 36, 44, 6, 55, 20, 3, 10, 43, 25, 39, 41, 45, 15, 21, 8, 18, 2, 61, 56, 14,\n];\n\n#[inline]\nfn rotl(x: u64, n: u32) -> u64 {\n    if n == 0 {\n        x\n    } else {\n        (x << n) | (x >> (64 - n))\n    }\n}\n\n/// One KECCAK-f[1600] permutation in place.\n///\n/// `pub(crate)` visibility is required only by the item-7 Kani cross-copy equivalence\n/// harness (`kani_proofs::proof_keccak_copies_equivalent`), which proves this\n/// permutation ("copy A", flat-`RHO` formulation) computes the exact same function as\n/// `event_log::keccak_f` ("copy B"). No behavioral change; compiled identically.\npub(crate) fn keccak_f(state: &mut [u64; 25]) {\n    for round in 0..24 {\n        // Theta\n        let mut c = [0u64; 5];\n        for x in 0..5 {\n            c[x] = state[x] ^ state[x + 5] ^ state[x + 10] ^ state[x + 15] ^ state[x + 20];\n        }\n        let mut d = [0u64; 5];\n        for x in 0..5 {\n            d[x] = c[(x + 4) % 5] ^ rotl(c[(x + 1) % 5], 1);\n        }\n        for x in 0..5 {\n            for y in 0..5 {\n                state[x + 5 * y] ^= d[x];\n            }\n        }\n        // Rho + Pi (matches the canonical Keccak reference C): the rotated lane\n        // A[col=x][row=y] lands at B[col=y][row=(2x+3y)%5], i.e. index\n        // `y + 5*((2*x+3*y)%5)`.\n        let mut b = [0u64; 25];\n        for x in 0..5 {\n            for y in 0..5 {\n                b[y + 5 * ((2 * x + 3 * y) % 5)] = rotl(state[x + 5 * y], RHO[x + 5 * y]);\n            }\n        }\n        // Chi\n        for y in 0..5 {\n            let row = &b[5 * y..5 * y + 5];\n            for x in 0..5 {\n                state[x + 5 * y] = row[x] ^ ((!row[(x + 1) % 5]) & row[(x + 2) % 5]);\n            }\n        }\n        // Iota\n        state[0] ^= RC[round];\n    }\n}\n\n/// Sponge over Keccak-f[1600]. `rate` is the block size in bytes (168 for SHAKE128,\n/// 136 for SHAKE256). `pad` is the domain suffix byte (0x1f for SHAKE, 0x06 for SHA-3).\n/// Squeezes exactly `out.len()` bytes.\nfn sponge(rate: usize, pad: u8, input: &[u8], out: &mut [u8]) {\n    let mut state = [0u64; 25];\n    // pad10*1 with the SHAKE/SHA-3 domain suffix. The suffix byte (0x1f for SHAKE,\n    // 0x06 for SHA-3) already contains the pad10*1 leading `1` as its LSB; we then\n    // zero-fill to the last byte of the rate block and set the trailing `1` (0x80).\n    let mut data = input.to_vec();\n    data.push(pad);\n    while data.len() % rate != rate - 1 {\n        data.push(0x00);\n    }\n    data.push(0x80);\n    // Absorb (rate is a multiple of 8, so lane-aligned).\n    for chunk in data.chunks(rate) {\n        for (j, byte) in chunk.iter().enumerate() {\n            let lane = j / 8;\n            let shift = (j % 8) * 8;\n            state[lane] ^= u64::from(*byte) << shift;\n        }\n        keccak_f(&mut state);\n    }\n    // Squeeze\n    let mut produced = 0;\n    while produced < out.len() {\n        for lane in 0..rate / 8 {\n            let bytes = state[lane].to_le_bytes();\n            for (k, b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {\n                let idx = produced + lane * 8 + k;\n                if idx < out.len() {\n                    out[idx] = *b;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        produced += rate;\n        if produced < out.len() {\n            keccak_f(&mut state);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// SHAKE128 (rate 168, pad 0x1f). Squeezes `out.len()` bytes.\npub fn shake128(input: &[u8], out: &mut [u8]) {\n    sponge(168, 0x1f, input, out);\n}\n\n/// SHAKE256 (rate 136, pad 0x1f). Squeezes `out.len()` bytes.\npub fn shake256(input: &[u8], out: &mut [u8]) {\n    sponge(136, 0x1f, input, out);\n}\n\n/// SHAKE256 XOF: absorbs `seed || i || j`, squeezes exactly `len` bytes.\n/// Used by ML-KEM uniform sampling (FIPS 203 §2 / Algorithm 10).\npub fn shake256_xof(seed: &[u8; 32], i: u8, j: u8, len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(34);\n    input.extend_from_slice(seed);\n    input.push(i);\n    input.push(j);\n    let mut out = vec![0u8; len];\n    sponge(136, 0x1f, &input, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// SHA3-256 (rate 136, pad 0x06). Squeezes 32 bytes.\npub fn sha3_256(input: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n    sponge(136, 0x06, input, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// SHA3-512 (rate 72, pad 0x06). Squeezes 64 bytes.\npub fn sha3_512(input: &[u8]) -> [u8; 64] {\n    let mut out = [0u8; 64];\n    sponge(72, 0x06, input, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// G(X) = SHAKE256(X, 64) (FIPS 203 §2).\npub fn xof_g(input: &[u8]) -> [u8; 64] {\n    let mut out = [0u8; 64];\n    sponge(136, 0x1f, input, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// H(X) = SHA3-256(X) (FIPS 203 §2).\npub fn xof_h(input: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n    sponge(136, 0x06, input, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// J(z, c) = SHAKE256(z || c, 32) — placeholder for future signing schemes.\npub fn xof_j(z: &[u8], c: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(z.len() + c.len());\n    input.extend_from_slice(z);\n    input.extend_from_slice(c);\n    let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n    sponge(136, 0x1f, &input, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// PRF(s, b, len) = SHAKE256(s || b, len) (FIPS 203 §2, seed-expansion).\npub fn prf(s: &[u8; 32], b: u8, len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(33);\n    input.extend_from_slice(s);\n    input.push(b);\n    let mut out = vec![0u8; len];\n    sponge(136, 0x1f, &input, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // Parse a hex string literal into a fixed array (test helper).\n    fn hex<const L: usize>(s: &str) -> [u8; L] {\n        let s = s.trim();\n        assert_eq!(s.len(), L * 2, "hex length mismatch");\n        let mut out = [0u8; L];\n        let bytes = s.as_bytes();\n        for i in 0..L {\n            let hi = (bytes[2 * i] as char).to_digit(16).unwrap();\n            let lo = (bytes[2 * i + 1] as char).to_digit(16).unwrap();\n            out[i] = ((hi << 4) | lo) as u8;\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    // FIPS 202 known-answer tests (empty-string anchors are unambiguous).\n    // SHAKE256("") = 46b9dd2b0ba88d13233b3feb743eeb243fcd52ea62b81b82b50c27646ed5762f\n    #[test]\n    fn kat_shake256_empty() {\n        let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n        shake256(&[], &mut out);\n        assert_eq!(\n            out,\n            [\n                0x46, 0xb9, 0xdd, 0x2b, 0x0b, 0xa8, 0x8d, 0x13, 0x23, 0x3b, 0x3f, 0xeb, 0x74, 0x3e,\n                0xeb, 0x24, 0x3f, 0xcd, 0x52, 0xea, 0x62, 0xb8, 0x1b, 0x82, 0xb5, 0x0c, 0x27, 0x64,\n                0x6e, 0xd5, 0x76, 0x2f\n            ]\n        );\n    }\n\n    // SHAKE128("") first 16 bytes = 7f9c2ba4e88f827d616045507605853e\n    #[test]\n    fn kat_shake128_empty() {\n        let mut out = [0u8; 16];\n        shake128(&[], &mut out);\n        assert_eq!(\n            out,\n            [\n                0x7f, 0x9c, 0x2b, 0xa4, 0xe8, 0x8f, 0x82, 0x7d, 0x61, 0x60, 0x45, 0x50, 0x76, 0x05,\n                0x85, 0x3e\n            ]\n        );\n    }\n\n    // SHAKE256("abc") = 483366601360a8771c6863080cc4114d8db44530f8f1e1ee4f94ea37e78b5739\n    #[test]\n    fn kat_shake256_abc() {\n        let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n        shake256(b"abc", &mut out);\n        assert_eq!(\n            out,\n            [\n                0x48, 0x33, 0x66, 0x60, 0x13, 0x60, 0xa8, 0x77, 0x1c, 0x68, 0x63, 0x08, 0x0c, 0xc4,\n                0x11, 0x4d, 0x8d, 0xb4, 0x45, 0x30, 0xf8, 0xf1, 0xe1, 0xee, 0x4f, 0x94, 0xea, 0x37,\n                0xe7, 0x8b, 0x57, 0x39\n            ]\n        );\n    }\n\n    // SHA3 KAT (FIPS 202) — anchors the newly-added SHA3-256/512; the old KEM\n    // only used SHAKE, so a SHA3 bug would have been invisible until now.\n    #[test]\n    fn kem_debug_sha3_kat() {\n        let s3_256_empty = sha3_256(&[]);\n        assert_eq!(\n            s3_256_empty,\n            hex::<32>("a7ffc6f8bf1ed76651c14756a061d662f580ff4de43b49fa82d80a4b80f8434a")\n        );\n        let s3_512_empty = sha3_512(&[]);\n        assert_eq!(\n            s3_512_empty,\n            hex::<64>("a69f73cca23a9ac5c8b567dc185a756e97c982164fe25859e0d1dcc1475c80a615b2123af1f5f94c11e3e9402c3ac558f500199d95b6d3e301758586281dcd26")\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Item 7 KEYSTONE (enforced/closing form): cross-copy equivalence of the two\n    /// hand-rolled Keccak-f[1600] permutations, proven as a FINITE INDEX-MAP comparison.\n    ///\n    /// The full-state `kani_proofs_strong::proof_keccak_copies_equivalent` (below) is the\n    /// STRONGEST form (all 2^1600 states, machine-checked) but its 24-round bit-blast\n    /// exceeds the standard CI budget (measured: did not close in 25 min) — the exact risk\n    /// the blueprint's §3.1 fallback ladder anticipated. This is the shipped fallback rung,\n    /// recorded here rather than silently claiming the strong form.\n    ///\n    /// It closes because the two copies are TEXTUALLY IDENTICAL in θ, χ, ι and differ ONLY\n    /// in the ρ+π step. So equivalence reduces to three finite checks over the real\n    /// constants of both modules, which — together with `proof_rotl_contract` (rotl ≡\n    /// rotate_left, machine-checked over all u64) and the existing FIPS-202 KATs pinning\n    /// both copies to correct output — establishes full-permutation equivalence:\n    ///   (ι) the 24 round constants are identical;\n    ///   (ρ) the rotation offsets are identical: copy A reads `RHO[x+5y]`, copy B `R[x][y]`;\n    ///   (π) the destination index is identical: A writes `y+5·((2x+3y)%5)`, B writes\n    ///       `dest_x+5·dest_y` with `dest_x=y, dest_y=(2x+3y)%5` = the same lane.\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_keccak_copies_equivalence_index_map() {\n        use crate::event_log::{KECCAK_R, KECCAK_RC};\n        // (ι) round constants identical — the only per-round constant either copy uses.\n        assert_eq!(\n            RC, KECCAK_RC,\n            "iota round constants diverge between the two copies"\n        );\n        for x in 0..5usize {\n            for y in 0..5usize {\n                // (ρ) rotation offset: copy A's flat RHO[x+5y] == copy B's 2D R[x][y].\n                assert_eq!(\n                    RHO[x + 5 * y],\n                    KECCAK_R[x][y],\n                    "rho offset diverges at lane ({x},{y})"\n                );\n                // (π) destination lane: A's `y + 5*((2x+3y)%5)` == B's `dest_x + 5*dest_y`.\n                let a_dest = y + 5 * ((2 * x + 3 * y) % 5);\n                let (dest_x, dest_y) = (y, (2 * x + 3 * y) % 5);\n                let b_dest = dest_x + 5 * dest_y;\n                assert_eq!(a_dest, b_dest, "pi destination diverges at lane ({x},{y})");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Item 7 (Bucket-B, native): sponge absorb/pad/squeeze index arithmetic depends on\n    /// `len`/`rate`, not byte values, so exercising the boundary lengths (0, rate-1, rate,\n    /// rate+1, 2·rate) over every deployed (rate, pad) exhausts the input-INDEPENDENT\n    /// control flow — the same guarantee a bounded Kani harness would give, natively.\n    #[test]\n    fn sponge_boundary_lengths_panic_free() {\n        // (rate, pad): SHAKE128, SHAKE256, SHA3-256, SHA3-512.\n        for &(rate, pad) in &[(168usize, 0x1fu8), (136, 0x1f), (136, 0x06), (72, 0x06)] {\n            for &len in &[0usize, rate - 1, rate, rate + 1, 2 * rate] {\n                let input = vec![0xA5u8; len];\n                let mut out = [0u8; 40]; // spans >1 squeeze block for rate 72\n                sponge(rate, pad, &input, &mut out); // must not panic / OOB\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Item 7 (space-grade roadmap §C): Kani bounded-model-checker proofs ──────────\n// Compiled ONLY under `cfg(kani)` (injected by `cargo kani`); every non-Kani Kani proves,\n// for ALL inputs within the stated bounds: no panic, no arithmetic overflow, no\n// out-of-bounds access, no assertion violation — at the Rust MIR level. It does NOT\n// prove codegen-level constant-time/timing (that stays with the dudect gate + the\n// item-14 assembly spot-check). See BLUEPRINT-ITEM-07-kani-wiring-2026-07-19.md §3.1.\n#[cfg(kani)]\nmod kani_proofs {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Contract the `RHO` table relies on: `rotl` is total for `n < 64` and equals\n    /// the stdlib `rotate_left` (including the `n == 0` guard at line 46).\n    #[kani::proof]\n    fn proof_rotl_contract() {\n        let x: u64 = kani::any();\n        let n: u32 = kani::any();\n        kani::assume(n < 64);\n        assert_eq!(rotl(x, n), x.rotate_left(n));\n    }\n\n    /// "Copy A" permutation is total on the whole 2^1600 state space: no panic, no\n    /// OOB in the θ/ρπ/χ `% 5` indexing, no overflow. Returns (ciphertext, shared_secret).\npub fn encaps_internal(pk: &[u8], m: &[u8; 32]) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {\n    let hek = sha3_256(pk);\n    let mut ginput = [0u8; 64];\n    ginput[..32].copy_from_slice(m);\n    ginput[32..].copy_from_slice(&hek);\n    let g = sha3_512(&ginput);\n    let mut k = [0u8; 32];\n    k.copy_from_slice(&g[0..32]);\n    let mut r = [0u8; 32];\n    r.copy_from_slice(&g[32..64]);\n    let ct = kpke_encrypt(pk, m, &r);\n    (ct.to_vec(), k.to_vec())\n}\n\n/// ML-KEM.Decaps_internal (FIPS 203 Algorithm 18) + consistency (implicit-rejection) gate.\n/// Returns the shared secret; if the ciphertext fails re-encryption consistency,\n/// the output is the implicit-rejection value derived from the secret + ct, so a\n/// tampered ciphertext NEVER yields the true shared secret.\npub fn decaps_internal(sk: &[u8], c: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let s_bytes = &sk[..K * 384];\n    let pk = &sk[K * 384..K * 384 + PK_LEN];\n    let pkh = &sk[K * 384 + PK_LEN..K * 384 + PK_LEN + 32];\n    // Recover m' = K-PKE.Decrypt.\n    let mut c_fixed = [0u8; KEM768_CT_LEN];\n    c_fixed.copy_from_slice(&c[..KEM768_CT_LEN]);\n    let mprime = kpke_decrypt(s_bytes, &c_fixed);\n    // K' = G(m' || H(ek)); G = SHA3-512 (FIPS 203 §2), matching encaps_internal.\n    let mut ginput = [0u8; 64];\n    ginput[..32].copy_from_slice(&mprime);\n    ginput[32..].copy_from_slice(pkh);\n    let g = sha3_512(&ginput);\n    let kp = &g[..32];\n    let r: [u8; 32] = g[32..64].try_into().unwrap();\n    // Re-encrypt with (m', r) and check it equals c; on mismatch -> implicit reject.\n    let c_prime = kpke_encrypt(pk, &mprime, &r);\n    if c_prime != c_fixed {\n        // Implicit rejection: H(sk || c). (Data-independent enough for the\n        // red-line gate here; FIPS-203 §9.1 uses J(z,c)=SHAKE256 — P91.2 will\n        // tighten this once the ACVP gate is in place.)\n        return xof_h(&[sk, c].concat()).to_vec();\n    }\n    kp.to_vec()\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests. The new RED→GREEN falsifiers (P91.0 header gate + P91.1 ring/param/keygen\n// gates) sit alongside self-consistency round-trips. These are the module's OWN\n// tests — note P91.2 forbids treating "its own tests pass" as evidence of\n// FIPS-203 conformance; that requires external ACVP vectors.\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // P91.0 — grep-gate: a false FIPS-203 / "Upgrade path" claim must not be\n    // re-addable silently. RED before the header defusal, GREEN after.\n    #[test]\n    fn kem_header_no_false_fips_claim() {\n        let src = include_str!("kem.rs");\n        let has_false_claim = src.contains("FIPS 203")\n            || src.contains("FIPS-203")\n            || src.contains("Upgrade path: none needed");\n        let has_marker = src.contains("NOT FIPS-203");\n        assert!(\n            !has_false_claim || has_marker,\n            "kem.rs contains a false FIPS-203 claim without the NOT FIPS-203 marker"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // P91.1 — the defining negacyclic property: x^255 * x == -1 (i.e. x^256 == -1).\n    // RED under the old cyclic ring (which gave +1), GREEN after the fix.\n    #[test]\n    fn kem_negacyclic_wrap() {\n        let mut a = [0i32; N];\n        a[N - 1] = 1; // x^255\n        let mut b = [0i32; N];\n        b[1] = 1; // x\n        let r = poly_mul(&a, &b);\n        // x^255 * x = x^256 = -1 mod (x^256 + 1) => coefficient at index 0 is Q-1.\n        assert_eq!(r[0], Q - 1, "x^255 * x must equal -1 (negacyclic)");\n        for i in 1..N {\n            assert_eq!(r[i], 0, "only the constant term may be nonzero");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kem_eta1_is_two() {\n        assert_eq!(ETA1, 2, "ML-KEM-768 requires eta1 = 2 (was 3)");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kem_ct_len_is_1088() {\n        assert_eq!(\n            CT_LEN, 1088,\n            "ML-KEM-768 ciphertext is 32*(du*k+dv) = 1088 (was 1536)"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(KEM768_CT_LEN, 1088);\n    }\n\n    // P91.1 — two-seed FO keygen produces spec-shaped keys and consumes both seeds.\n    #[test]\n    fn kem_two_seed_keygen_matches_fips() {\n        let d = [7u8; 32];\n        let z = [99u8; 32];\n        let (ek, dk) = keygen_internal(&d, &z);\n        assert_eq!(ek.len(), KEM768_EK_LEN, "ek length");\n        assert_eq!(dk.len(), KEM768_DK_LEN, "dk length");\n        // FO seed z is stored in the last 32 bytes of the secret key (FIPS 203 §7.2).\n        assert_eq!(\n            &dk[KEM768_DK_LEN - 32..],\n            &z[..],\n            "FO seed z must be stored in dk"\n        );\n        // A different z must change the keypair (z is actually consumed).\n        let (_ek2, dk2) = keygen_internal(&d, &[100u8; 32]);\n        assert_ne!(dk, dk2, "changing z must change the secret key");\n\n        // Round-trip: encaps -> decaps recovers the shared secret.\n        let m = [42u8; 32];\n        let (c, k_send) = encaps_internal(&ek, &m);\n        assert_eq!(c.len(), KEM768_CT_LEN, "ciphertext length");\n        let k_recv = decaps_internal(&dk, &c);\n        assert_eq!(k_send, k_recv, "shared secret mismatch");\n    }\n\n    // Self-consistency round-trip (kept from the original suite, now in the correct ring).\n    #[test]\n    fn kem_self_consistency() {\n        let d = [7u8; 32];\n        let z = [1u8; 32];\n        let (pk, sk) = keygen_internal(&d, &z);\n        let m = [42u8; 32];\n        let (c, k_send) = encaps_internal(&pk, &m);\n        let k_recv = decaps_internal(&sk, &c);\n        assert_eq!(k_send, k_recv, "shared secret mismatch");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kem_tamper_red_gate() {\n        let d = [9u8; 32];\n        let z = [2u8; 32];\n        let (pk, sk) = keygen_internal(&d, &z);\n        let m = [1u8; 32];\n        let (c, _k) = encaps_internal(&pk, &m);\n        let mut ct = c.clone();\n        ct[10] ^= 0xFF;\n        let k_tampered = decaps_internal(&sk, &ct);\n        let k_clean = decaps_internal(&sk, &c);\n        assert_ne!(\n            k_tampered, k_clean,\n            "tampered ct must not yield clean secret"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kem_soak_random_seeds() {\n        for s in 0u8..50 {\n            let d = [s; 32];\n            let z = [s.wrapping_mul(13).wrapping_add(5); 32];\n            let (pk, sk) = keygen_internal(&d, &z);\n            let m = [s.wrapping_mul(7).wrapping_add(3); 32];\n            let (c, k_send) = encaps_internal(&pk, &m);\n            let k_recv = decaps_internal(&sk, &c);\n            assert_eq!(k_send, k_recv, "roundtrip mismatch at seed {s}");\n            let mut ct = c.clone();\n            let idx = (s as usize) % ct.len();\n            ct[idx] ^= 0x01;\n            let k_t = decaps_internal(&sk, &ct);\n            assert_ne!(k_t, k_recv, "tamper not detected at seed {s}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── Item 7 (space-grade roadmap §C): native EXHAUSTIVE ML-KEM ring arithmetic ──\n    // Per RESEARCH-NATIVE-KANI-REPLACEMENT-FEASIBILITY-2026-07-19.md §2: every ML-KEM\n    // arithmetic contract is either a bounded-domain exhaustion (the csr.rs/65536-pair\n    // idiom) or a modulo-by-positive-Q inspection — the identical "for all inputs"\n    // guarantee as a Kani harness, zero toolchain dependency, in the fast hardening-gate.\n\n    /// `red` total, over the i64 edge cases (i64::MIN — the only true overflow risk since\n    /// `%` never overflows on a positive divisor — plus ±Q boundaries, 0, and a dense\n    /// sweep): result ∈ [0, Q) and ≡ x (mod Q), never panics. Universality over all 2^64\n    /// i64 is a 3-line inspection (`x % Q` total for Q>0; the `r<0` fixup lands in [1,Q));\n    /// this pins the edges that inspection reasons about.\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_red_total_edges_and_sweep() {\n        let check = |x: i64| {\n            let r = red(x);\n            assert!(r >= 0 && r < Q, "red({x}) = {r} not in [0,Q)");\n            // ≡ x (mod Q): (r - x) divisible by Q, computed in i128 to avoid overflow.\n            assert_eq!(\n                (r as i128 - x as i128).rem_euclid(Q as i128),\n                0,\n                "red({x}) wrong residue"\n            );\n        };\n        check(i64::MIN);\n        check(i64::MAX);\n        check(0);\n        for k in -5i64..=5 {\n            check(k * Q as i64);\n            check(k * Q as i64 + 1);\n            check(k * Q as i64 - 1);\n        }\n        // Dense sweep across a multi-period window straddling zero.\n        let mut x = -200_000i64;\n        while x <= 200_000 {\n            check(x);\n            x += 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// EXHAUSTIVE over all coefficient pairs (a, b) ∈ [0, Q)² (~1.1e7): the `poly_add`/\n    /// `poly_sub` per-element body `red(a ± b)` never overflows i32 and yields a value in\n    /// [0, Q) congruent to a ± b. This is the 65536-pair idiom, slightly larger.\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_exhaustive_poly_addsub_body() {\n        for a in 0..Q {\n            for b in 0..Q {\n                let s = red(a + b);\n                assert!(s >= 0 && s < Q);\n                assert_eq!(s, (a + b) % Q);\n                let d = red(a - b);\n                assert!(d >= 0 && d < Q);\n                assert_eq!(d, ((a - b) % Q + Q) % Q);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// EXHAUSTIVE poly_mul BODY LEMMA (NOT a full-function proof — the 65,536-iteration\n    /// induction is documented; the machine proves the step). The body's behavior depends\n    /// only on (r_val, term) ∈ [0, Q)² (~1.1e7), since `term = (ai·bj) % Q` is the sole\n    /// path ai,bj feed. Both the in-range accumulate branch and the negacyclic-wrap branch\n    /// (kem.rs:108-116) preserve the loop invariant `r[k] ∈ [0, Q)` with no i64 overflow.\n    /// The `ai·bj` product itself is ≤ (Q-1)² ≈ 1.1e7 « i64::MAX (checked on the corners).\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_exhaustive_poly_mul_body_lemma() {\n        // Product cannot overflow i64 anywhere in the domain (corner check).\n        let maxprod = (Q as i64 - 1) * (Q as i64 - 1);\n        assert!(maxprod < i64::MAX && maxprod < (1i64 << 62));\n        for r_val in 0..Q {\n            for term in 0..Q {\n                // in-range branch: r[idx] = (r_val + term) % Q\n                let add = ((r_val as i64 + term as i64) % Q as i64) as i32;\n                assert!(add >= 0 && add < Q);\n                // negacyclic-wrap branch: r[idx2] = (r_val - term) % Q, then += Q if < 0\n                let mut sub = ((r_val as i64 - term as i64) % Q as i64) as i32;\n                if sub < 0 {\n                    sub += Q;\n                }\n                assert!(sub >= 0 && sub < Q, "wrap branch left {sub} outside [0,Q)");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// EXHAUSTIVE over x ∈ [0, Q) × the deployed widths d ∈ {1, 4, 10, 12} (~13.3k):\n    /// `compress`/`decompress` are panic-/overflow-free with in-range outputs.\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_exhaustive_compress_decompress_bounds() {\n        for &d in &[1usize, 4, 10, 12] {\n            let bound = 1i32 << d;\n            for x in 0..Q {\n                let c = compress(d, x);\n                assert!(\n                    c >= 0 && c < bound,\n                    "compress({d},{x}) = {c} out of [0,2^d)"\n                );\n                let dec = decompress(d, c);\n                assert!(\n                    dec >= 0 && dec < Q,\n                    "decompress({d},{c}) = {dec} out of [0,Q)"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// `byte_encode`/`byte_decode` round-trip at the deployed widths with correctly-sized\n    /// buffers: index arithmetic stays in bounds (the genuine OOB risk class on\n    /// deserialization), and decode inverts encode within the domain. Widths, not byte\n    /// values, drive the indices (research §2), so exhausting the widths suffices.\n    #[test]\n    fn item7_byte_codec_bounds_and_roundtrip() {\n        for &d in &[1usize, 4, 10, 12] {\n            let mut poly = [0i32; N];\n            for (i, c) in poly.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n                *c = ((i * 7 + 3) as i32) % (1 << d); // in-domain sample coefficients\n            }\n            let mut buf = vec![0u8; 32 * d]; // exactly N*d bits\n            byte_encode(d, &poly, &mut buf); // must not OOB\n            let mut back = [0i32; N];\n            byte_decode(d, &buf, &mut back); // must not OOB\n            assert_eq!(poly, back, "byte codec round-trip broke at d={d}");\n        }\n    }\n}\n	10142	-1	-1		c2563b6e580dafa58323c8c15373db036d56b7ac0d53f48ee05f827ac3fea1475955a2c2adc8c8d7a251546935bdd2ae8a613d24dd680c68b66a3e2eff06f88ed79e704127bef2291191321af6bb9870d0d8c82e49bccc0d50c238b458898544e422f296a4c912099a7a8a565b5c2b546db54c205fab8cb480a1757431303571
```

## 10171 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/root_delegation.rs · LongTerm

Summary: root_delegation · 192 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/root_delegation.rs	root_delegation · 192 lines	//! pq/root_delegation.rs — R-3 `RootDelegationPolicy` (Layer D consensus / trust / capability).\n//!\n//! Per operator ruling A (recorded 2026-07-18, `DECISIONS.md` D10):\n//!   * `OperatorSigned`  — the operator's ML-DSA-65 root key is the sole sovereign root.\n//!   * `Overlay { depth }` — at most ONE delegation hop below the operator root is permitted\n//!                           (`depth <= 1` by construction; deeper chains are rejected).\n//!   * `Deferred`        — the Web-Of-Trust / FirstContactQr branch. The variant exists (type\n//!                           level) but its verify path is NOT wired in v1: it returns a typed\n//!                           `Unsupported` error rather than silently doing anything.\n//!\n//! This module lives under `pq/` precisely so it can reach the KAT-gated, byte-exact\n//! `crate::pq::dsa` ML-DSA-65 primitive WITHOUT pulling `pq` into the serde-free native\n//! build graph (the canonical order/money core stays feature-independent; `RootDelegationPolicy`\n//! is part of the opt-in mesh/transport identity seam, exactly like the rest of `pq`).\n//!\n//! No network, no clock, no I/O. `verify_root` is a pure predicate over a signature + pubkey.\n\nuse crate::pq::dsa::{keygen, sign, verify, MlDsa65Pk, MlDsa65Sig, MlDsa65Sk};\n\n/// Configured root-delegation model. Fail-closed by construction: until the operator\n/// selects a real policy, nothing delegates.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum RootDelegationPolicy {\n    /// Operator-signed root cert(s): offline, audited, pinned. The sovereign floor.\n    OperatorSigned,\n    /// An overlay delegation chain rooted at the operator's ML-DSA root, allowed to fan\n    /// out by at most `depth` hops below the operator. `depth` MUST be `<= 1` (exactly ONE\n    /// overlay hop per the operator ruling). Construct via [`RootDelegationPolicy::overlay`]\n    /// to enforce the invariant; a `depth > 1` is rejected at construction time.\n    Overlay { depth: u8 },\n    /// Deferred branch (Web-Of-Trust / FirstContactQr). Exists at the type level (so the\n    /// ruling's other options are representable) but is NOT wired in v1: `verify_root` returns\n    /// `RootVerifyError::Unsupported` for it. Never guessed, never silently allowed.\n    Deferred,\n}\n\nimpl RootDelegationPolicy {\n    /// Construct an `Overlay` policy, enforcing the invariant `depth <= 1`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err(RootVerifyError::MaxDepthExceeded)` if `depth > 1`, so a double-hop (or\n    /// deeper) overlay can never be represented. This is the construction-time gate that makes\n    /// the "exactly ONE overlay hop" rule unrepresentable-at-the-boundary rather than a runtime\n    /// check that could be bypassed.\n    pub fn overlay(depth: u8) -> Result<RootDelegationPolicy, RootVerifyError> {\n        if depth > 1 {\n            return Err(RootVerifyError::MaxDepthExceeded(depth));\n        }\n        Ok(RootDelegationPolicy::Overlay { depth })\n    }\n\n    /// Verify a root attestation under this policy, using the kernel's EXISTING ML-DSA-65\n    /// primitive (FIPS 204, KAT-gated, byte-exact vs NIST ACVP vectors — NO invented crypto).\n    ///\n    /// * `OperatorSigned` — `msg` MUST verify against `op_root_pk` (the operator's ML-DSA root\n    ///   public key). Returns `Ok(())` on a valid signature, `RootVerifyError::BadRootSignature`\n    /// otherwise.\n    /// * `Overlay { depth }` — `msg` MUST verify against `op_root_pk` as well (the overlay chain\n    ///   is still rooted at the operator; `depth` is the permitted fan-out hops, already bounded\n    ///   to `<= 1` by [`RootDelegationPolicy::overlay`]). Same verification as `OperatorSigned`;\n    ///   the `depth` bound is enforced at construction, so any `Overlay` value here is already\n    ///   admissible.\n    /// * `Deferred` — not wired in v1. Returns `Err(RootVerifyError::Unsupported)` every time.\n    pub fn verify_root(\n        &self,\n        msg: &[u8],\n        sig: &MlDsa65Sig,\n        op_root_pk: &MlDsa65Pk,\n    ) -> Result<(), RootVerifyError> {\n        match self {\n            RootDelegationPolicy::OperatorSigned => {\n                if verify(op_root_pk, msg, sig) {\n                    Ok(())\n                } else {\n                    Err(RootVerifyError::BadRootSignature)\n                }\n            }\n            RootDelegationPolicy::Overlay { depth: _ } => {\n                // The overlay chain is still rooted at the operator's ML-DSA key; the hop bound\n                // is enforced at construction. Verification is identical to OperatorSigned.\n                if verify(op_root_pk, msg, sig) {\n                    Ok(())\n                } else {\n                    Err(RootVerifyError::BadRootSignature)\n                }\n            }\n            RootDelegationPolicy::Deferred => Err(RootVerifyError::Unsupported),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Why a root attestation verification failed (or was refused).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum RootVerifyError {\n    /// The ML-DSA-65 signature over the root attestation did not verify against the operator\n    /// root public key.\n    BadRootSignature,\n    /// The `Deferred` policy variant is not wired in v1 and must not be used to authorize anything.\n    Unsupported,\n    /// Construction-time invariant violation: an `Overlay` with `depth > 1` (more than ONE\n    /// delegation hop below the operator root) is refused and never represented.\n    MaxDepthExceeded(u8),\n}\n\n/// Convenience: produce an operator-rooted ML-DSA-65 signature over `msg` from the operator\n/// root secret key. Used by tests and by the (future) signing path; deterministic in FIPS mode\n/// when `rnd` is fixed (we pass all-zeros here — caller may supply fresh entropy for production).\npub fn sign_root(op_root_sk: &MlDsa65Sk, msg: &[u8]) -> MlDsa65Sig {\n    let rnd = [0u8; 32];\n    sign(op_root_sk, msg, &rnd)\n}\n\n/// Deterministically derive an operator root keypair from a 32-byte seed.\npub fn operator_root_keygen(seed: &[u8; 32]) -> (MlDsa65Pk, MlDsa65Sk) {\n    keygen(seed)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn op_keypair() -> (MlDsa65Pk, MlDsa65Sk) {\n        // Deterministic seed; this is a test-only root, never a production key.\n        let seed = [7u8; 32];\n        operator_root_keygen(&seed)\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn operator_signed_root_accepted() {\n        let (pk, sk) = op_keypair();\n        let msg = b"root-attestation: operator-signed genesis";\n        let sig = sign_root(&sk, msg);\n        let policy = RootDelegationPolicy::OperatorSigned;\n        assert_eq!(policy.verify_root(msg, &sig, &pk), Ok(()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn single_overlay_hop_depth_1_accepted() {\n        let (pk, sk) = op_keypair();\n        let msg = b"root-attestation: overlay anchor #1";\n        let sig = sign_root(&sk, msg);\n        // depth == 1 is the exactly-one-hop overlay allowed by the operator ruling.\n        let policy = RootDelegationPolicy::overlay(1).expect("depth=1 must construct");\n        assert_eq!(policy.verify_root(msg, &sig, &pk), Ok(()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn double_hop_overlay_depth_2_rejected() {\n        // A depth-2 overlay (more than ONE delegation hop below the operator root) is the\n        // operator-ruling violation. The invariant is enforced at CONSTRUCTION so the bad state\n        // is unrepresentable: `overlay(2)` returns Err and no `RootDelegationPolicy` value with\n        // depth>1 can ever reach `verify_root`. This is the fail-closed boundary — callers must\n        // construct overlays via `overlay()`, never via the raw variant.\n        assert_eq!(\n            RootDelegationPolicy::overlay(2),\n            Err(RootVerifyError::MaxDepthExceeded(2))\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn deferred_policy_is_unsupported() {\n        let (pk, sk) = op_keypair();\n        let msg = b"root-attestation: web-of-trust (deferred)";\n        let sig = sign_root(&sk, msg);\n        let policy = RootDelegationPolicy::Deferred;\n        assert_eq!(\n            policy.verify_root(msg, &sig, &pk),\n            Err(RootVerifyError::Unsupported)\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn operator_signed_rejects_tampered_message() {\n        let (pk, sk) = op_keypair();\n        let sig = sign_root(&sk, b"root-attestation: legitimate");\n        let policy = RootDelegationPolicy::OperatorSigned;\n        // Same signature, different message -> must NOT verify.\n        assert_eq!(\n            policy.verify_root(b"root-attestation: forged", &sig, &pk),\n            Err(RootVerifyError::BadRootSignature)\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn depth_0_overlay_is_single_root_directly() {\n        // depth == 0 means "delegated directly by the operator, no further hop" — also allowed.\n        let (pk, sk) = op_keypair();\n        let msg = b"root-attestation: overlay depth 0";\n        let sig = sign_root(&sk, msg);\n        let policy = RootDelegationPolicy::overlay(0).expect("depth=0 must construct");\n        assert_eq!(policy.verify_root(msg, &sig, &pk), Ok(()));\n    }\n}\n	10172	-1	-1		ca3d3755dee321f7d205a2c3d154130d04ffbc46b02425dec3d3e8fdc567c6071a416d2396db72278142816b2381e0e88ee98d05d76a04e0b0653a0edd0c50ee47be7eb8676ec891d9c32810537ee53090fc3c2aa5e4e8f8c286b3a1aa8b511ffdf0f77603cad6ef52c05e4f5a40cb3028f7400e5f4d8b87935b768f1b662379
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/hybrid.rs	hybrid · 197 lines	//! Hybrid KEM — X25519 (classical) + ML-KEM-768 (post-quantum), BOTH mandatory.\n//!\n//! Per D4 (money/transaction data): node-to-node transit must survive a future\n//! quantum adversary. A hybrid combines a classical and a PQ scheme so the shared\n//! secret is secure iff AT LEAST ONE of them holds. The RED gate below FORBIDS a\n//! classical-only fallback: if either exchange fails to verify, the handshake is\n//! rejected outright (no downgrade).\n//!\n//! ponytail: X25519 uses the hand-rolled no_std `dowiz_core::pq::x25519` (Montgomery\n//! ladder over `p = 2^255 - 19`, KAT-gated vs RFC 7748 §6.1 and differential-tested\n//! vs `curve25519-dalek` in `kernel/src/pq/x25519.rs`). The combine KDF is\n//! SHAKE256(mlkem_ss || x_ss).\n//! ML-KEM correctness is KAT-gated in kem.rs.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::pq::keccak::shake256;\nuse crate::pq::kem;\nuse crate::pq::x25519::x25519;\n\n#[cfg(any(test, feature = "ct-gate"))]\nuse crate::ct_gate::ct_eq;\n\n/// A hybrid keypair: classical X25519 + post-quantum ML-KEM-768.\n/// `kem_seed` / `x_seed` are the caller-supplied entropy for keygen (RNG-free core).\npub struct HybridKeypair {\n    pub x_pk: [u8; 32],\n    pub x_sk: [u8; 32],\n    pub kem_pk: Vec<u8>,\n    pub kem_sk: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// Deterministically derive a hybrid keypair from caller entropy.\n/// `x_seed` and `kem_seed` SHOULD be independent draws (e.g. from entropy_mix).\npub fn hybrid_keygen(x_seed: &[u8; 32], kem_seed: &[u8; 32]) -> HybridKeypair {\n    // X25519: x_seed IS the scalar (it is clamped inside x25519 during use; for the\n    // static keypair we pre-clamp so the public key is consistent).\n    let mut sk = *x_seed;\n    sk[0] &= 248;\n    sk[31] &= 127;\n    sk[31] |= 64;\n    let base = [9u8; 32]; // curve25519 generator u-coordinate\n    let x_pk = x25519(&sk, &base);\n    // ML-KEM-768 KeyGen_internal takes the FIPS-203 two-seed (d, z) FO pair. We\n    // derive z from a deterministic transform of kem_seed so the deterministic\n    // test path stays reproducible; production callers should supply an\n    // independent z (P91.1 reconciled the one-seed keygen to (d, z)).\n    let kem_z = crate::pq::keccak::xof_h(kem_seed);\n    let (kem_pk, kem_sk) = kem::keygen_internal(kem_seed, &kem_z);\n    HybridKeypair {\n        x_pk,\n        x_sk: sk,\n        kem_pk,\n        kem_sk,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Hybrid ciphertext: carries the ML-KEM ciphertext, the ephemeral X25519 pubkey, and a\n/// key-confirmation tag binding both legs (see hybrid_decaps — this is the RED gate).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n#[cfg_attr(feature = "json-api", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]\npub struct HybridCiphertext {\n    pub kem_ct: Vec<u8>,\n    pub x_ephemeral: [u8; 32],\n    pub confirm: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Encapsulate toward `peer`: derive a shared secret requiring BOTH X25519 and ML-KEM.\n/// `m` is caller entropy for ML-KEM encapsulation; `eph_seed` is caller entropy for the\n/// ephemeral X25519 scalar. Returns (ciphertext, shared_secret_32).\npub fn hybrid_encaps(\n    peer: &HybridKeypair,\n    m: &[u8; 32],\n    eph_seed: &[u8; 32],\n) -> (HybridCiphertext, [u8; 32]) {\n    // PQ leg\n    let (kem_ct, mlkem_ss) = kem::encaps_internal(&peer.kem_pk, m);\n    // Classical leg: ephemeral X25519, shared = DH(eph_sk, peer.x_pk)\n    let mut eph = *eph_seed;\n    eph[0] &= 248;\n    eph[31] &= 127;\n    eph[31] |= 64;\n    let x_ephemeral = x25519(&eph, &[9u8; 32]);\n    let x_ss = x25519(&eph, &peer.x_pk);\n    // Combine: both secrets required; order-independent (sorted concat) so sender/recv\n    // agree regardless of which leg was computed first.\n    let (ss, tag) = combine(&mlkem_ss, &x_ss);\n    (\n        HybridCiphertext {\n            kem_ct,\n            x_ephemeral,\n            confirm: tag,\n        },\n        ss,\n    )\n}\n\n#[cfg(any(test, feature = "ct-gate"))]\nfn tag_eq(a: &[u8; 32], b: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n    ct_eq(a, b)\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(any(test, feature = "ct-gate")))]\nfn tag_eq(a: &[u8; 32], b: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n    // innovate: P91.2 — ct_eq wiring deferred (ct-gate feature not default).\n    // upgrade: enable ct-gate feature in production.\n    a == b\n}\n\n/// Decapsulate. RED gate: BOTH legs must succeed AND the key-confirmation tag must\n/// match. ML-KEM uses implicit rejection — on a tampered ct it returns H(sk||ct), a\n/// value the sender never produced, so `confirm` WILL NOT MATCH. The tag therefore\n/// catches tamper / wrong-peer / degraded-leg without leaking the secret. No classical-\n/// only fallback (D4).\npub fn hybrid_decaps(own: &HybridKeypair, ct: &HybridCiphertext) -> Result<[u8; 32], &'static str> {\n    let mlkem_ss = kem::decaps_internal(&own.kem_sk, &ct.kem_ct);\n    let x_ss = x25519(&own.x_sk, &ct.x_ephemeral);\n    let (ss, tag) = combine(&mlkem_ss, &x_ss);\n    if !tag_eq(&tag, &ct.confirm) {\n        return Err("key-confirmation-failed");\n    }\n    Ok(ss)\n}\n\n/// Combine the two leg secrets into (shared_secret, confirmation_tag).\n/// ss = SHAKE256(SHAKE256(mlkem||x || x||mlkem)); tag = SHAKE256(ss) — the tag lets the\n/// receiver detect a tampered/implicit-rejected ML-KEM leg without re-encapsulating.\nfn combine(mlkem_ss: &[u8], x_ss: &[u8; 32]) -> ([u8; 32], [u8; 32]) {\n    let mut a = mlkem_ss.to_vec();\n    a.extend_from_slice(x_ss);\n    let mut b = x_ss.to_vec();\n    b.extend_from_slice(mlkem_ss);\n    let mut combined = [0u8; 64];\n    let mut tmp = [0u8; 64];\n    shake256(&a, &mut tmp);\n    shake256(&tmp, &mut combined);\n    let mut ss = [0u8; 32];\n    ss.copy_from_slice(&combined[..32]);\n    let mut tag = [0u8; 32];\n    shake256(&ss, &mut tag);\n    (ss, tag)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_roundtrip_both_legs() {\n        let _ka = hybrid_keygen(&[1u8; 32], &[2u8; 32]);\n        let kb = hybrid_keygen(&[3u8; 32], &[4u8; 32]);\n        let (ct, ssa) = hybrid_encaps(&kb, &[5u8; 32], &[6u8; 32]);\n        let ssb = hybrid_decaps(&kb, &ct).expect("decaps must succeed");\n        assert_eq!(ssa, ssb, "shared secrets must match");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_tampered_kem_ct_rejected() {\n        let _ka = hybrid_keygen(&[1u8; 32], &[2u8; 32]);\n        let kb = hybrid_keygen(&[3u8; 32], &[4u8; 32]);\n        let (mut ct, _ssa) = hybrid_encaps(&kb, &[5u8; 32], &[6u8; 32]);\n        ct.kem_ct[0] ^= 0xFF; // corrupt the PQ leg\n        assert!(\n            hybrid_decaps(&kb, &ct).is_err(),\n            "tampered KEM ct must be rejected"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_wrong_peer_rejected() {\n        let _ka = hybrid_keygen(&[1u8; 32], &[2u8; 32]);\n        let kb = hybrid_keygen(&[3u8; 32], &[4u8; 32]);\n        let kc = hybrid_keygen(&[7u8; 32], &[8u8; 32]);\n        let (ct, _ssa) = hybrid_encaps(&kb, &[5u8; 32], &[6u8; 32]);\n        // kc is NOT the intended recipient; X25519 DH will not match, ML-KEM won't either.\n        assert!(\n            hybrid_decaps(&kc, &ct).is_err(),\n            "wrong peer must be rejected"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_no_classical_fallback() {\n        // Even if we could (we can't construct one here without a broken X25519), the\n        // gate forbids a classical-only path: a zero x_ephemeral yields all-zero x_ss.\n        let kb = hybrid_keygen(&[3u8; 32], &[4u8; 32]);\n        let ct = HybridCiphertext {\n            kem_ct: kem::encaps_internal(&kb.kem_pk, &[9u8; 32]).0,\n            x_ephemeral: [0u8; 32],\n            confirm: [0u8; 32],\n        };\n        assert!(\n            hybrid_decaps(&kb, &ct).is_err(),\n            "degenerate classical leg rejected"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	10186	-1	-1		9bc66fdc8e2d61a7c79f04a5c753722c8f96a0dfe751f5aeee779646d0d4e2c060333da3d4cd68c7864889eb0da58aaa8af83117db290e6892f1321ed6846d0efadcf75124b2d721d38333225dbaa8c8547b743f2dc863ed1886f0f4c3ddf5123d12ebd658eb13a9db4a939f33c4ffb85d3ad4246fb9ad0c11ebd4fc491f36da
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/volume.rs	volume · 378 lines	//! At-rest AES-256-GCM volume crypto — P2 (hybrid KEM wrap + ML-DSA envelope).\n//!\n//! Threat model (MANIFESTO / D4): data stored on disk / at rest in a node's\n//! custody must be confidential against a future quantum adversary. We therefore\n//! do NOT store a raw AES volume key. Instead we use a KEM-DEM construction:\n//!\n//!   1. The caller supplies a fresh 32-byte volume key `vk` (RNG-free core, C10).\n//!   2. The volume key is WRAPPED (encrypted) to the recipient node's *hybrid*\n//!      public key. Concretely: `hybrid_encaps` yields a shared secret `ss`\n//!      (X25519 + ML-KEM-768, BOTH mandatory); the data-encryption key is\n//!      `dk = KDF(ss)`; the volume key is sealed as `AES-256-GCM(vk, dk)`.\n//!      Only the holder of the recipient's hybrid secret key can recover `ss`,\n//!      hence only they can unwrap `vk`.\n//!   3. The plaintext blob is AES-256-GCM-encrypted under `vk`.\n//!   4. The whole `VolumeSeal` (hybrid wrap + wrapped-vk + blob ciphertext +\n//!      nonces) is ML-DSA-65 signed via [`crate::pq::envelope::seal`] so the\n//!      at-rest artifact's integrity/authorship is provable (reuses the L1 seam).\n//!\n//! Opening requires (a) the recipient's hybrid secret key to recover `vk`\n//! (both KEM legs must verify — the RED gate), and (b) the ML-DSA signature.\n//!\n//! ponytail: AES-256-GCM is the hand-rolled no_std `dowiz_core::pq::aes_gcm`\n//! (KAT-gated + differential-tested vs the RustCrypto `aes-gcm` crate in\n//! `kernel/src/pq/aes_gcm.rs`). The volume key, nonces, and KEM entropy are all\n//! caller-supplied — no OS RNG is used anywhere. We do NOT touch money\n//! constants or the D0–D9 decision surface.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::pq::aes_gcm::Aes256Gcm;\nuse crate::pq::envelope::{self, SignedEnvelope};\nuse crate::pq::hybrid::{hybrid_decaps, hybrid_encaps, HybridCiphertext, HybridKeypair};\nuse crate::pq::keccak::shake256;\n\n/// AES-256-GCM requires a 32-byte (256-bit) content-encryption key.\npub const VOLUME_KEY_LEN: usize = 32;\n/// AES-GCM standard 96-bit (12-byte) nonce.\npub const NONCE_LEN: usize = 12;\n/// Caller-supplied entropy length for the hybrid encaps legs.\npub const ENC_ENTROPY_LEN: usize = 32;\n\n/// Errors for the at-rest volume operations.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum VolumeError {\n    /// Hybrid decapsulation failed: wrong recipient / tampered wrap / degraded leg.\n    WrapRejected,\n    /// AES-256-GCM decrypt failed: wrong key or tampered ciphertext.\n    DecryptFailed,\n    /// ML-DSA envelope verification failed (hash mismatch or bad signature).\n    Envelope(envelope::EnvelopeError),\n}\n\n/// The signed, at-rest artifact: a hybrid volume-key wrap + AES-GCM blob.\n///\n/// The volume key `vk` itself never appears in the clear — it is wrapped to the\n/// recipient via the hybrid KEM (field `wrapped`, which carries the hybrid\n/// shared-secret encaps) and then sealed under the derived DEM key (field\n/// `wrapped_vk`). `nonce` + `ciphertext` are the AES-256-GCM output of the\n/// plaintext under `vk`. The entire structure is ML-DSA-65 signed (field `seal`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n#[cfg_attr(feature = "json-api", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]\npub struct VolumeSeal {\n    /// Hybrid encaps of the shared secret `ss` to the recipient's hybrid pubkey.\n    pub wrapped: HybridCiphertext,\n    /// Nonce for the volume-key wrap (`AES-256-GCM(vk, dk)`).\n    pub wrap_nonce: [u8; NONCE_LEN],\n    /// Volume key `vk` sealed under the DEM key `dk = KDF(ss)`.\n    pub wrapped_vk: Vec<u8>,\n    /// AES-256-GCM nonce (12 bytes) for the blob encryption under `vk`.\n    pub nonce: [u8; NONCE_LEN],\n    /// AES-256-GCM ciphertext (includes the 16-byte GCM tag) of the plaintext.\n    pub ciphertext: Vec<u8>,\n    /// ML-DSA-65 envelope over the canonical wire bytes (`wire_bytes`).\n    pub seal: SignedEnvelope,\n}\n\nimpl VolumeSeal {\n    /// Canonical wire bytes signed by the ML-DSA envelope. Stable, length-prefixed\n    /// serialization of every integrity-relevant field (so sign/verify agree).\n    fn wire_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut v = Vec::new();\n        let kem_ct = &self.wrapped.kem_ct;\n        v.extend_from_slice(&(kem_ct.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        v.extend_from_slice(kem_ct);\n        v.extend_from_slice(&self.wrapped.x_ephemeral);\n        v.extend_from_slice(&self.wrapped.confirm);\n        v.extend_from_slice(&self.wrap_nonce);\n        v.extend_from_slice(&(self.wrapped_vk.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        v.extend_from_slice(&self.wrapped_vk);\n        v.extend_from_slice(&self.nonce);\n        v.extend_from_slice(&(self.ciphertext.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        v.extend_from_slice(&self.ciphertext);\n        v\n    }\n}\n\n/// Derive the 32-byte data-encryption key from the hybrid shared secret.\n/// `dk = SHAKE256(ss)` — a one-way KDF binding the data key to the KEM output.\nfn derive_dk(ss: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut dk = [0u8; 32];\n    shake256(ss, &mut dk);\n    dk\n}\n\n/// Seal a plaintext blob at rest for `recipient`.\n///\n/// * `vk`        — caller-supplied 32-byte volume key (RNG-free, C10).\n/// * `blob_nonce`— caller-supplied 12-byte AES-GCM nonce for the blob (NEVER reuse with `vk`).\n/// * `wrap_nonce`— caller-supplied 12-byte AES-GCM nonce for the volume-key wrap.\n/// * `eph_seed`  — caller entropy for the ephemeral X25519 leg.\n/// * `m`         — caller entropy for the ML-KEM encaps leg.\n/// * `signer_sk` — ML-DSA-65 signer secret key (seals integrity/authorship).\n/// * `sign_rnd`  — caller entropy for the ML-DSA signature.\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\npub fn seal_volume(\n    plaintext: &[u8],\n    recipient: &HybridKeypair,\n    vk: &[u8; VOLUME_KEY_LEN],\n    blob_nonce: &[u8; NONCE_LEN],\n    wrap_nonce: &[u8; NONCE_LEN],\n    eph_seed: &[u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n    m: &[u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n    signer_sk: &[u8],\n    sign_rnd: &[u8; envelope::ENTROPY_LEN],\n) -> VolumeSeal {\n    // 1. Hybrid-encapsulate to the recipient; derive the DEM wrapping key from the ss.\n    let (wrapped, ss) = hybrid_encaps(recipient, m, eph_seed);\n    let dk = derive_dk(&ss);\n\n    // 2. Wrap the volume key under the DEM key (the actual KEM "wrap").\n    let wrap_cipher = Aes256Gcm::new_from_slice(&dk).expect("dk is exactly 32 bytes");\n    let wrapped_vk = wrap_cipher.encrypt(wrap_nonce, vk.as_slice());\n\n    // 3. AES-256-GCM-encrypt the plaintext under the volume key.\n    let blob_cipher = Aes256Gcm::new_from_slice(vk).expect("vk is exactly 32 bytes");\n    let ciphertext = blob_cipher.encrypt(blob_nonce, plaintext);\n\n    // 4. Build the wire bytes and ML-DSA-sign the artifact.\n    let mut seal = VolumeSeal {\n        wrapped,\n        wrap_nonce: *wrap_nonce,\n        wrapped_vk,\n        nonce: *blob_nonce,\n        ciphertext,\n        seal: SignedEnvelope {\n            payload: Vec::new(),\n            content_hash: [0u8; envelope::HASH_LEN],\n            sig: Vec::new(),\n        },\n    };\n    let wire = seal.wire_bytes();\n    seal.seal = envelope::seal(&wire, signer_sk, sign_rnd);\n    seal\n}\n\n/// Open a [`VolumeSeal`] given the recipient's hybrid secret key and the\n/// signer's ML-DSA public key. Returns the recovered plaintext only if BOTH the\n/// hybrid wrap opens (RED gate) AND the ML-DSA envelope verifies.\npub fn open_volume(\n    seal: &VolumeSeal,\n    recipient_sk: &HybridKeypair,\n    signer_pk: &[u8],\n) -> Result<Vec<u8>, VolumeError> {\n    // (a) RED gate: recover the hybrid shared secret — BOTH KEM legs must verify;\n    //     the wrong recipient / tampered wrap / degraded-leg is rejected here.\n    let ss = hybrid_decaps(recipient_sk, &seal.wrapped).map_err(|_| VolumeError::WrapRejected)?;\n    let dk = derive_dk(&ss);\n\n    // (b) Unwrap the volume key under the DEM key. Fails if the wrap was not for us.\n    let wrap_cipher = Aes256Gcm::new_from_slice(&dk).map_err(|_| VolumeError::DecryptFailed)?;\n    let vk = wrap_cipher\n        .decrypt(&seal.wrap_nonce, seal.wrapped_vk.as_slice())\n        .map_err(|_| VolumeError::DecryptFailed)?;\n\n    // (c) Verify the ML-DSA envelope over the canonical wire bytes. envelope::open\n    //     checks the content_hash AND the ML-DSA signature, and we assert the\n    //     recovered wire equals our locally derived wire (defends against a\n    //     substituted envelope payload post-sign, belt-and-suspenders).\n    let wire = seal.wire_bytes();\n    let recovered_wire = envelope::open(&seal.seal, signer_pk).map_err(VolumeError::Envelope)?;\n    if recovered_wire != wire {\n        return Err(VolumeError::Envelope(envelope::EnvelopeError::HashMismatch));\n    }\n\n    // (d) AES-256-GCM-decrypt the blob under the recovered volume key.\n    let blob_cipher = Aes256Gcm::new_from_slice(&vk).map_err(|_| VolumeError::DecryptFailed)?;\n    blob_cipher\n        .decrypt(&seal.nonce, seal.ciphertext.as_slice())\n        .map_err(|_| VolumeError::DecryptFailed)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::pq::envelope;\n\n    /// Build a deterministic hybrid keypair from two fixed 32-byte seeds.\n    fn hk(x: u8, k: u8) -> HybridKeypair {\n        let xs = [x; 32];\n        let ks = [k; 32];\n        crate::pq::hybrid::hybrid_keygen(&xs, &ks)\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_seal_open_same_recipient() {\n        let recipient = hk(1, 2);\n        let (signer_pk, signer_sk) = envelope::new_identity(&[3u8; 32]);\n\n        let plaintext = b"at-rest order manifest: zone kyiv-7 / 12 pizzas";\n        let vk = [7u8; VOLUME_KEY_LEN];\n        let blob_nonce = [8u8; NONCE_LEN];\n        let wrap_nonce = [9u8; NONCE_LEN];\n\n        let seal = seal_volume(\n            plaintext,\n            &recipient,\n            &vk,\n            &blob_nonce,\n            &wrap_nonce,\n            &[4u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &[5u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &signer_sk,\n            &[6u8; envelope::ENTROPY_LEN],\n        );\n\n        // Sanity: the volume key is NOT stored in the clear.\n        assert_ne!(\n            seal.wrapped_vk,\n            vk.to_vec(),\n            "volume key must be wrapped, not plaintext"\n        );\n        assert_ne!(\n            seal.ciphertext,\n            plaintext.to_vec(),\n            "blob must be ciphertext"\n        );\n\n        let recovered = open_volume(&seal, &recipient, &signer_pk)\n            .expect("same recipient + valid signer must open");\n        assert_eq!(recovered, plaintext.to_vec());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_seal_uses_hybrid_wrap() {\n        // Confirm the wrap went through the hybrid KEM: a recipient built from the\n        // SAME seeds recovers the plaintext, while the volume key is derived end-to-end.\n        let recipient = hk(11, 12);\n        let (signer_pk, signer_sk) = envelope::new_identity(&[13u8; 32]);\n        let plaintext = b"confidential volume blob";\n        let seal = seal_volume(\n            plaintext,\n            &recipient,\n            &[14u8; VOLUME_KEY_LEN],\n            &[15u8; NONCE_LEN],\n            &[15u8; NONCE_LEN],\n            &[16u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &[17u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &signer_sk,\n            &[18u8; envelope::ENTROPY_LEN],\n        );\n        let recovered = open_volume(&seal, &recipient, &signer_pk).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(recovered, plaintext.to_vec());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_wrong_recipient_rejected() {\n        // Encapsulate the volume key to peer A, then try to open with peer B's\n        // hybrid key. hybrid_decaps MUST fail (both legs won't verify) → Err.\n        let peer_a = hk(20, 21);\n        let peer_b = hk(22, 23);\n        let (signer_pk, signer_sk) = envelope::new_identity(&[24u8; 32]);\n\n        let seal = seal_volume(\n            b"secret",\n            &peer_a, // wrapped to A\n            &[25u8; VOLUME_KEY_LEN],\n            &[26u8; NONCE_LEN],\n            &[26u8; NONCE_LEN],\n            &[27u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &[28u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &signer_sk,\n            &[29u8; envelope::ENTROPY_LEN],\n        );\n\n        let res = open_volume(&seal, &peer_b, &signer_pk); // B tries to open\n        assert_eq!(\n            res,\n            Err(VolumeError::WrapRejected),\n            "wrong recipient must fail"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_tampered_ciphertext_rejected() {\n        let recipient = hk(30, 31);\n        let (signer_pk, signer_sk) = envelope::new_identity(&[32u8; 32]);\n        let mut seal = seal_volume(\n            b"secret-blob",\n            &recipient,\n            &[33u8; VOLUME_KEY_LEN],\n            &[34u8; NONCE_LEN],\n            &[34u8; NONCE_LEN],\n            &[35u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &[36u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &signer_sk,\n            &[37u8; envelope::ENTROPY_LEN],\n        );\n        // Flip a byte in the blob ciphertext after signing (breaks AES-GCM tag AND\n        // the envelope content_hash). Opening must fail — never yield plaintext.\n        seal.ciphertext[0] ^= 0xFF;\n        let res = open_volume(&seal, &recipient, &signer_pk);\n        assert!(\n            res.is_err(),\n            "tampered ciphertext must be rejected: {:?}",\n            res\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_wrong_signer_rejected() {\n        let recipient = hk(40, 41);\n        let (_real_pk, signer_sk) = envelope::new_identity(&[42u8; 32]);\n        let (other_pk, _other_sk) = envelope::new_identity(&[43u8; 32]);\n\n        let seal = seal_volume(\n            b"secret-blob",\n            &recipient,\n            &[44u8; VOLUME_KEY_LEN],\n            &[45u8; NONCE_LEN],\n            &[45u8; NONCE_LEN],\n            &[46u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &[47u8; ENC_ENTROPY_LEN],\n            &signer_sk,\n            &[48u8; envelope::ENTROPY_LEN],\n        );\n        // Verify against a different signer pubkey → envelope fails.\n        let res = open_volume(&seal, &recipient, &other_pk);\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res, Err(VolumeError::Envelope(_))),\n            "wrong signer must be rejected: {:?}",\n            res\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_deterministic_wrap_roundtrip() {\n        // Two seals to the same recipient with identical inputs MUST be bit-identical\n        // (deterministic crypto core, C10), and both open identically.\n        let recipient = hk(50, 51);\n        let (signer_pk, signer_sk) = envelope::new_identity(&[52u8; ## 10233 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/aes_gcm.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: aes_gcm · 407 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/pq/aes_gcm.rs	aes_gcm · 407 lines	//! AES-256-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D), hand-rolled, `no_std`, zero external crates.\n//!\n//! The last external crypto crate retired from the pq subsystem: AES-256 block\n//! cipher (14 rounds, table-based S-box) in CTR mode + GHASH authentication in\n//! GF(2^128). Only the AES-*encrypt* direction is needed (GCM runs CTR with an\n//! encrypt keystream in both seal and open), so there is no inverse S-box.\n//!\n//! Correctness is KAT-gated against the AES-256-GCM test vector from the GCM\n//! specification (McGrew–Viega), and differential-tested against the RustCrypto\n//! `aes-gcm` crate in the kernel (`kernel/src/pq/aes_gcm.rs`) on a deterministic\n//! vector set before that dependency is retired from the `pq` feature.\n//!\n//! innovate: the S-box is a table lookup, so AES round state (which mixes the key)\n//! indexes the table — this is NOT cache-timing-hardened against a co-located\n//! attacker. The consumers here are at-rest/backup/transfer envelopes, not a\n//! high-frequency network-exposed path; upgrade trigger is an AES-NI path\n//! ```record
```
```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/crypto_signer.rs	crypto_signer · 425 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! crypto_signer.rs — Per-call PQ ML-DSA-65 cryptographic signer for parse operations.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! Each parse call gets a fresh ML-DSA-65 keypair. The signature binds:\n//! - IP hash (SHA3-256 of the source IP)\n//! - Timestamp (unix microseconds)\n//! - Payload hash (SHA3-256 of the response content)\n//! - Nonce (random, prevents replay)\n//!\n//! This creates a cryptographically verifiable audit trail: every parsed\n//! response is signed with a fresh key, the key is bound to the IP+time,\n//! and the signature covers the content hash. Any tampering or replay is\n//! detectable by re-verifying the signature chain.\n//!\n//! # Design principles\n//! - Pure computation: no network, no OS calls beyond monotonic clock\n//! - ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) for post-quantum security\n//! - Fresh keypair per call (forward secrecy: compromising one key reveals nothing about others)\n//! - Deterministic signing (rnd=0 for testability, caller can supply rnd for randomness)\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A signed parse call — the full cryptographic attestation.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SignedParseCall {\n    /// ML-DSA-65 public key for this call (fresh keypair).\n    pub public_key: Vec<u8>,\n    /// ML-DSA-65 signature over the canonical message.\n    pub signature: Vec<u8>,\n    /// The canonical message that was signed: `ip_hash || timestamp_us || payload_hash || nonce`.\n    pub signed_message: Vec<u8>,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the source IP used for this call.\n    pub ip_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// Unix microseconds when the call was made.\n    pub timestamp_us: u64,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the response payload.\n    pub payload_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// 32-byte nonce (prevents replay).\n    pub nonce: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Build the canonical message to sign: `ip_hash || timestamp_us_le || payload_hash || nonce`.\n///\n/// This is the message that `SignedParseCall.verify` checks against. The binding\n/// is unforgeable: an attacker cannot produce a valid signature for a different\n/// (ip, timestamp, payload) tuple without knowing the signing key.\npub fn build_sign_message(\n    ip_hash: &[u8; 32],\n    timestamp_us: u64,\n    payload_hash: &[u8; 32],\n    nonce: &[u8; 32],\n) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut msg = Vec::with_capacity(32 + 8 + 32 + 32);\n    msg.extend_from_slice(ip_hash);\n    msg.extend_from_slice(&timestamp_us.to_le_bytes());\n    msg.extend_from_slice(payload_hash);\n    msg.extend_from_slice(nonce);\n    msg\n}\n\n/// Sign a parse call using ML-DSA-65.\n///\n/// Uses `crate::pq::dsa` for the actual signing. The seed is derived from\n/// `SHA3-256(ip_hash || timestamp_us || nonce)` so the keypair is deterministic\n/// from the call context (for testing), while the signature uses rnd=0 (FIPS\n/// deterministic mode).\npub fn sign_parse_call(\n    ip_hash: [u8; 32],\n    timestamp_us: u64,\n    payload_hash: [u8; 32],\n    nonce: [u8; 32],\n) -> SignedParseCall {\n    let msg = build_sign_message(&ip_hash, timestamp_us, &payload_hash, &nonce);\n\n    // Derive keypair seed from the call context (deterministic for testability).\n    let seed_input = {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(32 + 8 + 32);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&ip_hash);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&timestamp_us.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&nonce);\n        sha3_256(&buf)\n    };\n    let mut seed = [0u8; 32];\n    seed.copy_from_slice(&seed_input);\n\n    let (pk, sk) = crate::pq::dsa::keygen(&seed);\n\n    // Deterministic signing (rnd=0).\n    let rnd = [0u8; 32];\n    let sig = crate::pq::dsa::sign(&sk, &msg, &rnd);\n\n    SignedParseCall {\n        public_key: pk.bytes,\n        signature: sig.bytes,\n        signed_message: msg,\n        ip_hash,\n        timestamp_us,\n        payload_hash,\n        nonce,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Verify a signed parse call.\n///\n/// Returns `Ok(())` if the signature is valid, `Err(VerificationError)` otherwise.\n/// This is the audit-side function: a different agent or process verifies the call\n/// after the fact, ensuring the content was not tampered with and the IP+time binding\n/// holds.\npub fn verify_parse_call(signed: &SignedParseCall) -> Result<(), VerificationError> {\n    // Verify the IP hash is non-zero (was actually computed).\n    // Must check BEFORE message rebuild — a zeroed ip_hash would cause MessageMismatch,\n    // but the semantic error is ZeroIpHash.\n    if signed.ip_hash == [0u8; 32] {\n        return Err(VerificationError::ZeroIpHash);\n    }\n\n    // Verify the payload hash is non-zero.\n    if signed.payload_hash == [0u8; 32] {\n        return Err(VerificationError::ZeroPayloadHash);\n    }\n\n    // Rebuild the expected message.\n    let expected_msg = build_sign_message(\n        &signed.ip_hash,\n        signed.timestamp_us,\n        &signed.payload_hash,\n        &signed.nonce,\n    );\n\n    // Message must match.\n    if signed.signed_message != expected_msg {\n        return Err(VerificationError::MessageMismatch);\n    }\n\n    // Verify the ML-DSA-65 signature.\n    let pk = crate::pq::dsa::MlDsa65Pk {\n        bytes: signed.public_key.clone(),\n    };\n    let sig = crate::pq::dsa::MlDsa65Sig {\n        bytes: signed.signature.clone(),\n    };\n\n    if !crate::pq::dsa::verify(&pk, &signed.signed_message, &sig) {\n        return Err(VerificationError::SignatureInvalid);\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Errors that can occur during signature verification.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum VerificationError {\n    /// The signed message doesn't match the rebuilt canonical message.\n    MessageMismatch,\n    /// The ML-DSA-65 signature verification failed.\n    SignatureInvalid,\n    /// The IP hash is all zeros (was never computed from a real IP).\n    ZeroIpHash,\n    /// The payload hash is all zeros (was never computed from real content).\n    ZeroPayloadHash,\n}\n\n/// A chain of signed parse calls — the full audit trail.\n///\n/// Each entry is independently verifiable, but the chain also provides\n/// ordering evidence (timestamps should be monotonically increasing).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SignedParseChain {\n    /// Ordered list of signed calls (oldest first).\n    calls: Vec<SignedParseCall>,\n    /// Running hash over all signatures (SHA3-256 chain).\n    chain_hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\nimpl SignedParseChain {\n    /// Create an empty chain.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SignedParseChain {\n            calls: Vec::new(),\n            chain_hash: [0u8; 32],\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Append a signed call to the chain.\n    pub fn append(&mut self, call: SignedParseCall) {\n        // Update chain hash: SHA3-256(prev_chain_hash || sig_hash).\n        let sig_hash = sha3_256(&call.signature);\n        let mut chain_input = Vec::with_capacity(64);\n        chain_input.extend_from_slice(&self.chain_hash);\n        chain_input.extend_from_slice(&sig_hash);\n        self.chain_hash = sha3_256(&chain_input);\n        self.calls.push(call);\n    }\n\n    /// Verify the entire chain (every signature + monotonic timestamps).\n    pub fn verify(&self) -> Result<(), ChainVerificationError> {\n        let mut prev_ts = 0u64;\n        for (i, call) in self.calls.iter().enumerate() {\n            verify_parse_call(call).map_err(|e| ChainVerificationError::InvalidSignature {\n                index: i,\n                inner: e,\n            })?;\n\n            // Timestamps should be monotonically non-decreasing.\n            if call.timestamp_us < prev_ts {\n                return Err(ChainVerificationError::TimestampViolation {\n                    index: i,\n                    prev_ts,\n                    this_ts: call.timestamp_us,\n                });\n            }\n            prev_ts = call.timestamp_us;\n        }\n\n        // Verify the chain hash.\n        let mut expected_hash = [0u8; 32];\n        for call in &self.calls {\n            let sig_hash = sha3_256(&call.signature);\n            let mut chain_input = Vec::with_capacity(64);\n            chain_input.extend_from_slice(&expected_hash);\n            chain_input.extend_from_slice(&sig_hash);\n            expected_hash = sha3_256(&chain_input);\n        }\n        if self.chain_hash != expected_hash {\n            return Err(ChainVerificationError::ChainHashMismatch);\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Number of calls in the chain.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.calls.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the chain is empty.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.calls.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// The current chain hash.\n    pub fn chain_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        self.chain_hash\n    }\n\n    /// Get a call by index.\n    pub fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&SignedParseCall> {\n        self.calls.get(index)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Errors from chain verification.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ChainVerificationError {\n    /// A specific call's signature failed verification.\n    InvalidSignature {\n        index: usize,\n        inner: VerificationError,\n    },\n    /// Timestamps are not monotonically non-decreasing.\n    TimestampViolation {\n        index: usize,\n        prev_ts: u64,\n        this_ts: u64,\n    },\n    /// The running chain hash doesn't match.\n    ChainHashMismatch,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sign_and_verify_roundtrip() {\n        let ip_hash = sha3_256(b"192.168.1.1");\n        let timestamp_us = 1_700_000_000_000_000u64;\n        let payload = b"<html>Hello World</html>";\n        let payload_hash = sha3_256(payload);\n        let nonce = [1u8; 32];\n\n        let signed = sign_parse_call(ip_hash, timestamp_us, payload_hash, nonce);\n        assert_eq!(signed.ip_hash, ip_hash);\n        assert_eq!(signed.timestamp_us, timestamp_us);\n        assert_eq!(signed.payload_hash, payload_hash);\n\n        let result = verify_parse_call(&signed);\n        assert!(result.is_ok(), "verification failed: {:?}", result.err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_rejects_tampered_ip_hash() {\n        let ip_hash = sha3_256(b"192.168.1.1");\n        let timestamp_us = 1_700_000_000_000_000u64;\n        let payload_hash = sha3_256(b"content");\n        let nonce = [2u8; 32];\n\n        let mut signed = sign_parse_call(ip_hash, timestamp_us, payload_hash, nonce);\n        // Tamper with the IP hash.\n        signed.ip_hash[0] ^= 0xFF;\n\n        let result = verify_parse_call(&signed);\n        assert_eq!(result, Err(VerificationError::MessageMismatch));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_rejects_tampered_signature() {\n        let ip_hash = sha3_256(b"192.168.1.1");\n        let timestamp_us = 1_700_000_000_000_000u64;\n        let payload_hash = sha3_256(b"content");\n        let nonce = [3u8; 32];\n\n        let mut signed = sign_parse_call(ip_hash, timestamp_us, payload_hash, nonce);\n        // Tamper with the signature.\n        if !signed.signature.is_empty() {\n            signed.signature[0] ^= 0xFF;\n        }\n\n        let result = verify_parse_call(&signed);\n        assert_eq!(result, Err(VerificationError::SignatureInvalid));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_rejects_zero_ip_hash() {\n        let signed = SignedParseCall {\n            public_key: vec![0; 1952], // dummy\n            signature: vec![0; 3309],  // dummy\n            signed_message: vec![0; 104],\n            ip_hash: [0u8; 32], // zero!\n            timestamp_us: 1_700_000_000_000_000u64,\n            payload_hash: sha3_256(b"content"),\n            nonce: [4u8; 32],\n        };\n        let result = verify_parse_call(&signed);\n        assert_eq!(result, Err(VerificationError::ZeroIpHash));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_rejects_zero_payload_hash() {\n        let signed = SignedParseCall {\n            public_key: vec![0; 1952],\n            signature: vec![0; 3309],\n            signed_message: vec![0; 104],\n            ip_hash: sha3_256(b"192.168.1.1"),\n            timestamp_us: 1_700_000_000_000_000u64,\n            payload_hash: [0u8; 32], // zero!\n            nonce: [5u8; 32],\n        };\n        let result = verify_parse_call(&signed);\n        assert_eq!(result, Err(VerificationError::ZeroPayloadHash));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn different_nonces_produce_different_signatures() {\n        let ip = sha3_256(b"10.0.0.1");\n        let ts = 1_700_000_000_000_000u64;\n        let ph = sha3_256(b"data");\n\n        let a = sign_parse_call(ip, ts, ph, [1u8; 32]);\n        let b = sign_parse_call(ip, ts, ph, [2u8; 32]);\n        assert_ne!(a.signature, b.signature, "different nonces => different sigs");\n        assert_ne!(a.public_key, b.public_key, "different nonces => different keys");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chain_append_and_verify() {\n        let mut chain = SignedParseChain::new();\n        assert!(chain.is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(chain.chain_hash(), [0u8; 32]);\n\n        let ip = sha3_256(b"192.168.1.1");\n        let ph = sha3_256(b"content");\n\n        chain.append(sign_parse_call(ip, 1000, ph, [1u8; 32]));\n        chain.append(sign_parse_call(ip, 2000, ph, [2u8; 32]));\n        chain.append(sign_parse_call(ip, 3000, ph, [3u8; 32]));\n\n        assert_eq!(chain.len(), 3);\n        assert_ne!(chain.chain_hash(), [0u8; 32]);\n\n        let result = chain.verify();\n        assert!(result.is_ok(), "chain verify failed: {:?}", result.err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chain_detects_timestamp_violation() {\n        let mut chain = SignedParseChain::new();\n        let ip = sha3_256(b"192.168.1.1");\n        let ph = sha3_256(b"content");\n\n        chain.append(sign_parse_call(ip, 3000, ph, [1u8; 32]));\n        chain.append(sign_parse_call(ip, 1000, ph, [2u8; 32])); // out of order!\n\n        let result = chain.verify();\n        assert!(matches!(\n            result,\n            Err(ChainVerificationError::TimestampViolation { index: 1, .. })\n        ));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chain_hash_changes_with_appends() {\n        let mut chain = SignedParseChain::new();\n        let ip = sha3_256(b"192.168.1.1");\n        let ph = sha3_256(b"content");\n\n        let h0 = chain.chain_hash();\n        chain.append(sign_parse_call(ip, 1000, ph, [1u8; 32]));\n        let h1 = chain.chain_hash();\n        assert_ne!(h0, h1);\n\n        chain.append(sign_parse_call(ip, 2000, ph, [2u8; 32]));\n        let h2 = chain.chain_hash();\n        assert_ne!(h1, h2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn build_sign_message_is_correct_length() {\n        let msg = build_sign_message(&[0u8; 32], 12345, &[0u8; 32], &[0u8; 32]);\n        // 32 + 8 + 32 + 32 = 104 bytes\n        assert_eq!(msg.len(), 104);\n    }\n}\n	10261	-1	-1		dc7eb51dd68ba727bb0b444155951b319d92b9ddb3d9ec134864c4d4c1f5f949b4711da141cf52ff645d832922e19aac0fef0f94fb28059a967232088f4eeaaf4fb70658223e17310643f11887bbadd940f9f8f83dc0cf4b589222b4389b431f6dfa52b6b7cb7a0190479807436c03780ea14d2aaa87968ea319a7ce052c246d
```
