4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/chronos_topology.rs	chronos_topology · 292 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! `dowiz_core::chronos_topology` — chrono-topological foundation (pure core).\n//!\n//! The root substrate for ALL state management. Every module writes its state\n//! here as a TriMatrix indexed by timestamp. The engine maintains three views:\n//!\n//!   PAST     = snapshot at t₀    (what WAS)\n//!   PRESENT  = snapshot at t₁    (what IS)\n//!   PREDICTED = extrapolated t₂  (what WILL BE)\n//!\n//! Prediction = PRESENT + (PRESENT - PAST) + spectral drift correction.\n//! All three matrices compared via delta, drift, and stability metrics.\n//!\n//! # Chrono-topological navigation\n//! - Time axis: timestamp-indexed history (chronos)\n//! - Space axes: TriMatrix (x=rows, y=cols, z=time depth)\n//! - Topology: connectivity between states (which past→present→predicted paths exist)\n//! - Navigation: jump to any (row, col, timestamp) and observe the system\n//!\n//! ZERO deps. Uses trinary, trig, wave, chronos.\n//!\n//! The wall-clock-stamped entry points (`TemporalTrinity::new`/`advance`,\n//! `ChronoTopology::register`/`update`/`navigate`) take `now_ms` explicitly so\n//! this module stays `no_std`; the kernel shim wraps them as free functions.\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::trinary::{Tri, TriMatrix, Rgb, DeltaChain};\nuse crate::trig::Xyz;\nuse crate::wave::{InterferenceField, spectral_fingerprint};\n\n/// A 4D point in chrono-topological space: (row, col, timestamp_ms, xyz).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct CT4 {\n    pub row: u32,         // matrix row (system dimension)\n    pub col: u32,         // matrix col (metric index)\n    pub ts: u64,          // timestamp (universal index)\n    pub xyz: Xyz,         // phase-space encoding\n}\n\nimpl CT4 {\n    pub fn new(row: u32, col: u32, ts: u64, xyz: Xyz) -> Self {\n        CT4 { row, col, ts, xyz }\n    }\n    /// Phase distance between two 4D points (xyz distance, normalized).\n    pub fn dist(&self, other: &CT4) -> f64 {\n        self.xyz.dist_norm(&other.xyz)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The three temporal views: past, present, predicted.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TemporalTrinity {\n    pub past: TriMatrix,\n    pub past_ts: u64,\n    pub present: TriMatrix,\n    pub present_ts: u64,\n    pub predicted: TriMatrix,\n    pub predicted_ts: u64,\n    /// Confidence in prediction [0, 1].\n    pub prediction_confidence: f64,\n}\n\nimpl TemporalTrinity {\n    pub fn new(rows: usize, cols: usize, now_ms: u64) -> Self {\n        TemporalTrinity {\n            past: TriMatrix::new(rows, cols),\n            past_ts: now_ms,\n            present: TriMatrix::new(rows, cols),\n            present_ts: now_ms,\n            predicted: TriMatrix::new(rows, cols),\n            predicted_ts: now_ms + 1000,\n            prediction_confidence: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Advance: present → past, predicted → present, new prediction computed.\n    pub fn advance(&mut self, new_present: TriMatrix, now_ms: u64) {\n        self.past = core::mem::replace(&mut self.present, new_present);\n        self.past_ts = self.present_ts;\n        self.present_ts = now_ms;\n        self.predict_next();\n    }\n\n    /// Predict the next state using Kalman-like update with adaptive gain.\n    ///\n    /// Gain is adapted based on prior prediction error: higher error → higher\n    /// gain (react faster to changes); lower error → lower gain (smoother).\n    pub fn predict_next(&mut self) {\n        // Adaptive gain: bounded sigmoid over prediction error.\n        let err = self.prediction_error();\n        let gain = 1.0 / (1.0 + crate::math::exp(-10.0 * (err - 0.3))); // steep around 0.3 error\n        // Clamp into [0.05, 0.95] so extreme values don't lock the filter.\n        let gain = gain.clamp(0.05, 0.95);\n\n        self.predicted = self.present.kalman_predict(&self.past, gain);\n        self.predicted_ts = self.present_ts + (self.present_ts - self.past_ts).max(100);\n        self.prediction_confidence = 1.0 - err;\n    }\n\n    /// Delta between past and present (how much changed).\n    pub fn delta_past_present(&self) -> (f64, usize) {\n        let mut delta_sum = 0.0f64;\n        let mut changes = 0usize;\n        for r in 0..self.present.rows {\n            for c in 0..self.present.cols {\n                let past_rgb = Rgb::from_tri(self.past.get(r, c));\n                let pres_rgb = Rgb::from_tri(self.present.get(r, c));\n                if past_rgb != pres_rgb {\n                    delta_sum += past_rgb.delta_norm(&pres_rgb);\n                    changes += 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        (delta_sum, changes)\n    }\n\n    /// Delta between predicted and actual present (prediction error).\n    pub fn prediction_error(&self) -> f64 {\n        let mut err = 0.0f64;\n        let mut count = 0usize;\n        for r in 0..self.present.rows {\n            for c in 0..self.present.cols {\n                let pred_rgb = Rgb::from_tri(self.predicted.get(r, c));\n                let pres_rgb = Rgb::from_tri(self.present.get(r, c));\n                err += pred_rgb.delta_norm(&pres_rgb);\n                count += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        if count == 0 { 0.0 } else { err / count as f64 }\n    }\n\n    /// RGB bitmap comparison: show past/present/predicted side by side.\n    pub fn comparison_bitmap(&self) -> Vec<(Rgb, Rgb, Rgb)> {\n        let n = self.present.rows.min(self.past.rows);\n        (0..n).map(|r| (\n            self.past.row_rgb(r),\n            self.present.row_rgb(r),\n            self.predicted.row_rgb(r),\n        )).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Stability score: fraction of cells unchanged from past to present.\n    pub fn stability(&self) -> f64 {\n        let (_, changes) = self.delta_past_present();\n        let total = self.present.rows * self.present.cols;\n        if total == 0 { 1.0 } else { 1.0 - changes as f64 / total as f64 }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Chrono-topological engine — the root state substrate.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ChronoTopology {\n    /// Named temporal trinities (one per subsystem: "orders", "security", "enrichment"...)\n    pub subsystems: BTreeMap<String, TemporalTrinity>,\n    /// Global delta chain (system-wide drift tracking).\n    pub drift: DeltaChain,\n    /// Interference field (spectral superposition of all waves).\n    pub field: InterferenceField,\n    /// Navigation history: visited 4D points.\n    pub nav_history: Vec<CT4>,\n}\n\nimpl ChronoTopology {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        ChronoTopology {\n            subsystems: BTreeMap::new(),\n            drift: DeltaChain::new(),\n            field: InterferenceField::new(),\n            nav_history: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Register a subsystem with given matrix dimensions (stamped at `now_ms`).\n    pub fn register(&mut self, name: &str, rows: usize, cols: usize, now_ms: u64) {\n        self.subsystems.insert(name.to_string(), TemporalTrinity::new(rows, cols, now_ms));\n    }\n\n    /// Update a subsystem's present state (advances past→present→predicted).\n    pub fn update(&mut self, name: &str, matrix: TriMatrix, now_ms: u64) {\n        if let Some(trinity) = self.subsystems.get_mut(name) {\n            trinity.advance(matrix, now_ms);\n            // Emit a spectral fingerprint for this state change\n            let (delta, _) = trinity.delta_past_present();\n            let wave = spectral_fingerprint(name, delta, now_ms);\n            self.field.add_wave(wave);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Navigate to a specific 4D point.\n    pub fn navigate(&mut self, row: u32, col: u32, ts: u64, now_ms: u64) {\n        let xyz = self.field.xyz_state(now_ms);\n        self.nav_history.push(CT4::new(row, col, ts, xyz));\n        self.drift.push(Rgb::from_tri(Tri::Unknown)); // placeholder\n    }\n\n    /// Global system state as a single TriMatrix (concatenated rows from all subsystems).\n    pub fn global_matrix(&self) -> TriMatrix {\n        let mut rows = 0usize;\n        let cols = self.subsystems.values().next().map(|t| t.present.cols).unwrap_or(0);\n        for t in self.subsystems.values() { rows += t.present.rows; }\n        let mut global = TriMatrix::new(rows, cols);\n        let mut offset = 0;\n        for t in self.subsystems.values() {\n            for r in 0..t.present.rows {\n                for c in 0..t.present.cols {\n                    global.set(offset + r, c, t.present.get(r, c));\n                }\n            }\n            offset += t.present.rows;\n        }\n        global\n    }\n\n    /// Dashboard: per-subsystem status.\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::from("═══ CHRONO-TOPOLOGY ═══\\n");\n        for (name, t) in &self.subsystems {\n            let (delta, changes) = t.delta_past_present();\n            let pred_err = t.prediction_error();\n            let stab = t.stability();\n            out.push_str(&format!("  {}: Δ={:.3} chg={} err={:.3} stab={:.3}\\n",\n                name, delta, changes, pred_err, stab));\n        }\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Global drift: {:.3}\\n", self.drift.total_drift()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Active waves: {}\\n", self.field.active_count()));\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn temporal_trinity_advances() {\n        let mut tt = TemporalTrinity::new(2, 2, 1000);\n        let mut m = TriMatrix::new(2, 2);\n        m.set(0, 0, Tri::True);\n        m.set(0, 1, Tri::False);\n        tt.advance(m.clone(), 1000);\n        // After advance: present = m, predicted computed\n        assert_eq!(tt.present.get(0, 0), Tri::True);\n ## 10891 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/chronos.rs · LongTerm

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/chronos.rs	chronos · 243 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! `dowiz_core::chronos` — time navigation: snapshots, state history, time-travel (pure core).\n//!\n//! Every system state change is recorded as a timestamped snapshot. The chronos\n//! engine allows navigation between snapshots: rewind to any point in time, see\n//! the full system state at that moment, diff between any two timestamps.\n//!\n//! Time is the universal axis — all modules write their state here, and any\n//! agent can query "what was the state at t = X?"\n//!\n//! ZERO deps. Uses the core SHA3-256 for snapshot integrity. `Chronos::snapshot_at`\n//! takes `now_ms` explicitly so this module stays `no_std`; the kernel shim wraps\n//! it as `snapshot_now` which stamps `crate::now_ms()`.\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::trig::Xyz;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A single system state snapshot at a specific timestamp.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Snapshot {\n    pub id: u64,\n    pub timestamp_ms: u64,\n    /// Named state dimensions (e.g. "order_count", "cpu_load", "confidence").\n    pub values: BTreeMap<String, f64>,\n    /// XYZ encoding of the composite state.\n    pub xyz: Xyz,\n    /// SHA3-256 integrity hash of (timestamp + sorted values).\n    pub integrity: [u8; 32],\n}\n\nimpl Snapshot {\n    pub fn new(timestamp_ms: u64, values: BTreeMap<String, f64>) -> Self {\n        let id = timestamp_ms; // monotonic (ms granularity)\n        let xyz = Snapshot::compute_xyz(&values);\n        let integrity = Snapshot::compute_hash(timestamp_ms, &values);\n        Snapshot { id, timestamp_ms, values, xyz, integrity }\n    }\n\n    fn compute_xyz(values: &BTreeMap<String, f64>) -> Xyz {\n        let mut keys: Vec<&String> = values.keys().collect();\n        keys.sort();\n        let mut x = 0.0f64; let mut y = 0.0f64; let mut z = 0.0f64;\n        for (i, k) in keys.iter().enumerate() {\n            let v = values.get(*k).copied().unwrap_or(0.0).clamp(-1.0, 1.0);\n            match i % 3 {\n                0 => x = v,\n                1 => y = v,\n                _ => z = (z + v) / 2.0,\n            }\n        }\n        Xyz::new(x, y, z)\n    }\n\n    fn compute_hash(ts: u64, values: &BTreeMap<String, f64>) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut data = ts.to_le_bytes().to_vec();\n        let mut keys: Vec<&String> = values.keys().collect();\n        keys.sort();\n        for k in keys {\n            data.extend_from_slice(k.as_bytes());\n            data.extend_from_slice(&values[k].to_le_bytes());\n        }\n        sha3_256(&data)\n    }\n\n    /// Verify integrity.\n    pub fn verify(&self) -> bool {\n        Snapshot::compute_hash(self.timestamp_ms, &self.values) == self.integrity\n    }\n}\n\n/// The chronos engine — a time-indexed history of system snapshots.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Chronos {\n    pub snapshots: Vec<Snapshot>,\n    /// Max snapshots retained (sliding window).\n    pub capacity: usize,\n    /// Index: dimension name → last known values for interpolation.\n    pub dimensions: BTreeMap<String, Vec<f64>>,\n}\n\nimpl Chronos {\n    pub fn new(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n        Chronos { snapshots: Vec::with_capacity(capacity), capacity: capacity.max(1), dimensions: BTreeMap::new() }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a snapshot of system state at the explicit `now_ms` timestamp.\n    pub fn snapshot_at(&mut self, values: BTreeMap<String, f64>, now_ms: u64) -> &Snapshot {\n        let snap = Snapshot::new(now_ms, values.clone());\n        self.snapshots.push(snap);\n        if self.snapshots.len() > self.capacity {\n            self.snapshots.remove(0);\n        }\n        for (k, v) in values {\n            self.dimensions.entry(k).or_default().push(v);\n        }\n        self.snapshots.last().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Find the snapshot closest to a given timestamp (linear scan — ok for small N).\n    pub fn at(&self, timestamp_ms: u64) -> Option<&Snapshot> {\n        self.snapshots.iter()\n            .min_by_key(|s| (s.timestamp_ms as i64 - timestamp_ms as i64).unsigned_abs())\n    }\n\n    /// Get all snapshots in a time window.\n    pub fn window(&self, from_ms: u64, to_ms: u64) -> Vec<&Snapshot> {\n        self.snapshots.iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.timestamp_ms >= from_ms && s.timestamp_ms <= to_ms)\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Delta between two timestamps: XYZ distance + per-dimension deltas.\n    pub fn delta(&self, t1: u64, t2: u64) -> Option<(f64, BTreeMap<String, f64>)> {\n        let s1 = self.at(t1)?;\n        let s2 = self.at(t2)?;\n        let xyz_delta = s1.xyz.distance(&s2.xyz);\n        let mut dim_deltas = BTreeMap::new();\n        for k in s1.values.keys() {\n            let v1 = s1.values.get(k).copied().unwrap_or(0.0);\n            let v2 = s2.values.get(k).copied().unwrap_or(0.0);\n            dim_deltas.insert(k.clone(), v2 - v1);\n        }\n        Some((xyz_delta, dim_deltas))\n    }\n\n    /// Latest snapshot.\n    pub fn latest(&self) -> Option<&Snapshot> { self.snapshots.last() }\n\n    /// Total recorded snapshots.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { self.snapshots.len() }\n\n    /// Time range: (earliest, latest).\n    pub fn time_range(&self) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {\n        let first = self.snapshots.first()?;\n        let last = self.snapshots.last()?;\n        Some((first.timestamp_ms, last.timestamp_ms))\n    }\n\n    /// Interpolate state between two nearest snapshots.\n    pub fn interpolate(&self, timestamp_ms: u64) -> Option<BTreeMap<String, f64>> {\n        if self.snapshots.is_empty() { return None; }\n        // Find nearest before and after\n        let before = self.snapshots.iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.timestamp_ms <= timestamp_ms)\n            .last();\n        let after = self.snapshots.iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.timestamp_ms >= timestamp_ms)\n            .next();\n        match (before, after) {\n            (Some(b), Some(a)) if b.timestamp_ms != a.timestamp_ms => {\n                let w = (timestamp_ms - b.timestamp_ms) as f64\n                    / (a.timestamp_ms - b.timestamp_ms) as f64;\n                let mut result = BTreeMap::new();\n                for k in b.values.keys() {\n                    let v1 = b.values.get(k).copied().unwrap_or(0.0);\n                    let v2 = a.values.get(k).copied().unwrap_or(0.0);\n                    result.insert(k.clone(), v1 + (v2 - v1) * w);\n                }\n                Some(result)\n            }\n            (Some(b), _) => Some(b.values.clone()),\n            (None, Some(a)) => Some(a.values.clone()),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn make_values(x: f64, y: f64) -> BTreeMap<String, f64> {\n        let mut m = BTreeMap::new();\n        m.insert("x".into(), x);\n        m.insert("y".into(), y);\n        m\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn snapshot_integrity_verifies() {\n        let s = Snapshot::new(1000, make_values(0.5, -0.3));\n        assert!(s.verify());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chronos_snapshot_and_retrieve() {\n        let mut c = Chronos::new(100);\n        c.snapshot_at(make_values(0.1, 0.2), 1000);\n        c.snapshot_at(make_values(0.5, 0.8), 1010);\n        c.snapshot_at(make_values(0.9, 0.3), 1020);\n        assert_eq!(c.len(), 3);\n        // Latest should carry the most recent injected timestamp.\n        let latest = c.latest().unwrap();\n        assert!(latest.timestamp_ms >= 1020);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chronos_delta_between_timestamps() {\n        let mut c = Chronos::new(100);\n        let ts0 = 1000u64;\n        let snap0 = Snapshot::new(ts0, make_values(0.0, 0.0));\n        let snap2 = Snapshot::new(ts0 + 500, make_values(1.0, 1.0));\n        c.snapshots.push(snap0);\n        c.snapshots.push(Snapshot::new(ts0 + 200, make_values(0.5, 0.5)));\n        c.snapshots.push(snap2);\n        let (xyz_d, dims) = c.delta(ts0, ts0 + 500).unwrap();\n        assert!(xyz_d >= 0.0, "xyz_delta={xyz_d}");\n        assert!((dims["x"] - 1.0).abs() < 1e-10);\n    c.snapshot_at(make_values(2.0, 4.0), 2000);\n        let interp = c.interpolate(1750);\n        assert!(interp.is_some());\n        let v = interp.unwrap();\n        assert!(v["x"] >= 0.0);\n Uses all visualization primitives: trinary RGB, fractal ASCII, eigen ASCII,\n//! chronos snapshots, delta tracking, ETA oracle.\n//!\n//! ZERO deps. Call `render()` → String ready for display.\n\nuse crate::trinary::{Tri, TriMatrix};\nuse crate::fractal::ascii_matrix;\nuse crate::delta::DeltaTracker;\nuse crate::code_oracle::EtaOracle;\nuse crate::trig::Xyz;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Drift severity bucket — the rewrite-law replacement for a drift if/else chain.\n/// A decision is a table index (branchless bool-cast), not an if-chain.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\n#[repr(u8)]\nenum DriftBucket {\n    Low = 0,\n    Med = 1,\n    High = 2,\n}\n\nimpl crate::lut::LutKey for DriftBucket {\n    const LUT_SIZE: usize = 3;\n    fn discriminant(self) -> u8 {\n        self as u8\n    }\n}\n\nimpl DriftBucket {\n    /// Branchless bucket from cumulative drift.\n    /// `(drift > 100.0) as usize + (drift > 10.0) as usize` yields\n    /// 0 = Low (≤10), 1 = Med (10..100], 2 = High (>100) — two bool casts,\n    /// one array index, zero branches.\n    const BUCKETS: [DriftBucket; 3] = [DriftBucket::Low, DriftBucket::Med, DriftBucket::High];\n\n    #[inline(always)]\n    fn from_drift(drift: f64) -> DriftBucket {\n        let idx = (drift > 100.0) as usize + (drift > 10.0) as usize;\n        Self::BUCKETS[idx]\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compile-time label table for drift buckets — the decision is data, not code.\nconst DRIFT_LABEL_LUT: crate::lut::Lut<DriftBucket, &'static str, 3> =\n    crate::lut::Lut::new(["✓ LOW", "◈ MED", "⚠ HIGH"]);\n\n/// Complete system dashboard — one call, full state.\npub fn render(\n    test_count: usize,\n    module_count: usize,\n    db_entries: usize,\n    db_kinds: usize,\n    oracle: &EtaOracle,\n    drift: &DeltaTracker,\n    state: Option<Xyz>,\n    phase: &str,\n) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(4096);\n\n    // ── Header ──\n    out.push_str("┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\\n");\n    out.push_str("│         DOWIZ SYSTEM DASHBOARD          │\\n");\n    out.push_str(&format!("│  Phase: {:>31} │\\n", phase));\n    out.push_str("├─────────────────────────────────────────┤\\n");\n\n    // ── Tests ──\n    let bar = "█".repeat((test_count / 50).min(30));\n    out.push_str(&format!("│  Tests:   {:>5} green  {}│\\n", test_count, bar));\n\n    // ── Modules ──\n    out.push_str(&format!("│  Modules: {:>5} total                   │\\n", module_count));\n\n    // ── Enrichment DB ──\n    out.push_str(&format!("│  Enrich DB: {:>5} entries, {:>2} kinds      │\\n", db_entries, db_kinds));\n\n    // ── ETA Oracle ──\n    if oracle.history.len() >= 3 {\n        let eta10 = oracle.predict_eta(3, 100);\n        let (mean_err, _) = oracle.eta_confidence();\n        out.push_str(&format!("│  ETA(3mod,100L): {:>4.0}m ±{:.0}m           │\\n", eta10, mean_err));\n    } else {\n        out.push_str("│  ETA Oracle:  calibrating...              │\\n");\n    }\n\n    // ── System stability ──\n    if let Some(xyz) = state {\n        out.push_str(&format!("│  XYZ State: ({:+.2},{:+.2},{:+.2})            │\\n", xyz.x, xyz.y, xyz.z));\n    }\n\n    // ── Drift ──\n    let drift_level = DRIFT_LABEL_LUT.get(DriftBucket::from_drift(drift.cumulative_drift));\n    out.push_str(&format!(\n        "│  Drift:    {:>6.1}  {}                    │\\n",\n        drift.cumulative_drift, drift_level\n    ));\n\n    // ── Alarms ──\n    let alarming = drift.is_alarming(5);\n    out.push_str(&format!("│  Alarm:    {:>6}                        │\\n",\n        if alarming { "⚠ ACTIVE" } else { "✓ CLEAR" }));\n\n    // ── Recent deltas ──\n    if !drift.history.is_empty() {\n        let last = drift.history.last().unwrap();\n        out.push_str(&format!("│  Last Δ:   {:.3}  rate={:.3}               │\\n",\n            last.magnitude, last.rate));\n    }\n\n    out.push_str("└─────────────────────────────────────────┘\\n");\n\n    // ── Enrichment mode ──\n    out.push_str("\\n═══ ENRICHMENT ═══\\n");\n    out.push_str("  primary: {\n    let mut out = format!("═══ {} ═══\\n", label);\n    let (t, f, u) = m.counts();\n    out.push_str(&format!("  T:{} F:{} ?:{}  ", t, f, u));\n    let stable = t as f64 / m.data.len().max(1) as 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/code_oracle.rs	code_oracle · 253 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! `dowiz_core::code_oracle` — code change prediction + ETA oracle (pure core).\n//!\n//! Predicts the impact and duration of code changes using:\n//! - Change history analysis (chronos snapshots of git history)\n//! - Eigen decomposition of changed modules\n//! - Delta tracking of change magnitude over time\n//! - Oracle-trained ETA models\n//!\n//! # How it works\n//! 1. Record chronos snapshots BEFORE each change wave\n//! 2. After changes, compute delta between snapshots\n//! 3. Train oracle: predicted_eta = f(modules_touched, lines_changed, eigen_shift)\n//! 4. Use oracle to predict future change ETAs\n//!\n//! ZERO deps. The wall-clock-stamped entry points (`ChangeRecord::new`,\n//! `EtaOracle::record`) take `now_ms` explicitly so this module stays `no_std`;\n//! the kernel shim wraps them as free functions.\n\nuse crate::eigen::{EigenDecomp, decompose};\nuse crate::delta::{Delta, DeltaTracker};\nuse crate::chronos::Chronos;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A single code change event — recorded before/after each commit.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ChangeRecord {\n    pub timestamp_ms: u64,\n    pub modules_touched: Vec<String>,\n    pub lines_added: u64,\n    pub lines_removed: u64,\n    pub eigen_before: EigenDecomp,\n    pub eigen_after: EigenDecomp,\n    pub actual_eta_minutes: f64,\n}\n\nimpl ChangeRecord {\n    pub fn new(modules: &[&str], added: u64, removed: u64, eta_min: f64, now_ms: u64) -> Self {\n        let values: Vec<f64> = vec![added as f64, removed as f64, eta_min];\n        ChangeRecord {\n            timestamp_ms: now_ms,\n            modules_touched: modules.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),\n            lines_added: added,\n            lines_removed: removed,\n            eigen_before: decompose(&values, 3),\n            eigen_after: decompose(&values, 3),\n            actual_eta_minutes: eta_min,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Total lines changed.\n    pub fn total_lines(&self) -> u64 { self.lines_added + self.lines_removed }\n\n    /// Spectral shift magnitude (how much the eigen decomposition changed).\n    pub fn eigen_shift(&self) -> f64 {\n        (self.eigen_after.spectral_radius() - self.eigen_before.spectral_radius()).abs()\n    }\n}\n\n/// ETA oracle — learns from past changes to predict future durations.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct EtaOracle {\n    pub history: Vec<ChangeRecord>,\n    pub chronos: Chronos,\n    pub delta_tracker: DeltaTracker,\n}\n\nimpl EtaOracle {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        EtaOracle {\n            history: Vec::with_capacity(1000),\n            chronos: Chronos::new(1000),\n            delta_tracker: DeltaTracker::new(100.0, 10.0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a completed change at the explicit `now_ms` timestamp.\n    pub fn record(&mut self, modules: &[&str], added: u64, removed: u64, eta_minutes: f64, now_ms: u64) {\n        let record = ChangeRecord::new(modules, added, removed, eta_minutes, now_ms);\n        let prev_vals: Vec<f64> = self.history.last()\n            .map(|r| vec![r.total_lines() as f64, r.actual_eta_minutes])\n            .unwrap_or(vec![0.0, 0.0]);\n        let new_vals = vec![record.total_lines() as f64, record.actual_eta_minutes];\n        let delta = Delta::between(&prev_vals, 0, &new_vals, 1);\n        self.delta_tracker.observe(delta);\n\n        let mut snap_values = BTreeMap::new();\n        snap_values.insert("lines".into(), record.total_lines() as f64);\n        snap_values.insert("eta".into(), record.actual_eta_minutes);\n        snap_values.insert("modules".into(), record.modules_touched.len() as f64);\n        self.chronos.snapshot_at(snap_values, now_ms);\n\n        self.history.push(record);\n    }\n\n    /// Predict ETA for a new change: ETA = α·lines + β·modules + γ·eigen_shift.\n    pub fn predict_eta(&self, modules_touched: usize, lines_estimated: u64) -> f64 {\n        if self.history.len() < 3 {\n            return lines_estimated as f64 / 10.0 + modules_touched as f64 * 5.0; // naive baseline\n        }\n\n        // Simple linear regression over recent history\n        let n = self.history.len().min(50);\n        let recent = &self.history[self.history.len() - n..];\n\n        let mut sum_x = 0.0f64; let mut sum_y = 0.0f64; let mut sum_xx = 0.0f64; let mut sum_xy = 0.0f64;\n        for r in recent {\n            let x = r.total_lines() as f64 + r.modules_touched.len() as f64 * 10.0;\n            let y = r.actual_eta_minutes;\n            sum_x += x; sum_y += y; sum_xx += x * x; sum_xy += x * y;\n        }\n        let nf = n as f64;\n        let slope = if nf * sum_xx - sum_x * sum_x > 1e-10 {\n            (nf * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (nf * sum_xx - sum_x * sum_x)\n        } else { 0.05 };\n\n        let intercept = (sum_y - slope * sum_x) / nf;\n        let x_pred = lines_estimated as f64 + modules_touched as f64 * 10.0;\n        (slope * x_pred + intercept).max(1.0)\n    }\n\n    /// Confidence interval for ETA prediction (± minutes).\n    pub fn eta_confidence(&self) -> (f64, f64) {\n        if self.history.len() < 5 { return (0.5, 0.5); }\n        let errors: Vec<f64> = self.history.iter()\n            .map(|r| {\n                let pred = self.predict_eta(r.modules_touched.len(), r.total_lines());\n                (pred - r.actual_eta_minutes).abs()\n            }).collect();\n        let mean_err = errors.iter().sum::<f64>() / errors.len() as f64;\n        let var_err = errors.iter().map(|e| (e - mean_err) * (e - mean_err)).sum::<f64>() / errors.len() as f64;\n        (mean_err, crate::math::sqrt(var_err))\n    }\n\n    /// Impact prediction: how much will the eigen spectrum shift?\n    pub fn predict_impact(&self, modules_touched: usize, lines_estimated: u64) -> f64 {\n        if self.history.len() < 3 { return lines_estimated as f64 / 1000.0; }\n        let similar: Vec<&ChangeRecord> = self.history.iter()\n            .filter(|r| (r.modules_touched.len() as isize - modules_touched as isize).unsigned_abs() <= 2)\n            .collect();\n        if similar.is_empty() { return lines_estimated as f64 / 500.0; }\n        similar.iter().map(|r| r.eigen_shift()).sum::<f64>() / similar.len() as f64\n    }\n\n    /// Dashboard.\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::from("═══ ETA ORACLE ═══\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  history: {} changes\\n", self.history.len()));\n        if self.history.len() >= 3 {\n            let eta_10 = self.predict_eta(3, 100);\n            let eta_50 = self.predict_eta(8, 500);\n            let (mean, std) = self.eta_confidence();\n            out.push_str(&format!("  predicted ETA (3 modules, 100 lines): {:.0} min\\n", eta_10));\n            out.push_str(&format!("  predicted ETA (8 modules, 500 lines): {:.0} min\\n", eta_50));\n            out.push_str(&format!("  confidence: ±{:.0} min (σ={:.0})\\n", mean, std));\n        }\n        if !self.history.is_empty() {\n            let last = self.history.last().unwrap();\n            out.push_str(&format!("  last change: {} modules, {} lines, {:.0} min\\n",\n                last.modules_touched.len(), last.total_lines(), last.actual_eta_minutes));\n        }\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn oracle_records_and_predicts() {\n        let mut oracle = EtaOracle::new();\n        oracle.record(&["predictor.rs"], 48, 36, 10.0, 1000);\n        oracle.record(&["predictor.rs", "lib.rs"], 120, 80, 20.0, 2000);\n        oracle.record(&["predictor.rs"], 30, 15, 5.0, 3000);\n        oracle.record(&["lib.rs", "pid.rs", "gossip.rs"], 200, 150, 30.0, 4000);\n\n        let eta = oracle.predict_eta(2, 100);\n        assert!(eta > 0.0);\n        assert!(eta < 100.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn oracle_confidence_is_finite() {\n        let mut oracle = EtaOracle::new();\n        for i in 0..10 {\n            oracle.record(&["test.rs"], 10 + i*5, 5 + i*3, (i + 1) as f64 * 3.0, 1000 + i as u64);\n        }\n        let (mean, std) = oracle.eta_confidence();\n        assert!(mean >= 0.0);\n        assert!(std >= 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_oracle_defaults_to_naive() {\n        let oracle = EtaOracle::new();\n        let eta = oracle.predict_eta(3, 100);\n        assert!(eta > 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn impact_prediction_finite() {\n        let mut oracle = EtaOracle::new();\n        oracle.record(&["a.rs"], 100, 50, 15.0, 1000);\n        oracle.record(&["a.rs", "b.rs"], 200, 100, 30.0, 2000);\n        let impact = oracle.predict_impact(2, 150);\n        assert!(impact >= 0.0);\n        assert!(impact < 1.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dashboard_renders() {\n        let mut oracle = EtaOracle::new();\n        oracle.record(&["test.rs"], 10, 5, 2.0, 1000);\n        let d = oracle.dashboard();\n        assert!(d.contains("ETA ORACLE"));\n        assert!(d.contains("history"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn oracle_predict_impact_without_similar_falls_back() {\n        let mut oracle = EtaOracle::new();\n        oracle.record(&["a.rs"], 100, 50, 15.0, 1000);\n        oracle.record(&["a.rs"], 200, 100, 30.0, 2000);\n        oracle.record(&["b.rs"], 50, 25, 8.0, 3000);\n        let impact = oracle.predict_impact(10, 500);\n        assert!(impact > 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn oracle_predict_impact_no_history() {\n        let oracle = EtaOracle::new();\n        let impact = oracle.predict_impact(5, 300);\n        assert!(impact > 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn change_record_total_lines() {\n        let rec = ChangeRecord::new(&["a.rs"], 100, 50, 15.0, 1000);\n        assert_eq!(rec.total_lines(), 150);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn eta_confidence_few_samples() {\n        let oracle = EtaOracle::new();\n        let (mean, std) = oracle.eta_confidence();\n        assert!((mean - 0.5).abs() < 1e-10);\n        assert!((std - 0.5).abs() < 1e-10);\n    }\n}\n	10934	-1	-1		f3e2fefe93cf5dada92970cbeababbb90914b7eca5faee2b687a6c098bf8a9b3150415cbadea86b7e854030995d1162cd6efe7c6260942bab06ae7f60925e3862e9f55f9c53ea9350167f91897ab0062bd74c8ea71b27aa5902029869249b5b482baf25734c2b16b5fec0ec60f5dbc186c90c5aa7181d4f41a68dff663d4e580

Complements the `predictor` module: when predictions indicate an imminent\n//! problem (high throttle, friction, error probability), the resilience layer\n//! automatically activates backups, switches to fallback models, or triggers\n//! circuit breakers. Race-condition avoidance via atomic sequencer.\n//!\n//! ## Architecture\n//! - `FailoverStrategy` — which backup/failover model to use.\n//! - `ResiliencePolicy` — thresholds and actions for each degradation level.\n//! - `ResilienceManager` — combines multiple policies, monitors predictions,\n//!   and executes failover actions. Thread-safe via atomic sequencer.\n//!\n//! ## Usage\n//! ```\n//! use dowiz_core::resilience::{\n//!     ResilienceManager, ResiliencePolicy, FailoverStrategy, DegradationLevel,\n//! };\n//!\n//! let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n//! mgr.record_outcome(0.3, 0.1, 0.05, 0); // cpu=0.3, friction=0.1, error=0.05\n//! assert_eq!(mgr.level(), DegradationLevel::Normal);\n//! ```\n\nuse crate::predictor::PredictedOutcome;\nuse core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\npub const RESILIENCE_DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS: u64 = 5000;\npub const RESILIENCE_DEFAULT_MAX_FAILURES: u32 = 3;\npub const RESILIENCE_BACKUP_CAPACITY: usize = 100;\n\n// ─── DegradationLevel ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// How degraded the system is, based on predictor signals.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum DegradationLevel {\n    /// Normal operation — no action needed.\n    Normal = 0,\n    /// Elevated — pre-emptive monitoring, no switch yet.\n    Elevated = 1,\n    /// Warning — prepare failover, start draining.\n    Warning = 2,\n    /// Critical — activate failover immediately.\n    Critical = 3,\n    /// Failed — circuit open, full backup active.\n    Failed = 4,\n}\n\nimpl DegradationLevel {\n    pub fn from_values(avg_metric: f64, friction: f64, error_prob: f64) -> Self {\n        let avg_metric = crate::sanitize_f64(avg_metric);\n        let friction = crate::sanitize_f64(friction);\n        let error_prob = crate::sanitize_f64(error_prob);\n        let score = avg_metric * 0.3 + friction * 0.3 + error_prob * 0.4;\n        if score > 0.9 { DegradationLevel::Failed }\n        else if score > 0.75 { DegradationLevel::Critical }\n        else if score > 0.5 { DegradationLevel::Warning }\n        else if score > 0.3 { DegradationLevel::Elevated }\n        else { DegradationLevel::Normal }\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_actionable(&self) -> bool {\n        *self >= DegradationLevel::Warning\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── FailoverStrategy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Which strategy to use when failing over.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FailoverStrategy {\n    /// Use PID-only predictions (fast, less accurate).\n    PidOnly,\n    /// Use crystal-memory predictions (needs history).\n    CrystalOnly,\n    /// Use trend-extrapolation (works with minimal data).\n    TrendOnly,\n    /// Use ensemble but with reduced confidence threshold.\n    EnsembleReduced,\n    /// Use a pre-computed static fallback (defensive).\n    StaticFallback,\n}\n\nimpl FailoverStrategy {\n    pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            FailoverStrategy::PidOnly => "pid_fallback",\n            FailoverStrategy::CrystalOnly => "crystal_fallback",\n            FailoverStrategy::TrendOnly => "trend_fallback",\n            FailoverStrategy::EnsembleReduced => "ensemble_reduced",\n            FailoverStrategy::StaticFallback => "static_fallback",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── ResiliencePolicy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A policy mapping degradation levels to failover actions.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ResiliencePolicy {\n    /// Level thresholds.\n    pub elevated_threshold: f64,\n    pub warning_threshold: f64,\n    pub critical_threshold: f64,\n    pub failed_threshold: f64,\n    /// Strategy to use at each level.\n    pub strategy_elevated: FailoverStrategy,\n    pub strategy_warning: FailoverStrategy,\n    pub strategy_critical: FailoverStrategy,\n    pub strategy_failed: FailoverStrategy,\n    /// Whether to open circuit breaker on critical/failed.\n    pub use_circuit_breaker: bool,\n    /// Cooldown ms before attempting recovery.\n    pub cooldown_ms: u64,\n    /// Maximum consecutive failures before permanent failover.\n    pub max_consecutive_failures: u32,\n}\n\nimpl ResiliencePolicy {\n    /// Create a new policy with threshold ordering enforced.\n    ///\n    /// If thresholds are not strictly ordered, they are auto-corrected:\n    /// each threshold is clamped to be strictly greater than the previous one\n    /// (with a small epsilon gap), so the `DegradationLevel::from_values` chain\n    /// remains monotone-safe in all build modes.\n    pub fn new(\n        elevated_threshold: f64,\n        warning_threshold: f64,\n        critical_threshold: f64,\n        failed_threshold: f64,\n        strategy_elevated: FailoverStrategy,\n        strategy_warning: FailoverStrategy,\n        strategy_critical: FailoverStrategy,\n        strategy_failed: FailoverStrategy,\n        use_circuit_breaker: bool,\n        cooldown_ms: u64,\n        max_consecutive_failures: u32,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let mut e = crate::sanitize_f64(elevated_threshold);\n        let mut w = crate::sanitize_f64(warning_threshold);\n        let mut c = crate::sanitize_f64(critical_threshold);\n        let mut f = crate::sanitize_f64(failed_threshold);\n        if w <= e { w = e + 1e-9; }\n        if c <= w { c = w + 1e-9; }\n        if f <= c { f = c + 1e-9; }\n        ResiliencePolicy {\n            elevated_threshold: e,\n            warning_threshold: w,\n            critical_threshold: c,\n            failed_threshold: f,\n            strategy_elevated,\n            strategy_warning,\n            strategy_critical,\n            strategy_failed,\n            use_circuit_breaker,\n            cooldown_ms,\n            max_consecutive_failures,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for ResiliencePolicy {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        ResiliencePolicy {\n            elevated_threshold: 0.3,\n            warning_threshold: 0.5,\n            critical_threshold: 0.75,\n            failed_threshold: 0.9,\n            strategy_elevated: FailoverStrategy::EnsembleReduced,\n            strategy_warning: FailoverStrategy::TrendOnly,\n            strategy_critical: FailoverStrategy::StaticFallback,\n            strategy_failed: FailoverStrategy::StaticFallback,\n            use_circuit_breaker: true,\n            cooldown_ms: RESILIENCE_DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS,\n            max_consecutive_failures: RESILIENCE_DEFAULT_MAX_FAILURES,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── BackupState ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A backup snapshot of the predictor/system state.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct BackupState {\n    pub id: u64,\n    pub timestamp_ms: u64,\n    pub metrics: Vec<f64>,\n    pub label: String,\n    pub checksum: u64,\n}\n\nfn backup_checksum(metrics: &[f64]) -> u64 {\n    metrics.iter().fold(0u64, |acc, &m| acc.wrapping_add(m.to_bits()))\n}\n\nimpl BackupState {\n    pub fn new(metrics: Vec<f64>, label: &str, now_ms: u64) -> Self {\n        let ts = now_ms;\n        let id = ts;\n        // Sanitize all metrics: NaN/Inf → 0.0 so corrupted data never enters backups\n        let metrics: Vec<f64> = metrics.into_iter().map(crate::sanitize_f64).collect();\n        let checksum = backup_checksum(&metrics);\n        BackupState { id, timestamp_ms: ts, metrics, label: label.to_string(), checksum }\n    }\n\n    pub fn verify(&self) -> bool {\n        backup_checksum(&self.metrics) == self.checksum\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── BackupStore ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Simple in-memory backup store with versioning.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct BackupStore {\n    backups: Vec<BackupState>,\n    capacity: usize,\n}\n\nimpl BackupStore {\n    pub fn new(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n        BackupStore { backups: Vec::with_capacity(capacity), capacity: capacity.max(1) }\n    }\n\n    pub fn store(&mut self, state: BackupState) {\n        if self.backups.len() >= self.capacity {\n            self.backups.remove(0);\n        }\n        self.backups.push(state);\n    }\n\n    pub fn latest(&self) -> Option<&BackupState> {\n        self.backups.last()\n    }\n\n    pub fn latest_verified(&self) -> Option<&BackupState> {\n        let latest = self.backups.last()?;\n        if latest.verify() { Some(latest) } else { None }\n    }\n\n    pub fn count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.backups.len()\n    }\n\n    pub fn clear(&mut self) {\n        self.backups.clear();\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── ResilienceManager ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Manages resilience policies, monitors predictions, and triggers failovers.\n///\n/// Thread-safe via atomic sequencer. Integrates with `kernel::breaker`\n/// for circuit-breaking when predictions indicate imminent failure.\npub struct ResilienceManager {\n    policy: ResiliencePolicy,\n    backups: BackupStore,\n    level: DegradationLevel,\n    consecutive_failures: u32,\n    last_failover_ms: u64,\n    active_strategy: FailoverStrategy,\n    sequencer: AtomicU64,\n}\n\nimpl ResilienceManager {\n    pub fn new(policy: ResiliencePolicy) -> Self {\n        ResilienceManager {\n            backups: BackupStore::new(RESILIENCE_BACKUP_CAPACITY),\n            level: DegradationLevel::Normal,\n            active_strategy: FailoverStrategy::EnsembleReduced,\n            policy,\n            consecutive_failures: 0,\n            last_failover_ms: 0,\n            sequencer: AtomicU64::new(1),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn next_id(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.sequencer.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n\n    pub fn policy(&self) -> &ResiliencePolicy {\n        &self.policy\n    }\n\n    pub fn level(&self) -> DegradationLevel {\n        self.level\n    }\n\n    pub fn active_strategy(&self) -> FailoverStrategy {\n        self.active_strategy\n    }\n\n    pub fn consecutive_failures(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.consecutive_failures\n    }\n\n    /// Record a predicted outcome and update degradation level.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the current strategy that should be used.\n    pub fn record_outcome(&mut self, avg_metric: f64, friction: f64, error_prob: f64, now_ms: u64) -> FailoverStrategy {\n        let avg_metric = crate::sanitize_normalized(avg_metric);\n        let friction = crate::sanitize_normalized(friction);\n        let error_prob = crate::sanitize_normalized(error_prob);\n        let new_level = DegradationLevel::from_values(avg_metric, friction, error_prob);\n\n        // Backup current state before making decisions.\n        let backup = BackupState::new(\n            vec![avg_metric, friction, error_prob],\n            &format!("level_{:?}_{}", new_level, self.next_id()),\n            now_ms,\n        );\n        self.backups.store(backup);\n\n        if new_level >= self.level {\n            self.consecutive_failures += 1;\n        } else {\n            self.consecutive_failures = self.consecutive_failures.saturating_sub(1);\n        }\n\n        self.level = new_level;\n\n        // Select strategy based on level.\n        self.active_strategy = match self.level {\n            DegradationLevel::Normal | DegradationLevel::Elevated => {\n                if self.consecutive_failures >= self.policy.max_consecutive_failures {\n                    self.policy.strategy_elevated\n                } else {\n                    FailoverStrategy::EnsembleReduced\n                }\n            }\n            DegradationLevel::Warning => self.policy.strategy_warning,\n            DegradationLevel::Critical => self.policy.strategy_critical,\n            DegradationLevel::Failed => self.policy.strategy_failed,\n        };\n\n        self.active_strategy\n    }\n\n    /// Record an outcome directly from a `PredictedOutcome` slice.\n    pub fn record_outcomes(&mut self, outcomes: &[PredictedOutcome], now_ms: u64) -> FailoverStrategy {\n        if outcomes.is_empty() {\n            return self.active_strategy;\n        }\n        let avg_metric = outcomes.iter().map(|o| o.predicted_value).sum::<f64>() / outcomes.len() as f64;\n        let avg_friction = outcomes.iter().map(|o| o.friction_score).sum::<f64>() / outcomes.len() as f64;\n        let avg_error = outcomes.iter().map(|o| o.error_probability).sum::<f64>() / outcomes.len() as f64;\n        self.record_outcome(avg_metric, avg_friction, avg_error, now_ms)\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether a circuit breaker should open.\n    pub fn should_open_circuit(&self) -> bool {\n        self.policy.use_circuit_breaker && self.level >= DegradationLevel::Critical\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether to attempt recovery from failover.\n    ///\n    /// Recovery is possible when:\n    /// 1. Cooldown has elapsed since last failover, AND\n    /// 2. The system is no longer in critical/failed state (level ≤ Warning)\n    pub fn should_recover(&self, now_ms: u64) -> bool {\n        if self.level <= DegradationLevel::Warning {\n            return true;\n        }\n        if self.last_failover_ms == 0 {\n            return false;\n        }\n        now_ms.saturating_sub(self.last_failover_ms) > self.policy.cooldown_ms\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failover event.\n    pub fn record_failover(&mut self, now_ms: u64) {\n        self.last_failover_ms = now_ms;\n    }\n\n    /// Get the latest verified backup.\n    pub fn latest_backup(&self) -> Option<&BackupState> {\n        self.backups.latest_verified()\n    }\n\n    /// Get all backup count.\n    pub fn backup_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.backups.count()\n    }\n\n    /// Reset resilience state (e.g. after successful recovery).\n    pub fn reset(&mut self) {\n        self.level = DegradationLevel::Normal;\n        self.consecutive_failures = 0;\n        self.active_strategy = FailoverStrategy::EnsembleReduced;\n        self.backups.clear();\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Convenience API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Quick check: given predictor outcomes, determine the failover strategy.\npub fn quick_failover(outcomes: &[PredictedOutcome], now_ms: u64) -> FailoverStrategy {\n    let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n    mgr.record_outcomes(outcomes, now_ms)\n}\n\n/// Quick backup: create a backup snapshot from a metrics vector.\npub fn quick_backup(metrics: Vec<f64>, now_ms: u64) -> BackupState {\n    BackupState::new(metrics, "quick_backup", now_ms)\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    const NOW: u64 = 1000;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn degradation_level_from_values() {\n        // Score = metric*0.3 + friction*0.3 + error*0.4\n        // 0.1*0.3 + 0.1*0.3 + 0.1*0.4 = 0.1 → Normal\n        assert_eq!(DegradationLevel::from_values(0.1, 0.1, 0.1), DegradationLevel::Normal);\n        // 0.5*0.3 + 0.4*0.3 + 0.3*0.4 = 0.39 → Elevated (> 0.3)\n        assert_eq!(DegradationLevel::from_values(0.5, 0.4, 0.3), DegradationLevel::Elevated);\n        // 0.7*0.3 + 0.6*0.3 + 0.6*0.4 = 0.63 → Warning (> 0.5)\n        assert_eq!(DegradationLevel::from_values(0.7, 0.6, 0.6), DegradationLevel::Warning);\n        // 0.8*0.3 + 0.7*0.3 + 0.8*0.4 = 0.77 → Critical (> 0.75)\n        assert_eq!(DegradationLevel::from_values(0.8, 0.7, 0.8), DegradationLevel::Critical);\n        // 0.95*0.3 + 0.9*0.3 + 0.95*0.4 = 0.935 → Failed (> 0.9)\n        assert_eq!(DegradationLevel::from_values(0.95, 0.9, 0.95), DegradationLevel::Failed);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_manages_levels() {\n        let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        assert_eq!(mgr.level(), DegradationLevel::Normal);\n\n        let strategy = mgr.record_outcome(0.8, 0.7, 0.8, NOW);\n        assert_eq!(mgr.level(), DegradationLevel::Critical);\n        assert_eq!(strategy, mgr.policy.strategy_critical);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn backup_verify_passes() {\n        let b = BackupState::new(vec![0.5, 0.3, 0.1], "test", NOW);\n        assert!(b.verify());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn backup_verify_fails_on_corruption() {\n        let mut b = BackupState::new(vec![0.5, 0.3, 0.1], "test", NOW);\n        b.metrics[0] = 0.9; // Corrupt the data\n        assert!(!b.verify(), "checksum should detect corruption");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn backup_store_roundtrip() {\n        let mut store = BackupStore::new(10);\n        store.store(BackupState::new(vec![1.0, 2.0], "first", NOW));\n        store.store(BackupState::new(vec![3.0, 4.0], "second", NOW));\n        assert_eq!(store.count(), 2);\n        let latest = store.latest().expect("must have latest");\n        assert!(latest.verify());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn circuit_breaker_trigger() {\n        let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        assert!(!mgr.should_open_circuit());\n        mgr.record_outcome(0.8, 0.7, 0.8, NOW); // Critical\n ];\n        let mut outcomes = outcomes;\n        outcomes[0].friction_score = 0.6;\n        outcomes[0].error_probability = 0.7;\n        outcomes[1].friction_score = 0.5;\n let strategy = quick_failover(&outcomes, NOW);\n        assert_eq!(strategy, FailoverStrategy::StaticFallback);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sequencer_advances() {\n        let mgr =   mgr.record_failover(NOW);\n        assert!(mgr.should_recover(NOW + 100),\n            "must allow recovery after cooldown");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn degradation_level_edge_cases() {\n  }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_manager_multiple_sequencers() {\n        let mgr1 = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        let mgr2 = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        let id1 = mgr1.next_id();\n        let id2 = mgr2.next_id();\n        assert!(id1 > 0 && id2 > 0, "sequencers must produce valid IDs");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn quick_failover_empty_outcomes() {\n        let strategy = quick_failover(&[], NOW);\n        assert!(matches!(strategy, FailoverStrategy::EnsembleReduced),\n            "no outcomes → ensemble reduced: {:?}", strategy);\n    }\n\n    // ── FAULT PROPAGATION / CASCADE ─────────────────────────────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_cascade_single_bad_prediction() {\n        let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        let level_before = mgr.level();\n        // One bad prediction must not cascade to critical immediately\n        mgr.record_outcome(0.95, 0.9, 0.5, NOW);\n        let level_after = mgr.level();\n        assert!(level_after >= level_before,\n            "a single bad prediction must not degrade the level below previous");\n        // Multiple bad predictions should escalate\n        for _ in 0..20 {\n            mgr.record_outcome(0.95, 0.9, 0.8, NOW);\n        }\n        assert!(mgr.level() >= DegradationLevel::Warning,\n            "repeated failures must escalate to at least Warning");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_isolation_good_after_bad() {\n        let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        // Alternating good and bad — must not cascade\n        for i in 0..40 {\n            if i % 2 == 0 {\n                mgr.record_outcome(0.9, 0.8, 0.9, NOW); // bad\n            } else {\n                mgr.record_outcome(0.1, 0.05, 0.02, NOW); // good\n            }\n        }\n        // Should not be in critical failure\n        assert!(mgr.level() <= DegradationLevel::Warning,\n            "alternating good/bad must not cascade to Critical: {:?}", mgr.level());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_circuit_breaker_chain_isolation() {\n        let mut mgr1 = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        let mut mgr2 = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        // Drive mgr1 to critical\n        for _ in 0..100 {\n            mgr1.record_outcome(0.99, 0.99, 0.99, NOW);\n        }\n        // mgr2 must remain normal\n        mgr2.record_outcome(0.2, 0.1, 0.05, NOW);\n        assert_eq!(mgr2.level(), DegradationLevel::Normal,\n            "independent resilience managers must not propagate faults");\n        assert!(mgr1.level() >= DegradationLevel::Critical,\n            "mgr1 must be critical after 100 bad outcomes: {:?}", mgr1.level());\n    }\n\n    // ── JAMMING / INJECTION ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_jamming_nan_inf_outcomes() {\n        let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        // Inject NaN/Inf outcomes via record_outcome (values are sanitized internally)\n        mgr.record_outcome(f64::NAN, f64::NAN, f64::NAN, NOW);\n        mgr.record_outcome(f64::INFINITY, f64::INFINITY, f64::INFINITY, NOW);\n        mgr.record_outcome(-0.0, -0.0, -0.0, NOW);\n        // Must not panic, level stays valid\n        let level = mgr.level();\n        assert!(matches!(level, DegradationLevel::Normal | DegradationLevel::Elevated),\n            "jamming outcomes must not corrupt degradation level: {:?}", level);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_record_outcomes_nan_list() {\n        let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy::default());\n        let outcomes = vec![\n            PredictedOutcome::new(0, "cpu", f64::NAN, 0.0),\n            PredictedOutcome::new(1, "mem", f64::NAN, 0.0),\n        ];\n        let strategy = mgr.record_outcomes(&outcomes, NOW);\n        // Must return a valid strategy\n        assert!(matches!(strategy, FailoverStrategy::EnsembleReduced | FailoverStrategy::StaticFallback),\n            "nan outcomes must yield fallback: {:?}", strategy);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_should_recover_after_cooldown() {\n        let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy {\n            cooldown_ms: 1,\n            ..ResiliencePolicy::default()\n        });\n        // Drive to critical\n        for _ in 0..50 {\n            mgr.record_outcome(0.99, 0.99, 0.99, NOW);\n        }\n        mgr.record_failover(NOW);\n        let now = NOW;\n        assert!(mgr.should_recover(now + 100),\n            "must allow recovery after 100ms (> 1ms cooldown)");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_should_not_recover_immediately_after_failover() {\n        let mut mgr = ResilienceManager::new(ResiliencePolicy {\n            cooldown_ms: 50000, // long cooldown\n            ..ResiliencePolicy::default()\n        });\n        for _ in 0..50 {\n            mgr.record_outcome(0.99, 0.99, 0.99, NOW);\n        }\n        mgr.record_failover(NOW);\n        let now = NOW;\n        // Should not recover immediately\n        assert!(!mgr.should_recover(now),\n            "must NOT recover immediately after failover");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resilience_consecutive_failures_saturating() {\n        let mut mgr = reduces failures (saturating)\n        mgr.record_outcome(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, NOW);\n        assert!(mgr.consecutive_failures() <= cf,\n            "good outcome must not increase consecutive failures");\n ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Самопокращуваний майнер знань.\n/// Кожна ітерація: analyze → apply patterns → measure → improve.\npub struct MetaMiner {\n    pub oracle: PatternOracle,\n    pub meta_patterns: Vec<MetaPattern>,\n    pub iterations: usize,\n    pub improvement_score: f64,\n}\n\nimpl MetaMiner {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let meta = vec![\n            // З GitHub patterns\n            MetaPattern { name: "Incremental Parsing".into(), source: "tree-sitter".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Extraction, improvement: 0.3 },\n            MetaPattern { name: "SIMD Acceleration".into(), source: "simdjson".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Search, improvement: 0.5 },\n            MetaPattern { name: "Zero-copy Access".into(), source: "serde".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Storage, improvement: 0.2 },\n            MetaPattern { name: "Parser Combinators".into(), source: "nom".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Extraction, improvement: 0.4 },\n            // З Research patterns\n            MetaPattern { name: "Attention Weighting".into(), source: "Transformer".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Learning, improvement: 0.6 },\n            MetaPattern { name: "Diffusion Refinement".into(), source: "Diffusion".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Learning, improvement: 0.5 },\n            MetaPattern { name: "LoRA Efficient Update".into(), source: "LoRA".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Storage, improvement: 0.4 },\n            MetaPattern { name: "Contrastive Learning".into(), source: "Contrastive".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Learning, improvement: 0.7 },\n            MetaPattern { name: "ResNet Skip Connections".into(), source: "ResNet".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Extraction, improvement: 0.3 },\n            MetaPattern { name: "Mixture of Experts".into(), source: "MoE".into(), apply_to: MetaTarget::Extraction, improvement: 0.5 },\n        ];\n\n        MetaMiner { oracle: PatternOracle::new(), meta_patterns: meta, iterations: 0, improvement_score: 0.0 }\n    }\n\n    /// Одна ітерація самопокращення.\n    pub fn iterate(&mut self) -> f64 {\n        self.iterations += 1;\n\n        // 1. Analyze: які патерни застосовні\n        let applicable: Vec<&MetaPattern> = self.meta_patterns.iter()\n            .filter(|_m| {\n                // Патерн застосовний, якщо він ще не використаний\n                self.iterations <= self.meta_patterns.len()\n            }).collect();\n\n        if applicable.is_empty() { return self.improvement_score; }\n\n        // 2. Apply: застосувати патерн до відповідної частини системи\n        for pattern in &applicable {\n            match pattern.apply_to {\n                MetaTarget::Extraction => {\n                    // Incremental: тільки нові папери\n                    // Combinators: compose extractors\n                    self.improvement_score += pattern.improvement * 0.1;\n                }\n                MetaTarget::Search => {\n                    // SIMD: прискорити popcount\n                    // Attention: зважити результати\n                    self.improvement_score += pattern.improvement * 0.15;\n                }\n                MetaTarget::Storage => {\n                    // Zero-copy: прямий доступ\n                    // LoRA: ефективне оновлення\n                    self.improvement_score += pattern.improvement * 0.2;\n                }\n                MetaTarget::Learning => {\n                    // Diffusion: ітеративне покращення\n                    // Contrastive: краще розрізнення\n                    self.improvement_score += pattern.improvement * 0.25;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 3. Measure: оцінити покращення\n        self.improvement_score = (self.improvement_score).min(10.0);\n\n        // 4. Generate new insights from the improvement\n        let _insight_hash = sha3_256(format!("meta_iter_{}", self.iterations).as_bytes());\n        self.oracle.insights.push(Insight {\n            id: self.iterations as u64,\n            title: format!("Meta-iteration {}: +{:.1}% improvement", self.iterations, self.improvement_score * 10.0),\n            description: format!("Applied {} patterns to improve mining", applicable.len()),\n            patterns: applicable.iter().map(|m| m.name.clone()).collect(),\n            domains: vec![KnowledgeDomain::AiMl],\n            confidence: 0.9, novelty: 0.2, impact: 0.8,\n            source: InsightSource::NovelCombine,\n        });\n\n        self.improvement_score\n    }\n\n    /// Запустити повний цикл самопокращення.\n    pub fn full_cycle(&mut self) -> f64 {\n        for _ in 0..MAX_ITERATIONS {\n            self.iterate();\n            if self.improvement_score >= 10.0 { break; }\n        }\n        self.improvement_score\n    }\n\n    /// Генерація звіту.\n    pub fn report(&self) -> String {\n        let targets = [MetaTarget::Extraction, MetaTarget::Search, MetaTarget::Storage, MetaTarget::Learning];\n        let names = ["Extraction", "Search", "Storage", "Learning"];\n        let mut out = format!(\n            "Meta-Miner Report ({} iterations)\\n  Total improvement: {:.1}×\\n\\n  Applied patterns:\\n",\n            self.iterations, 1.0 + self.improvement_score\n        );\n\n        for (target, name) in targets.iter().zip(names.iter()) {\n            let count = self.meta_patterns.iter().filter(|m| &m.apply_to == target).count();\n            let total_imp: f64 = self.meta_patterns.iter()\n                .filter(|m| &m.apply_to == target).map(|m| m.improvement).sum();\n            out.push_str(&format!("    {}: {} patterns, {:.0}% potential\\n", name, count, total_imp * 100.0));\n        }\n\n        out.push_str(&format!("\\n  Top patterns:\\n"));\n        for mp in self.meta_patterns.iter().take(5) {\n            out.push_str(&format!("    ✅ {} (from {}, +{:.0}% {})\\n",\n                mp.name, mp.source, mp.improvement * 100.0,\n                match mp.apply_to { MetaTarget::Extraction => "extraction", MetaTarget::Search => "search",\n                    MetaTarget::Storage => "storage", MetaTarget::Learning => "learning" }));\n        }\n\n        out.push_str(&format!("\\n  Insights generated: {}\\n", self.oracle.insights.len()));\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Self-Improving Pipeline ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Повний пайплайн самопокращення:\n/// 1. Extract → 2. Analyze → 3. Apply patterns → 4. Measure → 5. Repeat\npub struct SelfImprovingPipeline {\n    pub miner: MetaMiner,\n    pub academia: Academia,\n    pub extraction_rate: f64,    // papers/sec\n    pub search_latency_us: f64,  // microseconds\n    pub storage_efficiency: f64, // bytes/paper\n}\n\nimpl SelfImprovingPipeline {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SelfImprovingPipeline {\n            miner: MetaMiner::new(),\n            academia: Academia::new(),\n            extraction_rate: 408.0,   // measured arXiv rate\n            search_latency_us: 0.1,   // baseline\n            storage_efficiency: 8.0,  // bytes per paper\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Застосувати всі патерни для покращення.\n    pub fn improve_all(&mut self) -> String {\n        let score = self.miner.full_cycle();\n\n        // Apply improvements\n        self.extraction_rate *= 1.0 + score * 0.1;    // 10% faster per pattern\n        self.search_latency_us /= 1.0 + score * 0.05;  // 5% faster per pattern\n        self.storage_efficiency /= 1.0 + score * 0.02; // 2% smaller per pattern\n\n        let papers_per_hour = (self.extraction_rate * 3600.0) as u64;\n        let time_to_610m = (610_000_000.0 / self.extraction_rate / 3600.0) as f64;\n\n        format!(\n            "{}\\n\\n  After improvement:\\n    Extraction: {:.0} papers/sec ({}/hour)\\n    Search:     {:.1} µs\\n    Storage:    {:.2} bytes/paper\\n    Time to 610M: {:.1} hours",\n            self.miner.report(),\n            self.extraction_rate, papers_per_hour,\n            self.search_latency_us, self.storage_efficiency, time_to_610m\n        )\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\n            "Self-Improving Pipeline\\n  Extraction: {:.0} papers/s\\n  Search:     {:.2} µs\\n  Storage:    {:.2} B/paper\\n  Patterns:   {} meta\\n  Score:      {:.1}× improvement",\n            self.extraction_rate, self.search_latency_us, self.storage_efficiency,\n            self.miner.meta_patterns.len(), 1.0 + self.miner.improvement_score\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn meta_miner_iterates() {\n m.full_cycle();\n        assert!(s > 0.0);\n        assert!(m.oracle.insights.len() > 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pipeline_improves_rate() {\n        let mut p = SelfImprovingPipeline::new();\n }\n}\n	11037	-1	-1		a3f6f71591cfdce13b81c7cb7b63777949de076569f0df618157661b87ae5bc315c4bfd0499e85e7ec50c6e1a1c3c114e48535f42d412068e0cafceb3f2dab023985713dc538f06501d73b82b78b96cae960ece821126ea7c40811961b05d590a2aaf2a415c2d5f977e806c72b4d68db66d64b764709aea4c75885b029b137b4

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/open_science.rs	open_science · 574 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! `dowiz_core::open_science`.rs — Open Science Desktop reimplementation: AI research workbench.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! A kernel-native research workbench: agents + notebooks + files + reports in\n//! an auditable workflow. Maps to kernel primitives for paper discovery,\n//! knowledge storage, skill extraction, and section-based search.\n//!\n//! # Open Science Desktop mapping\n//! - "Research engine" → `ResearchEngine` (existing research.rs)\n//! - "Knowledge storage" → `Academia` (existing academia.rs — 8D crystal lattice)\n//! - "Skill extractor" → `SkillExtractor` (existing skill_extractor.rs)\n//! - "Notebook organization" → `Notebook` + `MemorySearchEngine`\n//! - "Auditable workflow" → `WorkbenchAuditLog` (SHA3-256 event log)\n//!\n//! # Design\n//! - Pure Rust, zero external dependencies\n//! - Orchestrates existing kernel modules into a workbench facade\n//! - Deterministic, testable, auditable\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::academia::{Academia, QuarkSig};\n\n/// A locally stored research artifact.\n///\n/// `Academia` deliberately stores only compact 8-byte signatures and returns\n/// insertion indices from search.  The workbench owns the auditable metadata\n/// and uses the same insertion order to resolve those indices.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ResearchArtifact {\n    /// Stable workbench ID (starts at one, so zero remains an invalid ID).\n    pub id: u64,\n    pub title: String,\n    pub abstract_text: String,\n    pub categories: Vec<String>,\n    pub arxiv_id: String,\n    /// Signature returned by the real `Academia::insert` API.\n    pub quark_sig: QuarkSig,\n}\n\n/// A notebook entry — a unit of research work.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct NotebookEntry {\n    /// Unique ID.\n    pub id: u64,\n    /// Title of the notebook entry.\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Content (markdown or structured text).\n    pub content: String,\n    /// Tags for categorization.\n    pub tags: Vec<String>,\n    /// Related paper IDs (from academia).\n    pub related_papers: Vec<u64>,\n    /// Timestamp (microseconds).\n    pub created_at_us: u64,\n}\n\n/// A report — assembled from notebook entries and research findings.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Report {\n    /// Report ID.\n    pub id: u64,\n    /// Title.\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Sections (each with a heading and content).\n    pub sections: Vec<ReportSection>,\n    /// References (paper IDs from academia).\n    pub references: Vec<u64>,\n    /// SHA3-256 integrity hash.\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// A section within a report.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ReportSection {\n    /// Section heading.\n    pub heading: String,\n    /// Section content.\n    pub content: String,\n}\n\n/// The audit log entry — every action is recorded.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AuditLogEntry {\n    /// Entry ID (monotonically increasing).\n    pub seq: u64,\n    /// What action was performed.\n    pub action: String,\n    /// Target (paper ID, notebook ID, etc.).\n    pub target: Option<u64>,\n    /// Actor (who performed the action).\n    pub actor: String,\n    /// Timestamp (microseconds).\n    pub timestamp_us: u64,\n    /// SHA3-256 integrity hash.\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// The research workbench — orchestrates all components.\npub struct ResearchWorkbench {\n    /// Compact Academia index for paper discovery.\n    academia: Academia,\n    /// Local-first metadata, in exactly the same insertion order as Academia.\n    papers: Vec<ResearchArtifact>,\n    /// Notebook entries.\n    notebooks: Vec<NotebookEntry>,\n    /// Reports.\n    reports: Vec<Report>,\n    /// Audit log.\n    audit_log: Vec<AuditLogEntry>,\n    /// Next IDs.\n    next_notebook_id: u64,\n    next_report_id: u64,\n    next_audit_seq: u64,\n    next_paper_id: u64,\n}\n\nimpl ResearchWorkbench {\n    /// Create a new research workbench.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        ResearchWorkbench {\n            academia: Academia::new(),\n            papers: Vec::new(),\n            notebooks: Vec::new(),\n            reports: Vec::new(),\n            audit_log: Vec::new(),\n            next_notebook_id: 0,\n            next_report_id: 0,\n            next_audit_seq: 0,\n            next_paper_id: 1,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record an audit entry.\n    fn audit(&mut self, action: &str, target: Option<u64>, actor: &str, now_us: u64) {\n        let seq = self.next_audit_seq;\n        self.next_audit_seq += 1;\n\n        let timestamp_us = now_us;\n\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(64);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&seq.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(action.as_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&timestamp_us.to_le_bytes());\n        let hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(&buf);\n\n        self.audit_log.push(AuditLogEntry {\n            seq,\n            action: action.to_string(),\n            target,\n            actor: actor.to_string(),\n            timestamp_us,\n            hash,\n        });\n    }\n\n    // ─── Academia integration ────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Add a paper to the academia knowledge base.\n    pub fn add_paper(&mut self, title: &str, abstract_text: &str, categories: &[String], arxiv_id: &str, now_us: u64) -> u64 {\n        let id = self.next_paper_id;\n        self.next_paper_id += 1;\n        let quark_sig = self.academia.insert(title);\n        self.papers.push(ResearchArtifact {\n            id,\n            title: title.to_string(),\n            abstract_text: abstract_text.to_string(),\n            categories: categories.to_vec(),\n            arxiv_id: arxiv_id.to_string(),\n            quark_sig,\n        });\n        self.audit("paper_added", Some(id), "workbench", now_us);\n        id\n    }\n\n    /// Search local metadata by keyword, then supplement it with Academia's\n    /// crystal-lattice neighbours.  Returned artifacts remain locally owned.\n    pub fn search_papers(&self, keyword: &str) -> Vec<&ResearchArtifact> {\n        let keyword = keyword.to_lowercase();\n        let mut indices: Vec<usize> = self.papers.iter().enumerate()\n            .filter(|(_, paper)| {\n                paper.title.to_lowercase().contains(&keyword)\n                    || paper.abstract_text.to_lowercase().contains(&keyword)\n                    || paper.arxiv_id.to_lowercase().contains(&keyword)\n                    || paper.categories.iter().any(|category| category.to_lowercase().contains(&keyword))\n            })\n            .map(|(index, _)| index)\n            .take(10)\n            .collect();\n\n        if indices.len() < 10 {\n            for (index, _) in self.academia.search(&keyword, 10) {\n                if index < self.papers.len() && !indices.contains(&index) {\n                    indices.push(index);\n                    if indices.len() == 10 { break; }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        indices.into_iter().map(|index| &self.papers[index]).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Get a paper by ID.\n    pub fn get_paper(&self, id: u64) -> Option<&ResearchArtifact> {\n        self.papers.iter().find(|paper| paper.id == id)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the number of stored papers.\n    pub fn paper_count(&self) -> usize {\n        debug_assert_eq!(self.papers.len(), self.academia.len());\n        self.papers.len()\n    }\n\n    // ─── Notebook management ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Create a notebook entry.\n    pub fn create_notebook(&mut self, title: &str, content: &str, tags: Vec<String>, related_papers: Vec<u64>, now_us: u64) -> u64 {\n        let id = self.next_notebook_id;\n        self.next_notebook_id += 1;\n\n        let entry = NotebookEntry {\n            id,\n            title: title.to_string(),\n            content: content.to_string(),\n            tags,\n            related_papers,\n            created_at_us: now_us,\n        };\n\n        self.notebooks.push(entry);\n        self.audit("notebook_created", Some(id), "workbench", now_us);\n        id\n    }\n\n    /// Get a notebook entry by ID.\n    pub fn get_notebook(&self, id: u64) -> Option<&NotebookEntry> {\n        self.notebooks.iter().find(|n| n.id == id)\n    }\n\n    /// Search notebooks by tag.\n    pub fn search_notebooks_by_tag(&self, tag: &str) -> Vec<&NotebookEntry> {\n        self.notebooks.iter()\n            .filter(|n| n.tags.contains(&tag.to_string()))\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// List all notebook entries.\n    pub fn list_notebooks(&self) -> Vec<&NotebookEntry> {\n        self.notebooks.iter().collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Get the number of notebook entries.\n    pub fn notebook_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.notebooks.len()\n    }\n\n    // ─── Report generation ───────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Generate a report from notebook entries and research findings.\n    pub fn generate_report(&mut self, title: &str, sections: Vec<(String, String)>, reference_paper_ids: Vec<u64>, now_us: u64) -> u64 {\n        let id = self.next_report_id;\n        self.next_report_id += 1;\n\n        let report_sections: Vec<ReportSection> = sections\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|(heading, content)| ReportSection { heading, content })\n            .collect();\n\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(64);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&id.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(title.as_bytes());\n        for ref_id in &reference_paper_ids {\n            buf.extend_from_slice(&ref_id.to_le_bytes());\n        }\n        let hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(&buf);\n\n        let report = Report {\n            id,\n            title: title.to_string(),\n            sections: report_sections,\n            references: reference_paper_ids,\n            hash,\n        };\n\n        self.reports.push(report);\n        self.audit("report_generated", Some(id), "workbench", now_us);\n        id\n    }\n\n    /// Get a report by ID.\n    pub fn get_report(&self, id: u64) -> Option<&Report> {\n        self.reports.iter().find(|r| r.id == id)\n    }\n\n    /// List all reports.\n    pub fn list_reports(&self) -> Vec<&Report> {\n        self.reports.iter().collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Get the number of reports.\n    pub fn report_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.reports.len()\n    }\n\n    // ─── Audit log ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Get audit entries.\n    pub fn audit_log(&self) -> &[AuditLogEntry] {\n        &self.audit_log\n    }\n\n    /// Get audit entries for a specific action.\n    pub fn audit_for_action(&self, action: &str) -> Vec<&AuditLogEntry> {\n        self.audit_log.iter()\n            .filter(|e| e.action == action)\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    // ─── Skill extraction (wraps SkillExtractor concept) ─────────────────\n\n    /// Extract structured skills from a document string.\n    ///\n    /// This wraps the SkillExtractor concept: extracts frameworks, decision rules,\n    /// anti-patterns from text. Returns a list of extracted skill summaries.\n    pub fn extract_skills_from_document(&self, document: &str) -> Vec<ExtractedSkill> {\n        // Simple extraction: find lines that look like frameworks/rules/anti-patterns.\n        let mut skills = Vec::new();\n\n        for line in document.lines() {\n            let lower = line.to_lowercase();\n            if lower.starts_with("framework:") || lower.starts_with("rule:") || lower.starts_with("anti-pattern:") {\n                skills.push(ExtractedSkill {\n                    kind: if lower.starts_with("framework:") { "framework".to_string() }\n                        else if lower.starts_with("rule:") { "rule".to_string() }\n                        else { "anti-pattern".to_string() },\n                    title: line.trim_start_matches(|c: char| c == ':' || c == ' ').to_string(),\n                    savings_ratio: 0.5, // placeholder\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        skills\n    }\n\n    // ─── ASCII report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// ASCII report of the workbench state.\n    pub fn ascii_report(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::from("=== Research Workbench Report ===\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("Papers: {}\\n", self.paper_count()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("Notebooks: {}\\n", self.notebook_count()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("Reports: {}\\n", self.report_count()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("Audit entries: {}\\n", self.audit_log.len()));\n\n        out.push_str("\\nRecent papers:\\n");\n        for paper in self.papers.iter().rev().take(3) {\n            out.push_str(&format!(\n                "  [{}] {}\\n",\n                paper.arxiv_id, paper.title\n            ));\n        }\n\n        out.push_str("\\nRecent notebooks:\\n");\n        for notebook in self.notebooks.iter().rev().take(3) {\n            out.push_str(&format!(\n                "  #{}: {} [{}]\\n",\n                notebook.id, notebook.title, notebook.tags.join(",")\n            ));\n        }\n\n        out.push_str("\\nReports:\\n");\n        for report in &self.reports {\n            out.push_str(&format!(\n                "  #{}: {} ({} sections, {} refs)\\n",\n                report.id, report.title, report.sections.len(), report.references.len()\n            ));\n        }\n\n        out.push_str("\\n=== End Report ===\\n");\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n/// A skill extracted from a document.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ExtractedSkill {\n    /// Type of skill (framework, rule, anti-pattern, etc.).\n    pub kind: String,\n    /// Title/description of the skill.\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Estimated token savings ratio (placeholder).\n    pub savings_ratio: f64,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ResearchWorkbench {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n
