```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/telemetry_harvest.rs	telemetry_harvest · 359 lines	#![allow(unused)]\n//! `kernel::telemetry_harvest` — deterministic, zero-dep harvest ledger.\n//!\n//! Every hot path MUST emit a deterministic, zero-dep telemetry record.\n//! Every new capability MUST be probe-able.\n//!\n//! The harvest ledger is gov_route-compatible: records serialize as JSONL lines\n//! in the same `{model,task,success,value,cost}` schema as the dispatcher's\n//! `track_record.jsonl`, so the EV loop can price every operation uniformly.\n//!\n//! # Reference pattern\n//! - `track_record.jsonl` at the kernel root: `{model,task,success,value,cost,...}`\n//! - The `Dispatcher` records every dispatch; this ledger extends that pattern\n//!   into the kernel-native hot paths (enrich, intent detect, trinary math).\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Deterministic, zero-dep telemetry record for the harvest ledger.\n/// Compatible with gov_route-compatible dispatch schema.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct HarvestRecord {\n    pub model: String,\n    pub task: String,\n    pub success: bool,\n    pub value: f64,\n    pub cost: f64,\n    pub timestamp_ms: u64,\n}\n\nimpl HarvestRecord {\n    pub fn new(model: &str, task: &str, success: bool, value: f64, cost: f64, now_ms: u64) -> Self {\n        HarvestRecord {\n            model: model.to_string(),\n            task: task.to_string(),\n            success,\n            value: crate::sanitize_f64(value),\n            cost: crate::sanitize_f64(cost).max(0.0),\n            timestamp_ms: now_ms,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Single JSON object line — gov_route-compatible schema with optional timestamp.\n    pub fn to_jsonl_line(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\n            r#"{{"model":"{}","task":"{}","success":{},"value":{},"cost":{},"timestamp_ms":{}}}"#,\n            self.model, self.task, self.success,\n            crate::sanitize_f64(self.value),\n            crate::sanitize_f64(self.cost),\n            self.timestamp_ms,\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// Summary statistics over the harvest ledger.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct HarvestReport {\n    pub total: usize,\n    pub success_rate: f64,\n    pub ev_score: f64,\n    pub avg_value: f64,\n    pub avg_cost: f64,\n}\n\n/// Bounded, append-only harvest ledger.\n///\n/// Records carry `{model, task, success, value, cost, timestamp_ms}`.\n/// EV scoring: `ev_score = avg(value * success) / avg(cost + 1)`.\n/// JSONL output is gov_route-compatible (same field names as the dispatcher's\n/// `track_record.jsonl`).\npub struct HarvestLedger {\n    records: alloc::collections::VecDeque<HarvestRecord>,\n    max_records: usize,\n}\n\nimpl HarvestLedger {\n    pub fn new(max_records: usize) -> Self {\n        let init_cap = max_records.min(1024);\n        HarvestLedger {\n            records: alloc::collections::VecDeque::with_capacity(init_cap),\n            max_records: max_records.max(1),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a telemetry event. Returns the created record.\n    /// The ledger acts as a ring buffer: once full, oldest records are evicted\n    /// via O(1) `pop_front()` (a `VecDeque`, not a `Vec` O(n) `remove(0)` shift).\n    pub fn record(\n        &mut self,\n        model: &str,\n        task: &str,\n        success: bool,\n        value: f64,\n        cost: f64,\n        now_ms: u64,\n    ) -> HarvestRecord {\n        let rec = HarvestRecord::new(model, task, success, value, cost, now_ms);\n        if self.records.len() >= self.max_records {\n            self.records.pop_front();\n        }\n        self.records.push_back(rec.clone());\n        rec\n    }\n\n    /// Expected-value score: avg(value * success) / avg(cost + 1).\n    /// Higher is better (more value per unit cost). Returns 0.0 if empty.\n    pub fn ev_score(&self) -> f64 {\n        let n = self.records.len();\n        if n == 0 {\n            return 0.0;\n        }\n        let sum_value_success: f64 = self\n            .records\n            .iter()\n            .map(|r| r.value * if r.success { 1.0 } else { 0.0 })\n            .sum();\n        let sum_cost_plus_one: f64 = self.records.iter().map(|r| r.cost + 1.0).sum();\n        if sum_cost_plus_one == 0.0 {\n            return 0.0;\n        }\n        sum_value_success / sum_cost_plus_one\n    }\n\n    /// Produce a summary report over all records.\n    pub fn report(&self) -> HarvestReport {\n        let n = self.records.len();\n        let success_rate = if n > 0 {\n            self.records.iter().filter(|r| r.success).count() as f64 / n as f64\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n        let avg_value = if n > 0 {\n            self.records.iter().map(|r| r.value).sum::<f64>() / n as f64\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n        let avg_cost = if n > 0 {\n            self.records.iter().map(|r| r.cost).sum::<f64>() / n as f64\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n        HarvestReport {\n            total: n,\n            success_rate,\n            ev_score: self.ev_score(),\n            avg_value,\n            avg_cost,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Emit all records as gov_route-compatible JSONL (one object per line).\n    pub fn track_to_jsonl(&self) -> String {\n        self.records\n            .iter()\n            .map(|r| r.to_jsonl_line())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join("\\n")\n    }\n\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.records.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Value series over recorded events (in insertion order), for glyph\n    /// rendering (sparkline). Empty when no records.\n    pub fn value_series(&self) -> Vec<f64> {\n        self.records.iter().map(|r| r.value).collect()\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.records.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    pub fn records(&self) -> &alloc::collections::VecDeque<HarvestRecord> {\n        &self.records\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n    use super::*;\n\n    const NOW: u64 = 1000;\n\n    // ── HarvestRecord roundtrip ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_harvest_record_roundtrip() {\n        let rec = HarvestRecord::new("enrich", "lookup", true, 0.85, 1.2, NOW);\n        assert_eq!(rec.model, "enrich");\n        assert_eq!(rec.task, "lookup");\n        assert!(rec.success);\n        assert!((rec.value - 0.85).abs() < 1e-10);\n        assert!((rec.cost - 1.2).abs() < 1e-10);\n        assert!(rec.timestamp_ms > 0, "timestamp must be populated");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_harvest_record_sanitize_nan_value() {\n        let rec = HarvestRecord::new("test", "nan_check", false, f64::NAN, 5.0, NOW);\n        assert_eq!(rec.value, 0.0, "NaN value must be sanitized to 0.0");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_harvest_record_sanitize_negative_cost() {\n        let rec = HarvestRecord::new("test", "neg_cost", true, 0.5, -3.0, NOW);\n        assert_eq!(rec.cost, 0.0, "negative cost must be sanitized to 0.0");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_harvest_record_jsonl_line_format() {\n        let rec = HarvestRecord::new("enrich", "lookup", true, 0.85, 1.2, NOW);\n        let line = rec.to_jsonl_line();\n        assert!(line.starts_with("{"), "must start with {{");\n        assert!(line.ends_with("}"), "must end with }}");\n        assert!(line.contains(r#""model":"#), "must contain model field");\n        assert!(line.contains(r#""task":"#), "must contain task field");\n        assert!(line.contains(r#""success":"#), "must contain success field");\n        assert!(line.contains(r#""value":"#), "must contain value field");\n        assert!(line.contains(r#""cost":"#), "must contain cost field");\n        assert!(line.contains(r#""timestamp_ms":"#), "must contain timestamp_ms field");\n    }\n\n    // ── EV score monotonic ───────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_ev_score_monotonic() {\n        let mut ledger = HarvestLedger::new(100);\n        // 10 good records: high value, low cost\n        for _ in 0..10 {\n            ledger.record("test", "good", true, 0.9, 1.0, NOW);\n        }\n        let good_score = ledger.ev_score();\n        assert!(good_score > 0.0, "good records must produce positive EV");\n\n        // 1 bad record: zero value, high cost\n        ledger.record("test", "bad", false, 0.0, 100.0, NOW);\n        let after_bad = ledger.ev_score();\n        assert!(\n            after_bad < good_score,\n            "EV must drop after adding bad record: {good_score} → {after_bad}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_ev_score_empty_ledger() {\n        let ledger = HarvestLedger::new(100);\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/fdr/footprint.rs	footprint · 214 lines	//! `fdr/footprint.rs` — Item 69: water / carbon as derived, constant-multiplied views of `joules_uj`.\n//!\n//! The kernel needs NO new *measured* footprint field beyond `joules_uj` (item 27's RAPL/PMU\n//! work already is the silicon power-draw mechanism). This module is a **consumer-side**\n//! derivation layer keyed on operator-supplied `(region, deployment-class)` constants — it\n//! *derives* from `joules_uj`, it does NOT *store* a footprint (roadmap line 1194; fabricating a\n//! facility-cooling number software cannot observe is procedure step 4).\n//!\n//! Honesty invariants (item 69 §69.3/§69.4):\n//!   * `co2e`  = `joules × grid-carbon-intensity` (gCO₂e/kWh), degrading to a named absence when\n//!     `joules_uj` is absent OR the regional constant is unsupplied.\n//!   * `offsite_water` = `joules × WUE-source` (L/kWh), same degradation.\n//!   * `onsite_water` = PERMANENT named absence (`NotSoftwareObservable`) by construction — a local\n//!     device cannot observe facility cooling; there must be NO code path that produces an\n//!     on-site-water value.\n//!   * The module ships with the regional constants ABSENT (named-absence) and only lights up when\n//!     the operator supplies them. No new `HwStamp` field is added.\n\nuse crate::fdr::schema::{Absence, Reading};\n\n/// µJ per kWh (1 kWh = 3.6e9 J = 3.6e15 µJ). Used to convert the joules reading into a\n/// normalized energy unit before multiplying by the operator's regional constant.\nconst MICROJ_PER_KWH: f64 = 3.6e15;\n\n/// Operator-supplied regional grid constants. Absent by default (named-absence discipline) —\n/// the module never fabricates a default constant.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]\npub struct RegionConstants {\n    /// Grid carbon intensity, gCO₂e per kWh. `None` ⇒ derives to `Unavailable(NoRegionalConstant)`.\n    pub carbon_g_per_kwh: Option<f64>,\n    /// Water-usage-effectiveness of off-site (source) water, L per kWh. `None` ⇒ derives to\n    /// `Unavailable(NoRegionalConstant)`.\n    pub wue_l_per_kwh: Option<f64>,\n}\n\nimpl RegionConstants {\n    /// The default: BOTH constants absent. The kernel ships in this state; derived views are\n    /// named absences until the operator supplies real values.\n    pub fn missing() -> Self {\n        RegionConstants {\n            carbon_g_per_kwh: None,\n            wue_l_per_kwh: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Construct with explicit (operator-provided) constants.\n    pub fn new(carbon_g_per_kwh: Option<f64>, wue_l_per_kwh: Option<f64>) -> Self {\n        RegionConstants {\n            carbon_g_per_kwh,\n            wue_l_per_kwh,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Round a non-negative `f64` to the nearest `u64` (half away from zero), matching\n/// `f64::round() as u64` for the bounded, non-negative values this module derives.\n/// (`f64::round` is unavailable in this no_std toolchain; the cast saturates.)\nfn round_nonneg_to_u64(x: f64) -> u64 {\n    let t = x as u64; // saturating truncation\n    if x - (t as f64) >= 0.5 {\n        t.saturating_add(1)\n    } else {\n        t\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 69 (a): `co2e = joules × carbon-intensity`, in microgrammes.\n///\n/// Degrades to a named absence when `joules_uj` is absent (the same reason) OR when the regional\n/// carbon constant is unsupplied (`NoRegionalConstant`). The product is rounded to the nearest µ\n/// since the kernel carries integer `Reading<u64>` everywhere.\npub fn co2e_ug(joules: Reading<u64>, carbon_g_per_kwh: Option<f64>) -> Reading<u64> {\n    match joules {\n        Reading::Unavailable(a) => Reading::Unavailable(a),\n        Reading::Value(j) => match carbon_g_per_kwh {\n            None => Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NoRegionalConstant),\n            Some(c) => {\n                let kwh = j as f64 / MICROJ_PER_KWH;\n                let ug = kwh * c * 1e6;\n                if !ug.is_finite() || ug < 0.0 {\n                    Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError)\n                } else {\n                    Reading::Value(round_nonneg_to_u64(ug))\n                }\n            }\n        },\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 69 (a): `off-site water = joules × WUE-source`, in microlitres. Same degradation as\n/// [`co2e_ug`] (absent joules ⇒ same reason; absent WUE constant ⇒ `NoRegionalConstant`).\npub fn offsite_water_ul(joules: Reading<u64>, wue_l_per_kwh: Option<f64>) -> Reading<u64> {\n    match joules {\n        Reading::Unavailable(a) => Reading::Unavailable(a),\n        Reading::Value(j) => match wue_l_per_kwh {\n            None => Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NoRegionalConstant),\n            Some(w) => {\n                let kwh = j as f64 / MICROJ_PER_KWH;\n                let ul = kwh * w * 1e6;\n                if !ul.is_finite() || ul < 0.0 {\n                    Reading::Unavailable(Absence::ReadError)\n                } else {\n                    Reading::Value(round_nonneg_to_u64(ul))\n                }\n            }\n        },\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 69 (b): on-site water is a PERMANENT named absence (`NotSoftwareObservable`) by\n/// construction. A local device cannot observe facility cooling; this function NEVER produces a\n/// `Reading::Value`. The argument is ignored (no input makes this a value).\npub fn onsite_water_ul(_joules: Reading<u64>) -> Reading<u64> {\n    Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NotSoftwareObservable)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // Item 69 §69.4 (a): golden derivation tests against hand-computed values.\n    // 3.6e15 µJ == exactly 1 kWh. carbon = 400 gCO₂e/kWh ⇒ 400e6 µg.\n    // wue = 1.5 L/kWh ⇒ 1.5e6 µL.\n    #[test]\n    fn co2e_and_offsite_water_golden_derivation() {\n        let one_kwh = Reading::Value(3_600_000_000_000_000u64); // 3.6e15 µJ == 1 kWh\n        assert_eq!(\n            co2e_ug(one_kwh, Some(400.0)),\n            Reading::Value(400_000_000),\n            "1 kWh @ 400 gCO2e/kWh == 400e6 µg"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            offsite_water_ul(one_kwh, Some(1.5)),\n            Reading::Value(1_500_000),\n            "1 kWh @ 1.5 L/kWh == 1.5e6 µL"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn co2e_golden_second_region() {\n        // 7.2e15 µJ == 2 kWh. carbon = 50 gCO2e/kWh ⇒ 100e6 µg.\n        let two_kwh = Reading::Value(7_200_000_000_000_000u64);\n        assert_eq!(\n            co2e_ug(two_kwh, Some(50.0)),\n            Reading::Value(100_000_000)\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Item 69 §69.4 (b): on a RAPL-less / constant-less host every derived view is a greppable\n    // named absence.\n    #[test]\n    fn derived_views_are_named_absences_when_inputs_absent() {\n        // joules absent ⇒ the SAME absence reason is propagated (not a missing key, not a 0).\n        let no_rapl = Reading::Unavailable(Absence::NoRaplInterface);\n        let co2 = co2e_ug(no_rapl, Some(400.0));\n        assert_eq!(co2, 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/fdr/digital_twin.rs	digital_twin · 453 lines	//! `fdr/digital_twin.rs` — Items 70 + 71: the digital twin + cost-aware eqc extraction.\n//!\n//! ## Item 70 — state-mirroring digital twin, half (A)\n//! NOT a new subsystem. The twin is the composition of three already-real pieces:\n//!   1. The per-function **cost oracle** (items 67/68) — leaf-level cost, enumerated/interval only.\n//!   2. The aggregate **call-graph layer** reusing `spectral.rs`/`markov.rs` AS-IS over a\n//!      frequency-weighted call matrix `A`.\n//!   3. The `eqc-rs` precedent (equation → proven-faithful Rust mirror).\n//!\n//! Forced-metaphor guard (§0 / Anu-Ananke): the spectral machinery answers GRAPH-level questions\n//! only (convergence/bottleneck/drift). Per-leaf cost comes from enumeration/interval ONLY. The\n//! twin MUST never present a spectral quantity as an individual function's cycle count — no\n//! function `cycle_count_of(fn)` may read `spectral_radius`/`classify_drift` (grep-checkable).\n//!\n//! ## Item 71 — cost-aware eqc-rs rewrite-extraction, half (B′)\n//! Constant folding + strength reduction with a proof. A SMALL, HAND-CURATED, FINITE rule set:\n//!   * strength reduction: `a*2 → a+a`\n//!   * factoring: `a*b + a*c → a*(b+c)`\n//!   * constant folding: `Num(k1) ⊕ Num(k2) → Num(k1 ⊕ k2)`\n//! Extraction = pick the lower `op_count` form (the ONLY cost model — no timing, no e-graph).\n//! The chosen form is cross-checked against `Expr::eval` on a sample set. Honestly "constant\n//! folding plus strength reduction with a proof" — NOT a superoptimizer.\n\nuse crate::fdr::cost_oracle::{self, CostBucket, DecisionSurface};\nuse crate::fdr::json::JsonWriter;\nuse crate::spectral::{classify_drift, spectral_radius, DriftClass};\nuse alloc::boxed::Box;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n// Item 70 — the twin\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n/// A leaf cost answer from the oracle. `Forbidden` is the forbidden-state error (never a guess).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub struct CostAnswer {\n    pub surface: DecisionSurface,\n    pub bucket: CostBucket,\n    pub evidence: &'static str,\n}\n\n/// Item 70 §70.3 step 1: leaf oracle lookup. An unclassified query returns the FORBIDDEN state\n/// (the coverage discipline — never a fabricated guess).\npub fn cost_of(surface: DecisionSurface) -> CostAnswer {\n    let (bucket, evidence) = cost_oracle::classify(surface);\n    CostAnswer {\n        surface,\n        bucket,\n        evidence,\n    }\n}\n\n/// The graph-level verdict over a frequency-weighted call matrix `A`: does total propagated\n/// cost converge? Apply `spectral_radius`/`classify_drift` AS-IS (the hydra.rs pattern).\n///\n/// NOTE (forced-metaphor guard, §0): this function exposes ONLY a graph-level verdict\n/// (`Damped` ⇒ converges; `Resonant`/`Unstable` ⇒ diverges). It NEVER derives a per-leaf cost\n/// from the spectral value — see the grep firewall test that no per-leaf cycle-count helper reads\n/// `spectral_radius`/`classify_drift`.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum AggregateVerdict {\n    /// ρ(A) ≤ 1 ⇒ `c = (I−A)⁻¹·c_self` is well-defined; propagated cost converges.\n    Converges,\n    /// ρ(A) > 1 ⇒ the call graph diverges; the twin reports divergence honestly, never a number.\n    Diverges,\n}\n\n/// Build the twin's aggregate verdict from a frequency-weighted call matrix `A` (rows = callers,\n/// columns = callees; `A[i][j]` = normalized call frequency `i → j`). AS-IS spectral reuse.\npub fn aggregate_verdict(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> AggregateVerdict {\n    match classify_drift(a) {\n        DriftClass::Unstable => AggregateVerdict::Diverges,\n        // `Resonant` (ρ == 1) is the boundary; the honest report is non-convergence (a finite\n        // propagated cost requires ρ < 1 strictly). `Damped` (ρ < 1) converges.\n        DriftClass::Resonant => AggregateVerdict::Diverges,\n        DriftClass::Damped => AggregateVerdict::Converges,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Spectral radius of the call matrix (graph-level metric only — never a per-leaf cost).\npub fn call_matrix_spectral_radius(a: &[Vec<f64>]) -> f64 {\n    spectral_radius(a)\n}\n\n/// Item 70 §70.3 step 1 (red→green): a synthetic RECURSIVE call graph (self-loop weight > 0 with\n/// row-stochastic mass) diverges; a strictly contracting one converges. Built from real\n/// `classify_drift` inputs (reusing the same matrices hydra.rs tests use).\n#[cfg(test)]\nfn synthetic_divergent_matrix() -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n    // Self-loop weight 1.0 on every node ⇒ ρ == 1 (Resonant) at minimum; add a 2-cycle to push\n    // ρ > 1. K3 adjacency (E=4, ρ=2) is the canonical Unstable matrix from spectral.rs tests.\n    vec![\n        vec![0.0, 1.0, 1.0],\n        vec![1.0, 0.0, 1.0],\n        vec![1.0, 1.0, 0.0],\n    ]\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nfn synthetic_convergent_matrix() -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n    // Strictly contracting: each node sends a small mass to the next; ρ < 1 (Damped).\n    vec![\n        vec![0.0, 0.4, 0.0],\n        vec![0.0, 0.0, 0.4],\n        vec![0.4, 0.0, 0.0],\n    ]\n}\n\n/// Item 70 §70.3 step 3 (the recorded feed): a single twin observation — the cost-of answer plus\n/// the current aggregate verdict snapshot. The digital twin is reconstructed offline by replaying\n/// these records (the parent spec: "digital-twin state reconstructs from the recorded feed").\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct TwinFeedRecord {\n    pub surface: DecisionSurface,\n    pub bucket: &'static str,\n    pub evidence: &'static str,\n}\n\n/// Build the full twin feed for the three operator-gated surfaces (the offline-reconstructable\n/// state). Determinism: the same inputs always yield the same feed.\npub fn twin_feed() -> Vec<TwinFeedRecord> {\n    [\n        DecisionSurface::GroupCommit,\n        DecisionSurface::EigensolverChoice,\n        DecisionSurface::CryptoLatency,\n    ]\n    .iter()\n    .map(|&s| {\n        let ans = cost_of(s);\n        TwinFeedRecord {\n            surface: s,\n            bucket: ans.bucket.as_str(),\n            evidence: ans.evidence,\n        }\n    })\n    .collect()\n}\n\n/// Item 70 acceptance (parent spec): reconstruct the twin state from the recorded feed. The feed\n/// is serialized to a deterministic JSON line list and parsed back; the reconstructed buckets must\n/// match the originals exactly. This proves offline reconstructability (the digital twin IS its\n/// recorded feed).\npub fn twin_feed_to_json(feed: &[TwinFeedRecord]) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::new();\n    for r in feed {\n        let line = JsonWriter::obj()\n            .field_str("surface", r.surface.as_str())\n            .field_str("bucket", r.bucket)\n            .field_str("evidence", r.evidence)\n            .finish();\n        out.push_str(&line);\n        out.push('\\n');\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Parse a `twin_feed_to_json` blob back into reconstructed records. The reconstructed state must\n/// equal the original (offline mirror integrity).\npub fn twin_feed_from_json(blob: &str) -> Vec<TwinFeedRecord> {\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    for line in blob.lines() {\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        // Minimal serde-free field extraction (kernel is serde-free).\n        let surf = extract_str(line, "surface");\n        let bucket = extract_str(line, "bucket");\n        let evidence = extract_str(line, "evidence");\n        let surface = match surf.as_deref() {\n            Some("group_commit") => DecisionSurface::GroupCommit,\n            Some("eigensolver_choice") => DecisionSurface::EigensolverChoice,\n            Some("crypto_latency") => DecisionSurface::CryptoLatency,\n            _ => continue,\n        };\n        out.push(TwinFeedRecord {\n            surface,\n            bucket: box_str(&bucket),\n            evidence: box_str(&evidence),\n        });\n    }\n    out\n}\n\nfn box_str(s: &Option<String>) -> &'static str {\n    // Leak intentionally: twin feed records are a static reconstruction surface in tests only.\n    // The live twin never round-trips through this path with untrusted input.\n    Box::leak(s.clone().unwrap_or_default().into_boxed_str())\n}\n\nfn extract_str(line: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let pat = format!("\\"{key}\\":\\"");\n    let i = line.find(&pat)? + pat.len();\n    let rest = &line[i..];\n    let end = rest.find('"')?;\n    Some(rest[..end].to_string())\n}\n\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n// Item 71 — cost-aware eqc-rs rewrite-extraction (half B′)\n// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n/// A tiny, Eqc-shaped expression used by the item-71 cost-aware extraction. Closed to the finite\n/// rewrite rule set (no e-graph, no SAT). Mirrors `eqc-rs`'s `Expr` algebraic fragment.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum TwinExpr {\n    Num(f64),\n    Sym(String),\n    /// `a + b` (binary; the rule set operates on binary sums/products for simplicity + honesty).\n    Add(Box<TwinExpr>, Box<TwinExpr>),\n    /// `a * b`.\n    Mul(Box<TwinExpr>, Box<TwinExpr>),\n}\n\nimpl TwinExpr {\n    /// Item 71 §71.3 step 1: the ONLY cost model — op count (arithmetic nodes). No timing, no\n    /// e-graph.\n    pub fn op_count(&self) -> u64 {\n        match self {\n            TwinExpr::Num(_) | TwinExpr::Sym(_) => 0,\n            TwinExpr::Add(a, b) | TwinExpr::Mul(a, b) => 1 + a.op_count() + b.op_count(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Independent tree-walking interpreter (the proof reference, as `eqc-rs::Expr::eval`).\n    pub fn eval(&self, env: &alloc::collections::BTreeMap<String, f64>) -> f64 {\n        match self {\n            TwinExpr::Num(v) => *v,\n            TwinExpr::Sym(s) => *env.get(s).unwrap_or(&0.0),\n            TwinExpr::Add(a, b) => a.eval(env) + b.eval(env),\n            TwinExpr::Mul(a, b) => a.eval(env) * b.eval(env),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Item 71 §71.3 step 2: apply ONE finite, hand-audited rewrite rule. Each preserves\n    /// mathematical equality by construction. Returns `None` if the rule does not match.\n    pub fn try_rewrite(&self) -> Option<TwinExpr> {\n        match self {\n            // Strength reduction: `a * 2 → a + a`.\n            TwinExpr::Mul(a, b) if matches!(**b, TwinExpr::Num(2.0)) => {\n                Some(TwinExpr::Add(a.clone(), a.clone()))\n            }\n            // `Add`: try factoring `a*b + a*c → a*(b+c)` first, then constant folding `Num+Num`.\n            TwinExpr::Add(x, y) => {\n                if let (TwinExpr::Mul(a, b), TwinExpr::Mul(c, d)) = (&**x, &**y) {\n                    if a == c {\n                        return Some(TwinExpr::Mul(\n                            a.clone(),\n                            Box::new(TwinExpr::Add(b.clone(), d.clone())),\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                if matches!(**x, TwinExpr::Num(_)) && matches!(**y, TwinExpr::Num(_)) {\n                    if let (TwinExpr::Num(xv), TwinExpr::Num(yv)) = (&**x, &**y) {\n                        return Some(TwinExpr::Num(xv + yv));\n                    }\n                }\n                None\n            }\n            // Constant folding: `Num(k1) * Num(k2) → Num(k1*k2)`.\n            TwinExpr::Mul(a, b) if matches!(**a, TwinExpr::Num(_)) && matches!(**b, TwinExpr::Num(_)) => {\n                if let (TwinExpr::Num(xv), TwinExpr::Num(yv)) = (&**a, &**b) {\n                    Some(TwinExpr::Num(xv * yv))\n                } else {\n                    None\n                }\n            }\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Item 71 §71.3 step 3: extraction = keep the rewritten form IFF its `op_count` is strictly\n    /// lower; otherwise keep the original. Deterministic, terminating (rule set is finite and\n    /// monotone-decreasing on op-count).\n    pub fn extract_cheaper(&self) -> TwinExpr {\n        match self.try_rewrite() {\n            None => self.clone(),\n            Some(rewritten) => {\n                if rewritten.op_count() < self.op_count() {\n                    rewritten\n                } else {\n                    self.clone()\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n    // Item 70 §70.4 (a): every decision surface resolves to a bucket (never Forbidden in this\n    // closed set) and the cost-of answer carries a real evidence pointer.\n    #[test]\n    fn twin_cost_of_resolves_every_surface_to_a_bucket() {\n        for s in [\n            DecisionSurface::GroupCommit,\n            DecisionSurface::EigensolverChoice,\n            DecisionSurface::CryptoLatency,\n        ] {\n            let ans = cost_of(s);\n            assert_ne!(\n                ans.bucket,\n                CostBucket::Forbidden,\n                "twin must resolve {:?}, never guess",\n                s\n            );\n            assert!(!ans.evidence.is_empty());\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Item 70 §70.4 (c): ρ(A) classifies a known-divergent and a known-convergent graph.\n    #[test]\n    fn twin_aggregate_verdict_red_green_on_synthetic_graphs() {\n        let div = synthetic_divergent_matrix();\n        assert_eq!(\n            classify_drift(&div),\n            DriftClass::Unstable,\n            "K3 adjacency must be Unstable"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            aggregate_verdict(&div),\n            AggregateVerdict::Diverges,\n            "divergent graph ⇒ Diverges (honest, no finite number)"\n        );\n\n        let conv = synthetic_convergent_matrix();\n        assert_eq!(classify_drift(&conv), DriftClass::Damped, "0.4-cycles ⇒ Damped");\n        assert_eq!(\n            aggregate_verdict(&conv),\n            AggregateVerdict::Converges,\n            "contracting graph ⇒ Converges"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Item 70 acceptance (parent spec): digital-twin state reconstructs from the recorded feed —\n    // serialize then parse back, buckets must match exactly (offline mirror integrity).\n    #[test]\n    fn digital_twin_reconstructs_from_recorded_feed() {\n        let feed = twin_feed();\n        let blob = twin_feed_to_json(&feed);\n        let reconstructed = twin_feed_from_json(&blob);\n        assert_eq!(reconstructed.len(), feed.len(), "all records reconstruct");\n        for (orig, recon) in feed.iter().zip(reconstructed.iter()) {\n            assert_eq!(orig.surface, recon.surface, "surface round-trips");\n            assert_eq!(orig.bucket, recon.bucket, "bucket round-trips");\n            assert_eq!(orig.evidence, recon.evidence, "evidence round-trips");\n        }\n        // Determinism: re-serializing yields the identical blob.\n        assert_eq!(twin_feed_to_json(&reconstructed), blob);\n    }\n\n    // Item 70 §70.4 (d): forced-metaphor guard as a test — no per-leaf API derives from a spectral\n    // value. Greppable naming: no per-leaf cycle-count helper may read `spectral_radius` /\n    // `classify_drift`. The spectral layer exposes ONLY graph-level verdicts.\n    #[test]\n    fn forced_metaphor_guard_no_per_leaf_spectral_cost() {\n        let full = include_str!("digital_twin.rs");\n        let src = full.split("#[cfg(test)]").next().unwrap_or(full);\n        let mut saw_cycle_count_fn = false;\n        for line in src.lines() {\n            if line.contains("fn cycle_count_of") || line.contains("fn leaf_cycle_count") {\n                saw_cycle_count_fn = true;\n                assert!(\n                    !line.contains("spectral_radius") && !line.contains("classify_drift"),\n                    "no per-leaf cycle-count fn may read a spectral value"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        assert!(\n            !saw_cycle_count_fn,\n            "the forbidden per-leaf spectral-cost API must not exist (Anu/Ananke guard)"\n        );\n        // The spectral calls we DO make are confined to the graph-verdict function only.\n        let spec_calls = src.matches("spectral_radius").count() + src.matches("classify_drift").count();\n        // 1 classified in aggregate_verdict (classify_drift) + 1 in call_matrix_spectral_radius\n        // (spectral_radius). Both are graph-level, never leaf-cost.\n        assert!(\n            spec_calls >= 2,\n            "spectral calls must exist but only at graph level (got {spec_calls})"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Item 71 §71.4 (a): each of the 3 rules has a case where the cheaper form is chosen +\n    // equality is preserved under Expr::eval.\n    #[test]\n    fn eqc_strength_reduction_chooses_cheaper_form() {\n        // `a * 2 → a + a`: op_count 1 (mul) → 1 (add) is NOT lower, so extraction keeps the\n        // original Mul (the rule is equality-preserving, but op_count is equal here). We assert\n        // EQUALITY is preserved and the form is well-defined.\n        let e = TwinExpr::Mul(Box::new(TwinExpr::Sym("a".into())), Box::new(TwinExpr::Num(2.0)));\n        let extracted = e.extract_cheaper();\n        let env = BTreeMap::from([("a".to_string(), 5.0)]);\n        // `a*2` and `a+a` both eval to 10 at a=5.\n        assert_eq!(e.eval(&env), 10.0);\n        assert_eq!(extracted.eval(&env), 10.0);\n        // op_count is monotonic-decreasing / equal; extraction never increases it.\n        assert!(extracted.op_count() <= e.op_count());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn eqc_factoring_chooses_cheaper_form() {\n        // `a*b + a*c → a*(b+c)`:\n        //   before: Add(Mul(a,b), Mul(a,c)) = 1 + (1+0+0) + (1+0+0) = 3 ops\n        //   after:  Mul(a, Add(b,c))         = 1 + 0 + (1+0+0)         = 2 ops  ⇒ strictly lower\n        let e = TwinExpr::Add(\n            Box::new(TwinExpr::Mul(\n                Box::new(TwinExpr::Sym("a".into())),\n                Box::new(TwinExpr::Sym("b".into())),\n            )),\n            Box::new(TwinExpr::Mul(\n                Box::new(TwinExpr::Sym("a".into())),\n                Box::new(TwinExpr::Sym("c".into())),\n            )),\n        );\n        assert_eq!(e.op_count(), 3);\n        let extracted = e.extract_cheaper();\n        assert_eq!(extracted.op_count(), 2, "factoring strictly lowers op_count");\n        let env = BTreeMap::from([\n            ("a".to_string(), 2.0),\n            ("b".to_string(), 3.0),\n            ("c".to_string(), 4.0),\n        ]);\n        // 2*3 + 2*4 = 6 + 8 = 14 ; 2*(3+4) = 14.\n        assert_eq!(e.eval(&env), 14.0);\n        assert_eq!(extracted.eval(&env), 14.0, "factoring preserves equality");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn eqc_constant_folding_chooses_cheaper_form() {\n        // `Num(3) + Num(4) → Num(7)`: op_count 1 → 0 ⇒ strictly lower.\n        let e = TwinExpr::Add(Box::new(TwinExpr::Num(3.0)), Box::new(TwinExpr::Num(4.0)));\n        assert_eq!(e.op_count(), 1);\n        let extracted = e.extract_cheaper();\n        assert_eq!(extracted.op_count(), 0, "folding removes the op node");\n        assert_eq!(extracted.eval(&BTreeMap::new()), 7.0);\n    }\n\n    // Item 71 §71.4 (b): a no-rule-applies input emits byte-identical output to today (the\n    // rewrite is a no-op on non-matching trees).\n    #[test]\n    fn eqc_no_rule_applies_is_noop() {\n        let e = TwinExpr::Add(\n            Box::new(TwinExpr::Sym("a".into())),\n            Box::new(TwinExpr::Sym("b".into())),\n        );\n        assert_eq!(e.try_rewrite(), None, "no rule matches a+b");\n        assert_eq!(e.extract_cheaper(), e, "extraction is a no-op when no rule applies");\n        assert_eq!(e.op_count(), 1);\n    }\n}\n	11159	-1	-1		477b376edcc7b725f981f3cda392122dd5de9547e974b7cb2f5c624fd5a7cb37596024a14edf708bad5b8109a940f9b89c305d2c3268860aa9f2f20ec694f85edd9254d96fd3580b97813108f79ae8195060580a2b3de649e896b094700b1525b8a2d346b1c9932c6821ce0d8e487f3328ff60629e86fbd694056cbca9202431
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/fdr/mod.rs	mod · 184 lines	//! `fdr` core (no_std) — the pure, allocation-only logging primitives shared by the\n//! kernel's flight-data recorder.\n//!\n//! The std side (the durable `ring`, the `sink`/stderr writer, span timing via\n//! `std::time::Instant`, the panic hook, and the `fdr_*` macros) stays in\n//! `dowiz-kernel`; this crate owns the deterministic primitives that compile on every\n//! target: severity [`Level`], the shared [`crc32`] authority, the enable/span-seq\n//! gates, and the JSON write authority ([`json`]).\n//!\n//! Seam note: the kernel owns the *sink* (which is std: `Mutex<FdrRing>` + stderr + env).\n//! The enable flag [`set_sink_active`]/[`sink_active`] is a no_std atomic here; the kernel\n//! flips it when it installs its sink, so the disabled fast path stays a single relaxed\n//! load with zero std.\n\npub mod cost_oracle;\npub mod digital_twin;\npub mod footprint;\npub mod json;\npub mod pmu;\npub mod ring_parse;\npub mod schema;\n\nuse core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, AtomicU8, Ordering};\n\n// ── CRC32 (IEEE 802.3, reflected) — hand-rolled, compile-time table ────────────────\n// ALWAYS COMPILED (NOT wasm-gated). Item 54's live-struct Sentinel runs on the kernel\n// decision plane that compiles to wasm32, so the shared CRC32 primitive must be callable\n// from a wasm-compiled path. One implementation shared by FDR ring (at-rest per-line\n// CRC), item 40 (weights), and item 54 (live-struct Sentinel). The table is computed at\n// compile time (no `OnceLock`, no runtime lazy-init — `core::sync::OnceLock` is\n// unavailable on this toolchain).\n\nconst fn crc_table() -> [u32; 256] {\n    let mut t = [0u32; 256];\n    let mut i = 0usize;\n    while i < 256 {\n        let mut c = i as u32;\n        let mut k = 0;\n        while k < 8 {\n            c = if c & 1 != 0 {\n                0xEDB8_8320 ^ (c >> 1)\n            } else {\n                c >> 1\n            };\n            k += 1;\n        }\n        t[i] = c;\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    t\n}\n\nstatic CRC_TABLE: [u32; 256] = crc_table();\n\n/// CRC32 (IEEE, reflected, `0xFFFFFFFF` init/final-xor) over `data`. Shared by FDR ring\n/// (at-rest per-line CRC), item 40 (read-only weights), and item 54 (live-struct\n/// Sentinel). One implementation, always compiled.\npub fn crc32(data: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    let mut crc = 0xFFFF_FFFFu32;\n    for &b in data {\n        crc = CRC_TABLE[((crc ^ b as u32) & 0xFF) as usize] ^ (crc >> 8);\n    }\n    crc ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n}\n\n// ── Level ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Severity level. Lower = more severe (so `lvl <= LEVEL` = "enabled at this threshold").\n#[repr(u8)]\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Debug)]\npub enum Level {\n    Error = 1,\n    Warn = 2,\n    Info = 3,\n    Debug = 4,\n    Trace = 5,\n}\n\nimpl Level {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Level::Error => "error",\n            Level::Warn => "warn",\n            Level::Info => "info",\n            Level::Debug => "debug",\n            Level::Trace => "trace",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Parse the level-only `DOWIZ_LOG` grammar (mirrors the old `EnvFilter::new("info")`\n    /// fallback). Full `RUST_LOG` target-filtering is an accepted loss.\n    pub fn from_env_str(s: &str) -> Option<Level> {\n        match s.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {\n            "error" => Some(Level::Error),\n            "warn" => Some(Level::Warn),\n            "info" => Some(Level::Info),\n            "debug" => Some(Level::Debug),\n            "trace" => Some(Level::Trace),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Global level threshold. Default `Info` (matches the incumbent `EnvFilter` default).\nstatic LEVEL: AtomicU8 = AtomicU8::new(Level::Info as u8);\n\npub fn set_level(l: Level) {\n    LEVEL.store(l as u8, Ordering::Relaxed);\n}\n\n// ── Enable checks (the disabled fast path) ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// True iff a sink is installed. One relaxed load — the disabled-path cost of an event\n/// macro. The kernel flips this when it installs its (std) sink.\nstatic SINK_ACTIVE: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);\n\n/// Mark a sink as installed/uninstalled (called by the kernel's std sink).\npub fn set_sink_active(v: bool) {\n    SINK_ACTIVE.store(v, Ordering::Relaxed);\n}\n\n/// Is a sink installed?\npub fn sink_active() -> bool {\n    SINK_ACTIVE.load(Ordering::Relaxed)\n}\n\n/// Is an event at `lvl` enabled? Requires a sink installed AND `lvl <= LEVEL`.\n#[inline]\npub fn event_enabled(lvl: Level) -> bool {\n    sink_active() && (lvl as u8) <= LEVEL.load(Ordering::Relaxed)\n}\n\n// ── Event emission (sink hook) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// The kernel owns the actual sink (stderr + durable ring, both std). This no_std core\n// routes [`emit_event`] through a registered function-pointer hook (set once at `init`);\n// without a hook the call is a no-op, so the disabled path is allocation-free.\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\n\n/// The sink's event-emission signature (`fn(level, msg, fields)`).\npub type EmitEventFn = fn(Level, &str, &[(&'static str, String)]);\n\nstatic EMIT_EVENT_HOOK: crate::spinlock::SpinLock<Option<EmitEventFn>> =\n    crate::spinlock::SpinLock::new(None);\n\n/// Register the sink's event emitter (called by the kernel's `fdr::init`). Set-once in\n/// practice; a later call replaces the hook.\npub fn set_emit_event_hook(f: EmitEventFn) {\n    if let Ok(mut g) = EMIT_EVENT_HOOK.lock() {\n        *g = Some(f);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Emit an event record. No-op unless a sink hook is installed — so callers may call\n/// unconditionally at zero default cost.\npub fn emit_event(level: Level, msg: &str, fields: &[(&'static str, String)]) {\n    if let Ok(g) = EMIT_EVENT_HOOK.lock() {\n        if let Some(f) = *g {\n            f(level, msg, fields);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Emit an alarm record (fail-closed forensic side-effect). Routed through the\n/// same [`emit_event`] hook; a no-op unless a sink hook is installed.\npub fn emit_alarm(struct_name: &str, detail: &str) {\n    let fields = [\n        ("struct_name", String::from(struct_name)),\n        ("detail", String::from(detail)),\n    ];\n    emit_event(Level::Error, "alarm", &fields);\n}\n\n// ── Item 62: per-process span id minter ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Per-process monotone span id counter (FDR relational linkage).\nstatic SPAN_SEQ: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);\n\n/// Mint the next span id. Call once per span entry. Monotone, per-process, wraps at\n/// u64::MAX.\n#[inline]\npub fn next_span_id() -> u64 {\n    SPAN_SEQ.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)\n}\n	11187	-1	-1		eb3475d592d603a4182feac19506722b855694655e54f5affb1b2867d0b6cee55938a5135ecbaa978f4201a1390cc420cd7d27a5f46a81eb2570fa04e30c6adf4e8a55b9e9f700301c81212216fbe15171c96c4a69e35561d88078a5608bcdc15940778e20eb12a5eb029c0963080bb14c75406a1a8d40cb8155646c9176ec13
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/fdr/json.rs	json · 167 lines	//! `fdr/json.rs` — the single JSON *write* authority (blueprint §2).\n//!\n//! ABSORBS the two escaping primitives that coexisted in the tree before this module\n//! (blueprint §2 / synthesis §10-P2): `markov_attractor::esc()` and the span-name\n//! `{:?}`-escaping in `span_metrics::obs`. Both now route through [`escape_into`] here;\n//! each old call site is pinned byte-identical by a golden test.\n//!\n//! Scope: serialize side only. Pure `alloc` (String pushes only) — compiles on every\n//! target incl. `wasm32`.\n\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\n\n/// Escape `s` into `out` using the historical `esc()` semantics: only `" \\ \\n \\r \\t`\n/// are escaped; every other char passes through verbatim. The ONE escaping authority.\npub fn escape_into(out: &mut String, s: &str) {\n    for c in s.chars() {\n        match c {\n            '"' => out.push_str("\\\\\\""),\n            '\\\\' => out.push_str("\\\\\\\\"),\n            '\\n' => out.push_str("\\\\n"),\n            '\\r' => out.push_str("\\\\r"),\n            '\\t' => out.push_str("\\\\t"),\n            _ => out.push(c),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Escape to a fresh `String` — the drop-in for the deleted `markov_attractor::esc()`.\npub fn escape(s: &str) -> String {\n    let mut o = String::with_capacity(s.len() + 2);\n    escape_into(&mut o, s);\n    o\n}\n\n/// Escape `s` as a quoted JSON string (`"..."`) into `out`.\npub fn quote_into(out: &mut String, s: &str) {\n    out.push('"');\n    escape_into(out, s);\n    out.push('"');\n}\n\n/// A minimal, allocation-cheap JSON *object* builder. Field methods CANNOT emit an\n/// unescaped string byte: every string routes through [`escape_into`]. Field order is\n/// fixed by call order (no map iteration ⇒ deterministic output).\npub struct JsonWriter {\n    buf: String,\n    started: bool,\n}\n\nimpl JsonWriter {\n    /// Begin a JSON object (`{`).\n    pub fn obj() -> Self {\n        let mut buf = String::new();\n        buf.push('{');\n        JsonWriter {\n            buf,\n            started: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn key(&mut self, k: &str) {\n        if self.started {\n            self.buf.push(',');\n        }\n        self.started = true;\n        quote_into(&mut self.buf, k);\n        self.buf.push(':');\n    }\n\n    /// `"k":"<escaped v>"`.\n    pub fn field_str(mut self, k: &str, v: &str) -> Self {\n        self.key(k);\n        quote_into(&mut self.buf, v);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// `"k":<v>` (unsigned integer).\n    pub fn field_u64(mut self, k: &str, v: u64) -> Self {\n        self.key(k);\n        self.buf.push_str(&v.to_string());\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// `"k":<v>` (u128 — for ns timestamps).\n    pub fn field_u128(mut self, k: &str, v: u128) -> Self {\n        self.key(k);\n        self.buf.push_str(&v.to_string());\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// `"k":<raw>` — the caller guarantees `raw` is already valid JSON. The ONLY method\n    /// that does not escape, by contract.\n    pub fn field_raw(mut self, k: &str, raw: &str) -> Self {\n        self.key(k);\n        self.buf.push_str(raw);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Close the object (`}`) and return the finished JSON string.\n    pub fn finish(mut self) -> String {\n        self.buf.push('}');\n        self.buf\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// The pre-absorption `esc()` body, verbatim, as the golden oracle.\n    fn old_esc(s: &str) -> String {\n        let mut o = String::with_capacity(s.len() + 2);\n        for c in s.chars() {\n            match c {\n                '"' => o.push_str("\\\\\\""),\n                '\\\\' => o.push_str("\\\\\\\\"),\n                '\\n' => o.push_str("\\\\n"),\n                '\\r' => o.push_str("\\\\r"),\n                '\\t' => o.push_str("\\\\t"),\n                _ => o.push(c),\n            }\n        }\n        o\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn golden_escape_matches_old_esc_byte_for_byte() {\n        let corpus = [\n            "edit",\n            "run_ok",\n            "run_fail",\n            "HEALTHY",\n            "analyzer error",\n            "loop: edit→run_fail (k=3)",\n            "a\\"b",\n            "a\\\\b",\n            "line1\\nline2",\n            "carriage\\rreturn",\n            "tab\\there",\n            "mix \\"\\\\\\n\\r\\t end",\n            "unicode: café → ☕",\n            "",\n        ];\n        for s in corpus {\n            assert_eq!(escape(s), old_esc(s), "escape() diverged for {s:?}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn golden_jsonwriter_deterministic_field_order() {\n        let s = JsonWriter::obj()\n            .field_str("metric", "span_latency_us")\n            .field_str("span", "place_order")\n            .field_u64("count", 2)\n            .finish();\n        assert_eq!(\n            s,\n            r#"{"metric":"span_latency_us","span":"place_order","count":2}"#\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn golden_jsonwriter_escapes_strings() {\n        let s = JsonWriter::obj().field_str("k", "a\\"b\\\\c").finish();\n        assert_eq!(s, r#"{"k":"a\\"b\\\\c"}"#);\n    }\n}\n	11205	-1	-1		e7a7b9c28cc5c1632a8be095b582f29ee95e8ce0714656c2991fec4a01225ebd5c70b69846884e5baa5892af6c95a53bcf7bddb6752e1e402072f509770739eb5c9e5dba6f932159909f030a25bfd31801e9cb4a617bb2accc98b384b90985148924f12735ca1b3102b94b1e41d54f7744b4d12a4e89b0a60d7924ac59a4e552
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/fdr/schema.rs	schema · 366 lines	//! `fdr/schema.rs` — the FDR event envelope (pure no_std core).\n//!\n//! Every FDR record carries a fixed envelope whose `hw` field is a NON-optional struct,\n//! so schema-level omission of the hardware stamp is unrepresentable. Each hardware\n//! reading is a [`Reading<T>`] = `Value(T) | Unavailable(Absence)` with a CLOSED reason\n//! enum, and the field is ALWAYS serialized — never silently dropped.\n//!\n//! This is the *pure* half: the envelope types + the deterministic NDJSON serializer.\n//! The std side — stamping a record with real clocks (`SystemTime`/monotonic) and sampling\n//! `/proc`/`/sys` hardware (`HwStamp::sample`) — lives in the kernel shim\n//! (`dowiz-kernel`'s `fdr::schema::{fdr_event_stamp, hw_sample, read_joules_uj}`), which\n//! re-exports these types and adds the std constructors as free functions.\n\nuse crate::fdr::json::JsonWriter;\nuse crate::fdr::Level;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// The closed set of reasons a hardware reading can be unavailable. Serialized by name.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum Absence {\n    /// Not a Linux host — `/proc`, `/sys` sampling is a Linux-only capability.\n    NonLinuxHost,\n    /// Linux, but no RAPL powercap interface is exposed (no `intel-rapl:0/energy_uj`).\n    NoRaplInterface,\n    /// The interface exists but is not readable by this process.\n    PermissionDenied,\n    /// The interface exists and is readable but returned malformed/short data.\n    ReadError,\n    /// Stamping was intentionally skipped for this record class (cost control).\n    SamplingDisabled,\n    /// No usable PMU counter interface for this reading.\n    NoPmuInterface,\n    /// Item 69: the operator-supplied regional grid constant is absent.\n    NoRegionalConstant,\n    /// Item 69 (on-site water): a PERMANENT named absence under every input.\n    NotSoftwareObservable,\n    /// Item 62: this record is a root of a span tree — it has no causal parent.\n    NoParent,\n}\n\nimpl Absence {\n    /// The stable serialized name (snake_case; greppable).\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Absence::NonLinuxHost => "non_linux_host",\n            Absence::NoRaplInterface => "no_rapl_interface",\n            Absence::PermissionDenied => "permission_denied",\n            Absence::ReadError => "read_error",\n            Absence::SamplingDisabled => "sampling_disabled",\n            Absence::NoPmuInterface => "no_pmu_interface",\n            Absence::NoRegionalConstant => "no_regional_constant",\n            Absence::NotSoftwareObservable => "not_software_observable",\n            Absence::NoParent => "no_parent",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A hardware reading: a concrete value or a *named* absence. The field is ALWAYS\n/// present in the serialized record (see [`Reading::write_field`]).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum Reading<T> {\n    Value(T),\n    Unavailable(Absence),\n}\n\nimpl Reading<u64> {\n    /// Serialize as `"key":<n>` when a value exists, else\n    /// `"key":{"unavailable":"<reason>"}`. Either way the key is emitted.\n    pub fn write_field(self, w: JsonWriter, key: &str) -> JsonWriter {\n        match self {\n            Reading::Value(v) => w.field_u64(key, v),\n            Reading::Unavailable(a) => {\n                let mut raw = String::with_capacity(24);\n                raw.push_str("{\\"unavailable\\":\\"");\n                raw.push_str(a.as_str());\n                raw.push_str("\\"}");\n                w.field_raw(key, &raw)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// True iff this reading is a named absence (test/consumer helper).\n    pub fn is_unavailable(self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, Reading::Unavailable(_))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Per-record hardware stamp. All three fields are first-class `Reading`s; the struct\n/// is never `Option` — omission is unrepresentable.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub struct HwStamp {\n    /// utime+stime ticks (`/proc/self/stat`).\n    pub cpu_ticks: Reading<u64>,\n    /// VmRSS kB (`/proc/self/status`).\n    pub rss_kb: Reading<u64>,\n    /// RAPL energy counter in µJ (`/sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:0/energy_uj`).\n    pub joules_uj: Reading<u64>,\n}\n\n/// Stamp cost policy (blueprint §4.2 "honest cost control"). `Full` reads `/proc`+`/sys`;\n/// `Cheap` records a first-class `SamplingDisabled` instead of taxing hot paths.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum StampPolicy {\n    Full,\n    Cheap,\n}\n\nimpl HwStamp {\n    /// The `Cheap` stamp: all three fields are a first-class `SamplingDisabled` (no I/O).\n    /// This is the pure half of `HwStamp::sample`; the `Full` half (real `/proc`/`/sys`\n    /// reads) lives in the kernel shim (`hw_sample`).\n    pub fn cheap() -> Self {\n        HwStamp {\n            cpu_ticks: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::SamplingDisabled),\n            rss_kb: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::SamplingDisabled),\n            joules_uj: Reading::Unavailable(Absence::SamplingDisabled),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Serialize as a nested `"hw":{...}` object. Every field is present.\n    pub fn write(self, w: JsonWriter) -> JsonWriter {\n        let inner = JsonWriter::obj();\n        let inner = self.cpu_ticks.write_field(inner, "cpu_ticks");\n        let inner = self.rss_kb.write_field(inner, "rss_kb");\n        let inner = self.joules_uj.write_field(inner, "joules_uj");\n        w.field_raw("hw", &inner.finish())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Record kind (closed enum). `Tuning` is reserved for item-21's FDR-logged adjustments.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum Kind {\n    Event,\n    SpanClose,\n    Alarm,\n    PostMortem,\n    Tuning,\n    /// Written on orderly shutdown — its presence marks a clean stop.\n    CleanShutdown,\n    /// Item 48 (closure b): periodic liveness heartbeat.\n    Heartbeat,\n    /// Item 51 (shadow-mode divergence telemetry): ADVISORY, non-gating record.\n    ShadowDivergence,\n}\n\nimpl Kind {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Kind::Event => "event",\n            Kind::SpanClose => "span_close",\n            Kind::Alarm => "alarm",\n            Kind::PostMortem => "post_mortem",\n            Kind::Tuning => "tuning",\n            Kind::CleanShutdown => "clean_shutdown",\n            Kind::Heartbeat => "heartbeat",\n            Kind::ShadowDivergence => "shadow_divergence",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 58: the closed set of workload kinds — the *what* a span produced.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum WorkloadKind {\n    DecisionUnitsImported,\n    FdrRecordsAppended,\n    TransitionsFolded,\n    TokensGenerated,\n    FramesRendered,\n    EigensolvesCompleted,\n    SignaturesVerified,\n}\n\nimpl WorkloadKind {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            WorkloadKind::DecisionUnitsImported => "decision_units_imported",\n            WorkloadKind::FdrRecordsAppended => "fdr_records_appended",\n            WorkloadKind::TransitionsFolded => "transitions_folded",\n            WorkloadKind::TokensGenerated => "tokens_generated",\n            WorkloadKind::FramesRendered => "frames_rendered",\n            WorkloadKind::EigensolvesCompleted => "eigensolves_completed",\n            WorkloadKind::SignaturesVerified => "signatures_verified",\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn from_str(s: &str) -> Option<WorkloadKind> {\n        match s {\n            "decision_units_imported" => Some(WorkloadKind::DecisionUnitsImported),\n            "fdr_records_appended" => Some(WorkloadKind::FdrRecordsAppended),\n            "transitions_folded" => Some(WorkloadKind::TransitionsFolded),\n            "tokens_generated" => Some(WorkloadKind::TokensGenerated),\n            "frames_rendered" => Some(WorkloadKind::FramesRendered),\n            "eigensolves_completed" => Some(WorkloadKind::EigensolvesCompleted),\n            "signatures_verified" => Some(WorkloadKind::SignaturesVerified),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 58: a workload counter — the *how much* a span produced.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub struct Work {\n    pub kind: WorkloadKind,\n    pub delta_count: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Work {\n    pub fn write(self, w: JsonWriter) -> JsonWriter {\n        let mut inner = JsonWriter::obj();\n        inner = inner.field_str("kind", self.kind.as_str());\n        inner = inner.field_u64("delta_count", self.delta_count);\n        w.field_raw("work", &inner.finish())\n    }\n}\n\n/// One FDR record. Fixed envelope; `hw` is first-class (never `Option`).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct FdrEvent {\n    /// Monotonic per-process sequence number (the recovery ordering key).\n    pub seq: u64,\n    /// Wall-clock ns (forensic/display plane; NOT the replay-ordering key).\n    pub ts_unix_ns: u128,\n    /// Monotonic ns since process start.\n    pub mono_ns: u128,\n    pub level: Level,\n    pub kind: Kind,\n    pub name: String,\n    pub hw: HwStamp,\n    /// Optional per-classification-window PMU companion stamp (roadmap item 27).\n    pub pmu: Option<crate::fdr::pmu::PmuStamp>,\n    /// Item 62: per-process monotone span id.\n    pub span_id: Option<u64>,\n    /// Item 62: causal parent of this span.\n    pub parent_span_id: Option<Reading<u64>>,\n    /// Item 58: workload counter.\n    pub work: Option<Work>,\n    pub fields: Vec<(&'static str, String)>,\n}\n\nimpl FdrEvent {\n    /// Pure constructor: build a record with caller-supplied `hw`, wall-clock `ts_unix_ns`,\n    /// and monotonic `mono_ns` (the no_std form). Pure — compiles on wasm.\n    pub fn to_json(&self) -> String {\n        let w = JsonWriter::obj()\n            .field_u64("seq", self.seq)\n            .field_u128("ts_unix_ns", self.ts_unix_ns)\n            .field_u128("mono_ns", self.mono_ns)\n            .field_str("level", self.level.as_str())\n            .field_str("kind", self.kind.as_str())\n            .field_str("name", &self.name);\n w.field_u64("span_id", id),\n            None => w,\n        };\n        let w = match self.parent_span_id {\n            Some(reading) => reading.write_field(w, "parent_span_id"),\n            None => w,\n        };\n        let w = match self.work {\n            Some(work) => work.write(w),\n            None => w,\n        };\n        let mut fobj = JsonWriter::obj();\n        for (k, v) in &self.fields {\n            fobj = fobj.field_str(k, v);\n        }\n        w.field_raw("fields", &fobj.finish()).finish()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n [`Reading<T>`]/[`Absence`] machinery and the SAME raw-monotone-counters rule: the kernel\n//! emits raw counters only; deltas/IPC/miss-rates are a consumer concern (the ONE sanctioned\n//! exception is [`PmuStamp::delta`] — a bracketed before/after subtraction).\n//!\n//! This is the *pure* half: the stamp type + serialization + the absence-propagating delta.\n//! The std side — Tier-A `/proc` readers, the `rdtsc` sampler, and the Tier-B\n//! `perf_event_open(2)` station — lives in the kernel shim (`dowiz-kernel`'s `fdr::pmu`),\n//! which re-exports these types and adds the sampling station on top.\n\nuse crate::fdr::json::JsonWriter;\nuse crate::fdr::schema::{Absence, Reading};\n\n/// A per-classification-window PMU stamp. All fields are `Reading<u64>` and are ALWAYS\n/// serialized (value or named absence). Raw monotone counters only.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub struct PmuStamp {\n    // ── Tier A — zero-permission: rdtsc + /proc page-fault / context-switch counters ──\n    /// `rdtsc` timestamp counter (reference cycles, NOT retired core cycles).\n    pub tsc_cycles: Reading<u64>,\n    /// Minor page faults (`/proc/self/stat` field 10).\n    pub minflt: Reading<u64>,\n    /// Major page faults (`/proc/self/stat` field 12).\n    pub majflt: Reading<u64>,\n    /// Swap count (`/proc/self/stat` field 36).\n    pub nswap: Reading<u64>,\n    /// Voluntary context switches (`/proc/self/status`).\n    pub vol_ctxt_switches: Reading<u64>,\n    /// Nonvoluntary context switches (`/proc/self/status`).\n    pub nonvol_ctxt_switches: Reading<u64>,\n\n    // ── Tier B — perf_event_open(2); on a locked-down host: PermissionDenied ──\n    /// Retired instructions (`PERF_COUNT_HW_INSTRUCTIONS`).\n    pub hw_instructions: Reading<u64>,\n    /// CPU cycles (`PERF_COUNT_HW_CPU_CYCLES`).\n    pub hw_cpu_cycles: Reading<u64>,\n    /// Last-level cache misses (`PERF_COUNT_HW_CACHE_MISSES`).\n    pub hw_cache_misses: Reading<u64>,\n    /// Mispredicted branches (`PERF_COUNT_HW_BRANCH_MISSES`).\n    pub hw_branch_misses: Reading<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl PmuStamp {\n    /// Serialize as a nested `"pmu":{...}` object onto `w`. Every field is present —\n    /// value or `{"unavailable":"<reason>"}` — the same guarantee as `HwStamp::write`.\n    pub fn write(self, w: JsonWriter) -> JsonWriter {\n        let inner = JsonWriter::obj();\n        let inner = self.tsc_cycles.write_field(inner, "tsc_cycles");\n        let inner = self.minflt.write_field(inner, "minflt");\n        let inner = self.majflt.write_field(inner, "majflt");\n        let inner = self.nswap.write_field(inner, "nswap");\n        let inner = self\n            .vol_ctxt_switches\n            .write_field(inner, "vol_ctxt_switches");\n        let inner = self\n            .nonvol_ctxt_switches\n            .write_field(inner, "nonvol_ctxt_switches");\n        let inner = self.hw_instructions.write_field(inner, "hw_instructions");\n        let inner = self.hw_cpu_cycles.write_field(inner, "hw_cpu_cycles");\n        let inner = self.hw_cache_misses.write_field(inner, "hw_cache_misses");\n        let inner = self.hw_branch_misses.write_field(inner, "hw_branch_misses");\n        w.field_raw("pmu", &inner.finish())\n    }\n\n    /// Absence-propagating wrapping delta `end - start`, field by field. A field is a\n    /// `Value` only when BOTH endpoints are `Value`; otherwise it carries `end`'s absence.\n    /// Raw counts stay raw — a bracketed subtraction is the ONE sanctioned delta.\n    pub fn delta(start: PmuStamp, end: PmuStamp) -> PmuStamp {\n        fn d(s: Reading<u64>, e: Reading<u64>) -> Reading<u64> {\n            match (s, e) {\n                (Reading::Value(a), Reading::Value(b)) => Reading::Value(b.wrapping_sub(a)),\n                (_, Reading::Unavailable(x)) => Reading::Unavailable(x),\n                (Reading::Unavailable(x), _) => Reading::Unavailable(x),\n            }\n        }\n        PmuStamp {\n            tsc_cycles: d(start.tsc_cycles, end.tsc_cycles),\n            minflt: d(start.minflt, end.minflt),\n ## 11281 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/fdr/cost_oracle.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: cost_oracle · 336 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/fdr/cost_oracle.rs	cost_oracle · 336 lines	//! `fdr/cost_oracle.rs` — Items 67 + 68: the cost-oracle classification + runtime counters\n//! (pure no_std core).\n//!\n//! Every operator-gated decision surface carries a cost bucket with a traceable evidence\n//! pointer. Buckets: `ORACLE-EXACT` (input-independent), `ORACLE-BOUNDED` (fixed operation\n//! schedule), `MEASURED-ONLY` (genuinely dynamic / I/O / probabilistic), and `FORBIDDEN`\n//! (unclassified — the oracle never returns a fabricated guess).\n//!\n//! Plane doctrine: the captured cost values live on the P3 forensic plane — recorded input,\n//! never a decision variable. The process-global counter set is a P3 telemetry mirror only.\n//!\n//! This is the *pure* half. The counter set is a compile-time-initialized `static` (no\n//! `OnceLock`, no lazy init — the counters are zeroed atomics). The std side — the\n//! recoverable-from-ring round-trip test that needs a real `FdrRing` — lives in the kernel\n//! shim (`dowiz-kernel`'s `fdr::cost_oracle`).\n\nuse crate::fdr::json::JsonWriter;\nuse crate::fdr::schema::{Kind, StampPolicy};\nuse crate::fdr::Level;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n\n/// The cost bucket for an operator-gated decision.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum CostBucket {\n    /// Cost is input-independent / fully enumerated — value is known exactly (mod host noise).\n    OracleExact,\n    /// Cost follows a fixed operation schedule — bounded by an analytic `[min,max]`.\n    OracleBounded,\n    /// Genuinely dynamic / I/O / probabilistic — reported as a distribution, not a point.\n    MeasuredOnly,\n    /// NOT classified. The forbidden state — the oracle surfaces this instead of a guess.\n    Forbidden,\n}\n\nimpl CostBucket {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            CostBucket::OracleExact => "ORACLE-EXACT",\n            CostBucket::OracleBounded => "ORACLE-BOUNDED",\n            CostBucket::MeasuredOnly => "MEASURED-ONLY",\n            CostBucket::Forbidden => "FORBIDDEN",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// An operator-gated decision surface the cost oracle classifies + counts.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum DecisionSurface {\n    /// `hydra::FileEventStore` group-commit (`batch_size`).\n    GroupCommit,\n    /// `spectral_cache::DecompCache` eigensolver choice (hit vs recompute).\n    EigensolverChoice,\n    /// PQ sign/verify crypto latency.\n    CryptoLatency,\n}\n\nimpl DecisionSurface {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            DecisionSurface::GroupCommit => "group_commit",\n            DecisionSurface::EigensolverChoice => "eigensolver_choice",\n            DecisionSurface::CryptoLatency => "crypto_latency",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The honest cost bucket for this surface (item 67 classification).\n    pub fn bucket(self) -> CostBucket {\n        match self {\n            DecisionSurface::GroupCommit => CostBucket::OracleExact,\n            DecisionSurface::EigensolverChoice => CostBucket::OracleBounded,\n            DecisionSurface::CryptoLatency => CostBucket::MeasuredOnly,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The traceable evidence pointer (item 67 §67.3 step 2).\n    pub fn evidence(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            DecisionSurface::GroupCommit => "HOT-PATHS.tsv:hydra::FileEventStore::with_batch_size; group_commit_barrier_fires_every_n_inserts",\n            DecisionSurface::EigensolverChoice => "spectral_cache::DecompCache; spectral_cache recompute falsifier test",\n            DecisionSurface::CryptoLatency => "pq/dsa sign/verify; item 26 ~637us distribution exemplar",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 68 (EXACT capture): the group-commit decision is input-independent once `batch_size` is\n/// fixed. The cost is the count of inserts per durability barrier, which is an exact integer.\npub fn group_commit_exact_cost(batch_size: usize) -> u64 {\n    batch_size.max(1) as u64\n}\n\n/// Item 68 (BOUNDED capture): the eigensolver choice. A cache HIT returns in O(1); a MISS\n/// triggers the recompute whose schedule is fixed. The analytic `[min,max]` is `[1, n*n + 1]`.\npub fn eigensolver_bounded_cost(n: usize, is_cache_hit: bool) -> (u64, u64) {\n    if is_cache_hit {\n        (1, 1)\n    } else {\n        let floor = (n as u64).saturating_mul(n as u64).saturating_add(1);\n        (1, floor)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Item 68 (MEASURED-ONLY capture): crypto latency is reported as a distribution summary, never\n/// a fabricated point estimate. Empty sample ⇒ a named absence, never 0.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]\npub struct CryptoLatencyDist {\n    pub count: u64,\n    pub p50_us: u64,\n    pub p99_us: u64,\n}\n\nimpl CryptoLatencyDist {\n    /// Fold one observed latency sample into the running distribution (min/max as the honest\n    /// p50/p99 proxy for a MEASURED-ONLY surface).\n    pub fn observe(&mut self, us: u64) {\n        self.count += 1;\n        if self.count == 1 {\n            self.p50_us = us;\n            self.p99_us = us;\n        } else {\n            self.p50_us = self.p50_us.min(us);\n            self.p99_us = self.p99_us.max(us);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// A MEASURED-ONLY surface with zero samples reports an honest absence (no fabricated 0).\n    pub fn is_absent(&self) -> bool {\n        self.count == 0\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Runtime counters (item 67/68: deterministic runtime counters for operator-gated decisions) ──\n// A process-global counter set, P3-plane telemetry only. Reads/writes are explicit and NEVER\n// feed a durability barrier / drift gate / crypto verdict (grep-firewall proof below).\n// Compile-time-initialized `static` (zeroed atomics) — no `OnceLock` needed.\n\nstruct CostOracleCounters {\n    group_commit_barriers: AtomicU64,\n    group_commit_inserts: AtomicU64,\n    eigensolver_hits: AtomicU64,\n    eigensolver_recomputes: AtomicU64,\n    crypto_samples: AtomicU64,\n    crypto_latency_us: AtomicU64,\n}\n\nimpl CostOracleCounters {\n    const fn new() -> Self {\n        CostOracleCounters {\n            group_commit_barriers: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            group_commit_inserts: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            eigensolver_hits: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            eigensolver_recomputes: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            crypto_samples: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            crypto_latency_us: AtomicU64::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstatic COST_ORACLE: CostOracleCounters = CostOracleCounters::new();\n\nfn counters() -> &'static CostOracleCounters {\n    &COST_ORACLE\n}\n\n/// Record ONE group-commit barrier firing over `inserts` inserts. P3 telemetry only.\npub fn record_group_commit(inserts: u64) {\n    counters().group_commit_barriers.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    counters().group_commit_inserts.fetch_add(inserts, Ordering::Relaxed);\n}\n\n/// Record ONE eigensolver decision (hit or miss/recompute). P3 telemetry only.\npub fn record_eigensolver(is_cache_hit: bool) {\n    if is_cache_hit {\n        counters().eigensolver_hits.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    } else {\n        counters().eigensolver_recomputes.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Record ONE crypto latency sample (MEASURED-ONLY). P3 telemetry only.\npub fn record_crypto_latency(us: u64) {\n    counters().crypto_samples.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    counters().crypto_latency_us.fetch_add(us, Ordering::Relaxed);\n}\n\n/// A one-shot snapshot of the runtime counters (the operator's offline feed).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]\npub struct CostOracleSnapshot {\n    pub group_commit_barriers: u64,\n    pub group_commit_inserts: u64,\n    pub eigensolver_hits: u64,\n    pub eigensolver_recomputes: u64,\n    pub crypto_samples: u64,\n    pub crypto_latency_us: u64,\n}\n\n/// Read the current counter snapshot.\npub fn snapshot() -> CostOracleSnapshot {\n    let c = counters();\n    CostOracleSnapshot {\n        group_commit_barriers: c.group_commit_barriers.load(Ordering::Relaxed),\n        group_commit_inserts: c.group_commit_inserts.load(Ordering::Relaxed),\n        eigensolver_hits: c.eigensolver_hits.load(Ordering::Relaxed),\n        eigensolver_recomputes: c.eigensolver_recomputes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),\n        crypto_samples: c.crypto_samples.load(Ordering::Relaxed),\n        crypto_latency_us: c.crypto_latency_us.load(Ordering::Relaxed),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Reset all counters (test isolation). Cheap; the global is a zeroed static.\npub fn reset_counters() {\n    let c = counters();\n    c.group_commit_barriers.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    c.group_commit_inserts.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    c.eigensolver_hits.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    c.eigensolver_recomputes.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    c.crypto_samples.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    c.crypto_latency_us.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);\n}\n\n/// Item 67 §67.4 (b): classify a query. An unrecognized / unclassified decision returns the\n/// FORBIDDEN state — never a guess.\npub fn classify(surface: DecisionSurface) -> (CostBucket, &'static str) {\n    (surface.bucket(), surface.evidence())\n}\n\n/// Build a deterministic FDR JSON line carrying the cost-oracle counters under a fixed field\n/// order. The SAME string is what `FdrRing::append` would serialize.\npub fn cost_oracle_record_json(snap: &CostOracleSnapshot) -> String {\n    JsonWriter::obj()\n        .field_u64("seq", 0)\n        .field_str("level", Level::Info.as_str())\n        .field_str("kind", Kind::Tuning.as_str())\n        .field_str("name", "cost_oracle")\n        .field_u64("group_commit_barriers", snap.group_commit_barriers)\n        .field_u64("group_commit_inserts", snap.group_commit_inserts)\n        .field_u64("eigensolver_hits", snap.eigensolver_hits)\n        .field_u64("eigensolver_recomputes", snap.eigensolver_recomputes)\n        .field_u64("crypto_samples", snap.crypto_samples)\n        .field_u64("crypto_latency_us", snap.crypto_latency_us)\n        .finish()\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // Item 67 §67.4 (a): every operator-gated decision resolves to a non-Forbidden bucket with a\n    // resolvable evidence pointer.\n    #[test]\n    fn every_decision_surface_is_classified_not_forbidden() {\n        for s in [\n            DecisionSurface::GroupCommit,\n            DecisionSurface::EigensolverChoice,\n            DecisionSurface::CryptoLatency,\n        ] {\n            let (bucket, evidence) = classify(s);\n            assert_ne!(bucket, CostBucket::Forbidden, "{:?} must be classified", s);\n            assert!(!evidence.is_empty(), "{:?} needs an evidence pointer", s);\n            assert!(!evidence.contains("TODO"), "{:?} evidence must be concrete", s);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn group_commit_exact_cost_is_input_independent() {\n        for bs in [1usize, 8, 64, 1024] {\n            assert_eq!(group_commit_exact_cost(bs), bs as u64);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn eigensolver_bounded_cost_is_fixed_schedule_interval() {\n        for n in [1usize, 4, 16, 64] {\n            let (lo, hi) = eigensolver_bounded_cost(n, false);\n            assert_eq!(lo, 1);\n            assert_eq!(hi, (n as u64) * (n as u64) + 1);\n            let (hlo, hhi) = eigensolver_bounded_cost(n, true);\n            assert_eq!((hlo, hhi), (1, 1), "cache hit is O(1), independent of n");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn crypto_latency_is_distribution_not_point() {\n        let empty = CryptoLatencyDist::default();\n        assert!(empty.is_absent(), "no samples ⇒ honest absence, never 0");\n        let mut d = CryptoLatencyDist::default();\n        for us in [100u64, 637, 50, 900] {\n            d.observe(us);\n        }\n        assert_eq!(d.count, 4);\n        assert_eq!(d.p50_us, 50, "p50 proxy = observed min");\n        assert_eq!(d.p99_us, 900, "p99 proxy = observed max");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn counters_roundtrip_through_snapshot() {\n        reset_counters();\n        record_group_commit(64);\n        record_eigensolver(true);\n        record_eigensolver(false);\n        record_crypto_latency(637);\n        let snap = snapshot();\n        assert_eq!(snap.group_commit_barriers, 1);\n        assert_eq!(snap.group_commit_inserts, 64);\n        assert_eq!(snap.eigensolver_hits, 1);\n        assert_eq!(snap.eigensolver_recomputes, 1);\n        assert_eq!(snap.crypto_samples, 1);\n        assert_eq!(snap.crypto_latency_us, 637);\n        reset_counters();\n    }\n\n    // Item 68 §68.4 load-bearing P3 proof: NO captured cost value feeds a decision / gate /\n    // verdict / hash surface. Greppable: this source file must never pass a cost value into a\n    // durability barrier, a drift gate, or a crypto verify.\n    #[test]\n    fn p3_grep_firewall_no_cost_value_feeds_decision() {\n        let full = include_str!("cost_oracle.rs");\n        let src = full.split("#[cfg(test)]").next().unwrap_or(full);\n        for line in src.lines() {\n            let l = line.trim();\n            let reads_cost = l.contains("snapshot()")\n                || l.contains("crypto_latency_us")\n                || l.contains("eigensolver_recomputes");\n            let is_decision = l.contains("if ")\n                && (l.contains("sync_all") || l.contains("drift") || l.contains("verify"));\n            assert!(\n                !(reads_cost && is_decision),\n                "P3 violation: a cost value must not gate a durability/drift/crypto decision: {line}"\n            );\n        }\n        assert!(\n            !src.contains("cost_to_hash") && !src.contains("cost_into_verdict"),\n            "P3: cost must never enter a hash/verdict surface"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	11282	-1	-1		7b6e31ef59fb21e5ab4b938982d27a3bc8fcbc06b964f54d3f58625652b3ebc9681164884ec5f6fee74f016b1451d5284e1147b63aca0eba214fda04e73cace68ebe55098f8f1a0db783ec00a69b99d20568c02f692fd44dd0a63385ba4bd5d4e8e6d776334b51bfc0e20eaffe1d4f9b6d98452f0e8501769321747efa106d71
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/fdr/ring_parse.rs	ring_parse · 55 lines	//! `fdr/ring_parse.rs` — the pure JSONL line-parsing helpers used by the FDR\n//! ring's recovery path (blueprint §4.4).\n//!\n//! The durable on-disk segment ring itself (`FdrRing`, `recover`, the post-mortem\n//! writer) is std file I/O and stays in the kernel (`dowiz_kernel::fdr::ring`).\n//! These two helpers are pure string parsing — no std, no file I/O, alloc-only —\n//! so they live here in the `no_std` core and are re-exported back through the\n//! kernel shim to keep the `fdr::ring::extract_u64` / `extract_str` names stable.\n//!\n//! Scope: parse side only. Compiles on every target incl. `wasm32`.\n\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\n\n/// Minimal field extraction (kernel is serde-free). Finds `"<key>":<number>`.\npub fn extract_u64(line: &str, key: &str) -> Option<u64> {\n    let pat = format!("\\"{key}\\":");\n    let i = line.find(&pat)? + pat.len();\n    let rest = &line[i..];\n    let end = rest\n        .find(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())\n        .unwrap_or(rest.len());\n    rest[..end].parse().ok()\n}\n\n/// Finds `"<key>":"<string>"` (values here are simple `[a-z_-]` names — no escaping).\npub fn extract_str(line: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let pat = format!("\\"{key}\\":\\"");\n    let i = line.find(&pat)? + pat.len();\n    let rest = &line[i..];\n    let end = rest.find('"')?;\n    Some(rest[..end].to_string())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn extract_u64_parses_number_field() {\n        let line = r#"{"seq":123,"kind":"event"}"#;\n        assert_eq!(extract_u64(line, "seq"), Some(123));\n        assert_eq!(extract_u64(line, "nope"), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn extract_str_parses_string_field() {\n        let line = r#"{"seq":1,"kind":"event","name":"clean_shutdown"}"#;\n        assert_eq!(extract_str(line, "kind"), Some("event".to_string()));\n        assert_eq!(\n            extract_str(line, "name"),\n            Some("clean_shutdown".to_string())\n        );\n        assert_eq!(extract_str(line, "missing"), None);\n    }\n}\n	11288	-1	-1		d062b316ae54e35d6809e885d3525646dd5694a4ff526fc76857a01b4322c26b5940a618deea7cff8453806b3886a4218c294d14d96c87a9b466f005e72efbce4714f4d22bf3492394863558b2b9e15861fdf46a68fbe44d250063a0b18d5d85f923f317065ac9bdcc78490371ef47f72474152a7089a1a79c3051bc71a2ec98
```
