4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/reconstruction_memory.rs	reconstruction_memory · 489 lines	//! reconstruction_memory.rs — MemHarness reimplementation: memory as reconstruction, not replay.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! A kernel-native reconstruction memory engine. Instead of replaying stored\n//! experience verbatim (which causes negative transfer), this engine:\n//! 1. Records experience as structured memory entries (HarvestLedger-backed)\n//! 2. On recall, critiques the stored entry against current context\n//! 3. Reconstructs an adapted version that fits the present situation\n//! 4. Uses trigram pattern surface to find recurring experience patterns\n//!\n//! # MemHarness mapping\n//! - "policy model critiques and reconstructs" → `reconstruct()` method\n//! - "contextually-grounded prompt before action" → `recall_adapted()` method\n//! - "GRPO group-relative" → `group_compare()` compares multiple memory entries\n//! - "negative transfer avoidance" → critique rejects irrelevant memories\n//!\n//! # Design\n//! - Pure Rust, zero external dependencies\n//! - Uses existing kernel primitives: telemetry_harvest, trigram, markov\n//! - Deterministic reconstruction (no RNG in the reconstruction path)\n\nuse crate::telemetry::surface_recurring_patterns;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A memory entry — stored experience that can be reconstructed.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct MemoryEntry {\n    /// Unique ID for this memory.\n    pub id: u64,\n    /// What the memory is about (topic tag).\n    pub topic: String,\n    /// The stored experience (original form).\n    pub content: String,\n    /// Context tags that describe when this memory applies.\n    pub context_tags: Vec<String>,\n    /// Success/failure outcome when this memory was created.\n    pub outcome: f64, // 0.0 = failure, 1.0 = success\n    /// Timestamp of creation.\n    pub timestamp_us: u64,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the canonical bytes (integrity).\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// A reconstructed memory — the adapted version after critique.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ReconstructedMemory {\n    /// The original entry ID.\n    pub original_id: u64,\n    /// Whether the memory passed critique (relevant to current context).\n    pub passed_critique: bool,\n    /// The reconstructed/adapted content.\n    pub reconstructed_content: String,\n    /// Confidence in the reconstruction (0.0-1.0).\n    pub confidence: f64,\n    /// Why this memory was selected (critique reasoning).\n    pub critique_reason: String,\n}\n\n/// Critique verdict on a memory entry against current context.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum CritiqueVerdict {\n    /// Memory is relevant and can be used as-is.\n    Relevant,\n    /// Memory is partially relevant — needs reconstruction.\n    PartialReconstruction {\n        /// Which context tags matched.\n        matched_tags: Vec<String>,\n        /// Which context tags are missing.\n        missing_tags: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    /// Memory is irrelevant to current context — negative transfer risk.\n    Irrelevant {\n        /// Why it was rejected.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// The reconstruction memory engine.\npub struct ReconstructionMemory {\n    /// Underlying storage for memory entries.\n    entries: Vec<MemoryEntry>,\n    /// Monotonic ID counter.\n    next_id: u64,\n    /// Current context tags (what the agent is working on now).\n    current_context: Vec<String>,\n    /// Pattern surface cache (trigram-based recurring patterns).\n    pattern_cache: Option<crate::telemetry::PatternSurface>,\n}\n\nimpl ReconstructionMemory {\n    /// Create a new reconstruction memory engine.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        ReconstructionMemory {\n            entries: Vec::new(),\n            next_id: 0,\n            current_context: Vec::new(),\n            pattern_cache: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set the current context tags (what the agent is working on).\n    pub fn set_context(&mut self, tags: Vec<String>) {\n        self.current_context = tags;\n        self.pattern_cache = None; // invalidate cache\n    }\n\n    /// Add a memory entry. `timestamp_us` is caller-supplied wall-clock microseconds\n    /// (the no_std form — the host stamps its own clock).\n    pub fn remember(&mut self, topic: &str, content: &str, context_tags: Vec<String>, outcome: f64, timestamp_us: u64) -> u64 {\n        let id = self.next_id;\n        self.next_id += 1;\n\n        let mut entry = MemoryEntry {\n            id,\n            topic: topic.to_string(),\n            content: content.to_string(),\n            context_tags,\n            outcome,\n            timestamp_us,\n            hash: [0u8; 32],\n        };\n\n        // Compute hash.\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(64);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&id.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(topic.as_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(content.as_bytes());\n        entry.hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(&buf);\n\n        self.entries.push(entry);\n        id\n    }\n\n    /// Critique a memory entry against the current context.\n    pub fn critique(&self, entry: &MemoryEntry) -> CritiqueVerdict {\n        if self.current_context.is_empty() {\n            return CritiqueVerdict::Relevant; // no context = accept all\n        }\n\n        let mut matched = Vec::new();\n        let mut missing = Vec::new();\n\n        for tag in &self.current_context {\n            if entry.context_tags.contains(tag) {\n                matched.push(tag.clone());\n            } else {\n                missing.push(tag.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        if matched.is_empty() && missing.len() == self.current_context.len() {\n            CritiqueVerdict::Irrelevant {\n                reason: format!("no context tags matched (needed {:?}, had {:?})",\n                    self.current_context, entry.context_tags)\n            }\n        } else if missing.is_empty() {\n            CritiqueVerdict::Relevant\n        } else {\n            CritiqueVerdict::PartialReconstruction { matched_tags: matched, missing_tags: missing }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reconstruct a memory entry for the current context.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `ReconstructedMemory` with adapted content based on critique.\n    pub fn reconstruct(&self, entry: &MemoryEntry) -> ReconstructedMemory {\n        let critique = self.critique(entry);\n\n        match critique {\n            CritiqueVerdict::Relevant => {\n                ReconstructedMemory {\n                    original_id: entry.id,\n                    passed_critique: true,\n                    reconstructed_content: entry.content.clone(),\n                    confidence: 1.0,\n                    critique_reason: "fully relevant — used as-is".to_string(),\n                }\n            }\n            CritiqueVerdict::PartialReconstruction { matched_tags, missing_tags } => {\n                // Reconstruct: keep matched parts, note missing context\n                let reconstructed = format!(\n                    "[RECONSTRUCTED from memory #{}] {}\\n\\\n                     Matched context: {}\\n\\\n                     Missing context: {}\\n\\\n                     Original: {}",\n                    entry.id,\n                    entry.topic,\n                    matched_tags.join(", "),\n                    missing_tags.join(", "),\n                    entry.content\n                );\n\n                ReconstructedMemory {\n                    original_id: entry.id,\n                    passed_critique: true,\n                    reconstructed_content: reconstructed,\n                    confidence: 0.7, // partial match = lower confidence\n                    critique_reason: format!("partial match: {} tags matched, {} missing",\n                        matched_tags.len(), missing_tags.len()),\n                }\n            }\n            CritiqueVerdict::Irrelevant { reason } => {\n                ReconstructedMemory {\n                    original_id: entry.id,\n                    passed_critique: false,\n                    reconstructed_content: String::new(),\n                    confidence: 0.0,\n                    critique_reason: reason,\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Recall memories adapted to the current context.\n    ///\n    /// Returns reconstructed memories that passed critique, sorted by relevance.\n    pub fn recall_adapted(&self, limit: usize) -> Vec<ReconstructedMemory> {\n        let mut results = Vec::new();\n\n        for entry in &self.entries {\n            let reconstructed = self.reconstruct(entry);\n            if reconstructed.passed_critique {\n                results.push(reconstructed);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Sort by confidence descending.\n        results.sort_by(|a, b| b.confidence.partial_cmp(&a.confidence).unwrap_or(core::cmp::Ordering::Equal));\n\n        results.truncate(limit);\n        results\n    }\n\n    /// Group-relative comparison: compare multiple memory entries and rank them.\n    ///\n    /// This is the GRPO-inspired part: memories are compared within a group\n    /// (same topic) and ranked by outcome + relevance to current context.\n    pub fn group_compare(&self, topic: &str) -> Vec<(u64, f64, String)> {\n        // Collect entries matching the topic.\n        let mut group: Vec<&MemoryEntry> = self.entries.iter()\n            .filter(|e| e.topic == topic)\n            .collect();\n\n        if group.is_empty() {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n\n        // Score each entry: outcome * relevance_to_current_context\n        let mut scored: Vec<(u64, f64, String)> = group.iter().map(|e| {\n            let relevance = if self.current_context.is_empty() {\n                1.0\n            } else {\n                let matches = self.current_context.iter()\n                    .filter(|ctx| e.context_tags.contains(ctx))\n                    .count();\n                matches as f64 / self.current_context.len() as f64\n            };\n            let score = e.outcome * relevance;\n            (e.id, score, e.content.clone())\n        }).collect();\n\n        // Sort by score descending (group-relative ranking).\n        scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(core::cmp::Ordering::Equal));\n\n        scored\n    }\n\n    /// Find recurring patterns in memory }\n\n        // Tokenize memory content into outcome tokens.\n        let tokens: Vec<&str> = self.entries.iter()\n            .flat_map(|e| e.content.split_whitespace())\n            .collect();\n\n Some(surface)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the number of stored memories.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.entries.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Check if there are no memories.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.entries.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Get a memory entry by ID.\n    pub fn get(&self, id: u64) -> Option<&MemoryEntry> {\n        self.entries.iter().find(|e| e.id == id)\n    }\n\n    /// Clear all memories (for reset/testing).\n    pub fn clear(&mut self) {\n        self.entries.clear();\n        self.next_id = 0;\n        self.pattern_cache = None;\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII report of current memory state.\n    pub fn ascii_report(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::from("=== Reconstruction Memory Report ===\\n");\n If `/proc` or `/sys` is unavailable (wasm, non-Linux), all booleans are false,\n//! counts are zero. No panics, no hangs.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Hardware feature flags detected from `/proc/cpuinfo` + `/proc/meminfo`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CpuCaps {\n    /// AVX2 (256-bit integer SIMD).\n    pub avx2: bool,\n    /// FMA3 (fused multiply-add, `vfma*`).\n    pub fma: bool,\n    /// SHA-1 / SHA-256 hardware acceleration (NOT SHA3/Keccak).\n    pub sha_ni: bool,\n    /// AES hardware (AES-NI).\n    pub aes_ni: bool,\n    /// BMI2 (bit-manipulation, e.g. `bzhi`, `pext`, `pdep`).\n    pub bmi2: bool,\n    /// FSRM — fast short rep movsb (memcpy acceleration).\n    pub fsrm: bool,\n    /// L3 cache size in KiB (or 0 when unreadable).\n    pub l3_cache_kb: usize,\n    /// Total system RAM in MiB (or 0 when unreadable).\n    pub ram_total_mb: usize,\n    /// Number of logical processors.\n    pub cores: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for CpuCaps {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        CpuCaps {\n            avx2: false,\n            fma: false,\n            sha_ni: false,\n            aes_ni: false,\n            bmi2: false,\n            fsrm: false,\n            l3_cache_kb: 0,\n            ram_total_mb: 0,\n            cores: 0,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Derive a capability snapshot from the raw `/proc`/`/sys` strings (pure, no I/O). The\n/// kernel shim's `detect()` reads the files and forwards them here.\npub fn detect_from(cpuinfo: &str, meminfo: &str, l3_cache_size: &str) -> CpuCaps {\n    let flags: &str = cpuinfo\n        .lines()\n        .find(|l| l.starts_with("flags"))\n        .and_then(|l| l.split(':').nth(1))\n        .unwrap_or("");\n\n    let flags_lower = flags.to_lowercase();\n    let has_flag = |f: &str| flags_lower.split_whitespace().any(|w| w == f);\n\n    // ── cores ──\n    let cores = cpuinfo.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("processor")).count();\n\n    // ── L3 cache from /sys ──\n    let l3_cache_kb = parse_cache_size_kb(l3_cache_size).unwrap_or(0);\n\n    // ── RAM from /proc/meminfo ──\n    let ram_total_mb = meminfo\n        .lines()\n        .find(|l| l.starts_with("MemTotal:"))\n        .and_then(|l| {\n            let parts: Vec<&str> = l.split_whitespace().collect();\n            if parts.len() >= 2 {\n                parts[1].parse::<usize>().ok().map(|kb| kb / 1024)\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n\n    CpuCaps {\n        avx2: has_flag("avx2"),\n        fma: has_flag("fma"),\n        sha_ni: has_flag("sha_ni"),\n        aes_ni: has_flag("aes"),\n        bmi2: has_flag("bmi2"),\n        fsrm: has_flag("fsrm"),\n        l3_cache_kb,\n        ram_total_mb,\n        cores,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a cache-size string like `"32768K"` or `"32M"` → KiB.\npub fn parse_cache_size_kb(s: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    let s = s.trim();\n    if s.ends_with('K') {\n        s[..s.len() - 1].parse().ok()\n    } else if s.ends_with('M') {\n        s[..s.len() - 1].parse::<usize>().ok().map(|v| v * 1024)\n    } else {\n        None\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn default_is_all_false() {\n        let d = CpuCaps::default();\n        assert!(!d.avx2);\n        assert!(!d.fma);\n        assert!(!d.sha_ni);\n        assert!(!d.aes_ni);\n        assert!(!d.bmi2);\n        assert!(!d.fsrm);\n        assert_eq!(d.l3_cache_kb, 0);\n        assert_eq!(d.ram_total_mb, 0);\n        assert_eq!(d.cores, 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cache_size_parsing() {\n        assert_eq!(parse_cache_size_kb("32768K"), Some(32768));\n        assert_eq!(parse_cache_size_kb("32M"), Some(32 * 1024));\n        assert_eq!(parse_cache_size_kb(""), None);\n        assert_eq!(parse_cache_size_kb("xyz"), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn detect_from_parses_flags_and_counts() {\n        let cpuinfo = "processor : 0\\nprocessor : 1\\nflags : fpu vme avx2 fma aes bmi2 fsrm\\n";\n        let meminfo = "MemTotal: 16777216 kB\\n";\n        let caps = detect_from(cpuinfo, meminfo, "32M");\n        assert!(caps.avx2);\n        assert!(caps.fma);\n        assert!(caps.aes_ni);\n        assert!(caps.bmi2);\n        assert!(caps.fsrm);\n        assert!(!caps.sha_ni, "sha_ni not in flags");\n        assert_eq!(caps.cores, 2);\n        assert_eq!(caps.l3_cache_kb, 32 * 1024);\n        assert_eq!(caps.ram_total_mb, 16384);\n    }\n}\n	11333	-1	-1		eba7b37e0dc41b24eb7a82cf4832024860b09efcb77a6c086947001f9fe5b66339c52583d5871687e0775d0b48d2b7289cf367a3fb6e8468a488700e67ca5ecb1db5759d2752b3319595a16917992bebf0d9142e21ee6307d00706d4dac53d87e0e6f777b4c7116950ce1a36efdd62fc0d3c4d688c8bfc6107b11dd14286471a
```

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/numbat.rs	numbat · 520 lines	//! numbat.rs — Numbat reimplementation: endpoint visibility for AI agent actions.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! A kernel-native endpoint visibility system for AI agent activity:\n//! 1. **Detect** — monitor agent actions at the endpoint level\n//! 2. **Block** (optional) — intercept actions before execution\n//! 3. **Forensic reconstruction** — reconstruct what happened from logs\n//!\n//! # Numbat mapping\n//! - "endpoint visibility into AI agent activity" → `AgentActivityMonitor`\n//! - "local detection" → `detect_anomalous()` pattern matching\n//! - "optional pre-action blocking" → `BlockPolicy` trait\n//! - "forensic reconstruction" → `reconstruct_timeline()` from event_log\n//!\n//! # Design\n//! - Pure Rust, zero external dependencies\n//! - Uses existing kernel primitives: event_log (SHA3-256), fdr (flight data recorder),\n//!   self_harness (zone protection), workflow_gate (phase tracking)\n//! - Deterministic detection (no ML — rule-based pattern matching)\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::fdr::{emit_event, Level};\nuse alloc::boxed::Box;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Types of agent actions that can be monitored.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum AgentActionType {\n    /// Reading files or data.\n    Read,\n    /// Writing files or data.\n    Write,\n    /// Executing code or commands.\n    Execute,\n    /// Making network requests.\n    Network,\n    /// Using tools (LLM calls, etc.).\n    ToolUse,\n    /// Modifying state or configuration.\n    StateChange,\n}\n\nimpl AgentActionType {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            AgentActionType::Read => "read",\n            AgentActionType::Write => "write",\n            AgentActionType::Execute => "execute",\n            AgentActionType::Network => "network",\n            AgentActionType::ToolUse => "tool_use",\n            AgentActionType::StateChange => "state_change",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// An agent action event — recorded for visibility and forensics.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AgentAction {\n    /// Unique event ID.\n    pub event_id: u64,\n    /// Type of action.\n    pub action_type: AgentActionType,\n    /// What the action is doing (description).\n    pub description: String,\n    /// Whether the action was blocked.\n    pub blocked: bool,\n    /// The agent/module that performed the action.\n    pub source: String,\n    /// Timestamp (microseconds).\n    pub timestamp_us: u64,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the canonical bytes (integrity).\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// A block policy — decides whether an action should be blocked.\n///\n/// Implement this trait to create custom blocking rules.\npub trait BlockPolicy {\n    /// Check if an action should be blocked.\n    /// Returns (should_block, reason).\n    fn should_block(&self, action: &AgentAction) -> (bool, String);\n}\n\n/// Default block policy — blocks nothing (permissive).\npub struct AllowAllPolicy;\n\nimpl BlockPolicy for AllowAllPolicy {\n    fn should_block(&self, _action: &AgentAction) -> (bool, String) {\n        (false, String::new())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Strict block policy — blocks writes and state changes by default.\npub struct StrictWritePolicy {\n    /// Exceptions: actions allowed despite being writes.\n    exceptions: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl StrictWritePolicy {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        StrictWritePolicy {\n            exceptions: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn add_exception(&mut self, pattern: &str) {\n        self.exceptions.push(pattern.to_string());\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for StrictWritePolicy {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl BlockPolicy for StrictWritePolicy {\n    fn should_block(&self, action: &AgentAction) -> (bool, String) {\n        match action.action_type {\n            AgentActionType::Write | AgentActionType::StateChange => {\n                // Check exceptions.\n                for exception in &self.exceptions {\n                    if action.description.contains(exception) {\n                        return (false, format!("exception matched: {}", exception));\n                    }\n                }\n                (true, "write/state_change blocked by strict policy".to_string())\n            }\n            _ => (false, String::new()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Detection rule — pattern-based anomaly detection.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct DetectionRule {\n    /// Name of the rule.\n    pub name: String,\n    /// Action types this rule applies to.\n    pub action_types: Vec<AgentActionType>,\n    /// Pattern to match in the description.\n    pub pattern: String,\n    /// Severity when triggered.\n    pub severity: Level,\n    /// Whether this is an anomaly (true) or normal (false).\n    pub is_anomaly: bool,\n}\n\n/// The agent activity monitor — core visibility engine.\npub struct AgentActivityMonitor {\n    /// Recorded actions.\n    actions: Vec<AgentAction>,\n    /// Monotonic ID counter.\n    next_id: u64,\n    /// Block policy in use.\n    block_policy: Box<dyn BlockPolicy>,\n    /// Detection rules.\n    detection_rules: Vec<DetectionRule>,\n}\n\nimpl AgentActivityMonitor {\n    /// Create a new monitor with the given block policy.\n    pub fn new(block_policy: Box<dyn BlockPolicy>) -> Self {\n        AgentActivityMonitor {\n            actions: Vec::new(),\n            next_id: 0,\n            block_policy,\n            detection_rules: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record and optionally block an agent action.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the recorded action (with blocked flag set if policy blocked it).\n    pub fn record_action(\n        &mut self,\n        action_type: AgentActionType,\n        description: &str,\n        source: &str,\n        timestamp_us: u64,\n    ) -> AgentAction {\n        let event_id = self.next_id;\n        self.next_id += 1;\n\n        let action = AgentAction {\n            event_id,\n            action_type,\n            description: description.to_string(),\n            blocked: false,\n            source: source.to_string(),\n            timestamp_us,\n            hash: [0u8; 32],\n        };\n\n        // Check block policy.\n        let (should_block, reason) = self.block_policy.should_block(&action);\n        if should_block {\n            let mut blocked_action = action.clone();\n            blocked_action.blocked = true;\n            // Record the block reason.\n            emit_event(\n                Level::Warn,\n                &format!("ACTION BLOCKED [#{}]: {} — {}", event_id, description, reason),\n                &[],\n            );\n            // Store with blocked flag.\n            let hash = Self::compute_hash(&blocked_action);\n            blocked_action.hash = hash;\n            self.actions.push(blocked_action);\n            return self.actions.last().unwrap().clone();\n        }\n\n        // Check detection rules.\n        for rule in &self.detection_rules {\n            if rule.action_types.contains(&action.action_type)\n                && action.description.contains(&rule.pattern)\n            {\n                if rule.is_anomaly {\n                    emit_event(\n                        rule.severity,\n                        &format!("ANOMALY DETECTED [#{}]: {} matched rule '{}'",\n                            event_id, description, rule.name),\n                        &[],\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let hash = Self::compute_hash(&action);\n        let mut final_action = action;\n        final_action.hash = hash;\n        self.actions.push(final_action);\n        self.actions.last().unwrap().clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Add a detection rule.\n    pub fn add_detection_rule(&mut self, rule: DetectionRule) {\n        self.detection_rules.push(rule);\n    }\n\n    /// Detect anomalous actions in the recorded history.\n    pub fn detect_anomalous(&self) -> Vec<&AgentAction> {\n        self.actions.iter()\n            .filter(|a| {\n                for rule in &self.detection_rules {\n                    if rule.action_types.contains(&a.action_type)\n                        && a.description.contains(&rule.pattern)\n                        && rule.is_anomaly\n                    {\n                        return true;\n                    }\n                }\n                false\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Reconstruct the timeline of actions — forensic reconstruction.\n    ///\n    /// Returns actions in chronological order with their block status.\n    pub fn reconstruct_timeline(&self) -> Vec<AgentAction> {\n        self.actions.clone()\n    }\n\n\n    /// Get the number of recorded actions.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.actions.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Check if there are no recorded actions.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.actions.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Get actions by type.\n    pub fn actions_by_type(&self, action_type: AgentActionType) -> Vec<&AgentAction> {\n        self.actions.iter()\n            .filter(|a| a.action_type == action_type)\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Get blocked actions.\n    pub fn blocked_actions(&self) -> Vec<&AgentAction> {\n        self.actions.iter()\n            .filter(|a| a.blocked)\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Clear all recorded actions (for reset/testing).\n    pub fn clear(&mut self) {\n        self.actions.clear();\n        self.next_id = 0;\n    }\n\n    /// Compute SHA3-256 hash of an action's canonical bytes.\n    fn compute_hash(action: &AgentAction) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(128);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&action.event_id.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(action.action_type.as_str().as_bytes());\n        buf.push(0);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(action.description.as_bytes());\n        buf.push(0);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(action.source.as_bytes());\n        buf.push(0);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&(action.blocked as u8).to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&action.timestamp_us.to_le_bytes());\n        sha3_256(&buf)\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII report of current monitor state.\n    pub fn ascii_report(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::from("=== Agent Activity Monitor Report ===\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("Total actions: {}\\n", self.len()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("Blocked actions: {}\\n", self.blocked_actions().len()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("Detection rules: {}\\n", self.detection_rules.len()));\n\n        if !self.actions.is_empty() {\n            out.push_str("\\nRecent actions:\\n");\n            for action in self.actions.iter().rev().take(5) {\n                let status = if action.blocked { "BLOCKED" } else { "allowed" };\n                out.push_str(&format!(\n                    "  #{}: {} [{}] {} — {}\\n",\n                    action.event_id, action.action_type.as_str(),\n                    status, action.description, action.source\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n\n\n        out.push_str("\\n=== End Report ===\\n");\n        out\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for AgentActivityMonitor {\n    fn default() let mut monitor = AgentActivityMonitor::new(Box::new(AllowAllPolicy));\n        let action = monitor.record_action(\n            AgentActionType::Read,\n            "read file foo.txt",\n            "agent-1",\n            12345,\n        );\n        assert_eq!(action.event_id, 0);\n        assert!(!action.blocked);\n        assert_eq!(monitor.len(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn record_multiple_gets_incrementing_ids() {\n        let mut monitor = AgentActivityMonitor::new(Box::new(AllowAllPolicy));\n        monitor.record_action(AgentActionType::Read, "r1", "s", 12345);\n "agent-1",\n            12345,\n        );\n        assert!(action.blocked);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn strict_policy_allows_reads() {\n        let mut monitor = 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/telemetry_aggregator.rs	telemetry_aggregator · 309 lines	//! telemetry_aggregator.rs — Kernel-native telemetry aggregation.\n//!\n//! Replaces the bash script `hydra_metrics_sender.sh` and provides a unified\n//! kernel-native interface to the existing telemetry primitives:\n//! - `typed_metrics` — CPU/mem/GPU sampling\n//! - `telemetry` — self-improvement pattern surface (trigram-based)\n//! - `telemetry_harvest` — deterministic JSONL harvest ledger\n//! - `span_metrics` — P83 span instrumentation (feature-gated)\n//!\n//! # What this replaces\n//! The bash script `hydra_metrics_sender.sh` read JSONL artifacts from\n//! `tools/telemetry/logs/`, aggregated them, and wrote reports. The kernel\n//! now provides this natively:\n//! - `HarvestLedger` (telemetry_harvest) replaces JSONL log aggregation\n//! - `MetricSample` (typed_metrics) replaces /proc sampling in bash\n//! - `surface_recurring_patterns` (telemetry) replaces pattern analysis\n//! - `SpanMetricsObserver` (span_metrics) replaces span tracking\n//!\n//! # Design\n//! - Pure Rust, zero external dependencies\n//! - Combines existing kernel primitives into a single aggregation interface\n//! - Produces structured reports (not raw text dumps)\n//! - Feature-gated behind `telemetry` (same as span_metrics)\n\nuse crate::telemetry::{surface_recurring_patterns, PatternSurface};\nuse crate::telemetry_harvest::{HarvestLedger, HarvestReport};\nuse crate::typed_metrics::{MemSample, ProcCpuSample};\nuse alloc::collections::VecDeque;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A unified telemetry snapshot — aggregates all available kernel metrics\n/// into a single structured report.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TelemetrySnapshot {\n    /// Timestamp of the snapshot.\n    pub timestamp_us: u64,\n    /// CPU sample (if available from /proc).\n    pub cpu: Option<ProcCpuSample>,\n    /// Memory sample (if available from /proc).\n    pub mem: Option<MemSample>,\n    /// Harvest ledger summary (aggregate of all recorded events).\n    pub harvest_report: Option<HarvestReport>,\n    /// Recurring pattern surface (top-k trigrams from tool outcomes).\n    pub pattern_surface: Option<PatternSurface>,\n    /// Total events recorded in the harvest ledger.\n    pub total_events: usize,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the canonical snapshot bytes (for integrity).\n    pub snapshot_hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// The telemetry aggregator — combines all kernel telemetry primitives.\npub struct TelemetryAggregator {\n    /// The harvest ledger for event recording.\n    harvest_ledger: HarvestLedger,\n    /// Tool outcome tokens for pattern surface (self-improvement loop).\n    outcome_tokens: alloc::collections::VecDeque<String>,\n    /// Maximum outcome tokens to retain (sliding window).\n    max_tokens: usize,\n    /// Harvest ledger capacity, retained so the ledger can be reset.\n    max_records: usize,\n}\n\nimpl TelemetryAggregator {\n    /// Create a new aggregator with a harvest ledger capped at `max_records`.\n    pub fn new(max_records: usize) -> Self {\n        let max_records = max_records.max(1);\n        TelemetryAggregator {\n            harvest_ledger: HarvestLedger::new(max_records),\n            outcome_tokens: alloc::collections::VecDeque::new(),\n            max_tokens: 1000,\n            max_records,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a tool outcome event in the harvest ledger. `now_ms` is caller-supplied\n    /// monotonic milliseconds (the no_std form — the host stamps its own clock).\n    pub fn record_event(\n        &mut self,\n        model: &str,\n        task: &str,\n        success: bool,\n        value: f64,\n        cost: f64,\n        outcome_token: &str,\n        now_ms: u64,\n    ) {\n        self.harvest_ledger\n            .record(model, task, success, value, cost, now_ms);\n\n        // Track outcome token for pattern surface (O(1) ring eviction).\n        self.outcome_tokens.push_back(outcome_token.to_string());\n        if self.outcome_tokens.len() > self.max_tokens {\n            self.outcome_tokens.pop_front();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Take a full telemetry snapshot from caller-supplied samples + timestamp (the\n    /// no_std form — the host samples `/proc` and stamps its own wall clock).\n    pub fn snapshot(\n        &mut self,\n        timestamp_us: u64,\n        cpu: Option<ProcCpuSample>,\n        mem: Option<MemSample>,\n    ) -> TelemetrySnapshot {\n        let harvest_report = self.harvest_ledger.report();\n        let pattern_surface = if self.outcome_tokens.is_empty() {\n            None\n        } else {\n            let tokens: Vec<&str> = self.outcome_tokens.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n            Some(surface_recurring_patterns(&tokens, 5))\n        };\n\n        let total_events = self.harvest_ledger.len();\n\n        let mut snapshot = TelemetrySnapshot {\n            timestamp_us,\n            cpu,\n            mem,\n            harvest_report: Some(harvest_report),\n            pattern_surface,\n            total_events,\n            snapshot_hash: [0u8; 32], // filled below\n        };\n\n        // Compute hash of canonical bytes.\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(128);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&timestamp_us.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&(snapshot.cpu.is_some() as u8).to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&(snapshot.mem.is_some() as u8).to_le_bytes());\n        if let Some(ref report) = snapshot.harvest_report {\n            buf.extend_from_slice(&report.total.to_le_bytes());\n            buf.extend_from_slice(&report.success_rate.to_le_bytes());\n            buf.extend_from_slice(&report.ev_score.to_le_bytes());\n        }\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&total_events.to_le_bytes());\n        snapshot.snapshot_hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(&buf);\n\n        snapshot\n    }\n\n    /// Get the harvest ledger for direct access.\n    pub fn ledger(&self) -> &HarvestLedger {\n        &self.harvest_ledger\n    }\n\n    /// Get the number of events recorded.\n    pub fn event_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.harvest_ledger.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Get the configured harvest ledger capacity.\n    pub fn max_records(&self) -> usize {\n        self.max_records\n    }\n\n    /// Clear all recorded events (for reset/testing).\n    pub fn clear(&mut self) {\n        self.harvest_ledger = HarvestLedger::new(self.max_records);\n        self.outcome_tokens.clear();\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII report — human-readable summary of the current telemetry state.\n    pub fn ascii_report(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::from("=== Kernel Telemetry Report ===\\n");\n\n        out.push_str(&format!("Events recorded: {}\\n", self.event_count()));\n\n        let report = self.harvest_ledger.report();\n        out.push_str(&format!(\n            "  Success rate: {:.2}%\\n",\n            report.success_rate * 100.0\n        ));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  EV score: {:.4}\\n", report.ev_score));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Avg value: {:.4}\\n", report.avg_value));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Avg cost: {:.4}\\n", report.avg_cost));\n\n        if !self.outcome_tokens.is_empty() {\n            let tokens: Vec<&str> = self.outcome_tokens.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n            let surface = surface_recurring_patterns(&tokens, 3);\n            if !surface.top.is_empty() {\n                out.push_str("\\nTop recurring patterns:\\n");\n                for (tri, count) in &surface.top {\n                    out.push_str(&format!("  {:?} × {}\\n", tri, count));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        out.push_str("\\n=== End Report ===\\n");\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// Glyph report — the value series rendered as a sparkline (Phase C/F:\n    /// numeric telemetry series render via pixel glyphs, not raw ASCII).\n    pub fn glyph_report(&self) -> String {\n        let series = self.harvest_ledger.value_series();\n        if series.is_empty() {\n            return String::from("(no telemetry events)");\n        }\n        let spark = crate::glyph_dashboard::render_sparkline(&series);\n        format!("value sparkline: {spark}")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default TelemetryAggregator::new(100);\n        agg.record_event("test-model", "test-task", true, 1.0, 0.5, "success", 0);\n        assert_eq!(agg.event_count(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn glyph_report_empty_and_nonempty() {\n        let agg = TelemetryAggregator::new(100);\n        assert_eq!(agg.glyph_report(), "(no telemetry events)");\n\n        let mut agg2 = agg2.glyph_report();\n        assert!(g.contains("value sparkline:"));\n        assert!(g.chars().any(|c| ('\\u{2581}'..='\\u{2588}').contains(&c)));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn snapshot_contains_harvest_report() {\n        let mut agg = TelemetryAggregator::new(100);\n        agg.record_event("m", "t", true, 2.0, 1.0, "ok", 0);\n        agg.record_event("m", "t", false, 0.0, 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/academy_store.rs	academy_store · 148 lines	//! Academy internal store for Hydra.\n//!\n//! Each Hydra organism owns a local append-only academy journal and a\n//! searchable view over shared Academia entries. Every append is logged\n//! with full metadata; every read is deterministic.\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AcademyEntry {\n    pub ts_ns: u64,\n    pub cycle: u64,\n    pub actor: [u8; 32],\n    pub title: String,\n    pub source: String,\n    pub tags: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct AcademyStore {\n    pub entries: Vec<AcademyEntry>,\n    pub search_index: BTreeMap<String, Vec<usize>>,\n}\n\nimpl AcademyStore {\n    /// Append a new record to the journal.\n    pub fn append(\n        &mut self,\n        cycle: u64,\n        actor: [u8; 32],\n        title: impl Into<String>,\n        source: impl Into<String>,\n        tags: Vec<String>,\n    ) -> usize {\n        let entry = AcademyEntry {\n            ts_ns: 0,\n            cycle,\n            actor,\n            title: title.into(),\n            source: source.into(),\n            tags,\n        };\n        let idx = self.entries.len();\n        self.entries.push(entry);\n        self.reindex(idx);\n        idx\n    }\n\n    fn reindex(&mut self, idx: usize) {\n        let entry = &self.entries[idx];\n        let norm = entry.title.to_lowercase();\n        self.search_index.entry(norm).or_default().push(idx);\n    }\n\n    /// Search local journal by title substring. Returns matched indices.\n    pub fn search(&self, query: &str) -> Vec<usize> {\n        let q = query.to_lowercase();\n        self.search_index\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|(key, idxs)| {\n                if key.contains(&q) {\n                    Some(idxs.clone())\n                } else {\n                    None\n                }\n            })\n            .flatten()\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Get an entry by index.\n    pub fn get(&self, idx: usize) -> Option<&AcademyEntry> {\n        self.entries.get(idx)\n    }\n\n    /// Total entries.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.entries.len()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Serialize academy entries to a deterministic JSONL blob (one record per line,\n/// escaped via [`json_escape`] and the [`crate::hex_util::encode`] actor hex). Pure —\n/// the kernel shim's `journal_write` appends this to a file via the vfs seam.\npub fn journal_to_jsonl(entries: &[AcademyEntry]) -> String {\n    let mut buf = String::new();\n    for entry in entries {\n        buf.push_str(&format!(\n            "{{\\"ts_ns\\":{},\\"cycle\\":{},\\"actor\\":\\"{}\\",\\"title\\":\\"{}\\",\\"source\\":\\"{}\\",\\"tags\\":{:?}}}\\n",\n            entry.ts_ns,\n            entry.cycle,\n            crate::hex_util::encode(&entry.actor),\n            json_escape(&entry.title),\n            json_escape(&entry.source),\n            entry.tags\n        ));\n    }\n    buf\n}\n\n/// Helper to escape JSON strings manually. Order is load-bearing: the backslash\n/// is escaped FIRST so the subsequent `"` / control-char escapes are not\n/// themselves re-escaped. Escapes `"` as well — a JSON string without the quote\n/// escape is invalid and would corrupt the journal line.\nfn json_escape(s: &str) -> String {\n    s.replace('\\\\', "\\\\\\\\")\n        .replace('"', "\\\\\\"")\n        .replace('\\n', "\\\\n")\n        .replace('\\r', "\\\\r")\n        .replace('\\t', "\\\\t")\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn append_then_search_is_case_insensitive_substring() {\n        let mut store = AcademyStore::default();\n        store.append(0, [0u8; 32], "Quantum Lattice Theory", "arxiv", vec![]);\n        store.append(1, [1u8; 32], "Crystal Diffraction", "arxiv", vec![]);\n        assert_eq!(store.len(), 2);\n        // Lowercased index → case-insensitive substring match.\n        assert_eq!(store.search("lattice"), vec![0]);\n        assert_eq!(store.search("CRYSTAL"), vec![1]);\n        assert_eq!(store.search("diff"), vec![1]);\n        assert!(store.search("missing").is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(store.get(0).unwrap().title, "Quantum Lattice Theory");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn journal_to_jsonl_escapes_and_serializes() {\n        let entries = vec![AcademyEntry {\n            ts_ns: 1,\n            cycle: 0,\n            actor: [0xAB; 32],\n            title: "Title \\"quoted\\"\\nline".into(),\n            source: "src".into(),\n            tags: vec!["a".into()],\n        }];\n        let text = journal_to_jsonl(&entries);\n        assert!(text.contains("\\"actor\\":\\""), "actor hex must be present");\n        assert!(text.contains("Title \\\\\\"quoted\\\\\\""), "title JSON-escaped");\n        assert!(text.contains("\\\\nline"), "newline escaped");\n    }\n}\n	11423	-1	-1		cb96b753a598b0213263c683f02bdb1d08dea7f4e9704782c9ff6e0b03b82ff7995726285ec806da964672735cd7b53dec39d5b4796d24f9eacae25cc72eb86e2c84552b053b8245d401280037bb63d971f9e40a69fbfb496c242886295f95a9a306b702bec051f9b9994aa7f6cc5ab764b641aad78060e29f6934bb6d26be30
```

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/token_bucket.rs	token_bucket · 282 lines	//! `token_bucket.rs` — P11 §4 / F33 compute-budget primitive (pure no_std core).\n//!\n//! The *pure* half: the integer GCRA decision package ([`gcra_decide`]), the lock-free\n//! [`GcraTokenBucket`] (single `AtomicU64` TAT), and the monotonic [`TokenBucket`]\n//! (a [`SpinLock<Inner>`] of `tokens: f64` + `last_refill_ns`, with `now_ns` injected).\n//! NO `std` anywhere.\n//!\n//! The std side — stamping `now_ns` from the host's monotonic clock — lives in the kernel\n//! shim, which re-exports these types and adds [`crate::clock::now_ns()`]-stamping free\n//! functions (`token_bucket_try_acquire` / `token_bucket_available` / `gcra_*`).\n//!\n//! Poisoning (A6, fail-closed): the core [`SpinLock`] poisons only when a holder panics\n//! while the lock is held (test builds). On a poisoned lock, `try_acquire`/`available`\n//! degrade-closed (return `false`/`0.0`) rather than cascading the panic — the same\n//! no-cascade guarantee as the old `Mutex` + `into_inner` recovery, but *refuse* instead\n//! of *recover* (safe for a rate limiter: never grant from possibly-inconsistent state).\n//!\n//! Scope limit of the GCRA swap (verified, not assumed): valid ONLY for `refill_rate > 0.0`.\n//! At `refill_rate <= 0.0` `GcraTokenBucket` grants exactly once, ever — callers using\n//! `TokenBucket::new(_, 0.0)` as a drain-to-zero budget must keep using [`TokenBucket`].\n\nuse crate::autonomic::BoundedRate;\nuse crate::spinlock::SpinLock;\nuse core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n\n/// Pure GCRA (Generic Cell Rate Algorithm) transition — item 8's decision package.\n///\n/// `now_ns`/`tat_ns` are nanoseconds on some fixed monotonic base; `cost_ns` is this request's\n/// cost; `burst_ns` is the burst allowance. Returns the new TAT to store on grant, `None` on\n/// deny. Total (never panics) and degrade-closed: any addition that would overflow `u64` is\n/// treated as "exceeds the burst limit" (`None`) via `checked_add`.\npub fn gcra_decide(now_ns: u64, tat_ns: u64, cost_ns: u64, burst_ns: u64) -> Option<u64> {\n    let allow_at = tat_ns.max(now_ns);\n    let new_tat = allow_at.checked_add(cost_ns)?;\n    let limit = now_ns.checked_add(burst_ns)?;\n    (new_tat <= limit).then_some(new_tat)\n}\n\n/// Lock-free GCRA token bucket — a single `AtomicU64` holds the theoretical-arrival-time (TAT).\n/// The clock read happens OUTSIDE the CAS loop, so only the tiny integer CAS serializes under\n/// contention. `now_ns` is injected by the caller (the kernel shim stamps\n/// `crate::clock::now_ns()`), keeping this type `no_std`.\npub struct GcraTokenBucket {\n    /// Nanoseconds per token, computed ONCE here — never re-derived inside the CAS loop.\n    nanos_per_token: f64,\n    /// Burst allowance in nanoseconds (`capacity * nanos_per_token`, saturating to `u64::MAX`).\n    burst_nanos: u64,\n    tat: AtomicU64,\n}\n\nimpl GcraTokenBucket {\n    /// Create a full bucket. `capacity` caps the burst; `refill_rate` is tokens/second and MUST\n    /// be `> 0.0` for GCRA-equivalent semantics (see the module doc's scope limit).\n    pub fn new(capacity: f64, refill_rate: f64) -> Self {\n        let nanos_per_token = if refill_rate > 0.0 {\n            1e9 / refill_rate\n        } else {\n            f64::INFINITY\n        };\n        let burst_nanos = (capacity * nanos_per_token) as u64; // saturating f64->u64 cast\n        GcraTokenBucket {\n            nanos_per_token,\n            burst_nanos,\n            tat: AtomicU64::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Grant iff the pure [`gcra_decide`] transition allows it; CAS-retries on contention.\n    /// `now_ns` is the current monotonic nanosecond timestamp (injected by the caller).\n    pub fn try_acquire(&self, n: f64, now_ns: u64) -> bool {\n        let cost_ns = (n * self.nanos_per_token) as u64;\n        loop {\n            let tat = self.tat.load(Ordering::Relaxed);\n            match gcra_decide(now_ns, tat, cost_ns, self.burst_nanos) {\n                None => return false,\n                Some(new_tat) => {\n                    match self\n                        .tat\n                        .compare_exchange_weak(tat, new_tat, Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed)\n                    {\n                        Ok(_) => return true,\n                        Err(_) => continue,\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Current available token budget (derived from the TAT, no stored token count to refill).\n    pub fn available(&self, now_ns: u64) -> f64 {\n        let tat = self.tat.load(Ordering::Relaxed);\n        let spent_ns = tat.saturating_sub(now_ns);\n        let available_ns = self.burst_nanos.saturating_sub(spent_ns);\n        available_ns as f64 / self.nanos_per_token\n    }\n}\n\n/// The refill state of a [`TokenBucket`].\nstruct Inner {\n    tokens: f64,\n    last_refill_ns: u64,\n}\n\n/// A monotonic-clock token bucket. `capacity` caps the burst; `refill_rate` is tokens/second.\n/// `now_ns` (monotonic nanoseconds) is injected by the caller; the kernel shim stamps\n/// `crate::clock::now_ns()`.\npub struct TokenBucket {\n    capacity: f64,\n    refill_rate: f64,\n    inner: SpinLock<Inner>,\n}\n\nimpl TokenBucket {\n    /// Create a full bucket (starts at `capacity` tokens).\n    pub fn new(capacity: f64, refill_rate: f64) -> Self {\n        TokenBucket {\n            capacity,\n            refill_rate,\n            inner: SpinLock::new(Inner {\n                tokens: capacity,\n                last_refill_ns: 0,\n            }),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Lazy monotonic refill: `tokens = min(capacity, tokens + refill_rate * elapsed_secs)`.\n    /// Advances `last_refill_ns` to `now_ns` so sub-unit time is never lost. Underflow clamped\n    /// at 0. On a poisoned lock (a prior holder\n    /// panicked), degrade-closed (`false`) — never a cascade panic (A6).\n    pub fn try_acquire(&self, n: f64, now_ns: u64) -> bool {\n        let mut inner = match self.inner.lock() {\n            Ok(g) => g,\n            Err(_) => return false, // poisoned → degrade-closed\n        };\n        self.refill_locked(&mut inner, now_ns);\n        if inner.tokens >= n {\n            inner.tokens -= n;\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Current available token count (refills lazily first). `0.0` on a poisoned lock (A6).\n    pub fn available(&self, now_ns: u64) -> f64 {\n        let mut inner = match self.inner.lock() {\n            Ok(g) => g,\n            Err(_) => return 0.0, // poisoned → degrade-closed\n        };\n        self.refill_locked(&mut inner, now_ns);\n        inner.tokens\n    }\n\n    /// Item 21: bounded refill-rate reconfiguration. `BoundedRate` is unconstructible outside\n    /// `[MIN, MAX]`, so an out-of-bound rate is inexpressible. Re-fills under the OLD rate up\n    /// to `now_ns`, then installs the NEW rate (holding the lock the whole time so no acquire\n    /// can observe a stale `last_refill_ns` against the new rate). return, // poisoned → no-op\n        };\n        self.refill_locked(&mut inner, now_ns);\n        self.refill_rate = r.get();\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n 100), Some(30));\n        assert_eq!(gcra_decide(0, 30, 30, 100), Some(60));\n        assert_eq!(gcra_decide(0, 60, 30, 100), Some(90));\n        // 4th: 90 + 30 = 120 > 0 + 100 = 100 → deny.\n ([`BoundedRate::from_f64`]) or reject ([`BoundedRate::try_from_f64`]), so an\n//! out-of-bound rate is *inexpressible* — not merely avoided.\n//!\n//! Also the pure control-law half: the gain-scheduling table [`LAW_TABLE`],\n//! [`Adjustment`], the pure-data [`FdrAdjustment`], and the pure [`schedule`] /\n//! [`schedule_into_breaker`] functions. The std FDR serialization side\n//! An\n    /// out-of-bound input is brought back into `[MIN, MAX]`, so the over-grant\n    /// invariant can never be broken by an adjustment equation.\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn from_f64(v: f64) -> Self {\n        let v = if v.is_nan() {\n            BOUND_MIN\n        } else if v < BOUND_MIN {\n            BOUND_MIN\n        } else if v > BOUND_MAX {\n            BOUND_MAX\n        } else {\n            v\n        };\n        debug_assert!(v >= BOUND_MIN && v <= BOUND_MAX, "BoundedRate clamp broke");\n        BoundedRate { value: v }\n    }\n\n    /// Rejecting constructor — returns `None` iff `v` is outside `[MIN, MAX]` or NaN.\n    /// The public fallible entry point and the proof surface for the planted-fault\n    /// self-test: an unsafe law that would produce an out-of-bound rate is *rejected*.\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn try_from_f64(v: f64) -> Option<Self> {\n        if v < BOUND_MIN || v > BOUND_MAX || v.is_nan() {\n            None\n        } else {\n            Some(BoundedRate { value: v })\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The rate as a raw `f64`. Always within `[MIN, MAX]` (the invariant).\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn get(self) -> f64 {\n        self.value\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn bounds_are_inclusive() {\n        assert!(BoundedRate::try_from_f64(BoundedRate::MIN).is_some());\n        assert!(BoundedRate::try_from_f64(BoundedRate::MAX).is_some());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn try_from_rejects_out_of_bound_and_nan() {\n        assert!(BoundedRate::try_from_f64(BoundedRate::MAX + 1.0).is_none());\n        assert!(BoundedRate::try_from_f64(BoundedRate::MIN - 1.0).is_none());\n        assert!(BoundedRate::try_from_f64(f64::NAN).is_none());\n        assert!(BoundedRate::try_from_f64(f64::INFINITY).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn from_f64_clamps() {\n        assert_eq!(BoundedRate::from_f64(1e9).get(), BoundedRate::MAX);\n        assert_eq!(BoundedRate::from_f64(-1e9).get(), BoundedRate::MIN);\n        assert_eq!(BoundedRate::from_f64(f64::NAN).get(), BoundedRate::MIN);\n        assert_eq!(BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0).get(), 50.0);\n    }\n\n\n\n    use crate::breaker::{fit_from_rates, BreakerState, cooldown_base: 8,\n            cooldown_cap: 1024,\n        };\n        let w = SignalWeights {\n            conf: 1.0,\n            drift: 1.0,\n            cusum: 1.0,\n            constraint: 1.0,\n            disagreement: 1.0,\n            truth: 1.0,\n        };\n        let mut rates: Vec<(f32, bool)> = Vec::new();\n        for i in 0..20 {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 50.0, false));\n        }\n        for i in 20..40 {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 40.0, true));\n        }\n        fit_from_rates(&rates, 0.05, p, w).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// All 9 (DriftClass × Verdict) combos, in table order, for the oracles.\n    fn all_combos() -> [(DriftClass, Verdict); 9] {\n        [\n            (DriftClass::Damped, Verdict::Healthy),\n            (DriftClass::Damped, Verdict::LimitCycle),\n            (DriftClass::Damped, Verdict::StrangeAttractor),\n            (DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::Healthy),\n            (DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::LimitCycle),\n (DriftClass::Unstable, Verdict::StrangeAttractor),\n        ]\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn exhaustive_oracle_all_nine_combos_match_law_table() {\n        // Headline property: schedule produces the          let row = LAW_TABLE\n                .iter()\n                .find(|r| r.0 == class && r.1 == verdict)\n                .unwrap();\n            let expected_rate = "rate mismatch for {:?}/{:?}",\n                class, verdict\n            );\n            assert_eq!(\n                fdr.tag, row.2.tag,\n                "tag mismatch for {:?}/{:?}",\n We replay the same stream twice and assert\n        // the control outputs are identical.\n        let stream = [\n            (DriftClass::Damped, Verdict::Healthy),\n Verdict::StrangeAttractor),\n        ];\n        let run = |start: BoundedRate| -> Vec<(f64, &'static str, bool)> {\n            let mut rate = start;\n            let mut out = Vec::new();\n            for &(c, v) in stream.iter() {\n                let (next, fdr) = schedule(c, v, rate);\n                out.push((next.get(), fdr.tag, fdr.route_to_breaker));\n                rate = next;\n            }\n            out\n        };\n        let a = run(BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0));\n        let b = run(BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0));\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "replayed classification stream must 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/retrieval/index.rs	index · 221 lines	//! Deterministic trigram inverted index + exact verify (M1 / L0).\n//!\n//! Byte-level 3-grams (not char-level) so indexing is deterministic over UTF-8\n//! and cheap to hash/compare. Living-memory note names are ASCII, so byte\n//! trigrams are exact.\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A 3-byte key. `[u8;3]` is `Copy` + `Hash` + `Ord` ⇒ deterministic map keys.\npub type Trigram = [u8; 3];\n\n/// All trigrams of `s` (contiguous byte windows of length 3).\n/// Empty if `s.len() < 3`.\npub fn trigrams(s: &str) -> Vec<Trigram> {\n    let b = s.as_bytes();\n    if b.len() < 3 {\n        return Vec::new();\n    }\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(b.len() - 2);\n    for w in 0..b.len() - 2 {\n        out.push([b[w], b[w + 1], b[w + 2]]);\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Extract candidate trigrams from a *restricted wildcard pattern* by pulling\n/// literal runs of length ≥ 3. Metacharacters (`* + ? ( ) [ ] { } | ^ $ . \\`)\n/// end a run (a conservative superset — any meta byte terminates a run), so only\n/// guaranteed-literal bytes become index keys. A doc must contain ALL returned\n/// trigrams to possibly match ⇒ the candidate set is a safe superset of the\n/// true matches (verify prunes the rest → 0 false positives).\npub fn literal_trigrams(pattern: &str) -> Vec<Trigram> {\n    let b = pattern.as_bytes();\n    let mut runs: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::new();\n    let mut cur: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();\n    for &c in b {\n        let is_meta = matches!(\n            c,\n            b'*' | b'+'\n                | b'?'\n                | b'('\n                | b')'\n                | b'['\n                | b']'\n                | b'{'\n                | b'}'\n                | b'|'\n                | b'^'\n                | b'$'\n                | b'.'\n                | b'\\\\'\n        );\n        if is_meta {\n            if !cur.is_empty() {\n                runs.push(core::mem::take(&mut cur));\n            }\n        } else {\n            cur.push(c);\n        }\n    }\n    if !cur.is_empty() {\n        runs.push(cur);\n    }\n    let mut out: Vec<Trigram> = Vec::new();\n    for run in &runs {\n        if run.len() >= 3 {\n            for w in 0..run.len() - 2 {\n                out.push([run[w], run[w + 1], run[w + 2]]);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out.sort_unstable();\n    out.dedup();\n    out\n}\n\n/// Deterministic trigram inverted index over a corpus of `&str` documents.\n///\n/// Postings are literal-keyed and store **unique, sorted** doc-ids per trigram.\n/// No Bloom filter, no compression ⇒ bitwise reproducibility (blueprint §3).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TrigramIndex {\n    docs: Vec<String>,\n    /// trigram -> sorted-unique doc-ids that contain it.\n    postings: BTreeMap<Trigram, Vec<u32>>,\n}\n\nimpl TrigramIndex {\n    /// Build the index over `docs` (doc-id = position in `docs`).\n    pub fn new(docs: &[&str]) -> Self {\n        let mut postings: BTreeMap<Trigram, Vec<u32>> = BTreeMap::new();\n        for (id, doc) in docs.iter().enumerate() {\n            let id = id as u32;\n            let mut seen = trigrams(doc);\n            seen.sort_unstable();\n            seen.dedup();\n            for t in seen {\n                postings.entry(t).or_default().push(id);\n            }\n        }\n        // Dedupe + sort each posting list → literal-keyed determinism.\n        for v in postings.values_mut() {\n            v.sort_unstable();\n            v.dedup();\n        }\n        TrigramIndex {\n            docs: docs.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),\n            postings,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Incremental `add_document` (P95 §3.2) — append ONE doc's trigrams to the\n    /// inverted postings, appending the doc text and keeping each posting list\n    /// sorted+unique. doc-id = current `len()` (monotonic, decoupled from filename,\n    /// P95 §3.5). Byte-identical to `new` over the same ingestion sequence: postings\n    /// are built per-doc then sorted+dedup'd, same as the constructor.\n    pub fn add_document(&mut self, doc: &str) -> u32 {\n        let id = self.docs.len() as u32;\n        let mut seen = trigrams(doc);\n        seen.sort_unstable();\n        seen.dedup();\n        for t in seen {\n            let post = self.postings.entry(t).or_default();\n            post.push(id);\n        }\n        for v in self.postings.values_mut() {\n            v.sort_unstable();\n            v.dedup();\n        }\n        self.docs.push(doc.to_string());\n        id\n    }\n\n    /// Number of documents in the corpus.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.docs.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Read-only access to the stored document strings (used by persistence to\n    /// re-serialize the corpus deterministically, P95 §3.1).\n    pub fn docs(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {\n        self.docs.iter().map(|s| s.as_str())\n    }\n\n    /// Number of distinct trigrams indexed (the literal-keyed posting count).\n    pub fn postings_len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.postings.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Candidates = docs containing ALL `trigs` (set intersection).\n    /// * empty trigram set ⇒ all docs (no reduction possible);\n    /// * a missing trigram ⇒ zero candidates (match impossible).\n    ///\n    /// Counting is order-independent ⇒ bitwise-deterministic regardless of\n    /// BTreeMap iteration order.\n    fn candidates(&self, trigs: &[Trigram]) -> Vec<u32> {\n        if trigs.is_empty() {\n            return (0..self.docs.len() as u32).collect();\n        }\n        let mut counts: BTreeMap<u32, u32> = BTreeMap::new();\n        for t in trigs {\n            match self.postings.get(t) {\n                None => return Vec::new(),\n                Some(post) => {\n                    for &d in post {\n                        *counts.entry(d).or_insert(0) += 1;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        let k = trigs.len() as u32;\n        let mut cand: Vec<u32> = counts\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|(_, c)| *c == k)\n            .map(|(d, _)| d)\n            .collect();\n        cand.sort_unstable();\n        cand\n    }\n\n    /// Exact literal substring query. (commit 2/3); the crate is removed last (commit 3/3).\n//! 5. **Terminal state (a) — removed outright.** Not opt-in (a feature flag\n//!    would preserve a dead API for zero callers); a pattern matcher is not a\n//!    syscall/wire/ABI boundary.\n//!\n//! # Pattern language (a CLOSED contract — degrade-closed)\n//!\n//! - **literal byte** — matches that exact byte;\n//! - **`.`** — matches any single byte;\n//! - **`.*`** — matches any gap (the only quantifier, only as this two-byte\n//!   token: an unbounded run of any bytes, including empty).\n//!\n//! Any other metacharacter (`* + ? ( ) [ ] { } | ^ $ \\`, and a bare `*` not\n//! forming `.*`) is a **loud, typed rejection** at compile time\n//! (`PatternError::UnsupportedMeta { byte, pos }`) — parse-then-match, never a\n//! silent wrong answer (`arena.rs` degrade-closed discipline).\n//!\n//! # Semantics\n//!\n//! Unanchored **contains-match**, bit-identical to `regex::Regex::is_match`\n//! restricted to this subset **over the module's domain** (ASCII note names, no\n//! newlines — `fixtures.rs`). ONE deliberate divergence from `regex`'s default:\n//! this matcher's `.` matches any single byte *including* `\\n`, whereas\n//! `regex`'s default `.` excludes `\\n`. The two coincide exactly on newline-free\n//! input, which is the entire real domain (note names never contain newlines);\n//! the parity suite therefore proves equality over newline-free ASCII corpora,\n//! and the property is asserted (not assumed) by the differential tests below.\n//!\n//! # Algorithm (no backtracking exists ⇒ no pathological blowup)\n//!\n//! The pattern splits into fixed-length *segments* at `.*` boundaries (each\n//! segment is a run of `Lit`/`Any` atoms; leading/trailing/adjacent `.*` yield\n//! empty boundary segments, which are match-neutral for a contains-match). A\n//! match is a greedy left-to-right leftmost placement of each segment at-or-after\n//! the previous segment's end. Correctness rests on the classic glob lemma: with\n//! no nested quantifiers and every gap unbounded, placing each segment as early\n//! as possible never precludes a later match (exchange argument), so greedy\n//! leftmost is exact and **no backtracking is possible**. Nothing else reopens\n//! it.\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse core::fmt;\n\n/// A pattern used a metacharacter outside the supported subset\n/// {literal byte, `.`, `.*`}. Degrade-closed: the matcher NEVER guesses a\n/// meaning for an unsupported token — it rejects at compile time.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum PatternError {\n    /// An unsupported metacharacter `byte` appeared at byte offset `pos`.\n    UnsupportedMeta { byte: u8, pos: usize },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for PatternError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            PatternError::UnsupportedMeta { byte, pos } => write!(\n                f,\n                "unsupported pattern metacharacter {:?} (0x{:02x}) at byte {}; \\\n                 supported subset is {{literal, '.', '.*'}}",\n                *byte as char, byte, pos\n            ),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl core::error::Error for PatternError {}\n\n/// A single fixed-width match atom within a segment.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\nenum Atom {\n    /// A literal byte that must match exactly.\n    Lit(u8),\n    /// `.` — matches any single byte (see module doc on the newline caveat).\n    Any,\n}\n\n/// A compiled restricted pattern: fixed-length segments separated by `.*` gaps.\n/// `is_match` is an UNANCHORED contains-match.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Pattern {\n    /// Fixed-length segments in order; adjacent segments are joined by an\n    /// unbounded `.*` gap. Leading/trailing/adjacent `.*` produce empty boundary\n    /// segments, which impose no constraint for a contains-match.\n    segments: Vec<Vec<Atom>>,\n}\n\nimpl Pattern {\n    /// Parse `pattern` into segments, rejecting any unsupported metacharacter.\n    /// Byte-oriented, to match the byte-level trigram index (ASCII note names by\n    /// module contract).\n    pub fn compile(pattern: &str) -> Result<Pattern, PatternError> {\n        let b = pattern.as_bytes();\n        let mut segments: Vec<Vec<Atom>> = Vec::new();\n        let mut cur: Vec<Atom> = Vec::new();\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i < b.len() {\n            match b[i] {\n                // `.` immediately followed by `*` is the gap token `.*`;\n                // otherwise a single any-byte atom.\n                b'.' => {\n                    if i + 1 < b.len() && b[i + 1] == b'*' {\n                        segments.push(core::mem::take(&mut cur));\n                        i += 2;\n                    } else {\n                        cur.push(Atom::Any);\n                        i += 1;\n                    }\n                }\n                // Every other metacharacter — including a bare `*` (only `.*` is\n                // allowed) — is a hard, typed rejection.\n                b'*' | b'+' | b'?' | b'(' | b')' | b'[' | b']' | b'{' | b'}' | b'|' | b'^'\n                | b'$' | b'\\\\' => {\n                    return Err(PatternError::UnsupportedMeta { byte: b[i], pos: i });\n                }\n                c => {\n                    cur.push(Atom::Lit(c));\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        segments.push(cur);\n        Ok(Pattern { segments })\n    }\n\n    /// UNANCHORED contains-match: does `doc` contain a substring matched by this\n    /// pattern? Greedy leftmost placement of each segment after the previous\n    /// segment's end. No backtracking exists (the only quantifier is the\n    /// unbounded `.*` gap and segments are fixed-length).\n    pub fn is_match(&self, doc: &str) -> bool {\n        let hay = doc.as_bytes();\n        // Leftmost feasible start for the next segment. The unanchored head lets\n        // the first segment start anywhere; the unanchored tail lets the last\n        // segment end anywhere; each `.*` gap allows any run (including empty)\n        // between adjacent segments.\n        let mut from = 0usize;\n        for seg in &self.segments {\n            if seg.is_empty() {\n                // Empty boundary segment (leading/trailing/adjacent `.*`) — no\n                // constraint; `from` is unchanged.\n                continue;\n            }\n            match find_segment(hay, seg, from) {\n                Some(end) => from = end,\n                None => return false,\n            }\n        }\n        true\n    }\n}\n\n/// Leftmost occurrence of the fixed-length `seg` in `hay[from..]`; returns the\n/// index one past the match end, or `None`. `Lit` atoms match exactly, `Any`\n/// atoms match any byte. `seg` is non-empty (callers skip empty segments).\nfn find_segment(hay: &[u8], seg: &[Atom], from: usize) -> Option<usize> {\n    let n = seg.len();\n    // `None` when the segment is longer than what remains anywhere in `hay`.\n    let last_start = hay.len().checked_sub(n)?;\n    let mut start = from;\n    while start <= last_start {\n        let hit = seg\n            .iter()\n            .zip(&hay[start..start + n])\n            .all(|(atom, &c)| match atom {\n                Atom::Lit(l) => c == *l,\n historical pattern.\n    const BATTERY: &[&str] = &[\n        "",\n        ".*",\n        ".*.*",\n        "note",\n        "md", // <3 bytes ⇒ no-trigram fallback (all-docs scan) path\n        ".",\n PatternError> {\n        let b = pattern.as_bytes();\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i < b.len() {\n            match b[i] {\n                b'.' => {\n ("(ab)", b'(', 0),\n            ("a|b", b'|', 1),\n            ("[ab]", b'[', 0),\n            ("a{2}", b'{', 1),\n            ("^ab", b'^', 0),\n            ("ab$", b'$', 2),\n            ("a\\\\.b", 0u64;\n        for _ in 0..4000 {\n            // Build a subset pattern from {literal a/b/-, '.', '.*'}.\n            let plen = (rng() % 7) as usize;\n            let mut pat = String::new();\n            for _ in 0..plen {\n                match rng() % 5 {\n                    0 => pat.push('a'),\n                    1 => pat.push('b'),\n                    2 => pat.push('-'),\n                    3 => pat.push('.'),\n                    _ => pat.push_str(".*"),\n                }\n            }\n            // Guard: a trailing lone '.' that becomes '.<end>' is fine; a bare\n            // '*' can never be produced by this generator (only ".*" adds '*').\n            let compiled = match Pattern::compile(&pat) {\n                Ok(c) => c,\n                Err(_) => continue, // generator never emits an unsupported meta\n            };\n            let dlen = (rng() % 12) as usize;\n            let mut doc = String::new();\n            for _ in 0..dlen {\n                doc.push(alpha[(rng() % 3) as usize] as char); // a/b/- only in docs\n            }\n            let hr = compiled.is_match(&doc);\n            let nv = naive_ref_is_match(&pat, &doc).expect("subset compiles");\n            assert_eq!(hr, nv, "pattern={:?} doc={:?}", pat, doc);\n            checked += 1;\n        }\n        assert!(\n            checked > 3000,\n            "sweep must exercise most iterations (got {checked})"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── Frozen golden: the incumbent's verdict on the historical pattern ──────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn golden_seam_verdict_frozen_from_regex_incumbent() {\n        // `note-.*-recall` matched exactly doc 7 ("note-heat-kernel-recall.md")\n        // under the retired `regex` crate. Frozen here as the permanent golden\n        // (items-4+29 "byte-compatible" analogue): the hand-rolled seam must\n        // reproduce the incumbent's verdict forever.\n        let idx = TrigramIndex::new(FIXTURE);\n        assert_eq!(idx.query_pattern("note-.*-recall").unwrap(), vec![7]);\n        // 0 false positives at the seam over the whole fixture.\n        let compiled = Pattern::compile("note-.*-recall").unwrap();\n        let oracle: Vec<u32> = FIXTURE\n            .iter()\n            .enumerate()\n            .filter(|(_, d)| compiled.is_match(d))\n            .map(|(i, _)| i as u32)\n            .collect();\n        assert_eq!(idx.query_pattern("note-.*-recall").unwrap(), oracle);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn seam_query_pattern_equals_linear_matcher_oracle_over_synthetic() {\n        // query_pattern (trigram-narrowed + verify) must equal a brute-force\n        // linear scan with the SAME matcher over a 2000-doc corpus, for every\n        // battery pattern (proves trigram narrowing never drops a true match).\n        let corpus = synthetic_corpus(2000);\n        let docs: Vec<&str> = corpus.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n        let idx = TrigramIndex::new(&docs);\n        for p in BATTERY {\n            let compiled = Pattern::compile(p).unwrap();\n            let oracle: Vec<u32> = docs\n                .iter()\n                .enumerate()\n                .filter(|(_, d)| compiled.is_match(d))\n                .map(|(i, _)| i as u32)\n                .collect();\n            assert_eq!(idx.query_pattern(p).unwrap(), oracle, "pattern {:?}", p);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── Post-removal differential: hand-rolled vs the independent naive\n    //    reference (proptest). Before commit 3/3 an identical battery ran against\n    //    the live `regex` crate (bit-identical over the newline-free ASCII\n    //    domain); that oracle retired WITH the crate, its verdicts preserved by\n    //    the frozen golden above. Two independent implementations must agree\n    //    forever.\n\n    proptest::proptest! {\n        /// Property-based differential vs the independent naive reference — the\n        /// permanent post-removal cross-check (kept when the regex block is cut).\n        #[test]\n        fn prop_parity_vs_naive_reference(\n            pat in subset_pattern_strategy(),\n            doc in "[a-z0-9-]{0,40}",\n        ) {\n            let compiled = Pattern::compile(&pat).unwrap();\n            let nv = naive_ref_is_match(&pat, &doc).unwrap();\n            proptest::prop_assert_eq!(compiled.is_match(&doc), nv);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Strategy for a valid subset pattern: 0..=6 tokens, each a single literal\n    /// char from `[a-z0-9-]`, `.`, or `.*`.
