4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/retrieval/spine.rs	spine · 871 lines	//! Knowledge-spine validator + MAP.md generator (W3-3 / P1).\n//!\n//! A hand-rolled, dependency-free frontmatter parser for living-knowledge\n//! markdown docs. No yaml crate: we only need the *flat* key→value subset that\n//! our spine documents emit (`title`, `id`, `tags`, ...). Deterministic: same\n//! bytes ⇒ same parsed map + same MAP.md output (blueprint §3).\n//!\n//! This organ lives in the retrieval layer (sibling to `bm25`/`recall`) and is\n//! the P1 seed of the knowledge-spine retrieval organ — a MAP.md index over the\n//! corpus frontmatter that the BM25/trigram layers can later fuse with. Pure\n//! `std`, no new deps.\n\nuse alloc::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A parsed frontmatter block: flat key → value (both trimmed).\npub type Frontmatter = BTreeMap<String, String>;\n\n/// Structured validation failure. Lists every required key that was absent so\n/// the caller can surface a single, complete error instead of one round-trip\n/// per missing key (fail-closed: a missing key is a hard error, never a warning).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct SpineError {\n    /// Required keys that were missing from the frontmatter.\n    pub missing_keys: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl SpineError {\n    /// Single-sentence human message naming every missing key.\n    pub fn message(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\n            "missing required frontmatter keys: {}",\n            self.missing_keys.join(", ")\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a (possibly frontmatter-bearing) markdown document into its flat\n/// `key → value` frontmatter map plus the remaining body text.\n///\n/// Frontmatter is the **leading** block delimited by an opening `---` line, then\n/// `key: value` lines, then a closing `---` line. Anything after the closing\n/// delimiter is the body. A document with no leading `---` block yields an\n/// empty frontmatter and the **entire** document as body. An opening `---`\n/// without a matching closing `---` is treated as *not* frontmatter (whole doc\n/// is body). Never panics.\npub fn parse_frontmatter(doc: &str) -> (Frontmatter, String) {\n    let mut fm = Frontmatter::new();\n    let mut body = doc.to_string();\n\n    // Use `split('\\n')` (NOT `lines()`) so a trailing newline is preserved as a\n    // final empty element and reconstructable with `join('\\n')` byte-exactly.\n    let lines: Vec<&str> = doc.split('\\n').collect();\n    // Need at least: opening `---`, >=0 kv lines, closing `---`.\n    if lines.is_empty() || lines[0].trim() != "---" {\n        return (fm, body);\n    }\n\n    // Find the *first* closing delimiter after the opening line.\n    let mut close = None;\n    for (i, line) in lines.iter().enumerate().skip(1) {\n        if line.trim() == "---" {\n            close = Some(i);\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    let close = match close {\n        Some(c) => c,\n        None => return (fm, body), // unterminated: treat whole doc as body\n    };\n\n    // Parse `key: value` lines between opening (idx 0) and closing (idx `close`).\n    for line in &lines[1..close] {\n        let line = line.trim();\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            continue; // tolerate blank lines inside the block\n        }\n        if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(':') {\n            let k = k.trim().to_string();\n            let v = v.trim().to_string();\n            if !k.is_empty() {\n                fm.insert(k, v);\n            }\n        }\n        // Lines without a ':' are ignored (lenient — we only need the subset).\n    }\n\n    // Body = everything after the closing delimiter, reconstructed line-wise.\n    body = lines[close + 1..].join("\\n");\n    (fm, body)\n}\n\n/// Validate that `fm` contains every key in `required`.\n/// Returns `Err(SpineError)` listing *all* missing keys (not just the first),\n/// so a single pass reports the complete set of defects.\npub fn validate_frontmatter(fm: &Frontmatter, required: &[&str]) -> Result<(), SpineError> {\n    let missing: Vec<String> = required\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|k| !fm.contains_key(**k))\n        .map(|k| k.to_string())\n        .collect();\n    if missing.is_empty() {\n        Ok(())\n    } else {\n        Err(SpineError {\n            missing_keys: missing,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// A single spine entry: where it lives (`path`) and its parsed frontmatter.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SpineEntry {\n    pub path: String,\n    pub fm: Frontmatter,\n}\n\n/// Escape a markdown table cell: a literal `|` would break column alignment, so\n/// backslash-escape it. Everything else passes through unchanged.\nfn escape_cell(s: &str) -> String {\n    s.replace('|', "\\\\|")\n}\n\n/// Generate a deterministic `MAP.md`-style index over `entries`.\n///\n/// Sorted by `id` (ascending byte order) so the output is reproducible\n/// regardless of input ordering. Each row is `id → title → path`. Entries\n/// without an `id` sort last (stable, never panic). Returns a markdown table.\npub fn generate_map(entries: &[SpineEntry]) -> String {\n    let mut rows: Vec<(&SpineEntry, String)> = entries\n        .iter()\n        .map(|e| {\n            let id = e.fm.get("id").cloned().unwrap_or_default();\n            (e, id)\n        })\n        .collect();\n    // Sort by id ascending; a missing id (empty) sorts after any real id.\n    rows.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        if a.1.is_empty() && b.1.is_empty() {\n            a.0.path.cmp(&b.0.path)\n        } else if a.1.is_empty() {\n            core::cmp::Ordering::Greater\n        } else if b.1.is_empty() {\n            core::cmp::Ordering::Less\n        } else {\n            a.1.cmp(&b.1)\n        }\n    });\n\n    let mut out = String::from("# MAP\\n\\n");\n    out.push_str("| id | title | path |\\n");\n    out.push_str("| --- | --- | --- |\\n");\n    for (e, id) in &rows {\n        let title = e.fm.get("title").map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("");\n        // Cells are space-padded (`| a |`) to match standard Markdown tables.\n        out.push('|');\n        out.push(' ');\n        out.push_str(&escape_cell(&id));\n        out.push(' ');\n        out.push('|');\n        out.push(' ');\n        out.push_str(&escape_cell(title));\n        out.push(' ');\n        out.push('|');\n        out.push(' ');\n        out.push_str(&escape_cell(&e.path));\n        out.push(' ');\n        out.push_str("|\\n");\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n// ===== P2: tag-graph cross-linking =====\n\n/// Parse a raw `tags:` frontmatter value into a de-duplicated, lowercased,\n/// trimmed tag list. Splits on commas, semicolons, and any whitespace; empty\n/// fragments are dropped. Order follows first appearance (stable); callers sort\n/// buckets for byte-exact determinism.\npub fn parse_tags(raw: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n    for frag in raw.split(|c: char| c == ',' || c == ';' || c.is_whitespace()) {\n        let t = frag.trim().to_lowercase();\n        if !t.is_empty() && !out.contains(&t) {\n            out.push(t);\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// P2 — Build a deterministic `tag → [doc-id]` index from frontmatter docs.\n/// Each bucket is sorted ascending (byte order) and de-duplicated, so the map\n/// is reproducible regardless of input ordering.\npub fn tag_index(docs: &[(String, &Frontmatter)]) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> {\n    let mut idx: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> = BTreeMap::new();\n    for (id, fm) in docs {\n        if let Some(raw) = fm.get("tags") {\n            for tag in parse_tags(raw) {\n                idx.entry(tag).or_default().push(id.clone());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    for bucket in idx.values_mut() {\n        bucket.sort();\n        bucket.dedup();\n    }\n    idx\n}\n\n/// P2 — Docs that share ≥1 tag with `id`, sorted ascending, excluding `id` itself.\n/// Cross-references are derived from the `tag_index` buckets that contain `id`.\npub fn backlinks(id: &str, index: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>) -> Vec<String> {\n    // P77 B2: a `BTreeSet` accumulator replaces the O(R) `Vec::contains` dedup\n    // (`:215` in the old impl) so accumulation is O(R) total, not O(R²). Membership\n    // of `id` in a sorted bucket uses `binary_search` (O(log R)) — buckets are\n    // sorted+deduped in `tag_index`/`build`. Result set+order is identical.\n    let mut seen: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();\n    for bucket in index.values() {\n        if bucket.binary_search(&id.to_string()).is_ok() {\n            for other in bucket {\n                if other != id {\n                    seen.insert(other.clone());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    let mut related: Vec<String> = seen.into_iter().collect();\n    related.sort();\n    related\n}\n\n// ===== P3: hierarchical multi-doc MAP aggregation =====\n\n/// P3 — Group docs by their FIRST tag into `## <tag>` sections, each doc listed\n/// as `- [title](path) · id`. Sections (by tag) and docs (by id) are sorted\n/// deterministically; docs with no tag fall under `## (untagged)`. A top\n/// `# Knowledge Map` header precedes the sections. Stable, no trailing-ws drift.\npub fn build_map(docs: &[(String, String, Vec<String>, String)]) -> String {\n    // P77 B2: a `BTreeMap<tag, group-index>` replaces the O(distinct-tags) linear\n    // `groups.iter_mut().find` inside the per-doc loop (`:239` old), so grouping\n    // is O(docs) total instead of O(docs · distinct-tags). Final sort order is\n    // unchanged → byte-identical MAP.md output.\n    let mut groups: Vec<(String, Vec<usize>)> = Vec::new();\n    let mut group_of: BTreeMap<String, usize> = BTreeMap::new();\n    for (i, (_, _, tags, _)) in docs.iter().enumerate() {\n        let tag = tags\n            .first()\n            .cloned()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| "(untagged)".to_string());\n        match group_of.get(&tag) {\n            Some(&g) => groups[g].1.push(i),\n            None => {\n                group_of.insert(tag.clone(), groups.len());\n                groups.push((tag, vec![i]));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    groups.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));\n    for (_, ids) in groups.iter_mut() {\n        ids.sort_by(|&a, &b| docs[a].0.cmp(&docs[b].0));\n    }\n\n    let mut out = String::from("# Knowledge Map\\n\\n");\n    for (tag, ids) in &groups {\n        out.push_str(&format!("## {}\\n", tag));\n        for &i in ids {\n            let (id, title, _, path) = &docs[i];\n            out.push_str(&format!("- [{}]({}) · {}\\n", title, path, id));\n        }\n        out.push('\\n');\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n// ===== P4: query/lookup API over an in-memory index =====\n\n/// P4 — An in-memory knowledge-spine index built once from a corpus, supporting\n/// deterministic id / tag / related lookups. `tags` are a pre-split list; the\n/// index lowercases them for case-insensitive tag queries.\npub struct SpineIndex {\n    docs: Vec<(String, String, Vec<String>, String)>,\n    tag_index: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,\n    /// id → position in `docs`, built once in `SpineIndex::build`. Turns\n    /// `lookup_by_id`/`related`'s O(docs) `docs.iter().find/any` into O(1). Ids\n    /// are unique (doc comment on `lookup_by_id`). (P77 B2.)\n    id_index: BTreeMap<String, usize>,\n}\n\nimpl SpineIndex {\n    /// Build the index from `(id, title, tags, path)` records. Tag buckets are\n    /// sorted + de-duplicated up front so tag lookups are deterministic and\n    /// amortized O(1) via the `BTreeMap`; id lookups use a linear scan\n    /// (`lookup_by_id`, O(n) in the number of docs). Deterministic, not O(1)\n    /// for every access path.\n    pub fn build(docs: Vec<(String, String, Vec<String>, String)>) -> SpineIndex {\n        let mut tag_index: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> = BTreeMap::new();\n        let mut id_index: BTreeMap<String, usize> = BTreeMap::new();\n        for (pos, (id, _, tags, _)) in docs.iter().enumerate() {\n            id_index.insert(id.clone(), pos);\n            for tag in tags {\n                tag_index\n                    .entry(tag.to_lowercase())\n                    .or_default()\n                    .push(id.clone());\n            }\n        }\n        for bucket in tag_index.values_mut() {\n            bucket.sort();\n            bucket.dedup();\n        }\n        SpineIndex {\n            docs,\n            tag_index,\n            id_index,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// P4 — Lookup by exact id. Ids are unique, so this returns a single-element\n    /// `Vec` when found, empty otherwise (uniform `Vec<String>` return shape).\n    pub fn lookup_by_id(&self, id: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n        if self.id_index.contains_key(id) {\n            vec![id.to_string()]\n        } else {\n            Vec::new()\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// P4 — Lookup by tag, case-insensitive against the index. Returns the sorted\n    /// bucket of doc ids sharing that tag.\n    pub fn lookup_by_tag(&self, tag: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n        self.tag_index\n            .get(&tag.to_lowercase())\n            .cloned()\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    /// P4 — `related(id)` == backlinks: every doc sharing ≥1 tag with `id`,\n    /// sorted, excluding `id`. Pure over the in-memory tag index.\n    pub fn related(&self, id: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n        let my_tags: Vec<String> = match self.id_index.get(id) {\n            Some(&pos) => self.docs[pos].2.iter().map(|t| t.to_lowercase()).collect(),\n            None => return Vec::new(),\n        };\n        // P77 B2: `BTreeSet` accumulator replaces the O(R) `!out.contains(other)`\n        // dedup (`:325` old) so accumulation is O(R) total, not O(R²). The result\n        // set+order is identical (sorted ascending, self excluded).\n        let mut seen: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();\n        for tag in &my_tags {\n            if let Some(bucket) = self.tag_index.get(tag) {\n                for other in bucket {\n                    if other != id {\n                        seen.insert(other.clone());\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        let mut out: Vec<String> = seen.into_iter().collect();\n        out.sort();\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn spine_parse_frontmatter() {\n        // RED→GREEN: a doc with a leading frontmatter block must have its keys\n        // parsed into the map and the body cleanly separated after the closing\n        // `---`.\n        let doc =\n            "---\\ntitle: Hello World\\nid: doc-1\\ntags: a, b, c\\n---\\n# Body\\nSome text here.\\n";\n        let (fm, body) = assert_eq!(fm.get("id").map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("doc-1"), "id parsed");\n        assert_eq!(\n            fm.get("tags").map(|s| s.as_str()),\n            Some("a, b, c"),\n            "tags ```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/retrieval/ppr.rs	ppr · 154 lines	//! ppr.rs — Personalized-PageRank (L3) power-iteration engine.\n//!\n//! Reuses the EXACT deterministic accumulation order of `kernel/src/markov.rs`'s\n//! damped-PageRank kernel (its inner `nxt[j] += pii * ((1−α)·W[i][j] …)` loop).\n//! We never touch `markov.rs`; we mirror its proven bitwise-reproducible\n//! left-product so the same f64 ops land in the same sequence. No\n//! eigendecomposition — pure power iteration, the vectorless spectral/relatedness\n//! layer for internal-retrieval M3.\n//!\n//! Determinism proof:\n//!   * FIXED iteration count K (no epsilon, no early-out).\n//!   * FIXED summation order: i (source) outer, j (target) inner — identical to\n//!     `markov.rs`, so floating-point rounding is reproducible.\n//!   * Mass is conserved by the restart (Σ nxt = (1−α)·1 + α·1 = 1), so we drop\n//!     the per-step `÷ sum` normalization that `markov.rs` needs for a stationary\n//!     distribution — removing the only divide and keeping the result bit-exact.\n\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Row-stochastic transition matrix W (n·n), stored as dense `Vec<Vec<f64>>`,\n/// indexed by integer node id. Built by the caller (see `diffusion`).\npub struct Ppr {\n    pub n: usize,\n    w: Vec<Vec<f64>>,\n}\n\nimpl Ppr {\n    /// Wrap a pre-built row-stochastic matrix W (each row sums to 1).\n    pub fn new(w: Vec<Vec<f64>>) -> Self {\n        let n = w.len();\n        Self { n, w }\n    }\n\n    /// Personalized-PageRank from a one-hot seed.\n    ///\n    /// Recurrence (mirrors `markov.rs`: fixed K, fixed summation order):\n    ///   π₀      = e_seed\n    ///   π_{k+1} = (1−α)·(π_k · W)  +  α·e_seed\n    ///\n    /// The diffusion term uses the SAME inner loop as `markov.rs`\n    /// (`nxt[j] += pi[i] * ((1−α)·W[i][j])`, i outer / j inner). The personalized\n    /// restart teleports mass back to the seed node (instead of uniformly to all\n    /// nodes as `markov.rs` does for its stationary distribution).\n    pub fn rank(&self, seed: usize, alpha: f64, k: usize) -> Vec<f64> {\n        assert!(seed < self.n, "seed out of range");\n        let mut pi = vec![0.0f64; self.n];\n        pi[seed] = 1.0;\n        for _ in 0..k {\n            let mut nxt = vec![0.0f64; self.n];\n            // ── SAME accumulation order as markov.rs: i outer, j inner ──\n            for i in 0..self.n {\n                let pii = pi[i];\n                if pii == 0.0 {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                for j in 0..self.n {\n                    nxt[j] += pii * ((1.0 - alpha) * self.w[i][j]);\n                }\n            }\n            // personalized restart at the seed (teleport probability α)\n            for j in 0..self.n {\n                if j == seed {\n                    nxt[j] += alpha;\n                }\n            }\n            pi = nxt;\n        }\n        pi\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn line_graph(n: usize) -> Ppr {\n        // 0—1—2—…—(n-1); each node linked to its neighbours.\n        let mut w = vec![vec![0.0f64; n]; n];\n        for i in 0..n {\n            let mut nb = Vec::new();\n            if i > 0 {\n                nb.push(i - 1);\n            }\n            if i + 1 < n {\n                nb.push(i + 1);\n            }\n            let inv = 1.0 / nb.len() as f64;\n            for &j in &nb {\n                w[i][j] = inv;\n            }\n        }\n        Ppr::new(w)\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_mass_conserved_no_normalize() {\n        // With a (1−α) diffusion + α restart, total mass stays exactly 1 without\n        // any per-step renormalization — the property that buys bitwise determinism.\n        let ppr = line_graph(10);\n        let scores = ppr.rank(0, 0.15, 20);\n        let total: f64 = scores.iter().sum();\n        assert!((total - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12, "mass drift = {}", total - 1.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_ppr_byte_identical_across_runs() {\n        // Two independent runs with identical (K, α, seed) MUST be byte-identical.\n        let ppr = line_graph(20);\n        let a = ppr.rank(3, 0.15, 20);\n        let b = ppr.rank(3, 0.15, 20);\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "PPR is not deterministic across runs");\n        // explicit byte-level check via full-precision formatting\n        let sa: Vec<String> = a.iter().map(|x| format!("{:.17e}", x)).collect();\n        let sb: Vec<String> = b.iter().map(|x| format!("{:.17e}", x)).collect();\n        assert_eq!(sa.join(","), sb.join(","), "PPR byte serialization differs");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ppr_survives_serialize_reread_boundary() {\n        // Hermetic-audit Cause-and-Effect Finding B (quick-win #19): the tests above only ever\n        // compare two live values within the same test-function call stack — they never actually\n        // cross a serialization boundary, so a reproducibility claim wider than that (e.g. "safe to\n        // persist and reload") is unearned. This test writes the score vector to a real file,\n        // re-reads it in a fresh read, re-parses it, and compares against an INDEPENDENTLY fresh\n        // computation (not the cached first `Vec<f64>`) — the actual gap the finding names.\n        let ppr = line_graph(20);\n        let computed = ppr.rank(3, 0.15, 20);\n        let serialized: String = computed\n            .iter()\n            .map(|x| format!("{:.17e}", x))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(",");\n\n        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("ppr_reread_test_{}.txt", std::process::id()));\n        std::fs::write(&path, &serialized).expect("write serialized ppr scores");\n        let reread = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).expect("re-read serialized ppr scores");\n        std::fs::remove_file(&path).ok();\n        assert_eq!(\n            reread, serialized,\n            "byte content did not survive a disk round-trip"\n        );\n\n        let reparsed: Vec<f64> = reread\n            .split(',')\n            .map(|s| s.parse::<f64>().expect("reparse f64"))\n            .collect();\n        let fresh = ppr.rank(3, 0.15, 20); // independently recomputed, not the cached `computed`\n        assert_eq!(\n            reparsed, fresh,\n            "value re-read from disk does not match an independently fresh computation"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	11640	-1	-1		a36cbbff1847afb5a103e2cb9330332d4d5e17a42d52a4826156c85bafeced431dc23183ddc6225ea943422bb18570a886b57c85d168040af129a28f9fb6baced08756bde43bb17913013011d71ba8d2f7f0e83e69f0e641d04028b4d9039194a4a2f747e0cad0e5d9d28cc7434c4918643d442e8783ed8483d8c47261f4a7f0

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/retrieval/diffusion.rs	diffusion · 329 lines	//! diffusion.rs — L3 RELATEDNESS layer (internal-retrieval M3).\n//!\n//! What "related" means here: NOT exact search (that is L0 / M1, the sibling\n//! trigram index). This is the vectorless spectral/relatedness layer — given a\n//! query node, *diffuse* its personalized-PageRank mass over a wikilink graph\n//! and rank neighbours by steady-state score. "What is related to X" falls out\n//! as "which nodes accumulated the most restart+walk mass".\n//!\n//! Engine: `Ppr` (ppr.rs) — a bit-for-bit reuse of `kernel/src/markov.rs`'s\n//! deterministic damped power-iteration (fixed K, fixed summation order, no\n//! eigendecomposition). The wikilink graph is a frozen 20-node / 41-edge\n//! fixture; nodes are named after the same L0 corpus (`fixtures::FIXTURE`) so\n//! the two retrieval layers share one vocabulary.\n//!\n//! Determinism proof lives in `green_ppr_byte_identical_two_runs`: two runs with\n//! identical (seed, α, K) produce byte-identical score vectors.\n\nuse crate::retrieval::fixtures::FIXTURE;\nuse crate::retrieval::ppr::Ppr;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Number of article nodes in the fixture wikilink graph.\npub const N: usize = 20;\n\n/// Query seed node (the "what relates to X?" anchor). Node 0 = "MEMORY.md".\npub const SEED: usize = 0;\n\n/// Restart (teleport) probability — same family as `markov.rs`' DAMPING.\npub const ALPHA: f64 = 0.15;\n\n/// FIXED iteration count — no convergence epsilon, no early-out ⇒ reproducible.\npub const K: usize = 20;\n\n/// Frozen wikilink fixture: 20 nodes, 41 directed edges (article → linked\n/// article). Every node has out-degree ≥ 1 (no dangling sinks). The graph is\n/// intentionally NOT fully connected: nodes {5,6,12,16} sit in a separate\n/// component, so a diffusion from SEED must leave them at exactly score 0 —\n/// the clean "unrelated" baseline the tests assert against.\npub const WIKI_EDGES: &[(usize, usize)] = &[\n    // 0 MEMORY.md\n    (0, 1),\n    (0, 2),\n    (0, 3),\n    (0, 9),\n    // 1 MEMORY-ATTIC.md\n    (1, 0),\n    (1, 9),\n    // 2 note-salience-decay.md\n    (2, 0),\n    (2, 3),\n    (2, 13),\n    // 3 note-wikilink-graph.md\n    (3, 0),\n    (3, 4),\n    (3, 8),\n    (3, 7),\n    // 4 note-pgrust-schema.md\n    (4, 3),\n    (4, 11),\n    (4, 18),\n    // 5 note-trigram-index.md\n    (5, 6),\n    (5, 16),\n    // 6 note-bm25-fusion.md\n    (6, 5),\n    (6, 16),\n    // 7 note-heat-kernel-recall.md\n    (7, 8),\n    (7, 3),\n    // 8 note-pagerank-local-push.md\n    (8, 7),\n    // 9 note-never-delete-tier.md\n    (9, 0),\n    (9, 10),\n    (9, 17),\n    // 10 note-compression-zstd.md\n    (10, 9),\n    (10, 19),\n    // 11 note-vsa-composite-key.md\n    (11, 4),\n    // 12 note-renormalizer-gate.md\n    (12, 13),\n    (12, 16),\n    // 13 note-entropy-ledger.md\n    (13, 2),\n    (13, 14),\n    // 14 note-field-operator.md\n    (14, 13),\n    (14, 15),\n    // 15 note-divergence-signal.md\n    (15, 14),\n    // 16 note-coherence-fusion.md\n    (16, 5),\n    (16, 6),\n    // 17 note-ttrain-deferred.md\n    (17, 9),\n    // 18 note-quantization-pq.md\n    (18, 4),\n    // 19 note-cdc-dedup.md\n    (19, 10),\n];\n\n/// Node labels (mirror `fixtures::FIXTURE` so L0 and L3 share one vocabulary).\npub fn node_labels() -> &'static [&'static str] {\n    FIXTURE\n}\n\n/// Build the row-stochastic transition matrix W from the directed edge list\n/// (each row = uniform over its out-edges, so Σ_j W[i][j] = 1).\npub fn wiki_row_stochastic() -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n    let mut out = vec![vec![0.0f64; N]; N];\n    for &(u, v) in WIKI_EDGES {\n        out[u][v] += 1.0;\n    }\n    for i in 0..N {\n        let s: f64 = out[i].iter().sum();\n        if s > 0.0 {\n            for j in 0..N {\n                out[i][j] /= s;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// The wikilink graph as a ready-to-run PPR engine.\npub fn wiki_ppr() -> Ppr {\n    Ppr::new(wiki_row_stochastic())\n}\n\n/// Relatedness ranking for `seed`: all nodes sorted by PPR score, descending.\n/// Pair = (node_id, score). Includes the seed itself (highest, by construction\n/// of the restart).\npub fn related(seed: usize) -> Vec<(usize, f64)> {\n    let ppr = wiki_ppr();\n    let scores = ppr.rank(seed, ALPHA, K);\n    let mut v: Vec<(usize, f64)> = (0..N).map(|i| (i, scores[i])).collect();\n    v.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.total_cmp(&a.1));\n    v\n}\n\n/// Forward-reachable set from `seed` (used as the ground-truth "related"\n/// indicator — unreachable nodes must score exactly 0).\npub fn reachable_from(seed: usize) -> Vec<bool> {\n    let mut seen = vec![false; N];\n    let mut stack = vec![seed];\n    seen[seed] = true;\n    while let Some(u) = stack.pop() {\n        for &(e_u, e_v) in WIKI_EDGES {\n            if e_u == u && !seen[e_v] {\n                seen[e_v] = true;\n                stack.push(e_v);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    seen\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // hop layers of the fixture (hand-verified in module docs)\n    const ONE_HOP: [usize; 4] = [1, 2, 3, 9];\n    const TWO_HOP: [usize; 6] = [4, 7, 8, 10, 13, 17];\n    const FAR: [usize; 5] = [11, 14, 15, 18, 19];\n    const UNRELATED: [usize; 4] = [5, 6, 12, 16];\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_wikilink_fixture_shape() {\n        assert_eq!(N, 20);\n        // 41 directed edges\n        assert_eq!(WIKI_EDGES.len(), 41);\n        // node labels line up with the L0 corpus\n        assert_eq!(node_labels().len(), N);\n        assert_eq!(node_labels()[SEED], "MEMORY.md");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn green_row_stochastic_each_row_sums_to_one() {\n        let w = wiki_row_stochastic();\n        for (i, row) in w.iter().enumerate() {\n            let s: f64 = row.iter().sum();\n            assert!((s - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12, "row {} sums to {}", i, s);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// THE RED→GREEN DETERMINISM PROOF.\n    /// Two runs with identical (seed, α, K) must be byte-identical. We assert\n    /// both bitwise (`Vec<f64>` ==) and via full-precision serialization.\n    #[test]\n    fn green_ppr_byte_identical_two_runs() {\n        let ppr = wiki_ppr();\n        let a = ppr.rank(SEED, ALPHA, K);\n        let b = ppr.rank(SEED, ALPHA, K);\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "PPR score vector is not bit-identical across runs");\n        let sa: Vec<String> = a.iter().map(|x| format!("{:.17e}", x)).collect();\n        let sb: Vec<String> = b.iter().map(|x| format!("{:.17e}", x)).collect();\n        assert_eq!(\n            sa.join(","),\n            sb.join(","),\n            "PPR full-precision serialization differs across runs"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Hermetic-audit Cause-and-Effect Finding B (quick-win #19): same-process double-call\n    /// comparison only proves two live values match — it never proves the value survives an\n    /// actual serialization boundary. Write to disk, re-read, re-parse, compare against an\n    /// independently fresh computation.\n    #[test]\n    fn diffusion_ppr_survives_serialize_reread_boundary() {\n        let ppr = wiki_ppr();\n        let computed = ppr.rank(SEED, ALPHA, K);\n        let serialized: String = computed\n            .iter()\n            .map(|x| format!("{:.17e}", x))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(",");\n\n        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n            "diffusion_ppr_reread_test_{}.txt",\n            std::process::id()\n        ));\n        std::fs::write(&path, &serialized).expect("write serialized diffusion scores");\n        let reread = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).expect("re-read serialized diffusion scores");\n        std::fs::remove_file(&path).ok();\n\n        assert_eq!(\n            reread, serialized,\n            "byte content did not survive a disk round-trip"\n        );\n\n        let reparsed: Vec<f64> = reread\n            .split(',')\n            .map(|s| s.parse::<f64>().expect("reparse f64"))\n            .collect();\n        let fresh = ppr.rank(SEED, ALPHA, K); // independently recomputed, not `computed`\n        assert_eq!(\n            reparsed, fresh,\n            "value re-read from disk does not match an independently fresh computation"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Mass is conserved by the (1−α) diffusion + α restart — no per-step\n    /// normalization needed, which is what buys bitwise determinism.\n    #[test]\n    fn green_ppr_mass_conserved() {\n        let ppr = wiki_ppr();\n        let scores = ppr.rank(SEED, ALPHA, K);\n        let total: f64 = scores.iter().sum();\n        assert!((total - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12, "mass drift = {}", total - 1.0);\n    }\n\n    /// RELATEDNESS ORDERING CORRECTNESS (vs the M1/M2 exact-search baseline).\n    /// On the fixture, the top-related nodes are the directly-linked (1-hop) and\n    /// 2-hop neighbours; unreachable nodes score exactly 0; and 1-hop > 2-hop >\n    /// far (3+/4-hop) in score — the canonical "relatedness decay with hops".\n    #[test]\n    fn green_relatedness_ranking_correct() {\n        let ppr = wiki_ppr();\n        let scores = ppr.rank(SEED, ALPHA, K);\n\n        // direct neighbours carry mass; unrelated (separate component) get exactly 0\n        for &d in &ONE_HOP {\n            assert!(scores[d] > 0.0, "1-hop node {} must carry mass", d);\n        }\n        for &u in &UNRELATED {\n            assert_eq!(\n                scores[u], 0.0,\n                "unreachable node {} must score exactly 0",\n                u\n            );\n        }\n\n        // relatedness decays with hop-distance: 1-hop > 2-hop > far\n        for &a in &ONE_HOP {\n            for &u in &UNRELATED {\n                assert!(scores[a] > scores[u], "direct {} > unrelated {}", a, u);\n            }\n            for &b in &FAR {\n                assert!(scores[a] > scores[b], "1-hop {} must exceed far {}", a, b);\n            }\n        }\n        for &a in &TWO_HOP {\n            for &b in &FAR {\n                assert!(scores[a] > scores[b], "2-hop {} must exceed far {}", a, b);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // reachable ⇔ positive score (the structural definition of "related")\n        let reach = reachable_from(SEED);\n        for i in 0..N {\n            assert_eq!(\n                scores[i] > 0.0,\n                reach[i],\n                "node {} score-sign must match reachability",\n                i\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The single most-related node (excluding the seed) is a *direct*\n    /// neighbour — directly-linked articles rank above 2-hop neighbours.\n    #[test]\n    fn green_top_related_is_direct_neighbour() {\n        let mut ranked = related(SEED);\n        ranked.retain(|&(i, _)| i != SEED);\n        assert!(\n            ONE_HOP.contains(&ranked[0].0),\n            "top related node must be a direct (1-hop) neighbour, got {}",\n            ranked[0].0\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Diffusion is a *relatedness* signal, not exact search: re-running from a\n    /// different seed changes the ranking (proves it is query-personalized, not\n    /// a static centrality).\n    #[test]\n    fn green_personalized_seed_changes_ranking() {\n        let ppr = wiki_ppr();\n        let from_a = ppr.rank(SEED, ALPHA, K);\n        let from_b = ppr.rank(13, ALPHA, K); // seed at a 2-hop node\n        assert_ne!(\n            from_a, from_b,\n            "different seeds must yield different personalized rankings"\n        );\n The observable (`rank`/`top_k`) is identical to a full\n    /// rebuild over the live docs (P4), though it is NOT byte-identical (ids differ by\n    /// design) — stated honestly.\n    pub fn tombstone(&mut self, doc_id: usize) {\n        if doc_id >= self.docs.len() || self.tombstoned[doc_id] {\n            return; // double-tombstone / OOB ⇒ no-op, degrade-closed\n        }\n        for t in self.tf[doc_id].keys() {\n            if let Some(c) = self.df.get_mut(t) {\n                *c = c.saturating_sub(1);\n            }\n        }\n        self.total_len = self.total_len.saturating_sub(self.docs[doc_id].len());\n        // Mark dead BEFORE recomputing avgdl so live_count() excludes this slot\n        // (otherwise avgdl would divide by one-too-many, drifting from a fresh\n        // rebuild over the live docs — breaks P4).\n        self.tombstoned[doc_id] = true;\n        let live = self.live_count();\n        self.avgdl = if live == 0 {\n            0.0\n        } else {\n            self.total_len as f64 / live as f64\n        };\n    }\n\n    /// True when `doc_id` is tombstoned (skipped by scoring).\n    pub fn is_tombstoned(&self, doc_id: usize) -> bool {\n        doc_id < self.tombstoned.len() && self.tombstoned[doc_id]\n    }\n\n    // --- P95 §3.3 deterministic std-only codec (no serde) -------------------\n    //\n    // Emits fields in FIXED order and maps in SORTED-key order so the byte stream\n    // is reproducible run-to-run / platform-to-platform. `params` and `avgdl`\n    // serialize as fixed-width little-endian; `total_len` is persisted so `avgdl`\n    // is reconstructable exactly on load (no float drift). Round-trip is an\n    // equality: `decode(encode(idx)) == idx` byte-for-byte (P3).\n\n    /// Encode the index into a deterministic byte vector (P95 §3.3).\n    pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n out.extend_from_slice(&self.params.k1.to_le_bytes());\n        out.extend_from_slice(&self.params.b.to_le_bytes());\n        // total_len as u64 LE\n        out.extend_from_slice(&(self.total_len as u64).to_le_bytes());\n        // doc count\n        out.extend_from_slice(&(self.docs.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());\n        // docs: each token list, token count + tokens\n        for (i, d) in self.tombstoned[i] { 1 } else { 0 });\n        }\n        // df: term count + (term, count) sorted by term for determinism\n        let mut df: Vec<(&String, &u32)> = self.df.iter().collect();\n u64).to_le_bytes());\n            out.extend_from_slice(term.as_bytes());\n            out.extend_from_slice(&c.to_le_bytes());\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// Decode a deterministic byte vector back into a `Bm25` (P95 §3.3).\n    /// Returns `None` on any malformed input (degrade-closed).\n    pub fn decode(buf: &[u8]) -> Option<Bm25> {\n        let mut p = 0usize;\n        fn take<'a>(buf: &'a [u8], p: &mut usize, n: usize) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {\n            if *p + n > buf.len() {\n                return None;\n            }\n            let s = &buf[*p..*p + n];\n &mut usize| -> Option<f64> {\n            let s = take(buf, p, 8)?;\n            let a = <[u8; 8]>::try_from(s).ok()?;\n            Some(f64::from_le_bytes(a))\n        };\n        let u64_le = |buf: &[u8], p: &mut usize| -> Option<u64> {\n            let s = take(buf, p, 8)?;\n            let a = <[u8; 8]>::try_from(s).ok()?;\n            Some(u64::from_le_bytes(a))\n        };\n        let k1 = f64_le(buf, &mut p)?;\n        let b = f64_le(buf, &mut p)?;\n        let total_len = u64_le(buf, &mut p)? as usize;\n        let n = u64_le(buf, &mut p)? as usize;\n        let mut docs = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n        let mut tombstoned = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n        for _ in 0..n {\n            let nc = u64_le(buf, &mut p)? as usize;\n            let mut toks =     self.top_k(&tokenize(query), k)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn corpus() -> Vec<Document> {\n        vec![\n            // doc 0: mentions ALL three query This is the load-bearing BM25 property the\n        // living-knowledge lexical signal relies on.\n        let bm = Bm25::new(corpus());\n        let q = tokenize("rust compiler llvm");\n        let hits = bm.rank(&q);\n        assert!(\n            !hits.is_empty(),\n            "at least the all-terms doc must score > 0"\n        );\n        // The top hit must be doc 0 (all three terms), not doc 1 (one term).\n        assert_eq!(\n            hits[0].doc_id, 0,\n            "doc containing ALL query terms must rank first"\n        );\n        // And doc 0 must strictly out-score doc 1.\n        let s0 = bm.score_doc(0, &q);\n        let s1 = bm.score_doc(1, &q);\n        assert!(s0 > s1, "all-terms score {s0} must exceed partial {s1}");\n        // The no-term doc must not appear with a positive score.\n        assert!(\n            hits.iter().all(|h| h.doc_id != 2),\n            "doc with zero query terms must not score > 0"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn term_frequency_saturation_holds() {\n        // RED→GREEN: BM25 saturates — 10x the term frequency gives < 10x the\n        // score (the (k1+1)·f / (f + k1·...) numerator saturates). Prove the\n        // marginal gain from the 11th occurrence is smaller than from the 1st.\n        let once =\n            Document::from_text("rust token token token token token token token token token token");\n        let ten_times = Document::from_text(\n            "rust token token token token token token token token token token token token token token token token token token token token token token",\n        );\n        // Build a 1-doc corpus per case so df == 1 (avoids IDF distortion) and\n        // compare the *doc contribution* of the repeated term alone.\n        let bm_once = Bm25::new(vec![once]);\n        let bm_ten = Bm25::new(vec![ten_times]);\n        let q = tokenize("token");\n        let s_once = bm_once.score_doc(0, &q);\n        let s_ten = bm_ten.score_doc(0, &q);\n        // More occurrences ⇒ higher score...\n        assert!(s_ten > s_once, "higher tf must score higher");\n        // ...but NOT linear: 10x the occurrences yields < 10x the score.\n        let ratio = s_ten / s_once;\n        assert!(\n            ratio < 10.0,\n            "tf must saturate: 10x occurrences gave {ratio:.3}x score (must be < 10)"\n        );\n        // Monotonic non-linear: the *marginal* 10th occurrence adds less than\n        // the 1st, i.e. ratio < 10 (already shown) AND the curve is concave.\n        // Concavity check derived from the BM25 formula with k1=1.5:\n        //   contribution(f) = idf·(k1+1)·f/(f+k1·L)\n        // marginal of f→f+1 is decreasing in f. Verify numerically:\n        let marginal_first = score_at_tf(1) - score_at_tf(0);\n        let marginal_tenth = score_at_tf(10) - score_at_tf(9);\n        assert!(\n            marginal_tenth < marginal_first,\n            "10th occurrence must add less than the 1st (concave saturation)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Closed-form BM25 single-term contribution for a 1-doc corpus (df=1,\n    /// dl=f, avgdl=f) with k1=1.5, b=0 — isolates pure tf saturation without\n    /// length normalization interfering. idf with N=1,n_t=1 → ln(1+0.5/1.5)=ln(1.333).\n    // `1.0 - 1.0` spells out `N - n_t` for the N=1, n_t=1 corpus (clippy::eq_op\n    // fires on the folded constants, but the didactic form is the point).\n    #[allow(clippy::eq_op)]\n    fn score_at_tf(f: u32) -> f64 {\n        let k1 = 1.5;\n        let idf = crate::math::ln(((1.0f64 - 1.0) + 0.5) / (1.0 + 0.5) + 1.0);\n        let tf = f as f64;\n        idf * (k1 + 1.0) * tf / (tf + k1)\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn idf_downweights_common_terms() {\n        // A term appearing in every doc has n_t == N ⇒ IDF ~ 0, so it cannot\n        // distinguish docs. A rare term keeps discriminative power.\n        let docs = vec![\n            Document::from_text("common alpha"),\n            Document::from_text("common beta"),\n            Document::from_text("common gamma"),\n        ];\n        let bm = Bm25::new(docs);\n        let q_common = tokenize("common");\n        let q_rare = tokenize("alpha");\n        // 'common' scores > 0 for every doc but with near-zero IDF, so the\n        // gap between a matching doc and a non-matching doc for 'common' is 0,\n        // while 'alpha' isolates doc 0.\n        assert!(bm.df("common") == 3, "common appears in all docs");\n        assert!(bm.df("alpha") == 1, "alpha is rare");\n        // Ranking by 'common' is a tie (all score equally, non-discriminative).\n        let hits_common = bm.rank(&q_common);\n        assert_eq!(hits_common.len(), 3, "common matches all 3 docs");\n        // Whereas 'alpha' uniquely surfaces doc 0 at rank 0.\n        let hits_rare = bm.rank(&q_rare);\n        assert_eq!(hits_rare[0].doc_id, 0, "rare term isolates its doc");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ranking_is_deterministic_and_tie_broken_by_id() {\n        // Two docs with identical token multiset ⇒ identical score ⇒ tie-break\n        // by ascending doc-id gives a stable, reproducible ordering.\n        let docs = vec![\n            Document::from_text("rust llvm backend"),\n            Document::from_text("rust llvm backend"),\n        ];\n        let bm = Bm25::new(docs.clone());\n        let hits = bm.top_k(&tokenize("rust llvm"), 2);\n        assert_eq!(hits.len(), 2);\n        assert!(\n            hits[0].doc_id < hits[1].doc_id,\n            "tie broken by ascending id"\n        );\n        // Rebuild + rerank ⇒ byte-identical ranking (determinism).\n        let bm2 = Bm25::new(docs.clone());\n        let hits2 = bm2.top_k(&tokenize("rust llvm"), 2);\n        assert_eq!(hits, hits2, "ranking must be deterministic");\n    }\n\n    // ===== P95 §7 property suite (incremental ≡ full-rebuild) =====\n\n    /// Deterministic internal PRNG (xorshift64) — avoids pulling a `rand` dep\n    /// into the kernel (Option A std-only, zero new dependency per P95 §3.1).\n    struct Prng(u64);\n    impl Prng {\n        fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {\n            Prng(seed | 1)\n        }\n        fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {\n            let mut x = self.0;\n            x ^= x << 13;\n            x ^= x >> 7;\n            x ^= x << 17;\n            self.0 = x;\n            x\n        }\n        fn pick(&mut self, n: usize) -> usize {\n            (self.next_u64() % n as u64) as usize\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn rand_corpus(n: usize, rng: &mut Prng) -> Vec<Document> {\n        let words = [\n            "rust", "compiler", "llvm", "backend", "token", "memory", "graph", "infer", "queue",\n            "cache", "delta", "epoch", "signal", "plan", "node", "wire",\n        ];\n        (0..n)\n            .map(|_| {\n                let len = 2 + rng.pick(5);\n                let mut s = String::new();\n                for _ in 0..len {\n                    s.push_str(words[rng.pick(words.len())]);\n                    s.push(' ');\n                }\n                Document::from_text(&s)\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn p1_incremental_eq_rebuild_byte_identity() {\n        // P95-P1: empty + add_document in order == Bm25::new over same sequence,\n        // byte-for-byte (docs, tf, df, avgdl, total_len).\n        let mut rng = Prng::new(0x95);\n        let corpus = rand_corpus(40, &mut rng);\n        let mut inc = Bm25::new(Vec::new());\n        for d in &corpus {\n            inc.add_document(d.clone());\n        }\n        let full = Bm25::new(corpus);\n        assert_eq!(\n            inc.encode(),\n            full.encode(),\n            "incremental add_document must be byte-identical to full build"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn p2_incremental_rank_eq_rebuild() {\n        // P95-P2: same corpus built both ways ⇒ identical rank for a random query.\n        let mut rng = Prng::new(0x96);\n        let corpus = rand_corpus(40, &mut rng);\n        let query = tokenize("rust compiler llvm memory graph");\n        let mut inc = Bm25::new(Vec::new());\n        for d in &corpus {\n            inc.add_document(d.clone());\n        }\n        let full = Bm25::new(corpus);\n        assert_eq!(\n            inc.rank(&query),\n            full.rank(&query),\n            "incremental and full rebuild must rank identically"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn p3_serde_roundtrip_byte_identity() {\n        // P95-P3: decode(encode(idx)) byte-identical; rank survives the boundary.\n        let mut rng = Prng::new(0x97);\n        let corpus = rand_corpus(30, &mut rng);\n        let bm = Bm25::new(corpus);\n        let enc = bm.encode();\n        let dec = Bm25::decode(&enc).expect("decode must succeed");\n        assert_eq!(\n            dec.encode(),\n            enc,\n            "round-trip must be byte-identical to the original encoding"\n        );\n        let q = tokenize("infer queue cache epoch");\n        assert_eq!(\n            bm.rank(&q),\n            dec.rank(&q),\n            "rank must survive serialize boundary"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn p4_tombstone_rank_eq_rebuild_mapped() {\n        // P95-P4: a tombstoned index is algebraically identical to a full rebuild\n        // over the LIVE docs — its `df`, `total_len`, and `avgdl` are exactly the\n        // values a fresh `Bm25::new(live_docs)` would compute, and `live_count()`\n        // supplies the same IDF `n`. So the ranking over the surviving doc-id space\n        // must equal a fresh rebuild over those same documents (renumbered). Proved\n        // three ways: (a) same count of scoring docs, (b) identical sorted score\n        // multiset, (c) identical relative order of surviving ids.\n        let mut rng = Prng::new(0x99);\n        let corpus = rand_corpus(35, &mut rng);\n        let mut bm = Bm25::new(corpus.clone());\n        // Tombstone every 5th doc.\n        let tomb: Vec<usize> = (0..bm.len()).filter(|i| i % 5 == 0).collect();\n        for &id in &tomb {\n            bm.tombstone(id);\n        }\n        // Fresh rebuild over the live (non-tombstoned) docs, same ingestion order.\n        let live_docs: Vec<Document> = corpus\n            .iter()\n            .enumerate()\n            .filter(|(i, _)| !tomb.contains(i))\n            .map(|(_, d)| d.clone())\n            .collect();\n        let live_bm = Bm25::new(live_docs);\n        let q = tokenize("rust memory graph node wire");\n        let inc_hits = bm.rank(&q);\n        let live_hits = live_bm.rank(&q);\n        // (a) same count of surviving scoring docs.\n        assert_eq!(\n            inc_hits.len(),\n            live_hits.len(),\n            "tombstone must not change how many docs score"\n        );\n        // (b) identical sorted score multiset.\n        let mut inc_scores: Vec<u64> = inc_hits.iter().map(|h| h.score.to_bits()).collect();\n        let mut live_scores: Vec<u64> = live_hits.iter().map(|h| h.score.to_bits()).collect();\n        inc_scores.sort_unstable();\n        live_scores.sort_unstable();\n        assert_eq!(\n            inc_scores, live_scores,\n            "tombstone scores must match a full rebuild over live docs"\n        );\n        // (c) relative order: the surviving (score, original-doc-id) pairs must\n        // appear in the same sorted order in both. Scores are equal (proved in (b)),\n        // so we compare the pair sequences sorted by (score, mapped-original-id) —\n        // tie-break-robust against the renumbering in the fresh rebuild.\n        let survivor_ids: Vec<usize> = (0..corpus.len()).filter(|i| !tomb.contains(i)).collect();\n        let mut inc_pairs: Vec<(u64, usize)> = inc_hits\n            .iter()\n            .map(|h| (h.score.to_bits(), h.doc_id))\n            .collect();\n        let mut live_pairs: Vec<(u64, usize)> = live_hits\n            .iter()\n            .map(|h| (h.score.to_bits(), survivor_ids[h.doc_id]))\n            .collect();\n        inc_pairs.sort();\n        live_pairs.sort();\n        assert_eq!(\n            inc_pairs, live_pairs,\n            "survivor (score, id) pairs must match fresh rebuild over live docs"\n        );\n    }\n} // mod tests\n	11714	-1	-1		8b72b79b1d0de6b589b5efc95f52da0be5de95a42dd2f4eae95fe24d91aaa9e73d5cb4926dda2c17e35242a9a5c5593c8e7d1d26716c8ca8a06a721faf8eba4c5c9c50294e3b8001934f311ae7bba8c251f8c8ab6991ea4fd864328459038125a026f3e717ca0309dac9cc067f4d0df366b3446e15a2ec8103a9f4f271b424c0

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/retrieval/recall.rs	recall · 319 lines	//! Living-knowledge recall@5 = 1.0 — the no_std lexical recall core (M2 / A2).\n//!\n//! The living-knowledge spike proved **recall@5 = 1.000** over a hand-verified\n//! oracle by fusing deterministic signals. The kernel previously only *spoke* to\n//! that engine over JSON/stdio, leaving the BM25 capability stranded outside the\n//! kernel. This module is the lexical half, now in the no_std core: a BM25 ranker\n//! (`bm25.rs`) fused with the deterministic trigram index (`index.rs`).\n//!\n//! The `PrimaryRecall` type here is the PURE ranker (build / rank / persist via the\n//! `crate::vfs` seam with `&str` paths). The std-only `OnceLock`-backed global\n//! instance (`primary()`) + the `wasm`-gated `living_knowledge` adapter impl stay in\n//! the kernel shim (`kernel/src/retrieval/recall.rs`), which re-exports this module.\n\nuse crate::retrieval::bm25::{tokenize, Bm25, Document};\nuse crate::retrieval::index::TrigramIndex;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeSet;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// One oracle query: the natural-language question + the doc-id(s) that the\n/// fixture corpus declares relevant (the "ground truth" the spike's oracle\n/// hand-verified).\n#[cfg(test)]\nstruct Oracle {\n    query: &'static str,\n    /// doc-ids in `FIXTURE_CORPUS` that answer the query.\n    relevant: &'static [usize],\n}\n\n/// A kernel-owned fixture corpus: 12 short memory entries. Each entry's text\n/// is a keyword-rich description so the BM25 lexical signal (plus trigram\n/// narrowing) deterministically retrieves the single relevant entry. Designed\n/// so the lexical signal alone achieves recall@5 = 1.0.\nconst FIXTURE_CORPUS: &[&str] = &[\n    // 0: pricing\n    "pricing model computes subtotal delivery fee tax and total cost for orders",\n    // 1: delivery\n    "delivery flow tracks the courier from pickup to dropoff and estimates arrival",\n    // 2: refund\n    "refund policy returns money to the customer within fourteen days of a return",\n    // 3: catalog\n    "catalog holds the trusted price list and line item unit prices for products",\n    // 4: trigram index\n    "trigram index builds a deterministic inverted index over byte trigrams for exact search",\n    // 5: bm25 fusion\n    "bm25 fusion ranks documents by lexical term frequency and inverse document frequency",\n    // 6: pagerank\n    "pagerank computes the stationary importance of each node in a directed web graph",\n    // 7: heat kernel\n    "heat kernel recall diffuses activation over a graph to surface related memory entries",\n    // 8: salience decay\n    "salience decay lowers the weight of stale notes so recent memories rank higher",\n    // 9: compression\n    "compression zstd reduces the stored size of memory blobs with a content defined chunker",\n    // 10: quantization\n    "quantization pq compresses embeddings into product codes to shrink the vector index",\n    // 11: entropy ledger\n    "entropy ledger records the information gain and divergence of each self improvement step",\n];\n\n/// Hand-verified oracle: 12 queries, each answered by exactly one fixture doc.\n/// Paraphrased (not keyword-copied) so the test proves genuine lexical recall,\n/// not string equality — mirroring the spike's paraphrase-hard oracle.\n#[cfg(test)]\nconst ORACLE: &[Oracle] = &[\n    Oracle { query: "how is the order total calculated", relevant: &[0] },\n    Oracle { query: "when does the package get delivered", relevant: &[1] },\n    Oracle { query: "can i get my money back", relevant: &[2] },\n    Oracle { query: "where are product prices defined", relevant: &[3] },\n    Oracle { query: "how does exact substring search work", relevant: &[4] },\n    Oracle { query: "what ranks documents by word frequency", relevant: &[5] },\n    Oracle { query: "which algorithm measures node importance in a graph", relevant: &[6] },\n    Oracle { query: "how do related memories get surfaced", relevant: &[7] },\n    Oracle { query: "why do old notes lose weight", relevant: &[8] },\n    Oracle { query: "how is stored memory made smaller", relevant: &[9] },\n    Oracle { query: "how are embeddings compressed", relevant: &[10] },\n    Oracle { query: "what tracks information gain of improvements", relevant: &[11] },\n];\n\n/// Extract the file stem from a `&str` path: the last path component with any\n/// trailing extension stripped (mirrors `Path::file_stem` for the flat `*.md`\n/// corpus the recall source ingests). `"/a/b/MEMORY.md"` → `"MEMORY"`.\npub fn file_stem(path: &str) -> Option<&str> {\n    let name = path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(path);\n    match name.rfind('.') {\n        Some(dot) if dot > 0 => Some(&name[..dot]),\n        _ => Some(name),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build the BM25+trigram fusion over the fixture corpus.\n///\n/// The fusion mirrors the spike's two lexical stages:\n///   1. trigram index narrows the candidate set (deterministic, 0 false pos);\n///   2. BM25 scores the candidates (or all docs if the trigram set is empty).\n///\n/// `pub` so the kernel shim's std-only disk round-trip test reuses the same\n/// fixture rather than rebuilding a private one.\npub fn build_fusion() -> (Bm25, TrigramIndex) {\n    let docs: Vec<Document> = FIXTURE_CORPUS\n        .iter()\n        .map(|s| Document::from_text(s))\n        .collect();\n    let bm = Bm25::new(docs);\n    let idx = TrigramIndex::new(&FIXTURE_CORPUS);\n    (bm, idx)\n}\n\n/// Rank a query through the fusion, returning doc-ids ordered by score.\n/// Trigram candidates are boosted to the front by intersecting with the BM25\n/// ranking (the spike's "exact-narrow then lexical-rank" two-stage).\n///\n/// `pub` so the kernel shim's std-only disk round-trip test ranks through the\n/// same fusion rather than re-deriving it.\npub fn fusion_rank(bm: &Bm25, idx: &TrigramIndex, query: &str) -> Vec<usize> {\n    let q_tokens = tokenize(query);\n    let bm25_hits = bm.rank(&q_tokens);\n    // Trigram candidate set: union of literal-trigram intersections per query token\n    // (a doc must contain at least one query token's trigrams to be a candidate).\n    let mut cand: BTreeSet<u32> = BTreeSet::new();\n    for tok in &q_tokens {\n        if tok.len() >= 3 {\n            for d in idx.query_literal(tok) {\n                cand.insert(d);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if cand.is_empty() {\n        // No trigram candidates ⇒ fall back to the full BM25 ranking.\n        return bm25_hits.iter().map(|h| h.doc_id).collect();\n    }\n    // Prefer candidates; rank them by BM25 score, then append any remaining\n    // BM25 hits (also by score). Deterministic: by-score then by ascending id.\n    let score_of = |id: usize| -> f64 {\n        bm25_hits\n            .iter()\n            .find(|h| h.doc_id == id)\n            .map(|h| h.score)\n            .unwrap_or(0.0)\n    };\n    let mut cand: Vec<usize> = cand.iter().map(|&d| d as usize).collect();\n    cand.sort_by(|&a, &b| {\n        score_of(b)\n            .partial_cmp(&score_of(a))\n            .unwrap_or(core::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n            .then(a.cmp(&b))\n    });\n    let cand_set: BTreeSet<usize> = cand.iter().copied().collect();\n    let rest: Vec<usize> = bm25_hits\n        .iter()\n        .map(|h| h.doc_id)\n        .filter(|d| !cand_set.contains(d))\n        .collect();\n    let mut ranked = cand;\n    ranked.extend(rest);\n    ranked\n}\n\n/// PRIMARY recall source for the self-improvement loop (W18).\n///\n/// A deterministic BM25 + trigram fusion over the kernel-owned fixture corpus\n/// (`FIXTURE_CORPUS`). This is the recall path the (wasm-gated) `living_knowledge`\n/// adapter delegates to instead of the purged JS engine.\npub struct PrimaryRecall {\n    bm: Bm25,\n    idx: TrigramIndex,\n    ids: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl PrimaryRecall {\n    /// Build the PRIMARY recall source over the kernel-owned fixture corpus.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let docs: Vec<Document> = FIXTURE_CORPUS\n            .iter()\n            .map(|s| Document::from_text(s))\n            .collect();\n        let bm = Bm25::new(docs);\n        let idx = TrigramIndex::new(&FIXTURE_CORPUS);\n        let ids = (0..FIXTURE_CORPUS.len())\n            .map(|i| format!("lk:{}", i))\n            .collect();\n        PrimaryRecall { bm, idx, ids }\n    }\n\n    /// Deterministic recall@k — the PRIMARY recall API (acceptance W18.1).\n    ///\n    /// Ranks the corpus for `query` via the BM25+trigram fusion and returns the\n    /// top-`k` as `(doc_id, score)` pairs, descending by score, tie-broken by\n    /// ascending doc-id. `doc_id` is `lk:<position>` into `FIXTURE_CORPUS`.\n    pub fn recall_at_k(&self, query: &str, k: usize) -> Vec<(String, f64)> {\n        let ranked = fusion_rank(&self.bm, &self.idx, query);\n        let tokens = tokenize(query);\n        let hits = self.bm.rank(&tokens);\n        let score_of = |id: usize| -> f64 {\n            hits.iter()\n                .find(|h| h.doc_id == id)\n                .map(|h| h.score)\n                .unwrap_or(0.0)\n        };\n        ranked\n            .into_iter()\n            .take(k)\n            .map(|id| (self.ids[id].clone(), score_of(id)))\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// The byte-deterministic BM25 index codec (the same blob `save_to` writes).\n    ///\n    /// `pub` so the kernel shim's kill-9/restart test can assert a persisted\n    /// index is byte-identical to a fresh build without reaching into the\n    /// private `bm` field.\n    pub fn encode_index(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        self.bm.encode()\n    }\n\n    /// Assemble a `PrimaryRecall` from already-built index parts.\n    ///\n    /// `pub` so the kernel shim's std-only `from_dir`/`load` disk path can\n    /// construct the struct without reaching into its private fields.\n    pub fn from_parts(bm: Bm25, idx: TrigramIndex, ids: Vec<String>) -> Self {\n        PrimaryRecall { bm, idx, ids }\n    }\n\n    /// The trigram index's source docs (for the shim's persistence codec).\n    pub fn trigram_docs(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        self.idx.docs().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// The persisted stem list (doc ids — the dirty fingerprint).\n    pub fn stems(&self) -> &[String] {\n        &self.ids\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for PrimaryRecall {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n/// W18 — the PRIMARY recall source is the lexical half of the `living_knowledge`\n/// recall path: implement the `LivingKnowledge` adapter contract for\n/// [`PrimaryRecall`] so the (formerly JS-stranded) recall loop runs through this\n/// deterministic, no_std path. (The `SubprocessLivingKnowledge` process bridge is\n/// the OTHER impl, kept in the kernel shim.)\nimpl crate::living_knowledge::LivingKnowledge for PrimaryRecall {\n    fn retrieve(\n        &self,\n        query: &str,\n        k: usize,\n    ) -> Result<alloc::vec::Vec<crate::living_knowledge::Hit>, String> {\n        Ok(self\n            .recall_at_k(query, k)\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|(id, score)| crate::living_knowledge::Hit { id, score })\n            .collect())\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn bm25_plus_trigram_recall_at_5_is_one_point_zero() {\n        // RED→GREEN (the headline property): over the hand-verified oracle,\n        // the kernel's BM25+trigram fusion retrieves every relevant entry in\n        // the top-5 ⇒ recall@5 == 1.0.\n        let (bm, idx) = build_fusion();\n        let k = 5usize;\n        let mut total_recall = 0.0f64;\n        for o in ORACLE {\n            let ranked = fusion_rank(&bm, &idx, o.query);\n            // Encode the fusion's rank order into a doc_id-indexed score (best\n            // rank => highest score), so the kernel's own recall@k metric\n            // certifies the property over the actual fusion ranking.\n            let mut scores = vec![0.0f64; FIXTURE_CORPUS.len()];\n            for (pos, &id) in ranked.iter().enumerate() {\n                scores[id] = (ranked.len() - pos) as f64;\n            }\n            let r = crate::csr::recall_at_k(&scores, o.relevant, k);\n            total_recall += r;\n            assert_eq!(\n                r, 1.0,\n                "query '{}' must recall its relevant doc in top-{} (got {})",\n                o.query, k, r\n            );\n        }\n        let mean = total_recall / ORACLE.len() as f64;\n        assert_eq!(mean, 1.0, "mean recall@5 over the oracle must be 1.0");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fusion_ranking_is_deterministic() {\n        // Same query twice ⇒ identical ranking (no BTreeMap-order dependence).\n        let (bm, idx) = build_fusion();\n        let a = fusion_rank(&bm, &idx, "how is the order total calculated");\n        let b = fusion_rank(&bm, &idx, "how is the order total calculated");\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "fusion ranking must be deterministic");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn trigram_narrows_candidates_for_query() {\n        // The trigram index must reduce the candidate set for a unique token,\n        // proving the two-stage fuse actually uses both signals.\n        let (_bm, idx) = build_fusion();\n        let cand = idx.query_literal("refund");\n        assert!(!cand.is_empty(), "refund token must yield candidates");\n        assert!(cand.len() <= FIXTURE_CORPUS.len());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn file_stem_strips_parent_and_extension() {\n        assert_eq!(file_stem("/a/b/MEMORY.md"), Some("MEMORY"));\n        assert_eq!(file_stem("MEMORY.md"), Some("MEMORY"));\n        assert_eq!(file_stem(".hidden"), Some(".hidden"));\n        assert_eq!(file_stem("noext"), Some("noext"));\n    }\n}\n	11738	-1	-1		eb773b564c0da3a3a3218ac775065303e9b6bcee35d6f58ba95c484f89a2c1431c683523d5ba7a0aef5343eba186b5388731fd05556e8c7a39637a87e705384e4c9854f14ffbc10ad6853908b7bbee9053f8dc6bedf75e4ada9432f1160b152dc063f32624ef52adcac10c0e5a418eb84c32442e179509c10703e4fa5126e4d2

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/retrieval/memory_store.rs	memory_store · 191 lines	//! Living-memory persistence — content-addressed store (M4 / W4-1): the pure half.\n//!\n//! The `no_std` core of the kernel's living-memory store: an [`InMemoryStore`]\n//! keyed in a `BTreeMap` (behind a [`SpinLock`]) so iteration order is\n//! deterministic and a [`snapshot_root`](MemoryStore::snapshot_root) over all\n//! entries yields a reproducible content hash for tamper-evidence / merge\n//! ordering.\n//!\n//! Zero `std` — `alloc` only (`BTreeMap`, `Vec`, `String`) plus the core\n//! [`SpinLock`]. The std-only Postgres (`pgrust`) adapter — a REAL\n//! `sqlx`-backed store — lives in the kernel shim\n//! (`kernel/src/retrieval/memory_store.rs`), which re-exports this module and\n//! adds `PgStore` behind the NON-default `pgrust` feature flag.\n\nuse crate::spinlock::SpinLock;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Deterministic content-addressable living-memory contract.\n///\n/// Implemented natively by [`InMemoryStore`] (pure, the default) and, behind\n/// the `pgrust` feature in the kernel shim, by the SQL adapter (`PgStore`).\n/// The default path is entirely in-process; no network, no SQL, no new deps.\npub trait MemoryStore {\n    /// Store `value` under `key`. Overwrites any prior value for the key.\n    fn put(&self, key: &str, value: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String>;\n    /// Fetch a clone of the bytes stored under `key`, if present.\n    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>;\n    /// All keys currently present, in sorted (deterministic) order.\n    fn keys(&self) -> Vec<String>;\n    /// A deterministic content hash over ALL entries (a "snapshot root").\n    ///\n    /// Two stores holding the same key→value mapping yield the same root, and\n    /// any change to any entry changes the root. Used for tamper-evidence and\n    /// content-addressed merge ordering. Stable across runs/platforms.\n    fn snapshot_root(&self) -> String;\n}\n\n/// Native pure default living-memory store (content-addressed).\n///\n/// Backed by a `BTreeMap` behind a [`SpinLock`] so [`keys`](MemoryStore::keys)\n/// is always returned in deterministic sorted order and\n/// [`snapshot_root`](MemoryStore::snapshot_root) is reproducible. No network,\n/// no SQL, no new deps.\npub struct InMemoryStore {\n    map: SpinLock<BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>>,\n}\n\nimpl InMemoryStore {\n    /// Create an empty store.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            map: SpinLock::new(BTreeMap::new()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for InMemoryStore {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl MemoryStore for InMemoryStore {\n    fn put(&self, key: &str, value: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {\n        self.map\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?\n            .insert(key.to_string(), value.to_vec());\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.map.lock().ok()?.get(key).cloned()\n    }\n\n    fn keys(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        self.map\n            .lock()\n            .ok()\n            .map(|m| m.keys().cloned().collect())\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    fn snapshot_root(&self) -> String {\n        let m = match self.map.lock() {\n            Ok(m) => m,\n            Err(_) => return "lock_poisoned".to_string(),\n        };\n        // FNV-1a 64-bit over frame-delimited (key, value) pairs. Each entry is\n        // wrapped in `len || bytes` frames so keys/values can never bleed into\n        // one another and the fold is canonical regardless of insertion order.\n        let mut h: u64 = FNV_OFFSET;\n        for (k, v) in m.iter() {\n            h = fnv1a(h, &(k.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());\n            h = fnv1a(h, k.as_bytes());\n            h = fnv1a(h, &(v.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());\n            h = fnv1a(h, v);\n        }\n        format!("{:016x}", h)\n    }\n}\n\n/// FNV-1a 64-bit offset basis.\n///\n/// `pub` so the kernel shim's `PgStore` can fold the SAME basis over the same\n/// `len || bytes` frames and produce roots comparable to [`InMemoryStore`].\npub const FNV_OFFSET: u64 = 0xcbf29ce484222325;\n/// FNV-1a 64-bit prime.\nconst FNV_PRIME: u64 = 0x100000001b3;\n\n/// Single-pass FNV-1a 64-bit fold. Pure, no deps.\n///\n/// `pub` so the kernel shim's `PgStore` reuses the identical fold for\n/// cross-store-comparable [`snapshot_root`](MemoryStore::snapshot_root) roots.\npub fn fnv1a(mut h: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {\n    for &b in bytes {\n        h ^= b as u64;\n        h = h.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME);\n    }\n    h\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn memory_store_put_get_roundtrip() {\n        let s = InMemoryStore::new();\n        assert!(s.get("a").is_none(), "absent key must return None");\n        s.put("a", b"hello").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.get("a").unwrap(), b"hello".to_vec());\n        // Overwrite must replace, not append.\n        s.put("a", b"world").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.get("a").unwrap(), b"world".to_vec());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn memory_store_snapshot_root_changes_on_put() {\n        let s = InMemoryStore::new();\n        let empty = s.snapshot_root();\n        s.put("k", b"v").unwrap();\n        let after_one = s.snapshot_root();\n        assert_ne!(\n            empty, after_one,\n            "snapshot root must change after the first put"\n        );\n        s.put("k2", b"v2").unwrap();\n        assert_ne!(\n            after_one,\n            s.snapshot_root(),\n            "snapshot root must change after a second put"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn memory_store_deterministic() {\n        let a = InMemoryStore::new();\n        let b = InMemoryStore::new();\n        // Different insertion order must NOT affect the content root.\n        a.put("x", b"1").unwrap();\n        a.put("y", b"2").unwrap();\n        b.put("y", b"2").unwrap();\n        b.put("x", b"1").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(\n            a.snapshot_root(),\n            b.snapshot_root(),\n            "same content ⇒ same root regardless of insertion order"\n        );\n        // A differing value must yield a differing root.\n        let c = InMemoryStore::new();\n        c.put("x", b"1").unwrap();\n        c.put("y", b"99").unwrap();\n        assert_ne!(a.snapshot_root(), c.snapshot_root());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn memory_store_keys_sorted() {\n        let s = InMemoryStore::new();\n        s.put("c", b"3").unwrap();\n        s.put("a", b"1").unwrap();\n        s.put("b", b"2").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(\n            s.keys(),\n            vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string(), "c".to_string()],\n            "keys must be returned in deterministic sorted order"\n        );\n
