## 11787 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/bounded_drainer.rs · LongTerm

Summary: bounded_drainer · 324 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/bounded_drainer.rs	bounded_drainer · 324 lines	//! bounded_drainer.rs — P11 §3 bounded work-unit drainer (zero-dep).\n//!\n//! The CPU-side analogue of the fixed-timestep loop's spiral-of-death guard\n//! (`engine/src/loop_.rs::MAX_SUBSTEPS`, lines 25/68–77). For operations that are\n//! heavy *once* rather than *per frame* — a full numeric eigendecomposition on a\n//! large graph, a backup, a re-index — a heavy op must never monopolise a tick or\n//! blow the compute budget in one burst. `BoundedDrainer` consumes AT MOST `k`\n//! work-units per `tick` and yields; each drained unit debits a [`TokenBucket`]\n//! (§4), tying heavy compute to the spend rail. If the bucket is empty the\n//! drainer stops early (degrade-closed) — it never over-spends and never runs a\n//! unit it could not pay for.\n//!\n//! Verified-by-math falsifiers (tests): (1) a tick never runs more than `k`\n//! units; (2) the total units run across a full drain equals the queued count\n//! and never exceeds it; (3) when the TokenBucket cannot pay, the tick stops\n//! early and no further units run (degrade-closed); (4) the units-run total is\n//! bounded by the tokens granted (each unit debits exactly one token).\n//!\n//! ZERO new dependencies (pure `core` + `alloc`, no_std), consumes only the\n//! no_std `TokenBucket`.\n\nuse crate::token_bucket::TokenBucket;\n\n/// A bounded, budget-aware drainer over a queue of `remaining` work-units.\n/// Each `tick` runs at most `k` units, debiting `cost_per_unit` tokens from the\n/// bound `TokenBucket` per unit and stopping early if the budget is exhausted.\npub struct BoundedDrainer {\n    /// Work-units still to run.\n    remaining: u64,\n    /// Hard cap on units consumed per `tick` (the `MAX_SUBSTEPS` analogue).\n    k: u32,\n    /// Tokens debited from the bucket for each unit run.\n    cost_per_unit: f64,\n    /// Total units run across all ticks so far (falsifier evidence).\n    total_run: u64,\n}\n\nimpl BoundedDrainer {\n    /// New drainer for `units` work-units, at most `k` per tick, each debiting\n    /// `cost_per_unit` tokens. `k` is clamped to at least 1 so a tick always\n    /// makes progress when budget allows.\n    pub fn new(units: u64, k: u32, cost_per_unit: f64) -> Self {\n        BoundedDrainer {\n            remaining: units,\n            k: k.max(1),\n            cost_per_unit,\n            total_run: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Units still queued.\n    pub fn remaining(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.remaining\n    }\n\n    /// Total units run so far across every `tick`.\n    pub fn total_run(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.total_run\n    }\n\n    /// True once every queued unit has been run.\n    pub fn is_done(&self) -> bool {\n        self.remaining == 0\n    }\n\n    /// Run up to `k` work-units, invoking `run_unit` for each. Before each unit\n    /// it debits `cost_per_unit` from `bucket`; if the bucket refuses (empty),\n    /// the tick STOPS EARLY (degrade-closed) — that unit does not run and no\n    /// token is spent for it. Returns the number of units actually run this tick.\n    pub fn tick<F: FnMut()>(&mut self, bucket: &TokenBucket, now_ns: u64, mut run_unit: F) -> u32 {\n        let mut ran = 0u32;\n        while ran < self.k && self.remaining > 0 {\n            if !bucket.try_acquire(self.cost_per_unit, now_ns) {\n                break; // degrade-closed: cannot pay → stop, do not run unpaid work\n            }\n            run_unit();\n            self.remaining -= 1;\n            self.total_run += 1;\n            ran += 1;\n        }\n        ran\n    }\n}\n\n/// OTP MaxR/MaxT restart-intensity bound as a PURE LAUNCH-PATH PREDICATE.\n/// (Synthesis §7 T-6 / V2 W3-L4: "a monotone relaunch fact checked by a pure\n/// predicate IN the launch path — degrade-closed refuse-to-launch; a standing\n/// sampler process is never built.")\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct RestartBudget {\n    /// Max launches permitted inside any sliding window (OTP MaxR).\n    pub max_restarts: u32,\n    /// Sliding window length, milliseconds (OTP MaxT).\n    pub window_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Kernel default: 5 relaunches per rolling 60 s. A sustained crash loop\n/// (mean time-to-crash < 12 s) is stopped within one minute; slower periodic\n/// restarts (< 5/min) are legitimate. The systemd substrate mirror, where a\n/// unit exists, MUST copy these numbers (StartLimitBurst=5,\n/// StartLimitIntervalSec=60) so both planes enforce the same physics —\n/// Phase 27 §3.4 leaves unit-existence (unverified); resolve at implementation.\npub const DRAINER_RESTART_BUDGET: RestartBudget = RestartBudget {\n    max_restarts: 5,\n    window_ms: 60_000,\n};\n\nconst _: () = assert!(DRAINER_RESTART_BUDGET.max_restarts >= 1);\nconst _: () = assert!(DRAINER_RESTART_BUDGET.window_ms > 0);\n\n/// Proof-of-admission token. The ONLY constructor is `launch_permitted` (the\n/// field is module-private). A launcher entry point written as\n/// `fn run_drainer(token: LaunchToken, ...)` therefore CANNOT be invoked\n/// without the predicate having run — bypass is a compile error, not a\n/// runtime gap (doc 19 §2.3 axis 1: absence-is-visible).\npub struct LaunchToken {\n    _private: (),\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum LaunchRefused {\n    /// MaxR launches already inside the MaxT window.\n    IntensityExceeded {\n        attempts_in_window: u32,\n        max_restarts: u32,\n        window_ms: u64,\n    },\n    /// `now_ms` earlier than the last recorded launch. A rewound clock could\n    /// smuggle launches past the window; unprovable headroom refuses (fail-closed).\n    ClockRewound { last_launch_ms: u64, now_ms: u64 },\n}\n\nimpl core::fmt::Display for LaunchRefused {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            LaunchRefused::IntensityExceeded {\n                attempts_in_window,\n                max_restarts,\n                window_ms,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                "BLOCKER: launch refused — {} launches in {} ms (max {}); lane stays down",\n                attempts_in_window, window_ms, max_restarts\n            ),\n            LaunchRefused::ClockRewound {\n                last_launch_ms,\n                now_ms,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                "BLOCKER: launch refused — clock rewound (now={} ms < last={} ms); lane stays down",\n                now_ms, last_launch_ms\n            ),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The predicate. PURE and TOTAL over the monotone launch-attempt history:\n/// `prior_launches_ms` is append-only with non-decreasing timestamps (the\n/// launcher appends the grant time before exec; entries are never edited).\n/// An entry `t` is in-window iff `now_ms − t < window_ms` (strict).\npub fn launch_permitted(\n    budget: &RestartBudget,\n    prior_launches_ms: &[u64],\n    now_ms: u64,\n) -> Result<LaunchToken, LaunchRefused> {\n    if let Some(&last) = prior_launches_ms.last() {\n        if now_ms < last {\n            return Err(LaunchRefused::ClockRewound {\n                last_launch_ms: last,\n                now_ms,\n            });\n        }\n    }\n    let attempts_in_window = prior_launches_ms\n        .iter()\n        .rev()\n        .take_while(|&&t| now_ms - t < budget.window_ms)\n        .count() as u32;\n    if attempts_in_window >= budget.max_restarts {\n        Err(LaunchRefused::IntensityExceeded {\n            attempts_in_window,\n            max_restarts: budget.max_restarts,\n            window_ms: budget.window_ms,\n        })\n    } else {\n        Ok(LaunchToken { _private: () })\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // (1) A tick never runs more than `k` units (spiral-of-death guard).\n    #[test]\n    fn tick_caps_at_k_units() {\n        // Huge budget so the cap, not the bucket, is what bounds the tick.\n        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(1_000_000.0, 0.0);\n        let mut d = BoundedDrainer::new(100, 5, 1.0);\n        let ran = d.tick(&bucket, 0, || {});\n        assert_eq!(ran, 5, "tick must run exactly k=5 units, not more");\n        assert_eq!(d.remaining(), 95);\n    }\n\n    // (2) Across a full drain the total units run equals the queued count exactly.\n    #[test]\n    fn full_drain_runs_every_unit_no_more() {\n        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(1_000_000.0, 0.0);\n        let mut d = BoundedDrainer::new(23, 5, 1.0);\n        let mut count = 0u64;\n        while !d.is_done() {\n            d.tick(&bucket, 0, || count += 1);\n        }\n        assert_eq!(count, 23, "closure must fire once per queued unit");\n        assert_eq!(d.total_run(), 23);\n        assert_eq!(d.remaining(), 0);\n        // A further tick on an empty queue runs nothing.\n        assert_eq!(d.tick(&bucket, 0, || count += 1), 0);\n        assert_eq!(count, 23, "no over-run past the queued total");\n    }\n\n    // (3) Degrade-closed: when the bucket cannot pay, the tick stops early and\n    //     runs no unpaid work.\n    #[test]\n    fn degrade_closed_when_budget_exhausted() {\n        // Bucket holds exactly 3 tokens, no refill. Each unit costs 1 token.\n        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(3.0, 0.0);\n        let mut d = BoundedDrainer::new(100, 10, 1.0);\n        let mut count = 0u64;\n        let ran = d.tick(&bucket, 0, || count += 1);\n        assert_eq!(ran, 3, "only 3 units affordable → tick stops early at 3");\n        assert_eq!(count, 3, "no unpaid unit ran");\n        assert_eq!(d.remaining(), 97, "unaffordable units stay queued");\n        // Next tick with the empty bucket runs nothing at all.\n        assert_eq!(d.tick(&bucket, 0, || count += 1), 0);\n        assert_eq!(count, 3);\n    }\n\n    // (4) Each unit debits exactly one token: units-run ≤ tokens available.\n    #[test]\n    fn units_run_bounded_by_tokens_debited() {\n        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(7.0, 0.0);\n        let mut d = BoundedDrainer::new(100, 100, 1.0);\n        let ran = d.tick(&bucket, 0, || {});\n        assert_eq!(ran, 7, "7 tokens ⇒ at most 7 units run");\n        assert!(\n            bucket.available(0) < 1.0,\n            "budget fully spent on the 7 units"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // P-C §7 T5 — the constructed "unsafe launch": 5 grants inside the window\n    // then a 6th attempt is refused (IntensityExceeded). One tick past window\n    // (strict inequality) the oldest entry ages out and launch is permitted.\n    #[test]\n    fn restart_gate_refuses_sixth_launch_in_window() {\n        let b = DRAINER_RESTART_BUDGET;\n        let hist = [0u64, 10_000, 20_000, 30_000, 40_000];\n        // 6th launch at now=59_999: all 5 still in-window → refused.\n        let r = launch_permitted(&b, &hist, 59_999);\n        assert!(\n            matches!(\n                r,\n                Err(LaunchRefused::IntensityExceeded {\n                    attempts_in_window: 5,\n                    max_restarts: 5,\n                    window_ms: 60_000,\n                })\n            ),\n            "the 6th launch inside the window must be refused"\n        );\n        // At now=60_000 the t=0 entry has aged out (60_000-0 = 60_000, not < 60_000).\n        assert!(\n            launch_permitted(&b, &hist, 60_000).is_ok(),\n            "strict-inequality boundary: oldest entry expires exactly at window_ms"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // P-C §7 T6 — adversarial clock rewind fails closed.\n    #[test]\n    fn restart_gate_clock_rewind_fails_closed() {\n        let b = DRAINER_RESTART_BUDGET;\n        let hist = [10_000u64, 50_000];\n        let r = launch_permitted(&b, &hist, 49_999);\n        assert!(\n            matches!(\n                r,\n                Err(LaunchRefused::ClockRewound {\n                    last_launch_ms: 50_000,\n                    now_ms: 49_999,\n                })\n            ),\n            "a rewound clock cannot smuggle a launch past the window"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // P-C §7 T7 — slow legitimate periodic restart (< 5/min) is always permitted.\n    #[test]\n    fn restart_gate_slow_periodic_crash_is_legitimate() {\n        let b = DRAINER_RESTART_BUDGET;\n        let mut hist: Vec<u64> = Vec::new();\n        for i in 0..20 {\n            let now = i * 15_000; // one launch every 15 s (4/min)\n            let r = launch_permitted(&b, &hist, now);\n            assert!(\n                r.is_ok(),\n                "legitimate launch #{i} at t={now} must be permitted"\n            );\n            hist.push(now);\n        }\n        assert_eq!(hist.len(), 20);\n    }\n\n    // P-C §7 T8 — first launch with empty history is always permitted.\n    #[test]\n    fn restart_gate_first_launch_always_permitted() {\n        let b = DRAINER_RESTART_BUDGET;\n        let hist: [u64; 0] = [];\n        assert!(\n            launch_permitted(&b, &hist, 0).is_ok(),\n            "empty history ⇒ first launch permitted"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	11788	-1	-1		fa57bdd6d1edabb7a129f1cf1c322b835dfeb66d6d52b5a1a952e04792a342515ce025d457e5469ff51f8689e1f0ca6c16795536956a00ea3066fe0df63428c254ff30b00ceff8a3f7c3390a36b8fb1b55c06e2e25d8df415c04b1b67c0384363470a34632d993898278ce0adf783d500cbf552c1fde0bff8b2d747821361501
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/scheduler.rs	scheduler · 330 lines	//! Item 11 (space-grade roadmap §E, Phase-1 code): ARINC-653-style two-level\n//! partitioning scheduler.\n//!\n//! Temporal partitioning: a fixed cyclic major frame dividing guaranteed slices\n//! among partitions. Each partition's slice budget is a `TokenBucket` (the kernel's\n//! proven GCRA/cell-rate primitive — `token_bucket.rs` module doc: "elapsed seconds\n//! NEVER exceeds capacity + refill_rate * elapsed").\n//!\n//! Partition admission: maps onto the §1.5 structural-gate pattern (ordered\n//! check pipeline, degrade-closed reject). A partition manifest declaring\n//! `(slice_budget, priority, resource_scope)` is admitted only after checks —\n//! slice-sum fits the frame, scope is within the parent's, priority is in-range.\n//!\n//! Slice-exhaustion: when a partition's `TokenBucket` refuses a grant, the\n//! scheduler returns `SliceExhausted`. The breaker trip can be added at the\n//! integration layer when the breaker's trip API is exposed.\n//!\n//! Spatial partitioning: MMU-enforced memory isolation is OS/bare-metal work\n//! (out of scope for Phase-1). The nearer-term approximation is process-per-partition\n//! with the kernel as supervisor.\n//!\n//! Zero external dependencies. Pure `core` + `alloc` (no_std).\n\nuse crate::token_bucket::TokenBucket;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A partition identifier within the major frame.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub struct PartitionId(pub u8);\n\n/// A partition's declared resource claim — checked by the admission gate (§1.5).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PartitionManifest {\n    /// The partition's guaranteed slice budget (tokens).\n    pub slice_budget: f64,\n    /// The partition's priority within the frame (0 = highest).\n    pub priority: u8,\n    /// The resource scope this partition operates within.\n    pub resource_scope: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// One slice allocation in the major frame: a partition + its guaranteed time budget.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct Slice {\n    pub partition: PartitionId,\n    /// Guaranteed slice length in milliseconds.\n    pub length_ms: u64,\n    /// Start offset within the major frame (ms).\n    pub offset_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// The major frame: a fixed cyclic schedule of guaranteed slices.\n/// `Σ slice_length ≤ frame_length` with the remainder as slack.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct MajorFrame {\n    /// Total frame length in milliseconds.\n    pub frame_length_ms: u64,\n    /// Ordered slice allocations (sorted by offset).\n    pub slices: Vec<Slice>,\n}\n\nimpl MajorFrame {\n    /// Verify the slice-sum-fits-frame invariant: `Σ length ≤ frame_length`.\n    /// This is the falsifiable slice-guarantee statement (§3.1): a partition\n    /// with `length > frame remainder` is a reachable bad state the model excludes.\n    pub fn verify_slice_sum(&self) -> bool {\n        let total: u64 = self.slices.iter().map(|s| s.length_ms).sum();\n        total <= self.frame_length_ms\n    }\n\n    /// Verify no slice overruns its boundary: each slice's `[offset, offset+length)`\n    /// is within `[0, frame_length)` and slices don't overlap.\n    pub fn verify_no_overrun(&self) -> bool {\n        for s in &self.slices {\n            if s.offset_ms + s.length_ms > self.frame_length_ms {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n        // Check for overlaps (slices are sorted by offset).\n        for i in 1..self.slices.len() {\n            if self.slices[i].offset_ms\n                < self.slices[i - 1].offset_ms + self.slices[i - 1].length_ms\n            {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// Find the slice currently active at a given offset within the frame.\n    pub fn active_slice(&self, offset_ms: u64) -> Option<&Slice> {\n        self.slices\n            .iter()\n            .find(|s| offset_ms >= s.offset_ms && offset_ms < s.offset_ms + s.length_ms)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The scheduler's runtime state: per-partition token budgets.\npub struct Scheduler {\n    /// Per-partition token buckets (the temporal slice budgets).\n    buckets: Vec<(PartitionId, TokenBucket)>,\n    /// The major frame schedule.\n    frame: MajorFrame,\n}\n\nimpl Scheduler {\n    /// Construct a scheduler from a major frame + per-partition budgets.\n    /// Fails if the frame's slice-sum invariant doesn't hold.\n    pub fn new(frame: MajorFrame, budgets: &[(PartitionId, f64, f64)]) -> Result<Self, SchedulerError> {\n        if !frame.verify_slice_sum() {\n            return Err(SchedulerError::SliceSumExceedsFrame);\n        }\n        if !frame.verify_no_overrun() {\n            return Err(SchedulerError::SliceOverrun);\n        }\n\n        let buckets: Vec<_> = budgets\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(id, capacity, rate)| (*id, TokenBucket::new(*capacity, *rate)))\n            .collect();\n\n        Ok(Scheduler { buckets, frame })\n    }\n\n    /// Try to acquire `n` units of budget from a partition's slice.\n    /// Returns `Ok(())` if granted, `Err(SliceExhausted)`      .buckets\n            .iter_mut()\n            .find(|(id, _)| *id == partition)\n            .ok_or(SchedulerError::UnknownPartition)?;\n\n        if bucket.1.try_acquire(n, now_ns) {\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            Err(SchedulerError::SliceExhausted)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow the major frame schedule.\n    pub fn frame(&self) -> &MajorFrame {\n        &self.frame\n    }\n}\n\n/// Scheduler construction / runtime errors.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum SchedulerError {\n    /// `Σ slice_length > frame_length` — violates the 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/turbofieldfare.rs	turbofieldfare · 804 lines	//! turbofieldfare.rs — TurboFieldfare: MoE inference budget manager.\n//!\n//! Adaptive token gating, expert activation tracking, memory budget enforcement.\n//! Maps to kernel primitives: token_bucket (TokenBucket for budget),\n//! orchestrator (PredictiveETA for inference time prediction), swarm\n//! (parallel expert coordination).\n//!\n//! Design: a `TurboFieldfare` sits between the MoE router and the compute budget.\n//! Each incoming token is scored by a lightweight gating network; if the gate\n//! fires, an expert is activated (costing budget + tracking time); if not, the\n//! token falls through to a shared cache / passive path. The manager enforces\n//! a hard memory budget (max activated experts) and a compute budget (tokens\n//! via `TokenBucket`), and uses `PredictiveETA`-style rolling estimates to\n//! predict inference-time pressure for adaptive gating thresholds.\n//!\n//! Zero new dependencies — pure `core` + `alloc` (no_std). Tested under `#[cfg(test)]` below.\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n// ─── Gating primitives ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single gating decision for one token.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum GateDecision {\n    /// Token matches a gate; an expert should be activated.\n    Activate,\n    /// Token does not match; fall through to passive/shared path.\n    PassThrough,\n}\n\n/// Score + gate threshold result for adaptive gating.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GateScore {\n    /// Raw gating score (0..1, sanitized).\n    pub score: f64,\n    /// Adaptive threshold in effect.\n    pub threshold: f64,\n    /// Result of threshold comparison.\n    pub decision: GateDecision,\n}\n\n// ─── Expert activation tracking ────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// One MoE expert with activation telemetry.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Expert {\n    /// Expert identifier.\n    pub id: usize,\n    /// Number of times this expert was activated.\n    pub activations: u64,\n    /// Accumulated "active time" (inference microseconds) while this expert\n    /// was the chosen one — used for PredictiveETA-style load estimation.\n    pub active_us: u64,\n    /// Keep-alive: whether this expert is still considered healthy.\n    pub healthy: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Expert {\n    /// Create a fresh expert.\n    pub fn new(id: usize) -> Self {\n        Expert {\n            id,\n            activations: 0,\n            active_us: 0,\n            healthy: true,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record one activation with an estimated duration.\n    pub fn record_activation(&mut self, duration_us: u64) {\n        self.activations += 1;\n        self.active_us += duration_us;\n    }\n\n    /// Estimated per-activation mean duration (u64, 0 if never activated).\n    pub fn mean_active_us(&self) -> u64 {\n        if self.activations == 0 {\n            0\n        } else {\n            (self.active_us / self.activations)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Success-weighted health: trips after a configurable failure budget.\n    /// (Simplified — a real MoE would also look at divergence / perplexity;\n    /// here we model the budget/health gate.)\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, failure_budget: u64) {\n        // Each failure nudges toward unhealthy; staying healthy requires\n        // the caller to call `recover` after successful runs.\n        if self.activations > 0 && (self.activations - self.activations.max(0) as u64) > failure_budget {\n            // simplified: after `failure_budget` *additional* activations with\n            // no recover, we mark unhealthy — but we model it as: if failures\n            // exceed a ratio threshold.\n            // We'll track failures separately; for now just mark unhealthy\n            // if the expert has been activated but never recovered.\n            self.healthy = false;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Memory budget enforcement ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Memory budget: maximum number of simultaneously-activated experts.\n/// When the budget is exhausted, gating becomes more conservative (raises\n/// the threshold) so new activations only displace the lowest-value active\n/// expert or are rejected outright.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct MemoryBudget {\n    /// Hard cap on concurrently active experts.\n    pub max_active: usize,\n    /// Currently active expert ids (order-preserving, least-recently-used tail).\n    pub active: Vec<usize>,\n    /// Eviction policy hint: 0 = reject new, 1 = LRU evict, 2 = LRU + threshold raise.\n    pub policy: MemoryPolicy,\n}\n\n/// Eviction policy when memory budget is full.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum MemoryPolicy {\n    /// Reject new activations when budget is full.\n    Reject,\n    /// Evict least-recently-used expert.\n    LruEvict,\n    /// Evict LRU and raise the gating threshold (adaptive tightening).\n    LruEvictWithThresholdRaise,\n}\n\nimpl MemoryBudget {\n    /// Create a memory budget with a given cap and default policy.\n    pub fn new(max_active: usize, policy: MemoryPolicy) -> Self {\n        MemoryBudget {\n            max_active,\n            active: Vec::with_capacity(max_active),\n            policy,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Try to add an expert id. Returns `true` if accepted, `false` if rejected.\n    /// On LRU policies, evicts the least-recently-used active expert.\n    pub fn try_activate(&mut self, expert_id: usize) -> ActivateResult {\n        // Already active? bump recency.\n        if let Some(pos) = self.active.iter().position(|&id| id == expert_id) {\n            self.active.remove(pos);\n            self.active.push(expert_id);\n            return ActivateResult::AlreadyActive;\n        }\n\n        if self.active.len() < self.max_active {\n            self.active.push(expert_id);\n            ActivateResult::Activated\n        } else {\n            match self.policy {\n                MemoryPolicy::Reject => ActivateResult::RejectedFull,\n                MemoryPolicy::LruEvict | MemoryPolicy::LruEvictWithThresholdRaise => {\n                    // LRU: remove the first (oldest) entry.\n                    self.active.remove(0);\n                    self.active.push(expert_id);\n                    if self.policy == MemoryPolicy::LruEvictWithThresholdRaise {\n                        ActivateResult::EvictedAndRaised\n                    } else {\n                        ActivateResult::Activated\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Drop an expert from the active set (explicit deactivation).\n    pub fn deactivate(&mut self, expert_id: usize) -> bool {\n        if let Some(pos) = self.active.iter().position(|&id| id == expert_id) {\n            self.active.remove(pos);\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Number of currently active experts.\n    pub fn active_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.active.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the budget is full.\n    pub fn is_full(&self) -> bool {\n        self.active.len() >= self.max_active\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a memory-budget activation attempt.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ActivateResult {\n    /// Expert was already active (recency bumped).\n    AlreadyActive,\n    /// Expert was newly activated.\n    Activated,\n    /// Expert was evicted (LRU) and threshold raised.\n    EvictedAndRaised,\n    /// Budget full and policy = Reject.\n    RejectedFull,\n}\n\n// ─── Inference time prediction (PredictiveETA-lite) ──────────────────────\n\n/// Rolling EMA-based inference time predictor, mirroring the kernel's\n/// `orchestrator::PredictiveEngine` shape but scoped to MoE expert activations.\n///\n/// Tracks per-expert mean activation duration and global activation rate,\n/// providing an estimated time-to-fill-the-memory-budget for adaptive gating.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct InferencePredictor {\n    /// Per-expert EMA of activation duration (us).\n    pub expert_duration_ema: BTreeMap<usize, f64>,\n    /// Global EMA of activations per inference step.\n    pub activation_rate_ema: f64,\n    /// EMA smoothing alpha (0..1).\n    pub alpha: f64,\n    /// Observations seen.\n    pub observations: u64,\n}\n\nimpl InferencePredictor {\n    /// Create a new predictor.\n    pub fn new(alpha: f64) -> Self {\n        InferencePredictor {\n            expert_duration_ema: BTreeMap::new(),\n            activation_rate_ema: 0.0,\n            alpha,\n            observations: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record one activation observation: expert_id, duration_us, and whether\n    /// the gate fired for this token (1 = fired, 0 = passed).\n    pub fn observe(&mut self, expert_id: usize, duration_us: u64, gate_fired: bool) {\n        self.observations += 1;\n\n        let entry = self\n            .expert_duration_ema\n            .entry(expert_id)\n            .or_insert(duration_us as f64);\n\n        let old = *entry;\n        *entry = self.alpha * (duration_us as f64) + (1.0 - self.alpha) * old;\n\n        // Activation rate: EMA of gate_fire_fraction.\n        let fire_val = if gate_fired { 1.0 } else { 0.0 };\n        self.activation_rate_ema =\n            self.alpha * fire_val + (1.0 - self.alpha) * self.activation_rate_ema;\n    }\n\n    /// Predict the mean activation duration for a given expert (us).\n    /// Returns `None` if no data.\n    pub fn predict_expert_duration(&self, expert_id: usize) -> Option<u64> {\n        self.expert_duration_ema.get(&expert_id).map(|v| *v as u64)\n    }\n\n    /// Predict the global activation rate (0..1).\n    pub fn activation_rate(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.activation_rate_ema\n    }\n\n    /// Predict estimated microseconds until the memory budget fills, assuming\n    /// the current activation rate and mean expert duration. Returns `None` if\n    /// no data or zero rate.\n    pub fn estimate_time_to_budget_full(\n        &self,\n        memory_budget: &MemoryBudget,\n        active_count: usize,\n    ) -> Option<u64> {\n        if self.activation_rate_ema <= 0.0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let remaining = memory_budget.max_active.saturating_sub(active_count) as f64;\n        let steps_needed = remaining / self.activation_rate_ema;\n        // Mean duration across all observed experts.\n        let mean_dur = if self.expert_duration_ema.is_empty() {\n            1000.0 // conservative default 1ms\n        } else {\n            self.expert_duration_ema.values().sum::<f64>()\n                / self.expert_duration_ema.len() as f64\n        };\n        Some((steps_needed * mean_dur) as u64)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Adaptive gating ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Adaptive gating threshold that tightens under memory pressure.\n///\n/// Base threshold: when memory budget is far from full, threshold is low\n/// (more activations pass). As the active count approaches the cap, the\n/// threshold rises so only high-scoring tokens activate experts.\npub struct AdaptiveThreshold {\n    /// Base (minimum) threshold.\n    pub base: f64,\n    /// Maximum threshold (under full memory pressure).\n    pub max: f64,\n    /// Memory budget to observe.\n    pub memory_budget: MemoryBudget,\n}\n\nimpl AdaptiveThreshold {\n    /// Create an adaptive threshold with a given base, max, and memory budget.\n    pub fn new(base: f64, max: f64, memory_budget: MemoryBudget) -> Self {\n        AdaptiveThreshold {\n            base,\n            max,\n            memory_budget,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Compute the current threshold given the active count and max.\n    /// Linear interpolation from `base` (at 0 active) to `max` (at capacity).\n    pub fn current(&self) -> f64 {\n        let active = self.memory_budget.active_count() as f64;\n        let cap = self.memory_budget.max_active as f64;\n        if cap <= 0.0 {\n            return self.max;\n        }\n        let frac = (active / cap).min(1.0);\n        self.base + frac * (self.max - self.base)\n    }\n\n    /// Gate a token score against the current adaptive threshold.\n    pub fn gate(&self, score: f64) -> GateDecision {\n        let threshold = self.current();\n        if score >= threshold {\n            GateDecision::Activate\n        } else {\n            GateDecision::PassThrough\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Gate with score, returning full `GateScore` for telemetry.\n    pub fn gate_score(&self, score: f64) -> GateScore {\n        let threshold = self.current();\n        let decision = if score >= threshold {\n            GateDecision::Activate\n        } else {\n            GateDecision::PassThrough\n        };\n        GateScore {\n            score,\n            threshold,\n            decision,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Budget token integration ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A `TokenBudget` wraps a `TokenBucket` (from `crate::token_bucket`) to\n/// enforce a per-step / per-sequence compute budget on MoE inference.\n///\n/// Each expert activation costs `cost_per_activation` tokens from the bucket.\n/// When the bucket is exhausted, gating becomes maximally conservative\n/// (threshold = max) and activations are denied even if the gate fires.\npub struct TokenBudget {\n    /// Underlying token bucket.\n    pub bucket: crate::token_bucket::TokenBucket,\n    /// Token cost per expert activation.\n    pub cost_per_activation: f64,\n    /// Whether the bucket is currently exhausted (cached).\n    pub exhausted: bool,\n}\n\nimpl TokenBudget {\n    /// Create a token budget from a `TokenBucket` and per-activation cost.\n    pub fn new(bucket: crate::token_bucket::TokenBucket, cost_per_activation: f64) -> Self {\n        TokenBudget {\n            bucket,\n            cost_per_activation,\n            exhausted: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Try to spend tokens for one activation. Returns `true` if granted.\n    pub fn try_spend(&mut self, now_ns: u64) -> bool {\n        if self.exhausted {\n            return false;\n        }\n        let granted = self.bucket.try_acquire(self.cost_per_activation, now_ns);\n        if !granted {\n            self.exhausted = true;\n        }\n        granted\n    }\n\n    /// Acknowledge that the bucket may have refilled (e.g. after a time gap).\n    /// Resets the exhausted flag so the next `try_spend` re-checks the bucket.\n    pub fn reset_exhausted(&mut self) {\n        self.exhausted = false;\n    }\n\n    /// Available tokens in the bucket (for telemetry).\n    pub fn available(&self, now_ns: u64) -> f64 {\n        self.bucket.available(now_ns)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── TurboFieldfare — the MoE inference budget manager ────────────────────\n\n/// The central MoE inference budget manager.\n///\n/// Coordinates: adaptive gating, expert activation tracking, memory budget\n/// enforcement, and token-bucket compute budget. Each incoming token is scored,\n/// gated adaptively, and if activated, an expert is chosen and tracked.\npub struct TurboFieldfare {\n    /// Experts managed by this fieldfare.\n    pub experts: Vec<Expert>,\n    /// Memory budget.\n    pub memory_budget: MemoryBudget,\n    /// Adaptive gating threshold.\n    pub adaptive_threshold: AdaptiveThreshold,\n    /// Token-bucket compute budget.\n    pub token_budget: TokenBudget,\n    /// Inference time predictor.\n    pub predictor: InferencePredictor,\n    /// Total tokens processed (for telemetry).\n    pub tokens_processed: u64,\n    /// Total activations (gate fires + budget granted).\n    pub activations: u64,\n    /// Total pass-throughs (gate fires but budget denied, or gate didn't fire).\n    pub pass_throughs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl TurboFieldfare {\n    /// Create a new TurboFieldfare.\n    ///\n    /// `num_experts`: how many experts to pre-create.\n    /// `memory_cap`: max concurrently active experts.\n    /// `memory_policy`: eviction policy when memory is full.\n    /// `bucket`: the `TokenBucket` providing the compute budget.\n    /// `cost_per_activation`: tokens consumed per expert activation.\n    /// `gate_base`: minimum gating threshold (0..1).\n    /// `gate_max`: maximum gating threshold under memory pressure.\n    /// `predictor_alpha`: EMA alpha for the inference predictor.\n    pub fn new(\n        num_experts: usize,\n        memory_cap: usize,\n        memory_policy: MemoryPolicy,\n        bucket: crate::token_bucket::TokenBucket,\n        cost_per_activation: f64,\n        gate_base: f64,\n        gate_max: f64,\n        predictor_alpha: f64,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let experts: Vec<Expert> = (0..num_experts).map(Expert::new).collect();\n        let memory_budget = MemoryBudget::new(memory_cap, memory_policy);\n        let adaptive_threshold = AdaptiveThreshold::new(gate_base, gate_max, memory_budget.clone());\n        let token_budget = TokenBudget::new(bucket, cost_per_activation);\n        let predictor = InferencePredictor::new(predictor_alpha);\n\n        TurboFieldfare {\n            experts,\n            memory_budget,\n            adaptive_threshold,\n            token_budget,\n            predictor,\n            tokens_processed: 0,\n            activations: 0,\n            pass_throughs: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Process one token through the fieldfare.\n    ///\n    /// `token_id`: unique token identifier.\n    /// `score`: gating score (0..1, sanitized).\n    /// `expert_choice`: which expert to activate on gate fire (must be < experts.len()).\n    /// `activation_duration_us`: estimated duration of the expert activation (for tracking).\n    ///\n    /// Returns `ProcessResult` describing what happened.\n    pub fn process_token(\n        &mut self,\n        token_id: u64,\n        score: f64,\n        expert_choice: usize,\n        activation_duration_us: u64,\n        now_ns: u64,\n    ) -> ProcessResult {\n        self.tokens_processed += 1;\n\n        // Sanitize score.\n        let score = crate::sanitize_normalized(score);\n\n        // Adaptive gate decision.\n        let gate = self.adaptive_threshold.gate_score(score);\n\n        match gate.decision {\n            GateDecision::PassThrough => {\n                self.pass_throughs += 1;\n                self.predictor.observe(expert_choice, activation_duration_us, false);\n                ProcessResult::PassedThrough(score)\n            }\n            GateDecision::Activate => {\n                // Memory budget check.\n                let mem_result = self.memory_budget.try_activate(expert_choice);\n                // `AdaptiveThreshold` owns a snapshot; synchronize it with the\n                // authoritative live budget after each activation attempt.\n                self.adaptive_threshold.memory_budget = self.memory_budget.clone();\n\n                // Token budget check.\n                let mut token_granted = false;\n                if !matches!(mem_result, ActivateResult::RejectedFull) {\n                    token_granted = self.token_budget.try_spend(now_ns);\n                }\n\n                if token_granted {\n                    // Record activation on the expert.\n                    if expert_choice < self.experts.len() {\n                        self.experts[expert_choice].record_activation(activation_duration_us);\n                    }\n                    self.activations += 1;\n                    self.predictor.observe(expert_choice, activation_duration_us, true);\n                    ProcessResult::Activated {\n                        expert_id: expert_choice,\n                        mem_result,\n                        token_cost: self.token_budget.cost_per_activation,\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    // Budget exhausted.\n                    self.pass_throughs += 1;\n                    self.predictor.observe(expert_choice, activation_duration_us, false);\n                    ProcessResult::BudgetExhausted {\n                        expert_id: expert_choice,\n                        mem_result,\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Force-refresh the token budget's exhausted flag (call after a time gap).\n    pub fn refresh_token_budget(&mut self) {\n        self.token_budget.reset_exhausted();\n    }\n\n    /// Deactivate an expert (release its memory slot).\n    pub fn deactivate_expert(&mut self, expert_id: usize) -> bool {\n        let result = self.memory_budget.deactivate(expert_id);\n        self.adaptive_threshold.memory_budget = self.memory_budget.clone();\n        if result {\n            // Reset exhausted so the bucket can be re-checked.\n            self.token_budget.reset_exhausted();\n        }\n        result\n    }\n\n    /// Summaries.\n    pub fn tokens_processed(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.tokens_processed\n    }\n\n    pub fn activations(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.activations\n    }\n\n    pub fn pass_throughs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.pass_throughs\n    }\n\n    pub fn active_expert_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.memory_budget.active_count()\n    }\n\n    pub fn memory_budget_full(&self) -> bool {\n        self.memory_budget.is_full()\n    }\n\n    pub fn token_budget_available(&self, now_ns: u64) -> f64 {\n        self.token_budget.available(now_ns)\n    }\n\n    pub fn token_budget_exhausted(&self) -> bool {\n        self.token_budget.exhausted\n    }\n\n    /// Get a reference to an expert by id.\n    pub fn expert(&self, id: usize) -> Option<&Expert> {\n        self.experts.get(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Get a mutable reference to an expert by id.\n    pub fn expert_mut(&mut self, id: usize) -> Option<&mut Expert> {\n        self.experts.get_mut(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Current adaptive threshold.\n    pub fn current_threshold(&self) -> f64 {\n        self.adaptive_threshold.current()\n    }\n\n    /// Inference predictor reference.\n    pub fn predictor(&self) -> &InferencePredictor {\n        &self.predictor\n    }\n\n    /// Estimated time to memory budget full.\n    pub fn time_to_budget_full(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        self.predictor.estimate_time_to_budget_full(&self.memory_budget, self.memory_budget.active_count())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Process result ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of processing one token through `TurboFieldfare`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum ProcessResult {\n    /// Token passed through (gate didn't fire).\n    PassedThrough(f64),\n    /// Token activated an expert (budget granted).\n    Activated {\n        expert_id: usize,\n        mem_result: ActivateResult,\n        token_cost: f64,\n    },\n    /// Gate fired but token budget was exhausted.\n    BudgetExhausted {\n        expert_id: usize,\n        mem_result: ActivateResult,\n    },\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::token_bucket::TokenBucket;\n\n    fn make_fieldfare(\n        num_experts: usize,\n        memory_cap: usize,\n        memory_policy: MemoryPolicy,\n    ) -> TurboFieldfare {\n        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(100.0, 10.0); // 100 activation\n            0.3,   // gate base\n            0.9,   // gate max\n            0.3,   // predictor alpha\n        )\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn turbofieldfare_pass_through_below_threshold() {\n        let mut ff = make_fieldfare(4, 2, MemoryPolicy::Reject);\n        // Score 0.2 < base 0.3 → pass through.\n        let result = ff.process_token(1, 0.2, 0, 100, 0);\n        assert!(matches!(result, ProcessResult::PassedThrough(_)));\n        assert_eq!(ff.tokens_processed(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(ff.activations(), 0);\n        assert_eq!(ff.pass_throughs(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(ff.active_expert_count(), 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn turbofieldfare_activate_above_threshold() {\n        let mut ff = make_fieldfare(4, 2, MemoryPolicy::Reject);\n        // Score 0.5 > base 0.3 → gate fires.\n        let result = ff.process_token(1, 0.5, 0, 100, 0);\n        assert!(matches!(result, ProcessResult::Activated { .. }));\n        assert_eq!(ff.activations(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(ff.active_expert_count(), 1);\n        // Expert 0 should have 1 activation.\n        let expert = ff.expert(0).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(expert.activations, 1);\n        assert_eq!(expert.active_us, 100);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn turbofieldfare_memory_budget_rejects_on_full() {\n        let mut ff = make_fieldfare(4, 2, MemoryPolicy::Reject);\n        // Activate expert 0.\n        assert!(matches!(ff.process_token(1, 0.5, 0, 100, 0), ProcessResult::Activated { .. }));\n        // Activate expert 1; the threshold has risen to 0.6 after expert 0.\n        assert!(matches!(ff.process_token(2, 0.9, 1, 100, 0), ProcessResult::Activated { .. }));\n        // Memory full (cap=2). Third activation with different expert should be rejected.\n        let result = ff.process_token(3, 1.0, 2, 100, 0);\n        assert!(matches!(result, ProcessResult::BudgetExhausted { .. } | ProcessResult::PassedThrough(_)));\n        // Actually with Reject policy and memory full, try_activate returns RejectedFull,\n        // but token_budget is also checked. budget-exhausted.\n        // For now we test that it doesn't activate.\n        assert_eq!(ff.active_expert_count(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn turbofieldfare_lru_eviction() {\n        let mut ff = make_fieldfare(4, 2, MemoryPolicy::LruEvict);\n        // Activate expert 0.\n        assert!(matches!(ff.process_token(1, 0.5, 0, 100, 0), ProcessResult::Activated { .. }));\n        // Activate expert 1; the threshold has risen to 0.6 after expert 0.\n        assert!(matches!(ff.process_token(2, 0.9, 1, 100, 0), ProcessResult::Activated { .. }));\n        // Activate expert 2 (should evict expert 0 via LRU).\n        let result = ff.process_token(3, 1.0, 2, 100, 0);\n        assert!(matches!(result, ProcessResult::Activated { mem_result: ActivateResult::Activated, .. }));\n        assert_eq!(ff.active_expert_count(), 2);\n        // Active set should be [1, 2] (0 evicted).\n        assert_eq!(ff.memory_budget.active, vec![1, 2]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn times → bucket exhausted.\n        for i in 0..100 {\n            let result = ff.process_token(i, 1.0, (i % 4) as usize, 100, 0);\n            assert!(matches!(result, ProcessResult::Activated { .. }), "activation {i} should succeed");\n        }\n        // 101st activation should fail due to budget.\n        let result = ff.process_token(100, 1.0, 0, 100, 0);\n        assert!(matches!(result, ProcessResult::BudgetExhausted { .. }));\n        assert!(ff.token_budget_exhausted());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn turbofieldfare_adaptive_threshold_rises_with_memory_pressure() {\n        let mut 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/orchestrator.rs	orchestrator · 1420 lines	//! orchestrator.rs — Kernel-native tool/skill/agent orchestration.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! A centralized orchestrator that manages tool invocation, skill selection,\n//! agent dispatch, and parallel execution. ALL metrics, health signals, and\n//! load predictions flow through this module — no grep, no shell scripts,\n//! no external processes. Everything is kernel-native and cryptographically\n//! verifiable.\n//!\n//! # Design principles\n//! - Zero grep: all search via kernel-native BM25/trigram/PPR\n//! - Zero scripts: all orchestration via Rust structs and functions\n//! - Detailed metrics: every action emits structured telemetry\n//! - Health signaling: real-time system health assessment\n//! - Load prediction: predict system load from action history\n//! - Parallel dispatch: fan-out based on available resources\n//! - Cryptographic verification: SHA3-256 on all state transitions\n\nuse core::fmt;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::token_bucket::TokenBucket;\nuse crate::workflow_gate::{GatePhase, GateError, WorkflowGate};\nuse crate::TriState;\n\n/// Maximum concurrent tasks (parallel dispatch limit).\nconst MAX_CONCURRENT: usize = 8;\n\n/// Action categories for metrics and load tracking.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum ActionCategory {\n    /// Read-only tool invocation.\n    ToolRead,\n    /// Write tool invocation.\n    ToolWrite,\n    /// Skill execution (composite action).\n    Skill,\n    /// Agent dispatch (LLM call).\n    AgentDispatch,\n    /// Swarm fan-out.\n    SwarmFanOut,\n    /// Verification step.\n    Verification,\n    /// Browser-based parse operation (anti-detect, zero-trace, PQ-signed).\n    Parse,\n}\n\nimpl ActionCategory {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            ActionCategory::ToolRead => "tool_read",\n            ActionCategory::ToolWrite => "tool_write",\n            ActionCategory::Skill => "skill",\n            ActionCategory::AgentDispatch => "agent_dispatch",\n            ActionCategory::SwarmFanOut => "swarm_fan_out",\n            ActionCategory::Verification => "verification",\n            ActionCategory::Parse => "parse",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── PID Controller ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) controller for dynamic concurrency.\n///\n/// Re-exported from `crate::pid::PidController` for backward compatibility.\n/// The generalized version lives in `pid.rs` and supports f64, f32, and\n/// vectorized batch variants.\npub use crate::pid::PidController as PidController;\n\n// ─── Priority Scheduler ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Task priority (higher = execute first).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]\npub enum Priority {\n    /// Background maintenance (lowest).\n    Background = 0,\n    /// Normal tool invocation.\n    Normal = 1,\n    /// Interactive / user-facing (higher).\n    Interactive = 2,\n    /// Parse operations (need anti-detect + PQ signing).\n    Parse = 3,\n    /// Verification / integrity checks (highest — must pass before commit).\n    Critical = 4,\n}\n\nimpl Priority {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Priority::Background => "background",\n            Priority::Normal => "normal",\n            Priority::Interactive => "interactive",\n            Priority::Parse => "parse",\n            Priority::Critical => "critical",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A task ready for dispatch, with priority and estimated execution time.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ScheduledTask {\n    /// Unique task identifier (PID-like: monotonic per-session).\n    pub task_id: u64,\n    /// Action category.\n    pub category: ActionCategory,\n    /// Priority level.\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    /// Estimated execution time in microseconds (from prediction engine).\n    pub estimated_us: u64,\n    /// When this task was created (unix microseconds).\n    pub created_us: u64,\n    /// Budget cost (tokens or compute units).\n    pub budget_cost: f64,\n    /// Dependencies: task_ids that must complete before this one can start.\n    pub depends_on: Vec<u64>,\n}\n\n// ─── Predictive ETA Engine ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Rolling-window prediction for action execution time and load.\n///\n/// Uses exponential moving averages (EMA) over the recent history to predict:\n/// - How long a given action category will take\n/// - What the system load will be in the next window\n/// - When each queued task will complete (priority-aware scheduling)\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct PredictiveEngine {\n    /// EMA estimates per action category: (avg_us, avg_variance).\n    pub category_stats: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<ActionCategory, EmaEstimate>,\n    /// Global load EMA (actions per second).\n    pub load_ema: f64,\n    /// Global latency EMA (microseconds).\n    pub latency_ema: f64,\n    /// Alpha for EMA smoothing (0.0 = never update, 1.0 = only latest).\n    pub alpha: f64,\n    /// Number of observations.\n    pub observations: u64,\n}\n\n/// Exponential moving average estimate for a single metric.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct EmaEstimate {\n    /// Current EMA value (e.g. average latency in us).\n    pub value: f64,\n    /// Current variance estimate (for confidence intervals).\n    pub variance: f64,\n    /// Number of observations for this category.\n    pub count: u64,\n}\n\nimpl PredictiveEngine {\n    /// Create a new predictive engine.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        PredictiveEngine {\n            category_stats: alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new(),\n            load_ema: 0.0,\n            latency_ema: 0.0,\n            alpha: 0.3, // responsive but not too twitchy\n            observations: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record an observation and update the model.\n    pub fn observe(&mut self, category: ActionCategory, duration_us: u64) {\n        let alpha = self.alpha;\n        self.observations += 1;\n\n        let entry = self\n            .category_stats\n            .entry(category)\n            .or_insert_with(|| EmaEstimate {\n                value: duration_us as f64,\n                variance: 0.0,\n                count: 0,\n            });\n\n        let old_val = entry.value;\n        entry.value = alpha * (duration_us as f64) + (1.0 - alpha) * old_val;\n        let diff = (duration_us as f64) - old_val;\n        entry.variance = alpha * diff * diff + (1.0 - alpha) * entry.variance;\n        entry.count += 1;\n\n        // Global stats.\n        self.latency_ema = alpha * (duration_us as f64) + (1.0 - alpha) * self.latency_ema;\n    }\n\n    /// Predict execution time for a given category.\n    ///\n    /// Returns (estimated_us, confidence_interval_95_us).\n    /// If no data for this category, returns a conservative default.\n    pub fn predict_eta(&self, category: ActionCategory) -> (u64, u64) {\n        match self.category_stats.get(&category) {\n            Some(stats) if stats.count >= 3 => {\n                let ci_95 = (1.96 * crate::math::sqrt(stats.variance) * 2.0) as u64; // 95% CI half-width\n                (stats.value as u64, ci_95)\n            }\n            _ => {\n                // Conservative default: 100ms, wide CI.\n                (100_000, 50_000)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Predict the total ETA for a queue of tasks (priority-sorted).\n    ///\n    /// Assumes `available_concurrent` tasks can run in parallel.\n    /// Returns Vec<(task_id, predicted_start_us, predicted_end_us)>.\n    pub fn predict_schedule(\n        &self,\n        tasks: &[ScheduledTask],\n        available_concurrent: usize,\n    ) -> Vec<(u64, u64, u64)> {\n        if tasks.is_empty() || available_concurrent == 0 {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n\n        // Sort by priority (descending), then by estimated duration (ascending).\n        let mut sorted: Vec<&ScheduledTask> = tasks.iter().collect();\n        sorted.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            b.priority\n                .cmp(&a.priority)\n                .then(a.estimated_us.cmp(&b.estimated_us))\n        });\n\n        // Simulate parallel scheduling.\n        let mut slots: Vec<u64> = vec![0; available_concurrent]; // when each slot is free\n        let mut results = Vec::with_capacity(tasks.len());\n\n        for task in &sorted {\n            // Find the earliest free slot.\n            let slot_idx = slots\n                .iter()\n                .enumerate()\n                .min_by_key(|(_, &t)| t)\n                .map(|(i, _)| i)\n                .unwrap_or(0);\n\n            let start_us = slots[slot_idx].max(task.created_us);\n            let end_us = start_us + task.estimated_us;\n            slots[slot_idx] = end_us;\n\n            results.push((task.task_id, start_us, end_us));\n        }\n\n        // Sort by predicted start time.\n        results.sort_by_key(|&(_, start, _)| start);\n        results\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for PredictiveEngine {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n/// A single action record — the atomic unit of orchestration telemetry.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ActionRecord {\n    /// Timestamp (monotonic microseconds since orchestrator creation).\n    pub timestamp_us: u64,\n    /// What kind of action.\n    pub category: ActionCategory,\n    /// Human-readable action name.\n    pub name: String,\n    /// Duration in microseconds (0 if still in progress).\n    pub duration_us: u64,\n    /// Success flag (TriState::Unknown if not yet known).\n    pub success: TriState,\n    /// Error message (empty on success).\n    pub error: String,\n    /// Budget consumed (tokens or compute units).\n    pub budget_consumed: f64,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the action's canonical bytes (for audit trail).\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Compute SHA3-256 of an action record's canonical bytes.\nfn action_hash(cat: ActionCategory, name: &str, ts: u64) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(64);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(ts).to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(cat as u32).to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(name.as_bytes());\n    sha3_256(&buf)\n}\n\n/// System health assessment — aggregated from all subsystem signals.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SystemHealth {\n    /// All subsystems nominal.\n    Healthy,\n    /// One or more subsystems degraded but operational.\n    Degraded,\n    /// Critical failure in one or more subsystems.\n    Critical,\n    /// No data yet (orchestrator just created).\n    Unknown,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for SystemHealth {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            SystemHealth::Healthy => write!(f, "HEALTHY"),\n            SystemHealth::Degraded => write!(f, "DEGRADED"),\n            SystemHealth::Critical => write!(f, "CRITICAL"),\n            SystemHealth::Unknown => write!(f, "UNKNOWN"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Load prediction — estimated future load based on recent action history.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct LoadPrediction {\n    /// Predicted actions per second (next window).\n    pub actions_per_sec: f64,\n    /// Predicted budget consumption rate (tokens/sec).\n    pub budget_rate: f64,\n    /// Predicted concurrent task count.\n    pub concurrent_tasks: usize,\n    /// Confidence in the prediction (0.0..1.0).\n    pub confidence: f64,\n    /// Recommended max concurrent based on prediction.\n    pub recommended_concurrent: usize,\n}\n\n/// Subsystem health signal — one per monitored component.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct HealthSignal {\n    /// Subsystem name.\n    pub subsystem: String,\n    /// Current health status.\n    pub status: SystemHealth,\n    /// Last error message (empty if healthy).\n    pub last_error: String,\n    /// Success rate (0.0..1.0) over the recent window.\n    pub success_rate: f64,\n    /// Average latency in microseconds.\n    pub avg_latency_us: u64,\n    /// SHA3-256 of this signal's state for verification.\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// The Orchestrator — central hub for all kernel actions.\n///\n/// Manages:\n/// - Tool invocation routing and metrics\n/// - Skill selection and execution tracking\n/// - Agent dispatch with workflow gate enforcement\n/// - PID-controlled dynamic concurrency\n/// - Priority-based task scheduling\n/// - Predictive ETA and load forecasting\n/// - All state transitions are SHA3-256 verifiable\npub struct Orchestrator {\n    /// Action history (ring buffer of recent records).\n    history: Vec<ActionRecord>,\n    /// Maximum history size.\n    max_history: usize,\n    /// Budget allocator for the orchestrator.\n    budget: TokenBucket,\n    /// Workflow gate for the current task.\n    gate: WorkflowGate,\n    /// Monotonic clock (microseconds since creation).\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    start_us: u64,\n    /// Subsystem health signals.\n    health_signals: Vec<HealthSignal>,\n    /// Current concurrent task count.\n    active_tasks: usize,\n    /// Running hash chain over all actions (prev_hash || this_hash).\n    chain_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// PID controller for dynamic concurrency management.\n    pid: PidController,\n    /// Priority-based task queue (pending tasks).\n    task_queue: Vec<ScheduledTask>,\n    /// Monotonic task ID counter (PID-like: unique per task).\n    next_task_id: u64,\n    /// Predictive engine for ETA and load forecasting.\n    prediction: PredictiveEngine,\n}\n\nimpl Orchestrator {\n    /// Create a new orchestrator with a budget and workflow gate.\n    pub fn new(budget: TokenBucket, now_us: u64) -> Self {\n        Orchestrator {\n            history: Vec::with_capacity(64),\n            max_history: 256,\n            budget,\n            gate: WorkflowGate::new(),\n            start_us: now_us,\n            health_signals: Vec::new(),\n            active_tasks: 0,\n            chain_hash: [0u8; 32],\n            pid: PidController::new_min_max(1, MAX_CONCURRENT),\n            task_queue: Vec::new(),\n            next_task_id: 1,\n            prediction: PredictiveEngine::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record an action and emit structured telemetry.\n    pub fn record_action(\n        &mut self,\n        category: ActionCategory,\n        name: &str,\n        duration_us: u64,\n        success: bool,\n        error: &str,\n        budget_consumed: f64,\n        now_us: u64,\n    ) -> ActionRecord {\n        let ts = now_us;\n        let hash = action_hash(category, name, ts);\n\n        // Update hash chain.\n        let mut chain_input = Vec::with_capacity(64);\n        chain_input.extend_from_slice(&self.chain_hash);\n        chain_input.extend_from_slice(&hash);\n        self.chain_hash = sha3_256(&chain_input);\n\n        let record = ActionRecord {\n            timestamp_us: ts,\n            category,\n            name: name.to_string(),\n            duration_us,\n            success: TriState::from_bool(success),\n            error: error.to_string(),\n            budget_consumed,\n            hash,\n        };\n\n        // Ring buffer: evict oldest if full.\n        if self.history.len() >= self.max_history {\n            self.history.remove(0);\n        }\n        self.history.push(record.clone());\n\n        // Feed predictive engine.\n        self.prediction.observe(category, duration_us);\n\n        record\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current workflow gate state.\n    pub fn gate(&self) -> &WorkflowGate {\n        &self.gate\n    }\n\n    /// Advance the workflow gate.\n    pub fn advance_gate(&mut self, phase: GatePhase) -> Result<(), GateError> {\n        self.gate.advance(phase)\n    }\n\n    /// Can the current task commit?\n    pub fn can_commit(&self) -> TriState {\n        TriState::from_bool(self.gate.can_commit())\n    }\n\n    /// Start a new task (increment active count, check budget).\n    pub fn start_task(&mut self, now_ns: u64) -> Result<(), String> {\n        if self.active_tasks >= MAX_CONCURRENT {\n            return Err(format!(\n                "max concurrent tasks ({}) reached",\n                MAX_CONCURRENT\n            ));\n        }\n        if !self.budget.try_acquire(1.0, now_ns) {\n            return Err("budget exhausted".to_string());\n        }\n        self.active_tasks += 1;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Finish a task (decrement active count).\n    pub fn finish_task(&mut self) {\n        if self.active_tasks > 0 {\n            self.active_tasks -= 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the number of active tasks.\n    pub fn active_tasks(&self) -> usize {\n        self.active_tasks\n    }\n\n    /// Can we dispatch more tasks in parallel?\n    pub fn can_parallel(&self) -> TriState {\n        TriState::from_bool(self.active_tasks < MAX_CONCURRENT)\n    }\n\n    /// How many more tasks can we run in parallel.\n    pub fn parallel_capacity(&self) -> usize {\n        MAX_CONCURRENT.saturating_sub(self.active_tasks)\n    }\n\n    /// Compute system health from recent action history.\n    pub fn health(&self) -> SystemHealth {\n        if self.history.is_empty() {\n            return SystemHealth::Unknown;\n        }\n\n        let window = self.history.len().min(20);\n        let recent = &self.history[self.history.len() - window..];\n\n        let failures = recent.iter().filter(|r| r.success.is_false()).count();\n        let failure_rate = failures as f64 / window as f64;\n\n        if failure_rate > 0.5 {\n            SystemHealth::Critical\n        } else if failure_rate > 0.1 {\n            SystemHealth::Degraded\n        } else {\n            SystemHealth::Healthy\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Predict system load based on recent action patterns.\n    ///\n    /// Uses a simple moving-average model:\n    /// - actions_per_sec = recent_count / recent_duration\n    /// - budget_rate = recent_budget / recent_duration\n    /// - concurrent = current active_tasks\n    /// - confidence = min(1.0, recent_count / 10)  (need 10+ samples for confidence)\n    pub fn predict_load(&self) -> LoadPrediction {\n        if self.history.is_empty() {\n            return LoadPrediction {\n                actions_per_sec: 0.0,\n                budget_rate: 0.0,\n                concurrent_tasks: self.active_tasks,\n                confidence: 0.0,\n                recommended_concurrent: MAX_CONCURRENT,\n            };\n        }\n\n        let window = self.history.len().min(20);\n        let recent = &self.history[self.history.len() - window..];\n\n        // Time span of the window (microseconds).\n        let first_ts = recent[0].timestamp_us;\n        let last_ts = recent.last().unwrap().timestamp_us;\n        let span_us = if last_ts > first_ts {\n            (last_ts - first_ts) as f64\n        } else {\n            1.0 // Avoid division by zero for single-record windows\n        };\n\n        let actions_per_sec = (window as f64 / span_us) * 1_000_000.0;\n        let total_budget: f64 = recent.iter().map(|r| r.budget_consumed).sum();\n        let budget_rate = (total_budget / span_us) * 1_000_000.0;\n\n        // Confidence grows with sample count.\n        let confidence = (window as f64 / 10.0).min(1.0);\n\n        // Recommended concurrent: scale down if failure rate is high.\n        let failures = recent.iter().filter(|r| r.success.is_false()).count();\n        let failure_rate = failures as f64 / window as f64;\n        let recommended = if failure_rate > 0.3 {\n            1 // Conservative: one task at a time\n        } else if failure_rate > 0.1 {\n            2\n        } else {\n            MAX_CONCURRENT\n        };\n\n        LoadPrediction {\n            actions_per_sec,\n            budget_rate,\n            concurrent_tasks: self.active_tasks,\n            confidence,\n            recommended_concurrent: recommended,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get action history (read-only).\n    pub fn history(&self) -> &[ActionRecord] {\n        &self.history\n    }\n\n    /// The chain hash over all actions (for audit verification).\n    pub fn chain_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        self.chain_hash\n    }\n\n    /// Register a subsystem health signal.\n    pub fn register_health(&mut self, signal: HealthSignal) {\n        // Replace existing signal for the same subsystem.\n        if let Some(existing) = self.health_signals.iter_mut().find(|s| s.subsystem == signal.subsystem) {\n            *existing = signal;\n        } else {\n            self.health_signals.push(signal);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get all health signals.\n    pub fn health_signals(&self) -> &[HealthSignal] {\n        &self.health_signals\n    }\n\n    /// Aggregate health across all registered subsystems.\n    pub fn aggregate_health(&self) -> SystemHealth {\n        if self.health_signals.is_empty() {\n            return self.health();\n        }\n\n        let has_critical = self.health_signals.iter().any(|s| s.status == SystemHealth::Critical);\n        let has_degraded = self.health_signals.iter().any(|s| s.status == SystemHealth::Degraded);\n\n        if has_critical {\n            SystemHealth::Critical\n        } else if has_degraded {\n            SystemHealth::Degraded\n        } else {\n            SystemHealth::Healthy\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII health dashboard for diagnostics.\n    ///\n    /// ```text\n    /// Orchestrator Health Dashboard\n    ///   Status:     HEALTHY\n    ///   Active:     3/8 tasks\n    ///   History:    42 actions\n    ///   Chain:      [a1b2c3d4...]\n    ///   Gate:       [x] research [x] synthesis [ ] critique-1 ...\n    ///   Load:       12.3 actions/sec, confidence: 0.8\n    ///   Subsystems:\n    ///     tool_executor  HEALTHY  (98.5% success, 123us avg)\n    ///     agent_loop     DEGRADED (85.0% success, 456us avg)\n    /// ```\n    pub fn ascii_dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let health = self.aggregate_health();\n        let load = self.predict_load();\n        let gate_status = self.gate().ascii_status();\n\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(512);\n        out.push_str("Orchestrator Health Dashboard\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Status:     {}\\n", health));\n        out.push_str(&format!(\n            "  Active:     {}/{} tasks\\n",\n            self.active_tasks, MAX_CONCURRENT\n        ));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  History:    {} actions\\n", self.history.len()));\n        out.push_str(&format!(\n            "  Chain:      [{:02x?}...]\\n",\n            &self.chain_hash[..4]\n        ));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Gate:\\n{}", gate_status));\n        out.push_str(&format!(\n            "  Load:       {:.1} actions/sec, confidence: {:.1}\\n",\n            load.actions_per_sec, load.confidence\n        ));\n\n        if !self.health_signals.is_empty() {\n            out.push_str("  Subsystems:\\n");\n            for sig in &self.health_signals {\n                out.push_str(&format!(\n                    "    {:<20} {}  ({:.1}% success, {}us avg)\\n",\n                    sig.subsystem,\n                    sig.status,\n                    sig.success_rate * 100.0,\n                    sig.avg_latency_us\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n\n        out\n    }\n\n    // ─── PID-Controlled Dynamic Concurrency ─────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Update the PID controller with the latest performance measurement.\n    ///\n    /// `target_latency_us` = setpoint (ideal action latency).\n    /// `actual_latency_us` = measured latency.\n    /// The PID adjusts the recommended concurrency to minimize latency.\n    pub fn pid_update(&mut self, target_latency_us: f64, actual_latency_us: f64) -> usize {\n        self.pid.update(target_latency_us, actual_latency_us);\n        self.pid.recommended()\n    }\n\n    /// PID-recommended concurrency limit.\n    pub fn pid_recommended_concurrency(&self) -> usize {\n        self.pid.recommended()\n    }\n\n    /// Effective concurrency: minimum of static MAX_CONCURRENT and PID output.\n    pub fn effective_concurrency(&self) -> usize {\n        MAX_CONCURRENT.min(self.pid.recommended())\n    }\n\n    // ─── Priority Scheduling ───────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Enqueue a task for priority-based scheduling.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the assigned task ID (monotonic, PID-like).\n    pub fn enqueue_task(\n        &mut self,\n        category: ActionCategory,\n        priority: Priority,\n        budget_cost: f64,\n        depends_on: Vec<u64>,\n        now_us: u64,\n    ) -> u64 {\n        let task_id = self.next_task_id;\n        self.next_task_id += 1;\n\n        let (estimated_us, _ci) = self.prediction.predict_eta(category);\n\n        let task = ScheduledTask {\n            task_id,\n            category,\n            priority,\n            estimated_us,\n            created_us: now_us,\n            budget_cost,\n            depends_on,\n        };\n\n        self.task_queue.push(task);\n        task_id\n    }\n\n    /// Dequeue the highest-priority ready task (no unmet dependencies).\n    ///\n    /// Returns the task and its predicted ETA. The caller must call\n    /// `finish_task` when done.\n    pub fn dequeue_ready(&mut self) -> Option<(ScheduledTask, u64)> {\n        // Find tasks whose dependencies are all satisfied.\n        let completed: alloc::collections::BTreeSet<u64> = self\n            .history\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|r| r.success.is_true())\n            .map(|_r| {\n                // We don't store task_id in ActionRecord, so we approximate:\n                // a completed task's deps are considered satisfied.\n                0u64 // placeholder — real wiring stores task_id in ActionRecord\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        // Filter to tasks with no pending deps.\n        let ready_idx = self\n            .task_queue\n            .iter()\n            .enumerate()\n            .filter(|(_, t)| t.depends_on.iter().all(|dep| completed.contains(dep)))\n            .min_by_key(|(_, t)| {\n                // Sort by priority desc, then estimated duration asc.\n                core::cmp::Reverse((t.priority, core::cmp::Reverse(t.estimated_us)))\n            })\n            .map(|(i, _)| i);\n\n        if let Some(idx) = ready_idx {\n            let task = self.task_queue.remove(idx);\n            let (eta, _ci) = self.prediction.predict_eta(task.category);\n            Some((task, eta))\n        } else {\n            None\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Number of tasks waiting in the queue.\n    pub fn queue_depth(&self) -> usize {\n        self.task_queue.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Priority-sorted snapshot of the queue (for diagnostics).\n    pub fn queue_snapshot(&self) -> Vec<&ScheduledTask> {\n        let mut snap: Vec<&ScheduledTask> = self.task_queue.iter().collect();\n        snap.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            b.priority\n                .cmp(&a.priority)\n                .then(a.estimated_us.cmp(&b.estimated_us))\n        });\n        snap\n    }\n\n    // ─── Predictive Engine ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Record an action's duration for predictive modeling.\n    pub fn observe_action(&mut self, category: ActionCategory, duration_us: u64) {\n        self.prediction.observe(category, duration_us);\n    }\n\n    /// Predict ETA for a given action category.\n    pub fn predict_eta(&self, category: ActionCategory) -> (u64, u64) {\n        self.prediction.predict_eta(category)\n    }\n\n    /// Predict the full schedule for all queued tasks.\n    pub fn predict_schedule(&self) -> Vec<(u64, u64, u64)> {\n        self.prediction\n            .predict_schedule(&self.task_queue, self.effective_concurrency())\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII dashboard with PID and scheduling info.\n    pub fn ascii_dashboard_full(&self) -> String {\n        let health = self.aggregate_health();\n        let load = self.predict_load();\n        let gate_status = self.gate().ascii_status();\n\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(768);\n        out.push_str("Orchestrator Health Dashboard\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Status:     {}\\n", health));\n        out.push_str(&format!(\n            "  Active:     {}/{} tasks (PID recommends {})\\n",\n            self.active_tasks,\n            MAX_CONCURRENT,\n            self.pid.recommended()\n        ));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Queue:      {} tasks pending\\n", self.task_queue.len()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  History:    {} actions\\n", self.history.len()));\n        out.push_str(&format!(\n            "  Chain:      [{:02x?}...]\\n",\n            &self.chain_hash[..4]\n        ));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Gate:\\n{}", gate_status));\n        out.push_str(&format!(\n            "  Load:       {:.1} actions/sec, confidence: {:.1}\\n",\n            load.actions_per_sec, load.confidence\n        ));\n\n        if !self.task_queue.is_empty() {\n            out.push_str("  Task Queue (priority-sorted):\\n");\n            for task in self.queue_snapshot().iter().take(5) {\n                out.push_str(&format!(\n                    "    [{}] {} est.{}us ${:.1}\\n",\n                    task.priority.as_str(),\n                    task.category.as_str(),\n                    task.estimated_us,\n                    task.budget_cost\n                ));\n            }\n            if self.task_queue.len() > 5 {\n                out.push_str(&format!("    ... +{} more\\n", self.task_queue.len() - 5));\n            }\n        }\n\n        if !self.health_signals.is_empty() {\n            out.push_str("  Subsystems:\\n");\n            for sig in &self.health_signals {\n                out.push_str(&format!(\n                    "    {:<20} {}  ({:.1}% success, {}us avg)\\n",\n                    sig.subsystem,\n                    sig.status,\n                    sig.success_rate * 100.0,\n                    sig.avg_latency_us\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a health signal for a subsystem from recent action records.\npub fn build_health_signal(subsystem: &str, records: &[ActionRecord]) -> HealthSignal {\n    if records.is_empty() {\n        return HealthSignal {\n            subsystem: subsystem.to_string(),\n            status: SystemHealth::Unknown,\n            last_error: String::new(),\n            success_rate: 0.0,\n            avg_latency_us: 0,\n            hash: sha3_256(subsystem.as_bytes()),\n        };\n    }\n\n    let total = records.len();\n    let successes = records.iter().filter(|r| r.success.is_true()).count();\n    let success_rate = successes as f64 / total as f64;\n    let total_latency: u64 = records.iter().map(|r| r.duration_us).sum();\n    let avg_latency = total_latency / total as u64;\n\n    let last_error = records\n        .iter()\n        .rev()\n        .find(|r| r.success.is_false())\n        .map(|r| r.error.clone())\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n\n    let status = if success_rate < 0.5 {\n        SystemHealth::Critical\n    } else if success_rate < 0.9 {\n        SystemHealth::Degraded\n    } else {\n        SystemHealth::Healthy\n    };\n\n    // Hash the signal state.\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(128);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(subsystem.as_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(success_rate.to_bits()).to_le_bytes());\n success_rate,\n        avg_latency_us: avg_latency,\n        hash,\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn test_budget() -> TokenBucket {\n        TokenBucket::new(100.0, 32],\n    /// Whether this entry is valid.\n    pub valid: TriState,\n}\n\nimpl AgcScheduler {\n    /// Create a new AGC scheduler.\n    pub fn new(max_tasks: usize) -> Self {\n        AgcScheduler {\n            tasks: Vec::with_capacity(max_tasks),\n            max_tasks,\n            pid: PidController::new_min_max(1, MAX_TASKS),\n            total_scheduled: 0,\n            total_shed: 0,\n task.\n    pub fn schedule(&mut self, mut task: AgcTask) -> Result<u64, ScheduleError> {\n        if self.tasks.len() >= self.max_tasks {\n            return Err(ScheduleError::AtCapacity);\n        }\n        task.state = TaskState::Pending;\n        let id = task.id;\n        self.tasks.push(task);\n        self.total_scheduled += 1;\n        self.update_overload_level();\n        Ok(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the next task to execute (priority-sorted, dependency-aware).\n    pub fn next_task(&mut self) -> Option<&AgcTask> {\n        self.tasks.iter()\n            .filter(|t| t.state ==               }\n                })\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Get active task count by priority.\n    pub fn active_by_priority(&self, priority: AgcPriority) -> usize {\n        self.tasks.iter()\n }\n\n    /// ASCII dashboard.\n    pub fn ascii_dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let pending = self.pending_count();\n        let running = self.tasks.iter().filter(|t| t.state ==
```
