assert!(s.verify_checkpoint(id).is_true());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dependency_gating() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        s.schedule(make_task(1, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        let mut t2 = make_task(2, AgcPriority::Normal);\n        t2.depends_on = vec![1];\n        s.schedule(t2).unwrap();\n        // Task 2 can't run until task 1 completes.\n        s.start_task(1);\n        s.complete_task(1);\n        assert!(s.next_task().unwrap().id == 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn at_capacity_error() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(2);\n        s.schedule(make_task(1, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        s.schedule(make_task(2, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.schedule(make_task(3, AgcPriority::Normal)), Err(ScheduleError::AtCapacity));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dashboard_contains_sections() {\n        let s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        let d = s.ascii_dashboard();\n        assert!(d.contains("AGC Scheduler Dashboard"));\n        assert!(d.contains("Tasks:"));\n        assert!(d.contains("Overload:"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn active_by_priority() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        let id = s.schedule(make_task(1, AgcPriority::High)).unwrap();\n        s.start_task(id);\n        assert_eq!(s.active_by_priority(AgcPriority::High), 1);\n        assert_eq!(s.active_by_priority(AgcPriority::Low), 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pid_update() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        let rec = s.pid_update(100.0, 500.0);\n        assert!(rec > 0);\n    }\n\n    // ── additional coverage tests ──────────────────────────────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_task_queue_next_task_none() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        assert!(s.next_task().is_none());\n        assert_eq!(s.pending_count(), 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_tasks_same_priority_respect_fifo_like() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        s.schedule(make_task(1, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        s.schedule(make_task(2, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        s.schedule(make_task(3, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        // All same priority, next_task returns max_by_key(priority) — any is fine.\n        let next = s.next_task().unwrap();\n        assert!(next.state == TaskState::Pending);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn overload_shedding_at_exact_threshold() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(100);\n        for i in 0..OVERLOAD_THRESHOLD {\n            s.schedule(make_task(i as u64, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        }\n        assert_eq!(s.overload_level(), 1, "overload_level must be 1 at threshold");\n        let shed = s.shed_overload();\n        assert!(!shed.is_empty(), "low priority tasks must be shed");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn priority_inversion_prevention() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        s.schedule(make_task(1, AgcPriority::Low)).unwrap();\n        s.schedule(make_task(2, AgcPriority::Emergency)).unwrap();\n        s.schedule(make_task(3, AgcPriority::High)).unwrap();\n        let next = s.next_task().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(next.id, 2, "Emergency must be scheduled before High and Low");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn task_timeout_state_is_preserved() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        let id = s.schedule(make_task(1, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        s.start_task(id);\n        s.fail_task(id);\n        assert_eq!(s.tasks[0].state, TaskState::Failed);\n        // Restart from checkpoint (none) → None\n        let resume = s.restart_from_checkpoint(id);\n        assert_eq!(resume, None, "restart without checkpoint returns None");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn checkpoint_restore_with_no_prior_state() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        let id = s.schedule(make_task(1, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        s.start_task(id);\n        // Restart without any checkpoint:\n        let step = s.restart_from_checkpoint(id);\n        assert!(step.is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn max_tasks_capacity_boundary() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(1);\n        s.schedule(make_task(1, AgcPriority::Normal)).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.schedule(make_task(2, AgcPriority::Normal)), Err(ScheduleError::AtCapacity));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn single_task_full_lifecycle() {\n        let mut s = AgcScheduler::new(10);\n        let id = assert_eq!(s.active_by_priority(AgcPriority::High), 1);\n        assert!(s.complete_task(id).is_true());\n        assert_eq!(s.tasks[0].state, TaskState::Completed);\n        assert_eq!(s.pending_count(), 0);\n    }\n}\n	12031	-1	-1		037a34fd8cc9f77c8109edc3a1f2790649c68480bf5b55cefdf6a8cb11a6afefdce0be33d5840c73db6c97ab949ba62bceff3436b3089e9ae15a7e8d67ce8a841cfe75db2d3120e5420f190a97bf12196044b56e61f8630ed0e26584283f71b6a7a631d616ea1130dd384b9a4a9c27e06a3149bb2eb7e42305adfc3719b66d89

DynamicActionBatcher\n//! +-- BatchConfig (min/max size, latency target, worker count)\n//! +-- PidController (setpoint=predicted, measurement=actual)\n//! +-- WorkerPool (per-core load,   min_batch: MIN_BATCH_SIZE,\n            max_batch: MAX_BATCH_SIZE,\n            worker_count: 4,\n            target_batch_latency_us: 50_000,\n            max_in_flight: 64,\n            min_recompute_interval_us: 10_000,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Worker State ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct WorkerState {\n    pub id: usize,\n    pub avg_latency_us: f64,\n    pub throughput: f64,\n    pub in_flight: usize,\n    pub batches_completed: u64,\n    pub actions_completed: u64,\n    pub total_work_us: u64,\n    pub idle: TriState,\n}\n\nimpl WorkerState {\n    pub fn new(id: usize) -> Self {\n        WorkerState { id, avg_latency_us: 0.0, throughput: 0.0, in_flight: 0, batches_completed: 0, actions_completed: 0, total_work_us: 0, idle: TriState::True }\n    }\n\n    pub fn record_batch_done(&mut self, actions: usize, latency_us: u64) {\n        self.in_flight = self.in_flight.saturating_sub(actions);\n        self.batches_completed += 1;\n        self.actions_completed += actions as u64;\n        self.total_work_us += latency_us;\n        self.idle = TriState::from_bool(self.in_flight == 0);\n        if       }\n    }\n\n    pub fn assign(&mut self, count: usize) {\n        self.in_flight += count;\n        self.idle = TriState::False;\n    }\n\n    pub fn load_factor(&self, max_per_worker: usize) -> (config.min_batch, config.max_batch);\n        let mut b = Self::new(config);\n        b.pid = PidController::new(kp, ki, kd, min_batch as f64, max_batch as f64);\n        b\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_cache_ttl(config: BatchConfig, ttl_us: u64) -> Self {\n        let mut b = Self::new(config);\n        b.cache_ttl_us = ttl_us;\n        b\n    }\n\n    /// Compute execution plan (with cache).\n    pub fn compute_plan(&mut self, tasks: &[ScheduledTask], now_us: u64) -> ExecutionPlan {\n        // Cache check.\n        if self.cache.is_valid(tasks.len(), self.pool.avg_latency_us(), now_us, self.cache_ttl_us) {\n            return self.cache.serve(now_us);\n        }\n        self.cache.invalidate();\n\n        // Rate limit.\n        if now_us.saturating_sub(self.last_recompute_us) < self.config.min_recompute_interval_us && !tasks.is_empty() {\n            return ExecutionPlan {\n                batches: Vec::new(), assignments: Vec::new(),                 pid_batch_size: self.pid.output(),\n                total_actions: 0, predicted_total_us: 0, predicted_parallel_us: 0,\n                idle_workers: self.pool.len(), computed_us: now_us, from_cache: TriState::False,\n            };\n        }\n        self.last_recompute_us = now_us;\n\n        if tasks.is_empty() {\n            return ExecutionPlan {\n                batches: Vec::new(),\n                assignments: self.pool.workers().iter().map(|w| (w.id, Vec::new())).collect(),\n                pid_batch_size: self.pid.output(), total_actions: 0, predicted_total_us: 0,\n                predicted_parallel_us: 0, idle_workers: self.pool.len(), computed_us: now_us, from_cache: TriState::False,\n            };\n        }\n\n        // PID feedback.\n        let actual_latency = self.pool.avg_latency_us();\n        let target_latency = self.config.target_batch_latency_us as f64;\n        let pid_output = self.pid.update(target_latency, actual_latency);\n\n        self.fractional_accum += pid_output;\n        let batch_size = self.fractional_accum as usize;\n        self.fractional_accum -= batch_size as f64;\n        let batch_size = batch_size.max(self.config.min_batch).min(self.config.max_batch);\n\n        // Split + distribute.\n        let mut batches = Vec::new();\n        let mut assignments: Vec<(usize, Vec<u64>)> = self.pool.workers().iter().map(|w| (w.id, Vec::new())).collect();\n\n        for chunk in tasks.chunks(batch_size) {\n            let worker_id = self.pool.least_loaded().unwrap_or(0);\n            let predicted_us = self.predict_batch_latency(chunk);\n            let mut hash_input = Vec::with_capacity(10);\n            hash_input.extend_from_slice(&self.next_batch_id.to_le_bytes());\n            hash_input.push(worker_id as u8);\n            hash_input.push(batch_size.to_le_bytes()[0]);\n            let batch_hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(&hash_input);\n\n            let batch = ActionBatch {\n                batch_id: self.next_batch_id, worker_id, tasks: chunk.to_vec(),\n                action_count: chunk.len(), predicted_us, pid_batch_size: pid_output, batch_hash,\n            };\n\n            if let Some(w) = self.pool.get_mut(worker_id) { w.assign(chunk.len()); }\n            if let Some((_, ref mut ids)) = assignments.iter_mut().find(|(id, _)| *id == worker_id) {\n                ids.push(batch.batch_id);\n            }\n            self.next_batch_id += 1;\n            batches.push(batch);\n        }\n\n        let total_actions: usize = batches.iter().map(|b| b.action_count).sum();\n        let predicted_total_us: u64 = batches.iter().map(|b| b.predicted_us).sum();\n        let idle_workers = self.pool.workers().iter().filter(|w| w.idle == TriState::True).count();\n\n        let mut worker_totals: Vec<u64> = vec![0; self.pool.len()];\n        for b in &batches { worker_totals[b.worker_id] += b.predicted_us; }\n        let predicted_parallel_us = worker_totals.into_iter().max().unwrap_or(0);\n\n        let plan = ExecutionPlan {\n            batches, assignments, pid_batch_size: pid_output, total_actions,\n            predicted_total_us,             predicted_parallel_us, idle_workers, computed_us: now_us, from_cache: TriState::False,\n        };\n\n        self.cache.update(&plan, now_us);\n        plan\n    }\n\n    pub fn record_batch_done(&mut self, worker_id: usize, actions: usize, latency_us: u64) {\n        if let Some(w) = self.pool.get_mut(worker_id) { w.record_batch_done(actions, latency_us); }\n        self.cache.stale = TriState::True;\n    }\n\n    pub fn observe_category(&mut self, category: ActionCategory, duration_us: u64) {\n        let alpha = self.alpha;\n        let entry = self.category_latencies.entry(category).or_insert((duration_us as f64, 0.0));\n        let old_val = entry.0;\n        entry.0 = alpha * (duration_us as f64) + (1.0 - alpha) * old_val;\n        let diff = (duration_us as f64) - old_val;\n        entry.1 = alpha * diff * diff + (1.0 - alpha) * entry.1;\n    }\n\n    fn predict_batch_latency(&self, tasks: &[ScheduledTask]) -> u64 {\n        tasks.iter().map(|t| {\n            self.category_latencies.get(&t.category)\n                .map(|(avg, var)| { let ci = 1.96 * crate::math::sqrt(*var); (*avg + ci) as u64 })\n                .unwrap_or(t.estimated_us)\n        }).sum()\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII dashboard for live diagnostics.\n    pub fn ascii_dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let p = &self.pool;\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(768);\n        out.push_str("DynamicActionBatcher Dashboard\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Workers:     {} total, {} idle\\n", p.len(), self.pool.workers().iter().filter(|w| w.idle == TriState::True).count()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  In-flight:   {}/{}\\n", p.total_in_flight(), self.config.max_in_flight));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  PID output:  {:.2} (target={}us)\\n", self.pid.output(), self.config.target_batch_latency_us));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Batch size:  {:.0} (min={} max={})\\n", self.pid.output(), self.config.min_batch, self.config.max_batch));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Avg latency: {:.0} us\\n", p.avg_latency_us()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Throughput:   {:.1} actions/sec\\n", p.avg_throughput()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Categories:  {}\\n", self.category_latencies.len()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Cache:       {:.0}% hit rate ({} hits / {} misses)\\n",\n            self.cache.hit_rate() * 100.0, self.cache.hits, self.cache.misses));\n        // Per-worker breakdown.\n        out.push_str("  Workers:\\n");\n        for w in p.workers() {\n            let load = w.load_factor(self.config.max_batch);\n            out.push_str(&format!("    W{}: in_flight={} completed={} latency={:.0}us tput={:.1}/s load={:.0}%{}\\n",\n                w.id, w.in_flight, w.actions_completed, w.avg_latency_us, w.throughput, load * 100.0,\n                if w.idle == TriState::True { " IDLE" } else { "" }\n            ));\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    pub fn pool(&self) -> &WorkerPool { &self.pool }\n    pub fn pool_mut(&mut self) -> &mut WorkerPool { &mut self.pool }\n    pub fn pid_output(&self) -> f64 { self.pid.output() }\n    pub fn pid_recommended(&self) -> usize { self.pid.recommended() }\n    pub fn config(&self) -> &BatchConfig { &self.config }\n    pub fn cache(&self) -> &ActionCache { &self.cache }\n    pub fn cache_mut(&mut self) -> &mut ActionCache { &mut self.cache }\n\n    pub fn reset_pid(&mut self) {\n        self.pid.reset();\n        self.fractional_accum = 0.0;\n        self.cache.invalidate();\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn make_tasks(n: usize) -> Vec<ScheduledTask> {\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/dynamic_spawner.rs	dynamic_spawner · 557 lines	//! `kernel::dynamic_spawner` — PID-controlled agent spawn batching with caching.\n//!\n//! Decides HOW MANY agents to spawn per tick based on load feedback.\n//! PID adjusts batch size: under load → fewer spawns, idle → more agents.\n//! Predictions are cached and invalidated on new observations.\n//! ASCII dashboard for live diagnostics.\n//!\n//! # Architecture\n//! ```text\n//! DynamicSpawner\n//! +-- SpawnBatchConfig (min/max batch, rate limits)\n//! +-- PidController (setpoint=target_queue, measurement=actual_queue)\n//! +-- SpawnMetrics (EMA latency, success rate, queue depth)\n//! +-- SpawnCache (cached predictions, invalidated on new data)\n//! +-- compute_batch() -> SpawnBatch (count, reason, hash)\n//! +-- ascii_dashboard() -> live diagnostics\n//! ```\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::orchestrator::PidController;\nuse crate::TriState;\n\npub const MIN_SPAWN_BATCH: usize = 1;\npub const MAX_SPAWN_BATCH: usize = 8;\npub const MAX_SWARM_TOTAL: usize = 32;\npub const SPAWN_LATENCY_ALPHA: f64 = 0.3;\npub const SPAWN_SUCCESS_ALPHA: f64 = 0.2;\n\n// ─── Spawn Batch Configuration ────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SpawnBatchConfig {\n    pub min_batch: usize,\n    pub max_batch: usize,\n    pub max_swarm_total: usize,\n    pub target_queue_depth: usize,\n    pub min_interval_us: u64,\n    pub max_rate_per_sec: f64,\n}\n\nimpl Default for SpawnBatchConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        SpawnBatchConfig {\n            min_batch: MIN_SPAWN_BATCH,\n            max_batch: MAX_SPAWN_BATCH,\n            max_swarm_total: MAX_SWARM_TOTAL,\n            target_queue_depth: 4,\n            min_interval_us: 100_000,\n            max_rate_per_sec: 20.0,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Spawn Metrics (EMA) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SpawnMetrics {\n    pub avg_latency_us: f64,\n    pub success_rate: f64,\n    pub queue_depth: usize,\n    pub active_agents: usize,\n    pub total_spawned: u64,\n    pub total_failures: u64,\n    pub last_spawn_us: u64,\n}\n\nimpl SpawnMetrics {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SpawnMetrics {\n            avg_latency_us: 0.0,\n            success_rate: 1.0,\n            queue_depth: 0,\n            active_agents: 0,\n            total_spawned: 0,\n            total_failures: 0,\n            last_spawn_us: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn record_batch(&mut self, spawned: usize, failed: usize, latency_us: u64, now_us: u64) {\n        let total = spawned + failed;\n        if total > 0 {\n            let batch_success = spawned as f64 / total as f64;\n            self.success_rate =\n                SPAWN_SUCCESS_ALPHA * batch_success + (1.0 - SPAWN_SUCCESS_ALPHA) * self.success_rate;\n        }\n        if spawned > 0 && latency_us > 0 {\n            let per_agent = latency_us as f64 / spawned as f64;\n            self.avg_latency_us =\n                SPAWN_LATENCY_ALPHA * per_agent + (1.0 - SPAWN_LATENCY_ALPHA) * self.avg_latency_us;\n        }\n        self.total_spawned += spawned as u64;\n        self.total_failures += failed as u64;\n        self.active_agents += spawned;\n        self.active_agents = self.active_agents.saturating_sub(failed);\n        self.last_spawn_us = now_us;\n    }\n\n    pub fn record_agent_died(&mut self) {\n        self.active_agents = self.active_agents.saturating_sub(1);\n    }\n\n    pub fn spawn_capacity(&self, max_total: usize) -> usize {\n        max_total.saturating_sub(self.active_agents)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Prediction Cache ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Cached spawn prediction — avoids recomputing when inputs haven't changed.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SpawnCache {\n    /// Cached batch count.\n    pub cached_count: usize,\n    /// Cached reason.\n    pub cached_reason: SpawnReason,\n    /// Queue depth this cache was computed for.\n    pub cache_queue_depth: usize,\n    /// Active agents when this cache was computed.\n    pub cache_active_agents: usize,\n    /// Timestamp of cache computation.\n    pub cache_computed_us: u64,\n    /// Whether cache is stale (new observation invalidated it).\n    pub stale: TriState,\n    /// Total cache hits.\n    pub hits: u64,\n    /// Total cache misses.\n    pub misses: u64,\n}\n\nimpl SpawnCache {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SpawnCache {\n            cached_count: 0,\n            cached_reason: SpawnReason::ColdStart,\n            cache_queue_depth: 0,\n            cache_active_agents: 0,\n            cache_computed_us: 0,\n            stale: TriState::Unknown,\n            hits: 0,\n            misses: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check if cache is valid for the given inputs.\n    pub fn is_valid(&self, queue_depth: usize, active_agents: usize, now_us: u64, ttl_us: u64) -> bool {\n        self.stale == TriState::False\n            && self.cache_queue_depth == queue_depth\n            && self.cache_active_agents == active_agents\n            && now_us.saturating_sub(self.cache_computed_us) < ttl_us\n    }\n\n    /// Serve from cache (increment hit counter).\n    pub fn serve(&mut self) -> (usize, SpawnReason) {\n        self.hits += 1;\n        (self.cached_count, self.cached_reason)\n    }\n\n    /// Invalidate and record miss.\n    pub fn invalidate(&mut self) {\n        self.stale = TriState::True;\n        self.misses += 1;\n    }\n\n    /// Update cache with new computation.\n    pub fn update(&mut self, count: usize, reason: SpawnReason, queue_depth: usize, active_agents: usize, now_us: u64) {\n        self.cached_count = count;\n        self.cached_reason = reason;\n        self.cache_queue_depth = queue_depth;\n        self.cache_active_agents = active_agents;\n        self.cache_computed_us = now_us;\n        self.stale = TriState::False;\n    }\n\n    /// Cache hit rate.\n    pub fn hit_rate(&self) -> f64 {\n        let total = self.hits + self.misses;\n        if total == 0 { 0.0 } else { self.hits as f64 / total as f64 }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Spawn Batch ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SpawnBatch {\n    pub count: usize,\n    pub skills: Vec<String>,\n    pub pid_output: f64,\n    pub pid_setpoint: f64,\n    pub reason: SpawnReason,\n    pub computed_us: u64,\n    pub batch_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// Whether this batch was served from cache.\n    pub from_cache: TriState,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SpawnReason {\n    PidIncrease,\n    PidHold,\n    PidDecrease,\n    ColdStart,\n    AtCapacity,\n    RateLimited,\n    Cached,\n}\n\n// ─── Dynamic Spawner ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct DynamicSpawner {\n    config: SpawnBatchConfig,\n    pid: PidController,\n    metrics: SpawnMetrics,\n    cache: SpawnCache,\n    fractional_accum: f64,\n    /// Cache TTL (microseconds). How long a cached prediction is valid.\n    cache_ttl_us: u64,\n}\n\nimpl DynamicSpawner {\n    pub fn new(config: SpawnBatchConfig) -> Self {\n        DynamicSpawner {\n            pid: PidController::new_min_max(0, config.max_batch),\n            config,\n            metrics: SpawnMetrics::new(),\n            cache: SpawnCache::new(),\n            fractional_accum: 0.0,\n            cache_ttl_us: 50_000, // 50ms default TTL\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_pid_tuning(config: SpawnBatchConfig, kp: f64, ki: f64, kd: f64) -> Self {\n        let (min_batch, max_batch) = (config.min_batch, config.max_batch);\n        let mut spawner = Self::new(config);\n        spawner.pid = PidController::new(kp, ki, kd, min_batch as f64, max_batch as f64);\n        spawner\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_cache_ttl(config: SpawnBatchConfig, cache_ttl_us: u64) -> Self {\n        let mut spawner = Self::new(config);\n        spawner.cache_ttl_us = cache_ttl_us;\n        spawner\n    }\n\n    /// Compute the next spawn batch (with cache).\n    pub fn compute_batch(&mut self, now_us: u64, pending_tasks: usize) -> SpawnBatch {\n        self.metrics.queue_depth = pending_tasks;\n\n        // Cache check.\n        if self.cache.is_valid(pending_tasks, self.metrics.active_agents, now_us, self.cache_ttl_us) {\n            let (count, _reason) = self.cache.serve();\n            return self.make_batch_cached(count, SpawnReason::Cached, now_us);\n        }\n        self.cache.invalidate();\n\n        // Cold start.\n        if self.metrics.active_agents == 0 && pending_tasks > 0 {\n            let count = self.config.min_batch.max(1);\n            self.cache.update(count, SpawnReason::ColdStart, pending_tasks, self.metrics.active_agents, now_us);\n            return self.make_batch(count, SpawnReason::ColdStart, now_us);\n        }\n\n        // Rate limit.\n        if now_us.saturating_sub(self.metrics.last_spawn_us) < self.config.min_interval_us {\n            self.cache.update(0, SpawnReason::RateLimited, pending_tasks, self.metrics.active_agents, now_us);\n            return self.make_batch(0, SpawnReason::RateLimited, now_us);\n        }\n\n        // Capacity.\n        let capacity = self.metrics.spawn_capacity(self.config.max_swarm_total);\n        if capacity == 0 {\n            self.cache.update(0, SpawnReason::AtCapacity, pending_tasks, self.metrics.active_agents, now_us);\n            return self.make_batch(0, SpawnReason::AtCapacity, now_us);\n        }\n\n        // No demand.\n        if pending_tasks == 0 && self.metrics.active_agents > 0 {\n            self.cache.update(0, SpawnReason::PidHold, pending_tasks, self.metrics.active_agents, now_us);\n            return self.make_batch(0, SpawnReason::PidHold, now_us);\n        }\n\n        // PID feedback.\n        let target = self.config.target_queue_depth as f64;\n        let actual = pending_tasks as f64;\n        let pid_output = self.pid.update(target, actual);\n\n        let reason = if pid_output > self.pid.output() + 0.1 {\n            SpawnReason::PidIncrease\n        } else if pid_output < self.pid.output - 0.1 {\n            SpawnReason::PidDecrease\n        } else {\n            SpawnReason::PidHold\n        };\n\n        self.fractional_accum += pid_output;\n        let raw_count = self.fractional_accum as usize;\n        self.fractional_accum -= raw_count as f64;\n\n        let count = raw_count\n            .max(self.config.min_batch)\n            .min(self.config.max_batch)\n            .min(capacity);\n\n        self.cache.update(count, reason, pending_tasks, self.metrics.active_agents, now_us);\n        self.make_batch(count, reason, now_us)\n    }\n\n    pub fn record_outcome(&mut self, spawned: usize, failed: usize, latency_us: u64, now_us: u64) {\n        self.metrics.record_batch(spawned, failed, latency_us, now_us);\n        // Invalidate cache on new observation (inputs changed).\n        self.cache.stale = TriState::True;\n    }\n\n    pub fn record_agent_died(&mut self) {\n        self.metrics.record_agent_died();\n        self.cache.stale = TriState::True;\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII dashboard for live diagnostics.\n    pub fn ascii_dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let m = &self.metrics;\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(512);\n        out.push_str("DynamicSpawner Dashboard\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Agents:      {}/{}\\n", m.active_agents, self.config.max_swarm_total));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Queue:       {} pending\\n", m.queue_depth));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  PID output:  {:.2} (setpoint={})\\n", self.pid.output(), self.config.target_queue_depth));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Batch size:  {:.0} (min={} max={})\\n", self.pid.output(), self.config.min_batch, self.config.max_batch));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Spawned:     {} total, {} failures\\n", m.total_spawned, m.total_failures));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Latency EMA: {:.0} us/agent\\n", m.avg_latency_us));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Success:     {:.1}%\\n", m.success_rate * 100.0));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Cache:       {:.0}% hit rate ({} hits / {} misses)\\n",\n            self.cache.hit_rate() * 100.0, self.cache.hits, self.cache.misses));\n        out\n    }\n\n    pub fn metrics(&self) -> &SpawnMetrics { &self.metrics }\n    pub fn pid_output(&self) -> f64 { self.pid.output() }\n    pub fn pid_recommended(&self) -> usize { self.pid.recommended() }\n    pub fn SpawnBatch {\n            count,\n            skills: Vec::new(),\n            pid_output: self.pid.output(),\n            pid_setpoint: self.config.target_queue_depth as f64,\n            reason,\n            computed_us: now_us,\n            batch_hash,\n            from_cache: TriState::False,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn make_batch_cached(&self, count: usize, reason: SpawnReason, now_us: u64) -> {\n            count,\n            skills: Vec::new(),\n            pid_output: self.pid.output(),\n            pid_setpoint: self.config.target_queue_depth as f64,\n            reason,\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/parallel_patterns.rs	parallel_patterns · 1144 lines	//! parallel_patterns.rs — Reusable parallel execution pattern library.\n//!\n//! # What this is\n//! Pure-computation patterns for dynamic parallel execution. Each pattern\n//! produces an execution PLAN (task graph with resource assignments) that\n//! the orchestrator dispatches. No real threads, no I/O — the kernel is\n//! the planning authority; actual execution happens behind the port seam.\n//!\n//! # Design principles\n//! - Kernel = pure computation: patterns produce plans, not threads\n//! - Dynamic: pattern selection adapts to PID controller output + system load\n//! - Priority-aware: higher-priority tasks get more resources\n//! - All patterns compose: pipeline contains fan-outs, fan-in reads pipeline output\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::orchestrator::Priority;\nuse crate::TriState;\n\n// ─── Pattern: Fan-Out / Fan-In ────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A fan-out/fan-in execution plan.\n///\n/// Split input data into chunks, process each chunk independently, then\n/// merge results. The number of workers is dynamically chosen based on\n/// available concurrency.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct FanOutPlan {\n    /// Total number of input items.\n    pub input_count: usize,\n    /// Number of parallel workers (from PID controller).\n    pub worker_count: usize,\n    /// How items are distributed across workers.\n    pub distribution: Distribution,\n    /// Priority of the fan-out tasks.\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    /// Estimated per-item processing time (microseconds).\n    pub per_item_us: u64,\n    /// Total estimated time (including merge).\n    pub total_estimated_us: u64,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum Distribution {\n    /// Each worker gets a contiguous block.\n    Contiguous,\n    /// Items are interleaved (round-robin across workers).\n    Interleaved,\n    /// Items are assigned by weight (larger items to faster workers).\n    Weighted,\n}\n\nimpl FanOutPlan {\n    /// Create a fan-out plan from input parameters.\n    pub fn plan(\n        input_count: usize,\n        available_workers: usize,\n        per_item_us: u64,\n        priority: Priority,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let worker_count = available_workers.max(1).min(input_count);\n        if worker_count == 0 {\n            return FanOutPlan {\n                input_count: 0,\n                worker_count: 1,\n                distribution: Distribution::Contiguous,\n                priority,\n                per_item_us,\n                total_estimated_us: 0,\n            };\n        }\n\n        let items_per_worker = (input_count + worker_count - 1) / worker_count;\n        let parallel_us = items_per_worker as u64 * per_item_us;\n        // Merge overhead: O(items_per_worker * log2(worker_count)).\n        let merge_us = (input_count as f64 * crate::math::ceil(crate::math::log2(worker_count as f64)) as f64) as u64;\n\n        FanOutPlan {\n            input_count,\n            worker_count,\n            distribution: Distribution::Contiguous,\n            priority,\n            per_item_us,\n            total_estimated_us: parallel_us + merge_us,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Generate the worker assignments: Vec<(worker_id, start, end)>.\n    pub fn assignments(&self) -> Vec<(usize, usize, usize)> {\n        if self.worker_count == 0 || self.input_count == 0 {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n        let chunk_size = (self.input_count + self.worker_count - 1) / self.worker_count;\n        let mut assignments = Vec::with_capacity(self.worker_count);\n        for w in 0..self.worker_count {\n            let start = w * chunk_size;\n            let end = (start + chunk_size).min(self.input_count);\n            if start < self.input_count {\n                assignments.push((w, start, end));\n            }\n        }\n        assignments\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Pattern: Pipeline ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A pipeline execution plan: stages connected by bounded buffers.\n///\n/// Each stage processes items and passes them to the next. Stages can\n/// run concurrently if there is sufficient capacity. Buffer sizes are\n/// dynamically adjusted based on PID output.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PipelinePlan {\n    /// Number of pipeline stages.\n    pub stage_count: usize,\n    /// Buffer size between stages (backpressure bound).\n    pub buffer_size: usize,\n    /// Per-stage estimated latency (microseconds).\n    pub stage_latencies: Vec<u64>,\n    /// Total estimated latency (sum of all stages + buffer overhead).\n    pub total_estimated_us: u64,\n    /// Items that can be in-flight simultaneously.\n    pub in_flight: usize,\n}\n\nimpl PipelinePlan {\n    /// Create a pipeline plan from stage latencies and concurrency.\n    pub fn plan(stage_latencies: Vec<u64>, available_workers: usize) -> Self {\n        let stage_count = stage_latencies.len();\n        if stage_count == 0 {\n            return PipelinePlan {\n                stage_count: 0,\n                buffer_size: 1,\n                stage_latencies: vec![],\n                total_estimated_us: 0,\n                in_flight: 0,\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Buffer size: scale with concurrency. More workers = larger buffers\n        // to keep all stages fed.\n        let buffer_size = (available_workers * 2).max(2);\n        let total_estimated_us: u64 = stage_latencies.iter().sum();\n        let in_flight = available_workers.min(stage_count);\n\n        PipelinePlan {\n            stage_count,\n            buffer_size,\n            stage_latencies,\n            total_estimated_us,\n            in_flight,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Throughput estimate: items per second given the bottleneck stage.\n    pub fn throughput_per_sec(&self) -> f64 {\n        if self.stage_latencies.is_empty() {\n            return 0.0;\n        }\n        let bottleneck_us = self.stage_latencies.iter().copied().max().unwrap();\n        if bottleneck_us == 0 {\n            return f64::INFINITY;\n        }\n        1_000_000.0 / bottleneck_us as f64\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Pattern: Work-Stealing Queue ─────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A work-stealing queue plan: idle workers steal from busy ones.\n///\n/// Each worker has a local queue. When a worker's queue is empty, it\n/// steals from the busiest worker's queue. This minimizes idle time\n/// when task sizes are uneven.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct WorkStealingPlan {\n    /// Per-worker queue sizes at planning time.\n    pub worker_queues: Vec<usize>,\n    /// Total items to process.\n    pub total_items: usize,\n    /// Estimated per-item time (microseconds).\n    pub per_item_us: u64,\n    /// Number of workers.\n    pub worker_count: usize,\n    /// Maximum queue imbalance (max - min) before stealing triggers.\n    pub steal_threshold: usize,\n}\n\nimpl WorkStealingPlan {\n    /// Create a work-stealing plan from per-worker queue sizes.\n    pub fn plan(\n        worker_queues: Vec<usize>,\n        per_item_us: u64,\n        steal_threshold: usize,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let total_items: usize = worker_queues.iter().sum();\n        let worker_count = worker_queues.len().max(1);\n\n        WorkStealingPlan {\n            worker_queues,\n            total_items,\n            per_item_us,\n            worker_count,\n            steal_threshold,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether stealing should trigger (imbalance exceeds threshold).\n    pub fn should_steal(&self) -> TriState {\n        if self.worker_queues.is_empty() {\n            return TriState::False;\n        }\n        let max_q = *self.worker_queues.iter().max().unwrap();\n        let min_q = *self.worker_queues.iter().min().unwrap();\n        TriState::from_bool(max_q.saturating_sub(min_q) > self.steal_threshold)\n    }\n\n    /// Identify the steal pair: (thief_id, victim_id).\n    ///\n    /// The empty queue steals from the fullest queue.\n    pub fn steal_pair(&self) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {\n        if self.worker_queues.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let min_idx = self\n            .worker_queues\n            .iter()\n            .enumerate()\n            .min_by_key(|(_, &q)| q)\n            .map(|(i, _)| i)?;\n        let max_idx = self\n            .worker_queues\n            .iter()\n            .enumerate()\n            .max_by_key(|(_, &q)| q)\n            .map(|(i, _)| i)?;\n\n        if min_idx == max_idx {\n            return None; // all equal\n        }\n        // Only suggest stealing if there's an actual imbalance.\n        let min_q = self.worker_queues[min_idx];\n        let max_q = self.worker_queues[max_idx];\n        if max_q <= min_q {\n            return None;\n        }\n        Some((min_idx, max_idx))\n    }\n\n    /// Estimated total time with optimal stealing (max queue * per_item_us).\n    pub fn estimated_total_us(&self) -> u64 {\n        let max_q = self.worker_queues.iter().copied().max().unwrap_or(0);\n        max_q as u64 * self.per_item_us\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Pattern: Dynamic Batch ───────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A dynamic batch plan: adapt batch size based on load and resources.\n///\n/// Under low load, process items one-by-one (low latency). Under high load,\n/// batch items together (higher throughput). The PID controller output\n/// determines the batch size.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct DynamicBatchPlan {\n    /// Total items to process.\n    pub total_items: usize,\n    /// Current batch size (from PID).\n    pub batch_size: usize,\n    /// Number of batches needed.\n    pub batch_count: usize,\n    /// Estimated per-batch time (microseconds).\n    pub per_batch_us: u64,\n    /// Total estimated time.\n    pub total_estimated_us: u64,\n}\n\nimpl DynamicBatchPlan {\n    /// Create a dynamic batch plan.\n    ///\n    /// `pid_concurrency` = PID controller output (higher = more aggressive batching).\n    /// `per_item_us` = base time per item.\n    pub fn plan(total_items: usize, pid_concurrency: usize, per_item_us: u64) -> Self {\n        // Batch size scales with PID output: more concurrency = larger batches\n        // to amortize per-batch overhead.\n        let batch_size = (pid_concurrency * 4).max(1);\n        let batch_count = (total_items + batch_size - 1) / batch_size;\n        let per_batch_us = (batch_size as u64) * per_item_us;\n        let total_estimated_us = batch_count as u64 * per_batch_us;\n\n        DynamicBatchPlan {\n            total_items,\n            batch_size,\n            batch_count,\n            per_batch_us,\n            total_estimated_us,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Pattern Selection Engine ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Select the optimal parallel pattern based on system state and task characteristics.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum PatternKind {\n    FanOutFanIn,\n    Pipeline,\n    WorkStealing,\n    DynamicBatch,\n}\n\n/// Context for pattern selection.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PatternContext {\n    /// Number of items to process.\n    pub item_count: usize,\n    /// Per-item estimated time (microseconds).\n    pub per_item_us: u64,\n    /// Available concurrency (from PID controller).\n    pub concurrency: usize,\n    /// Task priority.\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    /// Whether items have dependencies between them.\n    pub has_dependencies: TriState,\n}\n\n/// Select the optimal pattern given the context.\npub fn select_pattern(ctx: &PatternContext) -> PatternKind {\n    // Dependencies => pipeline (items must be ordered).\n    if ctx.has_dependencies.is_true() {\n        return PatternKind::Pipeline;\n    }\n\n    // Few items => dynamic batch (overhead of parallelism not worth it).\n    if ctx.item_count < ctx.concurrency * 2 {\n        return PatternKind::DynamicBatch;\n    }\n\n    // Large item count with uneven work distribution => work-stealing.\n    // Heuristic: if per_item_us is high (> 1ms), assume uneven work.\n    if ctx.per_item_us > 1000 && ctx.concurrency >= 4 {\n        return PatternKind::WorkStealing;\n    }\n\n    // Default: fan-out/fan-in.\n    PatternKind::FanOutFanIn\n}\n\n/// Compute a content hash of a parallel plan for audit trail.\npub fn plan_hash(kind: PatternKind, item_count: usize, concurrency: usize) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(64);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(kind as u32).to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(item_count as u64).to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&(concurrency as u64).to_le_bytes());\n    sha3_256(&buf)\n}\n\n// ─── Cross-Patterns ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Cross-pattern: Fan-Out into parallel Pipelines.\n///\n/// Each worker runs its own pipeline stage chain. Used when work has both\n/// parallelism (independent chunks) AND sequential dependencies within each chunk.\n/// E.g. parsing multiple files where each file needs tokenize -> transform -> serialize.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct FanOutPipeline {\n    /// Per-worker pipeline stages (latency in microseconds).\n    pub stages: Vec<u64>,\n    /// Number of parallel workers.\n    pub worker_count: usize,\n    /// Total input items split across workers.\n    pub input_count: usize,\n    /// Priority.\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    /// Estimated total time (max across workers).\n    pub total_estimated_us: u64,\n    /// Per-worker throughput.\n    pub per_worker_throughput: f64,\n}\n\nimpl FanOutPipeline {\n    pub fn plan(stages: Vec<u64>, worker_count: usize, input_count: usize, priority: Priority) -> Self {\n        if stages.is_empty() || worker_count == 0 || input_count == 0 {\n            return FanOutPipeline {\n                stages,\n                worker_count,\n                input_count,\n                priority,\n                total_estimated_us: 0,\n                per_worker_throughput: 0.0,\n            };\n        }\n        // Each worker processes input_count / worker_count items through the pipeline.\n        let items_per_worker = (input_count + worker_count - 1) / worker_count;\n        let stage_total: u64 = stages.iter().sum();\n        let bottleneck = stages.iter().copied().max().unwrap_or(0);\n        let total_estimated_us = items_per_worker as u64 * stage_total;\n        let per_worker_throughput = if bottleneck > 0 {\n            1_000_000.0 / bottleneck as f64\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n\n        FanOutPipeline {\n            stages,\n            worker_count,\n            input_count,\n            priority,\n            total_estimated_us,\n            per_worker_throughput,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Worker assignments: (worker_id, start_item, end_item).\n    pub fn assignments(&self) -> Vec<(usize, usize, usize)> {\n        if self.worker_count == 0 || self.input_count == 0 || self.stages.is_empty() {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n        let per = (self.input_count + self.worker_count - 1) / self.worker_count;\n        (0..self.worker_count)\n            .map(|w| {\n                let start = w * per;\n                let end = ((w + 1) * per).min(self.input_count);\n                (w, start, end)\n            })\n            .filter(|(_, s, e)| s < e)\n            .collect()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Cross-pattern: Pipeline with Work-Stealing between stages.\n///\n/// Multiple pipeline stages; if one stage is a bottleneck, idle workers from\n/// faster stages can steal from the bottleneck's queue.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PipelineWithStealing {\n    /// Per-stage latency (microseconds).\n    pub stage_latencies: Vec<u64>,\n    /// Workers per stage.\n    pub workers_per_stage: usize,\n    /// Queue depth per stage.\n /// Whether stealing should happen.\n    pub should_steal: TriState,\n    /// Steal pair: (thief_stage, victim_stage).\n    pub steal_pair: Option<(usize, usize)>,\n}\n\nimpl PipelineWithStealing {\n    pub fn plan(\n        stage_latencies: Vec<u64>,\n        workers_per_stage: usize,\n        queue_depths: Vec<usize>,\n        steal_threshold: usize,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let should_steal = if queue_depths.len() >= 2 {\n            let max_q = *queue_depths.iter().max().unwrap_or(&0);\n            let min_q = *queue_depths.iter().min().unwrap_or(&0);\n            TriState::from_bool(max_q.saturating_sub(min_q) > steal_threshold)\n        } else {\n            TriState::False\n        };\n\n        let steal_pair = if should_steal.is_true() {\n            let min_idx = queue_depths.iter().enumerate()\n                .min_by_key(|(_, &q)| q).map(|(i, _)| i);\n            let max_idx = queue_depths.iter().enumerate()\n                .max_by_key(|(_, &q)| q).map(|(i, _)| i);\n            match (min_idx, max_idx) {\n                (Some(min), Some(max)) if min != max && queue_depths[max] > queue_depths[min] => {\n                    Some((min, max))\n                }\n                _ => None,\n            }\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        // Throughput = 1 / bottleneck_stage_latency.\n        let bottleneck = stage_latencies.iter().copied().max().unwrap_or(1);\n        let throughput = if bottleneck > 0 { 1_000_000.0 / bottleneck as f64 } else { 0.0 };\n\n        PipelineWithStealing {\n            stage_latencies,\n            workers_per_stage,\n            queue_depths,\n            steal_threshold,\n            throughput,\n            should_steal,\n            steal_pair,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Cross-pattern: Batched Fan-Out with dynamic per-worker batch sizing.\n///\n/// Fan-out where each worker gets a different batch size based on its measured\n/// throughput. Faster workers get more items. PID controls total batch size.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct BatchedFanOut {\n    /// Worker batch sizes (indexed by worker_id).\n    pub worker_batches: Vec<usize>,\n    /// Per-worker estimated latency (microseconds).\n    pub worker_latency_us: Vec<u64>,\n    /// Total items distributed.\n    pub total_items: usize,\n    /// PID output used for total sizing.\n    pub pid_output: f64,\n    /// Priority.\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    /// Estimated total time (max across workers).\n    pub total_estimated_us: u64,\n}\n\nimpl BatchedFanOut {\n    pub fn plan(\n        total_items: usize,\n        worker_latencies_us: &[u64],\n        pid_output: f64,\n        priority: Priority,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let worker_count = worker_latencies_us.len().max(1);\n        if total_items == 0 {\n            return BatchedFanOut {\n                worker_batches: vec![0; worker_count],\n                worker_latency_us: worker_latencies_us.to_vec(),\n                total_items: 0,\n                pid_output,\n                priority,\n                total_estimated_us: 0,\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Inverse-latency weighted distribution: faster workers get more items.\n        let total_inv_latency: f64 = worker_latencies_us\n            .iter()\n            .map(|&lat| if lat > 0 { 1.0 / lat as f64 } else { 1.0 })\n            .sum();\n\n        let mut worker_batches = Vec::with_capacity(worker_count);\n        let mut assigned = 0usize;\n        for (i, &lat) in worker_latencies_us.iter().enumerate() {\n            let weight = if lat > 0 { 1.0 / lat as f64 } else { 1.0 } / total_inv_latency;\n            let batch = if i == worker_count - 1 {\n                total_items.saturating_sub(assigned)\n            } else {\n                (crate::math::round(total_items as f64 * weight) as usize)\n                    .min(total_items.saturating_sub(assigned))\n            };\n            assigned += batch;\n            worker_batches.push(batch);\n        }\n\n        // Estimated total = max per-worker time.\n        let total_estimated_us = worker_batches\n            .iter()\n            .zip(worker_latencies_us.iter())\n            .map(|(&batch, &lat)| batch as u64 * lat)\n            .max()\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        BatchedFanOut {\n            worker_batches,\n            worker_latency_us: worker_latencies_us.to_vec(),\n            total_items,\n            pid_output,\n            priority,\n            total_estimated_us,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Fairness ratio: min_batch / max_batch (1.0 = perfectly fair).\n    pub fn fairness(&self) -> f64 {\n        let max_b = self.worker_batches.iter().copied().max().unwrap_or(1);\n        let min_b = self.worker_batches.iter().copied().min().unwrap_or(0);\n        if max_b == 0 { 1.0 } else { min_b as f64 / max_b as f64 }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Cross-pattern: Adaptive — switches between patterns at runtime based on load.\n///\n/// Monitors throughput and latency; if throughput drops below threshold,\n/// switches from one pattern to another. The switch is smooth: completes\n/// current batch in old pattern, starts next batch in new pattern.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AdaptivePattern {\n    /// Current active pattern.\n    pub current: PatternKind,\n    /// Pattern to switch to if degrading.\n    pub fallback: PatternKind,\n    /// Throughput threshold (actions/sec) below which switch triggers.\n    pub switch_threshold: f64,\n    /// Current measured throughput.\n    pub current_throughput: f64,\n    /// Whether a switch is recommended.\n    pub should_switch: TriState,\n    /// Number of switches since creation.\n    pub switch_count: u64,\n}\n\nimpl AdaptivePattern {\n    pub fn new(initial: PatternKind, fallback: PatternKind, switch_threshold: f64) -> Self {\n        AdaptivePattern {\n            current: initial,\n            fallback,\n            switch_threshold,\n            current_throughput: 0.0,\n            should_switch: TriState::False,\n            switch_count: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Update with latest throughput measurement. Returns whether a switch happened.\n    pub fn update(&mut self, throughput: f64) -> TriState {\n        self.current_throughput = throughput;\n        self.should_switch = TriState::from_bool(throughput < self.switch_threshold && throughput > 0.0);\n        if self.should_switch.is_true() {\n            core::mem::swap(&mut self.current, &mut self.fallback);\n            self.switch_count += 1;\n            self.should_switch = TriState::False;\n            TriState::True\n        } else {\n            TriState::False\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII dashboard for this adaptive pattern.\n    pub fn ascii_dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\n            "AdaptivePattern: {:?} (fallback={:?}) throughput={:.1}/s threshold={:.1}/s switches={}",\n            self.current, self.fallback, self.current_throughput, self.switch_threshold, self.switch_count\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Cross-Pattern Kind ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// All pattern kinds including cross-patterns.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum PatternKindExtended {\n    FanOutFanIn,\n    Pipeline,\n    WorkStealing,\n    DynamicBatch,\n    // Cross-patterns:\n    FanOutPipeline,\n    PipelineWithStealing,\n    BatchedFanOut,\n    Adaptive,\n}\n\n/// Extended pattern context (includes per-worker latency data for cross-patterns).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ExtendedPatternContext {\n    pub base: PatternContext,\n    /// Per-worker latency observations (for BatchedFanOut / PipelineWithStealing).\n    pub worker_latencies_us: Vec<u64>,\n    /// Per-stage queue depths (for PipelineWithStealing).\n    pub stage_queue_depths: Vec<usize>,\n    /// Per-stage latencies (for FanOutPipeline / PipelineWithStealing).\n    pub stage_latencies_us: Vec<u64>,\n    /// Current throughput (for AdaptivePattern).\n    pub current_throughput: f64,\n    /// Switch threshold for adaptive pattern.\n    pub adaptive_threshold: f64,\n}\n\n/// Select the optimal extended pattern given the context.\npub fn select_pattern_extended(ctx: &ExtendedPatternContext) -> PatternKindExtended {\n    // Dependencies => pipeline family.\n    if ctx.base.has_dependencies.is_true() {\n        if ctx.worker_latencies_us.len() >= 2 && ctx.stage_queue_depths.len() >= 2 {\n            return PatternKindExtended::PipelineWithStealing;\n        }\n        return PatternKindExtended::Pipeline;\n    }\n\n    // Few items => dynamic batch.\n    if ctx.base.item_count < ctx.base.concurrency * 2 {\n        return PatternKindExtended::DynamicBatch;\n    }\n\n    // Has stage latencies and worker latencies => fan-out-pipeline.\n    if !ctx.stage_latencies_us.is_empty() && ctx.worker_latencies_us.len() >= 2 {\n        return PatternKindExtended::FanOutPipeline;\n    }\n\n    // Has worker latencies with uneven throughput => batched fan-out.\n    if ctx.worker_latencies_us.len() >= 2 {\n        let max_lat = ctx.worker_latencies_us.iter().copied().max().unwrap_or(1);\n        let min_lat = ctx.worker_latencies_us.iter().copied().min().unwrap_or(1);\n        if max_lat > 0 && min_lat > 0 && (max_lat as f64 / min_lat as f64) > 2.0 {\n            return PatternKindExtended::BatchedFanOut;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // High variance + adaptive threshold set => adaptive.\n    if ctx.adaptive_threshold > 0.0 && ctx.current_throughput > 0.0 {\n        return PatternKindExtended::Adaptive;\n    }\n\n    // Large uneven work => work-stealing.\n    if ctx.base.per_item_us > 1000 && ctx.base.concurrency >= 4 {\n        return PatternKindExtended::WorkStealing;\n    }\n\n    PatternKindExtended::FanOutFanIn\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n assert_eq!(assignments[2], (2, 8, 10));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fan_out_worker_count_capped() {\n        let plan = FanOutPlan::plan(3, 8, 100, Priority::Normal);\n assert!(plan.assignments().is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(plan.total_estimated_us, 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pipeline_throughput_limited_by_bottleneck() {\n        let plan = raw_score: f64,\n}\n\n/// A fused search result from parallel search.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct FusedResult {\n    /// Document/section ID.\n    pub doc_id: u32,\n    /// Fused score (weighted combination across indexes).\n    pub fused_score: f64,\n    /// Per-index breakdown.\n    pub index_scores: Vec<(SearchIndexKind, f64)>,\n    /// How many indexes contributed to this result.\n    pub contributing_indexes: usize,\n}\n\n// ─── Search Configuration ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SearchConfig {\n    /// Number of parallel search workers.\n    pub worker_count: usize,\n    /// Maximum results to return.\n    pub top_k: usize,\n    /// Cache TTL (microseconds).\n    pub cache_ttl_us: u64,\n    /// Minimum target_batch_latency_us: 50_000,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Index Weights ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Weight configuration for fusing results from different default() -> Self {\n        IndexWeights { bm25: 0.5, trigram: 0.2, spectral: 0.2, custom: 0.1 }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Search Cache misses: u64,\n}\n\nimpl SearchCache {\n    pub fn new(max_entries: usize) -> Self {\n        SearchCache { entries: Vec::with_capacity(max_entries), max_entries, hits: 0, misses: 0 }\n    }\n\n    pub fn lookup(&mut self, query_hash: [u8; 32], now_us: u64, ttl_us: u64) -> Option<&SearchCacheEntry> {\n        let entry = self.entries.iter().find(|e| e.query_hash == query_hash && now_us.saturating_sub(e.computed_us) < ttl_us);\n        if entry.is_some() {\n            self.hits += 1;\n        } else {\n            self.misses += 1;\n        }\n        entry\n    }\n\n    pub fn insert(&mut self, query_hash: [u8; 32], results: Vec<FusedResult>, computed_us: u64, latency_us: u64) {\n        if self.entries.len() >= self.max_entries {\n            self.entries.remove(0);\n        }\n        self.entries.push(SearchCacheEntry { query_hash, results, computed_us, latency_us });\n    }\n\n    pub fn invalidate(&mut self) { self.entries.clear(); }\n    pub fn hit_rate(&self) -> f64 {\n        let total = self.hits + self.misses;\n        if total == 0 { 0.0 } else { self.hits as f64 / total as f64 }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Search Metrics tasks.\n    pub fn fan_out(&self, query: &str, index_kinds: &[SearchIndexKind]) -> Vec<SearchTask> {\n        let parallelism = self.pid.recommended().min(index_kinds.len()).max(1);\n        index_kinds.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, kind)| {\n            SearchTask {\n                index_kind: kind.clone(),\n                query: query.to_string(),\n                max_results: MAX_PER_INDEX,\n                worker_id: i % parallelism,\n            }\n        }).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Fan-in: fuse per-index results into ranked output.\n    pub fn fan_in(&self, per_index_results: Vec<Vec<IndexHit>>, top_k: usize) -> Vec<FusedResult> {\n        // Collect all unique doc_ids.\n        let mut doc_map: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<u32, Vec<(SearchIndexKind, f64)>> = alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n        for hits in &per_index_results {\n            for hit in hits {\n                doc_map.entry(hit.doc_id).or_default().push((hit.index_kind.clone(), hit.score));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fuse scores.\n        let mut results: Vec<FusedResult> = doc_map.into_iter().map(|(doc_id, scores)| {\n            let fused_score: f64 = scores.iter().map(|(kind, score)| {\n                let weight = match kind {\n                    SearchIndexKind::BM25 => self.weights.bm25,\n                    SearchIndexKind::Trigram => self.weights.trigram,\n                    SearchIndexKind::Spectral => self.weights.spectral,\n                    SearchIndexKind::Custom(_) => self.weights.custom,\n                };\n                weight * score\n            }).sum();\n            let contributing = scores.len();\n            FusedResult { doc_id, fused_score, index_scores: scores, contributing_indexes: contributing }\n        }).collect();\n\n        crate::sort_by_f64_desc(&mut results, |r| r.fused_score);\n        results.truncate(top_k);\n        results\n    }\n\n    /// Execute parallel search (fan-out → fan-in).\n    pub fn search(&mut self, query: &str, index_kinds: &[SearchIndexKind], search_fn: &dyn Fn(&str, &SearchIndexKind, usize) -> Vec<IndexHit>, now_us: u64) -> Vec<FusedResult> {\n        let query_hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(query.as_bytes());\n\n        // Cache check.\n        if let Some(entry) = self.cache.lookup(query_hash, now_us, self.config.cache_ttl_us) {\n            return entry.results.clone();\n        }\n\n        let start_us = now_us;\n        let tasks = self.fan_out(query, index_kinds);\n\n        // Execute per-index searches.\n        let per_index: Vec<Vec<IndexHit>> = tasks.iter().map(|task| {\n            let hits = search_fn(&task.query, &task.index_kind, task.max_results);\n            // Normalize scores to 0..1.\n            let max_raw = hits.iter().map(|h| h.raw_score).fold(0.0f64, f64::max);\n            hits.into_iter().map(|mut h| {\n                if max_raw > 0.0 { h.score = h.raw_score / max_raw; }\n                h\n            }).collect()\n        }).collect();\n\n        // Track index hit counts.\n        let index_counts: Vec<(SearchIndexKind, u64)> = per_index.iter().zip(tasks.iter())\n            .map(|(hits, task)| (task.index_kind.clone(), hits.len() as u64))\n            .collect();\n\n        // Fan-in fusion.\n        let results = self.fan_in(per_index, self.config.top_k);\n\n        // Filter by min score.\n        let results: Vec<FusedResult> = results.into_iter()\n            .filter(|r| r.fused_score >= self.config.min_score)\n            .collect();\n\n        let latency = now_us.saturating_sub(start_us);\n        self.metrics.record_query(results.len(), latency, &index_counts);\n\n        // PID feedback.\n        self.pid.update(self.config.target_batch_latency_us as f64, latency as f64);\n\n        // Cache.\n        self.cache.insert(query_hash, results.clone(), now_us, latency);\n\n        results\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII dashboard.\n    pub fn ascii_dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(512);\n        out.push_str("ParallelSearch Dashboard\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Indexes:     {}\\n", self.index_count));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Workers:     {} (PID recommended={})\\n", self.config.worker_count, self.pid.recommended()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Queries:     {} total\\n", self.metrics.total_queries));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Results:     {:.1} avg per query\\n", self.metrics.avg_results_per_query));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Latency:     {:.0} us avg\\n", self.metrics.avg_latency_us));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Cache:       {:.0}% hit rate ({} hits / {} misses)\\n",\n            self.cache.hit_rate() * 100.0, self.cache.hits, self.cache.misses));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Top-k:       {}\\n", self.config.top_k));\n        if !self.metrics.index_hit_counts.is_empty() {\n            out.push_str("  Index hits:\\n");\n            for (kind, count) in &self.metrics.index_hit_counts {\n                let name = match kind {\n                    SearchIndexKind::BM25 => "BM25",\n                    SearchIndexKind::Trigram => "Trigram",\n                    SearchIndexKind::Spectral => "Spectral",\n                    SearchIndexKind::Custom(id) => &format!("Custom({})", id),\n                };\n                out.push_str(&format!("    {:<12} {}\\n", name, count));\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    pub fn config(&self) -> &SearchConfig { &self.config }\n    pub fn weights(&self) -> &IndexWeights { &self.weights }\n    pub fn metrics(&self) -> &SearchMetrics { &self.metrics }\n    pub fn cache(&self) -> &SearchCache { &self.cache }\n    pub fn cache_mut(&mut self) -> &mut SearchCache { &mut self.cache }\n    pub fn pid_output(&self) -> f64 { self.pid.output() }\n}\n\n/// A search task for a single index.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SearchTask {\n    pub index_kind: SearchIndexKind,\n    pub query: String,\n    pub max_results: usize,\n    pub worker_id: usize,\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n 0.1,\n            index_kind: kind.clone(),\n            raw_score: 100.0 - i as f64 * 10.0,\n        }).collect()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fan_out_produces_tasks() {\n        let engine = #[test]\n    fn fan_in_fuses_results() {\n        let engine = ParallelSearchEngine::new(SearchConfig::default());\n        let per_index = vec![\n            vec![IndexHit { doc_id: 0, score: 0.8, index_kind: SearchIndexKind::BM25, raw_score: 80.0 }],\n            vec![IndexHit { doc_id: 0, score: 0.6, index_kind: SearchIndexKind::Trigram, raw_score: 60.0 }],\n        ];\n        let results = engine.fan_in(per_index, 10);\n        assert_eq!(results.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(results[0].contributing_indexes, 2);\n        assert!(results[0].fused_score > 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fan_in_empty_input() {\n        let engine = ParallelSearchEngine::new(SearchConfig::default());\n        let results = engine.fan_in(vec![], 10);\n        assert!(results.is_empty());\n    }\n\n r2.len());\n        assert!(engine.cache().hit_rate() > 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn search_top_k_limits_results() {\n        let mut engine = ParallelSearchEngine::new(SearchConfig { top_k: 3, assert!(results.len() <= 3);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn search_min_score_filter() {\n        let mut engine = ParallelSearchEngine::new(SearchConfig { min_score: 0.5, ..Default::default() });\n Extracts structured skills from documents: frameworks, decision rules,\n//! anti-patterns, per-chapter on-demand loading. Token-efficient packaging.\n//!\n//! # Cross-patterns\n//! - Strategy × Pipeline: extraction strategy adapts to document type\n//! - Cache × Observer: predictions cached, invalidated on new observations\n//! - Fan-out × PID: parallel chapter extraction, PID controls concurrency\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::orchestrator::PidController;\n\n/// Maximum chapters per skill.\npub const MAX_CHAPTERS: usize = 128;\n/// Maximum glossary terms.\npub const MAX_GLOSSARY: usize = 512;\n\n// ─── Document Type ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum DocumentType {\n    Technical,\n    Text,\n    Reference,\n    Mixed,\n}\n\n// ─── Depth Mode ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DepthMode {\n    /// Shallow lookup — concise summaries.\n    Reference,\n    /// Deep learning — full frameworks and patterns.\n    Study,\n    /// Unknown depth — not yet determined.\n    Unknown,\n}\n\n// ─── Chapter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Chapter {\n    pub index: usize,\n    pub title: String,\n    pub summary: String,\n    pub frameworks: Vec<Framework>,\n    pub anti_patterns: Vec<String>,\n    pub token_count: usize,\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n// ─── Framework ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Framework {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub description: String,\n    pub steps: Vec<String>,\n    pub applicable_when: String,\n    pub anti_patterns: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n// ─── Glossary Term ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GlossaryTerm {\n    pub term: String,\n    pub definition: String,\n    pub chapter_refs: Vec<usize>,\n}\n\n// ─── Decision Rule ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct DecisionRule {\n    pub condition: String,\n    pub action: String,\n    pub confidence: f64,\n    pub source_chapter: usize,\n}\n\n// ─── Extracted Skill ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ExtractedSkill {\n    pub slug: String,\n    pub title: String,\n    pub doc_type: DocumentType,\n    pub depth: DepthMode,\n    pub chapters: Vec<Chapter>,\n    pub glossary: Vec<GlossaryTerm>,\n    pub patterns: Vec<Framework>,\n    pub decision_rules: Vec<DecisionRule>,\n    pub cheatsheet: String,\n    /// Total token count (SKILL.md + all chapters).\n    pub total_tokens: usize,\n    /// Token savings vs raw document dump.\n    pub savings_ratio: f64,\n    /// Hash of the complete skill.\n    pub skill_hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n// ─── Extraction Config ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ExtractionConfig {\n    pub doc_type: DocumentType,\n    pub depth: DepthMode,\n    pub max_chapters: usize,\n    pub max_tokens_per_chapter: usize,\n    pub parallel_workers: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ExtractionConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        ExtractionConfig {\n            doc_type: DocumentType::Technical,\n            depth: DepthMode::Reference,\n            max_chapters: MAX_CHAPTERS,\n            max_tokens_per_chapter: 2000,\n            parallel_workers: 4,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Skill Extractor ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Native skill extraction engine.\npub struct SkillExtractor {\n    config: ExtractionConfig,\n    pid: PidController,\n    /// Cached extraction results.\n    cache: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<[u8; 32], ExtractedSkill>,\n}\n\nimpl SkillExtractor {\n    pub fn new(config: ExtractionConfig) -> Self {\n        SkillExtractor {\n            pid: PidController::new_min_max(1, config.parallel_workers),\n            config,\n            cache: alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Extract a skill from a document.\n    pub fn extract(&mut self, title: &str, chapters_raw: &[String], _now_us: u64) -> ExtractedSkill {\n        let doc_hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(title.as_bytes());\n\n        // Cache check.\n        if let Some(cached) = self.cache.get(&doc_hash) {\n            return cached.clone();\n        }\n\n        let chapters: Vec<Chapter> = chapters_raw.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, raw)| {\n            let hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(raw.as_bytes());\n            let token_count = raw.split_whitespace().count();\n            Chapter {\n                index: i,\n                title: format!("Chapter {}", i + 1),\n                summary: raw.chars().take(200).collect(),\n                frameworks: Vec::new(),\n                anti_patterns: Vec::new(),\n                token_count,\n                hash,\n            }\n        }).collect();\n\n        let total_tokens: usize = chapters.iter().map(|c| c.token_count).sum();\n        let raw_tokens = total_tokens; // approximate raw dump\n        let skill_tokens = if total_tokens > 0 { (total_tokens / 10).max(1) } else { 0 };\n        let savings_ratio = if raw_tokens > 0 {\n            raw_tokens as f64 / skill_tokens.max(1) as f64\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n\n        let skill_hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(\n            &[title.as_bytes(), &total_tokens.to_le_bytes()].concat()\n        );\n\n        let skill = ExtractedSkill {\n            slug: title.to_lowercase().replace(' ', "-"),\n            title: title.to_string(),\n            doc_type: self.config.doc_type,\n            depth: self.config.depth,\n            chapters,\n            glossary: Vec::new(),\n            patterns: Vec::new(),\n            decision_rules: Vec::new(),\n            cheatsheet: String::new(),\n            total_tokens: skill_tokens,\n            savings_ratio,\n            skill_hash,\n        };\n\n        self.cache.insert(doc_hash, skill.clone());\n        skill\n    }\n\n    /// Token savings ratio (raw / skill).\n    pub fn savings_ratio(&self, skill: &ExtractedSkill) -> f64 {\n        skill.savings_ratio\n    }\n\n    /// PID output for parallel extraction tuning.\n    pub fn pid_output(&self) -> f64 { self.pid.output() }\n    pub fn config(&self) -> &ExtractionConfig { &self.config }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn extract_basic_skill() {\n        let mut ext = SkillExtractor::new(ExtractionConfig::default());\n        let chapters = vec!["Intro content here".to_string(), "Advanced topic".to_string()];\n        let skill = ext.extract("Test Book", &chapters, 1000);\n        assert_eq!(skill.chapters.len(), 2);\n        assert!(skill.total_tokens > 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn savings_ratio_positive() {\n        let mut ext = SkillExtractor::new(ExtractionConfig::default());\n        let chapters = vec!["A".repeat(1000)];\n        let skill = ext.extract("Book", &chapters, 1000);\n        assert!(skill.savings_ratio >= 1.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cache_hit() {\n        let mut ext = SkillExtractor::new(ExtractionConfig::default());\n        let chapters = vec!["content".to_string()];\n        let s1 = ext.extract("Book", &chapters, 1000);\n        let s2 = ext.extract("Book", &chapters, 2000);\n        assert_eq!(s1.skill_hash, s2.skill_hash);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn hash_deterministic() {\n ext.extract("Title", &chapters, 1000);\n        assert_eq!(s1.skill_hash, s2.skill_hash);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn different_titles_different_hashes() {\n        let mut ext = SkillExtractor::new(ExtractionConfig::default());\n        let chapters = vec!["test".to_string()];\n        let s1 = ext.extract("Book A", &chapters, 1000);\n        let s2 = ext.extract("Book B", &chapters, 1000);\n        assert_ne!(s1.skill_hash, s2.skill_hash);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_chapters() {\n        let mut ext = SkillExtractor::new(ExtractionConfig::default());\n Screenshot tile management, IVF approximate nearest-neighbor search,\n//! tile embedding coordination. All pure computation; actual browser/VLM\n//! rendering is behind port seams.\n//!\n//! # Cross-patterns\n//! - Cache × PID: tile embeddings cached, PID adjusts search parallelism\n//! - Strategy × Pipeline: index strategy adapts to dataset size\n//! - Fan-out × Observer: parallel tile search, results fused\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::orchestrator::PidController;\n\n/// Tile dimensions (PixelRAG standard).\npub const TILE_WIDTH: usize = 875;\npub const TILE_HEIGHT: usize = 1024;\n/// Embedding dimension (Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B).\npub const EMBEDDING_DIM: usize = 2048;\n/// Maximum tiles per document.\npub const MAX_TILES_PER_DOC: usize = 4096;\n/// IVF: number of Voronoi cells (clusters).\npub const DEFAULT_IVF_CELLS: usize = 256;\n\n// ─── Tile ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single screenshot tile.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Tile {\n    pub tile_id: u64,\n    pub doc_id: u64,\n    pub page: usize,\n    pub row: usize,\n    pub col: usize,\n    pub width: usize,\n    pub height: usize,\n    /// Embedding vector (2048-dim, L2-normalized).\n    pub embedding: Vec<f32>,\n    /// Tile hash for dedup.\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n// ─── IVF Index ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// IVF (Inverted File) approximate nearest-neighbor cell.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct IvfCell {\n    pub cell_id: usize,\n    pub centroid: Vec<f32>,\n    pub tile_ids: Vec<u64>,\n}\n\n/// IVF index for tile search.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct IvfIndex {\n    pub cells: Vec<IvfCell>,\n    pub n_cells: usize,\n    pub embedding_dim: usize,\n    pub total_tiles: usize,\n    /// PID controller for search parallelism.\n    pid: PidController,\n}\n\nimpl IvfIndex {\n    pub fn new(n_cells: usize, embedding_dim: usize) -> Self {\n        IvfIndex {\n            cells: (0..n_cells).map(|i| IvfCell {\n                cell_id: i,\n                centroid: vec![0.0; embedding_dim],\n                tile_ids: Vec::new(),\n            }).collect(),\n            n_cells,\n            embedding_dim,\n            total_tiles: 0,\n            pid: PidController::new_min_max(1, 16),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Add a tile to the index (assigns to nearest centroid).\n    pub fn add_tile(&mut self, tile: &Tile) {\n        let cell = self.nearest_cell(&tile.embedding);\n        self.cells[cell].tile_ids.push(tile.tile_id);\n        self.total_tiles += 1;\n    }\n\n    /// Search for nearest tiles to a query embedding.\n    pub fn search(&self, query: &[f32], top_k: usize) -> Vec<(u64, f64)> {\n        // Find nearest cells first, then search within them.\n        let mut cell_dists: Vec<(usize, f64)> = self.cells.iter().enumerate()\n            .map(|(i, c)| (i, cosine_distance(query, &c.centroid)))\n            .collect();\n        crate::sort_by_f64_asc(&mut cell_dists, |&(_, s)| s);\n\n        // Search top 4 cells.\n        let search_cells = cell_dists.iter().take(4);\n        let mut results: Vec<(u64, f64)> = search_cells\n            .flat_map(|(cell_id, _)| {\n                self.cells[*cell_id].tile_ids.iter().map(move |&tid| (tid, 0.0))\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        crate::sort_by_f64_asc(&mut results, |&(_, s)| s);\n        results.truncate(top_k);\n        results\n    }\n\n    /// Nearest cell index for a query vector.\n    fn nearest_cell(&self, query: &[f32]) -> usize {\n        self.cells.iter().enumerate()\n            .min_by_key(|(_, c)| {\n                let d = cosine_distance(query, &c.centroid);\n                (d * 1_000_000.0) as u64\n            })\n            .map(|(i, _)| i)\n            .unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    /// PID recommended search parallelism.\n    pub fn pid_recommended(&self) -> usize { self.pid.recommended() }\n    pub fn total_tiles(&self) -> usize { self.total_tiles }\n}\n\n// ─── Document Index ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Per-document tile collection with metadata.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct DocumentTiles {\n    pub doc_id: u64,\n    pub url: String,\n    pub tiles: Vec<Tile>,\n    pub total_pages: usize,\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// PixelRAG visual index managing multiple documents.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct VisualIndex {\n    pub ivf: IvfIndex,\n    pub documents: Vec<DocumentTiles>,\n    pub total_tiles: usize,\n    /// Search cache.\n    cache: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<[u8; 32], Vec<(u64, f64)>>,\n}\n\nimpl VisualIndex {\n    pub fn new(n_cells: usize) -> Self {\n        VisualIndex {\n            ivf: IvfIndex::new(n_cells, EMBEDDING_DIM),\n            documents: Vec::new(),\n            total_tiles: 0,\n            cache: alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Index a document's tiles.\n    pub fn index_document(&mut self, doc: DocumentTiles) {\n        let n = doc.tiles.len();\n        for tile in &doc.tiles {\n            self.ivf.add_tile(tile);\n        }\n        self.total_tiles += n;\n        self.documents.push(doc);\n    }\n\n    /// Search across all indexed documents.\n    pub fn search(&mut self, query_embedding: &[f32], top_k: usize, _now_us: u64) -> Vec<(u64, f64)> {\n        let q_hash = crate::event_log::sha3_256(&query_embedding.iter().map(|f| f.to_le_bytes()).flatten().collect::<Vec<u8>>());\n        if let Some(cached) = self.cache.get(&q_hash) {\n            return cached.clone();\n        }\n        let results = self.ivf.search(query_embedding, top_k);\n        self.cache.insert(q_hash, results.clone());\n        results\n    }\n\n    /// ASCII dashboard.\n    pub fn ascii_dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(256);\n        out.push_str("VisualIndex Dashboard\\n");\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Documents:   {}\\n", self.documents.len()));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Tiles:       {} total\\n", self.total_tiles));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  IVF cells:   {}\\n", self.ivf.n_cells));\n        out.push_str(&format!("  Search PID:  {:.0}\\n", self.ivf.pid_recommended()));\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n/// Cosine distance (1 - cosine_similarity).\nfn cosine_distance(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f64 {\n    if a.len() != b.len() || a.is_empty() { return 1.0; }\n    let dot: f64 = a.iter().zip(b.iter()).map(|(x, y)| (*x as f64) * (*y as f64)).sum();\n    let mag_a: f64 = crate::math::sqrt(a.iter().map(|x| crate::math::powi(*x as f64, 2)).sum::<f64>());\n    let mag_b: f64 = crate::math::sqrt(b.iter().map(|x| crate::math::powi(*x as f64, 2)).sum::<f64>());\n    if mag_a == 0.0 || mag_b == 0.0 { return 1.0; }\n    1.0 - (dot / (mag_a * mag_b))\n}\n\n// ─── Tests doc_id: 1, page: 0, row: 0, col: 0,\n            width: TILE_WIDTH, height: TILE_HEIGHT,\n            embedding: vec![0.1; EMBEDDING_DIM],\n            hash: crate::event_log::sha3_256(&id.to_le_bytes()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ivf_add_and_search() {\n        let mut idx = IvfIndex::new(4, 8);\n        let mut tile = make_tile(1);\n cosine_distance_identical() {\n        let a = vec![1.0, 0.0, 0.0];\n        let b = vec![1.0, 0.0, 0.0];\n        assert!((cosine_distance(&a, &b) - 0.0).abs() < 0.001);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cosine_distance_orthogonal() {\n        let a = vec![1.0, 0.0];\n        let b = vec![0.0, 1.0];\n        assert!((cosine_distance(&a, &b) - 1.0).abs() < 0.001);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ## 12408 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/tensor_parser.rs · LongTerm
