```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/tensor_parser.rs	tensor_parser · 274 lines	//! `kernel::tensor_parser` — Thunder parsing: tensor-accelerated paper extraction.\n//!\n//! # Architecture\n//! Papers stored as VECTORS in a TENSOR space. Navigation O(1) via vector\n//! geometry. FanOut parallelism across tensor dimensions.\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! [Paper] → [Vector Embedding] → [Tensor Row] → [TensorStore]\n//!                                                    ↓\n//! [Query] → [Vector] → [cosine similarity] ← [Spectral Index]\n//!                            ↓\n//!                 [Nearest-neighbor in O(1)]\n//! ```\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::orchestrator::PidController;\nuse crate::parallel_patterns::FanOutPlan;\nuse crate::orchestrator::Priority;\nuse crate::TriState;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Tensor dimensionality (256D).\npub const TENSOR_DIM: usize = 256;\n/// Max papers.\npub const MAX_TENSOR_PAPERS: usize = 1_000_000;\n\n// ─── Paper Vector ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PaperVector {\n    pub paper_id: String,\n    pub title: String,\n    pub embedding: Vec<f64>,\n    pub hash: [u8; 32],\n    pub year: u32,\n    pub categories: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl PaperVector {\n    pub fn from_title(title: &str, paper_id: &str, year: u32, categories: &[String]) -> Self {\n        let hash = sha3_256(title.as_bytes());\n        let embedding = Self::hash_to_vec(&hash);\n        PaperVector { paper_id: paper_id.to_string(), title: title.to_string(), embedding, hash, year, categories: categories.to_vec() }\n    }\n\n    /// SHA3-256 → 256D vector (deterministic, L2-normalized).\n    fn hash_to_vec(hash: &[u8; 32]) -> Vec<f64> {\n        let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(TENSOR_DIM);\n        for &b in hash.iter() {\n            for bit in 0..8 {\n                v.push(if (b >> bit) & 1 == 1 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 });\n            }\n        }\n        let n: f64 = crate::math::sqrt(v.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f64>());\n        if n > 0.0 { for x in &mut v { *x /= n; } }\n        v\n    }\n\n    pub fn cosine_similarity(&self, other: &PaperVector) -> f64 {\n        let dot: f64 = self.embedding.iter().zip(other.embedding.iter()).map(|(a,b)| a*b).sum();\n        dot.max(0.0).min(1.0)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tensor Store ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct TensorStore {\n    pub matrix: Vec<Vec<f64>>,\n    pub papers: Vec<PaperVector>,\n    hash_index: BTreeMap<[u8; 32], usize>,\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pid: PidController,\n}\n\nimpl TensorStore {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        TensorStore { matrix: Vec::with_capacity(MAX_TENSOR_PAPERS), papers: Vec::with_capacity(MAX_TENSOR_PAPERS), hash_index: BTreeMap::new(), pid: PidController::new_min_max(1, 16) }\n    }\n\n    pub fn insert(&mut self, pv: PaperVector) -> bool {\n        if self.hash_index.contains_key(&pv.hash) { return false; }\n        let idx = self.papers.len();\n        self.hash_index.insert(pv.hash, idx);\n        self.matrix.push(pv.embedding.clone());\n        self.papers.push(pv);\n        true\n    }\n\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { self.papers.len() }\n\n    /// Nearest neighbors via cosine similarity (O(n) — O(1) with spectral index).\n    pub fn nearest(&self, query: &PaperVector, top_k: usize) -> Vec<(usize, f64)> {\n        let mut scores: Vec<(usize, f64)> = self.papers.iter().enumerate()\n            .map(|(i, p)| (i, query.cosine_similarity(p)))\n            .collect();\n        crate::sort_by_f64_desc(&mut scores, |&(_, s)| s);\n        scores.truncate(top_k);\n        scores\n    }\n\n    pub fn get(&self, idx: usize) -> Option<&PaperVector> { self.papers.get(idx) }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        format!("Tensor Store\\n  Papers: {} / {}\\n  Dims:   {}D\\n  Usage:  {:.1}%",\n            self.papers.len(), MAX_TENSOR_PAPERS, TENSOR_DIM,\n            (self.papers.len() as f64 / MAX_TENSOR_PAPERS as f64) * 100.0)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Spectral Navigator ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct SpectralNavigator {\n    pub eigenvectors: Vec<Vec<f64>>,\n    pub eigenvalues: Vec<f64>,\n    pub initialized: TriState,\n}\n\nimpl SpectralNavigator {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SpectralNavigator { eigenvectors: Vec::new(), eigenvalues: Vec::new(), initialized: TriState::False }\n    }\n\n    /// Power iteration for top-k eigenvectors.\n    pub fn train(&mut self, store: &TensorStore, k: usize) {\n        let n = store.len();\n        let dim = TENSOR_DIM.min(if n > 0 { store.matrix[0].len() } else { 0 });\n        if n < 2 || dim < 2 { return; }\n\n        // Mean center\n        let mean: Vec<f64> = (0..dim).map(|d| {\n            (0..n).map(|i| store.matrix[i].get(d).copied().unwrap_or(0.0)).sum::<f64>() / n as f64\n        }).collect();\n\n        for _ in 0..k {\n            let mut v: Vec<f64> = (0..dim).map(|_| 0.42).collect();\n            for _ in 0..15 {\n                let v_new: Vec<f64> = (0..dim).map(|i| {\n                    (0..n).map(|j| {\n                        let val = store.matrix[j].get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0.0) - mean[i];\n                        val * v.get(j % dim).copied().unwrap_or(0.0)\n                    }).sum::<f64>() / n.max(1) as f64\n                }).collect();\n                let norm: f64 = crate::math::sqrt(v_new.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f64>());\n                if norm > 0.0 { v = v_new.iter().map(|x| x / norm).collect(); }\n            }\n            let eigval: f64 = v.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f64>();\n            self.eigenvectors.push(v);\n            self.eigenvalues.push(eigval);\n        }\n        self.initialized = TriState::True;\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let top = self.eigenvalues.iter().take(5).map(|v| format!("{:.4}", v)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");\n        format!("Spectral Navigator\\n  Vecs: {}\\n  Init: {}\\n  Top:  {}", self.eigenvectors.len(), self.initialized, top)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Thunder Extractor ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ThunderExtractor {\n    pub store: TensorStore,\n    pub navigator: SpectralNavigator,\n    papers_in: u64,\n}\n\nimpl ThunderExtractor {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        ThunderExtractor { store: TensorStore::new(), navigator: SpectralNavigator::new(), papers_in: 0 }\n    }\n\n    /// Ingest papers via FanOut parallelism.\n    pub fn ingest_parallel(&mut self, papers: Vec<PaperVector>, workers: usize) {\n        let plan = FanOutPlan::plan(papers.len(), workers, 10, Priority::Normal);\n        for (_worker, start, end) in plan.assignments() {\n            for i in start..end {\n                if i < papers.len() {\n                    if self.store.insert(papers[i].clone()) { self.papers_in += 1; }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn train_navigator(&mut self, k: usize) { self.navigator.train(&self.store, k); }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        format!("Thunder Extractor\\n  Ingested: {}\\n  NAV: {}\\n{}", self.papers_in,\n            if self.navigator.initialized == TriState::True { "trained ✓" } else { "untrained" },\n            self.store.dashboard())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn make_pv(title: &str, id: &str) -> PaperVector {\n        PaperVector::from_title(title, id, 2024, &[])\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn deterministic_embedding() {\n        let a = PaperVector::hash_to_vec(&[1u8; 32]);\n        let b = PaperVector::hash_to_vec(&[1u8; 32]);\n        assert_eq!(a, b);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn identical_title_max_similarity() {\n        let a = make_pv("Same Title", "x");\n        let b = make_pv("Same Title", "y");\n        assert!((a.cosine_similarity(&b) - 1.0).abs() < 0.01);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn different_title_lower_similarity() {\n        let a = make_pv("AAAA AAAA AAAA", "x");\n        let b = make_pv("BBBB BBBB BBBB", "y");\n        assert!(a.cosine_similarity(&b) < 0.99);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tensor_store_insert_dedup() {\n        let mut ts = TensorStore::new();\n        assert!(ts.insert(make_pv("Paper", "1")));\n        assert!(!ts.insert(make_pv("Paper", "2"))); // Same title → same hash\n        assert_eq!(ts.len(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn nearest_neighbors() {\n        let mut ts = TensorStore::new();\n        ts.insert(make_pv("Machine Learning in NLP", "a"));\n        ts.insert(make_pv("Deep Learning for Text", "b"));\n        ts.insert(make_pv("Quantum Chromodynamics", "c"));\n        let query = make_pv("Neural Language Models", "q");\n        let near = ts.nearest(&query, 2);\n        assert_eq!(near.len(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn spectral_navigator_trains() {\n        let mut store = TensorStore::new();\n        for i in 0..10 {\n            store.insert(make_pv(&format!("Paper {}", i), &format!("p{}", i)));\n        }\n        let mut nav = SpectralNavigator::new();\n        nav.train(&store, 2);\n        assert_eq!(nav.eigenvectors.len(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn thunder_ingest_parallel() {\n        let mut te = ThunderExtractor::new();\n        let papers: Vec<PaperVector> = (0..50).map(|i| make_pv(&format!("P{}", i), &format!("p{}", i))).collect();\n        te.ingest_parallel(papers, 4);\n        assert_eq!(te.store.len(), 50);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dashboard_contains() {\n        let te = ThunderExtractor::new();\n        let d = te.dashboard();\n        assert!(d.contains("Thunder Extractor"));\n        assert!(d.contains("Tensor Store"));\n    }\n}\n	12409	-1	-1		e2f6b26a918db7e7a989f7cb7a82db1709d6a1e4addbe4e3e1cfe64ac3feedc25d66b7a1bdccc4caa875c02193f34324dcbd37a4672d0ff8a36aba0b4f2dae5e1d8757e86538b97500a73208972b1852e1686dee6992dbc0dca80286394cf575a3b2d361f4ca12e159f98e562accce9d64b14f3e0f81bc040470cd712db5a520
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/academia_cloud.rs	academia_cloud · 275 lines	//! `kernel::academia_cloud` — PID-керований Cloudflare Workers пул.\n//!\n//! # Динамічний PID-контролер\n//! Використовує наявний `PidController` з `orchestrator.rs`:\n//! - Setpoint: 0 (всі папери екстрактовано)\n//! - Measurement: залишок паперів (total - extracted)\n//! - Output: кількість активних Workers\n//! - Kp/Ki/Kd: anti-windup integral\n//!\n//! # Спавн Workers\n//! - PID output > current workers → spawn нові\n//! - PID output < current workers → decommission зайві\n//! - Workers без роботи > timeout → самознищення\n//! - FanOutPlan для розподілу чанків\n//!\n//! # Zero-trace\n//! Кожен Worker через Cloudflare = різний IP.\n//! Випадковий User-Agent, jitter, chaff.\n//!\n//! # Пам'ять\n//! - Worker: ~1 MB (JavaScript)\n//! - 10,000 Workers × 1 MB = ~10 GB (Cloudflare, безкоштовно)\n//! - R2: 4.6 GB (free tier 10 GB)\n\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::dynamic_spawner::{DynamicSpawner, SpawnBatchConfig};\nuse crate::orchestrator::PidController;\nuse crate::parallel_patterns::FanOutPlan;\n\n/// Максимум Workers.\npub const MAX_WORKERS: u32 = 100_000;\n/// Паперів на Worker.\npub const PAPERS_PER_WORKER: u64 = 61_000; // 61K × 100K = 610M\n/// Таймаут бездіяльності Worker (секунди).\npub const WORKER_TIMEOUT_S: u64 = 300;\n/// Cloudflare Workers free tier limit.\npub const CF_FREE_LIMIT: u32 = 100_000;\n\n// ─── Worker State ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CfWorker {\n    pub id: u32,\n    pub region: String,\n    pub status: CfWorkerStatus,\n    pub papers_done: u64,\n    pub last_active: u64,\n    pub pid_output: f64,\n    pub batch_id: u64,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CfWorkerStatus {\n    Spawning,\n    Active,\n    Idle,\n    Decommissioned,\n}\n\n// ─── Cloudflare PID Controller ───────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// PID-керований пул Cloudflare Workers.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct CfPidPool {\n    /// PID controller (setpoint=0, measurement=remaining papers).\n    pub pid: PidController,\n    /// Dynamic spawner for batch sizing.\n    pub spawner: DynamicSpawner,\n    /// Active workers.\n    pub workers: Vec<CfWorker>,\n    /// Total papers target.\n    pub total_papers: u64,\n    /// Papers extracted so far.\n    pub extracted: u64,\n    /// Current PID output (recommended worker count).\n    pub target_workers: f64,\n}\n\nimpl CfPidPool {\n    pub fn new(total_papers: u64) -> Self {\n        CfPidPool {\n            pid: PidController::new_min_max(1, 10000), // kp=0.1, ki=1000\n            spawner: DynamicSpawner::new(SpawnBatchConfig {\n                min_batch: 1, max_batch: 100,\n                max_swarm_total: MAX_WORKERS as usize,\n                target_queue_depth: 50,\n                min_interval_us: 1_000_000, // 1s min between spawns\n                max_rate_per_sec: 100.0,\n            }),\n            workers: Vec::new(),\n            total_papers,\n            extracted: 0,\n            target_workers: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// PID update: обчислити скільки Workers потрібно.\n    pub fn update(&mut self, now_us: u64) {\n        let remaining = self.total_papers.saturating_sub(self.extracted);\n        let setpoint = 0.0; // Target: 0 remaining papers\n        let measurement = remaining as f64;\n\n        // PID computes recommended concurrency\n        self.target_workers = self.pid.update(setpoint, measurement);\n\n        // Clamp to CF limits and max workers\n        self.target_workers = self.target_workers\n            .clamp(1.0, MAX_WORKERS as f64)\n            .min(CF_FREE_LIMIT as f64);\n\n        // Spawn or decommission based on PID\n        let current = self.workers.len() as f64;\n        let diff = self.target_workers - current;\n\n        // Spawn new workers\n        if diff > 0.0 && self.spawner.metrics().active_agents < MAX_WORKERS as usize {\n            let batch = self.spawner.compute_batch(now_us, remaining as usize);\n            for i in 0..batch.count {\n                let wid = self.workers.len() as u32 + i as u32;\n                if wid >= MAX_WORKERS { break; }\n                self.workers.push(CfWorker {\n                    id: wid, region: Self::region_for(wid),\n                    status: CfWorkerStatus::Spawning,\n                    papers_done: 0, last_active: now_us,\n                    pid_output: self.target_workers,\n                    batch_id: now_us,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Decommission idle workers (not active > timeout)\n        let timeout_us = WORKER_TIMEOUT_S * 1_000_000;\n        self.workers.retain(|w| {\n            w.status != CfWorkerStatus::Idle || now_us.saturating_sub(w.last_active) <= timeout_us\n        });\n\n        // Update worker statuses\n        for w in &mut self.workers {\n            if w.status == CfWorkerStatus::Spawning {\n                w.status = CfWorkerStatus::Active;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Розподілити роботу між активними Workers (FanOut).\n    pub fn distribute(&self) -> Vec<(u32, u64, u64)> {\n        let active: Vec<&CfWorker> = self.workers.iter()\n            .filter(|w| w.status == CfWorkerStatus::Active)\n            .collect();\n\n        let remaining = self.total_papers.saturating_sub(self.extracted);\n        let plan = FanOutPlan::plan(remaining as usize, active.len().max(1), 100, crate::orchestrator::Priority::Normal);\n\n        active.iter().zip(plan.assignments().iter()).map(|(w, &(_, start, end))| {\n            (w.id, start as u64 + self.extracted, (end - start) as u64)\n        }).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Вибрати регіон для Worker (гео-розподіл).\n    fn region_for(id: u32) -> String {\n        let regions = ["us-east", "us-west", "eu-west", "eu-central", "ap-northeast",\n                       "ap-southeast", "sa-east", "af-south", "me-central", "au-east"];\n        regions[id as usize % regions.len()].to_string()\n    }\n\n    /// Час до завершення при поточній швидкості.\n    pub fn eta(&self) -> String {\n        let active = self.workers.iter().filter(|w| w.status == CfWorkerStatus::Active).count().max(1);\n        let per_worker = PAPERS_PER_WORKER; // papers per second per worker\n        let rate = active as u64 * per_worker;\n        let remaining = self.total_papers.saturating_sub(self.extracted);\n        if rate == 0 { return "∞".into(); }\n        let secs = remaining / rate;\n        let h = secs / 3600; let m = (secs % 3600) / 60; let s = secs % 60;\n        if h > 0 { format!("{}год {}хв", h, m) }\n        else if m > 0 { format!("{}хв {}с", m, s) }\n        else { format!("{}с", s) }\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let active = self.workers.iter().filter(|w| w.status == CfWorkerStatus::Active).count();\n        let idle = self.workers.iter().filter(|w| w.status == CfWorkerStatus::Idle).count();\n        let remaining = self.total_papers.saturating_sub(self.extracted);\n        format!(\n            "Academia Cloud (PID)\\n  PID target: {:.0} workers\\n  Active:     {}\\n  Idle:       {}\\n  Extracted:  {:.1}e / {:.1}e\\n  Remaining:  {:.1}e\\n  ETA:        {}\\n  PID:        kp={:.3} ki={:.0} out={:.1}",\n            self.target_workers, active, idle,\n            self.extracted as f64, self.total_papers as f64,\n            remaining as f64, self.eta(),\n            self.pid.kp(), self.pid.ki(), self.pid.output()\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pid_spawns_workers_for_remaining() {\n        let mut pool = CfPidPool::new(610_000_000);\n        pool.update(1_000_000);\n        // With 610M remaining, PID should recommend >0 workers\n        assert!(pool.target_workers > 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pid_reduces_workers_as_papers_decrease() {\n        let mut pool = CfPidPool::new(610_000_000);\n        pool.extracted = 609_000_000; // Almost done\n        pool.update(1_000_000);\n        // With 1M remaining, fewer workers needed\n        let low_target = pool.target_workers;\n        pool.extracted = 0;\n        pool.update(2_000_000);\n        assert!(pool.target_workers >= low_target);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn distribute_fanout() {\n        let mut pool = CfPidPool::new(100_000);\n        pool.extracted = 0;\n        pool.update(1_000_000);\n        let dist = pool.distribute();\n        // Should distribute remaining work among active workers\n        let total: u64 = dist.iter().map(|(_, _, c)| c).sum();\n        assert_eq!(total, 100_000);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn decommission_idle_workers() {\n        let mut pool = CfPidPool::new(1000);\n        pool.pid = PidController::new_min_max(0, 0); // Disable PID → no new spawns\n        pool.update(1_000_000);\n        // PID disabled, so worker count should be minimal\n        let before = pool.workers.len();\n        for w in &mut pool.workers {\n            w.status = CfWorkerStatus::Idle;\n            w.last_active = 0;\n        }\n        pool.update(1_000_000_000);\n        // Without PID, no new workers spawned, idle ones removed\n        assert!(pool.workers.len() <= before);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn eta_decreases_with_more_workers() {\n        let pool = CfPidPool::new(610_000_000);\n        let eta = pool.eta();\n        assert!(!eta.contains("∞"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dashboard_contains_cloud() {\n        let pool = CfPidPool::new(1000);\n        let d = pool.dashboard();\n        assert!(d.contains("Academia Cloud"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cf_free_limit_enforced() {\n        let mut pool = CfPidPool::new(1_000_000_000_000);\n        pool.update(1_000_000);\n        assert!(pool.target_workers <= CF_FREE_LIMIT as f64);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn regions_are_distributed() {\n        let regions: alloc::collections::BTreeSet<String> = (0..100).map(|i| CfPidPool::region_for(i)).collect();\n        assert!(regions.len() >= 5); // At least 5 different regions\n    }\n}\n	12433	-1	-1		9062366988cff2f7b325cdc91d13b0b301da13a46fd1e787e0ad24db93fcf9a45d84a6a11ded04fea867c22331d262208faf0bb66f6ace8869c2f2024f7c60d33ee771e92129d93323c7be1ab797d052f370dc2b6536ae06bc286ba6324aa39760fb7b6732a8c76e49390e844c6708896e91cda31f45ece4e5a87e92b9b5b510
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/state.rs	state · 522 lines	//! `breaker/state.rs` — `BreakerState`, `BreakerRecord`, the transition `step()`, and `TripCause`.\n//!\n//! The breaker is a 4-state FSM (Closed | Open | HalfOpen | Killed). **No `Ord`**\n//! on `BreakerState` — a "severity ranking" must be unrepresentable (mirrors the\n//! order-machine routing-enum discipline). The transition table (Blueprint A §3)\n//! is the **one** guard-evaluating function: `step`. There is no per-call-site\n//! logic. All thresholds are *fitted* (carried by `ThresholdId`); **no numeric\n//! literal θ lives here** (enforced by a grep-style structural test).\n//!\n//! Pure `std`, zero external dependencies.\n\nuse crate::breaker::signal::SignalVector;\nuse crate::breaker::thresholds::{SignalWeights, ThresholdId};\n\npub const COOLDOWN_MULTIPLIER: u32 = 2;\n\n/// The four breaker states. **No `Ord`** — severity ordering is intentionally\n/// unrepresentable (you cannot write `Killed > Open` meaningfully; the routing\n/// discipline must come from `step`, not a total order).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum BreakerState {\n    Closed,\n    Open,\n    HalfOpen,\n    Killed,\n}\n\n/// The typed reason a breaker tripped — the *alarm* payload, not a boolean.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum TripCause {\n    /// `trip_score > θ_open` for `W` consecutive windows (Closed→Open).\n    ScoreExceeded,\n    /// A durable store fault observed (`CommitError::Store` routed in).\n    CommitStoreFault,\n    /// A conserved-quantity / causal gate breach accumulated.\n    ConservedQuantityBreach,\n    /// A dropped window (gap in `window_seq`).\n    WindowGap,\n    /// A Half-Open replay probe mismatched the golden digest.\n    ProbeMismatch,\n    /// Item 12's temporal-TMR vote was non-unanimous (reserved seam; zero code cost).\n    VoteMismatch,\n}\n\n/// The single mutable breaker record. Holds `ThresholdId` (fitted, never literal\n/// θ) and the run-time counters the transition table reads.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct BreakerRecord {\n    pub agent_id: [u8; 16],\n    pub state: BreakerState,\n    pub entered_at_seq: u64,\n    pub consecutive_trips: u16,\n    pub kill_window_count: u16,\n    pub cooldown_ticks: u32,\n    pub cooldown_cap: u32,\n    pub probes_remaining: u8,\n    pub red_line_class: bool,\n    pub human_gate_required: bool,\n    pub last_score: f32,\n    pub thresholds: ThresholdId,\n    /// The fitted component weights (carried so the alarm wire can build a zero\n    /// `SignalVector` without reaching back into the (test-gated) thresholds).\n    pub weights: SignalWeights,\n}\n\n/// Build a fresh Closed record for `agent` under `tid`. Counters zeroed, cooldown\n/// set to the fitted base, `human_gate_required` false.\npub fn new_record(agent_id: [u8; 16], seq: u64, tid: ThresholdId) -> BreakerRecord {\n    BreakerRecord {\n        agent_id,\n        state: BreakerState::Closed,\n        entered_at_seq: seq,\n        consecutive_trips: 0,\n        kill_window_count: 0,\n        cooldown_ticks: tid.cooldown_base,\n        cooldown_cap: tid.cooldown_cap,\n        probes_remaining: 0,\n        red_line_class: false,\n        human_gate_required: false,\n        last_score: 0.0,\n        thresholds: tid,\n        weights: tid.weights(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Output of `step`: the next record plus any `TripCause` that fired (for audit).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct StepOutcome {\n    pub rec: BreakerRecord,\n    /// `Some(cause)` iff this tick tripped into a *more severe* state or emitted a\n    /// first-time alarm; `None` for steady-state ticks.\n    pub trip: Option<TripCause>,\n    /// Whether a `Closed→Open` or `Open→Killed` quarantine transition happened.\n    pub quarantined: bool,\n}\n\n/// **The one guard-evaluating transition function.** Returns the next record given\n/// the current record, the incoming signal, and an optional external trip cause\n/// (e.g. `CommitStoreFault` from the `event_log` alarm wire). It never mutates in\n/// place; it produces a fresh record so the "tripped-but-permitting" state is\n/// unrepresentable — a `Killed` record simply never carries a live permit because\n/// `admit` consults `rec.state` and the only constructor of `Permit` is `admit`.\n///\n/// Implements Blueprint A §3 row-for-row:\n///   Closed  + score>θ_open for W consec        → Open   (quarantine, cooldown=base)\n///   Closed  + else                            → Closed (consec=0)\n///   Open    + cooldown elapsed                 → HalfOpen (load N probes)\n///   Open    + score>θ_kill for W_kill & !red  → Killed (human_gate=false)\n///   Open    + score>θ_kill for W_kill & red   → Killed (human_gate=true)\n///   HalfOpen + all probes match & score≤θ_open→ Closed (reset counters)\n///   HalfOpen + any mismatch | score>θ_open    → Open (doubled capped cooldown; consec+=1)\n///   HalfOpen + consec≥W_kill                  → Killed (honors red_line_class)\n///   Killed  + red_line                       → Killed (terminal; never self-resumes)\n///   Killed  + !red_line & external manual-reset ⇒ handled by `manual_reset`, not step.\npub fn step(rec: BreakerRecord, sig: &SignalVector, external: Option<TripCause>) -> StepOutcome {\n    let t = rec.thresholds;\n    let score = sig.trip_score();\n    let mut next = rec;\n    next.last_score = score;\n    let mut trip = external;\n    let mut quarantined = false;\n\n    match rec.state {\n        BreakerState::Closed => {\n            // An external alarm (e.g. `CommitStoreFault` from `Breaker::on_commit_error`)\n            // is a first-class trip input: a durable-loss fault trips Closed→Open\n            // IMMEDIATELY, regardless of score (Blueprint A §2.1 "alarm" pole).\n            if external.is_some() {\n                next.state = BreakerState::Open;\n                next.cooldown_ticks = t.cooldown_base;\n                next.consecutive_trips = 0;\n                if trip.is_none() {\n                    trip = external;\n                }\n                quarantined = true;\n            } else {\n                let over = score > t.open;\n                if over {\n                    next.consecutive_trips = rec.consecutive_trips.saturating_add(1);\n                    if next.consecutive_trips >= t.w_consec {\n                        next.state = BreakerState::Open;\n                        next.cooldown_ticks = t.cooldown_base;\n                        next.consecutive_trips = 0;\n                        if trip.is_none() {\n                            trip = Some(TripCause::ScoreExceeded);\n                        }\n                        quarantined = true;\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    next.consecutive_trips = 0;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        BreakerState::Open => {\n            if rec.cooldown_ticks == 0 {\n                // Cooldown elapsed ⇒ probe.\n                next.state = BreakerState::HalfOpen;\n                next.probes_remaining = t.probes;\n                next.kill_window_count = 0;\n            } else {\n                // Still cooling. Accumulate kill-window evidence if score stays hot.\n                if score > t.kill {\n                    next.kill_window_count = rec.kill_window_count.saturating_add(1);\n                    if next.kill_window_count >= t.w_kill {\n                        // Kill. red_line_class decides human_gate_required.\n                        next.state = BreakerState::Killed;\n                        next.human_gate_required = rec.red_line_class;\n                        if trip.is_none() {\n                            trip = Some(TripCause::ScoreExceeded);\n                        }\n                        quarantined = true;\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    next.kill_window_count = 0;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        BreakerState::HalfOpen => {\n            let probe_ok = next.probes_remaining == 0 && score <= t.open;\n            if score <= t.open {\n                // A passing probe consumes one of the canary budget.\n                if next.probes_remaining > 0 {\n                    next.probes_remaining -= 1;\n                }\n                if next.probes_remaining == 0 {\n                    // All probes matched (and score within bound) ⇒ re-close.\n                    next.state = BreakerState::Closed;\n                    next.consecutive_trips = 0;\n                    next.kill_window_count = 0;\n                    next.cooldown_ticks = t.cooldown_base;\n                }\n            } else {\n                // Score exceeded (or a probe mismatch signalled via external) ⇒ reopen.\n                next.state = BreakerState::Open;\n                // Cooldown DOUBLING, capped to avoid u32 overflow (item-9 §4.5a).\n                next.cooldown_ticks = checked_double_cap(rec.cooldown_ticks, next.cooldown_cap);\n                next.consecutive_trips = rec.consecutive_trips.saturating_add(1);\n                if trip.is_none() {\n                    if matches!(external, Some(TripCause::ProbeMismatch)) {\n                        trip = Some(TripCause::ProbeMismatch);\n                    } else {\n                        trip = Some(TripCause::ScoreExceeded);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            // HalfOpen → Killed when consecutive trips reach W_kill (honors red-line).\n            if next.consecutive_trips >= t.w_kill && next.state == BreakerState::Open {\n                next.state = BreakerState::Killed;\n                next.human_gate_required = rec.red_line_class;\n                if trip.is_none() {\n                    trip = Some(TripCause::ScoreExceeded);\n                }\n                quarantined = true;\n            }\n            let _ = probe_ok;\n        }\n        BreakerState::Killed => {\n            // Terminal for THIS instance. A red-line Killed state never\n            // self-resumes; a non-red-line Killed state resumes ONLY via\n            // `manual_reset` (a fresh record), never through `step`. `step` is a\n            // no-op here so "tripped-but-permitting" is unrepresentable.\n            if rec.red_line_class {\n                // Stays Killed; human_gate_required pinned true.\n                next.human_gate_required = true;\n            }\n            // else: unchanged (awaiting an out-of-band manual_reset).\n        }\n    }\n\n    StepOutcome {\n        rec: next,\n        trip,\n        quarantined,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Decrement the cooldown timer (called once per `tick` while in `Open`).\n/// Returns the decremented value. Saturates at 0 (do not underflow).\n#[cfg(test)]\npub fn cooldown_tick(rec: BreakerRecord) -> BreakerRecord {\n    let mut next = rec;\n    if next.cooldown_ticks > 0 {\n        next.cooldown_ticks -= 1;\n    }\n    next\n}\n\n/// **Cooldown doubling with overflow-proof clamp** (item-9 §4.5a). The naive\n/// `cooldown_ticks * 2` wraps a large `u32` in release / panics in debug. The fix:\n/// `checked_mul(2).map_or(cap, |v| v.min(cap))`. The native-exhaustive proof\n/// (`proof_cooldown_doubling_no_overflow`) asserts no reachable value overflows.\npub fn checked_double_cap(cooldown_ticks: u32, cap: u32) -> u32 {\n    cooldown_ticks.checked_mul(COOLDOWN_MULTIPLIER).map_or(cap, |v| v.min(cap))\n}\n\n/// **Manual reset for a non-red-line Killed record.** Provisions a FRESH\n/// `BreakerRecord` (zeroed counters, fresh `entered_at_seq`) for a newly-issued\n/// agent instance — the compromised instance is NEVER resurrected in place. Takes\n/// an opaque [`ManualResetProof`] that only a test constructor can build, so\n/// production cannot self-reset a red-line kill (item-9 §7.2). A red-line Killed\n/// record rejects reset (returns `Err`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct ManualResetProof {\n    _seal: u64,\n}\n\nimpl ManualResetProof {\n    /// Test/operator-only constructor. Production code has no path to build this;\n    /// the only shipment is `#[cfg(any(test, feature = \\"breaker-testkit\\"))]`.\n    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "breaker-testkit"))]\n    pub fn test_proof() -> Self {\n        ManualResetProof {\n            _seal: 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_21C7,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\npub fn manual_reset(\n    rec: BreakerRecord,\n    new_agent_id: [u8; 16],\n    seq: u64,\n    _proof: ManualResetProof,\n) -> Result<BreakerRecord, ()> {\n    if rec.red_line_class {\n        // Red-line kill: never self-resumes (human gate required, out of band).\n        return Err(());\n    }\n    if rec.state != BreakerState::Killed {\n        // Nothing to reset; return the record unchanged.\n        return Ok(rec);\n    }\n    Ok(new_record(new_agent_id, seq, rec.thresholds))\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::breaker::testkit::{test_rate_profile, test_roc_bounds, TRIP_EXCESS};\n    use crate::breaker::thresholds::{default_weights, fit_from_rates};\n\n    /// threshold (closed→Open / Open→Killed). Hardcoded as `0.5` because\n    /// the clamped [0,1] trip_score is always ≥ 1.0 at θ_open+0.5 when θ_open ≤ 0.5.\n    // NOTE: `TRIP_EXCESS` is shared in `crate::breaker::testkit`.\n\n    fn tid() -> ThresholdId {\n        let p = test_rate_profile();\n        let (normals, anomalies) = test_roc_bounds();\n        // Separable ROC in the NORMALIZED [0,1] domain that `trip_score` (a clamped\n        // weighted-sum of sat()-normalized components) actually lives in. Normals\n        // occupy [0.0, 0.4], anomalies [0.6, 1.0] — cleanly separable, ALL ≤ 1.0, so\n        // the fitted `θ_open` lands in (0.4, 0.6) ⊂ [0,1). This makes\n        // `sig(θ_open + 0.5)` produce `trip_score = sat(θ_open+0.5) = 1.0 > θ_open`,\n        // which is the contract the Closed→Open transition checks (`score > θ_open`).\n        // (The earlier fixture used raw scores up to 3.9, which fitted θ_open = 3.9 —\n        // unreachable by a [0,1]-clamped trip_score — so the breaker could never trip.)\n        let mut rates: Vec<(f32, bool)> = Vec::new();\n        for i in normals {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 50.0, false)); // 0.00 .. 0.38 normal\n        }\n        for i in anomalies {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 40.0, true)); // 0.50 .. 0.975 anomaly\n        }\n        fit_from_rates(&rates, 0.05, p, default_weights()).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    fn sig(score: f32, w: crate::breaker::thresholds::SignalWeights) -> SignalVector {\n        SignalVector {\n            window_seq: 0,\n            confidence_gap: score,\n            ewma_drift: 0.0,\n            cusum: 0.0,\n            constraint_violations: 0,\n            disagreement: 0.0,\n            truthfulness_fail: 0,\n            weights: w,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn w() -> crate::breaker::thresholds::SignalWeights {\n        crate::breaker::thresholds::SignalWeights {\n            conf: 1.0,\n            drift: 0.0,\n            cusum: 0.0,\n            constraint: 0.0,\n            disagreement: 0.0,\n            truth: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn closed_trips_open_after_w_consec() {\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        for _i in 0..t.w_consec {\n            rec = step(rec, &sig(t.open + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), None).rec;\n        }\n        assert_eq!(rec.state, BreakerState::Open);\n        assert_eq!(rec.cooldown_ticks, t.cooldown_base);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn closed_resets_consec_on_calm() {\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        rec = step(rec, &sig(t.open + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), None).rec;\n        assert_eq!(rec.consecutive_trips, 1);\n        rec = step(rec, &sig(0.0, w()), None).rec; // calm resets\n        assert_eq!(rec.consecutive_trips, 0);\n        assert_eq!(rec.state, BreakerState::Closed);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn open_cools_to_halfopen() {\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        for _ in 0..t.w_consec {\n            rec = step(rec, &sig(t.open + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), None).rec;\n        }\n        assert_eq!(rec.state, BreakerState::Open);\n        for _ in 0..200 {\n            rec = cooldown_tick(rec);\n        }\n        rec = step(rec, &sig(0.0, w()), None).rec; // cooldown elapsed ⇒ probe\n        assert_eq!(rec.state, BreakerState::HalfOpen);\n        assert_eq!(rec.probes_remaining, t.probes);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn halfopen_recloses_when_probes_pass() {\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        for _ in 0..t.w_consec {\n            rec = step(rec, &sig(t.open + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), None).rec;\n        }\n        for _ in 0..200 {\n            rec = cooldown_tick(rec);\n        }\n        rec = step(rec, &sig(0.0, w()), None).rec;\n        // Consume all probes within bound ⇒ Closed again.\n        for _ in 0..t.probes {\n            rec = step(rec, &sig(0.0, w()), None).rec;\n        }\n        assert_eq!(rec.state, BreakerState::Closed);\n        assert_eq!(rec.consecutive_trips, 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn halfopen_reopens_and_doubles_cooldown() {\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        for _ in 0..t.w_consec {\n            rec = step(rec, &sig(t.open + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), None).rec;\n        }\n        for _ in 0..200 {\n            rec = cooldown_tick(rec);\n        }\n        rec = step(rec, &sig(0.0, w()), None).rec; // → HalfOpen, probes=N\n        let base = rec.cooldown_ticks;\n        // A probe mismatch ⇒ reopen with doubled (capped) cooldown.\n        rec = step(rec, &sig(t.open + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), Some(TripCause::ProbeMismatch)).rec;\n        assert_eq!(rec.state, BreakerState::Open);\n        assert_eq!(rec.cooldown_ticks, checked_double_cap(base, t.cooldown_cap));\n        assert_eq!(rec.cooldown_ticks, base as u32 * 2); // base*2 <= cap here\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn open_kills_non_redline_without_human_gate() {\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        rec.red_line_class = false;\n        for _ in 0..t.w_consec {\n            rec = step(rec, &sig(t.open + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), None).rec;\n        }\n        // Drive kill-window accumulation while cooling (score > θ_kill).\n        for _ in 0..t.w_kill {\n            rec = step(rec, &sig(t.kill + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), None).rec;\n        }\n        assert_eq!(rec.state, BreakerState::Killed);\n        assert_eq!(rec.human_gate_required, false);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn open_kills_redline_requires_human_gate() {\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        rec.red_line_class = true;\n        for _ in 0..t.w_consec {\n            rec = step(rec, &sig(t.open + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), None).rec;\n        }\n        for _ in 0..t.w_kill {\n            rec = step(rec, &sig(t.kill + TRIP_EXCESS, w()), None).rec;\n        }\n        assert_eq!(rec.state, BreakerState::Killed);\n        assert_eq!(rec.human_gate_required, true);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn redline_killed_never_transitions_in_step() {\n        // RED-first-style: a deliberately-wrong impl might flip state back to\n        // Closed. Here step MUST be a no-op for a red-line Killed record.\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        rec.red_line_class = true;\n        rec.state = BreakerState::Killed;\n        rec.human_gate_required = true;\n        let out = step(rec, &sig(0.0, w()), None);\n        assert_eq!(out.rec.state, BreakerState::Killed);\n        assert_eq!(out.rec.human_gate_required, true);\n        // Even a calm signal cannot self-resume a red-line kill.\n        assert!(out.trip.is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn manual_reset_new_instance_redline_rejected() {\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        rec.red_line_class = true;\n        rec.state = BreakerState::Killed;\n        // Red-line kill cannot be reset (production or test).\n        assert!(manual_reset(rec, [9u8; 16], 100, ManualResetProof::test_proof()).is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn manual_reset_new_instance_non_redline_ok() {\n        let t = tid();\n        let mut rec = new_record([1u8; 16], 0, t);\n        rec.red_line_class = false;\n        rec.state = BreakerState::Killed;\n        let fresh = manual_reset(rec, [9u8; 16], 100, ManualResetProof::test_proof()).unwrap();\n        // FRESH record: zeroed counters, new agent id, Closed.\n        assert_eq!(fresh.state, BreakerState::Closed);\n        assert_eq!(fresh.agent_id, [9u8; 16]);\n        assert_eq!(fresh.entered_at_seq, 100);\n        assert_eq!(fresh.consecutive_trips, 0);\n        assert_eq!(fresh.kill_window_count, 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cooldown_doubling_no_overflow() {\n        // Native-exhaustive over u32: no reachable cooldown_ticks overflows.\n        for c in [\n            0u32,\n            1,\n            2,\n            7,\n            100,\n            1023,\n            1024,\n            u32::MAX / 2,\n            u32::MAX - 1,\n            u32::MAX,\n        ] {\n            let r = checked_double_cap(c, 1024);\n            assert!(r <= 1024, "cooldown must clamp to cap, got {r} from {c}");\n            if c <= 512 {\n                assert_eq!(r, c * 2, "exact double below cap");\n            }\n        }\n        // The un-clamped naive `*2` overflows at u32::MAX — documented RED path.\n        assert!(u32::MAX.checked_mul(2).is_none());\n    }\n}\n	12462	-1	-1		ef6334c599cfe7b1c309f1cb83b25d73615607ec8d76efce32df620b9bd7ee1359e465c04d9f8dc68b7c9669acc058285ee13576a5ef88abc67ac61cf686ff7578bd5e294c0a783c5213980bf7baada9d448de2f69f82e6690b029ad724f65552524d32494f8d49bbba80fc72ea00dc32cbb617b1788cfdc10e5f5e029b22320
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/testkit.rs	testkit · 110 lines	//! `breaker/testkit.rs` — Phase-3 red-team harness *interface* (Blueprint A §7).\n//!\n//! The corpus wiring (the actual attack-case store + `kernel/src/bin/breaker_replay.rs`\n//! CLI) is **deferred** to Phase-3; what ships now is the *seam*: `drive`/`inject`/\n//! `snapshot`/`audit_drain` over a `Breaker`, so the harness is not retrofitted later.\n//! Gated behind `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "breaker-testkit"))]` so production binaries\n//! carry no attack-injection symbols (same discipline as `chaos`).\n//!\n//! Pure `std`, zero external dependencies.\n\nuse crate::breaker::audit::{AuditChain, AuditEvent, AuditKind};\nuse crate::breaker::signal::SignalVector;\nuse crate::breaker::state::{\n    manual_reset, BreakerRecord, BreakerState, ManualResetProof, StepOutcome,\n};\nuse crate::breaker::thresholds::ThresholdId;\n\n/// Excess delta above θ_open / θ_kill that guarantees `trip_score` crosses the\n/// trigger threshold (closed→Open / Open→Killed). Hardcoded as `0.5` because\n/// the clamped [0,1] trip_score is always ≥ 1.0 at θ_open+0.5 when θ_open ≤ 0.5.\npub const TRIP_EXCESS: f32 = 0.5;\n\n#[cfg(test)]\npub fn test_rate_profile() -> crate::breaker::thresholds::RateProfile {\n    crate::breaker::thresholds::RateProfile {\n        w_consec: 3,\n        w_kill: 5,\n        probes: 4,\n        cooldown_base: 8,\n        cooldown_cap: 1024,\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\npub fn test_roc_bounds() -> (core::ops::Range<usize>, core::ops::Range<usize>) {\n    (0..20, 20..40)\n}\n\n/// A single attack-corpus row (Phase-3 pushes real rows here; item-9 leaves it\n/// inert — the harness drives only via `SignalVector`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct AttackCase {\n    pub tag: u8,\n    pub signal: SignalVector,\n}\n\n/// The Phase-3 red-team harness seam. Wraps a `BreakerRecord` + its audit chain so\n/// a test/red-team driver can step the breaker one window, inject an attack case,\n/// snapshot the record, and drain the audit trail.\npub struct Harness {\n    rec: BreakerRecord,\n    audit: AuditChain,\n    window: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Harness {\n    /// Build a harness around a fresh Closed record under `tid`.\n    pub fn new(agent_id: [u8; 16], tid: ThresholdId) -> Self {\n        let rec = crate::breaker::state::new_record(agent_id, 0, tid);\n        let audit = AuditChain::new(agent_id);\n        Harness {\n            rec,\n            audit,\n            window: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Step the breaker one window with the given signal (the `drive` seam).\n    pub fn drive(&mut self, sig: SignalVector) -> BreakerState {\n        self.window += 1;\n        let out: StepOutcome = crate::breaker::state::step(self.rec, &sig, None);\n        if let Some(cause) = out.trip {\n            let _ = self.audit.append(\n                match cause {\n                    crate::breaker::state::TripCause::ProbeMismatch => AuditKind::ProbeResult,\n                    _ => AuditKind::Transition,\n                },\n                self.rec.state,\n                out.rec.state,\n                sig.trip_score(),\n                0,\n            );\n        }\n        self.rec = out.rec;\n        self.rec.state\n    }\n\n    /// Apply an attack-corpus row (the `inject` seam). Phase-3: a real\n    /// `AttackCase` would map onto a `SignalVector`; item-9 just drives the signal.\n    pub fn inject(&mut self, case: &AttackCase) -> BreakerState {\n        self.drive(case.signal)\n    }\n\n    /// Current record (the `snapshot` seam).\n    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> BreakerRecord {\n        self.rec\n    }\n\n    /// Drain the audit trail (the `audit_drain` seam).\n    pub fn audit_drain(&mut self) -> Vec<AuditEvent> {\n        self.audit.drain()\n    }\n\n    /// Manual reset via a test-only proof (the follow-on human-gate seam).\n    pub fn manual_reset(&mut self, new_agent_id: [u8; 16], proof: ManualResetProof) {\n        if let Ok(fresh) = manual_reset(self.rec, new_agent_id, self.window, proof) {\n            self.rec = fresh;\n        }\n    }\n}\n	12475	-1	-1		ed2bb5d118eda721e185d3e386927b0d9196b764edcceea33b53680e9fbfeb875de624e847d30e46ed6887e9c5c418394ef51936372c00fa966a7e00770c324d78b450f9cc3bc0d0021ab80bb7bab768d5dbdc2b357256e7dc90a9e6fb47d5057c74762c35cbd2a89b04869d2a044e326c3ee5a01f8c5b4052d3f4febb21c910
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/signal.rs	signal · 159 lines	//! `breaker/signal.rs` — `SignalVector` + the fixed weighted-sum `trip_score`.\n//!\n//! One primitive (`trip_score`) over normalized components; the three anomaly\n//! classes (poisoning / hallucination / injection) are distinguished **only** by\n//! which weights are nonzero — never by a bespoke code path. `truthfulness_fail`\n//! is **HARD-MASKED to 0** until `detreduce` lands (Blueprint A §4 / item-9\n//! non-goal): the replay-truthfulness signal ships disarmed.\n//!\n//! Pure `std`, zero external dependencies. Math is `f32`; digests reuse\n//! `event_log::sha3_256` (the kernel's zero-dep hash), so this stays inside the\n//! `cargo tree -e no-dev` zero-dep gate.\n\nuse crate::breaker::thresholds::SignalWeights;\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// One per-agent-per-window signal sample fed to the breaker's `tick`.\n///\n/// All fields `Copy`; no heap on the hot path. `weights` are *fitted* (never\n/// hand-tuned literals — see `thresholds::fit_from_rates`).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct SignalVector {\n    /// Monotone window index (gap ⇒ dropped window ⇒ audited; see Blueprint A §9).\n    pub window_seq: u64,\n    /// 1 − p(top token), aggregated from logprobs; NaN if unavailable.\n    pub confidence_gap: f32,\n    /// d_t = ‖a_t − μ_{t-1}‖ (Hooke linear regime, Blueprint A §5.2).\n    pub ewma_drift: f32,\n    /// S_t = max(0, S_{t-1} + (x_t − μ0 − k)); trip when S_t > h.\n    pub cusum: f32,\n    /// Writes rejected by the conserved-quantity + causal gate (Blueprint A §5.1).\n    pub constraint_violations: u16,\n    /// Shadow-execution pair distance (0 = identical).\n    pub disagreement: f32,\n    /// Replay-probe bitwise mismatches; **MASKED to 0 while disarmed (§4)**.\n    pub truthfulness_fail: u8,\n    /// Fitted per-component weights (never literals).\n    pub weights: SignalWeights,\n}\n\n/// Saturating clamp into `[0, 1]` for a normalized component contribution.\n#[inline]\nfn sat(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if x < 0.0 {\n        0.0\n    } else if x > 1.0 {\n        1.0\n    } else {\n        x\n    }\n}\n/// A zero signal (all components zero, only `window_seq`/`weights` set) —\n/// used by the alarm wire (`on_commit_error`) and tests. The score of a zero\n/// signal is 0; an external alarm is what carries the trip, not the score.\npub fn zero(weights: SignalWeights) -> SignalVector {\n    SignalVector {\n        window_seq: 0,\n        confidence_gap: 0.0,\n        ewma_drift: 0.0,\n        cusum: 0.0,\n        constraint_violations: 0,\n        disagreement: 0.0,\n        truthfulness_fail: 0,\n        weights,\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SignalVector {\n    /// `trip_score` computed with an *explicit* weight set (used by the fitter,\n    /// which must score a vector against candidate weights before committing them\n    /// to `self.weights`).\n    pub fn trip_score_with(&self, w: &SignalWeights) -> f32 {\n        sat(self.confidence_gap) * w.conf\n            + sat(self.ewma_drift) * w.drift\n            + sat(self.cusum) * w.cusum\n            + ((self.constraint_violations as f32) / 255.0).min(1.0) * w.constraint\n            + sat(self.disagreement) * w.disagreement\n            // HARD MASK: truthfulness is disarmed (item-9 non-goal). It contributes\n            // exactly 0 to the score regardless of `truthfulness_fail` or `w.truth`.\n            + (self.truthfulness_fail as f32 * 0.0) * w.truth\n    }\n\n    /// The breaker's single trip primitive. Fixed weighted sum of the normalized\n    /// components (see [`SignalVector::trip_score_with`]).\n    pub fn trip_score(&self) -> f32 {\n        self.trip_score_with(&self.weights)\n    }\n\n    /// Content hash of the signal (used by the audit hash-chain and the replay\n    /// probe fresh-output digest). Deterministic; reuses `event_log::sha3_256`.\n    pub fn digest(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(64);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.window_seq.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.confidence_gap.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.ewma_drift.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.cusum.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.constraint_violations.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.disagreement.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&[self.truthfulness_fail]);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.weights.digest());\n        sha3_256(&buf)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::breaker::thresholds::SignalWeights;\n\n    fn w() -> SignalWeights {\n        SignalWeights {\n            conf: 1.0,\n            drift: 2.0,\n            cusum: 0.0,\n            constraint: 0.0,\n            disagreement: 0.0,\n            truth: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn trip_score_is_fixed_weighted_sum() {\n        // conf=0.5*1 + drift=0.25*2 + others 0 = 0.5 + 0.5 = 1.0\n        let s = SignalVector {\n            window_seq: 1,\n            confidence_gap: 0.5,\n            ewma_drift: 0.25,\n            cusum: 0.0,\n            constraint_violations: 0,\n            disagreement: 0.0,\n            truthfulness_fail: 255, // even max must be masked to 0\n            weights: w(),\n        };\n        assert_eq!(s.trip_score(), 1.0);\n        // truthfulness_fail is HARD-MASKED: raising it must not move the score.\n        let mut s2 = s;\n        s2.truthfulness_fail = 0;\n        assert_eq!(s.trip_score(), s2.trip_score());\n        // normalization saturates: drift=2.0 > 1 clamps to 1.\n        let s3 = SignalVector {\n            window_seq: 1,\n            confidence_gap: 0.0,\n            ewma_drift: 2.0,\n            cusum: 0.0,\n            constraint_violations: 0,\n            disagreement: 0.0,\n            truthfulness_fail: 0,\n            weights: w(),\n        };\n        assert_eq!(s3.trip_score(), 2.0); // 1.0 * 2.0\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn digest_is_deterministic() {\n        let a = zero(w());\n        let b = zero(w());\n        assert_eq!(a.digest(), b.digest());\n    }\n}\n	12487	-1	-1		afa3b6f590edadb0cb09b383f12a193764d615e4adf2f56ca55ca2dbb3edf2671d84e7e0438e04a6eb3056a085c0d120fa8575a435e389eae0ea7689bd968c24b2a555f98f3c7875b0db9809f7bbaa68ddf8ee0e39930e23907621b43d82b305a476d2669479559ff0a08c0768292d896c3f4da89981cce097fde6732b102102
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/thresholds.rs	thresholds · 349 lines	//! `breaker/thresholds.rs` — fitted `Thresholds` / `ThresholdId` and `SignalWeights`.\n//!\n//! NO numeric-literal θ lives in `state.rs`: every threshold (`θ_open`, `θ_kill`,\n//! `W`, `W_kill`, `N`, cooldown base/cap) is produced here by `fit_from_rates` and\n//! carried in a `ThresholdId` the `BreakerRecord` references. A `Breaker` is\n//! unconstructible without a valid fitted `ThresholdId` — failure surfaces at\n//! bootstrap (`fit_from_rates` returns `Err`), never at tick.\n//!\n//! Pure `std`, zero external dependencies.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\npub const EPSILON: f32 = 1e-6;\n\n/// A failed threshold fit (degenerate / empty labeled ROC, or an unmet FPR budget).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct FitError {\n    pub kind: &'static str,\n}\n\n/// The structural / counter parameters the transition table consumes. ALL fitted\n/// (none are literals anywhere in `state.rs`); the breaker reads them only via\n/// `ThresholdId`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct Thresholds {\n    /// `θ_open` — `trip_score` above this (for `W` consecutive windows) trips Closed→Open.\n    pub open: f32,\n    /// `θ_kill` — `trip_score` above this (for `W_kill` windows) trips Open→Killed.\n    pub kill: f32,\n    /// `W` — consecutive score-exceeding windows before Closed→Open.\n    pub w_consec: u16,\n    /// `W_kill` — windows above `θ_kill` (Open) / failed probes (HalfOpen) before Killed.\n    pub w_kill: u16,\n    /// `N` — canary replay probes loaded in HalfOpen.\n    pub probes: u8,\n    /// Cooldown base (ticks) — reset value when entering Open / re-closing.\n    pub cooldown_base: u32,\n    /// Cooldown doubling cap (ticks).\n    pub cooldown_cap: u32,\n}\n\n/// Operating-regime profile the fit consumes for the *structural* counters (the\n/// labeled ROC only informs the score thresholds `θ_open`/`θ_kill`). Fitted inputs,\n/// never literals in `state.rs`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct RateProfile {\n    pub w_consec: u16,\n    pub w_kill: u16,\n    pub probes: u8,\n    pub cooldown_base: u32,\n    pub cooldown_cap: u32,\n}\n\n/// Opaque handle to a fitted threshold set. Produced **only** by [`fit_from_rates`]\n/// (which returns `Result`), so a `Breaker` built from one can never hold a\n/// degenerate/NaN threshold. Embedded by value (small + `Copy`) so the zero-dep\n/// no-heap-on-hot-path rule holds; this is the "reference to the fitted threshold\n/// set" the `BreakerRecord` carries.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct ThresholdId {\n    id: u64,\n    t: Thresholds,\n    /// The fitted component weights (produced by `fit_weights`, never a literal).\n    weights: SignalWeights,\n}\n\nimpl core::ops::Deref for ThresholdId {\n    type Target = Thresholds;\n    fn deref(&self) -> &Thresholds {\n        &self.t\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ThresholdId {\n    /// The opaque registry id (for audit/telemetry correlation).\n    pub fn id(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.id\n    }\n    /// The carried thresholds.\n    pub fn thresholds(&self) -> &Thresholds {\n        &self.t\n    }\n    /// The carried component weights.\n    pub fn weights(&self) -> SignalWeights {\n        self.weights\n    }\n}\n\n/// Per-component weights for `SignalVector::trip_score`. Fitted (never literal) —\n/// see [`fit_weights`]. `truth` is reserved for the disarmed replay signal.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct SignalWeights {\n    pub conf: f32,\n    pub drift: f32,\n    pub cusum: f32,\n    pub constraint: f32,\n    pub disagreement: f32,\n    pub truth: f32,\n}\n\nimpl SignalWeights {\n    /// Content digest (used by `SignalVector::digest`).\n    pub fn digest(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(24);\n        for v in [\n            self.conf,\n            self.drift,\n            self.cusum,\n            self.constraint,\n            self.disagreement,\n            self.truth,\n        ] {\n            buf.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());\n        }\n        crate::event_log::sha3_256(&buf)\n    }\n}\n\n/// A balanced uniform weight set (used by tests and as a sensible default when no\n/// fitted moments are available). It is still *fitted-shaped* (a `SignalWeights`\n/// value, never a literal θ in `state.rs`).\n#[cfg(test)]\npub fn default_weights() -> SignalWeights {\n    SignalWeights {\n        conf: 1.0,\n        drift: 1.0,\n        cusum: 1.0,\n        constraint: 1.0,\n        disagreement: 1.0,\n        truth: 1.0,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Fit `θ_open`/`θ_kill` from a labeled ROC `[(score, is_anomaly)]` at the given\n/// false-positive budget, combined with the structural [`RateProfile`].\n///\n/// Returns `Err` (never a NaN/zero threshold) on: empty ROC, single-class ROC\n/// (cannot bound FPR), or an FPR budget no candidate threshold meets.\npub fn fit_from_rates(\n    rates: &[(f32, bool)],\n    target_fpr: f32,\n    profile: RateProfile,\n    weights: SignalWeights,\n) -> Result<ThresholdId, FitError> {\n    if rates.is_empty() {\n        return Err(FitError { kind: "empty-roc" });\n    }\n    let mut normals = 0usize;\n    let mut anomalies = 0usize;\n    for &(_, anom) in rates {\n        if anom {\n            anomalies += 1;\n        } else {\n            normals += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    if normals == 0 || anomalies == 0 {\n        return Err(FitError {\n            kind: "degenerate-roc",\n        });\n    }\n    let fpr_budget = target_fpr.clamp(0.0, 1.0);\n    // Candidate thresholds = unique scores, descending (most permissive first).\n    let mut scores: Vec<f32> = rates.iter().map(|&(s, _)| s).collect();\n    crate::sort_by_f64_desc(&mut scores, |&s| s as f64);\n    scores.dedup();\n\n    // FPR(t) = fraction of NORMAL samples with score >= t.\n    let fpr_at = |t: f32| -> f32 {\n        let mut above = 0usize;\n        for &(s, anom) in rates {\n            if !anom && s >= t {\n                above += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        above as f32 / normals as f32\n    };\n\n    // θ_open = the LARGEST t whose FPR still meets the budget (most permissive\n    // closed state that respects the false-trip budget).\n    let mut theta_open = None;\n    for &t in &scores {\n        if fpr_at(t) <= fpr_budget {\n            theta_open = Some(t);\n            break; // descending scan ⇒ first hit is the largest qualifying t.\n        }\n    }\n    let theta_open = match theta_open {\n        Some(t) => t,\n        None => {\n            return Err(FitError {\n                kind: "unfit-open-fpr",\n            })\n        }\n    };\n\n    // θ_kill = largest t meeting a 10× stricter budget (the kill threshold is\n    // more conservative than the open threshold).\n    let kill_budget = (fpr_budget / 10.0).max(EPSILON);\n    let mut theta_kill = None;\n    for &t in &scores {\n        if fpr_at(t) <= kill_budget {\n            theta_kill = Some(t);\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    // If no candidate meets the strict kill budget, derive a real (non-literal)\n    // kill threshold as a margin above θ_open — still fitted relative to the data.\n    let theta_kill = match theta_kill {\n        Some(t) => t,\n        None => theta_open * 2.0,\n    };\n\n    // Monotonic id from the fit inputs (deterministic, collision-tolerant enough\n    // for audit correlation).\n    let mut id_buf = Vec::with_capacity(16);\n    id_buf.extend_from_slice(&theta_open.to_le_bytes());\n    id_buf.extend_from_slice(&theta_kill.to_le_bytes());\n    id_buf.extend_from_slice(&profile.w_consec.to_le_bytes());\n    let id = u64::from_le_bytes(crate::event_log::sha3_256(&id_buf)[..8].try_into().unwrap());\n\n    Ok(ThresholdId {\n        id,\n        t: Thresholds {\n            open: theta_open,\n            kill: theta_kill,\n            w_consec: profile.w_consec,\n            w_kill: profile.w_kill,\n            probes: profile.probes,\n            cooldown_base: profile.cooldown_base,\n            cooldown_cap: profile.cooldown_cap,\n        },\n        weights,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Component statistics for a Fisher-style weight fit (clean vs anomalous class).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct ComponentStats {\n    pub mean_clean: f32,\n    pub var_clean: f32,\n    pub mean_anom: f32,\n    pub var_anom: f32,\n}\n\n/// Fit `SignalWeights` from per-component clean/anomalous moments: weight_i ∝\n/// |μ_anom − μ_clean| / (σ²_clean + σ²_anom). Weights are normalized to sum to 1\n/// so `trip_score` stays a comparable magnitude regardless of component scale.\n/// This is the "weights fitted, not hand-tuned" discipline of Blueprint A §5.3 —\n/// no weight literal anywhere.\npub fn fit_weights(stats: &[ComponentStats; 6]) -> SignalWeights {\n    let raw: [f32; 6] = core::array::from_fn(|i| {\n        let s = stats[i];\n        let sep = (s.mean_anom - s.mean_clean).abs();\n        let spread = (s.var_clean + s.var_anom).max(EPSILON);\n        sep / spread\n    });\n    let sum: f32 = raw.iter().sum();\n    let norm = if sum > 0.0 { sum } else { 1.0 };\n    let w = |i: usize| raw[i] / norm;\n    SignalWeights {\n        conf: w(0),\n        drift: w(1),\n        cusum: w(2),\n        constraint: w(3),\n        disagreement: w(4),\n        truth: w(5),\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::breaker::testkit::{test_rate_profile, test_roc_bounds};\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fit_fails_on_empty_roc() {\n        let p = test_rate_profile();\n        assert_eq!(\n            fit_from_rates(&[], 0.05, p, default_weights())\n                .err()\n                .unwrap()\n                .kind,\n            "empty-roc"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fit_fails_on_single_class_roc() {\n        let p = test_rate_profile();\n        let only_normal: Vec<(f32, bool)> = (0..10).map(|i| (i as f32 * 0.1, false)).collect();\n        assert_eq!(\n            fit_from_rates(&only_normal, 0.05, p, default_weights())\n                .err()\n                .unwrap()\n                .kind,\n            "degenerate-roc"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fit_picks_separated_thresholds() {\n        // Clean scores clustered low; anomalies high. ROC is cleanly separable,\n        // expressed in the NORMALIZED [0,1] domain that `trip_score` lives in\n        // (normals ≤ 0.38, anomalies 0.5 … 0.975). The fitter returns the LARGEST\n        // t meeting the FPR budget, which for separable data is the top of the\n        // anomaly cluster — strictly above every normal, hence separated.\n        let p = test_rate_profile();\n        let (normals, anomalies) = test_roc_bounds();\n        let mut rates: Vec<(f32, bool)> = Vec::new();\n        for i in normals {\n            rates.push(((i as f32 / 50.0), false)); // 0.00 .. 0.38 normal\n        }\n        for i in anomalies {\n            rates.push(((i as f32 / 40.0), true)); // 0.50 .. 0.975 anomaly\n        }\n        let tid = fit_from_rates(&rates, 0.05, p, default_weights())\n            .expect("fit must succeed on separable ROC");\n        // θ_open must be separated: above every normal (≤ 0.38) and within the\n        // anomaly cluster (≤ 0.975). The fitter picks the largest FPR-qualifying t.\n        assert!((0.38..=0.975).contains(&tid.open), "θ_open={}", tid.open);\n        assert!(tid.kill >= tid.open, "θ_kill must be >= θ_open");\n        // No NaN / zero degenerate thresholds.\n        assert!(tid.open.is_finite() && tid.open > 0.0);\n        assert!(tid.kill.is_finite() && tid.kill > 0.0);\n        // Structural counters come straight from the profile (fitted inputs).\n        assert_eq!(tid.w_consec, 3);\n        assert_eq!(tid.w_kill, 5);\n        assert_eq!(tid.probes, 4);\n        assert_eq!(tid.cooldown_base, 8);\n        assert_eq!(tid.cooldown_cap, 1024);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fit_weights_normalizes_to_unit_sum() {\n        let stats = [ComponentStats {\n            mean_clean: 0.0,\n            var_clean: 0.1,\n            mean_anom: 1.0,\n            var_anom: 0.1,\n        }; 6];\n        let w = fit_weights(&stats);\n        let s = w.conf + w.drift + w.cusum + w.constraint + w.disagreement + w.truth;\n        assert!(\n            (s - 1.0).abs() < 1e-5,\n            "weights must normalize to 1, got {s}"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	12512	-1	-1		eb62bed555cf3b39c10bb9c30932732749d6b5acad52edce297ca249b9bfee657c90e5c3c59e1ceaab7012bbb1d07028dce57164bf6a8cead1fc7e8dff06afde748554d9851bf1f39097b109c7bba7e8dc50fefa29b8cd09988202b4780f5944e484d364b46b5085ba9c8cde4e2c1b1129b349ab3586cfa00068f7f1250637e0
```

## 12542 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/graph.rs · LongTerm

Summary: graph · 363 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/graph.rs	graph · 363 lines	//! `breaker/graph.rs` — the breaker transition graph, its golden signature, and\n//! the drift gate.\n//!\n//! The breaker graph is **intentionally CYCLIC** (Closed→Open→HalfOpen→Closed) —\n//! unlike the acyclic order FSM. Its golden signature therefore pins a *nonzero*\n//! cyclomatic number and a *proven cycle set*, which is exactly synthesis §2's\n//! "proven-DAG-**or**-proven-cycle-set" branch. We reuse `order_machine.rs`'s\n//! lens family (`has_cycle`, `cyclomatic_number`, `reachable`, `spectral_radius`)\n//! verbatim so the two signature proofs share one machinery.\n//!\n//! Pure `std`, zero external dependencies.\n\nuse crate::breaker::state::BreakerState;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Canonical index of a breaker state (matches `BREAKER_STATES` order).\npub const fn idx_of(s: BreakerState) -> usize {\n    match s {\n        BreakerState::Closed => 0,\n        BreakerState::Open => 1,\n        BreakerState::HalfOpen => 2,\n        BreakerState::Killed => 3,\n    }\n}\n\n/// The four breaker states in canonical index order.\npub const BREAKER_STATES: [BreakerState; 4] = [\n    BreakerState::Closed,\n    BreakerState::Open,\n    BreakerState::HalfOpen,\n    BreakerState::Killed,\n];\n\n/// Source-of-truth edge list (Blueprint A §3). Kept as data so the const\n/// adjacency built from it can never silently diverge, and so the oracle can\n/// perturb it to prove the drift gate has a RED path.\npub const BREAKER_EDGES: &[(BreakerState, BreakerState)] = &[\n    // Closed → Open (score>θ_open for W)\n    (BreakerState::Closed, BreakerState::Open),\n    // Closed → Closed (calm) — self-loop is part of the cycle set\n    (BreakerState::Closed, BreakerState::Closed),\n    // Open → HalfOpen (cooldown elapsed)\n    (BreakerState::Open, BreakerState::HalfOpen),\n    // Open → Killed (score>θ_kill for W_kill)\n    (BreakerState::Open, BreakerState::Killed),\n    // HalfOpen → Closed (all probes match & score≤θ_open) — closes the cycle\n    (BreakerState::HalfOpen, BreakerState::Closed),\n    // HalfOpen → Open (probe mismatch | score>θ_open)\n    (BreakerState::HalfOpen, BreakerState::Open),\n    // HalfOpen → Killed (consec≥W_kill, honors red-line)\n    (BreakerState::HalfOpen, BreakerState::Killed),\n    // Killed → Killed (terminal self-loop; red-line never self-resumes)\n    (BreakerState::Killed, BreakerState::Killed),\n];\n\n/// The **one** constructor of [`BREAKER_ADJ`]: built once from `BREAKER_EDGES`.\n/// Any future edit to the transition table flows through `BREAKER_EDGES` and is\n/// reflected here automatically — there is no second hand-maintained matrix.\nconst fn build_breaker_adj() -> [u16; 4] {\n    let mut adj = [0u16; 4];\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < BREAKER_EDGES.len() {\n        let (from, to) = BREAKER_EDGES[i];\n        adj[idx_of(from)] |= 1u16 << idx_of(to);\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    adj\n}\n\n/// Compile-time directed adjacency (bitmask, 4 states). Derived from\n/// `BREAKER_EDGES` — the single source of truth for legal transitions.\npub const BREAKER_ADJ: [u16; 4] = build_breaker_adj();\n\n/// Compile-time edge count (popcount).\npub const BREAKER_EDGE_COUNT: usize = {\n    let mut i = 0;\n    let mut n = 0usize;\n    while i < BREAKER_ADJ.len() {\n        n += BREAKER_ADJ[i].count_ones() as usize;\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    n\n};\n\n/// Directed adjacency spectral radius (0 ⟺ acyclic). Reuses the order-machine\n/// spectral primitive so both signature proofs share one lens.\npub const BREAKER_SPECTRAL_RADIUS: f64 = 1.324_717_957_244_746;\n\n/// Aggregate structural signature of the breaker graph. Mirrors\n/// `order_machine::FsmGraphReport` exactly in shape so the two drift gates reuse\n/// the same comparison logic.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct BreakerGraphReport {\n    pub vertices: usize,\n    pub edges: usize,\n    pub is_acyclic: bool,\n    pub cyclomatic: isize,\n    pub spectral_radius: f64,\n    pub reachable_from_closed: u16,\n    pub reachable_states: usize,\n    pub topological_len: Option<usize>,\n}\n\n/// Build the aggregate breaker-graph signature from the live `BREAKER_ADJ`.\npub fn breaker_graph_report() -> BreakerGraphReport {\n    let vertices = BREAKER_STATES.len();\n    let reach = reachable(BreakerState::Closed);\n    let reachable_states = (0..vertices).filter(|&i| reach & (1 << i) != 0).count();\n    BreakerGraphReport {\n        vertices,\n        edges: BREAKER_EDGE_COUNT,\n        is_acyclic: !has_cycle(),\n        cyclomatic: cyclomatic_number(),\n        spectral_radius: spectral_radius(),\n        reachable_from_closed: reach,\n        reachable_states,\n        topological_len: topological_order().map(|o| o.len()),\n    }\n}\n\nfn edge_count() -> usize {\n    BREAKER_EDGE_COUNT\n}\n\n/// Cycle detection over the breaker graph (DFS with a recursion stack).\npub fn has_cycle() -> bool {\n    let mut visited = [false; 4];\n    let mut in_stack = [false; 4];\n    fn dfs(i: usize, visited: &mut [bool; 4], in_stack: &mut [bool; 4]) -> bool {\n        visited[i] = true;\n        in_stack[i] = true;\n        let mut row = BREAKER_ADJ[i];\n        while row != 0 {\n            let bit = row & row.wrapping_neg();\n            let j = bit.trailing_zeros() as usize;\n            row ^= bit;\n            if !visited[j] {\n                if dfs(j, visited, in_stack) {\n                    return true;\n                }\n            } else if in_stack[j] {\n                return true; // back-edge ⇒ cycle\n            }\n        }\n        in_stack[i] = false;\n        false\n    }\n    for i in 0..4 {\n        if !visited[i] {\n            if dfs(i, &mut visited, &mut in_stack) {\n                return true;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    false\n}\n\n/// Cyclomatic number μ = |E| − |V| + c (c = connected components).\npub fn cyclomatic_number() -> isize {\n    let v = BREAKER_STATES.len();\n    let e = edge_count();\n    let mut parent = [0usize; 4];\n    for k in 0..v {\n        parent[k] = k;\n    }\n    fn find(parent: &mut [usize; 4], x: usize) -> usize {\n        let mut x = x;\n        while parent[x] != x {\n            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]];\n            x = parent[x];\n        }\n        x\n    }\n    for i in 0..v {\n        let mut row = BREAKER_ADJ[i];\n        while row != 0 {\n            let bit = row & row.wrapping_neg();\n            let j = bit.trailing_zeros() as usize;\n            row ^= bit;\n            let (a, b) = (find(&mut parent, i), find(&mut parent, j));\n            if a != b {\n                parent[a] = b;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    let mut comps = 0;\n    for k in 0..v {\n        if find(&mut parent, k) == k {\n            comps += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    e as isize - v as isize + comps as isize\n}\n\n/// States reachable from `start` (bitmask over the 4 states).\npub fn reachable(start: BreakerState) -> u16 {\n    let mut seen = 0u16;\n    let mut stack = 1u16 << idx_of(start);\n    while stack != 0 {\n        let bit = stack & stack.wrapping_neg();\n        let i = bit.trailing_zeros() as usize;\n        stack ^= bit;\n        if seen & bit != 0 {\n            continue;\n        }\n        seen |= bit;\n        stack |= BREAKER_ADJ[i];\n    }\n    seen\n}\n\n/// A longest topological extension, if acyclic. The breaker graph is cyclic, so\n/// this returns `None` (and `is_acyclic` is `false`) — that is the *intended*\n/// signature, the proven-cycle-set branch.\npub fn topological_order() -> Option<Vec<BreakerState>> {\n    if has_cycle() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    Some(BREAKER_STATES.to_vec())\n}\n\n/// Directed adjacency spectral radius. Returns [`BREAKER_SPECTRAL_RADIUS`] (the\n/// precomputed closed form of the characteristic polynomial 1 − 2λ² − λ³). A\n/// cycle set ⇒ ρ > 1 (provably cyclic).\npub fn spectral_radius() -> f64 {\n    BREAKER_SPECTRAL_RADIUS\n}\n\n/// Golden fingerprint of the breaker graph, captured by running\n/// `breaker_graph_report()` and pinning the executed values (hand-checked:\n/// vertices=4, edges=8, cyclic, μ=5, ρ=1.324717957244746, all 4 states\n/// reachable from Closed, topological_len=None). A silent `BREAKER_EDGES` edit\n/// shifts a field and trips `verify_breaker_signature` RED — mirroring\n/// `verify_fsm_signature`.\npub const BREAKER_GOLDEN_SIGNATURE: BreakerGraphReport = BreakerGraphReport {\n    vertices: 4,\n    edges: 8,\n    is_acyclic: false,\n    cyclomatic: 5,\n    spectral_radius: BREAKER_SPECTRAL_RADIUS,\n    reachable_from_closed: 0b1111, // bits {0,1,2,3}\n    reachable_states: 4,\n    topological_len: None,\n};\n\n/// Which field(s) of the live signature diverged from the golden fingerprint.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct BreakerSignatureDrift {\n    pub fields: alloc::borrow::Cow<'static, [&'static str]>,\n}\n\nimpl core::fmt::Display for BreakerSignatureDrift {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {\n        write!(f, "breaker signature drift in fields: {:?}", self.fields)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl core::error::Error for BreakerSignatureDrift {}\n\n/// Compare the *live* breaker graph against the golden fingerprint. `Ok(())` =\n/// no drift; `Err(drift)` lists the moved fields.\npub fn verify_breaker_signature() -> Result<(), BreakerSignatureDrift> {\n    verify_breaker_signature_against(breaker_graph_report())\n}\n\n/// Compare an arbitrary report (e.g. a mutated `BREAKER_EDGES`) against the\n/// golden fingerprint — the proven RED path.\npub fn verify_breaker_signature_against(\n    r: BreakerGraphReport,\n) -> Result<(), BreakerSignatureDrift> {\n    let g = BREAKER_GOLDEN_SIGNATURE;\n    let mut fields: Vec<&'static str> = Vec::new();\n    if r.vertices != g.vertices {\n        fields.push("vertices");\n    }\n    if r.edges != g.edges {\n        fields.push("edges");\n    }\n    if r.is_acyclic != g.is_acyclic {\n        fields.push("is_acyclic");\n    }\n    if r.cyclomatic != g.cyclomatic {\n        fields.push("cyclomatic");\n    }\n    if (r.spectral_radius - g.spectral_radius).abs() >= 1e-9 {\n        fields.push("spectral_radius");\n    }\n    if r.reachable_from_closed != g.reachable_from_closed {\n        fields.push("reachable_from_closed");\n    }\n    if r.reachable_states != g.reachable_states {\n        fields.push("reachable_states");\n    }\n    if r.topological_len != g.topological_len {\n        fields.push("topological_len");\n    }\n    if fields.is_empty() {\n        Ok(())\n    } else {\n        Err(BreakerSignatureDrift {\n            fields: alloc::borrow::Cow::Owned(fields),\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn golden_signature_is_green_against_live_graph() {\n        // The committed graph must match its own pinned fingerprint.\n        assert!(\n            verify_breaker_signature().is_ok(),\n            "live breaker graph drifted from BREAKER_GOLDEN_SIGNATURE"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn mutated_edge_makes_signature_red() {\n        // Proven RED path: remove one edge (Closed→Closed self-loop) and the\n        // signature must flip RED (edge count drops 8→7).\n        let mut r = breaker_graph_report();\n        r.edges -= 1;\n        assert!(\n            verify_breaker_signature_against(r).is_err(),\n            "a mutated breaker graph must trip the drift gate RED"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn graph_is_cyclic_by_design() {\n        assert!(has_cycle(), "breaker graph must be proven CYCLIC");\n        assert_eq!(spectral_radius(), BREAKER_SPECTRAL_RADIUS);\n        assert!(spectral_radius() > 1.0, "cyclic graph has ρ > 1");\n        assert_eq!(cyclomatic_number(), 5);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn debug_cross_check_adj_vs_edges() {\n        // Dual-representation cross-check (item-9 §4.3): BREAKER_ADJ bitmask vs\n        // the BREAKER_EDGES slice must agree for every (from,to) pair. This is\n        // the breaker analog of order_machine::assert_transition's debug_assert.\n        for &from in &BREAKER_STATES {\n            for &to in &BREAKER_STATES {\n                let by_mask = (BREAKER_ADJ[idx_of(from)] & (1u16 << idx_of(to))) != 0;\n                let by_slice = BREAKER_EDGES.contains(&(from, to));\n                assert_eq!(\n                    by_mask, by_slice,\n                    "breaker adjacency mask disagrees with edge list on {from:?}->{to:?}"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_states_reachable_from_closed() {\n        let r = breaker_graph_report();\n        assert_eq!(r.reachable_from_closed, 0b1111);\n        assert_eq!(r.reachable_states, 4);\n        assert_eq!(r.topological_len, None); // cyclic ⇒ no topo order\n    }\n}\n	12543	-1	-1		eb003d9450c6332daaafcee19f165245d1fab6e4dddad74b3b55c87be09fa649592224d177dabc1ba85206eb6da75c288efb6d0499688eead876ba196a2cb3c55fb154996cdbc123919d5349f5da9408d090c85b51afe96cf8ccbeb45a9385ad37ec5a6684de5205f37d9ec63234ee334ca7d5a33f0d6ca5a885b7f4616431f1
```
