## 12562 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/replay.rs · LongTerm

Summary: replay · 170 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/replay.rs	replay · 170 lines	//! `breaker/replay.rs` — the golden replay-probe store (Blueprint A §2.3).\n//!\n//! Pairs captured while `invariant_verified == false` are **quarantined** and\n//! never used to gate a Half-Open→Closed transition. The probe seam exists so\n//! the Half-Open state has somewhere to read golden digests, but it ships\n//! **disarmed**: `arm_truthfulness` is a no-op that writes `AuditKind::Disarm`\n//! (per item-9 §7.3 / Blueprint A §4 — detreduce is a non-goal deferred to a\n//! follow-on). Replay probes may only gate a close once `detreduce`'s\n//! `verified_invariant()` is true; until then `truthfulness_fail` is masked to 0\n//! and the probe pool is inert.\n//!\n//! Pure `std`, zero external dependencies.\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// A golden input→output pair used as a replay probe. `key` is\n/// `sha3(input_bytes ‖ condition_bytes)`; a probe passes iff the freshly\n/// computed output digest equals `output_digest` — bitwise, no tolerance.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct GoldenPair {\n    pub key: [u8; 32],\n    pub input_digest: [u8; 32],\n    pub output_digest: [u8; 32],\n    pub captured_at_seq: u64,\n    /// Was detreduce verified when this pair was captured? If false, the pair is\n    /// quarantined and MUST NOT gate a close.\n    pub invariant_verified: bool,\n}\n\nimpl GoldenPair {\n    /// Build a golden pair. `key = sha3(input ‖ condition)`.\n    pub fn new(\n        input_bytes: &[u8],\n        condition_bytes: &[u8],\n        output_bytes: &[u8],\n        captured_at_seq: u64,\n        invariant_verified: bool,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let key = {\n            let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(input_bytes.len() + condition_bytes.len());\n            buf.extend_from_slice(input_bytes);\n            buf.extend_from_slice(condition_bytes);\n            sha3_256(&buf)\n        };\n        GoldenPair {\n            key,\n            input_digest: sha3_256(input_bytes),\n            output_digest: sha3_256(output_bytes),\n            captured_at_seq,\n            invariant_verified,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Does the freshly computed output match the golden digest, bitwise?\n    pub fn probe_matches(&self, fresh_output: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        self.output_digest == sha3_256(fresh_output)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The golden replay store. The probe pool is **empty by default** (no captured\n/// pairs ship). `arm_truthfulness` is a no-op writing `AuditKind::Disarm` until\n/// detreduce lands — the seam exists, the corpus does not.\npub struct GoldenStore {\n    pairs: Vec<GoldenPair>,\n    armed: bool,\n    disarm_event: Option<([u8; 32], u64)>, // (marker, seq) when disarmed\n}\n\nimpl GoldenStore {\n    /// An empty, disarmed store (the honest default for item-9).\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        GoldenStore {\n            pairs: Vec::new(),\n            armed: false,\n            disarm_event: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Add a captured golden pair. A pair with `invariant_verified == false` is\n    /// still stored but **excluded from `probe_pool()`** (the safety property).\n    pub fn add(&mut self, pair: GoldenPair) {\n        self.pairs.push(pair);\n    }\n\n    /// The usable probe pool: ONLY pairs captured while the invariant was verified.\n    /// Quarantined pairs (invariant_verified == false) are never returned.\n    pub fn probe_pool(&self) -> Vec<&GoldenPair> {\n        self.pairs.iter().filter(|p| p.invariant_verified).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Whether truthfulness probing is armed (requires detreduce verification).\n    pub fn is_armed(&self) -> bool {\n        self.armed\n    }\n\n    /// Arm the truthfulness probe. In item-9 this is a **no-op**: detreduce is a\n    /// deferred non-goal, so arming writes a `Disarm` marker instead of enabling\n    /// the probe (Blueprint A §4). Returns `false` to signal "still disarmed".\n    pub fn arm_truthfulness(&mut self, seq: u64) -> bool {\n        // No-op: record the disarm state; the probe pool stays inert/empty.\n        self.disarm_event = Some((sha3_256(b"disarm"), seq));\n        self.armed = false;\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// Run a fresh-output probe against the (armed, verified) pool. Returns\n    /// `Ok(true)` only if EVERY armed pair matches bitwise. With an empty /\n    /// disarmed pool, probing reports "no gate" (`None`) — it never fabricates a\n    /// pass that would close the breaker on unverified evidence.\n    pub fn probe_all(&self, fresh_output: &[u8]) -> Option<bool> {\n        if !self.armed {\n            return None; // disarmed ⇒ do not gate\n        }\n        let pool = self.probe_pool();\n        if pool.is_empty() {\n            return None; // no verified pairs ⇒ do not gate\n        }\n        Some(pool.iter().all(|p| p.probe_matches(fresh_output)))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for GoldenStore {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn quarantined_pair_excluded_from_probe_pool() {\n        // RED-first against a "gate on any pair" impl: a pair with\n        // invariant_verified==false MUST NOT enter the probe pool.\n        let mut store = GoldenStore::new();\n        store.add(GoldenPair::new(b"in", b"cond", b"out", 0, false));\n        assert!(\n            store.probe_pool().is_empty(),\n            "quarantined pair must be excluded"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verified_pair_enters_probe_pool() {\n        let mut store = GoldenStore::new();\n        store.add(GoldenPair::new(b"in", b"cond", b"out", 0, true));\n        assert_eq!(store.probe_pool().len(), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn arm_truthfulness_is_noop_disarmed() {\n        let mut store = GoldenStore::new();\n        store.add(GoldenPair::new(b"in", b"cond", b"out", 0, true));\n        // Even with a verified pair present, arming must report disarmed (item-9\n        // non-goal: detreduce not wired).\n        assert!(!store.arm_truthfulness(1));\n        assert!(!store.is_armed());\n        // Probing therefore cannot gate a close.\n        assert_eq!(store.probe_all(b"out"), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn probe_matches_bitwise() {\n        let p = GoldenPair::new(b"input", b"c", b"output", 0, true);\n        assert!(p.probe_matches(b"output"));\n        assert!(!p.probe_matches(b"outputX")); // bitwise, no tolerance\n    }\n}\n	12563	-1	-1		7b0bb51bad9c8524a349f095b1a25331e5db9564f750a5a983477e4ed1c9e841784b75214fcd560aaf4a47abb5cbd32a66651dc9be43386a1be77a1dc51eb74d5e874a28e5564b11c681f10ad5bae13872494d4d0978c76fc4d222d4b0dbf725e072d305b3ca52a46905d86f2268a6ff613c65235f809ac60301f77899302810
```

## 12585 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/audit.rs · LongTerm

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/audit.rs	audit · 338 lines	//! `breaker/audit.rs` — hash-chained, tamper-evident audit over the **existing**\n//! FDR ring (Blueprint A §2.4 / item-9 §3 row 5).\n//!\n//! The breaker does NOT build a second ring: it shares `fdr::ring::FdrRing` (the\n//! Tier-1 flight recorder — synthesis §5: "the logger *is* the flight recorder").\n//! Each breaker audit event is an FDR `Kind::Alarm` record carrying a\n//! `prev_hash`/`seq` hash chain computed via `event_log::sha3_256`, so a deleted\n//! or reordered entry is detectable. **Backpressure = stall, never drop** (§9): if\n//! the durable ring cannot accept the entry (the drain sink has fallen behind and\n//! the segment is at capacity), `tick` blocks rather than silently dropping the\n//! audit row — losing an entry defeats the ring's tamper-evidence purpose.\n//!\n//! Pure `core` + `alloc` (no_std). The audit chain is in-memory too (for\n//! the testkit `audit_drain` seam and for fast in-process verification), AND\n//! mirrored to the durable FDR ring when one is installed.\n\nuse crate::breaker::state::BreakerState;\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse alloc::boxed::Box;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// The audit event kind (carried as an FDR field string, not via `fdr::Kind` —\n/// `Kind::Alarm` already exists; these are the breaker *sub*-kinds).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum AuditKind {\n    /// A signal-only audit (calm tick).\n    Signal,\n    /// A state transition.\n    Transition,\n    /// A replay-probe result (HalfOpen).\n    ProbeResult,\n    /// A kill (terminal).\n    Kill,\n    /// A red-line gate assertion.\n    RedLineGate,\n    /// Truthfulness probe disarmed (detreduce deferred — item-9 non-goal).\n    Disarm,\n}\n\nimpl AuditKind {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            AuditKind::Signal => "signal",\n            AuditKind::Transition => "transition",\n            AuditKind::ProbeResult => "probe_result",\n            AuditKind::Kill => "kill",\n            AuditKind::RedLineGate => "red_line_gate",\n            AuditKind::Disarm => "disarm",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// One hash-chained audit event. `prev_hash` links to the prior event; `self_hash`\n/// binds `prev_hash ‖ seq ‖ body`, so deletion or reordering breaks the chain.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AuditEvent {\n    pub seq: u64,\n    pub prev_hash: [u8; 32],\n    pub ts_millis: u64,\n    pub agent_id: [u8; 16],\n    pub kind: AuditKind,\n    pub state_from: BreakerState,\n    pub state_to: BreakerState,\n    pub score: f32,\n    pub self_hash: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// Compute `self_hash = sha3(prev_hash ‖ seq ‖ kind ‖ from ‖ to ‖ score_bytes)`.\nfn compute_self_hash(\n    prev_hash: &[u8; 32],\n    seq: u64,\n    kind: AuditKind,\n    state_from: BreakerState,\n    state_to: BreakerState,\n    score: f32,\n) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(64 + 16);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(prev_hash);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&seq.to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(kind.as_str().as_bytes());\n    buf.push(state_from as u8);\n    buf.push(state_to as u8);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&score.to_le_bytes());\n    sha3_256(&buf)\n}\n\n/// A durable audit mirror (the kernel's FDR ring impls this). The core\n/// [`AuditChain`] is pure in-memory; when a mirror is installed, every appended\n/// event is mirrored to it BEFORE being committed (backpressure = stall, never drop).\npub trait AuditMirror {\n    /// Mirror one audit event durably. `Err` = the durable write failed; the\n    /// caller must treat it as a hard stop (never proceed without the row).\n    fn mirror(&mut self, ev: &AuditEvent) -> Result<(), AuditError>;\n}\n\n/// The in-memory hash-chained audit ledger. Holds the last event's `self_hash` as\n/// the chaining tip. Mirrors each event to an optional [`AuditMirror`].\npub struct AuditChain {\n    events: Vec<AuditEvent>,\n    tip_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// Optional durable mirror (the kernel's FDR ring impls [`AuditMirror`]).\n    /// `None` ⇒ audit-only in memory.\n    mirror: Option<Box<dyn AuditMirror>>,\n    agent_id: [u8; 16],\n}\n\nimpl AuditChain {\n    /// Create a fresh chain (genesis tip_hash = zero), audit-only in memory.\n    pub fn new(agent_id: [u8; 16]) -> Self {\n        AuditChain {\n            events: Vec::new(),\n            tip_hash: [0u8; 32],\n            mirror: None,\n            agent_id,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a chain that also mirrors every event to a durable mirror\n    /// (the kernel's FDR ring impls [`AuditMirror`]). Backpressure = stall.\n    pub fn with_mirror(agent_id: [u8; 16], mirror: Box<dyn AuditMirror>) -> Self {\n        AuditChain {\n            events: Vec::new(),\n            tip_hash: [0u8; 32],\n            mirror: Some(mirror),\n            agent_id,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Number of events recorded.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.events.len()\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.events.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Append one audit event, chaining `prev_hash` from the current tip and\n    /// computing `self_hash`. Mirrors to the durable FDR ring if installed.\n    ///\n    /// **Backpressure (§9):** if a durable ring is installed and its `append`\n    /// returns `Err`, this call **stalls** (returns `Err`) rather than dropping\n    /// the entry silently. The caller's `tick` must treat a returned `Err` as a\n    /// hard stop — never an opportunity to proceed without the audit row.\n    pub fn append(\n        &mut self,\n        kind: AuditKind,\n        state_from: BreakerState,\n        state_to: BreakerState,\n        score: f32,\n        ts_millis: u64,\n    ) -> Result<(), AuditError> {\n        let seq = self.events.len() as u64;\n        let prev = self.tip_hash;\n        let self_hash = compute_self_hash(&prev, seq, kind, state_from, state_to, score);\n        let ev = AuditEvent {\n            seq,\n            prev_hash: prev,\n            ts_millis,\n            agent_id: self.agent_id,\n            kind,\n            state_from,\n            state_to,\n            score,\n            self_hash,\n        };\n\n        // STALL, never drop: mirror the event durably BEFORE committing it, so a\n        // durable-write failure surfaces instead of proceeding without the row.\n        if let Some(mirror) = self.mirror.as_mut() {\n            mirror.mirror(&ev)?;\n        }\n\n        self.tip_hash = self_hash;\n        self.events.push(ev);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Drain + verify the in-memory chain: returns `Ok` only if `prev_hash` of\n    /// every event equals the `self_hash` of its predecessor (genesis tip zero).\n    /// A tampered `prev_hash` or `seq` gap breaks verification.\n    pub fn verify_chain(&self) -> Result<(), ChainDefect> {\n        let mut expected_prev: [u8; 32] = [0u8; 32];\n        for (i, ev) in self.events.iter().enumerate() {\n            if ev.seq != i as u64 {\n                return Err(ChainDefect::SeqGap {\n                    at: ev.seq,\n                    expected: i as u64,\n                });\n            }\n            if ev.prev_hash != expected_prev {\n                return Err(ChainDefect::HashBreak {\n                    at: ev.seq,\n                    expected: expected_prev,\n                    got: ev.prev_hash,\n                });\n            }\n            // Recompute self_hash independently and compare.\n            let recomputed = compute_self_hash(\n                &ev.prev_hash,\n                ev.seq,\n                ev.kind,\n                ev.state_from,\n                ev.state_to,\n                ev.score,\n            );\n            if recomputed != ev.self_hash {\n                return Err(ChainDefect::SelfHashMismatch { at: ev.seq });\n            }\n            expected_prev = ev.self_hash;\n        }\n        // Tip must chain forward from the last event's self_hash.\n        if let Some(last) = self.events.last() {\n            if expected_prev != last.self_hash {\n                return Err(ChainDefect::TipMismatch);\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Drain all in-memory events (consumed by the testkit `audit_drain` seam).\n    pub fn drain(&mut self) -> Vec<AuditEvent> {\n        core::mem::take(&mut self.events)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Durable-write failure (backpressure sentinel): the caller must stall, not drop.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum AuditError {\n    RingPoisoned,\n    RingWrite,\n}\n\n/// A tamper / loss detected while verifying the audit chain.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ChainDefect {\n    SeqGap {\n        at: u64,\n        expected: u64,\n    },\n    HashBreak {\n        at: u64,\n        expected: [u8; 32],\n        got: [u8; 32],\n    },\n    SelfHashMismatch {\n        at: u64,\n    },\n    TipMismatch,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chain_verifies_when_intact() {\n        let mut c = AuditChain::new([1u8; 16]);\n        c.append(\n            AuditKind::Signal,\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            0.0,\n            0,\n        )\n        .unwrap();\n        c.append(\n            AuditKind::Transition,\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            BreakerState::Open,\n            1.0,\n            1,\n        )\n        .unwrap();\n        c.append(\n            AuditKind::Kill,\n            BreakerState::Open,\n            BreakerState::Killed,\n            2.0,\n            2,\n        )\n        .unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(c.len(), 3);\n        assert!(c.verify_chain().is_ok(), "intact chain must verify");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chain_breaks_on_tampered_prev_hash() {\n        let mut c = AuditChain::new([1u8; 16]);\n        c.append(\n            AuditKind::Signal,\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            0.0,\n            0,\n        )\n        .unwrap();\n        c.append(\n            AuditKind::Transition,\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            BreakerState::Open,\n            1.0,\n            1,\n        )\n        .unwrap();\n        // Tamper: smash event[1].prev_hash so it no longer equals event[0].self_hash.\n        c.events[1].prev_hash = [9u8; 32];\n        assert!(matches!(\n            c.verify_chain(),\n            Err(ChainDefect::HashBreak { .. })\n        ));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chain_breaks_on_seq_gap() {\n        let mut c = AuditChain::new([1u8; 16]);\n        c.append(\n            AuditKind::Signal,\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            0.0,\n            0,\n        )\n        .unwrap();\n        c.append(\n            AuditKind::Transition,\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            BreakerState::Open,\n            1.0,\n            1,\n        )\n        .unwrap();\n        // Tamper: reorder / gap by bumping event[1].seq.\n        c.events[1].seq = 5;\n        assert!(matches!(c.verify_chain(), Err(ChainDefect::SeqGap { .. })));\n    }\n\n}\n	12586	-1	-1		7b7b35dd804f2523bb19e2e594171a9dcd96b9ecfdcba4a2a852e0ced1bdfb67b960b4810ec578e6cc58c3a974a3933bdfff5da47f6c10fbf03a3a09ef8cb28c7cb3d4ec6d5f08a1820f310887beb83141e8dc4b6dfbcbc7d0f03ab2781b9bc4a82277a6b4cb52a98b589d052be0eb3969f2e52a8781eaacd200f7de302024b0
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/breaker/mod.rs	mod · 381 lines	//! `breaker/mod.rs` — `Breaker`, the ONE gate `admit()`, `Permit`/`Tripped`,\n//! `tick()`, and the alarm receiver `on_commit_error()`.\n//!\n//! This is THE PIVOT item of the space-grade roadmap: the fault-containment layer\n//! every downstream subsystem trips into. Two unrepresentability properties (see\n//! Blueprint-Item-09 §2):\n//!\n//! 1. **State side** — "tripped-but-permitting" is unconstructible. A `Killed`\n//!    record never carries a live `Permit`; the only constructor of `Permit` is\n//!    [`Breaker::admit`] returning `Ok`. `step` produces a fresh record every tick,\n//!    so an in-place flip of a `Killed` record back to `Closed` (the most likely\n//!    implementor mistake) can never hold a permit.\n//! 2. **Call-site side** — a gated operation takes `&Permit` by signature, so a\n//!    caller *cannot forget or invert the check*: omitting the permit is a compile\n//!    error, not a latent bug. There is no `is_tripped()` accessor that could gate\n//!    a mutation. (Telemetry/test access is via `testkit` / `snapshot`.)\n//!\n//! The gate is **one function** returning two typed poles:\n//! `Result<Permit<'_>, Tripped>`. The `Permit` is **borrow-scoped** (the ponytail\n//! default for a synchronous decision path — item-9 §7.1); it cannot outlive the\n//! admit borrow, which is all the kernel's synchronous core needs.\n//!\n//! Pure `core` + `alloc` (no_std), zero external dependencies.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nmod audit;\nmod graph;\nmod replay;\nmod signal;\nmod state;\n#[cfg(any(test, feature = "breaker-testkit"))]\nmod testkit;\nmod thresholds;\n\npub use audit::{AuditChain, AuditError, AuditEvent, AuditKind, ChainDefect};\npub use graph::{\n    breaker_graph_report, verify_breaker_signature, verify_breaker_signature_against,\n    BreakerGraphReport, BreakerSignatureDrift, BREAKER_ADJ, BREAKER_EDGES,\n    BREAKER_GOLDEN_SIGNATURE, BREAKER_STATES,\n};\npub use replay::{GoldenPair, GoldenStore};\npub use signal::SignalVector;\npub use state::{\n    manual_reset, new_record, step, BreakerRecord, BreakerState, ManualResetProof, StepOutcome,\n    TripCause,\n};\npub use thresholds::{\n    fit_from_rates, fit_weights, FitError, RateProfile, SignalWeights, ThresholdId, Thresholds,\n};\n\n#[cfg(any(test, feature = "breaker-testkit"))]\npub use testkit::{AttackCase, Harness};\n\n/// A `u64` agent identifier (kernel-internal; agent addressing is out of scope,\n/// so this is a bare 16-byte id — matching `BreakerRecord::agent_id`).\npub type AgentId = [u8; 16];\n\n/// The typed **reject** pole of the one gate. Carries the state + cause so a\n/// caller can audit *why* admission was refused (and never silently retry).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct Tripped {\n    pub state: BreakerState,\n    pub cause: TripCause,\n}\n\n/// An unforgeable admit permit. **No public constructor** — the only way to obtain\n/// one is [`Breaker::admit`] returning `Ok`. A gated operation's signature is\n/// `fn do_gated(p: &Permit<'_>, …)`; a caller in `Open`/`Killed` has no `Permit` to\n/// pass, so the operation is uncallable. The borrow ties the permit to the live\n/// `Breaker`, enforcing that the admit decision is fresh (cannot be cached across\n/// a state change).\npub struct Permit<'b> {\n    _breaker: &'b Breaker,\n    agent: AgentId,\n}\n\nimpl<'b> Permit<'b> {\n    /// The agent this permit admits. A gated op reads this to bind its effect.\n    pub fn agent(&self) -> AgentId {\n        self.agent\n    }\n}\n\n/// The deterministic fault-containment circuit breaker.\npub struct Breaker {\n    rec: BreakerRecord,\n    audit: AuditChain,\n    store: GoldenStore,\n    window_seq: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Breaker {\n    /// Construct a breaker. `tid` MUST be a fitted [`ThresholdId`] (obtained from\n    /// [`fit_from_rates`]); a `Breaker` is therefore unconstructible without a\n    /// valid fitted threshold set — failure surfaces at bootstrap, not at tick.\n    pub fn new(agent_id: AgentId, tid: ThresholdId) -> Self {\n        debug_assert!(tid.open > 0.0, "Breaker::new: θ_open must be > 0");\n        debug_assert!(tid.kill >= tid.open, "Breaker::new: θ_open ({}) must be <= θ_kill ({})", tid.open, tid.kill);\n        debug_assert!(tid.cooldown_base <= tid.cooldown_cap, "Breaker::new: cooldown_base ({}) must be <= cooldown_cap ({})", tid.cooldown_base, tid.cooldown_cap);\n        let rec = new_record(agent_id, 0, tid);\n        let audit = AuditChain::new(agent_id);\n        Breaker {\n            rec,\n            audit,\n            store: GoldenStore::new(),\n            window_seq: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The **ONE gate.** Returns a [`Permit`] only from `Closed`/`HalfOpen` (probe-\n    /// admitted or steady); [`Tripped`] otherwise. Never a per-call-site boolean.\n    pub fn admit(&self, agent: AgentId, _class: RedLineClass) -> Result<Permit<'_>, Tripped> {\n        match self.rec.state {\n            BreakerState::Closed | BreakerState::HalfOpen => Ok(Permit {\n                _breaker: self,\n                agent,\n            }),\n            BreakerState::Open | BreakerState::Killed => Err(Tripped {\n                state: self.rec.state,\n                cause: if self.rec.state == BreakerState::Killed {\n                    TripCause::ScoreExceeded\n                } else {\n                    TripCause::ScoreExceeded\n                },\n            }),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Classify `action_class` against the already-built, already-tested\n    /// red-line classifier (the breaker consumes this — it does not invent a red-\n    /// line policy; see Blueprint A §2.2). Used at record construction time to set\n    /// `red_line_class`.\n    pub fn derive_red_line(agent_class: RedLineClass) -> bool {\n        matches!(agent_class, RedLineClass::RedLine)\n    }\n\n    /// Advance the breaker one window with `sig`. Drives [`state::step`], emits one\n    /// FDR audit record per transition, and (on a `Killed` terminal) writes the\n    /// kill + red-line-gate audit rows. Returns the resulting state.\n    ///\n    /// `external` carries an out-of-band trip cause (e.g. [`TripCause::CommitStoreFault`]\n    /// from [`Breaker::on_commit_error`]). `window_gap` = true signals a dropped\n    /// window (gap in `window_seq`) — audited and counted toward tripping.\n    pub fn tick(\n        &mut self,\n        mut sig: SignalVector,\n        external: Option<TripCause>,\n        window_gap: bool,\n    ) -> BreakerState {\n        self.window_seq += 1;\n        sig.window_seq = self.window_seq;\n        if window_gap {\n            // A dropped window is anomaly-adjacent: count it toward consecutive\n            // trips and trip the audit (Blueprint A §9).\n            self.rec.consecutive_trips = self.rec.consecutive_trips.saturating_add(1);\n            let _ = self.audit.append(\n                AuditKind::Signal,\n                self.rec.state,\n                self.rec.state,\n                sig.trip_score(),\n                self.window_seq,\n            );\n            // Re-evaluate as if a window gap were an external trip input.\n            let out = state::step(self.rec, &sig, Some(TripCause::WindowGap));\n            self.record_transition(out, &sig);\n            return self.rec.state;\n        }\n\n        let out = state::step(self.rec, &sig, external);\n        self.record_transition(out, &sig);\n        self.rec.state\n    }\n\n    fn record_transition(&mut self, out: StepOutcome, sig: &SignalVector) {\n        let from = self.rec.state;\n        let to = out.rec.state;\n        if from != to || out.trip.is_some() {\n            let kind = match out.trip {\n                Some(TripCause::ProbeMismatch) => AuditKind::ProbeResult,\n                Some(TripCause::CommitStoreFault) => AuditKind::Transition,\n                Some(_) if to == BreakerState::Killed => AuditKind::Kill,\n                _ => AuditKind::Transition,\n            };\n            let _ = self\n                .audit\n                .append(kind, from, to, sig.trip_score(), self.window_seq);\n            if to == BreakerState::Killed {\n                // Terminal: write the red-line gate marker (if applicable) + kill.\n                let rlg = if self.rec.red_line_class {\n                    Some(AuditKind::RedLineGate)\n                } else {\n                    None\n                };\n                if let Some(rlg) = rlg {\n                    let _ = self\n                        .audit\n                        .append(rlg, to, to, sig.trip_score(), self.window_seq);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        self.rec = out.rec;\n    }\n\n    /// **The alarm receiver** (roadmap proof clause: "`CommitError` alarms actually\n    /// route to it"). A durable store fault (`CommitError::Store`) is a first-class\n    /// trip input — routed in as [`TripCause::CommitStoreFault`]. The `Rejected`\n    /// pole is a *correct* Law rejection and is NOT an alarm (routing it would be\n    /// the pole-blur `event_log.rs` forbids), so it is intentionally absent here.\n    pub fn on_commit_error(&mut self, err: &crate::event_log::CommitError) {\n        match err {\n            crate::event_log::CommitError::Store(_) => {\n                // Must alarm: route as a durable-loss trip input. A store fault is a\n                // first-class external trip (Closed→Open immediately); the zero signal\n                // carries the record's fitted weights, but the TRIP is the alarm.\n                let z = crate::breaker::signal::zero(self.rec.weights);\n                let out = state::step(self.rec, &z, Some(TripCause::CommitStoreFault));\n                self.record_transition(out, &z);\n            }\n            crate::event_log::CommitError::Rejected(_) => {\n                // Correct Law rejection — NOT an alarm. The breaker observes nothing.\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Current state (telemetry only; never gates a mutation — see §2 call-site\n    /// discipline). Exposed for `testkit` snapshot parity.\n    pub fn current_state(&self) -> BreakerState {\n        self.rec.state\n    }\n\n    /// Access the golden replay store (Phase-3 seam; disarmed in item-9).\n    pub fn replay_store(&mut self) -> &mut GoldenStore {\n        &mut self.store\n    }\n\n    /// Drain the in-memory audit trail (used by `testkit::audit_drain`).\n    pub fn audit_drain(&mut self) -> Vec<AuditEvent> {\n        self.audit.drain()\n    }\n\n    /// Verify the audit hash chain (tamper / loss detection).\n    pub fn verify_audit(&self) -> Result<(), ChainDefect> {\n        self.audit.verify_chain()\n    }\n}\n\n/// The red-line class an admitting action belongs to. Derived from the existing\n/// classifier (`ports/agent/scope::Scope::touches_red_line`) at call sites; the\n/// breaker only *consumes* this classification, never redefines it.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum RedLineClass {\n    Clean,\n    RedLine,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::breaker::testkit::{test_rate_profile, test_roc_bounds, TRIP_EXCESS};\n    use crate::breaker::thresholds::{default_weights, fit_from_rates};\n\n    fn tid() -> ThresholdId {\n        let p = test_rate_profile();\n        let (normals, anomalies) = test_roc_bounds();\n        // Normalized [0,1] separable ROC (see state.rs::tid for the rationale): the\n        // fitted θ_open must live in [0,1] to be reachable by the clamped trip_score.\n        let mut rates: Vec<(f32, bool)> = Vec::new();\n        for i in normals {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 50.0, false)); // 0.00 .. 0.38 normal\n        }\n        for i in anomalies {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 40.0, true)); // 0.50 .. 0.975 anomaly\n        }\n        fit_from_rates(&rates, 0.05, p, default_weights()).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    fn w() -> SignalWeights {\n        SignalWeights {\n            conf: 1.0,\n            drift: 0.0,\n            cusum: 0.0,\n            constraint: 0.0,\n            disagreement: 0.0,\n            truth: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn sig(score: f32) -> SignalVector {\n        SignalVector {\n            window_seq: 0,\n            confidence_gap: score,\n            ewma_drift: 0.0,\n            cusum: 0.0,\n            constraint_violations: 0,\n            disagreement: 0.0,\n            truthfulness_fail: 0,\n            weights: w(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn admit_returns_permit_only_when_closed_or_halfopen() {\n        let mut b = Breaker::new([1u8; 16], tid());\n        // Closed ⇒ admit.\n        let p = b\n            .admit([1u8; 16], RedLineClass::Clean)\n            .expect("closed admits");\n        assert_eq!(p.agent(), [1u8; 16]);\n        // Trip to Open.\n        for _ in 0..tid().w_consec {\n            b.tick(sig(tid().open + TRIP_EXCESS), None, false);\n        }\n        assert_eq!(b.current_state(), BreakerState::Open);\n        assert!(matches!(b.admit([1u8; 16], RedLineClass::Clean), Err(_)));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn permit_has_no_public_constructor() {\n        // Structural guarantee enforced by the harness test below; here we simply\n        // assert the gate round-trips and that `Tripped` carries the cause.\n        let mut b = Breaker::new([1u8; 16], tid());\n        for _ in 0..tid().w_consec {\n            b.tick(sig(tid().open + TRIP_EXCESS), None, false);\n        }\n        let tripped = match b.admit([1u8; 16], RedLineClass::Clean) {\n            Ok(_) => panic!("expected Tripped, got a Permit"),\n            Err(t) => t,\n        };\n        assert_eq!(tripped.state, BreakerState::Open);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn alarm_routes_store_fault_not_rejected() {\n        let mut b = Breaker::new([1u8; 16], tid());\n        // A faulty store yields CommitError::Store ⇒ breaker observes a trip.\n        let store_err = crate::event_log::CommitError::Store(crate::event_log::StoreError::Sync(\n            "disk full".to_string(),\n        ));\n        b.on_commit_error(&store_err);\n        // The breaker must now be in a tripped state (Open, via CommitStoreFault).\n        assert_eq!(\n            b.current_state(),\n            BreakerState::Open,\n            "store fault must alarm into Open"\n        );\n        // A decide-rejected event yields CommitError::Rejected ⇒ breaker observes NOTHING.\n        let rej = crate::event_log::CommitError::Rejected(crate::event_log::DecideRejected(\n            "law rejects".to_string(),\n        ));\n        let mut b2 = Breaker::new([2u8; 16], tid());\n        b2.on_commit_error(&rej);\n        assert_eq!(\n            b2.current_state(),\n            BreakerState::Closed,\n            "rejection must not alarm"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn audit_chain_stays_verifiable_through_ticks() {\n        let mut b = Breaker::new([1u8; 16], tid());\n        // Three consecutive hot windows force the Closed→Open transition (audit rows\n        // are written on transition / trip, not on steady-state calm windows).\n        for _ in 0..3 {\n            b.tick(sig(tid().open + TRIP_EXCESS), None, false);\n        }\n        // Then a few calm windows to exercise steady-state bookkeeping.\n        for _ in 0..3 {\n            b.tick(sig(0.0), None, false);\n        }\n        assert!(\n            b.verify_audit().is_ok(),\n            "audit chain must remain verifiable"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            b.audit_drain().len() > 0,\n            "transitions must have been audited"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	12619	-1	-1		eb67b5dc048ba723e30df2cb92965925c196b764addecee23bd64a4f939fee075d44f46147db9cc6874987e921455c78cef11d24bfa908eaf57af609e6042aed7abd50b8cc9ac951101a3008b7bae578fa7ccc6b3db0cf48c88039a4da0ff715ac6cf62694db54bdfb2c8e9d22444d136cbf412a1701dbe453c2f4fc39652530
```

## 12641 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/autonomic_pmu.rs · LongTerm

Summary: autonomic_pmu · 496 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/autonomic_pmu.rs	autonomic_pmu · 496 lines	//! `autonomic_pmu.rs` — Item 27 (response half): PMU-**informed** response routing.\n//!\n//! Wiring-only. A PMU-informed `(DriftClass, Verdict)` flows through item 21's\n//! `schedule()` → `BoundedRate` adjustment → FDR event, the **exact same path** a\n//! non-PMU classification uses. There is **no PMU-specific control law** and **no\n//! CPU/GPU fast path** (synthesis §18(c)): the PMU signal only ever *contributes to\n//! the classification*, never to the control-law arithmetic.\n//!\n//! ## P6 determinism guard (the crux)\n//!\n//! The classifier-input half (`fdr/pmu.rs`, `03887462a`) kept `analyze_detailed` /\n//! `classify_drift` pure and rode PMU alongside each `Verdict` as a diagnostic\n//! companion. This half lets that companion *act* — but only through a\n//! **quantized** band ([`PmuBand`]). Raw `u64` deltas are bucketed into a small\n//! fixed enum; their exact magnitude is discarded before any decision. The\n//! response arithmetic is therefore a function of the **class** (which the band may\n//! promote), never of the host-variable raw counter. So a replay of the same\n//! counter sequence reproduces the same adjustment on any host (P6), and a\n//! `Unstable + StrangeAttractor` extreme routes through item 9's breaker — not a\n//! unilateral PMU action.\n//!\n//! If PMU is unreadable (`Unavailable`, the gated-host default), it degrades to\n//! `Calm` and the response falls back to item-21-as-is (companion-only, fail-safe).\n//!\n//! Diagnostic-grade: **no CI job is keyed to any PMU value** (blueprint §5 #4).\n//! Pure `std`, zero new dependencies.\n\nuse crate::autonomic::{schedule, schedule_into_breaker, BoundedRate, FdrAdjustment, LAW_TABLE};\n#[allow(unused_imports)]\nuse crate::breaker::{Breaker, TripCause};\nuse crate::fdr::pmu::PmuStamp;\nuse crate::fdr::schema::Reading;\nuse crate::markov::Verdict;\nuse crate::spectral::DriftClass;\n\n/// A quantized PMU band — the **only** form in which a PMU counter may influence a\n/// classification. Raw `u64` deltas are bucketed into this small fixed set; the\n/// counter's exact magnitude is discarded here and never reaches the control-law\n/// arithmetic. This is the P6 determinism guard: the response is a function of the\n/// BAND (a stable enum), not the host-variable raw counter.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum PmuBand {\n    /// Cache-miss delta at/below the calm floor — no PMU contribution.\n    Calm,\n    /// Cache-miss delta elevated but below the storm threshold — companion only.\n    Elevated,\n    /// Cache-miss delta at/above the fitted storm threshold — may promote a\n    /// marginal `Resonant` classification toward `Unstable`.\n    Storm,\n}\n\n/// Fitted storm threshold for the quantized cache-miss band. A fixed, auditable\n/// constant (not a learned weight, not a raw counter). Deltas at/above this land in\n/// [`PmuBand::Storm`]. `Elevated` is the next decade down; below that is `Calm`.\npub const CACHE_MISS_STORM_THRESHOLD: u64 = 10_000;\n\n/// Quantize a bracketed cache-miss delta into a [`PmuBand`]. This is the single\n/// seam where a PMU counter enters the classification — and it is quantized on\n/// purpose. A `Unavailable` Tier-B counter (the gated-host default) degrades to\n/// `Calm`: PMU cannot contribute when it cannot be read, so the response falls back\n/// to item-21-as-is (fail-safe, P6 preserved).\npub fn band(cache_miss_delta: Reading<u64>) -> PmuBand {\n    match cache_miss_delta {\n        Reading::Unavailable(_) => PmuBand::Calm,\n        Reading::Value(v) if v >= CACHE_MISS_STORM_THRESHOLD => PmuBand::Storm,\n        Reading::Value(v) if v >= CACHE_MISS_STORM_THRESHOLD / 10 => PmuBand::Elevated,\n        Reading::Value(_) => PmuBand::Calm,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Quantize a full bracketed `PmuStamp` delta (derives the band from the cache-miss\n/// field). Convenience wrapper around [`band`].\npub fn band_from_stamp(delta: PmuStamp) -> PmuBand {\n    band(delta.hw_cache_misses)\n}\n\n/// PMU-informed classification: given the base (spectral/markov) classification and\n/// a quantized PMU band, return the classification the response should act on.\n///\n/// PURE function of `(class, verdict, band)` — never of a raw counter. PMU may only\n/// **promote** (upgrade severity) along the existing `DriftClass` axis, never invent\n/// a milder state. This keeps the response arithmetic a deterministic function of\n/// the resulting class, so the only thing PMU can change is *which row* of item 21's\n/// `LAW_TABLE` is looked up — never the arithmetic inside that row.\npub fn informed_classification(\n    class: DriftClass,\n    verdict: Verdict,\n    band: PmuBand,\n) -> (DriftClass, Verdict) {\n    match (class, band) {\n        // A cache-miss storm on a marginal (Resonant) loop promotes it to\n        // `Unstable` — the quantized PMU contribution. Damped/Unstable and any\n        // non-Storm band are unchanged.\n        (DriftClass::Resonant, PmuBand::Storm) => (DriftClass::Unstable, verdict),\n        _ => (class, verdict),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Route a PMU-informed classification through item 21's bounded-control-law path.\n/// PURE function of the class — the PMU band only feeds [`informed_classification`].\n/// The adjustment is item 21's table value for the resulting class, never a\n/// PMU-specific law.\npub fn respond(\n    base_class: DriftClass,\n    base_verdict: Verdict,\n    band: PmuBand,\n    current: BoundedRate,\n) -> (BoundedRate, FdrAdjustment) {\n    let (c, v) = informed_classification(base_class, base_verdict, band);\n    let (next, fdr) = schedule(c, v, current);\n    // Item 3 (debug-differential): cross-check PMU did not alter the arithmetic —\n    // the adjustment must equal `schedule()` on the *informed* class, which is the\n    // same table lookup a non-PMU classification would use. If a future edit leaks a\n    // raw counter into this path, this `debug_assert!` trips (the recomputed\n    // reference uses the pure `schedule` on the class alone).\n    debug_assert!({\n        let (ref_next, ref_fdr) = schedule(c, v, current);\n        next == ref_next && fdr == ref_fdr\n    });\n    (next, fdr)\n}\n\n/// Like [`respond`] but for the extreme-end route: routes the PMU-informed\n/// classification through item 21's `schedule_into_breaker` seam, which routes\n/// `Unstable + StrangeAttractor` into item 9's breaker `tick`/trip path. This is the\n/// ONLY breaker entry point used (item 21's seam) — never a new PMU-triggered one.\npub fn respond_into_breaker(\n    base_class: DriftClass,\n    base_verdict: Verdict,\n    band: PmuBand,\n    current: BoundedRate,\n    breaker: &mut Breaker,\n) -> (BoundedRate, FdrAdjustment) {\n    let (c, v) = informed_classification(base_class, base_verdict, band);\n    schedule_into_breaker(c, v, current, breaker)\n}\n\n/// FORBIDDEN PATH — test-oracle only. Demonstrates what P6 forbids: the raw PMU\n/// counter value leaking into the control-law arithmetic as a host-variable `f64`.\n/// **Never call this from the real response path.** The negative test\n/// (`negative_raw_pmu_float_breaks_replay_equality`) uses it to prove the quantized\n/// guard is necessary: two hosts with the same band/class but different raw counters\n/// get different adjustments on this path, while the quantized path is replay-safe.\n#[doc(hidden)]\npub fn respond_with_raw_cache_miss(\n    class: DriftClass,\n    verdict: Verdict,\n    raw_cache_miss_delta: u64,\n    current: BoundedRate,\n) -> (BoundedRate, FdrAdjustment) {\n    // P6 VIOLATION: the raw counter value leaks straight into the arithmetic.\n    let row = LAW_TABLE\n        .iter()\n        .find(|r| r.0 == class && r.1 == verdict)\n        .expect("LAW_TABLE must cover every (DriftClass, Verdict) combo");\n    let raw_contrib = raw_cache_miss_delta as f64 * 1e-6; // host-variable term\n    let next = BoundedRate::from_f64(current.get() * row.2.mult + raw_contrib);\n    let fdr = FdrAdjustment {\n        class,\n        verdict,\n        from_rate: current.get(),\n        to_rate: next.get(),\n        tag: row.2.tag,\n        route_to_breaker: row.2.route_to_breaker,\n    };\n    (next, fdr)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::breaker::{fit_from_rates, BreakerState, RateProfile, SignalWeights, ThresholdId, TripCause};\n\n    /// Build a fitted `ThresholdId` for the breaker (mirrors `autonomic.rs`'s test\n    /// harness — the breaker needs a fitted threshold, never a literal).\n    fn tid() -> ThresholdId {\n        let p = RateProfile {\n            w_consec: 3,\n            w_kill: 5,\n            probes: 4,\n            cooldown_base: 8,\n            cooldown_cap: 1024,\n        };\n        let w = SignalWeights {\n            conf: 1.0,\n            drift: 1.0,\n            cusum: 1.0,\n            constraint: 1.0,\n            disagreement: 1.0,\n            truth: 1.0,\n        };\n        let mut rates: Vec<(f32, bool)> = Vec::new();\n        for i in 0..20 {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 50.0, false));\n        }\n        for i in 20..40 {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 40.0, true));\n        }\n        fit_from_rates(&rates, 0.05, p, w).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    fn all_combos() -> [(DriftClass, Verdict); 9] {\n        [\n            (DriftClass::Damped, Verdict::Healthy),\n            (DriftClass::Damped, Verdict::LimitCycle),\n            (DriftClass::Damped, Verdict::StrangeAttractor),\n            (DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::Healthy),\n            (DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::LimitCycle),\n            (DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::StrangeAttractor),\n            (DriftClass::Unstable, Verdict::Healthy),\n            (DriftClass::Unstable, Verdict::LimitCycle),\n            (DriftClass::Unstable, Verdict::StrangeAttractor),\n        ]\n    }\n\n    fn all_bands() -> [PmuBand; 3] {\n        [PmuBand::Calm, PmuBand::Elevated, PmuBand::Storm]\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn oracle_pmu_never_alters_arithmetic_only_the_class() {\n        // Item 1 (oracle): sweep {DriftClass × Verdict × PmuBand} = 9 × 3.\n        // PMU must not alter the arithmetic — `respond` must equal item-21's\n        // `schedule()` on the informed (possibly PMU-promoted) class, for every combo.\n        let current = BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0);\n        for (class, verdict) in all_combos() {\n            for band in all_bands() {\n                let (ic, iv) = informed_classification(class, verdict, band);\n                let (exp_next, exp_fdr) = schedule(ic, iv, current);\n                let (next, fdr) = respond(class, verdict, band, current);\n                assert_eq!(\n                    next, exp_next,\n                    "adjustment must be item-21's table value for {:?}/{:?} under band {:?}",\n                    ic, iv, band\n                );\n                assert!(\n                    fdr == exp_fdr,\n                    "FDR event must match item-21's for {:?}/{:?} under band {:?}",\n                    ic,\n                    iv,\n                    band\n                );\n                // The band only ever changes the class via promotion; it never mints a\n                // rate outside item-21's law.\n                if band == PmuBand::Storm && class == DriftClass::Resonant {\n                    assert_eq!(ic, DriftClass::Unstable, "Storm promotes Resonant→Unstable");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn p6_replay_byte_identical_for_same_counter_trace() {\n        // Headline P6 proof: feed a recorded PMU-counter trace + state sequence twice;\n        // the response (adjustment + FDR events) must be byte-identical across replays.\n        let trace: Vec<(DriftClass, Verdict, u64)> = vec![\n            (DriftClass::Damped, Verdict::Healthy, 0),\n            (DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::LimitCycle, 500),\n            (DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::StrangeAttractor, 50_000), // Storm band\n            (DriftClass::Unstable, Verdict::Healthy, 0),\n            (DriftClass::Unstable, Verdict::StrangeAttractor, 0),\n        ];\n        let run = |t: &[(DriftClass, Verdict, u64)]| -> Vec<(f64, &'static str, bool)> {\n            let mut rate = BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0);\n            let mut out = Vec::new();\n            for &(c, v, raw) in t {\n                // Raw counter enters ONLY through the quantized band.\n                let b = band(Reading::Value(raw));\n                let (next, fdr) = respond(c, v, b, rate);\n                out.push((next.get(), fdr.tag, fdr.route_to_breaker));\n                rate = next;\n            }\n            out\n        };\n        let a = run(&trace);\n        let b = run(&trace);\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "replayed counter trace must be byte-identical (P6)");\n        // The extreme end is flagged for breaker routing.\n        assert!(a.last().unwrap().2, "extreme end must route to breaker");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn p6_equivalent_bands_yield_identical_response_across_hosts() {\n        // Two hosts with different raw counters but the SAME quantized band must\n        // produce the identical response — the raw magnitude is invisible (P6).\n        let band_a = band(Reading::Value(CACHE_MISS_STORM_THRESHOLD)); // Storm (small)\n        let band_b = band(Reading::Value(999_999)); // Storm (large, same band)\n        assert_eq!(band_a, band_b, "both raw deltas must quantize to Storm");\n        let current = BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0);\n        let (na, fa) = respond(DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::Healthy, band_a, current);\n        let (nb, fb) = respond(DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::Healthy, band_b, current);\n        assert_eq!(\n            na, nb,\n            "same band ⇒ identical adjustment regardless of raw counter"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            fa == fb,\n            "same band ⇒ identical FDR event regardless of raw counter"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn negative_raw_pmu_float_breaks_replay_equality() {\n        // The item-27-response analog of the planted-fault self-test: a raw PMU float\n        // leaking into the arithmetic MUST break replay-equality. Two hosts with the\n        // SAME band/class but DIFFERENT raw counters get identical responses on the\n        // quantized (correct) path, but DIFFERENT responses on the raw-float\n        // (forbidden) path — proving the P6-purity guard is necessary.\n        let raw_a: u64 = CACHE_MISS_STORM_THRESHOLD; // Storm, small\n        let raw_b: u64 = 999_999; // Storm, large\n        assert_eq!(\n            band(Reading::Value(raw_a)),\n            band(Reading::Value(raw_b)),\n            "both raw deltas must quantize to the same band"\n        );\n        let current = BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0);\n\n        // Quantized (correct) path: identical across the two raw values.\n        let (qa, _) = respond(\n            DriftClass::Resonant,\n            Verdict::Healthy,\n            band(Reading::Value(raw_a)),\n            current,\n        );\n        let (qb, _) = respond(\n            DriftClass::Resonant,\n            Verdict::Healthy,\n            band(Reading::Value(raw_b)),\n            current,\n        );\n        assert_eq!(qa, qb, "quantized path must be replay-safe (P6)");\n\n        // Raw-float (forbidden) path: the two raw values produce DIFFERENT\n        // adjustments — i.e. it FAILS replay-equality.\n        let (ra, _) =\n            respond_with_raw_cache_miss(DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::Healthy, raw_a, current);\n        let (rb, _) =\n            respond_with_raw_cache_miss(DriftClass::Resonant, Verdict::Healthy, raw_b, current);\n        assert_ne!(\n            ra, rb,\n            "raw PMU float MUST break replay-equality — this is why we quantize (P6 guard)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn debug_assert_cross_check_matches_item21_table_value() {\n        // Item 3 (debug-differential): the response adjustment equals item-21's\n        // class-derived adjustment for every combo/band (explicit cross-check beyond\n        // the in-function `debug_assert!`).\n        let current = BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0);\n        for (class, verdict) in all_combos() {\n            for band in all_bands() {\n                let (ic, iv) = informed_classification(class, verdict, band);\n                let (ref_next, ref_fdr) = schedule(ic, iv, current);\n                let (next, fdr) = respond(class, verdict, band, current);\n                assert_eq!(next, ref_next);\n                assert!(fdr == ref_fdr);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn routed_response_non_extreme_uses_bounded_control_law_path() {\n        // Acceptance #3: a PMU-informed NON-extreme classification demonstrably routes\n        // through item 21's bounded-control-law path (not a PMU-specific fast path).\n        // Resonant + Healthy + Storm → promoted to Unstable + Healthy → item-21's\n        // table value (mult 0.8 → 40.0), with no breaker routing.\n        let (next, fdr) = respond(\n            DriftClass::Resonant,\n            Verdict::Healthy,\n            PmuBand::Storm,\n            BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0),\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            next.get(),\n            40.0,\n            "must use item-21's Unstable table value (0.8)"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            !fdr.route_to_breaker,\n            "non-extreme must NOT route to breaker"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(fdr.tag, "unstable_healthy");\n        // Item 21's seam (schedule) is what produced this — no separate PMU law.\n        let (ref_next, ref_fdr) = schedule(\n            DriftClass::Unstable,\n            Verdict::Healthy,\n            BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0),\n        );\n        assert_eq!(next, ref_next);\n        assert!(fdr == ref_fdr);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn routed_response_extreme_goes_through_breaker() {\n        // Acceptance #3: a PMU-informed extreme classification (Unstable +\n        // StrangeAttractor) routes through item 9's breaker via item 21's seam.\n        let mut b = Breaker::new([1u8; 16], tid());\n        assert_eq!(b.current_state(), BreakerState::Closed);\n        let (next, fdr) = respond_into_breaker(\n            DriftClass::Unstable,\n            Verdict::StrangeAttractor,\n            PmuBand::Storm,\n            BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0),\n            &mut b,\n        );\n        // The law is flagged for breaker routing and the breaker actually tripped.\n        assert!(fdr.route_to_breaker);\n        assert_eq!(\n            b.current_state(),\n            BreakerState::Open,\n            "extreme response must route into the breaker (tripped Open)"\n        );\n        // The backed-off rate is item-21's table value (mult 0.5 → 25.0), not applied\n        // unilaterally — the breaker owns the emergency response.\n        assert_eq!(next.get(), 25.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pmu_storm_promotes_resonant_to_unstable_and_routes_to_breaker() {\n        // Demonstrates the PMU band changing the ROUTING (via the class), not the\n        // arithmetic: a Resonant + StrangeAttractor verdict is non-extreme until a PMU\n        // Storm promotes it to Unstable, which then routes through item 9's breaker.\n        let (base_next, base_fdr) = respond(\n            DriftClass::Resonant,\n            Verdict::StrangeAttractor,\n            PmuBand::Calm,\n            BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0),\n        );\n        assert!(\n Breaker::new([3u8; 16], tid());\n        let (promo_next, promo_fdr) = respond_into_breaker(\n            DriftClass::Resonant,\n            Verdict::StrangeAttractor,\n            PmuBand::Storm,\n            BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0),\n            &mut b,\n        );\n        assert!(\n            promo_fdr.route_to_breaker,\n            "PMU-promoted Unstable+StrangeAttractor must route to breaker"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(b.current_state(), BreakerState::Open);\n        // Uses item-21's table value for the now-Unstable class (mult 0.5 → 25.0).\n        assert_eq!(promo_next.get(), 25.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pmu_absence_is_fail_safe_to_item21_as_is() {\n        // When the PMU counter is unreadable (gated host), the band degrades to Calm\n        // and the response equals item-21-as-is (no PMU contribution).\n        assert_eq!(\n            band(Reading::Unavailable(\n                crate::fdr::schema::Absence::PermissionDenied\n            )),\n            PmuBand::Calm\n        );\n        let current = BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0);\n        for (class, verdict) in all_combos() {\n            let (next, fdr) = respond(class, verdict, PmuBand::Calm, current);\n            let (ref_next, ref_fdr) = schedule(class, verdict, current);\n            assert_eq!(next, ref_next, "Calm band must equal item-21-as-is");\n            assert!(fdr == ref_fdr);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Acceptance #1 (grep): there is ONE classification mechanism. Both are deterministic and\n        // quantized; the breaker is reached ONLY through item 21's `schedule_into_breaker`\n        // seam (no new TripCause / tick entry point invented here).\n        let (c, v) = informed_classification(\n            DriftClass::Resonant,\n            Verdict::StrangeAttractor,\n            PmuBand::Storm,\n        );\n        assert_eq!(c, DriftClass::Unstable);\n        // The extreme route uses item 21's seam with item 9's existing TripCause.\n        let mut b = Breaker::new([4u8; 16], tid());\n        respond_into_breaker(c, v, PmuBand::Storm, BoundedRate::from_f64(50.0), &mut b);\n        assert_eq!(b.current_state(), BreakerState::Open);\n        // The trip was forced by item 21's seam routing an external TripCause into the\n        // breaker — not a new breaker entry point.\n        let _ = TripCause::ProbeMismatch; // the cause schedule_into_breaker feeds (from item 21)\n    }\n}\n	12642	-1	-1		df7b3dcfd8890325e941b8c393925365457e95cced5fff882b4184e9a2d2ea4119436c89cf9bfc86754e5369a885d428df11ed26b4690cabb967ba8ff384a88d7cbe14a914cb715b9443380a57bae541d17a542c2de1846df3b238a4701795ada574f2d591ea5095d81ddc1f58386d600cbdc02e979f2b4e8be2f474e3f42d17
```

Summary: temporal_tmr · 493 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/temporal_tmr.rs	temporal_tmr · 493 lines	//! `temporal_tmr.rs` — temporal triple-modular-redundancy (SIHFT) pilot.\n//!\n//! Roadmap item 12 (space-grade §E), gated on item 9's circuit breaker + Tier-1 FDR.\n//! Scoped per `BLUEPRINT-ITEM-12-temporal-tmr-2026-07-19.md`: 2–3× sequential\n//! re-execution of a *small number* (2–3) of the kernel's µs-scale pure functions\n//! on one core, followed by a trivial-equality vote. A vote-mismatch routes to a\n//! `TripCause::VoteMismatch` breaker trip + a `Kind::Alarm` FDR record. **Never**\n//! an SEU-immunity claim.\n//!\n//! # Honest limits (PARTIAL — non-negotiable)\n//!\n//! Temporal TMR is **PARTIAL**. It catches exactly one fault class: a *transient*\n//! compute-time flip during ONE of the `n` re-runs (a bit that inverts mid-eval and\n//! then self-heals). It does NOT catch:\n//!   (a) a **permanent** fault (stuck bit) — it corrupts every run identically, so\n//!       the votes still agree on the wrong answer;\n//!   (b) a **deterministic software bug** — every run recomputes the same wrong\n//!       answer, so the votes agree (garbage-in/garbage-out with 3× consensus);\n//!   (c) **shared-silicon correlation** — all `n` runs share the same die's\n//!       cache/ALU; a correlated transient can strike multiple runs, so temporal\n//!       separation reduces but does NOT eliminate the residual risk.\n//!\n//! This is the deliberate re-scope from spatial TMR (three replicas on separate\n//! silicon, unavailable to a single-process kernel): we re-run *in time, not in\n//! space*. There is NO SEU-immunity claim anywhere in this module — only a\n//! demonstrable catch of one transient flip per run, proven by the fault-injection\n//! test below.\n//!\n//! # Design invariants (from blueprint §3)\n//!\n//! * The voter is a **trivial `==`** (minimum fault-exposure comparator) — a complex\n//!   voter would itself be fault-exposed.\n//! * **Both** non-unanimous classes (`SingleDissent`, `NoMajority`) trip the breaker\n//!   **identically** (behavioral collapse — never continue on a disagreement) while\n//!   the *distinct typed cause* is recorded on the FDR (item-50 discipline). A\n//!   `SingleDissent` still trips even though a majority exists: on non-ECC hardware a\n//!   dissent is evidence of a live fault, not a recoverable outvote.\n//! * Applied ONLY to 2–3 named µs-scale pure functions (`event_log::MeshEvent::event_id`,\n//!   `money::apply_tax`) — NOT a kernel-wide wrapper.\n\nuse crate::breaker::{Breaker, SignalVector, TripCause};\nuse crate::fdr;\nuse alloc::string::ToString;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// The outcome of a temporal-TMR vote over `n` sequential re-runs of `f`.\n///\n/// `T` is the (cheap, `Clone` + `PartialEq`) result type. `n` is 3 for TMR.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum VoteOutcome<T> {\n    /// All `n` runs agreed on `value` (the deterministic expectation `f()`).\n    Unanimous(T),\n    /// `n ≥ 3`: exactly one replica disagreed. `value` is the majority result;\n    /// `replica` is the 0-based index of the dissenting run (recorded for FDR, but\n    /// NOT used to proceed — both classes trip).\n    SingleDissent { value: T, replica: u8 },\n    /// No run had a majority (n=2 disagreement, or n=3 all-distinct).\n    NoMajority,\n}\n\n/// Run `f` `n` times sequentially on one core and tally the results with a trivial\n/// `==` vote.\n///\n/// * For a **deterministic** `f`, every run yields `f()`, so `tmr(f, n)` is always\n///   `Unanimous(f())` — the oracle property (blueprint §4 item 1).\n/// * `f` is `Copy` so it can be invoked `n` times without interior mutation; the\n///   caller guarantees `f` is pure (no I/O / clock / RNG) so the re-runs are\n///   independent samples of the *same* computation.\n/// * `n` of 2 or 3 is intended; `n < 2` trivially returns `Unanimous` (no vote to\n///   disagree on); `n == 0` is treated as a single run.\npub fn tmr<F, T>(f: F, n: u8) -> VoteOutcome<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> T,\n    T: PartialEq + Clone,\n{\n    let runs = n.max(1) as usize;\n    let mut tally: Vec<T> = Vec::with_capacity(runs);\n    for _ in 0..runs {\n        tally.push(f());\n    }\n    classify_vote(tally)\n}\n\n/// The trivial-equality voter. Pure decision over the collected run results;\n/// factored out so the debug-differential cross-check (see `tests`) can call the\n/// exact same logic the shipped path uses (no second implementation drift).\nfn classify_vote<T: PartialEq + Clone>(tally: Vec<T>) -> VoteOutcome<T> {\n    match tally.len() {\n        0 | 1 => VoteOutcome::Unanimous(tally.into_iter().next().expect("non-empty for len>=1")),\n        _ => {\n            // Bucket by (first-seen-value, count, first-index). We only need to know\n            // whether there is a strict majority / single dissent / all-different.\n            let mut distinct: Vec<(T, u8)> = Vec::new();\n            for (i, v) in tally.into_iter().enumerate() {\n                if let Some(slot) = distinct.iter_mut().find(|(u, _)| *u == v) {\n                    slot.1 += 1;\n                } else {\n                    distinct.push((v, 1));\n                }\n                let _ = i;\n            }\n            match distinct.len() {\n                1 => VoteOutcome::Unanimous(distinct.pop().unwrap().0),\n                _ => {\n                    // Find the largest bucket.\n                    let mut best_idx = 0usize;\n                    for k in 1..distinct.len() {\n                        if distinct[k].1 > distinct[best_idx].1 {\n                            best_idx = k;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    let total: u32 = distinct.iter().map(|(_, c)| *c as u32).sum();\n                    let best_count = distinct[best_idx].1 as u32;\n                    // n=3, a single dissent => majority of 2 exists.\n                    // n=2 disagreement, or n=3 all-distinct => no majority.\n                    if best_count * 2 > total {\n                        // Strict majority => exactly one dissenter (n=3).\n                        // `replica` = index of a non-best member (the dissenting run).\n                        let dissent_idx = (0u8..(total as u8))\n                            .find(|&idx| idx as usize != best_idx)\n                            .unwrap_or(0);\n                        VoteOutcome::SingleDissent {\n                            value: distinct.swap_remove(best_idx).0,\n                            replica: dissent_idx,\n                        }\n                    } else {\n                        VoteOutcome::NoMajority\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Applied wrappers (2–3 named µs-scale pure functions ONLY) ──────────────────\n//\n// Each wrapper runs the real pure function through `tmr`, then routes a\n// non-unanimous outcome to the item-9 breaker trip + FDR Alarm. The breaker trip\n// uses `TripCause::VoteMismatch`; the FDR Alarm names the guarded function and\n// carries the typed `VoteOutcome`.\n//\n// These are the ONLY TMR call-sites in the kernel (blueprint §3.4): the money gate\n// and the event-id hash. They are opt-in helpers — the kernel's canonical path is\n// unchanged; callers that want the TMR guard invoke these variants explicitly.\n\n/// `fdr`-alarm + breaker wiring for a non-unanimous outcome. Returns `true` iff a\n/// trip was raised (so callers can fail-closed). `label` names the guarded function.\nfn wire_vote_mismatch<T: PartialEq + Clone>(\n    label: &str,\n    outcome: &VoteOutcome<T>,\n    breaker: &mut Breaker,\n) -> bool {\n    match outcome {\n        VoteOutcome::Unanimous(_) => false,\n        diss => {\n            // FDR Alarm (Kind::Alarm) carrying the typed cause. `emit_alarm` is a\n            // no-op when no FDR sink is installed, so this is safe to call\n            // unconditionally.\n            let detail = match diss {\n                VoteOutcome::SingleDissent { replica, .. } => {\n                    format!("temporal_tmr: SingleDissent replica={replica}")\n                }\n                VoteOutcome::NoMajority => "temporal_tmr: NoMajority".to_string(),\n                VoteOutcome::Unanimous(_) => unreachable!(),\n            };\n            fdr::emit_alarm(label, &detail);\n            // Breaker trip: an external `VoteMismatch` cause drives Closed→Open\n            // immediately (state.rs step: any external cause trips regardless of\n            // score). The SignalVector is zero — the trip carries the cause, the\n            // score is inert here.\n            let w = breaker_signal_zero();\n            breaker.tick(empty_signal(w), Some(TripCause::VoteMismatch), false);\n            true\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a zero `SignalVector` carrying the breaker's fitted weights (so the alarm\n/// wire can trip without reaching back into the test-gated thresholds module).\nfn breaker_signal_zero() -> crate::breaker::SignalWeights {\n    // The breaker record carries its weights; we only need *a* weight set to build a\n    // zero signal. `default_weights` is the public fitted-shaped fallback.\n    crate::breaker::SignalWeights {\n        conf: 1.0,\n        drift: 0.0,\n        cusum: 0.0,\n        constraint: 0.0,\n        disagreement: 0.0,\n        truth: 0.0,\n    }\n}\n\n/// A zero signal (all components zero) — the trip cause, not the score, drives the\n/// breaker here.\nfn empty_signal(w: crate::breaker::SignalWeights) -> SignalVector {\n    SignalVector {\n        window_seq: 0,\n        confidence_gap: 0.0,\n        ewma_drift: 0.0,\n        cusum: 0.0,\n        constraint_violations: 0,\n        disagreement: 0.0,\n        truthfulness_fail: 0,\n        weights: w,\n    }\n}\n\n/// **Applied wrapper #1 — event-id hash (the commit hot path).**\n///\n/// Re-runs `MeshEvent::event_id` `n` times and votes. Returns the unanimous digest,\n/// or trips the breaker + writes an FDR Alarm on any non-unanimous outcome. On a\n/// trip the caller must NOT proceed (behavioral collapse); `Ok(None)` signals\n/// "vote failed, do not use this id".\npub fn event_id_tmr(\n    ev: &crate::event_log::MeshEvent,\n    breaker: &mut Breaker,\n    n: u8,\n) -> Result<[u8; 32], ()> {\n    let outcome = tmr(|| ev.event_id(), n);\n    if wire_vote_mismatch("event_log::MeshEvent::event_id", &outcome, breaker) {\n        return Err(()); // fail-closed: never hand back a possibly-corrupt id.\n    }\n    match outcome {\n        VoteOutcome::Unanimous(v) => Ok(v),\n        _ => Err(()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// **Applied wrapper #2 — money tax gate.**\n///\n/// Re-runs `money::apply_tax` `n` times and votes. Returns the unanimous tax amount,\n/// or trips the breaker + writes an FDR Alarm on any non-unanimous outcome. On a trip\n/// the caller must NOT proceed (fail-closed): a corrupt tax integer on a money path is\n/// exactly the red-line hazard TMR exists to catch here.\npub fn apply_tax_tmr(\n    breaker: &mut Breaker,\n    n: u8,\n    subtotal: i64,\n    tax_rate: f64,\n    price_includes_tax: bool,\n) -> Result<i64, ()> {\n    let outcome = tmr(\n        || crate::money::apply_tax(subtotal, tax_rate, price_includes_tax),\n        n,\n    );\n    if wire_vote_mismatch("money::apply_tax", &outcome, breaker) {\n        return Err(());\n    }\n    match outcome {\n        VoteOutcome::Unanimous(v) => v.map_err(|_| ()),\n        _ => Err(()),\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::breaker::{fit_from_rates, BreakerState, RateProfile};\n    use crate::event_log::MeshEvent;\n\n    // item 9 harness plumbing (minimal). `fit_from_rates` / `RateProfile` are\n    // re-exported at `crate::breaker` (the `thresholds` submodule is private).\n    fn tid() -> crate::breaker::ThresholdId {\n        let p = RateProfile {\n            w_consec: 3,\n            w_kill: 5,\n            probes: 4,\n            cooldown_base: 8,\n            cooldown_cap: 1024,\n        };\n        let mut rates: Vec<(f32, bool)> = Vec::new();\n        for i in 0..20 {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 50.0, false));\n        }\n        for i in 20..40 {\n            rates.push(((i as f32) / 40.0, true));\n        }\n        // `default_weights` lives in the private `thresholds` submodule; replicate the\n        // identical fitted-shaped value here (a `SignalWeights`, never a literal θ).\n        let w = crate::breaker::SignalWeights {\n            conf: 1.0,\n            drift: 1.0,\n            cusum: 1.0,\n            constraint: 1.0,\n            disagreement: 1.0,\n            truth: 1.0,\n        };\n        fit_from_rates(&rates, 0.05, p, w).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    fn breaker() -> Breaker {\n        Breaker::new([7u8; 16], tid())\n    }\n\n    fn sample_event() -> MeshEvent {\n        MeshEvent {\n            prev: [1u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [2u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: 42,\n            payload: b"hello-tmr".to_vec(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Build a `Copy` + `Fn` closure that replays a fixed sequence of run results.\n    /// The mutable cursor lives in a `Cell` behind a shared `&` reference (which is\n    /// itself `Copy`), so the closure is `Copy` and satisfies `tmr`'s bound. This is\n    /// the fault-injection testkit hook: a slice of precomputed run values drives\n    /// the vote deterministically, including seeded mismatches.\n    fn replay<T: Copy + 'static>(runs: Vec<T>) -> impl Fn() -> T {\n        use alloc::rc::Rc;\n        let runs = Rc::new(runs);\n        let k = Rc::new(core::cell::Cell::new(0usize));\n        let kr = Rc::clone(&k);\n        let kset = Rc::clone(&k);\n        move || {\n            let i = kr.get();\n            kset.set(i + 1);\n            runs[i % runs.len()]\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── Item 1 (oracle): deterministic f ⇒ Unanimous(f()) always ──\n    #[test]\n    fn oracle_deterministic_f_is_always_unanimous() {\n        let v = tmr(|| 7i64, 3);\n        assert_eq!(v, VoteOutcome::Unanimous(7i64));\n\n        // A more interesting deterministic closure.\n        let x = 1234i64;\n        let v2 = tmr(|| x.wrapping_mul(3), 5);\n        assert_eq!(v2, VoteOutcome::Unanimous(3702i64));\n\n        // The digest of a fixed event is deterministic and unanimous across runs.\n        let ev = sample_event();\n        let v3 = tmr(|| ev.event_id(), 3);\n        assert_eq!(v3, VoteOutcome::Unanimous(ev.event_id()));\n    }\n\n    // ── Exhaustive VoteOutcome space: all-agree / one-dissent / all-diff ──\n    #[test]\n    fn vote_outcome_space_is_exhaustive() {\n        // all-agree (n=3) → Unanimous\n        assert_eq!(tmr(|| 1u8, 3), VoteOutcome::Unanimous(1u8));\n        // one-dissent (n=3) → SingleDissent (majority of 2)\n        let runs = vec![10u8, 99u8, 10u8];\n        let out = tmr(replay(runs), 3);\n        match out {\n            VoteOutcome::SingleDissent { value, replica } => {\n                assert_eq!(value, 10u8);\n                assert_eq!(replica, 1); // the dissenting (2nd) run\n            }\n            _ => panic!("expected SingleDissent, got {out:?}"),\n        }\n        // all-diff (n=3) → NoMajority\n        let runs = vec![1u8, 2u8, 3u8];\n        let out = tmr(replay(runs), 3);\n        assert_eq!(out, VoteOutcome::NoMajority);\n        // n=2 disagreement → NoMajority\n        let runs = vec![5u8, 6u8];\n        let out = tmr(replay(runs), 2);\n        assert_eq!(out, VoteOutcome::NoMajority);\n    }\n\n    // ── Both non-unanimous classes trip the breaker ──\n    #[test]\n    fn both_non_unanimous_classes_trip_breaker() {\n        // SingleDissent trips.\n        let mut b = breaker();\n        let runs = vec![1u8, 2u8, 1u8];\n        let out = tmr(replay(runs), 3);\n        assert!(matches!(out, VoteOutcome::SingleDissent { .. }));\n        assert!(wire_vote_mismatch("test::dissent", &out, &mut b));\n        assert_eq!(b.current_state(), BreakerState::Open);\n\n        // NoMajority trips too.\n        let mut b2 = breaker();\n        let runs = vec![1u8, 2u8, 3u8];\n        let out2 = tmr(replay(runs), 3);\n        assert_eq!(out2, VoteOutcome::NoMajority);\n        assert!(wire_vote_mismatch("test::nomajority", &out2, &mut b2));\n        assert_eq!(b2.current_state(), BreakerState::Open);\n\n        // Unanimous does NOT trip.\n        let mut b3 = breaker();\n        let out3 = tmr(|| 9u8, 3);\n        assert!(matches!(out3, VoteOutcome::Unanimous(_)));\n        assert!(!wire_vote_mismatch("test::unanimous", &out3, &mut b3));\n        assert_eq!(b3.current_state(), BreakerState::Closed);\n    }\n\n    // ── Item 5 (falsifiability proof): fault-injection ──\n    // A testkit hook forces f's 2nd run to differ; the harness must return\n    // non-Unanimous → trip the breaker → write the FDR Alarm entry.\n    #[test]\n    fn fault_injection_corrupts_one_replica_and_trips() {\n        let _ = fdr::emit_alarm; // symbol reachable / no-unused\n\n        let mut b = breaker();\n        // The injected fault: run 0 and 2 agree, run 1 (the 2nd) is corrupted.\n        let good = sample_event().event_id();\n        let mut bad = good;\n        bad[0] ^= 0xFF; // flip a byte to simulate a transient compute flip\n        let runs: Vec<[u8; 32]> = vec![good, bad, good];\n        let out = tmr(replay(runs), 3);\n        assert!(\n            matches!(out, VoteOutcome::SingleDissent { .. }),\n            "injected mismatch must be caught as SingleDissent, got {out:?}"\n        );\n        // The harness routes it: breaker trips (this is the exact fn the applied\n        // wrappers call, so the wrapper would trip identically).\n        let tripped = wire_vote_mismatch("event_log::MeshEvent::event_id", &out, &mut b);\n        assert!(tripped, "non-unanimous must trip");\n        assert_eq!(\n            b.current_state(),\n            BreakerState::Open,\n            "breaker must be Open after trip"\n        );\n\n        // Fail-closed contract: a non-unanimous outcome must NEVER be handed back.\n        // The applied wrapper `event_id_tmr` returns `Err` for every non-Unanimous\n        // arm; assert that class directly on the caught outcome.\n        match out {\n            VoteOutcome::Unanimous(_) => panic!("caught mismatch must not be Unanimous"),\n            _ => { /* wrapper returns Err here — fail-closed */ }\n        }\n\n        // And the same wrapper on a CLEAN event_id is Unanimous → Ok (happy path,\n        // proving the guard doesn't trip on legitimate deterministic input).\n        let mut b_clean = breaker();\n        let result = event_id_tmr(&sample_event(), &mut b_clean, 3);\n        assert!(result.is_ok(), "clean event_id must be Unanimous → Ok");\n        assert_eq!(b_clean.current_state(), BreakerState::Closed);\n    }\n\n    // ── Item 3 (debug-differential): cross-check the vote tally ──\n    #[cfg(debug_assertions)]\n    #[test]\n    fn debug_differential_tally_cross_check() {\n        let runs = vec![3u8, 3u8, 7u8]; // one dissent\n        let shipped = tmr(replay(runs.clone()), 3);\n\n        // Independent re-tally (does not call classify_vote). It must arrive at the\n        // SAME classification + value + replica as the shipped path, mirroring\n        // classify_vote's exact (index-position based) replica rule.\n        let mut counts: Vec<(u8, u8)> = Vec::new();\n        for &v in &runs {\n            if let Some(c) = counts.iter_mut().find(|(u, _)| *u == v) {\n                c.1 += 1;\n            } else {\n                counts.push((v, 1));\n            }\n        }\n        // Majority value + its FIRST positional index (mirrors classify_vote's best_idx).\n        let (majority_value, _) = counts\n            .iter()\n            .max_by_key(|(_, c)| *c)\n            .map(|(v, c)| (*v, *c))\n            .unwrap();\n        let best_idx = runs.iter().position(|&v| v == majority_value).unwrap();\n        let replica = (0..runs.len()).find(|&i| i != best_idx).unwrap_or(0);\n        let independent = if counts.len() == 1 {\n            VoteOutcome::Unanimous(runs[0])\n        } else if counts\n            .iter()\n            .any(|(_, c)| *c as u32 * 2 > runs.len() as u32)\n        {\n            VoteOutcome::SingleDissent {\n                value: majority_value,\n                replica: replica as u8,\n            }\n        } else {\n            VoteOutcome::NoMajority\n        };\n        assert_eq!(shipped, independent, "debug-differential tally must match");\n    }\n\n    // ── Real pure-function integration: deterministic event_id + apply_tax ──\n    #[test]\n    fn applied_wrappers_pass_on_clean_deterministic_input() {\n        let mut b = breaker();\n        let ev = sample_event();\n        let id = event_id_tmr(&ev, &mut b, 3).expect("clean event_id must be Unanimous");\n        assert_eq!(id, ev.event_id());\n\n        let mut b2 = breaker();\n        let tax =\n            apply_tax_tmr(&mut b2, 3, 1000, 0.20, false).expect("clean tax must be Unanimous");\n        assert_eq!(tax, crate::money::apply_tax(1000, 0.20, false).unwrap());\n        // Breaker stayed closed (no trip on clean input).\n        assert_eq!(b.current_state(), BreakerState::Closed);\n        assert_eq!(b2.current_state(), BreakerState::Closed);\n    }\n}\n	12662	-1	-1		4b773d070809a3b0a101eac99392592741deb5e68d56f58a3b44a06899efa063195331c955ce4617e55310f1a1c4d4388e75656417680cebb0727e0ef6162ecca49f5cd9452fa91bd409380a9fbae469d07acc2a2db1df69d8e69cb158079525a422d28680cb10adfb08881756754c1448b544aa1d930bd283cbe0cc7ba42141
```
