candidates.truncate(top_k);\n        candidates.iter().map(|&(i, s)| (i, s, self.labels[i].clone())).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// O(1) доступ: cell → список.\n    pub fn cell(&self, addr: usize) -> &Vec<usize> { &self.lattice[addr.min(65535)] }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let occupied = self.lattice.iter().filter(|c| !c.is_empty()).count();\n        format!("NdCrystalLattice ({}D)\\n  Entries: {}\\n  Occupied cells: {}/65536\\n  Density: {:.2}%",\n            self.dims, self.signatures.len(), occupied, 100.0 * occupied as f64 / 65536.0)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── n-Dimensional MoE (n-Mixture of Experts) ───────────────────────────\n// Кожен експерт = n-вимірне вкладення через кристалічну гратку.\n// Communication: всі N експертів обмінюються через гратку.\n\n/// n-вимірний експерт з кристалічним вкладенням.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct NdExpert {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub embedding: Vec<f64>,  // n-вимірне вкладення\n    pub signature: NdSignature,\n    pub weight_matrix: Matrix,\n    pub bias: Vec<f64>,\n    pub usage: u64,\n}\n\nimpl NdExpert {\n    pub fn new(name: &str, n_dims: usize, input_dim: usize, output_dim: usize) -> Self {\n        let mut embedding = vec![0.0; n_dims];\n        for i in 0..n_dims { embedding[i] = crate::math::sin((i as f64 * 1.618)) * 10.0; }\n        let embed_bytes: Vec<u8> = embedding.iter().map(|&v| (v as i8) as u8).collect();\n        let signature = NdSignature::from_data(&embed_bytes, n_dims.min(8));\n        NdExpert {\n            name: name.to_string(), embedding, signature,\n            weight_matrix: Matrix::new(output_dim, input_dim),\n            bias: vec![0.0; output_dim],\n            usage: 0,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// n-MoE: N експертів з кристалічною маршрутизацією.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct NdMoE {\n    pub experts: Vec<NdExpert>,\n    pub lattice: NdCrystalLattice,\n    pub n_dims: usize,\n    pub top_k: usize,\n}\n\nimpl NdMoE {\n    pub fn new(n_experts: usize, top_k: usize, n_dims: usize, input_dim: usize, output_dim: usize) -> Self {\n        let mut experts = Vec::new();\n        let mut lattice = NdCrystalLattice::new(n_dims.min(8));\n        for i in 0..n_experts {\n            let exp = NdExpert::new(&format!("exp_{}", i), n_dims, input_dim, output_dim);\n            let embed_bytes: Vec<u8> = exp.embedding.iter().map(|&v| (v as i8) as u8).collect();\n            lattice.insert(&embed_bytes, &exp.name);\n            experts.push(exp);\n        }\n        NdMoE { experts, lattice, n_dims, top_k }\n    }\n\n    /// Маршрутизація через кристалічну гратку: O(1) пошук найближчих експертів.\n    pub fn route(&self, input: &[f64]) -> Vec<usize> {\n        let query_bytes: Vec<u8> = input.iter().map(|&v| (v * 10.0) as i8 as u8).collect();\n        let results = self.lattice.search(&query_bytes, self.top_k);\n        results.iter().map(|(idx, _, _)| *idx).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Forward: топ-k експертів через гратку.\n    pub fn forward(&mut self, input: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64> {\n        let indices = self.route(input);\n        let mut output = vec![0.0; self.experts.first().map(|e| e.weight_matrix.rows).unwrap_or(0)];\n        for &idx in &indices {\n            if idx < self.experts.len() {\n                let out = self.experts[idx].weight_matrix.apply(input);\n                for j in 0..output.len().min(out.len()) { output[j] += out[j]; }\n                self.experts[idx].usage += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        if !indices.is_empty() {\n            let s = indices.len() as f64;\n            for j in 0..output.len() { output[j] /= s; }\n        }\n        output\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let total: usize = self.experts.iter().map(|e| e.weight_matrix.rows * e.weight_matrix.cols).sum();\n        let active = self.top_k * self.experts.first().map(|e| e.weight_matrix.rows * e.weight_matrix.cols).unwrap_or(0);\n        format!("NdMoE ({}D, {} experts, top-{})\\n  Crystal routing: O(1)\\n  Total params: {}\\n  Active/token: {} ({:.1}%)",\n            self.n_dims, self.experts.len(), self.top_k, total, active,\n            if total > 0 { 100.0 * active as f64 / total as f64 } else { 0.0 })\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Crystal Memory: жива пам'ять через кристалічну гратку ──────────────\n// Аналогічно Academia: n-вимірна гратка + O(1) пошук.\n// Заміна TopoChronoMemory на кристалічну версію.\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct CrystalMemory {\n    pub lattice: NdCrystalLattice,\n    pub dims: usize,\n    pub raw_data: Vec<Vec<f64>>,\n    pub weights: Vec<f64>,\n    pub timestamps: Vec<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl CrystalMemory {\n    pub fn new(dims: usize) -> Self {\n        CrystalMemory {\n            lattice: NdCrystalLattice::new(dims.min(8)),\n            dims, raw_data: Vec::new(), weights: Vec::new(), timestamps: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Записати спогад.\n    pub fn record(&mut self, label: &str, data: &[f64], weight: f64, now: u64) {\n        let bytes: Vec<u8> = data.iter().map(|&v| (v as i8) as u8).collect();\n        self.lattice.insert(&bytes, label);\n        self.raw_data.push(data.to_vec());\n        self.weights.push(weight);\n        self.timestamps.push(now);\n    }\n\n    /// Пошук через кристалічну гратку O(1).\n    pub fn retrieve(&self, query: &[f64], k: usize) -> Vec<(String, f64)> {\n        let qbytes: Vec<u8> = query.iter().map(|&v| (v as i8) as u8).collect();\n        let results = self.lattice.search(&qbytes, k);\n        results.iter().map(|(idx, score, label)| (label.clone(), *score as f64)).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Еволюція: забывання.\n    pub fn evolve(&mut self, decay: f64) {\n        for w in &mut self.weights { *w *= (1.0 - decay).max(0.0); if *w < 0.01 { *w = 0.01; } }\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        format!("Crystal Memory ({}D lattice)\\n  {}\\n  Records: {}", self.dims, self.lattice.dashboard(), self.raw_data.len())\n    }\n}\n	13590	-1	-1		a3f7f66c98cfa7e5a98bf3cbfb025b3b69de8785adfbe7e0a15fe6d883ecfde31dc4b6207dce843eea52562d90e17224dced7ba43c280aaae2caf6836f2ca844088551e9ef38b9751387b013f70b8ae2d970cc6e6192af65d4280a86390db134a0b6f2b534cb1179d9b88e842adc2d9b64f54d729f82fc8446f1edf229b1a5b0

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/memory_search.rs	memory_search · 864 lines	//! `kernel::memory_search` — unified memory search engine (indexed vector + spectral navigation).\n//!\n//! Composes the existing retrieval primitives into a single API for searching\n//! structured documents (like MEMORY.md) by section:\n//!   - **Indexed vector**: BM25 lexical scoring + TrigramIndex candidate narrowing\n//!   - **Spectral navigation**: CSR graph + PPR for "what relates to X" diffusion\n//!   - **Fusion**: weighted combination of lexical + spectral signals\n//!\n//! Replaces all `grep -rn "pattern" docs/` / `grep -F` / `awk` extraction\n//! with a single kernel-native call. Zero new deps, pure `std`.\n//!\n//! # Architecture\n//! ```text\n//! MemorySearchEngine\n//! +-- Lexical Layer\n//! |   +-- BM25 (retrieval/bm25.rs) -- Okapi scoring\n//! |   +-- TrigramIndex (retrieval/index.rs) -- candidate narrowing\n//! +-- Spectral Layer\n//! |   +-- CSR graph (csr.rs) -- section adjacency\n//! |   +-- PPR (retrieval/ppr.rs) -- personalized PageRank navigation\n//! +-- Fusion\n//!     +-- score = w_bm25 * bm25_norm + w_ppr * ppr_norm + w_tri * tri_norm\n//! ```\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse crate::retrieval::bm25::{self, Bm25, Document};\nuse crate::retrieval::index::TrigramIndex;\nuse crate::retrieval::ppr::Ppr;\n\n/// Weight for BM25 lexical signal in fusion.\npub const W_BM25: f64 = 0.5;\n/// Weight for PPR spectral signal in fusion.\npub const W_PPR: f64 = 0.3;\n/// Weight for trigram exact-match signal in fusion.\npub const W_TRIGRAM: f64 = 0.2;\n\n/// PPR teleport probability.\npub const PPR_ALPHA: f64 = 0.15;\n/// PPR fixed iteration count.\npub const PPR_K: usize = 20;\n\n/// A section parsed from a Markdown document.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct Section {\n    /// 0-based section index (order of appearance).\n    pub id: usize,\n    /// Section header text (without `## ` prefix).\n    pub header: String,\n    /// Full section text (header + body).\n    pub text: String,\n}\n\n/// A search hit from the memory engine.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct SearchResult {\n    /// Section index in the corpus.\n    pub section_id: usize,\n    /// Section header.\n    pub header: String,\n    /// Fused relevance score (0.0–1.0 range, higher = more relevant).\n    pub score: f64,\n    /// BM25 lexical score component.\n    pub bm25_score: f64,\n    /// PPR spectral score component.\n    pub ppr_score: f64,\n    /// Trigram exact-match score component.\n    pub trigram_score: f64,\n}\n\n/// The unified memory search engine.\n///\n/// Constructed from a Markdown document (split into `##` sections), then\n/// queried with natural-language or keyword queries. The engine fuses three\n/// signals — BM25 lexical scoring, trigram exact narrowing, and PPR spectral\n/// navigation — into a single ranked result list.\npub struct MemorySearchEngine {\n    /// Parsed sections from the document.\n    sections: Vec<Section>,\n    /// BM25 lexical index over section texts.\n    bm25: Bm25,\n    /// Trigram inverted index over section texts.\n    trigram: TrigramIndex,\n    /// Section adjacency CSR graph (built from term co-occurrence).\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    graph: crate::csr::Csr,\n    /// Row-stochastic transition matrix for PPR (derived from CSR).\n    transition: Vec<Vec<f64>>,\n}\n\nimpl MemorySearchEngine {\n    /// Build the engine from a Markdown document string.\n    ///\n    /// Splits on `## ` headers to define sections, builds BM25 + trigram indices,\n    /// constructs a term-overlap adjacency graph, and pre-computes the PPR\n    /// transition matrix.\n    pub fn new(document: &str) -> Self {\n        let sections = Self::split_sections(document);\n        let _n = sections.len();\n\n        // Build BM25 index over section texts\n        let docs: Vec<Document> = sections\n            .iter()\n            .map(|s| Document::from_text(&s.text))\n            .collect();\n        let bm25 = Bm25::new(docs);\n\n        // Build trigram index over section texts\n        let doc_strs: Vec<&str> = sections.iter().map(|s| s.text.as_str()).collect();\n        let trigram = TrigramIndex::new(&doc_strs);\n\n        // Build section adjacency graph (sections sharing terms are connected)\n        let graph = Self::build_adjacency_graph(&sections);\n        let transition = Self::csr_to_transition(&graph);\n\n        MemorySearchEngine {\n            sections,\n            bm25,\n            trigram,\n            #[cfg(test)]\n            graph,\n            transition,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Search the memory for relevant sections. Returns results sorted by\n    /// fused score (descending). Empty query returns empty results.\n    pub fn search(&self, query: &str) -> Vec<SearchResult> {\n        if query.is_empty() {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n\n        let n = self.sections.len();\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n\n        // Layer 1: BM25 lexical scoring\n        let bm25_hits = self.bm25.rank_text(query);\n        let bm25_max = bm25_hits.first().map(|h| h.score).unwrap_or(0.0);\n\n        // Layer 2: Trigram exact-match candidates\n        let tri_candidates = self.trigram.query_literal(query);\n\n        // Layer 3: PPR spectral navigation from top BM25 hit as seed\n        let ppr_scores = if !bm25_hits.is_empty() {\n            let seed = bm25_hits[0].doc_id;\n            self.ppr_from_seed(seed)\n        } else {\n            vec![0.0; n]\n        };\n        let ppr_max = ppr_scores.iter().copied().fold(0.0f64, f64::max);\n\n        // Fusion: combine all three signals\n        let mut results: Vec<SearchResult> = (0..n)\n            .map(|i| {\n                let bm25_norm = if bm25_max > 0.0 {\n                    self.bm25_score(i, &bm25_hits) / bm25_max\n                } else {\n                    0.0\n                };\n                let ppr_norm = if ppr_max > 0.0 {\n                    ppr_scores[i] / ppr_max\n                } else {\n                    0.0\n                };\n                let tri_norm = if tri_candidates.contains(&(i as u32)) {\n                    1.0\n                } else {\n                    0.0\n                };\n\n                let fused = W_BM25 * bm25_norm + W_PPR * ppr_norm + W_TRIGRAM * tri_norm;\n\n                SearchResult {\n                    section_id: i,\n                    header: self.sections[i].header.clone(),\n                    score: fused,\n                    bm25_score: bm25_norm,\n                    ppr_score: ppr_norm,\n                    trigram_score: tri_norm,\n                }\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        results.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            b.score\n                .partial_cmp(&a.score)\n                .unwrap_or(core::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n                .then(a.section_id.cmp(&b.section_id))\n        });\n        results\n    }\n\n    /// Top-k search results.\n    pub fn search_top_k(&self, query: &str, k: usize) -> Vec<SearchResult> {\n        let mut r = self.search(query);\n        r.truncate(k);\n        r\n    }\n\n    /// PPR spectral navigation from a seed section.\n    /// Returns PPR scores for all sections.\n    fn ppr_from_seed(&self, seed: usize) -> Vec<f64> {\n        let ppr = Ppr::new(self.transition.clone());\n        ppr.rank(seed, PPR_ALPHA, PPR_K)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the number of sections in the corpus.\n    pub fn section_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.sections.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Get a section by index.\n    pub fn section(&self, id: usize) -> Option<&Section> {\n        self.sections.get(id)\n    }\n\n    // ── Internal helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Split a Markdown document into sections by `## ` headers.\n    fn split_sections(document: &str) -> Vec<Section> {\n        let mut sections = Vec::new();\n        let mut current_header = String::new();\n        let mut current_body = String::new();\n        let mut id = 0;\n\n        for line in document.lines() {\n            if let Some(header) = line.strip_prefix("## ") {\n                // Save previous section (if any)\n                if !current_header.is_empty() || !current_body.is_empty() {\n                    let mut text = current_header.clone();\n                    if !current_body.is_empty() {\n                        text.push('\\n');\n                        text.push_str(&current_body);\n                    }\n                    sections.push(Section {\n                        id,\n                        header: current_header.clone(),\n                        text,\n                    });\n                    id += 1;\n                }\n                current_header = header.trim().to_string();\n                current_body.clear();\n            } else if !current_header.is_empty() {\n                if !current_body.is_empty() {\n                    current_body.push('\\n');\n                }\n                current_body.push_str(line);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Push final section\n        if !current_header.is_empty() {\n            let mut text = current_header.clone();\n            if !current_body.is_empty() {\n                text.push('\\n');\n                text.push_str(&current_body);\n            }\n            sections.push(Section {\n                id,\n                header: current_header,\n                text,\n            });\n        }\n\n        sections\n    }\n\n    /// Build a CSR adjacency graph connecting sections that share terms.\n    /// Two sections are connected if they share at least one significant term\n    /// (length >= 3, not a stop word). Edge weight = number of shared terms.\n    fn build_adjacency_graph(sections: &[Section]) -> crate::csr::Csr {\n        let n = sections.len();\n        if n == 0 {\n            return crate::csr::Csr {\n                row_ptr: vec![0],\n                col_idx: Vec::new(),\n                val: Vec::new(),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Tokenize each section and collect significant terms (len >= 3)\n        let section_terms: Vec<Vec<String>> = sections\n            .iter()\n            .map(|s| {\n                bm25::tokenize(&s.text)\n                    .into_iter()\n alloc::collections::BTreeMap<String, Vec<u32>> =\n            alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n        for (sid, terms) in section_terms.iter().enumerate() {\n            let mut seen = alloc::collections::BTreeSet::new();\n            for t in terms {\n                if seen.insert(t.clone()) {\n                    term_index\n                        .entry(t.clone())\n                        .or_default()\n                        .push(sid as u32);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Compute shared-term counts for each pair\n        let mut edge_counts: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<(u32, u32), u32> =\n            alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n        for sids in term_index.values() {\n            for i in 0..sids.len() {\n                for                    };\n                    *edge_counts.entry(key).or_insert(0) += 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Convert to edges (undirected: both directions)\n self.weights.push(weight);\n        self.timestamps.push(now);\n    }\n\n    /// Інтерполяція поверхні: обчислити точку S(u,v).\n    pub fn evaluate(&self, u: f64, v: f64, dims: usize) -> Vec<f64> {\n        let n = self.control_points.len();\n        if n == 0 { return vec![0.0; dims]; }\n        let mut result = vec![0.0; dims];\n        let mut total_weight = 0.0;\n        // Зважена сума найближчих точок (гаусове ядро)\n        for i in 0..n {\n            let du = u - self.u_coords[i];\n            let dv = v - self.v_coords[i];\n            let dist2 = du * du + dv * dv;\n            if dist2 > 100.0 { continue; }\n            let w = self.weights[i] * crate::math::exp(-dist2 * 0.5);\n            total_weight += w;\n            for j in 0..dims.min(self.control_points[i].len()) точки до (u1,v1) та (u2,v2)\n        let mut dist = 0.0;\n        let mut prev_u = u1;\n        let mut prev_v = v1;\n        for _ in 0..3 { // 3 сегменти апроксимації геодезичної\n            let gaussian_curvature(&self, u: f64, v: f64, eps: f64) -> f64 {\n        let d = self.control_points[0].len();\n        let suu = self.evaluate(u + eps, v, d);\n        let su = self.evaluate(u - eps, v, d);\n        let sv = self.evaluate(u, v - eps, d);\n        let svv = self.evaluate(u, v + eps, d);\n        let s = self.evaluate(u, v, d);\n        let du: Vec<f64> = su.iter().zip(&s).map(|(a, b)| a - b).collect();\n        let dv: Vec<f64> = sv.iter().zip(&s).map(|(a, b)| a - b).collect();\n        let duu: Vec<f64> = suu.iter().zip(&su).map(|(a, b)| a - b).collect();\n        let dvv: Vec<f64> = svv.iter().zip(&sv).map(|(a, b)| a - b).collect();\n        let e_f64: f64 = du.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum();\n        let e = crate::math::sqrt(e_f64);\n        let f_f64: f64 = lattice: Academia,\n}\n\nimpl SelfHeal {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SelfHeal {\n            gaps_found: 0,\n            gaps_fixed: 0,\n            corrections: Vec::with_capacity(64),\n pub fn scan(entries: &[PromptEntry]) -> Vec<String> {\n        let mut gaps = Vec::new();\n\n        for (i, entry) in entries.iter().enumerate() {\n            if entry.prompt_text.trim().is_empty() {\n                gaps.push(format!("entry[{}] ({:?}): empty prompt_text", i, entry.title));\n            }\n            if entry.trigger_keywords.is_empty() {\n                gaps.push(format!("entry[{}] ({:?}): no triggers", i, entry.title));\n            }\n            if entry.source.is_empty() {\n                gaps.push(format!("entry[{}] ({:?}): empty source", i, entry.title));\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut kind_counts: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<PromptKind, usize> =\n            alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n        for entry in entries {\n            *kind_counts.entry(entry.kind).or_insert(0) += 1;\n        }\n\n        for &kind in ALL_KINDS {\n            let count = kind_counts.get(&kind).copied().unwrap_or(0);\n            if count < MIN_KIND_ENTRIES {\n                gaps.push(format!(\n                    "kind {:?}: {} entries (min {})",\n                    kind, count, MIN_KIND_ENTRIES\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n\n        gaps\n    }\n\n    /// Auto-enrich triggerless entries using description text.\n    /// Extracts significant lowercase words (len>=3, not a stop word)\n    /// and adds Up to 12 extracted keywords\n    /// per entry.\n    pub fn enrich_triggers(entry: &mut PromptEntry) {\n        if !entry.trigger_keywords.is_empty() {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        let text = entry.prompt_text.to_lowercase();\n        let mut extracted: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let mut seen = alloc::collections::BTreeSet::new();\n\n        for word in text.split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric()) {\n            let w = word.trim();\n            if w.len() < 3 || STOP_WORDS.contains(&w) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if seen.insert(w.to_string()) {\n                extracted.push(w.to_string());\n                if extracted.len() >= 12 {\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if !extracted.is_empty() {\n            entry.trigger_keywords = extracted;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Fill missing kinds with synthetic entries from nearest neighbors\n    /// in the crystal lattice. Returns newly created entries.\n    pub fn fill_kind_gap(\n        entries: &mut Vec<PromptEntry>,\n        missing_kind: PromptKind,\n        _lattice: &Academia,\n    ) -> Vec<PromptEntry> {\n        let mut synthetic = Vec::new();\n\n        let kind_samples: Vec<&PromptEntry> =\n            entries.iter().filter(|e| e.kind == missing_kind).collect();\n\n        if kind_samples.len() >=  PromptKind::Skill => &[\n                "define a reusable skill for code review",\n                "create a skill specification for threat modeling",\n                "load the skill definition       );\n            synthetic.push(entry);\n        }\n\n        synthetic\n    }\n\n    /// Full healing cycle: detect, enrich, fill, report.\n    pub fn heal(&mut self, entries: &mut 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/blocklist.rs	blocklist · 505 lines	//! BLUEPRINT-P74 (M2 / M3 / M4) — signed, subscribable ABUSE blocklist.\n//!\n//! A hub operator *may* publish a cryptographically-signed list of known-abusive\n//! actor identities, and another operator *may* subscribe. Named "abuse", never\n//! "reputation" or "quality". Opt-in and hub-controlled; never a mandatory\n//! central ban list. It is **advisory**: it surfaces a signal to the operator,\n//! who makes a manual pool-membership decision (§16.3 — the venue owns its\n//! courier pool). It never auto-filters and never re-ranks.\n//!\n//! The signed artifact reuses the **default-built** `capability_cert::HybridSig`\n//! (Ed25519 ⊕ ML-DSA-65, RequireBoth AND-verify) — the same hybrid signer P59\n//! rides. The blueprint text referenced `crate::pq::hybrid::HybridSig`, which\n//! does not exist (`pq/hybrid.rs` is a KEM, not a signature); the real hybrid\n//! *signature* seam is `capability_cert`. Using it (instead of gating this\n//! module behind the `pq` feature) means M2 is exercised by `cargo test --lib`\n//! under DEFAULT features — strictly better for the acceptance gate, and\n//! consistent with "matching the signer" (the signer is itself default-built).\n//!\n//! # Honest limits (stated, not dressed as a solution)\n//!\n//! This is a *starting point* for abuse-signal sharing, not a solved\n//! trust-and-safety system. There is no consensus on who is abusive, no\n//! dispute/appeal flow, and the well-documented echo-chamber failure mode of\n//! shared blocklists applies in full. It shares *what an operator asserts*,\n//! signed, and nothing more.\n//!\n//! # No-scoring guarantee (the point of P74)\n//!\n//! `BlockedActor` carries an identity and a reason — NEVER a score, count, rank,\n//! or weight. The field-level NO-COURIER-SCORING CI guard auto-covers this type\n//! (no score-ish field name can be added). `SubscriptionTrust` has exactly ONE\n//! variant (`Advisory`); an `Enforcing`/`Ranking` variant is intentionally\n//! absent, so an auto-enforcing or ranking blocklist is *unrepresentable* — the\n//! §16.26/§16.59 red line becomes a hard boundary, not a code-review\n//! discipline. Nothing in the dispatch/matching path may call `is_flagged` (M4).\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::capability_cert::{AlgSuite, HybridSig};\nuse crate::moderation::ReportReason;\nuse crate::ports::agent::cap::SignatureVerifier;\nuse core::fmt;\n\n/// Scaling axis: entry count K. Whole-list re-sign + re-fetch is O(K); beyond\n/// this bound a Merkle-delta sync would win — named future, NOT built (§5.4).\npub const MAX_BLOCKLIST_ENTRIES: usize = 10_000;\n\n/// Domain-separated, prefix-tagged canonical namespace for a blocklist. The\n/// signature binds over these exact bytes (incl. entry order), so a reordered or\n/// truncated entry vector fails verification (M2 forgery teeth).\npub const DOMAIN_BLOCKLIST: &[u8] = b"dowiz.blocklist\\x01";\n\n/// One blocklist entry. Carries an identity and a reason — NEVER a score, count,\n/// rank, or weight (the field-level NO-COURIER-SCORING CI guard, §0, auto-covers\n/// this type: no score-ish field name can be added).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct BlockedActor {\n    pub actor: [u8; 32], // pubkey\n    pub reason: ReportReason,\n    pub evidence: Option<[u8; 32]>, // content-id of a supporting report event (optional)\n}\n\n/// A publisher's signed abuse list at a given epoch. Epoch replacement is the\n/// only mutation (revoke = publish a new epoch omitting the entry).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct AbuseBlocklist {\n    pub publisher: [u8; 32],\n    pub epoch: u64,\n    pub entries: Vec<BlockedActor>, // len <= MAX_BLOCKLIST_ENTRIES\n}\n\n/// Construction refusal — the only error a blocklist can hit (over-capacity).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum BlocklistRejected {\n    /// `entries.len()` exceeded `MAX_BLOCKLIST_ENTRIES`.\n    TooManyEntries(usize),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for BlocklistRejected {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::TooManyEntries(n) => {\n                write!(f, "blocklist has {n} entries > MAX_BLOCKLIST_ENTRIES")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl AbuseBlocklist {\n    /// Construct, refusing a list over `MAX_BLOCKLIST_ENTRIES` (the scaling\n    /// break point; beyond it a Merkle-delta sync is the named future).\n    pub fn new(\n        publisher: [u8; 32],\n        epoch: u64,\n        entries: Vec<BlockedActor>,\n    ) -> Result<Self, BlocklistRejected> {\n        if entries.len() > MAX_BLOCKLIST_ENTRIES {\n            return Err(BlocklistRejected::TooManyEntries(entries.len()));\n        }\n        Ok(Self {\n            publisher,\n            epoch,\n            entries,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Canonical, domain-separated, ORDER-SIGNIFICANT encoding. Verification\n    /// re-encodes canonically and AND-checks both signature halves over these\n    /// bytes, so a reordered entry vector (different bytes) or a truncated entry\n    /// list (different bytes) cannot verify against the original signature.\n    pub fn canonical_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        out.extend_from_slice(DOMAIN_BLOCKLIST);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&self.publisher);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&self.epoch.to_le_bytes());\n        out.extend_from_slice(&(self.entries.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        for e in &self.entries {\n            out.extend_from_slice(&e.actor);\n            out.push(e.reason as u8);\n            match &e.evidence {\n                Some(h) => {\n                    out.push(1);\n                    out.extend_from_slice(h);\n                }\n                None => {\n                    out.push(0);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n/// The wire artifact: a canonically-encoded list + a hybrid signature over that\n/// canonical encoding. Verification AND-checks both hybrid halves (B4 lesson) and\n/// re-encodes canonically to defeat reorder/truncation forgery.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct SignedBlocklist {\n    pub list: AbuseBlocklist,\n    pub sig: HybridSig,\n}\n\nimpl SignedBlocklist {\n    /// Sign a list with the RequireBoth hybrid signer. `verifier` is any\n    /// `SignatureVerifier` (production injects real Ed25519 ⊕ ML-DSA-65; tests\n    /// use `RefSigner`). The signature binds the canonical bytes, so any later\n    /// mutation of the list invalidates it.\n    pub fn sign<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n        list: AbuseBlocklist,\n        verifier: &V,\n        classical_secret: &[u8; 32],\n        pq_secret: &[u8; 32],\n    ) -> Self {\n        let msg = list.canonical_bytes();\n        let sig = HybridSig::sign(\n            verifier,\n            AlgSuite::MlDsa65Ed25519,\n            classical_secret,\n            pq_secret,\n            &msg,\n        );\n        SignedBlocklist { list, sig }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify under RequireBoth. Returns `false` on ANY of: unknown suite,\n    /// classical-half failure, pq-half failure, or a list whose canonical bytes\n    /// no longer match the signed message (reorder/truncation forgery).\n    pub fn verify<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n        &self,\n        verifier: &V,\n        classical_pub: &[u8; 32],\n        pq_pub: &[u8],\n    ) -> bool {\n        let msg = self.list.canonical_bytes();\n        self.sig.verify(verifier, classical_pub, pq_pub, &msg)\n    }\n}\n\n/// How a subscriber treats a list. There is exactly ONE variant: a subscription\n/// is ADVISORY. `Enforcing`/`Ranking` variants are intentionally absent — an\n/// auto-enforcing or ranking blocklist is unrepresentable, which is how the\n/// §16.26/§16.59 red line becomes a hard boundary rather than a review\n/// discipline.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SubscriptionTrust {\n    Advisory,\n}\n\n/// Operator-facing advisory lookup. Returns the reason an actor was flagged on\n/// any *verified, subscribed* list, or `None`. It returns NO score, count, or\n/// ordering, and NOTHING in the dispatch/matching path may call it (enforced by\n/// M4's guard). The return type `Option<ReportReason>` is compile-level proof it\n/// cannot return a number.\npub fn is_flagged(subscribed: &[AbuseBlocklist], actor: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<ReportReason> {\n    for list in subscribed {\n        for e in &list.entries {\n            if e.actor == *actor {\n                return Some(e.reason);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// P74 (M2/M3) operator subscription surface — the kernel-local production caller\n/// that ties [`SignedBlocklist::sign`] (publisher side) and [`is_flagged`]\n/// (subscriber side) together. A subscribing operator holds a set of *verified*\n/// lists and asks advisory abuse questions over them.\n///\n/// A list is only admitted to the subscribed set after its RequireBoth hybrid\n/// signature verifies against the publisher's advertised keys ([`subscribe`]);\n/// a forged/reordered/truncated list is refused and never enters the set. Queries\n/// ([`flagged_reason`]) run [`is_flagged`] over ONLY the verified set — the return\n/// type `Option<ReportReason>` is compile-level proof this surface can never emit a\n/// score, count, or ranking (§16.26/§16.59). It is advisory-only: it surfaces a\n/// reason to the operator and takes no action.\n///\n/// [`subscribe`]: BlocklistSubscriptions::subscribe\n/// [`flagged_reason`]: BlocklistSubscriptions::flagged_reason\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct BlocklistSubscriptions {\n    /// Verified, advisory lists this operator subscribes to.\n    verified: Vec<AbuseBlocklist>,\n}\n\nimpl BlocklistSubscriptions {\n    /// A fresh, empty subscription set.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            verified: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The publisher side: an operator signs its own `AbuseBlocklist` for\n    /// distribution. Thin wrapper over [`SignedBlocklist::sign`] naming it as the\n    /// operator-facing publish action.\n    pub fn publish<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n        list: AbuseBlocklist,\n        verifier: &V,\n        classical_secret: &[u8; 32],\n        pq_secret: &[u8; 32],\n    ) -> SignedBlocklist {\n        SignedBlocklist::sign(list, verifier, classical_secret, pq_secret)\n    }\n\n    /// The subscriber side: admit a signed list into the subscribed set IFF its\n    /// hybrid signature verifies against the publisher's advertised keys. Returns\n    /// `true` if admitted, `false` if the signature (or canonical bytes) did not\n    /// verify — a forged/reordered/truncated list never enters the set.\n    pub fn subscribe<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n        &mut self,\n        signed: SignedBlocklist,\n        verifier: &V,\n        publisher_classical_pub: &[u8; 32],\n        publisher_pq_pub: &[u8],\n    ) -> bool {\n        if signed.verify(verifier, publisher_classical_pub, publisher_pq_pub) {\n            self.verified.push(signed.list);\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Advisory lookup over the verified subscribed set. Delegates to [`is_flagged`]\n    /// — returns the reason an actor was flagged on any subscribed, verified list,\n    /// or `None`. No score, count, or ordering (compile-level via the return type).\n    pub fn flagged_reason(&self, actor: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<ReportReason> {\n        is_flagged(&self.verified, actor)\n    }\n\n    /// Number of verified lists in the subscribed set (test/observability aid).\n    pub fn subscribed_len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.verified.len()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::moderation::ReportReason;\n    use crate::ports::agent::cap::RefSigner;\n\n    fn pubs_of(cls_sk: [u8; 32], pq_sk: [u8; 32]) -> ([u8; 32], Vec<u8>) {\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        (v.classical_public(&cls_sk), v.pq_public(&pq_sk))\n    }\n\n    fn sample_list(epoch: u64) -> AbuseBlocklist {\n        AbuseBlocklist::new(\n            [1u8; 32],\n            epoch,\n            vec![\n                BlockedActor {\n                    actor: [11u8; 32],\n                    reason: ReportReason::Fraud,\n                    evidence: Some([22u8; 32]),\n                },\n                BlockedActor {\n                    actor: [33u8; 32],\n                    reason: ReportReason::Harassment,\n                    evidence: None,\n                },\n            ],\n        )\n        .unwrap()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m2_sign_verify_roundtrip() {\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        let (cpk, ppk) = pubs_of([2u8; 32], [3u8; 32]);\n        let list = sample_list(1);\n        let signed = SignedBlocklist::sign(list, &v, &[2u8; 32], &[3u8; 32]);\n        assert!(\n            signed.verify(&v, &cpk, &ppk),\n            "valid signed blocklist verifies"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m2_reorder_entries_fails_verify() {\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        let (cpk, ppk) = pubs_of([2u8; 32], [3u8; 32]);\n        // Sign the list in its canonical order.\n        let orig = sample_list(1);\n        let signed = SignedBlocklist::sign(orig, &v, &[2u8; 32], &[3u8; 32]);\n        assert!(signed.verify(&v, &cpk, &ppk), "original list verifies");\n        // Adversarial: keep the ORIGINAL signature but reorder the entries. The\n        // canonical re-encode now differs → AND-verify must reject.\n        let mut forged = signed.clone();\n        forged.list.entries.reverse();\n        assert!(\n            !forged.verify(&v, &cpk, &ppk),\n            "reordered entries with a stale sig must fail"\n        );\n        // Sanity: re-signing the reordered list is a NEW valid list (proves the\n        // guard is about the stale sig, not the order itself).\n        let resigned = SignedBlocklist::sign(forged.list.clone(), &v, &[2u8; 32], &[3u8; 32]);\n        assert!(\n            resigned.verify(&v, &cpk, &ppk),\n            "reordered list re-signed is valid"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m2_truncated_entries_fails_verify() {\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        let (cpk, ppk) = pubs_of([2u8; 32], [3u8; 32]);\n        let orig = sample_list(1);\n        let signed = SignedBlocklist::sign(orig, &v, &[2u8; 32], &[3u8; 32]);\n        assert!(signed.verify(&v, &cpk, &ppk), "original list verifies");\n        // Adversarial: drop an entry but keep the stale sig → no silent short-accept.\n        let mut forged = signed.clone();\n        forged.list.entries.pop();\n        assert!(\n            !forged.verify(&v, &cpk, &ppk),\n            "truncated entry list must fail verify"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m2_single_half_forgery_rejected() {\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        let (cpk, ppk) = pubs_of([2u8; 32], [3u8; 32]);\n        // Tamper the classical half (valid-pq, junk-classical) → AND-verify rejects.\n        let mut a = SignedBlocklist::sign(sample_list(7), &v, &[2u8; 32], &[3u8; 32]);\n        if !a.sig.classical.is_empty() {\n            a.sig.classical[0] ^= 0xFF;\n        }\n        assert!(\n            !a.verify(&v, &cpk, &ppk),\n            "single-half (classical) forgery rejected"\n        );\n        // Tamper the pq half (valid-classical, junk-pq) → AND-verify rejects.\n        let mut b = SignedBlocklist::sign(sample_list(7), &v, &[2u8; 32], &[3u8; 32]);\n        if !b.sig.pq.is_empty() {\n            b.sig.pq[0] ^= 0xFF;\n        }\n        assert!(\n            !b.verify(&v, &cpk, &ppk),\n            "single-half (pq) forgery rejected"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m2_over_cap_rejected_at_construction() {\n        let entries = (0..(MAX_BLOCKLIST_ENTRIES + 1))\n            .map(|i| BlockedActor {\n                actor: [i as u8; 32],\n                reason: ReportReason::Spam,\n                evidence: None,\n            })\n            .collect();\n        let res = AbuseBlocklist::new([1u8; 32], 1, entries);\n        assert_eq!(\n            res,\n            Err(BlocklistRejected::TooManyEntries(MAX_BLOCKLIST_ENTRIES + 1))\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m2_is_flagged_returns_option_reason() {\n        let list = sample_list(1);\n        // The return type is Option<ReportReason> — compile-level proof it cannot\n        // return a number (no count/score).\n        let r: Option<ReportReason> = is_flagged(&[list.clone()], &[11u8; 32]);\n        assert_eq!(r3, None);\n        let r4: Option<ReportReason> = is_flagged(&[], &[0u8; 32]);\n        assert!(r4.is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m2_subscription_trust_is_advisory_only() {\n        // The only admissible subscription posture is Advisory; an Enforcing /\n        // Ranking variant is unrepresentable (compile-time red line).\n        let t = SubscriptionTrust::Advisory;\n        assert_eq!(t, SubscriptionTrust::Advisory);\n        // exhaustive match — adding any other variant is a compile error here.\n        match t {\n            SubscriptionTrust::Advisory => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── M3: legal-takedown boundary (contract + isolation invariant) ─────────────\n    //\n    // The takedown surface lives on the CLOSED `dowiz-infra` side (P67's split)\n    // and is specified here only as an INVARIANT the hub kernel enforces by having\n    // NO such API. dowiz has zero visibility into hub data by design (§16.14):\n    // its only cross-hub lever is §16.53 liveness/availability, never content.\n    #[test]\n    fn m3_kernel_exposes_no_cross_hub_content_api() {\n        // The hub kernel has NO function that deletes, edits, or reads another\n        // hub's content on external instruction. This is asserted structurally\n        // below: the `moderation`/`blocklist` modules expose only\n        // report-commit, blocklist sign/verify, and the advisory `is_flagged`\n        // query. None of them accept a *target hub* or a *content-delete*\n        // instruction. A "takedown into a hub" is therefore inexpressible.\n        //\n        // Self-check: the advisory query returns a membership signal, never a\n        // mutation. It cannot delete or edit anything.\n        let absent: Option<ReportReason> = is_flagged(&[], &[0u8; 32]);\n        assert!(\n            absent.is_none(),\n            "advisory query is read-only, never a mutation"\n        );\n        // The only list-mutation operation is epoch REPLACEMENT (re-publish a\n        // new signed epoch omitting the entry) — a publisher acting on THEIR OWN\n        // list, never a cross-hub content edit.\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        let (cpk, ppk) = pubs_of([2u8; 32], [3u8; 32]);\n        let original = sample_list(1);\n        let signed = SignedBlocklist::sign(original.clone(), &v, &[2u8; 32], &[3u8; 32]);\n        assert!(\n            signed.verify(&v, &cpk, &ppk),\n            "publisher-signed epoch verifies (self-owned list)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── M4: no moderation datum reaches HRW / discovery (the point of P74) ──────\n    //\n    // M4's load-bearing runtime test lives in `bebop2/proto-cap/src/matcher.rs`\n    // (T4): it asserts `assign(order, cands, max)` is byte-identical with vs\n    // without reports + a verified subscribed blocklist against a candidate — and\n    // passes today because `assign`'s signature CANNOT accept moderation state.\n    //\n    // This kernel-side test is the STRUCTURAL mirror that runs under `cargo\n    // test --lib` (no `bebop-repo` in this workspace): it proves the blocklist\n    // / report types carry NO score/rank/reputation field that could ever become a\n    // dispatch input, and that `is_flagged`'s return type (`Option<ReportReason>`)\n    // is a membership signal, never a number dispatch could sort on. The no-scoring\n    // field CI guard (ci-no-courier-scoring.sh) covers `bebop2/`; here we assert\n    // the kernel types are likewise field-clean by construction.\n    #[test]\n    fn m4_advisory_returns_no_score_type() {\n        // Compile-time truth: `is_flagged` yields `Option<ReportReason>` — a\n        // categorical reason or `None`, never `u64`/`f64`/count. If dispatch\n        // ever wired this in, it could only branch on an enum, never rank.\n        fn takes_option_reason(_: Option<ReportReason>) {}\n        takes_option_reason(is_flagged(&[], &[0u8; 32]));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn m4_blocked_actor_has_no_score_field() {\n        // `BlockedActor` carries identity + reason + optional evidence. No\n        // score/rank/weight/reputation field exists. Adding one is a field-name\n        // CI guard violation (§0). Asserted by constructing one with exactly the\n        // three defined fields and confirming the type has no other accessor shape.\n        let e = BlockedActor {\n            actor: [5u8; 32],\n            reason: ReportReason::Spam,\n            evidence: None,\n        };\n        // Destructure exhaustively: any added field breaks this pattern match,\n        // making a score field unshippable without a deliberate, greppable edit.\n        let BlockedActor {\n            actor: _,\n            reason: _,\n            evidence: _,\n        } = e;\n    }\n}\n	13755	-1	-1		dbeeb5b3eb4e21274121d0c195063a4f5db2bc25f160fcc9a95fda66d1d5cb41394934a056cb7a1e834e806b2f179fe99f315d24712a04e0b067fa0ecf0ce9cee6af06d125bf7229d689790295bae1d15159546a29ff536bcec2b2805a9fc5376e32f3561ecb50a4d00b981f7a01cab03cf24423148481ce0379b6ec892aaef0
```

## 13836 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/mesh.rs · LongTerm

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/mesh.rs	mesh · 1125 lines	//! P34 — cross-repo mesh kernel wiring: signed-append over consented hubs.\n//!\n//! This module builds ONLY the kernel primitive — an append-only signed log\n//! (`MeshLog`) — plus a hub-transport *trait* (`HubTransport`). It does NOT\n//! perform any real cross-repo git push / network IO. The transport is\n//! config-driven: a caller supplies any concrete `HubTransport` implementation\n//! (a test stub, an HTTP client, an iroh node, …) — there is no hardcoded\n//! endpoint baked into the kernel.\n//!\n//! ## Cryptography — real, not invented\n//! Signing/verification use the kernel's EXISTING, KAT-gated ML-DSA-65\n//! primitive at [`crate::pq::dsa`] (FIPS 204, byte-exact vs NIST ACVP\n//! vectors). No new crypto is introduced here. The module is gated behind the\n//! `pq` feature for the same reason `pq` itself is: the canonical order/money\n//! core stays pure-std and serde-free; signing is a mesh/transport identity\n//! seam (see `lib.rs` `pq` feature rationale).\n//!\n//! ## Chain structure\n//! Each [`SignedEntry`] carries `prev_hash` (SHA3-256 of the previous entry's\n//! canonical bytes, zero for genesis), the opaque `payload`, the ML-DSA\n//! signature, and the signer's public key. [`MeshLog::verify_chain`] walks the\n//! chain and re-checks every signature — tampered payloads and broken `prev`\n//! links are both rejected.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::boxed::Box;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeSet;\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::pq::dsa::{keygen, sign, verify, MlDsa65Sk, RNDBYTES, SEEDBYTES};\npub use crate::pq::dsa::{MlDsa65Pk, MlDsa65Sig};\n\n// Item 24 (§4 hardening sweep over the mesh crypto surface): the signature / chain\n// verification path is a crypto surface — the moment gossip touches a signature it\n// inherits the full checklist (oracle + dudect + debug-differential + asm spot-check).\n// `ct_eq` is the kernel's reusable constant-time byte-equality primitive\n// (`ct_gate.rs`, roadmap item 6); we route the signature-structural comparison\n// through it so the gossip path is branch-free over the secret-dependent bytes\n// (synthesis §17(c): "not a lighter 'protocol' variant"). Test-only harness bits\n// (`mesh_oracle`, the dudect self-test) and the `ct_eq` dependency compile only under\n// `test`/`ct-gate`, exactly like `ct_gate` itself — zero footprint in a shipping build.\n#[cfg(any(test, feature = "ct-gate"))]\nuse crate::ct_gate::{ct_eq, T_THRESHOLD};\n\n/// A single append-only, signed entry in the mesh log.\n///\n/// The entry is content-addressed and chained: `prev_hash` binds it to the\n/// previous entry so the log is tamper-evident. The signature covers the\n/// entry's *canonical* bytes (see [`SignedEntry::signed_bytes`]).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct SignedEntry {\n    /// SHA3-256 of the previous entry's canonical bytes. Zero for the genesis\n    /// entry. This is the hash-chain link.\n    pub prev_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// Opaque payload (e.g. a serialized, consented hub event).\n    pub payload: Vec<u8>,\n    /// ML-DSA-65 signature over [`SignedEntry::signed_bytes`].\n    pub sig: Vec<u8>,\n    /// The signer's ML-DSA-65 public key (identity, NOT a score).\n    pub pubkey: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// Errors a [`MeshLog`] or [`HubTransport`] operation can produce. Fail-closed:\n/// every arm reports the failure instead of silently accepting.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum MeshError {\n    /// A signature failed to verify (forged, tampered payload, or wrong key).\n    BadSignature,\n    /// The chain's `prev_hash` link is broken: an entry does not point at the\n    /// hash of the entry that precedes it (a removed/reordered/corrupted entry).\n    BrokenLink {\n        /// The expected `prev_hash` (the chain tip before this entry).\n        expected: [u8; 32],\n        /// The `prev_hash` actually carried by the offending entry.\n        got: [u8; 32],\n    },\n    /// The genesis entry (sequence index 0) must have a zero `prev_hash`.\n    GenesisMustBeRoot,\n    /// A hub transport operation failed (e.g. a stub could not reach a hub).\n    Transport(String),\n}\n\n/// A signer capable of producing ML-DSA-65 signatures over an entry's canonical\n/// bytes. The kernel provides [`MlDsaSigner`]; a caller may supply their own\n/// (e.g. a hardware-backed or threshold signer) as long as it verifies against\n/// the returned public key.\npub trait Signer {\n    /// Sign `msg` and return the raw signature bytes.\n    fn sign(&self, msg: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>;\n    /// The public key this signer certifies (used to populate `SignedEntry::pubkey`).\n    fn pubkey(&self) -> Vec<u8>;\n}\n\n/// Kernel-native [`Signer`] backed by the existing ML-DSA-65 primitive.\n///\n/// Determinism note: pass a fixed `rnd` (e.g. all zeros for FIPS deterministic\n/// signing mode) so signatures are reproducible in tests. NEVER draw from an OS\n/// RNG here — the crypto hot path is RNG-free by design (see `pq::dsa`).\npub struct MlDsaSigner {\n    sk: MlDsa65Sk,\n    pk: MlDsa65Pk,\n    rnd: [u8; RNDBYTES],\n}\n\nimpl MlDsaSigner {\n    /// Derive a signer from a 32-byte seed (same seed → same keypair, since\n    /// `pq::dsa::keygen` is deterministic). `rnd` is the ML-DSA randomness\n    /// input; use `[0u8; 32]` for FIPS deterministic signing mode.\n    pub fn from_seed(seed: &[u8; SEEDBYTES], rnd: [u8; RNDBYTES]) -> Self {\n        let (pk, sk) = keygen(seed);\n        MlDsaSigner { sk, pk, rnd }\n    }\n\n    /// Public key bytes (identity).\n    pub fn pubkey_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        self.pk.bytes.clone()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Signer for MlDsaSigner {\n    fn sign(&self, msg: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n        sign(&self.sk, msg, &self.rnd).bytes\n    }\n    fn pubkey(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        self.pk.bytes.clone()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SignedEntry {\n    /// Canonical bytes that get signed/verified: the **payload only**.\n    ///\n    /// The signature authenticates the payload + signer; the chain *position*\n    /// is authenticated separately (see [`SignedEntry::content_hash`] and\n    /// [`MeshLog::verify_chain`]). This split is deliberate: it makes\n    /// "tampered payload" and "broken `prev_hash` link" two *distinct* failure\n    /// poles. A forger without the key cannot re-sign a mutated payload\n    /// (`BadSignature`), and cannot relink an entry to a different parent\n    /// without breaking the link check (`BrokenLink`) — the link is\n    /// content-addressed, not signed, so only a legitimate signer can form a\n    /// valid chain.\n    pub fn signed_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {\n        &self.payload\n    }\n\n    /// Verify this entry's signature against its embedded public key. Does NOT\n    /// check chain linkage (that is [`MeshLog::verify_chain`]'s job).\n    pub fn verify_sig(&self) -> bool {\n        let pk = MlDsa65Pk {\n            bytes: self.pubkey.clone(),\n        };\n        let sig = MlDsa65Sig {\n            bytes: self.sig.clone(),\n        };\n        let ok = verify(&pk, self.signed_bytes(), &sig);\n        // §4 checklist item 3 (debug-differential cross-check): in debug builds AND\n        // when the hardening harness is compiled in, assert the production verifier\n        // agrees with the simple retained reference oracle (`mesh_oracle::\n        // oracle_verify_sig`). Compiled out of release and out of a plain shipping\n        // build (no `ct-gate` feature) — zero production cost, continuous\n        // verification while developing/testing. Mirrors `ct_gate`'s "CI-time\n        // harness, not linked" discipline.\n        #[cfg(any(test, feature = "ct-gate"))]\n        debug_assert_eq!(\n            ok,\n            crate::mesh::mesh_oracle::oracle_verify_sig(self),\n            "mesh verify_sig disagrees with the retained reference oracle"\n        );\n        ok\n    }\n\n    /// Constant-time signature comparator for the gossip-admission path (item 24,\n    /// §4 checklist item 2). When a peer receives an entry, it must compare the\n    /// carried signature against the signature it already has on record (duplicate /\n    /// idempotency check) or against the expected tip signature. That comparison is\n    /// secret-dependent — a short-circuiting `!=` would leak *which* byte first\n    /// differed, an attacker-probable timing oracle. We route it through the kernel's\n    /// reusable `ct_eq` (`ct_gate.rs`, roadmap item 6) so the path is branch-free over\n    /// the signature bytes. The dudect self-test `mesh_sig_compare_dudect` proves this\n    /// comparator is constant-time and that a leaky variable-time comparator is rejected.\n    /// Compiled only under `test`/`ct-gate` — never in a shipping binary.\n    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "ct-gate"))]\n    pub fn sig_eq_ct(&self, expected_sig: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        ct_eq(&self.sig, expected_sig)\n    }\n\n    /// Content hash of this entry — the `prev_hash` the NEXT entry must carry.\n    /// SHA3-256 over `prev_hash || payload`, binding the whole entry (chain\n    /// position via `prev_hash` + payload) into one collision-resistant id. The\n    /// signature does NOT cover this, so a broken link is caught by the link\n    /// check, not masked as a signature failure.\n    pub fn content_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(32 + self.payload.len());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.prev_hash);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.payload);\n        sha3_256(&buf)\n    }\n}\n\n/// An append-only, signed, chain-linked log — the kernel primitive for\n/// cross-repo mesh wiring. Entries are signed with an ML-DSA-65 [`Signer`]\n/// (signed-append over consented hubs). The log itself holds no network code.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct MeshLog {\n    entries: Vec<SignedEntry>,\n}\n\nimpl MeshLog {\n    /// Empty log.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        MeshLog::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Number of entries.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.entries.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the log has no entries.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.entries.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow the entry at `index` (0 = genesis).\n    pub fn entry(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&SignedEntry> {\n        self.entries.get(index)\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow all entries in chain order.\n    pub fn entries(&self) -> &[SignedEntry] {\n        &self.entries\n    }\n\n    /// Append `payload`, signing it with `signer`. The new entry's `prev_hash`\n    /// is bound to the content hash of the current tip (genesis → zero). Returns\n    /// the signed entry. This is "signed-append": the entry is authenticated\n    /// before it enters the log.\n    pub fn append<S: Signer>(&mut self, payload: &[u8], signer: &S) -> SignedEntry {\n        let prev_hash = match self.entries.last() {\n            Some(prev) => prev.content_hash(),\n            None => [0u8; 32],\n        };\n        let entry = SignedEntry {\n            prev_hash,\n            payload: payload.to_vec(),\n            sig: Vec::new(),    // filled below\n            pubkey: Vec::new(), // filled below\n        };\n        let sig = signer.sign(&entry.signed_bytes());\n        let pubkey = signer.pubkey();\n        let entry = SignedEntry {\n            prev_hash,\n            payload: payload.to_vec(),\n            sig,\n            pubkey,\n        };\n        self.entries.push(entry.clone());\n        entry\n    }\n\n    /// Verify the entire chain from genesis to tip:\n    /// 1. every signature verifies against its embedded pubkey;\n    /// 2. each link's `prev_hash` equals the content hash of the preceding\n    ///    entry (genesis must be a root, i.e. zero `prev_hash`);\n    /// 3. no entry mutates in place (each entry's own content hash is internally\n    ///    consistent — a no-op here since we hold owned structs, but the link\n    ///    walk is what catches insertions/removals/reorders).\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(())` only if every entry is authentic and every link holds.\n    pub fn verify_chain(&self) -> Result<(), MeshError> {\n        let mut prev_hash: [u8; 32] = [0u8; 32];\n        for (i, e) in self.entries.iter().enumerate() {\n            // (1) signature must verify.\n            if !e.verify_sig() {\n                return Err(MeshError::BadSignature);\n            }\n            // (2) link check. Genesis must be a root.\n            if i == 0 {\n                if e.prev_hash != [0u8; 32] {\n                    return Err(MeshError::GenesisMustBeRoot);\n                }\n            } else if e.prev_hash != prev_hash {\n                return Err(MeshError::BrokenLink {\n                    expected: prev_hash,\n                    got: e.prev_hash,\n                });\n            }\n            // Advance the expected link for the next entry.\n            prev_hash = e.content_hash();\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Hub transport seam for the mesh log. Implementations are SUPPLIED BY THE\n/// CALLER and are config-driven — the kernel bakes in NO endpoint, NO protocol,\n/// NO network. A concrete impl might push to a consented git remote, an HTTP\n/// hub, an iroh node, or (in tests) an in-memory vector. The trait proves the\n/// wiring is transport-agnostic: signed entries leave the kernel only through\n/// `send`, and arrive back only through `recv`.\n///\n/// **No real cross-repo git push is performed by any kernel code.** This trait\n/// is the firewall that keeps the kernel network-free; the network half is a\n/// caller-supplied adapter, exactly like `event_log::EventStore`.\npub trait HubTransport {\n    /// Send one signed entry to the consented hub(s).\n    fn send(&self, e: &SignedEntry) -> Result<(), MeshError>;\n    /// Receive signed entries from the hub (e.g. for a peer's log to verify).\n    fn recv(&self) -> Result<Vec<SignedEntry>, MeshError>;\n}\n\n/// Item 23 — gossip reception as an extension of the ONE import pipeline.\n///\n/// This is the production caller the signed-log primitive was missing (item 22\n/// audit §3: `MeshLog`/`SignedEntry` were bench-only with zero real callers).\n/// It turns a gossip-received, ML-DSA-signed entry into a candidate unit that\n/// is admitted through `decision::import_unit` — **the same** six-check gate a\n/// locally-compiled unit uses. No second importer is built.\n///\n/// **Transport-firewall discipline (HubTransport `mesh.rs:250–265`): the\n/// signature is verified BEFORE the entry reaches `import_unit`.** A forged or\n/// tampered entry (`SignedEntry::verify_sig` ⇒ false) is rejected here and\n/// never enters the import pipeline, so the only bytes `import_unit` ever sees\n/// are authentic against the peer's embedded public key.\n///\n/// Wire-format note: the `payload` of a gossip `SignedEntry` is an\n/// opaque-but-parsable unit frame. We keep this item strictly zero-dep / no\n/// serde: the frame is decoded by a caller-supplied `decode` closure (the\n/// kernel defines the seam, the sync layer supplies the concrete wire codec).\npub struct GossipImport {\n    /// The transport through which signed peer entries arrive.\n    transport: Box<dyn HubTransport>,\n}\n\nimpl GossipImport {\n    /// Build a gossip receiver over a caller-supplied [`HubTransport`].\n    pub fn new<T: HubTransport + 'static>(transport: T) -> Self {\n        GossipImport {\n            transport: Box::new(transport),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Pull every entry the transport hands us, filter to the authentic ones,\n    /// and return them ready for `import_unit`. **Forged/tampered entries are\n    /// dropped here** (transport firewall) — they cannot reach the import gate.\n    ///\n    /// The returned metas carry `source = decision::import::Source::Gossip`.\n    pub fn receive_verified(&self) -> Result<Vec<GossipUnit>, MeshError> {\n        let entries = self.transport.recv()?;\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        for e in entries {\n            // Transport firewall: verify the signature against the embedded\n            // pubkey BEFORE the unit can be imported. Bad signature ⇒ skip; it\n            // never reaches `import_unit` (degrade-closed at the seam).\n            if !e.verify_sig() {\n                continue; // MeshError::BadSignature equivalent, enforced pre-pipeline\n            }\n            out.push(GossipUnit { entry: e });\n        }\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n}\n\n/// A gossip-received, signature-verified unit frame, ready to feed `import_unit`\n/// (with `Source::Gossip`). The signature has already been checked by the\npub struct GossipUnit {\n    /// The verified signed entry (its `payload` is the opaque unit frame).\n    pub entry: SignedEntry,\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Item 24 — §4 hardening sweep over the mesh crypto surface.\n//\n// The four checklist artifacts (oracle / dudect / debug-differential / asm spot-check)\n// applied to the gossip-message signature-verification path. The oracle is a\n// test-only crate-internal reference module retained forever as the differential\n// target (checklist item 1); the dudect self-test (item 2) routes the signature\n// comparison through `ct_eq` and proves a planted variable-time comparator is\n// rejected by the same Welch-t machinery; the debug-differential cross-check (item 3)\n// is the `debug_assert_eq!` inside `SignedEntry::verify_sig` (compiled out of\n// release); the asm spot-check (item 4) keys into the item-14 toolchain-bump trigger\n// (see docs/audits/toolchain/spot-check-1.96.1.md, surface inventory extension).\n//\n// Compiled ONLY under `test`/`ct-gate` — zero footprint in a shipping build, exactly\n// like `ct_gate` itself ("CI-time harness, not linked", SYNTHESIS §4 item 2).\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n#[cfg(any(test, feature = "ct-gate"))]\npub mod mesh_oracle {\n    //! Reference (obviously-correct) verifier/validator for the mesh crypto surface.\n    //!\n    //! This module is the §4 checklist item-1 oracle: a simple, deliberately\n    //! unoptimized reference implementation of gossip-message signature verification\n    //! and signature comparison, retained as the differential target against the\n    //! production `SignedEntry::verify_sig` / `sig_eq_ct`. It reuses the *same*\n    //! KAT-gated `pq::dsa::verify` primitive (item 22: no invented crypto) but is\n    //! structured as a standalone, easy-to-read reference so any future divergence\n    //! in the production path is caught by the debug-differential cross-check and by\n    //! the differential tests in `mesh_dudect::tests`.\n    use super::{MlDsa65Pk, MlDsa65Sig, SignedEntry};\n    use crate::pq::dsa::verify;\n\n    /// Obviously-correct reference for [`SignedEntry::verify_sig`]: re-verify the\n    /// signature against the embedded public key over the entry's signed bytes.\n    /// One-line, no tricks — this is the differential target, not a performance path.\n    pub fn oracle_verify_sig(e: &SignedEntry) -> bool {\n        let pk = MlDsa65Pk {\n            bytes: e.pubkey.clone(),\n        };\n        let sig = MlDsa65Sig {\n            bytes: e.sig.clone(),\n        };\n        verify(&pk, e.signed_bytes(), &sig)\n    }\n\n    /// Obviously-correct reference for [`SignedEntry::sig_eq_ct`]: a straightforward\n    /// boolean equality over the signature bytes (the reference is ALLOWED to be the\n    /// simple form — it is the differential target, and the constant-time property is\n    /// asserted separately by the dudect self-test, not by this reference).\n    pub fn oracle_sig_eq(a: &SignedEntry, expected_sig: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        a.sig == expected_sig\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(feature = "ct-gate")]\nmod mesh_dudect {\n    //! §4 checklist item 2 — dudect-style gate over the mesh signature comparison,\n    //! with the planted-leak self-test (SYNTHESIS §10/P7, the "verifier the author\n    //! cannot forge"). Uses the kernel's existing `ct_gate` Welch-t machinery so the\n    //! mesh surface reuses the SAME proven gate as the FO-tag-compare precedent.\n\n    use crate::ct_gate::{ct_eq, measure_leakage, T_THRESHOLD};\n\n    \n    \n\n    /// PLANTED LEAK (test-only): the classic variable-time signature comparison —\n    /// early-returns at the first differing byte, so its run-time leaks the position\n    /// of the first mismatch. The gate MUST reject this with the same machinery it\n    /// accepts `ct_eq`. This is the mesh analog of `ct_gate::tests::naive_eq`.\n    fn naive_sig_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        if a.len() != b.len() {\n            return false;\n        }\n        for i in 0..a.len() {\n            if a[i] != b[i] {\n                return false; // early return — the leak\n            }\n        }\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// dudect self-test (timing; `#[ignore]` so it stays out of the noisy default\n    /// suite — run in release by `scripts/hardening-gate.sh` step E, like the\n    /// `ct_gate` self-test). Proves (1) the planted variable-time comparator is\n    /// detected (|t| >= 4.5) and (2) the constant-time `ct_eq`-based comparator is\n    /// separated from it by a wide margin (>= 3x), replicating the item-6 gate's\n    /// load-bearing property on the mesh signature-compare surface.\n    #[test]\n    #[ignore = "timing self-test; run in release by scripts/hardening-gate.sh step E"]\n    fn mesh_sig_compare_dudect() {\n        // 3309-byte buffers (the ML-DSA-65 signature length, SIGNATUREBYTES). Class A:\n        // equal signatures (comparator scans all bytes). Class B: differ at byte 0.\n        let equal_l = [0u8; 3309];\n        let equal_r = [0u8; 3309];\n        let diff_l = [0u8; 3309];\n        let mut diff_r = [0u8; 3309];\n        diff_r[0] = 1;\n        let class_a = (&equal_l[..], &equal_r[..]);\n        let class_b = (&diff_l[..], &diff_r[..]);\n\n        const ROUNDS: usize = 300;\n        const BATCH: usize = 4096;\n\n        // (1) The planted leak MUST be detected — the non-negotiable, load-bearing\n        // property, carried over verbatim from `ct_gate`'s self-test.\n        let leak_t = (0..3)\n            .map(|_| measure_leakage(class_a, class_b, naive_sig_eq, ROUNDS, BATCH))\n            .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);\n        assert!(\n            leak_t >= T_THRESHOLD,\n            "PLANTED LEAK NOT DETECTED: naive_sig_eq |t|={leak_t:.2} < {T_THRESHOLD} — gate is blind"\n        );\n\n        // (2) The constant-time comparator's |t| — best-of-5 (min), the standard\n        // practical mitigation against a scheduling hiccup spiking one measurement.\n        let ct_t = (0..5)\n            .map(|_| measure_leakage(class_a, class_b, ct_eq, ROUNDS, BATCH))\n            .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);\n\n        // (3) HARD gate: the harness must DISTINGUISH leaky from constant-time by a\n        // wide margin (ratio holds regardless of the runner's absolute noise floor).\n        assert!(\n            leak_t >= 3.0 * ct_t,\n            "harness failed to SEPARATE leaky from constant-time: leak |t|={leak_t:.2}, ct |t|={ct_t:.2} (need >= 3x)"\n        );\n\n        // (4) Informational: on a quiet runner ct_eq lands well under the dudect\n        // cutoff; under load it can be elevated while the separation proof still holds.\n        let verdict = if ct_t < T_THRESHOLD {\n            format!("ct_eq |t|={ct_t:.2} (PASS, < {T_THRESHOLD})")\n        } else {\n            format!("ct_eq |t|={ct_t:.2} (elevated under load; separation proof still holds)")\n        };\n        println!(\n            "mesh dudect self-test PASS: planted-leak naive_sig_eq |t|={leak_t:.1} (DETECTED, >= {T_THRESHOLD}); \\\n             {verdict}; separation {:.1}x (>= 3x required)",\n            leak_t / ct_t.max(1e-9)\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Deterministic signer from a single seed byte, all-zero rnd (FIPS\n    /// deterministic signing mode → reproducible signatures).\n    fn signer(seed_byte: u8) -> MlDsaSigner {\n        let mut seed = [0u8; SEEDBYTES];\n        seed[0] = seed_byte;\n        MlDsaSigner::from_seed(&seed, [0u8; RNDBYTES])\n    }\n\n    // ── GREEN: a valid append+verify chain is accepted. ──\n    #[test]\n    fn valid_chain_is_accepted() {\n        let mut log = MeshLog::new();\n        let s = signer(1);\n        log.append(b"consent: hub-A <-> hub-B", &s);\n        log.append(b"event: order placed", &s);\n        log.append(b"event: order settled", &s);\n        assert_eq!(log.len(), 3);\n        assert!(log.verify_chain().is_ok(), "valid signed chain must verify");\n    }\n\n    // ── RED: a tampered payload is rejected. ──\n    #[test]\n    fn tampered_payload_is_rejected() {\n        let mut log = MeshLog::new();\n        let s = signer(2);\n        let _e0 = log.append(b"honest payload", &s);\n        let mut e1 = log.append(b"another honest payload", &s);\n        // Mutate the payload AFTER signing (an attacker tampering at rest / in\n        // transit). The stored signature no longer matches the bytes.\n        e1.payload = b"forged payload".to_vec();\n        // Replace the last entry with the tampered one.\n        log.entries.pop();\n        log.entries.push(e1);\n        match log.verify_chain() {\n            Err(MeshError::BadSignature) => {}\n            other => panic!("expected BadSignature, got {:?}", other),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── RED: a broken prev_hash link is rejected. ──\n    #[test]\n    fn broken_prev_link_is_rejected() {\n        let mut log = MeshLog::new();\n        let s = signer(3);\n        log.append(b"first", &s);\n        let mut e1 = log.append(b"second", &s);\n        // Sever the chain link: rewrite prev_hash to a wrong value while keeping\n        // the (still-valid) signature over the ORIGINAL bytes. Link check must\n        // catch it; signature check alone would not.\n        e1.prev_hash = [9u8; 32];\n        log.entries.pop();\n        log.entries.push(e1);\n        match log.verify_chain() {\n            Err(MeshError::BrokenLink { expected, got }) => {\n                assert_eq!(got, [9u8; 32]);\n                assert_ne!(expected, [9u8; 32]);\n            }\n            other => panic!("expected BrokenLink, got {:?}", other),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── GREEN (config-driven trait proof): a HubTransport impl supplied by a\n    //    test (in-memory) proves the transport is caller-supplied, not hardcoded\n    //    to any endpoint. send/recv round-trip signed entries. ──\n    #[test]\n    fn hub_transport_impl_supplied_by_test() {\n        // Config-driven stub: holds entries in a Vec; "endpoint" is just the\n        // struct's own memory, set entirely by the test — no baked-in URL/host.\n        struct MemHub {\n            outbox: core::cell::RefCell<Vec<SignedEntry>>,\n        }\n        impl HubTransport for MemHub {\n            fn send(&self, e: &SignedEntry) -> Result<(), MeshError> {\n                self.outbox.borrow_mut().push(e.clone());\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            fn recv(&self) -> Result<Vec<SignedEntry>, MeshError> {\n                Ok(self.outbox.borrow().clone())\n            }\n        }\n\n        let hub = MemHub {\n            outbox: core::cell::RefCell::new(Vec::new()),\n        };\n        let mut log = MeshLog::new();\n        let s = signer(4);\n        let e0 = log.append(b"wire to hub", &s);\n        // The kernel emits the signed entry through the caller-supplied transport.\n        hub.send(&e0).expect("transport send");\n        // And can pull it back / verify it on the other side.\n        let got = hub.recv().expect("transport recv");\n        assert_eq!(got.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(got[0].content_hash(), e0.content_hash());\n        // The received entry still verifies under the chain it would join.\n        let mut peer = MeshLog::new();\n        peer.entries.push(got[0].clone());\n        assert!(peer.verify_chain().is_ok());\n    }\n\n    // ── GREEN: signature of the genesis entry with nonzero prev_hash is caught. ──\n    #[test]\n    fn genesis_must_be_root() {\n        let mut log = MeshLog::new();\n        let s = signer(5);\n        let e = log.append(b"genesis", &s);\n        // Tamper only the prev_hash link of the genesis entry to nonzero while\n        // keeping the valid signature — link/root check must reject.\n        let mut bad = e;\n        bad.prev_hash = [1u8; 32];\n        let mut lone = MeshLog::new();\n        lone.entries.push(bad);\n        match lone.verify_chain() {\n            Err(MeshError::GenesisMustBeRoot) => {}\n            other => panic!("expected GenesisMustBeRoot, got {:?}", other),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── ITEM 23 (acceptance #4): a bad-signature gossip entry never reaches\n    //    `import_unit`. The transport firewall (`receive_verified`) drops it\n    //    before any import. We simulate a peer feed: one good entry + one\n    //    tampered entry; only the good one survives the firewall. ──\n    #[test]\n    fn gossip_bad_signature_never_reaches_import() {\n        let s = signer(7);\n        // Good, signed entry.\n        let good = {\n            let mut log = MeshLog::new();\n            log.append(b"unit-frame: dispatch-v2", &s)\n        };\n        // Forged entry: valid signature over a different payload, then tampered\n        // in place so verify_sig fails.\n        let mut forged = {\n            let mut log = MeshLog::new();\n            log.append(b"unit-frame: dispatch-v2", &s)\n        };\n        forged.payload = b"forged-frame".to_vec(); // signature no longer matches\n\n        struct FeedHub {\n            entries: core::cell::RefCell<Vec<SignedEntry>>,\n        }\n        impl HubTransport for FeedHub {\n            fn send(&self, _e: &SignedEntry) -> Result<(), MeshError> {\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            fn recv(&self) -> Result<Vec<SignedEntry>, MeshError> {\n                Ok(self.entries.borrow().clone())\n            }\n        }\n        let hub = FeedHub {\n            entries: core::cell::RefCell::new(vec![good, forged]),\n        };\n        let gossip = GossipImport::new(hub);\n        let verified = gossip.receive_verified().expect("transport recv ok");\n        // The forged entry is dropped at the firewall; only the authentic one\n        // is handed toward `import_unit` (Source::Gossip).\n        assert_eq!(\n            verified.len(),\n            1,\n            "bad-sig entry must not survive the firewall"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(verified[0].entry.payload, b"unit-frame: dispatch-v2");\n    }\n\n    // ── Item 24 §4 item 1 (oracle): the production verifier + the constant-time\n    //    signature comparator must agree with the retained reference oracle\n    //    (`mesh_oracle`) over a corpus of valid + adversarially-mutated signed\n    //    entries (the 5 red/green tests above are the seed; extended here to a\n    //    differential corpus). The oracle is the differential target retained\n    //    forever in `mesh_oracle` — if the production path ever diverges from this\n    //    simple reference, this test (and the in-path debug_assert_eq!) turns RED. ──\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_sig_matches_oracle_over_corpus() {\n        // Build a corpus: valid entries under several signers, plus adversarially\n        // mutated copies (tampered payload, broken link, wrong key, zeroed sig).\n        let s1 = signer(1);\n        let s2 = signer(2);\n\n        let mut good = MeshLog::new();\n        good.append(b"consent: hub-A <-> hub-B", &s1);\n        good.append(b"event: order placed", &s1);\n        good.append(b"event: order settled", &s2);\n\n        let mut tampered = MeshLog::new();\n        let _e0 = tampered.append(b"honest payload", &s2);\n        let mut e1 = tampered.append(b"another honest payload", &s2);\n        e1.payload = b"forged payload".to_vec();\n        tampered.entries.pop();\n        tampered.entries.push(e1);\n\n        let mut wrong_key = MeshLog::new();\n        let _w0 = wrong_key.append(b"first", &s1);\n        let mut w1 = wrong_key.append(b"second", &s1);\n        w1.pubkey = signer(9).pubkey_bytes(); // re-sign would be needed; we kept the OLD sig\n        wrong_key.entries.pop();\n        wrong_key.entries.push(w1);\n\n        let mut zeroed_sig = MeshLog::new();\n        let z = zeroed_sig.append(b"zero me", &s1);\n        let mut zbad = z;\n        zbad.sig = vec![0u8; zbad.sig.len()];\n        zeroed_sig.entries.pop();\n        zeroed_sig.entries.push(zbad);\n\n        for log in [&good, &tampered, &wrong_key, &zeroed_sig] {\n            for e in log.entries() {\n                // Production verifier vs. retained reference oracle — must always agree.\n                assert_eq!(\n                    e.verify_sig(),\n                    crate::mesh::mesh_oracle::oracle_verify_sig(e),\n                    "verify_sig disagreed with oracle on a corpus entry"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── Item 24 §4 item 1 (oracle, continued): `sig_eq_ct` (constant-time gossip\n    //    signature assert!(entry.sig_eq_ct(&entry.sig));\n        assert!(crate::mesh::mesh_oracle::oracle_sig_eq(&entry, &entry.sig));\n        // Different sig → both say unequal (one byte flipped).\n        let mut other_sig = entry.sig.clone();\n        other_sig[0] ^= 0xff;\n        assert!(!entry.sig_eq_ct(&other_sig));\n        assert!(!crate::mesh::mesh_oracle::oracle_sig_eq(&entry, &other_sig));\n    }\n\n  #[test]\n    fn single_entry_mesh_verifies() {\n        let mut log = MeshLog::new();\n        let s = signer(8);\n        log.append(b"single node", &s);\n        assert_eq!(log.len(), 1);\n        assert!(!log.is_empty());\n        assert!(log.entry(0).is_some());\n        assert!(log.verify_chain().is_ok());\n        // genesis entry must have zero prev_hash\n        assert_eq!(log.entry(0).unwrap().prev_hash, [0u8; 32]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn node_addition_increments_len() {\n        let mut log = MeshLog::new();\n        let s = signer(9);\n        for i
```
