refused while Locked (tamper = attack, not evolution). The\n    /// owner must re-seed or hit M9. Intervention flag does NOT bypass Locked.\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_commit_refused_while_locked() {\n        let mut h = Hydra::new(MemEventStore::new(), 3, base());\n        h.base_edges.push(TopoEdge {\n            from: 0,\n            to: 0,\n            weight: 2.0,\n        });\n        assert_eq!(h.integrity_check(), OrganismState::Locked);\n        let res = h.commit(ev(1, 1, b"x"), &[], true, |_| Ok::<u64, String>(1));\n        assert!(\n            matches!(res, Err(CommitError::Rejected(_))),\n            "Locked ⇒ commit refused even with intervention"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// G9 — breach alarm: when tamper is detected (Locked), raise an UNABOUNDED,\n    /// NO-per-event-consent alert to the whole hub. Suppressing it IS the exploit\n    /// (social-engineering the owner into silence). Carries node_id + group_size\n    /// only — NO code. If not Locked, no alert (no false alarms).\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_breach_alarm_unbounded_on_tamper() {\n        let mut h = Hydra::new(MemEventStore::new(), 3, base());\n        // Live: no alert.\n        assert_eq!(h.integrity_check(), OrganismState::Live);\n        assert!(\n            h.raise_breach_alarm([7u8; 32], 4096)\n                .expect("store ok")\n                .is_none(),\n            "no alert while Live"\n        );\n        // Tamper → Locked → alarm to full hub, any group size, no per-event consent.\n        h.base_edges.push(TopoEdge {\n            from: 0,\n            to: 0,\n            weight: 2.0,\n        });\n        assert_eq!(h.integrity_check(), OrganismState::Locked);\n        let a = h\n            .raise_breach_alarm([7u8; 32], 4096)\n            .expect("store ok")\n            .expect("alarm raised when Locked");\n        assert_eq!(a.node_id, [7u8; 32]);\n        assert_eq!(a.group_size, 4096, "unbounded fan-out to hub");\n        // Self-witness: the breach is now durable in the WORM log (anti-silent-heal).\n        let witnessed = h.log().store().contains(&{\n            use crate::event_log::MeshEvent;\n            let mut p = Vec::with_capacity(40);\n            p.extend_from_slice(&[7u8; 32]);\n            p.extend_from_slice(&4096u64.to_le_bytes());\n            MeshEvent {\n                prev: [0u8; 32],\n                actor_pubkey: BREACH_WITNESS_ACTOR,\n                actor_seq: 0,\n                payload: p,\n            }\n            .event_id()\n        });\n        assert!(witnessed, "breach self-witness row persisted in WORM log");\n        // group_size==0 is the only guard (no hub to warn).\n        assert!(h\n            .raise_breach_alarm([7u8; 32], 0)\n            .expect("store ok")\n            .is_none());\n    }\n\n    /// G9 — hub convergence: a node that RECEIVES a verified peer breach alert\n    /// records it into its OWN WORM log (external-witness), with no per-event\n    /// consent. The peer node_id is now durably "burnt" at this node too. Idempotent\n    /// on replay (distinct content-id per alert ⇒ each unique breach recorded once;\n    /// a re-delivery at a new log-len still produces the same event-id ⇒ duplicate no-op).\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_ingest_peer_breach_converges_hub() {\n        let mut node = Hydra::new(MemEventStore::new(), 3, base());\n        // A verified alert about a *peer* (caller already checked ML-DSA + witness_event_id).\n        let peer_alert = BreachAlert {\n            node_id: [9u8; 32],\n            group_size: 4096,\n        };\n        node.ingest_peer_breach(&peer_alert).expect("ingest ok");\n        // The peer breach is now durable in THIS node's WORM log.\n        let external_id = {\n            use crate::event_log::MeshEvent;\n            let mut p = Vec::with_capacity(40);\n            p.extend_from_slice(&[9u8; 32]);\n            p.extend_from_slice(&4096u64.to_le_bytes());\n            MeshEvent {\n                prev: [0u8; 32],\n                actor_pubkey: BREACH_WITNESS_ACTOR,\n                actor_seq: 0,\n                payload: p,\n            }\n            .event_id()\n        };\n        assert!(\n            node.log().contains(&external_id),\n            "peer breach recorded in this node's WORM log (hub converged)"\n        );\n        // Replay (same alert, new log len) => same content-id => duplicate no-op,\n        // no second row.\n        let before = node.log().len();\n        node.ingest_peer_breach(&peer_alert).expect("ingest ok");\n        assert_eq!(node.log().len(), before, "replay is idempotent");\n        // Self is still Live (ingesting a PEER breach does not lock this node).\n        assert_eq!(node.integrity_check(), OrganismState::Live);\n    }\n\n    /// G9 — receiver-side deterministic verification: a peer runs `witness_event_id`\n    /// WITHOUT trusting the sender. The digest must reproduce from node_id +\n    /// group_size alone, and the quoted witness row must exist in the broadcaster's\n    /// WORM log. Forgery (wrong node_id/group_size) yields a different digest.\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_breach_alert_receiver_verifiable() {\n        let alert = BreachAlert {\n            node_id: [7u8; 32],\n            group_size: 4096,\n        };\n        let id = alert.witness_event_id();\n        // Determinism: same inputs => same digest.\n        assert_eq!(\n            id,\n            BreachAlert {\n                node_id: [7u8; 32],\n                group_size: 4096\n            }\n            .witness_event_id()\n        );\n        // Forgery: tampered group_size yields a different digest (not kernel-gen).\n        assert_ne!(\n            id,\n            BreachAlert {\n                node_id: [7u8; 32],\n                group_size: 1\n            }\n            .witness_event_id()\n        );\n        assert_ne!(\n            id,\n            BreachAlert {\n                node_id: [8u8; 32],\n                group_size: 4096\n            }\n            .witness_event_id()\n        );\n        // A receiving core re-derives the broadcaster's witness id from the alert\n        // and checks it exists in the broadcaster's WORM log (received over mesh).\n        // The digest is fully determined by node_id + group_size => forge-proof.\n        let mut p = Vec::with_capacity(40);\n        p.extend_from_slice(&[7u8; 32]);\n        p.extend_from_slice(&4096u64.to_le_bytes());\n        let w = crate::event_log::MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: BREACH_WITNESS_ACTOR,\n            actor_seq: 0,\n            payload: p,\n        };\n        // Peer would have the broadcaster's log row; verify its id matches the\n        // alert's claimed digest (no trust in sender needed).\n        assert_eq!(\n            w.event_id(),\n            id,\n            "broadcaster witness id matches alert claim"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── Wire serde is fixed-layout + fails closed on truncation ──────────────\n    // The transport layer signs these 40 bytes; they MUST round-trip exactly and\n    // reject a mangled length (so a signature-stripped frame can't resurrect).\n    #[test]\n    fn breach_alert_bytes_roundtrip_and_reject_bad_len() {\n        let alert = BreachAlert {\n            node_id: [0xABu8; 32],\n            group_size: 7,\n        };\n        let b = alert.to_bytes();\n        assert_eq!(b.len(), 40);\n        let back = BreachAlert::from_bytes(&b).expect("roundtrip");\n        assert_eq!(back.node_id, [0xABu8; 32]);\n        assert_eq!(back.group_size, 7);\n        // Truncated / over-long payloads fail closed (no partial parse).\n        assert!(BreachAlert::from_bytes(&b[..39]).is_none());\n        assert!(BreachAlert::from_bytes(&b).is_some());\n        // Tamper with the length field changes the decoded group_size.\n        let mut tampered = b;\n        tampered[39] ^= 0xFF; // flips high byte of the LE group_size\n        let t = BreachAlert::from_bytes(&tampered).expect("still 40 bytes");\n        assert_ne!(t.group_size, 7, "length-field tamper must change value");\n    }\n\n    /// P-C §7 T2 — from Locked, releasing takes exactly `healthy_checks` (3)\n    /// consecutive samples with ρ <= release. Assert the exact state sequence.\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_locked_release_requires_streak() {\n        let mut h = Hydra::new(MemEventStore::new(), 3, base());\n        // Force Locked first: push a tampering self-loop (ρ=2).\n        h.base_edges.push(TopoEdge {\n            from: 0,\n            to: 0,\n            weight: 2.0,\n        });\n        assert_eq!(h.integrity_check(), OrganismState::Locked);\n        // Now rewrite the self-loop to a clearly-Damped weight (w=0.9990 <= release).\n        h.base_edges.last_mut().unwrap().weight = 0.9990;\n        let s1 = h.integrity_check(); // streak 1\n        let s2 = h.integrity_check(); // streak 2\n        let s3 = h.integrity_check(); // streak 3 → release on 3rd\n        assert_eq!(\n            [s1, s2, s3],\n            [\n                OrganismState::Locked,\n                OrganismState::Locked,\n                OrganismState::Live\n            ],\n            "Locked→Live must require exactly 3 consecutive healthy checks"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(h.healthy_streak(), 0, "streak resets after release");\n    }\n\n    /// P-C §7 T3 (adversarial graze) — from Locked, an intermittent sample that\n    /// lands in the dead band (release < ρ < trigger) must RESET the streak.\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_dead_band_holds_lock() {\n        let mut h = Hydra::new(MemEventStore::new(), 3, base());\n        h.base_edges.push(TopoEdge {\n            from: 0,\n            to: 0,\n            weight: 2.0,\n        });\n        assert_eq!(h.integrity_check(), OrganismState::Locked);\n        // Sequence: two healthy (≤release), one dead-band graze, three healthy.\n        // The graze must reset the streak so release is delayed by one check.\n        let weights = [0.9990, 0.9990, 0.999999, 0.9990, 0.9990, 0.9990];\n        let mut seq = Vec::new();\n        for &w in &weights {\n            h.base_edges.last_mut().unwrap().weight = w;\n            seq.push(h.integrity_check());\n        }\n        assert_eq!(\n            seq,\n            vec![\n                OrganismState::Locked,\n                OrganismState::Locked,\n                OrganismState::Locked,\n                OrganismState::Locked,\n                OrganismState::Locked,\n                OrganismState::Live,\n            ],\n            "a dead-band graze must reset the streak; release happens one check later"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// P-C §7 T4 — fail-closed latency is provably unchanged: a Live organism\n    /// trips to Locked on a single check at ρ = trigger exactly.\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_trigger_trips_in_one_check() {\n        let mut h = Hydra::new(MemEventStore::new(), 3, base());\n        // Clean acyclic base ⇒ Live.\n        assert_eq!(h.integrity_check(), OrganismState::Live);\n        // Push a self-loop at exactly w = 1.0 (ρ = trigger) ⇒ trips immediately.\n        h.base_edges.push(TopoEdge {\n            from: 0,\n            to: 0,\n            weight: 1.0,\n        });\n        assert_eq!(h.integrity_check(), OrganismState::Locked);\n        assert_eq!(h.healthy_streak(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// P-C §3.1 / §7 T1 (RED FIRST — proves the hysteresis bug). Adversarial\n    /// oscillation inducer: a self-loop edge on node 0 whose weight `w` is\n    /// dithered between `1.0 - DRIFT_BAND/2` and `1.0 + DRIFT_BAND/2` for 8\n    /// checks. A self-loop gives ρ = w exactly. Against the memoryless\n    /// `rho < 1.0 && rho.is_finite()` predicate this flaps every check (7\n    /// transitions); the post-fix hysteresis band collapses it to ≤ 2.\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_integrity_flap_without_hysteresis_regression() {\n        use crate::spectral::DRIFT_BAND;\n        // Start Live (acyclic base). Add a self-loop on node 0 whose weight we\n        // rewrite between checks to dither ρ across 1.0.\n        let mut h = Hydra::new(MemEventStore::new(), 3, base());\n        h.base_edges.push(TopoEdge {\n            from: 0,\n            to: 0,\n            weight: 1.0,\n        });\n        let low = 1.0 - DRIFT_BAND / 2.0; // = 0.9999995\n        let high = 1.0 + DRIFT_BAND / 2.0; // = 1.0000005\n        let mut states = Vec::new();\n        let mut prev: Option<OrganismState> = None;\n        let mut transitions = 0usize;\n        for i in 0..8 {\n            // Alternate low/high across the 8 checks.\n            let w = if i % 2 == 0 { low } else { high };\n            // Rewrite the self-loop weight directly (tests module mutates base_edges).\n            h.base_edges.last_mut().unwrap().weight = w;\n            let s = h.integrity_check();\n            if let Some(p) = prev {\n                if p != s {\n                    transitions += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            states.push(s);\n            prev = Some(s);\n        }\n        // Assert the oscillation is bounded. Pre-fix (memoryless) code produces\n        // 7 transitions; the hysteresis fix must hold it to ≤ 2.\n        assert!(\n            transitions <= 2,\n            "integrity_check flapped {transitions} times (states={states:?}); \\\n             hysteresis band must bound Live<->Locked transitions to ≤ 2"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Command-verification layer: on a bound catalog, a fully-valid allowed\n    /// command frame passes through and the mutation commits (Damped delta).\n    #[test]\n    fn hydra_command_filter_accepts_valid_command() {\n        use crate::ports::agent::command_filter::{CommandId, ExactCommand};\n        let mut catalog = CommandCatalog::new();\n        let nonce: u64 = 0x5566778899AABBCC;\n        let key: [u8; 32] = *b"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef";\n        let mac = CommandCatalog::mac(&key, CommandId::new(0x01), &[0xAB], nonce);\n        let mut wire = Vec::new();\n        wire.push(CommandId::new(0x01).discriminant());\n        wire.extend_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());\n        wire.push(0xAB);\n        wire.extend_from_slice(&nonce.to_le_bytes());\n        wire.extend_from_slice(&mac);\n        catalog.register(ExactCommand::new(CommandId::new(0x01), vec![0xAB]).with_mac(mac));\n        let h = Hydra::new(MemEventStore::new(), 3, base())\n               from: 2,\n                to: 0,\n                weight: 0.3,\n            }],\n            false,\n            |_| Ok::<u64, String>(1),\n            &wire,\n        );\n        assert!(\n            matches!(\n                res,\n                Ok((crate::event_log::AppendOutcome::Committed(_), Some(1)))\n            ),\n            "valid command bytes must commit: {res:?}"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Command-verification layer: short/malformed bytes reject before the\n    /// spectral gate — fail-closed, no mutation enters.\n    #[test]\n    fn ## 14324 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/chaos.rs · LongTerm

Summary: chaos · 384 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/chaos.rs	chaos · 384 lines	//! chaos.rs — deterministic, zero-dependency fault-injection harness (P-H / W-H1).\n//!\n//! One mechanism, two seams (Hermetic P2, Correspondence: one concept, one\n//! primitive):\n//!   * Seam A — [`ChaosStore<S>`]: a trait-boundary decorator over ANY\n//!     [`crate::event_log::EventStore`]. It generalizes the pre-existing\n//!     `FaultyStore` test double (which is preserved as a thin alias below, so\n//!     its RED-first tests keep passing with one injection authority).\n//!   * Seam B — the `chaos_point!` macro: an inline injection point for code\n//!     with no trait seam (e.g. mid-commit, inside a `Mutex` critical section).\n//!     That macro and its thread-local plumbing live in the *kernel* shim\n//!     (`dowiz-kernel::chaos`), because they need `std` (`thread_local!`); the\n//!     pure, deterministic schedule machinery below is `no_std`.\n//!\n//! ## Compiled out of production (standard §2 item 6)\n//!\n//! The *kernel* shim gates the whole module `#[cfg(any(test, feature =\n//! "chaos"))]`; in a release build the macro expands to `()` and `ChaosStore`\n//! is absent. This core module is unconditional (it is a pure data structure +\n//! a trait decorator, with no std and no side effects), so the kernel shim's\n//! `pub use dowiz_core::chaos::*;` can gate it as one unit.\n//!\n//! `FaultPlan` draws from the existing seeded [`crate::rng::Rng`] (SplitMix64 →\n//! PCG64), so every fault reproduces bit-identically from `(seed, plan)` — no\n//! wall-clock, no real sleep, no real network (Hermetic P6, Cause-and-Effect).\n//!\n//! Firing is recorded (`insert_calls`, call-count per site) so *ordering*\n//! properties are falsifiable (e.g. A1: the drift gate rejects BEFORE any store\n//! touch ⇒ `ChaosStore.insert_calls == 0`).\n\nuse crate::event_log::{EventStore, MeshEvent, StoreError};\nuse crate::rng::Rng;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Closed set of injection points. Adding a variant is a spec change reviewed\n/// against the P-H blueprint (F32 closed-set discipline, mirroring P24's site\n/// table — these are INJECTION points, distinct from P24's MEASUREMENT sites).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum ChaosSite {\n    /// Inside `ChaosStore::insert` (seam A).\n    StoreInsert,\n    /// Event-log commit path: after `decide` returns `Ok`, before\n    /// `store.insert` (seam B).\n    BetweenDecideAndInsert,\n    /// Spool consumer work: between `claim_next` and `ack` (seam B, driver level).\n    SpoolConsumerWork,\n}\n\n/// Closed enum of injectable faults. THE deliverable type of this phase.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub enum FaultInjection {\n    /// F1 — durability barrier fails: insert returns `Err(StoreError::Sync)`.\n    StoreSyncFail,\n    /// F2 — corrupted state at rest: persist a copy whose payload byte\n    /// `byte_index` is XOR'd by `xor_mask` (deterministic single-byte flip),\n    /// while the content-id passed in stays the one computed from the UN-corrupted\n    /// payload — modelling corruption between hash and persist (torn write, bad\n    /// sector). Detection requires the read-back walk `EventLog::verify_chain`\n    /// (P-H W-H4, **proposal**).\n    CorruptPayload { xor_mask: u8, byte_index: usize },\n    /// F3 — delayed response: a consumer holds a claim for `virtual_ms` of MOCK\n    /// time (no real sleep) before ack/crash — drives reclaim paths.\n    DelayResponse { virtual_ms: u64 },\n    /// F4 — forced panic mid-transaction at the armed site.\n    PanicMidTransaction,\n}\n\n/// When a scheduled fault fires. Deterministic; `Probability` draws from the\n/// seeded PCG64 stream, never from OS entropy.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub enum Trigger {\n    /// Fire on the n-th call (1-indexed) to the given site.\n    OnCall(u32),\n    /// Fire on every n-th call.\n    EveryNth(u32),\n    /// Always fire.\n    Always,\n    /// Fire with probability `p` (0.0..=1.0), drawn from the seeded stream.\n    Probability(f64),\n}\n\n/// A deterministic injection schedule. `seed` fully determines `Probability`\n/// draws; `arms` is consulted per (site, call-count).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct FaultPlan {\n    seed: u64,\n    stream: u64,\n    arms: Vec<(ChaosSite, FaultInjection, Trigger)>,\n    /// Per-(site) call counter, so `OnCall`/`EveryNth` are reproducible.\n    counts: BTreeMap<ChaosSite, u32>,\n}\n\nimpl FaultPlan {\n    /// Empty plan — every `chaos_point!` / `ChaosStore` is inert.\n    pub fn none() -> Self {\n        FaultPlan {\n            seed: 0,\n            stream: 1,\n            arms: Vec::new(),\n            counts: BTreeMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Build a plan from explicit arms. `seed`+`stream` drive any `Probability`\n    /// draws so the schedule is reproducible across runs.\n    pub fn new(seed: u64, stream: u64, arms: Vec<(ChaosSite, FaultInjection, Trigger)>) -> Self {\n        FaultPlan {\n            seed,\n            stream,\n            arms,\n            counts: BTreeMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Consult the plan for `site`, advancing its call counter and returning the\n    /// fault to inject (if any). Pure: no side effects beyond the counter; the\n    /// only entropy is the seeded RNG inside a `Probability` arm.\n    pub fn fire(&mut self, site: ChaosSite) -> Option<FaultInjection> {\n        let call = self.counts.entry(site).or_insert(0);\n        *call = call.saturating_add(1);\n        let n = *call;\n        for (s, fault, trig) in &self.arms {\n            if *s != site {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let hit = match *trig {\n                Trigger::OnCall(k) => n == k,\n                Trigger::EveryNth(k) => k != 0 && n % k == 0,\n                Trigger::Always => true,\n                Trigger::Probability(p) => {\n                    let mut rng =\n                        Rng::new(self.seed ^ 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15, self.stream ^ (n as u64));\n                    rng.next_f64() < p\n                }\n            };\n            if hit {\n                return Some(*fault);\n            }\n        }\n        None\n    }\n}\n\n/// Seam A: the `FaultyStore` generalization. Wraps ANY `EventStore`; consults\n/// the plan at `ChaosSite::StoreInsert`. Records `insert_calls` so ORDERING\n/// properties are falsifiable (see A1: drift-reject ⇒ `insert_calls == 0`).\npub struct ChaosStore<S: EventStore> {\n    pub inner: S,\n    pub plan: FaultPlan,\n    /// Number of times `insert` was *attempted* (consulted the plan), for\n    /// ordering assertions.\n    pub insert_calls: u32,\n    /// When `true`, `CorruptPayload` is applied to the persisted copy so the\n    /// read-back walk (`verify_chain`) is the only observer that sees it.\n    pub corrupt_copy: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<S: EventStore> ChaosStore<S> {\n    /// Wrap `inner` under `plan`. `corrupt_copy` enables F2 (default off).\n    pub fn new(inner: S, plan: FaultPlan) -> Self {\n        ChaosStore {\n            inner,\n            plan,\n            insert_calls: 0,\n            corrupt_copy: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Apply F2: XOR `byte_index` of the payload with `xor_mask`, returning a\n    /// mutated clone (the stored copy diverges from the hash used for the id).\n    fn apply_corrupt(ev: &MeshEvent, xor_mask: u8, byte_index: usize) -> MeshEvent {\n        let mut ev = ev.clone();\n        if byte_index < ev.payload.len() {\n            ev.payload[byte_index] ^= xor_mask;\n        }\n        ev\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<S: EventStore> EventStore for ChaosStore<S> {\n    fn contains(&self, id: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n        self.inner.contains(id)\n    }\n\n    fn insert(&mut self, id: [u8; 32], ev: MeshEvent) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n        self.insert_calls += 1;\n        match self.plan.fire(ChaosSite::StoreInsert) {\n            Some(FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail) => {\n                // F1 — fail the durability barrier WITHOUT touching `inner`.\n                Err(StoreError::Sync("chaos: injected StoreSyncFail".into()))\n            }\n            Some(FaultInjection::CorruptPayload {\n                xor_mask,\n                byte_index,\n            }) if self.corrupt_copy => {\n                // F2 — persist the corrupted twin; the `id` stays uncorrupted,\n                // so a later `verify_chain` walk is the only detector.\n                let corrupted = Self::apply_corrupt(&ev, xor_mask, byte_index);\n                self.inner.insert(id, corrupted)\n            }\n            Some(FaultInjection::PanicMidTransaction) => {\n                panic!("chaos: F4 PanicMidTransaction at StoreInsert");\n            }\n            _ => self.inner.insert(id, ev),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn get(&self, id: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<MeshEvent> {\n        // Mirror the inner store's `get` so F2 corruption is observable via the\n        // read-back walk (W-H4).\n        self.inner.get(id)\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.inner.len()\n    }\n\n    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.inner.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    fn tip(&self) -> Option<[u8; 32]> {\n        self.inner.tip()\n    }\n\n    fn set_tip(&mut self, id: [u8; 32]) {\n        self.inner.set_tip(id);\n    }\n}\n\n/// H1 §4 — the original test-only store whose durability barrier ALWAYS fails,\n/// modelled as a `ChaosStore` over an inert inner store with an `Always`\n/// `StoreSyncFail` arm. Kept as a thin alias so the three pre-existing RED-first\n/// tests (`append_over_faulty_store_surfaces_err_not_fake_committed`,\n/// `commit_after_decide_distinguishes_store_fault_from_law_reject`, and the\n/// `hydra.rs` usage) stay green with ONE injection authority.\n#[cfg(test)]\npub struct FaultyStore {\n    inner: ChaosStore<crate::event_log::MemEventStore>,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nimpl Default for FaultyStore {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nimpl FaultyStore {\n    /// New always-fail store.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        FaultyStore {\n            inner: ChaosStore::new(\n                crate::event_log::MemEventStore::new(),\n                FaultPlan::new(\n                    0,\n                    1,\n                    vec![(\n                        ChaosSite::StoreInsert,\n                        FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail,\n                        Trigger::Always,\n                    )],\n                ),\n            ),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nimpl EventStore for FaultyStore {\n    fn contains(&self, id: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n        self.inner.contains(id)\n    }\n    fn insert(&mut self, id: [u8; 32], ev: MeshEvent) -> Result<(), StoreError> {\n        self.inner.insert(id, ev)\n    }\n    fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.inner.len()\n    }\n    fn tip(&self) -> Option<[u8; 32]> {\n        self.inner.tip()\n    }\n    fn set_tip(&mut self, id: [u8; 32]) {\n        self.inner.set_tip(id);\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fault_plan_oncall_fires_once() {\n        let mut plan = FaultPlan::new(\n            1,\n            1,\n            vec![(\n                ChaosSite::StoreInsert,\n                FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail,\n                Trigger::OnCall(2),\n            )],\n        );\n        assert!(plan.fire(ChaosSite::StoreInsert).is_none()); // call 1\n        assert!(matches!(\n            plan.fire(ChaosSite::StoreInsert),\n            Some(FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail)\n        )); // call 2\n        assert!(plan.fire(ChaosSite::StoreInsert).is_none()); // call 3\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fault_plan_everynth_fires_periodically() {\n        let mut plan = FaultPlan::new(\n            1,\n            1,\n            vec![(\n                ChaosSite::StoreInsert,\n                FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail,\n                Trigger::EveryNth(3),\n            )],\n        );\n        for n in 1..=6 {\n            let hit = plan.fire(ChaosSite::StoreInsert).is_some();\n            assert_eq!(hit, n % 3 == 0, "EveryNth(3) should fire on call {n}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fault_plan_probability_is_seeded() {\n        // Same seed ⇒ identical draw sequence (reproducibility invariant).\n        let draw = |seed| {\n            let mut plan = FaultPlan::new(\n                seed,\n                1,\n                vec![(\n                    ChaosSite::StoreInsert,\n                    FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail,\n                    Trigger::Probability(0.5),\n                )],\n            );\n            (0..8)\n                .map(|_| plan.fire(ChaosSite::StoreInsert).is_some())\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            draw(0xabcd),\n            draw(0xabcd),\n            "Probability draws must be reproducible"\n        );\n        assert_ne!(\n            draw(0xabcd),\n            draw(0xdcba),\n            "different seed ⇒ different sequence"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn chaos_store_always_fail_keeps_tip_stable() {\n        let mut store = ChaosStore::new(\n            crate::event_log::MemEventStore::new(),\n            FaultPlan::new(\n                0,\n                1,\n                vec![(\n                    ChaosSite::StoreInsert,\n                    FaultInjection::StoreSyncFail,\n                    Trigger::Always,\n                )],\n            ),\n        );\n        let id = [7u8; 32];\n        let ev = MeshEvent {\n            prev: [0u8; 32],\n            actor_pubkey: [1u8; 32],\n            actor_seq: 1,\n            payload: b"x".to_vec(),\n        };\n        assert!(store.insert(id, ev).is_err());\n        assert_eq!(store.insert_calls, 1, "insert was attempted exactly once");\n        assert_eq!(store.len(), 0, "no event persisted on a failed barrier");\n    }\n}\n	14325	-1	-1		bb3efd591d8ce1a1ab21b019f516fb1768fe94856d56b686c9576c4481b4ebce5d4035a35ec74eeead5b522b60e68d6ad6f9453f7d681478c06efa8cc7cefcce148c56e9e476c8e5d6893108173b3a49d578ec0a2d91e9cfccb6a1a66a0fc70d7822d2b72dea50b8c8a58e4f3b44469865fbe12b578d2bc807b976fc7320b610

This module holds the parts of the composition root that are\n//! pure data / pure derivation and therefore safe in `no_std`:\n//!\n//!   (i)  the init order declared as a **DAG of plain data** (`NodeId`/`Capability`/\n//!        `InitNode`/`DAG` — source order is irrelevant, the real order is derived\n//!        by topological sort, never by declaration order),\n//!   (ii) [`init_order`] — Kahn topo-sort + cycle detection (fail-closed: a cyclic\n//!        declaration is a typed `InitError::CyclicDependency`, never a boot),\n//!   (iii) [`check_capabilities`] — fail-closed capability check over the derived\n//!        order (a node requiring a capability no upstream node provides refuses),\n//!   (iv)  the `InitError` vocabulary — with `StoreIo(String)` (the rendered io\n//!        error string, so the enum stays `no_std`-compatible), its `Display`\n//!        impl, and its `core::error::Error` impl (the no_std analogue of\n//!        `std::error::Error`, which it satisfies transitively),\n//!   (v)  [`CoreWriteToken`] — the zero-sized in-process write capability (item 65).\n//!\n//! The std-only durable-store wiring (`BootConfig`/`ProductionRoot`/`boot`, i.e.\n//! the `FileEventStore`/`EventLog<FileEventStore>` construction) lives in the\n//! kernel shim `dowiz_kernel::compose`, which starts with\n//! `pub use dowiz_core::compose::*;` and adds the std-only constructor.\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeSet;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::event_log::ChainDefect;\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Closed id/capability vocabulary (scope.rs discipline: pinned discriminants)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Init-graph node id. A closed enum with pinned `repr(u8)` discriminants so a\n/// reorder/rename is a mechanically-caught diff (not a silent renumber).\n#[repr(u8)]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum NodeId {\n    /// Opens the durable `FileEventStore` and wraps it in an `EventLog`.\n    DurableStore = 0,\n    /// Re-verifies the durable chain before it is trusted (`verify_chain`).\n    AuditChain = 1,\n    /// Sole minter of item 65's in-process capability tokens.\n    CapabilityMint = 2,\n}\n\n/// Capabilities a node PROVIDES on init, or REQUIRES before it may init. Closed\n/// enum — a capability no upstream node provides is a fail-closed startup error.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum Capability {\n    /// A live, durable `EventLog<FileEventStore>` exists.\n    DurableEventLog,\n    /// The durable chain has been verified (genesis reachable, no fork/cycle).\n    VerifiedAuditChain,\n    /// The root has minted a zero-sized `CoreWriteToken` (item 65 seam).\n    CoreWriteToken,\n}\n\n/// One node in the init DAG: its id, the nodes it must come *after*, and the\n/// capabilities it requires / provides. Pure data — no runtime graph mutation.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct InitNode {\n    pub id: NodeId,\n    /// Predecessor node ids (declares the ordering edges).\n    pub requires: &'static [NodeId],\n    /// Capabilities this node needs satisfied *before* it inits.\n    pub requires_caps: &'static [Capability],\n    /// Capabilities this node makes available to successors.\n    pub provides: &'static [Capability],\n}\n\n/// The declared production init DAG. Order here is **meaningless** — `init_order`\n/// derives the real sequence from the edges. (Acceptance #3: a permuted\n/// declaration yields the identical derived order.)\n///\n/// `pub` (rather than the original private `const`) so the kernel shim's `boot`\n/// can feed it to [`init_order`]/[`check_capabilities`] — the DAG remains the\n/// single source of truth, declared once here in the core.\npub const DAG: &[InitNode] = &[\n    InitNode {\n        id: NodeId::DurableStore,\n        requires: &[],\n        requires_caps: &[],\n        provides: &[Capability::DurableEventLog],\n    },\n    InitNode {\n        id: NodeId::AuditChain,\n        requires: &[NodeId::DurableStore],\n        requires_caps: &[Capability::DurableEventLog],\n        provides: &[Capability::VerifiedAuditChain],\n    },\n    InitNode {\n        id: NodeId::CapabilityMint,\n        requires: &[NodeId::AuditChain],\n        requires_caps: &[Capability::VerifiedAuditChain],\n        provides: &[Capability::CoreWriteToken],\n    },\n];\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Init errors (fail-closed: absence is a typed startup error, not a None)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum InitError {\n    /// A cyclic `requires` edge was declared — init order is undefined.\n    CyclicDependency(NodeId),\n    /// A node required a capability no already-initialized upstream node provides.\n    CapabilityAbsent {\n        node: NodeId,\n        capability: Capability,\n    },\n    /// The durable store could not be opened (IO / permission / fsync surface).\n    /// Carries the rendered error string (not the non-`no_std` `io::Error`\n    /// itself) so the enum stays core-compatible; the kernel shim renders the\n    /// `io::Error` via `e.to_string()` at the open site.\n    StoreIo(String),\n    /// The durable chain failed verify-chain (corruption / fork / cycle at rest).\n    ChainBroken(ChainDefect),\n}\n\nimpl core::fmt::Display for InitError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            InitError::CyclicDependency(n) => write!(f, "cyclic init dependency at {n:?}"),\n            InitError::CapabilityAbsent { node, capability } => {\n                write!(\n                    f,\n                    "node {node:?} missing required capability {capability:?}"\n                )\n            }\n            InitError::StoreIo(e) => write!(f, "durable store open failed: {e}"),\n            InitError::ChainBroken(d) => write!(f, "durable chain broken: {d:?}"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// `core::error::Error` is the no_std analogue of `std::error::Error` (they are\n// the SAME trait — `std` re-exports `core`'s). Implementing it here keeps\n// `InitError` usable as `Box<dyn std::error::Error>` in std hosts WITHOUT the\n// kernel shim having to add `impl std::error::Error` for a *foreign* type,\n// which the orphan rule (E0117) forbids.\nimpl core::error::Error for InitError {}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Pure graph derivation (Kahn topo-sort + cycle detection over the node DAG)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Map a node id to its index in `dag` (the DAG is the source of truth for ids).\nfn index_of(dag: &[InitNode], id: NodeId) -> usize {\n    dag.iter()\n        .position(|n| n.id == id)\n        .expect("NodeId referenced by an edge must exist in the DAG")\n}\n\n/// Derive the init order from the DAG edges (deliverable (i)/(iii)). A cyclic\n/// declaration returns `InitError::CyclicDependency` — the boot fails closed, the\n/// cycle is never "successfully" booted. Order is a pure function of the edges,\n/// independent of declaration order (acceptance #3).\npub fn init_order(dag: &[InitNode]) -> Result<Vec<NodeId>, InitError> {\n    let n = dag.len();\n    let mut indeg = vec![0usize; n];\n    let mut adj: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n];\n    for (i, node) in dag.iter().enumerate() {\n        for &req in node.requires {\n            let j = index_of(dag, req);\n            adj[j].push(i);\n            indeg[i] += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    // Stable ascending source queue ⇒ deterministic, lowest-id-first order.\n    let mut queue: Vec<usize> = (0..n).filter(|&i| indeg[i] == 0).collect();\n    let mut order: Vec<NodeId> = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n    while let Some(u) = queue.first().copied() {\n        queue.remove(0);\n        order.push(dag[u].id);\n        let mut ready = Vec::new();\n        for &v in &adj[u] {\n            indeg[v] -= 1;\n            if indeg[v] == 0 {\n                ready.push(v);\n            }\n        }\n        queue.extend(ready);\n        queue.sort_unstable(); // keep ascending ⇒ order invariant under permutation\n    }\n    if order.len() != n {\n        // At least one node remains with non-zero in-degree ⇒ a cycle.\n        let stuck = dag\n            .iter()\n            .enumerate()\n            .find(|(i, _)| indeg[*i] != 0)\n            .map(|(_, n)| n.id)\n            .unwrap_or(NodeId::DurableStore);\n        return Err(InitError::CyclicDependency(stuck));\n    }\n    Ok(order)\n}\n\n/// Fail-closed capability check (deliverable (ii)): walk the derived order and\n/// assert every node's `requires_caps` were `provides`-satisfied by an already\n/// initialized upstream node. Absence ⇒ `InitError::CapabilityAbsent`.\npub fn check_capabilities(dag: &[InitNode], order: &[NodeId]) -> Result<(), InitError> {\n    let mut provided: BTreeSet<Capability> = BTreeSet::new();\n    for &id in order {\n        let node = &dag[index_of(dag, id)];\n        for &cap in node.requires_caps {\n            if !provided.contains(&cap) {\n                return Err(InitError::CapabilityAbsent {\n                    node: id,\n                    capability: cap,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n        for &cap in node.provides {\n            provided.insert(cap);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// In-process write capability (item 65 token — minted solely by the root)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Zero-sized in-process write capability (item 65 token — minted solely by the\n/// root). Defined here as the seam; item 65 attaches the real attenuation model.\n/// The token TYPE is public so item 65 (and callers) can name it; the minting\n/// function (`ProductionRoot::mint_core_write`, in the kernel shim) is the\n/// visibility-gated sole constructor.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct CoreWriteToken;\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Acceptance #3 — a permuted declaration yields the identical derived order.\n    #[test]\n    fn permuted_declaration_yields_identical_order() {\n        const PERMUTED: &[InitNode] = &[\n            InitNode {\n                id: NodeId::CapabilityMint,\n                requires: &[NodeId::AuditChain],\n                requires_caps: &[Capability::VerifiedAuditChain],\n                provides: &[Capability::CoreWriteToken],\n            },\n            InitNode {\n                id: NodeId::AuditChain,\n                requires: &[NodeId::DurableStore],\n                requires_caps: &[Capability::DurableEventLog],\n                provides: &[Capability::VerifiedAuditChain],\n            },\n            InitNode {\n                id: NodeId::DurableStore,\n                requires: &[],\n                requires_caps: &[],\n                provides: &[Capability::DurableEventLog],\n            },\n        ];\n        let a = init_order(DAG).unwrap();\n        let b = init_order(PERMUTED).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "order must come from the DAG, not declaration order");\n        assert_eq!(\n            a,\n            vec![\n                NodeId::DurableStore,\n                NodeId::AuditChain,\n                NodeId::CapabilityMint\n            ]\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Acceptance #4 — a node requiring an unsatisfied capability refuses init.\n    #[test]\n    fn unsatisfied_capability_refuses_boot() {\n        // CapabilityMint requires CoreWriteToken, but nothing provides it.\n        const UNDERPROVISIONED: &[InitNode] = &[\n            InitNode {\n                id: NodeId::DurableStore,\n                requires: &[],\n                requires_caps: &[],\n                provides: &[Capability::DurableEventLog],\n            },\n            InitNode {\n                id: NodeId::CapabilityMint,\n                requires: &[NodeId::DurableStore],\n                requires_caps: &[Capability::CoreWriteToken],\n                provides: &[],\n            },\n        ];\n        let order = init_order(UNDERPROVISIONED).unwrap();\n        let err = check_capabilities(UNDERPROVISIONED, &order)\n            .expect_err("unsatisfied capability must fail boot");\n        assert!(\n            matches!(\n                err,\n                InitError::CapabilityAbsent {\n                    node: NodeId::CapabilityMint,\n                    capability: Capability::CoreWriteToken\n                }\n            ),\n            "expected CapabilityAbsent, got {err:?}"\n        );\n    }\n}\n	14343	-1	-1		9f173f87d8020321a18380fd981653479532b5653ddef43a3354ec4f11aee24b5ce1f18386e90a93c54749ea21543c30d7d108a6156a943a5dfbfa0fefdf7acfc6a256f96de7d10817dd330b779ae77af37b5c1a2f87564a98823680f19341477220f3e6815f52e5d949ee1e4a527f10083f6426374401968b13f4d5eb6e3cf3
```
