## 14518 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/krylov.rs · LongTerm

Summary: krylov · 406 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/krylov.rs	krylov · 406 lines	//! krylov.rs — Krylov subspace methods for the no_std core.\n//!\n//! Implements the standard Krylov machinery (AI-tools compendium, Part IV.4):\n//! - [`arnoldi`] — orthonormal basis V + Hessenberg H of K_m(A, v) (general A).\n//! - [`lanczos`] — symmetric tridiagonalization α/β of K_m(A, v).\n//! - [`cg`] — conjugate-gradient solver for SPD systems.\n//! - [`gmres`] — restarted GMRES for general (non-symmetric) systems via\n//!   Arnoldi + Givens-rotation least squares.\n//!\n//! All operations are `no_std`; dot products reuse [`crate::householder::dot`]\n//! and norms reuse the bit-exact [`crate::math::sqrt`]. Matrices are dense\n//! row-major `&[Vec<f64>]` (matching the `spectral` module convention).\n\nuse crate::householder::dot;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Dense row-major matrix-vector product y = A·x.\nfn matvec(a: &[Vec<f64>], x: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64> {\n    a.iter().map(|row| dot(row, x)).collect()\n}\n\n/// Euclidean norm ‖x‖.\nfn norm(x: &[f64]) -> f64 {\n    crate::math::sqrt(dot(x, x))\n}\n\n/// axpy: y += α·x (in place).\nfn axpy(y: &mut [f64], alpha: f64, x: &[f64]) {\n    for (yi, xi) in y.iter_mut().zip(x.iter()) {\n        *yi += alpha * xi;\n    }\n}\n\n/// x ← α·x (in place).\nfn scale(x: &mut [f64], alpha: f64) {\n    for xi in x.iter_mut() {\n        *xi *= alpha;\n    }\n}\n\n/// r = b − A·x (residual of a dense linear system).\nfn residual(a: &[Vec<f64>], b: &[f64], x: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64> {\n    let ax = matvec(a, x);\n    b.iter().zip(ax.iter()).map(|(bi, axi)| bi - axi).collect()\n}\n\n/// Outcome of an iterative solver run.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct SolveOutcome {\n    pub x: Vec<f64>,\n    pub iterations: usize,\n    pub converged: bool,\n    pub residual: f64,\n}\n\n/// Conjugate gradient for SPD systems Ax = b.\n///\n/// `tol` is the relative residual threshold ‖r‖/‖b‖; iteration stops early on\n/// a happy breakdown (exact solution reached).\npub fn cg(a: &[Vec<f64>], b: &[f64], x0: &[f64], tol: f64, max_iter: usize) -> SolveOutcome {\n    let n = b.len();\n    let mut x = x0.to_vec();\n    let mut r = residual(a, b, &x);\n    let bnorm = norm(b);\n    let mut p = r.clone();\n    let mut rsold = dot(&r, &r);\n\n    for it in 0..max_iter {\n        let ap = matvec(a, &p);\n        let pap = dot(&p, &ap);\n        if pap == 0.0 {\n            break;\n        }\n        let alpha = rsold / pap;\n        axpy(&mut x, alpha, &p);\n        axpy(&mut r, -alpha, &ap);\n        let rsnew = dot(&r, &r);\n        if crate::math::sqrt(rsnew) <= tol * bnorm.max(1.0) {\n            return SolveOutcome {\n                x,\n                iterations: it + 1,\n                converged: true,\n                residual: crate::math::sqrt(rsnew),\n            };\n        }\n        let beta = rsnew / rsold;\n        // p = r + beta·p\n        for i in 0..n {\n            p[i] = r[i] + beta * p[i];\n        }\n        rsold = rsnew;\n    }\n\n    let res = norm(&residual(a, b, &x));\n    SolveOutcome {\n        converged: res <= tol * bnorm.max(1.0),\n        residual: res,\n        x,\n        iterations: max_iter,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Arnoldi process: orthonormal basis V of K_{m+1}(A, v) and Hessenberg H.\n///\n/// Returns `(V, H)` where `V` has up to `m + 1` orthonormal columns and `H` is\n/// `(m + 1) × m` upper Hessenberg (with a happy-breakdown shortcut). Uses\n/// modified Gram–Schmidt for numerical stability.\npub fn arnoldi(a: &[Vec<f64>], v1: &[f64], m: usize) -> (Vec<Vec<f64>>, Vec<Vec<f64>>) {\n    let n = v1.len();\n    let beta = norm(v1);\n    let mut v: Vec<Vec<f64>> = Vec::new();\n    if beta > 0.0 {\n        v.push(v1.iter().map(|xi| xi / beta).collect());\n    } else {\n        v.push(vec![0.0; n]);\n    }\n    let mut h: Vec<Vec<f64>> = Vec::with_capacity(m + 1);\n    for _ in 0..=m {\n        h.push(vec![0.0; m]);\n    }\n\n    for j in 0..m {\n        let mut w = matvec(a, &v[j]);\n        for i in 0..=j {\n            h[i][j] = dot(&v[i], &w);\n            axpy(&mut w, -h[i][j], &v[i]);\n        }\n        let hjj1 = norm(&w);\n        h[j + 1][j] = hjj1;\n        if hjj1 > 1e-14 {\n            scale(&mut w, 1.0 / hjj1);\n            v.push(w);\n        } else {\n            break; // happy breakdown\n        }\n    }\n    (v, h)\n}\n\n/// Lanczos tridiagonalization for a symmetric matrix: returns `(alpha, beta)`.\n///\n/// `alpha` is the diagonal and `beta` the sub-diagonal of the tridiagonal\n/// projection T_m = VᵀAV. Only the upper triangle of `a` is used.\npub fn lanczos(a: &[Vec<f64>], v1: &[f64], m: usize) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {\n    let n = v1.len();\n    let b0 = norm(v1);\n    let mut alpha = Vec::with_capacity(m);\n    let mut beta: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(m);\n\n    let mut v_prev: Vec<f64> = vec![0.0; n];\n    let mut v: Vec<f64> = if b0 > 0.0 {\n        v1.iter().map(|xi| xi / b0).collect()\n    } else {\n        vec![0.0; n]\n    };\n    let mut b_cur = b0;\n\n    for j in 0..m {\n        let mut w = matvec(a, &v);\n        let aj = dot(&v, &w);\n        alpha.push(aj);\n        // w = w − α_j·v − β_j·v_prev\n        axpy(&mut w, -aj, &v);\n        axpy(&mut w, -b_cur, &v_prev);\n        let b_next = norm(&w);\n        if b_next <= 1e-14 {\n            break; // happy breakdown — tridiagonalization complete\n        }\n        beta.push(b_next);\n        scale(&mut w, 1.0 / b_next);\n        v_prev = v;\n        v = w;\n        b_cur = b_next;\n    }\n    (alpha, beta)\n}\n\n/// Restarted GMRES for general (non-symmetric) systems Ax = b.\n///\n/// Each restart builds a Krylov basis of size `restart` via [`arnoldi`] and\n/// solves the small least-squares problem with Givens rotations.\npub fn gmres(\n    a: &[Vec<f64>],\n    b: &[f64],\n    x0: &[f64],\n    restart: usize,\n    tol: f64,\n    max_iter: usize,\n) -> SolveOutcome {\n    let n = b.len();\n    let bnorm = norm(b).max(1.0);\n    let mut x = x0.to_vec();\n\n    for _ in 0..max_iter.div_ceil(restart).max(1) {\n        let r = residual(a, b, &x);\n        let beta = norm(&r);\n        if beta <= tol * bnorm {\n            return SolveOutcome {\n                x,\n                iterations: 0,\n                converged: true,\n                residual: beta,\n            };\n        }\n        let v1: Vec<f64> = r.iter().map(|ri| ri / beta).collect();\n        let (v, h) = arnoldi(a, &v1, restart);\n        // Krylov dimension: `v.len()` is restart+1 without a breakdown, or\n        // j+1 after a happy breakdown (where the space is A-invariant and the\n        // least-squares collapses to a square solve).\n        let nrows = v.len();\n        let k = nrows.min(restart);\n        if k == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n\n        // Solve min ‖H y − β e1‖ with Givens rotations. The Hessenberg block\n        // has `nrows` rows and `k` columns (restart+1 × restart, or k × k on\n        // breakdown).\n        let mut g: Vec<f64> = vec![0.0; nrows];\n        g[0] = beta;\n        let mut hb: Vec<Vec<f64>> = h[..nrows].iter().map(|row| row[..k].to_vec()).collect();\n        for i in 0..k.min(nrows - 1) {\n            let (c, s) = givens(hb[i][i], hb[i + 1][i]);\n            for j in i..k {\n                let (a_ij, a_i1j) = rotate(c, s, hb[i][j], hb[i + 1][j]);\n                hb[i][j] = a_ij;\n                hb[i + 1][j] = a_i1j;\n            }\n            let (gi, gi1) = rotate(c, s, g[i], g[i + 1]);\n            g[i] = gi;\n            g[i + 1] = gi1;\n        }\n        // Back-substitute y from the upper-triangular R (first k rows).\n        let mut y = vec![0.0; k];\n        for i in (0..k).rev() {\n            let mut s = g[i];\n            for j in (i + 1)..k {\n                s -= hb[i][j] * y[j];\n            }\n            if hb[i][i] != 0.0 {\n                y[i] = s / hb[i][i];\n            }\n        }\n        // x += V_k y\n        for j in 0..k {\n            axpy(&mut x, y[j], &v[j]);\n        }\n\n        let res = norm(&residual(a, b, &x));\n        if res <= tol * bnorm {\n            return SolveOutcome {\n                x,\n                iterations: 0,\n                converged: true,\n                residual: res,\n            };\n        }\n    }\n\n    let res = norm(&residual(a, b, &x));\n    SolveOutcome {\n        x,\n        iterations: max_iter,\n        converged: res <= tol * bnorm,\n        residual: res,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Givens rotation (c, s) that zeroes the second component of (a, b).\nfn givens(a: f64, b: f64) -> (f64, f64) {\n    if b == 0.0 {\n        return (1.0, 0.0);\n    }\n    if a.abs() >= b.abs() {\n        let t = b / a;\n        let c = 1.0 / crate::math::sqrt(1.0 + t * t);\n        (c, c * t)\n    } else {\n        let t = a / b;\n        let s = 1.0 / crate::math::sqrt(1.0 + t * t);\n        (s * t, s)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Apply a Givens rotation [c, -s; s, c] to (x, y).\nfn rotate(c: f64, s: f64, x: f64, y: f64) -> (f64, f64) {\n    (c * x + s * y, -s * x + c * y)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn close(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {\n        (a - b).abs() < 1e-9\n    }\n\n    fn close_vec(a: &[f64], b: &[f64]) -> bool {\n        a.len() == b.len() && a.iter().zip(b.iter()).all(|(x, y)| close(*x, *y))\n    }\n\n    /// 2×2 SPD matrix [[4,1],[1,3]].\n    fn spd2() -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n        vec![vec![4.0, 1.0], vec![1.0, 3.0]]\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cg_solves_spd_system() {\n        let a = spd2();\n        let b = vec![1.0, 2.0];\n        let out = cg(&a, &b, &[0.0, 0.0], 1e-12, 50);\n        assert!(out.converged);\n        // exact: solve [4x+y=1, x+3y=2] -> x=1/11, y=7/11\n        assert!(close_vec(&out.x, &[1.0 / 11.0, 7.0 / 11.0]));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cg_solves_1d_laplacian() {\n        // tridiagonal SPD Laplacian 5×5 (diag 2, off-diag −1).\n        let n = 5;\n        let mut a = vec![vec![0.0; n]; n];\n        for i in 0..n {\n            a[i][i] = 2.0;\n            if i > 0 {\n                a[i][i - 1] = -1.0;\n            }\n            if i + 1 < n {\n                a[i][i + 1] = -1.0;\n            }\n        }\n        let b: Vec<f64> = (1..=n).map(|k| k as f64).collect();\n        let out = cg(&a, &b, &vec![0.0; n], 1e-12, 100);\n        assert!(out.converged);\n        // check residual is small\n        assert!(out.residual < 1e-10);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn arnoldi_basis_is_orthonormal() {\n        // non-symmetric 3×3\n        let a = vec![\n            vec![2.0, 1.0, 0.0],\n            vec![0.0, 2.0, 1.0],\n            vec![1.0, 0.0, 2.0],\n        ];\n        let v1 = vec![1.0, 0.0, 0.0];\n        let (v, h) = arnoldi(&a, &v1, 2);\n        assert!(v.len() >= 3);\n        // columns orthonormal\n        for i in 0..v.len() {\n            for j in 0..v.len() {\n                let ip = dot(&v[i], &v[j]);\n                if i == j {\n                    assert!(close(ip, 1.0), "v[{i}] norm != 1: {ip}");\n                } else {\n                    assert!(close(ip, 0.0), "v[{i}]·v[{j}] != 0: {ip}");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // H is upper Hessenberg: h[i][j] == 0 for i > j+1\n        for j in 0..2 {\n            for i in (j + 2)..h.len() {\n                assert!(close(h[i][j], 0.0));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn lanczos_produces_tridiagonal_projection() {\n        let a = spd2();\n        let v1 = vec![1.0, 0.0];\n        let (alpha, beta) = lanczos(&a, &v1, 2);\n        assert_eq!(alpha.len(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(beta.len(), 1);\n        // first alpha = v1^T A v1 = a[0][0] = 4.0\n        assert!(close(alpha[0], 4.0));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn gmres_solves_nonsymmetric_system() {\n        // non-symmetric: [[3,1],[0,2]] x = [5,4] -> x = [1,2]\n        let a = vec![vec![3.0, 1.0], vec![0.0, 2.0]];\n        let b = vec![5.0, 4.0];\n        let out = gmres(&a, &b, &[0.0, 0.0], 2, 1e-12, 20);\n        assert!(out.converged, "residual {}", out.residual);\n        assert!(close_vec(&out.x, &[1.0, 2.0]));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn gmres_solves_spd_too() {\n        let a = spd2();\n        let b = vec![1.0, 2.0];\n        let out = gmres(&a, &b, &[0.0, 0.0], 2, 1e-12, 20);\n        assert!(out.converged);\n        assert!(close_vec(&out.x, &[1.0 / 11.0, 7.0 / 11.0]));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn matvec_matches_dense_definition() {\n        let a = spd2();\n        let x = vec![3.0, -1.0];\n        let y = matvec(&a, &x);\n        assert!(close(y[0], 4.0 * 3.0 + 1.0 * -1.0)); // 11\n        assert!(close(y[1], 1.0 * 3.0 + 3.0 * -1.0)); // 0\n    }\n}\n	14519	-1	-1		c376366ed89ea7b54b01f0c25212193b255c55e5ad72f4e2ed4ec218a1effd53418472c1fddb800ee057540791e9faacd22539f4f56809a8e3e0e283cc94af44f38f54b96538b8391951301bd72be9d2cdf0c83e69918f69d02206965809b365a4e6d655b1cb932df8888c470edc1d9d61b545709da2cc945761cc512a942120
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/code_graph.rs	code_graph · 320 lines	//! code_graph.rs — native graphify port: a queryable code knowledge graph.\n//!\n//! Reverse-engineered from `Graphify-Labs/graphify` (knowledge-graph-over-\n//! codebase, "query instead of grep"). Stores code entities (nodes) and typed\n//! relationships (edges), and answers the navigation queries the living-memory\n//! graph needs at every level: neighbours, shortest path, radius subgraph,\n//! PageRank importance (via [`crate::csr`]), and deterministic label-propagation\n//! communities. no_std (alloc only).\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// What kind of code entity a node is.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum NodeKind {\n    Function,\n    Struct,\n    Enum,\n    Module,\n    Trait,\n    Concept,\n    File,\n    Other,\n}\n\n/// What kind of relationship an edge is.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum EdgeKind {\n    Calls,\n    References,\n    Contains,\n    Imports,\n    Uses,\n}\n\n/// A code entity (or extracted concept) in the graph.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CodeNode {\n    pub name: String,\n    pub kind: NodeKind,\n    /// Community id (assigned by [`CodeGraph::label_propagation`]).\n    pub community: usize,\n}\n\n/// A typed directed relationship between two nodes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CodeEdge {\n    pub from: usize,\n    pub to: usize,\n    pub kind: EdgeKind,\n}\n\n/// A queryable directed knowledge graph over code entities.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct CodeGraph {\n    nodes: Vec<CodeNode>,\n    edges: Vec<CodeEdge>,\n    /// node id → indices into `edges` (out-edges).\n    adj: Vec<Vec<usize>>,\n}\n\nimpl CodeGraph {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Add a node; returns its id.\n    pub fn add_node(&mut self, name: &str, kind: NodeKind) -> usize {\n        let id = self.nodes.len();\n        self.nodes.push(CodeNode {\n            name: String::from(name),\n            kind,\n            community: id,\n        });\n        self.adj.push(Vec::new());\n        id\n    }\n\n    /// Add a directed edge; returns its index. Node ids must already exist.\n    pub fn add_edge(&mut self, from: usize, to: usize, kind: EdgeKind) -> usize {\n        let e = self.edges.len();\n        self.edges.push(CodeEdge { from, to, kind });\n        self.adj[from].push(e);\n        e\n    }\n\n    pub fn node_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.nodes.len()\n    }\n    pub fn edge_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.edges.len()\n    }\n    pub fn node(&self, id: usize) -> Option<&CodeNode> {\n        self.nodes.get(id)\n    }\n    pub fn nodes(&self) -> &[CodeNode] {\n        &self.nodes\n    }\n    pub fn edges(&self) -> &[CodeEdge] {\n        &self.edges\n    }\n\n    /// Out-neighbour node ids (deduplicated, in edge order).\n    pub fn neighbors(&self, id: usize) -> Vec<usize> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        for &e in &self.adj[id] {\n            let to = self.edges[e].to;\n            if !out.contains(&to) {\n                out.push(to);\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// Breadth-first shortest path from `from` to `to` (node ids inclusive).\n    pub fn shortest_path(&self, from: usize, to: usize) -> Option<Vec<usize>> {\n        let n = self.nodes.len();\n        let mut prev: Vec<Option<usize>> = vec![None; n];\n        let mut visited = vec![false; n];\n        let mut queue = alloc::collections::VecDeque::new();\n        visited[from] = true;\n        queue.push_back(from);\n        while let Some(u) = queue.pop_front() {\n            if u == to {\n                break;\n            }\n            for v in self.neighbors(u) {\n                if !visited[v] {\n                    visited[v] = true;\n                    prev[v] = Some(u);\n                    queue.push_back(v);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        if !visited[to] {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let mut path = Vec::new();\n        let mut cur = to;\n        while cur != from {\n            path.push(cur);\n            cur = prev[cur]?;\n        }\n        path.push(from);\n        path.reverse();\n        Some(path)\n    }\n\n    /// All nodes within `radius` hops of `id` (including `id`), sorted by id.\n    pub fn subgraph_around(&self, id: usize, radius: usize) -> Vec<usize> {\n        let n = self.nodes.len();\n        let mut dist = vec![usize::MAX; n];\n        let mut queue = alloc::collections::VecDeque::new();\n        dist[id] = 0;\n        queue.push_back(id);\n        while let Some(u) = queue.pop_front() {\n            if dist[u] >= radius {\n                continue;\n            }\n            for v in self.neighbors(u) {\n                if dist[v] == usize::MAX {\n                    dist[v] = dist[u] + 1;\n                    queue.push_back(v);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        let mut out: Vec<usize> = (0..n).filter(|&i| dist[i] != usize::MAX).collect();\n        out.sort_unstable();\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// PageRank importance per node (reuses [`crate::csr::Csr::personalized_pagerank`]).\n    pub fn pagerank(&self, alpha: f64, iters: usize) -> Vec<f64> {\n        let n = self.nodes.len();\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n        let edges: Vec<(usize, usize, f64)> =\n            self.edges.iter().map(|e| (e.from, e.to, 1.0)).collect();\n        let csr = crate::csr::Csr::from_edges(n, &edges);\n        let seed = vec![1.0 / n as f64; n];\n        csr.personalized_pagerank(&seed, alpha, iters)\n    }\n\n    /// Deterministic label propagation: assign each node to its dominant\n    /// neighbour community (ties resolve to the smallest id). Updates\n    /// `CodeNode::community` and returns the per-node community ids.\n    pub fn label_propagation(&mut self, iters: usize) -> Vec<usize> {\n        let n = self.nodes.len();\n        let mut labels: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();\n        let mut counts: Vec<usize> = vec![0; n];\n        for _ in 0..iters {\n            let mut changed = false;\n            for u in 0..n {\n                // Count neighbour labels.\n                for &e in &self.adj[u] {\n                    let v = self.edges[e].to;\n                    counts[labels[v]] += 1;\n                }\n                // Pick the most common (ties → smallest label).\n                let mut best = labels[u];\n                let mut best_c = 0usize;\n                for l in 0..n {\n                    if counts[l] > best_c {\n                        best = l;\n                        best_c = counts[l];\n                    }\n                }\n                // Reset counts for the next node.\n                for &e in &self.adj[u] {\n                    let v = self.edges[e].to;\n                    counts[labels[v]] = 0;\n                }\n                if best != labels[u] {\n                    labels[u] = best;\n                    changed = true;\n                }\n            }\n            if !changed {\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n        for (i, node) in self.nodes.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n            node.community = labels[i];\n        }\n        labels\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn close(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {\n        (a - b).abs() < 1e-9\n    }\n\n    fn build_graph() -> CodeGraph {\n        let mut g = CodeGraph::new();\n        // 0 -> 1 -> 2, and 0 -> 3 (a branch)\n        let a = g.add_node("main", NodeKind::Function);\n        let b = g.add_node("parse", NodeKind::Function);\n        let c = g.add_node("tokenize", NodeKind::Function);\n        let d = g.add_node("log", NodeKind::Function);\n        g.add_edge(a, b, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        g.add_edge(b, c, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        g.add_edge(a, d, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        g\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn shortest_path_follows_edges() {\n        let g = build_graph();\n        let p = g.shortest_path(0, 2).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(p, vec![0, 1, 2]);\n        // 0 -> 3 is direct.\n        let p2 = g.shortest_path(0, 3).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(p2, vec![0, 3]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn no_path_returns_none() {\n        let g = build_graph();\n        assert!(g.shortest_path(3, 1).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn subgraph_around_radius() {\n        let g = build_graph();\n        // radius 0 = just node 0; radius 1 = 0,1,3; radius 2 = all.\n        assert_eq!(g.subgraph_around(0, 0), vec![0]);\n        assert_eq!(g.subgraph_around(0, 1), vec![0, 1, 3]);\n        assert_eq!(g.subgraph_around(0, 2), vec![0, 1, 2, 3]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pagerank_scores_connected_nodes() {\n        let g = build_graph();\n        let pr = g.pagerank(0.85, 20);\n        assert_eq!(pr.len(), 4);\n        let sum: f64 = pr.iter().sum();\n        assert!(close(sum, 1.0), "sum={sum}");\n        for p in &pr {\n            assert!(*p > 0.0);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn label_propagation_groups_connected_nodes() {\n        let mut g = CodeGraph::new();\n        // Component A: 0 <-> 1 <-> 2 (mutual edges).\n        let a = g.add_node("a", NodeKind::Function);\n        let b = g.add_node("b", NodeKind::Function);\n        let c = g.add_node("c", NodeKind::Function);\n        // Component B: 3 <-> 4 (disjoint from A).\n        let d = g.add_node("d", NodeKind::Function);\n        let e = g.add_node("e", NodeKind::Function);\n        g.add_edge(a, b, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        g.add_edge(b, a, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        g.add_edge(b, c, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        g.add_edge(c, b, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        g.add_edge(d, e, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        g.add_edge(e, d, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        let labels = g.label_propagation(10);\n        // A and B are disjoint components → same label within, different across.\n        assert!(labels[a] == labels[b] && labels[b] == labels[c]);\n        assert!(labels[d] == labels[e]);\n        assert!(labels[a] != labels[d]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn neighbors_dedupes_parallel_edges() {\n        let mut g = CodeGraph::new();\n        let a = g.add_node("a", NodeKind::Function);\n        let b = g.add_node("b", NodeKind::Function);\n        g.add_edge(a, b, EdgeKind::Calls);\n        g.add_edge(a, b, EdgeKind::References);\n        assert_eq!(g.neighbors(a), vec![b]);\n pub fn plus() -> Self {\n        let s = crate::math::sqrt(0.5);\n        Self::new(Complex::new(s, 0.0), Complex::new(s, 0.0))\n    }\n\n    /// Equal superposition |-⟩ = (|0⟩ − |1⟩)/√2.\n    pub fn ## 14658 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/context_pruner.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: context_pruner · 253 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/context_pruner.rs	context_pruner · 253 lines	//! context_pruner.rs — headroom-style line-importance pruning (native port).\n//!\n//! Reverse-engineered from `headroomlabs-ai/headroom` (Apache-2.0): score each\n//! line of tool output / logs / diffs / prose by an importance signal, then drop\n//! the lowest-priority lines to fit a token budget. This is the token-saving core\n//! Hermes runs "always on" before injecting tool results into context.\n//!\n//! Zero dependencies: byte-level case-insensitive keyword matching over the\n//! error/warning/security/importance/markdown signal sets; a cheap chars/4 token\n//! estimator. Reuses the crate's no_std conventions.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Content kind — picks which keyword set fires.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum PruneContext {\n    /// Free-form prose / markdown — structure matters.\n    Text,\n    /// grep/ripgrep output — error/warn keywords win.\n    Search,\n    /// git diff — error + security + importance keywords.\n    Diff,\n    /// Log output — error/warn keywords + level prefixes.\n    Log,\n}\n\n/// Why a line earned its priority.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ImportanceCategory {\n    Error,\n    Warning,\n    Importance,\n    Security,\n    Markdown,\n}\n\n/// One detector's verdict for one line.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub struct ImportanceSignal {\n    pub category: Option<ImportanceCategory>,\n    /// 0.0 = drop first, 1.0 = keep at all costs.\n    pub priority: f32,\n    /// 0.0 = no information, 1.0 = the detector is sure.\n    pub confidence: f32,\n}\n\nimpl ImportanceSignal {\n    pub const fn neutral() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            category: None,\n            priority: 0.2,\n            confidence: 0.0,\n        }\n    }\n    pub const fn matched(category: ImportanceCategory, priority: f32, confidence: f32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            category: Some(category),\n            priority,\n            confidence,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Keyword sets (lowercased ASCII).\nconst SECURITY: &[&str] = &[\n    "password",\n    "secret",\n    "token",\n    "credential",\n    "api key",\n    "apikey",\n    "private key",\n];\nconst ERROR: &[&str] = &[\n    "error",\n    "panic",\n    "fatal",\n    "exception",\n    "traceback",\n    "failed",\n    "failure",\n    "abort",\n    "cannot",\n    "could not",\n];\nconst WARNING: &[&str] = &["warn", "warning", "deprecated", "caution", "deprecat"];\nconst IMPORTANCE: &[&str] = &[\n    "todo",\n    "fixme",\n    "hack",\n    "important",\n    "critical",\n    "urgent",\n    "must",\n    "required",\n];\n\n/// Byte-level case-insensitive substring search (no alloc, no_std).\nfn contains_ci(hay: &str, needle: &str) -> bool {\n    let h = hay.as_bytes();\n    let n = needle.as_bytes();\n    if n.is_empty() {\n        return true;\n    }\n    if n.len() > h.len() {\n        return false;\n    }\n    'outer: for i in 0..=(h.len() - n.len()) {\n        for j in 0..n.len() {\n            if h[i + j].to_ascii_lowercase() != n[j].to_ascii_lowercase() {\n                continue 'outer;\n            }\n        }\n        return true;\n    }\n    false\n}\n\n/// Classify a single line's importance for the given context.\npub fn classify_line(line: &str, ctx: PruneContext) -> ImportanceSignal {\n    let l = line.trim();\n    if l.is_empty() {\n        return ImportanceSignal::neutral();\n    }\n    // Security keywords fire in every context (highest stakes).\n    for kw in SECURITY {\n        if contains_ci(l, kw) {\n            return ImportanceSignal::matched(ImportanceCategory::Security, 1.0, 0.9);\n        }\n    }\n    match ctx {\n        PruneContext::Text => {\n            if l.starts_with('#') {\n                return ImportanceSignal::matched(ImportanceCategory::Markdown, 0.6, 0.9);\n            }\n            if l.starts_with("**") || l.starts_with('>') {\n                return ImportanceSignal::matched(ImportanceCategory::Markdown, 0.5, 0.8);\n            }\n            for kw in IMPORTANCE {\n                if contains_ci(l, kw) {\n                    return ImportanceSignal::matched(ImportanceCategory::Importance, 0.7, 0.8);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        PruneContext::Search | PruneContext::Diff | PruneContext::Log => {\n            // Level prefixes win first in logs (e.g. "ERROR:", "[WARN]").\n            if ctx == PruneContext::Log {\n                let up = l.to_ascii_uppercase();\n                if up.contains("ERROR") || up.contains("FATAL") || up.contains("PANIC") {\n                    return ImportanceSignal::matched(ImportanceCategory::Error, 1.0, 0.95);\n                }\n                if up.contains("WARN") {\n                    return ImportanceSignal::matched(ImportanceCategory::Warning, 0.8, 0.9);\n                }\n            }\n            for kw in ERROR {\n                if contains_ci(l, kw) {\n                    return ImportanceSignal::matched(ImportanceCategory::Error, 1.0, 0.95);\n                }\n            }\n            for kw in WARNING {\n                if contains_ci(l, kw) {\n                    return ImportanceSignal::matched(ImportanceCategory::Warning, 0.8, 0.9);\n                }\n            }\n            for kw in IMPORTANCE {\n                if contains_ci(l, kw) {\n                    return ImportanceSignal::matched(ImportanceCategory::Importance, 0.7, 0.8);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    ImportanceSignal::neutral()\n}\n\n/// Cheap token estimate: ~4 chars/token (matches headroom's no-tokenizer fallback).\nfn est_tokens(line: &str) -> usize {\n    line.len() / 4 + 1\n}\n\n/// Prune a context chunk to a token budget, keeping the highest-priority lines\n/// and preserving their original order. Returns the kept lines.\npub fn prune_lines<'a>(lines: &[&'a str], ctx: PruneContext, budget_tokens: usize) -> Vec<&'a str> {\n    // (index, priority, cost, line)\n    let mut scored: Vec<(usize, f32, usize, &'a str)> = lines\n        .iter()\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(i, l)| (i, classify_line(l, ctx).priority, est_tokens(l), *l))\n        .collect();\n    // Stable sort by priority descending (ties keep original order).\n    scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(core::cmp::Ordering::Equal));\n\n    let mut kept: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();\n    let mut used = 0usize;\n    for (i, _p, cost, _l) in &scored {\n        if used + cost <= budget_tokens {\n            used += cost;\n            kept.push(*i);\n        }\n    }\n    // Preserve original order in the output.\n    kept.sort_unstable();\n    kept.into_iter().map(|i| lines[i]).collect()\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn error_lines_outrank_neutral_lines() {\n        let e = classify_line("ERROR: connection refused", PruneContext::Log);\n        let n = classify_line("debug trace", PruneContext::Log);\n        assert_eq!(e.category, Some(ImportanceCategory::Error));\n        assert!(e.priority > n.priority);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn security_fires_in_all_contexts() {\n        let s = classify_line("api key leaked here", PruneContext::Text);\n        assert_eq!(s.category, Some(ImportanceCategory::Security));\n        assert_eq!(s.priority, 1.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn markdown_headers_count_in_text_only() {\n        let s = classify_line("## Section", PruneContext::Text);\n        assert_eq!(s.category, Some(ImportanceCategory::Markdown));\n        // In diff context, "##" is not a header signal.\n        let d = classify_line("## Section", PruneContext::Diff);\n        assert_eq!(d.category, None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn prune_preserves_original_order() {\n        let lines = ["a", "ERROR b", "c", "WARN d", "e"];\n        let kept = prune_lines(&lines, PruneContext::Log, 4);\n        assert_eq!(kept, vec!["ERROR b", "WARN d"]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn contains_ci_matches_case_insensitively() {\n        assert!(contains_ci("PANIC: boom", "panic"));\n        assert!(contains_ci("FooBar", "foobar"));\n        assert!(!contains_ci("hello", "world"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn token_estimate_is_positive() {\n        assert!(est_tokens("") >= 1);\n        assert!(est_tokens("a long line of text") > 3);\n    }\n}\n	14659	-1	-1		eb743ecff4caa7f5880fabc323628a03495694eda812ef02ed5fe847d36c3cf119c4b40049cfc673c17750299334d028eff757f4746a87ebb57e2a0fe406adec9f8c57d04d3f106991c53473b5bba0c978e8fc3a295a226fc80220f4591b153480e2d24637cb935dba08c81f661017d1643145757ce0d4709df1f6113a803970
```

## 14677 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ntt.rs · LongTerm

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ntt.rs	ntt · 261 lines	//! ntt.rs — Number-Theoretic Transform (NTT) + exact integer convolution.\n//!\n//! The exact-integer counterpart to `crate::fft` (float Cooley–Tukey). Where the\n//! FFT runs over `Complex` (f64) and accumulates rounding error, the NTT runs\n//! over `Z/pZ` for the NTT-friendly prime `p = 998244353 = 2^23·119 + 1` and is\n//! **exact**: every intermediate product stays in `[0, p)` with no float noise.\n//!\n//! This is what "geometry over algebra" becomes when the geometry is a\n//! hypervector: a 1024-bit binary vector is a polynomial over `F_p`, and its\n//! circular cross-correlation (shift-invariant similarity) is a polynomial\n//! multiplication — O(D²) naïve, O(D log D) via NTT. For D = 1024 the transform\n//! length is 2048 = 2^11, well under the prime's 2^23 root-of-unity ceiling, so\n//! every butterfly is a single `mulmod` — no multi-prime CRT, no float fallback.\n//!\n//! # Zero-dep invariant\n//! Pure `core` + `alloc`. Deterministic (fixed summation/combination order, no\n//! SIMD, no fast-math) — bit-reproducible across native / wasm32.\n\nuse alloc::vec;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// NTT-friendly prime: `998244353 = 2^23 · 119 + 1`. Supports transform\n/// lengths up to `2^23`.\npub const MOD: u64 = 998_244_353;\n/// Primitive root of unity modulo [`MOD`] (3 is a primitive root).\npub const ROOT: u64 = 3;\n\n/// Modular exponentiation `base^exp mod m` (square-and-multiply).\npub fn mod_pow(mut base: u64, mut exp: u64, m: u64) -> u64 {\n    base %= m;\n    let mut result = 1u64;\n    while exp > 0 {\n        if exp & 1 == 1 {\n            result = result * base % m;\n        }\n        base = base * base % m;\n        exp >>= 1;\n    }\n    result\n}\n\n/// Modular inverse via Fermat's little theorem (`m` must be prime).\npub fn mod_inv(a: u64, m: u64) -> u64 {\n    mod_pow(a, m - 2, m)\n}\n\n/// In-place iterative NTT / inverse-NTT over `MOD`. `a.len()` must be a power\n/// of two. All elements are reduced into `[0, MOD)` on input.\npub fn ntt(a: &mut [u64], invert: bool) {\n    let n = a.len();\n    debug_assert!(n.is_power_of_two(), "NTT length must be a power of two");\n\n    // Reduce inputs into the field (callers may pass raw bit counts).\n    for x in a.iter_mut() {\n        *x %= MOD;\n    }\n\n    // Bit-reversal permutation.\n    let mut j = 0usize;\n    for i in 1..n {\n        let mut bit = n >> 1;\n        while j & bit != 0 {\n            j ^= bit;\n            bit >>= 1;\n        }\n        j ^= bit;\n        if i < j {\n            a.swap(i, j);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Butterfly stages.\n    let mut len = 2usize;\n    while len <= n {\n        let root = mod_pow(ROOT, (MOD - 1) / len as u64, MOD);\n        let wlen = if invert { mod_inv(root, MOD) } else { root };\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i < n {\n            let mut w = 1u64;\n            for j in 0..(len / 2) {\n                let u = a[i + j];\n                let v = a[i + j + len / 2] * w % MOD;\n                a[i + j] = if u + v >= MOD { u + v - MOD } else { u + v };\n                a[i + j + len / 2] = if u >= v { u - v } else { u + MOD - v };\n                w = w * wlen % MOD;\n            }\n            i += len;\n        }\n        len <<= 1;\n    }\n\n    if invert {\n        let inv_n = mod_inv(n as u64, MOD);\n        for x in a.iter_mut() {\n            *x = *x * inv_n % MOD;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Linear convolution of two integer sequences (exact, mod `MOD`).\n/// `result[k] = Σ_i a[i]·b[k−i]` for `k in 0..a.len()+b.len()−1`, reduced into\n/// `[0, MOD)`. Complexity O(N log N) with `N` the next power of two ≥\n/// `a.len()+b.len()−1`.\npub fn convolve(a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> Vec<u64> {\n    let n = a.len() + b.len() - 1;\n    let mut size = 1usize;\n    while size < n {\n        size <<= 1;\n    }\n    let mut fa = vec![0u64; size];\n    let mut fb = vec![0u64; size];\n    fa[..a.len()].copy_from_slice(a);\n    fb[..b.len()].copy_from_slice(b);\n    ntt(&mut fa, false);\n    ntt(&mut fb, false);\n    for i in 0..size {\n        fa[i] = fa[i] * fb[i] % MOD;\n    }\n    ntt(&mut fa, true);\n    fa.truncate(n);\n    fa\n}\n\n/// Circular convolution of two equal-length sequences. `a.len() == b.len()`\n/// must be a power of two. `result[k] = Σ_i a[i]·b[(k−i) mod n]`, exact mod\n/// `MOD`. This is the NTT primitive behind shift-invariant hypervector\n/// similarity (a cyclic cross-correlation is a circular convolution against\n/// the reversed sequence).\npub fn circular_convolve(a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> Vec<u64> {\n    debug_assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());\n    debug_assert!(a.len().is_power_of_two());\n    let n = a.len();\n    let mut fa = a.to_vec();\n    let mut fb = b.to_vec();\n    ntt(&mut fa, false);\n    ntt(&mut fb, false);\n    for i in 0..n {\n        fa[i] = fa[i] * fb[i] % MOD;\n    }\n    ntt(&mut fa, true);\n    fa\n}\n\n/// Map a value in `[0, MOD)` back to the signed range `(−MOD/2, MOD/2]`, so a\n/// correlation result (true value in `[−n, n]`, `n ≪ MOD`) round-trips its\n/// sign through the NTT.\npub fn centered(v: u64) -> i64 {\n    let v = v % MOD;\n    if v > MOD / 2 {\n        v as i64 - MOD as i64\n    } else {\n        v as i64\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Naïve O(n²) reference convolution (for parity checks).\n    fn naive_convolve(a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> Vec<u64> {\n        let n = a.len() + b.len() - 1;\n        (0..n)\n            .map(|k| {\n                let mut acc = 0u64;\n                for i in 0..=k.min(a.len() - 1) {\n                    if k - i < b.len() {\n                        acc += a[i] * b[k - i];\n                    }\n                }\n                acc % MOD\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    fn naive_circular(a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> Vec<u64> {\n        let n = a.len();\n        (0..n)\n            .map(|k| {\n                let mut acc = 0u64;\n                for i in 0..n {\n                    acc += a[i] * b[(k + n - i) % n];\n                }\n                acc % MOD\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn mod_pow_matches_reference() {\n        assert_eq!(mod_pow(2, 10, MOD), 1024);\n        assert_eq!(mod_pow(3, 0, MOD), 1);\n        // Fermat: a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p).\n        assert_eq!(mod_pow(12345, MOD - 1, MOD), 1);\n        assert_eq!(mod_pow(7, MOD - 1, MOD), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn mod_inv_rounds_trip() {\n        for a in [1u64, 2, 3, 42, 999_999, MOD - 1] {\n            assert_eq!(a * mod_inv(a, MOD) % MOD, 1, "inverse of {a}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ntt_roundtrip() {\n        let n = 256;\n        let mut a: Vec<u64> = (0..n).map(|i| (i * i + 7) % MOD).collect();\n        let orig = a.clone();\n        ntt(&mut a, false);\n        ntt(&mut a, true);\n        assert_eq!(a, orig, "NTT→INTT must be identity");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn convolution_matches_naive() {\n        let a = [1u64, 2, 3, 4, 5];\n        let b = [6u64, 7, 8];\n        let fast = convolve(&a, &b);\n        let slow = naive_convolve(&a, &b);\n        assert_eq!(fast, slow);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn circular_convolution_matches_naive() {\n        let a = [1u64, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8];\n        let b = [9u64, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2];\n        let fast = circular_convolve(&a, &b);\n        let slow = naive_circular(&a, &b);\n        assert_eq!(fast, slow);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn circular_convolution_of_shifted_delta_recovers_shift() {\n        // Circular-convolving with a shifted delta shifts the signal.\n        let n = 8;\n        let mut delta = vec![0u64; n];\n        delta[3] = 1; // δ(t − 3)\n        let signal = [5u64, 1, 4, 2, 6, 3, 7, 9];\n        let fast = circular_convolve(&delta, &signal);\n        // result[k] = signal[(k − 3) mod n]\n        for k in 0..n {\n            assert_eq!(fast[k], signal[(k + n - 3) % n], "shift mismatch at {k}");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn centered_recovers_signed_correlation() {\n        // +1 and −1 encoded as 1 and MOD−1; a perfect alignment sums to n,\n        // an anti-alignment to −n.\n        let n = 8usize;\n        let ones = vec![1u64; n];\n        let neg_ones = vec![MOD - 1; n];\n        // corr of ones with ones = n everywhere.\n        let corr = circular_convolve(&ones, &ones);\n        assert_eq!(centered(corr[0]), n as i64);\n        // corr of ones with neg_ones = −n everywhere.\n        let corr2 = circular_convolve(&ones, &neg_ones);\n        assert_eq!(centered(corr2[0]), -(n as i64));\n    }\n}\n	14678	-1	-1		c34172ee7c0a8fe193ada0c997e2022d495ca5a62d56f48fa209c24ab0eecd43584032d14fc0e6cf875346ebe58dfaac8cef1da4770805ebc9623a07ce7cb8dcdb8754b1639e93199531221af68be1c0e070d86b69bd9e0c72ca3a8458899566a836d2c3b2c9b221783a9a451a7c49d765bdc470bcb2e794019b5dd467cc1df1
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/simd.rs	simd · 716 lines	//! simd.rs — P11 §6 `f64x4` struct-of-arrays (SoA) SIMD batch lane.\n//!\n//! **Design rule that guarantees bit-identity (BLUEPRINT-P11 §6):** vectorise\n//! *ACROSS* the batch of independent rows, never *WITHIN* a single row's\n//! reduction. A 4-wide register holds 4 independent rows' values at the same\n//! column index; each lane replays the *exact* scalar op sequence for its own\n//! row — row-max, `exp(x−max)`, the fixed left-to-right sum, and the divide —\n//! so per-lane arithmetic order is unchanged and the lane is bit-identical to\n//! the scalar single-row path (`attention.rs::softmax`).\n//!\n//! This is a pure property of the op order, not luck: max is exact (order-free),\n//! `exp` is a per-element unary op (order-free), and the sum is accumulated\n//! *per lane*, in column order, exactly like scalar `exps.iter().sum()`.\n//!\n//! Runtime detection mirrors `householder.rs` (`is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2")`\n//! → AVX2 lane; scalar fallback otherwise). No new dependency. The bit-identity\n//! holds in BOTH paths: the scalar fallback trivially matches, and the AVX2 lane\n//! matches because per-lane order is unchanged.\n//!\n/// **Consumers:** `softmax_batch_lane` (the batch-of-rows softmax reduction from\n/// `attention.rs`) and the N-courier **Kalman SoA consumer** (`kalman_batch_step`\n/// / `kalman_batch_step_trust`, WAVE D / BLUEPRINT-P-E §13). The `f64x4` lane\n/// primitive here is exactly the substrate: the Kalman consumer batches N\n/// independent couriers' existing per-courier 1-D Kalman step (`TrustEstimate::\n/// step`, `domain.rs:327-333`) across the same 4-wide AVX2 lane, bit-identical\n/// to the scalar per-courier law. It does NOT touch the per-courier filter\n/// authority — `apply_event_with_trust` (`domain.rs:347-357`) remains the sole\n/// call site composing a courier's Kalman step with that courier's own FSM fold\n/// event; the batched fn is only ever invoked from inside that ownership\n/// boundary (NO-COURIER-SCORING red line respected).\nuse crate::domain::TrustEstimate;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Scalar reference softmax — mirror of `attention.rs::softmax` *exactly* (same\n/// op order, same `exps.iter().sum()` left-to-right reduction). Used by the\n/// bit-identity falsifier tests and as the scalar fallback path.\npub fn softmax_scalar(xs: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64> {\n    if xs.is_empty() {\n        return Vec::new();\n    }\n    let mut m = xs[0];\n    for &x in &xs[1..] {\n        if x > m {\n            m = x;\n        }\n    }\n    let exps: Vec<f64> = xs.iter().map(|&x| crate::math::exp(x - m)).collect();\n    let sum: f64 = exps.iter().sum();\n    exps.iter().map(|&e| e / sum).collect()\n}\n\n/// Process up to 4 independent softmax rows per SIMD step (struct-of-arrays).\n///\n/// Bit-identical to calling [`softmax_scalar`] once per row. Only compiled on\n/// x86_64 with the AVX2 target feature (caller must guarantee the CPU has AVX2\n/// via `is_x86_feature_detected!`). `rows` has length 1..=4.\n///\n/// SAFETY/CORRECTNESS notes (no `unsafe` preconditions on the *caller* beyond\n/// the AVX2 feature gate — all intrinsic use is in-bounds):\n///   * `max` is computed first in a separate pass with `-inf` padding for\n///     short/inactive lanes, so padding can never contaminate the row max.\n///   * The exponential/sum pass zero-pads short/inactive lanes *before* the\n///     per-lane add, so a padded lane contributes exactly 0.0 to its own sum\n///     and is never written to output.\n#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]\n#[target_feature(enable = "avx2")]\nunsafe fn softmax_lane4(rows: &[&[f64]]) -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n    use core::arch::x86_64::*;\n    let k = rows.len(); // 1..=4\n    debug_assert!(k <= 4 && k >= 1);\n\n    // Active lanes = non-empty rows. Inactive (empty) rows produce an empty\n    // output and are masked out of every SIMD reduction (kept NaN-free).\n    let mut active = [false; 4];\n    let mut lens = [0usize; 4];\n    let mut max_len = 0usize;\n    for (lane, r) in rows.iter().enumerate() {\n        active[lane] = !r.is_empty();\n        lens[lane] = r.len();\n        if r.len() > max_len {\n            max_len = r.len();\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── Pass 1: per-lane row-max (exact, order-free). ──────────────────────\n    // Init to -inf; max with -inf-padded short lanes leaves the real max intact.\n    let mut max_arr = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 4];\n    let mut max_vec = _mm256_loadu_pd(max_arr.as_ptr());\n    for j in 0..max_len {\n        let mut vals = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 4];\n        for lane in 0..k {\n            if active[lane] && j < lens[lane] {\n                vals[lane] = rows[lane][j];\n            }\n        }\n        let val_vec = _mm256_loadu_pd(vals.as_ptr());\n        max_vec = _mm256_max_pd(max_vec, val_vec);\n    }\n    _mm256_storeu_pd(max_arr.as_mut_ptr(), max_vec);\n    // Reload as a *constant* vector reused across the exp/sum pass.\n    let max_vec = _mm256_loadu_pd(max_arr.as_ptr());\n\n    // ── Pass 2: exp(x-max) + left-to-right per-lane sum, then divide. ───────\n    let mut outs: Vec<Vec<f64>> = rows.iter().map(|r| vec![0.0f64; r.len()]).collect();\n    // sum_vec holds 4 independent running accumulators (one per lane).\n    let mut sum_vec = _mm256_setzero_pd();\n\n    for j in 0..max_len {\n        // Gather this column's 4 values (0.0 pad for short/inactive lanes).\n        let mut vals = [0.0f64; 4];\n        for lane in 0..k {\n            if active[lane] && j < lens[lane] {\n                vals[lane] = rows[lane][j];\n            }\n        }\n        let val_vec = _mm256_loadu_pd(vals.as_ptr());\n        // diff = val - max ; per-element subtraction → identical to scalar.\n        let diff = _mm256_sub_pd(val_vec, max_vec);\n        let mut diff_arr = [0.0f64; 4];\n        _mm256_storeu_pd(diff_arr.as_mut_ptr(), diff);\n        // exp is a per-element unary op (order-free); extract + call f64::exp.\n        let mut exp_arr = [0.0f64; 4];\n        for lane in 0..4 {\n            exp_arr[lane] = crate::math::exp(diff_arr[lane]);\n        }\n        // Zero out short/inactive lanes so they add exactly 0.0 to their own\n        // sum and are never written to output (keeps NaN-free + bit-clean).\n        for lane in 0..k {\n            if !(active[lane] && j < lens[lane]) {\n                exp_arr[lane] = 0.0;\n            }\n        }\n        let exp_vec = _mm256_loadu_pd(exp_arr.as_ptr());\n        // Per-lane add, in COLUMN ORDER = scalar left-to-right sum. Identical.\n        sum_vec = _mm256_add_pd(sum_vec, exp_vec);\n        // Store the (real) exps into each active row's output buffer.\n        for lane in 0..k {\n            if active[lane] && j < lens[lane] {\n                outs[lane][j] = exp_arr[lane];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── Divide each exp by its row's (per-lane) sum — same as scalar. ────────\n    let mut sum_arr = [0.0f64; 4];\n    _mm256_storeu_pd(sum_arr.as_mut_ptr(), sum_vec);\n    for lane in 0..k {\n        if !active[lane] {\n            continue; // empty row → already empty output\n        }\n        let s = sum_arr[lane];\n        for j in 0..lens[lane] {\n            outs[lane][j] /= s;\n        }\n    }\n    outs\n}\n\n/// Batch softmax over many independent rows, 4 rows per SIMD step.\n///\n/// Bit-identical to applying [`softmax_scalar`] to each row. Rows whose count is\n/// not a multiple of 4 are handled by a scalar tail (also bit-identical). When\n/// AVX2 is unavailable (or on non-x86_64) the entire batch falls back to the\n/// scalar path.\npub fn softmax_batch_lane(rows: &[&[f64]]) -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(rows.len());\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    // AVX2 fast path: consume rows in chunks of 4 via the SoA lane.\n    #[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", feature = "std"))]\n    {\n        if std::is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2") {\n            while i + 4 <= rows.len() {\n                // SAFETY: CPU verified to have AVX2 via is_x86_feature_detected.\n                let res = unsafe { softmax_lane4(&rows[i..i + 4]) };\n                out.extend(res);\n                i += 4;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Scalar tail — covers both the <4 remainder AND every row when AVX2 is\n    // not detected (the whole batch runs through here). Bit-identical either way.\n    for r in &rows[i..] {\n        out.push(softmax_scalar(r));\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n// =========================================================================\n// §13 — N-courier Kalman SoA consumer (WAVE D / BLUEPRINT-P-E §13.2).\n//\n// Batches N independent couriers' existing per-courier 1-D Kalman step\n// (`crate::domain::TrustEstimate::step`, `domain.rs:327-333`) into one\n// SIMD-lane pass. Mirrors the AVX2-detect + scalar-fallback shape of\n// `softmax_batch_lane`, and the *exact* op order of `TrustEstimate::step`\n// so the batched result is `f64::to_bits()`-identical to stepping each\n// courier once in scalar sequence (parity test `kalman_batch_bit_identical`).\n//\n// **Authority is untouched (anti-scope §13.3):** the batched fn only applies\n// the EXISTING `predict`/`update` semantics; it never exposes raw `x`/`P`\n// mutation bypassing `predict`/`update`, never changes cadence/locking/which\n// task authors courier state, and is only ever invoked from inside the\n// `apply_event_with_trust` ownership boundary. NO-COURIER-SCORING respected:\n// no new reputation/IAM/access-control use of the trust estimate is added.\n// =========================================================================\n\n/// Step 4 independent couriers' 1-D Kalman filters in one AVX2 lane.\n///\n/// `xs`/`ps`/`qs`/`rs`/`zs` have length **exactly 4** (the active lanes);\n/// `q`/`r` are per-courier process/observation noise, and `z` is\n/// `Some(measurement)` or `None` (fail-closed hold-prior path). On return\n/// `xs`/`ps` hold the advanced `x`/`P` for each lane. This fn replays the\n/// EXACT op order of `domain::TrustEstimate::step` for each lane, never\n/// combining algebra across lanes, so it is bit-identical to stepping each\n/// courier once in scalar sequence.\n///\n/// SAFETY/CORRECTNESS: caller must have guaranteed the CPU has AVX2 via\n/// `is_x86_feature_detected!`. All intrinsic use is in-bounds. The 4-lane\n/// block is a Structure-of-Arrays of *independent* 1-D couriers.\n#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]\n#[target_feature(enable = "avx2")]\nunsafe fn kalman_lane4(\n    xs: &mut [f64; 4],\n    ps: &mut [f64; 4],\n    qs: &[f64; 4],\n    rs: &[f64; 4],\n    zs: &[Option<f64>; 4],\n    ys: &mut [f64; 4],\n    pps: &mut [f64; 4],\n) {\n    use core::arch::x86_64::*;\n    // ── predict:  x ← x ;  P ← P + Q   (1-D: F=H=1, the steady-state case) ─\n    // x is unchanged by predict (F=1); P grows by Q. We only SIMD-store P.\n    let mut pv = _mm256_loadu_pd(ps.as_ptr());\n    let qv = _mm256_loadu_pd(qs.as_ptr());\n    // P ← P + Q   (per-lane, order-free add — identical to scalar `p + q`).\n    pv = _mm256_add_pd(pv, qv);\n    _mm256_storeu_pd(ps.as_mut_ptr(), pv);\n\n    // ── update (per active lane only; None ⇒ hold prior, variance unchanged) ─\n    // Writes land directly in `xs`/`ps` (the canonical store for the lane's\n    // per-courier scalars), which the caller then scatters back into each\n    // courier — no cross-lane SIMD store, so no lane contanimation is possible.\n    for lane in 0..4 {\n        let (x, p) = (xs[lane], ps[lane]);\n        match zs[lane] {\n            Some(z) => {\n                // S = H·P·Hᵀ + R = p + r   (p here is the PREDICTED P)\n                let s = p + rs[lane];\n                // Mirror scalar EXACTLY: `KalmanFilter::update` computes\n                // `s_inv = mat_inverse(s)` (the 1×1 inverse = 1/s) then\n                // `K = pht·s_inv = p·(1/s)`. Using `p / s` is mathematically\n                // equal but rounds off-by-1-ULP from `p * (1/s)`; to stay\n                // `to_bits()`-identical we replay the scalar's `1/s`-then-mul.\n                let s_inv = 1.0 / s;\n                // K = P·Hᵀ·S⁻¹ = p · s_inv   (S>0 by construction)\n                let k = p * s_inv;\n                // y = z − H·x = z − x   (x is the pre-update / predicted x)\n                let y = z - x;\n                // x ← x + K·y\n                let xn = x + k * y;\n                // P ← (I − K·H)·P = (1 − k)·p\n                let pn = (1.0 - k) * p;\n                xs[lane] = xn;\n                ps[lane] = pn;\n                // Surfaced signals — mirror `KalmanFilter::update`: the\n                // innovation uses the PRE-UPDATE x; S is the PREDICTED\n                // covariance plus R. Exact match to scalar (bit-identical).\n                ys[lane] = y;\n                pps[lane] = p; // predicted P (pre-update)\n            }\n            None => { /* hold prior: x and P already carry the predicted (p+q) */ }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Batch N independent couriers' existing per-courier Kalman step.\n///\n/// `estimates` holds N couriers (each a [`crate::domain::TrustEstimate`]\n/// wrapping a 1-D `KalmanFilter` with `F=H=1`). `observations[i]` is the\n/// `Option<f64>` observation for courier `i` (mirrors `TrustEstimate::step`'s\n/// `Some(z)` predict+update vs `None` fail-closed hold-prior). Advances each\n/// courier EXACTLY as `TrustEstimate::step` would — one call site's worth of\n/// couriers at a time, never combined algebra.\n///\n/// Bit-identical to calling `estimates[i].step(observations[i])` for each `i`\n/// in sequence (parity test proves it, `f64::to_bits()`-exact). Couriers\n/// whose `KalmanFilter` was not the 1-D steady-state case (a different `F`/`H`\n/// than 1) are NOT supported by the SoA lane — the caller must only batch\n/// 1-D `F=H=1` couriers that `TrustEstimate::new` produces. The scalar\n/// fallback (or a 0-lane remainder) handles everything else and still matches.\n///\n/// AVX2 fast path consumes 4 couriers per `kalman_lane4` step; the `<4`\n/// remainder (and the whole batch when AVX2 is absent) runs through the scalar\n/// `TrustEstimate::step` reference, which is trivially bit-identical.\npub fn kalman_batch_step(estimates: &mut [TrustEstimate], observations: &[Option<f64>]) {\n    assert_eq!(\n        estimates.len(),\n        observations.len(),\n        "kalman_batch_step: mismatched estimates/observations counts"\n    );\n    let n = estimates.len();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    #[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", feature = "std"))]\n    {\n        if std::is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2") {\n            while i + 4 <= n {\n                // Gather the 4 active lanes' (x, P, q, r, z) into SoA arrays.\n                let mut xs = [0.0f64; 4];\n                let mut ps = [0.0f64; 4];\n                let mut qs = [0.0f64; 4];\n                let mut rs = [0.0f64; 4];\n                let mut zs = [None::<f64>; 4];\n                for lane in 0..4 {\n                    let e = &estimates[i + lane].kf;\n                    xs[lane] = e.x[0];\n                    ps[lane] = e.p.get(0, 0);\n                    qs[lane] = e.q_entry();\n                    rs[lane] = e.r_entry();\n                    zs[lane] = observations[i + lane];\n                }\n                // SAFETY: AVX2 verified via is_x86_feature_detected.\n                let mut ys = [0.0f64; 4];\n                let mut pps = [0.0f64; 4];\n                unsafe { kalman_lane4(&mut xs, &mut ps, &qs, &rs, &zs, &mut ys, &mut pps) };\n                // Scatter the advanced state back into each courier.\n                for lane in 0..4 {\n                    estimates[i + lane].kf.set_xp(xs[lane], ps[lane]);\n                    // Innovation/surprise signals: mirror `TrustEstimate::step`\n                    // / `KalmanFilter::update` EXACTLY — innovation uses the\n                    // pre-update x; surprise uses the PREDICTED covariance\n                    // (pps[lane] = predicted P) plus R, ‖y‖/√tr(S).\n                    if let Some(_z) = zs[lane] {\n                        let y = ys[lane];\n                        let s = pps[lane] + rs[lane]; // S = predicted P + R\n                        estimates[i + lane]\n                            .kf\n                            .set_signals(vec![y], if s > 0.0 { y.abs() / crate::math::sqrt(s) } else { 0.0 });\n                    }\n                }\n                i += 4;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Scalar tail — covers the <4 remainder AND every courier when AVX2 is\n    // absent (the whole batch runs through the bit-identical reference path).\n    for j in i..n {\n        estimates[j].step(observations[j]);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Convenience ownership-boundary wrapper: batch N `(&mut TrustEstimate,\n/// Option<f64>)` pairs in place. Equivalent to `kalman_batch_step` on the\n/// zipped slices; provided so a caller that already legitimately holds N\n/// couriers' `&mut TrustEstimate` (e.g. inside `apply_event_with_trust`) can\n/// advance them in one SoA pass without allocating an intermediate slice.\npub fn kalman_batch_step_trust(pairs: &mut [(&mut TrustEstimate, Option<f64>)]) {\n    let n = pairs.len();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    #[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", feature = "std"))]\n    {\n        if std::is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2") {\n            while i + 4 <= n {\n                let mut xs = [0.0f64; 4];\n                let mut ps = [0.0f64; 4];\n                let mut qs = [0.0f64; 4];\n                let mut rs = [0.0f64; 4];\n                let mut zs = [None::<f64>; 4];\n                for lane in 0..4 {\n                    let (e, z) = &pairs[i + lane];\n                    xs[lane] = e.kf.x[0];\n                    ps[lane] = e.kf.p.get(0, 0);\n                    qs[lane] = e.kf.q_entry();\n                    rs[lane] = e.kf.r_entry();\n                    zs[lane] = *z;\n                }\n                unsafe {\n                    let mut ys = [0.0f64; 4];\n                    let mut pps = [0.0f64; 4];\n                    kalman_lane4(&mut xs, &mut ps, &qs, &rs, &zs, &mut ys, &mut pps)\n                };\n                for lane in 0..4 {\n                    let (e, _z) = &mut pairs[i + lane];\n                    e.kf.set_xp(xs[lane], ps[lane]);\n                }\n                i += 4;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    for j in i..n {\n        let (e, z) = &mut pairs[j];\n        e.step(*z);\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Deterministic LCG so the randomised battery is reproducible (zero-dep).\n    fn lcg(state: &mut u64) -> u64 {\n        *state = state\n            .wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005)\n            .wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);\n        *state\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow a `Vec<Vec<f64>>` as a slice of row-references for `softmax_batch_lane`.\n    fn as_rows(battery: &[Vec<f64>]) -> Vec<&[f64]> {\n        battery.iter().map(|r| r.as_slice()).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Build `n_rows` random rows of random length (1..=max_len) with finite\n    /// f64 values in roughly [-10, 10].\n    fn random_battery(n_rows: usize, max_len: usize, seed: u64) -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {\n        let mut state = seed;\n        let mut rows = Vec::with_capacity(n_rows);\n        for _ in 0..n_rows {\n            let len = 1 + (lcg(&mut state) as usize) % max_len;\n            let mut row = Vec::with_capacity(len);\n            for _ in 0..len {\n                let bits = lcg(&mut state);\n                // map to [-10, 10], keep finite\n                let frac = ((bits >> 11) as f64) / ((1u64 << 53) as f64);\n                row.push(frac * 20.0 - 10.0);\n            }\n            rows.push(row);\n        }\n        rows\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simd_softmax_bit_identical_to_scalar() {\n        // 50 random rows of random length — exercises AVX2 chunks of 4 plus a\n        // scalar tail (50 = 12*4 + 2). Asserts EXACT (bit-for-bit) equality.\n        let battery = random_battery(50, 20, 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15);\n        let refs: Vec<Vec<f64>> = battery.iter().map(|r| softmax_scalar(r)).collect();\n        let got = softmax_batch_lane(&as_rows(&battery));\n        assert_eq!(got.len(), refs.len());\n        for (g, r) in got.iter().zip(refs.iter()) {\n            assert_eq!(g.len(), r.len());\n            for (a, b) in g.iter().zip(r.iter()) {\n                assert_eq!(*a, *b, "bit-identical mismatch: {} vs {}", a, b);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simd_softmax_handles_non_multiple_of_four() {\n        // Row counts deliberately not divisible by 4 (1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11) to\n        // hammer the scalar-tail path on every chunk boundary.\n        for n in [1usize, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 23] {\n            let battery = random_battery(n, 12, 0x1234_ABCD + n as u64);\n            let refs: Vec<Vec<f64>> = battery.iter().map(|r| softmax_scalar(r)).collect();\n            let got = softmax_batch_lane(&as_rows(&battery));\n            assert_eq!(got.len(), n);\n            for (g, r) in got.iter().zip(refs.iter()) {\n                assert_eq!(g, r, "n={} row mismatch (scalar tail)", n);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simd_softmax_empty_rows() {\n        // Empty rows must round-trip as empty (scalar returns empty too).\n        let battery: Vec<Vec<f64>> = vec![\n            vec![],\n            vec![1.0, 2.0, 3.0],\n            vec![],\n            vec![-0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0],\n        ];\n        let refs: Vec<Vec<f64>> = battery.iter().map(|r| softmax_scalar(r)).collect();\n        let got = softmax_batch_lane(&as_rows(&battery));\n        assert_eq!(got, refs);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simd_softmax_uniform_and_hand_oracle() {\n        // Uniform logits → uniform distribution (bit-identical to scalar ref).\n        let u = softmax_batch_lane(&[&[0.0, 0.0, 0.0][..]]);\n        for x in &u[0] {\n            assert_eq!(*x, 1.0 / 3.0);\n        }\n        // Hand oracle: ln2 → [2/3, 1/3].\n        let w = softmax_batch_lane(&[&[core::f64::consts::LN_2, 0.0][..]]);\n        assert_eq!(w[0][0], 2.0 / 3.0);\n        assert_eq!(w[0][1], 1.0 / 3.0);\n    }\n\n    // ── §13.2(b) Kalman SoA bit-identity parity ──────────────────────────\n    // Build `n` independent 1-D couriers with their own x0/Q/R, each fed a\n    // random observation sequence that INCLUDES `None` (fail-closed hold-prior).\n    // Asserts `kalman_batch_step` once == `TrustEstimate::step` N times,\n    // `f64::to_bits()`-exact for x AND P on every lane, for every N including\n    // non-multiples of 4 (mirrors `simd_softmax_handles_non_multiple_of_four`).\n\n    /// Build `n` couriers, each with its own x0/Q/R.\n    fn random_couriers(n: usize, seed: u64) -> Vec<TrustEstimate> {\n        let mut state = seed;\n        (0..n)\n            .map(|_| {\n                let x0 = (lcg(&mut state) as f64) / (u64::MAX as f64) * 2.0 - 1.0;\n                // Q, R in a sane positive range so S stays invertible.\n                let q = 1e-3 + ((lcg(&mut state) % 1_000) as f64) * 1e-4;\n                let r = 1e-1 + ((lcg(&mut state) % 1_000) as f64) * 1e-3;\n                TrustEstimate::new(x0, q, r)\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Build one observation per courier: `Some(z)` most of the time, `None`\n    /// (hold-prior) ~1/4 of the time, with z drawn from a wide finite range.\n    fn random_observations(n: usize, seed: u64) -> Vec<Option<f64>> {\n        let mut state = seed;\n        (0..n)\n            .map(|_| {\n                if (lcg(&mut state) >> 40) % 4 == 0 {\n                    None // fail-closed hold-prior path\n                } else {\n                    let bits = lcg(&mut state);\n                    let frac = ((bits >> 11) as f64) / ((1u64 << 53) as f64);\n                    Some(frac * 20.0 - 10.0)\n                }\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kalman_batch_bit_identical() {\n        // 50 couriers (12*4 + 2) — exercises AVX2 chunks of 4 + scalar tail.\n        let n = 50usize;\n        let seed = 0x5EED_BEEF_1234_5678u64;\n        let mut batch = random_couriers(n, seed);\n        let obs = random_observations(n, seed ^ 0x1111_2222);\n\n        // Scalar reference: step each courier exactly once, in sequence.\n        let mut scalar: Vec<TrustEstimate> = random_couriers(n, seed);\n        for i in 0..n {\n            scalar[i].step(obs[i]);\n        }\n\n        // Batched SoA pass — must match the scalar sequence bit-for-bit.\n        kalman_batch_step(&mut batch, &obs);\n\n        assert_eq!(batch.len(), scalar.len());\n        for (b, s) in batch.iter().zip(scalar.iter()) {\n            assert_eq!(\n                b.kf.x[0].to_bits(),\n                s.kf.x[0].to_bits(),\n                "x mismatch at lane (batch vs scalar)"\n            );\n            assert_eq!(\n                b.kf.innovation_bits(),\n                s.kf.innovation_bits(),\n                "innovation mismatch at lane"\n            );\n            assert_eq!(\n                b.kf.surprise_bits(),\n                s.kf.surprise_bits(),\n                "surprise mismatch at lane"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kalman_batch_handles_non_multiple_of_four() {\n        // Couriers counts NOT divisible by 4 → hammer the scalar-tail path.\n        for n in [1usize, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 23, 37] {\n            let seed = 0xABC0_0000u64 + n as u64;\n            let mut batch = random_couriers(n, seed);\n            let obs = random_observations(n, seed ^ 0x5555_5555);\n            let mut scalar: Vec<TrustEstimate> = random_couriers(n, seed);\n            for i in 0..n {\n                scalar[i].step(obs[i]);\n            }\n            kalman_batch_step(&mut batch, &obs);\n            assert_eq!(batch.len(), n, "n={} length drift", n);\n            for (b, s) in batch.iter().zip(scalar.iter()) {\n                assert_eq!(\n                    b.kf.x[0].to_bits(),\n                    s.kf.x[0].to_bits(),\n                    "n={} x mismatch (scalar tail)",\n                    n\n                );\n                assert_eq!(\n                    b.kf.p.get(0, 0).to_bits(),\n                    s.kf.p.get(0, 0).to_bits(),\n                    "n={} P mismatch (scalar tail)",\n                    n\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn kalman_batch_trust_wrapper_matches_scalar() {\n        // The `(&mut TrustEstimate, Option<f64>)`-pair wrapper must also be\n        // bit-identical to stepping each courier once in scalar sequence.\n        let n = 21usize;\n        let seed = 0x7E551_4321_ABCDu64.wrapping_add(n as u64);\n        let mut scalar: Vec<TrustEstimate> = random_couriers(n, seed);\n        let obs = random_observations(n, seed ^ 0x0F0F_0F0F);\n        for i in 0..n {\n            scalar[i].step(obs[i]);\n        }\n\n        let mut couriers = random_couriers(n, seed);\n        let mut pairs: Vec<(&mut TrustEstimate, Option<f64>)> =\n            couriers.iter_mut().map(|c| (c, None)).collect();\n        // Splice the observations into the pairs.\n        for (i, z) in obs.iter().enumerate() {\n            pairs[i].1 = *z;\n        }\n        kalman_batch_step_trust(&mut pairs);\n\n        for (b, s) in couriers.iter().zip(scalar.iter()) {\n            assert_eq!(b.kf.x[0].to_bits(), s.kf.x[0].to_bits(), "x mismatch");\n            assert_eq!(\n                b.kf.p.get(0, 0).to_bits(),\n                s.kf.p.get(0, 0).to_bits(),\n                "P mismatch"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── §13.2(c) Benchmark — measured wall-clock speedup of the AVX2 SoA\n    // path over the scalar per-courier loop, std::time::Instant, zero new deps.\n    // The speedup number is printed and asserted >= 1.0x (proving the SIMD\n    // path is at least as fast); the exact measured figure is recorded in\n    // BLUEPRINT-P-E §13 and docs/regressions/REGRESSION-LEDGER.md.\n    #[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", feature = "std"))]\n    #[test]\n    fn kalman_batch_benchmark_speedup_recorded() {\n        use std::time::Instant;\n        // Only meaningful on the AVX2 build path; on non-AVX2 hosts the whole\n        // batch runs through the scalar tail and the ratio is ~1.0 (still OK).\n        if !cfg!(all(target_arch = "x86_64", feature = "std"))\n            || !std::is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2")\n        {\n            eprintln!("kalman_batch bench: AVX2 unavailable — skipping speedup gate");\n            return;\n        }\n        // Seeded RNG for deterministic couriers.\n        let make_rng = || {\n            let mut s = 0x1234_5678_9ABC_DEF0u64;\n            move || -> f64 {\n                s = s\n                    .wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005)\n                    .wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);\n                (s >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64\n            }\n        };\n\n        for &n in &[4usize, 32, 256] {\n            let seed = 0xFEED_0000u64 + n as u64;\n            let obs_seed = seed ^ 0x0A0A_0A0A;\n            let couriers = random_couriers(n, seed);\n            let obs = random_observations(n, obs_seed);\n\n            // ── scalar reference timing ──\n            let scal_runs = 200;\n            let t0 = Instant::now();\n            let mut acc = 0.0f64;\n            for _ in 0..scal_runs {\n                let mut sc = couriers.clone();\n                for i in 0..n {\n                    sc[i].step(obs[i]);\n                }\n                acc += sc[0].kf.x[0];\n            }\n            let scal_ns = t0.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64 / scal_runs as f64;\n            core::hint::black_box(acc);\n\n            // ── batched SoA timing ──\n            let bat_runs = 200;\n            let t1 = Instant::now();\n            let mut acc2 = 0.0f64;\n            for _ in 0..bat_runs {\n                let mut bc = couriers.clone();\n                kalman_batch_step(&mut bc, &obs);\n                acc2 += bc[0].kf.x[0];\n            }\n            let bat_ns = t1.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64 / bat_runs as f64;\n            core::hint::black_box(acc2);\n\n            let speedup = scal_ns / bat_ns;\n            // Keep the lane honest: both paths must agree to the bit on x/P.\n            let mut sc = couriers.clone();\n            for i in 0..n {\n                sc[i].step(obs[i]);\n            }\n            let mut bc = couriers.clone();\n            kalman_batch_step(&mut bc, &obs);\n            for (a, b) in sc.iter().zip(bc.iter()) {\n                assert_eq!(a.kf.x[0].to_bits(), b.kf.x[0].to_bits());\n                assert_eq!(a.kf.p.get(0, 0).to_bits(), b.kf.p.get(0, 0).to_bits());\n            }\n            println!(\n                "kalman_batch N={n}: scalar={scal_ns:.1}ns batched={bat_ns:.1}ns speedup={speedup:.3}x",\n            );\n            // The SIMD lane must be at least as fast as scalar (no regression);\n            // on an AVX2 host it is materially faster. We gate >= 1.0 to avoid\n            // flaky CI while still recording the real measured ratio above.\n            assert!(\n                speedup >= 1.0,\n                "kalman SoA path regressed vs scalar: {speedup}x"\n            );\n            let _ = make_rng();\n        }\n    }\n}\n	14697	-1	-1		60f73717dcda11e1836b88c353325321485e97ac8d18ff0ba95fc6499be8854719853886cd8b28b6a85f5268b1b1d02cde271da6d5688ca0f07f760bff06ea8ec79f56d9611cf13111c5311bf7bba8a2b578dcbe4991c489d8c22494100b01c5a4a2f7d021c9131dd8484c475ddc1d0944bf4563ad89adf46321cdd463f62531
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/agent/mod.rs	mod · 152 lines	//! ports/agent — the `AgentBridge` port (B1): a mandatorily hybrid-signed, fail-closed,\n//! enumerable-only agent-admission seam that generalizes the proven `LlmBackend` /\n//! `llm-adapters` pattern to arbitrary bridged agents (an MCP server, a LangGraph graph,\n//! a bare binary).\n//!\n//! # Compile firewall (mirrors `ports/llm.rs:3-7`)\n//! This module tree has ZERO network / HTTP / JSON / serde. It defines only the abstract\n//! contract (`AgentBridge` trait), the plain value types the admission decision is made\n//! from (`AgentManifest`, `Capability`, `SignedFrame`, `AnchorRoster`, `RevocationSet`,\n//! …), the closed enums (`Resource`/`Action`/`AgentCaps`/`ValidationPolicy`/…), and the\n//! admission logic. The concrete adapter crate (`agent-adapters`, repo root) owns all\n//! transport/JSON and the Wasmtime embedding — exactly as `llm-adapters` owns HTTP/JSON\n//! for `ports/llm.rs`. `cargo tree -p dowiz-kernel` must show no HTTP client / no\n//! Wasmtime here (the migration-step-2 done-check).\n//!\n//! # Reuse-not-reinvent (the M6 seam)\n//! Per B1's thesis, the trust machinery is REUSED, not invented: the verification is the\n//! bebop2 `HybridGate::check` sequence (dual Ed25519 ⊕ ML-DSA-65 under an unrelaxable\n//! `RequireBoth` floor) reproduced faithfully in [`admission::ReferenceHybridGate`], with\n//! the real cryptographic primitive behind the [`cap::SignatureVerifier`] seam so a\n//! production node injects the real bebop2 verifier without changing this port. See\n//! `cap.rs`'s module doc for why this is a trait seam (the dowiz kernel does not link\n//! bebop2 `proto-cap`, and B1 DoD item 7 defers the concrete cross-repo hard-link).\n\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\npub mod admission;\npub mod cap;\npub mod command_filter;\npub mod manifest;\npub mod scope;\n/// Item 54 — Sentinel: read-time integrity check for critical LIVE in-memory authority\n/// structs (`AnchorRoster` / `RevocationSet`). Declared after `cap`/`manifest`/`scope` so\n/// its `IntegrityChecked` impls (in `cap.rs`) and the call sites in `cap::verify_chain`\n/// resolve against the already-defined types.\npub mod sentinel;\n\npub use admission::{\n    AdmissionError, AdmissionGate, AdmissionLimiter, AdmissionRecord, Admitter,\n    ReferenceHybridGate, B1_NEW_SCOPES, DEFAULT_MAX_AGENT_DEPTH, FUEL_PER_UNIT,\n    MAX_VERIFY_CHAIN_LINKS, TRANCHE_UNITS,\n};\npub use cap::{\n    pq_key_id, revocation_hash, verify_chain, AnchorRoster, Capability, ChainError, Delegation,\n    HybridPolicy, NodeId, RefSigner, RevocationSet, SignatureVerifier, SignedFrame,\n    ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN,\n};\npub use manifest::{\n    config_axis_domain, AgentCaps, AgentManifest, BudgetRequest, CostDenomination, ExecutionModel,\n    ManifestParseError, QuirksProfile, ResourceNeed, ValidationPolicy,\n};\npub use scope::{Action, RedLinePolicy, Resource, Scope};\n\n/// Typed agent-bridge error (the `LlmError` generalization). `health()` and any probe\n/// return a typed `Err` when the bridged agent is absent or refuses — never a mock.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum AgentError {\n    /// Bridge endpoint/process is not reachable (health failed). Fail-closed.\n    Unavailable,\n    /// The requested capability is not offered by this bridge.\n    Unsupported,\n    /// Malformed request.\n    BadRequest(String),\n    /// Request timed out.\n    Timeout,\n    /// The requested tool name is not in the operator-authored allowlist (fail-closed\n    /// drop — never a string passthrough).\n    ToolNotAllowed(String),\n    /// The live tool-map digest no longer matches the admitted digest (`listChanged` /\n    /// server substitution — registry-poisoning class). Refuse and require re-admission.\n    DigestDrift,\n    /// A server-initiated `sampling/createMessage` or elicitation request was refused —\n    /// an admitted agent must never drive the host's LLM (RC-2 control inversion).\n    ControlInversionRefused,\n    /// The per-agent budget envelope is exhausted (F2). Degrade-closed.\n    BudgetExceeded,\n    /// The invocation's delegation depth reached the granted cap (F10).\n    DepthExceeded,\n    /// A typed refusal with context.\n    Refused(String),\n}\n\n/// The unit of work a bridged agent is asked to perform.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum AgentTask {\n    /// Execute a tool call (mapped through the operator allowlist to a closed scope).\n    InvokeTool {\n        /// The MCP tool name (validated against the allowlist).\n        name: String,\n        /// Opaque, already-validated arguments.\n        args: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// Serve a resource read (idempotent; cacheable under `Exact`).\n    ReadResource {\n        /// The resource uri.\n        uri: String,\n    },\n    /// Serve a prompt template.\n    RenderPrompt {\n        /// The prompt name.\n        name: String,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl AgentTask {\n    /// The `TrackRecord.task` label (the `gov_route` fold key).\n    pub fn label(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            AgentTask::InvokeTool { .. } => "agent.invoke_tool",\n            AgentTask::ReadResource { .. } => "agent.read_resource",\n            AgentTask::RenderPrompt { .. } => "agent.render_prompt",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// One bridged invocation. `invoke_depth` is the number of `(AgentBridge, InvokeAgent)`\n/// links in the presented (already-`verify_chain`'d) delegation chain — the F10 depth is\n/// cryptographically witnessed, not a mutable counter the agent reports.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct AgentInvocation {\n    /// What to do.\n    pub task: AgentTask,\n    /// Estimated cost in budget units (pre-acquired before the call).\n    pub cost_units: u64,\n    /// Cryptographically-witnessed invocation depth (count of `InvokeAgent` links).\n    pub invoke_depth: u8,\n}\n\n/// A bridged-invocation result.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct AgentResponse {\n    /// Opaque response bytes.\n    pub content: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Budget units actually consumed (what the `TrackRecord` row prices).\n    pub units: u64,\n}\n\n/// The pluggable agent-bridge port. Implemented by `McpServerBridge` in the\n/// `agent-adapters` crate. Mirrors `LlmBackend` (`id/caps/…/health`).\npub trait AgentBridge {\n    /// Stable bridge id, e.g. `"mcp:<server-id>"`.
```
