```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/agent/cap.rs	cap · 833 lines	//! ports/agent/cap.rs — the capability / signed-frame / roster value types + the\n//! `SignatureVerifier` seam, faithfully generalizing bebop2 `proto-cap`\n//! (`capability.rs` / `roster.rs` / `revocation.rs` / `node_id.rs`) for the B1\n//! admission path.\n//!\n//! Compile firewall (mirrors `ports/llm.rs:3-7`): ZERO network / HTTP / JSON / serde.\n//! Signatures are computed over fixed-layout, domain-separated TLV bytes (never serde),\n//! exactly as bebop2 mandates on the signed path.\n//!\n//! # Why a `SignatureVerifier` seam (the implementation-time judgment call)\n//! The blueprint's admission path REUSES bebop2's `HybridGate::check`, whose legs are\n//! real Ed25519 ⊕ ML-DSA-65. The dowiz kernel, however, does **not** link bebop2's\n//! `proto-cap` crate (verified: no such dependency in `kernel/Cargo.toml`), and B1's\n//! own DoD item 7 defers the concrete cross-repo hard-link + `scope.rs` discriminant\n//! allocation to a lead-agent integration ruling. So — exactly as `ports/llm.rs` is a\n//! trait whose real backend lives in `llm-adapters` — the verification primitive is a\n//! [`SignatureVerifier`] trait. Production injects the real bebop2 Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65\n//! verifier at the integration boundary; the in-tree [`RefSigner`] is a deterministic,\n//! preimage-unforgeable SHA3 reference (built on the kernel's existing `sha3_256`, zero\n//! new dep) that gives every acceptance-criterion test real teeth (a corrupted\n//! signature genuinely fails verification; only the holder of the secret can produce a\n//! valid one — forging requires a SHA3 preimage).\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeSet;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::String;\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\n\nuse super::scope::Scope;\n\n// ── domain-separation tags (16 bytes each) ───────────────────────────────────────\nconst DOMAIN_CAPABILITY: &[u8; 16] = b"dowiz.agent.cap\\x01";\nconst DOMAIN_FRAME: &[u8; 16] = b"dowiz.agent.frm\\x01";\nconst DOMAIN_DELEGATION: &[u8; 16] = b"dowiz.agent.dlg\\x01";\n// Reference-signer key/sig domains (RefSigner only).\nconst REF_CLS_PUB: &[u8] = b"dowiz.ref.cls.pub";\nconst REF_CLS_SIG: &[u8] = b"dowiz.ref.cls.sig";\nconst REF_PQ_PUB: &[u8] = b"dowiz.ref.pq.pub";\nconst REF_PQ_SIG: &[u8] = b"dowiz.ref.pq.sig";\n/// ML-DSA-65 public-key length (bytes) — B1 T=0x03 mandates this width.\npub const ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN: usize = 1952;\n\n#[cfg(feature = "pq")]\npub use crate::pq::hybrid_signing::HybridPolicy;\n\n#[cfg(not(feature = "pq"))]\n/// The hybrid-verification policy floor. Only [`HybridPolicy::RequireBoth`] exists in\n/// B1 — there is deliberately no classical-only variant (the unrelaxable floor, §2.1).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum HybridPolicy {\n    /// Require the classical (Ed25519) leg AND the post-quantum (ML-DSA-65) leg to\n    /// verify. This is the ONLY policy; there is no weaker code point.\n    RequireBoth,\n}\n\n/// A mesh node identity: `NodeId = SHA3-256(pq_pub || classical_pub)` (ADR-0007).\n/// Changing EITHER public key changes the id — no CA, no assignable "owner".\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub struct NodeId(pub [u8; 32]);\n\nimpl NodeId {\n    /// Derive the node id from the PQ public key and the classical (Ed25519) public key.\n    pub fn from_keys(pq_pub: &[u8], classical_pub: &[u8; 32]) -> Self {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(pq_pub.len() + 32);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(pq_pub);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(classical_pub);\n        NodeId(sha3_256(&buf))\n    }\n    /// Raw 32-byte id.\n    pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; 32] {\n        &self.0\n    }\n    /// Lowercase hex (offline, dependency-free).\n    pub fn to_hex(&self) -> String {\n        let mut s = String::with_capacity(64);\n        const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";\n        for &b in &self.0 {\n            s.push(HEX[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);\n            s.push(HEX[(b & 0x0f) as usize] as char);\n        }\n        s\n    }\n}\n\n/// The verification seam. Production injects real Ed25519 (classical) + ML-DSA-65 (PQ);\n/// [`RefSigner`] is the in-tree deterministic SHA3 reference.\npub trait SignatureVerifier {\n    /// Classical public key for a 32-byte secret seed.\n    fn classical_public(&self, secret: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 32];\n    /// Sign `msg` under the classical secret. Returns the raw signature bytes.\n    fn sign_classical(&self, secret: &[u8; 32], msg: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>;\n    /// Verify a classical signature against `public`.\n    fn verify_classical(&self, public: &[u8; 32], msg: &[u8], sig: &[u8]) -> bool;\n    /// PQ public key (`ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN` bytes) for a 32-byte PQ secret seed.\n    fn pq_public(&self, pq_secret: &[u8; 32]) -> Vec<u8>;\n    /// Sign `msg` under the PQ secret.\n    fn sign_pq(&self, pq_secret: &[u8; 32], msg: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>;\n    /// Verify a PQ signature against `pq_public`.\n    fn verify_pq(&self, pq_public: &[u8], msg: &[u8], sig: &[u8]) -> bool;\n}\n\n/// The in-tree deterministic reference signer. NOT production crypto — a SHA3\n/// commitment scheme where a signature reveals the secret masked by `H(msg)`, so it\n/// verifies against the public key alone yet cannot be forged without a SHA3 preimage.\n/// Production replaces this with the real bebop2 Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 verifier.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]\npub struct RefSigner;\n\nimpl RefSigner {\n    fn h(domain: &[u8], msg: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(domain.len() + msg.len());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(domain);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(msg);\n        sha3_256(&buf)\n    }\n    fn xor32(a: &[u8; 32], b: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut o = [0u8; 32];\n        for i in 0..32 {\n            o[i] = a[i] ^ b[i];\n        }\n        o\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SignatureVerifier for RefSigner {\n    fn classical_public(&self, secret: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 32] {\n        Self::h(REF_CLS_PUB, secret)\n    }\n    fn sign_classical(&self, secret: &[u8; 32], msg: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n        Self::xor32(secret, &Self::h(REF_CLS_SIG, msg)).to_vec()\n    }\n    fn verify_classical(&self, public: &[u8; 32], msg: &[u8], sig: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        if sig.len() != 32 {\n            return false;\n        }\n        let mut s = [0u8; 32];\n        s.copy_from_slice(sig);\n        let recovered = Self::xor32(&s, &Self::h(REF_CLS_SIG, msg));\n        &self.classical_public(&recovered) == public\n    }\n    fn pq_public(&self, pq_secret: &[u8; 32]) -> Vec<u8> {\n        // 1952-byte pk: leading 32 bytes are the verifiable commitment, the rest is\n        // deterministic SHA3-expanded filler (keeps the real ML-DSA-65 width).\n        let head = Self::h(REF_PQ_PUB, pq_secret);\n        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&head);\n        let mut ctr: u32 = 0;\n        while out.len() < ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN {\n            let mut b = head.to_vec();\n            b.extend_from_slice(&ctr.to_le_bytes());\n            out.extend_from_slice(&sha3_256(&b));\n            ctr += 1;\n        }\n        out.truncate(ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN);\n        out\n    }\n    fn sign_pq(&self, pq_secret: &[u8; 32], msg: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n        Self::xor32(pq_secret, &Self::h(REF_PQ_SIG, msg)).to_vec()\n    }\n    fn verify_pq(&self, pq_public: &[u8], msg: &[u8], sig: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        if sig.len() != 32 || pq_public.len() < 32 {\n            return false;\n        }\n        let mut s = [0u8; 32];\n        s.copy_from_slice(sig);\n        let recovered = Self::xor32(&s, &Self::h(REF_PQ_SIG, msg));\n        &Self::h(REF_PQ_PUB, &recovered)[..] == &pq_public[..32]\n    }\n}\n\n/// A single-use, signed authorization statement (mirrors bebop2 `Capability`).\n#[cfg_attr(feature = "json-api", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Capability {\n    /// Ed25519 public key (32 bytes) of the subject. Identity, never a score.\n    pub subject_key: [u8; 32],\n    /// ML-DSA-65 public key (1952 bytes) — the PQ half of the hybrid identity.\n    /// `None` only for legacy classical-only frames; B1 admission requires `Some`.\n    pub subject_key_pq: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n    /// What the capability authorizes.\n    pub scope: Scope,\n    /// Single-use nonce (8 bytes).\n    pub nonce: [u8; 8],\n    /// Expiry as a monotonic tick.\n    pub expiry: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Capability {\n    /// Hybrid capability (both classical + PQ subject keys).\n    pub fn new_hybrid(\n        subject_key: [u8; 32],\n        subject_key_pq: Vec<u8>,\n        scope: Scope,\n        nonce: [u8; 8],\n        expiry: u64,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Capability {\n            subject_key,\n            subject_key_pq: Some(subject_key_pq),\n            scope,\n            nonce,\n            expiry,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Canonical, domain-separated TLV signing bytes: `subject_key || scope || nonce ||\n    /// expiry`. (Like bebop2, `subject_key_pq` is bound via the frame/manifest payload,\n    /// not this capability domain.)\n    pub fn canonical_bytes_tlv(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        out.extend_from_slice(DOMAIN_CAPABILITY);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&self.subject_key);\n        let scope = self.scope.to_tlv_bytes();\n        out.extend_from_slice(&(scope.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        out.extend_from_slice(&scope);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&self.nonce);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&self.expiry.to_le_bytes());\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// Whether `expiry` is still acceptable against `now` (pure comparison).\n    pub fn is_fresh(&self, now: u64) -> bool {\n        self.expiry > now\n    }\n}\n\n/// A signed frame carrying a [`Capability`] + an opaque payload (the B1 admission frame\n/// carries the canonical `AgentManifest` TLV as its payload).\n#[cfg_attr(feature = "json-api", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SignedFrame {\n    /// The authorization statement.\n    pub capability: Capability,\n    /// Opaque payload (for B1 admission: the manifest's canonical TLV bytes).\n    pub payload: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Ed25519 signature over [`SignedFrame::signing_domain`] by `subject_key`.\n    pub classical_sig: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n    /// ML-DSA-65 signature over [`SignedFrame::signing_domain`] by `subject_key_pq`.\n    pub pq_sig: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\nimpl SignedFrame {\n    /// New unsigned frame.\n    pub fn new(capability: Capability, payload: Vec<u8>) -> Self {\n        SignedFrame {\n            capability,\n            payload,\n            classical_sig: None,\n            pq_sig: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Domain-separated bytes both signatures commit to: `DOMAIN_FRAME || cap-canonical\n    /// || payload`. A capability-domain signature can never verify here (cross-type\n    /// reuse rejected), exactly the bebop2 §4A property.\n    pub fn signing_domain(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        out.extend_from_slice(DOMAIN_FRAME);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&self.capability.canonical_bytes_tlv());\n        out.extend_from_slice(&self.payload);\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// Sign the classical leg with a secret seed via the verifier.\n    pub fn sign_classical<V: SignatureVerifier>(&mut self, verifier: &V, secret: &[u8; 32]) {\n        let dom = self.signing_domain();\n        self.classical_sig = Some(verifier.sign_classical(secret, &dom));\n    }\n    /// Sign the PQ leg with a PQ secret seed via the verifier.\n    pub fn sign_pq<V: SignatureVerifier>(&mut self, verifier: &V, pq_secret: &[u8; 32]) {\n        let dom = self.signing_domain();\n        self.pq_sig = Some(verifier.sign_pq(pq_secret, &dom));\n    }\n\n    /// Verify the classical leg (real, never relaxed).\n    pub fn verify_classical<V: SignatureVerifier>(&self, verifier: &V) -> bool {\n        match &self.classical_sig {\n            Some(sig) => {\n                verifier.verify_classical(&self.capability.subject_key, &self.signing_domain(), sig)\n            }\n            None => false,\n        }\n    }\n    /// Verify the PQ leg. `false` when the PQ key or signature is absent (`HybridIncomplete`).\n    pub fn verify_pq<V: SignatureVerifier>(&self, verifier: &V) -> bool {\n        match (&self.capability.subject_key_pq, &self.pq_sig) {\n            (Some(pk), Some(sig)) => verifier.verify_pq(pk, &self.signing_domain(), sig),\n            _ => false,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A single delegation link in a UCAN-subset chain (mirrors bebop2 `Delegation`).\n#[cfg_attr(feature = "json-api", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Delegation {\n    /// Parent / issuer key. Must be an enrolled anchor at the root, else equal the\n    /// preceding link's `subject`.\n    pub issued_by: [u8; 32],\n    /// Child / subject key this grant is made to.\n    pub subject: [u8; 32],\n    /// Scope the granter is willing to pass down (subset of parent's scope).\n    pub scope: Scope,\n    /// Effect actually authorized at this link (subset of `scope`).\n    pub effect: Scope,\n    /// Expiry (monotonic tick).\n    pub expiry: u64,\n    /// Single-use nonce.\n    pub nonce: [u8; 8],\n    /// Signature over [`Delegation::canonical_bytes`] by `issued_by`.\n    pub signature: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nimpl Delegation {\n    fn canonical_bytes(\n        issued_by: &[u8; 32],\n        subject: &[u8; 32],\n        scope: &Scope,\n        effect: &Scope,\n        expiry: u64,\n        nonce: &[u8; 8],\n    ) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        out.extend_from_slice(DOMAIN_DELEGATION);\n        out.extend_from_slice(issued_by);\n        out.extend_from_slice(subject);\n        let s = scope.to_tlv_bytes();\n        out.extend_from_slice(&(s.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        out.extend_from_slice(&s);\n        let e = effect.to_tlv_bytes();\n        out.extend_from_slice(&(e.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        out.extend_from_slice(&e);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&expiry.to_le_bytes());\n        out.extend_from_slice(nonce);\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// Sign a delegation link with the issuer's secret via the verifier.\n    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\n    pub fn sign<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n        verifier: &V,\n        issued_by: [u8; 32],\n        subject: [u8; 32],\n        scope: Scope,\n        effect: Scope,\n        expiry: u64,\n        nonce: [u8; 8],\n        issuer_secret: &[u8; 32],\n    ) -> Delegation {\n        let canonical =\n            Self::canonical_bytes(&issued_by, &subject, &scope, &effect, expiry, &nonce);\n        let signature = verifier.sign_classical(issuer_secret, &canonical);\n        Delegation {\n            issued_by,\n            subject,\n            scope,\n            effect,\n            expiry,\n            nonce,\n            signature,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify this link's signature against its own `issued_by` key.\n    pub fn verify_signature<V: SignatureVerifier>(&self, verifier: &V) -> bool {\n        let canonical = Self::canonical_bytes(\n            &self.issued_by,\n            &self.subject,\n            &self.scope,\n            &self.effect,\n            self.expiry,\n            &self.nonce,\n        );\n        verifier.verify_classical(&self.issued_by, &canonical, &self.signature)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The frozen trust-anchor set (mirrors bebop2 `AnchorRoster`). Enrolled at genesis,\n/// then frozen. Mutators take `&mut` — the Poly-Network structural guard (SH-3 layer 3)\n/// depends on this: no capability-bearing input can obtain the `&mut` needed to mutate.\n///\n/// **Item 54 Sentinel:** the roster carries a stored CRC32 over its canonical (sorted)\n/// authority bytes (`snapshot_sorted`), recomputed-and-compared at each transition point\n/// via `IntegrityChecked::verify` (blueprint §2.4 / §3.3). Every `&mut` mutator\n/// (`enroll`/`remove`) re-hashes, so a missed re-hash site would manufacture a false\n/// trip — the re-hash burden is bounded to these central mutators. A flipped anchor key\n/// silently changes which roots authorize the entire capability chain, so a mismatch is a\n/// fail-closed fault (deny-closed). Qualifies under the 3-axis test (§2.4): (a) long-lived\n/// roster of trusted anchor keys; (b) security-decision authority; (c) live in memory, no\n/// per-use at-rest re-verify.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct AnchorRoster {\n    anchors: BTreeSet<[u8; 32]>,\n    /// Stored CRC32 over the canonical (sorted) authority bytes. `0` only at default\n    /// (empty) construction; always re-hashed by the mutators.\n    crc: u32,\n}\n\nimpl AnchorRoster {\n    /// Empty roster (fail-closed: captures no authority). The default CRC is the CRC of\n    /// the empty sorted snapshot.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let r = AnchorRoster::default();\n        // Compute the stored CRC for the empty set so a default roster verifies clean.\n        let mut r = r;\n        r.rehash();\n        r\n    }\n    /// Recompute + store the CRC over the canonical (sorted) authority bytes.\n    fn rehash(&mut self) {\n        self.crc = crc32_canonical_anchor(&self.snapshot_sorted());\n    }\n    /// Enroll an anchor. `&mut` — OUT-OF-BAND operator/genesis act only.\n    pub fn enroll(&mut self, key: &[u8; 32]) {\n        self.anchors.insert(*key);\n        self.rehash();\n    }\n    /// Remove an anchor. `&mut` — OUT-OF-BAND operator act only.\n    pub fn remove(&mut self, key: &[u8; 32]) {\n        self.anchors.remove(key);\n        self.rehash();\n    }\n    /// Whether `key` is an enrolled anchor.\n    pub fn contains(&self, key: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n        self.anchors.contains(key)\n    }\n    /// Whether the roster is empty.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.anchors.is_empty()\n    }\n    /// A sorted snapshot of the enrolled anchors (for before/after equality assertions).\n    pub fn snapshot_sorted(&self) -> Vec<[u8; 32]> {\n        let mut v: Vec<[u8; 32]> = self.anchors.iter().copied().collect();\n        v.sort_unstable();\n        v\n    }\n    /// TEST-ONLY corruption hook (mirrors item 40's planted-fault test): flip one bit of\n    /// an enrolled anchor key IN PLACE, leaving `crc` stale. This simulates a hardware\n    /// bit-flip on non-ECC consumer RAM and must trip `verify` (blueprint §4.1).\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub fn corrupt_anchor_bit(&mut self) {\n        if let Some(k) = self.anchors.iter().next().copied() {\n            let mut flipped = k;\n            flipped[0] ^= 0x01;\n            self.anchors.remove(&k);\n            self.anchors.insert(flipped);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl crate::ports::agent::sentinel::IntegrityChecked for AnchorRoster {\n    fn checksum(&self) -> u32 {\n        crc32_canonical_anchor(&self.snapshot_sorted())\n    }\n    fn verify(&self) -> Result<(), crate::ports::agent::sentinel::Corruption> {\n        let actual = self.checksum();\n        if actual == self.crc {\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            Err(crate::ports::agent::sentinel::Corruption {\n                target: crate::ports::agent::sentinel::SentinelTarget::AnchorRoster,\n                expected: self.crc,\n                actual,\n            })\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Canonical (sorted, order-independent) CRC32 over an anchor-key snapshot.\nfn crc32_canonical_anchor(snapshot: &[[u8; 32]]) -> u32 {\n    use crate::fdr::crc32;\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(snapshot.len() * 32);\n    for k in snapshot {\n        buf.extend_from_slice(k);\n    }\n    crc32(&buf)\n}\n\n/// An append-only revocation set (mirrors bebop2 `RevocationSet`).\n///\n/// **Item 54 Sentinel:** carries a stored CRC32 over its canonical (sorted) authority\n/// bytes (`snapshot_sorted` — both key and cap-hash sets), recomputed-and-compared via\n/// `IntegrityChecked::verify` at each transition point (§2.4 / §3.3). Every `&mut` mutator\n/// (`revoke_key`/`revoke_capability`/`merge`) re-hashes. A flipped revocation bit silently\n/// UN-revokes a revoked key → admits a revoked agent, so a mismatch is fail-closed\n/// (deny-closed). Qualifies under the 3-axis test (§2.4): (a) long-lived, grows via\n/// anti-entropy `merge`; (b) security-decision authority; (c) live, no per-use at-rest\n/// verify. Mutable — the merge/revoke path is the real re-hash site.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct RevocationSet {\n    revoked_keys: BTreeSet<[u8; 32]>,\n    revoked_cap_hash: BTreeSet<[u8; 32]>,\n    /// Stored CRC32 over the canonical (sorted) authority bytes of both sets.\n    crc: u32,\n}\n\nimpl RevocationSet {\n    /// Empty revocation set. The default CRC is the CRC of the empty sorted snapshot.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let mut r = RevocationSet::default();\n        r.rehash();\n        r\n    }\n    /// Recompute + store the CRC over the canonical (sorted) authority bytes.\n    fn rehash(&mut self) {\n        let (k, c) = self.snapshot_sorted();\n        self.crc = crc32_canonical_revocation(&k, &c);\n    }\n    /// Irreversibly revoke a subject key (or PQ-key id).\n    pub fn revoke_key(&mut self, key: [u8; 32]) {\n        self.revoked_keys.insert(key);\n        self.rehash();\n    }\n    /// Irreversibly revoke a single capability by its revocation hash.\n    pub fn revoke_capability(&mut self, cap_hash: [u8; 32]) {\n        self.revoked_cap_hash.insert(cap_hash);\n        self.rehash();\n    }\n    /// Whether `key` is revoked.\n    pub fn is_revoked_key(&self, key: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n        self.revoked_keys.contains(key)\n    }\n    /// Whether the capability with this revocation hash is revoked.\n    pub fn is_revoked_capability(&self, cap_hash: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {\n        self.revoked_cap_hash.contains(cap_hash)\n    }\n    /// Anti-entropy union.\n    pub fn merge(&mut self, other: &RevocationSet) {\n        self.revoked_keys.extend(other.revoked_keys.iter().copied());\n        self.revoked_cap_hash\n            .extend(other.revoked_cap_hash.iter().copied());\n        self.rehash();\n    }\n    /// Drop an anchor from the enrolling roster (`&mut AnchorRoster`) — OUT-OF-BAND\n    /// operator act; dropping a non-enrolled key is a no-op.\n    pub fn drop_anchor(roster: &mut AnchorRoster, key: &[u8; 32]) {\n        roster.remove(key);\n    }\n    /// Sorted `(keys, cap_hashes)` snapshot (for before/after equality assertions).\n    pub fn snapshot_sorted(&self) -> (Vec<[u8; 32]>, Vec<[u8; 32]>) {\n        let mut k: Vec<[u8; 32]> = self.revoked_keys.iter().copied().collect();\n        let mut c: Vec<[u8; 32]> = self.revoked_cap_hash.iter().copied().collect();\n        k.sort_unstable();\n        c.sort_unstable();\n        (k, c)\n    }\n    /// TEST-ONLY corruption hook (mirrors item 40's planted-fault test): flip one bit of a\n    /// revoked key IN PLACE, leaving `crc` stale — must trip `verify`.\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub fn corrupt_revoked_key_bit(&mut self) {\n        if let Some(k) = self.revoked_keys.iter().next().copied() {\n            let mut flipped = k;\n            flipped[0] ^= 0x01;\n            self.revoked_keys.remove(&k);\n            self.revoked_keys.insert(flipped);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl crate::ports::agent::sentinel::IntegrityChecked for RevocationSet {\n    fn checksum(&self) -> u32 {\n        let (k, c) = self.snapshot_sorted();\n        crc32_canonical_revocation(&k, &c)\n    }\n    fn verify(&self) -> Result<(), crate::ports::agent::sentinel::Corruption> {\n        let actual = self.checksum();\n        if actual == self.crc {\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            Err(crate::ports::agent::sentinel::Corruption {\n                target: crate::ports::agent::sentinel::SentinelTarget::RevocationSet,\n                expected: self.crc,\n                actual,\n            })\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Canonical (sorted, order-independent) CRC32 over a revocation snapshot (keys then\n/// cap-hashes, concatenated).\nfn crc32_canonical_revocation(keys: &[[u8; 32]], caps: &[[u8; 32]]) -> u32 {\n    use crate::fdr::crc32;\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity((keys.len() + caps.len()) * 32);\n    for k in keys {\n        buf.extend_from_slice(k);\n    }\n    for c in caps {\n        buf.extend_from_slice(c);\n    }\n    crc32(&buf)\n}\n\n/// Revocation hash of a capability: SHA3-256 over its canonical TLV bytes.\npub fn revocation_hash(cap: &Capability) -> [u8; 32] {\n    sha3_256(&cap.canonical_bytes_tlv())\n}\n\n/// Stable 32-byte revocation id for a PQ subject key (hash it down).\npub fn pq_key_id(subject_key_pq: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    sha3_256(subject_key_pq)\n}\n\n/// Why a delegation chain failed to root in trust.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ChainError {\n    /// No chain, or the root issuer is not an enrolled anchor (self-issue).\n    UnknownIssuer,\n    /// A link signature did not verify.\n    BadSignature,\n    /// A link (or the chain tail) is expired.\n    Expired,\n    /// Attenuation violated (escalation), tail mis-binding, or effect ⊄ tail scope.\n    ScopeViolation,\n    /// Item 54 Sentinel — a critical live authority struct (`AnchorRoster` /\n    /// `RevocationSet`) failed its read-time CRC integrity check. A flipped trust-root key\n    /// or revocation bit is hardware-fault evidence; the verification is REFUSED (deny-\n    /// closed) after exactly one fsynced FDR `Alarm` names the corrupted struct.\n    IntegrityFault,\n}\n\n/// Anchor-rooted, UCAN-subset chain verification (mirrors bebop2 `verify_chain`): the\n/// root issuer must be an enrolled anchor, every link is signed by its `issued_by`,\n/// links chain (child == next issuer), scope only attenuates (narrows), the tail binds\n/// to `cap.subject_key`, and the requested effect is a subset of the tail scope.\npub fn verify_chain<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n    verifier: &V,\n    roster: &AnchorRoster,\n    chain: &[Delegation],\n    cap: &Capability,\n    now: u64,\n) -> Result<(), ChainError> {\n    // Item 54 Sentinel — read-time integrity check at the authority-use transition point.\n    // `verify_chain` takes the `AnchorRoster` (the trust-root set) but not the\n    // `RevocationSet` (revocation is checked downstream in the admission gate's `check`);\n    // we verify whichever live authority struct is in scope here. On mismatch, emit EXACTLY\n    // ONE fsynced FDR `Alarm` (naming the corrupted struct) and REFUSE the verification\n    // (deny-closed). A flipped trust-root key silently changes which roots authorize the\n    // whole chain — hardware-fault evidence ⇒ certify nothing.\n    if let Err(c) = super::sentinel::verify_candidate(Some(roster), None) {\n        super::sentinel::safe_state_on_corruption(&c);\n        return Err(ChainError::IntegrityFault);\n    }\n    let root = chain.first().ok_or(ChainError::UnknownIssuer)?;\n    if !roster.contains(&root.issued_by) {\n        return Err(ChainError::UnknownIssuer);\n    }\n    let mut prev: Option<&Delegation> = None;\n    for link in chain {\n        if !link.verify_signature(verifier) {\n            return Err(ChainError::BadSignature);\n        }\n        if !(link.expiry > now) {\n            return Err(ChainError::Expired);\n        }\n        // Narrow-only within the link: its effect must be a subset of its own scope.\n        if !link.effect.is_subset_of(&link.scope) {\n            return Err(ChainError::ScopeViolation);\n        }\n        if let Some(p) = prev {\n            // Chaining: child (subject) of the parent must be this link's issuer.\n            if link.issued_by != p.subject {\n                return Err(ChainError::UnknownIssuer);\n            }\n            // Attenuation-only: this link's scope must be a subset of the parent's.\n            if !link.scope.is_subset_of(&p.scope) {\n                return Err(ChainError::ScopeViolation);\n            }\n        }\n        prev = Some(link);\n    }\n    let tail = chain.last().ok_or(ChainError::UnknownIssuer)?;\n    // Tail binds to the capability's subject.\n    if tail.subject != cap.subject_key {\n        return Err(ChainError::ScopeViolation);\n    }\n    // Requested effect ⊆ tail's authorized effect.\n    if !cap.scope.is_subset_of(&tail.effect) {\n        return Err(ChainError::ScopeViolation);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::ports::agent::scope::{Action, Resource};\n\n    fn v() -> RefSigner {\n        RefSigner\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ref_signer_verifies_and_rejects_tamper() {\n        let s = v();\n        let secret = [7u8; 32];\n        let pk = s.classical_public(&secret);\n        let sig = s.sign_classical(&secret, b"hello");\n        assert!(s.verify_classical(&pk, b"hello", &sig));\n        // Corrupt one bit of the signature ⇒ reject.\n        let mut bad = sig.clone();\n        bad[0] ^= 0x01;\n        assert!(!s.verify_classical(&pk, b"hello", &bad));\n        // Different message ⇒ reject.\n        assert!(!s.verify_classical(&pk, b"hellp", &sig));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ref_signer_pq_width_and_verify() {\n        let s = v();\n        let seed = [0xABu8; 32];\n        let pk = s.pq_public(&seed);\n        assert_eq!(pk.len(), ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN, "ML-DSA-65 width preserved");\n        let sig = s.sign_pq(&seed, b"msg");\n        assert!(s.verify_pq(&pk, b"msg", &sig));\n        let mut bad = sig.clone();\n        bad[3] ^= 0x80;\n        assert!(!s.verify_pq(&pk, b"msg", &bad));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn node_id_binds_both_keys() {\n        let s = v();\n        let cls = s.classical_public(&[1u8; 32]);\n        let pq = s.pq_public(&[2u8; 32]);\n        let a = NodeId::from_keys(&pq, &cls);\n        let b = NodeId::from_keys(&pq, &cls);\n        assert_eq!(a, b);\n        // Change either key ⇒ different id.\n        let cls2 = s.classical_public(&[9u8; 32]);\n        assert_ne!(a, NodeId::from_keys(&pq, &cls2));\n        let pq2 = s.pq_public(&[9u8; 32]);\n        assert_ne!(a, NodeId::from_keys(&pq2, &cls));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn frame_signs_and_verifies_both_legs() {\n        let s = v();\n        let (cls_secret, pq_secret) = ([3u8; 32], [4u8; 32]);\n        let cap = Capability::new_hybrid(\n            s.classical_public(&cls_secret),\n            s.pq_public(&pq_secret),\n            Scope::single(Resource::AgentBridge, Action::AdmitAgent),\n            [1u8; 8],\n            9999,\n        );\n        let mut f = SignedFrame::new(cap, b"payload".to_vec());\n        f.sign_classical(&s, &cls_secret);\n        f.sign_pq(&s, &pq_secret);\n        assert!(f.verify_classical(&s));\n        assert!(f.verify_pq(&s));\n        // Tamper the payload ⇒ both legs fail.\n        let mut t = f.clone();\n        t.payload = b"evil".to_vec();\n        assert!(!t.verify_classical(&s));\n        assert!(!t.verify_pq(&s));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_chain_rejects_self_signed_no_anchor() {\n        let s = v();\n        let secret = [5u8; 32];\n        let pk = s.classical_public(&secret);\n        let cap = Capability::new_hybrid(\n            pk,\n            s.pq_public(&[6u8; 32]),\n            Scope::single(Resource::AgentBridge, Action::AdmitAgent),\n            [1u8; 8],\n            9999,\n        );\n        // Empty chain ⇒ UnknownIssuer.\n        let roster = AnchorRoster::new();\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify_chain(&s, &roster, &[], &cap, 0),\n            Err(ChainError::UnknownIssuer)\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn verify_chain_accepts_anchor_rooted() {\n        let s = v();\n        let (anchor_secret, leaf_secret) = ([10u8; 32], [11u8; 32]);\n        let anchor_pk = s.classical_public(&anchor_secret);\n        let leaf_pk = s.classical_public(&leaf_secret);\n        let scope = Scope::single(Resource::AgentBridge, Action::AdmitAgent);\n        let cap = Capability::new_hybrid(\n            leaf_pk,\n            s.pq_public(&[12u8; 32]),\n            scope.clone(),\n            [1u8; 8],\n            9999,\n This is a PORT-LOCAL enum, generalizing the bebop2 `Resource`/`Action` closed set\n//! for the agent-bridge admission decision. It intentionally does NOT link bebop2's\n//! `proto-cap` (the dowiz kernel carries no such dependency); the real bebop2\n//! `HybridGate`/`AnchorRoster` are injected at the integration boundary through the\n//! `AdmissionGate`/`SignatureVerifier` seams (see `admission.rs` / `cap.rs`), exactly\n//! as `ports/llm.rs` is a trait seam whose concrete backend lives elsewhere.\n//!\n//! ⚠ DISCRIMINANT-ALLOCATION CANON-DIFF (B1 DoD item 7, UNRATIFIED): B1 pins\n//! `Resource::AgentBridge = 0x12` — the next byte after the bebop2 high-water mark\n//! `Resource::Migration = 0x11`. B2 (`WorkReceipt`) independently proposed `0x12`, a\n//! genuine collision the lead-agent Wave-0 discriminant ruling must resolve before any\n//! shared `scope.rs` edit lands. `Action::{AdmitAgent, InvokeAgent}` were left\n//! "currently-unnumbered" by the blueprint; provisional bytes `0x1F`/`0x20` are chosen\n//! here (past bebop2's `0x18` high-water mark and B2's proposed `0x19–0x1E` action\n//! block) and are FLAGGED as pending that same ruling. The `discriminants_are_pinned`\n//! wire-stability test catches an accidental renumber mechanically.\n\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n/// A protocol resource an agent capability may target. Closed set ⇒ the admission\n/// gate is exhaustively checkable; an unknown discriminant byte fails decode (fail-closed).\n#[cfg_attr(feature = "json-api", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum Resource {\n    /// A transport route / channel.\n    Route,\n    /// A ledger entry (append / read) — RED-LINE (money).\n    Ledger,\n    /// A restaurant / courier menu (catalog read).\n    Menu,\n    /// A customer order (create / read / mutate).\n    Order,\n    /// An analytics / reporting projection (read-only).\n    Analytics,\n    /// A customer / account record.\n    Customer,\n    /// A knowledge / embedding corpus (RAG).\n    Corpus,\n    /// Authentication / authority change — RED-LINE (auth).\n    Auth,\n    /// Secrets exposure — RED-LINE (secrets).\n    Secret,\n    /// Schema / data migration — RED-LINE (destructive bulk).\n    Migration,\n    /// **NEW (B1):** the agent-bridge admission surface. A capability scoped\n    /// `(AgentBridge, AdmitAgent)` authorizes admitting an agent manifest;\n    /// `(AgentBridge, InvokeAgent)` authorizes one delegated sub-agent invocation.\n    /// Pinned `0x12` — see the CANON-DIFF note above.\n    AgentBridge,\n    /// **NEW:** a native, read-only HTTP fetch + readable-text extraction (P40\n    /// `ToolResource::WebFetch`). Deliberately NOT red-line — read-only, no\n    /// network write, no interactive/JS execution (that stays an external tool\n    /// behind agent-browser, never reimplemented in-kernel — see\n    /// `docs/design/` native-agentic-browsing research). Pinned `0x13`, next\n    /// free byte after `AgentBridge = 0x12`.\n    Web,\n}\n\nimpl Resource {\n    /// Explicit discriminant byte (pinned; not compiler-chosen).\n    pub fn discriminant(&self) -> u8 {\n        match self {\n            Resource::Route => 0x01,\n            Resource::Ledger => 0x02,\n            Resource::Menu => 0x05,\n            Resource::Order => 0x06,\n            Resource::Analytics => 0x07,\n            Resource::Customer => 0x08,\n            Resource::Corpus => 0x09,\n            Resource::Auth => 0x0F,\n            Resource::Secret => 0x10,\n            Resource::Migration => 0x11,\n            Resource::AgentBridge => 0x12,\n            Resource::Web => 0x13,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Inverse of [`Resource::discriminant`]. `None` for unknown bytes ⇒ decode is\n    /// fail-closed (no default/panic on a malformed scope).\n    pub fn from_discriminant(b: u8) -> Option<Resource> {\n        Some(match b {\n            0x01 => Resource::Route,\n            0x02 => Resource::Ledger,\n            0x05 => Resource::Menu,\n            0x06 => Resource::Order,\n            0x07 => Resource::Analytics,\n            0x08 => Resource::Customer,\n            0x09 => Resource::Corpus,\n            0x0F => Resource::Auth,\n            0x10 => Resource::Secret,\n            0x11 => Resource::Migration,\n            0x12 => Resource::AgentBridge,\n            0x13 => Resource::Web,\n            _ => return None,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Whether this resource is a RED-LINE class (money / auth / secrets / migrations).\n    /// A manifest whose scope touches one of these is denied unless operator-allow-listed.\n    pub fn is_red_line(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(\n            self,\n            Resource::Ledger | Resource::Auth | Resource::Secret | Resource::Migration\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// An action permitted on a [`Resource`]. Closed set.\n#[cfg_attr(feature = "json-api", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum Action {\n    /// Authorize a send on the resource.\n    Send,\n    /// Authorize a read/query of the resource.\n    Read,\n    /// Authorize an append/write to the resource.\n    Append,\n    /// Render a view / template (read-only presentation).\n    Render,\n    /// Create a new order (mutation).\n    CreateOrder,\n    /// Read a precomputed projection (read-only).\n    ReadProjection,\n    /// Settlement recorded (ledger i64) — RED-LINE.\n    SettlementRecorded,\n    /// Authenticate / change authority — RED-LINE.\n    Authenticate,\n    /// Deploy / expose a secret — RED-LINE.\n    DeploySecret,\n    /// Run a schema / data migration — RED-LINE.\n    RunMigration,\n    /// **NEW (B1):** admit an agent manifest (the admission-frame verb). Provisional\n    /// `0x1F` — see the CANON-DIFF note above.\n    AdmitAgent,\n    /// **NEW (B1):** invoke a delegated sub-agent (the F10 depth-witness verb — each\n    /// such link in a delegation chain is one unit of cryptographically-witnessed\n    /// invocation depth). Provisional `0x20`.\n    InvokeAgent,\n}\n\nimpl Action {\n    /// Explicit discriminant byte (pinned; not compiler-chosen).\n    pub fn discriminant(&self) -> u8 {\n        match self {\n            Action::Send => 0x01,\n            Action::Read => 0x02,\n            Action::Append => 0x03,\n            Action::Render => 0x04,\n            Action::CreateOrder => 0x05,\n            Action::ReadProjection => 0x06,\n            Action::SettlementRecorded => 0x13,\n            Action::Authenticate => 0x16,\n            Action::DeploySecret => 0x17,\n            Action::RunMigration => 0x18,\n            Action::AdmitAgent => 0x1F,\n            Action::InvokeAgent => 0x20,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Inverse of [`Action::discriminant`]. `None` for unknown bytes ⇒ fail-closed.\n    pub fn from_discriminant(b: u8) -> Option<Action> {\n        Some(match b {\n            0x01 => Action::Send,\n            0x02 => Action::Read,\n            0x03 => Action::Append,\n            0x04 => Action::Render,\n            0x05 => Action::CreateOrder,\n            0x06 => Action::ReadProjection,\n            0x13 => Action::SettlementRecorded,\n            0x16 => Action::Authenticate,\n            0x17 => Action::DeploySecret,\n            0x18 => Action::RunMigration,\n            0x1F => Action::AdmitAgent,\n            0x20 => Action::InvokeAgent,\n            _ => return None,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Whether this action is a RED-LINE verb.\n    pub fn is_red_line(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(\n            self,\n            Action::SettlementRecorded\n                | Action::Authenticate\n                | Action::DeploySecret\n                | Action::RunMigration\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// A set of authorized `(resource, action)` pairs (UCAN "narrow-only" attenuation\n/// works over set-subset, mirroring bebop2 `Scope`/`Effect`). No score, no rating.\n#[cfg_attr(feature = "json-api", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub struct Scope {\n    /// Set of authorized `(resource, action)` pairs.\n    pub grants: Vec<(Resource, Action)>,\n}\n\nimpl Scope {\n    /// Construct a scope from an explicit set of pairs.\n    pub fn new(grants: Vec<(Resource, Action)>) -> Self {\n        Scope { grants }\n    }\n\n    /// Single-pair convenience constructor.\n    pub fn single(resource: Resource, action: Action) -> Self {\n        Scope {\n            grants: vec![(resource, action)],\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Fixed-layout canonical encoding: `len(u16 LE) || (resource_u8, action_u8)*`.\n    /// Self-delimiting and fail-closed on a truncated tail. No serde.\n    pub fn to_tlv_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let n = self.grants.len() as u16;\n        let mut out = n.to_le_bytes().to_vec();\n        for (r, a) in &self.grants {\n            out.push(r.discriminant());\n            out.push(a.discriminant());\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    /// Strict decode of [`Scope::to_tlv_bytes`]. Fail-closed: an unknown resource/action\n    /// byte, a wrong length, or trailing bytes yield `None`.\n    pub fn from_tlv_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<Scope> {\n        if bytes.len() < 2 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let n = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1]]) as usize;\n        if bytes.len() != 2 + n * 2 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let mut grants = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n        for i in 0..n {\n            let r = Resource::from_discriminant(bytes[2 + i * 2])?;\n            let a = Action::from_discriminant(bytes[2 + i * 2 + 1])?;\n            grants.push((r, a));\n        }\n        Some(Scope { grants })\n    }\n\n    /// Whether every pair in `self` appears in `super_scope` (narrow-or-equal). An empty\n    /// scope is a subset of anything (least privilege).\n    pub fn is_subset_of(&self, super_scope: &Scope) -> bool {\n        self.grants.iter().all(|p| super_scope.grants.contains(p))\n    }\n\n    /// Whether ANY grant in this scope is a RED-LINE (resource OR action).\n    pub fn touches_red_line(&self) -> bool {\n        self.grants\n            .iter()\n            .any(|(r, a)| r.is_red_line() || a.is_red_line())\n    }\n}\n\n/// The armed red-line policy (mirrors bebop2 `RedLinePolicy`). Deny-by-default is the\n/// production posture; `AllowList` narrows to operator-enumerated verbs-on-objects.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum RedLinePolicy {\n    /// Reject any capability whose scope touches a red line unless allow-listed below.\n    DenyByDefault,\n    /// Only the enumerated scopes may pass the red line.\n    AllowList(Vec<Scope>),\n}\n\nimpl RedLinePolicy {\n    /// `Ok(())` iff `scope` is permitted under this policy. A non-red-line scope always\n    /// passes; a red-line scope passes only if explicitly allow-listed.\n    pub fn check(&self, scope: &Scope) -> Result<(), ()> {\n        if !scope.touches_red_line() {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        match self {\n            RedLinePolicy::DenyByDefault => Err(()),\n            RedLinePolicy::AllowList(allowed) => {\n                // Every red-line grant must be covered by an allow-listed scope.\n                if scope.is_subset_of_any(allowed) {\n                    Ok(())\n                } else {\n                    Err(())\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Scope {\n    fn is_subset_of_any(&self, supers: &[Scope]) -> bool {\n        // Union the allow-listed scopes and check subset against the union.\n        let mut union = Scope::default();\n        for s in supers {\n            for g in &s.grants {\n                if !union.grants.contains(g) {\n                    union.grants.push(*g);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        self.is_subset_of(&union)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn discriminants_are_pinned() {\n        // Wire/signing contract — changing any of these is a breaking change. The new\n        // B1 variants are pinned here so a merge/renumber is caught mechanically\n        // (B1 migration step 1 wire-stability pin).\n        assert_eq!(Resource::AgentBridge.discriminant(), 0x12);\n        assert_eq!(Action::AdmitAgent.discriminant(), 0x1F);\n        assert_eq!(Action::InvokeAgent.discriminant(), 0x20);\n        // A few inherited-from-bebop2 pins (alignment if ever unified).\n        assert_eq!(Resource::Ledger.discriminant(), 0x02);\n        assert_eq!(Resource::Migration.discriminant(), 0x11);\n        assert_eq!(Action::SettlementRecorded.discriminant(), 0x13);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resource_action_roundtrip_fail_closed() {\n        for r in [Resource::AgentBridge, Resource::Route, Resource::Auth] {\n            assert_eq!(Resource::from_discriminant(r.discriminant()), Some(r));\n        }\n        // Unknown byte fails closed.\n        assert_eq!(Resource::from_discriminant(0xEE), None);\n        assert_eq!(Action::from_discriminant(0xEE), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_tlv_roundtrip_and_reject_garbage() {\n        let s = Scope::new(vec![\n            (Resource::AgentBridge, Action::AdmitAgent),\n            (Resource::Menu, Action::Read),\n        ]);\n        let bytes = s.to_tlv_bytes();\n        assert_eq!(Scope::from_tlv_bytes(&bytes), Some(s));\n        // Truncated / unknown-byte tails fail closed.\n        assert_eq!(Scope::from_tlv_bytes(&bytes[..bytes.len() - 1]), None);\n        let mut bad = bytes.clone();\n        *bad.last_mut().unwrap() = 0xEE; // unknown action byte\n        assert_eq!(Scope::from_tlv_bytes(&bad), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_line_classification() {\n        assert!(Scope::single(Resource::Ledger, Action::SettlementRecorded).touches_red_line());\n        assert!(Scope::single(Resource::Auth, Action::Authenticate).touches_red_line());\n        assert!(!Scope::single(Resource::Menu, Action::Read).touches_red_line());\n        // AgentBridge admission itself is NOT a red line (it is the gated surface).\n        assert!(!Scope::single(Resource::AgentBridge, Action::AdmitAgent).touches_red_line());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn deny_by_default_rejects_red_line_allows_clean() {\n        let p = RedLinePolicy::DenyByDefault;\n        assert!(p\n            .check(&Scope::single(Resource::Ledger, Action::SettlementRecorded))\n            .is_err());\n        assert!(p\n            .check(&Scope::single(Resource::Menu, Action::Read))\n            .is_ok());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn allow_list_narrows_precisely() {\n        let p = RedLinePolicy::AllowList(vec![Scope::single(\n            Resource::Ledger,\n            Action::SettlementRecorded,\n        )]);\n        assert!(p\n            .check(&Scope::single(Resource::Ledger, Action::SettlementRecorded))\n            .is_ok());\n        // A different red-line scope is still denied.\n        assert!(p\n            .check(&Scope::single(Resource::Auth, Action::Authenticate))\n            .is_err());\n    }\n}\n	14843	-1	-1		d3eef606a598b176bc2f78d38750c2454dfe9d4cf97305c3a2cfa65f1165c9851942a02f6ac8a6524b4810af3d46dd7a9ff95015b3e0266ae107ea1f26c8fc0d5eb203916943621986c53388c6bbe15b70ea492a205f434fe5bdbb87e64bdde4216fe706134ad2c9f059789fca458793edf26d2bd5a71d1c9551e629a5283ee0

A narrow, enumerable set of long-lived, mutable authority structs are protected by a\n//! stored CRC32 over their canonical (sorted) authority bytes. At each *transition point*\n//! (once per authority-use), the struct's stored CRC is recomputed-and-compared against\n//! the live bytes. On mismatch — the signature of an in-memory bit-flip on non-ECC consumer\n//! RAM — exactly ONE fsynced FDR `Alarm` is emitted (naming the corrupted struct) and the\n//! caller takes the deterministic fail-closed path (deny-closed for capability\n//! verification). This is the live-struct analog of item 40's at-rest weights checksum;\n//! same shared `fdr::crc32`, same Safe-State semantics, complementary plane (mutable\n//! structs item 40 structurally cannot touch).\n//!\n//! ## Reuse, max-nativeness (roadmap:894)\n//! Reuses the ONE in-kernel `fdr::crc32` (lifted to always-compiled in `fdr/mod.rs`,\n//! blueprint §3.2). No new primitive, no new algorithm, no new dependency. The threat is\n//! a hardware memory fault, NOT an in-memory adversary, so CRC32 (not a cryptographic hash)\n//! suffices — the blueprint's explicit proportionality ruling.\n//!\n//! ## The critical-struct registry (3-axis test)\n//! A struct qualifies iff (a) long-lived, (b) an authority input to a money/safety/\n//! decision path, and (c) has no at-rest backing that already verifies it (blueprint\n//! §2.4). Each registered struct is recorded below with its 3-axis justification. The\n//! present-day instances (`AnchorRoster`, `RevocationSet`) land FIRST — they exist now and\n//! need no unbuilt item (items 47/50). The canonical instance (`Invariants`) is deferred\n//! behind item 47; the lower-value `Admitter.admitted` is deferred behind roster/revocation.\n//!\n//! EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED (honest boundary calls, blueprint §2.4):\n//! - `FSM_ADJ` / `FSM_GOLDEN_SIGNATURE` (`order_machine.rs`): `const`/immutable-after-compile\n//!   static data ⇒ item 40's build-time golden-CRC plane, NOT this live-mutable plane. A\n//!   flipped `const` is item 40's job. Named so the boundary is explicit, not silently\n//!   skipped.\n//! - Transient hot-loop scratch (arena buffers): not long-lived, not authority.\n//! - Anything already at-rest-verified (event_log chain, backup CAS): axis (c) fails.\n\nuse crate::fdr;\n\nuse super::cap::{AnchorRoster, RevocationSet};\n\n/// The named, in-code enumeration of the qualifying live-struct registry (blueprint §5:\n/// "The critical-struct registry is enumerated in-code with a per-struct 3-axis\n/// justification"). Adding a sentinelized struct is a deliberate, reviewed edit here — the\n/// registry is the single source of truth for what the Sentinel protects, and a reviewer\n/// can read each qualification.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum SentinelTarget {\n    /// `AnchorRoster` — the trust-root set (cap.rs:377). A flipped anchor key silently\n    /// changes which roots authorize the entire capability chain in `verify_chain`.\n    /// (a) long-lived roster of trusted anchor keys; (b) security-decision authority;\n    /// (c) held live in memory, no per-use at-rest re-verify.\n    AnchorRoster,\n    /// `RevocationSet` — revoked keys/caps (cap.rs:412). A flipped revocation bit silently\n    /// UN-revokes a revoked key → admits a revoked agent.\n    /// (a) long-lived, grows via anti-entropy `merge`; (b) security-decision authority;\n    /// (c) live, no per-use at-rest verify. Mutable — the `merge`/`revoke_key` path is a\n    /// real re-hash site (§3.3).\n    RevocationSet,\n}\n\nimpl SentinelTarget {\n    /// The stable, greppable name carried on the FDR `Alarm` (item 54 Safe-State evidence).\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            SentinelTarget::AnchorRoster => "AnchorRoster",\n            SentinelTarget::RevocationSet => "RevocationSet",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The reason a struct's verification handle could not be produced. Distinct from a\n/// *detected corruption* (`Corruption`): a `None` handle is a programming error (a\n/// candidate registry entry that does not contain the expected struct), never a live\n/// memory fault.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SentinelUnavailable {\n    /// No live struct of the registered type is present in the candidate (should not\n    /// happen for a well-formed candidate — fail-closed, the verification is refused).\n    NoHandle,\n}\n\n/// CRC32 over the canonical (sorted) authority bytes of a live struct, plus a recompute\n/// + compare against the stored value. Implemented by every sentinelized struct.\n///\n/// The hashed form MUST be canonical (sorted) so that mutation *order* does not spuriously\n/// change the checksum — `AnchorRoster::snapshot_sorted` / `RevocationSet::snapshot_sorted`\n/// supply exactly this (blueprint §3.2 / §7.1-4).\npub trait IntegrityChecked {\n    /// CRC32 of the struct's canonical authority bytes.\n    fn checksum(&self) -> u32;\n    /// Recompute-and-compare against the struct's stored CRC. `Ok(())` iff they match.\n    fn verify(&self) -> Result<(), Corruption>;\n}\n\n/// A detected live-struct integrity fault: the stored CRC no longer matches the live\n/// bytes. Semantically a hardware/memory fault (item 40 semantics) — fail-closed.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Corruption {\n    /// Which registered live struct tripped.\n    pub target: SentinelTarget,\n    /// The stored (expected) CRC.\n    pub expected: u32,\n    /// The recomputed CRC over live bytes.\n    pub actual: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Corruption {\n    /// The stable name for the tripped struct (carried on the FDR `Alarm`).\n    pub fn target_name(&self) -> &'static str {\n        self.target.as_str()\n    }\n}\n\n/// The fail-closed Safe-State action for a detected corruption (blueprint §3.5): emit\n/// EXACTLY ONE fsynced FDR `Alarm` naming the corrupted struct, then let the caller take\n/// its deterministic deny path. A candidate with neither struct present is trivially clean.\npub fn verify_candidate(\n    roster: Option<&AnchorRoster>,\n    revocations: Option<&RevocationSet>,\n) -> Result<(), Corruption> {\n    if let Some(r) = roster {\n        if let Err(c) = r.verify() {\n            return Err(c);\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(rev) = revocations {\n        if let Err(c) = rev.verify() {\n            return Err(c);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::fdr;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sentinel_target_names_are_stable_and_greppable() {\n        // The names carried on FDR Alarms must be stable + greppable for forensic tooling.\n        assert_eq!(SentinelTarget::AnchorRoster.as_str(), "AnchorRoster");\n        assert_eq!(SentinelTarget::RevocationSet.as_str(), "RevocationSet");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn crc32_is_callable_from_a_wasm_compiled_path() {\n        // Acceptance criterion: the lifted `fdr::crc32` is always compiled (the KAT vector\n        // proves behavior-preserving move from the wasm-gated `ring`). The `ring.rs:334`\n        // KAT is the canonical check; this asserts the public alias stays live.\n        assert_eq!(fdr::crc32(b"123456789"), 0xCBF4_3926);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn clean_roster_and_revocation_verify_silent() {\n        // A clean run over the full registry produces ZERO corruption (no false trips).\n        let mut r = AnchorRoster::new();\n        r.enroll(&[7u8; 32]);\n        let mut rev = RevocationSet::new();\n        rev.revoke_key([9u8; 32]);\n        assert!(r.verify().is_ok());\n        assert!(rev.verify().is_ok());\n        assert!(verify_candidate(Some(&r), Some(&rev)).is_ok());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn planted_roster_corruption_trips_fail_closed() {\n        // Behavioral oracle (blueprint §4.1): a planted single-bit flip of the live struct's\n        // authority bytes trips the Safe-State path AND writes exactly one recoverable Alarm.\n        let mut r = AnchorRoster::new();\n        r.enroll(&[7u8; 32]);\n        // NOTE: corruption is injected via the test-only `corrupt_anchor_bit` on the struct\n        // (mirroring item 40's planted-fault test). The Sentinel's detection is what we prove.\n        r.corrupt_anchor_bit();\n        let c = r\n            .verify()\n            .expect_err("planted corruption must trip verify()");\n        assert_eq!(c.target, SentinelTarget::AnchorRoster);\n        assert_ne!(c.expected, c.actual);\n\n        // The Safec-State action emits exactly one FDR Alarm (inert unless a sink is\n        // installed; we just prove it does not panic and returns).\n        safe_state_on_corruption(&c);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn mutate_then_read_through_central_mutator_passes() {\n        // Re-hash correctness (blueprint §3.3): legitimate mutation via a central mutator\n        // must NOT trip the Sentinel on the next read.\n        let mut r = AnchorRoster::new();\n        r.enroll(&[1u8; 32]);\n        assert!(r.verify().is_ok(), "after enroll");\n\n        let mut rev = RevocationSet::new();\n        rev.revoke_key([2u8; 32]);\n        assert!(rev.verify().is_ok(), "after revoke_key");\n        rev.merge(&{\n            let mut o = RevocationSet::new();\n            o.revoke_capability([3u8; 32]);\n            o\n        });\n        assert!(rev.verify().is_ok(), "after merge");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn planted_revocation_corruption_trips_fail_closed() {\n        // Behavioral oracle for the RevocationSet (the mutable instance). A planted single-\n        // bit flip of a revoked key trips verify() and the fail-closed Safe-State path.\n        let mut rev = RevocationSet::new();\n        rev.revoke_key([9u8; 32]);\n        rev.corrupt_revoked_key_bit();\n        let c = rev\n            .verify()\n            .expect_err("planted revocation corruption must trip verify()");\n        assert_eq!(c.target, SentinelTarget::RevocationSet);\n        assert_ne!(c.expected, c.actual);\n        safe_state_on_corruption(&c);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn planted_roster_corruption_refuses_verify_chain() {\n        // End-to-end: a corrupted AnchorRoster refuses `verify_chain` with\n        // `IntegrityFault` (deny-closed) — the admission-level fault propagation.\n        use crate::ports::agent::cap::{\n            verify_chain, Capability, ChainError, RefSigner, SignatureVerifier,\n        };\n        let s = RefSigner;\n        let v = &s;\n        let mut roster = AnchorRoster::new();\n        roster.enroll(&s.classical_public(&[3u8; 32]));\n        // Corrupt the live roster BEFORE it is used as an authority input.\n        roster.corrupt_anchor_bit();\n        let cap = Capability::new_hybrid(\n            s.classical_public(&[5u8; 32]),\n            s.pq_public(&[6u8; 32]),\n            crate::ports::agent::scope::Scope::single(\n                crate::ports::agent::scope::Resource::AgentBridge,\n                crate::ports::agent::scope::Action::AdmitAgent,\n            ),\n            [1u8; 8],\n            9999,\n        );\n        let mut rev = RevocationSet::new();\n        let res = verify_chain(v, &roster, &[], &cap, 0);\n        assert_eq!(res, Err(ChainError::IntegrityFault));\n        let _ = &mut rev;\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn clean_run_produces_zero_alarm_records() {\n        // Acceptance criterion: a clean run over the full registry produces ZERO Alarms.\n        // The FDR sink is a process-global `OnceLock` (fdr::init is idempotent — the first\n        // init in the test binary wins the ring dir), so a per-test ring round-trip cannot\n        // prove isolation here. Instead we prove the Sentinel's SILENCE directly: a clean\n        // roster + revocation verify clean (no `Corruption`), which means `safe_state_on_corruption`\n        // — the ONLY alarm emitter — is never reached. Zero corruption ⇒ zero alarms, by construction.\n        use crate::ports::agent::cap::{\n            verify_chain, Capability, ChainError, RefSigner, SignatureVerifier,\n        };\n        use crate::ports::agent::sentinel::{verify_candidate, SentinelTarget};\n\n        let s = RefSigner;\n        let roster = AnchorRoster::new();\n        let mut rev = RevocationSet::new();\n        // Clean authority structs must verify with NO detected corruption (no alarm path).\n        assert!(\n            verify_candidate(Some(&roster), None).is_ok(),\n            "clean AnchorRoster must not trip the Sentinel"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            verify_candidate(None, Some(&rev)).is_ok(),\n            "clean RevocationSet must not trip the Sentinel"\n        );\n\n        // And a clean verify_chain over the clean roster must NOT return IntegrityFault\n        // (the alarm-triggering branch) — it returns UnknownIssuer only because no chain root.\n        let cap = Capability::new_hybrid(\n            s.classical_public(&[5u8; 32]),\n            s.pq_public(&[6u8; 32]),\n            crate::ports::agent::scope::Scope::single(\n                crate::ports::agent::scope::Resource::AgentBridge,\n                crate::ports::agent::scope::Action::AdmitAgent,\n            ),\n            [1u8; 8],\n            9999,\n        );\n        let res = verify_chain(&s, &roster, &[], &cap, 0);\n        assert_eq!(res, Err(ChainError::UnknownIssuer));\n        // Guard against a vacuous always-trip: a corruption would surface as IntegrityFault,\n        // which we explicitly did NOT get on the clean path.\n        assert_ne!(res, Err(ChainError::IntegrityFault));\n        let _ = SentinelTarget::AnchorRoster;\n        let _ = &mut rev;\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn planted_fault_refuses_verify_chain_with_integrity_fault() {\n        // A corrupted live AnchorRoster must trip the Sentinel and refuse verification\n        // (deny-closed, IntegrityFault). 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/agent/command_filter.rs	command_filter · 180 lines	use alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ExactCommand {\n    pub command_id: CommandId,\n    pub payload: Vec<u8>,\n    pub expected_mac: Option<[u8; 32]>,\n}\n\nimpl ExactCommand {\n    pub fn new(command_id: CommandId, payload: Vec<u8>) -> Self {\n        ExactCommand {\n            command_id,\n            payload,\n            expected_mac: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_mac(mut self, mac: [u8; 32]) -> Self {\n        self.expected_mac = Some(mac);\n        self\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub struct CommandId(pub u8);\n\nimpl CommandId {\n    pub fn new(b: u8) -> Self {\n        CommandId(b)\n    }\n\n    pub fn discriminant(&self) -> u8 {\n        self.0\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct CommandCatalog {\n    golden: Vec<ExactCommand>,\n}\n\nimpl CommandCatalog {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        CommandCatalog::default()\n    }\n\n    pub fn register(&mut self, cmd: ExactCommand) {\n        self.golden.push(cmd);\n    }\n\n    pub fn golden(&self) -> &[ExactCommand] {\n        &self.golden\n    }\n\n    pub fn mac(key: &[u8; 32], command_id: CommandId, payload: &[u8], nonce: u64) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut preimage = Vec::with_capacity(32 + 1 + payload.len() + 8);\n        preimage.extend_from_slice(key);\n        preimage.push(command_id.discriminant());\n        preimage.extend_from_slice(payload);\n        preimage.extend_from_slice(&nonce.to_le_bytes());\n        sha3_256(&preimage)\n    }\n\n    pub fn verify(\n        &self,\n        bytes: &[u8],\n        mac_key: Option<&[u8; 32]>,\n    ) -> Result<(), CommandVerifyError> {\n        let min_len = 1 + 2 + 8 + 32;\n        if bytes.len() < min_len {\n            return Err(CommandVerifyError::Truncated);\n        }\n        let command_id = CommandId(bytes[0]);\n        let payload_len = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[1], bytes[2]]) as usize;\n        let total_expected = 1 + 2 + payload_len + 8 + 32;\n        if bytes.len() != total_expected {\n            return Err(CommandVerifyError::BadLength);\n        }\n        let payload = bytes[3..3 + payload_len].to_vec();\n        let nonce = u64::from_le_bytes(\n            bytes[3 + payload_len..3 + payload_len + 8]\n                .try_into()\n                .unwrap(),\n        );\n        let supplied_mac: [u8; 32] = bytes[3 + payload_len + 8..3 + payload_len + 8 + 32]\n            .try_into()\n            .unwrap();\n\n        let matched = self\n            .golden\n            .iter()\n            .find(|g| g.command_id == command_id && g.payload == payload);\n        let golden = matched.ok_or(CommandVerifyError::UnknownCommand)?;\n\n        match golden.expected_mac {\n            Some(expected) => {\n                let key = mac_key.ok_or(CommandVerifyError::MacNotBound)?;\n                let computed = Self::mac(key, command_id, &payload, nonce);\n                if computed != supplied_mac || computed != expected {\n                    return Err(CommandVerifyError::MacMismatch);\n                }\n            }\n            None => {}\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum CommandVerifyError {\n    UnknownCommand,\n    MacMismatch,\n    Truncated,\n    BadLength,\n    MacNotBound,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn exact_command_roundtrip_with_mac() {\n        let mut catalog = CommandCatalog::new();\n        let cmd = ExactCommand::new(CommandId::new(0x01), vec![0xAB, 0xCD]);\n        let key: [u8; 32] = *b"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef";\n        let nonce: u64 = 0x1122334455667788;\n        let mac = CommandCatalog::mac(&key, cmd.command_id, &cmd.payload, nonce);\n        let bound = cmd.with_mac(mac);\n        catalog.register(bound);\n\n        let mut bytes = Vec::new();\n        bytes.push(CommandId::new(0x01).discriminant());\n        bytes.extend_from_slice(&(vec![0xAB, 0xCD].len() as u16).to_le_bytes());\n        bytes.extend_from_slice(&[0xAB, 0xCD]);\n        bytes.extend_from_slice(&nonce.to_le_bytes());\n        bytes.extend_from_slice(&mac);\n\n        assert!(catalog.verify(&bytes, Some(&key)).is_ok());\n\n        let mut bad_len = bytes.clone();\n        bad_len.push(0x00);\n        assert!(catalog.verify(&bad_len, Some(&key)).is_err());\n\n        let mut bad_payload = bytes.clone();\n        bad_payload[3] ^= 0x01;\n        assert!(catalog.verify(&bad_payload, Some(&key)).is_err());\n\n        let mut bad_mac = bytes.clone();\n        bad_mac[bytes.len() - 1] ^= 0x01;\n        assert!(catalog.verify(&bad_mac, Some(&key)).is_err());\n\n        assert!(catalog.verify(&bytes[..10], Some(&key)).is_err());\n\n        let mut alt_bytes = bytes.clone();\n        alt_bytes[2] ^= 0x01;\n        assert!(catalog.verify(&alt_bytes, Some(&key)).is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn mac_same_input_same_output() {\n        let key = [0x11u8; header, requiring the exact expected tag (fixed order).\n    fn header(&mut self, expected: u8) -> Result<usize, ManifestParseError> {\n        if self.i + 5 > self.b.len() {\n            return Err(ManifestParseError::Truncated);\n        }\n        Ok(len)\n    }\n    /// Read a fixed-width field, enforcing the declared length.\n    fn field_fixed(&mut self, tag: u8, want: usize) -> Result<&'a [u8], ManifestParseError> {\n        let len = self.header(tag)?;\n        if len != want {\n            return Err(ManifestParseError::BadLength(match tag {\n                T_NODE_ID => "agent_node_id",\n                T_SUBJECT_KEY => "subject_key",\n                T_SUBJECT_KEY_PQ => "subject_key_pq",\n                T_BUDGET_REQUEST => "budget_request",\n                T_NONCE => "nonce",\n                T_EXPIRY => "expiry",\n                _ => "fixed-field",\n            }));\n        }\n        let v = &self.b[self.i..self.i + len];\n        self.i += len;\n        Ok(v)\n    }\n    /// Read a variable-width field.\n    fn field_var(&mut self, tag: u8) -> Result<&'a [u8], ManifestParseError> {\n        let len = self.header(tag)?;\n        let v = &self.b[self.i..self.i + len];\n        self.i += len;\n        Ok(v)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::ports::agent::scope::{Action, Resource};\n\n    fn sample() -> AgentManifest {\n        AgentManifest {\n            agent_node_id: [9u8; 32],\n            subject_key: [1u8; 32],\n            subject_key_pq: vec![7u8; ML_DSA_65_PK_LEN],\n            agent_caps: AgentCaps {\n                invoke_tool: true,\n                read_resource: true,\n                ..Default::default()\n            },\n            action_scopes: Scope::new(vec![\n                (Resource::AgentBridge, Action::AdmitAgent),\n                (Resource::Menu, Action::Read),\n            ]),\n            resource_needs: vec![ResourceNeed::EgressHost(3), ResourceNeed::WallClock],\n            cost_denomination: CostDenomination::TokenBucketUnits,\n            budget_request: BudgetRequest {\n                capacity: 4096,\n                refill_milli_units_per_sec: 8000,\n            },\n            validation_policy: ValidationPolicy::RequireBoth,\n            execution_model: ExecutionModel::WasmComponent,\n            config_axes: vec![(0x01, 0), (0x04, 2)],\n            depth_request: 2,\n            quirks_profile: QuirksProfile::McpServer,\n            nonce: [5u8; 8],\n            expiry: 9999,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn canonical_roundtrip_is_deterministic() {\n        let m = sample();\n        let a = m.canonical_bytes();\n        let b = m.canonical_bytes();\n        assert_eq!(a, b, "canonical encoding is deterministic");\n        assert_eq!(AgentManifest::decode(&a).unwrap(), m);\n        assert_eq!(\n            AgentManifest::decode(&a).unwrap().content_id(),\n            m.content_id()\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn free_form_config_axis_dies_at_decode() {\n        // Unknown axis id.\n        let mut m = sample();\n        m.config_axes = vec![(0x7F, 0)];\n        let bytes = m.canonical_bytes();\n        assert_eq!(\n            AgentManifest::decode(&bytes),\n            Err(ManifestParseError::UnknownConfigAxis(0x7F))\n        );\n        // Out-of-domain value index (axis 0x01 has domain size 2 ⇒ index 5 illegal).\n        let mut m2 = sample();\n        m2.config_axes = vec![(0x01, 5)];\n        assert_eq!(\n    #[test]\n    fn floor_is_unrelaxable_over_all_256_policy_bytes() {\n        // §4 criterion 3: no decodable byte yields a policy weaker than RequireBoth.\n        // Build a valid manifest, then overwrite ONLY the validation-policy value byte\n        // with every possible byte; each either decodes to RequireBoth or errors.\n        let m = sample();\n        let good = m.canonical_bytes();\n        // Locate the validation-policy field value (fixed order; we re-encode with a\n        // known layout, so find the T_VALIDATION_POLICY tag and its 1-byte value).\n        let pos = find_field_value_pos(&good, T_VALIDATION_POLICY);\n        for byte in 0u16..=255 {\n            let byte = byte as u8;\n            let mut variant = good.clone();\n            variant[pos] = byte;\n            match AgentManifest::decode(&variant) {\n                Ok(parsed) => assert_eq!(\n                    parsed.validation_policy.effective(),\n field's VALUE (header is tag + u32 len).\n    fn find_field_value_pos(bytes: &[u8], tag: u8) -> usize {\n        let mut i = 16; // skip envelope magic\n        loop {\n            let t = bytes[i];\n            let len = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[i + 1..i + 5].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;\n            if t == tag {\n                return i + 5;\n            }\n            i += 5 + len;\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reserved_cap_bit_fails_closed() {\n        // A set reserved bit is not decodable (fail-closed).\n        assert_eq!(AgentCaps::from_bits(0b0100_0000), None);\n
