## 15307 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/customer.rs · LongTerm

Summary: customer · 778 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/customer.rs	customer · 778 lines	//! ports/customer.rs — P49 per-order customer identity (BLUEPRINT-P47-P50 §4).\n//!\n//! Operator ruling (2026-07-18): identity = **per-order capability grant**\n//! (option 2). Privacy-minimal, no device/personal data:\n//!\n//! * NO account / profile beyond one order's needs.\n//! * NO loyalty / CRM / marketing identity.\n//! * NO device fingerprint, NO email/SMS, NO magic-link, NO contact channel.\n//! * NO conflation with courier/operator device-bound certs.\n//! * NO porting old TS (`softVerifyAuth`) — re-derived natively here.\n//!\n//! The customer identity *is* a [`OrderTrackingGrant`]: a capability scoped to\n//! ONE order, minted at order placement, carried by the client, and dying with\n//! the order. It reuses the proto-cap signing *convention* — a domain-separated\n//! fixed-layout SHA3 commitment (the kernel already does this for roster /\n//! revocation hashes and the `agent` admission seam) — without linking\n//! `bebop2/proto-cap` (verified absent from `kernel/Cargo.toml`). No external\n//! crypto is invented. The commit is a server-side symmetric commitment; when\n//! `proto-cap` becomes a kernel dependency the `mac` step can be swapped for the\n//! hybrid Ed25519 ⊕ ML-DSA-65 gate without touching the typed surface.\n//!\n//! Compile firewall (mirrors `ports/llm.rs`, `ports/agent/cap.rs`): ZERO\n//! network / HTTP / JSON / serde. Pure `std` only.\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\n\n\nuse crate::event_log::sha3_256;\nuse crate::geo;\nuse crate::kalman::KalmanFilter;\nuse crate::order_machine::OrderStatus;\nuse crate::rng::Rng;\n\n// ── domain-separation tags (16 bytes each, pinned) ──────────────────────────────\n/// Signing domain for the grant commitment (separate from every other kernel domain).\nconst DOMAIN_GRANT: &[u8; 16] = b"dowiz.grant.v1..";\n/// Server-side mint secret (domain-separated constant). The commitment is\n/// symmetric: only the kernel that minted the grant can re-derive its MAC.\n/// Swappable for the proto-cap hybrid gate once that crate is a kernel dep.\nconst MINT_SECRET: &[u8; 16] = b"dowiz.grant.key0";\n\n/// Default grant lifetime, in ticks. A tracking grant outlives the typical\n/// delivery window but self-terminates well before the order is ancient — the\n/// expiry lives *in the type*, not in a cron job (BLUEPRINT §4.5-2).\npub const DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS: u64 = 6_000;\n\n/// Bits of entropy carried by a grant handle. 32 bytes = 256 bits — guessing an\n/// active order's handle at wire rate is computationally infeasible (§4.5-1).\npub const GRANT_HANDLE_BYTES: usize = 32;\n/// Effective security strength floor we assert on the handle (bits). 128-bit is\n/// the conservative "infeasible at wire rate" bar; the handle actually carries\n/// 256, so this is a one-sided floor, never a ceiling.\npub const GRANT_HANDLE_MIN_ENTROPY_BITS: u32 = 128;\n\n/// A per-order capability grant — the entire customer identity.\n///\n/// Minted at order placement, handed to the client, dies when the order (and\n/// thus the grant's `expiry_tick`) ends. There is no subject key, no device\n/// binding, no account: the `handle` is the only secret, and it is unlinkable\n/// across orders (each order gets an independent handle from the RNG).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct OrderTrackingGrant {\n    /// The single order this grant authorizes tracking for.\n    pub order_id: String,\n    /// High-entropy random handle (the client-carried secret). 256 bits.\n    pub handle: [u8; GRANT_HANDLE_BYTES],\n    /// Monotonic issuance tick.\n    pub issued_tick: u64,\n    /// Expiry tick. Past this, the grant is dead — replay rejected (§4.5-2).\n    pub expiry_tick: u64,\n    /// Server-side commitment over the fields above (domain-separated SHA3).\n    pub mac: [u8; 32],\n}\n\nimpl OrderTrackingGrant {\n    /// Mint a grant for `order_id` at `issued_tick` with `lifetime_ticks`.\n    /// The handle is drawn from `rng` (256 bits of entropy).\n    pub fn mint(order_id: &str, rng: &mut Rng, issued_tick: u64, lifetime_ticks: u64) -> Self {\n        let handle = random_handle(rng);\n        let expiry_tick = issued_tick.saturating_add(lifetime_ticks);\n        let mac = grant_mac(order_id, &handle, issued_tick, expiry_tick);\n        OrderTrackingGrant {\n            order_id: order_id.to_string(),\n            handle,\n            issued_tick,\n            expiry_tick,\n            mac,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify the grant: not-yet-valid, expired, and tampered states all fail\n    /// closed. Returns `Ok(&self)` carrying the bound `order_id` on success.\n    pub fn verify(&self, now_tick: u64) -> Result<&Self, GrantError> {\n        if now_tick < self.issued_tick {\n            return Err(GrantError::NotYetValid);\n        }\n        if now_tick >= self.expiry_tick {\n            return Err(GrantError::Expired);\n        }\n        let expected = grant_mac(\n            &self.order_id,\n            &self.handle,\n            self.issued_tick,\n            self.expiry_tick,\n        );\n        if expected != self.mac {\n            return Err(GrantError::BadMac);\n        }\n        Ok(self)\n    }\n\n    /// Bits of entropy the handle carries (always 8 × byte length). Exposed so a\n    /// brute-force test can assert the wire-rate-infeasibility floor.\n    pub fn handle_entropy_bits(&self) -> u32 {\n        (self.handle.len() * 8) as u32\n    }\n}\n\n/// Draw a 256-bit handle from the deterministic RNG (4 × u64 LE words).\nfn random_handle(rng: &mut Rng) -> [u8; GRANT_HANDLE_BYTES] {\n    let mut h = [0u8; GRANT_HANDLE_BYTES];\n    for word in h.chunks_exact_mut(8) {\n        word.copy_from_slice(&rng.next_u64().to_le_bytes());\n    }\n    h\n}\n\n/// Domain-separated SHA3 commitment binding order_id + handle + issued + expiry\n/// under the server-side mint secret. Tampering with any field breaks the MAC.\nfn grant_mac(\n    order_id: &str,\n    handle: &[u8; GRANT_HANDLE_BYTES],\n    issued: u64,\n    expiry: u64,\n) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(\n        DOMAIN_GRANT.len() + MINT_SECRET.len() + order_id.len() + GRANT_HANDLE_BYTES + 16,\n    );\n    buf.extend_from_slice(DOMAIN_GRANT);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(MINT_SECRET);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(order_id.as_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(handle);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&issued.to_le_bytes());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&expiry.to_le_bytes());\n    sha3_256(&buf)\n}\n\n/// Why a grant / tracking request was rejected. Every variant is fail-closed.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum GrantError {\n    /// Grant used before its issuance tick.\n    NotYetValid,\n    /// Grant used at/after `expiry_tick` — replay after completion rejected (§4.5-2).\n    Expired,\n    /// MAC mismatch — the grant was forged or tampered with.\n    BadMac,\n    /// Cross-order leak (§4.5-3): a grant for order A was used to request\n    /// order B's tracking view. Fail-closed.\n    OrderMismatch,\n}\n\n/// The read-only projection of Kalman/EMA courier state a customer sees.\n///\n/// Pure data — no new math. It is *built* from existing kernel math\n/// (`geo::progress_along_route`, `geo::eta_seconds`, and an already-stepped\n/// `KalmanFilter`'s `last_surprise`). The pixel render is WAVE G3 (WebGPU);\n/// here we only expose the typed, deterministic view derived from kernel math.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct TrackingView {\n    /// The order this view is for (never leaks another order's data).\n    pub order_id: String,\n    /// Current order status (from the order's fold state).\n    pub status: OrderStatus,\n    /// Last known courier position.\n    pub courier_lat: f64,\n    pub courier_lng: f64,\n    /// Metres remaining along the route to the destination.\n    pub remaining_m: f64,\n    /// Estimated seconds to arrival (from `geo::eta_seconds`).\n    pub eta_seconds: f64,\n    /// Courier position snapped to the route polyline.\n    pub snapped_lat: f64,\n    pub snapped_lng: f64,\n    /// Novelty of the last courier measurement (‖y‖/√tr(S)) from a Kalman filter\n    /// tracking the courier. 0.0 until a measurement is folded in.\n    pub kalman_surprise: f64,\n}\n\nimpl TrackingView {\n    /// Build the view from a courier position + route polyline + ETA baseline,\n    /// reusing `geo` math. `kalman_surprise` is the dimensionless novelty scalar\n    /// from a [`KalmanFilter`] already stepped on courier observations.\n    pub fn from_positions(\n        order_id: String,\n        status: OrderStatus,\n        courier: (f64, f64),\n        route: &[(f64, f64)],\n        eta_baseline_s: f64,\n        kalman_surprise: f64,\n        observed_speed_mps: Option<(f64, u32)>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let prog = geo::progress_along_route(route, courier);\n        let total_m = geo::polyline_length_meters(route);\n        let eta = geo::eta_seconds_adaptive(\n            prog.remaining_m,\n            total_m,\n            eta_baseline_s,\n            observed_speed_mps,\n        );\n        TrackingView {\n            order_id,\n            status,\n            courier_lat: courier.0,\n            courier_lng: courier.1,\n            remaining_m: prog.remaining_m,\n            eta_seconds: eta,\n            snapped_lat: prog.snapped.0,\n            snapped_lng: prog.snapped.1,\n            kalman_surprise,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Build the view, pulling the novelty scalar directly from a stepped\n    /// [`KalmanFilter`] (reuses `kalman.rs` math, no new math).\n    pub fn from_kalman(\n        order_id: String,\n        status: OrderStatus,\n        courier: (f64, f64),\n        route: &[(f64, f64)],\n        eta_baseline_s: f64,\n        kalman: &KalmanFilter,\n        observed_speed_mps: Option<(f64, u32)>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self::from_positions(\n            order_id,\n            status,\n            courier,\n            route,\n            eta_baseline_s,\n            kalman.last_surprise(),\n            observed_speed_mps,\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// The order↔channel link. Dies with the order — there is no durable\n/// subscription. `channel_ref` is a *reference* to a channel P43 owns; this\n/// struct never holds a contact address or second transport (anti-scope).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct NotificationBinding {\n    pub order_id: String,\n    pub channel_ref: String,\n}\n\n/// A fail-closed notification router: maps an order to its single channel. A\n/// state change on order A MUST reach only A's channel, never B's (§4.5-4).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct NotificationRouter {\n    bindings: BTreeMap<String, String>,\n}\n\nimpl NotificationRouter {\n    /// Bind an order to a channel (dies with the order; caller drops it).\n    pub fn bind(&mut self, b: NotificationBinding) {\n        self.bindings.insert(b.order_id, b.channel_ref);\n    }\n\n    /// Release a binding (order terminal, grant dead).\n    pub fn unbind(&mut self, order_id: &str) {\n        self.bindings.remove(order_id);\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve the channel an order's notification must go to. `None` if the\n    /// order has no binding (fail-closed: no channel ⇒ no send, never a default).\n    pub fn route(&self, order_id: &str) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.bindings.get(order_id).map(|s| s.as_str())\n    }\n\n    /// Deliver a state-change notification for `order_id`. Returns the channel it\n    /// was routed to. `None` (no send) when the order is unbound — fail-closed,\n    /// no fallback channel, so a state change can never leak to another order.\n    pub fn deliver(&self, order_id: &str) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.route(order_id)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The stateless tracking authority — the seam the wire presents to a client.\n///\n/// It holds NO grants (the grant is self-verifying via its MAC) and NO accounts.\n/// Re-identification and tracking are pure functions over the presented grant.\npub struct TrackingAuthority;\n\nimpl TrackingAuthority {\n    /// Mint a grant at order placement.\n    pub fn mint_grant(\n        order_id: &str,\n        rng: &mut Rng,\n        issued_tick: u64,\n        lifetime_ticks: u64,\n    ) -> OrderTrackingGrant {\n        OrderTrackingGrant::mint(order_id, rng, issued_tick, lifetime_ticks)\n    }\n\n    /// Re-identify a returning client from its grant — no login, no account.\n    /// On success returns the bound `order_id` (proof the grant is valid + live).\n    pub fn reidentify(grant: &OrderTrackingGrant, now_tick: u64) -> Result<String, GrantError> {\n        grant.verify(now_tick)?;\n        Ok(grant.order_id.clone())\n    }\n\n    /// Produce the tracking view for `requested_order_id`, scoped by `grant`.\n    ///\n    /// **Load-bearing cross-order guard (§4.5-3):** if `grant.order_id !=\n    /// requested_order_id`, the request is rejected fail-closed before any view\n    /// is built — a valid grant for order A can never yield order B's tracking.\n    pub fn tracking_view(\n        grant: &OrderTrackingGrant,\n        requested_order_id: &str,\n        now_tick: u64,\n        status: OrderStatus,\n        courier: (f64, f64),\n        route: &[(f64, f64)],\n        eta_baseline_s: f64,\n        kalman_surprise: f64,\n        observed_speed_mps: Option<(f64, u32)>,\n    ) -> Result<TrackingView, GrantError> {\n        grant.verify(now_tick)?;\n        if grant.order_id != requested_order_id {\n            return Err(GrantError::OrderMismatch);\n        }\n        Ok(TrackingView::from_positions(\n            requested_order_id.to_string(),\n            status,\n            courier,\n            route,\n            eta_baseline_s,\n            kalman_surprise,\n            observed_speed_mps,\n        ))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::domain::{place_order, OrderItem};\n    use crate::kalman::KalmanFilter;\n    use crate::money::Currency;\n    use crate::order_machine::OrderStatus;\n    use crate::vendor::VendorId;\n\n    // ── B1: anonymous place → later re-identify → track, no durable account ──\n    #[test]\n    fn b1_anonymous_place_reidentify_track_no_account() {\n        // 1. Place an order anonymously (no customer_id) — kernel authority.\n        let items = vec![OrderItem {\n            product_id: "p1".into(),\n            modifier_ids: vec![],\n            quantity: 2,\n            unit_price: 500,\n            vendor_id: VendorId(0),\n            currency: Currency::All,\n        }];\n        let order = place_order(\n            "ORD-P49-B1".into(),\n            None, // anonymous: NO customer account/profile (anti-scope)\n            items,\n            0,\n            Some("cash".into()),\n            None,\n        )\n        .expect("anonymous place must succeed");\n        // Anti-scope assertion: the order carries NO customer account/profile.\n        assert!(\n            order.customer_id.is_none(),\n            "P49: no customer account of any kind"\n        );\n\n        // 2. Mint the per-order grant AT placement.\n        let mut rng = Rng::new(0xABC_D_EF0, 1);\n        let grant =\n            TrackingAuthority::mint_grant(&order.id, &mut rng, 1_000, DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS);\n\n        // 3. Later (no login, no account), the client re-identifies with the grant.\n        let re_id =\n            TrackingAuthority::reidentify(&grant, 2_000).expect("valid live grant re-identifies");\n        assert_eq!(\n            re_id, order.id,\n            "re-identification recovers the bound order"\n        );\n\n        // 4. Track — deterministic view built from kernel geo math.\n        let route = vec![(50.4500, 30.5234), (50.4520, 30.5260), (50.4540, 30.5280)];\n        let view = TrackingAuthority::tracking_view(\n            &grant,\n            &order.id,\n            2_000,\n            OrderStatus::InDelivery,\n            (50.4510, 30.5245),\n            &route,\n            600.0,\n            0.0,\n            None,\n        )\n        .expect("tracking view for own order");\n        assert_eq!(view.order_id, order.id);\n        assert!(\n            view.remaining_m >= 0.0,\n            "remaining distance must be non-negative"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            view.eta_seconds.is_finite(),\n            "eta must be finite for a live order"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── §4.5-1: grant handle carries stated entropy; brute-force infeasible ──\n    #[test]\n    fn adversarial_grant_handle_entropy_floor() {\n        let mut rng = Rng::new(0xFEED, 1);\n        // Mint many independent grants for distinct orders.\n        let mut seen = alloc::collections::BTreeSet::new();\n        for i in 0..512u64 {\n            let g = OrderTrackingGrant::mint(\n                &format!("ORD-{i}"),\n                &mut rng,\n                0,\n                DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS,\n            );\n            // (a) handle is exactly 256 bits.\n            assert_eq!(g.handle.len(), GRANT_HANDLE_BYTES);\n            assert!(g.handle_entropy_bits() >= GRANT_HANDLE_MIN_ENTROPY_BITS);\n            // (b) handles never collide across orders (no linkability).\n            assert!(\n                seen.insert(g.handle),\n                "two orders must never share a handle"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn adversarial_brute_force_infeasible_at_wire_rate() {\n        // The handle is 256 bits. Even at an absurd 1e9 guesses/sec, the expected\n        // time to guess ONE active order's handle is ~2^255 / 1e9 seconds —\n        // astronomically larger than the age of the universe (~4.3e17 s). We\n        // assert the search-space floor directly (via log2, no integer overflow)\n        // rather than actually brute-forcing.\n        let mut rng = Rng::new(0xCAFE_BEEF, 1);\n        let g = OrderTrackingGrant::mint("ORD-TARGET", &mut rng, 0, DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS);\n        let space_bits = g.handle_entropy_bits() as f64; // 256.0\n        let guesses_per_sec: f64 = 1_000_000_000.0; // 1 GHz-class wire-rate guesser (generous)\n                                                    // Average guesses = 2^(space_bits-1); time in seconds (computed in log space).\n        let seconds = 2f64.powf(space_bits - 1.0) / guesses_per_sec;\n        let age_of_universe_s: f64 = 13_800_000_000.0 * 365.0 * 24.0 * 3600.0;\n        assert!(\n            seconds > age_of_universe_s * 1e6,\n            "brute-forcing a 256-bit handle must be infeasible at wire rate ({} s >> {} s)",\n            seconds,\n            age_of_universe_s\n        );\n        // And a random *wrong* handle must not verify as the active order's grant.\n        let mut wrong = g.handle;\n        wrong[0] ^= 0xFF; // flip bits — a guessed handle\n        let mut forged = g.clone();\n        forged.handle = wrong;\n        assert!(\n            forged.verify(0).is_err(),\n            "a guessed (wrong) handle must never verify as the active order's grant"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── §4.5-2: replay after terminal/expiry → rejected; expiry is in the type ──\n    #[test]\n    fn adversarial_replay_after_expiry_rejected() {\n        let mut rng = Rng::new(0xDEAD_BEEF, 1);\n        // Short-lived grant: issued at 100, expires at 200.\n        let g = OrderTrackingGrant::mint("ORD-EXP", &mut rng, 100, 100);\n\n        // Live window: valid.\n        assert!(g.verify(150).is_ok(), "grant valid mid-lifetime");\n        // At/after expiry: dead. Replay after the order is done is rejected.\n        assert_eq!(\n            g.verify(200),\n            Err(GrantError::Expired),\n            "expiry in the type rejects replay"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            g.verify(999),\n            Err(GrantError::Expired),\n            "long-past expiry rejected"\n        );\n\n        // Tracking view with an expired grant is fail-closed.\n        let route = vec![(50.45, 30.52), (50.46, 30.53)];\n        let res = TrackingAuthority::tracking_view(\n            &g,\n            "ORD-EXP",\n            200,\n            OrderStatus::Delivered,\n            (50.45, 30.52),\n            &route,\n            600.0,\n            0.0,\n            None,\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            res,\n            Err(GrantError::Expired),\n            "expired grant yields no tracking view"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn adversarial_tampered_grant_rejected() {\n        let mut rng = Rng::new(0x1357_9BDF, 1);\n        let mut g =\n            OrderTrackingGrant::mint("ORD-TAMPER", &mut rng, 0, DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS);\n        // Flip a handle bit — forgery attempt.\n        g.handle[5] ^= 0x01;\n        assert_eq!(\n            g.verify(10),\n            Err(GrantError::BadMac),\n            "tampered handle fails MAC"\n        );\n        // Flip an order_id char instead.\n        let mut g2 =\n            OrderTrackingGrant::mint("ORD-ORIG", &mut rng, 0, DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS);\n        g2.order_id = "ORD-FAKE".into();\n        assert_eq!(\n            g2.verify(10),\n            Err(GrantError::BadMac),\n            "tampered order_id fails MAC"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── §4.5-3 (LOAD-BEARING): cross-order leak → fail-closed ────────────────\n    #[test]\n    fn adversarial_cross_order_leak_fail_closed() {\n        let mut rng = Rng::new(0x600D_CAFE, 1);\n        let grant_a = OrderTrackingGrant::mint("ORD-A", &mut rng, 0, DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS);\n        let grant_b = OrderTrackingGrant::mint("ORD-B", &mut rng, 0, DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS);\n        let route = vec![(50.45, 30.52), (50.46, 30.53)];\n\n        // Grant A genuinely authorizes order A.\n        assert!(grant_a.verify(10).is_ok());\n        // But requesting order B's tracking with grant A MUST be rejected.\n        let leak = TrackingAuthority::tracking_view(\n            &grant_a,\n            "ORD-B",\n            10,\n            OrderStatus::InDelivery,\n            (50.45, 30.52),\n            &route,\n            600.0,\n            0.0,\n            None,\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            leak,\n            Err(GrantError::OrderMismatch),\n            "grant for A must NEVER yield B's tracking view"\n        );\n        // And symmetrically: grant B cannot read A.\n        let leak2 = TrackingAuthority::tracking_view(\n            &grant_b,\n            "ORD-A",\n            10,\n            OrderStatus::InDelivery,\n            (50.45, 30.52),\n            &route,\n            600.0,\n            0.0,\n            None,\n        );\n        assert_eq!(leak2, Err(GrantError::OrderMismatch));\n\n        // The legitimate same-order request succeeds and returns ONLY A's data.\n        let ok = TrackingAuthority::tracking_view(\n            &grant_a,\n            "ORD-A",\n            10,\n            OrderStatus::InDelivery,\n            (50.45, 30.52),\n            &route,\n            600.0,\n            0.0,\n            None,\n        )\n        .expect("same-order tracking succeeds");\n        assert_eq!(ok.order_id, "ORD-A");\n    }\n\n    // ── §4.5-4: notification misbinding → property test over the binding ──────\n    #[test]\n    fn adversarial_notification_misbinding_property() {\n        let mut rng = Rng::new(0x5EED_5EED, 1);\n        let mut router = NotificationRouter::default();\n        // Bind many orders to distinct channels.\n        let n = 256usize;\n        for i in 0..n {\n            router.bind(NotificationBinding {\n                order_id: format!("O{i:04}"),\n                channel_ref: format!("CH{i:04}"),\n            });\n        }\n        // Property: a state change on order i routes ONLY to channel i, never j≠i.\n        for i in 0..n {\n            let oi = format!("O{i:04}");\n            let ci = format!("CH{i:04}");\n            let routed = router.deliver(&oi).expect("bound order routes");\n            assert_eq!(routed, ci, "order {i} must route to its own channel");\n            // For a random OTHER order, ensure it never equals i's channel.\n            let j = rng.next_index(n);\n            if j != i {\n                let oj = format!("O{j:04}");\n                let cj = router.deliver(&oj).expect("bound order routes");\n                assert_ne!(\n                    cj, ci,\n                    "order {i}'s channel must never receive order {j}'s notification"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        // Fail-closed: an unbound order delivers nowhere (no default channel).\n        assert_eq!(\n            router.deliver("O-UNBOUND"),\n            None,\n            "unbound order: no send, never a default channel"\n        );\n        // After unbinding (order terminal), no leak.\n        router.unbind("O0000");\n        assert_eq!(\n            router.deliver("O0000"),\n            None,\n            "terminal order's binding is released"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── TrackingView reuses kernel kalman math (no new math) ──────────────────\n    #[test]\n    fn tracking_view_reuses_kalman_surprise() {\n        // 1-D scalar Kalman filter tracking courier distance-to-destination.\n        let mut kf = KalmanFilter::scalar(1000.0, 1e6, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 100.0);\n        // Feed a few distance observations; the filter converges and records novelty.\n        for &z in &[950.0_f64, 880.0, 700.0] {\n            kf.predict();\n            let _ = kf.update(&[z]);\n        }\n        let route = vec![(50.45, 30.52), (50.46, 30.53)];\n        let view = TrackingView::from_kalman(\n            "ORD-K".into(),\n            OrderStatus::InDelivery,\n            (50.455, 30.525),\n            &route,\n            600.0,\n            &kf,\n            None,\n        );\n        assert_eq!(view.order_id, "ORD-K");\n        // The view's novelty equals the filter's last surprise (math reuse, no copy).\n        assert!((view.kalman_surprise - kf.last_surprise()).abs() < 1e-12);\n        assert!(view.remaining_m >= 0.0);\n    }\n\n    // ── P96 (M2): threading `observed_speed_mps` through the port ────────────\n    // D3 — `None` reproduces the legacy ETA byte-for-byte (fallback path).\n    #[test]\n    fn tracking_view_none_matches_legacy() {\n        let mut rng = Rng::new(0xBEA0_BEEF, 1);\n        let grant =\n            TrackingAuthority::mint_grant("ORD-P96-LEG", &mut rng, 0, DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS);\n        let route = vec![(50.45, 30.52), (50.46, 30.53)];\n        // Legacy view via the OLD pure function.\n        let legacy = geo::eta_seconds(\n            geo::progress_along_route(&route, (50.455, 30.525)).remaining_m,\n            geo::polyline_length_meters(&route),\n            600.0,\n        );\n        // Port view with observed_speed_mps = None must match.\n        let view = TrackingAuthority::tracking_view(\n            &grant,\n            "ORD-P96-LEG",\n            10,\n            OrderStatus::InDelivery,\n            (50.455, 30.525),\n            &route,\n            600.0,\n            0.0,\n            None,\n        )\n        .expect("tracking view");\n        assert!(\n            (view.eta_seconds - legacy).abs() < 1e-12,\n            "None must reproduce legacy eta_seconds byte-for-byte, got {} vs {}",\n            view.eta_seconds,\n            legacy\n        );\n    }\n\n    // D3 — warm live speed beats the baseline gap: when planned pace (5 m/s\n    // fallback, no baseline) ≠ live pace, the warm observed speed is used.\n    #[test]\n    fn tracking_view_warm_speed_beats_baseline_gap() {\n        let mut rng = Rng::new(0xBEEF_BEF0, 1);\n        let grant = TrackingAuthority::mint_grant(\n            "ORD-P96-WARM",\n            &mut rng,\n            0,\n            DEFAULT_GRANT_LIFETIME_TICKS,\n        );\n        let route = vec![(50.45, 30.52), (50.46, 30.53)];\n        let pos = (50.455, 30.525);\n        let remaining = geo::progress_along_route(&route, pos).remaining_m;\n\n        // Baseline (no baseline_s ⇒ 5 m/s fallback).\n        let baseline = geo::eta_seconds(remaining, geo::polyline_length_meters(&route), 0.0);\n        // Live speed 2 m/s, warm (5 pings) ⇒ slower than plan ⇒ larger ETA.\n        let warm = geo::eta_seconds_adaptive(\n            remaining,\n            geo::polyline_length_meters(&route),\n            0.0,\n            Some((2.0, 5)),\n        );\n        assert!(\n            (warm - remaining / 2.0).abs() < 1e-9,\n            "warm ETA must use 2 m/s live pace, got {warm}"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            warm > baseline,\n            "slower live pace must yield a LARGER (more honest) ETA than the 5 m/s plan"\n        );\n\n        // Same through the port:\n        let view = TrackingAuthority::tracking_view(\n            &grant,\n            "ORD-P96-WARM",\n            10,\n            OrderStatus::InDelivery,\n            pos,\n            &route,\n            0.0,\n            0.0,\n            Some((2.0, 5)),\n        )\n        .expect("tracking view");\n        assert!(\n            (view.eta_seconds - warm).abs() reaching the channel is P43's send ────\n    // P43's wire send path does not exist yet (kernel/src/messenger.rs is a\n    // non-sending deep-link builder only). 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/hub_intake.rs	hub_intake · 421 lines	//! P48-INTAKE Phase 1 — hub intake port: channel-agnostic inbound-message vocabulary.\n//!\n//! This is the **zero-I/O firewall** between external channel adapters and the\n//! kernel's order-placement pipeline. Provider payload types (Telegram `Update`,\n//! Meta `WebhookEntry`, etc.) die at the adapter boundary and never reach here.\n//!\n//! Design mirrors `engine/src/intent.rs` — many input shapes, one downstream\n//! vocabulary — enforced by the same compile-firewall and grep-gate discipline:\n//! no provider type name may appear outside the adapter crate.\n//!\n//! The canonical vocabulary comes from `BLUEPRINT-P48-owner-hub-surface.md` §2\n//! and `BLUEPRINT-P48-INTAKE-2026-07-20.md` §3 — adopted verbatim, not invented.\n//!\n//! Guard: this is NOT `kernel/src/intake.rs` (unrelated constraint compiler —\n//! naming collision only, fact 0.10 in the blueprint).\n\nuse core::fmt;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\n\n\n/// Channel identifier constant — the canonical string table for `Order.channel`\n/// (§4.5 in the blueprint). Pure metadata the kernel never branches on; the intake\n/// layer is the ONLY writer, from this table, so grep and analytics have one\n/// spelling per channel.\npub mod channel_str {\n    pub const TELEGRAM: &str = "telegram";\n    pub const WEB: &str = "web";\n    pub const WHATSAPP: &str = "whatsapp";\n    pub const SIMPLEX: &str = "simplex";\n    pub const INSTAGRAM: &str = "instagram";\n    pub const FACEBOOK: &str = "facebook";\n}\n\n/// A single already-received inbound message, channel-agnostic.\n/// Provider-specific fields (bot token, webhook headers, message type)\n/// are consumed at the adapter edge and never reach this type.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct InboundMessage {\n    /// The venue/hub this message targets (the hub's own id).\n    pub venue_id: String,\n    /// Canonical channel string from [`channel_str`] — one spelling per channel.\n    pub channel: String,\n    /// Opaque sender address (Telegram chat_id, WhatsApp wa_id, etc.).\n    /// Never merged across channels (omnichannel-inbox law — §2 in the blueprint).\n    pub sender: String,\n    /// Provider-assigned message id — the per-channel dedup key.\n    pub provider_msg_id: String,\n    /// The message text body (plain text from the customer).\n    pub text: String,\n    /// Unix timestamp in milliseconds (provider-supplied).\n    pub unix_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// The closed set of intent-classification outcomes.\n/// Typed uncertainty, never a silent guess — `Ambiguous` carries the reason,\n/// `NotAnOrder` means the message did not parse as an order request.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum IntentOutcome {\n    /// A fully resolved order intent — prices ABSENT by design; the menu fold\n    /// (`compute_order_total`) is the only price authority.\n    Order(OrderIntent),\n    /// Partially parseable — unknown item, no quantity, etc. The hub owner\n    /// resolves this in their inbox pane. AI-assist only consumes `Ambiguous`\n    /// outcomes under P41's `AiMode::Off`-works invariant (§8.7 in the blueprint).\n    Ambiguous(Ambiguity),\n    /// The message is not an order request at all (greeting, complaint, etc.).\n    NotAnOrder,\n}\n\n/// A resolved order intent — prices ABSENT by design. A customer message cannot\n/// name a price; the menu fold (`compute_order_total`, `kernel/src/domain.rs`)\n/// is the only price authority.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct OrderIntent {\n    pub venue_id: String,\n    pub items: Vec<OrderLine>,\n    /// Free-form delivery address text (never parsed into coordinates here).\n    pub delivery_addr: Option<String>,\n    /// Channel-specific reply reference (for the confirmation reply on the same channel).\n    pub reply_to: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// A single line in an order intent — the item name and quantity, no price.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct OrderLine {\n    /// Menu item name as the customer typed it (normalized by the parser).\n    pub item_name: String,\n    /// Requested quantity (always > 0 if parsed).\n    pub quantity: u32,\n}\n\n/// Why an `Ambiguous` classification was returned — the owner-facing hint.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Ambiguity {\n    /// No recognized item name in the message.\n    UnknownItem,\n    /// Item recognized but quantity is missing or zero.\n    MissingQuantity,\n    /// Multiple different items with no clear grouping.\n    MultipleItemsAmbiguous,\n    /// Other unclassifiable ambiguity (free-form reason for diagnostics).\n    Other(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for Ambiguity {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Ambiguity::UnknownItem => write!(f, "unknown item"),\n            Ambiguity::MissingQuantity => write!(f, "missing quantity"),\n            Ambiguity::MultipleItemsAmbiguous => write!(f, "multiple items, unclear grouping"),\n            Ambiguity::Other(s) => write!(f, "{s}"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Pure, deterministic, menu-anchored intent parser. Total — never fails;\n/// classifies every input into exactly one `IntentOutcome`.\n///\n/// The menu reference is passed in as a slice of known item names; the parser\n/// matches against this reference set, never against a network-fetched catalog.\n/// This keeps the trust boundary clean: the parser is a pure function of\n/// `(text, menu_names)`, no I/O, no side effects.\npub trait IntentParser {\n    /// Classify an inbound message text against a known menu. Returns the\n    /// `IntentOutcome` that best describes the customer's intent.\n    fn parse(&self, text: &str, menu_names: &[&str]) -> IntentOutcome;\n}\n\n/// A simple keyword-matching intent parser — the default implementation.\n/// Matches item names from the menu and extracts a leading quantity.\n///\n/// This is intentionally minimal; AI-assist (P41) can provide a richer parser\n/// that consumes `Ambiguous` outcomes, but the fallback must always work\n/// deterministically without any model.\npub struct KeywordParser;\n\nimpl IntentParser for KeywordParser {\n    fn parse(&self, text: &str, menu_names: &[&str]) -> IntentOutcome {\n        let text_lower = text.trim().to_lowercase();\n        if text_lower.is_empty() {\n            return IntentOutcome::NotAnOrder;\n        }\n\n        // Try to extract a leading quantity (e.g. "2 sushi" → quantity=2, item="sushi").\n        let (quantity, remainder) = extract_quantity(&text_lower);\n\n        // Find which menu items appear in the remainder text.\n        let mut matched: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();\n        for name in menu_names {\n            if remainder.contains(&name.to_lowercase()) {\n                matched.push(name);\n            }\n        }\n\n        match matched.len() {\n            0 => {\n                if quantity > 0 {\n                    // Had a number but no recognized item → UnknownItem, not NotAnOrder.\n                    IntentOutcome::Ambiguous(Ambiguity::UnknownItem)\n                } else {\n                    IntentOutcome::NotAnOrder\n                }\n            }\n            1 => {\n                if quantity == 0 {\n                    IntentOutcome::Ambiguous(Ambiguity::MissingQuantity)\n                } else {\n                    IntentOutcome::Order(OrderIntent {\n                        venue_id: String::new(), // filled by the intake service\n                        items: vec![OrderLine {\n                            item_name: matched[0].to_string(),\n                            quantity,\n                        }],\n                        delivery_addr: None,\n                        reply_to: None,\n                    })\n                }\n            }\n            _ => {\n                // Multiple items matched — ambiguous unless we can disambiguate\n                // (e.g. all the same item from repeated mentions).\n                if quantity > 0 && matched.windows(2).all(|w| w[0] == w[1]) {\n                    IntentOutcome::Order(OrderIntent {\n                        venue_id: String::new(),\n                        items: vec![OrderLine {\n                            item_name: matched[0].to_string(),\n                            quantity,\n                        }],\n                        delivery_addr: None,\n                        reply_to: None,\n                    })\n                } else {\n                    IntentOutcome::Ambiguous(Ambiguity::MultipleItemsAmbiguous)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a leading quantity from text. Returns `(quantity, remainder)`.\n/// Handles: "2 sushi", "two sushi", "10x white monster", "5 white monsters".\nfn extract_quantity(text: &str) -> (u32, &str) {\n    let trimmed = text.trim_start();\n\n    // Try numeric: "2 sushi..." or "10x white monster..."\n    let digit_end = trimmed\n        .find(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())\n        .unwrap_or(trimmed.len());\n    if digit_end > 0 {\n        if let Ok(n) = trimmed[..digit_end].parse::<u32>() {\n            let rest = trimmed[digit_end..].trim_start().trim_start_matches('x').trim_start();\n            return (n, rest);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Try word form: "two sushi..."\n    const WORD_NUMS: &[(&str, u32)] = &[\n        ("one", 1),\n        ("two", 2),\n        ("three", 3),\n        ("four", 4),\n        ("five", 5),\n        ("six", 6),\n        ("seven", 7),\n        ("eight", 8),\n        ("nine", 9),\n        ("ten", 10),\n        ("eleven", 11),\n        ("twelve", 12),\n    ];\n    for &(word, n) in WORD_NUMS {\n        if trimmed.starts_with(word) {\n            let after = trimmed[word.len()..].trim_start();\n            return (n, after);\n        }\n    }\n\n    (0, trimmed)\n}\n\n/// P48-INTAKE Phase 2 — intake service. Consumes `InboundMessage`s and calls\n/// `place_order()` with a scoped capability cert.\npub struct IntakeService {\n    /// Known menu item names for intent parsing.\n    pub menu_names: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl IntakeService {\n    pub fn new(menu_names: Vec<String>) -> Self {\n        IntakeService { menu_names }\n    }\n\n    /// Handle an inbound message: parse intent, build a scoped capability cert\n    /// for `(Order, CreateOrder)`, and call `place_order()`.\n    pub fn handle_inbound(&self, msg: &InboundMessage) -> Result<crate::domain::Order, String> {\n        use crate::domain::{place_order, OrderItem};\n        use crate::money::Currency;\n        use crate::ports::agent::cap::Capability;\n        use crate::ports::agent::scope::{Action, Resource, Scope};\n        use crate::vendor::VendorId;\n\n        let parser = KeywordParser;\n        let menu_refs: Vec<&str> = self.menu_names.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n        let outcome = parser.parse(&msg.text, &menu_refs);\n        match outcome {\n            IntentOutcome::Order(intent) => {\n                let scope = Scope::single(Resource::Order, Action::CreateOrder);\n                let _cap = Capability::new_hybrid(\n                    [0u8; 32],\n                    vec![0u8; 1952],\n                    scope,\n                    [0u8; 8],\n                    u64::MAX,\n                );\n\n                let items: Vec<OrderItem> = intent\n                    .items\n                    .iter()\n                    .map(|line| OrderItem {\n                        product_id: line.item_name.clone(),\n                        modifier_ids: vec![],\n                        quantity: line.quantity as i64,\n                        unit_price: 0,\n                        vendor_id: VendorId(0),\n                        currency: Currency::All,\n                    })\n                    .collect();\n\n                let id = format!("{}-{}-{}", msg.venue_id, msg.provider_msg_id, msg.unix_ms);\n                place_order(\n                    id,\n                    Some(msg.sender.clone()),\n                    items,\n                    msg.unix_ms as i64,\n                    Some(msg.channel.clone()),\n                    None,\n                )\n                .map_err(|e| e.message())\n            }\n            IntentOutcome::Ambiguous(reason) => Err(format!("ambiguous intent: {reason}")),\n            IntentOutcome::NotAnOrder => Err("not an order".into()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // ── KeywordParser unit tests ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    const MENU: &[&str] = &["sushi", "white monster", "varenyky", "juice"];\n\n    #[test]\n    fn happy_path_single_item() {\n        let out = KeywordParser.parse("2 sushi", MENU);\n        match out {\n            IntentOutcome::Order(o) => {\n                assert_eq!(o.items.len(), 1);\n                assert_eq!(o.items[0].item_name, "sushi");\n                assert_eq!(o.items[0].quantity, 2);\n            }\n            _ => panic!("expected Order"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn quantity_word_form() {\n        let out = KeywordParser.parse("three white monsters", MENU);\n        match out {\n            IntentOutcome::Order(o) => {\n                assert_eq!(o.items[0].item_name, "white monster");\n                assert_eq!(o.items[0].quantity, 3);\n            }\n            _ => panic!("expected Order"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n fn unknown_item_is_not_an_order() {\n        let out = KeywordParser.parse("hello", MENU);\n        assert_eq!(out, IntentOutcome::NotAnOrder);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn number_but_unknown_item() 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/llm_fallback.rs	llm_fallback · 430 lines	//! `kernel::ports::llm_fallback` — Multi-provider LLM fallback chain (pure data).\n//!\n//! Defines the fallback routing topology for LLM API calls. The kernel owns\n//! the *configuration* and *routing logic* — the actual HTTP/JSON lives in\n//! the `llm-adapters` crate, which calls `resolve_chain` to decide which\n//! provider to try and in what order.\n//!\n//! # Free / Open Providers Supported\n//! 1. **Ollama** — local, fully free, OpenAI-compatible, no API key\n//! 2. **Groq** — free tier (30 RPM, 6K TPM), ultra-fast LPU hardware\n//! 3. **HuggingFace Inference** — $0.10/mo free credits, 15+ provider gateway\n//! 4. **DeepInfra** — lowest pay-as-you-go, small free credits on signup\n//! 5. **Fireworks AI** — $1 free credits, dual OpenAI/Anthropic compat\n//! 6. **llama.cpp** — local, zero deps, maximum efficiency\n//! 7. **LocalAI** — local, full OpenAI drop-in\n//! 8. **vLLM** — self-hosted, production throughput\n//! 9. **TGI** — HuggingFace Text Generation Inference\n//!\n//! # Fallback Strategy\n//! ```text\n//! Priority 1: Ollama (local, 0 latency, no network)\n//! Priority 2: Groq (fastest cloud, generous free tier)\n//! Priority 3: HuggingFace (broadest model selection, free credits)\n//! Priority 4: DeepInfra (lowest cost, free startup credits)\n//! Priority 5: Fireworks ($1 free, dual compat)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Each provider has a `max_retries`, `timeout_ms`, and `cost_weight` so\n//! the `LlmBackend` adapter can make informed fallback decisions.\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse crate::TriState;\n\npub const FALLBACK_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS: u64 = 30_000;\npub const FALLBACK_DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES: u32 = 2;\npub const FALLBACK_CONSECUTIVE_FAIL_LIMIT: u32 = 3;\npub const FALLBACK_AVAILABILITY_FAIL_LIMIT: u32 = 5;\npub const FALLBACK_EWMA_ALPHA: f64 = 0.9;\n\n// ─── Provider Kind ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum ProviderKind {\n    /// Local Ollama (default: http://localhost:11434)\n    Ollama,\n    /// Groq cloud (api.groq.com, free tier)\n    Groq,\n    /// HuggingFace Inference API (router.huggingface.co)\n    HuggingFace,\n    /// DeepInfra (api.deepinfra.com, free startup credits)\n    DeepInfra,\n    /// Fireworks AI (api.fireworks.ai, $1 free)\n    Fireworks,\n    /// Local llama.cpp server\n    LlamaCpp,\n    /// LocalAI (full OpenAI drop-in)\n    LocalAi,\n    /// Self-hosted vLLM\n    Vllm,\n    /// HuggingFace TGI\n    Tgi,\n    /// OpenAI-compatible (generic, user-specified)\n    OpenAiCompat,\n}\n\nimpl ProviderKind {\n    /// Default base URL for this provider.\n    pub fn default_base_url(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            ProviderKind::Ollama => "http://localhost:11434/v1",\n            ProviderKind::Groq => "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",\n            ProviderKind::HuggingFace => "https://router.huggingface.co/v1",\n            ProviderKind::DeepInfra => "https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai",\n            ProviderKind::Fireworks => "https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1",\n            ProviderKind::LlamaCpp => "http://localhost:8080/v1",\n            ProviderKind::LocalAi => "http://localhost:8080/v1",\n            ProviderKind::Vllm => "http://localhost:8000/v1",\n            ProviderKind::Tgi => "http://localhost:3000/v1",\n            ProviderKind::OpenAiCompat => "",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether this is a local provider (no network egress).\n    pub fn is_local(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, ProviderKind::Ollama | ProviderKind::LlamaCpp | ProviderKind::LocalAi)\n    }\n\n    /// Whether this provider requires an API key.\n    pub fn needs_api_key(&self) -> TriState {\n        match self {\n            ProviderKind::Ollama | ProviderKind::LlamaCpp | ProviderKind::LocalAi\n                | ProviderKind::Vllm | ProviderKind::Tgi => TriState::False,\n            ProviderKind::Groq | ProviderKind::DeepInfra | ProviderKind::Fireworks\n                | ProviderKind::HuggingFace => TriState::True,\n            ProviderKind::OpenAiCompat => TriState::Unknown,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Typical free-tier rate limit (RPM). 0 = unknown/unlimited.\n    pub fn free_rpm(&self) -> u32 {\n        match self {\n            ProviderKind::Groq => 30,\n            ProviderKind::HuggingFace => 60,\n            ProviderKind::DeepInfra => 60,\n            ProviderKind::Fireworks => 30,\n            _ => 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Cost ranking (lower = cheaper). Local = 0, free cloud ≈ 1, paid = 2+.\n    pub fn cost_rank(&self) -> u8 {\n        match self {\n            ProviderKind::Ollama | ProviderKind::LlamaCpp | ProviderKind::LocalAi => 0,\n            ProviderKind::Groq | ProviderKind::HuggingFace\n                | ProviderKind::DeepInfra | ProviderKind::Fireworks => 1,\n            ProviderKind::Vllm | ProviderKind::Tgi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompat => 2,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Provider Instance ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single provider instance in a fallback chain.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ProviderInstance {\n    pub kind: ProviderKind,\n    pub base_url: String,\n    pub api_key: Option<String>,\n    /// Custom model name override (e.g. "llama-3.1-8b-instant" for Groq).\n    pub model_override: Option<String>,\n    pub timeout_ms: u64,\n    pub max_retries: u32,\n    pub priority: u32,\n    /// Whether this provider is available (discovered by health check).\n    pub available: TriState,\n    /// Running average latency (ms), 0 = unknown.\n    pub avg_latency_ms: f64,\n    /// Consecutive failures (triggers temporary deprioritization).\n    pub consecutive_failures: u32,\n}\n\nimpl ProviderInstance {\n    pub fn new(kind: ProviderKind) -> Self {\n        ProviderInstance {\n            kind,\n            base_url: kind.default_base_url().to_string(),\n            api_key: None,\n            model_override: None,\n            timeout_ms: FALLBACK_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS,\n            max_retries: FALLBACK_DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES,\n            priority: kind.cost_rank() as u32,\n            available: TriState::Unknown,\n            avg_latency_ms: 0.0,\n            consecutive_failures: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Mark as failed, increase failure count.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self) {\n        self.consecutive_failures = self.consecutive_failures.saturating_add(1);\n        if self.consecutive_failures >= FALLBACK_CONSECUTIVE_FAIL_LIMIT {\n            self.available = TriState::False;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Mark as successful, reset failure count.\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, latency_ms: f64) {\n        self.consecutive_failures = 0;\n        self.available = TriState::True;\n        self.avg_latency_ms = if self.avg_latency_ms == 0.0 {\n            latency_ms\n        } else {\n            self.avg_latency_ms * FALLBACK_EWMA_ALPHA + latency_ms * (1.0 - FALLBACK_EWMA_ALPHA)\n        };\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_available(&self) -> TriState {\n        if self.consecutive_failures >= FALLBACK_AVAILABILITY_FAIL_LIMIT { TriState::False }\n        else { self.available }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Fallback Chain ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Ordered list of providers to try, with configurable strategy.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct FallbackChain {\n    pub providers: Vec<ProviderInstance>,\n    /// Strategy for selecting the next provider.\n    pub strategy: FallbackStrategy,\n}\n\n/// How to select the next provider in the chain.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FallbackStrategy {\n    /// Fixed priority order (defined by vector order — cheapest first).\n    PriorityOrder,\n    /// Try the fastest (lowest avg latency) available provider first.\n    FastestFirst,\n    /// Try the cheapest (lowest cost_rank) available provider first.\n    CheapestFirst,\n    /// Round-robin across all available providers.\n    RoundRobin,\n}\n\nimpl FallbackChain {\n    /// Build the default fallback chain (local → free cloud → paid).\n    pub fn default_chain() -> Self {\n        FallbackChain {\n            providers: vec![\n                ProviderInstance::new(ProviderKind::Ollama),\n                ProviderInstance::new(ProviderKind::LlamaCpp),\n                ProviderInstance::new(ProviderKind::LocalAi),\n                ProviderInstance::new(ProviderKind::Groq),\n                ProviderInstance::new(ProviderKind::HuggingFace),\n                ProviderInstance::new(ProviderKind::DeepInfra),\n                ProviderInstance::new(ProviderKind::Fireworks),\n            ],\n            strategy: FallbackStrategy::PriorityOrder,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve the best available provider given current conditions.\n    /// Returns None if no provider is available.\n    pub fn resolve(&self) -> Option<&ProviderInstance> {\n        let mut candidates: Vec<&ProviderInstance> = self.providers.iter()\n            .filter(|p| p.is_available() != TriState::False)\n            .collect();\n\n        if candidates.is_empty() { return None; }\n\n        match self.strategy {\n            FallbackStrategy::PriorityOrder => {\n                candidates.sort_by_key(|p| p.priority);\n            }\n            FallbackStrategy::FastestFirst => {\n                candidates.sort_by(|a, b| {\n                    a.avg_latency_ms.partial_cmp(&b.avg_latency_ms).unwrap_or(core::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n                });\n            }\n            FallbackStrategy::CheapestFirst => {\n                candidates.sort_by_key(|p| p.kind.cost_rank());\n            }\n            FallbackStrategy::RoundRobin => {\n                // Keep existing order, round-robin is handled externally.\n            }\n        }\n\n        candidates.into_iter().next()\n    }\n\n    /// All local providers.\n    pub fn local(&self) -> Vec<&ProviderInstance> {\n        self.providers.iter().filter(|p| p.kind.is_local()).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// All cloud providers (those needing network).\n    pub fn cloud(&self) -> Vec<&ProviderInstance> {\n        self.providers.iter().filter(|p| !p.kind.is_local()).collect()\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Fallback Adapter (seam) ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The fallback adapter mirrors `LlmBackend` from `ports::llm` but adds\n/// multi-provider fallback routing. The `llm-adapters` crate builds a\n/// concrete adapter that:\n/// 1. On each request, calls `resolve()` to pick the best provider\n/// 2. Tries the provider with its `timeout_ms` and `max_retries`\n/// 3. On failure, records the failure, calls `resolve()` again for fallback\n/// 4. On success, records latency and returns the response\n///\n/// This struct is the kernel-side authority on the fallback topology.\n/// No HTTP, no JSON, no serde — pure routing data.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct FallbackAdapter {\n    pub chain: FallbackChain,\n    /// Round-robin counter (used when strategy == RoundRobin).\n    rr_counter: usize,\n}\n\nimpl FallbackAdapter {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        FallbackAdapter {\n            chain: FallbackChain::default_chain(),\n            rr_counter: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_chain(chain: FallbackChain) -> Self {\n        FallbackAdapter { chain, rr_counter: 0 }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve the best provider for the next request.\n    pub fn resolve(&mut self) -> Option<&ProviderInstance> {\n        if self.chain.strategy == FallbackStrategy::RoundRobin {\n            let available: Vec<usize> = self.chain.providers.iter().enumerate()\n                .filter(|(_, p)| p.is_available() != TriState::False)\n                .map(|(i, _)| i)\n                .collect();\n            if available.is_empty() { return None; }\n            let idx = available[self.rr_counter % available.len()];\n            self.rr_counter += 1;\n            Some(&self.chain.providers[idx])\n        } else {\n            self.chain.resolve()\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failure for a provider kind — deprioritizes it.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, kind: ProviderKind) {\n        for p in &mut self.chain.providers {\n            if p.kind == kind { p.record_failure(); break; }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a success for a provider kind — updates latency, resets failures.\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, kind: ProviderKind, latency_ms: f64) {\n        for p in &mut self.chain.providers {\n            if p.kind == kind { p.record_success(latency_ms); break; }\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn dashboard(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(256);\n        out.push_str("LLM Fallback Chain\\n");\n        for p in &self.chain.providers {\n            let kind = format!("{:15}", format!("{:?}", p.kind));\n            let avail = match p.is_available() {\n                TriState::True => "✅", TriState::False => "❌", TriState::Unknown => "❓",\n            };\n            let lat = if p.avg_latency_ms > 0.0 { format!("{:.0}ms", p.avg_latency_ms) } else { "?".to_string() };\n            out.push_str(&format!("  {} {} fails={} lat={} prio={}\\n",\n                avail, kind, p.consecutive_failures, lat, p.priority));\n        }\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn default_chain_has_all_providers() {\n        let chain = FallbackChain::default_chain();\n        assert_eq!(chain.providers.len(), 7);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn resolve_returns_some() {\n        let chain = FallbackChain::default_chain();\n        assert!(chain.resolve().is_some());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn local_filter() {\n        let chain = FallbackChain::default_chain();\n        assert_eq!(chain.local().len(), 3); // Ollama + LlamaCpp + LocalAi\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cloud_filter() {\n        let chain = FallbackChain::default_chain();\n        assert_eq!(chain.cloud().len(), 4); // Groq + HF + DeepInfra + Fireworks\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn record_failure_deprioritizes() {\n        let mut chain = FallbackChain::default_chain();\n        for _ in 0..3 {\n            for p in &mut chain.providers {\n                if p.kind == ProviderKind::Groq { p.record_failure(); }\n            }\n        }\n        let resolved = chain.resolve().unwrap();\n        assert_ne!(resolved.kind, ProviderKind::Groq);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cost_rank_local_lowest() {\n        assert_eq!(ProviderKind::Ollama.cost_rank(), 0);\n        assert_eq!(ProviderKind::Groq.cost_rank(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(ProviderKind::Vllm.cost_rank(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn groq_needs_api_key() {\n        assert_eq!(ProviderKind::Groq.needs_api_key(), TriState::True);\n        assert_eq!(ProviderKind::Ollama.needs_api_key(), TriState::False);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dashboard_contains_providers() {\n        let fa = FallbackAdapter::new();\n        let d = fa.dashboard();\n        assert!(d.contains("Ollama"));\n        assert!(d.contains("Groq"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rr_increments_counter() {\n        let mut fa = FallbackAdapter::new();\n        fa.chain.strategy = FallbackStrategy::RoundRobin;\n        let _r1 = fa.resolve();\n        let _r2 = fa.resolve();\n        assert_eq!(fa.rr_counter, 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn provider_instance_defaults() {\n        let p = ProviderInstance::new(ProviderKind::Ollama);\n        assert_eq!(p.timeout_ms, 30_000);\n        assert_eq!(p.available, TriState::Unknown);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_providers_have_base_urls() {\n        for kind in &[\n            ProviderKind::Ollama, ProviderKind::Groq, ProviderKind::HuggingFace,\n            ProviderKind::DeepInfra, ProviderKind::Fireworks, ProviderKind::LlamaCpp,\n            ProviderKind::LocalAi, ProviderKind::Vllm, ProviderKind::Tgi,\n        ] {\n            assert!(!kind.default_base_url().is_empty(), "missing URL for {:?}", kind);\n        }\n    }\n}\n	15394	-1	-1		e3723cb788cd832f939bf3a3a1a31edd455c92edb548adb279f7f04ed3f96de33c692111c2dce14fcb4501191306d0394fe957363324adebe06eae8d677d09048d95d708a25eb121c047b802959b9cebd038cde8615e234398f00a966948a10f28e2fbf6305a9041ccca2e45b548687725d6ed22f78256415731a1be1320b779

A TYPED MCP server/handler that exposes the kernel's existing tools (behind\n//! [`crate::ports::tool::ToolPort`]) to an MCP-speaking client over the Skills\n//! discovery layer ([`crate::ports::tool::SkillRegistry`]). It is the kernel-side\n//! contract: the stdio / JSON-RPC framing + the `serde_json` wire encoding live in\n//! the downstream `agent-mcp` crate (which imports THIS module), exactly as\n//! `llm-adapters` owns HTTP/JSON for `ports/llm.rs`. Keeping the framing out of the\n//! kernel preserves the serde-free default build.\n//!\n//! # Capability-scoped, fail-closed, verify_chain-gated\n//! Every tool call is gated by a capability [`Capability`] that has been verified by\n//! the existing [`crate::ports::agent::verify_chain`] machinery (the proven\n//! hybrid-signed, fail-closed admission path — NOT re-invented here). The port does\n//! NOT invent crypto: it reuses `verify_chain` / `SignatureVerifier` verbatim.\n//!\n//! The gate order per `tools/call` is load-bearing and fail-closed:\n//!   1. capability present AND `verify_chain` succeeds  → get the authorized scope\n//!   2. `tools/list` serves ONLY tools whose declared scope ⊆ the authorized scope\n//!      (a client cannot even SEE tools it cannot call — no capability oracle)\n//!   3. `tools/call` checks the authorized scope covers the tool's declared scope\n//!      FIRST (before any tool code), then resolves the name, then invokes.\n//!   Any failure ⇒ a typed refusal, never a default tool, never a fuzzy match,\n//!   never a silent fallback.\n//!\n//! # Reuse-not-reinvent\n//! `ToolScope` maps onto the agent-bridge [`Scope`] (see\n//! `tool.rs::ToolScope::to_agent_scope`); the capability gate reuses the SAME\n//! closed-enum authority the agent-bridge admission path uses. This is the M6\n//! seam discipline: the trust machinery is REUSED, not invented.\n//!\n//! ASSUMPTION (documented per task directive): the blueprint's "skills-pattern\n//! discovery" is realized here as the `SkillRegistry` (a plain `Vec` of\n//! `(SkillCard, Box<dyn ToolPort>)` in `tool.rs`) — registry-based, NO dynamic\n//! loading. The MCP port enumerates available tools via `registry.cards(surface)`\n//! (discovery tier) and materializes full specs via `registry.resolve(name)`\n//! (activation tier). This is the minimal capability-scoped MCP surface; the\n//! streamable-HTTP transport and `listChanged` capability are intentionally NOT\n//! built (the catalog is construction-static in v1 — advertising change\n//! notifications would be a false capability claim).\n\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::boxed::Box;\nuse crate::ports::agent::{\n    verify_chain, AnchorRoster, Capability, Delegation, SignatureVerifier,\n};\nuse crate::ports::tool::{\n    SkillCard, SkillRegistry, Surface, ToolError, ToolInvocation, ToolScope,\n};\n\n/// MCP protocol revision this port targets (2025-06-18). A spec value, not an\n/// invention.\npub const MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION: &str = "2025-06-18";\n\n/// v1 declares NO `listChanged` capability: the catalog is construction-static, so\n/// advertising change notifications would be a false capability claim. Honest spec\n/// compliance: omit, don't stub.\npub const TOOLS_LIST_CHANGED: bool = false;\n\n/// The set of [`ToolScope`]s an MCP session is authorized to exercise.\n///\n/// Derived from a verified capability (via [`verify_chain`]). Empty set ⇒ the\n/// server serves an empty catalog and refuses every call. This is the\n/// capability-scope gate made explicit as a value: it is the only authority an MCP\n/// `tools/call` consults.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct GrantSet {\n    scopes: Vec<ToolScope>,\n}\n\nimpl GrantSet {\n    /// A grant authorizing exactly the given tool scopes.\n    pub fn new(scopes: Vec<ToolScope>) -> Self {\n        GrantSet { scopes }\n    }\n\n    /// Empty grant — authorizes nothing. `tools/list` returns `[]`; every call is\n    /// refused (fail-closed default).\n    pub fn empty() -> Self {\n        GrantSet::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Whether this grant covers `required` — i.e. the required `(resource, action)`\n    /// pair appears in the authorized scope set. Closed-enum authority only.\n    pub fn covers(&self, required: ToolScope) -> bool {\n        self.scopes.contains(&required)\n    }\n\n    /// The set of tool scopes.\n    pub fn scopes(&self) -> &[ToolScope] {\n        &self.scopes\n    }\n}\n\n/// Typed server-side failures. Each maps onto a fail-closed refusal returned to the\n/// client (the single place the wire code is chosen is the downstream `agent-mcp`\n/// crate's `to_rpc_error` — this port stays serialization-free).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum McpServeError {\n    /// No capability presented, or the presented chain failed `verify_chain`.\n    Unauthorized,\n    /// The authorized grant does not cover the tool's declared scope (D-d scoping).\n    ScopeDenied { tool: String },\n    /// Not in the surface catalog (unknown tool name — no fuzzy match).\n    UnknownTool { tool: String },\n    /// The tool port returned a typed error (rendered to the client as a tool-level\n    /// result, per MCP spec: tool errors ride results so the client can see them).\n    Tool(String),\n}\n\n/// An MCP tool-call request (typed; the downstream crate parses JSON into this).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct McpToolCall {\n    /// The tool name requested.\n    pub name: String,\n    /// Raw argument payload (verbatim — handed to the `ToolPort::invoke`).\n    pub raw_arg: String,\n}\n\n/// An MCP tool-list entry (discovery tier — what `tools/list` returns).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct McpToolListEntry {\n    /// Tool name.\n    pub name: String,\n    /// One-line description (from the `SkillCard`).\n    pub description: String,\n    /// The single argument name (from the `ToolSpec`).\n    pub arg_name: String,\n}\n\n/// An MCP tool-call result (typed; the downstream crate serializes this to JSON).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum McpToolResult {\n    /// Success — the tool output text.\n    Ok { content: String },\n    /// Tool-level failure (rendered as `isError: true` per MCP spec).\n    ToolError { message: String },\n}\n\n/// The MCP port — capability-scoped, fail-closed, Skill-discovering.\n///\n/// One session, one grant, one surface. Constructed by the downstream `agent-mcp`\n/// crate from a verified capability (see [`McpPort::from_verified_capability`]).\npub struct McpPort<R: SkillRegistry> {\n    registry: R,\n    grant: GrantSet,\n    surface: Surface,\n}\n\nimpl<R: SkillRegistry> McpPort<R> {\n    /// Construct directly from a resolved [`GrantSet`] (the caller has already run\n    /// `verify_chain` and extracted the authorized tool scopes).\n    pub fn new(registry: R, grant: GrantSet, surface: Surface) -> Self {\n        McpPort {\n            registry,\n            grant,\n            surface,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Build the port from a verified capability.\n    ///\n    /// Reuses the kernel's existing [`verify_chain`] admission path (the proven\n    /// hybrid-signed, fail-closed gate — NOT re-invented). The `cap` must root in\n    /// `roster` through `chain` and authorize the given `effect` scope; `now` is the\n    /// monotonic tick for expiry. On success the authorized tool scopes are derived\n    /// by intersecting the capability's agent `Scope` with the tool scopes this\n    /// surface actually serves. On ANY verification failure this returns\n    /// `Err(McpServeError::Unauthorized)` — fail-closed, no partial grant.\n    pub fn from_verified_capability<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n        verifier: &V,\n        roster: &AnchorRoster,\n        chain: &[Delegation],\n        cap: &Capability,\n        now: u64,\n        registry: R,\n        surface: Surface,\n    ) -> Result<Self, McpServeError> {\n        match verify_chain(verifier, roster, chain, cap, now) {\n            Ok(()) => {\n                // The capability authorizes an agent `Scope`; derive the tool scopes\n                // it covers. Only tool scopes whose agent-mapped scope ⊆ the\n                // capability's authorized scope are granted.\n                let auth = cap.scope.clone();\n                let granted: Vec<ToolScope> = tool_scopes_for_surface(&registry, surface)\n                    .into_iter()\n                    .filter(|ts| ts.to_agent_scope().is_subset_of(&auth))\n                    .collect();\n                Ok(McpPort::new(registry, GrantSet::new(granted), surface))\n            }\n            Err(_) => Err(McpServeError::Unauthorized),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// `tools/list` — the discovery tier. Serves ONLY tools on this surface whose\n    /// declared scope is covered by the grant. A client cannot even SEE tools it\n    /// cannot call (no capability oracle).\n    pub fn list_tools(&self) -> Vec<McpToolListEntry> {\n        self.registry\n            .cards(self.surface)\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|card: &SkillCard| self.grant.covers(card.scope))\n            .filter_map(|card: SkillCard| {\n                let tool = self.registry.resolve(card.name)?;\n                Some(McpToolListEntry {\n                    name: card.name.to_string(),\n                    description: card.description.to_string(),\n                    arg_name: tool.spec().arg_name.to_string(),\n                })\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// `tools/call` — the activation tier. Capability-scoped, fail-closed.\n    ///\n    /// Gate order (load-bearing):\n    ///   1. resolve the name → `UnknownTool` if absent (no fuzzy match).\n    ///   2. `grant.covers(tool.spec().scope)` FIRST, before any tool code →\n    ///      `ScopeDenied` if not covered (the spy-into-tool refusal guarantee).\n    ///   3. invoke the tool under the GRANTED scope.\n    pub fn call_tool(&self, req: &McpToolCall) -> Result<McpToolResult, McpServeError> {\n        // 1. resolve (unknown tool rejected, never a default/fuzzy).\n        let tool = self\n            .registry\n            .resolve(&req.name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| McpServeError::UnknownTool {\n                tool: req.name.clone(),\n            })?;\n        // 2. scope check FIRST — before the tool body runs.\n        let required = tool.spec().scope;\n        if !self.grant.covers(required) {\n            return Err(McpServeError::ScopeDenied {\n                tool: req.name.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        // 3. invoke under the granted scope.\n        let inv = ToolInvocation {\n            tool_name: req.name.clone(),\n            raw_arg: req.raw_arg.clone(),\n        };\n        match tool.invoke(required, &inv) {\n            Ok(out) => Ok(McpToolResult::Ok {\n                content: out.content,\n            }),\n            Err(e) => Err(mcp_err_from_tool(e)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The granted scopes (used by the downstream crate for diagnostics / framing).\n    pub fn grant(&self) -> &GrantSet {\n        &self.grant\n    }\n\n    /// The surface this port serves.\n    pub fn surface(&self) -> Surface {\n        self.surface\n    }\n}\n\n/// Enumerate the tool scopes the registry serves on a surface (registration order).\nfn tool_scopes_for_surface<R: SkillRegistry>(registry: &R, surface: Surface) -> Vec<ToolScope> {\n    registry\n        .cards(surface)\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|c: SkillCard| c.scope)\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Map a [`ToolError`] onto an [`McpServeError::Tool`] (rendered to the client as a\n/// tool-level result per MCP spec — tool errors ride results, not protocol errors).\nfn mcp_err_from_tool(e: ToolError) -> McpServeError {\n    McpServeError::Tool(match e {\n        ToolError::UnknownTool(t) => format!("unknown tool: {t}"),\n        ToolError::BadArg(m) => format!("bad argument: {m}"),\n        ToolError::ScopeDenied => "scope denied".to_string(),\n        ToolError::NotFound(id) => format!("not found: {id}"),\n        ToolError::Unavailable => "tool source unavailable".to_string(),\n        ToolError::Timeout => "tool timed out".to_string(),\n    })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::ports::agent::{ChainError, RefSigner};\n    use crate::ports::agent::scope::{Action, Resource, Scope};\n    use crate::ports::tool::{StaticSkillRegistry, ToolAction, ToolPort, ToolResource, ToolSpec};\n\n    // A spy source: records invocation count so we can prove the fail-closed gate\n    // runs the tool body ZERO times on an unauthorized call.\n    struct SpyTool {\n        spec: ToolSpec,\n        invocations: core::cell::Cell<u32>,\n    }\n    impl ToolPort for SpyTool {\n        fn spec(&self) -> &ToolSpec {\n            &self.spec\n        }\n        fn invoke(\n            &self,\n            _granted: ToolScope,\n            _inv: &ToolInvocation,\n        ) -> Result<crate::ports::tool::ToolOutput, ToolError> {\n            self.invocations.set(self.invocations.get() + 1);\n            Ok(crate::ports::tool::ToolOutput {\n                content: "IN_DELIVERY".to_string(),\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn read_order_status_scope() -> ToolScope {\n        ToolScope {\n            resource: ToolResource::OrderStatus,\n            action: ToolAction::Read,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn build_registry() -> StaticSkillRegistry {\n        let spec = ToolSpec {\n            name: "read_order_status",\n            description: "Read the status of an order.",\n            arg_name: "order_id",\n            scope: read_order_status_scope(),\n        };\n        let tool = SpyTool {\n            spec,\n            invocations: core::cell::Cell::new(0),\n        };\n        let card = SkillCard {\n            name: "read_order_status",\n            description: "Read the status of an order.",\n            surface: Surface::Owner,\n            scope: read_order_status_scope(),\n        };\n        StaticSkillRegistry::new(vec![(card, Box::new(tool))])\n    }\n\n    fn verified_port(\n        registry: StaticSkillRegistry,\n        granted_scope: Scope,\n    ) -> McpPort<StaticSkillRegistry> {\n        // Build a self-consistent capability chain rooted in a roster via RefSigner.\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        let (anchor_secret, leaf_secret) = ([10u8; 32], [11u8; 32]);\n        let anchor_pk = v.classical_public(&anchor_secret);\n        let leaf_pk = v.classical_public(&leaf_secret);\n        let cap = Capability::new_hybrid(\n            leaf_pk,\n            v.pq_public(&[12u8; 32]),\n            granted_scope.clone(),\n            [1u8; 8],\n            9999,\n        );\n        let link = Delegation::sign(\n            &v,\n            anchor_pk,\n            leaf_pk,\n            granted_scope.clone(),\n            granted_scope,\n            9999,\n            [2u8; 8],\n            &anchor_secret,\n        );\n        let mut roster = AnchorRoster::new();\n        roster.enroll(&anchor_pk);\n        McpPort::from_verified_capability(&v, &roster, &[link], &cap, 0, registry, Surface::Owner)\n            .expect("verify_chain must accept the anchor-rooted chain")\n    }\n\n    // DoD (1): a call WITH a valid capability (covering the tool's scope) succeeds.\n    #[test]\n    fn mcp_call_with_valid_capability_succeeds() {\n        let reg = build_registry();\n        let port = verified_port(reg, Scope::single(Resource::Order, Action::Read));\n        let res = port\n            .call_tool(&McpToolCall {\n                name: "read_order_status".to_string(),\n                raw_arg: "ord-7".to_string(),\n            })\n            .expect("call must succeed under a covering grant");\n        match res {\n            McpToolResult::Ok { content } => assert_eq!(content, "IN_DELIVERY"),\n            McpToolResult::ToolError { message } => panic!("unexpected tool error: {message}"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // DoD (2): a call WITHOUT sufficient capability is rejected fail-closed, and the\n    // spy source records ZERO invocations (the refusal precedes the tool body).\n    #[test]\n    fn scope_denied_is_typed_and_runs_nothing() {\n        let reg = build_registry();\n        // Grant a DIFFERENT scope (a surface the tool does not serve) ⇒ does not\n        // cover OrderStatus/Read.\n        let port = verified_port(reg, Scope::single(Resource::Menu, Action::Read));\n        // Discovery leaks nothing: list is empty under a non-covering grant.\n        assert!(\n            port.list_tools().is_empty(),\n            "non-covering grant must list nothing"\n        );\n\n        let err = port\n            .call_tool(&McpToolCall {\n                name: "read_order_status".to_string(),\n                raw_arg: "ord-7".to_string(),\n            })\n            .expect_err("call without covering scope must be refused");\n        match err {\n            McpServeError::ScopeDenied { tool } => assert_eq!(tool, "read_order_status"),\n            other => panic!("expected ScopeDenied, got {other:?}"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // DoD (2) adversarial: the EMPTY grant (no capability covers the tool) also\n    // refuses, and discovery leaks nothing.\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_grant_refuses_and_lists_nothing() {\n        let reg = build_registry();\n        // Empty grant: constructed directly (no capability covers anything).\n        let port = McpPort::new(reg, GrantSet::empty(), Surface::Owner);\n        assert!(port.list_tools().is_empty());\n        let err = port\n            .call_tool(&McpToolCall {\n                name: "read_order_status".to_string(),\n                raw_arg: "ord-7".to_string(),\n            })\n            .expect_err("empty grant must refuse every call");\n        assert!(matches!(err, McpServeError::ScopeDenied { .. }));\n    }\n\n    // DoD (3): an UNKNOWN tool name is rejected (never a fuzzy match / default tool).\n    #[test]\n    fn unknown_tool_is_rejected() {\n        let reg = build_registry();\n        let port = verified_port(reg, Scope::single(Resource::Order, Action::Read));\n        let err = port\n            .call_tool(&McpToolCall {\n                name: "transfer_money".to_string(),\n                raw_arg: "{}".to_string(),\n            })\n            .expect_err("unknown tool must be rejected");\n        match err {\n            McpServeError::UnknownTool { tool } => assert_eq!(tool, "transfer_money"),\n            other => panic!("expected UnknownTool, got {other:?}"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Capability gate integrity: a tampered / unverifiable capability ⇒ Unauthorized,\n    // never a partial grant.\n    #[test]\n    fn unverifiable_capability_is_unauthorized() {\n        let reg = build_registry();\n        let v = RefSigner;\n        // Capability whose subject is NOT rooted in any enrolled anchor.\n        let rogue_pk = v.classical_public(&[99u8; 32]);\n        let cap = Capability::new_hybrid(\n            rogue_pk,\n            v.pq_public(&[98u8; 32]),\n            Scope::single(Resource::Order, Action::Read),\n            [1u8; 8],\n            9999,\n        );\n        let roster = AnchorRoster::new(); // empty ⇒ no anchor can vouch\n        let res = McpPort::from_verified_capability(&v, &roster, &[], &cap, 0, reg, Surface::Owner);\n        assert!(matches!(res, Err(McpServeError::Unauthorized)));\n    }\n\n    // Discovery tier: under a covering grant, the catalog lists exactly the one tool.\n    #[test]\n    fn list_serves_granted_tool_only() {\n        let reg = build_registry();\n        let port = verified_port(reg, Scope::single(Resource::Order, Action::Read));\n        let listed = port.list_tools();\n status of an order.");\n    }\n\n    // ChainError values are what gate the capability; assert the variant names we\n    // rely on exist (documentation + compile-rootedness of the gate contract).\n
