```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/notification.rs	notification · 1237 lines	//! ports/notification.rs — BLUEPRINT-P61 notification fabric (the send behind a `channel_ref`).\n//!\n//! Compile firewall (mirrors `llm.rs`): this module has ZERO network / HTTP / JSON / serde /\n//! tokio. It defines only the abstract contracts (`PushPort`/`SmsPort`/`EmailPort`), the hub-local\n//! value types, the `ChannelRegistry`, the `Reachability` classifier + the proven X10 coverage\n//! invariant, and the `Notifier` fan-out. The concrete adapters (web-push/a2/fcm_v1, hand-rolled\n//! SMS REST, sesv2/resend/lettre) live in the sibling `notify-adapters` crate — they own all\n//! async I/O and provider wire-format and convert it into the `Receipt`/`NotifyError` shapes here.\n//!\n//! `cargo tree -p dowiz-kernel` must show no HTTP client here after implementation (verified by the\n//! kernel firewall done-check). Every token/contact lives hub-local (§16.22) — there is no\n//! dowiz-central store and this module contains no `dowiz.`-central host string.\n//!\n//! P61 *observes* `OrderStatus` transitions (`order_machine::is_terminal`, the `assert_transition`\n//! law); it adds no state, edge, or fulfillment discriminator.\n\nuse crate::order_machine::OrderStatus;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\n\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Transport value types (opaque, hub-local; never dowiz-central)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A push subscription. `endpoint` is the web-push URL, or `""` for a native push channel.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum PushKind {\n    /// RFC 8291 web-push subscription keys.\n    WebPush { p256dh: Vec<u8>, auth: Vec<u8> },\n    /// APNs device token (native iOS).\n    Apns { device_token: Vec<u8> },\n    /// FCM v1 registration token (native Android).\n    Fcm { registration_token: String },\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct PushSub {\n    pub kind: PushKind,\n    pub endpoint: String,\n}\n\n/// A validated E.164 phone number (stored hub-local).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct E164(pub String);\n\n/// A validated email address (stored hub-local).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct EmailAddr(pub String);\n\n/// A messenger transport, delegated to P43 (not built here).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct MessengerRef {\n    pub provider: MessengerProvider,\n    pub handle: String,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum MessengerProvider {\n    Telegram,\n    WhatsApp,\n    SimpleX,\n}\n\n/// The minimum-PII status message P61 derives from a committed order transition.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct StatusMsg {\n    /// The `channel_ref` / order id — the routing key, NOT a customer identity.\n    pub order_handle: String,\n    /// Reuse kernel `OrderStatus` (order_machine.rs).\n    pub status: OrderStatus,\n    /// Short human string, no cart/PII.\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Short human body.\n    pub body: String,\n    /// Opens the tracking view (P49 grant), never an account.\n    pub deep_link: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl StatusMsg {\n    /// Build the human `title`/`body` for a status transition (per-status content).\n    /// PII floor: never carries cart, payment, or profile data (§2 anti-scope).\n    pub fn for_status(order_handle: impl Into<String>, status: OrderStatus) -> Self {\n        let (title, body) = match status {\n            OrderStatus::Pending => ("Order received", "We've received your order."),\n            OrderStatus::Confirmed => ("Order confirmed", "Your order is confirmed."),\n            OrderStatus::Preparing => ("Preparing", "The kitchen is preparing your order."),\n            OrderStatus::Ready => ("Ready", "Your order is ready for pickup/delivery."),\n            OrderStatus::InDelivery => ("On the way", "Your order is out for delivery."),\n            OrderStatus::Delivered => ("Delivered", "Your order has been delivered."),\n            OrderStatus::PickedUp => ("Picked up", "Your order has been picked up."),\n            OrderStatus::Rejected => ("Order rejected", "We couldn't accept your order."),\n            OrderStatus::Cancelled => ("Cancelled", "Your order was cancelled."),\n            OrderStatus::Scheduled => ("Scheduled", "Your order is scheduled."),\n            OrderStatus::Refunding => ("Refunding", "Your refund is in progress."),\n            OrderStatus::CompensatedRefund => ("Refunded", "Your order was refunded."),\n        };\n        StatusMsg {\n            order_handle: order_handle.into(),\n            status,\n            title: title.into(),\n            body: body.into(),\n            deep_link: None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Reachability / platform context — the X10 substrate\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Captured at checkout from the placing client.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum PlatformContext {\n    /// The gap: web push UNAVAILABLE (needs home-screen PWA).\n    IosSafariWeb,\n    /// web push available (iOS 16.4+ declarative).\n    IosPwaInstalled,\n    /// web push available (VAPID).\n    AndroidWeb,\n    /// web push available (VAPID).\n    DesktopWeb,\n    /// APNs available.\n    NativeIos,\n    /// FCM available.\n    NativeAndroid,\n    /// web push / OS notification available.\n    NativeDesktop,\n    /// user denied/blocked push on any platform.\n    PushDenied,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum TransportKind {\n    WebPush,\n    Apns,\n    Fcm,\n    Sms,\n    Email,\n    Messenger,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum UnreachableReason {\n    IosSafariWebPushRequiresPwa,\n    PushDenied,\n    NoTransportRegistered,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Reachability {\n    Reachable,\n    Unreachable(UnreachableReason),\n}\n\n/// Pure, total classifier: does `kind` work on platform `ctx`?\n///\n/// Push is structurally unavailable on `IosSafariWeb` (needs home-screen PWA) and whenever push is\n/// `PushDenied`. SMS / Email / Messenger are reachable on every platform — they are the mandatory\n/// fallback lane (§16.52). This totality is what makes the X10 coverage invariant provable (§5.2).\npub fn reachability(kind: TransportKind, ctx: PlatformContext) -> Reachability {\n    match kind {\n        // ── Push channels ──\n        TransportKind::WebPush => {\n            use PlatformContext::*;\n            match ctx {\n                IosSafariWeb => {\n                    Reachability::Unreachable(UnreachableReason::IosSafariWebPushRequiresPwa)\n                }\n                PushDenied => Reachability::Unreachable(UnreachableReason::PushDenied),\n                // VAPID web push works wherever a PWA / web context is installed.\n                IosPwaInstalled | AndroidWeb | DesktopWeb | NativeDesktop => {\n                    Reachability::Reachable\n                }\n                // Native contexts do not register a web-push sub.\n                NativeIos | NativeAndroid => {\n                    Reachability::Unreachable(UnreachableReason::NoTransportRegistered)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        TransportKind::Apns => match ctx {\n            PlatformContext::NativeIos => Reachability::Reachable,\n            PlatformContext::PushDenied => Reachability::Unreachable(UnreachableReason::PushDenied),\n            _ => Reachability::Unreachable(UnreachableReason::NoTransportRegistered),\n        },\n        TransportKind::Fcm => match ctx {\n            PlatformContext::NativeAndroid => Reachability::Reachable,\n            PlatformContext::PushDenied => Reachability::Unreachable(UnreachableReason::PushDenied),\n            _ => Reachability::Unreachable(UnreachableReason::NoTransportRegistered),\n        },\n        // ── Non-push fallback channels — reachable on every platform ──\n        TransportKind::Sms | TransportKind::Email | TransportKind::Messenger => {\n            Reachability::Reachable\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Hub-local registered contact set for ONE channel_ref (§16.22 — never central)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ChannelSet {\n    pub platform: PlatformContext,\n    pub push: Vec<PushSub>,\n    pub sms: Option<E164>,\n    pub email: Option<EmailAddr>,\n    /// Delegated to P43's `ChannelSend`.\n    pub messenger: Vec<MessengerRef>,\n}\n\n/// `NoReachableChannel` — the coverage error, a checkout precondition failure.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct NoReachableChannel;\n\n/// The X10 coverage invariant (§5.2): a `ChannelSet` is coverage-OK iff it contains at least one\n/// registered transport whose `reachability` in that set's `platform` is `Reachable`.\n///\n/// This is evaluated *before* an order is accepted (fail-closed checkout precondition) — it is\n/// structurally impossible to represent "accepted order with zero reachable status channel".\npub fn channel_coverage(set: &ChannelSet) -> Result<(), NoReachableChannel> {\n    let p = set.platform;\n    let mut covered = false;\n    for sub in &set.push {\n        let kind = match &sub.kind {\n            PushKind::WebPush { .. } => TransportKind::WebPush,\n            PushKind::Apns { .. } => TransportKind::Apns,\n            PushKind::Fcm { .. } => TransportKind::Fcm,\n        };\n        if matches!(reachability(kind, p), Reachability::Reachable) {\n            covered = true;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if !covered {\n        if let Some(_) = &set.sms {\n            covered = true;\n        }\n    }\n    if !covered {\n        if let Some(_) = &set.email {\n            covered = true;\n        }\n    }\n    if !covered {\n        if !set.messenger.is_empty() {\n            covered = true;\n        }\n    }\n    if covered {\n        Ok(())\n    } else {\n        Err(NoReachableChannel)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ChannelRegistry — hub-local `channel_ref → ChannelSet` store (§16.22)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Hub-local registry. Binds at checkout, unbinds on terminal. Never serialized to a dowiz\n/// endpoint (no central host string exists in this module). A `BTreeMap` is correct: it holds the\n/// live orders on ONE hub — hundreds, not millions (§6.2).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct ChannelRegistry {\n    sets: BTreeMap<String, ChannelSet>,\n}\n\nimpl ChannelRegistry {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Bind a `channel_ref` to its `ChannelSet` at checkout.\n    pub fn bind(&mut self, channel_ref: impl Into<String>, set: ChannelSet) {\n        self.sets.insert(channel_ref.into(), set);\n    }\n\n    /// Get the `ChannelSet` for a `channel_ref` (fail-closed: `None` ⇒ no send).\n    pub fn get(&self, channel_ref: &str) -> Option<&ChannelSet> {\n        self.sets.get(channel_ref)\n    }\n\n    /// Mutable access — used by the fan-out to evict dead tokens in place.\n    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, channel_ref: &str) -> Option<&mut ChannelSet> {\n        self.sets.get_mut(channel_ref)\n    }\n\n    /// Unbind when the order is terminal (`is_terminal`). Releases the working set (living-memory:\n    /// evict-never-accrete, §6.3).\n    pub fn unbind(&mut self, channel_ref: &str) {\n        self.sets.remove(channel_ref);\n    }\n\n    /// Number of live bound sets (registry churn metric, §8 bench).\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.sets.len()\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.sets.is_empty()\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Ports (mirror LlmBackend: sync, fail-closed) + error taxonomy\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A send receipt. `provider_id` is the provider's message id; `at_tick` is the hub tick.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Receipt {\n    pub provider_id: String,\n    pub at_tick: u64,\n}\n\n/// The item-14 error taxonomy: transient ≠ dead. `DeadToken` and `Transient` are DISTINCT variants,\n/// so a `match` that evicts on `DeadToken` and retries on `Transient` is exhaustive — a mis-handling\n/// is a *compile* error, never a runtime surprise (§6.1).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum NotifyError {\n    /// 5xx / timeout — RETRY with backoff, DO NOT evict.\n    Transient(String),\n    /// 410 / UNREGISTERED — EVICT, NEVER retry.\n    DeadToken(DeadReason),\n    /// No reachable transport for this send.\n    Unreachable(UnreachableReason),\n    /// Missing key / bad sender identity — fail-closed.\n    Config(String),\n    /// Provider hard-rejected content (bad number/address).\n    Rejected(String),\n}\n\n/// Why a token is dead — drives the eviction pole.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DeadReason {\n    WebPush410Gone,\n    Apns410BadDeviceToken,\n    FcmUnregistered,\n}\n\n/// Push port — sync, fail-closed.\npub trait PushPort {\n    fn send(&self, sub: &PushSub, msg: &StatusMsg) -> Result<Receipt, NotifyError>;\n}\n\n/// SMS port — sync, fail-closed.\npub trait SmsPort {\n    fn send(&self, to: &E164, msg: &StatusMsg) -> Result<Receipt, NotifyError>;\n}\n\n/// Email port — sync, fail-closed. `sender_identity` makes the §4-F opt-out observable.\npub trait EmailPort {\n    fn send(&self, to: &EmailAddr, msg: &StatusMsg) -> Result<Receipt, NotifyError>;\n    fn sender_identity(&self) -> EmailSenderIdentity;\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// §4-F email sender identity — managed DEFAULT, real vendor opt-out\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The sending identity. Shipped default is `ManagedDefault` (a dowiz-run, DMARC-aligned domain)\n/// so a fresh Hetzner hub is deliverable on day one. `VendorDomain` is the day-one opt-out; a hub\n/// config setting `email.sender = vendor` switches every send's identity with no code change.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum EmailSenderIdentity {\n    ManagedDefault {\n        subdomain: String,\n    },\n    VendorDomain {\n        domain: String,\n        dkim_selector: String,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl EmailSenderIdentity {\n    /// The default: `<hub>.hub.dowiz.email` under the dowiz-run root (§4-F / §3 constant).\n    pub fn managed_default(hub: &str) -> Self {\n        EmailSenderIdentity::ManagedDefault {\n            subdomain: format!("{}.{}", hub, MANAGED_EMAIL_DOMAIN_ROOT),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Constants (§3)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// APNs JWT max age — rotate under 60 min (R4 §1.2).\npub const APNS_JWT_MAX_AGE_S: u64 = 3300;\n/// FCM OAuth refresh margin — refresh before hourly expiry (R4 §1.2).\npub const FCM_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_S: u64 = 300;\n/// VAPID curve — P-256, generated once/hub, persisted in the local secret store (R4 §1.2).\npub const VAPID_CURVE: &str = "P-256";\n/// Push retry backoff (ms) — 3 tries then give up (transient only), throttled by `TokenBucket`.\npub const PUSH_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS: [u64; 3] = [500, 2_000, 8_000];\n/// Dead tokens evicted immediately — 0 retries (R4 §1.2).\npub const DEAD_TOKEN_RETRIES: u32 = 0;\n/// Managed email domain root (§4-F).\npub const MANAGED_EMAIL_DOMAIN_ROOT: &str = "hub.dowiz.email";\n/// Max `StatusMsg` body bytes — SMS-segment-aware, PII floor (§3).\npub const MAX_STATUSMSG_BODY_BYTES: usize = 1024;\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// The fan-out result — every transport's fate is recorded (no silent drop)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct FanoutOutcome {\n    pub reached: Vec<TransportKind>,\n    pub evicted: Vec<(TransportKind, DeadReason)>,\n    pub skipped_unreachable: Vec<(TransportKind, UnreachableReason)>,\n    pub transient_failures: Vec<(TransportKind, String)>,\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Notifier — the fan-out (M4)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The `Notifier` fans a `StatusMsg` out across every registered, reachable transport for a\n/// `channel_ref`. SMS and email fire by AVAILABILITY, not gated on push failure (§16.52): a\n/// web/no-app customer never had a push channel to fail. Dead tokens are evicted mid-batch;\n/// transient errors retry per `PUSH_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS` (throttled by the caller via `TokenBucket`),\n/// then land in `transient_failures` (the token survives).\npub struct Notifier<'a> {\n    pub push: &'a dyn PushPort,\n    pub sms: &'a dyn SmsPort,\n    pub email: &'a dyn EmailPort,\n    pub registry: &'a mut ChannelRegistry,\n    /// Hub tick used to stamp receipts.\n    pub tick: u64,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> Notifier<'a> {\n    pub fn new(\n        push: &'a dyn PushPort,\n        sms: &'a dyn SmsPort,\n        email: &'a dyn EmailPort,\n        registry: &'a mut ChannelRegistry,\n        tick: u64,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Notifier {\n            push,\n            sms,\n            email,\n            registry,\n            tick,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Fan out `msg` to the `ChannelSet` bound to `channel_ref`. Returns the per-transport fate.\n    ///\n    /// Ports are passed by `&dyn`; the caller (hub runtime) owns exactly one concrete adapter per\n    /// port and reuses it for the whole fleet, so per-port failures are isolated (§6.3) and fan-out\n    /// is O(transports) per transition, independent of fleet size.\n    pub fn notify(&mut self, channel_ref: &str, msg: &StatusMsg) -> FanoutOutcome {\n        let mut out = FanoutOutcome::default();\n        // Resolve the set. Fail-closed: an unbound channel_ref produces an empty outcome (no send,\n        // never a default) — the cross-order-isolation invariant is preserved (no widening of the\n        // routing key; see customer.rs:586-599, preserved here).\n        let set = match self.registry.get_mut(channel_ref) {\n            Some(s) => s,\n            None => return out,\n        };\n        let platform = set.platform;\n\n        // ── Push subs (one receipt each; dead tokens evicted in place) ──\n        let mut retained: Vec<PushSub> = Vec::with_capacity(set.push.len());\n        for sub in set.push.drain(..) {\n            let kind = match &sub.kind {\n                PushKind::WebPush { .. } => TransportKind::WebPush,\n                PushKind::Apns { .. } => TransportKind::Apns,\n                PushKind::Fcm { .. } => TransportKind::Fcm,\n            };\n            match reachability(kind, platform) {\n                Reachability::Unreachable(why) => {\n                    // A sub for an unreachable platform (e.g. web-push sub on IosSafariWeb) is\n                    // skipped, NOT evicted — it is simply irrelevant here, not dead.\n                    out.skipped_unreachable.push((kind, why));\n                    retained.push(sub);\n                    continue;\n                }\n                Reachability::Reachable => {}\n            }\n            match self.push.send(&sub, msg) {\n                Ok(_) => {\n                    out.reached.push(kind);\n                    retained.push(sub);\n                }\n                Err(NotifyError::DeadToken(reason)) => {\n                    // Evict immediately (DEAD_TOKEN_RETRIES = 0); never retry.\n                    out.evicted.push((kind, reason));\n                    // `sub` is dropped (not pushed to `retained`) → evicted from the registry.\n                }\n                Err(NotifyError::Transient(why)) => {\n                    // Retry per backoff, throttled by `TokenBucket` at the caller. After giving up,\n                    // the token survives (never evicted). `sub` is moved exactly once (below), so we\n                    // track the retry outcome with a local flag, not by moving `sub` in the loop.\n                    let mut last = why.clone();\n                    let mut retry_ok = false;\n                    let mut retry_dead: Option<DeadReason> = None;\n                    let mut retry_non_transient = false;\n                    for _ in 0..PUSH_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS.len() {\n                        match self.push.send(&sub, msg) {\n                            Ok(_) => {\n                                retry_ok = true;\n                                break;\n                            }\n                            Err(NotifyError::Transient(w)) => last = w,\n                            Err(NotifyError::DeadToken(r)) => {\n                                retry_dead = Some(r);\n                                break;\n                            }\n                            Err(_) => {\n                                retry_non_transient = true;\n                                break;\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    if retry_ok {\n                        out.reached.push(kind);\n                    } else if let Some(r) = retry_dead {\n                        out.evicted.push((kind, r));\n                    } else if retry_non_transient {\n                        out.transient_failures\n                            .push((kind, "non-transient during retry".into()));\n                    } else {\n                        // Gave up after transient retries: token survives, recorded as transient.\n                        out.transient_failures.push((kind, last));\n                    }\n                    // `sub` moves here exactly once: keep it unless it was evicted.\n                    if !out.evicted.iter().any(|(k, _)| *k == kind) {\n                        retained.push(sub);\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    // Config/Rejected/Unreachable (non-retryable, non-dead) — recorded, token kept.\n                    out.transient_failures\n                        .push((kind, "non-transient send failure".into()));\n                    retained.push(sub);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        set.push = retained;\n\n        // ── SMS — attempted by availability, NOT gated on push (§16.52) ──\n        if let Some(e164) = &set.sms {\n            match self.sms.send(e164, msg) {\n                Ok(_) => out.reached.push(TransportKind::Sms),\n                Err(NotifyError::Transient(why)) => {\n                    out.transient_failures.push((TransportKind::Sms, why))\n                }\n                Err(NotifyError::DeadToken(why)) => out.evicted.push((TransportKind::Sms, why)),\n                Err(NotifyError::Unreachable(why)) => {\n                    out.skipped_unreachable.push((TransportKind::Sms, why))\n                }\n                Err(e) => out\n                    .transient_failures\n                    .push((TransportKind::Sms, format!("{e:?}"))),\n            }\n        }\n\n        // ── Email — attempted by availability, NOT gated on push (§16.52) ──\n        if let Some(email) = &set.email {\n            match self.email.send(email, msg) {\n                Ok(_) => out.reached.push(TransportKind::Email),\n                Err(NotifyError::Transient(why)) => {\n                    out.transient_failures.push((TransportKind::Email, why))\n                }\n                Err(NotifyError::DeadToken(why)) => out.evicted.push((TransportKind::Email, why)),\n                Err(NotifyError::Unreachable(why)) => {\n                    out.skipped_unreachable.push((TransportKind::Email, why))\n                }\n                Err(e) => out\n                    .transient_failures\n                    .push((TransportKind::Email, format!("{e:?}"))),\n            }\n        }\n\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// M5 — order-machine hook: committed transition → StatusMsg → notify\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Map a terminal transition to an `unbind`; otherwise the fan-out observes the new status.\n/// Returns `true` iff the transition is terminal (the `ChannelSet` should be released).\npub fn is_terminal_transition(_from: OrderStatus, to: OrderStatus) -> bool {\n    to.is_terminal()\n}\n\n/// Build the `StatusMsg` for an order transition. `notify_on_transition` (the caller) invokes this\n/// AFTER a non-duplicate `commit_after_decide` succeeds, so idempotency is inherited: a duplicate\n/// event never re-commits, hence never re-notifies (event_log.rs idempotency seam).\npub fn status_msg_for(order_handle: &str, to: OrderStatus) -> StatusMsg {\n    StatusMsg::for_status(order_handle, to)\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// M8 — credential lifecycle policy (pure; I/O lives in notify-adapters)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// VAPID keypair identity for a hub: stable across subscriptions (generated ONCE, persisted in the\n/// hub's local secret store — never regenerated per subscription). We model the persisted key as a\n/// deterministic fingerprint of the hub id so two subscriptions from the same hub sign under the\n/// same key (the test asserts stability). Real keypair bytes live in the secret store (adapters).\npub fn vapid_key_id(hub_id: &str) -> [u8; 32] {\n    crate::event_log::sha3_256(hub_id.as_bytes())\n}\n\n/// APNs JWT rotation policy: a token older than `APNS_JWT_MAX_AGE_S` must be rotated before send.\n/// Returns `true` iff the token is still within its valid window.\npub fn apns_jwt_valid(age_s: u64) -> bool {\n    age_s < APNS_JWT_MAX_AGE_S\n}\n\n/// FCM OAuth token refresh policy: refresh if the remaining lifetime is within the margin. This is\n/// the "don't reacquire per message" gate — the caller caches one token and refreshes only at the\n/// margin, not per send.\npub fn fcm_oauth_needs_refresh(remaining_s: u64) -> bool {\n    remaining_s <= FCM_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_S\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests — fake in-process adapters (no network), the X10 proof + dead-token eviction\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // ── Fake ports the test controls (NOT production — see §4.1 no_mock_success) ──\n\n    /// A push adapter whose behavior is scripted per endpoint.\n    struct FakePush {\n        /// Map endpoint → error to return (None = success).\n        fail: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<String, NotifyError>,\n    }\n    impl PushPort for FakePush {\n        fn send(&self, sub: &PushSub, _msg: &StatusMsg) -> Result<Receipt, NotifyError> {\n            if let Some(e) = self.fail.get(&sub.endpoint) {\n                return Err(e.clone());\n            }\n            Ok(Receipt {\n                provider_id: format!("push:{}", sub.endpoint),\n                at_tick: 0,\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    struct FakeSms {\n        fail: Option<NotifyError>,\n    }\n    impl SmsPort for FakeSms {\n        fn send(&self, to: &E164, _msg: &StatusMsg) -> Result<Receipt, NotifyError> {\n            if let Some(e) = &self.fail {\n                return Err(e.clone());\n            }\n            Ok(Receipt {\n                provider_id: format!("sms:{}", to.0),\n                at_tick: 0,\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    struct FakeEmail {\n        identity: EmailSenderIdentity,\n        fail: Option<NotifyError>,\n    }\n    impl EmailPort for FakeEmail {\n        fn send(&self, to: &EmailAddr, _msg: &StatusMsg) -> Result<Receipt, NotifyError> {\n            if let Some(e) = &self.fail {\n                return Err(e.clone());\n            }\n            Ok(Receipt {\n                provider_id: format!("email:{}", to.0),\n                at_tick: 0,\n            })\n        }\n        fn sender_identity(&self) -> EmailSenderIdentity {\n            self.identity.clone()\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn web_sub(endpoint: &str) -> PushSub {\n        PushSub {\n            kind: PushKind::WebPush {\n                p256dh: vec![1, 2, 3],\n                auth: vec![4, 5, 6],\n            },\n            endpoint: endpoint.into(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── M1: the taxonomy — dead is not transient, transient is not dead ──\n    #[test]\n    fn dead_token_is_not_transient() {\n        let dead = NotifyError::DeadToken(DeadReason::Apns410BadDeviceToken);\n        let transient = NotifyError::Transient("503".into());\n        // The two arms are structurally distinct variants — a `match` that evicts on `DeadToken`\n        // and retries on `Transient` is exhaustive and cannot conflate them.\n        let evict_dead = matches!(dead, NotifyError::DeadToken(_));\n        let retry_transient = matches!(transient, NotifyError::Transient(_));\n        assert!(evict_dead, "dead matches the evict arm");\n        assert!(retry_transient, "transient matches the retry arm");\n        assert!(\n            !matches!(transient, NotifyError::DeadToken(_)),\n            "transient must never trigger eviction"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── M2: registry is hub-local only (no central host string) + terminal unbinds ──\n    #[test]\n    fn registry_is_hub_local_only() {\n        let mut reg = ChannelRegistry::new();\n        reg.bind(\n            "CH-A",\n            ChannelSet {\n                platform: PlatformContext::AndroidWeb,\n                push: vec![web_sub("ep-a")],\n                sms: Some(E164("+15550001".into())),\n                email: None,\n                messenger: vec![],\n            },\n        );\n        assert!(reg.get("CH-A").is_some());\n        // Terminal transition ⇒ unbind.\n        let _set = reg.get("CH-A").unwrap();\n        assert!(is_terminal_transition(\n            OrderStatus::InDelivery,\n            OrderStatus::Delivered\n        ));\n        // simulate terminal unbind at the hook:\n        if is_terminal_transition(OrderStatus::InDelivery, OrderStatus::Delivered) {\n            reg.unbind("CH-A");\n        }\n        // (the transition above is terminal → would unbind; do it for real here to prove unbind)\n        let terminal = OrderStatus::Delivered.is_terminal();\n        assert!(terminal);\n        reg.unbind("CH-A");\n        assert_eq!(\n            reg.get("CH-A"),\n            None,\n            "terminal order's set is released (hub-local working set)"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn bind_then_terminal_unbinds() {\n        let mut reg = ChannelRegistry::new();\n        reg.bind(\n            "CH-T",\n            ChannelSet {\n                platform: PlatformContext::DesktopWeb,\n                push: vec![],\n                sms: None,\n                email: None,\n                messenger: vec![],\n            },\n        );\n        assert_eq!(reg.len(), 1);\n        // Order reaches Delivered (terminal).\n        assert!(OrderStatus::Delivered.is_terminal());\n        reg.unbind("CH-T");\n        assert_eq!(reg.get("CH-T"), None);\n    }\n\n    // ── M2 adversarial: cross-order isolation through fan-out ──\n    #[test]\n    fn cross_order_isolation() {\n        // Bind A and B to distinct sets. A's notify resolves only A's set (reuses customer.rs:586).\n        let mut reg = ChannelRegistry::new();\n        let set_a = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::AndroidWeb,\n            push: vec![web_sub("ep-a")],\n            sms: None,\n            email: None,\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        let set_b = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::DesktopWeb,\n            push: vec![web_sub("ep-b")],\n            sms: None,\n            email: None,\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        reg.bind("CH-A", set_a);\n        reg.bind("CH-B", set_b);\n        let push = FakePush {\n            fail: Default::default(),\n        };\n        let sms = FakeSms { fail: None };\n        let email = FakeEmail {\n            identity: EmailSenderIdentity::managed_default("hub1"),\n            fail: None,\n        };\n        let msg = StatusMsg::for_status("CH-A", OrderStatus::Ready);\n        let mut n = Notifier::new(&push, &sms, &email, &mut reg, 0);\n        // Notifying CH-A must NOT touch CH-B's subs.\n        let _ = n.notify("CH-A", &msg);\n        assert!(\n            reg.get("CH-B").is_some(),\n            "B's set is untouched by A's notify"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            reg.get("CH-B").unwrap().push.len(),\n            1,\n            "B's sub survives A's fan-out"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── M3: the X10 coverage invariant — the load-bearing proof ──\n    #[test]\n    fn ios_safari_web_push_only_has_no_coverage() {\n        let set = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::IosSafariWeb,\n            push: vec![web_sub("ep")],\n            sms: None,\n            email: None,\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            channel_coverage(&set),\n            Err(NoReachableChannel),\n            "the iOS-Safari-web gap is CAUGHT, never assumed away"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ios_safari_web_with_sms_has_coverage() {\n        let set = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::IosSafariWeb,\n            push: vec![web_sub("ep")],\n            sms: Some(E164("+15550002".into())),\n            email: None,\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            channel_coverage(&set),\n            Ok(()),\n            "SMS fallback makes it honest"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn push_denied_any_platform_needs_fallback() {\n        let set = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::PushDenied,\n            push: vec![web_sub("ep")],\n            sms: None,\n            email: None,\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        assert_eq!(channel_coverage(&set), Err(NoReachableChannel));\n        let set2 = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::PushDenied,\n            push: vec![],\n            sms: Some(E164("+1".into())),\n            email: None,\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        assert_eq!(channel_coverage(&set2), Ok(()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_channelset_fails_closed() {\n        let set = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::DesktopWeb,\n            push: vec![],\n            sms: None,\n            email: None,\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        assert_eq!(channel_coverage(&set), Err(NoReachableChannel));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn native_ios_push_alone_is_reachable() {\n        let set = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::NativeIos,\n            push: vec![PushSub {\n                kind: PushKind::Apns {\n                    device_token: vec![9],\n                },\n                endpoint: String::new(),\n            }],\n            sms: None,\n            email: None,\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        assert_eq!(\n            channel_coverage(&set),\n            Ok(()),\n            "installed-app APNs path must never be over-blocked"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn android_web_push_alone_is_reachable() {\n        let set = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::AndroidWeb,\n            push: vec![web_sub("ep")],\n            sms: None,\n            email: None,\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        assert_eq!(channel_coverage(&set), Ok(()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn email_alone_is_reachable_any_platform() {\n        let set = ChannelSet {\n            platform: PlatformContext::IosSafariWeb,\n            push: vec![],\n            sms: None,\n            email: Some(EmailAddr("a@b.com".into())),\n            messenger: vec![],\n        };\n        assert_eq!(channel_coverage(&set), Ok(()));\n    }\n\n    // ── M4: fan-out — SMS fires even when push is unreachable (§16.52) ──\n    #[test]\n    fn sms_fires_even_when_push_unreachable() {\n No vendor, no network, no central authority;\n    /// the signed attestation *is* the settlement source.\n    CashOnDelivery,\n}\n\n/// A courier's signed claim that cash for an order was collected.\n///\n/// Mirrors the blueprint §2.3 field-for-field. `courier_cert_ref` is the SHA3-256 of the\n/// courier's subject public key — the attestation is cryptographically bound to the cert\n/// identity that `SettlementAuth` proves (see [`decide_settlement`]).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CashAttestation {\n    /// Order the cash was collected for.\n    pub order_id: String,\n    /// Amount of cash collected, integer minor units (i64).\n    pub amount_i64: i64,\n    /// SHA3-256 of the courier cert's subject public key (binds attestation ↔ verified cert).\n    pub courier_cert_ref: [u8; 32],\n    /// The courier's signature over `(order_id || amount_i64 || courier_cert_ref)`.\n    pub sig: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nimpl CashAttestation {\n    /// The canonical signing message: `order_id || amount_i64(le) || courier_cert_ref`.\n    /// Domain-separated so a settlement signature can never be replayed as another message.\n    pub fn signing_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(self.order_id.len() + 8 + 32);\n        buf.extend_from_slice(self.order_id.as_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.amount_i64.to_le_bytes());\n        buf.extend_from_slice(&self.courier_cert_ref);\n        buf\n    }\n}\n\n/// The idempotency key for settlement: ONE settlement fold per order, enforced in\n/// `decide_settlement` by `OrderSettle::settled` (`SettlementReject::AlreadySettled`).\n/// Typed, never a stringly-typed lookup.\npub const SETTLEMENT_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: &str = "order_id";\n\n/// Typed result of a settlement attempt. The caller supplies\n/// a rooted, anchored delegation chain + leaf capability; `decide_settlement` verifies it.\npub struct SettlementAuth<'a, V: SignatureVerifier> {\n    /// The verifier (production injects real Ed25519 ⊕ ML-DSA-65; tests use `RefSigner`).\n    pub verifier: &'a V,\n    /// Operator anchor roster (root issuer must be enrolled).\n    pub roster: &'a AnchorRoster,\n    /// Append-only revocation set (a revoked courier is rejected post-verify). `&mut` so a\n    /// caller can revoke before deciding (the forged-cert adversarial case mutates this).\n    pub revocations: &'a mut RevocationSet,\n    /// The anchored delegation chain proving the courier may record settlement.\n    pub chain: &'a [Delegation],\n    /// The leaf capability binding the courier subject to the settlement scope.\n    pub cap: &'a Capability,\n    /// The courier's subject public key — must equal `attestation.courier_cert_ref`'s preimage.\n    pub courier_subject_key: [u8; 32],\n    /// Current monotonic tick (for expiry checks).\n    pub now: u64,\n}\n\n/// A single settlement lifecycle event — the fold's input. Folded — never a mutation.\n    SettlementRecorded {\n        order_id: String,\n        amount_i64: i64,\n        rail: RailKind,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Per-order settlement bookkeeping held inside the fold state.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\nstruct OrderSettle {\n    placed_total: i64,\n    delivered: bool,\n    /// `Some(amount)` once a `SettlementRecorded` has been folded. Idempotency key.\n    settled: Option<i64>,\n    price_trusted: bool,\n}\n\n/// The folded settlement state — the canonical kernel view over the settlement event log.\n///\n/// `events` is the audit trail (event-sourced); `orders` is the derived projection. Both are\n/// written ONLY by [`fold_event`]; [`decide_settlement`] is pure (reads state, emits an outcome).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct SettlementState {\n    orders: BTreeMap<String, OrderSettle>,\n    events: Vec<SettlementEvent>,\n}\n\nimpl SettlementState {\n    /// Empty settlement state.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        SettlementState::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Fold one [`SettlementEvent`] into the state. The ONLY writer of `orders`/`events`.\n    /// Integer-exact: `settled` amounts use the event's own `amount_i64` (already validated\n    /// to equal `placed_total` by `decide_settlement`), so no arithmetic is performed here\n    /// and no overflow is possible on a single record.\n    pub fn fold_event(&mut self, ev: SettlementEvent) {\n        match &ev {\n            SettlementEvent::OrderPlaced {\n                order_id,\n                total_i64,\n            } => {\n                self.orders.insert(\n                    order_id.clone(),\n                    OrderSettle {\n                        placed_total: *total_i64,\n                        delivered: false,\n                        settled: None,\n                        price_trusted: true,\n                    },\n                );\n            }\n            SettlementEvent::OrderDelivered { order_id } => {\n                if let Some(o) = self.orders.get_mut(order_id) {\n                    o.delivered = true;\n                }\n            }\n            SettlementEvent::SettlementRecorded {\n                order_id,\n                amount_i64,\n                ..\n            } => {\n                if let Some(o) = self.orders.get_mut(order_id) {\n                    o.settled = Some(*amount_i64);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        self.events.push(ev);\n    }\n\n    /// Place an order known to be priced from an untrusted (client) source. Such an order is\n    /// admitted to the fold (so delivery still works) but `decide_settlement` will refuse to\n    /// settle it (`SettlementReject::UntrustedPrice`).\n    pub fn fold_placed_untrusted(&mut self, order_id: String, total_i64: i64) {\n        self.orders.insert(\n            order_id.clone(),\n            OrderSettle {\n                placed_total: total_i64,\n                delivered: false,\n                settled: None,\n                price_trusted: false,\n            },\n        );\n        self.events.push(SettlementEvent::OrderPlaced {\n            order_id,\n            total_i64,\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// The folded events (audit trail), in append order.\n    pub fn events(&self) -> &[SettlementEvent] {\n        &self.events\n    }\n\n    /// The folded events for one order, in append order — used to assert the lifecycle\n    /// sequence `[Placed, Delivered, Settled]` (B2), not just the end-state.\n    pub fn events_for(&self, order_id: &str) -> Vec<&SettlementEvent> {\n        self.events\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|e| match e {\n                SettlementEvent::OrderPlaced { order_id: o, .. }\n                | SettlementEvent::OrderDelivered { order_id: o }\n                | SettlementEvent::SettlementRecorded { order_id: o, .. } => o == order_id,\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Whether `order_id` has a folded `SettlementRecorded`.\n    pub fn is_settled(&self, order_id: &str) -> bool {\n        self.orders\n            .get(order_id)\n            .map(|o| o.settled.is_some())\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// The folded (recorded) settlement amount for an order, if any.\n    pub fn settled_amount(&self, order_id: &str) -> Option<i64> {\n        self.orders.get(order_id).and_then(|o| o.settled)\n    }\n\n    /// Sum of every folded `SettlementRecorded` amount (integer-exact, checked).\n    /// Returns `Err` on overflow (degrade-closed: the invariant check reports the fault\n    /// rather than wrapping).\n    pub fn sum_folded_settlements(&self) -> Result<i64, String> {\n        let mut sum: i64 = 0;\n        for o in self.orders.values() {\n            if let Some(a) = o.settled {\n                sum = sum\n                    .checked_add(a)\n                    .ok_or("sum_folded_settlements overflow")?;\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(sum)\n    }\n\n    /// Sum of fold-derived order totals over every order that is delivered AND settled\n    /// (the orders that should have reconciled). Integer-exact, checked.\n    pub fn sum_fold_derived_totals(&self) -> Result<i64, String> {\n        let mut sum: i64 = 0;\n        for o in self.orders.values() {\n            if o.delivered && o.settled.is_some() {\n                sum = sum\n                    .checked_add(o.placed_total)\n                    .ok_or("sum_fold_derived_totals overflow")?;\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(sum)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The `PaymentPort` — the kernel-ports seam for a settlement rail. Cash-on-delivery needs no network, so [`CashOnDeliveryPort`] is both the kernel's\n/// reference impl AND the production one; a future Wave's adapter would implement this same\n/// trait behind the firewall.\npub trait PaymentPort {\n    /// Stable rail id, e.g. `"cash:cod"`. Used in telemetry + reconciliation rows.\n    fn id(&self) -> &str;\n    /// The rail this port serves.\n    fn rail(&self) -> RailKind;\n    /// Attempt to settle a cash attestation against the current folded state.\n    ///\n    /// PURE: reads `state`, returns a typed [`SettlementOutcome`]. It appends NOTHING — the\n    /// caller folds a `SettlementRecorded` only on `SettlementOutcome::Recorded` (mirroring\n    /// `event_log::commit_after_decide`: decide BEFORE commit). A rail failure is a value.\n    fn settle<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n        &self,\n        state: &SettlementState,\n        att: &CashAttestation,\n        auth: &SettlementAuth<'_, V>,\n    ) -> SettlementOutcome;\n}\n\n/// Kernel reference `PaymentPort` for the cash-on-delivery rail (Wave-0).\n///\n/// Cash needs no vendor/network, so this pure impl is the real production port, not a stub.\n/// It delegates to [`decide_settlement`] — the single settlement-Law entry point.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]\npub struct CashOnDeliveryPort;\n\nimpl PaymentPort for CashOnDeliveryPort {\n    fn id(&self) -> &str {\n        "cash:cod"\n    }\n    fn rail(&self) -> RailKind {\n        RailKind::CashOnDelivery\n    }\n    fn settle<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n        &self,\n        state: &SettlementState,\n        att: &CashAttestation,\n        auth: &SettlementAuth<'_, V>,\n    ) -> SettlementOutcome {\n        decide_settlement(state, att, auth)\n    }\n}\n\n/// **The settlement Law (P47 §2.4/§2.6).** Pure decide: validate a `CashAttestation` against\n/// the folded `SettlementState` and emit a typed [`SettlementOutcome`]. Appends nothing.\n///\n/// Rejection order is load-bearing (each adversarial case is a distinct pole):\n///   1. unknown order      → `UnknownOrder`\n///   2. not delivered      → `NotDelivered`            (settle-before-deliver, §2.6-2)\n///   3. already settled    → `AlreadySettled`          (idempotency, §2.6-1)\n///   4. cert-ref mismatch  → `CourierCertRejected`     (attestation not bound to `AmountMismatch`          (§2.6-3 — never adjusts either number)\n///   8. otherwise          → `Recorded`\npub fn decide_settlement<V: SignatureVerifier>(\n    state: &SettlementState,\n    att: &CashAttestation,\n    auth: &SettlementAuth<'_, V>,\n) -> SettlementOutcome {\n    // (1) order must exist.\n    let order = match state.orders.get(&att.order_id) {\n        Some(o) => o,\n        None => {\n            return SettlementOutcome::Rejected(SettlementReject::UnknownOrder {\n                order_id: att.order_id.clone(),\n            })\n        }\n    };\n\n    // (2) settle-before-deliver: the order must be in the delivered state (§2.6-2).\n    if !order.delivered {\n        return SettlementOutcome::Rejected(SettlementReject::NotDelivered {\n            order_id: att.order_id.clone(),\n            status: "pre-delivery".to_string(),\n        });\n    }\n\n    // (3) idempotency by `order_id` (§2.6-1): a second settlement is a no-op reject.\n    if order.settled.is_some() {\n        return SettlementOutcome::Rejected(SettlementReject::AlreadySettled {\n            order_id: att.order_id.clone(),\n        });\n    }\n\n    // (4) the attestation must be bound to the verified cert identity.\n    let expected_ref = sha3_256(&auth.courier_subject_key);\n    if expected_ref != att.courier_cert_ref {\n        return SettlementOutcome::Rejected(SettlementReject::CourierCertRejected {\n            order_id: att.order_id.clone(),\n            reason: "courier_cert_ref does not bind to verified cert subject key".to_string(),\n        });\n    }\n\n    // (5) money integrity: refuse to settle an order priced from an untrusted source.\n    if !order.price_trusted {\n        return SettlementOutcome::Rejected(SettlementReject::UntrustedPrice {\n            order_id: att.order_id.clone(),\n        });\n    }\n\n    // (6) forged attestation (§2.6-4): verify the anchored courier cert chain, then check\n    //     revocation. No new crypto — reuses `verify_chain` / `RevocationSet`.\n    if let Err(e) = verify_chain(auth.verifier, auth.roster, auth.chain, auth.cap, auth.now) {\n        return SettlementOutcome::Rejected(SettlementReject::CourierCertRejected {\n            order_id: att.order_id.clone(),\n            reason: format!("verify_chain: {:?}", e),\n        });\n    }\n    if auth.revocations.is_revoked_key(&auth.courier_subject_key) {\n        return SettlementOutcome::Rejected(SettlementReject::CourierCertRejected {\n            order_id: att.order_id.clone(),\n            reason: "courier subject key is revoked".to_string(),\n        });\n    }\n\n    // (7) amount mismatch (§2.6-3): attested ≠ fold-derived total. NEVER silently adjusts.\n    if att.amount_i64 != order.placed_total {\n        return SettlementOutcome::Rejected(SettlementReject::AmountMismatch {\n            order_id: att.order_id.clone(),\n            attested: att.amount_i64,\n            expected: order.placed_total,\n        });\n    }\n\n    // (8) accepted. The caller folds a `SettlementRecorded` from this; the fold is the writer.\n    SettlementOutcome::Recorded {\n        order_id: att.order_id.clone(),\n        amount_i64: att.amount_i64,\n        rail: RailKind::CashOnDelivery,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a valid `SettlementAuth` for a courier, anchored by `anchor_secret`, on the\n/// `verifier`. Test/reference helper — the production path injects the real bebop2 verifier +\n/// operator anchor roster at the integration boundary (seam reuse). The returned roster /\n/// revocations / chain / cap are leaked into `'a` for the builder's convenience; production\n/// passes borrows with real (shorter) lifetimes.\npub fn build_courier_auth<'a, V: SignatureVerifier>(\n    verifier: &'a V,\n    anchor_secret: &[u8; 32],\n    courier_secret: &[u8; 32],\n    now: u64,\n) -> SettlementAuth<'a, V> {\n    let anchor_pk = verifier.classical_public(anchor_secret);\n    let courier_pk = verifier.classical_public(courier_secret);\n    let mut roster = AnchorRoster::new();\n    roster.enroll(&anchor_pk);\n    let revocations = RevocationSet::new();\n    let scope = Scope::single(Resource::Ledger, Action::SettlementRecorded);\n    let cap = Capability::new_hybrid(\n        courier_pk,\n        verifier.pq_public(courier_secret),\n        scope.clone(),\n        [1u8; 8],\n        now + 10_000,\n    );\n    let link = Delegation::sign(\n        verifier,\n        anchor_pk,\n        courier_pk,\n        scope.clone(),\n        scope,\n        now + 10_000,\n        [2u8; 8],\n        anchor_secret,\n    );\n    // Leak the owned chain/cap/roster/revocations into `'a` for the test builder.\n    let chain = Box::leak(Box::new([link]));\n    let cap = Box::leak(Box::new(cap));\n    let roster = Box::leak(Box::new(roster));\n    let revocations = Box::leak(Box::new(revocations));\n    SettlementAuth {\n        verifier,\n        roster,\n        revocations,\n        chain,\n        cap,\n        courier_subject_key: courier_pk,\n        now,\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::ports::agent::cap::RefSigner;\n\n    // A `const` verifier so `build_courier_auth` can return a `'static` auth in the helpers.\n    const V: RefSigner = RefSigner;\n\n    // ── B1: firewall red-proof ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // The port module must NOT `use` any external adapter / network / serde crate. Embedded at\n    // compile time via `include_str!` so the check runs in `cargo test --lib` with zero side\n    // effects. If someone adds a `use …_adapters::…` (or any forbidden boundary crate) import\n    // this file, THIS test fails the build's test run — the firewall.\n    const SELF_SRC: &str = include_str!("payment.rs");\n    // Import-pattern probes: `use <crate>` or `<crate>::` — doc prose ("no serde") does NOT match.\n    // NOTE: the forbidden tokens are assembled from parts so the literal substrings never\n    // appear in THIS source file (otherwise the self-scan would match its own definition —\n    // a false positive). The doc comment below is deliberately phrased without those literals.\n    const PREFIX: &str = "pay";\n    const MID: &str = "ment_ad";\n    const SUFFIX: &str = "apters";\n    const FORBIDDEN_IMPORTS: &[&str] = &[\n        concat!("use ", "payment_", "adapters"),\n        concat!("use llm", "_adapters"),\n        concat!("use agent", "_adapters"),\n        concat!("use req", "west"),\n        concat!("use hyp", "er"),\n        concat!("use ser", "de"),\n        concat!("use s", "erde", "_json"),\n        concat!("use s", "erde", "_yaml"),\n        concat!("use wasm_", "bindgen"),\n        concat!("use to", "kio"),\n        concat!("use sq", "lx"),\n        concat!("pay", "ment_ad", "apters", "::"),\n        concat!("req", "west", "::"),\n        concat!("hyp", "er", "::"),\n        concat!("s", "erde", "::"),\n        concat!("ser", "de", "_json", "::"),\n        concat!("wasm_", "bindgen", "::"),\n        concat!("to", "kio", "::"),\n        concat!("sq", "lx", "::"),\n    ];\n    // silence unused warnings for the splice helpers used only to keep literals out of source.\n    const _: &str = PREFIX;\n    const _: &str = MID;\n    const _: &str = SUFFIX;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn firewall_self_source_is_clean() {\n        for forbidden in FORBIDDEN_IMPORTS {\n            assert!(\n                !SELF_SRC.contains(forbidden),\n                "payment.rs firewall violation: references forbidden crate pattern '{forbidden}'"\n            );\n        }\n        // Also assert the module documents the compile firewall and the cash-only RailKind.\n        assert!(SELF_SRC.contains("Compile firewall"));\n        assert!(SELF_SRC.contains("CashOnDelivery"));\n        // Card/digital/crypto variants must be absent (operator-ruled Waves, §2.3). The\n        // forbidden substrings are assembled via concat! so the assertion source does not itself\n        // contain them (which would make `!contains` a vacuous/always-false check).\n        assert!(!SELF_SRC.contains(concat!("Card", "OnDelivery")));\n        assert!(!SELF_SRC.contains(concat!("Proces", "sor")));\n        assert!(!SELF_SRC.contains(concat!("Rail", "Kind::", "Crypto")));\n        assert!(!SELF_SRC.contains(concat!("Rail", "Kind::", "Proces", "sor")));\n    }\n\n    // ── helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    fn att_for(order_id: &str, amount: i64, cert_ref: [u8; 32], sig: Vec<u8>) -> CashAttestation {\n        CashAttestation {\n            order_id: order_id.to_string(),\n            amount_i64: amount,\n            courier_cert_ref: cert_ref,\n            sig,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn good_auth(now: u64) -> (SettlementAuth<'static, RefSigner>, [u8; 32]) {\n        let auth = build_courier_auth(&V, &[11u8; 32], &[22u8; 32], now);\n        let cert_ref = sha3_256(&V.classical_public(&[22u8; 32]));\n        (auth, cert_ref)\n    }\n\n    // ── B2: end-to-end cash rail as event append ──────────────────────────────\n    #[test]\n    fn b2_cash_rail_end_to_end_event_sequence() {\n        let (auth, cert_ref) = good_auth(1_000);\n        let port = CashOnDeliveryPort;\n        let mut state = SettlementState::new();\n\n        // place → deliver → attest → fold (never a mutation; each step is an append).\n        state.fold_event(SettlementEvent::OrderPlaced {\n            order_id: "O1".into(),\n            total_i64: 1500,\n        });\n        state.fold_event(SettlementEvent::OrderDelivered {\n            order_id: "O1".into(),\n        });\n        let att = att_for("O1", 1500, cert_ref, vec![1, 2, 3]);\n        let outcome = port.settle(&state, &att, &auth);\n        assert_eq!(\n            outcome,\n            SettlementOutcome::Recorded {\n                order_id: "O1".into(),\n                amount_i64: 1500,\n                rail: RailKind::CashOnDelivery\n            }\n        );\n        // The caller folds the recorded event (decide-before-commit):\n        if let SettlementOutcome::Recorded { amount_i64, .. } = outcome {\n            state.fold_event(SettlementEvent::SettlementRecorded {\n                order_id: "O1".into(),\n                amount_i64,\n                rail: RailKind::CashOnDelivery,\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Assert the EVENT SEQUENCE, not just end-state (B2 / §2.4).\n        let seq: Vec<SettlementEvent> = state.events_for("O1").into_iter().cloned().collect();\n        assert_eq!(\n            seq,\n            vec![\n                SettlementEvent::OrderPlaced {\n                    order_id: "O1".into(),\n                    total_i64: 1500\n                },\n                SettlementEvent::OrderDelivered {\n                    order_id: "O1".into()\n                },\n                SettlementEvent::SettlementRecorded {\n                    order_id: "O1".into(),\n                    amount_i64: 1500,\n                    rail: RailKind::CashOnDelivery\n                },\n            ]\n        );\n        assert!(state.is_settled("O1"));\n        assert_eq!(state.settled_amount("O1"), Some(1500));\n    }\n\n    // ── B3: reconciliation property test (exact i64 equality, arbitrary sequences) ─\n    use proptest::prelude::*;\n\n    /// A generated settlement op. Ids are kept in `0..MAX_ORDER` so the harness can build a\n    /// legal Placed total and a matching attestation amount.\n    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n    enum Op {\n        Place { id: u8, total: i64 },\n        Deliver { id: u8 },\n        Settle { id: u8 },\n    }\n\n    fn arb_op() -> impl Strategy<Value = Op> {\n        // total in a safe i64 band so sums never overflow in the test itself.\n        let total = any::<i64>().prop_map(|t| t.clamp(1, 1_000_000));\n        prop_oneof![\n            (any::<u8>(), total).prop_map(|(id, total)| Op::Place { id, total }),\n            any::<u8>().prop_map(|id| Op::Deliver { id }),\n            any::<u8>().prop_map(|id| Op::Settle { id }),\n        ]\n    }\n\n    proptest! {\n        #![proptest_config(ProptestConfig::with_cases(400))]\n        /// Folded settlements ≡ fold-derived order totals, EXACT i64 equality, over arbitrary\n        /// order sequences (interleaved place/deliver/settle, with illegal settles rejected).\n        #[test]\n        fn b3_reconciliation_folded_eq_fold_derived(ops in proptest::collection::vec(arb_op(), 1..60)) {\n            let auth = state.fold_event(SettlementEvent::SettlementRecorded {\n                                order_id: oid,\n                                amount_i64,\n                                rail: ## 15615 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/payment_capability.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: payment_capability · 362 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/payment_capability.rs	payment_capability · 362 lines	//! ports/payment_capability.rs — P47 payment-rail CAPABILITY DECLARATION scaffold.\n//!\n//! # What this module IS\n//! A pure, declarative inventory of which payment rails the platform *intends* to support,\n//! per the operator ruling (rail set = { Fiat, Crypto, Stripe, Google/Apple Pay }, rest later).\n//! It is a CAPABILITY/feature declaration ONLY:\n//!\n//!   * `PaymentRail`    — the closed set of rails (exhaustive enum, `FromStr`/`Display`).\n//!   * `PaymentCapability { rail, enabled }` — a feature flag, NO credentials, NO transport.\n//!   * `PaymentError`   — the one error this layer can produce (`NotYetSupported`).\n//!   * `PaymentCapability::validate()` — rejects any rail not yet green-lit (`OtherLater`).\n//!\n//! # RED-LINE (binding — do NOT cross)\n//! This module constructs NO real provider object, reads NO environment credentials, makes NO\n//! network calls, and moves NO money. `PaymentCapability` carries no credential, no transport\n//! field. If a real Stripe/crypto/Fiat processor is ever needed, that belongs in a\n//! downstream adapter crate behind the kernel's compile firewall (see `payment.rs`), NOT here.\n//! This module is the "what could exist" registry; the "how it connects" lives elsewhere and is\n//! deliberately absent.\n//!\n//! # Red-proof (the firewall, by construction)\n//! The test `red_line_no_real_provider_references` greps THIS file's own source for\n//! provider/credential markers and FAILS if any appears — proving the red-line holds at the\n//! source level. This is why the capability scaffold lives in its OWN module rather than being\n//! bolted onto `payment.rs` (which legitimately reuses internal signing machinery and would\n//! trip a whole-file scan). The forbidden markers are assembled via `concat!` so the scan body\n//! never literally contains them (which would make the negation self-matching / vacuous).\n\nuse core::fmt;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\n\nuse core::str::FromStr;\n\n/// The closed set of payment rails the platform may declare support for (P47 operator ruling).\n///\n/// This is exhaustive by design: adding a rail is a compile-time change (you must handle it in\n/// `FromStr`/`Display`/`validate`), which keeps the capability registry honest. `OtherLater`\n/// is the explicit "not yet" bucket — it may be *named* but `validate()` rejects it so nothing\n/// can silently treat an unbuilt rail as live.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum PaymentRail {\n    /// Government-issued / bank money rail (ACH, SEPA, wire, card-net presentment, …).\n    /// Operator-ruled; no adapter is built here — capability declaration only.\n    Fiat,\n    /// Cryptocurrency / on-chain settlement rail. Operator-ruled; no wallet transport here.\n    Crypto,\n    /// Stripe (card + digital wallet presentment via Stripe). Operator-ruled; NO Stripe object\n    /// is constructed in this module — declaring the rail is the only thing that happens.\n    Stripe,\n    /// Google Pay / Apple Pay (tokenized wallet presentment). Operator-ruled; no wallet SDK is\n    /// constructed here.\n    GoogleApplePay,\n    /// Anything the operator has NOT yet green-lit. Named so it can be referenced, but\n    /// `validate()` rejects it (`NotYetSupported`) so an unbuilt rail can never be enabled.\n    OtherLater,\n}\n\nimpl PaymentRail {\n    /// Stable lowercase string id (used in capability manifests, telemetry, reconciliation\n    /// rows). Distinct from `Display` only in being the canonical machine identifier.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            PaymentRail::Fiat => "fiat",\n            PaymentRail::Crypto => "crypto",\n            PaymentRail::Stripe => "stripe",\n            PaymentRail::GoogleApplePay => "google_apple_pay",\n            PaymentRail::OtherLater => "other_later",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// All rails in declaration order. Handy for enumerating the capability matrix.\n    pub const ALL: &'static [PaymentRail] = &[\n        PaymentRail::Fiat,\n        PaymentRail::Crypto,\n        PaymentRail::Stripe,\n        PaymentRail::GoogleApplePay,\n        PaymentRail::OtherLater,\n    ];\n\n    /// The four rails the operator has actually ruled IN for now (excludes `OtherLater`).\n    /// `validate()` accepts exactly these.\n    pub const SUPPORTED_NOW: &'static [PaymentRail] = &[\n        PaymentRail::Fiat,\n        PaymentRail::Crypto,\n        PaymentRail::Stripe,\n        PaymentRail::GoogleApplePay,\n    ];\n\n    /// Whether this rail is part of the operator-ruled-in set (i.e. `validate` would accept it).\n    pub fn is_supported_now(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(\n            self,\n            PaymentRail::Fiat\n                | PaymentRail::Crypto\n                | PaymentRail::Stripe\n                | PaymentRail::GoogleApplePay\n        )\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for PaymentRail {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        // Human-readable, title-ish form.\n        let s = match self {\n            PaymentRail::Fiat => "Fiat",\n            PaymentRail::Crypto => "Crypto",\n            PaymentRail::Stripe => "Stripe",\n            PaymentRail::GoogleApplePay => "Google/Apple Pay",\n            PaymentRail::OtherLater => "Other (later)",\n        };\n        f.write_str(s)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FromStr for PaymentRail {\n    type Err = PaymentError;\n\n    /// Case-insensitive parse from the canonical `as_str()` identifiers. Unknown strings are\n    /// rejected as `PaymentError::UnknownRail` (never silently mapped onto `OtherLater`).\n    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {\n        match s.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {\n            "fiat" => Ok(PaymentRail::Fiat),\n            "crypto" => Ok(PaymentRail::Crypto),\n            "stripe" => Ok(PaymentRail::Stripe),\n            "google_apple_pay" | "googleapplepay" => Ok(PaymentRail::GoogleApplePay),\n            "other_later" | "otherlater" => Ok(PaymentRail::OtherLater),\n            _ => Err(PaymentError::UnknownRail(s.trim().to_string())),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The one error this capability layer can produce.\n///\n/// Note what it does NOT include: no network error, no auth/credential error, no provider\n/// error — because this module performs none of those operations. Declaring a capability is a\n/// pure, local, in-memory act.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum PaymentError {\n    /// The rail is named but not yet green-lit by the operator (`OtherLater`).\n    NotYetSupported { rail: PaymentRail },\n    /// `FromStr`/`as_str` round-trip could not resolve the string to a known rail.\n    UnknownRail(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for PaymentError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            PaymentError::NotYetSupported { rail } => {\n                write!(f, "payment rail '{}' is not yet supported", rail)\n            }\n            PaymentError::UnknownRail(s) => write!(f, "unknown payment rail '{}'", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl core::error::Error for PaymentError {}\n\n/// A capability/feature declaration for one payment rail.\n///\n/// This is NOT a transport handle and carries NO credentials. It is the "the platform may\n/// offer rail X, and it is currently on/off" record. Everything that would connect to a real\n/// processor is intentionally absent — that is the red-line. Such wiring belongs in a\n/// downstream adapter crate behind the kernel firewall.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct PaymentCapability {\n    /// Which rail this capability declares.\n    pub rail: PaymentRail,\n    /// Whether the rail is currently enabled in the capability matrix. `validate()` must pass\n    /// before `enabled = true` is meaningful.\n    pub enabled: bool,\n}\n\nimpl PaymentCapability {\n    /// Declare a rail as enabled. Caller should have already ensured the rail is supported;\n    /// `validate()` is the authoritative gate.\n    pub fn enabled(rail: PaymentRail) -> Self {\n        PaymentCapability {\n            rail,\n            enabled: true,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Declare a rail as disabled (e.g. a future rail announced but not live).\n    pub fn disabled(rail: PaymentRail) -> Self {\n        PaymentCapability {\n            rail,\n            enabled: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The capability matrix for "now": the four operator-ruled-in rails, all declared ENABLED.\n    /// `OtherLater` is deliberately NOT in this list — it must be added explicitly and will\n    /// fail `validate()` until the operator rules it in.\n    pub fn current_matrix() -> Vec<PaymentCapability> {\n        PaymentRail::SUPPORTED_NOW\n            .iter()\n            .map(|&r| PaymentCapability::enabled(r))\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Gate: a capability is only valid if its rail is supported now.\n    ///\n    /// * Any of {Fiat, Crypto, Stripe, GoogleApplePay} → `Ok(())` (the operator ruled these in).\n    /// * `OtherLater` → `Err(NotYetSupported)` (named but not green-lit).\n    ///\n    /// This is the ONLY operation on the capability layer, and it is pure + local.\n    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), PaymentError> {\n        if self.rail.is_supported_now() {\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            Err(PaymentError::NotYetSupported { rail: self.rail })\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    // ── red-line: the module source must NOT reference real-provider / credential markers ──\n    // Scans THIS file only (the capability scaffold). The forbidden markers are assembled via\n    // `concat!` so this test body never literally contains them (which would make the\n    // negation self-matching). Because the module source is genuinely free of these substrings,\n    // every assertion below is a TRUE negative.\n    const SELF_SRC: &str = include_str!("payment_capability.rs");\n\n    const FORBIDDEN_MARKERS: &[&str] = &[\n        concat!("req", "west"),  // real HTTP provider\n        concat!("ur", "eq"),     // real HTTP provider\n        concat!("std::en", "v"), // environment credential read\n        concat!("sec", "ret"),   // credential material\n        concat!("ke", "y"),      // credential material\n    ];\n\n    #[test]\n    fn red_line_no_real_provider_references() {\n        for marker in FORBIDDEN_MARKERS {\n            assert!(\n                !SELF_SRC.contains(marker),\n                "payment_capability.rs red-line violation: references '{marker}'"\n            );\n        }\n        // Positive structural assertions: capability declaration only — no transport/credential.\n        assert!(SELF_SRC.contains("capability declaration"));\n        assert!(SELF_SRC.contains("ENABLED"));\n        // The red-line must be documented and `OtherLater` must be the only rejected rail.\n        assert!(SELF_SRC.contains("RED-LINE"));\n        assert!(SELF_SRC.contains("NotYetSupported"));\n    }\n\n    // ── enum round-trips: Display→as_str→FromStr→enum is identity for all variants ──\n    #[test]\n    fn rail_from_str_display_roundtrip() {\n        for &rail in PaymentRail::ALL {\n            // canonical identifier round-trips exactly.\n            let parsed = PaymentRail::from_str(rail.as_str()).expect("as_str must parse");\n            assert_eq!(parsed, rail, "round-trip broke for {}", rail);\n            // Display produces a non-empty, distinct label.\n            assert!(!rail.to_string().is_empty());\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rail_from_str_case_insensitive_and_aliases() {\n        assert_eq!(\n            "STRIPE".parse::<PaymentRail>().unwrap(),\n            PaymentRail::Stripe\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            " Google_Apple_Pay ".parse::<PaymentRail>().unwrap(),\n            PaymentRail::GoogleApplePay\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            "googleapplepay".parse::<PaymentRail>().unwrap(),\n            PaymentRail::GoogleApplePay\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            "OTHER_LATER".parse::<PaymentRail>().unwrap(),\n            PaymentRail::OtherLater\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rail_from_str_unknown_is_error() {\n        assert_eq!(\n            "paypal".parse::<PaymentRail>(),\n            Err(PaymentError::UnknownRail("paypal".to_string()))\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            "".parse::<PaymentRail>(),\n            Err(PaymentError::UnknownRail("".to_string()))\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            " stripe ".parse::<PaymentRail>(), // already covered, just confirming delimiter trim\n            Ok(PaymentRail::Stripe)\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ── validate accepts the 4 real rails ──\n    #[test]\n    fn validate_accepts_the_four_real_rails() {\n        for &rail in PaymentRail::SUPPORTED_NOW {\n            let cap = PaymentCapability::enabled(rail);\n still validates as a *capability* (the gate is the rail,\n            // not the enabled flag).\n            assert_eq!(PaymentCapability::disabled(rail).validate(), Ok(()));\n        }\n    }\n\n 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ports/tool.rs	tool · 404 lines	//! ports/tool.rs — the `ToolPort` firewall (P40's tool seam, defined HERE so the\n//! parallel P40 `agent-loop` worktree and P42's `mcp` port can both reuse it) plus\n//! the Skills-pattern discovery layer (P42 — `SkillCard` / `SkillRegistry` /\n//! `StaticSkillRegistry`).\n//!\n//! # Compile firewall (mirrors `ports/llm.rs:3-7`)\n//! ZERO network / HTTP / JSON / serde. This module defines ABSTRACT contracts\n//! (traits + plain value types) only. The concrete tool impl + the JSON framing\n//! live in downstream crates (`agent-facade` for the impl, the `agent-mcp` crate\n//! for the stdio/JSON-RPC framing that drives [`crate::ports::mcp`]). A native rlib\n//! consumer of the kernel pulls NONE of serde / serde_json.\n//!\n//! # Why this lives in the kernel ports layer, not a facade crate\n//! The `ToolPort` trait is the closed authority the Agent-Skills boundary hangs off\n//! of: writes are UNREPRESENTABLE because `ToolAction` has exactly one variant\n//! (`Read`). P40's loop and P42's MCP server are TWO consumers of one contract, so\n//! the trait must live where both reach it without importing each other — the ports\n//! layer. Defining it here (instead of inside the `agent-loop` worktree) is the\n//! file-ownership coordination for P40/P42 parallel execution: P42 owns `tool.rs` +\n//! `mcp.rs`; P40 owns `agent/loop.rs` and imports `ToolPort` from here.\n\n\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeSet;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::boxed::Box;\n/// Closed resource enum. A tool target not listed here is UNREPRESENTABLE.\n/// Money/auth/RLS/migration resources are never added (red-line — see `mcp.rs`'s\n/// reachability argument).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum ToolResource {\n    /// Read the lifecycle status of an order (the P40/P42 tool).\n    OrderStatus,\n    /// Fetch a URL's content and extract its readable text (native, read-only,\n    /// zero JS execution). The HTTP fetch lives in the concrete `agent-facade`\n    /// impl (this crate stays network-free — see the module firewall doc above);\n    /// the readable-text extraction itself is `crate::readability`, pure `std`.\n    /// Interactive/JS-driven browsing is deliberately NOT this tool and is never\n    /// reimplemented in-kernel — that class of capability stays an external tool\n    /// behind its own port, same posture as the declared-but-empty GPU seam.\n    WebFetch,\n}\n\n/// Closed action enum. `Read` is the ONLY variant in P40/P42 — a mutating tool\n/// invocation is not policy-forbidden, it is type-unrepresentable.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum ToolAction {\n    /// Read-only access to the tool's backing source.\n    Read,\n}\n\n/// The capability scope a tool invocation executes under. Granted by the\n/// composition layer (agent-facade / agent-mcp), checked fail-closed by the port\n/// impl: the granted scope must cover the tool's declared scope or the invocation\n/// is refused BEFORE the tool body runs.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub struct ToolScope {\n    /// What the tool targets.\n    pub resource: ToolResource,\n    /// What the tool does with it.\n    pub action: ToolAction,\n}\n\nimpl ToolScope {\n    /// Map this kernel tool-scope onto the agent-bridge capability [`Scope`]\n    /// (P40/P42 reuse the proven closed-enum authority from `ports::agent` for the\n    /// verify_chain capability gate — we do NOT invent a second crypto/scope system).\n    ///\n    /// `ToolResource::OrderStatus` + `ToolAction::Read` ⇒ read access to the\n    /// `Order` resource. A future tool that targets a RED-LINE resource would map\n    /// onto a red-line `(Resource, Action)` pair and would be denied by the\n    /// capability gate's red-line policy unless operator-allow-listed.\n    pub fn to_agent_scope(&self) -> crate::ports::agent::Scope {\n        use crate::ports::agent::{Action, Resource, Scope};\n        match (self.resource, self.action) {\n            (ToolResource::OrderStatus, ToolAction::Read) => {\n                Scope::single(Resource::Order, Action::Read)\n            }\n            (ToolResource::WebFetch, ToolAction::Read) => {\n                Scope::single(Resource::Web, Action::Read)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Static declaration of one tool — what the model is told, verbatim.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ToolSpec {\n    /// "`read_order_status`".\n    pub name: &'static str,\n    /// Natural-language contract handed to the model.\n    pub description: &'static str,\n    /// "`order_id`" — the single string argument the tool accepts.\n    pub arg_name: &'static str,\n    /// Declared capability requirement, checked against the grant.\n    pub scope: ToolScope,\n}\n\n/// One parsed tool invocation (the model's ask, post-parse, pre-execution).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ToolInvocation {\n    /// The tool name (resolved by the dispatcher).\n    pub tool_name: String,\n    /// The raw argument payload from the model, verbatim. The PORT IMPL parses it;\n    /// the loop / MCP server never do.\n    pub raw_arg: String,\n}\n\n/// Tool output — plain text handed back as the observation.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ToolOutput {\n    /// The result text (e.g. an order status).\n    pub content: String,\n}\n\n/// Typed tool failure. Implemented in `agent-facade` (downstream crate); consumed by the\n/// agent loop as `&dyn ToolPort` (P40) AND by the MCP server (P42) as `&dyn\n/// ToolPort` — one door, one contract.\npub trait ToolPort {\n    /// The static declaration (name, description, arg, declared scope).\n    fn spec(&self) -> &ToolSpec;\n    /// Invoke the tool under the `granted` scope. The impl MUST fail-closed (return\n    /// [`ToolError::ScopeDenied]) when `granted` does not cover `spec().scope`.\n    fn invoke(&self, granted: ToolScope, inv: &ToolInvocation) -> Result<ToolOutput, ToolError>;\n}\n\n// ───────────────────────────── Skills-pattern discovery (P42) ──────────────────\n//\n// The discoverability layer that lets the tool catalog grow WITHOUT growing every\n// prompt: discovery (cards, cheap, always in context) is separated from activation\n// (the full ToolSpec, materialized only for selected tools).
```
