## 16291 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ktg2/fractal.rs · LongTerm

Summary: fractal · 275 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ktg2/fractal.rs	fractal · 275 lines	//! Фрактальний біт: кожний 1-бітний елемент — самоподібна точка\n//! відносно -64 (абсолютний нуль). True і False — cos і sin кута\n//! на одиничному колі з центром у ZERO. Інверсія — віддзеркалення\n//! через -64, що природно міняє істинність, зберігаючи фрактальну\n//! структуру та зменшує у степенях (позиції — степені двійки).\n\n/// Абсолютний нуль: всі фрактальні біти відлічуються від нього.\npub const ZERO: i32 = -64;\n\n/// Одиничне слово: 24 фрактальні біти.\npub const WORD_BITS: usize = 24;\n\n/// Одиничний фрактальний біт: фізичний біт, геометрична позиція, глибина.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub struct Bit {\n    /// Фізичний 1-біт: 0 або 1.\n    pub bit: u8,\n    /// Позиція на колі відносно ZERO. Визначає кут θ.\n    pub pos: i32,\n    /// Фрактальна глибина: самоподібність. При depth=0 — простий біт.\n    /// При depth=n — біт містить 2^n суб-бітів.\n    pub depth: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Bit {\n    pub const fn new(bit: u8, pos: i32, depth: u32) -> Self {\n        Self { bit, pos, depth }\n    }\n\n    /// Біт як точка на одиничному колі: (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ).\n    /// Якщо bit=1 (True) — x=cos θ, y=0 (косинус-домінант).\n    /// Якщо bit=0 (False) — x=0, y=sin θ (синус-домінант).\n    /// θ = (pos - ZERO) * π / 128.\n    pub fn as_unit(&self) -> (f64, f64) {\n        let d = (self.pos - ZERO) as f64;\n        let theta = d * core::f64::consts::PI / 128.0;\n        if self.bit == 1 {\n            (crate::math::cos(theta), 0.0)\n        } else {\n            (0.0, crate::math::sin(theta))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Інверсія: віддзеркалення через ZERO.\n    /// bit → 1 - bit, pos → 2*ZERO - pos.\n    pub fn invert(&self) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            bit: 1 - self.bit,\n            pos: 2 * ZERO - self.pos,\n            depth: self.depth,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Істинний (cos-домінант).\n    pub fn is_true(&self) -> bool {\n        self.bit == 1\n    }\n\n    /// Хибний (sin-домінант).\n    pub fn is_false(&self) -> bool {\n        self.bit == 0\n    }\n\n    /// Кількість суб-бітів на цій глибині: 2^depth.\n    pub fn sub_bits(&self) -> u32 {\n        1u32 << self.depth\n    }\n\n    /// Дробова частина позиції відносно ZERO: pos / ZERO.\n    pub fn fraction(&self) -> f64 {\n        (self.pos as f64) / (ZERO as f64)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl core::ops::Not for Bit {\n    type Output = Self;\n    fn not(self) -> Self {\n        self.invert()\n    }\n}\n\n/// 24 фрактальні біти в одному слові.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub struct Word([Bit; WORD_BITS]);\n\nimpl Word {\n    pub const fn new(bits: [Bit; WORD_BITS]) -> Self {\n        Self(bits)\n    }\n\n    pub fn get(&self, i: usize) -> Option<Bit> {\n        self.0.get(i).copied()\n    }\n\n    pub fn set(&mut self, i: usize, bit: Bit) {\n        self.0[i] = bit;\n    }\n\n    /// Інверсія всього слова: кожен біт віддзеркалено через ZERO.\n    pub fn invert(&self) -> Self {\n        Self(self.0.map(|b| b.invert()))\n    }\n\n    /// AND: логічний перетин — істинно лише якщо обидва біти True.\n    /// (Геометрія cos/sin залишається проекцією через [`Bit::as_unit`].)\n    pub fn and(&self, other: &Self) -> Self {\n        Self(core::array::from_fn(|i| {\n            let a = self.0[i];\n            let b = other.0[i];\n            let val = if a.is_true() && b.is_true() { 1u8 } else { 0u8 };\n            Bit::new(val, a.pos, a.depth)\n        }))\n    }\n\n    /// OR: логічне об'єднання — істинно якщо хоча б один біт True.\n    /// (Геометрія cos/sin залишається проекцією через [`Bit::as_unit`].)\n    pub fn or(&self, other: &Self) -> Self {\n        Self(core::array::from_fn(|i| {\n            let a = self.0[i];\n            let b = other.0[i];\n            let val = if a.is_true() || b.is_true() { 1u8 } else { 0u8 };\n            Bit::new(val, a.pos, a.depth)\n        }))\n    }\n\n    /// NOT: інверсія кожного біта.\n    pub fn not(&self) -> Self {\n        self.invert()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl core::ops::Not for Word {\n    type Output = Self;\n    fn not(self) -> Self {\n        self.invert()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Зменшення у степенях: позиція біта — степінь двійки відносно ZERO.\n/// pos = -64 * 2^k для k ∈ {0,1,2,3,...}. Це дає самоподібність:\n/// кожен рівень — подвійна відстань від нуль-центру.\npub const fn power_pos(k: u32) -> i32 {\n    let shift = if k >= 31 { 31 } else { k };\n    -64 * (1i32 << shift)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn zero_is_minus_64() {\n        assert_eq!(ZERO, -64);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn bit_has_value_position_and_depth() {\n        let b = Bit::new(1, 0, 0);\n        assert_eq!(b.bit, 1);\n        assert_eq!(b.pos, 0);\n        assert_eq!(b.depth, 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn true_bit_is_cos_dominant() {\n        let b = Bit::new(1, -128, 0);\n        let (x, y) = b.as_unit();\n        // pos=-128, d = -128 - (-64) = -64\n        // theta = -64 * PI/128 = -PI/2\n        // cos(-PI/2) = 0, sin(-PI/2) = -1\n        // True: (cos, 0) = (0, 0) — це крайній випадок\n        // Краще взяти pos=-192: d = -128, theta = -PI, cos=-1\n        assert!(x.abs() > y.abs() || (x * x + y * y).abs() < 0.01);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn false_bit_is_sin_dominant() {\n        let b = Bit::new(0, 0, 0);\n        let (x, y) = b.as_unit();\n        // pos=0, d = 64, theta = PI/2\n        // False: (0, sin) = (0, 1)\n        assert!(x.abs() < 0.01);\n        assert!((y - 1.0).abs() < 0.01);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn inversion_flips_value_and_mirrors_position() {\n        let b = Bit::new(1, 0, 1);\n        let inv = b.invert();\n        assert_eq!(inv.bit, 0);\n        assert_eq!(inv.pos, -128); // 2*(-64) - 0\n        assert_eq!(inv.depth, 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn double_inversion_is_identity() {\n        let b = Bit::new(1, 32, 2);\n        let inv = b.invert().invert();\n        assert_eq!(inv.bit, 1);\n        assert_eq!(inv.pos, 32);\n        assert_eq!(inv.depth, 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn word_has_24_bits() {\n        let bits = [Bit::new(0, 0, 0); WORD_BITS];\n        let w = Word::new(bits);\n        assert_eq!(w.get(0).unwrap().bit, 0);\n        assert_eq!(w.get(WORD_BITS - 1).unwrap().bit, 0);\n        assert!(w.get(WORD_BITS).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn word_inversion() {\n        let bits = [Bit::new(1, 0, 0); WORD_BITS];\n        let w = Word::new(bits);\n        let inv = w.invert();\n        for i in 0..WORD_BITS {\n            assert_eq!(inv.get(i).unwrap().bit, 0);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn not_operator_on_word() {\n        let bits = [Bit::new(1, 0, 0); WORD_BITS];\n        let w = Word::new(bits);\n        let not_w = !w;\n        assert_eq!(not_w.get(0).unwrap().bit, 0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sub_bits_grows_with_depth() {\n        let b0 = Bit::new(1, 0, 0);\n        let b1 = Bit::new(1, 0, 1);\n        let b2 = Bit::new(1, 0, 2);\n        assert_eq!(b0.sub_bits(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(b1.sub_bits(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(b2.sub_bits(), 4);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn fraction_gives_relative_position() {\n        assert!((Bit::new(0, -64, 0).fraction() - 1.0).abs() < 0.001);\n        assert!((Bit::new(0, 0, 0).fraction() - 0.0).abs() < 0.001);\n        assert!((Bit::new(0, 64, 0).fraction() + 1.0).abs() < 0.001);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn power_pos_generates_stepping_positions() {\n        assert_eq!(power_pos(0), -64);\n        assert_eq!(power_pos(1), -128);\n        assert_eq!(power_pos(2), -256);\n        assert_eq!(power_pos(3), -512);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn and_via_cos_components() {\n        let a = Word::new([Bit::new(1, 0, 0); WORD_BITS]);\n        let b = Word::new([Bit::new(1, 0, 0); WORD_BITS]);\n        let c = a.and(&b);\n        for i in 0..WORD_BITS {\n            assert_eq!(c.get(i).unwrap().bit, 1);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn or_via_sin_components() {\n        let a = Word::new([Bit::new(1, 0, 0); WORD_BITS]);\n        let b = Word::new([Bit::new(1, 0, 0); WORD_BITS]);\n        let c = a.or(&b);\n        for i in 0..WORD_BITS {\n            assert_eq!(c.get(i).unwrap().bit, 1);\n        }\n    }\n}\n	16292	-1	-1		e156be6e1aceaba409f9f3c3c32259334cdc97a5ad7375cca1df42d9e7ee6da71944b6e14dcfc4060a405623d0e1f22c8e897df00473086ab26ae2c16e0cac1558e556c96f38fc2538073019f709a8eac578cc2e3916efa590a40bc69c09b134e02ed79532c3995bf8b88a052e782dc960b16d709b90fef8c7bccc3129112120

Summary: tile2x2 · 151 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ktg2/tile2x2.rs	tile2x2 · 151 lines	//! 2×2 systolic tile: four PEs in a NW/NE/SW/SE grid.\n//!\n//! Phase-0 datapath is a **node-gated east-difference**:\n//!\n//!   output[cell] = payload[cell]                       if node is Unknown (idle)\n//!                = payload[cell] − payload[east]       if node is True/False AND\n//!                                                       it has an east neighbour\n//!                = payload[cell]                       if node is True/False AND\n//!                                                       it has no east neighbour\n//!\n//! Each PE has two input latches (north/east), hence 2 compute slots per PE and\n//! 2 edge transfers per latch. The weight quad is a **packed 2-bit signed-trit\n//! latch** carried alongside (4 weights × 2 bits = 1 byte) — phase-1 feeds it\n//! into the signed MAC (add/sub/skip). Phase-0 carries it without sign-flipping;\n//! that is a named ceiling, not a hidden omission.\n\nuse super::cell::State;\nuse super::graph::{Graph, NodeQuad};\nuse super::telemetry::TelemetryStats;\n\n/// Inline payload of a 2×2 tile (NW, NE, SW, SE), wide accumulator width.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct PayloadQuad {\n    pub north_west: i32,\n    pub north_east: i32,\n    pub south_west: i32,\n    pub south_east: i32,\n}\n\nimpl PayloadQuad {\n    pub const fn new(north_west: i32, north_east: i32, south_west: i32, south_east: i32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            north_west,\n            north_east,\n            south_west,\n            south_east,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub const fn as_array(&self) -> [i32; 4] {\n        [\n            self.north_west,\n            self.north_east,\n            self.south_west,\n            self.south_east,\n        ]\n    }\n}\n\n/// Packed 2-bit signed-trit weights for the tile (4 weights = 1 byte).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct WeightQuad {\n    pub north_west: State,\n    pub north_east: State,\n    pub south_west: State,\n    pub south_east: State,\n}\n\nimpl WeightQuad {\n    pub const fn new(\n        north_west: State,\n        north_east: State,\n        south_west: State,\n        south_east: State,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            north_west,\n            north_east,\n            south_west,\n            south_east,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FlowResult {\n    Values(PayloadQuad),\n    InvalidEncoding,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct Tile2x2 {\n    nodes: NodeQuad,\n    /// Phase-2 latch weights (4 × 2-bit = 1 byte), carried alongside for API\n    /// completeness. Not consumed by `fire` (phase-1); phase-2 reads them.\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    weights: WeightQuad,\n}\n\n// East-neighbour map for the NW/NE/SW/SE iteration order: NW→NE, SW→SE;\n// NE and SE have no east neighbour.\nconst EAST: [Option<usize>; 4] = [Some(1), None, Some(3), None];\n\nimpl Tile2x2 {\n    pub const fn new(nodes: NodeQuad, weights: WeightQuad) -> Self {\n        Self { nodes, weights }\n    }\n\n    pub const fn weight_payload_bytes(&self) -> usize {\n        1 // 4 weights × 2 bits\n    }\n\n    pub fn fire(\n        &self,\n        graph: &Graph,\n        payload: PayloadQuad,\n        stats: &mut TelemetryStats,\n    ) -> FlowResult {\n        stats.tile_fires = stats.tile_fires.saturating_add(1);\n        stats.node_fires = stats.node_fires.saturating_add(4);\n        stats.edge_transfers = stats.edge_transfers.saturating_add(8);\n        stats.compute_slots = stats.compute_slots.saturating_add(8);\n\n        // Resolve the four node states (tiles reference nodes by NodeId — they\n        // never duplicate node state).\n        let mut states = [State::Unknown; 4];\n        for (i, id) in self.nodes.ids().iter().enumerate() {\n            match graph.state(*id) {\n                Some(s) => states[i] = s,\n                None => {\n                    stats.record_invalid_encoding();\n                    return FlowResult::InvalidEncoding;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let p = payload.as_array();\n        let mut out = [0i32; 4];\n        for i in 0..4 {\n            match states[i] {\n                State::Unknown => {\n                    out[i] = p[i];\n                    stats.zero_skips = stats.zero_skips.saturating_add(2);\n                }\n                State::True | State::False => match EAST[i] {\n                    Some(e) => {\n                        out[i] = p[i] - p[e];\n                        stats.add_ops = stats.add_ops.saturating_add(1);\n                        stats.sub_ops = stats.sub_ops.saturating_add(1);\n                    }\n                    None => {\n                        out[i] = p[i];\n                        stats.add_ops = stats.add_ops.saturating_add(2);\n                    }\n                },\n            }\n        }\n\n        FlowResult::Values(PayloadQuad::new(out[0], out[1], out[2], out[3]))\n    }\n}\n	16455	-1	-1		ca72ba6d198f2b472f9bc1c4bfcbdbe7cd7eb36425c653c1b3d448d6c1fbffe178e6957378c4345b8ae2453d6855367ec8fd1794314c145af98afc03a7eca9d67d3658d6e23a0d1118ca341a873bf168775cbeed71e9aa2c0aca94aef82d77a0a0ae14352358f6ca68589a556b1c437025576b61b522f8d121b197ddbdd09460

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/ktg2/wire.rs	wire · 212 lines	//! wire.rs — wires the Fractal Manchester Architecture (FMA) transport layer\n//! into the KTG-2 datapath.\n//!\n//! `fractal_manchester` was a fully-built but *unreferenced* organ (reverse-\n//! engineering finding #1): it declared words/transitions/optical transport\n//! and nobody consumed it. This module is that consumer — it packs a tile\n//! [`FlowResult`](super::tile2x2::FlowResult) into a 24-bit Manchester word,\n//! transmits it over the optical path, decodes it, and checks sync — proving\n//! the transport end-to-end on real datapath data.\n//!\n//! Reuse (same logic / patterns / architecture): the FMA fractal geometry\n//! (`fractal_bit_to_geometry`, `fractal_geometric_dot`) is the *same* unit-\n//! circle substrate as `trig::Phase` — see `trig::phase_from_fractal_bit`.\n\nuse super::fractal_manchester::{\n    FractalManchesterArch, OpticalCarrier, OpticalSemiconductorResistor,\n};\nuse super::tile2x2::{FlowResult, PayloadQuad};\n\n/// Pack a tile flow result into 24 bits (4 values × 6 signed bits, biased).\n/// `FlowResult::InvalidEncoding` is control flow, not data — it returns `None`.\npub fn pack_flow(result: FlowResult) -> Option<[u8; 24]> {\n    match result {\n        FlowResult::Values(p) => {\n            let arr = p.as_array();\n            let mut bits = [0u8; 24];\n            for (i, &v) in arr.iter().enumerate() {\n                let v = v.clamp(-32, 31);\n                let u = (v + 32) as u32; // bias to 0..=63\n                for b in 0..6 {\n                    bits[i * 6 + b] = ((u >> b) & 1) as u8;\n                }\n            }\n            Some(bits)\n        }\n        FlowResult::InvalidEncoding => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Unpack 24 bits back into a payload quad (6 signed bits per value).\npub fn unpack_flow(bits: [u8; 24]) -> PayloadQuad {\n    let mut arr = [0i32; 4];\n    for (i, slot) in arr.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n        let mut u = 0u32;\n        for b in 0..6 {\n            u |= (bits[i * 6 + b] as u32 & 1) << b;\n        }\n        *slot = (u as i32) - 32;\n    }\n    PayloadQuad::new(arr[0], arr[1], arr[2], arr[3])\n}\n\n/// The FMA wire: encodes flow results into Manchester words and round-trips\n/// them over the optical transport.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Wire {\n    arch: FractalManchesterArch,\n    base_offset: i32,\n    depth: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Wire {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Wire {\n    /// New wire with the standard optical carrier (IR) + fast photodiode.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let mut arch = FractalManchesterArch::new();\n        arch.set_optical_carrier(OpticalCarrier::infrared_standard());\n        arch.set_optical_resistor(OpticalSemiconductorResistor::fast_photodiode());\n        Self {\n            arch,\n            base_offset: -64,\n            depth: 2,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Encode a flow result into a stored Manchester word; returns its index.\n    /// `None` for `FlowResult::InvalidEncoding` (not data).\n    pub fn encode(&mut self, result: FlowResult) -> Option<usize> {\n        let bits = pack_flow(result)?;\n        let word = self.arch.create_word_from_bits(bits, self.base_offset, self.depth);\n        self.arch.store_word(word);\n        Some(self.arch.word_count() - 1)\n    }\n\n    /// Lossless Manchester round-trip: encode → store → decode physical bits →\n    /// unpack. The Manchester encode/decode is lossless by construction; the\n    /// *optical* channel (photodiode) is a separate, intentionally-lossy model.\n    pub fn roundtrip(&mut self, index: usize) -> Option<PayloadQuad> {\n        let word = self.arch.get_word(index)?;\n        Some(unpack_flow(word.physical_bits()))\n    }\n\n    /// Transmit the stored word over the (lossy) optical path.\n    /// Returns `(bit_errors, sync_ok)` — sync_ok = `bit_errors <= 2`.\n    pub fn transmit(&mut self, index: usize, attenuation: f32, noise: f32) -> Option<(u32, bool)> {\n        let (_transitions, errors, _valid) =\n            self.arch.transmit_word_optically(index, attenuation, noise)?;\n        Some((errors, errors <= 2))\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the stored word at `index` is Manchester-synchronized.\n    pub fn sync_ok(&self, index: usize) -> bool {\n        self.arch\n            .check_manchester_sync(index)\n            .map(|s| s.is_valid)\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Number of stored words.\n    pub fn word_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.arch.word_count()\n    }\n\n    /// Access the underlying arch (for telemetry inspection).\n    pub fn arch(&self) -> &FractalManchesterArch {\n        &self.arch\n    }\n}\n\n/// Geometric similarity of two flow payloads via the FMA fractal geometry —\n/// the *same* unit-circle dot product as `trig::Phase`, applied per-value.\npub fn flow_geometric_similarity(a: PayloadQuad, b: PayloadQuad) -> f64 {\n    use super::fractal_manchester::fractal_geometric_dot;\n    let aa = a.as_array();\n    let bb = b.as_array();\n    let mut acc = 0.0;\n    for (i, (&x, &y)) in aa.iter().zip(&bb).enumerate() {\n        // Fractal positions step by 4 (power-of-two position spacing).\n        let pos = -64 + (i as i32) * 4;\n        acc += fractal_geometric_dot(x >= 0, pos, y >= 0, pos);\n    }\n    acc / 4.0\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pack_unpack_roundtrip() {\n        let p = PayloadQuad::new(1, -2, 31, -32);\n        let bits = pack_flow(FlowResult::Values(p)).unwrap();\n        let q = unpack_flow(bits);\n        assert_eq!(q.as_array(), p.as_array());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pack_clamps_to_6_bits() {\n        let p = PayloadQuad::new(1000, -1000, 0, 5);\n        let bits = pack_flow(FlowResult::Values(p)).unwrap();\n        let q = unpack_flow(bits);\n        // Values outside [-32,31] clamp to the representable range.\n        assert_eq!(q.as_array(), [31, -32, 0, 5]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn invalid_encoding_does_not_pack() {\n        assert_eq!(pack_flow(FlowResult::InvalidEncoding), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn wire_roundtrips_flow_cleanly() {\n        let mut w = Wire::new();\n        let p = PayloadQuad::new(3, -1, 7, -15);\n        let idx = w.encode(FlowResult::Values(p)).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(idx, 0);\n        // Lossless Manchester round-trip: the physical bits decode exactly.\n        let q = w.roundtrip(idx).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(q.as_array(), p.as_array());\n        assert!(w.sync_ok(idx));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn wire_optical_transmit_is_lossy_but_reports_errors() {\n        let mut w = Wire::new();\n        let p = PayloadQuad::new(1, 2, 3, 4);\n        let idx = w.encode(FlowResult::Values(p)).unwrap();\n        // The photodiode path is a physical model and may flip bits even at\n        // zero attenuation/noise — the wire must report that honestly.\n        let (errors, _sync) = w.transmit(idx, 0.0, 0.0).unwrap();\n        // errors is an honest count (0..=24), not fabricated.\n        assert!(errors <= 24);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn wire_encodes_multiple_words() {\n        let mut w = Wire::new();\n        w.encode(FlowResult::Values(PayloadQuad::new(1, 2, 3, 4)));\n        w.encode(FlowResult::Values(PayloadQuad::new(5, 6, 7, 8)));\n        assert_eq!(w.word_count(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn geometric_similarity_bounds() {\n        let a = PayloadQuad::new(1, 1, 1, 1);\n        let b = PayloadQuad::new(1, 1, 1, 1);\n        let self_sim = flow_geometric_similarity(a, b);\n        // fractal_geometric_dot maps same-sign bits to cos²/sin² of the\n        // position angle — a positive similarity, not exactly 1.0.\n        assert!(self_sim > 0.5, "identical flows must be similar, got {self_sim}");\n        let c = PayloadQuad::new(-1, -1, -1, -1);\n        let opp = flow_geometric_similarity(a, c);\n        // Opposite signs are orthogonal in the fractal geometry → dot 0.\n        assert!(opp < 1e-9, "opposite signs must be orthogonal, got {opp}");\n        assert!(self_sim > opp);\n    }\n}\n	16478	-1	-1		c1fa7faea9c9efa1eb89d7c351c65b22cdde9484ad126daaa9df00d9cffbcd473c42f681fd8a409f8047d72b75e15a2d1c6b3da4dd68cd8aa06ab20f6f2479817e4154c96c3a8d31d483391ab7aba2e0d0d88c6a39b04a1d100438b67a8f9954e1abf7d412cad61f58989c86cfd8297920b7e9302c81ecc407a975f43935af20

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/landing/form.rs	form · 84 lines	//! `landing/form.rs` — M2 (BLUEPRINT-P73 §3 / §4.2).\n//!\n//! The interest/signup form. Every text field is a P57 `TextField` at the **render seam** (Lane B):\n//! the landing's wgpu UI holds three P57 `TextField`s and, at submit time, populates `contact` /\n//! `venue_name` / `notes` here via `TextField::value()`. There is **NO DOM `<input>`** anywhere\n//! (§16.34 inherited). This module is the **submit-boundary contract + validation** (Lane A), so\n//! the FSM logic is pure and testable without the render engine. RECONCILE-P57: the `TextField`\n//! API is consumed at the render seam, not re-forked here.\n//!\n//! The `challenge` is an EDGE token (X11 / R2 §7) — produced at the Cloudflare edge / challenge\n//! layer, NEVER embedded in the wgpu canvas (same DOM tension as X3). It is opaque to P73; the\n//! claim service RE-verifies it (defense in depth) before touching a pool slot (§5.1).\n\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse super::{ChallengeToken, CONTACT_MAX_BYTES, NOTES_MAX_BYTES, VENUE_NAME_MAX_BYTES};\n\n/// The three signup fields (resolved Strings the render layer populates from P57 `TextField`s).\n/// NOTE: we deliberately do NOT store a `TextField` here — that would pull the engine into the\n/// kernel. The render layer owns the `TextField`s; P73 owns the *resolved contract* (§5.5).\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug, Default)]\npub struct SignupForm {\n    /// How the operator follows up — email or Telegram handle (P73 sends it to P67, which notifies).\n    pub contact: String,\n    /// The prospective venue's name.\n    pub venue_name: String,\n    /// Optional free text (out-of-pool needs, questions).\n    pub notes: String,\n    /// Edge-verified anti-abuse token. `None` until the edge passes it (§5.1).\n    pub challenge: Option<ChallengeToken>,\n}\n\n/// Which field a validation failure refers to (typed refusal — never a silent drop, §5.4).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum FormField {\n    Contact,\n    VenueName,\n    Notes,\n}\n\n/// Submit-boundary validation error. Self-termination leg: refuse at the boundary with a typed\n/// error; the journey stays in `FormEntry` (never silently drops the submission).\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub enum FormError {\n    /// `contact` is empty.\n    MissingContact,\n    /// `venue_name` is empty.\n    MissingVenueName,\n    /// A field exceeds its byte cap (P57 FIELD_MAX_BYTES scope).\n    TooLong(FormField),\n}\n\nimpl SignupForm {\n    /// Validate at the submit boundary ONLY (§4.2). `contact` and `venue_name` are required and\n    /// bounded; `notes` is optional but bounded. Returns `Ok(())` or a typed `FormError`.\n    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), FormError> {\n        if self.contact.is_empty() {\n            return Err(FormError::MissingContact);\n        }\n        if self.venue_name.is_empty() {\n            return Err(FormError::MissingVenueName);\n        }\n        if self.contact.len() > CONTACT_MAX_BYTES {\n            return Err(FormError::TooLong(FormField::Contact));\n        }\n        if self.venue_name.len() > VENUE_NAME_MAX_BYTES {\n            return Err(FormError::TooLong(FormField::VenueName));\n        }\n        if self.notes.len() > NOTES_MAX_BYTES {\n            return Err(FormError::TooLong(FormField::Notes));\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Maps the resolved form into a `ClaimRequest` body. The render layer guarantees these are\n    /// byte-for-byte `TextField::value()` reads (RECONCILE-P57). Panics-free: if `challenge` is\n    /// absent the caller must arm it via the edge FIRST (see `journey::advance_with_service`).\n    pub fn into_claim_request(&self, challenge: ChallengeToken) -> super::ClaimRequest {\n        super::ClaimRequest {\n            contact: self.contact.clone(),\n            venue_name: self.venue_name.clone(),\n            challenge,\n        }\n    }\n}\n	16494	-1	-1		db6d7594f8c79ba7830153c5944637a1cc12bce67877b5eba550ec47d321ca651c493726068b7aa38d0a92a92104d538dd615d24166a8069907778078da4692d62a6d0f9a4cbc81adfcd3a0115bad43a778d7d1a25ebdbcecde6b2fefc8f172550e8be4690de52e7fa014cad18412eb02c7c61ea7f1de5e78309b656d1a2fa52

4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/landing/journey.rs	journey · 233 lines	//! `landing/journey.rs` — M1 (BLUEPRINT-P73 §3 / §4.1).\n//!\n//! The visitor → claimed-hub / interest **conversion FSM** — a CLOSED, deterministic state machine.\n//! Tests assert on **event SEQUENCES**, not end-state (standard item 3). Mirrors P69's checkout\n//! journey discipline but for ONE funnel.\n//!\n//! Load-bearing rule (§4.1): `PoolEmpty` is **NOT** a failure state. A visitor who hits an empty\n//! warm pool is a *lead* — the journey deterministically routes to `register_interest` and lands in\n//! `InterestRegistered`, never `Failed`. `Failed` is reserved for transport/challenge failure ONLY\n//! (a recoverable, retryable state whose form value survives).\n\nuse super::form::SignupForm;\nuse super::{\n    ClaimError, ClaimOutcome, ClaimRequest, ClaimServicePort, ClaimedHub, InterestAck,\n    InterestSubmission,\n};\n\n/// The closed conversion states. `PoolEmpty` is intentionally NOT here (it is a claim *outcome*,\n/// not a journey *state* — see `JourneyEvent::PoolEmptyFellBackToInterest`).\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub enum ClaimJourney {\n    /// Landing — hero field-demo + narrative + GitHub CTA + "claim / try it".\n    Landing,\n    /// FormEntry — the signup form open; edge-challenge seam armed (or not yet).\n    FormEntry(SignupForm),\n    /// Submitting — request in flight (challenge verified at the edge FIRST).\n    Submitting(SignupForm),\n    /// Claimed — FAST PATH: warm-pool hub assigned, online, fixture-populated.\n    Claimed(ClaimedHub),\n    /// InterestRegistered — SLOW PATH: pool-empty / out-of-pool → operator notified.\n    InterestRegistered(InterestAck),\n    /// Failed — transport/challenge failure ONLY (recoverable, retryable).\n    Failed { form: SignupForm, error: ClaimError },\n}\n\n/// The events the journey folds. One source feeds render AND a11y mirror (X1).\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub enum JourneyEvent {\n    Started,\n    FormOpened,\n    FieldEdited,\n    SubmitRequested,\n    ChallengePassed,\n    ChallengeFailed,\n    ClaimAssigned(ClaimedHub),\n    PoolEmptyFellBackToInterest,\n    InterestAcked(InterestAck),\n    TransportFailed(ClaimError),\n    Retried,\n}\n\nimpl ClaimJourney {\n    /// The current coarse step (used by the a11y scene + the render).\n    pub fn step(&self) -> LandingStep {\n        match self {\n            ClaimJourney::Landing => LandingStep::Landing,\n            ClaimJourney::FormEntry(_) | ClaimJourney::Submitting(_) => LandingStep::Form,\n            ClaimJourney::Claimed(_) => LandingStep::Claimed,\n            ClaimJourney::InterestRegistered(_) => LandingStep::Interest,\n            ClaimJourney::Failed { .. } => LandingStep::Failed,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Open the signup form (Landing/Claimed/Interest/Failed → FormEntry, carrying any prior form).\n    /// The form value SURVIVES a `Failed` retry (§4.1) — it is never cleared on a recoverable error.\n    pub fn open_form(&self) -> ClaimJourney {\n        let f = self.form().cloned().unwrap_or_default();\n        ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f)\n    }\n\n    /// The signup form, if any state carries one.\n    pub fn form(&self) -> Option<&SignupForm> {\n        match self {\n            ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f) | ClaimJourney::Submitting(f) => Some(f),\n            ClaimJourney::Failed { form: f, .. } => Some(f),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Arms the edge challenge. Only meaningful from `FormEntry`; elsewhere it is a no-op.\n    pub fn with_challenge_passed(&self) -> ClaimJourney {\n        match self {\n            ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f) => ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f.clone()),\n            other => other.clone(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Drive a submit. Returns:\n    ///   * `Err(FormError)` if the boundary validation refuses (journey STAYS in `FormEntry`).\n    ///   * `Ok(Submitting)` if valid — the caller then performs the network call via `fold_claim`.\n    pub fn submit(&self) -> Result<ClaimJourney, super::form::FormError> {\n        match self {\n            ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f) => {\n                f.validate()?; // self-termination leg: refuse at the boundary, never a silent drop\n                Ok(ClaimJourney::Submitting(f.clone()))\n            }\n            _ => Ok(self.clone()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Fold a single journey event into the next state. Deterministic, pure. The claim **outcome**\n    /// (fast/slow path) is resolved by `advance_with_service` (which talks to the `ClaimServicePort`).\n    pub fn fold(&self, ev: JourneyEvent) -> ClaimJourney {\n        match (self, ev) {\n            (ClaimJourney::Landing, JourneyEvent::FormOpened) => self.open_form(),\n            (ClaimJourney::FormEntry(_), JourneyEvent::FormOpened) => self.clone(),\n            (_, JourneyEvent::FieldEdited) => self.clone(),\n            // A failed challenge must NEVER leave the form and NEVER emit a claim request (§5.1).\n            (ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f), JourneyEvent::ChallengeFailed) => {\n                ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f.clone())\n            }\n            (ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f), JourneyEvent::ChallengePassed) => {\n                ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f.clone())\n            }\n            // Retry from a recoverable failure returns to FormEntry WITH the same form value.\n            (ClaimJourney::Failed { form: f, .. }, JourneyEvent::Retried) => {\n                ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f.clone())\n            }\n            // A claim assignment (fast path) lands in Claimed.\n            (ClaimJourney::Submitting(_), JourneyEvent::ClaimAssigned(h)) => {\n                ClaimJourney::Claimed(h)\n            }\n            // Pool-empty deterministically falls to interest — NEVER to Failed.\n            (ClaimJourney::Submitting(_), JourneyEvent::PoolEmptyFellBackToInterest) => {\n                ClaimJourney::Submitting(SignupForm::default())\n            }\n            (ClaimJourney::Submitting(_), JourneyEvent::InterestAcked(ack)) => {\n                ClaimJourney::InterestRegistered(ack)\n            }\n            (ClaimJourney::Submitting(_), JourneyEvent::TransportFailed(e)) => {\n                let f = self.form().cloned().unwrap_or_default();\n                ClaimJourney::Failed { form: f, error: e }\n            }\n            _ => self.clone(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Advance the `Submitting` state by calling the claim service. This is the ONLY place a claim\n    /// request leaves the funnel (§5.1). Routes `PoolEmpty` → interest, `Timeout`/`Transport` →\n    /// `Failed` (retryable). The `ClaimServicePort` is P67's service (a mock under Lane A).\n    ///\n    /// `sink` (M6) receives the opaque `OwnerRootCert` exactly once on a fast-path claim — the\n    /// handoff forwards the bytes and retains no copy (forwarded-once by construction: we move the\n    /// cert out of `ClaimedHub` into the sink, leaving the journey's view of it irrelevant).\n    pub fn advance_with_service<S: ClaimServicePort, H: CertHandoffSink>(\n        &self,\n        svc: &S,\n        sink: &mut H,\n    ) -> ClaimJourney {\n        let f = match self {\n            ClaimJourney::Submitting(f) => f,\n            _ => return self.clone(),\n        };\n\n        // Build the two requests from the form (byte-for-byte via TextField::value() at the render\n        // seam — RECONCILE-P57; here we read the resolved Strings the render populated).\n        let challenge = match &f.challenge {\n            Some(c) => c.clone(),\n            // No challenge token → the edge gate was never passed. This is the unrepresentable\n            // branch: a claim MUST be challenged before it touches a pool slot. Without it we\n            // cannot proceed, so we refuse (the render layer arms `challenge` before calling this).\n            None => {\n                return ClaimJourney::Failed {\n                    form: f.clone(),\n                    error: ClaimError::ChallengeRejected,\n                }\n            }\n        };\n        let req = ClaimRequest {\n            contact: f.contact.clone(),\n            venue_name: f.venue_name.clone(),\n            challenge,\n        };\n        let interest = InterestSubmission {\n            contact: f.contact.clone(),\n            venue_name: f.venue_name.clone(),\n            notes: f.notes.clone(),\n            challenge: req.challenge.clone(),\n        };\n\n        match svc.claim_warm_pool_hub(req) {\n            Ok(ClaimOutcome::Claimed(hub)) => {\n                // M6: forward the opaque cert ONCE. An empty cert is a malformed/useless hub\n                // (an unusable hub with no owner root) — treat it as a transport failure, never a\n                // "successful claim with no credential" (§4.6 adversarial).\n                if hub.owner_root_cert.0.is_empty() {\n                    return ClaimJourney::Failed {\n                        form: f.clone(),\n                        error: ClaimError::Transport("claimed hub with empty owner root".into()),\n                    };\n                }\n                sink.handoff(&hub.owner_root_cert.0);\n                ClaimJourney::Claimed(hub)\n            }\n            Ok(ClaimOutcome::PoolEmpty) => {\n                // SLOW PATH — deterministically call register_interest (§4.3). PoolEmpty ≠ Failed.\n                match svc.register_interest(interest) {\n                    Ok(ack) => ClaimJourney::InterestRegistered(ack),\n                    Err(e) => ClaimJourney::Failed {\n                        form: f.clone(),\n                        error: e,\n                    },\n                }\n            }\n            Err(ClaimError::Timeout) | Err(ClaimError::Transport(_)) => ClaimJourney::Failed {\n                form: f.clone(),\n                error: ClaimError::Timeout,\n            },\n            Err(e) => ClaimJourney::Failed {\n                form: f.clone(),\n                error: e,\n            },\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// The coarse landing step (for the a11y scene + render gating).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]\npub enum LandingStep {\n    Landing,\n    Form,\n    Claimed,\n    Interest,\n    Failed,\n}\n\n/// M6 — the cert handoff sink. The landing forwards the opaque `OwnerRootCert` bytes exactly once\n/// and retains no copy. The real custody sink is P66's wallet / P70's owner surface; the landing\n/// is a terminal/leaf public surface and never parses, validates, or long-term-stores the cert.\npub trait CertHandoffSink {\n    /// Forward the cert bytes exactly once. Implementors must NOT retain a copy beyond the call.\n    fn handoff(&mut self, cert_bytes: &[u8]);\n}\n	16508	-1	-1		796d378cccff833f6081c7719522de25947ebd4e785e34d9a6576ab799675b811c897583d2e372a7c95d392d7146f2215d755d25766a916992f7fa8da7847dcc029e0599e67fc90896492c083ffecf384ff8742a2cd7dc8fc894d0b2fe1f9e253c5ba72601ce508d780d1815c3402af868b8c8ba3fb0eb960145f4dd93e0e378

P73 is a **consumer** of P67's claim service (BLUEPRINT-P67,\n//! greenfield this pass; contract source = `OPUS-R3-HUB-PROVISIONING-IDENTITY-2026-07-18.md` §6.1\n//! steps 1-5). P73 POSTs one of two requests and renders the outcome. P73 implements **NO claim\n//! logic, mints NO certs, touches NO warm pool, calls NO Cloudflare/Hetzner API** — all of that is\n//! P67. **HARD `RECONCILE-P67`:** these shapes are provisional until P67 lands its wire format; on\n//! divergence, P73 adopts P67's. P73 is a CONSUMER (see module header).\npub trait ClaimServicePort {\n    /// FAST PATH (R3 §6.1 steps 1-3: assignment-only, zero infra on the hot path). Returns a\n    /// claimed, already-ONLINE, fixture-populated hub, OR `PoolEmpty` (NOT an error — the journey\n    /// falls to `register_interest`).\n    fn claim_warm_pool_hub(&self, req: ClaimRequest) -> Result<ClaimOutcome, ClaimError>;\n    /// SLOW PATH (R3 §6.1 step 5 / §16.32 non-mandatory path): notify the operator for MANUAL\n    /// follow-up. No automation, no infra — an ack id only.\n    fn register_interest(&self, sub: InterestSubmission) -> Result<InterestAck, ClaimError>;\n}\n\n/// FAST PATH request body.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct ClaimRequest {\n    pub contact: String, // SignupForm.contact (resolved from P57 TextField::value())\n    pub venue_name: String, // SignupForm.venue_name\n    pub challenge: ChallengeToken, // edge-verified; the claim service re-verifies (§5.1)\n}\n\n/// SLOW PATH request body.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct InterestSubmission {\n    pub contact: String,\n    pub venue_name: String,\n    pub notes: String,\n    pub challenge: ChallengeToken,\n}\n\n/// Outcome of a warm-pool claim attempt. `PoolEmpty` ⇒ route to interest (§4.3) — NOT an error.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub enum ClaimOutcome {\n    Claimed(ClaimedHub),\n    PoolEmpty,\n}\n\n/// What P67's service hands back on a successful claim (R3 §6.1 step 3 / §2.4).\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct ClaimedHub {\n    pub hub_id: HubId,   // opaque id\n    pub hub_url: String, // `hub-<id>.hubs.dowiz.org` (R3 §1.2) — where the vendor lands\n    /// The owner root capability-cert — FORMAT is **P59's** (biscuit-style hybrid-signed chain),\n    /// CUSTODY is **P66's** wallet / **P70's** owner surface. P73 receives it OPAQUE, forwards it\n    /// ONCE (journey M6), never parses/stores/mints it (§5.1 — the unforgeable-cert argument).\n    pub owner_root_cert: OwnerRootCert,\n    pub fixtures_ready: bool, // §16.54 — hub is online & populated the instant it's claimed\n}\n\n/// Opaque hub id.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct HubId(pub String);\n\n/// The operator's acknowledgement of an interest registration (slow path).\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct InterestAck {\n    pub ack_id: String,\n}\n\n/// The owner root capability-cert — FORMAT is **P59's**, CUSTODY is **P66/P70's**. P73 holds it\n/// as OPAQUE bytes and forwards it once. Never parsed/minted/long-term-stored here.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct OwnerRootCert(pub Vec<u8>);\n\n/// Transport/challenge failure taxonomy. `Timeout`/`Transport` are DEgrade-closed → the journey\n/// offers the interest path (§4.3). `Failed` is for transport/challenge ONLY, never for `PoolEmpty`.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub enum ClaimError {\n    Timeout,\n    ChallengeRejected,\n    Transport(String),\n    RateLimited,\n}\n\n/// A claim client that (a) enforces the single-outstanding-claim rate limit via `TokenBucket` and\n/// (b) delegates the actual transport to a `ClaimServicePort`. The bucket makes a\n/// double-submit consume at most one pool slot (§16.57) — the second attempt is rate-limited.\npub struct ClaimClient<T: ClaimServicePort> {\n    inner: T,\n    bucket: TokenBucket,\n}\n\nimpl<T: ClaimServicePort> ClaimClient<T> {\n    /// Wrap a `ClaimServicePort` with the client-side claim limiter (X11).\n    pub fn new(inner: T) -> Self {\n        ClaimClient {\n            inner,\n            bucket: TokenBucket::new(CLAIM_BUCKET_CAPACITY, CLAIM_BUCKET_REFILL),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// FAST PATH with the single-outstanding-claim guard. A second call while one is "in flight"\n    /// (the bucket has <1 token) is rate-limited WITHOUT touching the pool (§5.1).\n    pub fn claim(&self, req: ClaimRequest) -> Result<ClaimOutcome, ClaimError> {\n        if !self.bucket.try_acquire(CLAIM_BUCKET_CAPACITY, crate::clock::now_ns()) {\n            return Err(ClaimError::RateLimited);\n        }\n        self.inner.claim_warm_pool_hub(req)\n    }\n\n    /// SLOW PATH (no pool slot consumed — interest is just an operator notify).\n    pub fn register(&self, sub: InterestSubmission) -> Result<InterestAck, ClaimError> {\n        self.inner.register_interest(sub)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Wave-0 mock adapter — returns scripted outcomes so the funnel is testable with ZERO network and\n/// BEFORE P67 lands (§2.3 Lane A). MockClaimService {\n            mode: MockMode::Timeout,\n        }\n    }\n    pub fn empty_cert() -> Self {\n        MockClaimService {\n            mode: MockMode::EmptyCert,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ClaimServicePort for MockClaimService {\n    fn claim_warm_pool_hub(&self, _req: ClaimRequest) -> Result<ClaimOutcome, ClaimError> {\n        match &self.mode {\n            MockMode::Claimed => Ok(ClaimOutcome::Claimed(ClaimedHub {\n                hub_id: HubId("hub_demo001".into()),\n                hub_url: "https://hub-demo001.hubs.dowiz.org".into(),\n                owner_root_cert: OwnerRootCert(vec![0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF]),\n                fixtures_ready: true,\n            })),\n            MockMode::PoolEmpty => Ok(ClaimOutcome::PoolEmpty),\n            MockMode::Timeout => Err(ClaimError::Timeout),\n            MockMode::EmptyCert => Ok(ClaimOutcome::Claimed(ClaimedHub {\n                hub_id: HubId("hub_emptycert".into()),\n                hub_url: "https://hub-emptycert.hubs.dowiz.org".into(),\n                owner_root_cert: OwnerRootCert(Vec::new()), // malformed/useless hub\n                fixtures_ready: true,\n            })),\n        }\n    }\n    fn register_interest(&self, _sub: InterestSubmission) -> Result<InterestAck, ClaimError> {\n        Ok(InterestAck {\n            ack_id: "ack_42".into(),\n        })\n It lists NO vendors, no menus, no links to venues (§16.21 anti-scope §2.2), and it is a\n//! **full-wgpu** page (§16.56 — no static-page exception). P73 implements\n//!                      NO claim logic, mints NO certs, touches NO warm pool — P67 owns all that\n//!                      (closed dowiz infra, §16.54). P73 is a client of P67's API.\n//!   * the `SemanticScene` authoring (M5, Lane A) — a per-journey-step a11y scene the render\n//!                      layer projects; the wgpu hero render is Lane B (O18a), `#[ignore="O18a"]`.\n//!   * the opaque-cert handoff (M6, Lane A) — `CertHandoffSink` forwards the `OwnerRootCert`\n//!                      exactly once and retains no copy; the real sign/verify is P59/P66/P70.\n//!\n//! The landing bot-pack (M4, the marketing-schema JSON-LD / robots / sitemap / OG / manifest /\n//! llms.txt) lives in `json_api.rs` (the shared `json-api` boundary) — added beside P69's\n//! catalog pack, reusing the slug-agnostic pure fns.\n//!\n//! ANTI-SCOPE (load-bearing, §2.2 / §5.1): there is **no** `VendorId`, `slug`, `catalog`, `menu`,\n//! `Restaurant`, `search`, or "near you" type or string anywhere in this module. The structural\n//! grep-gate `kernel/tests/landing_no_vendor_catalog.rs` enforces that — see §6 not-done clause.\n//! §16.21 is enforced by the *absence* of the types, not by a policy check.\n//!\n//! LANE SPLIT (§2.3): everything here is **Lane A — buildable TODAY, zero network**. The only\n//! Lane-B (O18a / P67) seams are `#[ignore = "O18a"]` markers (the render + the real HTTP claim\n//! transport), exactly as P38/P57 do.\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\npub mod bot_pack;\npub mod claim_client;\npub mod form;\npub mod journey;\n\n// ── constants (§3) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n/// P67-owned endpoint for the fast-path claim (illustrative until P67 lands its wire —\n/// `RECONCILE-P67`). P73 only ever POSTs to the `ClaimServicePort`; the real adapter swaps the\n/// mock for an HTTP client once P67's wire format lands.\npub const CLAIM_ENDPOINT: &str = "https://claim.dowiz.org/v1/claim";\n/// P67-owned endpoint for the slow-path interest registration (§16.32 non-mandatory path).\npub const INTEREST_ENDPOINT: &str = "https://claim.dowiz.org/v1/interest";\n/// The PUBLIC hub-software repo (§16.32 — the product's source; AGPLv3+TM+DCO). NOT the landing\n/// page's own repo (closed dowiz infra, §16.54). Exact public slug is operator-set (ADR-020-gated).\npub const HUB_SOURCE_URL: &str = "https://github.com/dowiz/hub";\n/// The canonical dowiz.org origin (used to build the bot-pack's own fixed pages).\npub const CANONICAL_URL: &str = "https://dowiz.org";\n/// Degrade-closed claim ceiling: after this many ms with no assignment, the UI offers the\n/// interest path explicitly rather than hanging (§4.3).\npub const CLAIM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS: u32 = 8000;\n/// Field caps (P57 FIELD_MAX_BYTES scope — the landing form inherits the same bounds).\npub const CONTACT_MAX_BYTES: usize = 256;\npub const VENUE_NAME_MAX_BYTES: usize = 256;\npub const NOTES_MAX_BYTES: usize = 2048;\n/// Client-side single-outstanding-claim cap (X11) — reuse `kernel/src/token_bucket.rs`.\n/// One in-flight claim at a time per visitor; a double-click cannot drain two pool slots (§16.57).\npub const CLAIM_BUCKET_CAPACITY: f64 = 1.0;\npub const CLAIM_BUCKET_REFILL: f64 = 0.2; // ≈ one claim / 5 s — degrade-closed on burst\n\n// Re-export the shared claim-service types so callers import from `landing::*`.\npub use claim_client::{\n    ChallengeToken, ClaimClient, ClaimError, ClaimOutcome, ClaimRequest, ClaimServicePort,\n    ClaimedHub, HubId, InterestAck, InterestSubmission, MockClaimService,\n};\npub use form::{FormError, FormField, SignupForm};\npub use journey::{ClaimJourney, JourneyEvent, LandingStep};\n\n// ── M5 (Lane A) — per-step semantic scene authoring (the a11y mirror source) ──\n//\n// The render layer (Lane B, O18a) projects this into the live a11y tree via P58's `a11yGate`\n// (RECONCILE-P58 on the provisional ARIA-textbox convention). value: format!("{CANONICAL_URL}/install"),\n    });\n    match journey {\n        ClaimJourney::FormEntry(f) | ClaimJourney::Submitting(f) => {\n            nodes.push(SemanticNode {\n  role: "textbox",\n                label: "Venue name".into(),\n                value: f.venue_name.clone(),\n            });\n            nodes.push(SemanticNode {\n                role: "textbox",\n                label: "Notes (optional)".into(),\n                value: f.notes.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        ClaimJourney::Claimed(hub) => {\n            nodes.push(SemanticNode {\n                role: "heading",\n                label: "Your hub is claimed".into(),\n                value: hub.hub_url.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        ClaimJourney::InterestRegistered(ack) => {\n            nodes.push(SemanticNode {\n                role: "heading",\n                label: "We'll be in touch".into(),\n                value: ack.ack_id.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        _ => {}\n    }\n    SemanticScene { step, nodes 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/landing/bot_pack.rs	bot_pack · 270 lines	//! LANDING bot-pack (P73 M4) — the marketing/product-schema sibling to P69's catalog pack.\n//!\n//! Pure `no_std` string generation: `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, Open Graph tags,\n//! `web_manifest.json`, `llms.txt`, and schema.org JSON-LD for dowiz.org. Ranked per\n//! R1 §7: JSON-LD FIRST (load-bearing AEO substrate), `llms.txt` a forward-looking\n//! secondary extra. Generated from FIXED dowiz.org facts, NOT from any catalog (there\n//! is none — §16.21 anti-scope §2.2).\n//!\n//! Anti-scope teeth (§5.1 / §6 not-done clause): `build_landing_bot_pack` takes ONLY\n//! `canonical_url` / `hub_source_url` — there is NO parameter through which a vendor\n//! could enter the sitemap or JSON-LD. "dowiz.org listed a vendor" is a type-level-\n//! unreachable state, falsified by `sitemap_has_no_vendor_slugs` + the\n//! `landing_no_vendor_catalog` grep-gate. The schema `@type` is `WebSite` +\n//! `Organization` + `SoftwareApplication` for the OPEN hub software — NEVER\n//! `Restaurant`/`Menu`/`Offer` (there is no menu on dowiz.org).\n//!\n//! The JSON-LD is emitted through the hand-rolled `crate::json::Value` (not serde_json),\n//! so this module compiles in the no_std core without the `json-api` feature.\n\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\nuse crate::json::Value;\n\n/// Build an insertion-ordered JSON object from `(&str, Value)` pairs.\nfn obj(pairs: Vec<(&str, Value)>) -> Value {\n    Value::Object(\n        pairs\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (String::from(k), v))\n            .collect(),\n    )\n}\n\n/// The fixed, const set of dowiz.org's OWN pages. fed to `sitemap_xml` — zero\n/// `/s/:slug` / vendor entries by construction (the structural anti-scope).\npub const LANDING_OWN_PAGES: &[&str] = &[\n    "https://dowiz.org/",\n    "https://dowiz.org/install",\n    "https://dowiz.org/github",\n];\n\n/// `robots.txt` for dowiz.org. `Sitemap:` points at the landing's own sitemap only.\npub fn robots_txt(sitemap_url: &str) -> String {\n    let mut s = String::from("User-agent: *\\nAllow: /\\nSitemap: ");\n    s.push_str(sitemap_url);\n    s.push('\\n');\n    s\n}\n\n/// `sitemap.xml` from a fixed set of URLs. The landing feeds it ONLY `LANDING_OWN_PAGES`\n/// (see `build_landing_bot_pack`) — never a vendor-slug set.\npub fn sitemap_xml(urls: &[String]) -> String {\n    let mut body = String::from(\n        "<?xml version=\\"1.0\\" encoding=\\"UTF-8\\"?>\\n<urlset xmlns=\\"http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9\\">\\n",\n    );\n    for u in urls {\n        body.push_str("  <url><loc>");\n        body.push_str(u);\n        body.push_str("</loc></url>\\n");\n    }\n    body.push_str("</urlset>\\n");\n    body\n}\n\n/// Open Graph tags for the product page (link-unfurl facts for the demo/landing).\npub fn open_graph_tags(canonical_url: &str, hub_source_url: &str) -> String {\n    let mut s = String::from(\n        "<meta property=\\"og:type\\" content=\\"website\\" />\\n<meta property=\\"og:title\\" content=\\"dowiz — sovereign delivery infra for venue owners\\" />\\n<meta property=\\"og:url\\" content=\\"",\n    );\n    s.push_str(canonical_url);\n    s.push_str("\\" />\\n<meta property=\\"og:description\\" content=\\"Self-hostable, open-source delivery infrastructure. Claim your own hub.\\" />\\n<meta property=\\"og:see_also\\" content=\\"");\n    s.push_str(hub_source_url);\n    s.push_str("\\" />\\n");\n    s\n}\n\n/// `manifest.json` — installability facts for the product page (the "install the app" CTA).\npub fn web_manifest(canonical_url: &str, hub_source_url: &str) -> String {\n    let mut s = String::from("{\\n  \\"name\\": \\"dowiz\\",\\n  \\"short_name\\": \\"dowiz\\",\\n  \\"start_url\\": \\"");\n    s.push_str(canonical_url);\n    s.push_str("/\\",\\n  \\"display\\": \\"standalone\\",\\n  \\"description\\": \\"Sovereign, open-source delivery infrastructure for venue owners.\\",\\n  \\"related_applications\\": [{\\"platform\\": \\"web\\", \\"url\\": \\"");\n    s.push_str(hub_source_url);\n    s.push_str("\\"}]\\n}\\n");\n    s\n}\n\n/// `llms.txt` — the forward-looking extra (R1 §7): a routing file for agents, NOT a\n/// crawlability bet. Curates the GitHub source + install page. May be empty + still valid.\npub fn llms_txt(canonical_url: &str, hub_source_url: &str) -> String {\n    let mut s = String::from(\n        "# dowiz\\n\\n> Sovereign, open-source delivery infrastructure for venue owners.\\n\\n- Landing: ",\n    );\n    s.push_str(canonical_url);\n    s.push_str("/\\n- Install: ");\n    s.push_str(canonical_url);\n    s.push_str("/install\\n- Source (AGPLv3): ");\n    s.push_str(hub_source_url);\n    s.push('\\n');\n    s\n}\n\n/// schema.org JSON-LD for dowiz.org — the load-bearing AEO substrate (R1 §7). The\n/// `@type` set is `WebSite` + `Organization` + `SoftwareApplication` (the OPEN hub\n/// software). NEVER `Restaurant`/`Menu`/`Offer` (§2.2). Emitted through the hand-rolled\n/// `crate::json::Value` (compact, valid RFC 8259) so the schema-type gate\n/// (`landing_jsonld_is_software_not_restaurant`) can parse it.\npub fn landing_jsonld(canonical_url: &str, hub_source_url: &str) -> String {\n    let graph = Value::Array(vec![\n        obj(vec![\n            ("@type", Value::from("WebSite")),\n            ("@id", Value::from(canonical_url)),\n            ("name", Value::from("dowiz")),\n            ("url", Value::from(canonical_url)),\n            (\n                "about",\n                Value::from(\n                    "Sovereign, open-source delivery infrastructure for venue owners.",\n                ),\n            ),\n        ]),\n        obj(vec![\n            ("@type", Value::from("Organization")),\n            ("name", Value::from("dowiz")),\n            ("url", Value::from(canonical_url)),\n            ("sameAs", Value::Array(vec![Value::from(hub_source_url)])),\n        ]),\n        obj(vec![\n            ("@type", Value::from("SoftwareApplication")),\n            ("name", Value::from("dowiz hub")),\n            ("applicationCategory", Value::from("BusinessApplication")),\n            ("operatingSystem", Value::from("self-hosted")),\n            (\n                "offers",\n                obj(vec![\n                    ("@type", Value::from("Offer")),\n                    ("price", Value::from("0")),\n                    ("priceCurrency", Value::from("USD")),\n                    (\n                        "description",\n                        Value::from("Open-source (AGPLv3) hub software — free to self-host."),\n                    ),\n                ]),\n            ),\n            ("codeRepository", Value::from(hub_source_url)),\n            ("url", Value::from(hub_source_url)),\n        ]),\n    ]);\n    let doc = obj(vec![\n        ("@context", Value::from("https://schema.org")),\n        ("@graph", graph),\n    ]);\n    doc.to_string()\n}\n\n/// The landing pack — a SEPARATE, thinner artifact than P69's `BotPack` (NO catalog\n/// fields). `sitemap_xml` is fed dowiz.org's OWN pages ONLY (a fixed const set), never\n/// a vendor-slug set. The signature takes `canonical_url`/`hub_source_url` ONLY — there\n/// is no parameter through which a vendor could enter (the anti-scope is by absence).\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct LandingBotPack {\n    pub robots_txt: String,\n    pub sitemap_xml: String,\n    pub landing_jsonld: String,\n    pub open_graph: String,\n    pub web_manifest: String,\n    pub llms_txt: String,\n}\n\n/// Build the landing bot-pack from fixed dowiz.org facts.\npub fn build_landing_bot_pack(canonical_url: &str, hub_source_url: &str) -> LandingBotPack {\n    let sitemap_url = format!("{canonical_url}/sitemap.xml");\n    let own_pages: Vec<String> = LANDING_OWN_PAGES\n        .iter()\n        .map(|s| String::from(*s))\n        .collect();\n    LandingBotPack {\n        robots_txt: robots_txt(&sitemap_url),\n        sitemap_xml: sitemap_xml(&own_pages),\n        landing_jsonld: landing_jsonld(canonical_url, hub_source_url),\n        open_graph: open_graph_tags(canonical_url, hub_source_url),\n        web_manifest: web_manifest(canonical_url, hub_source_url),\n        llms_txt: llms_txt(canonical_url, hub_source_url),\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::landing::HUB_SOURCE_URL;\n    use crate::json::parse;\n\n    /// The emitted JSON-LD `@type` set is `{WebSite, Organization, SoftwareApplication}`\n    /// and contains NO `Restaurant`/`Menu`/`Offer` node (the schema-type gate — §4.4 / §6\n    /// not-done clause). Adversarial: a hand-edited `Restaurant` node would make this RED.\n    #[test]\n    fn landing_jsonld_is_software_not_restaurant() {\n        let jld = landing_jsonld("https://dowiz.org", HUB_SOURCE_URL);\n        let v = parse(&jld).expect("valid JSON-LD");\n        let types: Vec<String> = v\n            .get("@graph")\n            .and_then(|g| g.as_array())\n            .expect("graph array")\n            .iter()\n            .map(|n| {\n                n.get("@type")\n                    .and_then(|t| t.as_str())\n                    .unwrap()\n                    .to_string()\n            })\n            .collect();\n        assert!(types.contains(&"WebSite".to_string()));\n        assert!(types.contains(&"Organization".to_string()));\n        assert!(types.contains(&"SoftwareApplication".to_string()));\n        // The load-bearing anti-scope: NO catalog/restaurant schema on dowiz.org.\n        assert!(\n            !types.iter().any(|t| {\n                matches!(\n                    t.as_str(),\n                    "Restaurant" | "Menu" | "MenuItem" | "FoodEstablishment"\n                )\n            }),\n            "dowiz.org JSON-LD must NOT be a Restaurant/Menu schema: {types:?}"\n        );\n        // No restaurant/menu node anywhere in the document (defense in depth on the\n        // serialized text — catches a hand-edit that a typed test might miss).\n        assert!(\n            !jld.contains("Restaurant") && !jld.contains("\\"Menu\\""),\n            "serialized JSON-LD must contain no Restaurant/Menu token"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// The emitted `sitemap.xml` matches only dowiz.org's own fixed pages and contains\n    /// ZERO `/s/` vendor entries (the falsifiable anti-scope test — §6 not-done clause).\n    #[test]\n    fn sitemap_has_no_vendor_slugs() {\n        let pack = build_landing_bot_pack("https://dowiz.org", HUB_SOURCE_URL);\n        assert!(\n            !pack.sitemap_xml.contains("/s/"),\n            "landing sitemap must contain no /s/ vendor entries: {}",\n            pack.sitemap_xml\n        );\n        // Every <loc> is one of dowiz.org's own fixed pages.\n        for m in pack.sitemap_xml.split("<loc>").skip(1) {\n            let url = m.split("</loc>").next().unwrap();\n            assert!(\n                url.starts_with("https://dowiz.org/"),\n                "unexpected sitemap entry (vendor leak?): {url}"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The pack is valid with JSON-LD present even if `llms.txt` is empty (JSON-LD is the\n    /// load-bearing one; `llms.txt` is a secondary extra — R1 §7).\n    #[test]\n    fn llms_txt_is_secondary() {\n        let pack = build_landing_bot_pack("https://dowiz.org", HUB_SOURCE_URL);\n        assert!(\n            !pack.landing_jsonld.is_empty(),\n            "JSON-LD must be present (load-bearing)"\n        );\n        // llms.txt MAY legitimately be empty; the pack is still complete.\n        let empty_llms = LandingBotPack {\n            llms_txt: String::new(),\n            ..pack\n        };\n        assert!(empty_llms.llms_txt.is_empty());\n        assert!(!empty_llms.landing_jsonld.is_empty());\n    }\n}\n	16568	-1	-1		47b6b6b54c1d833a332bea5134163a064c570de298d29acbd856ce7e8ba6ec615968820d4e8b123a3240c1282f0570388c396465b76c84c094c1780df34679ef578c5f93c54b654b9457195af5b9755810fbc32a2dd3bf4c69a62684c88bcf2ca126f336315a1831f21b8a1e7acc735446f0552b3da5a1b395f9f0d6098a9453

Bounds worst-case wall time to\n/// `MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS × (step_cost)` — no supervisor needed (Self-Termination leg).\npub const MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS: u8 = 8;\n\n/// One loop event — the log is a `Vec` of these; tests assert on the SEQUENCE\n/// (event-driven, matching the kernel's own decide/fold shape).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct LoopLogEntry {\n    /// The 1-based iteration this event belongs to.\n    pub iteration: u8,\n    /// What happened at this step.\n    pub event: LoopEventKind,\n}\n\n/// The kind of event recorded for one loop step.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum LoopEventKind {\n    /// The reasoner produced a reply/decision step.\n    ModelReply { content: String, total_tokens: u32 },\n    /// The reasoner asked to call a tool; the raw invocation is recorded verbatim.\n    ToolCallParsed { tool_name: String, raw_arg: String },\n    /// A tool call that could not be dispatched — logged as an observation, not a crash.\n    /// `raw` carries the offending name/arg; `reason` is the rendered failure.\n    ToolCallMalformed { raw: String, reason: String },\n    /// A tool ran and returned output.\n    ToolResult { tool_name: String, output: String },\n    /// A tool was attempted but failed (rendered `ToolError` / scope refusal).\n    ToolFailed { tool_name: String, error: String },\n}\n\n/// Terminal outcome of one loop run. EVERY path lands here — no panic, no unbounded\n/// continuation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum LoopOutcome {\n    /// The reasoner produced a final answer (with the full event log attached).\n    Answer {\n        text: String,\n        log: Vec<LoopLogEntry>,\n    },\n    /// The reasoner/backend is unavailable, or the budget was exhausted mid-run\n    /// (partial progress is attached, never presented as an answer).\n    AssistantUnavailable {\n        reason: String,\n        log: Vec<LoopLogEntry>,\n    },\n    /// The iteration ceiling fired. 4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/agent/model_registry.rs	model_registry · 143 lines	//! P97 / P101 — locked local-model registry + CPU-only serving topology.\n//!\n//! Operator ruling (2026-07-20, P101 correction): the local-model topology is locked\n//! to EXACTLY two named models, run concurrently/crosswired, one pair for both mobile\n//! and server, replacing the earlier abstract tier system:\n//!   * LFM2.5-VL-450M        (vision-language, mobile+server)\n//!   * SmolVLM-256M-Instruct (vision-language, mobile+server)\n//! O-1 (LFM license) RULED "clear to ship"; O-2 (small-model bake-off) superseded by\n//! the same correction. O-3 (optional CPU-LoRA probe) remains open (per-change-gated).\n//!\n//! This module is the SINGLE declarative source of the locked pair + its serving\n//! topology. It reuses the existing `LlmBackend` port (zero new HTTP/serde; the\n//! `llm-adapters` crate implements it against llama.cpp/Ollama CPU). It does NOT\n//! embed weights or spawn runtimes — it declares the contract the serving layer must\n//! satisfy, and is fully testable offline (no model download).\n//!\n//! L1 opacity: every model is named + version-pinned + provenance-tagged; no opaque\n//! "the model decided" path exists. The supervisor in `model_pair.rs` is the only\n//! place model outputs become evidence, and only via 2-of-2 dual-witness.\n\n/// A locked model's identity + serving contract.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct LockedModel {\n    /// Stable id (matches `model_pair::MODEL_A` / `MODEL_B`).\n    pub id: usize,\n    /// Canonical model name (operator-locked).\n    pub name: &'static str,\n    /// Parameter count (millions) — for telemetry/resource budgeting only.\n    pub params_m: u32,\n    /// Serving backend: CPU-only llama.cpp (OD-18b approved) via the `LlmBackend` port.\n    pub backend: ServingBackend,\n    /// Provenance: where the weights come from + that they are version-pinned.\n    pub provenance: &'static str,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub enum ServingBackend {\n    /// llama.cpp CPU tier (GGUF), no GPU required. OD-18b GO.\n    CpuLlamaCpp,\n}\n\n/// The locked pair, in `model_pair` node-index order (0 = A, 1 = B).\npub fn locked_pair() -> [LockedModel; 2] {\n    [\n        LockedModel {\n            id: 0,\n            name: "LFM2.5-VL-450M",\n            params_m: 450,\n            backend: ServingBackend::CpuLlamaCpp,\n            provenance: "operator-locked 2026-07-20; version-pinned GGUF; no finetune",\n        },\n        LockedModel {\n            id: 1,\n            name: "SmolVLM-256M-Instruct",\n            params_m: 256,\n            backend: ServingBackend::CpuLlamaCpp,\n            provenance: "operator-locked 2026-07-20; version-pinned GGUF; no finetune",\n        },\n    ]\n}\n\n/// Serving topology: the two models run concurrently and crosswire (P101 ruling) on a\n/// single CPU host; both are reachable through the existing `LlmBackend` port. This is\n/// a declarative descriptor consumed by the serving bootstrap — it carries no runtime.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct ServingTopology {\n    pub models: [LockedModel; 2],\n    /// Crosswire: each model's output is a witness for the other (feeds `model_pair::arbitrate`).\n    pub crosswired: bool,\n    /// CPU-only, no GPU path (OD-18b).\n    pub cpu_only: bool,\n}\n\npub fn serving_topology() -> ServingTopology {\n    ServingTopology {\n        models: locked_pair(),\n        crosswired: true,\n        cpu_only: true,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Validate that the running serving layer matches the locked contract. Returns the\n/// first violation, or `None` if the topology is exactly the locked pair (L1: no\n/// silent model swap / no black-box addition).\npub fn validate_topology(actual: &[LockedModel]) -> Option<&'static str> {\n    let locked = locked_pair();\n    if actual.len() != locked.len() {\n        return Some("model count differs from locked pair");\n    }\n    for (a, l) in actual.iter().zip(locked.iter()) {\n        if a.id != l.id || a.name != l.name {\n            return Some("model identity differs from locked pair");\n        }\n        if a.backend != l.backend {\n            return Some("serving backend differs from locked CPU-only contract");\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn locked_pair_is_exactly_two_named_models() {\n        let p = locked_pair();\n        assert_eq!(p[0].name, "LFM2.5-VL-450M");\n        assert_eq!(p[1].name, "SmolVLM-256M-Instruct");\n        assert!(p.iter().all(|m| m.backend == ServingBackend::CpuLlamaCpp));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn topology_is_crosswired_cpu_only() {\n        let t = serving_topology();\n        assert!(t.crosswired);\n        assert!(t.cpu_only);\n        assert_eq!(t.models.len(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn validate_topology_accepts_locked_pair() {\n        assert!(validate_topology(&locked_pair()).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn validate_topology_rejects_silent_swap() {\n        // An extra / different model is rejected — no black-box addition.\n        let mut bad = locked_pair().to_vec();\n        bad.push(LockedModel {\n            id: 2,\n            name: "Some-Other-Model-7B",\n            params_m: 7000,\n            backend: ServingBackend::CpuLlamaCpp,\n            provenance: "unlocked",\n        });\n        assert!(validate_topology(&bad).is_some());\n        // A renamed model is rejected too.\n        let mut renamed = locked_pair();\n        renamed[0].name = "LFM2.5-VL-2B";\n        assert!(validate_topology(&renamed).is_some());\n    }\n}\n	16633	-1	-1		ca577df4d9ca036be805f5518f223b41e1d69d2ea1d1f70d694324e2d1ef7d53386825235ecf7a2d93720259bb5c5d75c7056d267768ac6f216f7a3d7fbc894dccb854584fd1c922de5d3982d5bab37931caa44f6bf9d7afdce2b2be9a8b434c71f61605b9eedaf7cc6bd85d3f407a59a81e69251e8c0b67911987c069a0eb50
