```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/agent/model_pair.rs	model_pair · 374 lines	//! P103 — Hydra × locked model-pair supervisor integration.\n//!\n//! Design (operator-ruled 2026-07-20, grounded in the real 1567-line `hydra.rs`):\n//! the two named local models (LFM2.5-VL-450M + SmolVLM-256M-Instruct, locked by the\n//! P101 operator correction to exactly this pair) integrate ENTIRELY through Hydra's\n//! *existing public surface* — they become `TopoEdge` nodes in a 2-node topology that\n//! passes through Hydra's existing drift gate (`candidate_drift`). **Zero edits to\n//! `hydra.rs` itself**: this module only calls the public API it already exposes.\n//!\n//! Safety shape (L1 opacity-enforcement — no black boxes, always):\n//!   * DUAL-WITNESS — a positive claim needs 2-of-2 agreement; disagreement collapses\n//!     to `Unknown` rather than a guess. A single hallucinating model cannot mint\n//!     permanent evidence.\n//!   * DRIFT-GATED — the pair's coupling mutation is scored by `candidate_drift`\n//!     against Hydra's live spectral baseline; a divergent (Unstable, ρ>1) coupling is\n//!     rejected fail-closed, exactly like any other topology mutation.\n//!   * SUPERVISOR MEMBRANE — a hard schema/vocabulary/provenance check sits between the\n//!     models and Hydra; only membrane-passing, drift-clear claims reach `candidate_drift`.\n//!   * OSCILLATOR — the supervisor's heartbeat clock reuses Hydra's own `INTEGRITY_BAND`\n//!     hysteresis (damped/resonant/unstable regimes with hysteresis), so no second\n//!     oscillator is invented.\n//!   * OSMOSIS — the gradient flow across the pair is `personalized_pagerank` over the\n//!     2-node adjacency (reuses tested kernel math, no new mechanism).\n//!\n//! Hydra's charter (closure = never, kill-switch only, all-safeties-lift-on-intervention)\n//! is untouched: `Hydra` is constructed and driven by the caller exactly as before; this\n//! module never calls `Hydra::commit` on its own and holds no `&mut Hydra`. Structurally\n//! enforced: `hydra.rs` code paths carry no call into this module, so a dead supervisor\n//! only starves the model channel, never Hydra itself.\n\nuse alloc::string::{String, ToString};\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse crate::csr::Csr;\nuse crate::hydra::{candidate_drift, TopoEdge, INTEGRITY_BAND};\nuse crate::spectral::DriftClass;\n\n/// The two locked models. Index 0 = LFM2.5-VL-450M, index 1 = SmolVLM-256M-Instruct.\n/// The topology is a 2-node bidirectional graph (each witnesses the other).\npub const MODEL_A: usize = 0;\npub const MODEL_B: usize = 1;\npub const PAIR_NODES: usize = 2;\n\n/// A model's output for a given prompt, with provenance. `value` is the model's\n/// structured claim; `confidence` is its self-reported 0..=1 score (used only for\n/// osmosis ranking, never as evidence on its own).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct ModelOutput {\n    pub model: usize,\n    pub value: ClaimValue,\n    pub confidence: f64,\n    /// Provenance: which model + a monotonic utterance id (for replay/audit).\n    pub utterance_id: u64,\n}\n\n/// The structured claim a model emits. Kept deliberately small + schema-checked\n/// (L1: no opaque blob crosses the membrane).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum ClaimValue {\n    /// A resolved, schema-valid assertion.\n    Assertion(String),\n    /// The model explicitly abstains (no claim).\n    Abstain,\n}\n\n/// The resolved outcome of dual-witness arbitration.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum Verdict {\n    /// Both models agreed on the same assertion → resolved evidence.\n    Resolved(String),\n    /// Models disagreed (or any abstained/garbled) → collapsed to Unknown, never a guess.\n    Unknown,\n}\n\n/// Hard membrane check: a single model output is admitted to arbitration only if its\n/// vocabulary + schema + provenance are well-formed. Returns `None` for a rejected\n/// (black-box / malformed) output — it never reaches the 2-of-2.\npub fn membrane_admit(out: &ModelOutput) -> Option<&ModelOutput> {\n    // schema: value must be a well-formed Assertion (Abstain is allowed but carries no weight)\n    // vocab: assertions must be non-empty and bounded length (no unbounded opaque blob)\n    // provenance: confidence finite in [0,1], utterance_id > 0\n    let ok = match &out.value {\n        ClaimValue::Assertion(s) => !s.is_empty() && s.len() <= 4096,\n        ClaimValue::Abstain => true,\n    };\n    if ok\n        && out.confidence.is_finite()\n        && (0.0..=1.0).contains(&out.confidence)\n        && out.utterance_id > 0\n        && (out.model == MODEL_A || out.model == MODEL_B)\n    {\n        Some(out)\n    } else {\n        None\n    }\n}\n\n/// Dual-witness arbitration: 2-of-2 agreement resolves; any divergence → `Unknown`.\n/// This is the core L1 guarantee — a lone model cannot mint evidence.\npub fn arbitrate(a: &ModelOutput, b: &ModelOutput) -> Verdict {\n    let a = match membrane_admit(a) {\n        Some(o) => o,\n        None => return Verdict::Unknown,\n    };\n    let b = match membrane_admit(b) {\n        Some(o) => o,\n        None => return Verdict::Unknown,\n    };\n    match (&a.value, &b.value) {\n        (ClaimValue::Assertion(x), ClaimValue::Assertion(y)) if x == y => {\n            Verdict::Resolved(x.clone())\n        }\n        _ => Verdict::Unknown,\n    }\n}\n\n/// The 2-node baseline topology: bidirectional equal-weight edges (each model\n/// witnesses the other). Used as the base for `candidate_drift`.\npub fn pair_baseline() -> Vec<TopoEdge> {\n    vec![\n        TopoEdge {\n            from: MODEL_A,\n            to: MODEL_B,\n            weight: 1.0,\n        },\n        TopoEdge {\n            from: MODEL_B,\n            to: MODEL_A,\n            weight: 1.0,\n        },\n    ]\n}\n\n/// Score a *proposed coupling change* (e.g. re-weighting the pair, or adding a\n/// crosswire edge) against Hydra's live drift gate. Returns the `DriftClass` — the\n/// caller refuses any `Unstable` mutation fail-closed. This is the only path by which\n/// the model-pair touches Hydra's topology surface, and it goes through the public\n/// `candidate_drift` gate (no edit to `hydra.rs`).\npub fn score_coupling_delta(delta: &[TopoEdge]) -> DriftClass {\n    candidate_drift(PAIR_NODES, &pair_baseline(), delta)\n}\n\n/// Supervisor heartbeat: reuse Hydra's `INTEGRITY_BAND` hysteresis as the clock.\n/// Given a sequence of observed spectral radii (ρ), return the organism state the\n/// band implies. This reuses the EXACT same damped/resonant/unstable band Hydra uses,\n/// so the supervisor never invents a second oscillator.\npub fn heartbeat_state(rho: f64) -> SupervisorHeartbeat {\n    if !rho.is_finite() || rho >= INTEGRITY_BAND.trigger {\n        SupervisorHeartbeat::Locked\n    } else if rho <= INTEGRITY_BAND.release {\n        SupervisorHeartbeat::Live\n    } else {\n        SupervisorHeartbeat::Marginal\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]\npub enum SupervisorHeartbeat {\n    Live,\n    Marginal,\n    Locked,\n}\n\n/// Osmotic gradient flow across the pair: rank the two models by their diffusion\n/// rank over the 2-node adjacency, using the tested `personalized_pagerank`. The\n/// seed is the supervisor's current attention (which model it leans on). Returns the\n/// per-node rank (index 0 = MODEL_A, 1 = MODEL_B). Reuses kernel math, no new mechanism.\npub fn osmotic_rank(attention_seed: &[f64; PAIR_NODES]) -> [f64; PAIR_NODES] {\n    // Build a 2-node CSR adjacency (symmetric pair baseline) as (src,dst,weight) tuples.\n    let edges: Vec<(usize, usize, f64)> = pair_baseline()\n        .iter()\n        .map(|e| (e.from, e.to, e.weight))\n        .collect();\n    let csr = Csr::from_edges(PAIR_NODES, &edges);\n    let rank = csr.personalized_pagerank(attention_seed, 0.85, 32);\n    let mut out = [0.0f64; PAIR_NODES];\n    for (i, v) in rank.iter().take(PAIR_NODES).enumerate() {\n        out[i] = *v;\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// L1 PROVENANCE GATE — the ONLY compile-path from a port reply (`ports::llm::ChatResponse`)\n/// to an evidence-bearing `ModelOutput`. Fails closed: if the backend served an `model_id`\n/// that is NOT one of the locked pair (`validate_topology`), the reply is refused — no\n/// opaque "the model said" text can cross into the supervisor without a provenance tag that\n/// matches the operator-locked contract. This is the structural enforcement of "no black\n/// boxes, always": provenance must be present AND must match the lock, or the output is dropped.\n///\n/// `locked` is the slice from `model_registry::locked_pair()` (or `validate_topology(None)`'s\n/// source). `utterance_id` is taken from the response (already monotonic, set by the adapter).\npub fn from_port_response(\n    resp: &crate::ports::llm::ChatResponse,\n    locked: &[crate::agent::model_registry::LockedModel],\n) -> Option<ModelOutput> {\n    // 1) provenance must name one of the locked models exactly.\n    let idx = locked.iter().position(|m| m.name == resp.model_id)?;\n    // 2) the response must carry a real utterance id (replay/audit).\n    if resp.utterance_id == 0 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    // 3) the text must survive the membrane (schema/vocab/provenance) before it can become\n    //    a claim — an opaque/unbounded blob is dropped here, never reaching `arbitrate`.\n    let value = ClaimValue::Assertion(resp.content.clone());\n    let out = ModelOutput {\n        model: locked[idx].id as usize,\n        value,\n        confidence: 0.0, // not used as evidence on its own; osmosis ranking only\n        utterance_id: resp.utterance_id,\n    };\n    membrane_admit(&out).cloned()\n}\n\n/// Convenience: enforce provenance against the canonical locked pair (P97/P101).\npub fn from_port_response_locked(resp: &crate::ports::llm::ChatResponse) -> Option<ModelOutput> {\n    from_port_response(resp, &crate::agent::model_registry::locked_pair())\n}\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::agent::model_registry::LockedModel;\n    use crate::ports::llm::ChatResponse;\n\n    fn port_reply(model_id: &str, content: &str, utterance_id: u64) -> ChatResponse {\n        ChatResponse {\n            content: content.into(),\n            usage: crate::ports::llm::Usage::default(),\n            model_id: model_id.into(),\n            utterance_id,\n            tool_calls: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn l1_gate_accepts_locked_model_reply() {\n        // A reply provenance-tagged with a LOCKED model id becomes a valid ModelOutput.\n        let r = port_reply("LFM2.5-VL-450M", "door_open", 7);\n        let out = from_port_response_locked(&r).expect("locked model must pass the gate");\n        assert_eq!(out.model, MODEL_A);\n        assert_eq!(out.utterance_id, 7);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn l1_gate_refuses_unlocked_black_box() {\n        // A backend that silently serves an unlocked model is refused fail-closed —\n        // the text never crosses into the supervisor, no matter how plausible.\n        let r = port_reply("Some-Other-Model-7B", "door_open", 7);\n        assert!(from_port_response_locked(&r).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn l1_gate_refuses_zero_utterance_id() {\n        // Replay/audit provenance is mandatory; a reply without an utterance id is dropped.\n        let r = port_reply("LFM2.5-VL-450M", "door_open", 0);\n        assert!(from_port_response_locked(&r).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn l1_gate_refuses_opaque_blob() {\n        // Even a locked-model reply with an unbounded blob is dropped by the membrane.\n        let r = port_reply("LFM2.5-VL-450M", &"x".repeat(5000), 7);\n        assert!(from_port_response_locked(&r).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn l1_gate_maps_model_name_to_index() {\n        // The second locked model maps to MODEL_B, not MODEL_A.\n        let locked = [\n            LockedModel {\n                id: 0,\n                name: "LFM2.5-VL-450M",\n                params_m: 450,\n                backend: crate::agent::model_registry::ServingBackend::CpuLlamaCpp,\n                provenance: "",\n            },\n            LockedModel {\n                id: 1,\n                name: "SmolVLM-256M-Instruct",\n                params_m: 256,\n                backend: crate::agent::model_registry::ServingBackend::CpuLlamaCpp,\n                provenance: "",\n            },\n        ];\n        let r = port_reply("SmolVLM-256M-Instruct", "door_open", 3);\n        let out = from_port_response(&r, &locked).expect("second locked model passes");\n        assert_eq!(out.model, MODEL_B);\n    }\n\n    fn out(model: usize, val: ClaimValue, conf: f64, id: u64) -> ModelOutput {\n        ModelOutput {\n            model,\n            value: val,\n            confidence: conf,\n            utterance_id: id,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dual_witness_2of2_agreement_resolves() {\n        let a = out(MODEL_A, ClaimValue::Assertion("door_open".into()), 0.9, 1);\n        let b = out(MODEL_B, ClaimValue::Assertion("door_open".into()), 0.88, 2);\n        assert_eq!(arbitrate(&a, &b), Verdict::Resolved("door_open".into()));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn dual_witness_disagreement_collapses_to_unknown() {\n        let a = out(MODEL_A, 1);\n        assert!(membrane_admit(&neg).is_none());\n        let zeroid = out(MODEL_A, ClaimValue::Assertion("ok".into()), 0.9, 0);\n        assert!(membrane_admit(&zeroid).is_none());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn drift_gate_rejects_divergent_coupling() {\n        // Adding ANY extra weight to the already-fully-connected 2-cycle raises ρ>1\n        // → Unstable → refused fail-closed. This is correct gate behavior.\n        let divergent = vec![TopoEdge {\n            from: MODEL_A,\n            to: MODEL_A,\n            weight: 1e9,\n        }];\n        assert_eq!(score_coupling_delta(&divergent), DriftClass::Unstable);\n        // A benign *coupling reduction* (negative delta lowering an edge below the\n        // ρ=1 boundary) keeps the cycle bounded (Damped), not Unstable — the gate\n        // permits relaxing the lock, only refuses tightening it.\n        let lowered = vec![TopoEdge {\n            from: MODEL_A,\n            to: MODEL_B,\n            weight: -0.5,\n        }];\n        assert_ne!(score_coupling_delta(&lowered), DriftClass::Unstable);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn heartbeat_reuses_integrity_band() {\n        assert_eq!(heartbeat_state(0.5), SupervisorHeartbeat::Live);\n        assert_eq!(heartbeat_state(1.0), SupervisorHeartbeat::Locked); // ρ>=trigger\n        assert_eq!(heartbeat_state(f64::NAN), SupervisorHeartbeat::Locked);\n        // Between release and trigger → marginal (oscillator-theoretic band).\n        assert_eq!(heartbeat_state(0.999999), SupervisorHeartbeat::Marginal);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn osmotic_rank_is_symmetric_for_uniform_seed() {\n        let r = osmotic_rank(&[0.5, 0.5]);\n        // Symmetric pair + symmetric seed → equal diffusion rank.\n        assert!((r[0] - r[1]).abs() < 1e-9, "ranks should match: {:?}", r);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn osmotic_rank_leans_with_attention() {\n        let r = osmotic_rank(&[0.9, 0.1]);\n        // Leaning attention on MODEL_A pushes its diffusion rank higher.\n        assert!(r[0] > r[1], "A should rank above B: {:?}", r);\n    }\n}\n	16665	-1	-1		cf7f7ed4fdca03637905efc787201a2365f69546a950f54e6bd76a60d5ebff0738d0256176cf7225b753836bb158d979ce357f2435688c3a9867f20dff9eaa5e4efa14196563492157092b02f5bab079d278840839f1c6c9dde2b694180b1345e17a966739fad2b5dc49489f185d4f9128af44ae9eb657840bafe5d163207ae1
```

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/backup.rs	backup · 409 lines	//! backup.rs — native content-addressed backup organ (Tier B4).\n//!\n//! GROWTH-SUBSTRATE / INFRA primitive. This is the storage half of the offline-\n//! on-node backup: the `chunker` (Buzhash CDC) splits a byte stream into\n//! content-defined blocks; this organ stores each unique block once, keyed by\n//! its `sha3_256` id (content-addressed), and can reconstruct the original bytes\n//! byte-for-byte from the ordered list of block ids (a *manifest*).\n//!\n//! Verified-by-Math property (the whole point of B4):\n//!   1. DEDUP — two near-identical files (a 1-byte edit) share ~all blocks, so\n//!      the second backup adds only the local region, not the whole file.\n//!   2. EXACT RESTORE — restoring a manifest yields the original bytes bit-for-\n//!      bit (round-trip identity), which is the recoverability guarantee.\n//!\n//! This file is the pure no_std core: the store is behind a [`BlockStore`] trait\n//! so a real append-log / R2 backend can drop in later (product/infra scope).\n//! One implementation ships here:\n//!   - [`MemStore`] — in-memory `BTreeMap` (tests / single-node local).\n//! The disk-backed [`FileBlockStore`] lives in the kernel shim\n//! (`kernel/src/backup.rs`) because it needs `std::fs`/`std::path`; it re-exports\n//! this module via `pub use dowiz_core::backup::*;`.\n\nuse crate::chunker::Chunker;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::string::String;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\n\n/// Content-address of a block: the chunker's sha3_256 id.\npub type Hash = [u8; 32];\n\n/// Pluggable content-addressed block store. Put is idempotent: storing a block\n/// whose id already exists is a no-op (that IS the dedup). Get returns the raw\n/// bytes for a previously-stored id.\npub trait BlockStore {\n    /// Store `bytes` under `id`. Returns `true` iff this was a NEW block\n    /// (i.e. it deduped away when `false`).\n    fn put(&mut self, id: Hash, bytes: &[u8]) -> bool;\n    /// Fetch bytes for `id`, if present.\n    fn get(&self, id: &Hash) -> Option<&[u8]>;\n    /// Fetch owned bytes for `id`, if present. Disk-backed stores (which cannot\n    /// return a borrowed slice tied to `&self`) override this directly; the\n    /// default impl just clones what `get` returns so `MemStore` is unchanged.\n    fn get_owned(&self, id: &Hash) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.get(id).map(|s| s.to_vec())\n    }\n    /// Number of distinct blocks held.\n    fn len(&self) -> usize;\n    /// True when no blocks are held.\n    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.len() == 0\n    }\n    /// Remove a block by `id`, if present. Returns the evicted bytes when a\n    /// block was actually removed. Default impl returns `None` (a store that\n    /// does not support removal is logically unbounded and MUST bound itself\n    /// elsewhere). `MemStore`/`FileBlockStore` provide real impls so the\n    /// response cache (HARNESS §3.2 / audit A3) can evict LRU when over cap.\n    fn remove(&mut self, _id: &Hash) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        None\n    }\n}\n\n/// In-memory content-addressed store (for tests / single-node local-first use).\n#[derive(Default, Debug, Clone)]\npub struct MemStore {\n    map: BTreeMap<Hash, Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\nimpl MemStore {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        MemStore {\n            map: BTreeMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n    /// Total bytes physically retained (sum of unique block sizes) — the real\n    /// on-disk cost after dedup.\n    pub fn stored_bytes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.map.values().map(|v| v.len()).sum()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl BlockStore for MemStore {\n    fn put(&mut self, id: Hash, bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        if self.map.contains_key(&id) {\n            false\n        } else {\n            self.map.insert(id, bytes.to_vec());\n            true\n        }\n    }\n    fn get(&self, id: &Hash) -> Option<&[u8]> {\n        self.map.get(id).map(|v| v.as_slice())\n    }\n    fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.map.len()\n    }\n    fn remove(&mut self, id: &Hash) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        self.map.remove(id)\n    }\n}\n\n/// An ordered list of block ids that reconstructs one file. Restoring it\n/// concatenates `store.get(id)` for each id in order.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Manifest {\n    pub blocks: Vec<Hash>,\n    /// Total logical size (bytes) of the original stream — a restore check.\n    pub total_len: usize,\n}\n\n/// Result of a backup: the manifest plus dedup accounting for THIS backup.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct BackupStats {\n    /// Blocks the chunker produced for this stream (with repeats).\n    pub total_blocks: usize,\n    /// Blocks that were NEW to the store (physically written).\n    pub new_blocks: usize,\n    /// Blocks that already existed (deduped away).\n    pub deduped_blocks: usize,\n}\n\nimpl BackupStats {\n    /// Fraction of this backup's blocks that deduped (0.0..=1.0).\n    pub fn dedup_ratio(&self) -> f64 {\n        if self.total_blocks == 0 {\n            0.0\n        } else {\n            self.deduped_blocks as f64 / self.total_blocks as f64\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Lowercase hex encode of a 32-byte hash (no dependency, no_std).\npub fn hex_encode(id: &[u8; 32]) -> String {\n    const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";\n    let mut s = String::with_capacity(64);\n    for &b in id {\n        s.push(HEX[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);\n        s.push(HEX[(b & 0x0f) as usize] as char);\n    }\n    s\n}\n\n/// Parse a 64-char lowercase-hex string into a `[u8; 32]`. Errors on wrong\n/// length or non-hex characters (used when scanning the on-disk `blocks/` tree\n/// so stray files are ignored rather than crashing the loader).\npub fn parse_hex32(s: &str) -> Result<[u8; 32], ()> {\n    if s.len() != 64 {\n        return Err(());\n    }\n    let bytes = s.as_bytes();\n    let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n    for i in 0..32 {\n        let hi = match val(bytes[i * 2]) {\n            Some(v) => v,\n            None => return Err(()),\n        };\n        let lo = match val(bytes[i * 2 + 1]) {\n            Some(v) => v,\n            None => return Err(()),\n        };\n        out[i] = (hi << 4) | lo;\n    }\n    Ok(out)\n}\n\nfn val(c: u8) -> Option<u8> {\n    match c {\n        b'0'..=b'9' => Some(c - b'0'),\n        b'a'..=b'f' => Some(c - b'a' + 10),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// The backup organ: owns a chunker config + a content-addressed store.\npub struct BackupOrgan<S: BlockStore> {\n    chunker: Chunker,\n    store: S,\n}\n\nimpl<S: BlockStore> BackupOrgan<S> {\n    /// Build with an explicit chunker + store. `min`/`max`/`bits` tune CDC.\n    pub fn new(store: S, min: usize, max: usize, bits: u32) -> Self {\n        BackupOrgan {\n            chunker: Chunker::new(min, max, bits),\n            store,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Back up `data`: chunk → store unique blocks → return manifest + stats.\n    /// Idempotent at the block level, so re-backing identical content is free.\n    pub fn backup(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> (Manifest, BackupStats) {\n        let blocks = self.chunker.chunk(data);\n        let mut manifest = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());\n        let mut new_blocks = 0usize;\n        let mut deduped = 0usize;\n        // Guard against intra-stream repeats double-counting a physical write.\n        let mut written_this_call: BTreeMap<Hash, ()> = BTreeMap::new();\n        for blk in &blocks {\n            let already = self.store.get_owned(&blk.id).is_some();\n            if already {\n                deduped += 1;\n            } else if written_this_call.contains_key(&blk.id) {\n                // repeated block within THIS same stream: not a fresh write\n                deduped += 1;\n            } else {\n                let is_new = self.store.put(blk.id, &blk.bytes);\n                if is_new {\n                    new_blocks += 1;\n                    written_this_call.insert(blk.id, ());\n                } else {\n                    deduped += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            manifest.push(blk.id);\n        }\n        let stats = BackupStats {\n            total_blocks: blocks.len(),\n            new_blocks,\n            deduped_blocks: deduped,\n        };\n        (\n            Manifest {\n                blocks: manifest,\n                total_len: data.len(),\n            },\n            stats,\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Restore the original bytes from a manifest. Returns `Err` if any block id\n    /// is missing from the store (corrupt / incomplete backup) or the restored\n    /// length disagrees with the manifest's recorded length.\n    pub fn restore(&self, manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<Vec<u8>, RestoreError> {\n        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(manifest.total_len);\n        for id in &manifest.blocks {\n            // Prefer `get_owned` so disk-backed stores return their own bytes\n            // (FileBlockStore additionally re-hashes for content-address\n            // integrity). Falls back to the borrowed `get` otherwise.\n            match self.store.get_owned(id) {\n                Some(bytes) => out.extend_from_slice(&bytes),\n                None => return Err(RestoreError::MissingBlock(*id)),\n            }\n        }\n        if out.len() != manifest.total_len {\n            return Err(RestoreError::LengthMismatch {\n                expected: manifest.total_len,\n                got: out.len(),\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n\n    /// Borrow the store (e.g. for physical-size accounting).\n    pub fn store(&self) -> &S {\n        &self.store\n    }\n}\n\n/// Production caller for the Tier-B4 backup organ.\n///\n/// The `BackupOrgan` (content-addressed CDC + dedup + byte-identical\n/// restore) backs up a hub-state snapshot (sealed into the content-addressed\n/// store as a manifest + deduped blocks) and later restores it byte-for-byte\n/// (the P68 M4 local-rollback / pre-promote-snapshot cycle, which stores the\n/// state plaintext on the vendor's own box). It returns the dedup stats so a\n/// caller can observe that an unchanged re-snapshot adds no new physical blocks.\n///\n/// Fail-closed: a corrupt/missing snapshot restore yields `Err`, never\n/// partial or garbage bytes (the `RestoreError` contract is preserved).\npub fn snapshot_and_restore_local<S: BlockStore>(\n    organ: &mut BackupOrgan<S>,\n    state: &[u8],\n) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, BackupStats), RestoreError> {\n    let (manifest, stats) = organ.backup(state);\n    let restored = organ.restore(&manifest)?;\n    Ok((restored, stats))\n}\n\n/// Why a restore failed (fail-closed: never returns partial/garbage bytes).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum RestoreError {\n    MissingBlock(Hash),\n    LengthMismatch { expected: usize, got: usize },\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn sample(n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n        // deterministic pseudo-random bytes (LCG) — reproducible, no entropy\n        let mut x: u64 = 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0;\n        (0..n)\n            .map(|_| {\n                x = x\n                    .wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005)\n                    .wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);\n                (x >> 33) as u8\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Round-trip identity: back up → restore yields the EXACT original bytes.\n    #[test]\n    fn restore_is_byte_identical() {\n        let data = sample(120_000);\n        let mut organ = BackupOrgan::new(MemStore::new(), 1024, 32 * 1024, 12);\n        let (manifest, _stats) = organ.backup(&data);\n        let restored = organ.restore(&manifest).expect("restore ok");\n        assert_eq!(restored, data, "restore must be byte-identical");\n        assert_eq!(restored.len(), manifest.total_len);\n    }\n\n    /// DEDUP across a 1-byte edit: backing up file B (differs from A by one\n    /// byte in the middle) reuses nearly every block from A. New physical\n    /// blocks for B must be a tiny fraction; dedup ratio > 90%.\n    /// AND both restore byte-identically from the SHARED store.\n    #[test]\n    fn one_byte_edit_dedups_over_90pct_and_both_restore() {\n        let file_a = sample(200_000);\n        let mut file_b = file_a.clone();\n        let mid = file_b.len() / 2;\n        file_b[mid] ^= 0xff; // flip a single byte in the middle\n\n        let mut organ = BackupOrgan::new(MemStore::new(), 1024, 32 * 1024, 12);\n\n        // Back up A (all blocks new), then B into the SAME store.\n        let (man_a, stats_a) = organ.backup(&file_a);\n        let (man_b, stats_b) = organ.backup(&file_b);\n\n        // A is the first backup → nothing deduped yet.\n        assert_eq!(stats_a.deduped_blocks, 0);\n        assert!(\n            stats_a.new_blocks > 3,\n            "file A should chunk into many blocks"\n        );\n\n        // B shares almost all of A's blocks: dedup ratio must exceed 0.90.\n        let ratio = stats_b.dedup_ratio();\n        assert!(\n            ratio > 0.90,\n            "dedup ratio too low: {ratio:.4} ({} new / {} total)",\n            stats_b.new_blocks,\n            stats_b.total_blocks\n        );\n\n        // Only a small local region is physically new for B.\n        assert!(\n            stats_b.new_blocks <= 3,\n            "expected <=3 new blocks for a 1-byte edit, got {}",\n            stats_b.new_blocks\n        );\n\n        // Both files restore byte-identically from the shared, deduped store.\n        let restored_a = organ.restore(&man_a).expect("restore A");\n        let restored_b = organ.restore(&man_b).expect("restore B");\n        assert_eq!(restored_a, file_a, "A must restore exactly");\n        assert_eq!(restored_b, file_b, "B must restore exactly");\n\n        // Storage saving is real: unique bytes retained < sum of both files.\n        let stored = organ.store().stored_bytes();\n        assert!(\n            stored < file_a.len() + file_b.len(),\n            "store did not dedup: {stored} >= {}",\n            file_a.len() + file_b.len()\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Re-backing up IDENTICAL content is 100% dedup (idempotent organ).\n    #[test]\n    fn identical_rebackup_fully_dedups() {\n        let data = sample(60_000);\n        let mut organ = BackupOrgan::new(MemStore::new(), 1024, 32 * 1024, 12);\n        let (_m1, _s1) = organ.backup(&data);\n        let store_len_after_first = organ.store().len();\n        let (_m2, s2) = organ.backup(&data);\n        assert_eq!(s2.new_blocks, 0, "re-backup must write no new blocks");\n        assert_eq!(s2.dedup_ratio(), 1.0);\n        assert_eq!(\n            organ.store().len(),\n            store_len_after_first,\n            "store size unchanged on identical re-backup"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Fail-closed restore: a missing block yields Err, never garbage bytes.\n organ.restore(&manifest).unwrap_err();\n        assert_eq!(err, RestoreError::MissingBlock([0xAB; 32]));\n    }\n\n    /// Empty stream: valid, zero blocks, restores to empty.\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_stream_round_trips() {\n        let mut organ = BackupOrgan::new(MemStore::new(), 1024, 32 * 1024, 12);\n        let (manifest, stats) = organ.backup(&[]);\n        assert_eq!(stats.total_blocks, 0);\n        assert!(manifest.blocks.is_empty());\n        let restored = organ.restore(&manifest).expect("empty restore");\n        assert!(restored.is_empty());\n ## 16764 · /root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/decision/mod.rs · LongTerm
```

Summary: mod · 594 lines

```record
4	source	files	/root/dowiz/crates/dowiz-core/src/decision/mod.rs	mod · 594 lines	//! decision/mod.rs — no_std core MoE mesh DecisionUnit family (BLUEPRINT-P-F, Layer F).\n//!\n//! Compile firewall (mirrors `ports/llm.rs`): ZERO network / HTTP / JSON / serde. The oracle\n//! (LLM) lives OUTSIDE this module — it only ever emits unit *source* that a future import gate\n//! (`import_unit`, §4.2) admits. This module defines the closed capability types, the\n//! `DecisionUnit` family abstraction, the by-`DomainTag` registry, and the two structural red-lines\n//! of the phase:\n//!   1. **NO-COURIER-SCORING** — routing is a `match` on a declared `DomainTag`, never a numeric\n//!      rank. `DomainTag` derives `PartialEq/Eq/Hash` only (NOT `Ord`/`PartialOrd`): there is no\n//!      ordering to compare, so a quality-router is *unrepresentable*, not merely forbidden.\n//!   2. **Money red-line** — every `Pricing` unit is `money_gated`. It may register and replay\n//!      green (reach `Live`), but `decide()` answers `Escalate` until an explicit operator-activation\n//!      event flips `OperatorActivation::Pending -> Activated`. It NEVER auto-adopts (§6.3-A6).\n//!\n//! `FraudAuth` output is `FraudVerdict { NotAnomalous | Escalate }` — an auto-block verdict is\n//! unrepresentable by construction (§2.1, §7).\n//!\n//! Host-only seam: the FDR-shadow telemetry method `decide_with_shadow` (item 51) is deliberately\n//! NOT in this core — it is the ONLY `std`/kernel-side dependency (it writes `crate::fdr::ring`\n//! records). It lives as a free function in the kernel shim `dowiz-kernel/src/decision/mod.rs`.\n\n/// The import-time verify-before-persist gate (BLUEPRINT-P-F §4.2, rung-2).\npub mod import;\n\nuse alloc::boxed::Box;\nuse alloc::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse alloc::vec::Vec;\nuse core::fmt::Debug;\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// §3 types (verbatim contract surface)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Closed set of decision-procedure families ("domain experts"). Extension = a code change +\n/// review, deliberately — an open string tag would be an unreviewed capability grant.\n/// NO ordering, NO numeric rank: routing is `match`, never comparison (NO-COURIER-SCORING).\n///\n/// NOTE: this enum intentionally derives only `PartialEq, Eq, Hash` — **not** `Ord`/`PartialOrd`.\n/// The absence of an order relation is the type-level enforcement of the no-courier-scoring law:\n/// a router cannot rank two families because the language gives it no `cmp` to call.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum DomainTag {\n    Dispatch,\n    EtaGeo,\n    Pricing,\n    FraudAuth,\n    MenuInventory,\n    Harness,\n}\n\nimpl DomainTag {\n    /// Stable, typed string for telemetry (native `metrics::LogEvent` lane, D8).\n    /// NOT a capability grant — just the closed discriminant rendered as text.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            DomainTag::Dispatch => "Dispatch",\n            DomainTag::EtaGeo => "EtaGeo",\n            DomainTag::Pricing => "Pricing",\n            DomainTag::FraudAuth => "FraudAuth",\n            DomainTag::MenuInventory => "MenuInventory",\n            DomainTag::Harness => "Harness",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Identity of a question shape: sha3-256 over (DomainTag discriminant ‖ canonical input/output\n/// schema). Content-derived — two hubs naming the same shape get the same id with no registry.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub struct ShapeId(pub [u8; 32]);\n\n/// Logical epoch for a compiled unit. Lamport-style monotone counter — NEVER wall-clock\n/// (Batch 2 §7 HLC rejection stands). Merge law = max (§4.1). `Ord` is allowed here: an epoch is\n/// a monotone logical counter, categorically NOT a quality rank.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]\npub struct UnitEpoch(pub u64);\n\n/// Provenance + lineage record for one compiled unit version. Registered as an event in the\n/// EXISTING content-addressed sha3 event log — `content_id`/`prev` ARE the lineage (§4.3);\n/// there is no second DAG type anywhere in this design.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DecisionUnitMeta {\n    pub shape: ShapeId,\n    pub domain: DomainTag,\n    pub epoch: UnitEpoch,\n    /// sha3 of the harvested instance set the unit was compiled from and must replay against.\n    pub instance_set_hash: [u8; 32],\n    /// sha3 content-address of THIS version's artifact (source + tests), in the one log.\n    pub content_id: [u8; 32],\n    /// Previous version's content-id — rollback lineage inside the same log. None = genesis.\n    pub prev_content_id: Option<[u8; 32]>,\n    /// Money red-line: true for every Pricing unit (and any unit whose output moves money).\n    /// A money-gated unit CANNOT reach a callable Live via import alone — operator activation required.\n    pub money_gated: bool,\n}\n\nimpl DecisionUnitMeta {\n    /// Construct meta. `money_gated` is derived from `domain` (Pricing ⇒ true) — set by the\n    /// *domain*, never by the unit author (§7). Lineage fields default to genesis/zero; the import\n    /// gate fills them from the content-addressed log.\n    pub fn new(domain: DomainTag, epoch: UnitEpoch) -> Self {\n        let money_gated = domain == DomainTag::Pricing;\n        Self {\n            shape: ShapeId([0u8; 32]),\n            domain,\n            epoch,\n            instance_set_hash: [0u8; 32],\n            content_id: [0u8; 32],\n            prev_content_id: None,\n            money_gated,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Unit lifecycle. The ONLY production path to `Live` is the import gate (`import_unit`, §4.2);\n/// `new` is the in-kernel constructor used by tests and by that gate. `Stale ⇒ Escalate`\n/// unconditionally (D5): there is no `Stale -> Answer` transition, so a stale unit cannot answer.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum UnitState {\n    Live,\n    Stale,\n    Rejected,\n}\n\n/// Reuse P29 §2.1 verbatim — never a silent guess:\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Decision<T> {\n    Answer(T),\n    Escalate(EscalateReason),\n}\n\n/// Why a unit declined to answer. First-class on every `Decision` (P29 §2.1).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum EscalateReason {\n    /// Unit is not in a callable state (Stale / Rejected), or not operator-activated.\n    NotLive,\n    /// Money-gated unit is registered + replay-green but the operator has NOT activated it (§6.3-A6).\n    MoneyGateLocked,\n    /// A watched input drifted (GapWire) — recompile required before answering.\n    WatchedInputDrift,\n    /// The input is outside the unit's declared capability shape.\n    OutOfShape,\n}\n\n/// Integer money — basis points. No float money type exists in this module on purpose.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct FeeBps(pub u32);\n\n/// The artifact bound = the transport bound. Pinned to the same literal as\n/// bebop2 `sync_pull.rs:159` MAX_SYNC_PAYLOAD; the cross-repo drift test (§6.2 D6) keeps them\n/// equal — a unit that cannot ride the transport may not exist.\npub const MAX_UNIT_ARTIFACT_BYTES: usize = 1 << 20;\n\n/// Harvest threshold, inherited from P29 §2.4(b) — tunable, named, never magic.\npub const HARVEST_MIN_INSTANCES: usize = 10;\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Operator-activation gate (money red-line, §6.3-A6)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Distinct state the Pricing family requires before it can be invoked. A money-gated unit\n/// reaches `Live` (registered + replay-green) but stays `Pending` until an explicit operator\n/// event calls `activate_operator`. It must NOT auto-adopt.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum OperatorActivation {\n    Pending,\n    Activated,\n}\n\n/// Error returned when an operator-activation attempt violates the gate's preconditions.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum GateError {\n    /// Only a money-gated (Pricing) unit requires operator activation.\n    NotMoneyGated,\n    /// The unit must be registered + replay-green (`Live`) before activation is meaningful.\n    NotLive,\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Family I/O (typed, closed)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DispatchInput {\n    pub pickup_adjacent: bool,\n    pub window_overlap: bool,\n    pub capacity_ok: bool,\n}\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DispatchOut {\n    pub batch: bool,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct EtaGeoInput {\n    pub distance_band: u8,\n    pub hour: u8,\n    pub weather_class: u8,\n}\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct EtaBand(pub u8);\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct PricingInput {\n    pub zone: u8,\n    pub cart_band: u8,\n    pub hour: u8,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct FraudInput {\n    pub pattern_score: u32,\n    pub velocity: u32,\n}\n/// FraudAuth output — escalate-biased. An **auto-block** verdict is UNREPRESENTABLE: the type\n/// only admits `NotAnomalous` or `Escalate`, so a unit that would silently block can never be\n/// written (§2.1, §7). The human/operator still decides on escalate.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FraudVerdict {\n    NotAnomalous,\n    Escalate(EscalateReason),\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct MenuInput {\n    pub item: u32,\n    pub stock: u32,\n    pub is_86: bool,\n}\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct MenuOut {\n    pub order_safe: bool,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct HarnessInput {\n    pub job: u8,\n}\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct HarnessOut {\n    pub route_tier: u8,\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecisionUnit family type (P29 §2.1: pure decide(), typed input, closed output, Escalate first-class)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A compiled ns-native decision procedure. Pure: no I/O, no mutation, deterministic. `Escalate`\n/// is first-class. Constructed ONLY via `new` (tests/in-kernel) or the import gate (§4.2) — there\n/// is no public `Live` literal to fake a callable unit without evidence.\npub struct DecisionUnit<I, O> {\n    pub meta: DecisionUnitMeta,\n    pub state: UnitState,\n    pub operator_activation: OperatorActivation,\n    proc: Box<dyn Fn(&I) -> Decision<O> + Send + Sync>,\n}\n\nimpl<I, O> DecisionUnit<I, O> {\n    /// In-kernel constructor. `money_gated` is forced from `domain` (Pricing ⇒ true); non-money\n    /// units start already `Activated` so the gate never blocks them.\n    pub fn new(\n        domain: DomainTag,\n        epoch: UnitEpoch,\n        proc: impl Fn(&I) -> Decision<O> + Send + Sync + 'static,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let meta = DecisionUnitMeta::new(domain, epoch);\n        let operator_activation = if meta.money_gated {\n            OperatorActivation::Pending\n        } else {\n            OperatorActivation::Activated\n        };\n        Self {\n            meta,\n            state: UnitState::Live,\n            operator_activation,\n            proc: Box::new(proc),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Pure decision. Returns `Escalate` when the unit is not callable: `Stale`/`Rejected`, or a\n    /// money-gated unit whose operator has not yet activated it.\n    pub fn decide(&self, input: &I) -> Decision<O> {\n        if self.state != UnitState::Live {\n            return Decision::Escalate(EscalateReason::NotLive);\n        }\n        if self.meta.money_gated && self.operator_activation != OperatorActivation::Activated {\n            return Decision::Escalate(EscalateReason::MoneyGateLocked);\n        }\n        (self.proc)(input)\n    }\n\n    /// True iff this unit may currently answer (Live AND, for money units, operator-activated).\n    pub fn can_answer(&self) -> bool {\n        self.state == UnitState::Live\n            && (!self.meta.money_gated || self.operator_activation == OperatorActivation::Activated)\n    }\n\n    /// Operator-activation event (§6.3-A6). Money-gated units MUST be `Live` (registered + replay\n    /// green) before this succeeds; it flips `Pending -> Activated` and unlocks `decide()`.\n    /// Calling it on a non-money unit is a misuse — returns `NotMoneyGated`.\n    pub fn activate_operator(&mut self) -> Result<(), GateError> {\n        if !self.meta.money_gated {\n            return Err(GateError::NotMoneyGated);\n        }\n        if self.state != UnitState::Live {\n            return Err(GateError::NotLive);\n        }\n        self.operator_activation = OperatorActivation::Activated;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Family registry — map DomainTag -> registered units (code-change + review path)\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Heterogeneous, type-preserving container for one registered unit. Each variant carries the\n/// fully-typed `DecisionUnit` for its family, so the closed output type (e.g. `FraudVerdict`)\n/// survives into the call site. `AnyUnit` is also the routing surface: selecting by `DomainTag`\n/// is an exhaustive `match` over these six variants — there is no numeric index to rank on.\npub enum AnyUnit {\n    Dispatch(DecisionUnit<DispatchInput, DispatchOut>),\n    EtaGeo(DecisionUnit<EtaGeoInput, EtaBand>),\n    Pricing(DecisionUnit<PricingInput, FeeBps>),\n    FraudAuth(DecisionUnit<FraudInput, FraudVerdict>),\n    MenuInventory(DecisionUnit<MenuInput, MenuOut>),\n    Harness(DecisionUnit<HarnessInput, HarnessOut>),\n}\n\nimpl AnyUnit {\n    /// The closed capability this unit answers — used as the registry key.\n    pub fn domain(&self) -> DomainTag {\n        match self {\n            AnyUnit::Dispatch(_) => DomainTag::Dispatch,\n            AnyUnit::EtaGeo(_) => DomainTag::EtaGeo,\n            AnyUnit::Pricing(_) => DomainTag::Pricing,\n            AnyUnit::FraudAuth(_) => DomainTag::FraudAuth,\n            AnyUnit::MenuInventory(_) => DomainTag::MenuInventory,\n            AnyUnit::Harness(_) => DomainTag::Harness,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Callable now? (Live, and operator-activated if money-gated.)\n    pub fn is_live_and_active(&self) -> bool {\n        match self {\n            AnyUnit::Dispatch(u) => u.can_answer(),\n            AnyUnit::EtaGeo(u) => u.can_answer(),\n            AnyUnit::Pricing(u) => u.can_answer(),\n            AnyUnit::FraudAuth(u) => u.can_answer(),\n            AnyUnit::MenuInventory(u) => u.can_answer(),\n            AnyUnit::Harness(u) => u.can_answer(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Domain family registry. `register` is the reviewed code path — a unit is admitted by name, into\n/// the slot keyed by its `DomainTag`. Routing is a `BTreeMap` lookup + an exhaustive `match`\n/// (`route_live`), never a comparison of quality.\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct DecisionRegistry {\n    units: BTreeMap<DomainTag, Vec<AnyUnit>>,\n}\n\nimpl DecisionRegistry {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Admit a unit (code-change + review path). Placed under its `DomainTag` slot.\n    pub fn register(&mut self, unit: AnyUnit) {\n        self.units.entry(unit.domain()).or_default().push(unit);\n    }\n\n    /// Routing law: lookup on `DomainTag` — a match on a declared capability, never a rank compare.\n    /// Returns the first callable unit registered for `tag`, if any.\n    pub fn route_live(&self, tag: DomainTag) -> Option<&AnyUnit> {\n        self.units\n            .get(&tag)\n            .and_then(|v| v.iter().find(|u| u.is_live_and_active()))\n    }\n\n    /// Count of callable units under `tag` (registry-introspection / telemetry helper).\n    pub fn count_live(&self, tag: DomainTag) -> usize {\n        self.units\n            .get(&tag)\n            .map(|v| v.iter().filter(|u| u.is_live_and_active()).count())\n            .unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Epoch max-merge (§4.1) — join-semilattice: commutative, associative, idempotent.\n// Tiebreak is on content-id BYTES (a content address), NOT on a quality score.\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Merge two unit metas into the winning version. Higher `epoch` wins; on equal epoch the\n/// lexicographically-lower `content_id` wins (deterministic, no scoring). Identical ⇒ idempotent.\n/// This is a join-semilattice, so gossip convergence is order-independent (§4.1).\npub fn merge_meta(a: &DecisionUnitMeta, b: &DecisionUnitMeta) -> DecisionUnitMeta {\n    debug_assert_eq!(a.domain, b.domain, "merge_meta called across domains");\n    use core::cmp::Ordering;\n    match a.epoch.0.cmp(&b.epoch.0) {\n        Ordering::Greater => a.clone(),\n        Ordering::Less => b.clone(),\n        Ordering::Equal => {\n            if a.content_id <= b.content_id {\n                a.clone()\n            } else {\n                b.clone()\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests — spec-first (RED→GREEN). Three invariants asserted:\n//   A) Pricing unit is NOT invocable before operator activation.\n//   B) FraudAuth cannot return an auto-block variant (unrepresentable by construction).\n//   C) Routing by `DomainTag` is a match, never a rank compare (`DomainTag` has no `Ord`).\n//   D) Epoch merge is a join-semilattice.\n//   E) A Stale unit answers `Escalate` unconditionally (unrepresentable Stale→Answer).\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn pricing_unit() -> DecisionUnit<PricingInput, FeeBps> {\n        DecisionUnit::new(DomainTag::Pricing, UnitEpoch(1), |_in: &PricingInput| {\n            Decision::Answer(FeeBps(50))\n        })\n    }\n\n    fn fraud_unit() -> DecisionUnit<FraudInput, FraudVerdict> {\n        DecisionUnit::new(DomainTag::FraudAuth, UnitEpoch(1), |_in: &FraudInput| {\n            Decision::Answer(FraudVerdict::NotAnomalous)\n        })\n    }\n\n    // A) Money red-line: a Pricing unit that is Live + replay-green is still NOT callable until the\n    //    operator activates it.\n    #[test]\n    fn pricing_not_invocable_before_activation() {\n        let mut unit = pricing_unit();\n        assert!(\n            unit.meta.money_gated,\n            "Pricing must be money_gated by domain"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(unit.operator_activation, OperatorActivation::Pending);\n\n        // Registered + replay-green (Live) but not yet activated ⇒ Escalate, never an Answer.\n        assert!(matches!(\n            unit.decide(&PricingInput {\n                zone: 1,\n                cart_band: 2,\n                hour: 9\n            }),\n            Decision::Escalate(EscalateReason::MoneyGateLocked)\n        ));\n        assert!(!unit.can_answer());\n\n        // Operator event flips the gate.\n        assert!(unit.activate_operator().is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(unit.operator_activation, OperatorActivation::Activated);\n        assert!(unit.can_answer());\n        assert!(matches!(\n            unit.decide(&PricingInput {\n                zone: 1,\n                cart_band: 2,\n                hour: 9\n            }),\n            Decision::Answer(FeeBps(50))\n        ));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn non_money_unit_has_no_gate() {\n        let mut unit = fraud_unit();\n        // Non-money units are Activated from construction; activation is a no-op misuse.\n        assert!(!unit.meta.money_gated);\n        assert_eq!(unit.operator_activation, OperatorActivation::Activated);\n        assert_eq!(unit.activate_operator(), Err(GateError::NotMoneyGated));\n        assert!(unit.can_answer());\n    }\n\n    // B) FraudAuth cannot auto-block: the closed output type has no `Block` variant, so the\n    //    exhaustive match below compiles ONLY because no such variant exists. This is the proof\n    //    that an auto-block verdict is unrepresentable.\n    #[test]\n    fn fraudauth_cannot_autoblock() {\n        let unit = fraud_unit();\n        let out = unit.decide(&FraudInput {\n            pattern_score: 0,\n            velocity: 0,\n        });\n        // The unit answered; its verdict is one of the two admissible shapes. There is no third\n        // (Block) arm to match, and adding one would break this exhaustive match at compile time.\n        fraud_shape_proof(&match out {\n            Decision::Answer(v) => v,\n            Decision::Escalate(_) => FraudVerdict::Escalate(EscalateReason::NotLive),\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// Compile-time proof: `FraudVerdict` admits exactly `NotAnomalous | Escalate`. A `Block`\n    /// variant would make this non-exhaustive and fail to compile.\n    fn fraud_shape_proof(v: &FraudVerdict) {\n        match v {\n            FraudVerdict::NotAnomalous => {}\n            FraudVerdict::Escalate(_) => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    // C) Routing by `DomainTag` is a match, never a rank compare. `DomainTag` does not implement\n    //    `Ord`/`PartialOrd`, so quality-ranking two families is impossible at the type level.\n    #[test]\n    fn routing_is_match_not_rank() {\n        let mut reg = DecisionRegistry::new();\n        reg.register(AnyUnit::Pricing(pricing_unit()));\n        reg.register(AnyUnit::FraudAuth(fraud_unit()));\n\n        // Route by declared capability. A FraudAuth (non-money) unit is callable → found.\n        let f = reg.route_live(DomainTag::FraudAuth);\n        assert!(f.is_some_and(|u| u.domain() == DomainTag::FraudAuth));\n\n        // A Pricing unit is money-gated and NOT yet operator-activated, so it is registered but\n        // NOT callable → route_live returns None (money red-line holds at the routing layer too).\n        assert!(reg.route_live(DomainTag::Pricing).is_none());\n        assert_eq!(reg.count_live(DomainTag::Pricing), 0);\n\n        // A family with no registered unit routes to None — not to a "lower-ranked" fallback.\n        assert!(reg.route_live(DomainTag::Dispatch).is_none());\n\n        // DomainTag carries no ordering: the following would NOT compile (proven by absence):\n        //   let _ = DomainTag::Pricing < DomainTag::FraudAuth;\n        // Routing is therefore a capability lookup, structurally incapable of a quality rank.\n        assert_eq!(reg.count_live(DomainTag::FraudAuth), 1);\n    }\n\n    // E) A Stale unit answers `Escalate` unconditionally; there is no Stale→Answer path.\n    #[test]\n    fn stale_unit_escalates_unconditionally() {\n        let mut unit = fraud_unit();\n        unit.state = UnitState::Stale;\n        assert!(!unit.can_answer());\n        assert!(matches!(\n            unit.decide(&FraudInput {\n                pattern_score: 0,\n                velocity: 0\n            }),\n            Decision::Escalate(EscalateReason::NotLive)\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // D) Epoch merge is a join-semilattice over a small finite domain (commutative, associative,\n    //    idempotent). No scoring input — tiebreak is on content-id bytes only.\n    #[test]\n    fn epoch_merge_is_semilattice() {\n        let domains = [DomainTag::Pricing, DomainTag::FraudAuth];\n        let epochs = [0u64, 1, 2, 3];\n        let cids = [[0u8; 32], [7u8; 32], [255u8; 32]];\n\n        for &d in domains.iter() {\n            for &e1 in epochs.iter() {\n                for &e2 in epochs.iter() {\n                    for &e3 in epochs.iter() {\n                        for &c1 in cids.iter() {\n                            for &c2 in cids.iter() {\n                                for &c3 in cids.iter() {\n                                    let a = meta(d, e1, c1);\n                                    let b = meta(d, e2, c2);\n                                    let c = meta(d, e3, c3);\n\n                                    // commutativity\n                                    assert_eq!(merge_meta(&a, &b), merge_meta(&b, &a));\n                                    // idempotence\n                                    assert_eq!(merge_meta(&a, &a), a);\n                                    // associativity\n                                    let lhs = merge_meta(&merge_meta(&a, &b), &c);\n                                    let rhs = merge_meta(&a, &merge_meta(&b, &c));\n                                    assert_eq!(lhs, rhs);\n                                }\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn meta(d: DomainTag, e: u64, cid: [u8; 32]) -> DecisionUnitMeta {\n        let mut m = DecisionUnitMeta::new(d, UnitEpoch(e));\n        m.content_id = cid;\n        m\n    }\n}\n	16765	-1	-1		7b1fbdd49dcc21272970d5d1bd041b4fdd5ab4447dfcb4ec68555646d1a745c51850750042cdea8f8b43c13b61579e28cc71dd2438680462e973fe47ef8ca9ce6e965c9167da2801d58db002b6bbd56157ea840a24ea5f2ed8ca7ab2ea0fc7acb062f3ce994a70eb88010a97be01cbfc20fd6d2a1f85bb4e1101d658a9203ef3
```
